p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer continues through 1 Corinthians 16 with the devoted leaders, the ones who serve behind the scenes and refresh others. He teaches that it matters who you follow, that unity and music in worship are tied to God’s presence, and that “Anathema” in verse 22 is about not loving the Lord Jesus Christ. He closes by saying that loving Jesus means keeping his commandments and learning how to treat other people, and that making Jesus Lord of your life keeps false leaders from leading you astray.
What does it mean to be alert and stand fast in the faith?

He tells the congregation “you are to … be alert,” not just to come and wait for the minister, and to “stand fast in the faith.” He says the faith is “The Scriptures, in Jesus Christ,” and urges “Have the courage of your convictions. Have the guts to stand up for what the Scriptures say.”
What does it mean to be alert and stand fast in the faith?

Now he goes into the attendees, the members, and devoted leaders. A different area of leadership. We had the young leader, we had the skilled leader, and now we got devoted leaders. And he talks to the congregation and says, “Be alert.” Congregation, you are to what? Be alert. You’re not supposed to come just to wait for the minister to get you into the third heaven and all that. You’re to come in alert. Hallelujah. You’re supposed to live on Monday alert, wide awake. “Stand fast in the faith.” That’s your job, to stand fast in the faith. What faith? The Scriptures, in Jesus Christ. Amen. Don’t be swaying, don’t be swerving. “Be brave,” and “be strong.” Have the courage of your convictions. Have the guts to stand up for what the Scriptures say. The Bible says homosexuality is wrong. Then have the guts to stand up and say, “Jesus and the Bible says this is wrong. I don’t care what Obama says, Bush says, Oprah says, or anybody else. Jesus said it’s wrong, the apostles said it’s wrong. By golly, it’s wrong.”
What does it mean to be alert and stand fast in the faith?
1 Corinthians 16:13-14: Watch, stand fast in the faith, be brave, be strong. Let all that you do be done with love.
Who are the devoted leaders in 1 Corinthians 16, and what do they do?

He says they are not a skilled minister, an apostle with signs and wonders, or a young minister, but “just devoted ministers” who are “addicted to ministry.” He says “Every church needs them,” and he lists cleaning the church, doing the books, mowing the lawn, visiting the sick and inviting people to their homes. He explains that “refresh” means “you relieve someone of the burden, you refresh them.”
Who are the devoted leaders in 1 Corinthians 16, and what do they do?

See, have courage to stand up for truth. Amen. “Let all that you do be done with love.” Love, not works, no harm. “I urge you, brethren,” talking to the church, you know, “the household of Stephanas, the first fruits of [unclear], that they have devoted themselves to the ministry of the saints.” They’re not Apollos, a skilled minister. They’re not the apostles that he talked about earlier with signs and wonders and so forth. They’re not a young minister. They’re just devoted ministers. They’re committed. One definition of the word is they’re addicted. They’re addicted to ministry, that they can’t do without it. How many would like to have that kind of desire in your heart, where you miss the church when you’re gone, even for a good reason, because you’re addicted to it? Hallelujah. These are devoted. They’re committed leaders. Every church needs them and every church should have them. And he tells the congregation to submit to such, “and all who work and labor with us.” See, and then he gives two others: Fortunatus, [unclear]. Yeah. Uh, “refreshed.” See, he said they refreshed me, they supplied what was lacking. It’s like being out plowing the field, you know, and somebody, your wife, comes and brings you a nice cold glass of lemonade. Whoa, refreshes you, and you can get your strength and keep going. Or one of your sons comes out and takes the plow: “Dad, go sit under the tree, I’ll plow for a while.” That would be unique in our homes, wouldn’t it? They can’t even make their bed, let alone plow a field. They think it’s, they think it’s really mean when you ask them, “Take out the garbage.” My gosh, you have to leave your Nintendo game for two minutes to take out the garbage. How horrible! But see, that’s what “refresh” means. It means you relieve someone of the burden, you refresh them. And this is what devoted people do. Without the devoted leaders in a church, the other leaders are very limited in what can be done. Are you there? And so devoted leaders are very important. Committed leaders. You can call them subordinate leaders or whatever you want. Paul calls them devoted, committed people. They clean the church, they clean the bathrooms, they do the books, they, you know, they mow the lawn, they, you know, they do things all the time. They visit the sick, they, you know, they encourage people to come to church and they encourage them after service and so forth. Invite them over to their house. These are devoted leaders.
Who are the devoted leaders in 1 Corinthians 16, and what do they do?

1 Corinthians 16:15-16: I urge you, brethren—you know the household of Stephanas, that it is the firstfruits of Achaia, and that they have devoted themselves to the ministry of the saints— that you also submit to such, and to everyone who works and labors with us. 1 Corinthians 16:17-18: I am glad about the coming of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus, for what was lacking on your part they supplied. For they refreshed my spirit and yours. Therefore acknowledge such men.
How can devoted people help a new Christian?

He says most American Christians are “selfish people” who “don’t know where the hospitality is,” and tells of a couple who “took me under their wing as a young Christian,” fed him, shared the word and called him on Sunday mornings. He says that without them “I don’t know if I would have made it over the hump.”
How can devoted people help a new Christian?

Most American Christians are selfish people. They don’t want their basketball game interfered with. “I, leave me alone. I ain’t invite nobody over.” They never invite anybody over. They don’t know where the hospitality is. And the Bible tells us that we are to be what? Hospitable. Am I talking to the right group? Yeah. See, these are devoted people. I tell you, it was those devoted people. I was telling my brother Gary, the [unclear] were a couple back there that took me under their wing as a young Christian and got me through the hump where Satan was trying to say, “Ah, nothing happened. You know, you just, you know, that’s a bunch of [unclear]. You’re not different,” and all the rest. Man, they took me, invited me over their house, and, you know, they fed me, and we sang songs, and they shared the word with me. And they would call me up and said, “Are you coming to church?” And I tell you, I was in bed fast asleep. “Oh yeah, I’m coming.” I wasn’t planning on coming to church, but they called me early Sunday morning: “Are you coming to church today?” “Oh yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.” Man, I had to get out of that bed and [unclear]. I needed that. They never spoke that I know of, they never preached a message. I never heard one of them prophesy or speak in tongues and interpret or anything else. But let me tell you, without them I don’t know if I would have made it over the hump. I needed those kind of people. And when I got to their home, they were an example of a Christian. And I love those people, and I tell you, I’m going to greet them heavily when I get to heaven. They were very important to my growth in God. Leadership is important, very important. Don’t think it’s not important where you choose to go to church and the leadership there. Very important. “My people, children are their oppressors.” You know, children are running most homes today. Oh man, we go to little leagues, we go to dance recitals, we, you know, the Americans think that they are going to ingrain character in their kids by all this secular involvement.
Are children running American homes, and do sports build character?

He says “children are running most homes today,” and that Americans think they will “ingrain character in their kids” through secular activities. He says that growing up in baseball and football leagues “I didn’t see one kid change,” and that the husband “is one of the most neglected members of the home.”
Are children running American homes, and do sports build character?

I grew up in Detroit. I was in those baseball leagues and football leagues and so forth. I didn’t see one kid change. Not one. We just played sports, and when we got done we went back to our neighborhood and dared anybody to bother us. You know it’s true. Children, I mean, the husband in most American homes is one of the most neglected members of the home, because the kids, even though he may work six days a week, the kids just consume their time. Are you out there? Hallelujah, that’s one for the men.
Are children running American homes, and do sports build character?
Isaiah 3:12: As for My people, children are their oppressors, And women rule over them. O My people! Those who lead you cause you to err, And destroy the way of your paths.”
What does he say about leading in the home?

He says “if you don’t let Jesus run your life, your woman will,” and that “a good woman wants a good man who’s got control of his life.” To the women he says “you got to be teachable and you got to learn to submit to God’s structure,” and “It’s not your job to make him what he’s supposed to be.”
What does he say about leading in the home?

“Women rule over them.” Now here’s one, not for the men. Man, if you don’t let Jesus run your life, your woman will. God created us to be men. A good woman wants a good man who’s got control of his life, heading somewhere down the road, following the examples that the Bible says. And if you don’t do it, you’re going to be following your woman, and they’re going to be following their emotions, and I tell you, disaster after disaster comes when that’s set in motions. Hallelujah. Now, for you women looking at me like that, you want me to balance this out? Well, you know, those women can lead too. Yes you can, and you are a leader in the home. Let me tell you, if you’re going to be a good leader, you got to be teachable, and you got to learn to submit to God’s structure. You got to learn to expect God to make that man what he’s supposed to be. It’s not your job to make him what he’s supposed to be. Boy, that was good. That turns us off. Say, “You be an example. Show us. You don’t be telling us to do things that you’re not doing.” Yeah. Hallelujah. “Oh my people, those who lead you cause you to err and destroy the way of your paths.” Again in Isaiah 9:16, “The leaders of these people cause them to err, and they that are led of them are,” what? Destroyed. Who your leader is is important. Who you’re following, the doctrine. That’s why I tell you, go back to the apostles, go back to Jesus. Like the Berean church. They didn’t believe those apostles. They took what they said and went to the Scriptures to see if the apostles were telling them the
What does he say about leading in the home?
Isaiah 9:16: For the leaders of this people cause them to err, And those who are led by them are destroyed.
Why does it matter who your leader is, and what about false prophets?

He quotes “Many pastors have destroyed my vineyard” and “The prophets prophesy falsely,” and says he hears “a lot of junk” in both Pentecostal and Baptist circles. He says “you’re a self-made prophet” if you are not speaking by the leading of the Holy Ghost, and “you can’t blame leaders only, because that’s what they want to hear.”
Why does it matter who your leader is, and what about false prophets?

truth. Amen. “Many pastors have destroyed my vineyard,” Jeremiah 12:10. You think leadership isn’t important? Leadership is very important, and having the essentials, and having the skills is very important, and every leader has to start somewhere in their youth and work their way up. Jeremiah 5:31, “The prophets prophesy falsely.” Good Lord, is that ever true, whether it’s in us Pentecostal circles where we believe in prophecy and we have tongues and interpretation, I hear a lot of junk, or whether you are Baptist and you believe prophecy is just an inspired preacher, I hear a lot of junk. How many have heard a lot of junk? How can you be a prophet? Prophecy means spoken by the inspiration of the Holy Ghost. And if you’re not speaking by the leading of the Holy Ghost, that’s not a, you’re a self-made prophet, you’re not a real one. I don’t care what denomination you’re in. “My people love to have it so.” Here’s the kicker, that’s what the people want to hear. The churches are filling up with preachers that tell them what they want to hear, so you can’t blame leaders only, because that’s what they want to hear. So they find leaders that tell them what they want to hear. But what will you do in the end? What’s the end? The judgment. You got to stand before Christ. What are you going to do? You’re going to say, “Well, I, you know, I followed this guy and he led me astray”? You’re supposed to follow Christ. You’re supposed to follow Paul and Peter and these apostles. You’re not supposed to follow some preacher. He is supposed to follow Christ himself
Why does it matter who your leader is, and what about false prophets?

Jeremiah 12:10: “Many rulers have destroyed My vineyard, They have trodden My portion underfoot; They have made My pleasant portion a desolate wilderness. Jeremiah 5:31: The prophets prophesy falsely, And the priests rule by their own power; And My people love to have it so. But what will you do in the end?
How do I find a good pastor, and is a good leader enough?

He quotes Jeremiah 3:15, “I will give you pastors according to my heart, which will feed you with knowledge and understanding,” and says “They are out there. You need to find them.” He adds that you can have a good leader and still live a wrong life, as King Jotham “did what was right in the sight of the Lord” but “the people still acted corruptly.”
How do I find a good pastor, and is a good leader enough?

and preach the Scriptures. Amen. Jeremiah 3:15, “I will give you pastors according to my heart, which will feed you with knowledge and understanding.” They are out there. You need to find them. Can I hear an amen? Young believers need to especially find somebody that can teach them the word of God, whether it’s devoted leaders that know the word of God, whether it’s young leaders that know the word of God, or whether it’s skilled leaders that know the word of God. They got to seek out that thing and get under good teaching so they can grow and be strong. Now, you can have a good leader and you can still live a wrong life. 2 Chronicles 27:2, King Jotham “did what was right in the sight of the Lord,” but the people still acted corruptly. They didn’t follow the leader, they did their own thing.
How do I find a good pastor, and is a good leader enough?

Jeremiah 3:15: And I will give you shepherds according to My heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding. 2 Chronicles 27:2: And he did what was right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father Uzziah had done (although he did not enter the temple of the LORD). But still the people acted corruptly.
Is being a believer enough if I do not follow what the Bible teaches?

He says Paul was a good leader, yet the Corinthians were doing “incest, idols,” and “the choice is yours” whether to follow the Bible’s instructions or “do your own thing.” He says Americans think “because I’m a believer, everything’s okay,” but “faith in being a son of God is not the end of it.”
Is being a believer enough if I do not follow what the Bible teaches?

Paul’s church growth seminar to the Corinthian church. Was Paul a good leader? Absolutely. Does this letter to the Corinthian church show us they’re following him? No, they’re doing incest, idols. Oh man, they’re doing all kinds of things, and they had a great leader. The bottom line, church, is the choice is yours. You can choose to get a good leader and you can choose to follow the instructions of the Bible that that leader teaches, or you can choose to do your own thing. And what will you do in the end? You got to stand before Christ and give an answer, and you’re going to say, “Well, I’m a believer.” How you think that’s going to go over? That’s what Americans have us thinking: because I’m a believer, everything’s okay. See, I have eight kids, and all of them believe that I’m their dad, and they know my standards, but that doesn’t make them one that lives right. They have to choose to live right, and so do we. See, faith in being a son of God is not the end of it. Let me show you the power in unity, when the congregation, the young leaders, the devoted leaders, and the skilled leaders get together and become one. Genesis 7, “the people are one.” Genesis 11:6, “the people are one, they have one language,” and this is what they began to do, and “now nothing that they purpose to do will be” what? Withheld or impossible for
What is the real problem with the church in America?

He answers “disunity.” He points to Genesis 11:6, where “the people are one,” and 2 Chronicles 5:13, where singers and musicians were “as one in praising and thanking the Lord” and the glory of the Lord filled the house. He says the healing of America is “God’s people getting their act together.”
What is the real problem with the church in America?

them. So what’s the real problem with the church in America? Disunity. Now, let’s continue. 2 Chronicles 5:13, “As the trumpeters and cymbals and instruments of music and singers were as one in praising and thanking the Lord, the glory of the Lord filled the house of God.” The presence of God came and filled the house of God, and God spoke. That’s where you got the message, “If my people which are called by my name will humble themselves and pray and turn from their wicked ways, I will hear from heaven, forgive their sin, and heal their nation.” So what’s the source of the healing of America? Is it the Democrats or
What is the real problem with the church in America?

Genesis 11:6: And the LORD said, “Indeed the people are one and they all have one language, and this is what they begin to do; now nothing that they propose to do will be withheld from them. 2 Chronicles 5:13: indeed it came to pass, when the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking the LORD, and when they lifted up their voice with the trumpets and cymbals and instruments of music, and praised the LORD, saying: “For He is good, For His mercy endures forever,” that the house, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud, 2 Chronicles 7:14: if My people who are called by My name will humble themselves, and pray and seek My face, and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin and heal their land.
Why does the church use music and singing?

He says “God does not need music. He has chosen to use music and use singing,” and the church should be filled with instruments “because God ordained it.” He says “singing and music can do more than my messages can,” and that “he inhabits the praises of his people.”
Why does the church use music and singing?

Republicans? No. Is it the rich people or the poor people? No. It’s God’s people getting their act together. Now, church, that was good. I don’t know if that got into you, but that’s good. Now listen, God does not need music. He has chosen to use music and use singing, and this church should be filled with instruments because God ordained it, but you have to take time to learn one. We should have good singers. You say, “We’re a small,” I don’t care, there’s enough here to get the job done. All you have to do is take some TV time and learn an instrument. Are you out there? See, Timothy cared for the church, so he spent time. And church, I’m telling you, I keep telling you year after year, singing and music can do more than my messages can. There’s something about connecting a message with music that God anoints and gets into people, and they’re singing, singing, “Blessed assurance, Jesus is mine.” Remember when Fanny came out with that song, everybody in America was singing it, and they forgot Billy Sunday’s message after they left that day, but they got the [unclear] in them. Are you there? Do you understand that he inhabits the praises of his people? Do you understand he really comes when we get together with our music and our voices, and together we worship the Lord? No, looky-loose, we worship the Lord, he will come, and he will speak to people, and he will touch

He reads Paul’s words in verse 22, “If anyone … does not love the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be Anathema,” and says it means “excommunicated, banned.” He says people are separated from Jesus “because they don’t love him,” and sets beside it Paul’s wish in Romans 9:3, saying “that’s compassion.”

people. See, it’s not only important that we’re in unity around doctrine and structure of the church, it’s important we’re in unity in worship and praising God and getting involved. Now, in closing, Paul’s going to turn to the leader of leaders, Jesus Christ, and this is what he says, and this is a powerful statement. I don’t know if you’re ready for this, but here it comes. Paul says, “If anyone,” in verse 22, “does not love the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be Anathema. Maranatha.” Anathema means excommunicated, banned, something devoted. You see, when I accept Christ, I’m what? Devoted unto him. Something devoted that is banned. And why are they banned? Why are they excommunicated? Why are they separated from Jesus? Because they don’t love him. Now, let’s watch the use of the word real quickly. Watch the use of the word, 1 Corinthians 12:3, we read, “No one speaking by the Spirit of God calls Jesus accursed.” You see, the Muslims who say Jesus didn’t die on the cross and Jesus is not God, and the Mormons who have their little thing about Jesus, you are not speaking by the Spirit of God, because nothing can separate Jesus from God, because Jesus is God. Amen. See, that’s how it’s used. You’re not speaking by the Spirit, you’re speaking from head knowledge. Romans 9:3, “I wish,” Paul said, “I wish that myself were anathema,” a curse, separated from God, from Christ, “for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh.” He wished he could die and go to hell and be separated from God and all of Israel would come to God. That’s how much he knew the seriousness of not loving Jesus. Are you getting that? He was willing to go to hell for a whole nation. Now, folks, that’s compassion. Of course he couldn’t. He says, “I wish I could.” He knew that couldn’t be, but that was his heart. He didn’t want anybody going to hell. He didn’t know anybody separated from Jesus Christ. I mean, I would raise my hand and say, “Lord, I need a little bit of that kind of compassion and care.” Yeah, I need a little bit. If I just had a little bit. [unclear] 1:8, “Though we, the apostles,” any man, any woman, any man here is any

1 Corinthians 16:22: If anyone does not love the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be accursed. O Lord, come! 1 Corinthians 12:3: Therefore I make known to you that no one speaking by the Spirit of God calls Jesus accursed, and no one can say that Jesus is Lord except by the Holy Spirit. Romans 9:3: For I could wish that I myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my countrymen according to the flesh,
What does he say about religions that began with a message from an angel?

He says the Muslim and Mormon religions each began with a man “supposedly encountering an angel from heaven,” and that “angels from heaven don’t make mistakes.” He says “If he saw anything, it was a demon giving him wrong instruction,” and that Paul says anyone who preaches another gospel should be anathema.
What does he say about religions that began with a message from an angel?

person “or an angel from heaven.” Now, let me ask you, who started the Muslim religion? A guy supposedly encountering an angel from heaven. Who started the Mormon religion? Some guy supposedly encountering an angel from heaven. How many you know, angels from heaven don’t make mistakes? How many of you know, in the Book of Mormon, that he said they had horses in America back there when Moroni was over here? How you know horses didn’t come to America until the 1400s, when the Spaniards, 1500s when the Spaniards brought them over, got loose, they bred, and they kept breeding, and they kept importing horses from the, uh, West Indies and so forth, and then the Indians got a hold of them. And boy, how many know angels know that? How many know angels would know that? How many you know he ain’t talking to no angel? And I could give you other problems. See, he says, “though an angel.” If he saw anything, it was a demon giving him wrong instruction. And why anybody would want to be part of that religion, if they read this Bible, is beyond my cranial understanding. Hallelujah. That’s why he said he give you pastors to feed you with knowledge and understanding. That’s truth, is what’s going to set you free. Knowledge is what’s going to keep you from being destroyed. “If they preach any other gospel than that which we have preached to you and you have received, let them be anathema.” Let them be banned, let them be excommunicated, get them
What does he say about religions that began with a message from an angel?
Galatians 1:8: But even if we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel to you than what we have preached to you, let him be accursed.
How do we show that we love Jesus?

He quotes John 14:15, 23 and 24, where loving Jesus means to “keep my commandments.” He says Jesus came “to teach us how to get along with each other,” and that Galatians 5:14 says “The law is fulfilled in one word,” “Love your neighbor as yourself.”
How do we show that we love Jesus?

out. Now, folks, that’s a serious statement he’s making, and that’s the way it’s used in the Scriptures. And then he says, “If anyone does not love the Lord Jesus Christ.” Man, Paul said some things that’s not politically correct today. Nobody in the Protestant church feels like they’re going to hell. You ever go to a funeral where they say, “This guy’s going to hell,” or “This is a bad guy”? No, never. We all live in this delusion. Now, so would it be important to know how to love Jesus? It would be very important. John 14:15, “If you love me,” what do you do? “Keep my commandments.” Duh. Again, John 14:23, “If anyone loves me,” he will what? “Keep my commandments.” John 14:24, “He who does not love me does not keep my commandments.” Now, does it take Greek and Hebrew to understand that? Why did Jesus come? To teach us how to get along with each other, how to live with each other. That’s what his commandments is all about. That’s why he died on the cross, to change the way you acted toward other people. Galatians 5:14, “The law is fulfilled in one word,” you shall what? “Love your neighbor as yourself.” So the whole law, “Thou shalt not commit adultery, thou shalt not steal, thou shalt not kill,” blah blah blah blah blah blah, is what? Love each other. That’s why he died on the cross. He had to die on the cross to forgive you of hating other people and mistreating other people, and he also died to change you and to teach you how to treat other people.
How do we show that we love Jesus?

John 14:15: “If you love Me, keep My commandments. John 14:23-24: Jesus answered and said to him, “If anyone loves Me, he will keep My word; and My Father will love him, and We will come to him and make Our home with him. He who does not love Me does not keep My words; and the word which you hear is not Mine but the Father’s who sent Me. Galatians 5:14: For all the law is fulfilled in one word, even in this: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”
Did Jesus die to make us rich, or to change how we treat people?

He says Christ “didn’t come to make you rich,” and calls prosperity preaching “not scriptural.” He says “He came to die that you might learn how to treat those next to you.” On healing he says “healing is real, but it’s real when it’s real,” and “You can’t pretend it happened because your faith is so worked up.”
Did Jesus die to make us rich, or to change how we treat people?

It’s not, listen to me, it’s not prosperity like these people preach. He didn’t come to make you rich. They’re lying to you. There’s [unclear] in the Scriptures. The Bible says the poor you will always have with you. There’s nothing wrong with being poor if that’s your lot in life, you’ve done everything you can not to be poor. You know, you’re not a second-class citizen. These people that preach prosperity, and you give them your money and they live rich and you live poor, that’s not scriptural. “Gain is godliness” is what? Not to be followed. Paul said it plainly, and yet that’s what Christians are into now: prosperity, faith, and, “Well, I believe, and so I’m going to receive.” Faith, faith, faith, the faith camp, or have you in a delusion that all you do is believe, and, man, you’re going to get rich, and you’re going to be president, and you’re going to be a famous basketball player and a football player and a musician or whatever, because you believe in God. That isn’t it. Possibility thinking and positive thinking, you can think all you want that you’re going to be some great singer or musician. That is not scriptural, that because you think so, it’s going to be so. Are you with me? He came to die that you might learn how to treat those next to you. [unclear] That’s why he died. And that’s the whole purpose of the law, is to teach you how to treat one another. Healing. You know, in our charismatic Pentecostal circles, you know, we’re a Spirit-filled church, they fabricate healings. You can’t fabricate healings. You can’t get the people worked up, and, you know, [unclear] comes up and, you know, they got muscular [unclear] and all this, they’re walking like this, and then you [unclear] them and they shake, and then they walk across the stage like this, and they, “Oh, God healed,” and he ain’t healed. That leg’s still lame. Folks, healing is real, but it’s real when it’s real. You can’t pretend it happened because your faith is so worked up. Are you with me? He would rather you learn how to treat other people. That’s why he died. Now that’s good preaching. Psychology has crept into the church. It’s horrible. Nowhere did Christ preach psychology. “Poor is a priority.” You give me one scripture where Jesus took one time and gave to the poor. But you’re a great Christian if you give to the poor and you help the drunkard and you help the drug addict and, you know, the down-and-outer. Not one time did Jesus do it. Are you
Does he say helping the poor is the church’s priority?

He says Jesus told us to remember the poor, “but he did not make it a priority. He made it one segment of the church.” He says “we better help them by teaching them a job skill,” and “we can’t make a church out of it.”
Does he say helping the poor is the church’s priority?

there? Did he tell us to remember the poor? Yes. But he did not make it a priority. He made it one segment of the church. And Christians really get high off helping people, down and out and the poor and all the rest, and all we do is give them money to go to the casinos and live, drink their booze and get their drugs. Are you out there? I mean, no, we better help them by teaching them a job skill, and they learn how to work in one fashion or another. And are we to really remember those who are poor, in need, really poor? Yes. But, folks, we can’t make a church out of it. Christ came to teach you how to treat others, and that’s his priority, and we got to get it right. Our children supposed to honor their parents. Our parents supposed to raise their children up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord and be an example of disciplining and handling the money. Yes. Ain’t that right? That’s why Christ
What does it mean to make Jesus Lord of your life?

He says Christ’s death “starts right in the home,” with husbands and wives who love each other and children who see it. Using the parable in Luke 19, he says “Jesus is the leader that you really need in your life,” and “it’s vitally important that you make Jesus Lord of your life. If you let him lead you, false leaders can’t lead you astray.”
What does it mean to make Jesus Lord of your life?

died. It starts right in the home. Are husbands and wives supposed to love each other? Yeah. What’s the greatest thing you can give your kid? Seeing you guys enjoying one another. A marriage that works, you’re happy, you’re sacrificing for each other, the children see it. That’s why he died on the cross. Luke 19:14, in the parable of the Lord going to war to win a kingdom, speaking of Jesus. He come to win us. Hallelujah. We are his kingdom, his citizens. The Lord went off to war, and his citizens, what? Hated him and said, “We don’t want this man ruling over us.” See, Jesus is the leader that you really need in your life. “We will not have this man to rule over us.” So then the Lord comes back, as you know, the parable, and he deals with those that he gave talents to, and then he says this: “Bring those enemies of mine,” and then he says who the enemies are, who did not want me to rule over them, “and slay them before me.” Church, it’s vitally important that you make Jesus Lord of your life. If you let him lead you, false leaders can’t lead you astray.
What does it mean to make Jesus Lord of your life?

Luke 19:14: But his citizens hated him, and sent a delegation after him, saying, ‘We will not have this man to reign over us.’ Luke 19:27: But bring here those enemies of mine, who did not want me to reign over them, and slay them before me.’ ”
What does “refresh” mean in this message?

He says “that’s what refresh means. It means you relieve someone of the burden, you refresh them.” He compares it to someone bringing a cold glass of lemonade to a person plowing, or a son taking over the plow.
What jobs does he say devoted people do in a church?
He says “they clean the church, they clean the bathrooms, they do the books,” mow the lawn, visit the sick, encourage people to come to church and invite them over to their house.
What does he say about hospitality?
He says “the Bible tells us that we are to be what? Hospitable,” and that most American Christians “never invite anybody over.”
Did the people who helped him need to preach or prophesy?

No. He says “They never preached a message. I never heard one of them prophesy or speak in tongues and interpret or anything else,” yet “without them I don’t know if I would have made it over the hump.”
Does he say it matters which church you choose?
Yes. He says “Don’t think it’s not important where you choose to go to church and the leadership there. Very important.”
Who does he say we are supposed to follow?

He says “You’re supposed to follow Christ. You’re supposed to follow Paul and Peter and these apostles. You’re not supposed to follow some preacher.” Of the judgment he asks, “what are you going to do?”
What does he say about preachers who tell people what they want to hear?
He says “The churches are filling up with preachers that tell them what they want to hear, so you can’t blame leaders only, because that’s what they want to hear.”
What does he say his own children show about faith?
He says “I have eight kids, and all of them believe that I’m their dad, and they know my standards, but that doesn’t make them one that lives right. They have to choose to live right, and so do we.”
What does he say is the source of healing for America?
He asks whether it is the Democrats or Republicans, or the rich people or the poor people, and answers no each time: “It’s God’s people getting their act together.”
What does he say about Protestants and the idea of hell?
He says “Nobody in the Protestant church feels like they’re going to hell,” and that at funerals nobody says someone is going there: “We all live in this delusion.”
Why does he say Jesus died on the cross?
He says “That’s why he died on the cross, to change the way you acted toward other people,” and “to forgive you of hating other people and mistreating other people.”
What does he say about psychology in the church?
He says “Psychology has crept into the church. It’s horrible. Nowhere did Christ preach psychology.”
What does he say about children and parents?
He says “Our children supposed to honor their parents,” and parents are supposed to raise their children up “in the nurture and admonition of the Lord” and be an example.
What is the greatest thing you can give your child?
He asks, “What’s the greatest thing you can give your kid?” and answers “Seeing you guys enjoying one another.”

p: In this Easter message the speaker reviews the beating and crucifixion of Jesus and the miracles at His death, then teaches “God Bless You”: the blessing of Acts 3:26 is God turning us from sin. He uses Lazarus, Zacchaeus and Mary Magdalene as examples and a chemical demonstration to show how sin hurts us and those around us, ending with a prayer.
What did the soldiers do to Jesus before the crucifixion? (Matthew 27)

The speaker says a whole band of soldiers scourged Jesus with a whip with pieces of glass and bone on the ends, put a crown of thorns on His head, mocked Him as King of the Jews, beat His head with a staff and plucked His beard. He says this is the Easter story and that the soldiers “delivered him up to be crucified.”
What did the soldiers do to Jesus before the crucifixion? (Matthew 27)

And uh this morning we want to know what happened, what it means to us, why it’s important, and uh we want to hear from God’s word this morning. It’s very important, so we thank you for joining us this morning. It starts in Matthew 27. Bible says that there were a whole band of soldiers, not just a few, not just four or five, a whole band. And when I looked up the word in the Greek, the band, it could possibly be hundreds of soldiers, maybe not, I don’t know, I didn’t do enough study, but if there were hundreds beating Jesus, that’s a horrible thing. There were. Now this is what they did to him. The Bible says that they scourged him. They took the whip of the cat-o’-nine-tails, the tails, the the whip had at the end of it gl— pieces of glass, pieces of bone, pieces of things that just would rip the flesh right off of Jesus Christ, rip the flesh right off of anybody that they whipped. And they began to do that to Jesus over and over. The Bible says, I’ll show you at the end of this slide, that they drove a crown of thorns under his head. They mocked him. You know, the the thing was he was, he was called the King of the Jews, so of course the Romans, they didn’t want another king. they That was a threat to them, so they really beat up on this King of the Jews. They made a crown of thorns, put it in his head, they spat on him, they bowed the knee before him mocking him. They beat his head in with the staff. They gave him a staff, they gave him a robe to wear in the crown of thorns, and they bowed before him. Then they took that staff and they started beating him in the head. Jesus Christ, he had bumps all over his head. The Bible says they plucked his beard. And this is all just, this is the Easter story, you guys all know about it, and they delivered him up to be crucified.
What does Isaiah 52:14 say about how Jesus was disfigured, and why does His blood matter? (Isaiah 52:14)

He says Isaiah 52:14 shows Jesus’ face and appearance were marred more than any man’s, and that He bore the pain and punishment for us. He says Jesus’ blood “is the key” and “allows us to be forgiven from sin.”
What does Isaiah 52:14 say about how Jesus was disfigured, and why does His blood matter? (Isaiah 52:14)

And the Bible says in Isaiah 52:14 that his face and his whole appearance was marred, disfigured more than any man, it says, and his form beyond that of the sons of men. Jesus Christ went through the most horrific, horrible beating in all the world. Isaiah tells us that it was more disfigurement and scarring that any man suffered. When that whip went off on his back, you know, they just didn’t stop. There wasn’t a number they stopped it. They just kept going, and he bore that pain and that punishment for us, of course, as you know. And the blood of Jesus started to flow as they began to whip him, as they put put the crown of thorns on him. The blood started to flow from his face, all down his body, and we know that that blood is the key. It’s most p— it’s very powerful. It’s the blood that allows us to be forgiven from sin. It covers our sin, and we need that blood. His blood is so powerful.
What does Isaiah 52:14 say about how Jesus was disfigured, and why does His blood matter? (Isaiah 52:14)
Isaiah 52:14: Just as many were astonished at you, So His visage was marred more than any man, And His form more than the sons of men;
What happened when they crucified Jesus? (Matthew 27:35, Matthew 27:45)

He says the soldiers took His garments and cast lots, which was a prophecy being fulfilled, and that Jesus was stripped and “bore this embarrassment for us.” He says darkness covered the whole land from noon to 3:00 p.m., which was a miracle and not an eclipse.
What happened when they crucified Jesus? (Matthew 27:35, Matthew 27:45)

And before they put him on the cross, they took his garments and they cast lots for him. You guys all know the story. That was a prophecy that was supposed to be fulfilled. But you guys got to understand here, they took his garments, they stripped him. He didn’t have any clothes on. It’s embarrassing. He bore this embarrassment for us. He was naked on the cross. They put him up and everybody saw him, all of the people that were following him, the disciples that were there, John, Mary the mother. He was naked. That’s embarrassing. And they crucified Jesus. In Matthew 27:45 it starts, it says, from the 6th hour to the 9th hour, or from 12:00, that’s noon, like noontime is normally when the sun’s at its highest point, from noon to 3:00 p.m. there was darkness over the whole land.
What happened when they crucified Jesus? (Matthew 27:35, Matthew 27:45)
Matthew 27:45: Now from the sixth hour until the ninth hour there was darkness over all the land.
Why does he say no one could kill Jesus, and what did the torn veil mean?

He says “nobody could come up and kill Jesus,” that He had to give up His spirit at 3:00 p.m., and that as soon as He did the earth quaked and the temple veil was torn from top to bottom. He says the veil separated the holy of holies, where only a priest could meet with God.
Why does he say no one could kill Jesus, and what did the torn veil mean?

Now that’s, of course, a miracle, because there’s the sun’s supposed to be out, but God was doing something. So there was darkness over the whole land. They could see each other, but there was darkness, and it wasn’t smoke, it wasn’t an eclipse. God brought darkness. And at 3:00 p.m. Jesus gave up his spirit. The Bible says that no man could kill him. He had to give up his spirit. He had to let go. That’s important to understand. You see, nobody could come up and kill Jesus. If somebody cut off his arm, he could just put it right back on, healed it, and went on his way, cuz he’s God. Nobody could kill him. And as soon as he gave up his spirit, the earth quaked. The veil of the temple, you got to understand, the veil separated the holy of holies from the holy place. The holy of holies was the place where you could come and meet with God, and you could all you had to be a certain person. You had to be a priest to go into that holy of holies. And God, not a man, he ripped it from the bottom, the top to the bottom, he ripped it in two.
What does the torn veil and the new covenant mean for us? (1 Peter 2:9, Jeremiah 31:34)

He says the veil ripped in two fulfilled the new covenant, so “I don’t have to go through the pastor… the priest. I can come to Jesus Christ myself.” He cites 1 Peter 2:9 that believers are “a holy priesthood,” and says the rocks split and graves opened when Jesus died.
What does the torn veil and the new covenant mean for us? (1 Peter 2:9, Jeremiah 31:34)

Fulfilling the new covenant. The new covenant that says that all shall know me, from the least to the greatest. I don’t have to go through the pastor, I don’t have to go through the priest. I can come to Jesus Christ myself. I can talk to God. If I follow the pattern of the temple, if I come before him with thanksgiving and praise and go to the holy place, and through the holy place to the holy [unclear], I can meet with Christ myself. The Bible says in Second Peter, or 1 Peter 2:9, that we are a special people, a holy priesthood. See, when we accept accept Christ, we become a priest. we We can go in and we can meet with him ourselves. That’s very powerful. God’s fulfilling his covenant that he set in Ezekiel and Hebrews. Bible says that the rocks split. They’re standing there as Jesus, when he gave up his spirit, the rocks all around just split open. A lot of you guys know this rock right here, this huge rock, it would split when Jesus died. A miracle, of course. The graves, the Bible [unclear], were open, and the people in those graves did not rise until Jesus first rose, because he was the first one to rise. Now this is important.
What does the torn veil and the new covenant mean for us? (1 Peter 2:9, Jeremiah 31:34)

Jeremiah 31:34: No more shall every man teach his neighbor, and every man his brother, saying, ‘Know the LORD,’ for they all shall know Me, from the least of them to the greatest of them, says the LORD. For I will forgive their iniquity, and their sin I will remember no more.” 1 Peter 2:9: But you are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, His own special people, that you may proclaim the praises of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light;
What did the soldiers say when they saw the earthquake? (Matthew 27:54)

He says the centurion and the men with him, “quite possibly the men that were whipping him,” saw the earthquake and the rocks split and began to fear greatly, saying “This was the Son of God.” He says they were not writing scripture but were witnesses who were convinced, and that God wanted to reach even those who whipped Him.
What did the soldiers say when they saw the earthquake? (Matthew 27:54)

Because God wasn’t sitting there alone on the cross. There were people watching and seeing these things, and you guys need to know that the Bible isn’t full of baloney. These are witnesses. These are people writing these records down. And in Matthew 27:54 it says, now, in “the centurion, and they that were with him.” You see, these men were quite possibly the men that were whipping him, the men that were beating him. When they saw all these things, when they saw the earthquake, he says that they were watching Jesus. They weren’t going around on doing their own thing. They were watching Jesus, and it says they saw the earthquake, they saw these things that were done, they saw the rocks split, they saw the darkness covered the land, and they began to fear in their hearts, saying, “What have I done? I just I just whipped Jesus. I just I just beat him over the head.” What if they feared greatly, saying, “This was the Son of God.” And here you have it. These people were not people that were writing the scriptures. They were just there seeing all this happen, and they were convinced in their heart this is the Son of God. Amazing. And God wanted wanted to reach them. God wanted to reach those guys who whipped him, who took him out, who beat him over the head, who put the crown of thorns on him. You see, they were trying to suppress a king of the Jews. They didn’t know he was God until now. And fear fell upon them, and we know that many soldiers turned to Jesus. So let’s bow our heads this morning, and we just want to pray and thank Jesus this morning for his blood. Lord Jesus, we come before you this morning and we thank you for the blood that you shed on the cross. Lord Jesus, your blood covers all sin. God, your blood has no boundaries. God, there’s nothing that you cannot do with your blood. It is so powerful, God. Lord Jesus, we thank you for the cross, and Lord Jesus, we ask that you touch us with your blood and touch us with your spirit this morning. Amen.
What did the soldiers say when they saw the earthquake? (Matthew 27:54)
Matthew 27:54: So when the centurion and those with him, who were guarding Jesus, saw the earthquake and the things that had happened, they feared greatly, saying, “Truly this was the Son of God!”
What blessing of God is for all people? (Acts 3:26)

After a prayer thanking Jesus for His blood, he introduces the message “God Bless You” and asks what blessing is for all people, nations, ages and stages of life. He says it is not prosperity, since much of the world lives in poverty, and then points to Acts 3:26, that God sent Jesus to bless you by turning each of you from sin.
What blessing of God is for all people? (Acts 3:26)

Amen. Now that was just a review. We want to know what happened, and this morning we have a special message, and this message is titled “God Bless You.” I was going to sneeze and have somebody say “God bless.” Now I want to ask the question, what blessing, what blessing of God is for all people, all nations, all ages, all stages of life, no matter where you’re at? The Bible says that there’s a blessing. Is it prosperity? Now we know that, a lot you know, God cares about the whole world, and a lot of the world lives in poverty. Are Are we more blessed than them because because we’re, you know, we have more money in America? No. Is it miracles? Is it healings? We find this blessing in Acts 3:26. When God raised up his servant, it says his servant is Jesus, is talking about, he sent him first to you to bless you, and it says, by turning turning each of you from sin, from wicked ways.
What blessing of God is for all people? (Acts 3:26)
Acts 3:26: To you first, God, having raised up His Servant Jesus, sent Him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from your iniquities.”
Why is turning from sin a blessing? (John 11:25)

He says some people look at turning from sin and say “that’s not a blessing,” but he wants to learn why it is. He reads Jesus’ words to Martha, I am the resurrection, I am the life, and he that believeth in me, though he were dead, shall live, and says it is important for the next story.
Why is turning from sin a blessing? (John 11:25)

And we want to learn this morning, you know, some of us might look at that, or some people look at that and they say, “That’s not a blessing. I don’t understand. What do you mean?” But we want to learn this morning why turning from sin is a blessing. And he does this blessing. He uses this. He said to Martha in John 11:25, he said to her, “I am the resurrection, I am the life, and he that believeth in me, though he were dead, dead shall live.” And this is an important, me I’m going to read it one more time: “He that believeth in me, though he were dead, shall live.” And this is important to remember. I’m going to show you in this next story, and I’m sure you guys have heard the story of Lazarus. If you haven’t, you’re going to hear it now.
Why is turning from sin a blessing? (John 11:25)
John 11:25: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in Me, though he may die, he shall live.
What happened when Jesus raised Lazarus? (John 11)

He says Jesus knew Lazarus was sick but waited until he had died, and that after four days in the tomb Jesus shouted “Lazarus, come forth” and Lazarus came out bound in grave clothes. He says this is “not just a miracle,” and that Jesus also said “Loose him and let him go.”
What happened when Jesus raised Lazarus? (John 11)

And there was a man, Mary and Martha’s brother, whom Jesus knew, and he died, and Jesus purposely waited till he died before he came and visited. He waited till Lazarus got sick. He knew that Lazarus was sick, but he stayed where he was at. He didn’t come to where Lazarus was. He waited till he died, and Lazarus had been in the tomb and he was dead for 4 days. And Martha says to Jesus, “By now his body stinks. Why didn’t you come and heal my brother?” And of course Jesus says, “I am the resurrection, I am the life.” Now Jesus goes to the tomb. He asks him to open the door and he says, “Lazarus.” He cried out, he shouted, “Lazarus, come forth,” and Lazarus came forth. The Bible says he was bound hand and foot. He was bound in grave clothes. His face was bound. He couldn’t see. But Jesus Christ brought him, raised him to life, and this is not just a miracle.
What happened when Jesus raised Lazarus? (John 11)

John 11:43-44: Now when He had said these things, He cried with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come forth!” And he who had died came out bound hand and foot with graveclothes, and his face was wrapped with a cloth. Jesus said to them, “Loose him, and let him go.”
What is the message of Lazarus’ story about sin? (Romans 6:23, Ephesians 2:1)

He says the story is “a message,” that Jesus calling “come forth” is about coming out of sin, and that sin kills our spiritual man. He cites Romans 6:23, that the wages of sin is death, and says Jesus can raise up our spiritual man and “loose us” from the bondage of sin as He did Lazarus.
What is the message of Lazarus’ story about sin? (Romans 6:23, Ephesians 2:1)

He also said, “Loose him and let him go.” And this story is not just a miracle. It’s not just a healing. It’s not just an event, uh, some miraculous work. It’s a message this morning. We’ve got to understand that when Jesus called to Lazarus and said, “Come forth,” he’s talking about sin, coming out of sin. In Romans 3:23, the Bible says, or 6:23, it says that the wages of of sin is death. And you see, sin will kill our spiritual man. When when when sin is in control of our life, it kills our spiritual man. And you see, Jesus wants to call, he’s crying out to you, he’s saying, “Come forth. I can bring you out of sin. I can raise you up. I can raise your spiritual man up from the dead. I can do that for you. I can change you. I can loose you from the bondage that is holding you together.” You see, Lazarus was bound. He was in the tomb. There is no way for him to get out. But there was one way: Jesus Christ. And that is a powerful, the powerful message of his resurrection, that though we were dead in trespasses and sins, though we are, you know, were bound by sin, Jesus Christ can come and he can loose us and set us free from that.
What is the message of Lazarus’ story about sin? (Romans 6:23, Ephesians 2:1)
Romans 6:23: For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord. Ephesians 2:1: And you He made alive, who were dead in trespasses and sins,
Who was Zacchaeus, and why did Jesus go to his house? (Luke 19:1-7)

He says Zacchaeus was a rich chief tax collector, “a thief… a liar,” who climbed a tree to see Jesus because he was short and searching, and Jesus said “I must abide at your house.” He says the crowd thought Zacchaeus was a sinner and wondered why the Son of God would go to his house.
Who was Zacchaeus, and why did Jesus go to his house? (Luke 19:1-7)

A man named Zacchaeus. He was a rich man. He was the chief tax collector. He was, he had everything, so he thought. The Bible says he was a thief, he was a liar, and of course we know he was a bad example to his kids. He’ come home, and he’s a thief, he’s a liar, and he’s home. You know, if I knew my dad was doing that, sorry, Dad, I wouldn’t have much respect for you, but he was rich. And Zacchaeus went and climbed up the tree when Jesus was coming into town. He climbed up a tree because he was short. He climbed up a tree because there was a crowd and he wanted to see Jesus. He was searching for something. And when Jesus came to his spot where the tree was, he said to Zacchaeus, “I must abide at your house.” Thank you. And as soon as Jesus said that, the people all around the community, they knew that Zacchaeus was a jerk, they knew he was a sinner, and they said, “He’s going to go to this guy’s house? He’s a sinner, he’s an idiot. Why is Jesus going to go? The Son of God’s going to go to his house? Why does it come to my house?”
Who was Zacchaeus, and why did Jesus go to his house? (Luke 19:1-7)
Luke 19:5: And when Jesus came to the place, He looked up and saw him, and said to him, “Zacchaeus, make haste and come down, for today I must stay at your house.”
How did Zacchaeus change, and does the speaker say we must be poor? (Luke 19:8-9)

He says Zacchaeus said he would give half of his goods to the poor and restore four times what he stole, and Jesus said “Salvation has come to this house.” He says Zacchaeus “met the resurrection,” and that giving half does not mean you have to be poor: “he can still live honestly.”

And Zacchaeus, when Jesus arrived and came into his house, he responded and he said, “I give half.” You, I mean, I don’t even know if they had a conversation. items.d: In “A Phenomenal Event,” Pastor David G. Kincer begins with Isaiah 10:1-3 and says leaders who make unrighteous laws will face God’s judgment. He then teaches Isaiah 11, the seven spirits of the Holy Spirit…
p: In “A Phenomenal Event,” Pastor David G. Kincer begins with Isaiah 10:1-3 and says leaders who make unrighteous laws will face God’s judgment. He then teaches Isaiah 11, the seven spirits of the Holy Spirit, the judgment of the Branch from Jesse, and the phenomenal event of the wolf dwelling with the lamb, which he links to the remnant, Isaiah 65 and the nations rallying to Jesus. He ends with praise in that day in Isaiah 12.

I don’t have to go anywhere to find God. He will meet me right where I am at. It’s just as cold where I’m at as it is over there where I’m going. So, I might as well just stay where I’m at and let Jesus heat me up.
Could we know less than we think we know?
Daniel 12:4: “But you, Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book until the time of the end; many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall increase.”
What does he tell young people to expect and pursue?

He tells young people to stay in morality and keep pursuing righteousness and truth in God’s word, because they will be part of the remnant that ushers in a move of God that shakes the nations. He says there will be a period when everyone is afraid of the church because it is united around Jesus and his word.
What does he tell young people to expect and pursue?

Amen. Let him bring the summer season. Now church, you young people, I’m telling you, you got something big to look forward to. And remember when Christ came the first time, they only understood as he revealed it to them. They weren’t there saying, “Oh, Bob, Jesus is coming. The Messiah is coming. He’s going to be born of the earth.” They weren’t out there passing out tracks and saying he’s coming at all. They didn’t know he was coming until he said he was coming. And they didn’t know what he was going to do. Did he say what he’s going to do? And they didn’t know the the fulfillment of prophecies until he said, “This is the fulfillment of these prophecies.” Are you there? Yes. But I can guarantee you young people, you stay in morality. You stay pursuing righteousness, truth in God’s word. You’re going to be part of the remnant that’s going to usher in a move of God that’s going to shake the nations of the earth. And there’s going to be a period where everybody’s going to be afraid of the church. They’re going to respect the church that much because we’re not a bunch of divided idiots. We are united around Jesus and his word. And see, that’s going to be the witness that’s going to judge these people that reject the message of the gospel. Are you there? Okay. And quickly, there’s praise in that day. In that day you will say, “Oh Lord, I will praise you.” How many don’t want to that day you just want to do it now. Yeah.
What does Isaiah 12 say about praise in that day?

He reads Isaiah 12 and says that in that day you will say, “Oh Lord, I will praise you,” and that God can comfort and restore anyone who repents and asks forgiveness. He says to draw water from the wells of salvation with joy, call upon his name, and cry out and shout in the midst of the Holy One of Israel.
What does Isaiah 12 say about praise in that day?

Yeah. Though you were angry with me, your anger is turned away and you comfort me. Hallelujah. If you’re here today and you’ve been a bad boy and and you know God is disciplining you for your uh behavior, he can come and comfort you. He can come and change you. He can come and restore you. You just need to ask him forgiveness. Repent. Agree that you’re wrong and ask him to come. Behold, God is my salvation. I will trust and not be afraid. I will not be what? Afraid. Hallelujah. For Yah the Lord is my strength and my song. Not Osteen, not Warren, not some pastor of Mountainside Church. God himself is my strength and my song. How many know he says he compasses about with songs of deliverance? Music and singing is vitally important in the church and it should be coming from the spirit back to the God. It should be anointed of God. Not just going through motions of singing. God’s ordained music and singing in the church to bring his glory and touch people’s lives and change people’s lives and to teach them his ways. Hallelujah. Not to entertain them. He’s also become my salvation. Therefore, with joy will you draw water from the wells of salvation. With what? Joy. And it is a joyful thing when you’re released from bondage. Continuing 12:4. In that day, see the same time period. You will say, “Praise the Lord.” You will say, “Call upon his name.” You will declare his deeds among the people. Hallelujah. God’s going to move you. You’re not going to be no silent saint in that day. How many know I don’t want to wait for that big expedition to come. How many know we can experience things in our day? Make mention that his name is exalted. You know, to make mention, you got to tell people, man, the Jesus, he’s he’s a name above every name. Jesus is God. You know, you got to mention, you got to talk it. Ain’t no silent prayers and silent, you know, uh, don’t wear your religion on your Yes, we’re going to wear religion on our sleeve. In fact, it’s not a religion. It’s Jesus Christ. It’s the living word. And we’re going to put it right out there where you can see it. Amen. This is known in all the earth. Duh. Now you know it. Cry out and shout, “Oh, inhabitant of Zion.” Shout. My goodness. That’s for Pentecostal weirdos. No, it’s for anybody that’s touched God and got understanding. We can shout unto God with the voice of triumph. And in that day, you will. For great is the Holy One of Israel in your midst. Where is he at? In our midst, folks. Hallelujah.
What does Isaiah 12 say about praise in that day?

Isaiah 12:1-6: And in that day you will say: “O LORD, I will praise You; Though You were angry with me, Your anger is turned away, and You comfort me. Behold, God is my salvation, I will trust and not be afraid; ‘For YAH, the LORD, is my strength and song; He also has become my salvation.’ ” Therefore with joy you will draw water From the wells of salvation. And in that day you will say: “Praise the LORD, call upon His name; Declare His deeds among the peoples, Make mention that His name is exalted. Sing to the LORD, For He has done excellent things; This is known in all the earth. Cry out and shout, O inhabitant of Zion, For great is the Holy One of Israel in your midst!”
What does he say is the name of the Messiah in Isaiah 11:1?
He says Jesus came through the bloodline of Jesse, David and Judah, and that his name in the Bible is called the Branch, a name we never use.
Does he say the Holy Ghost is God?
He says the Holy Ghost is a prominent member of God, he is God, and that God is Jesus and Jesus is God. He says he does not understand why the church argues about the baptism of the Holy Ghost.
Does he say the Holy Ghost is limited to tongues or prophecy?
He says we want to limit him to just tongues or prophecy or education, but being full of the Holy Ghost means you have the whole thing, as a glass that is full is not a quarter full.
What does he say we must do to receive the Holy Ghost?
He says all he can do is preach it, and you have to reach out and get it and pursue it, and that he highly recommends the Holy Ghost to people.
What does he say the holy mountain is?
He says the holy mountain is the church, where there is unity and a lack of war, and that the earth will be full of the knowledge of the Lord as the waters cover the sea.
What does he say the "second time" in Isaiah 11 means?

He says if there is a second time there had to be a first time, and that the Lord will reach out his hand a second time to reclaim the remnant, the people who are left from the four quarters of the earth.
Can someone who rejects Jesus be part of the remnant?

He says no: if an atheist or a Muslim rejects Jesus it disqualifies him from being the remnant, because once you have heard the gospel the rules change, and those who have not believed in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ are condemned already.
How long does he say animals ate only plants?
He says there was a period of over 1,600 years where the lion ate straw, and all animals ate plants until after the flood, when they ate meat.
How much of the world does he say the early apostles reached?

He says the early church did not reach the whole world and did not know there was another world out there, and that the apostles went to places such as India, Spain, Italy, Egypt, Libya, Arabia and Assyria, and he could not find a record of them going to Britain.
What does he say about the many denominations?

He says God started restoration and we keep building another group, another denomination, until in our generation there are new ones. He says that in that day people will look to Jesus Christ, not a denomination or some leader.
What does the Arctic tern illustrate?

He says the Arctic tern flies over 40,000 miles to go 12,000, which he compares to Christians zigzagging from church to church and preacher to preacher. He says our basic instinct should be going to the book and staying where we are, because God will meet us right where we are.
What does he say about music and singing in church?

He says music and singing is vitally important in the church and should come from the spirit back to God, anointed of God, not just going through motions. He says God ordained it to bring his glory, touch and change people’s lives and teach them his ways, not to entertain them.
Does he say we should keep our faith silent?

He says we are not going to be silent saints in that day, that we should make mention that his name is exalted, and that it is not a religion but Jesus Christ, the living word, which we put right out where you can see it.
