items.ser: A Powerful Side of Eternal Life · Part 1
tg: A Powerful Side of Eternal Life
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer likens eternal life to a three-legged stool of believe, obey and know, with God holding it together. He explains that the Bible uses the word “know” for a personal, intimate encounter, illustrating it with the woman who touched Jesus’ garment, Mary, and his own stories of electricity and a gunshot. He then teaches the difference between believers and disciples, what the truth sets us free from, and why the Word of God cuts people to the heart.
What is eternal life, according to John 17:3?

He says Jesus defines eternal life in John 17:3 as knowing “the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent.” He adds that believing in Christ equals eternal life, obeying God’s Word equals eternal life, and the Word of God makes us strong.
What is eternal life, according to John 17:3?

Remember in John 17:3, this is eternal life. See, He’s going to define what eternal life is: “that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent.” See, the Bible defines things, like we just learned today in one of the songs. What is the joy of the Lord, according to the Bible? Your strength. The joy of the Lord is [your strength]. Remember, in math, “is” equals, it’s the equal symbol, you see. And if you don’t have the joy of the Lord, you’re not strong. Let the Bible define itself. All right. Now, the Word of God makes us strong also. There’s always two banks to a river, but the Word of God will direct you to what? The joy of the Lord. Yeah, why do we want to walk around sad when we can walk around glad? Remember last week: believing in Christ equals eternal life. All right. Also, obeying God’s Word equals eternal life. All right. Now, everybody is born into eternity; it’s just whether you will spend--
What is eternal life, according to John 17:3?
John 17:3: And this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent.
Is believing and obeying all it takes to have eternal life? (the three-legged stool)

He likens eternal life to a three-legged stool: believe, obey, and a third leg he takes up that morning, with God holding it all together. He says “You can’t separate Jesus and God,” and with one leg missing “I would have to apply my own strength,” so “we need all three legs.”
Is believing and obeying all it takes to have eternal life? (the three-legged stool)

Eternity, what place you spend eternity at, is the equation here. All right. Now, I’m going to liken eternal life to a three-legged stool. Three-legged stool. One of them is believe, the other one is obey, and we’re going to hit the third one this morning. And of course, the top holds it all together, and that is God. Remember, Jesus said you got to believe on the One who sent Me for eternal life. You can’t separate Jesus and God. See, some people try to separate Jesus from God, you can’t do that, and some people try to separate God from Jesus and have only Jesus only. You can’t do either. They’re both in the equation. Can I hear an amen? They’re both in the equation. Okay. Now, as you know, if I had a three-legged stool up here and I took one leg off, I would have to work to use that as a seat. I would have to apply my own strength, you see. So we need all three legs to this. Amen. Now, let’s take a look at how “know” is used in the Bible, the word “know.” All right, and we’re going to find it is used as a personal--
What does it mean to “know” God in the Bible?

He says the word “know” in the Bible is used as an individual, personal, intimate encounter: “the personal, intimate, resulting encounter, resulting meeting with God and Jesus Christ.” He says “your pastor can’t get you through there,” and “when you individually touch Him, there is a result.”
What does it mean to “know” God in the Bible?

Individual--and, uh, your pastor can’t get you through there. There’s no big author that can get you into that. You yourself individually, personally, intimately. It means the touch, is it, the closeness, the touch, the personal, intimate, resulting encounter, resulting meeting with God and Jesus Christ. When you individually touch Him, there is a result. This is what you’re going to find the word “know” is used as. Am I clear? All right. Example: Luke 8:46. The woman with the issue of blood came up, got on her hands and knees, and touched the hem of His garment, and Jesus stopped the whole thing. There were a lot of people touching Jesus, you see, and when Jesus said, “Who touched Me?” the apostles reminded Him, “Everybody’s touching You. You know, the crowd just pushing into You.” He said, “No, no, no, somebody touched Me. Something happened. See, power went out of Me.” Now, let me remind you, this woman believed.
What does it mean to “know” God in the Bible?
Luke 8:46: But Jesus said, “Somebody touched Me, for I perceived power going out from Me.”
Why was the woman with the issue of blood not healed until she touched Jesus?

He says she believed, understood and obeyed by coming to the crowd, “but she still wasn’t healed” until she crawled through the crowd and touched the hem of His garment. “Faith is only one step in the knowledge and understanding of God,” he says.
Why was the woman with the issue of blood not healed until she touched Jesus?

Before, and she wasn’t healed. For all these people so sold on faith, faith is only one step in the knowledge and understanding of God. This woman obeyed and came to the crowd, because Jesus has invited everyone to come and He would heal them. So she believed, and she responded and came to that crowd, but she still wasn’t healed. She understood by watching that Jesus was healing people, and here she understood that’s what Jesus was doing. So she believed, she had understanding, and she obeyed, but she wasn’t healed. She wasn’t healed till she got down on her hands and knees, crawled through that crowd, and touched the hem of His garment, and [virtue] flowed out of Him. That’s when Jesus said, “I know someone touched Me.” An individual touched Me, and there was a result of healing.
What does Mary’s “I know not a man” teach about knowing?

He says in Luke 1:34 the word “know” points to a personal encounter, not just knowledge. Mary knew that to have a baby you need a man, “but that didn’t give her a baby”; it was when the power of God overshadowed her and the Spirit of the Lord came upon her that she conceived.
What does Mary’s “I know not a man” teach about knowing?

Number two, Luke 1:34. Mary said, “How shall this be,” that I’m going to have a child, I’m going to get pregnant and have a child, “seeing I know not a man.” I’m a virgin. I know not a man. I haven’t personally been in touch with a man resulting in the possibility of a baby being born. Allelujah. Now, the word “know” generally means to understand and have knowledge of, you see. And my point with the woman with the issue of blood is she had knowledge, but it didn’t do anything. See, Mary had knowledge that to have a baby you had to have a man, okay, but that didn’t give her a baby. The knowledge didn’t do it. Her belief in it didn’t do it. Do you understand? It wasn’t till the power of God overshadowed her and the Spirit of the Lord came upon her, and then there was a power, a virtue that went into Mary, and then she--
What does Mary’s “I know not a man” teach about knowing?
Luke 1:34: Then Mary said to the angel, “How can this be, since I do not know a man?”
Can you really know something without experiencing it? (his electricity story)

He says you can believe electricity can hurt you, “but you don’t know electricity until you come in contact with it.” He tells how he was shocked by a live wire while repairing a radio and again by a TV capacitor, and says “there was a result.”
Can you really know something without experiencing it? (his electricity story)

Conceived. The baby started growing in her womb. Are you there? See, that’s how the word “know” is used. Now, let me give you an example, my own example. We can talk about power all we want. You can understand electricity. You can know not to put your finger in that electric socket. All right, you can believe that electricity can hurt you, but you don’t know electricity until you come in contact with it. And I had a great idea today, but I couldn’t perform it: a little generator that you crank, the faster you crank it the more volts come out, and then you’re going to feel the electricity. Then you know what electricity is. When I was in [unclear] Technical School, they were teaching me to repair radios and TVs and all that stuff, and I had a radio, and somebody brought it to me, and it didn’t have a cord on it. So, you know, I knew electricity. I just cut off the end of a cord, plugged it in, put the terminals where, you know, the electricity would go into the radio, and was testing out this radio and all that. And then I forgot that there were bare wires there, and I bared the wires, I wrapped it around the terminals where I could get the radio going, and I forgot, and my hand--while I was looking one way, my hand went another, and it hit that live wire. Well, me went one way, the radio went another way, and the cord went another way. Let me tell you, I experienced-- Electricity. The cord went over and hit the radiator. We had a radiator; our house was heated by a radiator, steam. And instead of blowing the fuse, it started a fire. A metal, a metal [unclear], I got a flame six inches high shooting up. I’m over here trying to get my business back together, the radio is over on the floor somewhere, you see. I experienced-- Electricity. Now, that’s not all. I was fixing a TV once, and I forgot that they had a capacitor in them, and it has, you know, 30 to 40,000 volts in it, maybe more, and you’re supposed to discharge that capacitor. Well, you know, I’m young, you learn the hard way sometimes, you know what I mean? You’re reminded of the rules you read, but the hard way. And if you know a capacitor, you don’t have to touch it to get zapped. All you got to do is get close enough for that powerful electricity to jump across, and I had my hand passing through, and that electric--boy, you think [unclear] can dance? You should have seen me dance. You see, there was a result. Are you with me? You see, and that’s how the word is used. You see, you can be afraid of a gun. You can have knowledge of a gun, that it can hurt you, it can kill you. You can know how the gun operates, but you don’t know what it is to be shot until you’re shot. And I was up in the mountains about a mile into the ravine, and I’m turned around, and I was heading back down the mountain. I was close to the top, and I heard this shot go off.
Can you know what a gun does without being shot?

He says “you can have all the knowledge you want, but until you experience it, you don’t know what’s happening.” He tells of being shot in the leg on a mountain and says “it was the experience that did that,” which is how he says the word “know” is used many times in the Bible.
Can you know what a gun does without being shot?

Ding. And then I felt like somebody hit me with a punch, with a hammer, and that punch was going right through my leg. Now, it all happened just like that, but my mind did not record it that way. My mind recorded it in slow motion. I could literally feel what I thought was a chisel, a punch going through my leg one centimeter at a time. Okay, but it all happened quickly. All right. See, you can have all the knowledge you want, but until you experience it, you don’t know what’s happening. All right, and I’m sitting there, my mind: this thing is going through my leg. Ah, my mind hadn’t registered it as a bullet yet. But anyway, then my body, uh, went into-- Shock. Yeah, my body went into shock. I’m on the side of a mountain, literally, the mountain’s like this. I’m not on a trail, as you know, Dave Kincer don’t take trails. I make my own trails. So when my body went into shock, I collapsed, and of course I went rolling down that mountain about 100, 150 feet, just rolled until I hit a bush and stopped. And I laid there, and I got my thoughts together, and I stood up, and I looked, and sure enough there’s a hole right there in my pants. There’s a hole over here, just like the book said it would be. Blood’s coming out on this side. So I unbuckled my belt, let down my pants, and I looked at it. Boy, over here it looked like somebody hit me with a hammer, just black and blue, nice round circle and just a little-- Opening. When I looked over to this side, a little bit different. Blood’s flowing out, muscle tissue hanging out, flesh tissue hanging out. I go, “This isn’t good.” So I’m up in the mountains, my car is down by the highway, and so I got my thoughts together, and I said, “Well, I got to get out of here before I pass out, because if I lose a lot of blood I’m going to faint and pass out. I got to get out of here, got to get out where somebody can find me.” So I took off, and let me tell you, I just went through brush, nothing got in my way. The shortest route from me to my car is the route I took. Knocked bushes down, didn’t matter. Ah, but see, I experienced the power of what a gun can do. I can describe it to you, see, the knowledge didn’t do that. The belief in it didn’t do that. It was the experience that did that. And this is how the word “know” is used many times in the Bible. Do you get it?
Is belief alone enough for eternal life? (John 10:27)

He reads John 10:27, “My sheep hear My voice, I know them,” and calls it an “intimate, resulting, personal encounter.” Belief is “one of the things,” he says, obedience is one of the things, and knowing Jesus is “one of the requirements” for eternal life.
Is belief alone enough for eternal life? (John 10:27)

Hallelujah. Don’t I live an interesting life? John 10:27: “My sheep hear My voice, I know them.” See, He says, “I know them.” That intimate, resulting, personal encounter. “They follow Me, and I give them” what? What is the result here? Eternal life. So is just belief necessary for eternal life? It’s one of the things. Is just obedience necessary for eternal life? It’s one of the things. Is knowing Jesus necessary for eternal life? Yes, it’s one of the requirements. And this is why the Congregational church, after Martin Luther put his thesis on the wall of the Catholic church and started the Lutheran movement, then the Presbyterians came in with a presbyter government and started their movement. They were not much different than the--
Is belief alone enough for eternal life? (John 10:27)
John 10:27: My sheep hear My voice, and I know them, and they follow Me.
Why must you experience salvation and be born again?

He says “you must be born again” and “there has to be a spiritual encounter.” Of Martin Luther he says “he got justification by faith, and that’s as far as he went,” and of those Jesus holds he says “when I know Him, nothing can touch me.”
Why must you experience salvation and be born again?

Catholics. But the Congregationalists came in and said, “No, the congregation has to be involved in government,” and there’s two things the Congregationalists brought: the congregation has to be involved in government, not just a few leaders, and you must experience salvation. See, you must be born again. There has to be a spiritual encounter. Hallelujah. [Unclear] Luther, he got justification by faith, and that’s as far as he went. Are you there, church? Hallelujah. And they will never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of My hand. When I know Him, nothing can touch me. All right, more examples of “know” used as a personal, intimate, resulting encounter, but this time it’s using the Word of God and the Spirit of God. All right, John 14--uh, John 8:31, Jesus--
Why must you experience salvation and be born again?

John 10:28: And I give them eternal life, and they shall never perish; neither shall anyone snatch them out of My hand. John 8:31: Then Jesus said to those Jews who believed Him, “If you abide in My word, you are My disciples indeed.
What is the difference between a believer and a disciple?

Referring to John 8:31, he says the Jews who believed were “believers but not disciples because they weren’t living in His Word,” and “believers aren’t disciples, and there’s a big difference.” He says the missing third leg is “having a personal encounter with Jesus Christ” that results in eternal life and discipleship, and that “that truth sets me free.”
What is the difference between a believer and a disciple?

Said to the Jews who believed on Him--now, were they believers? Were they believers? Yeah, okay, they were believers, but not achievers. Well, that was good. Why? He says, “If you abide in My word, then you’re My disciples indeed.” You see, they were believers but not disciples, because they weren’t living in His Word. See, believers aren’t disciples, and there’s a big difference. Hallelujah. America is at a place, and it’s been here for decades, that we gloat over our faith and our belief, and we’re missing the third leg of this thing, which is the most important one: that is having a personal encounter with Jesus Christ that results-- In eternal life and discipleship. “You shall know the truth”--see, when I have an intimate, personal encounter with the Word of God, that truth sets me free. See, they were believers, but they weren’t free. They weren’t disciples. So why we--why do we brag so much about being believers? Because we’ve been taught that’s all that’s necessary. But Paul said, “What I have not cease to declare to you the whole counsel of God,” and how many--you know, the key to a successful life is the whole counsel in the natural, isn’t that right? You know, you just can’t take recreation time, oh, recreation time, and just try to build your life on it. You got to have work time, family time, spouse time, as we learned last week in a home Bible study we had. You got to be balanced in--
What is the difference between a believer and a disciple?
John 8:32: And you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.” Acts 20:27: For I have not shunned to declare to you the whole counsel of God.
What does the truth set you free from, and free to do?

He says “I’m free from sin,” “I’m free from Satan,” “I’m free to serve Jesus Christ,” and free to worship Him, to lift his hands and to dance. Freedom does not come from clothes: “I’m not free because I wear a suit, and I’m not free because I don’t wear a suit. I’m free because I know Him.”
What does the truth set you free from, and free to do?

Everything. All right. “Free.” What am I free from? Well, number one, I’m free from sin. Number two, I’m free from Satan. Number three, I’m free to serve Jesus Christ. Number four, I’m free to worship Him. I’m free to lift up my hand, I’m free to dance. You see, I was telling one of the young people last month, I met somebody that said they were free because they wear casual clothes. I go, “Man, there’s nothing in the Bible about freedom and casual clothes.” So I started wearing a suit. I said, “I’m free no matter what I wear.” Amen. It amazes me how we read--reduce the Bible down to some nonsense. I’m not free because I wear a suit, and I’m not free because I don’t wear a suit. I’m free because I know Him, and I know His Word, and I’ve experienced its--
Why do some believers stay jealous, quarrelsome and divided?

He says believers “can do anything they want, but they’re wimps, they’re babies,” and from their Bible study that “babies are jealous, they quarrel and argue all the time, and they divide.” He says “we need to grow up.”
Why do some believers stay jealous, quarrelsome and divided?

Power. So I can lift my hands, I can dance, I can kneel before God, I can do these things. Why? Because I’m free. I can go to church instead of staying home on Sunday morning. Why? Because I’m free from my flesh running my life. Hallelujah. Believers, they can do anything they want, but they’re wimps, they’re babies, and we learned in our Bible study that babies are jealous, they quarrel and argue all the time, and they divide. Are you there? And that’s what America’s full of: a bunch of quarreling, jealous, dividing believers. We need to grow up. Allelujah. We’ve learned four stages last week of the Christian growth, biblical stages. All right.
What happened when Peter preached on the day of Pentecost? (Acts 2:37)

He says the people who heard Peter “were cut to the heart”: pricked, stirred in their heart, mind and emotion. He says the wind and the tongues did not do that; it happened when Peter “preached the word that he knew, the word that was alive to him.”
What happened when Peter preached on the day of Pentecost? (Acts 2:37)

Now, these disciples knew the truth, and so they went and spoke it. Acts 2:37: when they heard the word on the day of Pentecost, the words of Peter, they were cut to the heart. See, what was the result of hearing a word that Peter knew? The result was the people that heard it were cut to the heart. They were pricked at their heart, they were stirred in their heart, their mind, their emotion. You see, the wind didn’t do that. That us Pentecostals put such an emphasis on the fiery tongues, didn’t do that. All those people speaking the mighty works of God in 15 different languages didn’t do this. When Peter stood up and preached the word that he knew, the word that was alive to him, see, intimate to him, then the people were--
What happened when Peter preached on the day of Pentecost? (Acts 2:37)
Acts 2:37: Now when they heard this, they were cut to the heart, and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles, “Men and brethren, what shall we do?”
What did the people do after being cut to the heart, and why did Stephen’s hearers react differently?

He says those cut to the heart were told to repent and be baptized and they would receive the Holy Ghost. When Stephen preached in Acts 7:54, he says, “they ground their teeth at him, they got fighting mad,” dragged him out of the city and stoned him.
What did the people do after being cut to the heart, and why did Stephen’s hearers react differently?

Pricked in their heart. So the people said, “What must they do?” So what was the result? They were cut to the heart, and they told him to repent, be what? Baptized, and you shall receive the Holy Ghost. All three things. All right. Now, you got to understand there’s a different encounter here in Acts 7:54, when Stephen preached the word to these people, these accusers, these opponents. They [unclear] the same [unclear], and he preached the word that he knew. [Unclear] cut to the heart, but they ground their teeth at him, they got fighting mad, they dragged him out of the city and stoned him. And see, this is our opponents. I told you the Word of God, when you preach it, the Word of God, it is not--
What did the people do after being cut to the heart, and why did Stephen’s hearers react differently?

Acts 2:38: Then Peter said to them, “Repent, and let every one of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins; and you shall receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. Acts 7:54: When they heard these things they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed at him with their teeth.
Is the Word of God neutral, and why do some people attack the Bible?

He says the Word of God “is not neutral. It either makes you mad or it makes you glad.” He says opponents attack the Bible because “they don’t want to hear that they’ve got to repent of their sins,” that “the Word cuts,” and “don’t take it personally.”
Is the Word of God neutral, and why do some people attack the Bible?

Neutral. It either makes you mad or it makes you glad. And our opponents want to destroy us. They want to bash the Bible, they want to get rid of the Bible: the atheists, the homosexuals, the humanists, the hedonists, the liberals, and all these people in America. They attack the Bible. Why? Because they don’t want to hear that they’ve got to repent of their sins. So when people, you know, react adversely to--just remember that’s part of the package. The Word cuts. They can reject it, but it cuts. Amen. Don’t take it personally. Now, number five, John 14:17: “the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither sees Him nor knows Him.” See, the world doesn’t know the Spirit of truth, but you know Him. He’s talking to His disciples: “You know Him, He is with you and shall be in you.” Now, who was with them?
Is the Holy Spirit with you when you invite Jesus in? (John 14:17)

He says you can’t separate the three parts of God, and that when we invite Jesus into our life, “You’re saved.” He says Jesus plainly says the Holy Spirit is with you, and “the baptism of the Holy Ghost is later, is another experience.”
Is the Holy Spirit with you when you invite Jesus in? (John 14:17)

Jesus. See, God said, “I will pour out My Spirit.” I’m telling you, you can’t separate these three parts of God, and yet you have to, to understand them. Hallelujah. So you see, unlike the Pentecostal brethren who believe you got to be filled with the Holy Ghost and speaking in tongues to be saved, because that’s the sign of the Holy Ghost, Jesus plainly says the Holy Spirit is what? With you. When we invite Jesus into our life, does He come? Yeah. Is He a Spirit? Yeah. You’re saved. You see, the baptism of the Holy Ghost is later, is another experience.
Is the Holy Spirit with you when you invite Jesus in? (John 14:17)
John 14:17: the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither sees Him nor knows Him; but you know Him, for He dwells with you and will be in you.
What does John 17:3 say eternal life is?
He reads that eternal life is that they may know the only true God and Jesus Christ whom He sent. He says the Bible defines things, and that “the word of God will direct you to” the joy of the Lord.
What does he say the joy of the Lord is?
He says the joy of the Lord is your strength: “if you don’t have the joy of the Lord, you’re not strong.” He asks, “why do we want to walk around sad when we can walk around glad?”
What are the three legs of the stool he uses for eternal life?
He names believe and obey, and says the third leg is knowing God and Jesus Christ through a personal encounter. He says God holds it all together at the top.
Can you separate Jesus from God?
No. He says “some people try to separate Jesus from God, you can’t do that, and some people try to separate God from Jesus and have only Jesus only. You can’t do either.” Both are in the equation.
Can my pastor or a big author get me into a relationship with God?
He says “your pastor can’t get you through there. There’s no big author that can get you into that.” It has to be you yourself, individually, personally, intimately.
Is faith by itself enough, according to this message?
He says faith is “only one step in the knowledge and understanding of God.” He points to the woman who believed and obeyed, but who was not healed until she touched Jesus.
How does Mary show that knowledge alone is not enough?
He says Mary knew that to have a baby you needed a man, “but that didn’t give her a baby.” It took the power of God overshadowing her.
Why does he talk about electricity?
It is his own example of knowing by contact: “you can understand electricity,” but you don’t know it until you come in contact with it. He tells of being shocked by a radio cord and a capacitor.
Is obedience enough for eternal life without knowing Jesus?
He says belief is one of the things, obedience is one of the things, and “knowing Jesus necessary for eternal life? Yes, it’s one of the requirements.”
What does he say the Congregationalists brought?
He says they said the congregation has to be involved in government, not just a few leaders, and that “you must experience salvation.”
Why does he say believers are not always disciples?
He says “they were believers but not disciples because they weren’t living in His Word.” He says we brag about being believers “because we’ve been taught that’s all that’s necessary.”
Does he say what you wear makes you free?
No. He says “there’s nothing in the Bible about freedom and casual clothes,” and that he is free no matter what he wears, because he knows Him and His Word.
What does being “cut to the heart” mean in this message?
He says it means being pricked at the heart, stirred in the heart, mind and emotion, when a person hears a word that the preacher knew personally.
What were people told to do after they were cut to the heart?
He says they asked what they must do and were told to repent and be baptized, and they would receive the Holy Ghost.
Does he say speaking in tongues is required to be saved?

No. He says that, unlike those who believe you must be filled with the Holy Ghost and speak in tongues to be saved, Jesus plainly says the Holy Spirit is with you and “You’re saved.” He says the baptism of the Holy Ghost is a later experience.

items.t: A Powerful Side of Eternal Life Part 2 How Important Can Eternal Life be to Us Individually?

items.ser: A Powerful Side of Eternal Life · Part 2
tg: A Powerful Side of Eternal Life
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer continues his teaching that eternal life is a personal, intimate, resulting encounter with God and Jesus Christ, using the new covenant promise that all shall know the Lord, Paul’s desire to know Christ, and Job’s “I know that my Redeemer lives.” He shares how his own encounter kept him consistent, then argues that the Bible calls people to repentance rather than therapy. He closes by saying a big crowd is not God’s approval and asking listeners whether they have ever really met the Master.
What power does the Holy Spirit give when you receive Him? (Acts 1:8)

He says the result of an intimate, personal encounter with the Holy Spirit is power to “be a witness, be evidence, be proof,” not power to roll on the floor or dance like a chicken. He says Peter “simply stood up and preached the word, and the word worked.”
What power does the Holy Spirit give when you receive Him? (Acts 1:8)

So we see here the result is receiving the Holy Spirit in us, not just with us but in us. Now that brings us to Acts 1:8: “You shall receive what? Power, after the Holy Spirit shall come upon you.” What’s the result when you come into an intimate, personal encounter with the Holy Spirit here? Power. Power to roll on the floor? No. Power to dance like a chicken, all these things that I saw back there as a young Christian? No. Power to what? Be a witness, be evidence, be proof, both in Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria, and the uttermost parts of the world. Hallelujah. And Peter, when he stood up and preached that simple message about Jesus and 4,000 were added to the church, he was
What power does the Holy Spirit give when you receive Him? (Acts 1:8)
Acts 1:8: But you shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you shall be witnesses to Me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.”
What is eternal life? (a personal, intimate, resulting encounter)

He states that “eternal life is a personal, intimate, resulting encounter, resulting meeting with God and Jesus Christ.” He recalls Jesus saying that if you love Him and keep His commandments, He and the Father will make their home in you, and asks, “How many want the whole package?”
What is eternal life? (a personal, intimate, resulting encounter)

experiencing the power to witness and the result. Amen. And he didn’t roll on the floor, he didn’t do a jitter, big jiggle, he simply stood up and preached the word, and the word worked. A witness from the power of the Holy Spirit. That was good if you can handle it all. Right. Now, eternal life is, I’m going to make this statement now from the evidence that I gave you: eternal life is a personal, intimate, resulting encounter, resulting meeting with God and Jesus Christ. All right. Jesus said, “If you love Me, you’ll keep My commandments, and Me and My Father will come and make our abode in you.” How many want the whole package? Yeah, we want it all.
What is eternal life? (a personal, intimate, resulting encounter)
John 14:23: Jesus answered and said to him, “If anyone loves Me, he will keep My word; and My Father will love him, and We will come to him and make Our home with him.
Who can know the Lord under the new covenant? (Hebrews 8:11)

He says the new covenant promises that all shall know the Lord, “from the least of them to the greatest,” and that this personal knowing is “not just the Pentecostals, not just the Baptist, everyone that believes and comes can have” it. He says it is “not limited, it’s in the covenant.”
Who can know the Lord under the new covenant? (Hebrews 8:11)

Hallelujah. Now, Hebrews 8:11, this is the new covenant: “None shall teach his neighbor and his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ for all shall know Me, from the least of them to the greatest.” All shall have a personal, intimate, resulting encounter with Jesus Christ. That’s in the covenant. Not just the Pentecostals, not just the Baptist, everyone that believes and comes can have this personal knowing of Jesus Christ. Amen. Not limited, it’s in the covenant. And if you feel wimpy, they got the word “least” in there. If you feel like you’re a mighty man of God already, they got the “greatest” in there. You still need it. Amen.
Who can know the Lord under the new covenant? (Hebrews 8:11)
Hebrews 8:11: None of them shall teach his neighbor, and none his brother, saying, ‘Know the LORD,’ for all shall know Me, from the least of them to the greatest of them.
Do we still know Christ only as He was in the flesh? (2 Corinthians 5:16)

He says we have heard the story of Jesus’ life, death and resurrection, but Paul says we know Him that way no longer because He is risen, on His throne, and with us in Spirit as “Christ in us, the hope of glory.” He says this is “the difference between being born again and just a believer.”
Do we still know Christ only as He was in the flesh? (2 Corinthians 5:16)

2 Corinthians 5:16: “Though we have known Christ according to the flesh, yet we know Him thus no longer.” Okay. We heard the story: Jesus came and He was born of a virgin, and He, you know, lived with His parents, and, you know, He went to the temple and dazzled the scribes and the priests there in the temple with His knowledge of the Scriptures, and then He went back and He became a carpenter, and then, you know, He got baptized, and got baptized in the Holy Ghost, and preached and did miracles and all that, and died on the cross and rose. We know that part of Jesus. Amen. But what Paul said, “For this reason, I’m sorry, yet now we know Him that way no longer.” Why? Because He’s not in the flesh anymore. He has risen. He is in His throne in heaven. He poured out Himself back in the church on the day of Pentecost. He is with us now in Spirit. We don’t know Him just in the flesh. We know Him what? As Christ in us, the hope of glory, the Spirit of Christ. Can I hear an amen? And we know Him. “For this reason, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creature; old things have passed away, and all things become new.” See, this is the difference between being born again and just a believer. And the Congregationalists were right: the Bible plainly tells us there is power in the birthing in our new spiritual life. And eternal life is that encounter with Jesus Christ. Isn’t that powerful? Hallelujah.
Do we still know Christ only as He was in the flesh? (2 Corinthians 5:16)

2 Corinthians 5:16: Therefore, from now on, we regard no one according to the flesh. Even though we have known Christ according to the flesh, yet now we know Him thus no longer. 2 Corinthians 5:17: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.
What does Paul mean by “that I may know Him”? (Philippians 3:10)

He says Paul counted everything he gained in this world as worthless compared to knowing Christ and the power of His resurrection. He says too many people stay at the blood and the death, but “we have a resurrected Savior,” and that Christianity is “not a philosophy, it’s a reality.”
What does Paul mean by “that I may know Him”? (Philippians 3:10)

Philippians 3:10 says, “That I may know Jesus.” I count all things worthless, anything I gain in this world, Paul says I count it as dung. I wanted the knowledge of Christ, and I want to know Him and the power of His resurrection. You see, too many people stay at the blood and the death, but we have a resurrected Savior, and the same Spirit that raised Christ from the dead dwells where? In us. Folks, that’s what makes Christianity different. We have a living God that lives in us, guides us, directs us, empowers us. This is not a philosophy, it’s a reality. You can’t reduce Christianity down just to another philosophy. An encounter with a supernatural God is a very powerful thing.
What does Paul mean by “that I may know Him”? (Philippians 3:10)
Philippians 3:10: that I may know Him and the power of His resurrection, and the fellowship of His sufferings, being conformed to His death,
What is the understanding Jesus has given us? (1 John 5:20)

He reads that Jesus has given us an understanding, and says that understanding is not only being saved by grace through faith but “that we may know Him,” a “personal, intimate, resulting encounter that changes my life.” He says those who deny that Jesus is the true and only God are “antichrist; they’re opposing who Christ is.”
What is the understanding Jesus has given us? (1 John 5:20)

John 5:20: “We know the Son of God has come and given us an understanding.” Now listen to this. This we know, that Jesus Christ has come, and this Jesus has given us an understanding. Now what is that understanding? That I’m saved by grace through faith? No. That we may know Him: personal, intimate, resulting encounter that changes my life. I’m a new creature. “We know Him who is true. He’s given us an understanding that we are in Him,” Jesus Christ. And look at this: “This is the true God and eternal life.” Now, I submit to you two questions. Is Jesus the true and only God according to this verse? People that say He is not are antichrist; they’re opposing who Christ is.
What is the understanding Jesus has given us? (1 John 5:20)

1 John 5:20: And we know that the Son of God has come and has given us an understanding, that we may know Him who is true; and we are in Him who is true, in His Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God and eternal life.
How did knowing God change his life, and do you have to be a preacher to know Him?

He tells of repenting at the altar and feeling “the weight of sin just lift off,” then being filled with the baptism of the Holy Spirit and having the Word revealed “line upon line, precept upon precept.” He says others who got saved with him backslid but he stayed consistent “because I experienced these things,” and that you don’t have to be a preacher for God to come to you personally.
How did knowing God change his life, and do you have to be a preacher to know Him?

Now, I submit to you another thing. Did Jesus give us the mental understanding that we could know Him? Absolutely. Is it in His new covenant? Absolutely. And then He explains what knowing is. And I don’t know about you, but this is what changed my life. See, when I actually went up to the altar and repented of my sins, I had an encounter with God there. Literally, I felt the weight of sin just lift off my life. I didn’t even know I had it. When I got filled with the baptism of the Holy Spirit, the love and the power that came, and the force within me to go to the Word and learn the Word. You see, I experienced these things. I experienced salvation, I experienced the baptism of the Holy Ghost, and I experienced the Word being revealed to me little by little, line upon line, precept upon precept, and it made the difference in the world in my life. And while others that got saved when I got saved, and in the area I got saved, departed and went their own way and backslid, I stayed consistent. Why? Because I experienced these things in my life. And when troubles come, they didn’t trouble me. When temptation come, I didn’t have to give in to it. Are you there? I’m just trying to give you an illustration. Mr. Barnes, he’s been around ever since I’ve known him. Say it’s not just me, I know all kinds of people. They’re not famous, they don’t write books, but Christ was real to them. They know Him, and they stayed consistent with Him. Hallelujah. I mean, you know, you don’t have to be a preacher to know God and be a light to the world. That’s right. You don’t have to be a preacher for God to come to you and personally cause you to experience the things of God. Absolutely. They’re for all of us.
What did Job know about his Redeemer? (Job 19:25)

He says Job used the word “I know” and had “a personal, intimate, resulting encounter with my God,” even without Scripture telling him Jesus would come back to the earth. He says Job knew that after his body was gone “in my flesh I will see Him,” and “that’s eternal life.”
What did Job know about his Redeemer? (Job 19:25)

Now, in Job, this isn’t a new thing. In Job, I love this verse. I can still remember reading my Bible through for the first time, and this verse just woke me up. This message has been around. See, Job is back there when Abraham lived, long time ago. I know. Job 19:25: “That my Redeemer lives.” See, he used that word “I know.” I’ve had a personal, intimate, resulting encounter with my God. He said, “He shall stand at last on the earth.” Job had no Scripture telling him that Jesus Christ was going to come back to the earth after He came the first time. “He is, Jesus shall stand at the last day on the earth after my skin is destroyed.” After I die, “this I know, that in my flesh I will see God, whom I will see for myself.” He said, yes, my body is going to go to the grave, the worms are going to eat me, but I know my Redeemer is going to come in the last day, and in my flesh I will see Him. That’s eternal life. That’s exactly what Paul said, wasn’t it? And folks, with this kind of an encounter and experience, let me tell you, Christianity is just a motor. I mean, it’s a powerful engine within you driving you upward all the time. Amen.
What did Job know about his Redeemer? (Job 19:25)
Job 19:25: For I know that my Redeemer lives, And He shall stand at last on the earth;
Why does knowing Jesus decide where you spend eternity? (Luke 23:43)

He says that if eternal life is knowing Him, the end result is spending eternity with Jesus, while those who reject Him “will spend eternity away from Jesus, because we’re all born into eternity.” He points to Jesus telling the thief on the cross, “Today you’re going to be with Me in paradise.”
Why does knowing Jesus decide where you spend eternity? (Luke 23:43)

Hallelujah. Luke 23:43: “Today shall you be with Me in paradise.” Okay, He turned to the thief on the cross, one of them, and said, “Today you’re going to be with Me in paradise.” Why is that important? Because if eternal life is knowing Him, then what is, you know, what’s the end result? The end result is I spend eternity with Jesus, while you that reject Him and don’t want to know Him will spend eternity away from Jesus, because we’re all born into eternity. But this is eternal life, that I may know Him, that I may spend eternity with Jesus Christ. Hallelujah. “To be absent in the body is to be present with the Lord.” That is eternal life. Did you get it?
Why does knowing Jesus decide where you spend eternity? (Luke 23:43)

Luke 23:43: And Jesus said to him, “Assuredly, I say to you, today you will be with Me in Paradise.” 2 Corinthians 5:8: We are confident, yes, well pleased rather to be absent from the body and to be present with the Lord.
If the Bible only mentions a sin a few times, is it a small issue?

He recounts answering the argument that the Bible opposes homosexuality only six times by asking how many times it opposes stealing, and how many times it mentions sex with children. His point: “If the Bible mentions it one time, it’s law.”
If the Bible only mentions a sin a few times, is it a small issue?

Now let me talk about my opponents for a little bit. Okay, talking to homosexuals recently, their argument was that the Bible only opposes homosexuality six times, so therefore it’s not a big issue. I said, “Sir, how many times does the Bible oppose stealing?” Well, they don’t know, of course, and neither do you, because I’m in debates with them and I got to get answers. I’m fighting with them, I’m trying to free them. I said, “Eight times. Does that mean stealing is okay?” I said, “Let me ask you again, sir. How many times in the Bible is sex with children mentioned?” And they go, “Well, it says, you know, you’ve got to not offend the little kids, and not, but it doesn’t say, ‘Thou shalt not have sex with children.’” I said, “How many times does the Bible say that?” And of course they don’t know. I said, “Zero.” I said, “Are you telling me it’s okay to have sex with an 8-year-old kid, a four-year-old kid?” I said, “Your argument is stupid. If the Bible mentions it one time, it’s law.” Amen.
Can therapy change people, or does it take the power of knowing Christ?

He says he watched churches “go from the power of the Word to therapy,” both telling people it is okay and not okay to be homosexual, and says “therapy is not in the Bible.” He says one therapy group’s leaders left it, and concludes “therapy doesn’t work. The power of knowing Christ does.”
Can therapy change people, or does it take the power of knowing Christ?

Exodus International is a group that started in Melodyland Church back in the ‘60s, ‘70s. They used reparative therapy, they called it, “pray the gay away,” to get homosexuals to stop being homosexual. Therapy is a mental, medical way of trying to get people to change behavior or physical deficiencies and so forth. All right. And I watched this psycho stuff coming into the church. All right, I watched churches go from the power of the Word to therapy. And Melodyland was the leader of it, one of the leaders. Big church, famous people come from all over to go there to their charismatic conferences and so forth. And I’ve been to a couple of them myself, not the conferences but meetings where special, like David Wilkerson came in. They were very powerful, but you can’t stay powerful if you build on the wrong foundation. So through therapy, even today, they’re trying to treat human behavior through mental treatment, trying to convince them, talk them out of it. And the other side’s the same thing. I saw a documentary, and other Christians are trying to tell homosexuals, this group, they brought these young people in and said, “Now look in the mirror.” They looked in the mirror. “Now who do you see?” “That’s me.” I said, “Now say, ‘I see a child of God.’” And they would say, “I see a child of God.” See, “Now you’re a child of God.” So we got therapy going on on both sides: it’s okay to be a homosexual, it’s not okay being a homosexual. Let me tell you, folks, therapy is not in the Bible. Are you there? And it wasn’t in there when I was a young Christian, and I stood up to Melodyland back there as a young Christian. I challenged them because they challenged me. They said I was teaching a bad doctrine, so we got into a little corral once, and I won that corral. The people lied. I wasn’t teaching that at all. They said I was teaching Jesus wasn’t coming. I didn’t teach that. I just didn’t teach He was coming the way they were teaching, that’s all. Hallelujah. Now, Melodyland was a round church. It used to be the Melodyland Theater, and big singers and everything come there, and then they turned it into this charismatic center. And of course it failed. And the leaders of this Exodus International, two leaders, Gary Cooper, who died from AIDS, left the group. These were the ones that were changing homosexuals’ lives. They left the group with a man named Michael [unclear]. They both left their wives and they lived in a homosexual relationship, and Gary died of AIDS. And what’s the point here? Therapy doesn’t work. The power of knowing Christ does. If we don’t have power of the Word, power of the Spirit, power of Jesus, we have nothing more than the world does.
What does the Bible use to change people: therapy or repentance?

He says “the Bible never uses therapy to change people’s lives. The Bible uses repentance”: admit you are wrong, confess you have violated God’s Word, turn from the way you were going, and go to Christ and the Word. He says this “is the power of the gospel under salvation” and can’t be replaced with therapy or psychology.
What does the Bible use to change people: therapy or repentance?

Now, the Bible never uses therapy to change people’s lives. The Bible uses repentance. The Bible says repent. The Bible says admit you’re wrong, confess that you’re wrong, that you have violated God’s Word. The Bible says use self-control. We’ve got to preach repentance. Repent means you turn from what you were doing, the way you were going. It’s your responsibility to turn and denounce that wrong and admit you were wrong and go to Christ and go to that Word, and He will build you up, because He can’t lie. You can’t replace that with therapy, you can’t replace that with psychology. That is the power of the gospel under salvation.
Can someone believe in God and still not be free from sin?

He says he knows people who believe in God and think they are Christians “but they’re not free. Why? Because they don’t know Him.” He says that until a person decides to repent and follow the Word, “the thief is going to stay a thief, the drug addict is going to stay a drug addict,” and that people want to keep what they’re doing and still go to heaven.
Can someone believe in God and still not be free from sin?

Amen. And we saw back there that believers were not free. And there’s a lot of homosexuals I know that believe in God and they believe they’re Christians, but they’re not free. Why? Because they don’t know Him. I can pray in tongues, I can pray in English, I can pray with fortitude, I can pray with theatrics, but until they decide to repent and admit they’re wrong and follow the Word and seek the Word and seek Jesus, they are going to stay a homosexual. The thief is going to stay a thief. The drug addict is going to stay a drug addict. Now, is that the gospel? Yeah. Nowhere in the Bible do you find them using therapy. They used the Word of God and it worked. Of course, people can reject it, but see, they want to reject it but they want acceptance in the rejection. They still want to go to heaven, but they want to reject repentance, they want to reject self-control, they want to keep doing what they’re doing, but they still want to go to heaven. So they want you to approve their belief as a justifiable way to get into heaven.
Should churches rely on programs and spectacle to draw a crowd?

He says some circles get “hooped up in the Spirit” without preaching repentance, and others get hooped up in programs and theatrics, with the next attraction always bigger. He says “that ain’t what the Bible people did. They preached the word and the Lord added to the church as He saw fit.”
Should churches rely on programs and spectacle to draw a crowd?

Now that was a good statement. And so in the Pentecostal circles, we get all hooped up in the Spirit and the presence and, you know, tongues and prophecy and all this, and we’re not preaching repentance and people aren’t getting delivered. And outside those circles they’re all hooped up in programs and, you know, theatrics of special programs and, you know, bring an elephant in and get the people to come in, and what are you going to do next Sunday? You got to bring a tiger in to get the people to come in. And what do you do next? Well, you got to have a skydiver come down and land in the parking lot. You know, that ain’t what the Bible people did. They preached the word and the Lord added to the church as He saw fit.
Is a big crowd a sign of God’s approval?

He says “the crowd is not God’s approval,” because the crowd left Jesus when He asked for commitment and He kept the same message, being after disciples and a personal encounter. He closes by asking whether you have ever really met the Master and had an encounter where the power touched your life.
Is a big crowd a sign of God’s approval?

Melodyland was one of the first mega churches. It doesn’t even exist today, and I knew it wouldn’t exist. He was after people that He could know, have an intimate, personal encounter with, turn them into a new creature, change their life. The lead church is known by its leadership, and the church. Are you with me? Hallelujah. I submit to you today that this is eternal life: a personal, intimate, resulting encounter with God. What does he say is the result of a personal encounter with the Holy Spirit?

How does he define eternal life?
He says “eternal life is a personal, intimate, resulting encounter, resulting meeting with God and Jesus Christ.” He calls it the third leg of the three-legged stool from his earlier message.

No. He says it is “in the covenant, not just the Pentecostals, not just the Baptist, everyone that believes and comes can have this personal knowing of Jesus Christ.”
What does he say is the difference between being born again and just a believer?

He says we no longer know Christ only “in the flesh”; we know Him “as Christ in us, the hope of glory,” and “if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creature.” He says “this is the difference between being born again and just a believer.”
Does he say Jesus is the true and only God?

He reads the verse and says “this is the true God and eternal life,” asking whether Jesus is the true and only God according to it. He says people who say He is not are “antichrist; they’re opposing who Christ is.”
What does he say happened when he repented and was baptized in the Holy Spirit?

He says he “felt the weight of sin just lift off,” then was filled with the baptism of the Holy Spirit, with love, power and a drive to learn the Word. He says he experienced salvation, the baptism of the Holy Ghost and the Word being revealed little by little.
Do you have to be a preacher to know God?
No. He says there are all kinds of people who are not famous and don’t write books but Christ was real to them, and “you don’t have to be a preacher to know God and be a light to the world.”
What did Job say about seeing God?
He says Job knew his Redeemer lives and would stand on the earth, and that “in my flesh I will see God, whom I will see for myself.” He adds, “That’s eternal life.”
Who does he say will spend eternity away from Jesus?

He says those who reject Jesus and don’t want to know Him “will spend eternity away from Jesus,” and that everyone is born into eternity; the question is what place you spend it. He says eternal life is knowing Him and spending eternity with Him.
How many times must the Bible mention something for it to be law?
He says that “if the Bible mentions it one time, it’s law,” and illustrates it by asking how many times the Bible mentions stealing, and how many times it says not to have sex with children.
Is therapy found in the Bible?

He says “therapy is not in the Bible” and that it wasn’t there when he was a young Christian. He says he watched churches move from the power of the Word to therapy, which he describes as a mental, medical way of trying to change behavior.
What does “repent” mean according to this message?

He says “repent means you turn from what you were doing, the way you were going.” It is your responsibility to turn, denounce the wrong, admit you were wrong, and go to Christ and the Word, and “He will build you up because He can’t lie.”
Can a person pray in tongues and still need to repent?

He says he can pray in tongues, in English, with fortitude or with theatrics, “but until they decide to repent and admit they’re wrong and follow the Word and seek the Word and seek Jesus,” they stay as they are.
Is the crowd a sign of God’s approval?
No. He says, “the crowd is not God’s approval,” noting the crowd left Jesus when He asked for commitment, and that Paul did not change his message when the province of Asia rejected him.
What question does he leave listeners with?
He asks, “Have you ever really met the Master? Have you ever really had an encounter with God where you knew the power had come into you, had touched your life?”

items.ser: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors · Overview (after the Adding series)
tg: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors
p: In “Adding,” a Vine Cluster guest speaker (who refers to Mr. Kincer in the third person) walks through 2 Peter 1:5-10 and says believers must add virtue, knowledge, self-control, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness and agape love to their faith so they will not be barren. He contrasts Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego—who kept adding and were found ten times better—with Solomon, who received great wisdom but threw out virtue and fell. He closes with the promise that if you add to your faith you will never fall and will receive a rich welcome into the eternal kingdom.
What does “add to your faith” mean in 2 Peter 1:5?

He says the term implies you can’t stay in one place: as soon as you hear it you say you’ve got to do more than just believe or accept Christ in your heart—you’ve got to move on. The first addition is virtue, moral excellence.
What does “add to your faith” mean in 2 Peter 1:5?

We’re going to step back and take a broad view and look at it. We’re going to go to that verse in Second Peter 1:5, and now you guys know it by heart. And you have all these things. And the term “add to your faith,” it implies that you can’t stay in one’s place. It’s such a good word. As soon as you hear it, you say, “I’ve got to do more than just believe. I’ve got to do more than just accept Christ in my heart. I’ve got to move on.” And it’s so good. And we’re going to look at this scripture and how much God is going to do for us. So “add to your faith virtue.” The virtue it’s talking about there is the moral excellence. As we learned, you’re committed to, you know, when you come to Christ.
What does “add to your faith” mean in 2 Peter 1:5?
2 Peter 1:5: But also for this very reason, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue, to virtue knowledge,
What is virtue or moral excellence in this sermon?

He says moral excellence means saying no to sin: you don’t abort babies, you don’t have sex outside of marriage, you throw the drugs out. Just by saying no and living that way, he says God begins to bless you before you even add the other things.
What is virtue or moral excellence in this sermon?

You have to say no to sin. The moral excellence: you don’t abort babies anymore, you’re not going out and have sex outside of marriage, you throw the drugs out, you say no to that stuff. And just by saying no to that, just by living a moral excellent life, it will bless you. Just by saying no, you haven’t even added these other things, but by getting rid of the sin and let God do a work in your life, it begins to bless you. And that’s just the first step. And then he says to add knowledge. And as we teach here, you’ve got to read the Scriptures when you go home. It’s not just Sunday morning. Mr. [unclear] can’t come up in 15 minutes and fill you with enough bread to last a week. Amen. We’ve got to read, we’ve got to study the Scriptures, we’ve got to know for ourselves.
What is virtue or moral excellence in this sermon?
2 Peter 1:5: But also for this very reason, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue, to virtue knowledge,
What does he say about self-control and patience?

He says self-control includes controlling your mind and your tongue—the Bible calls the tongue an unruly evil—and that marriage and kids are a crash course in tongue control. Patience is needed with parents, spouses, children and yourself.
What does he say about self-control and patience?

Self-control: you know, it’s also like the moral excellence, you have to say no, but self-control is also self-controlling your mind, taking care of it first in your mind, stopping that. The tongue: the Bible says the tongue is an unruly evil. Controlling the tongue—oh, man. Living in this life, getting married, having kids, you just have to learn. It’s a crash course in tongue control, right? Amen. You live with somebody, everything’s changing and you don’t know what’s going on. And patience—patience, my God, I need patience. Just like I was saying, you get married, you have kids, or just being a teenager having patience with your parents. Man, I’m telling you, that’s right. They can be tough. It can seem tough being a child. As parents, a husband and wives—patience. Man, you know, you’ve said these things over and over. You’ve got to have patience. Or maybe you don’t get it and you’ve got to have patience with yourself.
What does he say about self-control and patience?
James 3:8: But no man can tame the tongue. It is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.
What kind of love does he say we must add?

He points to agape love as defined in 1 Corinthians 13, not the world’s love. He says Jesus had so much love for the Pharisees that He came into conflict with them, because real love tells people when they are wrong.
What kind of love does he say we must add?

Like godliness—Christlike. Brotherly kindness: we come in here this morning, there are so many people loving one another, being kind sincerely. It was good. It was such a good feeling this morning in this place. And agape love, as defined in 1 Corinthians 13—you guys know that scripture. We all know about love, and it’s not love that’s defined by the world. It’s a different kind of love. It’s a love Jesus had. So much love for the Pharisees that he came in conflict with them. He rocked their world. He approached them and he said, “No, you’re wrong,” why? Because he loved them. And people don’t see love that way. They feel like it’s only a fuzzy. God is going to conflict with you. He’s going to approach you. Why? Because he loves you and he knows what’s best for you. He’s the Creator. Somewhere we’ve got to come to the realization that God really is the Creator. God really has so much power we don’t even understand it. And we sit here and we say to God, “What do you know, God?” What? He knows everything.
What kind of love does he say we must add?

1 Corinthians 13: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal. And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing. And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, but have not love, it profits me nothing. Love suffers long and is kind; love does not envy; love does not parade itself, is not puffed up; does not behave rudely, does not seek its own, is not provoked, thinks no evil; does not rejoice in iniquity, but rejoices in the truth; bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. Love never fails. But whether there are prophecies, they will fail; whether there are tongues, they will cease; whether there is knowledge, it will vanish away. For we know in part and we prophesy in part. But when that which is perfect has come, then that which is in part will be done away. When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child; but when I became a man, I put away childish things. For now we see in a mirror, dimly, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I shall know just as I also am known. And now abide faith, hope, love, these three; but the greatest of these is love.
What does 2 Peter 1:8 say if these things abound?

After Mr. Kincer has gone through the list, he reads that if these additions abound you will be neither barren nor unfruitful. He compares barrenness to Death Valley and says God wants us flourishing and bearing fruit.
What does 2 Peter 1:8 say if these things abound?

But it goes on to say—we want to look at these. You know, we talked a lot about these things, and Mr. Kincer has gone through. But after this, after the verse in 2 Peter 1:8, it’s very important what it says afterwards. It says, “For if these things”—talking about the additions to faith—“if these things abound, you will be neither barren nor unfruitful.” Barren: useless. You know, a desert is just—you go out there, it’s cracked. Death Valley. You can ride on it, you can tear it up, but that’s about it, you know. And it’s okay to be in a desert, but God wants us to be flourishing. God wants us to bear fruit. And yes, we do go through times of no water, and it causes us to dig deep. But when we apply these things, when these things abound in us, when we are exercising, when we take the knowledge and we go to the Scriptures and we get knowledge, we go to high school and we’re actually paying attention, and we go to college because we’re trying to add knowledge to ourselves—you know, God is going to bless those things. When we are more adding virtue, saying no. Amen.
What does 2 Peter 1:8 say if these things abound?
2 Peter 1:8: For if these things are yours and abound, you will be neither barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
How does bearing fruit help other people?
He says when you bear fruit you have something to give out, like an orchard whose oranges go throughout California and nourish people. Christ wants to transform who we are and people around us.
How does bearing fruit help other people?

When we add self-control, when we are trying to add patience, God is going to honor that. And it says right here, if these things abound you will neither be barren nor unfruitful—that means you’re going to be fruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ. And you see, the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ—Christ wants to transform who we are, and not just us but people around us. You see, when you bear fruit you have something to give out. You have a tree, an orchard. It gets sent out throughout all of California, and people partake of that, and they get nourishment and vitamin C from oranges and all this stuff. Amen. Because somebody took the time to plant, somebody took the time to water, somebody took the time to take care and add to that seed.
How does bearing fruit help other people?
2 Peter 1:8: For if these things are yours and abound, you will be neither barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
What happens if someone lacks these qualities?

From 2 Peter 1:9 he says whoever lacks them is blind and shortsighted, like the Pharisees who believed in God and learned Scriptures but didn’t add Christ and forgot they were cleansed from old sins. Sin will creep in and hurt you.
What happens if someone lacks these qualities?

Second Peter 1 verse 9. You know, God is so—he’s like, you know, you’re going to be so—if these things abound in you, you’re going to be blessed, you’re going to be fruitful. And on the other side, if you don’t, it’s rough. You know, in the Old Testament, if you listen to Me, you’re going to be blessed. You’re going to be—oh man—you’re going to be great throughout the earth. If you don’t, you’re going to have a big problem. You’re not going to have blessing. You’re going to have problems in your life. Line: Second Peter 1:9. And those here that are young, and you’ll find as you grow up, if we don’t add these things, you’re going to find that sin is going to creep in. Sin is going to hurt you. “Whoever lacks these things”—these qualities—“is blind, shortsighted, seeing only what is near to him.” Blind, just like the Pharisees. The Pharisees, they weren’t adding to their faith. They believed in Abraham, they believed in God, but they didn’t add anything. They were adding knowledge, they were learning the Scriptures, but they missed it. They were blind. They couldn’t see. They weren’t adding Christ. “And has forgotten that he was cleansed from his old sins.” Again, here we see adding to our faith. We come out of sin. We’re cleansed from sin. Christ died on the cross to cleanse us, to get rid of that, to make us a new creature. It’s plain in the Scriptures, the process that we need to go through.
What happens if someone lacks these qualities?
2 Peter 1:9: For he who lacks these things is shortsighted, even to blindness, and has forgotten that he was cleansed from his old sins.
What promise does 2 Peter 1:10 give if you add to your faith?

He says if you do these things—if you add to your faith—you will never fall, and you will receive a rich welcome into the eternal kingdom. He wants that rich welcome, and says Jesus spoke of valuable mansions for His people.
What promise does 2 Peter 1:10 give if you add to your faith?

Amen. And such a powerful promise in 2 Peter 1:10. It goes on to say, if you do these things—if you add to your faith—you will never fall. And that is a promise worth seeking after. That is such a powerful promise. It says, and you will receive a rich welcome into the eternal kingdom. There’s different kind of welcomes. There’s a rich welcome and a poor welcome. And “oh yeah, yeah, you believe, come on in,” and “oh, there he is, the guy who added to his faith, the guy who did—come on in.” Man, you know, I don’t know what that means, a rich welcome, but I want a rich welcome. You know, Jesus keeps saying, “These things in My house are many mansions.” You know, he’s got something for us, and he’s saying mansions to let us know they’re valuable. So he’s got valuable things for his people. But we’ve got to add. He wants to reward us. He wants to reward his people. We have to add to our faith.
What promise does 2 Peter 1:10 give if you add to your faith?

2 Peter 1:10: Therefore, brethren, be even more diligent to make your call and election sure, for if you do these things you will never stumble; John 14:2: In My Father’s house are many mansions; if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you.
How did Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego add to their faith?

From Daniel 1:4 he says they were already adding knowledge and wisdom as young men with no blemish, skillful and teachable. He urges young people to stand out, believe in God and add to their faith the way he did in school.
How did Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego add to their faith?

Daniel 1:4. It says that the servant, the prince of the eunuchs, was to go out and find men, children of Israel, with no blemish, well-favored, skillful in wisdom and cunning in knowledge and understanding science, and teachable. Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego—I always say the name because I can’t remember their original names—they were already working on adding to their faith. They believed. They believed in God, and they were adding knowledge, they were adding wisdom. See, these young men stood out. And you guys, as young people, we’ve got to decide as young people to be individuals, to stand out. Cry, believe in God, stand and add to your faith. It’s going to have the best effect in your life. As a young person in high school I was different, and people around me were different. When I went to college I was different. When I was in college I actually listened. When I was in high school I listened. I did my work. And I tell you, that has blessed me ever since I’ve been out of college. And it’s going to hurt you if you don’t. If you don’t add.
How did Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego add to their faith?

Daniel 1:4: young men in whom there was no blemish, but good-looking, gifted in all wisdom, possessing knowledge and quick to understand, who had ability to serve in the king’s palace, and whom they might teach the language and literature of the Chaldeans.
How did God add to Daniel’s knowledge?

He reads Daniel 1:17 and 1:20: they had a level of knowledge, then God gave them more, and the king found them ten times better. Their greatest ability was submitting to adding to their faith, not being magical geniuses.
How did God add to Daniel’s knowledge?

And you see, Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, they were chosen because they stood out. They stood—they were adding to their faith. And it says in chapter 1 verse 17, you see they had knowledge, but then God gave them. Read this right here: God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom. You see, they had a level of knowledge, they had a level of wisdom, but then God came and gave them more. He added to their knowledge. I want that kind of knowledge. I want that kind of wisdom. I want that kind of understanding working in my home and my life and my family. But you see, these guys stood up for Christ. They had to begin to add faith. You have to start doing it. They stood out. They qualified. They were just qualifying. They weren’t chosen yet. They weren’t chosen yet. But God, in the middle of their qualification, from qualification to when they were chosen, God gave them more knowledge. God gave them wisdom and understanding. And it says in Daniel verse 20, in all matters of wisdom and understanding the king found them ten times better. And he found them ten times better because God gave them. God gave them knowledge. You know, they weren’t some magical awesome people. They didn’t have their own great ability. Their greatest ability was submitting to adding to their faith.
How did God add to Daniel’s knowledge?

Daniel 1:17: As for these four young men, God gave them knowledge and skill in all literature and wisdom; and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams. Daniel 1:20: And in all matters of wisdom and understanding about which the king examined them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and astrologers who were in all his realm.
Does God meet you in the middle when you add?

He says when you add, God meets you in the middle and gives you more—Nebuchadnezzar found them ten times better—and the New Testament says to whom who has, more will be given. You don’t have to be a genius; you choose to add.
Does God meet you in the middle when you add?

And you don’t have to be a super smart person. You don’t have to be a genius. You know, I would read Daniel, I say, “Gosh, this guy, he just had so much ability.” No. He made a choice as a young person to add to his faith, to exercise what the Bible said to do. And somewhere God met him in the middle of that and gave him more knowledge, more understanding, because God did it. And you see, when you add, God is going to meet you in the middle somewhere, and he’s going to give you more. He’s going to—the Bible says in the New Testament, to whom who has, more will be given. And you see, we’ve got to add to our faith. We’ve got to discipline ourselves. And King Nebuchadnezzar found them ten times better than all in his realm.
Does God meet you in the middle when you add?
Matthew 13:12: For whoever has, to him more will be given, and he will have abundance; but whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
What did God give Solomon, and did Solomon keep adding?

From 1 Kings 4:29 he says God gave Solomon wisdom, great insight and breadth of understanding; his wisdom was greater than the men of the East and Egypt. But he notes the Bible doesn’t say Solomon was adding to his faith.
What did God give Solomon, and did Solomon keep adding?

And we’re going to look at our second person. First Kings 4:29. God gave Solomon wisdom. You know, Solomon—I can’t see where—it doesn’t say in the Bible that he was adding to his faith. You know, I didn’t find that. So we’re going straight to the place where God gave him something. He asked for wisdom. He came to God and said, “I want wisdom to rule this people.” And it says in verse 29 that God gave Solomon wisdom, very great insight, breadth of understanding as measureless as the sand of the seashore. Solomon was given so much knowledge. He was given knowledge of things that we are finding out today in science. He was given knowledge by God that created everything. And people would come to hear all of this knowledge. Solomon’s wisdom was greater than the wisdom of all the men of the east. I mean, how do they find this stuff out? How do they know? He was wiser than all the men of the east, greater than all the wisdom of Egypt—all the wisdom combined, it sounds like. You see, God had blessed this guy. He was wiser than any other man. But if you read in First Kings 11 verse 1 through 4, it says, “But King Solomon loved many strange women.” King Solomon started to marry. He had 700 wives and 300 concubines.
What did God give Solomon, and did Solomon keep adding?
1 Kings 4:29: And God gave Solomon wisdom and exceedingly great understanding, and largeness of heart like the sand on the seashore.
How did Solomon fall after receiving wisdom?

From 1 Kings 11:1-4 he says Solomon loved many strange women—700 wives and 300 concubines—and they turned his heart to idols. He threw out virtue, self-control and knowledge; God was angry and brought judgment, which matches 2 Peter’s warning.
How did Solomon fall after receiving wisdom?

He—it says the Scripture, the Bible says that his wives began to turn his heart away from God. And then we find later on that he is praising and giving thanks to another god, to an idol. And you see, Solomon, he threw out adding to his faith. He threw out virtue. You know, he wasn’t supposed to marry all those girls. That wasn’t right. He threw it out. He threw out self-control. He threw out knowledge of Christ. He threw out the Scriptures. You know, knowledge—he knew who created everything. He threw it out. He threw out virtue and godliness. And his wives turned away his heart. Later on in his life God was angry with him and brought judgment on the land. You see, in Second Peter we learned that you’re going to be blessed when you add to your faith, and if you don’t there’s going to be punishment. And that’s exactly what happened with Solomon. God gave him all this wisdom. God gave him these things. But he turned away. He left his addition.
How did Solomon fall after receiving wisdom?

1 Kings 11:1-4: But King Solomon loved many foreign women, as well as the daughter of Pharaoh: women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Sidonians, and Hittites— from the nations of whom the LORD had said to the children of Israel, “You shall not intermarry with them, nor they with you. Surely they will turn away your hearts after their gods.” Solomon clung to these in love. And he had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines; and his wives turned away his heart. For it was so, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned his heart after other gods; and his heart was not loyal to the LORD his God, as was the heart of his father David.
What does “Daniel continued” mean for us?

He reads Daniel 1:21 that Daniel continued into the first year of King Cyrus, and has everyone say “continued.” Daniel kept adding and became more mature; if you add to your faith you will never fall and will receive a rich welcome.
What does “Daniel continued” mean for us?

But it says in Daniel 1:21 that Daniel continued even into the first year of King Cyrus. Daniel continued. Everybody say “continued.” Continued. Daniel continued. He continued to add to his faith.
