He continued to add. He didn’t neglect. He didn’t turn his heart from God. And if you read Daniel 1 through 12, you see Daniel becoming more and more mature, more excellent, more and more. Amen. And God is showing him more and more. And he wants to show you more and more. If you do these things you will never fall. If you add to your faith you’ll never fall, and you’ll receive a rich welcome into the eternal kingdom of our Lord Jesus.
What does “Daniel continued” mean for us?

Daniel 1:21: Thus Daniel continued until the first year of King Cyrus. 2 Peter 1:10: Therefore, brethren, be even more diligent to make your call and election sure, for if you do these things you will never stumble;
Is believing enough, or must you do more?
He says “add to your faith” means you’ve got to do more than just believe or accept Christ in your heart—you’ve got to move on.
Can a Sunday sermon alone feed you for the week?
He says Mr. [unclear] can’t fill you in 15 minutes with enough bread to last a week; you’ve got to read and study the Scriptures yourself.
Is controlling the tongue part of self-control?
Yes. He says the Bible calls the tongue an unruly evil, and living with someone is a crash course in tongue control.
He says Jesus had so much love for them that He came into conflict with them and said they were wrong, because He loved them.
He says barren means useless, like a cracked desert or Death Valley you can only ride on and tear up.
What is a rich welcome versus a poor welcome?
He contrasts a casual “yeah, you believe, come on in” with “oh, there he is, the guy who added to his faith, the guy who did—come on in.” and says he wants the rich welcome.
Why should young people stand out?
He says Daniel and his friends stood out as they added knowledge and wisdom, and that deciding as a young person to believe and add will have the best effect in your life.
Why were Daniel and his friends ten times better?
He says the king found them ten times better because God gave them knowledge—not because they were magical—after they submitted to adding to their faith.
How many wives and concubines does he say Solomon had?
He says Solomon had 700 wives and 300 concubines, and that his wives turned his heart away from God to an idol.
Will you never fall if you add to your faith?
He closes with 2 Peter’s promise: if you do these things and add to your faith you will never fall, and you’ll receive a rich welcome into the eternal kingdom of our Lord Jesus.

items.d: The speaker defines brotherly love as loving the true church and says it confirms new birth (1 Peter 1:22–23). God and the apostles teach it (1 Thessalonians 4; John 13:34); loving the brethren is serving…
items.ser: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors · Part 10
tg: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors
p: The speaker defines brotherly love as loving the true church and says it confirms new birth (1 Peter 1:22–23). God and the apostles teach it (1 Thessalonians 4; John 13:34); loving the brethren is serving Jesus because the church is his body (Acts 9:4; Matthew 25:40). He warns that not discerning the Lord’s body brings sickness and death (1 Corinthians 11:29), describes the church as a place of healing, word, repentance, and good works, and urges assembling to stir up love (Hebrews 10:24–26).
What is the Bible definition of brotherly love?

He says brotherly love is to love the true church, its membership, the true believer, and that it is confirmation of being born again—a change from wrong behavior and thinking to right by the Scriptures. He reads 1 Peter 1:22–23 about purifying souls in obeying the truth unto genuine brotherly love, loving one another fervently with a pure heart.
What is the Bible definition of brotherly love?

We’re again going to 2 Peter chapter 1 verses 4 through 5, and we’re going to be talking about adding brotherly love to godliness, self-control, knowledge, virtue, and faith. The Bible definition of brotherly love is to love the true church, the true church’s membership, the true believer. Brotherly love is confirmation of being born again—is going to be our first look at brotherly love. It’s a confirmation of being born again. Born again is a change from wrong behavior and thinking to a right behavior and thinking by the Scriptures. In 1 Peter chapter 1 verse 22 and 23, you have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto a genuine brotherly love. See that you love one another with a pure heart fervently—enthusiastically. See that you love one another with enthusiasm. Being born again, not of corruptible seed but incorruptible, by the word of God.
What is the Bible definition of brotherly love?

1 Peter 1:22-23: Since you have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit in sincere love of the brethren, love one another fervently with a pure heart, having been born again, not of corruptible seed but incorruptible, through the word of God which lives and abides forever, 2 Peter 1:5-7: But also for this very reason, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue, to virtue knowledge, to knowledge self-control, to self-control perseverance, to perseverance godliness, to godliness brotherly kindness, and to brotherly kindness love.
Is brotherly love confirmation that you have been born again?

He says most people know John 3 about being born of the Spirit, but Jesus also said his word is spirit—so both the Spirit and the word change our lives. Brotherly love confirms you have really been born again, and it is taught by God himself and his apostles.
Is brotherly love confirmation that you have been born again?

Most people understand that in John chapter 3 we are born again by the Spirit, but you also got to understand in John Jesus said my word is spirit. And not only does the Spirit come and personally change our lives, but the word of God comes and changes our life and moves us to apply the things of God in our life. So brotherly love is the confirmation that you’ve really been born again. Brotherly love is taught by God himself and his apostles.
What did God and Jesus teach about loving one another?

He reads 1 Thessalonians 4:9 that you are taught by God to love one another, and John 13:34 to love one another as Jesus loved you. By this all will know you are his disciples. He contrasts teachers who will not consent to Jesus’ wholesome words (1 Timothy 6:3).
What did God and Jesus teach about loving one another?

In 1 Thessalonians 4:9 through 12, concerning brotherly love, you have no need that I write unto you, as you are taught by God to love one another. God has taught you personally by Spirit when you got born again to love one another, and you do to all the brethren in Macedonia. You do that. But in 1 Timothy 6:3, if any man teach and consent not to wholesome words, even the words of our Lord Jesus Christ—okay, what did Jesus teach? John 13:34, love one another as I have loved you. Tells us how to love one another as he loved us. By this shall all men know you’re my disciples. He says there is an end result of loving one another, loving the true church, and is that other people outside will know that you are my disciplined ones, my pupils, my disciples.
What did God and Jesus teach about loving one another?

1 Thessalonians 4:9-12: But concerning brotherly love you have no need that I should write to you, for you yourselves are taught by God to love one another; and indeed you do so toward all the brethren who are in all Macedonia. But we urge you, brethren, that you increase more and more; that you also aspire to lead a quiet life, to mind your own business, and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you, that you may walk properly toward those who are outside, and that you may lack nothing. John 13:34-35: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another; as I have loved you, that you also love one another. By this all will know that you are My disciples, if you have love for one another.” 1 Timothy 6:3: If anyone teaches otherwise and does not consent to wholesome words, even the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the doctrine which accords with godliness,
Should brotherly love go beyond your own culture and nation?

He cites John 16:13 that the Spirit guides into all truth, and says the apostles urge believers to increase more and more—not only love brethren in Macedonia or the same culture and nationality, but love the brethren worldwide, state to state and nation to nation. They also seek a quiet life, working with your own hands, paying your own bills.
Should brotherly love go beyond your own culture and nation?

John 16:13, the Spirit of truth will guide you into all truth. So the Spirit comes and teaches us, Jesus comes and teaches us, God comes and teaches us himself to love the church of the living God. He goes on to say in 1 Thessalonians 4:9, we urge you—now it’s the apostles talking—we the apostles urge you, brethren, to increase more and more. Don’t just love the brethren in Macedonia. Just don’t love people in your same culture, your same nationality, whatever, but increase more and more. Go on to the next state. Go on to the next nation. Love the brethren worldwide. Increase more and more. And he says we also aspire you—we seek that you lead a quiet life. You’re not a lawless people doing violence and killing people and robbing—a quiet life—and take care of your own affairs, working with your own hands. Drive your own self to work. Don’t expect other Christians to do things for you. Pay your own bills. Balance your own checkbook. Get your act together and work, as we commanded you.
Should brotherly love go beyond your own culture and nation?

John 16:13: However, when He, the Spirit of truth, has come, He will guide you into all truth; for He will not speak on His own authority, but whatever He hears He will speak; and He will tell you things to come. 1 Thessalonians 4:9-12: But concerning brotherly love you have no need that I should write to you, for you yourselves are taught by God to love one another; and indeed you do so toward all the brethren who are in all Macedonia. But we urge you, brethren, that you increase more and more; that you also aspire to lead a quiet life, to mind your own business, and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you, that you may walk properly toward those who are outside, and that you may lack nothing.
What results does he say come from a quiet, working life among outsiders?

He says you will walk properly toward outsiders, may lack nothing, can pay bills and feed yourself, and must live within your means. Acts 2:42 continued in the apostles’ doctrine; 1 John 4:20 asks how you can love God whom you have not seen if you do not love your brother whom you have seen. Loving the brethren is loving Jesus.
What results does he say come from a quiet, working life among outsiders?

And number one, he says the result is you will walk properly to those who are outside. They’ll see that and say that’s good. And you may lack nothing. You can pay your bills. You can feed yourself. And we’ve got to live within our means to do that. And that’s the apostles talking. Acts 2:42, they continued steadfastly in the apostles’ doctrine. Okay, what’s one of the apostles’ doctrine? 1 John 4:20, he who does not love his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen? You see, the apostles taught brotherly love. God himself comes to us and teaches us to love the true church. Now loving the brethren, the church, is loving Jesus. Loving the brethren, loving the church, is loving Jesus.
What results does he say come from a quiet, working life among outsiders?

Acts 2:42: And they continued steadfastly in the apostles’ doctrine and fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and in prayers. 1 John 4:20: If someone says, “I love God,” and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who does not love his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen?
How does Romans 12 describe practicing brotherly love?

He reads Romans 12:10–13: be kindly affectionate with brotherly love, in honor prefer one another, not lagging in diligence, fervent in spirit, serving the Lord, rejoicing in hope, patient in tribulation, steadfast in prayer, distributing to the needs of the saints, given to hospitality—invite people home and put them first.
How does Romans 12 describe practicing brotherly love?

We’re going to go to Romans chapter 12 verse 10 through 13. Be kindly affectionate one to another with brotherly love. And then he tells us how to do it: in honor giving preference—they’re number one. You make your brother number one. Not lagging in diligence—working hard at making your brother number one and loving your brother. Fervent in spirit in loving your brother and making them number one. Serving the Lord. Rejoicing in hope. Patient in tribulation. Steadfast in prayer. When the church goes through trouble, just hang tight. Be patient with your brothers and sisters. Distributing to the needs of the saints and given to hospitality. Invite people to your house to put them first and to encourage them in the things of God.
How does Romans 12 describe practicing brotherly love?

Romans 12:10-13: Be kindly affectionate to one another with brotherly love, in honor giving preference to one another; not lagging in diligence, fervent in spirit, serving the Lord; rejoicing in hope, patient in tribulation, continuing steadfastly in prayer; distributing to the needs of the saints, given to hospitality.
How is loving your brother serving the Lord Jesus?

He reads Acts 9:4—Jesus told Saul, why are you persecuting me?—though Saul was persecuting the church. Messing with the church is messing with Jesus. The church is Christ’s body (1 Corinthians 12:27; Colossians 1:24); Matthew 25:40 says as you did it to the least of these my brethren you did it to me.
How is loving your brother serving the Lord Jesus?

Now we’re going to focus in on this serving the Lord. How is that serving the Lord when I love my brother? How am I ministering to Jesus when I’m loving my brother, making them number one? And so we’re going to ask this question: How is brotherly love serving the Lord Jesus Christ? And we’re going to go to Acts chapter 9 verse 4. When Saul saw the light, Jesus appeared to Saul on the road, and he said to Saul, why are you persecuting me? And Saul says, well who are you? And Jesus replied, I am Jesus whom you are persecuting. Now Paul was not persecuting Jesus—Jesus was in heaven—but he was persecuting the church, and Jesus is plainly saying when you mess with the church you’re messing with me. And we find in 1 Corinthians 12:27 that we are the body of Christ. Colossians 1:24, Christ for the sake of his body, which is the church. The church is the body of Christ. And Matthew 25:40, as you did it to the least of these my brethren you did it unto me. You see, we are the body of Christ—the eyes, the mouth, the hands, the feet of Christ on the earth—and how we treat our fellow Christian believer, our true believer brother in Christ, is how we’re treating God.
How is loving your brother serving the Lord Jesus?

Acts 9:4-5: Then he fell to the ground, and heard a voice saying to him, “Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?” And he said, “Who are You, Lord?” Then the Lord said, “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting. It is hard for you to kick against the goads.” 1 Corinthians 12:27: Now you are the body of Christ, and members individually. Colossians 1:24: I now rejoice in my sufferings for you, and fill up in my flesh what is lacking in the afflictions of Christ, for the sake of His body, which is the church, Matthew 25:40: And the King will answer and say to them, ‘Assuredly, I say to you, inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these My brethren, you did it to Me.’
What does 1 Corinthians 11 say happens if you mistreat the Lord’s body?

He reads that not discerning the Lord’s body—his church—causes many to be sick and weak, and many have died, for purposely mistreating God’s people. He warns Christian humanists to be careful how they speak evil of the true church; he says he has seen people die early or become sickly and depressed for attacking the church.
What does 1 Corinthians 11 say happens if you mistreat the Lord’s body?

Now knowing that, you’ve got to understand in 1 Corinthians 11 that it is taken seriously about our attitude toward the real body of Christ, toward the real church, the real believers. And he says in 1 Corinthians 11:29, you’re not discerning the Lord’s body, which is what—his church, which is Jesus. For this cause many are sick and weakly among you, and many have already died, because you have mistreated purposely the body of Christ, the people of God. So I say to Christian humanists, be careful how you treat and how you speak evil and attack the true church, because Jesus will correct you. And folks, I have seen people die early for attacking the church. I have seen people sickly and mentally depressed and cast down. God does back up his word. When you purposely, on purpose, attack God’s people, Jesus will deal with that.
What does 1 Corinthians 11 say happens if you mistreat the Lord’s body?

1 Corinthians 11:29-30: For he who eats and drinks in an unworthy manner eats and drinks judgment to himself, not discerning the Lord’s body. For this reason many are weak and sick among you, and many sleep.
What needs of the saints should the church meet?

Besides food, clothing, shelter, and medicine, he lists healing of mind, emotions, spirit, and body (Luke 9:11); hearing the word, not opinions or psychology (Luke 10:39–42); a place to repent (Luke 15:7); and maintaining good works and job skills so you are not unfruitful (Titus 3:14).
What needs of the saints should the church meet?

Now the deeds of the saints—you see, that’s how we serve the Lord, by serving his people. Now the needs of the saints—what might the needs of the saints be besides food, clothing, shelter, and medicine? Okay. In Luke 9:11, they came to him and Jesus healed all them that had need of healing. There are people who need healing in their mind and their emotions, in their spirit and in their physical body. So the church is to be a place of healing. In Luke 10:39, Mary sat at Jesus’s feet hearing his word, and Jesus said one thing is needful, and Mary chose that good part. The church should have the word of God spoken in it—not opinions and psychology and philosophies, but the word of God, the living word of God. Luke 15:7, more joy over one that repents than 99 just persons who need no repentance. So the church should be a place where people can repent, change their thinking and change their ways. Titus 3:14, learn to maintain good works to meet the necessary needs so you will not be unfruitful, both natural and spiritual. If you get an education, get a job skill, and work hard and be honest, you will provide for yourself. If you seek God he will give you the true riches of his kingdom.
What needs of the saints should the church meet?

Luke 9:11: But when the multitudes knew it, they followed Him; and He received them and spoke to them about the kingdom of God, and healed those who had need of healing. Luke 10:39-42: And she had a sister called Mary, who also sat at Jesus’ feet and heard His word. But Martha was distracted with much serving, and she approached Him and said, “Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Therefore tell her to help me.” And Jesus answered and said to her, “Martha, Martha, you are worried and troubled about many things. But one thing is needed, and Mary has chosen that good part, which will not be taken away from her.” Luke 15:7: I say to you that likewise there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine just persons who need no repentance. Titus 3:14: And let our people also learn to maintain good works, to meet urgent needs, that they may not be unfruitful.
What if a church says it is rich and needs nothing?

He reads Revelation 3:17—miserable, poor, blind, and naked spiritually—and 2 Peter that lacking these added qualities makes you blind. The church should build self-control (1 Corinthians 7:5) and perfect what is lacking in faith (1 Thessalonians 3:10)—virtue, knowledge, self-control, godliness, patience, and brotherly love.
What if a church says it is rich and needs nothing?

In Revelation chapter 3 verse 17, you say I am rich—this is to the church; he’s talking to believers—I have need of nothing, and you don’t know that you’re miserable, poor, blind, and naked. You’re in pain. You’re poor spiritually. You’re blind spiritually. And you are naked—you don’t have the clothes of righteousness. And remember in 2 Peter, he that lacks these things is blind and can’t see afar off. When we don’t add to our faith we become blind. 1 Corinthians 7:5, so Satan does not tempt you because of your lack of self-control. A church should be a place where people can build up their strength in controlling themselves. 1 Thessalonians 3:10, we might perfect that which is lacking in your faith. You see, we need to add virtue, knowledge, self-control, godliness, patience, and brotherly love.
What if a church says it is rich and needs nothing?

Revelation 3:17: Because you say, ‘I am rich, have become wealthy, and have need of nothing’—and do not know that you are wretched, miserable, poor, blind, and naked— 2 Peter 1:9: For he who lacks these things is shortsighted, even to blindness, and has forgotten that he was cleansed from his old sins. 1 Corinthians 7:5: Do not deprive one another except with consent for a time, that you may give yourselves to fasting and prayer; and come together again so that Satan does not tempt you because of your lack of self-control. 1 Thessalonians 3:10: night and day praying exceedingly that we may see your face and perfect what is lacking in your faith?
What should church services be for, according to Hebrews 10?

He says not entertaining and socializing, but provoking one another to love and good works, not forsaking assembling, coming to give and stir up, exhorting one another all the more as the day approaches. The purpose is to build people from babyhood to fatherhood in Christ.
What should church services be for, according to Hebrews 10?

Now the urgency of church services to meet the needs of the saints is very important. Hebrews 10:24, we shouldn’t be here for entertaining and socializing. We should be here for the purpose that the church is—provoke, stir up one another to love and to good works. That’s what a church service should be about. And how do we do it? Not forsaking the assembling of yourselves together, as some are, and not coming to get all the time but come to give, to stir up. He says exhort one another, encourage one another in love and good works, and so much the more as you see the day approaching. The purpose of the church is to keep building the people up from babyhood to childhood to young adulthood to fatherhood in Christ. It’s urgent and it’s important that we do that.
What should church services be for, according to Hebrews 10?

Hebrews 10:24-25: And let us consider one another in order to stir up love and good works, not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as is the manner of some, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching.
What does he say about willfully hurting a brother after knowing the truth?

He reads that if we sin willfully after receiving the knowledge of the truth there remains no more sacrifice for sins, but a fearful expectation of judgment. He says purposely hurting or speaking to hurt a brother falls under that, and that we must apply brotherly love at every growth stage; God will deal with those who do not love his church.
What does he say about willfully hurting a brother after knowing the truth?

He goes on to say if we sin willfully after receiving the knowledge of the truth there remains no more sacrifice for sins. If I purposely and intentionally do something to hurt you or speak of you to hurt you, God said there’s no more sacrifice for your sin, but a fearful looking of judgment and fiery indignation which shall devour the adversaries. I submit to you today that we need to apply brotherly love to our faith and love our brother who is a genuine follower of Christ, whether they are a baby, child stage, young adult stage, or the mature stage. God will deal with people that do not love his church. You.
What does he say about willfully hurting a brother after knowing the truth?

Hebrews 10:26-27: For if we sin willfully after we have received the knowledge of the truth, there no longer remains a sacrifice for sins, but a certain fearful expectation of judgment, and fiery indignation which will devour the adversaries.
What qualities does he say brotherly love is added to?
He says they are adding brotherly love to godliness, self-control, knowledge, virtue, and faith from 2 Peter 1.
Are we born again only by the Spirit, or also by the word?
He says John 3 teaches birth by the Spirit, but Jesus also said his word is spirit—so the word of God also changes our life and moves us to apply the things of God.
How will all men know you are Jesus’ disciples?
He reads John 13:34–35: love one another as I have loved you; by this all men will know you are my disciples.
What does “lead a quiet life” and work with your own hands mean here?

He says you are not lawless—doing violence, killing, or robbing—but take care of your own affairs, work with your hands, pay your bills, balance your checkbook, and do not expect other Christians to do everything for you.
Why did Jesus ask Saul why he was persecuting him?
He says Saul was persecuting the church, not Jesus in heaven, but Jesus said when you mess with the church you are messing with me.
What does Matthew 25:40 mean for treating fellow believers?
He says as you did it to the least of these my brethren you did it unto me—how we treat a true believer brother is how we are treating God.
What warning does he give Christian humanists about the true church?
He says be careful how you treat, speak evil of, and attack the true church, because Jesus will correct you and backs up his word when you purposely attack God’s people.
What “one thing is needful” does he apply to the church from Mary?
He says Mary sat at Jesus’ feet hearing his word and chose the good part—so the church should speak the living word of God, not opinions, psychology, and philosophies.
What does Revelation 3:17 say to a self-satisfied church?
He says believers who claim to be rich and need nothing do not know they are miserable, poor, blind, and naked—without the clothes of righteousness.
Should you come to church mainly to get or to give?
He says not forsaking assembling, and not coming to get all the time but come to give, to stir up—exhort and encourage one another in love and good works.
At what growth stages should you love a genuine follower of Christ?
He says love your brother whether they are a baby, child stage, young adult stage, or the mature stage; God will deal with people who do not love his church.

items.d: The speaker defines godliness as the condition of respecting and obeying God, and says the Bible’s definition of godliness is Jesus Christ (1 Timothy 3:16). He teaches that godliness is profitable for this…
items.ser: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors · Part 9
tg: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors
p: The speaker defines godliness as the condition of respecting and obeying God, and says the Bible’s definition of godliness is Jesus Christ (1 Timothy 3:16). He teaches that godliness is profitable for this life and the next (1 Timothy 4:8), contrasts it with humanism and Christian humanism (1 Timothy 6; 2 Timothy 3; Titus 1:16), argues Great Society policies did not end poverty, and urges holy conduct and godliness that hasten the day of the Lord (2 Peter 3).
What is godliness, according to the dictionary and the Bible?

He says godly means respecting and obeying God, and -ness means the condition of—so godliness is possessing that condition. The dictionary definition is that; the Bible definition of godliness is Jesus Christ, citing 1 Timothy 3:16.
What is godliness, according to the dictionary and the Bible?

Thank you. We’re going to add godliness to self-control, knowledge, virtue, and faith. Godly means respecting and obeying God. The suffix -ness means the condition of. So it’s the possession, it’s the condition of respecting and obeying God. Joyfulness is the condition of being joyful—you possess joy. Now that is the dictionary definition. The Bible definition of godliness is Jesus Christ. First Timothy 3:16.
What is godliness, according to the dictionary and the Bible?

1 Timothy 3:16: And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifested in the flesh, Justified in the Spirit, Seen by angels, Preached among the Gentiles, Believed on in the world, Received up in glory.
What does 1 Timothy 3:16 say about the mystery of godliness?

He reads that God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen by angels, preached among the Gentiles, believed on in the world, and received up. He says this is clear scripture that Jesus was God in the flesh and that Jesus possessed the condition of respecting and obeying God.
What does 1 Timothy 3:16 say about the mystery of godliness?

Great is the mystery, the hidden thing of godliness. Mystery is something hidden. It’s not hidden anymore. Number one, God was manifest—visible—he appeared in the flesh. Here’s another scripture that says Jesus is God. For those who want to debate that Jesus was only the Son of God, here’s another clear scripture that Jesus was God in the flesh. Justified in the Spirit: when Jesus was baptized, a dove came down, the Holy Spirit in the form of a dove. He was seen by angels. Angels appeared both at his birth and before his birth, after he was tempted in the wilderness, and the angel rolled the stone away. Among—he preached among the Gentiles. God preached among the Gentiles in the body of Jesus Christ. He was believed on in the world, both with Gentiles and Jews, even though he said, I’ve not called but to the Jews and not the Gentiles. He was received up after he died on the cross. So Jesus possessed the condition of respecting and obeying God.
What does 1 Timothy 3:16 say about the mystery of godliness?

1 Timothy 3:16: And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifested in the flesh, Justified in the Spirit, Seen by angels, Preached among the Gentiles, Believed on in the world, Received up in glory.
How is godliness part of growing into good works?

He reads 1 Timothy 2:10 about women professing godliness with good works. He says “becomes” means proper or suitable—if you profess godliness you should act right—and also means to grow into, like a caterpillar becoming a butterfly. Godliness is profitable for obtaining two promises.
How is godliness part of growing into good works?

All right, now godliness is part of the growing, the changing process which results in good works for Christians. First Timothy 2:10. After saying, telling women not to let it be the adorning of the outward, he says but that which becomes a woman—that’s which is proper for a woman, suitable for a woman professing godliness with good works. Now this word becomes, as I said, means proper or suitable. If you’re going to profess godliness, you should be acting right, behaving right. But it also means to grow into, like the caterpillar. Caterpillar becomes a butterfly. The caterpillar goes into the cocoon and grows and develops and changes into a totally new, different kind of creature—from an ugly creature to a beautiful butterfly. Godliness, the Bible says, is profitable for obtaining two promises.
How is godliness part of growing into good works?

1 Timothy 2:9-10: in like manner also, that the women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with propriety and moderation, not with braided hair or gold or pearls or costly clothing, but, which is proper for women professing godliness, with good works.
What two promises does he say godliness is profitable for?

He reads 1 Timothy 4:7–8 to exercise yourself toward godliness, which has promise of the life that now is and of that which is to come. He says godly Christians avoid preventable deaths and costs from AIDS, STDs, alcohol, drugs, and tobacco, and that godliness is important for eternal life, not only faith and grace.
What two promises does he say godliness is profitable for?

First Timothy 4:7, exercise, train, discipline yourself. You know we do this bodily exercising and all this, but we’ve got to train and exercise ourselves toward godliness, because godliness is profitable for all things, having two promises: the promise of life that now is, and that which is to come. Godly Christians in this life avoid preventable deaths, injuries, and medical costs of AIDS and sexually transmitted diseases, which take thirty thousand lives a year in America. Alcohol takes 85,000; drugs 17,000; tobacco 450,000; and 460,000 children are sexually abused every year. Godly Christians don’t do these things, and it gives you eternal life. Everybody’s always talking about faith and grace to get eternal life. This plainly says godliness is important for eternal life now.
What two promises does he say godliness is profitable for?

1 Timothy 4:7-8: But reject profane and old wives’ fables, and exercise yourself toward godliness. For bodily exercise profits a little, but godliness is profitable for all things, having promise of the life that now is and of that which is to come.
How does he say God describes humanism and its followers?

He reads 1 Timothy 6:3–5 that anyone who will not consent to the wholesome words of Jesus or doctrine agreeing with godliness is proud, knows nothing, and is obsessed with disputes. He says withdraw from those who treat godliness as a means of wealth, and that godliness with contentment is great gain.
How does he say God describes humanism and its followers?

God’s view, God’s description of humanism and its followers. First Timothy 6:3, if anyone teaches otherwise and does not consent to wholesome words, even to the words of our Lord Jesus Christ—we have no right to teach what Jesus didn’t teach—or to the doctrine which agrees with godliness, that condition of respecting God and obeying him. If someone does that, he is proud. You’re just a proud, cocky, arrogant person, and gee, God says you don’t know anything. You’re obsessed with disputes and arguments over words. People today just arguing and debate about nonsense. Who suppose godliness is a means of gain or a means of wealth—from such withdraw yourself. Get away from these people. They will infect you with their unwholesome words and their own words instead of Christ. And then he goes on to say, now godliness with contentment is great gain. See, having the condition of respecting God and obeying God with being satisfied where you’re at.
How does he say God describes humanism and its followers?

1 Timothy 6:3-6: If anyone teaches otherwise and does not consent to wholesome words, even the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the doctrine which accords with godliness, he is proud, knowing nothing, but is obsessed with disputes and arguments over words, from which come envy, strife, reviling, evil suspicions, useless wranglings of men of corrupt minds and destitute of the truth, who suppose that godliness is a means of gain. From such withdraw yourself. Now godliness with contentment is great gain.
Did Lyndon Johnson’s Great Society end poverty, according to the sermon?

He says in 1964 Johnson called for ending poverty, joblessness, and hunger; he calls him a humanist and liberal. He cites poverty, jobless, and hunger rates still about 15% / 40% / 15% by 2014 after $17 trillion of debt, and says it did not work because Jesus said the poor you have always (Matthew 26:11; Deuteronomy 15:11).
Did Lyndon Johnson’s Great Society end poverty, according to the sermon?

In 1964 Lyndon B. Johnson called for an ending to poverty, joblessness, and hunger in the USA. He became known as the Great Society bill or law. Okay, they’re going to stamp out—he’s a humanist. He was a liberal. But when you look at the facts, the proper poverty rate back in 1965 was 15%; 2014, 15%. Jobless rate—the adults that can work that wasn’t working—in 1970, 40%; to 2014, 40%. The hunger rate 1965 15%, 2014 15%. They did not eradicate hunger, poverty, or the jobless, but they did spend 17 trillion dollars going in debt, and a lot of that money was trying to eradicate poverty and hunger and joblessness. It didn’t work. Why? Because Jesus said in Matthew 26:11, you will have the poor with you always. You’re not going to change the word of God. The poor is going to be around, and that proves the Bible’s true, by the way, people looking for proof. Deuteronomy 15:11, the poor will never cease out of the land. Matthew 24, there will be wars, famines, earthquakes, troubles. And we have wars, famines, and earthquakes, and these people can’t do a thing about it. Why? Because God said it’s going to be.
Did Lyndon Johnson’s Great Society end poverty, according to the sermon?

Matthew 26:11: For you have the poor with you always, but Me you do not have always. Deuteronomy 15:11: For the poor will never cease from the land; therefore I command you, saying, ‘You shall open your hand wide to your brother, to your poor and your needy, in your land.’ Matthew 24:6-7: And you will hear of wars and rumors of wars. See that you are not troubled; for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet. For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. And there will be famines, pestilences, and earthquakes in various places.
Why haven’t religions and popular teachings ended poverty and wars?

He reads Mark 7:7 about teaching commandments of men. He says prosperity, possibility, positive, faith, and purpose-driven teaching, plus Muslims, denominations, and political or science philosophy, have not eradicated poverty, hunger, wars, or joblessness, because God said those things will be—until we get hold of godliness and Jesus.
Why haven’t religions and popular teachings ended poverty and wars?

Mark 7:7, in vain—worthlessness—they worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men, and laying aside the commandments of God. And that’s what we got. We got men deciding, humans deciding what’s going to be and what’s going to work. Prosperity teaching, possibility teaching, positive teaching, persuaded or faith teaching, or purpose-driven teaching—and the preachers haven’t changed poverty, hunger, or jobless conditions either, but they sure make a lot of money selling tapes and books. They live rich. Neither has religion. The Muslims isn’t changed in the world. Denominations—they’re not changing these things. Philosophy, whether it’s political or science philosophy—they are not eradicating poverty, hunger, wars, joblessness. Why? Because God said they will be. And until we get a hold of godliness and Jesus who is godliness, we’re not going to eradicate anything. Hallelujah. And that’s a good place for an amen. It hasn’t worked. It hasn’t worked. Then religion—they just keep on being religious, including Christian denominations, and it’s not working. When are we going to realize we got to do it God’s way? And add to—add to means you didn’t have it before. You didn’t get it when you got saved. You didn’t get it when you confessed your sins. You didn’t get it when you repented from your sins or got water baptized or got baptized in the Holy Ghost. You get it when you get it, and you didn’t have it then, and you got to add it to your life. Hallelujah.
Why haven’t religions and popular teachings ended poverty and wars?

Mark 7:7-8: And in vain they worship Me, Teaching as doctrines the commandments of men.’ For laying aside the commandment of God, you hold the tradition of men—the washing of pitchers and cups, and many other such things you do.”
What is Christian humanism, and what does 2 Timothy 3 warn about?

He defines Christian humanism as Christians who add humanistic teaching and philosophy to their life. He reads 2 Timothy 3 that in the last days men will have a form of godliness but deny its power, ever learning and never able to come to the truth—from such turn away. He says stay away so you are not tainted, yet reach them as a harvest field.
What is Christian humanism, and what does 2 Timothy 3 warn about?

Bible’s prediction of Christian humanism coming in the last days. Christian humanism is Christians who add humanistic teaching and philosophy and beliefs to their life. In Second Timothy 3:1, in the last days difficult times will come. Men shall have a form of godliness, an appearance of godliness, but deny its power. Remember the Bible says our faith is not to be in the intellect of men but in the power of God, and God has power to bring this about. Ever learning and never able to come to the recognition of the truth. These also reject the truth—men of corrupt minds. From such turn away. Christians that add humanistic teachings and doctrines and methods into their life are Christian humanists. You got to stay away from them so you don’t get tainted, and you gotta reach them like the harvest field. Remember, Jesus is godliness. See, they’re rejecting Jesus.
What is Christian humanism, and what does 2 Timothy 3 warn about?

2 Timothy 3:1-5: But know this, that in the last days perilous times will come: For men will be lovers of themselves, lovers of money, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, unloving, unforgiving, slanderers, without self-control, brutal, despisers of good, traitors, headstrong, haughty, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God, having a form of godliness but denying its power. And from such people turn away!
How do Christian humanists deny Jesus, according to Titus 1:16?

He reads that they profess to know him with their mouth but in works deny him—disown him—being abominable, disobedient, and reprobate unto every good work. He says you cannot be satisfied with only faith, Holy Ghost baptism, and second-coming doctrine; you need the qualities God promised, including godliness.
How do Christian humanists deny Jesus, according to Titus 1:16?

How do Christian humanists deny Jesus in godliness? Titus 1:16, they profess that they know him with their mouth, but in works, actions, behavior they deny him. Deny is a strong word—they disown him—being abominable and disobedient unto every good work reprobate. And remember, good works is where we grow to godliness, which produces good works. How many need a little godliness in your life? Yeah. We got to add this stuff. You can’t be satisfied with just your faith and your baptism of the Holy Ghost and your second-coming doctrine. You need these qualities that God has promised us.
How do Christian humanists deny Jesus, according to Titus 1:16?
Titus 1:16: They profess to know God, but in works they deny Him, being abominable, disobedient, and disqualified for every good work.
Why is godliness serious in light of the day of the Lord?

He reads 2 Peter 3:10–12 that the heavens will pass away and the earth be burned up, so what manner of people ought you to be in holy conduct and godliness, looking for and hastening the coming of the day of the Lord. He says Jesus is coming for a mature, blameless church the gates of hell cannot prevail against—not today or tomorrow as we are.
Why is godliness serious in light of the day of the Lord?

The seriousness of godliness for all people. Second Peter 3:10, the Lord’s day will come as a thief in the night. The heavens will pass away with a great noise. Elements will melt with fervent heat. The earth and the works in it will be burned up. Therefore, since all these things will be dissolved, what manner of people ought you to be in holy conduct and godliness, looking for and hastening—speeding up—the coming of the day of the Lord. That’s a serious thing. He’s going to renovate this earth by fire, and we’re going to be accountable to our conduct and did we measure up to godliness and good works and godliness and conduct. Will speed up the coming of the Lord. So there has to be a visitation, coming of God that’s going to turn the church to godliness. He’s not coming today. He’s not coming tomorrow. He’s coming for a church that is mature, the gates of hell cannot prevail against, that is blameless and righteous and holy, and he has the power to accomplish that. And he will accomplish it.
Why is godliness serious in light of the day of the Lord?

2 Peter 3:10-12: But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night, in which the heavens will pass away with a great noise, and the elements will melt with fervent heat; both the earth and the works that are in it will be burned up. Therefore, since all these things will be dissolved, what manner of persons ought you to be in holy conduct and godliness, looking for and hastening the coming of the day of God, because of which the heavens will be dissolved, being on fire, and the elements will melt with fervent heat?
What should gathering as a church be for?

He reads Hebrews 10:24–25 to consider one another to provoke unto love and good works, not forsaking assembling. Church should stir people to godliness and good works, not entertainment or flattery. He says the early church would rather die or stay in prison than deny Christ, and that Jesus—not Christian or secular humanists—will win by a visitation of godliness.
What should gathering as a church be for?

And so we see the seriousness of the situation. Christian humanists must reconsider their beliefs. In Hebrews 10:24, consider one another to provoke one another and to love and do good works, not forsaking the assembling of yourselves together. When we come to church it should be for the purpose of encouraging, stirring up people to godliness and doing good works. Shouldn’t be for entertainment and patting each other on the back and flattering each other, but exhort one another, encourage one another. You see, the early church died—and whereas in prison rather—than deny Christ. See, they obtained this thing. They wouldn’t deny truth. They wouldn’t deny godliness. Christian nor secular humanists will win. They won’t get the last word. Jesus will win by a visitation of godliness before returning for his blameless, prevailing-over-the-gates-of-hell and mature bride. The bride has made herself ready. He is making his church ready. There is a visitation coming.
What should gathering as a church be for?

Hebrews 10:24-25: And let us consider one another in order to stir up love and good works, not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as is the manner of some, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching.
Does godliness include sexual morality and truth-telling?

He asks why Christians divorce when they are supposed to have power. He says with power we do not commit homosexuality, adultery, or child sexual abuse, and we do not lie like the president, Congress, governors, school teachers, and textbooks. Godliness does not embrace lying; there is power in godliness because there is power in the God we serve.
Does godliness include sexual morality and truth-telling?

Sexual sin, divorce—why are Christians divorcing? We’re supposed to have power. Sexual sin—we have power. We don’t commit homosexuality. We don’t commit adultery. We don’t have sex with kids and abuse kids. We don’t lie either, like the president, Congress, governors, school teachers, textbooks in school are doing. Godliness does not embrace lying. There’s power in godliness, because there’s power in the God that we serve. Thank you.
What is the difference between the dictionary and Bible definitions of godliness?
He says the dictionary definition is the condition of respecting and obeying God; the Bible definition of godliness is Jesus Christ (1 Timothy 3:16).
What does the caterpillar-to-butterfly picture mean for godliness?

He says “becomes” means to grow into: the caterpillar goes into the cocoon and changes into a totally new creature, from an ugly creature to a beautiful butterfly—like growing in godliness into good works.
How does he compare bodily exercise and training toward godliness?
He says we do bodily exercising, but we must train and exercise ourselves toward godliness because it is profitable for all things with promise for this life and the life to come.
What does he say about godliness with contentment?

He says godliness with contentment is great gain—having the condition of respecting and obeying God while being satisfied where you are at—and to withdraw from those who treat godliness as a means of wealth.
What does Matthew 26:11 mean for anti-poverty programs in this sermon?
He says Jesus said you will have the poor with you always, so you are not going to change the word of God; the poor will be around, which he says proves the Bible true (also Deuteronomy 15:11).
What does “add to” mean for godliness after salvation?
He says add to means you did not have it before—you did not get it when you got saved, confessed, repented, were water baptized, or baptized in the Holy Ghost; you have to add it to your life.
What is a “form of godliness” that denies its power?
He says in the last days men will have an appearance of godliness but deny its power; faith is not to be in the intellect of men but in the power of God—from such turn away.
What kind of church does he say Jesus is coming for?

He says Jesus is not coming today or tomorrow; he is coming for a mature church the gates of hell cannot prevail against, that is blameless, righteous, and holy, and he has the power to accomplish that.
What does he say the early church would rather do than deny Christ?
He says they would rather die, and stay in prison rather than deny Christ; they would not deny truth or godliness.
What “visitation of godliness” does he expect before Jesus returns?
He says Jesus will win by a visitation of godliness before returning for his blameless, mature bride; the bride has made herself ready, and he is making his church ready.

He says godliness does not embrace lying, and contrasts that with lying by the president, Congress, governors, school teachers, and textbooks; there is power in godliness because there is power in God.

items.d: In this short fifth session on Bible morality, the speaker teaches that knowledge must be added to faith and virtue, and lists the five rewards of 2 Peter 1. He gives the marks of someone with Bible knowledge…
items.ser: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors · Part 5
tg: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors
p: In this short fifth session on Bible morality, the speaker teaches that knowledge must be added to faith and virtue, and lists the five rewards of 2 Peter 1. He gives the marks of someone with Bible knowledge, cites Hosea 4:6 and Romans 6:23, and recounts Bible examples of sin’s consequences and God’s dealings with nations. He closes with calls to respond to Jesus, to defend religious freedom, and to separate spiritual harm from criminal harm.
What does it mean to “add” knowledge to virtue and faith?

He says “add means you put something in that you didn’t have before,” and that his faith, water baptism, repentance, confession and Holy Ghost baptism “didn’t give it to me,” meaning knowledge. He says “when I added virtue it didn’t give me knowledge,” so it has to be added.
What does it mean to “add” knowledge to virtue and faith?

We appreciate you joining with us in this session of Bible morality. Banned by wimps. And born by warriors. In this fifth session. We’re going to look at adding knowledge. To virtue and faith. Add means. You put something in that you didn’t have before. My faith. Didn’t give it to me my water baptism. Didn’t give it to me my repentance didn’t give it to me my confession of sin didn’t give it to me my Holy Ghost baptism. Didn’t give it to me when I added virtue it didn’t give me knowledge. See I have to add add means you got something now you didn’t have before.
What are the five rewards of God’s promises in 2 Peter 1:4–10?

He lists that you become “partakers of the divine nature,” that you “escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust,” that “you will not be barren nor unfruitful,” that “you’ll be able to see afar off,” and that “you were never stumble you were never fall.” He says these come as you add virtue and then knowledge to your faith.
What are the five rewards of God’s promises in 2 Peter 1:4–10?

Now there are five rewards of God’s promises in Second Peter 1 verses 4 through 10 we are given exceeding the great and precious promises that you might be number one reward partakers of the divine nature that’s the result of the baptism of the Holy Ghost number two you’ve escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust that is the remission of sin forgiveness of sin deliverance of sin through believing in Christ being water baptized repenting and confessing your sins you see that’s the reward then he says add to your faith virtue add to virtue knowledge and then he gives us a number three reward you will not be barren nor unfruitful. Love joy peace long-suffering gentleness kindness meekness faith and temperance can be yours you will not be blind and you’ll be able to see afar off the destruction or the good of what your choices are going to be and make the right decision and act out the right behavior reward number five if you do emphasis do these things you were never stumble you were never fall.
What are the five rewards of God’s promises in 2 Peter 1:4–10?

2 Peter 1:4-10: by which have been given to us exceedingly great and precious promises, that through these you may be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust. But also for this very reason, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue, to virtue knowledge, to knowledge self-control, to self-control perseverance, to perseverance godliness, to godliness brotherly kindness, and to brotherly kindness love. For if these things are yours and abound, you will be neither barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ. For he who lacks these things is shortsighted, even to blindness, and has forgotten that he was cleansed from his old sins. Therefore, brethren, be even more diligent to make your call and election sure, for if you do these things you will never stumble;
What are the characteristics of someone with Bible knowledge?

He says faith “is just the foundation stone,” and that one with knowledge “spares his words” and has “a calm spirit.” He says such people can “make right decisions,” “don’t follow the crowd to do wrong,” and begin to gain knowledge when “we make a choice to look down on evil despise evil and to depart from evil.”
What are the characteristics of someone with Bible knowledge?

Very powerful promises. And the Bible has given us these great exceedingly great and precious promises and there are seven of these. Promises that we are to add to our faith faith is just the foundation stone of the goal of God so let’s look at the characteristics of one possessing Bible knowledge Proverbs 17:27. He who has knowledge spares his words a man of understanding is of a calm spirit wow. Second Chronicles 1:10-12 God gave Solomon wisdom and knowledge to judge the people to be able to make right decisions. Of knowing what’s right and wrong he could make right decisions for the people Nehemiah 10 28 all having knowledge and understanding separate from the people of the lands to the law of God in other words they don’t follow the crowd to do wrong people with knowledge follow God no matter what the crowd does Proverbs 1:7 the fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge and the fear of the Lord in Proverbs 8:13 and 16:6 is to depart from and hate evil so when we make a choice to look down on evil despise evil and to depart from evil we have begun to get the knowledge of the Lord. The characteristics of one without or rejecting Bible knowledge.
What are the characteristics of someone with Bible knowledge?

Proverbs 17:27: He who has knowledge spares his words, And a man of understanding is of a calm spirit. 2 Chronicles 1:10-12: Now give me wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people; for who can judge this great people of Yours?” Then God said to Solomon: “Because this was in your heart, and you have not asked riches or wealth or honor or the life of your enemies, nor have you asked long life—but have asked wisdom and knowledge for yourself, that you may judge My people over whom I have made you king— wisdom and knowledge are granted to you; and I will give you riches and wealth and honor, such as none of the kings have had who were before you, nor shall any after you have the like.” Nehemiah 10:28: Now the rest of the people—the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the Nethinim, and all those who had separated themselves from the peoples of the lands to the Law of God, their wives, their sons, and their daughters, everyone who had knowledge and understanding— Proverbs 1:7: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, But fools despise wisdom and instruction. Proverbs 8:13: The fear of the LORD is to hate evil; Pride and arrogance and the evil way And the perverse mouth I hate. Proverbs 16:6: In mercy and truth Atonement is provided for iniquity; And by the fear of the LORD one departs from evil.
What happens to people who lack or reject Bible knowledge? (Hosea 4:6)

He reads “my people are destroyed for lack of knowledge” and “my people have gone into captivity because they have no knowledge.” He says death in Romans 6:23 means “physical death,” “spiritual death the lake of fire,” and “the miseries of sin,” and that going “against Bible morality… brings pain and misery.”
What happens to people who lack or reject Bible knowledge? (Hosea 4:6)

Hosea 4 verse 6 my people are destroyed for lack of knowledge Isaiah 5:13 my people have gone into captivity because they have no knowledge Romans 3:20 by the law is the knowledge of sin and so knowing the laws of God the word of God is very important but in the same book of Romans 6:23 the wages of sin the payment for sin is death and this word death encompasses three areas physical death spiritual death the lake of fire number two and the miseries of sin the pain and the suffering that comes because we choose a life of immorality. We go against Bible morality and it brings pain and misery in to our life now the secular humanist and the atheists the free thinkers the liberals and all these people they unite and come against Bible morality and make it illegal we need to unite and get back to Bible morality.
What happens to people who lack or reject Bible knowledge? (Hosea 4:6)

Hosea 4:6: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I also will reject you from being priest for Me; Because you have forgotten the law of your God, I also will forget your children. Isaiah 5:13: Therefore my people have gone into captivity, Because they have no knowledge; Their honorable men are famished, And their multitude dried up with thirst. Romans 3:20: Therefore by the deeds of the law no flesh will be justified in His sight, for by the law is the knowledge of sin. Romans 6:23: For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
What Bible examples does he give of death and misery caused by sin?

He gives examples from Genesis and Chronicles, including the first murder, the flood “because the whole world was given to violence and sexual immorality,” and Sodom “destroyed… because of sexual immorality and violence.” He also lists Noah’s drunkenness, Lot’s daughters, David’s sin and its consequences, and a king who killed his brothers and was plagued “with the disease of the bowels.”
What Bible examples does he give of death and misery caused by sin?

We’re going to give some scriptural examples of preventable physical death preventable. Eternal death and preventable miseries because of our sin Genesis 4:11 came the first criminal murdered Abel God sentenced him to hard labor and banishment. Okay in Genesis 6:7 mankind was destroyed now God used capital punishment. Because the whole world was given to violence and sexual immorality. And Genesis 9:21 Noah got drunk got naked and his son saw him they covered him up and the next day he cursed his own son and Genesis 19:24 Sodom was destroyed. with [unclear] brimstone from heaven because of sexual immorality and violence. 19:35 of Genesis Lot got drunk committed incest with his two daughters got them pregnant and their offspring were outcasts for 900 years 10 generations. Second Samuel 13:2. [unclear] the son of David raped his virgin sister and her brother killed him. David. Had sexual relationship with Uriah’s wife Bathsheba. God punished him by killing the baby the baby died as an infant brought incest from his own children having sex with his wives and he was dethroned for a period of time in Second Chronicles 21:9. Joram killed his own brothers six brothers and the nobles the powerful people in the community and so God came and plagued him with the disease of the bowels.
What Bible examples does he give of death and misery caused by sin?

Genesis 4:11-12: So now you are cursed from the earth, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand. When you till the ground, it shall no longer yield its strength to you. A fugitive and a vagabond you shall be on the earth.” Genesis 6:7: So the LORD said, “I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth, both man and beast, creeping thing and birds of the air, for I am sorry that I have made them.” Genesis 19:24: Then the LORD rained brimstone and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah, from the LORD out of the heavens. 2 Chronicles 21:4: Now when Jehoram was established over the kingdom of his father, he strengthened himself and killed all his brothers with the sword, and also others of the princes of Israel.
How does he say God dealt with nations that sinned? (Ezekiel 14)

He says Herod Agrippa was struck “for letting the people acknowledge him with as God,” and that “nations warred with Israel enslaved them and destroyed them for sin without repentance.” He cites Ezekiel 14 where God says “I will send war I will send famine” and that “no one would be saved except by their righteousness.” He says the United Nations “cannot prevent these things” unless they promote Bible morality.
How does he say God dealt with nations that sinned? (Ezekiel 14)

Just like in the New Testament Herod Agrippa was smitten with the disease of the bowels with worms for letting the people acknowledge him with as God. And he accepted that acknowledgment. Now. God had told Israel if they sinned if they didn’t follow Bible morality bad things were going to happen and we find in the Bible that nations warred with Israel enslaved them and destroyed them for sin without repentance in Ezekiel 14 it says. When the people sin and don’t repent I will send war I will send famine I will send wild beasts and plagues to punish them for their sin and though Daniel and Noah and Job were there no one would be saved except by their righteousness. Their own righteousness not daniels or somebody else’s and God named Assyria Babylon Persian and Greek empires that would deal with Israel and they did Jesus was predicted to come in the next empire after the grecian empire Rome. And all of these empires were predicted to come to an end because sinners correcting sinners sinners still have to be corrected. How does he say God dealt with nations that sinned? (Ezekiel 14)

Acts 12:21-23: So on a set day Herod, arrayed in royal apparel, sat on his throne and gave an oration to them. And the people kept shouting, “The voice of a god and not of a man!” Then immediately an angel of the Lord struck him, because he did not give glory to God. And he was eaten by worms and died. Ezekiel 14:12-20: The word of the LORD came again to me, saying: “Son of man, when a land sins against Me by persistent unfaithfulness, I will stretch out My hand against it; I will cut off its supply of bread, send famine on it, and cut off man and beast from it. Even if these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they would deliver only themselves by their righteousness,” says the Lord GOD. “If I cause wild beasts to pass through the land, and they empty it, and make it so desolate that no man may pass through because of the beasts, even though these three men were in it, as I live,” says the Lord GOD, “they would deliver neither sons nor daughters; only they would be delivered, and the land would be desolate. “Or if I bring a sword on that land, and say, ‘Sword, go through the land,’ and I cut off man and beast from it, even though these three men were in it, as I live,” says the Lord GOD, “they would deliver neither sons nor daughters, but only they themselves would be delivered. “Or if I send a pestilence into that land and pour out My fury on it in blood, and cut off from it man and beast, even though Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it, as I live,” says the Lord GOD, “they would deliver neither son nor daughter; they would deliver only themselves by their righteousness.” Hebrews 13:8: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. Matthew 24:6-9: And you will hear of wars and rumors of wars. See that you are not troubled; for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet. For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. And there will be famines, pestilences, and earthquakes in various places. All these are the beginning of sorrows. “Then they will deliver you up to tribulation and kill you, and you will be hated by all nations for My name’s sake.
What does he say we should do about immorality, and whom does he call “wimps”?

He asks what we will do with Jesus telling us to “repent believe confess be water baptized,” be filled with the Holy Spirit and add “Bible morality and knowledge to your faith.” He lists sexual sin, murder, lying, stealing and harming a neighbor, and says “wimps believe” and “they have faith in something” but “don’t repent they don’t confess they don’t get water baptized.”
What does he say we should do about immorality, and whom does he call “wimps”?

What will you do today with Jesus telling you to repent believe confess be water baptized for the remission of sins be filled with the Holy Spirit adding Bible morality and knowledge to your faith. What are you going to do about immoral sex whether it’s homosexuality incest orgies sex outside of marriage what are you going to do. Murder lying stealing not honoring good parents and basically just not loving your neighbor as yourself and doing harm verbally and physically to your neighbor wimps believe remember and they have faith in something. They will join a church or a secular group. But they don’t repent they don’t confess they don’t get water baptized they are not filled with the Holy Spirit they do not add Bible morality and knowledge to their faith remember Congress.
What does he say we should do about immorality, and whom does he call “wimps”?
Mark 12:31: And the second, like it, is this: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”
What does he say about the First Amendment and choosing to be a “warrior”?

He reads the First Amendment and says “we must choose to respond to Jesus above our opinions our own faith our church’s opinions.” He says we must choose “if we are going to be a wimp or a warrior” and “stand up for the first amendment right,” and that Congress and the Supreme Court “respect and establish the religion of secular humanism and the religion of atheism.”
What does he say about the First Amendment and choosing to be a “warrior”?

Shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion or prohibiting the free exercise thereof. or abridging the freedom of speech or the freedom of the press and the right for the people to peaceably assemble and to petition the government for grievances we must choose to respond to Jesus above our opinions our own faith our church’s opinions and our church’s faith we must choose if we are going to be a wimp or a warrior fighting against anti-Bible morality bullies we must choose to stand up for the First Amendment right a free exercise of religion and freedom of speech freedom of press and being able to assemble today like we are right now and petition our government against the grievances that we have against him the violation of the First Amendment by Congress and the Supreme Court to respect and establish the religion of secular humanism and the religion of atheism as violated the First Amendment and.
What does he say about civil rights, crime and spiritual harm?

He says “moral crime is not the color of one’s skin” or an ethnic group or sex, “these things does not hurt directly anyone,” whereas “a criminal a sinner violates nature’s moral laws… that physically hurt innocent people and it is to be punished by civil rulers.” He says “spiritual harm is dealt with by teaching spiritual truths” while “crime is not a civil right,” and says some church groups are accepting practices the Bible does not.
What does he say about civil rights, crime and spiritual harm?

Prohibited us who believe in Bible morality and Bible truth from exercising our religion. Distorting civil rights by false comparisons. And moral crime is not the color of one’s skin an ethnic or cultural group a male or a female rich nor poor tall nor short thick or thin circumcised or not circumcised religious person or an atheist. These things does not hurt directly anyone. A criminal a sinner violates nature’s moral laws and that is in a preamble to the Constitution and the Bible moral laws that physically hurt innocent people and it is to be punished by civil rulers. Spiritual harm is dealt with by teaching spiritual truths. But criminal harm immoral harm is dealt with by the punishment of the criminal. Crime is not a civil right. Crime is not to be authorized. And legislated. By our civil government church groups. Are accepting homosexual. People into membership. Marriages. And not only it’s homosexuals not accepted in the Bible but neither is adultery and fornication those things have to be changed.
What does he say is the result of the baptism of the Holy Ghost?
He says “partakers of the divine nature” is “the result of the baptism of the Holy Ghost,” while escaping corruption is “the remission of sin forgiveness of sin deliverance.”
What does he say faith is?
He says “faith is just the foundation stone of the goal of God,” and that there are “seven of these” promises that we “are to add to our faith.”

He says “the fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge” and “is to depart from and hate evil.”
What three kinds of death does he describe?
He says death means “physical death spiritual death the lake of fire” and “the miseries of sin the pain and the suffering that comes because we choose a life of immorality.”
What does he say about Daniel, Noah and Job in Ezekiel 14?
