He says “spiritual harm is dealt with by teaching spiritual truths,” but “criminal harm immoral harm is dealt with by the punishment of the criminal,” and “crime is not to be authorized and legislated by our civil government.”

items.t: Adding Love: God, Neighbors, and Enemies
items.d: The speaker says love must be added to faith: as a noun God is love (1 John 4:8), and as a verb we love God, neighbor, and enemies with action (Matthew 22; 5:44). Loving God means keeping commandments; loving…
items.ser: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors · Part 12
tg: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors
p: The speaker says love must be added to faith: as a noun God is love (1 John 4:8), and as a verb we love God, neighbor, and enemies with action (Matthew 22; 5:44). Loving God means keeping commandments; loving neighbor means doing no harm (Romans 13:8). Luke 6’s turn-the-cheek pattern is for non-criminal neighbors who dislike you; sinners/criminals are a different subject requiring higher response as sons of the Father.
What is love as a noun in 1 John?
He says we add love because we did not have it at salvation. A noun is a person, place, or thing; 1 John 4:8 and 4:16 say God is love—so love is a person, God.
What is love as a noun in 1 John?

And we’re going to talk about adding love to our faith. The New Testament word for love—definition is affection, goodwill, and a love feast. And so we have to add to our faith virtue, knowledge, self-control, patience, godliness, brotherly love. And the reason we’re adding is because we didn’t have them when we got saved, so we got to add them. The Bible definition, the Bible explanation, is way superior to your Greek or Hebrew definition of a word. And 1 John—we’re going to look at love from a noun perspective, used as a noun. A noun is a person, place, or thing. 1 John 4:8 and 1 John 4:16 says God is love.
What is love as a noun in 1 John?

1 John 4:8: He who does not love does not know God, for God is love. 1 John 4:16: And we have known and believed the love that God has for us. God is love, and he who abides in love abides in God, and God in him.
How does Colossians 1:13 connect Jesus and love/God?
He says God translated us into the kingdom of his love Son—translations say “dear Son,” but he says the word is agape love—so Jesus is God’s Son, Jesus is God. To add love we add God to our life.
How does Colossians 1:13 connect Jesus and love/God?

So love is a person, and that person is God, and we got to add love to our faith. Colossians 1:13, God has delivered us from the power of darkness and translated us into the kingdom of his—your translations almost all of them will say dear Son, but the word is more powerful than that. It’s the same word, agape love. See, he translated us into the kingdom of his love Son, who is love, God. So Jesus is God’s Son—or in other words, Jesus is God. Another place that proves that Jesus is God. That’s the noun. If we’re going to add love, we got to add God to our life, his love. All right. His love—Bible use of love used as a verb, okay, an action word.
How does Colossians 1:13 connect Jesus and love/God?
Colossians 1:13: He has delivered us from the power of darkness and conveyed us into the kingdom of the Son of His love,
What three love commands does he list as actions?

He cites love the Lord your God, love your neighbor as yourself, and love your enemies (Matthew 5:44)—each requiring behavior/expression. God is love, and love is action toward God, self, neighbor, and enemy.
What three love commands does he list as actions?

Matthew 22:37, love the Lord your God. All right, we’re supposed to love God who is love. We’re supposed to love Love. Matthew 22:39, love your neighbor as yourself. We’re supposed to love—and an action. This is an action. There has to be some kind of behavior, some kind of expression to our neighbor and to our God. See, we got to add that to our faith. And then the more difficult one for most people is Matthew 5:44, love your enemies. Oh my gosh, love your enemies. You see, you got to have an action, a behavior of love toward your enemies. So love is an action in all three of these scriptures. All right. God is love, and love is an action toward my neighbor, toward myself, toward my enemy, and toward my God. There is an action involved.
What three love commands does he list as actions?

Matthew 22:37-39: Jesus said to him, “‘You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’ This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like it: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ Matthew 5:44: But I say to you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who spitefully use you and persecute you,
How do you love God with action, not only words?

He reads 1 John 5:3 and 2 John 6: love of God is keeping his commandments and walking after them. Verbally saying I love God means nothing unless action backs it up—doing what pleases him, not yourself.
How do you love God with action, not only words?

Now, how to love God—the action, the verb. What do I do to love God? You see, do I just say I love God—that’s an action—or is there more to it? 1 John 5:3, this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments. You see, I demonstrate my love for God by obeying his word, especially his laws. 2 John 6, this is love, that we walk after his commandments. You see, just verbally saying I love God doesn’t mean a hill of beans unless action backs it up, and we honor and keep his laws, his commandments, his words. We do what pleases him, not ourself. How do we love with action—the verb—our neighbor and ourself?
How do you love God with action, not only words?

1 John 5:3: For this is the love of God, that we keep His commandments. And His commandments are not burdensome. 2 John 1:6: This is love, that we walk according to His commandments. This is the commandment, that as you have heard from the beginning, you should walk in it.
How do you love your neighbor and yourself?

He reads Romans 13:8—love does no harm to a neighbor, so love fulfills the law. If you obey God’s law and do nothing verbally, financially, or physically to hurt your neighbor, you fulfill loving God and neighbor. You must first not harm yourself.
How do you love your neighbor and yourself?

You see, how is that done? Romans 13:8, love does no harm to a neighbor; therefore love fulfills the law. You see, if you love God you’ll obey his law. If you do nothing verbally, financially, physically to hurt your neighbor, you have fulfilled both loving God and your neighbor. Ain’t that beautiful? So love is an action. And before you’re going to be able to love your neighbor, you got to love yourself. You can’t do anything to verbally, physically, spiritually, financially harm yourself—then you can pass that on to others. Ain’t that beautiful? Hallelujah.
How do you love your neighbor and yourself?

Romans 13:8-10: Owe no one anything except to love one another, for he who loves another has fulfilled the law. For the commandments, “You shall not commit adultery,” “You shall not murder,” “You shall not steal,” “You shall not bear false witness,” “You shall not covet,” and if there is any other commandment, are all summed up in this saying, namely, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.” Love does no harm to a neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.
How do you love enemies in your own household or community?

He says a man’s enemies can be of his own household. Will you hate back and war, or find a way to deal with opposition? He turns to Luke 6:27—subject: love your enemies—then do good, bless, and pray for those who hate, curse, and spitefully use you.
How do you love enemies in your own household or community?

Now comes the toughy. How do you love your enemies? I mean, you know the Bible says a man’s enemies can be those of his own household. Yeah, you can have opposition in your own home. How you going to love them? You know, you’re going to hate him back? You’re going to get into a war? You live in a community—you’re going to get into a war? Or you going to find a way to deal with those that are in opposition to you? How to love your enemy—here we go. Luke 6:27. Okay, we all know our English. We graduated from public school. We are sharp. We know that the subject of this paragraph is love your enemies. We know that the following explains and elaborates on the subject, and we know the end sums it up. Right? Are you English experts out there? Subject: love your enemies. All right. Do good to those who hate you. Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, sure. Bless those who curse you—those who go, you’ll never amount to nothing.
How do you love enemies in your own household or community?
Luke 6:27-28: “But I say to you who hear: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, bless those who curse you, and pray for those who spitefully use you.
What personal example does he give of being cursed and insulted?

He tells of moving from Kentucky to Detroit, mocked as a dumb hillbilly with an accent, excluded from baseball, falsely accused in court four times—and applies Luke 6: turn the other cheek, and if they take your cloak do not withhold the tunic, digging into what that means.
What personal example does he give of being cursed and insulted?

When I went to Detroit from Kentucky, those northerners hated me. They laughed at me and mocked at me. I had an accent and I was a dumb hillbilly, and they called me a dumb hillbilly. And I had never experienced the world yet. I was down there in that cozy little country setting, and man, no bullies, no gangs, no nothing. And to be a hillbilly—never amount to nothing. You—I didn’t even know how to play baseball. Never played baseball in my life. And so they tag you, you know—you’re this, you’re that—and they despise you. They don’t want you on their baseball team. You ain’t know how to hold a bat, you stupid hillbilly. Pray for those who spitefully use you or insult you, slander you, falsely accuse you. I’ve been to court four times from people falsely accusing me, slandering me, defaming my character—four times. To him who strikes you on the cheek, offer the other. You know, somebody hate you so much because you’re a hillbilly so long that you finally go, I’m not a stupid hillbilly, and they smack you upside the head—you are too. Come to your senses. Supposed to turn the other cheek. He who takes your cloak, do not withhold your tunic. Cloak is a coat like we wear, and the tunic is an inner garment. You know, so basically they take your coat and you give them your tunic—you’re naked. And the Bible’s against running around naked, and most people in society don’t want you run around naked, because most of us aren’t worth looking at naked. You know, people read this and you got to understand—you got to dig into this to know what he’s talking about.
What personal example does he give of being cursed and insulted?

Luke 6:27-30: “But I say to you who hear: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, bless those who curse you, and pray for those who spitefully use you. To him who strikes you on the one cheek, offer the other also. And from him who takes away your cloak, do not withhold your tunic either. Give to everyone who asks of you. And from him who takes away your goods do not ask them back.
Did Jesus give everyone whatever they asked for under Luke 6?

He notes Luke extends give to everyone that asks of you, but Jesus did not run around naked or give everybody everything. The wrap-up is as you want men to do to you, do to them likewise—an illustration for loving brother and neighbor who are not criminals.
Did Jesus give everyone whatever they asked for under Luke 6?

So give to everyone—now he just doesn’t use the enemies—he says give to everyone that asks of you. And know—hey, I want your car—okay, here you are. Hey, I want your house—okay, here you are. Hey, I want your clothes—okay, here you are. Your tools—okay, here you are. And not just your enemies—now it’s everybody. And how many of you know Jesus didn’t run around naked? He didn’t give them everything. He didn’t give everybody what they asked for. And we’ll get further into that. He who takes away your goods, don’t ask them back. They borrowed from you for so long they just take it for granted they can come and get your lawnmower or edger or whatever they need anytime they want—don’t ask them back. Now you notice—ask—so they’ve been asking; they just stop asking. We’re getting to the end of the subject, so he’s wrapping it up, and he summarizes it as saying, as you want men to do to you, do to them likewise.
Did Jesus give everyone whatever they asked for under Luke 6?
Luke 6:30-31: Give to everyone who asks of you. And from him who takes away your goods do not ask them back. And just as you want men to do to you, you also do to them likewise.
Who is the Luke 6 illustration for—neighbors or criminals?

He says it is for brother and neighbor who are not criminals—they may dislike your race, hair, talk, or hometown (his Appalachian hillbilly example) but are not stealing or beating you. Loving to get love back is what sinners do.
Who is the Luke 6 illustration for—neighbors or criminals?

You see, so obviously this is an illustration of how to love your brother and your neighbor who is not criminals. They just don’t like you. Maybe they don’t like your race. Maybe they don’t like the color of your hair. Maybe they don’t like the way you talk, where you’re from—like this stupid hillbilly from the Appalachian mountains. But they’re not out stealing from you. They’re not out beating you up, kicking you on the ground. They’re not criminals. He goes on to say this: if you love—he’s starting another subject—to receive. If you give out things to get back, you love to get love, you lend to get something out of the act of lending, if you do good because you want that person to acknowledge you and do something for you—he says, what do you more than others? Sinners do that. Now he switches to sinners.
Who is the Luke 6 illustration for—neighbors or criminals?

Luke 6:32-35: “But if you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them. And if you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners do the same. And if you lend to those from whom you hope to receive back, what credit is that to you? For even sinners lend to sinners to receive as much back. But love your enemies, do good, and lend, hoping for nothing in return; and your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High. For He is kind to the unthankful and evil.
What does he mean by sinners/criminals as a switched subject?

He says sinners are malicious, purposeful violators of God’s word—another word is criminal. Sons of the Father do better than sinners: no verbal attack back, try to avoid beating back. He says most of the American church is not close to that maturity and must get uncomfortable to change the nation.
What does he mean by sinners/criminals as a switched subject?

Sinners are malicious, purposeful violators of God’s word. Another word for sinners in our language is criminal. Okay. Criminals. So he’s switching the subject now. See. And he goes on to say, if you want to be sons of your Father, you do things better than the sinner. Hallelujah. People verbally attack you—you don’t verbally attack back. They physically get angry and want to beat you up—you don’t want to beat back. You try to avoid it. Are you there? You see, this is maturity. This is sons of God. How you know most of the church in America aren’t even close to being a son of God and maturity, and we’re quite comfortable with it. But we got to get uncomfortable with it so that we can change this nation.
Why do we have to add love to faith?
He says we did not have these qualities when we got saved, so we have to add virtue, knowledge, self-control, patience, godliness, brotherly love, and love.
What does “God is love” mean as a noun here?
He says love is a person, and that person is God (1 John 4:8, 4:16).
Which verse does he use for “love the Lord your God”?
He says Matthew 23:37 in the caption flow for loving God; the wording matches the great commandment usually cited as Matthew 22:37. (Editor note: possible misnamed reference.)
How does love fulfill the law in Romans 13?
He says love does no harm to a neighbor; if you do nothing to hurt your neighbor verbally, financially, or physically, you fulfill loving God and neighbor.
Can enemies be people in your own home?
Yes. He says the Bible says a man’s enemies can be those of his own household—you can have opposition at home.
What does he say about being falsely accused?
He says he has been to court four times from people falsely accusing him, slandering him, and defaming his character—and Luke 6 says pray for those who spitefully use you.
What does cloak and tunic mean in his explanation?
He says the cloak is like a coat and the tunic an inner garment—so giving both would leave you naked; dig into the passage to know what Jesus is talking about.
How does he say Luke 6 sums up?
As you want men to do to you, do to them likewise—wrapping the subject of loving enemies who are not criminals.
What if you love only to get love back?
He says if you love to get love, lend to get something, or do good to be acknowledged, you do no more than sinners.
How do sons of the Father respond to attack?
He says they do not verbally attack back; if others want to beat them up they try to avoid beating back—that is maturity.

items.t: Adding Love: How Did Jesus Love His Enemies?
items.d: The speaker asks how Jesus applied “love your enemies.” He shows Jesus walking through a synagogue mob (Luke 4), hiding from stoners (John 8:59), denouncing Pharisees (Matthew 23), calling Herod a fox (Luke…
items.ser: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors · Part 11
tg: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors
p: The speaker asks how Jesus applied “love your enemies.” He shows Jesus walking through a synagogue mob (Luke 4), hiding from stoners (John 8:59), denouncing Pharisees (Matthew 23), calling Herod a fox (Luke 13), and not performing for Herod (Luke 23)—arguing that pattern is for non-criminal neighbors having a bad day, while maturity starts by changing yourself toward spouse and family.
Did Jesus turn the other cheek when the synagogue tried to throw him off a cliff?

He reads Luke 4: that Jesus spoke truth, they were angry unlike psychological self-esteem preachers, dragged him to throw him over a cliff—and he did not turn the cheek; passing through their midst he went his way with supernatural power, without blessing or praying for them, because they were criminals wanting to kill him.
Did Jesus turn the other cheek when the synagogue tried to throw him off a cliff?

And we’re going to talk about adding love to our faith. We’re going to take a look at how Jesus applied these statements of loving your enemy. Did Jesus always turn the other cheek? Luke 4:28, Jesus went to the synagogue and he preached and spoke things there, and when the people in the synagogue heard what he had to say, they weren’t very happy. They were angry. They were mad. Not like your psychological self-esteem preachers of today in America. He said the truth and the truth made them mad. And they dragged him out of the city, took him to the peak of the hill to throw him over the cliff. Now here he is—they’re mad, they’re going to throw him over the cliff. Now here’s Jesus—his chance to turn the other cheek. Go, yeah, go ahead and throw me.
Did Jesus turn the other cheek when the synagogue tried to throw him off a cliff?

Luke 4:28-30: So all those in the synagogue, when they heard these things, were filled with wrath, and rose up and thrust Him out of the city; and they led Him to the brow of the hill on which their city was built, that they might throw Him down over the cliff. Then passing through the midst of them, He went His way.
Did Jesus turn the other cheek when they picked up stones in John 8?
He says if we gave in to every criminal nobody would be alive. In John 8:59 they took up stones; Jesus did not bless them or invite the stones—he hid himself to keep them from their criminal intent.
Did Jesus turn the other cheek when they picked up stones in John 8?

He didn’t. He, passing through the midst of them, went his way. He flexed his muscles, his supernatural power, then just walked right through them. He didn’t turn the other cheek. He didn’t go the extra mile. He didn’t bless them. He didn’t speak good about them, and he didn’t pray for them. Are you there? So Jesus didn’t even apply his own sermon here. Why? Because these were criminals. They wanted to kill him. If we gave in to every criminal, nobody would be alive, and you wouldn’t have anything. John 8:59, they took up stones to stone him.
Did Jesus turn the other cheek when they picked up stones in John 8?
John 8:59: Then they took up stones to throw at Him; but Jesus hid Himself and went out of the temple, going through the midst of them, and so passed by.
Why does he say the criminal realm changes “love your enemy”?
He says Jesus did not keep that word there because it is out of context in the criminal realm. A family member mad at you is one thing; a criminal wanting to kill you or steal is another.
Why does he say the criminal realm changes “love your enemy”?

Now okay, here’s Jesus—he’s preaching again, and again they don’t like what he’s saying. And they get mad. They throw a temper tantrum and they pick up stones—they’re going to stone him. And did he turn the other cheek? Did he bless them and say, oh you wonderful people, you’re such good Jews? Oh yeah, and I have to be patient with you, God isn’t finished with you yet, so you just go ahead and throw the stones? He didn’t do that at all. He hid himself. The Son of God, God himself, hid from them to keep them from carrying out their criminal intent.
Did Jesus always bless those who cursed him?

He reads Matthew 23:15, woe to scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites who make converts twice sons of hell—calling that not a blessing and not political correctness. He says Jesus did not pray for them or do them good when spitefully insulted; he was straightening them out.
Did Jesus always bless those who cursed him?

Are you with me? Are you getting this? Hallelujah. Yeah. He didn’t keep his own word because it’s out of context where that word is. When you get into the criminal realm it changes everything. And a family member get mad at you and all—that’s one thing. A criminal wanting to kill you, steal your car, steal your house—steal—that’s another thing. Did Jesus always bless those that cursed him? Matthew 23:15, woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites. Boy, that don’t sound like political correctness to me. How about you? You hypocrites, you phonies, you say one thing and you do another. You travel land and sea to make one proselyte, one convert, and you make him twice as much a son of hell as you are. In other words, you’re going to hell and everybody following you is going to hell too.
Did Jesus always bless those who cursed him?
Matthew 23:15: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you travel land and sea to win one proselyte, and when he is won, you make him twice as much a son of hell as yourselves.
What did Jesus call the Pharisees in Matthew 23:33?

He reads “you serpents, you generation of vipers”—not a garter snake but a cobra, poisonous and destructive—and “how can you escape the condemnation of hell?” He asks when radio or TV preachers last said that.
What did Jesus call the Pharisees in Matthew 23:33?

Now is that a blessing? You know why. Did he pray for them? No, he didn’t pray for them. Are you there? Did he do good things because they spitefully insulted him and all that? No, he didn’t do anything. He’s trying to straighten them out. Are you with me, church? Matthew 23:33, you serpents—here he is—you serpents. He’s down there preaching again. You serpents, you generation of vipers. Not just a garter snake—you are a cobra. You’re poisonous. You’re destructive. How can you escape the condemnation of hell? You’re going to hell. When’s the last time you hear the preacher on radio or TV say that statement?
What did Jesus call the Pharisees in Matthew 23:33?
Matthew 23:33: Serpents, brood of vipers! How can you escape the condemnation of hell?
What did Jesus say when told Herod wanted to kill him?
He says Jesus did not bless or pray forgiveness for Herod; he said go tell that fox he would preach and do miracles and be glorified—nobody had power to kill him; he would lay down his life.
What did Jesus say when told Herod wanted to kill him?

No, we’re so brainwashed into being spiritually, politically correct. We don’t want to offend anybody. Oh yeah, let them die and go to hell. They’re really offended there for eternity, but don’t dare offend them now. God. Luke 13:31, they come and said Herod the governor, the king, the politician, the leader, the civil leader, wants to kill you. Did he bless Herod? Oh, blessed Herod? Oh. Did he pray for Herod? Oh God, forgive him for he doesn’t know what he does. Are you there? No, he didn’t. He said, you go tell that fox. That wasn’t a good word.
What did Jesus say when told Herod wanted to kill him?

Luke 13:31-32: On that very day some Pharisees came, saying to Him, “Get out and depart from here, for Herod wants to kill You.” And He said to them, “Go, tell that fox, ‘Behold, I cast out demons and perform cures today and tomorrow, and the third day I shall be perfected.’
Who is the “love your enemy” pattern for, according to the sermon?
He says Jesus did not follow that pattern with criminals because it is for those who are not criminals—just having a bad day, season, or year—and you are still supposed to respond right to them.
Who is the “love your enemy” pattern for, according to the sermon?

That wasn’t a good word at all. That tomorrow I’m going to preach, second day I’m going to preach and do miracles, and the third day I’m going to be glorified, and you’re going to see it, and there’s nothing you can do about it, Herod. I’m going to do it. You ain’t killing me. I’m laying down my life. Nobody has power to kill me. Are you with me? Jesus did not follow that love-your-enemy pattern. Why? Because it is a pattern for those who are not criminals—they’re just having a bad day. In fact, some of us are having a bad season—it’s more than a day—and some of us are having a bad year. I mean this thing has dragged out. And you are supposed to respond right.
Did Jesus always give or perform for those who asked, like Herod?

He reads Luke 23:8—Herod hoped for a miracle, a show. Jesus answered him nothing; John the Baptist had already told Herod it was unlawful to have Herodias. He critiques Christians who run to healing ministries looking for a show.
Did Jesus always give or perform for those who asked, like Herod?

Hallelujah. Now folks, that was good stuff. Now. Did Jesus always give to those that ask? I said, anybody ask you, just give it away, give it away. Did he always pray for those who spitefully used him? Luke 23:8, Herod hoped to see some miracle done by Jesus. You know, here’s Jesus coming into the throne room and Herod’s—oh man, he wants to see a miracle. He heard all these miracles. He wanted to kill Jesus, but now Jesus is here—he wants to see a miracle. He wants a show. He wants a performance. That’s what a lot of Christians are into that run to the quote-unquote healing ministries. They’re looking for a show. And they put on one themselves even if God isn’t healing, and it’s really disgusting.
Did Jesus always give or perform for those who asked, like Herod?

Luke 23:8-9: Now when Herod saw Jesus, he was exceedingly glad; for he had desired for a long time to see Him, because he had heard many things about Him, and he hoped to see some miracle done by Him. Then he questioned Him with many words, but He answered him nothing.
Did Jesus give the ointment money to the poor when Judas asked?

He cites John 12:5—Judas wanted the ointment sold for the poor—and says Jesus did not. He claims there is no record of Jesus giving to the poor; his program was saving the soul, with widows and orphans a peripheral, qualified side issue—not America’s big “help the poor” social-good focus.
Did Jesus give the ointment money to the poor when Judas asked?

They act like they’re healed. They act like something supernatural is going on when it’s not. And what did Jesus do? He answered Herod nothing. He didn’t say one word. He didn’t pray for Herod. He didn’t even give him one word. He zipped his lip and just looked at him. Because John the Baptist had already given Herod the word that he needed to hear: it’s not lawful for you to have Herodias, your brother’s wife. So Jesus had nothing else to say because Herod hadn’t corrected that message yet—he hadn’t responded to that message. John 12:5, this woman comes in and anoints Jesus’ feet with ointment. Judas and some other ones there go, hey, don’t do that—sell that ointment and give it to the poor.
Did Jesus give the ointment money to the poor when Judas asked?

John 12:4-8: But one of His disciples, Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, who would betray Him, said, “Why was this fragrant oil not sold for three hundred denarii and given to the poor?” This he said, not that he cared for the poor, but because he was a thief, and had the money box; and he used to take what was put in it. But Jesus said, “Let her alone; she has kept this for the day of My burial. For the poor you have with you always, but Me you do not have always.”
Whom does he say Jesus prayed for instead of politicians and addicts?

He says you never hear Jesus praying for the rich, politicians, or people in authority, nor for the drug addict and alcoholic in that sense—he prayed for his apostles and disciples, focused on building the church; the rich must convert and come in like everyone else.
Whom does he say Jesus prayed for instead of politicians and addicts?

Did he do that? No. He didn’t give to those that asked him. There is no record of Jesus giving anything to the poor. Are you guys aware of that in the Bible? He wasn’t on a help-the-poor program. He was on a saving-the-soul program. Which tells us the priority of the church is to save the soul and get them to grow. And a peripheral section of it is to help those widows and orphans that are in need, if they qualify. That’s a real small side issue. What is the big issue in America? Help the poor, do some kind of social good thing, and you’re a great Christian. No. Jesus kept the focus on saving the soul and them to grow. Wow, that’s good.
Who is “the enemy” in his conclusion about love?

He says the enemy here is your neighbor, your brother, your spouse—people close enough to have a bad day, week, month, or year. You patiently turn the cheek while waiting for God to change them, when God is waiting for you to change first.
Who is “the enemy” in his conclusion about love?

And we got Christians doing good deeds and they’re not growing. And we got people receiving the good deeds and they’re not getting their souls saved. You never hear him praying for the rich or for the politicians or people in authority. You never hear him praying for them. But you hear him praying for his apostles, his disciples. Amen. Yes. Wow. He’s focused on the church and building the church and changing people’s lives is what he’s focused on. And if the rich want to be a part of it, they got to convert and come in like everybody else. Yeah. He didn’t pray for the drug addict and the alcoholic. He prayed for his disciples.
Does changing a spouse or child start with you?

He says if you want them to love you and treat you right, love them and treat them right—it starts with you, your character and heart—not a magic prayer while you are not working. That is maturity; America needs to hear it.
Does changing a spouse or child start with you?

Hallelujah. Conclusion: the enemy here is your neighbor, your brother. Nobody’s closer to you than your brother. Nobody’s closer to you than your spouse. How many know your spouse can have a bad day? In fact, they may have a bad week, a bad month, and a bad year, and you’re patiently turning the other cheek, going the extra mile, waiting for God to change them—when God’s waiting for you to change to change them. Did you hear that one? Yeah. You want somebody changed—change yourself first. Start with yourself. That’s the Bible way. Well otherwise you’re falling into I’m going to do something so I can get something back.
Is doing good to get something back maturity?
He says otherwise you fall into doing something to get something back, and that is not maturity. You do what you need to do because you need to do it.
Is doing good to get something back maturity?

You see. And that’s not maturity. Hallelujah. You do something because you need to do it. If you want your spouse or your children or your parents to love you—love them. You want them to treat you right—treat them right. It starts with you. Wow, that’s good stuff. Hallelujah. We want a magic prayer: Lord, change my husband, change my wife, change my child. It ain’t working. Why? Because you ain’t working. It starts with you—your character, your heart. Hallelujah. And America needs to hear this. You out there in America, you need to hear this stuff. So. You.
What happened when Jesus preached in the synagogue in Luke 4?
He says they were angry at the truth, dragged him to throw him off a cliff, and he walked through their midst rather than turning the other cheek.
Why does he say Jesus did not apply his own “love enemy” sermon there?
Because they were criminals who wanted to kill him; giving in to every criminal would leave nobody alive.
What does “twice as much a son of hell” mean in this sermon?
He says the Pharisees travel to make one convert and make him twice a son of hell—they are going to hell and so are their followers.
What does he say about not wanting to offend people?
He says we are brainwashed into spiritual political correctness—don’t offend them now, even if they die and go to hell offended for eternity.
Was “tell that fox” a blessing on Herod?
He says it was not a good word at all; Jesus was not blessing or praying for Herod.
Why did Jesus say nothing to Herod at the trial spectacle?
Because John the Baptist had already given Herod the word he needed—it is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife—and Herod had not responded.
What does he criticize about some healing ministries?
He says a lot of Christians run to quote-unquote healing ministries looking for a show and put one on even if God is not healing—which he calls disgusting.
What does he say is the church’s priority versus helping the poor?
He says Jesus kept the focus on saving the soul and growth; helping widows and orphans who qualify is a small peripheral issue, not the big American social-good measure of being a great Christian.
How should you treat a spouse having a bad year?
He says patiently turn the other cheek and go the extra mile, but understand God is waiting for you to change in order to change them.
What is “the Bible way” to get someone else to change?
He says start with yourself—change yourself first; wanting a magic prayer while you are not working will not work.

items.t: Adding Love: How to Love Criminals
items.d: The speaker distinguishes loving criminals from loving neighbors. Using Boko Haram kidnappings, a trafficking re-entry case, and a firefighter child-abuse case, he says force, strong law, conversion, and…
items.ser: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors · Part 13
tg: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors
p: The speaker distinguishes loving criminals from loving neighbors. Using Boko Haram kidnappings, a trafficking re-entry case, and a firefighter child-abuse case, he says force, strong law, conversion, and removal—not cheek-turning or medical missions alone—restrain the malicious. Esther’s exposure of Haman and Romans 13:4 show civil authority as God’s avenger; James 5:20 calls for converting the sinner.
How is loving the criminal different from loving a neighbor?

He says this is a different program: loving the sinner/criminal who maliciously violates God’s word and your freedom. He points to Boko Haram kidnapping teenage girls into slavery and forced “marriage,” citing their religion’s allowance of young marriage because Muhammad did.
How is loving the criminal different from loving a neighbor?

And we’re going to talk about adding love to our faith—how to love the sinner, the criminal, the one that maliciously, purposely violates the word of God, violates your freedom, your rights. This is a different program. How do you love these people? I got Boko Haram up here, the leader of it, a group over in Africa who just kidnapped 200 young ladies in their teens from 13 to like 17 years old. We all read about it. Force them into slavery because he says his religion you can have slaves. Force them to marry—they call it marriage. She has no choice, because in their religion, the Muslim religion, you can marry girls as young as 9 years old because Muhammad did. He has kidnapped over 500 girls. He has kidnapped boys to go into his military. These girls are forced to carry water, clean, cook, and do everything, and then at night have sex. They don’t have any freedom. They don’t have any choice.
Do groups like Boko Haram listen to prayer, negotiation, or force?

He mocks praying they are “good guys” and negotiating; America and Nigeria try to negotiate, but they listen to the sword. Revelation: they that live by the sword die by the sword. Only stronger force contains those who use force.
Do groups like Boko Haram listen to prayer, negotiation, or force?

Now you’re going to go to this guy and his group with their guns and their brutality and go, I’m praying for you, you guys are really good guys in heart, I know you, I especially—I talk to your mom and your mom says you’re a good boy? You think you’re going to negotiate? America and Nigeria is trying to negotiate with this group. They don’t listen to negotiations. They listen to the sword. In Revelation, they that live by the sword die by the sword. There’s only one thing they listen to is force, because they use force. The only thing that will contain them is a more stronger force.
Do groups like Boko Haram listen to prayer, negotiation, or force?
Revelation 13:10: He who leads into captivity shall go into captivity; he who kills with the sword must be killed with the sword. Here is the patience and the faith of the saints.
Do medical and dental missions fix brutal groups, in his view?
He says American Christians think fixing teeth and giving medicine wins them to Christ, but then they are healthier to do more brutal stuff—stupid thinking that needs to change.
Do medical and dental missions fix brutal groups, in his view?

And American Christians—well, we’ll go over and we’ll have a medical and dental program and try to win them to Christ. So we go in and fix their teeth and we give them medicine, and now they’re healthier to do more brutal stuff. This is the way we think in America, and this is the message that need to get out. We need to change this stupid thinking.
What trafficking case does he cite involving illegal re-entry?

He names Isaiah Mendez and his brother: repeatedly arrested for illegal re-entry, returned with food and money, then caught running a slavery program forcing girls into labor and sex with many men daily. They were convicted and imprisoned.
What trafficking case does he cite involving illegal re-entry?

This guy here, Isaiah Mendez, and his brother had already been arrested for illegal re-entry into the USA. Oh, you’re here illegally—we’ll just take you back. We’ll feed you, give you a nice bed till we get you back there, and we’ll give you some money so you got money to spend when you get back to Mexico. Now you stay in Mexico. Okay, they’re right back. They get arrested again and they get arrested again. They’re illegals. But then they caught them running a slavery program. They enslaved hundreds to thousands of girls forced to labor, forced to work, and forced to have sex with men—up to 40 men a day at $30 for 15 minutes. That takes 10 hours.
Does he call open-border policy humanitarianism?

He says Republicans and Democrats welcome the sick, criminals, bombers, and sex molesters and call it humanitarianism, but it is not when entrants enslave and force people. Bible strangers are welcome if they obey the law of the land; close the border.
Does he call open-border policy humanitarianism?

And the Republicans and a Democrat—they don’t want anybody not coming over to America. We’re the land of the free and home of the brave. We want your sick, your criminals—we want your bomb—we want your sex molesters—bring them on. And they try to tell us Americans that is humanitarianism. It’s not humanitarianism when you got people coming in and enslaving and forcing people to do what they don’t want to do. Amen. And they’re brainwashing us. They need to close that border down. There in the Bible strangers are welcome in the land if they obey the law of the land, if they obey just like anybody else. They don’t have a right to violate it. Is that a good amen? The Bible has answers for these things. They were convicted and found guilty and they’re in prison right now.
What firefighter abuse case does he describe?

He describes a Connecticut fire chief and another firefighter arrested in Vermont for aggravated sexual assault and trafficking involving a boy from age 12; they pleaded not guilty; one then committed suicide. He rejects assuming “innocent” claims equal honesty.
What firefighter abuse case does he describe?

This guy here is a fire chief, Connecticut fire department. He, 39 years old, and his friend, another firefighter, 42 years old, were arrested recently by the Vermont state police, charged with aggravated sexual assault and slave trafficking to have sex with them and other men. And this boy was 12 years old. And for years they forced him to have sex with them and other young men that they brought into their apartment. They got caught. They were arrested—him and his friend, his buddy, were arrested. They both pleaded in the court not guilty. We didn’t do nothing. Not guilty. Next week he killed himself. He committed suicide. Why? He could not handle the public going through his past and going through what his action is. So he took the chicken way out, the coward way out, and killed himself—yet he wasn’t guilty?
Will blessing and praying convert such a predator?
He says no—doing good will not convert him. He needed strong discipline, punishment, and laws, and if that failed, removal from society so he could not hurt anybody.
Will blessing and praying convert such a predator?

You know, I don’t know where we get this idea of people going to be honest with us. Oh, he says he’s innocent. You see criminals walking into the police station—I’m a child molester, I’m a murderer, I’m a rapist? Oh yeah, yeah. No. Oh, I’m an upstanding citizen. Are you there? Twelve years old till in his 20s, and finally the boy come to his senses and goes there’s something wrong here, went to the authorities. They found it true, got the evidence, and the guy killed himself. You think blessing him and praying for him was going to change him? You think doing good to this guy is going to convert him? No. He needed strong discipline, strong punishment, strong laws, and if that didn’t work he needed to be removed out of society so he couldn’t hurt anybody. Could that be an amen?
What does Esther and Haman teach about dealing with the wicked?

He recounts Esther 7: Esther exposes Haman as adversary and enemy before the king, who had authority to deal with him without praying or speaking good—and Haman was hanged on his own gallows. The key: wicked, purposeful, habitual intent to hurt and kill.
What does Esther and Haman teach about dealing with the wicked?

Esther chapter 7:6. Esther was one of the wives of the king of Persia. Here—uh—that takes fortitude in itself to handle being married to a pagan king with a whole bunch of other wives. This lady’s got her act together, unlike a lot of American women who fall apart any little pressure that comes in their home or whatever. This lady had a relationship with God that was powerful. And Haman was a guy that didn’t like her guardian Mordecai, because Mordecai was a righteous man, stood for righteousness and righteous laws. And so he wanted to kill Mordecai because Mordecai would not bow to him. He wouldn’t give in to his civil leadership authority, because Mordecai knew his wicked heart. He knew he was out to kill all Jews. And Haman had this plan to kill all Jews and Mordecai. So Esther goes to the king and says, king, I want you to come to my quarters and I’m going to feed you a meal, and I want you invite Haman. And so the king he comes down there and his wife fixes him a beautiful meal, and she’s a beautiful lady, the Bible says. I mean the king’s in hog heaven. He just—he’s got a beautiful wife, he’s got a beautiful meal. Boy, I tell you. And he says, okay now Esther, what else you want done? He said, I want you to come back tomorrow. I’m going to feed you another great meal. Man, I’ll be even more beautiful tomorrow. And so the king comes back the next day, and then in the meal Esther turns to the king and said, this man Haman is our adversary and enemy—he’s wicked. And when she said that, Haman got afraid before the king. Why? The king had authority to deal with him. King didn’t have to pray for anybody. He didn’t have to speak good to anybody. He had the authority to straighten him out or to set him free. So Haman right quick is afraid, and the king walked out on the balcony to think things over, and Haman knelt down before Queen Esther begging her—you know, don’t do this, don’t do this. And he comes back in and he sees Haman on his wife, took him out and hung him on the gallows that he wanted to hang Mordecai and the Jews on. Hallelujah.
What does Esther and Haman teach about dealing with the wicked?
Esther 7:6: And Esther said, “The adversary and enemy is this wicked Haman!” So Haman was terrified before the king and queen.
How then do you love criminals, according to the sermon?

He cites James 5:20—convert the sinner—and Romans 13:4—civil authorities as avengers of wrath on evildoers. Turn or burn now (pay the price), not merely hell later. You do not turn the other cheek; that is why Jesus did not use that principle in those situations.
How then do you love criminals, according to the sermon?

But the key here: he’s wicked. He’s maliciously, on purpose, habitually wanting to hurt people, wanting to kill people, wanting to take their freedom and their rights away from them. That’s a big difference. That’s right. James 5:20, convert the sinner from the error of his way and you will save a soul from death and you’ll hide a multitude of sins. All right. Number one, civil authorities need to deal with wicked people. Number two, we got to convert them. They got to change—their one way they got to convert to another way. Their evil way they got to convert to a right way. And that’s how you deal with criminals. They got to be converted. And God in Romans 13:4 instituted civil authorities to be the avenger to execute wrath upon him that does evil like Haman did. You see, either they turn or they’re going to burn. And I’m not talking about hell—they’re going to burn now. They got to pay the price. Now. You can’t be out there hurting people in society. That’s how you love the criminal. You don’t turn the other cheek. These people don’t listen to turn the other cheek. They don’t listen to going the other mile. They don’t listen to you finding something good in them to talk about. Are you there? See, that’s why Jesus did not use this principle in these situations.
How then do you love criminals, according to the sermon?

James 5:20: let him know that he who turns a sinner from the error of his way will save a soul from death and cover a multitude of sins. Romans 13:4: For he is God’s minister to you for good. But if you do evil, be afraid; for he does not bear the sword in vain; for he is God’s minister, an avenger to execute wrath on him who practices evil.
What does he say Boko Haram did?
He says they kidnapped about 200 teenage girls (and over 500 girls total), boys for military, forced labor and sex, with no freedom or choice.
What Revelation principle does he apply to violent groups?
They that live by the sword die by the sword—force is what they listen to, so stronger force contains them.
What happened to the Mendez brothers in his account?
They were convicted, found guilty, and are in prison for the slavery/trafficking program after repeated illegal re-entries.
What does he say the Bible says about strangers in the land?
Strangers are welcome if they obey the law of the land like anybody else; they do not have a right to violate it.
What does he make of the not-guilty plea then suicide?
He says the man pleaded not guilty then killed himself rather than face public exposure of his actions—calling it the coward way out—and rejects assuming criminals will walk in and confess.
What does he admire about Esther?
He says she had fortitude as wife of a pagan king with many wives and a powerful relationship with God, unlike many who fall apart under little pressure.
Did the Persian king need to pray for Haman?
He says the king had authority to straighten him out or set him free—he did not have to pray or speak good to him.
What does “turn or burn” mean here?
He says either criminals convert to a right way or they burn now—pay the price under civil wrath—not only referring to hell.
Why did Jesus not use turn-the-other-cheek with criminals?
Because these people do not listen to cheek-turning, going the extra mile, or finding something good to say about them.
What two steps does he give for dealing with criminals?
One, civil authorities deal with the wicked; two, convert them from an evil way to a right way (James 5:20).

items.t: Adding Love: You are to Blame
items.d: After citing a homosexual couple’s court-documented child sexual abuse and challenging pride in gay identity amid HIV/AIDS stats, the speaker blames humanists since the 1960s, Obama and Democrats, silent…
items.ser: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors · Part 14
tg: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors
p: After citing a homosexual couple’s court-documented child sexual abuse and challenging pride in gay identity amid HIV/AIDS stats, the speaker blames humanists since the 1960s, Obama and Democrats, silent Republicans, pastors and a pope soft on evolution/homosexuality, silent Christians, and NEA/AFT for school secularization. He calls Christians out of the closet as warriors who obey God’s laws, protect neighbors, and make laws that convert or remove criminals—and asks whether America has added love and the other 2 Peter qualities.
What abuse case does he open with?

He describes a homosexual couple in the newspapers who obtained a baby boy and, per court record, sexually abused him from 22 months to age six, videotaped it, taught it as normal, and involved other men—while publicly praised as a happy couple. He asks if such people will listen.
What abuse case does he open with?

These guys. They are a homosexual couple. They made the newspapers how they were married. You know, I’ve been married all these years. And then the guy on the left decides that they want a child. So they get the baby. It’s a boy. At 22 months they started playing with his pp. This is the court record. They start letting him fondle their pp. They fly him all over the world for money to let other men play with his pp and their pp. And this went on until the boy was six years old when they got caught. And the reason they got caught—they videotaped everything. And somebody got a hold of one of the tapes and go, this isn’t normal. And all the while they’re in the newspapers—man, look at this happy homosexual couple, oh boy they got their own kid—and all the time they were sexually molesting this boy and teaching this boy that this was a normal lifestyle. That’s right in the court records. They arrested several other men that they had on video sexually abusing this boy. You think they’re going to listen?
Will turn-the-cheek or negotiation change such abusers?

He says if an innocent child cannot melt your heart, your heart is unmeltable. No turn the other cheek, seeing good in them, or negotiation will change them—only the force of civil laws and authority.
Will turn-the-cheek or negotiation change such abusers?

No. They have an agenda. If a little kid cannot melt your heart—an innocent child cannot melt your heart—your heart is unmeltable. To sit there and do something to an innocent little kid, you are beyond, beyond. No turn the other cheek. No I see something good in you. No negotiation is going to change these guys. There’s only one thing that will change them, and that’s the force of civil laws and authority.
What challenge does he make to “proud to be gay” public statements?

Responding to an Apple CEO saying he is proud to be gay, he asks what sexual acts one is proud of, cites millions with HIV and over 30,000 North American deaths yearly from AIDS/STDs, and asks how that pride relates to molesters—saying somebody needs to say this from the church.
What challenge does he make to “proud to be gay” public statements?

Just this week Apple CEO come out and I’m proud to be gay. I write and say, what are you proud of? Are you proud to stick your penis in the butthole of another man and then in his mouth—is that what you’re proud of? Are you proud to let another man stick his penis in your butthole and then in your mouth—is that something to be proud of? You see, this needs to be said on the news. We need to get into their acts. items.d: In “Are Public Schools Successful?”, Pastor David G. Kincer traces the rise of public education in America, the Protestants’ early reservations, and the beliefs of the groups he says shaped government schools.…
p: In “Are Public Schools Successful?”, Pastor David G. Kincer traces the rise of public education in America, the Protestants’ early reservations, and the beliefs of the groups he says shaped government schools. He says the results have not met the schools’ goals, and he answers with Proverbs 22:6, Proverbs 27:12, Hosea 4:6 and Proverbs 4:7: train children in the way they should go, make them prudent, and make understanding the supreme thing. He calls for change, competition, and home, private and Christian schools as options.
Are public schools the best choice for our children?

He asks whether public schools are successful and says they are now government schools, where the government, the humanists and the teachers unions decide what is taught. He says early-1800s reformers argued tax-funded schools would create good citizens and prevent crime and poverty.
Are public schools the best choice for our children?

In this session we will ask the question: are public schools successful? Are they the best choice for our children? Are public schools successful, and are they the best choice in America for our children? Now, in reality the public schools are no longer public schools; they are government schools, as the public have no say anymore. It is the government, the humanist and the teachers unions that decide what academics, what truths and what lies are taught. Now we’re going to look at the rise of public education in the USA. The early 1800s, anti-Christian school reformers, because schools were home schools and Christian schools back then. They strongly favored, you, by Unitarian and liberal churches and socialists, and they argued that public schools funded by property tax would create good citizens, prevent crime, unite society around secularism, of course, and prevent poverty. That’s in the early 1800s.
What did Protestants first think about public schools?
He says Protestants had reservations and decided to give public schools a test; in 1849 they favored them, saying the Bible deficiencies could be supplied outside the school.
What did Protestants first think about public schools?

Now, the Protestants at that time, they had some reservation, they had some cautions about public school systems supported by taxes, and so they were going to give it a test. And, uh, in 1849 they favored it, but they said this: “The benefits of the system are so many, and the benefits are so great for a public school, that its religious or Bible deficiencies, that can be supplied outside the public school, are not a sufficient reason for abandoning it.”
Is Sunday school enough to balance public school?

He says Protestants promised parochial schools if the experiment failed, but children get a lopsided portion: 40 hours a week of public school with secular teachers and texts against about 3 hours a week of church.
Is Sunday school enough to balance public school?

They go on to say, “If, after a full and faithful experiment, that it is proven that loyalty to the religious interest or Bible interest of our children forbids the support of public education, we will establish parochial schools in which full doctrinal, religious, Bible instruction is possible.” But the problem here is, we’re given a lopsided portion: 40 hours a week to public school, with 3 hours a week to church, Sunday school and teaching. And the secular teachers and the secular text, versus Christian teachers with Christian text, Bible text, has a lopsided impact, and that’s something that the Protestants overlooked.
How did public education rise in America?

He lists points such as support from Unitarian and liberal churches and socialists, property-tax funding, Catholics keeping their parochial schools, the McGuffey Readers, the National Teachers Association in 1857 and the federal Department of Education in 1867.
How did public education rise in America?

Now we’re going to give you eight points in the rise of public education. Two, we’ve already hit: Unitarian, liberal churches and socialists greatly favor it, that ought to ring your bell; funded by property tax, now I can lose my property if I don’t pay my taxes. Number three, the Protestants has reservations until 1960 that they never followed up on. Number four, the Catholics kept their parochial schools, their local church schools, and rejected totally the public schools. The King James Bible and McGuffey Readers were the prominent readers in the early public schools, so the Protestants got fooled and thought they had no problem. But in 1857, point number five, National Teachers Association, now we got a union. 1867, the federal Department of Education, now we got the feds involved, and they started giving money grants in [unclear].
What beliefs shaped the early public school movement?

He says compulsory attendance laws came by 1918 and education became a civil monopoly. He says liberal Unitarians and socialists persuaded people that the Bible has errors and that all religions lead to the same God, and wanted a socialist government.
What beliefs shaped the early public school movement?

By 1918 every state had a compulsory attendance law. And number eight, this wound up being a civil monopoly on education with no competition. We’re going to give you four inviting persuasions during the public schools’ rise, people trying to persuade you to go their way. First, the liberal Unitarian Christians and the socialists in the early 1800s. They persuaded people that the Bible is not literal, it’s not truth, it’s got errors in it; you got to re- use reason, not the Bible; all religions lead to the same God; there’s no virgin birth, no second coming, Jesus isn’t God, no sin atonement, no resurrection, no miracles, no- evolution is the way they say creation happened; government gives aid to the poor, the sick, the social ills, and public education. They want a socialist government, and they had no opposition from cons- from conservatives from 1926 to 1960.
What did Bible fundamentalists believe, and why did they leave politics?

He says they held that the Bible is truth, Jesus is God, born of a virgin, died for sin, rose and is coming again, but they dropped out of politics after the Scopes trial. He compares the Communist Manifesto and an American socialist manifesto, both calling for government-run schools.
What did Bible fundamentalists believe, and why did they leave politics?

In the early 1800s, the Bible fundamentalists had the opposite beliefs, and they wrote a book about it in 1915: the Bible is a book of truth, it doesn’t have errors in it; that Jesus is God; he was born of a virgin; the Trinity; Jesus died for sin and rose again; he’s coming back again; there’s an eternal judgment; there are supernatural miracles; there’s a six-day creation; and people are supposed to help them- themselves and help others, not government. They support capitalism, and they dropped out of politics after the Scopes trial of 1926, leaving the humanists, the socialists and the liberals unopposed until the 1960s. In 1848 the Communist Manifesto was written. The American Socialist Manifesto was written in 1919; it was exactly the same, they just changed the name to socialist. Property, banks, transportation, media, factories and farms all belong to the government; a heavy income tax supported it; equal pay for everyone; no inheritance; redistribution of the population; they abolished all religions; and they established free education for all children, and the government ran schools. Asia went communist, Europe went socialist, and they’re trying to get America.
What is secular humanism, according to the sermon?

He says secular humanism arose in 1933 believing in evolution, no supernatural God, no prayer, and reason instead of the Bible, promoted through the schools. He points to Soviet government schools as a result.
What is secular humanism, according to the sermon?

The religion of secular humanism arised in 1933. They believed, like the liberals and the Unitarian church: evolution, no creation, no life after death, the scientific method is all we need, no supernatural God, no prayer, no worship, we need reason and intellect, not the Bible, and we’re going to promote our beliefs about through the educational system; churches and their rituals and their methods, their activities, must be altered and changed; capitalism is inadequate; socialized, equal distribution economy is what the humanists promoted. So what was the results of humanism in public schools? Well, in the Soviet Union, 1917, compulsory attendance, tax-supported government schools taught students to be loyal to a government that sent millions to slave labor camps in Siberia, starved to death peasants in the Ukraine, closed all churches, persecuted Christians, seized all property, and murdered 50 million opponents simply because they opposed them.
What happened when governments controlled the schools?

He says in Nazi Germany compulsory public schools turned children into “genocidal monsters,” and that American public schools have produced more addiction, teen sex, dropouts, illiteracy and school violence.
What happened when governments controlled the schools?

The schools provided the willing hands, and the police and the army provided the fear. The National Socialists ruled Germany from 1933 to 1945, using its compulsory attendance, tax-supported public schools to turn ordinary German children into genocidal monsters. German soldiers and the secret police committed horrible atrocities against any citizens that opposed the government. And time forbids the facts on China, Cuba and other dictator humanist nations committing atrocities on mankind. In the United States of America, in the public schools, has produce more alcoholics, more addicts, drug addicts, more smokers, more teen sex, more, more sexually transmitted diseases and more immorality; produced more dropouts from high school, functional illiterates, and more school violence. Not a very good result in the American public schools.
Does more money improve public schools?

He says more tax money and even lotteries brought lower results, with America 28th in eighth-grade math and 17th in science. He says most students lack drive and duty, and government schools have not achieved their goals.
Does more money improve public schools?

They took more tax money to try to improve education, even the lotteries, the government got in the gambling business to help support education, with lower results. More money, lower results. The international scoring: we are 28th in eighth-grade math and 17th in eighth-grade science in the industrialized global nations. Most students lack drive, they lack effort, they lack duty and responsibility to get educated and learn a job skill. Entertainment seems to be their main focus. In America, government schools thus has not achieved its goals, but they have promoted socialism, humanism and immorality, not only in our public schools but in society.
What does “train up a child in the way he should go” mean for schools?
From Proverbs 22:6 he lists what children should not be taught, and from Proverbs 27:12 and Hosea 4:6 he says schools should produce prudent students with the knowledge to make good decisions.
What does “train up a child in the way he should go” mean for schools?

Well, the solutions to education, for your consideration. Proverbs 22:6: train up a child in the way he should go. A child shouldn’t be taught to become a homosexual, a thief, an adulterer, liar, a sluggard, a lazy person that doesn’t work, ignorant, can’t read, can’t write, can’t communicate, can’t calculate, and they shouldn’t be taught to be a criminal. Teen sex and all of its sexually transmitted diseases shouldn’t be taught. They shouldn’t be taught to use alcohol, drugs, tobacco, which is killing thousands of Americans every year and physically harming millions of Americans every year. Profanity and witchcraft and such like should not be taught. We should be training them up in the way they should go. Proverbs 27:12: a prudent person foresees the evil, the danger, the harm, and hides himself, but the simple, the open-minded, they go on and are punished. And the school system should be producing prudent students that have avoids the dangers. My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge, Hosea 4:6. A school system should give children knowledge to make good decisions, so that they don’t do things that will damage them financially, physically, or even bring death upon them.
What does “train up a child in the way he should go” mean for schools?

Proverbs 22:6: Train up a child in the way he should go, And when he is old he will not depart from it. Proverbs 27:12: A prudent man foresees evil and hides himself; The simple pass on and are punished. Hosea 4:6: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I also will reject you from being priest for Me; Because you have forgotten the law of your God, I also will forget your children.
How important is education in the Bible?
Quoting Proverbs 4, he says wisdom is the supreme thing, and God says educating our children and ourselves is the top priority; we can’t cut cost or time.
How important is education in the Bible?

In Proverbs also, it’s at Proverbs 4, it says wisdom is the supreme thing, and in all your getting, get wisdom, and get understanding; if it cost you all you have, get understanding. And so God says that educating our children and ourselves is the top priority, and we got to put every amount of time is needed and every amount of money that’s needed. We can’t cut cost and we can’t cut time to educate our children to be prudent young people. Now, with these facts that I’ve presented to you, public schools are not the best choices.
How important is education in the Bible?
Proverbs 4:7: Wisdom is the principal thing; Therefore get wisdom. And in all your getting, get understanding.
What are the alternatives to public schools?

He calls for a competitive system where the best school wins the tax money and the parents’ approval, and until then names home schools, private schools and Christian schools as options. He faults Protestants, humanists, liberals and the Democratic Party.
What are the alternatives to public schools?

Consider this: 40% of legislators and 40% of public school teachers put their kids in private schools. Legislators and public school teachers should, because they’re involved, to know what’s going on, rise up and fight for a change in the public school system. We need to ax the failed unions and the Department of Education; they haven’t done their job. We need to form and start a competitive system where the best school wins the tax money and the approval of the parent. Until then, the home schools, the private schools and Christian schools are a possible alternative, a possible option, for those who want their kids trained up in the way they should go. We can fault Protestants for supporting bad government schools all these years and for quitting on public issues. We can fault the humanists and the liberals, who are 20% of the population of America; they are 52% of the Democratic Party. So we can fault the Democratic Party, the humanists and liberals, because they’re the ones promoting this kind of education in the American schools.
Who needs to unite for good schools?
He says Catholics, Protestants and moral people need to unite for good public schools, because our children’s future is at stake.
Who needs to unite for good schools?
Catholics, Protestants and moral people need to unite for good public schools. Folks, our children’s future is at stake, and the Bible says it is the supreme thing, is to get understanding.
Why does he call public schools “government schools”?
He says the public have no say anymore; the government, the humanists and the teachers unions decide what is taught.
How much time do children spend in school versus church?
He says 40 hours a week in public school against 3 hours a week of church and Sunday school.
What did Catholics do about public schools?
He says they kept their parochial schools and rejected the public schools.
What books were used in early public schools?
He says the King James Bible and McGuffey Readers were the prominent readers.
When did every state have compulsory attendance?
He says by 1918 every state had a compulsory attendance law.
Why does he say Christians dropped out of politics?
He says Bible fundamentalists dropped out of politics after the Scopes trial, leaving humanists, socialists and liberals unopposed until the 1960s.
What does he say children should not be taught?
He lists things such as becoming a thief, liar or lazy person, teen sex, alcohol, drugs, tobacco, profanity and witchcraft.
What does Proverbs 27:12 teach about prudence?
He says a prudent person foresees the danger and hides himself, but the simple go on and are punished.
What does “my people are destroyed for lack of knowledge” mean here?
He applies Hosea 4:6 to say a school system should give children knowledge to make good decisions.
Where does he say many legislators and teachers send their children?
He says 40% of legislators and 40% of public school teachers put their kids in private schools.
What change does he propose for schools?
He says to ax the failed unions and the Department of Education and form a competitive system where the best school wins the tax money.

items.d: In “Babies Grow,” Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from 1 Peter 2 on the four stages of a newborn baby in Christ: desiring the milk of the Word, coming to Jesus, being built up as God’s spiritual house and…
p: In “Babies Grow,” Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from 1 Peter 2 on the four stages of a newborn baby in Christ: desiring the milk of the Word, coming to Jesus, being built up as God’s spiritual house and priesthood, and offering spiritual sacrifices. He covers the milk of the Word in Hebrews 6:1-2, the weaknesses of babies in 1 Corinthians 3 and Galatians 5, and why praise, as a baby’s powerful tool, defeats the enemy.
What are the four stages of a newborn baby in Christ? (1 Peter 2:2-5)

He says the four baby stages are: desiring the pure milk of the Word, coming to Jesus Christ (not a church, a minister or a group), being built up as a spiritual house and priesthood, and offering spiritual sacrifices. He says that if you are not doing these things “you haven’t been born again,” and you are still in the embryo stage.
What are the four stages of a newborn baby in Christ? (1 Peter 2:2-5)

And we are going to be talking about the newborn baby stage in Christ. There are four baby stages, and they’re not necessarily in order or how they are carried out by God. In 1 Peter 2:2 it says, “As newborn babies,” we’re not in the embryo anymore, we’re not being developed inside, we got an outside birth, “newborn babies.” Number one, the first stage listed here in Peter is “desire the pure,” sincere, “milk of the word,” the genuine milk of the Word, “that you may grow thereby.” And so you don’t want to go to [unclear]’s books, my books, or Robert’s books; you want to go to God’s book. Okay, that is the pure, genuine Word of God. All right, if you go to other people’s books, make sure it lines up with this book. All right, that’s number one, and the reason we need to go to the Word is so we can grow. Young people, you’re not going to grow if you don’t get into the Word, you don’t get into Bible studies in a church where they’re teaching the Word. If they’re just entertaining you, you’re going to wind up being a non-growing Christian. Okay, stage number one. Stage number two, in verse 4: “Coming to Jesus, a living stone rejected by men but chosen by God and precious.” Okay, the second stage of this baby Christianity is they come to Jesus Christ. They don’t come to a church, they don’t come to a minister, they don’t come to a group, they come to Jesus Christ and His righteousness, which people reject, and that’s why they reject Christ: they don’t want to live righteous, they don’t want to live in truth. But newborn babies come to Jesus. Number three: “You also, as living stones, are being built up a spiritual house and a holy priesthood.” So the third one is, babies are in a stage of being built by God into a spiritual house, not a carnal house, not an earthly house, not a fleshly house, but a spiritual house, and not only that, they are being built up to be a priest. In the Old Testament we had a high priest and we had other priests, but in the New Testament everybody is a priest. That’s the baby stage, these four. Now if you’re not in the Word and growing, you’re back in the embryo stage of last message.
