What does it mean that Christians are “kings and priests”? (Revelation 1:6)

“That you should show forth” the what? “Praises of Him who has called you out of darkness and into His marvelous light.” Revelations 1:6: Jesus has made us kings and priests unto God. Now, if you know your Bible, priests both ministered to God and ministered to the people. So see, I come to minister to God through prayer and worship and learning His Word and so forth, but I also come to serve the people. And when the people aren’t in my agenda, I’m off balance, and when God isn’t on my agenda, I’m off balance. I’m a priest who ministers to God, and then because I minister to God and He touches me, then I can, then I can with some power minister to others. All right, you guys got that? Now we are the spiritual house being built up. Very powerful stuff.
What does it mean that Christians are “kings and priests”? (Revelation 1:6)
Revelation 1:6: and has made us kings and priests to His God and Father, to Him be glory and dominion forever and ever. Amen.
What are the spiritual sacrifices of babies: praise and partnership? (Hebrews 13:15-16)

He says the first sacrifice is praise, “the fruit of our lips,” meaning to boast about and brag about Jesus Christ and His Word, and the second is to do good. He says “fellowship” here is partnership, a commitment to work together toward the goal of the church, not just talking together.
What are the spiritual sacrifices of babies: praise and partnership? (Hebrews 13:15-16)

All right, now we’ll go to the fourth one: what are the four spiritual sacrifices of babies? You know, the fourth stage was they offer up spiritual sacrifices. What are these four spiritual sacrifices of babies? Okay, number one, Hebrews 13:15: “By Him, therefore, let us offer the sacrifice of” what? Praise. You learned Friday what the word “praise” means. What does the word “praise” mean? I heard you guys say it: to boast about, to brag about. Okay, Jesus Christ and His Word. Okay, that is “the fruit of your lips.” It tells you where the praise comes from. If I zip my lip, there’s no praise. “The fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name.” Now, how many know we should be thankful that our name is written in the Lamb’s Book of Life? Yes. We should be thankful that Jesus forgave us. If nothing else, “Lord, thank You for saving me. Thank You, Lord, for putting my name in heaven.” You got powerful things to praise Him and thank Him for. All right, that is number one, the sacrifice of praise. Say the word “praise.” Praise, praise. Praise should be a very high priority in the church. Praise is mentioned in joy way more times than mourning and sorrow and all that stuff. Number two, Hebrews 13:15 and 16: “Do not forget to do good.” And number three, fellowship, “for with such sacrifices,” plural, “God is well pleased.” So these sacrifices are three. Fellowship is not what you think it is here. It isn’t just us coming together and talking. Fellowship here is partnership, koinonia, partnership, commitment to work together, to partner together to the end result that’s profitable for the whole. See, I can fellowship with you without partnering with you. I can come in, fellowship and say, “Hi, Jacob, how you doing? It’s good to see you,” and, but when I partner with him, I work with him for the end goal of the church. It’s not me doing my thing, it’s not him doing his thing, it’s us doing what we need to do to reach the goal of the church. Are you with me? So when you’re a partner in a business, you make sure you are productive and the product is the best quality, because the end result is a profitable business. And that’s the word in here, “partner.” I must show up for work, I must be involved in this.
What are the spiritual sacrifices of babies: praise and partnership? (Hebrews 13:15-16)

Hebrews 13:15-16: Therefore by Him let us continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name. But do not forget to do good and to share, for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.
Why does he say babies’ praise defeats the enemy and the avenger? (Psalm 8:2)

He says Jesus quoted Psalm 8:2, “out of the mouth of babies and sucklings,” and that God has given baby Christians “a very powerful tool”: if you praise and thank Him, He will use it to defeat your enemies and the avenger, who is Satan. He says “you never hear them say, ‘Let’s praise about it.’”
Why does he say babies’ praise defeats the enemy and the avenger? (Psalm 8:2)

Jesus said unto them, “Have you never read?” I want to show you why your praise is so important. “Have you never read?” And that’s the problem, we don’t read. “Out of the mouth of babies,” out of the mouth of what stage? Babies “and sucklings You have perfected,” or prepared, “praise.” See, this is Jesus talking. All right, then we go to Psalm 8:2 that He quoted, and it says in Psalm 8:2, “Out of the mouth of babies and sucklings You have ordained,” or appointed, “strength, because of Your enemies, that You might still the enemy and the avenger.” Now, young people, God has given babies, young Christians, a very powerful tool. If you will praise Him, if you will thank Him, He will use it as a tool to defeat your enemies and defeat the avenger, who is Satan. You see? Are you there? Now everybody wants to call on a prayer hotline or 24-hour hotline or something else. I guarantee you, if you will operate this principle and get up in the morning and praise and thank God and come to church and praise and thank God, that God will go before you and defeat your enemies and defeat the avenger. You see, the avenger has a right to come and hold you accountable for your sin, that’s Satan. But praise, God says, “Back off.” Amen. Yeah. Yes. You see, we need God in here. When you praise Him and you speak well of Him and you boast to Him, when the Satan comes to say, “Hey, this guy deserves to be punished, be sick and lose his job and all this because he’s disobeyed in this area,” God says, “Back off. He’s a baby growing, and he’s praising Me. Stay in your place.” Very powerful tool. Hallelujah. You always hear baby Christians say, “I pray about it.” Well, let’s pray about it. You never hear them say, “Let’s praise about it.” You know, “I got this problem in my life.” “Well, let’s pray about it.” Why don’t you switch it around and say, “Let’s praise about it”? God said if I, as a baby, would praise Him, I would thank Him, I would lift up my voice unto Him with my lips, that He would still the enemy and the avenger. Wow, that was good. You got that, young ones? Sometimes you can’t follow these older ones. They get into retirement and the old folks’ mentality, and they just kind of putting in their time, you know, punching the clock, waiting to die and go to heaven. You got to follow people that are following Christ, like Paul says, “Follow me as I follow Christ.” Hallelujah. That’s true. A lot of Christians, older ones, just waiting to go to heaven, watching the clouds go by, or watching the TV screen go by, or bowling, or whatever else, just waiting for the rapture, and they’re not operating the principles that bring power to the church. They’re selfish. They don’t come to church with praise because they’re not interested in where God delivers other people or not.
Why does he say babies’ praise defeats the enemy and the avenger? (Psalm 8:2)

Matthew 21:16: and said to Him, “Do You hear what these are saying?” And Jesus said to them, “Yes. Have you never read, ‘Out of the mouth of babes and nursing infants You have perfected praise’?” Psalm 8:2: Out of the mouth of babes and nursing infants You have ordained strength, Because of Your enemies, That You may silence the enemy and the avenger.
What does it mean to present your body as a living sacrifice? (Romans 12:1-2)

He says “the body’s got to be involved”: lifting hands, lifting voices, kneeling, bowing, dancing and praying. He says “transformed” means changed into something beautiful through a process, and the “renewing of your mind” is “the complete changing of your thinking.”
What does it mean to present your body as a living sacrifice? (Romans 12:1-2)

The fourth one: “Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your reasonable service.” Bible, the people always tell me, “Well, I don’t want to be in the flesh, I want the Spirit, I want to be in the Spirit.” The Bible says, “Let all flesh praise the Lord.” How you going to lift your hands without your flesh responding? How you going to bow until you tell your body to respond? Your body has got to be involved. So present your body as a what? Living sacrifice. Not only living, holy, but doing the things God tells us to do: lifting our hands, lifting our voices, kneeling, bowing, dancing, playing instruments, worshiping God, praying. You see, the body’s got to be involved. You’ve got to engage your body to get this stuff done. “And do not be conformed to this world.” Don’t imitate the world, young people, “but be transformed.” That word “transformed” is “metamorphous,” changed into a beautiful creature. You see, changed into something beautiful, change totally, and it is a process. That’s why we’re in the baby stage, we’re in a process. And when you’re in the baby stage and you know it’s okay, don’t throw babies out of the church. Don’t throw yourself out of the church. Just recognize, I’m a baby, I’ve got to change. And we do that by giving our bodies a living sacrifice. And the word “renewing of your mind” really means the complete changing of your thinking. How many need some changing in your thinking? Yeah. And it comes from the sacrifice of your body: reading the Word, studying the Word, going to church, praying, discipline this body to do what God said to do, and then God takes it and makes it a spiritual power. Thank God for the baby stage. Now see, somehow I learned this as a young Christian, and when people would attack me and accuse me, I didn’t worry about it, because I knew I was in the process of being changed. I couldn’t teach it like I’m telling you, but I knew I was in that process, and I knew somewhere tomorrow this problem I had, this sin I had, the selfishness I had, would be gone, because that’s what He promised. But as years went by, then I can teach it clearly because I understand, and it’s in the book. Look, the sad thing is people are staying babies when they need to go on.
What does it mean to present your body as a living sacrifice? (Romans 12:1-2)

Romans 12:1-2: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your reasonable service. And do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, that you may prove what is that good and acceptable and perfect will of God.
Does praise work? (2 Chronicles 5:13 and following God’s pattern)

He checks whether praise worked in the Bible, pointing to the trumpeters and singers who praised as one so that “the presence of God came when they praised Him.” He says music is a tool and “don’t worship music, use music to worship God,” and that God’s presence came when the pattern was followed, not when we decide what we want to do.
Does praise work? (2 Chronicles 5:13 and following God’s pattern)

All right. Now in closing, does praise work? Okay, and you’ll see I do this with a lot of God’s principles. I go back to the Bible and I check out if it worked, because God is the same what? Yesterday, today, and forever. Okay, so we go to [unclear] Chronicles 5:13: “As the trumpeters and singers were as one to make one sound in praising,” what’s the word? Praising and thanking the Lord, saying, “For He is good, for His mercy endures forever,” that then the house was filled with a cloud, even the house of the Lord. The presence of God came when they praised Him. Music is very important in the church, but let me tell you, it is not to be worshiped. Jesus, we got no record of Him using music, we got no record of Him having concerts, but we do have a record that it is a tool that the church is to use to praise and worship Him. Are you with me? Don’t worship music, use music to worship God. All right, next one. Hebrews 8:5 in Exodus 25:40: “Make all things according to the pattern shown to you on the mount.” Mr. Barnes covered this clearly. There was a pattern that had to be followed, and when it was followed in Exodus 40:34, the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle. But they had to first follow the pattern, they had to first follow God’s order, then the presence come. We want God to bless what we decide we want to do. We don’t want to lift our hands, we don’t want to bow, we don’t want to shout to the Lord with a voice of triumph. So, you know, we go, “This is us, bless me.” God says, “No, you change, and I’ll bless you.”
Does praise work? (2 Chronicles 5:13 and following God’s pattern)

2 Chronicles 5:13: indeed it came to pass, when the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking the LORD, and when they lifted up their voice with the trumpets and cymbals and instruments of music, and praised the LORD, saying: “For He is good, For His mercy endures forever,” that the house, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud, Hebrews 8:5: who serve the copy and shadow of the heavenly things, as Moses was divinely instructed when he was about to make the tabernacle. For He said, “See that you make all things according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.” Exodus 25:40: And see to it that you make them according to the pattern which was shown you on the mountain. Exodus 40:34: Then the cloud covered the tabernacle of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
How did praise free Jonah and Paul and Silas?

He says Jonah, in the belly of the fish, praised and thanked God instead of calling “the 24-hour hotline,” and was released. He says Paul and Silas, beaten and shackled at midnight, prayed and sang praises, and an earthquake opened the doors and set every prisoner free.
How did praise free Jonah and Paul and Silas?

Amen. Hallelujah. We got to follow the pattern. All right, now Jonah 2:9 and 10. You guys all know the story of Jonah, right? Yeah, he rebelled against God, didn’t want to go preach to the sinners, so they threw him overboard and a fish swallowed him. Now he’s down in the belly of this big fish that God created, special fish. Okay, special fish God created, and if you don’t think God can get you, He’s got a lot of fish waiting for you. You may not be a fish in the water, but He’s got a fish waiting for you. That fish swallow you. So here’s Jonah in the dark belly of the, well, all right, and this fish is swimming all around the ocean and all this, and Jonah comes to his senses, and this is what he did before he was released from the fish: “I will sacrifice unto You with a voice of thanksgiving. I will pay that which I have vowed.” And the Lord spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land. See, Jonah said, like we do, “Lord, I’m going to serve You,” and then he decided he didn’t want to in this area. All right, so in the belly of the fish he came to his senses. Instead of praying, instead of calling the 24-hour hotline, he began to praise God and thank God for this fish, thank God for being thrown overboard, thank God that God would come and tell him to go to Nineveh with a message. And then God spoke to the fish and, whoop, Jonah was released from his situation. See, it does work. It worked back then at midnight. Midnight, Paul and Silas are in prison. They’re shackled, rats running all over, human dung everywhere, human, ear, on everywhere. They had to go to the bathroom in the shackles, they, you, ah, it was the pits, it stunk, it was horrible. Now they are there, they had just been beaten for the testimony of Christ, for preaching the gospel, so their back is raw, they’re in these shackles. Instead of calling the 24-hour hotline, instead of saying, “Church, pray for us, oh God, that’s such a bad thing,” they prayed and sang what? Praises unto God, and the prisoners heard them. What? None of this silent stuff. The prisoners heard them, and suddenly there was a great earthquake, so the foundations of the prisons were shaken, immediately all the doors were open, and all the prisoners’ bands were loosed. Every prisoner was set free. You want to be set free from the bondage of sin, from bondages of habits and addictions and so forth? I guarantee you, if you will use this principle of praise that babies have a right to use, you may not be perfect yet, you may have some sin in your life, but if you will use this principle of praise, God will liberate you, and God will spew you out of your predicament.
How did praise free Jonah and Paul and Silas?

Jonah 2:9-10: But I will sacrifice to You With the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay what I have vowed. Salvation is of the LORD.” So the LORD spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah onto dry land. Acts 16:25-26: But at midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them. Suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken; and immediately all the doors were opened and everyone’s chains were loosed.
Can praise move a city or a nation?

He says the American church wants “the latest band” and music without praising or focusing on Jesus, and there is “no growth.” Pointing to the crowd that praised Jesus entering Jerusalem so that the city “was moved,” he says that if the church praises, God “has the power to perform” what He promised, and “we got to change things from the top down, and that’s Jesus.”
Can praise move a city or a nation?

Amen. But not the American church. We want to come with the latest band, we want to come with the best singers, and we want to enjoy music like we do Monday through Friday going to work. We want to hear the same kind of music, you know, just put a little God, you know, word “Jesus” in it or something, and, uh, music does nothing for you. You’re not meeting with God, nothing is happening in your life. Why? Because you’re not operating the principle of praise, and you’re not focusing on Jesus, who is the liberator, the healer, the deliverer, the forgiver, the builder of the church. You’re not focusing on Him, and so you’re going and you’re coming, day after day, Sunday after Sunday, week after week, and no growth. And God forbid that you get up in the morning and thank God and praise God first thing. But I submit to you, praise works. How many want to see [unclear] reach for the gospel? America. Okay, look here. Jesus had been to Jerusalem every feast day since He was born, and nowhere is this recorded that the city was moved when Jesus came in, but a great multitude would spread their clothes and the tree branches on the road, crying out, “Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is He that comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!” And when He had come into Jerusalem, the city was what? Moved. It was shaken, and they responded and said what? “Who is this man?” He had been there every feast day since he was born, and they never, ever were moved to ask who Jesus was. And I submit to the church in America, if we will come in and sacrifice the praise, the fruit of our lips, lifting our hands, lifting our voices unto Him, that God who is the same yesterday, today, and forever, the God who promised these things also has the power to perform them, and we can see our families moved, we can see [unclear] move, we see California move, and America moved, because God will move them. Amen. Doesn’t matter who’s elected and all this stuff; it’s going to matter what God does with the ones who are elected. Now I’m not saying don’t vote, don’t take that wrong. I’m saying don’t lean on the fact if we get the right person in office, things are going to change. We got to change things from the top down, and that’s Jesus.
Can praise move a city or a nation?

Matthew 21:8-10: And a very great multitude spread their clothes on the road; others cut down branches from the trees and spread them on the road. Then the multitudes who went before and those who followed cried out, saying: “Hosanna to the Son of David! ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the LORD!’ Hosanna in the highest!” And when He had come into Jerusalem, all the city was moved, saying, “Who is this?”
What does he say the embryo stage is?

He says if you are not in the Word and growing, not coming to Jesus, and not letting God build you by the Word and the Spirit, “you’re still in the embryo stage.” In other words, “you haven’t been born again.”
Who does he say we come to?
He says we come “to Jesus only,” and not to a church, a minister or a group.
How much time does he say a believer should spend with God and His Word?
He says you “should be spending an hour a day with God and His Word, growing,” and should be in the house of God learning the Word and “getting built.”
What three baptisms does he list?

He lists baptism in the body of Christ, “where God places in as He sees fit,” baptism in the Holy Ghost, “where the power of God comes upon you to be a witness unto Him,” and baptism in water, “where your old man of sin is put to death and you rise a new creature.”
What does he say about the resurrection of the dead?

He says there is going to be a resurrection of the dead, that God knows where everyone is whether “buried at sea” or cremated, and that you will live in an undecaying body forever, “either in hell or in heaven.”
Does he say everyone will give account to God?
Yes. He says “everyone shall give account of himself to God,” and one day people “got to stand before Jesus and give an account of everything they said and everything they did, and that is no joke.”
What does he say repentance looks like for a baby Christian?

He says a baby Christian “is one that’s turned from sin,” stopping being a thief, stopping sexual immorality and stopping getting drunk and high, and turning to right. He says you may still struggle but “you’re turning from them, that’s the baby stage.”
What does he mean by being yoked with Jesus?
He says when two oxen are yoked, the weak one follows the lead of the strong one, so he had to “yoke up with Jesus” and let Him be his example and teacher rather than “brother so-and-so.”
Does he say Luke 10:19 is about handling snakes?
No. He says some people “handle snakes and so forth,” but that the “serpents and scorpions” are spirits of the kingdom of darkness, and “you’re destroying them, and you’re tearing them down.”
Does he say it’s okay to be a baby Christian?
Yes. He says “there’s nothing wrong with the baby stage if that’s where I’m at,” but “I got to grow in this power.” The thing to thank God for is that your name is in the Book of Life.
What does he say the new commandment is?
He says it is to love one another: “we quote it, but we don’t do it.”
What does he call refusing to assemble, give an hour, or tithe?
He calls it rebellion. He says when the Bible says to watch one hour, pay your tithe, or assemble together and “we won’t do it, what is it? Rebellion.”
What does he say the goal of assembling together is?
He says it is “his habitation,” God’s presence coming. It is “not to get a lady, not to get a man, not to get someone to buy my product,” but to assemble for His presence to come.
What does he say about praying about a problem versus praising about it?

He says baby Christians always say “I pray about it,” but “you never hear them say, ‘Let’s praise about it.’” He says God said that if a baby would praise Him, He would “still the enemy and the avenger.”

items.d: In this message, the seventh lesson in his Revelation study, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the beast of Revelation 13 is directly connected to Satan, that the waters it comes from are people, and that…
p: In this message, the seventh lesson in his Revelation study, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the beast of Revelation 13 is directly connected to Satan, that the waters it comes from are people, and that the antichrist is defined in Scripture. He says Satan lost power at the cross and now has only limited power with God’s permission, then discusses worship, blasphemy of God’s name, the three and a half years, and persecution of Christians.
What are the beasts, the saints and the harvests in this lesson? (Revelation 13:1)

He says this is the seventh lesson, on the first and second beast, on “the believers, those written in the Book of Life,” and on the harvests. Reading Revelation 13:1, he says John saw a beast with seven heads and 10 horns and “the name of blasphemy” on its heads, and that blasphemy “means to speak evil of, speak bad about.”
What are the beasts, the saints and the harvests in this lesson? (Revelation 13:1)

This is our seventh lesson, and we’re going to be talking this morning about the beast, plural, first and second beast. We’re going to be talking about the saints, and are the believers, those written in the Book of Life, and we’re going to be talking about the harvest, it should be plural, harvests. Okay. In Revelation 13:1, John saw a beast having seven heads and 10 horns, and on the heads was the name of blasphemy. Okay, blasphemy means to speak evil of, speak bad about. And this beast was given its power, uh, from the dragon, and his seat, his position, and great authority from the dragon. The dragon gave the first beast his power, his seat, and great authority.
What are the beasts, the saints and the harvests in this lesson? (Revelation 13:1)
Revelation 13:1: Then I stood on the sand of the sea. And I saw a beast rising up out of the sea, having seven heads and ten horns, and on his horns ten crowns, and on his heads a blasphemous name.
Is the beast connected to Satan? (Revelation 12:3, 13:2)

He says the dragon gave the first beast his power, seat and great authority, and since “the fiery red dragon” of Revelation 12:3 is Satan with seven heads and 10 horns, “this beast is directly connected to who? Satan himself.” He says “we don’t need theories, we need what? Just truth.”
Is the beast connected to Satan? (Revelation 12:3, 13:2)

Now, we got to remember that Revelation 12:3 told us the fiery red dragon, which was who? Satan, plainly tells us. There had how many heads? Seven heads and 10 horns. So this beast is directly connected to who? Satan himself. I mean, you know, you don’t have to have some antichrist rising up over in Asia, uh, like Jerry Falwell said in 1900 or so, the late 1800s, 1980s, uh, that some antichrist was born over in Asia, and, and, you know, he’s dead and gone, and so is that theory. We don’t need theories, we need what? Just truth. And if we don’t know it, we just need to say, “We, you know, it’s not been given to us yet.” But we know that this beast is connected with Satan, because it’s the same connection here.
Is the beast connected to Satan? (Revelation 12:3, 13:2)

Revelation 12:3: And another sign appeared in heaven: behold, a great, fiery red dragon having seven heads and ten horns, and seven diadems on his heads. Revelation 13:2: Now the beast which I saw was like a leopard, his feet were like the feet of a bear, and his mouth like the mouth of a lion. The dragon gave him his power, his throne, and great authority.
Is the beast one person or people? (Revelation 17:15, Daniel 8:20)

Reading Revelation 17:15, he says the waters the beast comes up out of are “multitudes, nations, and tongues,” so “it’s people.” He says a kingdom is the people in it, not just a king: “a king can be bad, or a king can be good, the people can be good with a bad king,” so “the key is the people here.”
Is the beast one person or people? (Revelation 17:15, Daniel 8:20)

Now, we also know that the waters, this beast comes up out of the waters, out of the seas, and we know that the waters in Revelation 17:15, the waters where the whore sits, we’ll be getting into her next week, are multitudes, nations, and tongues. Okay, the Bible tells us what the waters are. Right. Hallelujah. So it’s people. This thing is going to be in people. A nation is nothing more than people with a certain culture and certain laws and a certain government that they abide by. It’s always people. So it’s people that this beast comes through, works through, and so forth. In Daniel chapter 8:20 and also Daniel chapter 7, we all know this theory, we hear it all the time, of the beast being a king. But if you read, the ram with two horns are the kings of Media and Persia, the male goat is the what? Is the what? Kingdom. Who lives in a kingdom? Who lives in a kingdom? People. So it doesn’t have to be the king. In fact, in the Bible it says that Jotham was a good man, but the people did corruptly, and then it turns around and says Manasseh seduced the people of God to do corruptly. So a king can be bad, or a king can be good, the people can be good with a bad king, or the people can be what? Yeah, vice versa. The key is the people here. Amen.
Is the beast one person or people? (Revelation 17:15, Daniel 8:20)

Revelation 17:15: Then he said to me, “The waters which you saw, where the harlot sits, are peoples, multitudes, nations, and tongues. Daniel 8:20: The ram which you saw, having the two horns—they are the kings of Media and Persia. 2 Chronicles 27:2: And he did what was right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father Uzziah had done (although he did not enter the temple of the LORD). But still the people acted corruptly. 2 Chronicles 33:9: So Manasseh seduced Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to do more evil than the nations whom the LORD had destroyed before the children of Israel.
What are the three kingdoms, and how does the Bible define the antichrist?

He says there are three kingdoms: God’s, man’s, and “the kingdom of darkness, kingdom of sin, Satan,” and each is made of people acting out their ruler. He says the beast “is never called the antichrist in scripture,” and that the antichrists are “those who say Jesus has not come in the flesh” and people “who do not believe in the Father and the Son.”
What are the three kingdoms, and how does the Bible define the antichrist?

We know that there are three kingdoms in the Bible: the kingdom of God, the spiritual kingdom; the kingdom of man, like the United States, natural area; and the kingdom of darkness, kingdom of sin, Satan. See, we know that. And so the kingdom of Satan, connecting with people who do wrong, are a kingdom of people that are acting out the ruler of that kingdom, Satan. The kingdom of light, the kingdom of righteousness, the kingdom of God, are people who are acting out the king of that kingdom, and that is righteousness. Amen. Nothing confusing about that at all, is there? No. See, there’s things that we know. We know the beast, nor the son of perdition, is never called the antichrist in scripture. Never. They have to bring it together. The Bible never says, in fact it says the antichrist are those who say Jesus has not come in the flesh. Plainly tells us who the antichrist are. It defines the antichrist, and he says, John, in John chapter 2, he says there are how many? Many antichrists. And then again in John chapter 2, it says that the antichrists are people who do not believe in the Father and the Son. Whoo. And so the Jesus-only people have a problem here. The Jews have a problem here. You got to believe in God and what? Jesus Christ, his Son, who came, and that was God, by the way, and died for the sins of the world. See, the Bible tells, see, we know these things. They, this is not fantasy, we know this stuff, if you read your Bible. This is just common sense, it’s just simple doctrine. How many are learning something already? I’m glad. The rest of you are that smart. Ah.
What are the three kingdoms, and how does the Bible define the antichrist?

1 John 2:18: Little children, it is the last hour; and as you have heard that the Antichrist is coming, even now many antichrists have come, by which we know that it is the last hour. 2 John 7: For many deceivers have gone out into the world who do not confess Jesus Christ as coming in the flesh. This is a deceiver and an antichrist. 1 John 2:22: Who is a liar but he who denies that Jesus is the Christ? He is antichrist who denies the Father and the Son.
How did Satan lose his power? (John 12:31–32, Hebrews 2:14)

He says one of the beast’s heads was wounded to death and healed, and he turns to Jesus’ words that “now is the judgment of this world.” He says that when Jesus died on the cross “he is bringing Satan down, destroying his power,” and reading Hebrews 2:14 he says Jesus’ death rendered Satan powerless.
How did Satan lose his power? (John 12:31–32, Hebrews 2:14)

Now we’re going to go on in Revelation to another three-and-a-half-year period and talk about more of this beast. Okay, the beast who had seven heads and 10 horns, one of those heads was wounded to death, and it was healed. Okay. Now, you know, theories are just wonderful, and you can bring in, you know, the United Nations and everything else if you want, but let’s just stick to scripture. All right, let’s just stick to scripture. Let me tell you about someone who had power, lost it, and got it again, from the scriptures. Are you ready for this? Here’s Dave Kincer’s spiritual imagination. All right. “Now is the judgment of this world.” Jesus, Jesus is talking here. “Now shall the prince of this world be” what? “Cast out. And if I be lifted up, I’ll draw all men unto me.” Okay, when Jesus died on the cross, he is bringing Satan down, destroying his power, destroying the authority that he had. Yes. Okay, Hebrews 2:14: “Through death He might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the Devil.” See, Jesus said he’s cast down, and I’m going to be lifted up, and when I’m lifted up, he’s cast down, and here it says in Hebrews that when Jesus died, he what? Destroyed, rendered powerless Satan. Amen. Oh, the big bad beast.
How did Satan lose his power? (John 12:31–32, Hebrews 2:14)

John 12:31-32: Now is the judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world will be cast out. And I, if I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all peoples to Myself.” Hebrews 2:14: Inasmuch then as the children have partaken of flesh and blood, He Himself likewise shared in the same, that through death He might destroy him who had the power of death, that is, the devil,
Was Satan given power again? (John 14:30, Ephesians 2:2)

Citing John 14:30 and Ephesians 2:2, he says Satan is “the prince of this world” who works in the children of disobedience, and that “the power was taken, and then limited power was given.” He says “Satan has been given power again to seduce people, deceive people, and war with the saints,” and that the beast and Satan have the same seven heads and 10 horns.
Was Satan given power again? (John 14:30, Ephesians 2:2)

All right, but look at here, and remember this beast is connected directly to Satan. Now, John 14:30: “After this I will not talk much with you, for the prince of this world comes and has nothing in me.” Ephesians 2:2: “In times past you walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of, to the power of the air, the spirit that now works in the children of disobedience, fulfilling the desires of the flesh and the mind, children of” what? Wrath. Now, Satan has been given power again to seduce people, deceive people, and war with the saints. The power was taken, and then limited power was given. Do you see that? He had power, Jesus rendered powerless, and then he was given limited power again. Hallelujah. How many heads and horns did the beast have? Seven and 10. How many heads and horns did Satan have? Seven and 10. You know, we don’t have to have somebody rising up in, in Russia or Asia or whatever to be the antichrist and the big bad guy and all this. We’ve got him. Amen. And people that follow the kingdom of darkness are his citizens, of his kingdom, carrying this out. We know this stuff, don’t we? But it’s so basic, God help us, that we... it’s that simple.
Was Satan given power again? (John 14:30, Ephesians 2:2)

John 14:30: I will no longer talk much with you, for the ruler of this world is coming, and he has nothing in Me. Ephesians 2:2: in which you once walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit who now works in the sons of disobedience, Revelation 13:7: It was granted to him to make war with the saints and to overcome them. And authority was given him over every tribe, tongue, and nation.
Can Satan touch us without God’s permission? (Luke 4:5–6, Job)

He says the Devil showed Jesus all the kingdoms and God has given Satan “a limited power,” and that he has power over the nations only “if he gets permission” from Jesus Christ, as with Job. He says “aren’t you glad that Satan can’t touch you unless God gives him permission,” and that God knows “you’re able to handle it.”
Can Satan touch us without God’s permission? (Luke 4:5–6, Job)

Now, the Devil, taking Jesus up into a high mountain, showed Jesus all the kingdoms in the world in a moment of time, a twinkling of an eye. The Devil said to him, “All this power I give you, and the glory of them, for that is delivered unto me, and to whomsoever will I give it.” And so God has given Satan a limited power, and he does have power over the nations if he gets permission from who? Jesus Christ himself. In Job, didn’t he have to get permission from God to touch Job? Yes. Hallelujah. See, he created the waster to destroy. God can’t go around destroying people. See, God is good. God can’t lie. There’s things that God can’t do. People say, “Well, if he’s God, he can do anything.” No, there’s things he can’t do. He can’t lie, he can’t sin, and he can’t harm people. So what did he do? He created Satan to do this, and Satan can only do it with whose permission? Yeah. Jesus is head over what? The principalities and powers of darkness, the head of the church, the head of the nations, isn’t that right? And the head of his kingdom. Does this make sense to you? It makes a lot of sense. Aren’t you glad that Satan can’t touch you unless God gives him permission? And if God gives him permission, aren’t you glad that the Bible says he knows you’re able to handle it? Oh man, that was a big relief back there when I was a young Christian. Hallelujah. Praise God.
Can Satan touch us without God’s permission? (Luke 4:5–6, Job)

Luke 4:5-7: Then the devil, taking Him up on a high mountain, showed Him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said to Him, “All this authority I will give You, and their glory; for this has been delivered to me, and I give it to whomever I wish. Therefore, if You will worship before me, all will be Yours.” Job 1:12: And the LORD said to Satan, “Behold, all that he has is in your power; only do not lay a hand on his person.” So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD. 1 Corinthians 10:13: No temptation has overtaken you except such as is common to man; but God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you are able, but with the temptation will also make the way of escape, that you may be able to bear it.
What does it mean to worship the dragon and the beast? (Revelation 13:4)

He says worship “means giving homage to someone, respecting someone, adoring someone,” so when we follow Jesus we are worshiping him, and “worship just isn’t lifting your hands and raising your voice.” He says the beast causes the world to worship the dragon and the beast, and “you follow one, you’re following the other.” He says we are the temple of God, built of living stones.
What does it mean to worship the dragon and the beast? (Revelation 13:4)

Now, we read on there in Revelation that this beast causes all the world to worship the dragon and worship the beast. Now, worship means giving homage to someone, respecting someone, adoring someone, and see, when we follow someone’s footsteps, we are worshiping them. We’re respecting them, we’re giving homage to them. So when we, what, follow Jesus, we are worshiping him. Worship just isn’t lifting your hands and raising your voice. The Bible says, “Worship the Lord in the beauty of holiness,” right living. You say, “Which is greater, lifting your hands in the sacrifice of praise or everyday life living for him?” Yeah. Which one are the people out there going to see? The everyday life. See, that’s worship. Hallelujah. And he causes the whole world to worship the dragon and the beast. You see, they, you notice how they’re connected? You follow one, you’re following the other. Now, this beast blasphemed God, speaks evil of God, and, uh, blasphemes God’s name, Jesus’s name, and blasphemes his temple. What is the temple of God? We learned that last week. We are. See, God doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands. He don’t need a temple built over there in Jerusalem. He is building a human temple, living stones, said Peter. Said, hallelujah, we are. See, the Spirit of God dwells in us, we’re the temple of God.
What does it mean to worship the dragon and the beast? (Revelation 13:4)

Revelation 13:4: So they worshiped the dragon who gave authority to the beast; and they worshiped the beast, saying, “Who is like the beast? Who is able to make war with him?” Psalm 29:2: Give unto the LORD the glory due to His name; Worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness. Hebrews 13:15: Therefore by Him let us continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name. Acts 17:24: God, who made the world and everything in it, since He is Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in temples made with hands. 1 Peter 2:5: you also, as living stones, are being built up a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
What does it mean that the beast blasphemes God’s name? (Revelation 13:6, John 1:1)

He says the beast blasphemes the church and the name of God, which he says is “the Lord Jesus Christ of Nazareth.” He says some national leaders say “God” and not “Jesus” because “the universal God is what’s being promoted,” and when you won’t say Jesus “you are blaspheming the name of God.” He says “Jesus said he was God,” and cites John 1:1.
What does it mean that the beast blasphemes God’s name? (Revelation 13:6, John 1:1)

So he blasphemes the church. See, he blasphemes the name of God. What is the name of God? The Lord Jesus Christ of Nazareth. Are you there? Listen, Obama and Bush, both as leaders, has blasphemed the church, blasphemed the scriptures, blasphemed Jesus. Neither one of them will use the name of Jesus. They use God. Why? Because the universal God is what’s being promoted by these people, that all religions lead to the same God. That’s why they won’t say Jesus. And when you won’t say Jesus, you are blaspheming the name of God. Which name is a name above all names, is it God or Jesus? Yes. Why? It specifically says who God is and who God was when he dwelt among us. And that’s why these people want to bring down the name of Jesus. The name of Jesus either makes you come to him or breaks you, and you want to run from him. God, no problem. I can make God anything I want to be. You can’t make Jesus anything. Or they can. They say he’s a human being, they say he’s a prophet, but he, no, Jesus said he was God. The scriptures, John 1:1, says he’s God. Jesus is who God... God himself came down in human flesh, became one of us, and died for us, and we called his name Jesus of Nazareth, not Jesus of Mexico City. All right, let’s get that straight. Amen. Now, and he made him Lord and Christ, isn’t that right? He is all controlling, and he is the Messiah. See, we know these things.
What does it mean that the beast blasphemes God’s name? (Revelation 13:6, John 1:1)

Revelation 13:6: Then he opened his mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme His name, His tabernacle, and those who dwell in heaven. Philippians 2:9: Therefore God also has highly exalted Him and given Him the name which is above every name, John 1:1: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. Acts 2:36: “Therefore let all the house of Israel know assuredly that God has made this Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Christ.”
Is the three and a half years in Revelation a literal period? (Revelation 13:5)

He says the beast’s power is in his speech “for three and a half years,” but that he has already shown that focus is “shaky,” with “four times 3 and 1/2 years, that’s 14 years.” He says singling things down to three-and-a-half-year periods and a seven-year tribulation gives “real problems from the scriptures.”
Is the three and a half years in Revelation a literal period? (Revelation 13:5)

Now, his power is in his speech, and he does this for three and a half years. Okay, it says three and a half years. A lot of focus is on this three and a half years, and I tell you, I’ve already showed you where that is shaky. I’ve already showed you there is four times 3 and 1/2 years, that’s 14 years. Now today you’re going to see another problem of 3 and 1/2 years. When you try to single things down into three and 1/2 year periods and a seven-year period of tribulation and all the rest, you got some real problems from the scriptures, real problems. All right, for instance, let me ask you, was the early church blasphemed by the Roman Empire and the citizens of the Roman Empire? Yes, absolutely. Did they persecute the church? Absolutely.
Is the three and a half years in Revelation a literal period? (Revelation 13:5)
Revelation 13:5: And he was given a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies, and he was given authority to continue for forty-two months.
Has the church been persecuted since the beginning?

He says the early church was blasphemed and persecuted by the Roman Empire, and that Christians have been persecuted “from the early church to the present time,” so “you’re worried about a little three-and-a-half-year period?” He says Satan “comes to rob, steal, kill, and what? Destroy,” and that Christians through the ages “stayed with Jesus.”
Has the church been persecuted since the beginning?

Were the Christians persecuted from the early church to the present time? Yes. Were they blasphemed? Were they talked about? Yes. And you’re worried about a little three-and-a-half-year period? This has been going on since Jesus ascended. When we showed you the millions of Christians who had lost their life throughout the ages of persecution, and not just Christians, you can just be of a different color, a different race, a different culture, and another culture will persecute you, kill you, and mistreat you. This stuff has been going on for ages. Why? Because this beast, Satan, working in people, and the Satan is called a thief, he comes to rob, steal, kill, and what? Destroy. And when people follow him, yeah, they have cultural problems, race problems, and all the rest. Why? Because that’s what Satan does, he’s out to destroy. [unclear] you don’t have to wait for a 3 and 1/2 year period. Are you with me? We don’t know why the three-and-a-half-year period is there. We know this stuff has been going on ever since Jesus ascended, and we know the early church did not bow and give in, and we know that Christians throughout the ages did not bow and give in. See, they didn’t worship the Satan, they didn’t worship evil, they didn’t go that route, whether it was a government, whether it was a people, whether it was a group, they stayed with Jesus. Can I hear an amen?
Has the church been persecuted since the beginning?
John 10:10: The thief does not come except to steal, and to kill, and to destroy. I have come that they may have life, and that they may have it more abundantly.
Who does he say is being persecuted today? (Revelation 13:7, Daniel 7:21)

Reading that the beast “makes war and overcomes the saints,” he says Daniel spoke of another beast that overcame the saints, and that leaders persecuted Jesus and his church up to now. He says “Christians in America right now are the persecuted group,” gives examples of what he says Christians are not allowed to say or preach, and says “these theory people” have our eyes on a seven-year period instead. These are his views.
Who does he say is being persecuted today? (Revelation 13:7, Daniel 7:21)

This beast makes war and overcomes the saints, and he has power over the nations. He overcomes the saints for three and a half years. Daniel talked about another beast that overcame the saints for a period of time. I submit to you that even while Jesus was here, government leaders, religious leaders, and people that identified with him persecuted Jesus, they killed Jesus, they persecuted his church, they killed people in the church up to this present time. But you see, these theory people got us thinking about a 7-year period up there, and we’re missing what is happening in our own nation. Christians in America right now are the persecuted group. It’s not the blacks, it’s not the Mexicans, it’s the Christians. You can’t call a homosexual a homosexual, you can’t call them a queer. The Bible calls him a homosexual, the, the Bible calls him a sodomite. There’s a lot of things you can’t do. You can’t use the name of Jesus, you can’t preach, you know, sexual immorality and so forth, and they say it’s a hate crime, a hate crime, you understand? And see, we got our eyes on these stupid theories and we don’t see what’s happening in our own generation. Hallelujah. That was a good, that was good. And see, that’s one of Satan’s gimmicks: if he can get our eyes on something else and not really what’s happening around us and who we are, we’re going to find out again who we are during this time, and we are a powerful people.
Who does he say is being persecuted today? (Revelation 13:7, Daniel 7:21)

Revelation 13:7: It was granted to him to make war with the saints and to overcome them. And authority was given him over every tribe, tongue, and nation. Daniel 7:21: “I was watching; and the same horn was making war against the saints, and prevailing against them,
Why does he say Christians have lost the power of the word?

He says Christians “have never” been “in total control” in 2,000 years and have always been subservient to governments that limit them, such as China. He says Christians in this country are “in dreamland” and “don’t see the decay around us,” and that “we have lost the power of the word to stand up for truth.” He cites polls on views of homosexuality as support. These are his views.
Why does he say Christians have lost the power of the word?

I submit to you, Christians have never, throughout the history, these last 2,000 years, been in total control. We’ve always been subservient to some government that wants to limit us. Could that be an amen? China limits him so bad, you can’t even preach over there, people get arrested and they get killed. It’s been going on for 2,000 years. Am I right? When you look at it right, you see it right. And we have slowly, in the last 40 years, 50 years, lost this nation. It started in the ‘60s, and Christians are so in dreamland, they don’t see the decay around us. And in fact, many Christians today believe there is no hell, there is no lake of fire, that Jesus was not born of a virgin. It’s growing every time. In the ‘70s, when the homosexuals came out, 90% of the people said that was wrong. Now it’s less than 50% of Americans are saying that homosexuality is wrong. Why? The Christians have let the word of God decay to such a place, and them undermine the word of God, say it’s just a book of fables, it’s just a book of faith, you know, it’s got weird things in it. They’re, they’re lying. And Christians are so caught up in this nonsense of the second coming, and, and, you know, helping the poor and helping the sick, that we have lost the power of the word to stand up for truth. We’re accepting lies. Could that be true? According to the polls, that is true.
What does he say blasphemy means?
He says “blasphemy means to speak evil of, speak bad about.”
Does he say an antichrist has to rise up somewhere?

He says “you don’t have to have some antichrist rising up over in Asia” and that “we don’t need theories, we need what? Just truth.” He says if we don’t know something, “it’s not been given to us yet.”
What does he say the waters in Revelation 17:15 are?

He says the Bible tells us the waters are “multitudes, nations, and tongues,” so “it’s people,” and that “a nation is nothing more than people with a certain culture and certain laws and a certain government.”
Does he say the beast has to be a king?
He says no: “it doesn’t have to be the king.” He points to Daniel’s ram and goat as kingdoms, and asks “who lives in a kingdom? People.” He says “the key is the people here.”
What are the three kingdoms he describes?
He names “the kingdom of God, the spiritual kingdom,” “the kingdom of man, like the United States,” and “the kingdom of darkness, kingdom of sin, Satan.”
How does he say Scripture defines the antichrist?
He says the Bible “defines the antichrist” as “those who say Jesus has not come in the flesh,” and that there are “many antichrists.”
What does he say happened to Satan’s power when Jesus died?

He says when Jesus died on the cross “he is bringing Satan down, destroying his power, destroying the authority that he had,” and that Hebrews 2:14 says Jesus’ death destroyed the one who had the power of death.
Does he say Satan has power today?
He says “the power was taken, and then limited power was given,” and “Satan has been given power again to seduce people, deceive people, and war with the saints.”
Can Satan do whatever he wants, according to him?
He says no: God has given Satan “a limited power,” and “aren’t you glad that Satan can’t touch you unless God gives him permission?”
What does he say worship means?

He says worship “means giving homage to someone, respecting someone, adoring someone,” and “worship just isn’t lifting your hands and raising your voice.” He cites “worship the Lord in the beauty of holiness, right living.”
What does he say the temple of God is?
He says “God doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands” and “he don’t need a temple built over there in Jerusalem.” He says “the Spirit of God dwells in us, we’re the temple of God.”
What does he say about the name of Jesus?
He says “the name of Jesus either makes you come to him or breaks you,” and that Jesus “said he was God.” He says the scriptures, John 1:1, say “he’s God.”
How long does he say persecution of Christians has been going on?
He says “this has been going on since Jesus ascended,” and that people of a different color, race or culture can also be persecuted by another culture.
How does he say early Christians responded to persecution?
He says “the early church did not bow and give in,” “they didn’t worship the Satan, they didn’t worship evil,” and “they stayed with Jesus.”
Does he say Christians have ever been in total control?
He says no: “Christians have never, throughout the history, these last 2,000 years, been in total control,” and have “always been subservient to some government that wants to limit us.”

items.d: In this second lesson on the beasts of Revelation 13, Pastor David G. Kincer says those written in the Book of Life will not worship the beast, and that the saints are still here, not raptured out. He explains…
p: In this second lesson on the beasts of Revelation 13, Pastor David G. Kincer says those written in the Book of Life will not worship the beast, and that the saints are still here, not raptured out. He explains the second beast’s false wonders and speaking idol, questions three-and-a-half-year charts and date-setting, offers his own explanation of 666, and teaches that sorcerers and false signs have only limited power.
Who does not worship the beast? (Revelation 13:8, 14:12)

He says “all worship the beast and Satan, except some people,” “those in the Book of Life,” the ones “that got born again.” He says they “didn’t join a church” or get a baptismal certificate; they “were touched by God.” He says churches “just put people on the roll book,” Jesus said “you got to be born again of the word and the Spirit,” and the saints’ faith is “in Jesus Christ, not in a church, not in a person, not in a minister.”
Who does not worship the beast? (Revelation 13:8, 14:12)

All worship the beast and Satan, except some people. And who are these people? [unclear]. Guess what that is? It’s not bacon and lettuce. Those in the Book of Life. Those in the Book of Life won’t worship the natural people who are expressing the kingdom of darkness, and they won’t worship the king of the kingdom of darkness. They won’t do it. Can I hear an amen? Amen. See, all the earth worships, but the ones written in the Book of Life, the ones that got born again, the ones that really got the real deal when they came to Christ, they didn’t join a church, they didn’t get a baptismal certificate and, and go through a ritual. They were touched by God, they responded to God, they got birthed by God, and they follow him. Amen. Churches just put people on the roll book, they just want attendance. You come, okay, we’ll put you on the roll book. He’s saved? How? No. Jesus said you got to be born again of the word and the Spirit. Of what? The word and the Spirit. And how are they going to get birthed in the word if we don’t preach the word? Are you with me? Hallelujah. And it says, “This is the patience and the faith of the saints.” Why? They’re going to stick with Jesus no matter what. These people are patient, they know God is going to fulfill his will. These people have their faith in Jesus Christ, not in a church, not in a person, not in a minister. Their faith is in Jesus Christ, and they are patiently waiting for Jesus to fulfill his word in them and in the world.
Who does not worship the beast? (Revelation 13:8, 14:12)

Revelation 13:8: All who dwell on the earth will worship him, whose names have not been written in the Book of Life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world. John 3:5: Jesus answered, “Most assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God. Revelation 14:12: Here is the patience of the saints; here are those who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus.
Are the saints raptured out, or kept through difficulty?
Asked whether these saints are raptured, he says “No, they’re still here.” He says “Jesus is big enough to keep us in any kind of difficulty of this world” and “we don’t have to get raptured out.”
Are the saints raptured out, or kept through difficulty?

Hallelujah. Powerful, isn’t it? And where are they at? Are they raptured? No, they’re still here. I’ve showed you last week and the week before, they’re still here. These people are still here. Let me know, Jesus is big enough to keep us in any kind of difficulty of this world. We don’t have to get raptured out. We’re not that weak. Some of us are weak, we want to be raptured out.
What does he say is the difference between a believer and a Christian? (Revelation 13:11)

He says the second beast “has all the power of the first beast,” including “the ability to speak,” and compares that to two recent national leaders he says “claimed to be Christians, and they lied to us.” He says “Christian means I came from Christ, I follow Christ, I act like Christ,” that “believer’s a stage,” and “just move on down the line” to maturity: “stick with the King.”
What does he say is the difference between a believer and a Christian? (Revelation 13:11)

Now, a second beast comes up, and the second beast has all the power of the first beast. So he’s got the ability to speak. That’s what the first beast had, the power to speak. Obama has great speaking abilities. Bush had great speaking abilities. I use them both because one was a Republican, one was a Democrat, both of them claimed to be Christians, and they lied to us. What does the word Christian mean? Yes. [unclear] means from or like, you know, a, a mannerism. Ephesians means what? You come from Ephesus. Yes. Christian means I came from Christ, I follow Christ, I act like Christ. See, there’s a big difference between a believer and a Christian. And believer’s a stage, don’t get me wrong, there’s nothing wrong, we got to go through the stages, am I right? Yeah. We got to believe, you know, we got to follow and all that. There’s nothing wrong if you’re a believer today, it’s fine, just move on down the line. This is an assembly line. We got to move on down the assembly line, and the, the great master assembly man puts us together. Amen. Just stick with the assembly line, man. Like it said in the prophecy today, stick with the King. He does want you to be perfect. Perfect is maturity, and the key is to stick with the King, like it said in the prophecy today. Just hang in there, don’t disqualify yourself because you got some faults. Just stick with the assembly line, the master craftsman will get the parts and get everything in you as you do. Now that was good. Amen. Remember, the saints are patient, and their trust is in Jesus to do what he said.

He says no: “no one” knows. He recalls that “they said he was coming in 1960, 1962” and later, and says “our generations might be here another thousand years from now.”
What does he say the sorcerers of Egypt really needed to do?
He says “what they really needed was to overpower Moses and turn the blood back to water,” but they could not, because God gave them only “limited supernatural power.”
What does he say about someone telling people their addresses?

He says “you can find where I live in the phone book,” and “I need a source of power to live in this life for Christ and do what’s right.” He says “limited knowledge” like that “doesn’t fool those that are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life.” This is his account.
What does he say about vague prophetic words?
He says “tell me exactly what you see,” not general words about cars and rivers. He says “us Spirit-filled people have got to get the program,” because “we’re one of the worst for this nonsense.”

items.d: In this third lesson, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Revelation 14 that the 144,000 with the Lamb on Zion are the church, written with God’s name as overcomers, and that “virgins” means spiritual purity…
p: In this third lesson, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Revelation 14 that the 144,000 with the Lamb on Zion are the church, written with God’s name as overcomers, and that “virgins” means spiritual purity kept through repentance. He covers first fruits, servants, brethren and remnant, the gospel harvest, the two harvests, and why he says we are to fear God, ending that the church, not the beast, is the powerful one.
Who are the 144,000 with the Lamb on Mount Zion? (Revelation 14:1, 3:12)

He says “Zion is the church,” so the 144,000 with the Lamb are the people of God, and that he has “no idea what 144,000 is” beyond 12 times 12. Reading Revelation 3:12, he says the overcomer gets God’s name written on him, that we overcome “by our faith in Jesus Christ,” and “we have the name of God written on us” if we pursue God as overcomers.
Who are the 144,000 with the Lamb on Mount Zion? (Revelation 14:1, 3:12)

Now let’s get to the people of God. I like this part of Revelation here: 144,000 with the Lamb on Zion, Revelation 14. Zion is what? Yeah, Hebrews 12 and other places, Zion is the church. So here is 144,000 with the Lamb. There are two tribes missing, one tribe is mentioned twice in the listing. All right, and you know God don’t make those kind of mistakes. So obviously he’s not interested in 12 tribes, is he? And he’s really not interested in 144,000. I have no idea what 144,000 is, except, you know, 12 times 12 is 144 and 120,000, you know. And they have their Father’s name written in their forehead. Okay, well, this is a no-brainer. We know Zion is the church, we know the Lamb, Jesus, is why we are saved, isn’t that right? Jesus dying on the cross, we know that. And all of us, what, have to believe in the Lamb, ain’t that right? Now, if we can get the name of God on our forehead, we got it. Revelation 3:12, remember this teaching, very first, second one, first, first or second one: “He who overcomes, I will make him a pillar in the temple of my God.” Now, who’s the temple of God? The people, the believers. “And he shall go out no more. I will write on him the name of my God.” Wow. This 144,000 had what written on them? The name of God. I have written on me, if I’m an overcomer. And how do we overcome? By our faith in Jesus Christ. “He that overcometh the world.” Are we overcomers of the world? Are we destined to do that? Do we give up because we haven’t quite made it yet? No, man, we’re on the assembly line, just hang tight, the thing’s coming. Hallelujah. “And the name of the city of my God.” What’s the city of God? The church, the New Jerusalem, “which comes down out of heaven from my God, and I will write on him” what? “My new name.” Are you there, church? Now, if we’re pursuing God to be overcomers and conquerors in this life, we have the name of God written on us. Hallelujah. We are Zion, we are the church.
Who are the 144,000 with the Lamb on Mount Zion? (Revelation 14:1, 3:12)

Revelation 14:1: Then I looked, and behold, a Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with Him one hundred and forty-four thousand, having His Father’s name written on their foreheads. Hebrews 12:22: But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, to an innumerable company of angels, Revelation 3:12: He who overcomes, I will make him a pillar in the temple of My God, and he shall go out no more. I will write on him the name of My God and the name of the city of My God, the New Jerusalem, which comes down out of heaven from My God. And I will write on him My new name. 1 John 5:4: For whatever is born of God overcomes the world. And this is the victory that has overcome the world—our faith. Revelation 21:2: Then I, John, saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.
What is the new song, and are the 144,000 literal Jewish virgins? (Revelation 14:3–4)

He says the new song is ours, citing the psalm “He hath put a new song in my heart” and “psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs.” He says “there isn’t some 144 Jews over there in Palestine that God is going to raise up to be virgins,” that God “is interested in the whole world,” and that the first thing is to “get redeemed, repent, and get saved.” He says “there’s nothing wrong with getting married and having sex in marriage,” so “it can’t be this virgin thing.”
What is the new song, and are the 144,000 literal Jewish virgins? (Revelation 14:3–4)

Hallelujah. Now, he says they had a new song. Well, what does the Psalm say? “He hath put a new song in my heart, a song of praise unto my God, and many shall see and turn and put their trust in the Lord.” It says over and over, sing unto the Lord a new song. In Ephesians it says speak and sing to yourself as “psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs.” New songs, we are the ones that have the new song. Are you getting this? Say, “Oh me,” or “Amen.” You see, there isn’t some 144 Jews over there in Palestine that God is going to raise up to be virgins. They don’t even believe in Christ. And that’s what these theory people, they try to make their theories come to pass. God is interested in the whole world, he’s not willing that any should perish, isn’t that right? Now, let’s continue. “Redeemed from the earth.” I don’t even have to show scripture, that we all know we’ve been redeemed by the blood of the Lamb, right? Every one of us. Okay, so see, it’s still us. The first thing we got to do is get redeemed, repent, and get saved. Ah, here we are. They’re virgins. They’re virgins, and it plainly says they’re virgin, never knew a woman, that’s what it says. Okay. And they follow the Lamb. Okay, hallelujah. Well, that leaves out Peter, John, King David, Job, Noah, and the God that wrote the book in the very beginning of the book said it is good for a man to leave his mother and father and cleave to his wife. There’s nothing wrong with getting married and having sex in marriage. God can’t contradict his word, so it can’t be this virgin thing. Are you out there?
What is the new song, and are the 144,000 literal Jewish virgins? (Revelation 14:3–4)

Psalm 40:3: He has put a new song in my mouth— Praise to our God; Many will see it and fear, And will trust in the LORD. Ephesians 5:19: speaking to one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord, 2 Peter 3:9: The Lord is not slack concerning His promise, as some count slackness, but is longsuffering toward us, not willing that any should perish but that all should come to repentance. Revelation 14:3-4: They sang as it were a new song before the throne, before the four living creatures, and the elders; and no one could learn that song except the hundred and forty-four thousand who were redeemed from the earth. These are the ones who were not defiled with women, for they are virgins. These are the ones who follow the Lamb wherever He goes. These were redeemed from among men, being firstfruits to God and to the Lamb. Genesis 2:24: Therefore a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and they shall become one flesh.
What does he say it means to be a “spiritual virgin”? (2 Corinthians 11:2, Isaiah 54:5, Revelation 19:7)

He says Paul’s words to the Corinthians, “I’ve espoused you to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin,” mean “the absence of sin, the absence of walking in darkness and disobeying God,” not “fleshly virginity.” He says “I become a spiritual virgin” through Christ’s blood and “I maintain that through the principle of repentance.” He cites Isaiah 54:5 and Revelation 19:7 and says “adulthood is 20 years old,” telling young people to “hang tight.” These are his views.
What does he say it means to be a “spiritual virgin”? (2 Corinthians 11:2, Isaiah 54:5, Revelation 19:7)

I mean, how many of you are going to be willing to become an overcomer by not having sexual relationships while here on earth? No hands are jumping up. You know, you wanted to get married, you wanted to have kids, am I right? Who put that in you? Your Creator. And then he’s going to punish you because you’re not a virgin? It doesn’t make sense. But this does, are you ready? “I’ve espoused you to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin.” To who? Who’s he talking to? The Corinthian believers. I’m preaching to you and I’m praying with you and, and, and we’re working together that you become this pure, chaste virgin that Jesus is looking for. He’s not talking about fleshly virginity there. He’s talking about the absence of sin, the absence of walking in darkness and disobeying God. You young’uns getting this? Hallelujah. “You should be married.” Romans 7:14: “You should be married to another, even to him,” should be capitalized, that’s Jesus, “who is raised from the dead.” We should be married to who? Jesus, who is raised from the dead, and he marries what? Virgins. How do we become virgins when we were sinners? His blood. His blood cleanses from what? All sin. I become a virgin, I become a spiritual virgin, and I maintain that through the principle of repentance. If I mess up, I repent and I am restored back to what? Being a spiritual virgin. Now, this makes sense. Isaiah 54:5: “Your Maker, your Husband, the Lord of hosts is his name, your Redeemer.” See, the Redeemer and the Husband, it’s all one package. Hallelujah. Revelation 19:7: “The marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife,” his what? “Wife has made herself ready.” That’s us. We’re ready, Lord. We’re mature. Men marry mature women, and women marry mature men. We don’t marry kids. Sex with kids and all that’s out in the Bible, that’s ridiculous. “Sex by eight or you’re too late” is just ridiculous. Are you with me? And adulthood is 20 years old. You young ones, look at me, the Bible says adulthood is 20 years old. How old? 20. You hang tight to your 20 and you’ll live a life that’s right. Hang tight and live right. Don’t you get to be 14, you got breasts sticking out, and you know, you got pubic hair and so forth, and you think, “Man, I’m more grown.” No, you’re not. Wait till you’re 20. Hang in there. Yes, that’s a good place for a hallelujah.
What does he say it means to be a “spiritual virgin”? (2 Corinthians 11:2, Isaiah 54:5, Revelation 19:7)

2 Corinthians 11:2: For I am jealous for you with godly jealousy. For I have betrothed you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ. Romans 7:4: Therefore, my brethren, you also have become dead to the law through the body of Christ, that you may be married to another—to Him who was raised from the dead, that we should bear fruit to God. 1 John 1:7: But if we walk in the light as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus Christ His Son cleanses us from all sin. Isaiah 54:5: For your Maker is your husband, The LORD of hosts is His name; And your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel; He is called the God of the whole earth. Revelation 19:7: Let us be glad and rejoice and give Him glory, for the marriage of the Lamb has come, and His wife has made herself ready.”
Who are the first fruits, and how is the church presented without blemish? (1 Corinthians 15:20, James 1:18, Ephesians 5:27)

He says “just because you got the equipment doesn’t mean you’re capable of using it yet,” then that the first fruits are “we are, the church,” citing 1 Corinthians 15:20 and James 1:18. He says the church is “an overcomer in this world in spite of the beast,” and reading Ephesians 5:27 he says the blood keeps us “faultless before Christ as long as we admit our sin and we keep going to him.”
Who are the first fruits, and how is the church presented without blemish? (1 Corinthians 15:20, James 1:18, Ephesians 5:27)

He said, “Well, he gave me this equipment, surely I got to use it.” Don’t you dare. He gave you hands, but don’t drive a car at nine. Right? Amen. Hallelujah. Yeah. Yeah. Just because you got the equipment doesn’t mean you’re capable of using it yet, and using it rightly. Hallelujah. Now, he says these are the first fruits, no deceit or faults in them. These are the first fruits. 1 Corinthians 15:20: “Christ has risen from the dead and become the first fruits of them that slept.” James 1:18: “Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of first fruits of his creation.” So who are the first fruits? We are, the church. These people are missing the whole focus of Revelation, that is, the church is an overcomer in this world, in spite of the beast, in spite of Satan, and everything that comes against us, we are overcomers. And that’s why we’re here today. Our forefathers overcame, not all of them. They handed this stuff down to us. Ephesians 5:27: “Present the church to himself, the bride, a glorious church with no spot, no wrinkle, no blemish, but holy.” What’s he going to present to himself? This first fruit people that are without blemish, no faults. Why are we have no faults, even though we have faults? The blood. And we’re on the assembly line, we’re following Christ, and the blood covers us, the blood keeps cleansing us, the blood keeps keeping us a virgin, a spiritual virgin for Christ, faultless before Christ, as long as we admit our sin and we keep going to him. We’re on the assembly line, he keeps changing us. And if you don’t change, you’re going to burn.
Who are the first fruits, and how is the church presented without blemish? (1 Corinthians 15:20, James 1:18, Ephesians 5:27)

1 Corinthians 15:20: But now Christ is risen from the dead, and has become the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep. James 1:18: Of His own will He brought us forth by the word of truth, that we might be a kind of firstfruits of His creatures. Ephesians 5:27: that He might present her to Himself a glorious church, not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but that she should be holy and without blemish.
What does he say about hell and the church prevailing? (Matthew 16:18)

He says “the people want to laugh at the Bible … they’re going to burn,” and reading Matthew 16:18 he says “we’re supposed to be overcoming the gates of hell.” Of people who claim hell is just the grave, he says “they’re lying to you,” because “there’s a power in hell” and the church prevails against it. These are his views.
What does he say about hell and the church prevailing? (Matthew 16:18)

The people want to laugh at the Bible and all that, they’re going to burn. Matthew 16:18: “The gates of hell shall not prevail against” what? The church. See, we’re supposed to be overcoming the gates of hell. And these people that say that, “Oh, hell isn’t like that, it isn’t a place of the fire, and it isn’t a place, it’s just a place where you go and you’re in the grave,” they’re lying to you. It says the church does not prevail against hell. What good does it do to prevail against someone that’s dead and has no life after that? There’s a power in darkness, there’s a power in hell, there’s a power in that judgment, and the church, what? Prevails against it. We overcome it. Okay, the saints are likened to servants in Revelation, the brethren, the remnant, and the bride. The servant does things out of duty.
What does he say about hell and the church prevailing? (Matthew 16:18)
Matthew 16:18: And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it.
What are the servants, the brethren, the remnant and the bride? (Revelation 12:11, 12:17)

He says servants “just do it because it’s their duty,” the brethren “overcome Satan by the blood of the Lamb,” and the remnant “keep the commandments of God and follow Christ.” He says Satan “makes war with those that believe, even do something about it,” and the bride is last.
What are the servants, the brethren, the remnant and the bride? (Revelation 12:11, 12:17)

They don’t feel like it, they don’t want to, they just do it because it’s their duty, and all of us are to be servants. Then there’s the brethren. The brethren are a little different. They overcome Satan “by the blood of the Lamb, and they loved not their life unto death, and the word of their testimony.” The brethren are [unclear], they overcome Satan, they don’t let sin and Satan rule and control their life. Are you there? The remnant are they that, what? Keep the commandments of God and follow Christ. That’s us. We’re supposed to keep the commandments of God and follow Christ, isn’t that right? We’re supposed to go from believer to servant to discipleship to being brethren to being the remnant. That he makes war with the remnant, you know why? Because they keep the command. He’s not interested in people that just believe and don’t follow Christ. Satan makes war with those that believe, even do something about it. So if you don’t have problems in your life, it’s a good chance you’re not much, a, you’re not, you haven’t gone past the servanthood.
What are the servants, the brethren, the remnant and the bride? (Revelation 12:11, 12:17)

Revelation 12:11: And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, and they did not love their lives to the death.
