Revelation 12:17: And the dragon was enraged with the woman, and he went to make war with the rest of her offspring, who keep the commandments of God and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.
What is the harvest where the gospel is preached to all nations? (Revelation 14:6–7)

He says the saints are still here and the gospel is preached “to all nations, saying, fear God, praise and worship God, the judgment is come.” He says “nothing has happened like this in history” as the emphasis on praising and worshiping Jesus, and that people in many churches cannot hide behind “I was raised this way.” He says he will show who Babylon is “without leaving the book of Revelation.” He also names churches and denominations; see the editor note.
What is the harvest where the gospel is preached to all nations? (Revelation 14:6–7)

In fact, if you don’t do things just because it’s your duty, you’re probably just a weak wimp believer. You haven’t gotten out of the baby crib yet. Could that be an amen? And then the bride. Oh, the bride prepared for her husband. Okay, last but not least, the harvest. The gospel is preached. See, the saints are still here, right? We just found out the saints are still here, and the gospel is being preached by who? The saints, the people of God. God’s wrath and God’s judgment and the harvest. Here we go. The gospel is preached. It says there to all nations, saying, “Fear God, praise and worship God, the judgment is come.” Okay, and nothing has happened like this in history like our generation, where there’s an emphasis on praising and worshiping Jesus Christ. The Baptists are doing it now. Catholics have a separate group in the back room that are doing it. They’re praising and worshiping God. Why? God said this would happen before he would come. Hallelujah. And you don’t have to, you can sit there like a dodo bird and go, “Well, you know, I was raised this way, and I’m shy, and I was, you know, born a Baptist, I’ll die a Baptist,” or whatever. I just told you the Baptists are being converted to the Bible. They’re praising and worshiping and singing choruses, and the judgment has come. All right, and what do we preach? We preach to fear God, turn from your sins, praise and worship him, follow him, pray and seek him, for there’s a judgment coming where you’re going to be accountable for what you say and do. Now, here’s God’s wrath, judgment: Babylon has fallen. We’ll be getting into that very clearly. I’m going to show you clearly who Babylon is from the Bible without leaving the book of Revelation. That sound fair? So see, this is like the old series, you know, they, they ended it with a what’s going to happen next. Everybody’s got Babylon this and Babylon that. The Bible plainly tells us who Babylon is, Revelation does: the beast worshipers, and those that have the Mark.
What is the harvest where the gospel is preached to all nations? (Revelation 14:6–7)

Revelation 14:6-7: Then I saw another angel flying in the midst of heaven, having the everlasting gospel to preach to those who dwell on the earth—to every nation, tribe, tongue, and people— saying with a loud voice, “Fear God and give glory to Him, for the hour of His judgment has come; and worship Him who made heaven and earth, the sea and springs of water.” Revelation 14:8: And another angel followed, saying, “Babylon is fallen, is fallen, that great city, because she has made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication.”
What does he say the two prophets and “limited supernatural power” are? (Revelation 11)

He says the beast worshipers are being challenged by the saints and by “two prophets who have supernatural powers” who counteract the second beast, “a display of full supernatural power against a display of limited supernatural power.” Of the two witnesses killing people with fire from their mouths, he says “I highly doubt that’s really what he’s talking about.”
What does he say the two prophets and “limited supernatural power” are? (Revelation 11)

I mean, you got to remember, we just left two prophets that were calling down fire from heaven and tormenting mankind. We got these supernatural people doing super... we got two supernatural powers working against each other here. Are you, are you there? Do you remember the two witnesses, the two prophets, that tormented people on earth for three and a half years, bringing fire? They would kill them with fire from their mouth. We’ve never seen that, and I highly doubt that’s really what he’s talking about. Are you there? So the beast worshipers, they that worship the beast, they are being challenged by the word of God from the saints of God who won’t worship the beast. At the same time they’re getting a challenge, and not only are they challenging, when this supernatural beast comes up, these two prophets who have supernatural powers are counteracting the supernatural power of the second beast, if you can read it right. And it’s a display of full supernatural power against a display of limited supernatural power. Hallelujah.
What does he say the two prophets and “limited supernatural power” are? (Revelation 11)
Revelation 11:5: And if anyone wants to harm them, fire proceeds from their mouth and devours their enemies. And if anyone wants to harm them, he must be killed in this manner.
What is the patience of the saints, and which group do you want to be in? (Revelation 13:10, 14:12)

He says the beast worshipers “enter into eternal torment,” and “this is the patience of the saints”: the saints are “patiently waiting for God to remove these people” and “turn the table on them.” He asks which group you want to be in, the one that takes 666 and “can buy and sell,” or the one that says “I’m following Christ,” even if we do not have “full victory” now.
What is the patience of the saints, and which group do you want to be in? (Revelation 13:10, 14:12)

And they’re going to enter into eternal torment, not just tormented now while they’re here on earth, they’re going to go into the torment, the hell fire and brimstone and all that. And then he comes up and says, “This is the patience of the saints.” They that lead into captivity shall, what, go into captivity. They that kill with the sword shall be killed with the sword. And so the saints are just patiently waiting for God to remove these people, this beast, and put them into captivity, and these that want to use force to get their way, they go, they’re just waiting for God to turn the table on them. Are you there? Now, which group you want to be? You want to be the one that takes the 666 and you can buy and sell and go on through life, and then when you’re confronted with Jesus Christ, you’re in trouble? Or you want to be one that says, “I’m following Christ, I’m following what’s right, and yes, it may look bleak for us now, and we may not have full victory and full control over everything in this earth, but it’s coming”?
What is the patience of the saints, and which group do you want to be in? (Revelation 13:10, 14:12)

Revelation 13:10: He who leads into captivity shall go into captivity; he who kills with the sword must be killed with the sword. Here is the patience and the faith of the saints. Revelation 14:12: Here is the patience of the saints; here are those who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus.

He says “there’s two harvests”: the harvest of the earth, which is “us” (“the dead in Christ will rise”), and then “the wrath of God’s wine press.” He says the wrath, the second coming and the day of judgment are “all one package.”

And everyone with the mark’s in serious trouble. Ain’t that what it says? Man, don’t get me no more, I don’t even want to get close to the kingdom of Satan. Then there’s two harvests. He says the harvest is ripe. The angel says, “Put in your sickle and reap the harvest, for the harvest is ripe.” It’s ready. Isn’t that what Jesus said? “Look upon the fields, for they are white, ripe for the harvest.” And here comes the harvest of the earth. That’s us, folks. That’s us, those of us who are, and the dead in Christ will rise. That’s us. We’re going to be harvested. And oops, and then there is a second harvest. Ain’t that cute? And then there is the wrath of God’s wine press, where the blood went up to the horses’ bridles. I mean, here we got the wrath, judgment, it’s eternal, they’re going to be tormented, and it’s at the same time, the day of wrath, the second coming, the day of judgment, all one package.

Revelation 14:14-16: Then I looked, and behold, a white cloud, and on the cloud sat One like the Son of Man, having on His head a golden crown, and in His hand a sharp sickle. And another angel came out of the temple, crying with a loud voice to Him who sat on the cloud, “Thrust in Your sickle and reap, for the time has come for You to reap, for the harvest of the earth is ripe.” So He who sat on the cloud thrust in His sickle on the earth, and the earth was reaped. John 4:35: Do you not say, ‘There are still four months and then comes the harvest’? Behold, I say to you, lift up your eyes and look at the fields, for they are already white for harvest! Revelation 14:19-20: So the angel thrust his sickle into the earth and gathered the vine of the earth, and threw it into the great winepress of the wrath of God. And the winepress was trampled outside the city, and blood came out of the winepress, up to the horses’ bridles, for one thousand six hundred furlongs.

He says this message “scared me to come to Jesus,” and that “we are to be afraid of God,” which he explains as to “respect him” and “be scared of him.” He cites “fear the one who is able to cast your soul into hell,” and says a ruler who heard Paul preach on righteousness and judgment “trembled, but he would not change his life.”

And I don’t know about you, but I’m glad this kind of message scared the hell out of me. It scared me to come to Jesus, and I found out Jesus was real. And these people that want to diminish the Bible by saying, “You’re just putting fear in people.” We are to be afraid of God. We are to respect him, and we are to be scared of him. It says, “Fear the one who is able to cast your soul into hell.” Don’t fear the one that can just hurt you physically. They can take away your job, they can take away your income and ability to buy and sell. Fear him who has the power to cast you into hell. And we’re supposed to tremble. Didn’t Herod tremble when Paul preached to him of righteousness and the judgment to come? He trembled, but he would not change his life. And the church needs this message to cause God to move people to tremble and be afraid of God.

Matthew 10:28: And do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. But rather fear Him who is able to destroy both soul and body in hell. Acts 24:25: Now as he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was afraid and answered, “Go away for now; when I have a convenient time I will call for you.”
What does he say the final judgment is like? (Revelation 20–21)

He says everyone stands before God “on your own merit,” “weighed in the balance,” by “what you did with the word of God and how you lived your life.” He says judgment on earth is “temporary to get your attention,” while the final judgment is eternal, with “a new earth and a new heaven” for the righteous and “a lake of fire” for the unrighteous. These are his statements about eternal punishment.
What does he say the final judgment is like? (Revelation 20–21)

On that day, one day you got to stand before, young people, you got to stand before God. Old people, nobody can stand there with you. Not your husband, not your wife, not your, your parents. You are there on your own merit. You’re going to be weighed in the balance, and it’s not your opinions, it’s going to count. It’s what you did with the word of God and how you lived your life, and did you admit you were wrong when you made mistakes. It’s a serious thing, and this judgment is eternal. Judgment down here is temporary to get your attention, but this judgment is eternal. Young people, there is a lake of fire. There is a new earth and a new heaven where the righteous live in, and a lake of fire where the unrighteous live in for eternity. And it says they are tormented forever before the throne and before the Lamb. They see Jesus up there, they see God up there, and yet they’re down there tormented in the flame of the lake of fire, and they can look up and see us blessed and rewarded, and that’s double torment.
What does he say the final judgment is like? (Revelation 20–21)

Revelation 21:1: Now I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away. Also there was no more sea. Revelation 20:14-15: Then Death and Hades were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death. And anyone not found written in the Book of Life was cast into the lake of fire. Revelation 14:10: he himself shall also drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out full strength into the cup of His indignation. He shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels and in the presence of the Lamb.
Who does he say the two beasts are, and will wickedness grow? (Matthew 13:30)

He says people who follow Satan “are the children of Satan” and people who follow God “are the children of God,” so “the beast can simply be people who carry out Satan’s actions and will and purposes in this life.” Reading “let both grow together until the harvest,” he says wickedness will grow and so will righteousness, “so don’t get rattled by it.”
Who does he say the two beasts are, and will wickedness grow? (Matthew 13:30)

Now, I told you who the two beasts were from the book of Revelation. We know that the Bible says that people who follow Satan are the children of Satan, and the people that follow God are the children of God. And so the beast can simply be people who carry out Satan’s actions and will and purposes in this life, and the people of God are those that do the opposite. And though we may make mistakes, we have a God that forgives and keeps us going, whereas the people of wickedness just keep, what, getting more wicked. Isn’t that what it says in the parable? “Let both grow together until the harvest.” So see, wickedness is going to grow, and so is righteousness. Isn’t that good news? God promised we would grow in righteousness, and he says the wicked are going to grow in wickedness, so don’t get rattled by it. We are destined to be overcomers if we pursue God.
Who does he say the two beasts are, and will wickedness grow? (Matthew 13:30)

1 John 3:10: In this the children of God and the children of the devil are manifest: Whoever does not practice righteousness is not of God, nor is he who does not love his brother. Matthew 13:30: Let both grow together until the harvest, and at the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, “First gather together the tares and bind them in bundles to burn them, but gather the wheat into my barn.” ’ ”
Why does he say we should publicly acknowledge Jesus? (Matthew 10:32–33)

He says “if you don’t publicly acknowledge him, he won’t acknowledge you.” He says God has chosen “these simple, humble acts,” such as worshiping, coming to church, raising hands and telling coworkers “I’m a Jesus boy,” to bring us to himself, and that God uses that “humiliating act” “to strengthen you and develop you and mature you.”
Why does he say we should publicly acknowledge Jesus? (Matthew 10:32–33)

Amen. How many will raise your hand, “Jesus, I’m on your side”? Yes. You got to pu... see, if you don’t publicly acknowledge him, he won’t acknowledge you. Ain’t that right? And these simple, humble acts is what God has chosen to bring us to himself and touch us with his supernatural power. It’s in that act of humiliation, humbling yourself to worship and pray, humbling yourself to come to church, humbling yourself to raise your hands and sing unto him, humbling yourself to say “I’m a Jesus boy” to your fellow workers. That’s what God uses, that humiliating act, to strengthen you and develop you and mature you. Hallelujah. So in the book of Revelation, who is the powerful one, the beast or the church? The church.
Why does he say we should publicly acknowledge Jesus? (Matthew 10:32–33)

Matthew 10:32-33: “Therefore whoever confesses Me before men, him I will also confess before My Father who is in heaven. But whoever denies Me before men, him I will also deny before My Father who is in heaven.
In Revelation, who is the powerful one, the beast or the church? (Romans 4:21)

He asks who the powerful one is in the book of Revelation and answers “the church.” He says God has “the power to perform what he promised,” and “we know he has the power to keep me … to mature me,” so “we patiently wait for him to do it.” He attributes the “power to perform” words to Paul’s letter to the Galatians; see the editor note.
In Revelation, who is the powerful one, the beast or the church? (Romans 4:21)

Hallelujah. Now, does God have power to back up what he said? Does he? Yes. That’s what Paul wrote to the Galatians. Faith in God is faith that says God has the power to perform what he promised. God, and that’s the patience of the saints. We know he has the power to do that. We know he has the power to keep me. We know he has the power to mature me. We know he has the power to overcome the principalities and powers of this life. We know that, and so we patiently wait for him to do it.
In Revelation, who is the powerful one, the beast or the church? (Romans 4:21)
Romans 4:21: and being fully convinced that what He had promised He was also able to perform.
What does he say Zion is?
He says “Zion is the church,” citing Hebrews 12, and later “we are Zion, we are the church.”
What does he say is written on the 144,000?
He says it is “the name of God,” and ties it to Revelation 3:12: “He who overcomes, I will make him a pillar in the temple of my God… I will write on him the name of my God.”
What does he say we should do if we have not yet overcome?
He asks, “Do we give up because we haven’t quite made it yet?” and answers, “No, man, we’re on the assembly line, just hang tight.”
What does he say the new song is?
He says “we are the ones that have the new song,” and points to the psalm’s “new song in my heart” and “psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs.”
Does he say the 144,000 must be physical virgins?
He says no: “God can’t contradict his word, so it can’t be this virgin thing,” since God said it is good for a man to leave his mother and father “and cleave to his wife.”
What does he say “chaste virgin” means?
He says Paul is “not talking about fleshly virginity,” but “the absence of sin, the absence of walking in darkness and disobeying God.”
What does he say the marriage of the Lamb is?
Reading Revelation 19:7, “the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife” “has made herself ready,” he says “that’s us. We’re ready, Lord. We’re mature.”
Who does he say the first fruits are?
He says “we are, the church,” and that the church is “an overcomer in this world in spite of the beast, in spite of Satan.”
How does he say we can be without fault when we still have faults?
He says “the blood keeps cleansing us,” keeping us “faultless before Christ as long as we admit our sin and we keep going to him,” and that “if you don’t change, you’re going to burn.”
Why does he say Satan makes war with the remnant?
He says “he’s not interested in people that just believe and don’t follow Christ,” and “Satan makes war with those that believe, even do something about it.”
What does he say about believers who do nothing out of duty?
He says “if you don’t do things just because it’s your duty, you’re probably just a weak wimp believer,” who “haven’t gotten out of the baby crib yet.”
What does he say we preach in light of the judgment?

He says “we preach to fear God, turn from your sins, praise and worship him, follow him, pray and seek him,” because “there’s a judgment coming where you’re going to be accountable for what you say and do.”
Who does he say can stand with us before God?
He says “nobody can stand there with you,” not a husband, wife or parents: “you are there on your own merit.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer uses Acts 18 to show how the church in Corinth was built, going from no Christians to thousands in under three years without a building, seminars or recorded miracles. He…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer uses Acts 18 to show how the church in Corinth was built, going from no Christians to thousands in under three years without a building, seminars or recorded miracles. He lists what Paul did: worked to support himself, reasoned from the Scriptures, used a team, preached a compelling message, faced rejection, and relied on God’s word and presence.
How does the Bible show a church being built? (Acts 18:1)

He says people buy books and seminars on church growth, but “there is an illustration in the Bible of a church being built, how it was built,” in Acts 18. He begins with Paul leaving Athens and coming to Corinth, and shows maps and a drawing of the city.
How does the Bible show a church being built? (Acts 18:1)

You’ve heard a lot about church growth. Seminars and, uh, people go to these things and they tell people how to build a mega church and so forth. They write books about it, but there is an illustration in the Bible of a church being built, how it was built. We find this in Acts 18:1, and it always amazes me how people will buy books and not go to the Book. So let’s take a look in the Bible how a church gets started and what happens after that. Okay, it says in Acts 18, verse 1: “Paul left Athens and came to Corinth.” You can see Corinth up here, uh, that little narrow space between Athens and the lower part of the, uh, peninsula. There, here’s another view of it, uh, showing also the same area, but the Roman provinces or Roman states, and the seven churches of Asia, of course, are over here. There is a satellite view of that little narrow area where Corinth is, and here is a drawing of the archaeologist that uncovered Corinth, of, uh, the layout downtown. Up at the top there are markets, then you got all these temples right here. You got the temple of, uh, Apollo, Hermes, [unclear], and, uh, all these Greek and Roman gods. You got the bath houses and so forth, shops all over the place, just a typical city.
How does the Bible show a church being built? (Acts 18:1)
Acts 18:1: After these things Paul departed from Athens and went to Corinth.
What was the city of Corinth like when Paul arrived?

He says history describes Corinth as filled with gamblers, legalized temple prostitution, slaves, amusements and idol temples, with “a lack of standards” but “a freedom of thought.” He asks whether it sounds like America today and says it did, with about 500,000 people.
What was the city of Corinth like when Paul arrived?

Uh, when you look up the civilization at that time of Corinth, history tells us it was filled with gamblers, legalized temple prostitutions including males, uh, business ventures, agriculture, manufacturing, trade, especially bronze. They had paved roads where they charged for cargo going between the narrow place from sea to sea, because they didn’t want to sail around it. They had athletes there, they had, uh, the games were there. They had homeless slaves, they had regular slaves, they had slave masters, uh, a lot of amusements. They had prostitutes, both male and female, that weren’t in the temple; they were abundant. They had a lack of standards, but they had a freedom of thought in that city. Everybody had their own opinion, their own thought, and everything was okay. Does it sound like America today? Yeah, sounds like a normal city in America today. Uh, there was about 500,000 people according to history in this city at this time when Paul comes to Corinth. And, uh, they had in their marketplaces, the Greeks would always, uh, sacrifice their meats to their idols and then they would sell the meat in the markets, and this created a problem for Christians, if you remember.
How could Paul build a church of 15,000 in under three years?

He asks how Paul went “from no Christianity to 15,000 people in the church in no more than three years,” without a building. He says the usual advice is miracles, seeker-friendly programs and entertainment, and he sets out to see what Paul actually did.
How could Paul build a church of 15,000 in under three years?

Um, now let’s say, according to today’s marketing principles, you try to reach 500,000 people, 1% respond, and so that would be what? 5,000 believers. Right. So how did Paul do this? How did he build a church here with these kind of people? Multicultural, people, different races, uh, different religions. The Jewish religion was there and other religions. How did he do this in no more than three years, going from no Christianity to 15,000 people in the church in no more than three years? Isn’t that a good question? Question, because I used to hear all the time when I was a young preacher and a young believer, that, “Boy, if you get the miracles, people will believe.” And so, uh, according to that theory, you know, he must have been doing a lot of miracles. These church seminars and all that, they say you got to have a seeker-friendly, you got to do things to entertain them and get their attention and so forth. Okay, let’s see what Paul did to create a mega church in less than three years, and didn’t even have a building. Sounds good.
Why did Paul work to support himself? (Acts 18:2-3)

He says the first thing, “against all of these church building seminars,” is that Paul worked to support himself and his co-workers, making tents with Aquila and Priscilla. He says persecution and lack of money, with no missionary support from Antioch or Jerusalem, did not stop him.
Why did Paul work to support himself? (Acts 18:2-3)

So this next slide says the starting of a church. All right, starting of a church, number one, which is against all of these church building seminars: Paul worked to support himself and his co-workers. Now that’s a switch. Are you there? Paul made tents with two Christian Jews forced from Rome, Aquila and Priscilla. So in the midst of tribulation, in the midst of persecution, all Jews were removed from Rome, including Christians. Okay, Jews are Jews by nationality, and Jews are also Jews by their religion. Today’s present Israel, most of the Jews there are secular, they’re just Jews by bloodline, and then you got the Jews that observe their religion. Did you know that? Yeah, there’s a difference. See, you can be an American or you can be a Christian American. We are a Christian nation, but that doesn’t mean you’re a Christian, but you’re still an American. All right, so here we got persecution, and you know, persecution didn’t stop Paul from building a church, and the lack of money didn’t stop Paul. He didn’t have any missionary support coming from Antioch, he didn’t have any missionary support coming from the church in Jerusalem. He was out there working on his own, providing for himself and his staff members.
Why did Paul work to support himself? (Acts 18:2-3)

Acts 18:2-3: And he found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla (because Claudius had commanded all the Jews to depart from Rome); and he came to them. So, because he was of the same trade, he stayed with them and worked; for by occupation they were tentmakers.
How did Paul reach people in the synagogue? (Acts 18:4)

He says Paul reasoned in the synagogue every Saturday, persuading Jews and Greeks, speaking the Word of God. He says there was “no dance company, no drama, no orchestra, no music, no nursery, no children’s church, no youth group,” just “convincing people from the Scriptures.”
How did Paul reach people in the synagogue? (Acts 18:4)

The second thing we see here is in verse 4 of Acts 18: “He reasoned in the synagogue every Saturday, persuading Jews and Greeks.” Greeks are non-Jews. You got to remember that in the temple in Jerusalem the Gentiles were not allowed in the inner circle. They were only allowed on the porch of the Gentiles, the area of the Gentiles. But in the synagogues, everybody was welcomed to come in and observe and see what was going on. And so Paul went to the synagogue, and sure enough there were non-Jews there checking out what the Jewish religion was, and he was persuading, convincing, pleading his case. In other words, he was speaking the Word of God. No dance company, no drama, no orchestra, no music, no nursery, no children’s church, no youth group, he was just simply convincing people from the Scriptures something that they needed to hear. Do you have that? Do you understand that so far? He’s using nothing that the churches in America use trying to build a congregation.
How did Paul reach people in the synagogue? (Acts 18:4)
Acts 18:4: And he reasoned in the synagogue every Sabbath, and persuaded both Jews and Greeks.
What moved Paul to persuade people? (2 Corinthians 5:10-11)

He reads 2 Corinthians 5:10 and says Paul understood “everybody’s going to be judged by the things they do,” and did not want people to experience “the terror, the fear of the Lord, the eternal lake of fire.” He says “people aren’t going to avoid hell if you don’t tell them and convince them about Jesus Christ and the Word.”
What moved Paul to persuade people? (2 Corinthians 5:10-11)

In 2 Corinthians 5:10 he says, “We must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that everyone may receive the things done in his body according to what he has done, whether it be good or bad. Knowing, therefore, the terror of the Lord, we” what? “Persuade men.” See, what moved him to do this, to persuade men? He understood everybody’s going to be judged by the things they do, whether they’re good or whether they’re bad, and so he didn’t want people to be experiencing the terror, the fear of the Lord, the eternal lake of fire, so he tried to persuade them how to escape it. So in other words, church, we got to open our mouth. People aren’t going to avoid hell if you don’t tell them and convince them about Jesus Christ and the Word. Could that be an amen?
What moved Paul to persuade people? (2 Corinthians 5:10-11)

2 Corinthians 5:10-11: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive the things done in the body, according to what he has done, whether good or bad. Knowing, therefore, the terror of the Lord, we persuade men; but we are well known to God, and I also trust are well known in your consciences.
Why did Paul use a team? (Acts 18:5, Ecclesiastes 4:9-12)

He says Jesus sent the disciples out two by two, and cites Ecclesiastes 4:9, “two are better than one,” and that “a threefold cord is not” easily broken. He counts five on Paul’s team, including Priscilla, and says that a woman involved in leadership answers those who say you can’t have a woman pastor.
Why did Paul use a team? (Acts 18:5, Ecclesiastes 4:9-12)

Thirdly, he used a team. In verse 5: “Silas and Timothy arrived from Macedonia.” They were up there in Philippi and Thessalonica and so forth, and they had been with Paul, and now they come down to join him again at Corinth. And team is important. Jesus sent out the disciples two by two, didn’t He? As a team. Why? Because in Ecclesiastes 4:9, “Two are better than one. If they fall, one will lift up his companion. Two can keep warm, but one alone can’t keep warm. Two can overcome opponents,” robbers, those that are opposing, those that are attacking, “but one is at their mercy, and a threefold cord is not” what? “Easily broken.” So three are better than two, four are better than three. Duh. He had five on the team here now: him, Paul, Silas, Priscilla, and Aquila. A woman. Wow. And if you read your church building today, they’ll tell you you can’t have a woman pastor. Well, here’s a woman involved in leadership. Are you there?
Why did Paul use a team? (Acts 18:5, Ecclesiastes 4:9-12)

Acts 18:5: When Silas and Timothy had come from Macedonia, Paul was compelled by the Spirit, and testified to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ. Ecclesiastes 4:9-12: Two are better than one, Because they have a good reward for their labor. For if they fall, one will lift up his companion. But woe to him who is alone when he falls, For he has no one to help him up. Again, if two lie down together, they will keep warm; But how can one be warm alone? Though one may be overpowered by another, two can withstand him. And a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
What message did Paul preach in Corinth? (Acts 18:5)

He says Paul’s message was not “positive thinking, possibility thinking, purpose-driven thinking, … prosperity thinking.” He says Paul was “compelled” to show the Jews that Jesus is the Christ, the Messiah, the Prophet and the King they were looking for, all in one Person.
What message did Paul preach in Corinth? (Acts 18:5)

Now, the fourth thing is the message. What he was preaching to persuade, to convince, to plead his case, the message. The message he had was not positive thinking, possibility thinking, purpose-driven thinking, uh, prosperity thinking. His message was that he was compelled. There was a force in him, a drive within him. Have you ever felt that drive in you, that push of God in you? See, that’s what he had. And what was it about? He was pressed, he was compelled, he was moved, forced in the Spirit to testify, confirm, and show to the Jews that Jesus was Christ, He was the Messiah. Now, all of you know this, old-timers here, that the Jews were looking for three things in the New Testament. What was the first one? The Messiah, the Christ. They were looking for Him to come. What was the second one? The Prophet. They were looking for the Prophet that was promised in Deuteronomy. What was the third one? The King. See, God promised a king out of David’s seed. And so they were looking for these three, and they thought there were going to be three different people, and it was all in one Person, Jesus Christ. And so he’s convincing these Jews, he’s telling them, “This is the Messiah, the Prophet, the King that you guys are looking for. Jesus is Him.” Hallelujah.
What message did Paul preach in Corinth? (Acts 18:5)
Acts 18:5: When Silas and Timothy had come from Macedonia, Paul was compelled by the Spirit, and testified to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.
Why does the love of Christ compel us to persuade others? (2 Corinthians 5:14-15)

He says “the love of Christ compels us,” and that love shows in a move to persuade people. He explains that if One died for all, then all died, “that those who live should live no longer for themselves, but for Him who died for them and rose again.”
Why does the love of Christ compel us to persuade others? (2 Corinthians 5:14-15)

And see, he was pressed in his spirit, moved by his spirit to preach this Word. In 2 Corinthians 5:14, “the love of Christ compels us.” “For God so loved the world, He gave His only begotten Son” is more than just a little football scripture, John 3:16, at the stadium. It explains for us, out of love God did this stuff. So does God love the world? Yes. If we know God, are we going to love the world? Yes. And that love is going to show forth in what? A compelling, a move to what? Persuade them. “Because we judge this: that if One died for all, then all” what? “Died.” Did you get that? See, He died for us. Therefore, as a simile, we all died with Him, “that those who live should live no longer for themselves, but for Him who died for them and rose again.” See, this is what he’s compelling to say to these people, that not only do we accept the salvation, we accept Christ, but it should move us to live for Him. This love, that we say we love God, there should be a force compelling to live for Him. Now. Amen.
Why does the love of Christ compel us to persuade others? (2 Corinthians 5:14-15)

2 Corinthians 5:14-15: For the love of Christ compels us, because we judge thus: that if One died for all, then all died; and He died for all, that those who live should live no longer for themselves, but for Him who died for them and rose again. John 3:16: For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life.
What should you do when people reject the message? (Acts 18:6)

He says if Paul had 15,000 believers, “485,000 people rejected him,” and that those who reject are actually “opposing themselves” because the gospel pricks their hearts, so you do not have to take it personally. He says Paul shook his raiment and went to the Gentiles, as Jesus told His disciples to do, and that family members who compromise lose their power to win someone to Christ.
What should you do when people reject the message? (Acts 18:6)

Now, number five: rejection of the message. Oh, we hate rejection. That’s why we like to keep our mouth shut, because we get rejected more. If Paul had 15,000 believers, that means that 485,000 people rejected him. Think about it. And this is what turns a lot of Christians off: they get rejected, so they just start shutting up. “When they opposed themselves.” I like the way they said it: these people that reject are rejecting God and what they can have, so they’re actually opposing themselves. You see, because the gospel is so powerful, it pricks the hearts. They have to fight that in themselves to say, “No, I don’t want it.” So they’re not rejecting you, they’re rejecting what? That pricking in their heart of the Scriptures, and said, “No, I don’t want it.” So they’re actually opposing themselves. Do you understand that? See, that can help you not to take it personally. “And they blaspheme.” Blaspheme means what? Speak evil of, harmful of. And so Paul shook his raiment, saying, “Your blood be upon your own heads. I am clean. From now on I will go to the Gentiles,” the non-Jews. Now, this is what Jesus told them to do in Luke 9:5 and Matthew 10:14: “Whosoever will not receive you nor your words, when you go out of that city, shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them.” And that’s what Paul did. He said, you know, don’t get down in the dumps over it. You know, your family can reject the message, your sons, your daughters can reject the message, believers can reject the message. These Jews were believers in God, but they were rejecting the message. Can that be happening in America, that there’s a lot of people that, you know, say they love Christ, but they reject living for Him? And so he did what Jesus told him to do. I know a lot of families, and when their family member doesn’t want to serve God, they just kind of negotiate and compromise and, uh, trying to keep a connection or something, and then they have no power to help win him to Christ, because they’re giving in to what that person wants to do. Are you there?
What should you do when people reject the message? (Acts 18:6)

Acts 18:6: But when they opposed him and blasphemed, he shook his garments and said to them, “Your blood be upon your own heads; I am clean. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.” Luke 9:5: And whoever will not receive you, when you go out of that city, shake off the very dust from your feet as a testimony against them.” Matthew 10:14: And whoever will not receive you nor hear your words, when you depart from that house or city, shake off the dust from your feet.
Were there miracles in Corinth, and what is the real miracle? (Acts 18:8)

He says “there’s no recorded miracles being done here in Corinth at all,” only “the preaching of the Word.” He says the real miracle is salvation, changed lives, and that healing the sick is part of God’s package but “no more important than the Word.”
Were there miracles in Corinth, and what is the real miracle? (Acts 18:8)

A rejection is going to come. Well, that’s not positive thinking. That’s, you can’t say that. Well, it’s true, it’s truth. They’re going to reject you. They may reject you 10 times, they may reject you for the rest of their life, they may never decide to believe and live for Christ. But “many believed and were baptized,” and none of this shows any recording of any miracles. All was done by what? Preaching Jesus Christ. There’s no recorded miracles being done here in Corinth at all. No demons cast out, no sick being healed, people weren’t coming and burning their magic books like it happened in other places, no aprons, prayer cloths used, nothing. Just the preaching of the Word, and that’s how powerful the Word is. See, God decides when He does things. God decided to do miracles in certain places and to use aprons and prayer cloths. He didn’t decide to do anything like that here, just the Word. Got it, church? The Word is that powerful. And what is the real miracle here, by the way? Salvation, changed lives. That’s the real miracle, being healed from your sin, being changed from a prostitute, a homosexual, a thief, a gambler, to one that doesn’t do it anymore is a miracle. Hallelujah. See, we got to think right. And if God does heal the sick, that’s fine, that’s part of His package, but we shouldn’t make it any higher than it’s supposed to be. You know, when you’re sick, yeah, you want to be healed, I mean, come on, geez. If you got a demon and, no, your child’s got a demon, yeah, you want it to be cast out, but it’s no more important than the Word. And the Word is the most important, because you can’t even cast out a demon but by the Word. “Now many believed”: Justus, one that worshiped God and lived right by the synagogue; Crispus was the chief ruler of the synagogue, and all of his family accepted the message. And “many,” say that word “many.” Now, “many” is used when Christ, uh, multiplied the loaves and the fishes. He said there were many, and then it says how many? 5,000 men plus women and children. That gets us back up to 15,000, and there’s always more women than men. I don’t know what it is with us knuckleheaded men, we’re a little slow. And so it was over 15,000 people. He’s got a mega church here and no building to meet in. Are you there? I mean, this is something.
Were there miracles in Corinth, and what is the real miracle? (Acts 18:8)
Acts 18:8: Then Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his household. And many of the Corinthians, hearing, believed and were baptized.
How did God get involved in the message? (Acts 18:9-11)

He says the Lord told Paul in a night vision, “be not afraid, speak, hold not your peace,” and that visions and dreams are always about the message, not about seeing things. He says Paul stayed a year and six months teaching “the Word of God,” not psychology or positive thinking.
How did God get involved in the message? (Acts 18:9-11)

Now the next one is God got involved in the message. Verse 9: “The Lord said to Paul by night vision, ‘Be not afraid, speak, hold not your peace.’” And I always told you, when angels come, when visions come, and dreams come, it’s always a message. Not for you to go and say, “I saw Jesus, I saw Jesus, oh, I had a vision.” No, the message is what’s going to change your life. It’s not seeing things, it’s the message. And He says, “You keep speaking.” So He was giving Paul a responsibility to open his mouth. And He told Paul, don’t be afraid. He said, “I am with you. No man shall hurt you. I have much people.” How many? Much people in this city. “Paul continued there a year and six months, teaching” what? The Word of God. Not psychology, not possibility thinking, not positive thinking, not purpose-driven thinking, not prosperity thinking, but he preached the Word of God.
How did God get involved in the message? (Acts 18:9-11)

Acts 18:9-11: Now the Lord spoke to Paul in the night by a vision, “Do not be afraid, but speak, and do not keep silent; for I am with you, and no one will attack you to hurt you; for I have many people in this city.” And he continued there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
Why should older believers stay driven, and what does Mark 16:20 say about “working with them”?

He says Paul was an old man and “he ain’t retiring,” and that younger believers need to see older ones “still compelled, still driven.” On Mark 16:20 he says the words “with them” are in italics and not in the original, and that “the Word worked” even through Judas, because the power is in speaking the Word.
Why should older believers stay driven, and what does Mark 16:20 say about “working with them”?

Now, most of us here are senior saints. Do you get this? Paul is an old man. He ain’t retiring. Yeah, teaching the Word. He’s moved, he’s compelled. And do our younger believers need to see us old ones stable, still compelled, still driven? Yes. It’s infectious. It will catch on with them. Mark 16:20: “They went out and preached everywhere, the Lord working with them.” “With them” is in italics. Why is it in italics? Because it’s not in the original Scripture. It’s put there by the writers to help you understand. When you see it’s in italics, it means it’s not in the original Scripture, they put it there to help you understand. Here they messed up the understanding. All right, have I got your attention? Watch this: “working with” the Word. I put that in. When you see parentheses in my things, it’s usually me putting in a description. Okay, I’m telling you this is what it should be, but let’s just read it: “They went out and preached everywhere, the Lord working with them and confirming the word through the accompanying signs,” or “signs following.” Now I’m going to take out the italics. Now let’s read it: “They went out and preached everywhere, the Lord working with and confirming the word.” Is what it should say. But He needs a vessel. Yeah, Judas was a vessel. He was a thief, he was a betrayer, but the Word worked through Judas. The Word worked. The power is in speaking what? The Word. That’s why you don’t have to wait to be perfect, to grow up to maturity, because the Word is mature, the Word is perfect, and the Word will work regardless of your level in God.
Why should older believers stay driven, and what does Mark 16:20 say about “working with them”?
Mark 16:20: And they went out and preached everywhere, the Lord working with them and confirming the word through the accompanying signs. Amen.
What were the signs in Corinth?

He says the signs were souls saved and lives transformed: “homosexuals aren’t homosexuals anymore, adulterers aren’t adulterers anymore,” and the same for prostitutes, gamblers and drunkards. He says “that’s the power of the Word” and calls this “a great illustration in the Bible how a church is to be built.”
What were the signs in Corinth?

Hallelujah. Now, what are the signs here in Corinth? Souls are saved, lives are transformed from all of these walks of life: homosexuals aren’t homosexuals anymore, adulterers aren’t adulterers anymore, prostitutes aren’t prostitutes anymore, gamblers aren’t gamblers anymore, drunkards aren’t drunkards anymore. See, that’s the power of the Word. And we have a great illustration in the Bible how a church is to be built. There is no Christian in this city when Paul came. He started on virgin territory. We don’t have that here. We got so many religions out there to deal with, it’s not even funny. But Paul had to deal with Jews that didn’t want to accept the message, also didn’t. Now these Jews take Paul to court to silence the message. He go before the judgment seat. These guys are preaching contrary to the law. They go to the Roman judge. The Roman judge threw it out of court: “I’m not going to hear you guys, this is your own problems.” So the Jews beat Sosthenes, a ruler of the synagogue, in the courtroom, and the court did nothing.
What should Christians do when opposition and rejection come? (Acts 18:12-17)

He says the Jews took Paul to court to silence the message, and the Roman judge threw it out. He says life is normal in America like in Corinth, God has many people to reach, and “when people reject it, move on and find somebody that’s worth putting time into.”
What should Christians do when opposition and rejection come? (Acts 18:12-17)

Are Christians getting pushed around in America today? Yeah, and America is doing what? Nothing. You say anything about the Muslims, you’re in trouble. You say anything about blacks or Mexicans or some minority, right, you’re in trouble. But you say anything about Christianity, no problem. What I’m trying to tell you is life is normal in America, just like it was at Athens, and yet God had many people, or I’m sorry, Corinth, God had many people in Corinth that He wanted to reach and change their lives. And we got to get over, “Oh, this is a rough harvest field. Oh, things are so bad. Oh, the homosexuals are taking over, and the atheists are taking over.” We got to let God arise, and He will draw people to Himself, and those that reject, we got to learn that when people reject it, move on and find somebody that’s worth putting time into. I had to learn that as a young Christian, to quit fooling around with these sap suckers and move on to people that really wanted to touch God and move on in God. And that’s what Paul did.
What should Christians do when opposition and rejection come? (Acts 18:12-17)

Acts 18:12-17: When Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews with one accord rose up against Paul and brought him to the judgment seat, saying, “This fellow persuades men to worship God contrary to the law.” And when Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, “If it were a matter of wrongdoing or wicked crimes, O Jews, there would be reason why I should bear with you. But if it is a question of words and names and your own law, look to it yourselves; for I do not want to be a judge of such matters.” And he drove them from the judgment seat. Then all the Greeks took Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment seat. But Gallio took no notice of these things.
How big does he say the church in Corinth became?

He says it went “from no Christianity to 15,000 people in the church in no more than three years.” He bases this on 500,000 people in the city and the “many” who believed, comparing it to the 5,000 men plus women and children Jesus fed.
What does he say church-building seminars teach?
He says they say you have to be “seeker-friendly” and “do things to entertain them and get their attention,” and that earlier he heard that if you get the miracles, people will believe.
Did Paul have missionary support in Corinth?
No. He says Paul “didn’t have any missionary support coming from Antioch” or from the church in Jerusalem, and was “out there working on his own, providing for himself and his staff members.”
What did Paul not use to build the church?

He says there was no dance company, drama, orchestra, music, nursery, children’s church or youth group. He says Paul was “just simply convincing people from the Scriptures something that they needed to hear.”
What does he say “the terror of the Lord” moved Paul to do?
He says it moved Paul to persuade people, because everyone will be judged and Paul did not want anyone experiencing “the eternal lake of fire.”
What three things does he say the Jews were looking for?
He says they looked for the Messiah, the Prophet promised in Deuteronomy, and the King out of David’s seed, and “it was all in one person, Jesus Christ.”
Why does he say people reject the message?
He says the gospel “pricks the hearts,” and people have to fight that in themselves to say “no, I don’t want it,” so “they’re not rejecting you, they’re rejecting” that pricking of the Scriptures.
What does he say about families that compromise?

He says when a family member doesn’t want to serve God, families “negotiate and compromise,” and then “they have no power to help win him to Christ, because they’re giving in to what that person wants to do.”
Does he say people may reject the message for life?
Yes. He says “they may reject you 10 times, they may reject you for the rest of their life, they may never decide to believe and live for Christ,” but many believed and were baptized.
Does he say healing and casting out demons are unimportant?
No. He says “if God does heal the sick, that’s fine, that’s part of His package,” and you want a demon cast out, “but it’s no more important than the Word.”
What does he say about visions and dreams?
He says “when angels come, when visions come, and dreams come, it’s always a message,” and “the message is what’s going to change your life. It’s not seeing things.”
Does he say the Word works only through perfect people?
No. He says “you don’t have to wait to be perfect, to grow up to maturity, because the Word is mature, the Word is perfect, and the Word will work regardless of your level in God.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer walks through the opening of 1 Corinthians to show what a young church possessed: holiness, calling on and summoning Jesus, grace as divine enablement, understanding of…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer walks through the opening of 1 Corinthians to show what a young church possessed: holiness, calling on and summoning Jesus, grace as divine enablement, understanding of Scripture, stability, the gifts of the Spirit, looking for His coming, and fellowship with Christ. He contrasts this with the American church and urges believers to start the year seeing the Word of God as bigger than the opposition.
Will following Jesus bring persecution, even from people close to you?

He says Jesus warned, “Beware of men, for they will deliver you up to the councils,” and that they will “beat you in their synagogues” and bring you before governors and kings “for My sake.” He adds that brother will betray brother, and father the son.
Will following Jesus bring persecution, even from people close to you?

Paul stayed a good while before leaving. So he was there a year and a half, and then a good while. We don’t know what the good while is, but the way I said it, it couldn’t be no more than three years. It could have been a lot less; could have been two and a half years. “Beware of men, for they will deliver you up to the councils,” Jesus said in Matthew 10:17. “They’ll beat you in their synagogues. They’ll bring you before governors and kings for My sake,” because you’re living for Me, because you’re proclaiming Me, “for a testimony against them,” and a testimony against nonbelievers. Unbelievers. He says in Matthew 13:12, “Brother shall betray brother to death, father the son, and children—their parents.”
Will following Jesus bring persecution, even from people close to you?

Matthew 10:17: But beware of men, for they will deliver you up to councils and scourge you in their synagogues. Matthew 10:21: “Now brother will deliver up brother to death, and a father his child; and children will rise up against parents and cause them to be put to death. Acts 18:18: So Paul still remained a good while. Then he took leave of the brethren and sailed for Syria, and Priscilla and Aquila were with him. He had his hair cut off at Cenchrea, for he had taken a vow.
Can you live for Christ on behalf of your children or spouse?

He says parents cannot live for Christ for their children: “God doesn’t have any stepchildren,” and each adult child has to decide to live for Him. He says a spouse may go another way too, and believers must “stick with the Bible” and not water everything down.
Can you live for Christ on behalf of your children or spouse?

Parents, you know, you can’t get down in the dumps because your kid decides to go sin after you raised him in a Christian school and in a Christian home and all the rest. They become an adult, they got to choose for themselves what road they’re going to take. Your job is to get them there; their job is to take the baton and live for Him. God doesn’t have any stepchildren. You can’t live for Christ for your children; they got to decide to live for Him themselves. Your spouse may decide to go another way, and it’s happening in America, isn’t it? They want to twist who God is and who Jesus is, and they want to water everything down, and they want you to accept them with their own beliefs, and you can’t do it, because you can’t change the Bible. You got to stick with the Bible. Can I hear an amen?
How do you stay consistent when family pressure and Satan’s attacks come?

He says a believer cannot “go along” with a spouse just to keep harmony at home, because “we’re supposed to be a light to the world, not a shadow.” He says Satan hits in several areas, naming health, position and money, and that you have to “rise above these things” and stay consistent.
How do you stay consistent when family pressure and Satan’s attacks come?

Seniors, spouses get a hair in their nose and want to do things, you know, you can’t go, “Well, I got to keep harmony in my home, so I got to go along.” [unclear] on that. We’re supposed to be a light to the world, not a shadow. I’ve been taken to court four times, so I know it’s true. I know about persecution. I know Satan has four areas he’ll hit you in. He happened to hit me and my family. Sometimes it’s health, sometimes it’s, uh, position, sometimes it’s, uh, money. You know, it just seems like you can’t keep a steady job.
What should a young church or a young Christian possess?

He says Paul was training a new church in Corinth and asks, “will He do it for all churches? Absolutely.” He says Corinth was not a church of “worshiping a hero,” and he lists ten things from 1 Corinthians 1 that a young Christian should be possessing.
What should a young church or a young Christian possess?

You know, you got to rise above these things that Satan tries to distract you with and stay consistent. Now here is Paul training a new church. We jump over to 1 Corinthians. He writes a letter to them later. You see, a little bit later he writes back to this church and gives them instruction. Wow. And I want you to see right quick here the powerful statements he makes about this new church. And, folks, God is not a what? Respecter of persons. If He will do this for the Corinthian church, will He do it for all churches? Absolutely. Watch how he writes to these people. I mean, something happened in Corinth. It wasn’t like your mega churches today, where people are worshiping a hero or something. These people had something. Watch this, this is powerful. You ready? Ten things. Ten things that you should be possessing even as a young Christian.
What does it mean to be sanctified, holy and “called to be saints”?

He says Paul did not say the Corinthians were going to be holy, but that “they are,” set apart for holiness and right living after turning from their sins. “Called to be saints” means morally blameless, which they were not yet, but they were “shooting for that mark.”
What does it mean to be sanctified, holy and “called to be saints”?

Ready? “Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother.” Remember who got beat in front of the court? Sosthenes. Here he’s helping write this, uh, letter, this book. Hallelujah. See, his beating, his persecution, didn’t change him at all. He’s still with Paul, he’s still in the church, he’s still communicating, serving God. And number one: “to the church of God at Corinth, to them that are” what? Sanctified. They’re holy. He said, didn’t say they’re going to be holy; they are. What? Holy. Set apart for holiness, right living. They turn from their sins, their prostitution, their, their homosexuality, their lying, and their stealing, and all these things they had experienced. Holiness. Isn’t that good? Look at the next one: “called to be saints.” You see, saints are blameless people. People that are blameless morally. Blameless. Now they’re called to be morally blameless, so obviously they’re not quite morally blameless yet. Ain’t that right? But they are what? Shooting for that mark. Isn’t that powerful? This church is not even three years old, and they’re experiencing things in God. “And in every place,” with all that, “in every place call upon the name of Jesus Christ.” Okay, so they’re calling on the name of Jesus Christ. Now that word “calling” means this: it’s not just inviting, or invoking, or hollering. It is summoning.
What does it mean to be sanctified, holy and “called to be saints”?

1 Corinthians 1:1: Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother, 1 Corinthians 1:2: To the church of God which is at Corinth, to those who are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be saints, with all who in every place call on the name of Jesus Christ our Lord, both theirs and ours:
What does it mean to “call on the name of Jesus Christ” in church?

He says “calling on the name of Jesus Christ” means summoning, like a court summons: “Can you send a substitute? No.” These believers summoned His presence, expecting and demanding that Jesus be there, while many people “go to church and never touch Jesus.”
What does it mean to “call on the name of Jesus Christ” in church?

See, it’s acquiring. When you get a court summons, do you go? Yes. Can you send a substitute? No. Can you say, “I’m too busy, excuse me”? No, you ought to appear. Then see, what is he saying? These people summon Jesus Christ. They summon His presence. He appears in their midst, not by the physical eye, but His presence touching our presence, our spirit. Amen. Do you see that? Now see, these are things this young church were possessing. When they come together, they were expecting, they were demanding, that Jesus Christ be there, like He said, “If two or three are gathered together, I will be” where? “In the midst.” They summoned Him. And so many people go to church and never touch Jesus, but yet this Corinthian church were touching Him. They were summoning Him. Isn’t that beautiful? I think that’s tremendous. Folks, I mean, our mega churches today don’t have anything like this. We’ve gotten off of these basic things. Now remember, these are ex-prostitutes, homosexuals, idolaters, gamblers, Jews, non-Jews, slaves, slave masters, sailors, merchants, soldiers, drunkards, contractors, athletes and entertainers. They were all coming to Christ: different races, different nationalities, different cultures.
What does it mean to “call on the name of Jesus Christ” in church?
Matthew 18:20: For where two or three are gathered together in My name, I am there in the midst of them.”
What is grace? Is it just God’s favor?

He says grace is more than “just favor”: it shows in “the divine influence upon your life, divine enablement to live a lifestyle different than you lived before.” He says the American church has done members “a disservice” by teaching that God favors you no matter what you do.
What is grace? Is it just God’s favor?

Verse three of 1 Corinthians 1: “Grace be to you and peace from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ. I thank my God always on your behalf for the grace of God given you by Jesus Christ.” And this is where the American church has done the church members a disservice. They keep telling them grace is just favor, God just favors you no matter what you do, He favors you. But it’s much more than that. He favors you, and it shows in a result of the divine influence upon your life, divine enablement to live a lifestyle different than you lived before. That’s the full measure of grace. That’s the whole purpose of grace: that He favors you, He loves you, He’s going to work with you so that people will see that there’s a divine influence, a divine enablement, that changed your life from this way to His way.
What is grace? Is it just God’s favor?
1 Corinthians 1:3-4: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. I thank my God always concerning you for the grace of God which was given to you by Christ Jesus,
Why should Christians learn the Scriptures well enough to speak them?

He says being enriched “in all utterance and all knowledge” means we have to “get into the Book” and into Bible studies that teach it, because “when you understand something, you can speak it.” He calls knowing the Scriptures the true wealth of the church.
Why should Christians learn the Scriptures well enough to speak them?

Amen. And these guys experienced this. And it says in the next verse, verse 5, that “in everything you are enriched by Him, in all utterance and all knowledge.” So in everything: the holiness, the summoning Christ, the grace, and now speaking and understanding. Did Jesus open the disciples’ understanding to understand the Scriptures? Can we understand the Scriptures? Yes. But to understand them, we got to get into the Book, and we got to get into Bible studies that are teaching that Book, and then we can speak it. See, when you understand something, you can speak it. See, the people that run the horse program, I don’t know a lot of things about horses, but they do, and they can speak it.
Why should Christians learn the Scriptures well enough to speak them?
1 Corinthians 1:5: that you were enriched in everything by Him in all utterance and all knowledge,
What does it mean to be “confirmed” and stable in Christ?

He says “confirm” means “stable, unchanging,” and that the young Corinthian Christians might make a mistake but “got back up and kept moving forward.” He says the American church has a lot of “instability,” with people who can’t overcome alcohol, drugs or anger because they are not experiencing these things.
What does it mean to be “confirmed” and stable in Christ?

Amen. That’s what God says He wants us to know: the Scriptures, that way we can what? Speak it. And that makes us wealthy. That’s the true wealth of the church. “Even as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you.” That word “confirm” is to be stable, unchanging. These young Christians were stable. They weren’t going in and out, up and down. They were unchanging. They might make a mistake here and there, but they got back up and kept moving forward. How many would like to be stable in God? Now, in the American church, we got a lot of instability. We got big buildings, and we got great authors, and book authors, and preachers, and everything else, and God’s people can’t handle the slightest tribulation or problems in their life. They can’t overcome alcohol, they can’t overcome drugs, they can’t overcome anger, they ain’t going to overcome nothing. Why? Because they’re not experiencing these things.
What does it mean to be “confirmed” and stable in Christ?
1 Corinthians 1:6: even as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you,
Should a church have all the spiritual gifts at work?

He says the Corinthians “come behind in no gift”: no spiritual ability was lacking when the church came together, and “the nine gifts were expressed.” He says an American church today usually has “one gift expressed,” depending on the circle, and sometimes “nothing.”
Should a church have all the spiritual gifts at work?

They’re given dramas and dance companies and preachers that preach with, you know, [unclear] excellence, and we’re not getting the Word in us. Hallelujah. Now, this is a good message for us to start this year with. Amen. Senior saints, amen. A young church, and they possess these things. It’s just extraordinary. It’s just amazing. Verse seven, “you become—you come behind in no gift.” Spiritual abilities, they didn’t lack any of them. Now, one person didn’t have them all, but when the church came together, they were there. See, the nine gifts were expressed. Do we have them at an American church today? No. We usually got one gift expressed. If you’re in certain circles, it’s prophecy; if you’re in other circles, it’s tongues; if you’re in other circles, it’s, uh, uh, healing; if you’re in other circles, it’s nothing. Ah, they just throw out the gifts.
Should a church have all the spiritual gifts at work?
1 Corinthians 1:7: so that you come short in no gift, eagerly waiting for the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ,
What does it mean to look for the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ?

He says looking for the coming of the Lord means being faithful and wise, thinking, living and talking with superiority, because you may meet Him when you die and don’t have to “wait for the rapture.” He cites Matthew 24:46 and says Jesus told them to “watch, be ready.”
What does it mean to look for the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ?

“And the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.” You say, “Oh, big deal, the coming of the Lord.” Well, you got to understand what he means by the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ. Well, I know what it means: He’s coming again. That’s right, but you got to understand your part in it. See, how are you supposed to think about the coming of the Lord? These guys were looking for the coming, and Jesus wasn’t coming for 2,000 years down the road or more, but they’re what? Looking. They’re what? Looking. And don’t you believe these people to tell you. See, they didn’t even understand. They thought He was coming in, you know, right then and during their lifetime. That does not mean that at all. Let me show you what it means. Are you ready for this? Matthew 24:46: “Blessed is he that is faithful and a wise servant, whom his master, when he comes, will find so doing.” Doing what? Being wise and faithful, ain’t that right? So they’re looking for the coming of Christ. What does that mean? They’re being faithful, and they’re talking with superiority, thinking with superiority, and living a superior life. Remember what wisdom was in Proverbs: superior thinking, superior living, and superior talking. Why? Because He can come and take you. You can die, you know. You don’t have to wait for the rapture. You’re going to meet Him when your heart starts beating. So you should be what? Faithful, and you should be a wise servant. Now look, but if that servant begins to beat his fellow servants, mistreat them, and to eat and drink with the drunkards, the master of that servant will come on a day when he’s not looking for him, and it goes on to say bad things. So see, when we’re saying we’re looking for Christ’s return, we’re saying what? I am faithful, I am living a wise life, I am speaking wisely, I am thinking wisely, because Christ may show up, or I may die and I will appear before Him. So it’s a lifestyle. And this is what Jesus told them to do: watch, be ready.
What does it mean to look for the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ?
Matthew 24:46: Blessed is that servant whom his master, when he comes, will find so doing.
What does it mean to be “blameless” in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ?

He says, “It doesn’t matter if He comes in your lifetime or not.” God will make them stable and unchanging to the end and keep them blameless, which he defines as “unaccusable” in the day of the Lord Jesus Christ, because Christ will finish the good work He began.
What does it mean to be “blameless” in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ?

It doesn’t matter if He comes in your lifetime or not. It is the attitude, it is the motive of your heart. Are you with Me? “Who shall also confirm you.” What’s “confirm” mean? Stable, unchanging. See, He’s going to confirm you, make you stable, unchanging, and to the end. What’s the end? That day when He comes the second time and judges the world, “that you may be blameless.” And what’s blameless? Unaccusable. “In the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.” How many of you want to be unaccusable in the day of the Lord Jesus Christ? How many? You know, this Corinthian church is on its way. It’s sanctified, it’s calling on the Lord, summoning Him, it’s looking for the return of Christ, they have the gifts of the Spirit working in the church. I mean, isn’t this beautiful? They are stable, they’re unchanging, they might make some mistakes, they are saints that are looking forward to being blameless, knowing that Christ will finish the good work that He began in us, and on that day they will be blameless.
What does it mean to be “blameless” in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ?
1 Corinthians 1:8: who will also confirm you to the end, that you may be blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
What is the “fellowship” of God’s Son, and what is eternal life?

He says the last thing the Corinthians had was “the fellowship of His Son”: not a ministry or church group but “an intimate relationship with Christ.” He cites John 17:3 and defines eternal life as “knowing God and Jesus Christ,” not “head knowledge.”
What is the “fellowship” of God’s Son, and what is eternal life?

Hallelujah. Ain’t that powerful? Now, senior saints, he did this with five people in his team. We got more than five here this morning. We got a head start. Verse 9: “God is faithful, by whom we were called unto the” what? “Fellowship.” Here’s the last one. See, “the fellowship of His Son.” Not some ministry, not some church group. These guys are in partnership with Jesus Christ. Not Paul, not Aquila, not Priscilla, not Silas, not Timothy. They are in partnership with Christ. They are in an intimate relationship with Christ. This is the biggest thing these guys had: they actually know Him. How, you know, that makes a difference. Not head knowledge. This is a real possession of Christ, a fellowship, a partnership with Him. It says in John 17:3, “This is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent.” Definition of eternal life is what? Knowing God and Jesus Christ, an intimate relationship. The Bible says that Joseph knew not Mary until after Jesus was born; in other words, he didn’t have an intimate relationship with Mary. And see, we have this intimacy with God. We know God, we fellowship with Him, we partner with Him. We’re not partnered with just Silas and Timothy and Paul. We’re partnered with Jesus Himself, and that makes the difference.
What is the “fellowship” of God’s Son, and what is eternal life?

1 Corinthians 1:9: God is faithful, by whom you were called into the fellowship of His Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. John 17:3: And this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent. Matthew 1:25: and did not know her till she had brought forth her firstborn Son. And he called His name JESUS.
How do we know that we know Jesus?

He cites 1 John 2:3, “We know that we know Him if we keep His commandments,” and says it is imperative that people meet and know Jesus in their salvation. “It’s not the baptismal certificate, it’s not what church you belong to, it’s who you know.”
How do we know that we know Jesus?

1 John 2:3: “We know that we know Him if we keep His commandments.” See, “He that says, ‘I know Him,’ and keeps them not is a liar, and the truth is not in him.” So is it imperative, very important, that people in their salvation meet and know Jesus Christ? Yes. It’s not the baptismal certificate, it’s not what church you belong to, it’s who you know. And this is what changed the Corinthians in this wild, wild city that any normal modern ministry would look at and go, “This city is impossible.” And yet the Word of God changed these people’s lives, and they knew Him. They encountered Christ.
How do we know that we know Jesus?
1 John 2:3-4: Now by this we know that we know Him, if we keep His commandments. He who says, “I know Him,” and does not keep His commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.
How should Christians face a new year, and will the nations worship?

He says to “stop looking at all the opposition and the problems” and see that the Word of God is bigger than this world. He closes with the overcomers’ song in Revelation 15, where “all nations shall come,” and says “shall” means it is impossible for it not to happen.
How should Christians face a new year, and will the nations worship?

Hallelujah. Now, we got a year ahead of us, and we got to start looking and seeing like Paul looked and saw. Amen. We got to stop looking at all the opposition and the problems and see that the Word of God is bigger than this world. It’s bigger than anybody’s lack of faith, or whatever. Now, I chose Revelation 15:3 because the verse before this says, “These that overcame the beast,” they that overcame his mark, the number of his name, and his image. And in Revelation 12, the same people overcame Satan by the blood of the Lamb and the word of their testimony, and loved not their life to death. These people who what? Overcame. Then these people sang the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying, “great and marvelous”—why, there’s, they’re overcomers, they’re seeing the good stuff, “great and marvelous are Thy works, Lord God Almighty, just and true are Your ways, You King of saints. Who shall not fear You, O Lord, and honor Your name? For You only are holy, and all nations shall come.” That word “shall” means it is impossible for it not to happen. “They will come and worship before You,” whether they believe in You or not, they’re going to come. But we want to be like Paul, to get the nations to come and worship Him because they accept Him, amen, and not reject Him.
How should Christians face a new year, and will the nations worship?

Revelation 15:2-4: And I saw something like a sea of glass mingled with fire, and those who have the victory over the beast, over his image and over his mark and over the number of his name, standing on the sea of glass, having harps of God. They sing the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying: “Great and marvelous are Your works, Lord God Almighty! Just and true are Your ways, O King of the saints! Who shall not fear You, O Lord, and glorify Your name? For You alone are holy. For all nations shall come and worship before You, For Your judgments have been manifested.” Revelation 12:11: And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, and they did not love their lives to the death.
How long did Paul stay at Corinth?

He says Paul stayed “a year and a half, and then a good while.” He says nobody knows what the good while is, but the way he said it, it couldn’t be no more than three years and could have been two and a half.
What should parents do when a grown child chooses sin after a Christian upbringing?

He says parents can’t “get down in the dumps”: “Your job is to get them there; their job is to take the baton and live for Him.” He says you can’t live for Christ for your children; they have to decide to live for Him themselves.
Will God do for churches today what He did for the church at Corinth?
He asks, “If He will do this for the Corinthian church, will He do it for all churches? Absolutely.” He says something happened in Corinth that is not like the mega churches of today.
What does he say about the man who was beaten in front of the court and is named in 1 Corinthians 1:1?
He says his beating and persecution “didn’t change him at all”: he is still with Paul, in the church, communicating and serving God, and is helping write the letter.
Were the Corinthians already holy, or just going to be?

He says the verse does not say they are going to be holy; “they are.” He explains holy as set apart for holiness and right living, since they had turned from their sins and the things they had experienced.
Why does he compare calling on Jesus to a court summons?

He says when you get a court summons you go, you can’t send a substitute and you can’t say you’re too busy. In the same way, the Corinthians summoned His presence and He appeared in their midst, “not by the physical eye,” but touching “our spirit.”
What kinds of people made up the Corinthian church?
