He lists ex-prostitutes, homosexuals, idolaters, gamblers, Jews, non-Jews, slaves, slave masters, sailors, merchants, soldiers, drunkards, contractors, athletes and entertainers. He says they were “all coming to Christ: different races, different nationalities, different cultures.”
What does he say is the full measure of grace?
He says it is not only that God favors and loves you but that He is going to work with you so that people will see “a divine influence, a divine enablement, that changed your life.”
Why does he say the American church has a lot of instability?

He says there are big buildings, authors and preachers, but God’s people “can’t handle the slightest tribulation or problems in their life.” They can’t overcome alcohol, drugs or anger, he says, “because they’re not experiencing these things.”
Which spiritual gifts does he say American churches usually express?

He says an American church usually has “one gift expressed”: in certain circles prophecy, in others tongues, in others healing, and in other circles “nothing.” He says the Corinthians lacked none of the gifts when the church came together.
Do you have to wait for the rapture to meet Jesus?
He says “you don’t have to wait for the rapture,” because you can die and appear before Him. So he says you should be faithful and a wise servant now.
What does he say “watch, be ready” means?

He says it is a lifestyle: “I am faithful, I am living a wise life, I am speaking wisely, I am thinking wisely,” because Christ may show up or you may die and appear before Him. He says it is “the attitude” and “the motive of your heart.”
Does a baptismal certificate or church membership make you right with God?
He says, “It’s not the baptismal certificate, it’s not what church you belong to, it’s who you know.” He says it is imperative that people in their salvation meet and know Jesus Christ.
What does he say about the overcomers’ song in Revelation 15?

He says the people who overcame sang the song of Moses and the song of the Lamb: “great and marvelous are Thy works.” He says “all nations shall come” means it is impossible for it not to happen, and that they will come and worship whether they believe or not.

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Matthew 5:14-16 that Christians are the light of the world and are responsible both to do good works that bring honor to the Father and to speak the word of…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Matthew 5:14-16 that Christians are the light of the world and are responsible both to do good works that bring honor to the Father and to speak the word of salvation. He explains that grace and works do not conflict, which “works of the law” we are not saved by, and why quiet Christianity is not enough, ending with Paul’s converting gospel before Felix in Acts 24:25.
What does it mean that Christians are the light of the world? (Matthew 5:14-16)
He reads Matthew 5:14-16 and asks, “why are Christians hiding out?” He says our responsibility is to let our light shine before men, which means that they “may see your good works.”
What does it mean that Christians are the light of the world? (Matthew 5:14-16)

Uh, we’re going to be talking about Christians’ responsibility. Matthew 5:14-16: “You are the light of the world,” talking to us, and as they say down south, “A city that is set on the hill cannot be hid.” Why are Christians hiding out? They hide out in their homes, they hide out in the church. They’re worthless. “Nor do they light a lamp and put it under a bushel. A city set on a hill cannot be hid. They put the lamp on a lampstand so it gives light to all that are in the house.” He’s just using a natural illustration; that doesn’t make the book an allegorical book. He’s just given us natural illustrations to understand spiritual things. “Let your light shine before men.” So what is our responsibility? To let our light shine. That is our responsibility. You accept Christ, you accept salvation, you accept eternal life, He puts a responsibility on you to let your light shine before who?
What does it mean that Christians are the light of the world? (Matthew 5:14-16)

Matthew 5:14-16: “You are the light of the world. A city that is set on a hill cannot be hidden. Nor do they light a lamp and put it under a basket, but on a lampstand, and it gives light to all who are in the house. Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven.
Should Christians keep their faith private, or let others see it?

He says people “should see our religion,” and that when men see our good works they “will give honor to your Father in heaven.” He asks, “do you want the world giving honor to God, or are you looking for honor?”
Should Christians keep their faith private, or let others see it?

Men, you see. And He tells us what that shining of the light is: “that they may see your good works.” That’s the shining light. These politicians that say, “I don’t wear my religion on my arm, on my sleeve”: that’s ridiculous. People should see our religion. Right here it says it. Hallelujah. And if you do that, He said those men that you do good works before will give honor to your Father in heaven. Now, do you want the world giving honor to God, or are you looking for honor? So.
Do grace, faith and good works conflict? (Ephesians 2:8-10)

He says “grace and faith and works do not conflict with each other.” We are saved by grace through faith with nothing we can do to earn it, yet we are “created to do” good works, and he says people who “eliminate works” are reading only part of the passage.
Do grace, faith and good works conflict? (Ephesians 2:8-10)

Who’s the light of the world? Those of us who are following Jesus. What does the light of the world do? Good works. And who is to see our good works? Men. Now, grace and faith and works do not conflict with each other. We need to get this clear. There is so much emphasis on grace and faith and no works. I want you to get this in your head, your cranial vacuum; I want to fill it up with some truth right now. All right. “It is by grace that you have been saved through faith, and this is not of yourselves.” Nothing you could do about it. “It is the gift of God.” God freely did it. “Not by works, so that no man can boast.” I can’t win enough souls to get into heaven. I can’t pray enough hours to get into heaven. I can’t take communion enough to get into heaven, to be saved from my sin. There’s absolutely nothing, for my point, that I can do besides believe the gospel, accept His favor, His death on the cross for my sins. Is that an amen? It’s free. Now, “not of works.” Now, if they would just continue reading, the subject hasn’t stopped yet. He’s still talking about salvation. “We are God’s workmanship.” He’s fashioning us. See, He’s fashioning us into what? A people that are created, they that in Christ Jesus are what? A new creation. Okay, this grace and faith that brought salvation also is the thing that got us born again, made a new creature. Do you see that? We are a new creature, old things passed away, all things made new. We are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus to do what? But we just read, “not by works,” but we were created to do what? Good works. We have a responsibility to do good works. “Let your light so shine before men that they may see your” what? Good works. And it’s right here in the Scripture, that they eliminate works.
Do grace, faith and good works conflict? (Ephesians 2:8-10)

Ephesians 2:8-10: For by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, lest anyone should boast. For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand that we should walk in them.
Is helping the poor and the sick the main good work of the church?

He says we are saved by grace, not works, but because we are saved “He created us to be people that have our light shining by doing good works.” He says yes, we are supposed to help the poor, but that Jesus’ priority “was to save souls” and the priority of the church is to get the gospel out and “not leave the other undone.”
Is helping the poor and the sick the main good work of the church?

And people go to church and they hear the same dumbbell things every Sunday, and they just take, they don’t get into the Word for themselves and ask Jesus to open the Word up to them, and they don’t go at the outside sources to get the Word, and so we just wind up with a bunch of dumbed-down Christians. No, we can’t get saved by the works, but because we’re saved, He created us to be people that have our light shining by doing good works, so people can see the difference and bring honor to the God that we give credit to for the way our life is now. Folks, that’s good stuff. Hallelujah. Good works is not just helping the poor, giving medical attention to people that are sick, giving clothing to the naked. Show me one place in the Bible where Jesus gave any clothing to anyone. Show, show me one place in the Bible where Jesus gave money to the poor. Show me one place in the Bible where He stopped everything He was doing to go visit all the sick people. I got you thinking. See, if we’d learn how to read this book, we could separate ourselves from these dumb authors of the day that are imprisoning our mind. Yes, we’re supposed to help the poor, the Bible says that, but Jesus never took it out of His priority schedule to do it. His priority was to save souls. Isn’t that right? To bring the gospel to people. That is the priority of the church, to get the gospel out to people who need to get saved, and not leave the other undone. Are you with me?
What everyday things does he count as good works?

He lists working and providing for your family, abstaining from sexual activity until married to a person of the opposite sex, and abstaining from alcohol and drugs as good works, and says abstaining from sex outside marriage “places no burden on the community.” He says preachers “need to tell the congregation the truth” even if people leave.
What everyday things does he count as good works?

Working and providing for your family is a good work, folks, scripturally a good work. Work is Bible. You don’t put a burden on your community. Abstaining from sexual activity till married, and married to the opposite sex, not the same sex, places no burden on the community. That’s a good work. And also we avoid sexually transmitted diseases that 50% of Americans have. Abstaining from alcohol and drugs puts no burden on the community for the medical attention, and the legal problems, and the law enforcement to try to take care of the problems, and the job-related downtime. That’s a good work. Not to have anything to do with alcohol and drugs, is that an amen, church? That’s a good thing. See, these people want to do their things and then they want us to foot the bill to get them out of their problem, and we’re spending billions and billions of dollars correcting these problems after they happen, instead of putting restraints on them to prevent the problem. Christians today are shacking up sexually, cooking up sexually, drugging up; they get high on marijuana and alcohol; they really are up on welfare and not working; they like the tobacco and dying early; divorcing or not marrying at all is the way our society’s going. Okay, and Christians are doing that. Is that a good work? Is divorce a good work? No. Is not getting married a good work and just shacking up? No, it’s not good works. And preachers need to tell the congregation the truth. Can I hear an amen? They may not like it, they may leave. Well, they shouldn’t have been there in the first place if they’re not going to accept Jesus’s gospel and change their life.
What “works” does the Bible mean when it says we are not saved by works?

He says the works we are not saved by are the “works of the law,” and he points to Galatians 2:16, Romans 3:28 and Hebrews 10:1. He says these are the shadow laws that “are illustrating what Christ was going to do,” not moral laws like honoring parents or not stealing.
What “works” does the Bible mean when it says we are not saved by works?

What are the works that we are not saved by? “Not by works, so that no man can boast.” What are these works that we’re not saved by? Isn’t that a good question? All right. Galatians 2:16: “A man is not justified by the works of the law but by the faith of” who? Jesus Christ. See, so the works we’re not saved by is what? Works of the law. Romans 3:28 says, “A man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.” Okay. I go back to the law and I read, I read in the law: “The Lord thy God is one God. Thou shalt have, make no graven images in heaven and earth below, earth, or in the middle of the earth, or whatever, anything in the earth. Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain. Thou shalt remember the Sabbath day and keep it holy, and you shall work six days and keep the seventh day a day of rest and a day for God. Thou shalt honor thy mother and thy father. Thou shalt not steal. Thou shalt not kill. Thou shalt not commit adultery. Thou shalt not defraud your neighbor,” greed. “Covet.” “And thou shalt not bear false witness.” So what they’re saying is, I don’t have to keep those laws. I can have an idol, and the Catholic Church has all kinds of them. See, I don’t have to take a day, I don’t have to work six days, and I don’t have to give God any debt, and I can take God’s name and I can live any way I want and bring [unclear] to His name. I can kick my parents out of the house and take the house over. I can go murder, I can go steal Mr. Barnes’s new car. He got, “I’m not under works, brother, I want your car.” Does that make sense to you? See, there’s no sense when you’re throwing out good laws. So what laws is he talking about? What part of the law are we not saved or justified by? Hebrews 10:1: “The law was a shadow of things to come.” A what? Shadow of things to come. Now, honoring your parents, is that a shadow? No, that’s definite. Not stealing, is that a shadow of things to come? No, that’s definite. That’s a civil law; that’s treating people right; that’s under the law of love your neighbor yourself. Verse 4 of Hebrews 10: “It is not possible that the blood of bulls and goats should take away sins.” So what works of the law is he talking about? The shadow laws that are illustrating what Christ was going to do when He come to really save people. And so yes, the shadow law has been done away with. You see, we can eat shrimp today because it’s a shadow of holiness to come. We live right now, we do good works. Hallelujah. Got it.
What “works” does the Bible mean when it says we are not saved by works?

Galatians 2:16: knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law but by faith in Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Christ Jesus, that we might be justified by faith in Christ and not by the works of the law; for by the works of the law no flesh shall be justified. Romans 3:28: Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith apart from the deeds of the law. Hebrews 10:1: For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with these same sacrifices, which they offer continually year by year, make those who approach perfect. Hebrews 10:4: For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and goats could take away sins.
What good works did Jesus point to for eternal life? (the rich man)

He says the rich man asked what good thing to do to have eternal life, and Jesus answered “keep the commandments.” He says Jesus was quoting the Ten Commandments, which “are civil laws that stay with us,” and that we do not have a right to say we are saved to sin.
What good works did Jesus point to for eternal life? (the rich man)

Now, what are good works that obtain eternal life, that give you salvation? There’s good works. So this guy comes, this rich guy comes, and he asks Jesus, “What good thing shall I do?” He didn’t ask what shall I believe in. He says what good thing, because we’re supposed to do what? Good works. What good work shall I do that I may have eternal life, which is knowing Jesus, if you will enter into what? Life. What of the grace and faith thing? He didn’t say that, did he? Did he? “If you want eternal life, you want to possess it, then keep the commandments.” And so the guy is a smart aleck and he says, “Well, which ones? Which commandments? There’s a whole lot of them, you know.” That’s us, you know, we’re always trying to trap the preacher and trap the Bible. “Which one?” And Jesus said, “You shall not murder.” So what’s He quoting? The Ten Commandments, which are civil laws that stay with us. We still work the civil laws. You can’t commit adultery: sexual immorality, including homosexuality, including sex with animals, including orgies, and including incest. This word encompasses it all. You can’t steal, nor bear false witness, lie, blame somebody for something they didn’t do. “Honor your father and your mother.” It doesn’t say if they honor you. It says honor them. “Love your neighbor as yourself.” Now, He substituted “love your neighbor as yourself” with the covetous law, the last six commandments, and He substituted “love your neighbor,” which is the second commandment. Got it? Now, folks, we got to still do these. These are works that obtain eternal life. These are good works, aren’t they? They didn’t stop. I don’t have a right to say I’m saved to sin, and even Romans said it plainly: “Am I saved to sin?” Then he said, “God forbid.” What? [unclear] Are Christians responsible to do good work too? All right. Isaiah 60:1: “Arise, shine, for your light has come.”
What good works did Jesus point to for eternal life? (the rich man)

Matthew 19:16-19: Now behold, one came and said to Him, “Good Teacher, what good thing shall I do that I may have eternal life?” So He said to him, “Why do you call Me good? No one is good but One, that is, God. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.” He said to Him, “Which ones?” Jesus said, “‘You shall not murder,’ ‘You shall not commit adultery,’ ‘You shall not steal,’ ‘You shall not bear false witness,’ ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ ” Romans 6:1-2: What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin that grace may abound? Certainly not! How shall we who died to sin live any longer in it?
What does Isaiah 60 say about our light, and what is the “dawn”?

He reads Isaiah 60:1 as present tense: “Arise, shine, for your light has come.” He says the word “dawn” means a gradual light, so a young Christian’s light may be dim, but it is promised to grow “brighter and brighter” until the complete day.
What does Isaiah 60 say about our light, and what is the “dawn”?

That’s present tense. You got it? Wake up. “Your light [unclear]. What are you looking for? You got it. The glory of the Lord is risen upon you.” His glory is His presence. Okay. “Darkness covers the earth and thick darkness the people.” Number one, your light shines to the peoples. Peoples: different society levels, different races, different colors, different languages. “The Lord will rise upon you and His glory appears over you; nations,” now, we got a whole conglomerate of people in America. You got all races, you got languages, you got different cultures, you got different levels of society and all the rest. That’s a nation. “Nations shall come to your light,” and what’s this one? “Kings,” civil leaders, “to the brightness of your dawn.” Dawn is that gradual light. See, yes, you may not be, as a young Christian, very bright in your light shining, but this word “dawn” is what gives you the understanding that yes, my light’s a little dim, I’m young in God, but I’ve been promised my light will go brighter and brighter and brighter and brighter until the complete day, until I’m completely shining. And that’s important for you to know.
What does Isaiah 60 say about our light, and what is the “dawn”?

Isaiah 60:1-3: Arise, shine; For your light has come! And the glory of the LORD is risen upon you. For behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, And deep darkness the people; But the LORD will arise over you, And His glory will be seen upon you. The Gentiles shall come to your light, And kings to the brightness of your rising.
What else is light besides good works? (the Word, John 1:1-4)

He says the Word is life, life is the light, and “the spoken word is the light,” as long as you back it up with your lifestyle. He connects John 1:1, John 6:63 and John 1:14 to say that Jesus is the Word, life, truth and light.
What else is light besides good works? (the Word, John 1:1-4)

Do civil leaders need to hear or need to see our good works? Yeah. Did hear this gospel of eternal life through faith and grace and keeping His commandments? Yes. And who has the responsibility to hit these civil leaders? We do. We can’t get in our little hurt churches and our little houses and just stay there. Are you with me? Now, what else is light besides good works for peoples, nations, and civil leaders? John 1:1: “In the beginning was the Word, the Word was with God, the Word was God.” “In Him,” the Word, “was life.” In Him, Jesus, the Word was life, and that life was the what? “Light of men.” Okay. John 6:63: “The words I speak to you, they are spirit, and they are life.” Life in Jesus, and the Word is life, and life is the light. So the Word spoken is the light. You got that? The spoken word is the light, as well as you back it up with your lifestyle. Is that correct? Do you see that? Now, it’s also truth. John 1:14: “The Word became flesh and dwelt amongst us. We beheld His glory, the glory of the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and” what? Truth. So see, Jesus was God, Jesus was life, Jesus was the Word, and Jesus is light. So the Word is light, and the spoken word is what brings light to people.
What else is light besides good works? (the Word, John 1:1-4)

John 1:1-4: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was in the beginning with God. All things were made through Him, and without Him nothing was made that was made. In Him was life, and the life was the light of men. John 6:63: It is the Spirit who gives life; the flesh profits nothing. The words that I speak to you are spirit, and they are life. John 1:14: And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld His glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth.
Why did Paul and Barnabas turn to the Gentiles? (Acts 13:46-47)

He says Paul and Barnabas spoke the word of God to the Jews first, and “since you reject it and do not consider yourselves worthy of eternal life, we turn to the Gentiles.” He says people will reject the Word “and still claim they’re going to heaven,” with “no change, no new creation, no born again.” He also says “we need to get studious” and “really learn how to learn.”
Why did Paul and Barnabas turn to the Gentiles? (Acts 13:46-47)

Now, is that clear? See, we need to get studious. We need to really learn how to learn. And we go to church and we just sit there: “When’s he going to get over with? When’s he going to...?” We’re not even paying any attention. We need to learn. “Sanctify them through Thy truth. Thy word is” what? Truth. So the Word is truth, life, life, it’s Jesus, and so forth. Now look at this one, Acts 13:46: Paul and Barnabas answered the Jews boldly, confidently, “All right, we had to speak the word of God to you first.” What did they do with the Word of God? They spoke it. And he had to speak it to you first, because that’s what Jesus told him: “You go to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” That’s what Jesus told them. So they obeyed, and the Jews were rejecting it, and so he says, “We have to speak the word of God to you first.” See the light, we gave you the light first. “But since you reject it and do not consider yourselves worthy of eternal life, we turn to the Gentiles.” See, they reject it. People are going to reject the Word. They’re going to reject the Word and still claim they’re going to heaven. This is what these Jews did right here: they rejected the Word and still claim to be believers in God and going to heaven. Do you know people like that? They’re not obeying the Word at all; they just want to go to heaven the way they are. No change, no new creation, no born again. “For this is what the Lord has commanded us: ‘I have made you a light for the Gentiles.’” Okay. Jesus told us back there that we were the light of the world, to do good works that they might what? People would honor God.
Why did Paul and Barnabas turn to the Gentiles? (Acts 13:46-47)

John 17:17: Sanctify them by Your truth. Your word is truth. Acts 13:46-47: Then Paul and Barnabas grew bold and said, “It was necessary that the word of God should be spoken to you first; but since you reject it, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, behold, we turn to the Gentiles. For so the Lord has commanded us: ‘I have set you as a light to the Gentiles, That you should be for salvation to the ends of the earth.’ ”
What message will change people’s lives? (the word of salvation)

He says the church has family seminars, financial seminars and divorce-recovery seminars, but “the thing that’s going to save the world is this message of” salvation. He says we can be born again, become new creatures, and be restored when we fall, and “you can’t substitute this with other stuff.”
What message will change people’s lives? (the word of salvation)

Now here He’s saying, “I’ve made you a light,” to speak the Word. What word? “That you may bring salvation to the ends of the earth.” What’s the word they’re speaking? The word of salvation. Say it: salvation. You know, in the church we got family seminars, we got financial seminars, we got, you know, divorce recovery seminars, we got all the things. The thing that’s going to save the world is this message of what? Salvation. “The word of the Lord spread through the whole region.” What word spread? The word of salvation. That who spoke? Paul and Barnabas. The thing that’s going to revolutionize people’s lives is this message of salvation. It’s real. We can be born again, we can become new creatures in Christ Jesus, we can be restored when we fall backward. These things are for us, and it’s in the message of salvation. Hallelujah. You can’t substitute this with other stuff. John 3:19: “This is the verdict.” Now, is there a judgment being made here? That’s a powerful word. Here’s the verdict, I’ve made the decision, this is my judgment: “Light has come into the world, but men love” what? “Darkness instead of light because their deeds were evil.”
What message will change people’s lives? (the word of salvation)

Acts 13:47: For so the Lord has commanded us: ‘I have set you as a light to the Gentiles, That you should be for salvation to the ends of the earth.’ ” Acts 13:49: And the word of the Lord was being spread throughout all the region.
Why do people love darkness and hate the light? (John 3:19-21)

He reads John 3:19, that men love “darkness instead of light because their deeds were evil.” He says people who reject the light “want to be told they’re wrong” in a church that tells them they’re okay, and he urges finding “a teacher of the Word” and getting that Word in you.
Why do people love darkness and hate the light? (John 3:19-21)

Does that mean we stop preaching that word because people don’t want to hear it? That’s what the American church has done. “Everyone who does evil hates” what? “The light.” See, when you say you’re a Christian and you are committing homosexual sin or sexual sin or stealing, your acts, your behavior tells us you hate the light. How can you say you’re a Christian when this Scripture says if you do these things, you hate the light? You’re a hater. See, when you reject the light, you hate Jesus, you hate the Word, you hate truth. “They will not come to the light.” See, they won’t come to Christianity, they won’t come to Jesus, they won’t come to the Word, for fear that their deeds will be exposed. They want to be told they’re wrong, so they find a church that tells them they’re okay. The blind lead the blind and they all fall into the ditch. Yeah, if you want to go to the ditch, then follow these dumb ministers. If you want to be delivered, if you want wisdom and understanding, if you want to be a real, committed, true Christian, then find you a teacher of the Word and get that Word in you, and that Word will set you free and deliver you and heal you and do everything that it says it would do, including grow. “But whoever lives by the truth,” see, that’s the good works people, “they come to the light,” see, “and the light exposes, so that it may be seen plainly that what he has done has been done through God.” See, we don’t have a problem with the light because we want to be like the light. Even if we are not there yet, we come in with confidence that He’s going to finish the good work He began in us. So we come to the light, we don’t have a problem being exposed. We want to be exposed, we want to be changed, we want to come to repentance in every area so that we can have a light that shines completely, not just the dawning light. Amen.
Why do people love darkness and hate the light? (John 3:19-21)

John 3:19-21: And this is the condemnation, that the light has come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. For everyone practicing evil hates the light and does not come to the light, lest his deeds should be exposed. But he who does the truth comes to the light, that his deeds may be clearly seen, that they have been done in God.”
Do good works save anyone? (what Jesus did in His first thirty years)

He says Jesus did good works until He was thirty and not one person was saved or healed, so “the good works didn’t save anybody.” Good works bring honor to the Father, he says, but “it’s the spoken word of salvation that brings salvation,” and people need both to see the good works and to hear the Word.
Do good works save anyone? (what Jesus did in His first thirty years)

Yes, so don’t ever feel bad about your dawning light. You got a little light, that’s okay. It’s going to grow, it’s going to keep growing, but you got to be in the Word for it to grow. Now, I’ve said this many a time, and let me tell it to you again. Jesus, who did good works from the time He was born till He was 30 years old, He never sinned, He never disrespected His parents, He worked at a job, never committed adultery, never lied. And not one person was saved, not one person was healed, not one person hated Him and wanted to kill Him. The good works didn’t save anybody. It brings honor to the Father, but it’s the spoken word of salvation that brings salvation. And Jesus’ first words were what? “Repent, believe the gospel, get baptized for the remission of sin.” That was His message. Now, do we need both light shining in our life? People need to see the good works and bring honor to God who gave us the power to do that. Isn’t that right? But they need to hear the Word if they’re going to get saved.
Is being a nice, quiet Christian enough?

He says “sitting in our homes” and being a quiet Christian “isn’t going to cut it,” and that this includes not speaking out on political issues, right issues and moral issues. He says Christians are the light of the world by doing good works and by speaking the word of truth, to peoples, nations and kings.
Is being a nice, quiet Christian enough?

And sitting in our homes and being a nice, quiet Christian isn’t going to cut it. Sitting in America and not speaking out on political issues, right issues, moral issues isn’t going to cut it. Christians are the light of the world by doing good works, and our opponents will give honor to God. Christians are the light of the world by speaking the word of truth, and people will get saved. Christians are the light of the world by speaking the word of truth, by speaking to peoples the word of truth, nations and kings. And Christians, Acts 9:15, the Lord said to Ananias, “Go your way, for Paul is a chosen vessel unto Me to bear My name before” what? “The Gentiles,” the unbeliever, “the kings and the children of Israel.”
Is being a nice, quiet Christian enough?
Acts 9:15: But the Lord said to him, “Go, for he is a chosen vessel of Mine to bear My name before Gentiles, kings, and the children of Israel.

He points to Paul before Felix in Acts 24:25: “righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come.” He says this is the power of the converting gospel: repent and turn to do right, use self-control, and know there is a judgment coming.

Acts 26:17: “I’m sending you to open their eyes, turn them from darkness to” what? “Light, and from the power of Satan to the power of God.” You know, the Bible says that He has the power to perform what He promised. Acts 24:25: Paul reasoned of “righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come.” Now, here is the converting gospel, right here. Paul was before Felix, the governor, of the government, and he told Felix, he reasoned, he used logic, he logically presented the truth in an orderly manner. Righteousness, number one: repent from sin, turn to do right. Number two: Self-control. You got to put some effort into this, you got to put some work into this. And these people that say “not by works,” if you don’t put work into it, you’re not going to conquer it. You got to say no to sin, you got to use self-control to get to church, to learn the Bible, you got to bring some discipline in your life. Can I hear it, amen? This is the power of the converting gospel. Paul’s got it right here, summed up for us. And “the judgment to come”: Felix, if you don’t repent and turn and do right, if you don’t use self-control, you’re going to burn. There’s a judgment coming, and you’re going to burn. And Felix, what? Shook in fear. You ever seen anybody shaking in fear? And this is something missing in the church. You know, we’re not getting saved from the fear of the Lord, from a jarring experience of God, that if we don’t change our life we’re going to go to hell. God’s displeased with us. Now, I think this is plain, folks. The converting gospel is righteousness, self-control, discipline: yourself, stop doing bad things. Don’t wait for God to call you from heaven. And he’s also telling the king, that’s a way, you better rule, you better rule with right laws, you better teach people to control themselves, and if they don’t, they’re going to be punished, because you’re the king. It says Bible morality is the proof that we are Christians.

Acts 26:17-18: I will deliver you from the Jewish people, as well as from the Gentiles, to whom I now send you, to open their eyes, in order to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those who are sanctified by faith in Me.’ Acts 24:25: Now as he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was afraid and answered, “Go away for now; when I have a convenient time I will call for you.”
Is Bible morality the proof that we are Christians?

He says Jesus said “you will know them by their fruits,” and that Bible morality is the proof that we are Christians. He says speaking it to everyone shows we care and gives people “an opportunity to” convert and change their life.
Is Bible morality the proof that we are Christians?

Didn’t Jesus say, “You will know them by their fruits,” not their faith? You know them by what? Their fruits. You see, how can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit? Jesus said, say, you know the root of the tree by the fruit. And Bible morality is speaking it, and speaking it to everyone shows we care. They’re totally wrong, we’re not hating people by telling them the truth. We care for them, we have a compassion for them, and gives them an opportunity to what? Convert and change their life. How many can raise your hand, say you agree this is the gospel that needs to get out to America? Yes. How many really believe God will back up that gospel with His power and actually convert people?
Is Bible morality the proof that we are Christians?

Matthew 7:16-20: You will know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes from thornbushes or figs from thistles? Even so, every good tree bears good fruit, but a bad tree bears bad fruit. A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, nor can a bad tree bear good fruit. Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire. Therefore by their fruits you will know them.
What does he say about people who say they don’t wear their religion on their sleeve?
He calls it “ridiculous” and says “people should see our religion.”
Does he say we can be saved by works?
No. He says “I can’t win enough souls to get into heaven,” cannot pray or take communion enough, and that there is nothing he can do “besides believe the gospel.” He adds, “It’s free.”
Why does he say we were created in Christ Jesus?
He says the same grace and faith that brought salvation made us a new creature, and we were “created to do” good works. He says “we have a responsibility to do good works.”
What does he say about Jesus and helping the poor?

He asks readers to show him one place where Jesus gave clothing or money to the poor, or stopped everything to visit all the sick. He says we are supposed to help the poor but “His priority was to save souls.”
What does he say about the shadow laws, like eating shrimp?
He says the shadow laws were illustrating what Christ would do, and “the shadow law has been done away with.” He says we can eat shrimp today “because it’s a shadow of holiness to come.”
Does he say the Ten Commandments still apply?
Yes. He says Jesus’ answer to the rich man quotes the Ten Commandments, which “are civil laws that stay with us,” and that honoring your father and mother and loving your neighbor still apply.
Does he say civil leaders need to hear the gospel?

Yes. He asks whether civil leaders need to hear or see our good works and answers “yes,” and says “we do” have the responsibility to reach them. He says Christians cannot “get in our little hurt churches and our little houses and just stay there.”
What does he say the Word is?
He says Jesus is God, life, the Word and light, so “the Word is light, and the spoken word is what brings light to people.” He quotes the Word becoming flesh, full of grace and truth.
Should Christians stop preaching because people don’t want to hear it?
No. He asks, “does that mean we stop preaching that word because people don’t want to hear it?” and says “that’s what the American church has done.”
Should I feel bad if my light is only a little light?
No. He says “don’t ever feel bad about your dawning light,” that it is okay and “it’s going to grow,” but “you got to be in the Word for it to grow.”
What does he say were Jesus’ first words?
He says Jesus’ first words were “repent, believe the gospel, get baptized for the remission of sin,” and that this was His message.
What does he say is missing in the church?
He says Felix “shook in fear” and that something missing in the church is people “getting saved from the fear of the Lord,” knowing that if they don’t change their life they’re going to hell.
Does he say telling people the truth is hating them?
No. He says “we’re not hating people by telling them the truth. We care for them, we have a compassion for them,” and it gives them a chance to convert and change their life.

items.d: The speaker sets three choices from Matthew 13:30 and Malachi 3:18: be good (best), be wicked (worst), or try good without God (humanism). Humanists and Bible followers can grow together if they agree on doing…
items.ser: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors · Part 16
tg: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors
p: The speaker sets three choices from Matthew 13:30 and Malachi 3:18: be good (best), be wicked (worst), or try good without God (humanism). Humanists and Bible followers can grow together if they agree on doing good (Galatians 6:10) and punishing harm. He charges humanist billboards with lies (Jefferson quote, Piltdown Man, faith vs proof) and summarizes: neither camp may harm others; harmers must be punished; unite around not hurting while choosing among following Jesus, rejecting Jesus without harm, or criminal wickedness.
What three crucial choices does he set out?

From Matthew 13:30 and Malachi 3:18 he names choosing to be good (best), wicked (worst), or trying to do good without God as humanists do—or a Christian who believes but does not serve God. Being a humanist does not necessarily mean wicked, nor a Christian necessarily not wicked.
What three crucial choices does he set out?

Today we’re going to look at clarity on crucial choices—whether we make bad choices, we can make better choices, and we can make the best choices. We’re going to be dealing with three choices this morning. In Matthew 13:30, let both the good and the wicked grow together until the harvest at the end of the world. In Malachi 3:18, you shall again discern between the righteous and the wicked—first choice, second choice—but then he’s adding another choice between one who serves God, which would be one that does good and right, and one who doesn’t, which could be a humanist that doesn’t believe in God and the Bible, or a Christian that believes in God but does not serve God. So we got these three choices: to choose to be good, which is the best choice; to be wicked, which is the bad choice, the worse; and a choice to try to do good without God, which the humanists try to do. Now being a humanist doesn’t necessarily mean you are wicked, and being a Christian does not necessarily mean you’re not wicked.
What three crucial choices does he set out?

Matthew 13:30: Let both grow together until the harvest, and at the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, “First gather together the tares and bind them in bundles to burn them, but gather the wheat into my barn.” ’ ” Malachi 3:18: Then you shall again discern Between the righteous and the wicked, Between one who serves God And one who does not serve Him.
What does he say unites listed humanist groups?

He says Manifesto II lists many humanist types who claim the humanist tradition; all reject Jesus and the Bible, and though the manifesto says merely rejecting God is not equivalent to humanism, he says they all base philosophy on Bible and Jesus as myth and no God.
What does he say unites listed humanist groups?

Now the religion of secular humanism in its Manifesto II tries to separate bad humanists from their manifesto humanist, and they list the different humanist organizations: scientific, ethical, democratic, religious humanist, Marxist humanist, freethought, atheist, deist, rationalism, agnostics, skeptics, ethical cultural, and liberal religions—all claim to be heir to the humanist tradition, they say. And I want to make a note that all of these groups reject Jesus and the Bible. But in trying to separate the different humanist groups they list them and they say this statement: but views that merely reject God and the Bible, theism, are not equivalent to humanism. But they all got one thing that they base their philosophy on, and that is the Bible is a myth and Jesus is a myth and there is no God.
Where do humanists and Bible followers agree on “good”?

He cites humanist billboards “good without God” and Buffett/Gates charity, and Galatians 6:10 do good to all. The Manifesto’s “short of harming others” means both camps must punish, correct, or remove evil so others are not hurt—or else their ideology is wicked.
Where do humanists and Bible followers agree on “good”?

Now the Bible said that the wicked and the righteous and the one that don’t serve God are supposed to grow together. So how do we do this? Number one, the humanist and the Bible followers agree on good. The humanists say that Warren Buffett and Bill Gates are good without God because they give billions to charity. They also have billboards going all throughout the country: Are you good without God? Millions are. They have another one that says millions of people are good without God—you don’t need religion to be a good moral person. And so humanists say they’re out for good. They believe in good. They believe we should do good. And the Bible says in Galatians 6:10, as we have opportunity let us do good to all people. And so we are in agreement that we’re supposed to do good. So good is the basics for living together and growing together. In the Humanist Manifesto it says, short of harming others, individuals should be permitted to express and pursue their desired lifestyles. The key here is short of harming others. So we must conclude that humanists and Bible followers must deal with bad people—whether they’re bad humanists or bad Bible followers. To get along we must agree that evil must be punished, corrected, or removed from society so they can’t hurt others. And also if humanist or Bible followers do not agree to do good and punish criminals, they are a wicked ideology, a wicked system of faith, a wicked philosophy, because they’re not agreeing to do good.
Where do humanists and Bible followers agree on “good”?
Galatians 6:10: Therefore, as we have opportunity, let us do good to all, especially to those who are of the household of faith.
What Jefferson billboard claim does he call a lie?

He reads Proverbs 14:5 on false witness. He says humanist billboards quote Thomas Jefferson rejecting Christianity as fables—Jefferson never said that—and they lie about Bible, Jesus, and separation of church and state to leave only secular humanism free speech in public.
What Jefferson billboard claim does he call a lie?

Now some things are disagreed on that may not directly harm others—like killing directly harms others, stealing directly harms others, sexual abuse and drug abuse and any mistreatment of other people directly hurts them. And so we’re going to look at a few things that humanist and Bible followers disagree on that may not directly hurt others. Proverbs 14:5, a faithful witness does not lie, but a false witness will utter lies. The humanists have billboards around the nation that says, I do not find in Christianity one redeeming feature; it is founded on fables and mythology—and they say that’s a quote of Thomas Jefferson. And Thomas Jefferson never said that. That is a blatant lie. They also lie about the Bible, Jesus, separation of church and state, thus leaving only secular humanism for free speech in public places. And that makes them an unfaithful, a false witness.
What Jefferson billboard claim does he call a lie?
Proverbs 14:5: A faithful witness does not lie, But a false witness will utter lies.
What Piltdown Man and “faith” arguments does he make?

He says Piltdown was taught 40 years as missing link from mixed bones and used in the Scopes trial—an unfaithful witness. John 8:31 and 17:17 say God’s word is truth. Billboard “celebrate reason” ignores Bible morals and early science claims. Humanists have no proof humanism works, so their philosophy is also faith; Bible followers may likewise use faith.
What Piltdown Man and “faith” arguments does he make?

On evolution they’ve taught lies like this—Piltdown Man for 40 years they said he was the missing link from fragments of a skull, a human skull, and then the jawbone of an orangutan that they said was human, and some teeth that came from a chimpanzee that they filed down and put in there that say it was human. And they said this was the missing link for 40 years, and they used it in the Scopes trial. That’s an unfaithful witness. John 8:31 says continue in my word and you shall know the truth and the truth shall set you free. John 17:17, your word is truth. The Bible never says it’s a book of faith. The Bible says it’s a book of truth. They have a billboard that says, you know it’s a myth this season—celebrate reason, celebrate intellect. But this same Bible says not to kill, not to steal, not immoral sex; you work six days; you work, provide for yourself; get knowledge; get love. These things are not myths. The Bible also says that the earth was a sphere, it was hung on nothing, the water cycle—the evaporation and rain coming—and the ocean currents before science even knew these things. And they quote that faith is that which has no proof—it’s based on what has no proof—and they say you want to believe something that is true because you want it to be true—that’s faith. Well, humanist, you have no proof that humanism works, and so you’re basing your humanist philosophy, your humanistic ideas, on faith, because you have no proof. So if you can use faith to back up what you want to get across to America, what is wrong with Christians and Bible followers using faith to back up the Bible?
What Piltdown Man and “faith” arguments does he make?

John 8:31-32: Then Jesus said to those Jews who believed Him, “If you abide in My word, you are My disciples indeed. And you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.” John 17:17: Sanctify them by Your truth. Your word is truth. Matthew 19:17: So He said to him, “Why do you call Me good? No one is good but One, that is, God. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.” Ecclesiastes 7:20: For there is not a just man on earth who does good And does not sin.
What does he say about “In Good We Trust” and mass-killing leaders?

He says humanist billboards put “In Good We Trust” against “In God We Trust,” yet leaders since the French Revolution—Mao, Pol Pot, Stalin—killed twenty-some million. Claiming never to lie, steal, or sexually sin is self-deception; even Christians work at being good and make mistakes.
What does he say about “In Good We Trust” and mass-killing leaders?

In Matthew 19:17 there is none good but God. Ecclesiastes 7:20, there’s not a just man on earth who does good and does not sin. Yet you humanists have this billboard around the nation: In Good We Trust—on our quarter instead of In God We Trust. You have more than three leaders, nations, that have killed 20 and some million people since the French Revolution—Mao of China, Pol Pot of Cambodia, and Stalin of Russia. That’s not good. Again you are—good without God, millions are—and what you’re telling us is you never lie, you never steal, you never commit sexual immorality, you don’t mistreat people, you don’t hate people. You are deceiving yourself. Even us Christians are trying and working at being good people. We make mistakes.
What does he say about immigration, work, and “something for nothing”?

He cites one law for citizen and stranger (Numbers 15:16), labor as God’s gift (Ecclesiastes 3:13), and if you don’t work you don’t eat—against a billboard blaming capitalism and a manifesto guaranteed salary. Promoting something for nothing is like false religion promising heaven with no obligation to do good.
What does he say about immigration, work, and “something for nothing”?

Numbers 15:16, there’s one law and one custom for citizens of a nation and the stranger that comes into a nation. Ecclesiastes 3:13, all must eat, drink, enjoy the good of his labor—must labor; it is a gift of God. And the Bible says if you don’t work you don’t eat. Yet you have a billboard that says we don’t have an immigration problem, we have a capitalism problem, because in your manifesto you said that you want to guarantee a yearly salary, minimum salary, to everyone in the nation—when the Bible says that the poor work for wealth, field droppings, corners of the field left for them, or they had to beg, or they had to sell themselves to someone in the nation for six years. When you promote something for nothing you’re just like false religions that promote eternal life without any obligation to do good. And a lot of religions are promoting something for nothing—all I got to do is believe in Jesus or believe in Allah or believe in something, and everything’s going to be okay, I’m going to go to heaven, and I don’t have to do good and I don’t have to do righteous. That is something for nothing.
What does he say about immigration, work, and “something for nothing”?

Numbers 15:16: One law and one custom shall be for you and for the stranger who dwells with you.’ ” Ecclesiastes 3:13: and also that every man should eat and drink and enjoy the good of all his labor—it is the gift of God.
How can God’s people, humanists, and the wicked grow together?

First, neither humanists nor God-followers may lie or harm others physically, financially, mentally, or spiritually. Second, when either hurts others they must be punished or corrected as criminals, and if they will not change, separated from society.
How can God’s people, humanists, and the wicked grow together?

Now how can God’s people and humanists and the wicked grow or increase together? We’re going to summarize it. How can this possibly work out? Okay, we’ve given you the steps. We’re going to sum those steps. First of all, humanist nor God followers may lie to other people or do harm to other people physically, financially, mentally, or spiritually if we’re going to grow together and work together as a community, as a nation. Neither humanists that don’t believe in God nor God followers that believe in God have an excuse to hurt other people. All right. Secondly, when humanists or God followers hurt others they must be punished. You know, just because you’re a believer in Christ does not give you permission to hurt others, and because you don’t believe in God doesn’t give you permission to hurt others. And when we do we need to be punished or corrected for the wicked behavior, as we are no longer just believers or non-believers but we are criminals—and criminals need to be corrected, punished, and if we don’t change our harmful ways we need to be separated from society.
What three choices does he sum up at the end?

Remember God cannot lie, God is love, love does no harm (Romans 13:10); laws should protect citizens from harm. Manifesto agrees “short of harming others.” Three choices: follow Jesus and don’t harm; reject Jesus and don’t harm (humanist); or follow/reject but hurt others—criminal wickedness requiring punishment. We must do good, not only talk.
What three choices does he sum up at the end?

Now we’ve got to remember and recall that God cannot lie, that God is love, and love does no harm to a neighbor. And in Romans 13:10 it says love fulfills the law. Every law written should be written to protect its citizens from harm, both from government and other citizens—and that’s the kind of laws that work. We got to remember these things, these high priorities. Next is we got to remember in the Humanist Manifesto they said, short of harming others, individuals should be permitted to express their likings and pursue their lifestyles as they desire. But the key is short of harming others. They agree with the Bible that they believe is a myth—we don’t have a right to hurt others. So we can unite around good, around not hurting others, and live amongst each other though one of us believes in God and the other doesn’t. So summing it up, there’s three choices: follow Jesus, the Bible, and don’t harm others; reject Jesus, the Bible, and don’t harm others—that would be the humanist; and number three, follow or reject Jesus in the Bible but we hurt others by criminal wicked behavior requiring punishment. In summation, we cannot just talk about doing good—we must do good.
What three choices does he sum up at the end?
Romans 13:10: Love does no harm to a neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.
What does Matthew 13:30 say about good and wicked growing together?
Let both grow together until the harvest at the end of the world.
What third discernment does Malachi 3:18 add?
Discern between the righteous and the wicked, and between one who serves God and one who does not.
What Manifesto phrase does he say is the key to living together?
Short of harming others—individuals may pursue lifestyles, but evil must still be punished, corrected, or removed.
What Bible verse does he pair with humanist “do good”?
Galatians 6:10—as we have opportunity let us do good to all people.
Did Thomas Jefferson say Christianity has no redeeming feature?
He says humanist billboards claim that quote, but Jefferson never said it—a blatant lie.
Does he say the Bible calls itself a book of faith or of truth?
He says the Bible never says it is a book of faith; it says it is a book of truth (John 17:17).
What scientific claims does he say the Bible made early?
Earth as a sphere hung on nothing, the water cycle, and ocean currents before science knew them—and commands not to kill, steal, or do immoral sex.
Which leaders does he cite against “good without God”?
Mao of China, Pol Pot of Cambodia, and Stalin of Russia—killing twenty-some million since the French Revolution.
What does Numbers 15:16 say about citizens and strangers?
One law and one custom for citizens and the stranger who comes into the nation.
What is his final line on talking versus doing good?
In summation, we cannot just talk about doing good—we must do good.

items.d: In “Conference Report,” a Vine Cluster Church member, asked by Pastor David G. Kincer to be a witness, reports what he heard at a pastors’ conference: calls to preach righteousness without fear, stories of…
p: In “Conference Report,” a Vine Cluster Church member, asked by Pastor David G. Kincer to be a witness, reports what he heard at a pastors’ conference: calls to preach righteousness without fear, stories of believers attacked for their convictions, and a plea for the church to unite and get involved. Pastor Kincer then closes, saying the church cannot justify silence and that America needs a message of hope, illustrated by David and Goliath and by Paul at Corinth.
What was this conference report about?

A church member, asked by the pastor to be a witness, shares what he heard at a pastors’ conference. He says he left very encouraged and also heavy-hearted for what is going on in the country, and that the speakers encouraged the church that America does not belong to Satan, because Jesus said all authority has been given to him.
What was this conference report about?

But I want to share with you what I. Received from the conference Mr. Kincer has asked me to share with the church to be a witness and share what God is doing what God is saying in this group and I left very encouraged. And also very on my heart just heavy for what’s going on right now in our country. And I just want to share what I experienced what. I heard. There were a lot of good pastors that spoke. They gave excellent messages encouraging the church that the kingdom does not. America does not belong to Satan. The kingdom it says in Matthew at the end when he says go out and teach make disciples of all nations he says all authority. All authority has been given unto me Jesus Christ all authority. And I thought that was another great scripture about Jesus Christ having authority. Having authority over all the nations so. I just want to share real quick I’m sorry it’s not going to be quick. Uh. So I’m coming to bring news to be a witness and share with you guys what what they shared with us so it was a Watchman on the Wall group in. Uh it’s a part of Family Research Council and uh. Our the first speaker when I showed up I was late because I couldn’t get a flight any earlier I had to you know I got there a little late so I drove in sat down and there was already a speaker in progress and his name was David Welch and I’m just going to go through the speakers and what God was saying through these speakers and what God was saying to me during this time and at the end what God was speaking to me during the whole event and the attitude and this is very it’s very interesting I.
What was this conference report about?

Matthew 28:18-19: And Jesus came and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to Me in heaven and on earth. Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
What was it like to be at the conference in person?

He says that getting emails about people being attacked feels distant, but there he felt very close to the attacks and to well-known people willing to speak to a group of fewer than a hundred. He says their hearts were begging pastors to wake up, stand and unite, and that everyone who believes in Christ and believes in freedom was welcomed.
What was it like to be at the conference in person?

As part of the church. Part of America you sign up for these emails and you get this information about people that are being attacked and you feel very distant but when I was there. They were right there they were experiencing it I felt very close to the attacks. I felt very close to the people who were willing to come to a group of less than a hundred people. Very famous people willing to come to a small group and say pastors it’s time it’s time we wake up and stand. And these guys their hearts were just begging begging anyone we need to unite. There was they had worship several a couple times and there was a lady in there who was very flamboyant very loud very charismatic you know I consider myself to be charismatic but I wasn’t doing what she was doing I was raising my hands praising God kneeling and all that stuff but she was more than I was but you know they never came to her threw her out never suppressed her never corrected her uh. I know that they invite Catholics into their group and I’m just sharing the whole atmosphere it was a very you know come we want everyone everyone that believes in Christ believes in freedom and it was very powerful very powerful experience and I hope I can translate that to you this morning. Anyway he’s in charge of the Houston’s pastors council they have a council in Houston where they get all the pastors together and unite on certain issues and he was sharing how. We need to basically they’re very direct and you know when you go to Texas it’s like a breath of fresh air you know it’s Midwest people they’re very nice they believe in good things good values it’s like I came to church you know it’s like being with you guys every Sunday.
Should pastors be afraid to preach the truth?

He says he heard over and over that pastors cannot be afraid of the numbers or of being attacked, and must preach truth and stand for what is right. He connects Matthew 28:18 with Daniel 4, where Nebuchadnezzar says God has authority over every kingdom, and reports the message that we have handed judgment over to wicked people.
Should pastors be afraid to preach the truth?

You know when I go to work it’s a lot different when I go places it’s a lot different when I come to church I’ve got good people to be around it it’s wonderful and in Texas it’s a lot different anyway he was sharing and explaining that we need to preach to the church and I heard this over and over that we need to not be afraid of the numbers we need to start preaching truth and these are people big pastors are saying this. They’re saying you guys you can’t be afraid. To preach the truth you can’t be afraid to stand up for what’s right because of fear that some people are going to leave because of fear that you’re going to be attacked. It was very good very good. He brought up Matthew 28 verse 18 and he said all authority which says all authority has been given unto me and he sent out his disciples he said go and make disciples of all nations all authority. We learned through the story of Nebuchadnezzar that [unclear] chapter 4 of what book is that what is it Daniel that’s right chapter 4 of Daniel Nebuchadnezzar writes to the world and says God has authority over every kingdom over everything. And it hasn’t changed and this scripture confirms that. It’s very powerful. And in Romans 13 of course that’s the that’s the chapter that talks about how to submit unto authority and he was saying how we handed over our authority we’ve handed over judgment to the I have the enemy down here we’ve handed judgment over to wicked people and that was the gist of his message. And then you have Pastor Willie Davis of [unclear] Community Church and uh he’s a pastor of a big church there and he was uniting with Pastor Steve [unclear], Steve [unclear] is the pastor of the church that hosted the event and they unite on issues like abortion they would go and take their people to Austin Texas the state capitol.
Should pastors be afraid to preach the truth?

Matthew 28:18: And Jesus came and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to Me in heaven and on earth. Daniel 4:34-35: And at the end of the time I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted my eyes to heaven, and my understanding returned to me; and I blessed the Most High and praised and honored Him who lives forever: For His dominion is an everlasting dominion, And His kingdom is from generation to generation. All the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing; He does according to His will in the army of heaven And among the inhabitants of the earth. No one can restrain His hand Or say to Him, “What have You done?” Romans 13:1: Let every soul be subject to the governing authorities. For there is no authority except from God, and the authorities that exist are appointed by God.
What does Amos 5:21-24 say about justice and righteousness?

He reads Amos 5:21-24, where God says he hates their feast days, and links it to “better to obey than sacrifice” from the story of Saul. He says verse 24, “let justice run down like water and righteousness like a mighty stream,” touched him, because we have a trickle and need a flood of righteousness, and churches are not even preaching sin.
What does Amos 5:21-24 say about justice and righteousness?

And they would flood the capitol building with their church community members to stand for issues. Very powerful to hear very excellent I thought that was very tremendous. And he brought out Amos 5 21-24. And if you guys have your bibles let’s turn there it’s a very short scripture. And it starts in 21 says. And this is Amos or the word of the Lord talking to the Israelites. Saying I hate and I despise your feast days I do not savor your sacred assemblies though you offer me burnt offerings your grain offerings I will not accept them nor will I regard your fat and peace offerings basically this is right in line with the scripture that talks about it is better to obey. Than sacrifice and I know we know about that scripture how Saul he went and he wanted to present the sacrifice. Before Samuel came and he didn’t follow the right order. And Samuel God was telling him it’s better to obey. Than to sacrifice I don’t care about your sat you know your feast days and all that if you are not turning obeying and listening to my voice. And the powerful part you know and God touched me is when he brought out the 24th verse he said but let justice run down like water and righteousness like a mighty stream here you have these big [unclear] pastors are talking about righteousness they’re talking and telling the pastors you guys need to talk about righteousness you guys need to preach morality we need to bring back righteousness in our community. And I thought gosh where am I am I at Mountainside am I listening to Mr. Kincer right now. This is just powerful. And maybe they interpret righteousness differently but we know where righteousness is it’s right living living the right way. Amen. And uh you know I don’t know if he knew the scripture he brought out here but it was so powerful let justice run down like water. And righteousness like a mighty stream and that’s exactly what we need right now we’ve got a trickle we need a flood we need a flood of righteousness. He was saying how churches are not even preaching sin again I was like where am I. We cannot be ashamed.
What does Amos 5:21-24 say about justice and righteousness?

Amos 5:21-24: “I hate, I despise your feast days, And I do not savor your sacred assemblies. Though you offer Me burnt offerings and your grain offerings, I will not accept them, Nor will I regard your fattened peace offerings. Take away from Me the noise of your songs, For I will not hear the melody of your stringed instruments. But let justice run down like water, And righteousness like a mighty stream. 1 Samuel 15:22: So Samuel said: “Has the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, As in obeying the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, And to heed than the fat of rams.
Why does he say pastors’ sermons were subpoenaed?

He reports that the speakers said the mayor of Houston subpoenaed pastors’ sermons and notes to see whether they had spoken against homosexuality and same-sex marriage, and the pastors refused. He says people now fear losing their jobs for speaking out, and he shares a report that a 20-week abortion law the church lobbied for meant one baby was not aborted.
Why does he say pastors’ sermons were subpoenaed?

They say it’s peace and justice to remove God. And as you know this is all in. They’re getting together because the mayor of Houston Texas has subpoenaed Steve [unclear] and other pastors in the area and required their messages and their sermons to get. Their notes and see if they have a you know spoken against homosexuality same-sex marriage and uh these guys are saying no we’re not gonna give you our messages I would give you them for free if I knew you’d listen but since you’re demanding me and I’m a Texan. I was talking to Blake he said don’t mess with Texas don’t mess with Texas. And. Finally we have people that are standing up it’s very good. But it’s true they say that it’s peace to remove God they say that it’s justice. For. Homosexuality for that to be promoted to be approved. You know they’re saying that that is right they’re saying that that is justice. They don’t want God’s word heard. And that’s what he brought out. And then we have Mr. [unclear]. And he was pastor he’s the pastor of Grace Community Church a church of ten thousand. Anyway that kind of sums up his I’m sorry that kind of gives you. His attitude and when you’re there. And you’re in you’re with these people it’s a lot different you know I get these emails and it’s like oh this guy is getting attacked oh they’re gonna attack you know God’s in control God God what are you gonna do God please do something well it’s a lot different when you’re there and these men are being attacked their families are being attacked you know. I don’t I don’t know why they’re being subpoenaed they might be trying to get rid of this guy you know what he’s supposed to do what is he supposed to do he’s part of a church. We don’t want to be shut down they’re shutting down businesses because they won’t serve same sex marriage couples I mean that’s putting fear into people you know what if I speak out against it and my company hears about it and they fire me that’s my livelihood. That’s how I support my family. And that’s what it’s turning into anybody who speaks publicly out speaks out publicly about something is in danger of being fired from their job and this is gonna this is it seems like this is gonna be affecting us at home. Not just not just on the airwaves. Gosh. And like I said earlier I have these notes down here that. I want to share a story real quick he had his church members go to the state capitol and lobby and fight for the abortion law changing it from 24 weeks to 20 weeks you know they’re just trying to get something better than before you know they’re trying to fight for to make some headway and they did they made it because they were there and they fought for it and he had a member of his congregation that had that adopted a child and she called him and said you won’t believe what happened. The girl that had this baby went to get an abortion but could not because of the 20-week law. And she was just thanking him so much and I mean it’s powerful.
Are people losing jobs for their beliefs about marriage?

He shares reports from speakers who said they lost a commentator job or a television show over their stance on natural marriage, and says “I’m just a witness here.” He says the brothers had to decide whether to cave in and be moderate or stand for what is right, and that every speaker had articles written attacking them.
Are people losing jobs for their beliefs about marriage?

And here you have this life that would have been killed. And then of course we had Craig James and the Benham brothers Craig James ran for senator and uh. During his senate race he said that he believes in natural marriage and he does not believe in same-sex marriage and uh you know years later he was he was asked by Fox Sports sports to come and be a commentator. And uh they found out about his stance and they said see you later right Mr. Thompson yes they kicked him out and so he was there and again we have someone else who’s being kicked out and I’m just sharing what they’re bringing up okay I’m just a witness here these are not my opinions these are actual things that are happening to people and of course you got the Benham brothers I don’t know if you guys heard about them but they were. Starting a show with HDTV. About I’m not sure real estate or properties I’m not sure but because of their stance their show was canceled because they were being pressured by homosexual activists to shut the show up now what you don’t hear a lot is that these guys had a moment. Where they. We’re deciding what side to be on. These guys were deciding the the brothers were deciding you know here we are trying to spread the good news through this good show about our good families you know raising up good kids and be an example light that way but maybe God has something different in mind so these guys had to decide are we going to cave in and say it’s okay say you know that’s all right you know and just be moderate or are we gonna stand for what’s right so they got with Mr. Perkins the Family Research Council and they. They found out what to say and they they stood they said you know we had to be like David we had I can’t remember their analogy it was good it was good these guys their father is a preacher their father is a pastor and he speaks out on a lot of issues and their father called them up and said what are you guys doing. Talking like that you love this you love that come on you gotta you gotta stand up for what’s right. And so they had to come to a decision. So it was very encouraging and these guys were willing to talk to a group of less than a hundred fifty people at times it was very small. I I mean all these speakers were very good.
What did the conference say about separation of church and state?

He reports a speaker who answered pastors’ excuses, such as “it’s a political issue,” by saying the gospel is to change. He says separation of church and state came from people persecuted by a state church, so the state would not intervene with the church, and quotes “let’s not be politically correct but biblically correct.”
What did the conference say about separation of church and state?

First class I was looking up each one as they came up I was looking up their names online and all of them have articles written about them just attacking them. They’re on the front lines. And then uh the best speaker of that night was Mr. Raphael Cruz. And he is the father of Ted Cruz he’s the senator of Texas. And. He basically. Brought a message out. Saying that basically I thought I was here at church again you know he brought out secular humanism second and bringing up the history and showing us I was like who am I listening to here. It sounds very familiar. And he was calling out the pastor’s excuses what kind of excuses do we have and he said these are the excuses I get God just called me to share the gospel and he said what is the gospel. And he went and showed through the you know he showed us the gospel is to change. That’s what the gospel is about. He gets other uh excuses it’s a political issue. And he just made it so plain I have a recording on my little phone that I made and it’s hard to hear it uh it’s very low but if you have a way to bump it up it was a very good very good message. And he brought up separation of church and state and as we know we’ve learned in this church we know what that is all about and he plainly brought it out you’re sitting there and you’re saying wow you know the he just said plainly they came from a place where they were being persecuted where the the church of England was telling them what to do and they didn’t want that same thing here in America and when he brought it out that way you just say yeah of course. He said separation of church and state because you don’t want the state intervening with the church. One of his statements was let’s not be politically correct but biblically correct. And he brought out Mr. Charles Wesley that says. If there’s a problem if righteousness is. Going down if there’s a moral there’s a moral decline in America the pulpit is responsible just a call to the pastors to to buck up. Wake up we can’t be teaching what we’re teaching right now it can’t be about that anymore we’ve got to stand. And uh I just you know it hit me.
What did the handouts teach about marriage and the family?

He says being asked to share made him check what was true rather than give his opinion. He shows free pamphlets on the Bible’s teaching on marriage and the family, harms of same-sex marriage, and who should decide how children are educated, and says they echo what the church has heard.
What did the handouts teach about marriage and the family?

And then of course we have Mr. Perkins and he is the president of the Family Research Council. And uh I just want to share let me see here. No okay. I I. You know when Mr. Kincer asked me to come and share about this group all of a sudden it hits you okay I have to make sure that I’m sharing truth. I can’t just give you my opinion you know and I start to understand Mr. Kincer’s you go away from these things and it’s like well I’ve got to prove things I got to know what’s right I can’t just take what they’re telling me and so I had to look a lot of these guys up and I looked up Mr. Perkins and he was interviewed on Chris Matthews’s show and and was talking with Barney Frank and and he did not back down he said no he it was very good you guys need to look up some of his interviews. The problem is they won’t let him talk he doesn’t get to say much but I want to show. Mr. Kincer is not the only one that has pamphlets on these things. So here’s this one’s called the Bible’s teaching on marriage and the family and basically it talks about the Bible and why homosexual same-sex marriage is wrong homosexuality is wrong there you go debating homosexuality. And let me let me remind you he’s a lot more he’s very diplomatic. All right. You know our pamphlets are not diplomatic. He’s very diplomatic and I’m going to ask Mr. Kincer to read some of these to see if he’s just too diplomatic and then this one is very good it’s the top 10 harms. Of same-sex marriage he’s willing to say that it’s harmful he’s willing to say these are harmful things that come from that lifestyle and he’s saying you know we you guys we can’t just just believe this idea that people are born that way there’s no scientific evidence there’s no scientific this and that stuff we’ve heard here all all day all night there you go.
