Who should ch who should decide how children are educated and again I thought I was listening to Mr. Kincer about Horace Mann John Dewey it’s all in here. Saying that there’s no competition that’s what it says in here who wrote this Tony Perkins not Mr. Kincer. It was good this one I didn’t read sorry I can’t tell anything about that. But this is what they believe. It’s powerful. And I gotta come and I gotta share you know you learn a lot by what they write what they’re trying to put out and they’re actually trying to stand against these things they’re actually trying to be a voice it’s very good. Now there is an urgency in this meeting these people were basically begging us begging pastors begging church people.
Why does he say Christians need to get involved?

He says the speakers were begging pastors and church people to get involved, and he was convicted because he was not helping. He notes they asked for no money, and says a large church pastor nearby with a message titled “we must obey God rather than men” shows “we’re not alone” and we must unite.
Why does he say Christians need to get involved?

Begging us we need to get involved. We need. You know here you have all these famous people Tony Perkins he goes to Washington DC and he will lobby he will he will talk he will bring a case before the United States capital. And you know for me I’m convicted because I have you know I’m not helping anybody do that I’m not getting involved. And I just got to think to myself what am I doing. Now all of these things that they handed out were free they didn’t charge me for anything they didn’t ask for money at all. The food was free I I want to send them money just for the food at least. But they didn’t ask for money and I thought that was very commendable they didn’t ask you know for your 25 or buy this book no they didn’t ask that I said can I have some of these pamphlets they said take all you want. Now I want to bring up this guy I missed his message but the title of his message on the paper was we must obey God rather than men and this is important because Jack [unclear] is a pastor of Calvary Chapel Chino Hills and this is in southern California as you know and this is important because he’s a pastor I’m sorry he’s got the church there is about ten thousand people. So church. If you’ve had this idea. In your heart that no nobody’s willing to stand nobody is willing you know no big pastor’s willing to stand there’s people that are doing it and we’re not alone. Uh we just got to unite we’ve just got to come together. She he had commission or he has employed somebody not imply I’m not sure if he employed but he has someone that fights. On a regular basis a department a you know. Someone dedicated to fighting against prop- or fighting for Prop 8, fighting against SB 48 or what is it SB what what is it do we know the one where they’re teaching in the schools that homosexuality history and all that that was approved whatever anyway he’s fighting against that. And he’s very political from what I hear. So we have here a pastor in our very close by that is standing for these things. And I’m just sharing that with you I didn’t hear his message but you can tell by the title we must obey God rather than men that he’s hitting home.
Why does he say Christians need to get involved?
Acts 5:29: But Peter and the other apostles answered and said: “We ought to obey God rather than men.
What testimony did the fired fire chief share?

He retells a speaker’s testimony of growing up poor, wanting to be a husband and father, living by Bible standards and rising to a top fire administration post, then being fired after 34 years over a book that called same-sex marriage a sin. He calls it bullying that takes away freedom of speech.
What testimony did the fired fire chief share?

And one of the another great speaker. I’m a three quarter of the way three quarters away done I’m I want to be admitted a witness we’re talking about two days here okay I am summarizing it down in about you know 20 minutes 10 30 minutes. And uh here we have Kelvin Cochran. And if you were to hear this guy’s testimony you would cry. His testimony was that he he grew up and you have to hear him say it he says we we grew up poor with my mother and my father and when my father left my mother we weren’t just poor we were pole we couldn’t afford the we couldn’t afford the o and the r anymore. We would have mayonnaise sandwiches my mom can only afford to buy mayonnaise and bread and syrup. And I’m like how do you live on that they would have mayonnaise sandwiches anyway you got to hear this guy’s mess this testimony. And. He would go to church they were part of a church and he would see the nice the nice mom and dads and their fancy cars their shiny cars get out and he said. He would say the the church people would ask him what do you want to be when you grow up and he would say I want to be a husband I want to be a father because that was to him a goal to reach to because he didn’t have a dad he didn’t and he said I don’t want to be poor. And so they gave him some standards from the Bible to live by and he says I’ve been living by these standards for a long time and it I was. I became the first black man to be in the fire department. And he was promoted very quickly and he was appointed by president Obama to have the highest fire administration position in America. All right the highest position Kelvin Cochran. But he had written a book in 1992. Where he says he does not agree he does not agree with same-sex marriage he calls it a sin he calls it wrong. And I’m going to read you a quote. And this is his quote I was fired for having the audacity to believe that sex was created for procreation and should be in the bonds of holy matrimony between a man and a woman. And after 34 years of faithful service to the community he was fired from his job and I don’t know if he’s. Been reinstated at Atlanta or I’m not sure but he was released fired from his job and see that puts fear that’s such that’s such bullying. You’re not allowed to have an opinion you’re not allowed your freedom of speech. And they said that he was distributing books and of course they want to twist that. You know it’s not like he was going around his communist workplace and say you need to read this book no he wasn’t doing that. But somebody was offended. By his book and he was fired. And. When you’re there.
What if these attacks are not happening to me?

He reports the warning that by the time it hits you, you won’t be able to get involved, and says that convicted him because it was exactly his attitude. He tells of a former candidate who stayed away from hard issues until he heard a man preach, and says the message was “we’ve got to stand, we’ve got to unite.”
What if these attacks are not happening to me?

When you’re there it’s a lot different. You know. This man my brother. Is being attacked. And then we have Rick Scarborough. And basically what he brought out was. Reminding us that reminding me he’s saying since these things aren’t happening to you guys you know you hear the story of this you hear the story of that and it’s not happening to you so you don’t get involved. But when it hits by the time it hits you you won’t be able to get involved. And because it’s not happening to me it’s okay and that convicted me because that’s exactly my attitude it wasn’t happening to me so I’m just gonna live on my merry way. And at the end Mr. Rick Santorum was there and like I said this is a group of 50. Less than 100 and it would dwindle and you know small group and this man came. He ran for president I don’t know if you guys know that but willing to speak and he shared some very powerful things about his testimony. In the middle of his career he. Changed. At the beginning he said I knew what issues to stay away from I knew to stay away from same-sex marriage I knew you know it’s not hard to see danger stay away from that you know he was he was completely moderate but then he said I went to a church service heard a man preach. And the truth hit me. And he changed. And basically what he’s doing what he’s saying is. I’m begging you people. We’ve got to stand. We’ve got to unite. He said America needs you. And I’m just trying to be a witness this morning what what happened what they were saying the gist of their messages. And uh I want to share something real quickly from their website the Family Research Council their website. And uh just to give you an understanding says tony has a tremendous burden to reclaim the culture of for Christ and believes that this revival will begin in the churches across America and reach across denominations.
Who are my brothers and sisters, according to Jesus?

He reads Matthew 12:48-50, “whoever does the will of my father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother,” and says God told him those people are his brothers and sisters. From First Corinthians 12:26 he says if one member suffers, all suffer, and he feels responsible because they are fighting alone.
Who are my brothers and sisters, according to Jesus?

Racial and economic lines and build on shared values of family and freedom now to me that sounds very familiar. We have been hearing that we need to unite. With other churches no matter their denomination. People that are for morality Bible morality. And unite for the cause. Now if you have your bibles I’d ask you to turn to Matthew [unclear] 12:48. It says in the scriptures here but he answered and said to the one who told him who is my mother and who are my brothers. And he stretched out his hand toward his disciples and said here are my mother and my brothers. For whoever does the will of my father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother. And God just put that on my heart. And he said Mike you know those people are your brothers. They’re your sisters. Do you care about what’s happening to them. You know in a brotherhood and in a family if somewhere to mess with Christina and Stephanie and Joe. I would be going to their aid. And these guys are standing for right principles. And they’re just it seems like they don’t have the support they need from the church. And I was convicted in my heart just saying church. Here these men are brothers and they’ve got to fight it all by themselves. And I feel responsible. As they are my brothers. First Corinthians chapter 12 verse 26. Says if one member suffers all the members suffer with it if one member is honored all the members rejoice with it. Mr. Cruz he brought out the scripture that when the righteous are in authority the people rejoice. And it was powerful you know we need to get involved you know there was no question about getting involved or the Satan has authority in in in political areas we shouldn’t be involved no that that was out of the out of the question. Now are you now you are the body of Christ and members individually.
Who are my brothers and sisters, according to Jesus?

Matthew 12:48-50: But He answered and said to the one who told Him, “Who is My mother and who are My brothers?” And He stretched out His hand toward His disciples and said, “Here are My mother and My brothers! For whoever does the will of My Father in heaven is My brother and sister and mother.” 1 Corinthians 12:26-27: And if one member suffers, all the members suffer with it; or if one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it. Now you are the body of Christ, and members individually. Proverbs 29:2: When the righteous are in authority, the people rejoice; But when a wicked man rules, the people groan.
Why does Jesus’ prayer for unity in John 17 matter?

He reads John 17:11 and 17:21-23, “that they all may be one,” and says God told him we need to be united in the spirit, not just the letter. Then the pastor says he is glad the member could experience other people saying what the church has been saying for 30 years.
Why does Jesus’ prayer for unity in John 17 matter?

And John 17 this is really what God was speaking to me. Later I got the other verses regarding your brother because it’s true they are our brothers. In John 17 verse we’ll start with eleven turn with me to John 17 verse 11. Now I am no longer in the world but these are in the world and have come to you I’ve come to you. Holy father keep through your name those whom you have given me that they may be one as we are. And I’ve been taught as a young person that the unity is so important to unite with other churches unite with other denominations. But it’s really hitting me. We’ve got to unite. And. They had a a form to fill out where you write down and you commit and you say I’m gonna unite or not unite I’m gonna do these three things. And God hit me he said. Michael we need to be united in the spirit. The same spirit needs to burn in every person’s heart in every church. Not just the letter not just verbally the spirit has to be united. And I’m trying to translate the effect. That this event had. How important it is. John 17 verse 21. That they all may be one as you father are in me and I in you and they also may be one in us that the world may believe that you sent me. I in them and you and me that you that they may be made perfect. In one. Perfect complete. Okay. I’m glad Michael can go back there and experience this for. I’ve listened to most of those messages. From the conference it’s nothing new for me. But I’m glad Mike got to experience these other people saying what we’ve been saying for 30 years all right.
Why does Jesus’ prayer for unity in John 17 matter?

John 17:11: Now I am no longer in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to You. Holy Father, keep through Your name those whom You have given Me, that they may be one as We are. John 17:21-23: that they all may be one, as You, Father, are in Me, and I in You; that they also may be one in Us, that the world may believe that You sent Me. And the glory which You gave Me I have given them, that they may be one just as We are one: I in them, and You in Me; that they may be made perfect in one, and that the world may know that You have sent Me, and have loved them as You have loved Me.
Should Christians stay silent because it is the end time?

The pastor says no matter how small we are, we cannot justify being silent and not getting involved with what is going on in America. He says these things are supposed to happen, but that does not mean we stop preaching the gospel and sit on the sideline, and that America needs a message of hope, not despair.
Should Christians stay silent because it is the end time?

Now. We do and I am looking forward that’s why I’m sitting back I’m looking for a grassroots organization. That we can unite with that is throughout America. It saves a lot of time when you don’t have to start your own from scratch. And I’ve been following this group and some other groups for quite some time. But anyway just let me admonish. That no matter how small we are. We cannot justify. Being silent and not getting involved with what’s going on in America. Let me just share a couple of scriptures with you real quick David. All right these people are always saying we’re at the end time oh you know Jesus is coming any minute and uh all this trouble and all this plagues and everything you can be seated if you’d like. You know these things are supposed to happen and all this and that’s true I say you’re right they’re supposed to happen. But that doesn’t mean we stop preaching the gospel and living right and taken a seat on the sideline and watching the destruction of the world when way can have an effect. And God spoke to me in the year in this thing that America needs to hear a message of hope. Not a message of despair and destruction and it’s the end they need a message of hope illustration number one David was an adolescent young man.
What does David and Goliath teach about hope?

He says Goliath was the propaganda voice for the Philistines and Israel’s army hid, until a teenager, David, asked who he thought he was to speak against God. He says David cut off the head, the army rose up and drove the Philistines out, and “one person brought unity because one person brought hope.”
What does David and Goliath teach about hope?

The Philistine army had come. To oppose Israel and invade Israel and destroy Israel. And a big giant named Goliath nine and a half foot tall came out every day and defied that army and to find God’s people and he was the propaganda voice for the Philistines. And when he started speaking as I said before the Israel marines hid behind the rocks. The Israel army went home. And the militias left scared to death their knees knocking they won’t do anything. They didn’t run home they didn’t hide behind the rock it they aren’t doing anything and little David comes up an adolescent young man a teenager. He heard this guy and said who is he think he is. Speaking against God and God’s people. And as you know the story David went out and cut the head off that’s important. You cut the head off you destroy the whole organization right you get to the leaders and the rest of the organization crumbles. Understand we got to go right to the heads of these these opposing groups. We’ve got to go right after them you understand that. If we stop the leaders we stop the movement. When David. Felled that giant [unclear] the militia. They rose up started fighting the marines got out from behind the rocks and they started fighting in the army heard about it on the other side of the Jordan and back home where they went and they came back and they drove those Philistines out of the country.
What does David and Goliath teach about hope?

1 Samuel 17:45-51: Then David said to the Philistine, “You come to me with a sword, with a spear, and with a javelin. But I come to you in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied. This day the LORD will deliver you into my hand, and I will strike you and take your head from you. And this day I will give the carcasses of the camp of the Philistines to the birds of the air and the wild beasts of the earth, that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel. Then all this assembly shall know that the LORD does not save with sword and spear; for the battle is the LORD’s, and He will give you into our hands.” So it was, when the Philistine arose and came and drew near to meet David, that David hurried and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine. Then David put his hand in his bag and took out a stone; and he slung it and struck the Philistine in his forehead, so that the stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the earth. So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and a stone, and struck the Philistine and killed him. But there was no sword in the hand of David. Therefore David ran and stood over the Philistine, took his sword and drew it out of its sheath and killed him, and cut off his head with it. And when the Philistines saw that their champion was dead, they fled.
Why did God tell Paul not to be afraid in Corinth?

He says the Jews in Corinth opposed and abused Paul, but Jesus told him not to be afraid and to preach, because he had many people in that city, so Paul preached there a year and a half. He says God is telling this church there are many in Elsinore and in California on his side who need a message of hope.
Why did God tell Paul not to be afraid in Corinth?

See one person brought unity because one person brought hope. And an adolescent. Saul second illustration. He went to Corinth. He preached Christ crucified he was the messiah the anointed one to come the Jews didn’t like it. Corinth was a merchant city and the Jews [unclear] and it’s Bible we’re supposed to you know there’s nothing wrong with that and so they’re there but they didn’t want Paul coming in and saying the messiah has come because they were teaching he hadn’t come he’s still going to come and the Jews are still saying it today. And so not only didn’t they like the message and not respond to the message but they opposed Paul and abused Paul. And God Jesus came to Paul. And said Paul. Don’t you be afraid of these people. He said you preach my gospel I have many in this city. And Paul. Dropped away his fear. Preached the gospel. For a year and a half at Corinth. Until God moved him on and that’s the message God is saying to this church there are many people in Elsinore. That are on my side but they need a message of hope they need instruction they need someone tell them this is the way walking in it they need someone united there’s many people in California as bad as California is and leading the nation in wickedness.
Why did God tell Paul not to be afraid in Corinth?

Acts 18:9-11: Now the Lord spoke to Paul in the night by a vision, “Do not be afraid, but speak, and do not keep silent; for I am with you, and no one will attack you to hurt you; for I have many people in this city.” And he continued there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
Who has authority over the nations?
He reports the speakers’ message that America does not belong to Satan, because Jesus Christ said all authority has been given to him, over all the nations.
Were believers from other churches welcomed at the conference?
He says the atmosphere was “we want everyone” who believes in Christ and believes in freedom, including people from other traditions, and a very charismatic woman was never corrected.
He says maybe others interpret righteousness differently, but “we know where righteousness is”: right living, living the right way.
Who is responsible when morals decline?
He reports a quote that if there is a moral decline in America the pulpit is responsible, which he calls a call to pastors to wake up and stand.
Why did he check what the speakers said?
He says being asked to share made him realize he had to share truth, not just his opinion, so he had to prove things and look the speakers up instead of just taking what they said.
Did the conference ask for money?
He says the handouts and food were free and they never asked for money, which he thought very commendable.
What kind of unity does God want among churches?
He says God told him “we need to be united in the spirit,” with the same spirit burning in every church, not just the letter or words.
Is the church planning to join with others?
The pastor says he is looking for a grassroots organization throughout America to unite with, because it saves time not to start your own from scratch.
If Jesus is coming soon, should we stop trying to change things?

The pastor says these things are supposed to happen, but that does not mean we stop preaching the gospel and living right and take a seat on the sideline watching the destruction when we can have an effect.
Why does he point out that David cut off Goliath’s head?
He says when you cut the head off you destroy the whole organization; if we stop the leaders we stop the movement, so we must go right to the heads of opposing groups.
What does he say California needs?
He says there are many people in California, as bad as it is, who are on God’s side but need a message of hope, instruction and someone to tell them “this is the way.”

items.d: In “Cruel and Unusual Punishments,” Pastor David G. Kincer quotes the Supreme Court’s 1958 “evolving standards of decency” line, reviews U.S. penalties (prison, parole, probation, restitution, fines, death)…
items.ser: Clarity on Crucial Choices · Full sermon
p: In “Cruel and Unusual Punishments,” Pastor David G. Kincer quotes the Supreme Court’s 1958 “evolving standards of decency” line, reviews U.S. penalties (prison, parole, probation, restitution, fines, death), and contrasts Bible restitution, stripes, limited servitude, refuge cities and death for murder—with no OT prisons. He argues some modern sentences are unusually light for violent crimes named in the transcript, and from 1 Timothy and Deuteronomy that punishment should be public so others fear and turn from evil.
What did the Supreme Court say about cruel and unusual punishment in 1958?

He quotes that the Eighth Amendment must draw its meaning from the evolving standards of decency of a maturing society, and tells of a half-day deserter who lost citizenship—the Court called that cruel and unusual for that crime.
What did the Supreme Court say about cruel and unusual punishment in 1958?

Today we’re going to look at the issue of the Eighth Amendment of the Constitution: what is cruel and unusual punishment? What is cruel and unusual punishment that the Constitution says we cannot punish people with? The Supreme Court in 1958 made this statement: the Eighth Amendment must draw its meaning from the evolving standards of decency that mark the progress of a maturing society. A soldier had deserted for half a day, came back, turned himself in; he was sent to the brig, he was discharged with an undesirable discharge, and then they took his citizenship away. And the Supreme Court said no—the Eighth Amendment—that is cruelty and that is an unusual severe punishment for that crime. So remember they said this statement: the Eighth Amendment must draw its meaning from the evolving standards
What punishments does he say America uses?
He lists prison (about 2.3 million), parole (800,000+), probation (2.5 million), restitution (which he doubts is really collected), and community service at a charity for so many hours.
What punishments does he say America uses?

of a progressing mature society. In America we have several punishments. We have prison, and we have 2.3 million people in prison, and we have eight-tenths of a million—800,000 or more—on parole from prison. And then we have the probation: you know, first-timer, we’ll put you on probation, you know, you just check in with us and be a nice guy. Two and a half million are on probation in America. Then you have restitution. And honestly, all the people I know, I have never heard one of them thieves having to pay back even what they stole plus the loan added to it, so I don’t know about this one, but they say it’s a law. Community service: so you pick your charity, you did a bad thing like some famous people do, so you pick a charity and you go work in that charity for so many hours—that is your punishment.
How often is the death penalty used, in his figures?

He puts a question mark on it: 15,000 murders in 2014 and only 35 executions—doesn’t sound carried out in a progressive mature society. Bible civil penalties he lists: restitution, fines, and at most 40 stripes.
How often is the death penalty used, in his figures?

Then you have fines where you pay a dollar amount for your punishment and then you’re just free to go. And then you have the death penalty—and I got a question mark there, because there were 15,000 murders in 2014 and only 35 people were executed with the death penalty. Doesn’t sound like it’s carried out in this progressive and a decent mature society. Civil punishments in the Bible: we have restitution; you have fines when you have a dispute with your neighbor, an argument or a court contest over something, and the loser has to pay a fine; and then you have beatings of 40 at the most stripes, okay.
Does Bible “servitude” mean slavery, in his teaching?

He says no: debtors hired themselves out up to six years to pay bills—not slavery. Refuge cities protected accidental killers from the avenger of blood until trial. Courts could beat bullies (39 stripes to stay under 40).
Does Bible “servitude” mean slavery, in his teaching?

So everybody beat 39 times so they didn’t go over the mark. And that was over a physical dispute: you’re a bully, you’re going around beating up 11-, 12-, 13-, 14-year-old guys and you’re 18, 19, 20, or your threesome in your little group is beating up people in the community—then the courts can beat you. All right. Servitude is very misunderstood in the Bible. Everybody that attacks the Bible says that slavery—that is not slavery. That is: you went into debt, or you had a bad business adventure, you couldn’t pay your bills, so you went and hired yourself out to someone for six years, or in that period of six years, to pay off that debt. It couldn’t last any more than six years, so it’s not slavery at all. Refuge cities were for people who accidentally killed someone: your axe handle, your axe flew off and hurt your neighbor and killed him, and so you could run to the city of refuge so the avenger of blood, the family, couldn’t come and kill you until you had a trial and found innocent.
What counts as cruel and unusual in the Bible?

He says the OT has no prison sentences—dealt with that day. Cruel examples: death for theft, death without trial by a mob, and torture (totally forbidden). Jail today is like a city of refuge until trial.
What counts as cruel and unusual in the Bible?

And then you had murder and you had the death penalty. And over here we have little symbols of that: death penalty was carried out by stoning or a sword; this is the whipping lash; and a jail is our city of refuge today—you go to jail to protect you from people and protect society from you until you’ve had a trial and found guilty. There are no prisons in the Old Testament laws—no prison sentences at all. Everything was dealt with that day, at that time, at that moment, and done and decided. So cruel and unusual punishment in the Bible would be death for a theft: you kill a person because they steal your horse—the Bible would say that was cruel and unusual punishment for that crime. Death without a trial: the mob, they accuse you of something, they think you’re guilty, and they just take you and they hang you and they stone you—that’s cruel and unusual in the Bible. Torture is totally forbidden in the Bible—no torture at all. False witness:
What happened to false witnesses, and what modern cases does he raise?

False witnesses received the penalty they sought for the accused. He then turns to on-screen modern crime cases (named in the transcript) that he says show offenders back in society harming the innocent.
What happened to false witnesses, and what modern cases does he raise?

they were examined, and if they were found to be a false witness, what they’ve brought that person to court for was done to them. If they brought that person to court to be stoned, then they were stoned. So you didn’t want to get in that court as a false witness. Now, cruel and unusual punishment—up on your screen is John Cooey. He’s age 46. He’s been arrested 24 times for drug violations. He’s a habitual user of crack cocaine. He’s been arrested for burglary, concealed weapons, disorderly intoxication, disorderly exposure, disorderly conduct under the influence of alcohol and drugs, driving. He committed fraud. He had some insufficient funds. He was charged with larceny, and his driver’s license had been suspended for 99 years. He had been arrested twice for fondling and abusing children, sexually abusing children. Okay. He was high on cocaine one day. He goes into the trailer in the same park and gets this girl out, age nine, Jessica.
Why does he ask why offenders were back in society?

After describing violent crimes against children and teens (details in the transcript), he asks why the offender was free to harm an innocent girl, and notes another offender got probation then short sentences after repeat rapes.
Why does he ask why offenders were back in society?

Takes her to his trailer where his sister and her lover lived—and you can see all three of them are on drugs. I mean, come on, anybody can tell something’s wrong there. And he rapes this nine-year-old girl, tore her vagina from the rape, put her in a closet to stay there all day without food till he got home. And my point is this: why was he back in society to harm this innocent girl? Secondly, we got Josh up there. He got a teenage girl drunk, 13 years old, intoxicated, and raped her, and he was given probation. Two years later, after he got off probation, he got a 14-year-old girl drunk and raped her, and he served one year.
What sentences does he call unusual for the crime?

He says three years for a pattern of getting girls drunk and raping them is an unusual punishment for a very bad crime, and the cruelty falls on the victim—including one buried alive (case named in the transcript).
What sentences does he call unusual for the crime?

Well, after he got out, he got a 16-year-old girl drunk and raped her, and unbelievably he got three years in prison. He was sentenced at three years in prison. I tell you that is an unusual punishment for a very bad crime. And the cruelty is to the young girl who lost her life. He took her and he put her in plastic bags and buried her alive. That was John Cooley. He buried her alive. Melinda Loveless—she’s 16 years old. She is a homosexual lady teenager. And she loved the girl
What other violent cases does he cite as under-punished?

He recounts a jealous teen torture-murder over a same-sex relationship and a rape-mutilation case that received eight years (names and details in the transcript), asking if that is maturing-society decency.
What other violent cases does he cite as under-punished?

up on your screen there, Shanda. And they had sexual relationships. That girl was 12 years old. Melinda is 16 years old. Well, Shanda switched partners and went to have sex with a 14-year-old girl, and Melinda got jealous, talked to her friends into luring her out of her home at midnight, took her to a place and beat her with her fist, beat her with a tire iron, shoved that tire iron up her anus, beat her over the head some more, tried to choke her—this was over an eight-hour period—tried to choke her to death. She passed out and then came back. They beat her more with the tire iron.
Is light sentencing the “decency” of a maturing society?
He asks whether treating the criminal with such decency that serious crime has no real penalty is the direction the Court says we are heading, and notes one victim survived after hikers found her.
Is light sentencing the “decency” of a maturing society?

And then she went home and her parents were there, with this girl in the trunk of her car out in the yard, and finally put gasoline on this girl and burned her to death. She died from the burning. Lawrence Singleton. Mary Vincent was having car trouble. This guy stopped and offered her a ride to the gas station and so forth, took her to a secluded place, raped her repeatedly, and then took an axe and cut off her arms. And he got eight years. Now, for that kind of cruel crime, is this the decency of a maturing society?
What is the Bible purpose of punishment?
From 1 Timothy 5:20, rebuke sinners before all that others may fear. From Deuteronomy 17:12, put away evil so all hear and fear and do no more presumptuously.
What is the Bible purpose of punishment?

Is this the direction we’re going, where the criminal is treated with such decency that there is no real penalty for a serious crime? Is this—for the Supreme Court says we are heading—two hikers came by. She was walking with her hands up trying to keep the bleeding down. Just happened two hikers came by and took the girl to the hospital, and she’s alive today. Purpose of punishment: 1 Timothy 5:20, them that sin rebuke before all, that others also may fear. Deuteronomy 17:12: you shall put away the evil from Israel; all the people will hear and fear and do no more presumptuously.
What is the Bible purpose of punishment?

1 Timothy 5:20: Those who are sinning rebuke in the presence of all, that the rest also may fear. Deuteronomy 17:12: Now the man who acts presumptuously and will not heed the priest who stands to minister there before the LORD your God, or the judge, that man shall die. So you shall put away the evil from Israel.
What does he call cruel and unusual punishment today?

From Deuteronomy 19:19 he says punishment should be publicized to deter. Cruel and unusual, to him, is authorities not punishing and publicizing, not informing citizens of destructive results, and missing morals and self-control—the puzzle piece—not decency.
What does he call cruel and unusual punishment today?

So penalizing is for deterring crime. Deuteronomy 19:19: put evil away from your midst, and those that remain shall hear and fear and shall from henceforth commit no more such evil. Punishment is to be publicized, to be public, to cause those that are coming up behind to stay away from a life of crime. Now, cruel and unusual punishment is civil authorities not discouraging future criminals by punishing present criminals and publicizing it; civil authorities not informing uninformed citizens of immoral behaviors’ destructive and life-ending results; and the conclusion that no morals, no knowledge of morals, lack of self-control is the missing social puzzle piece in America. And it is not decency when we do not punish the criminal for the proper crime.
What does he call cruel and unusual punishment today?
Deuteronomy 19:19: then you shall do to him as he thought to have done to his brother; so you shall put away the evil from among you.
He quotes the 1958 Court: the Eighth Amendment must draw its meaning from the evolving standards of decency that mark the progress of a maturing society.
How many people does he say are in prison or on supervision?
About 2.3 million in prison, 800,000+ on parole, and 2.5 million on probation.
He says the Bible allows at most 40 stripes, so they beat 39 so they didn’t go over the mark.
What were cities of refuge for?
For someone who accidentally killed another (axe head flying off) so the avenger of blood couldn’t kill them before a trial.
Were there prisons in Old Testament law?
He says no prison sentences at all; everything was dealt with that day, at that time, and decided.
He says torture is totally forbidden in the Bible—no torture at all.
What penalty did a false witness get?
Whatever penalty they sought for the accused was done to them—if they sought stoning, they were stoned.
Why rebuke before all, per 1 Timothy 5:20?
So that others also may fear.
Yes. From Deuteronomy he says those that remain shall hear and fear and commit no more such evil; punishment should cause those coming up to stay away from crime.
What does he call the missing social puzzle piece?
No morals, no knowledge of morals, and lack of self-control—and it is not decency when we do not punish the criminal for the proper crime.

items.d: In “Deflective Defective Disciples Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer says many of Jesus’ disciples in John 6 left because they wanted what they could get rather than what they could give, and he applies that to…
p: In “Deflective Defective Disciples Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer says many of Jesus’ disciples in John 6 left because they wanted what they could get rather than what they could give, and he applies that to prosperity preaching and other teaching he calls fractured. He plays recorded clips of public figures and ministers speaking about heaven, other religions and sin, and responds to them. Whose faith should we have: our own, our group’s, or Jesus’s?

Now, we have over here: faith, my faith, my faith, anything I choose, is I’m convinced of, I’m right. All right. Over on the left you got Jesus’s faith. Jesus’s faith is in the scriptures. See, when the rich man came to Jesus and said, “Well, what must I do to have eternal life?” he says, “What does the scripture say?” [Editor’s note: in Luke the question “What is written in the law?” is put to a lawyer (Luke 10:25-26); the rich ruler of Luke 18:18 is answered with the commandments.] See, Jesus’s faith was in the word of God and in the Father. He said, “I do nothing except what the Father tells me to do.” See, Jesus’s faith was in the Father, and it was in the scriptures. Over here, my faith, what I believe, I can come up with any concocted ideal I want to. For instance, like [unclear] Hindus go to heaven. That’s what he said in his interview. He was in India, and, oh, those are nice people, and they’re going to heaven also. There’s Buddhists in India, they’re going to heaven. All right, the Muslims and the Mormons are going to heaven. See, that’s what they said: my faith, I believe they’re going to heaven. Well, that’s wonderful, but what does this side say? Are you getting the picture now? The Catholics, the Protestants and the Jews all come up with the— they all have some weird doctrines, and the problem with these groups is their faith is in their group. Catholics really believe, because they’re Catholics, most of them, they’re going to go to heaven. Their faith is in the Catholic church. But so are Protestants. Baptists, their faith is in the Baptist; Pentecostal, their faith is in the Pentecostal. Your faith has to be in Jesus Christ and his word. Are you hearing me? Your faith cannot be in your faith. Your faith has to be in his faith.
Whose faith should we have: our own, our group’s, or Jesus’s?

Luke 10:25-26: And behold, a certain lawyer stood up and tested Him, saying, “Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?” He said to him, “What is written in the law? What is your reading of it?” John 5:19: Then Jesus answered and said to them, “Most assuredly, I say to you, the Son can do nothing of Himself, but what He sees the Father do; for whatever He does, the Son also does in like manner.
He says they deflected because they had a defect. He says a disciple is one that’s disciplined, a pupil and follower of Christ, and he says not everybody in the Bible turned out to be heroes.
Can you decide to serve God on your own?

He says no: Jesus said the Father and he have to be involved in your conversion and salvation. He says it is not joining a church or being a Jew, Protestant or Catholic, and that the Spirit of God has to be involved.
What does he say eternal life means?

He says a couple of weeks earlier they learned that eternal life is to know God and Jesus Christ, not just live forever. He says the disciples who stayed had experienced God being involved in their salvation, and that it is not a hand-me-down Christianity.
What does God want us to give him?

He says God wants a Bible morality lifestyle: living right and stopping sinning. He says praise is wonderful and prayer is wonderful, but what God wants back from you is for you to live right, no matter if you are a Catholic, a Jew or a Protestant.
Why does he say the crowd followed Jesus in John 6?

He says they followed him because they saw the signs he performed on those who were diseased, and later because he fed them with the loaves and fishes. He says Jesus told them plainly that they now wanted free food, which he describes as wanting what we can get out of God.
What are the “P’s” he warns against?

He lists prosperity, psychotherapy, Purpose Driven, possibility thinking, positive thinking and individual prophecy. He says these followers are fractured and are deflecting from Christ, wanting something instead of giving him something.
What does he say the Bible calls for instead of therapy and positive thinking?
He says Jesus wants us to give him Bible morality, not grace and faith, prosperity, positive thinking or psychotherapy, and that in the Bible it is self-control: just stop what you’re doing.
What does he say the Mormon church told him about Jesus Christ?

He says he called their headquarters, did not act like somebody else, and asked questions. He says they told him Jesus Christ is not God, is not eternal without a beginning and an end, and did not exist until Mary, and he says the Bible teaches he existed before Mary.
Where does the Bible use the phrase “my faith”?

He says it is found only twice: once where someone says I will show you my faith by my works, and once in Jesus’s words to a church in Revelation, where he says you did not deny my faith. He says the phrase is used in conjunction with lifestyle, not just words.
Do the demons believe in God?

He says the demons believe and they are not going to heaven, they tremble, so saying you believe is not enough. He says what people say they believe is insignificant; it is what God told us to believe that is significant.
What does 1 Corinthians 2:5 say about where our faith should be?

He says it says your faith should not be in the wisdom of men but in the power of God. He says Paul meant that faith cannot be done intellectually: it has to be in the supernatural power of God involved in your life.
What does he say Jesus’s faith was in?
He says Jesus’s faith was in the scriptures and in the Father. He points to Jesus saying he does nothing except what the Father tells him to do.
Can your faith be in your church or denomination?

He says no: the problem with Catholics, Protestants and Jews alike is that their faith is in their group. He says your faith has to be in Jesus Christ and his word, and your faith cannot be in your faith but has to be in his faith.

items.d: In “Deflective Defective Disciples Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer continues the previous message by saying the Bible’s “I believe” statements are about believing Jesus is the Son of God and that God will do…
p: In “Deflective Defective Disciples Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer continues the previous message by saying the Bible’s “I believe” statements are about believing Jesus is the Son of God and that God will do what he said. He argues from Acts and 1 Corinthians that Christians and ministers are meant to judge, reads Revelation 21:8 on who goes to the lake of fire, and criticizes ministers he says flatter people. He points to Jeremiah 3:15 as God’s solution and calls believers to virtue and to speak up.
Do Christians need personal prophecy, and will good people go to heaven without Christ?

Pastor Kincer lists prosperity, positive thinking, possibility, Purpose Driven and psychotherapy thinking, and adds personal prophecy thinking, which he says is a dime a dozen in many Spirit-filled circles. He says he does not need personal prophecy; he needs the Bible, the sure word of prophecy. He says the claim that atheists, humanists and anyone who is good can go to heaven is lying, and that the end result of Jesus’s faith is a disciple pursuing the divine nature and doing good works.
Do Christians need personal prophecy, and will good people go to heaven without Christ?

Adultery, homosexuality, incest, intoxication. Okay, see, “my faith,” “I believe,” nothing’s wrong with it. Prosperity, positive thinking, possibility— you ever met these people that won’t say a negative thing? There: possibility thinking, prosperity thinking, Purpose Driven thinking, psychotherapy thinking, and one I didn’t have up there is this personal prophecy thinking. My gosh. And in a lot of Spirit-filled circles, you know, personal prophecy is just a dime a dozen. Just everybody’s giving out personal prophecies. Where is that in the Bible? They’re just flat out wrong. I don’t need no personal prophecy; I need the book. I need the Bible. Amen. It’s the sure word of prophecy, that’s what the Bible says. Atheist and humanist and everybody’s got their own ideas. And in one of these they talked about atheists, and they said, yeah, everybody can go to heaven. And as Oprah put it, if you’re good— generosity, kindness and love— you can go to heaven no matter what. They’re just lying. Now, over here the end result is a Christian, a disciple of the divine nature. They’re pursuing the divine nature. Hallelujah, because that’s what this faith, Jesus’s faith, whole focus is on: you being a light to the world, living for him by doing good works.
Do Christians need personal prophecy, and will good people go to heaven without Christ?
2 Peter 1:19: And so we have the prophetic word confirmed, which you do well to heed as a light that shines in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts;
Who goes to the lake of fire according to Revelation 21:8, and should preachers challenge sin?

He reads Revelation 21:8 and says it plainly tells who is going to the lake of fire, including the unbelieving, abominable, murderers, sexually immoral, sorcerers, idolaters and all liars. He says homosexuals miss out on two counts, sexual immorality and abomination, and that you cannot change the Bible because you want to be nice to people. He says preachers are not challenging Christians living in sexual immorality, and that America and the homosexual need to hear it so he can get saved and change his ways.
Who goes to the lake of fire according to Revelation 21:8, and should preachers challenge sin?

Now, Revelation 21:8: “The cowardly, the unbelieving, the abominable”— abomination means God hates it, all right— “murderers, sexually immoral, sorcerers,” which is witchcraft, “idolaters, and all liars shall have their part in the lake which burns with fire and brimstone, which is the second death.” And Joel Osteen doesn’t know, and T. D. Jakes doesn’t know, that these people are going to hell, and Rick Warren doesn’t know, and Oprah doesn’t know. It’s very plain in Revelation. This is just one scripture. He tells us plainly who’s going to the lake of fire, and homosexuals miss out on two counts: sexual immorality and abomination. It’s listed under both. Adultery, incest— these sins, will you burn for them? You can’t change the Bible because you want to be nice to people. Can I hear an amen? And Christians are living in sexual immorality and doing all kinds of stupid things, and the preachers aren’t challenging them on Sunday to stop it, and everybody thinks they’re okay. Folks, you can’t change this. Idolatry is an abomination. Idolatry is listed twice up there, under abominations and under idolatry. Are you with me? And all liars: these guys are lying. How many liars go to hell? All of them. Now, folks, this is flagrant lying just so they can get crowds and money. They like the money, man. They live in million-dollar mansions and they drive big cars, and they got all these people coming wanting to hear their flattering messages. And America needs to hear that that’s wrong, and the Christians need to hear, the homosexual needs to hear that he’s wrong, so that he can get saved and change his ways. Can I hear an amen?
Who goes to the lake of fire according to Revelation 21:8, and should preachers challenge sin?

Revelation 21:8: But the cowardly, unbelieving, abominable, murderers, sexually immoral, sorcerers, idolaters, and all liars shall have their part in the lake which burns with fire and brimstone, which is the second death.”
What does “I believe” mean in the Bible?

He says “I believe” is used four times in the passages he reads and every time it means believing that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, the only begotten Son of God, or believing that God will do what he said he would do. He reads the statements in John 11, John 9, Acts 8 and Acts 27, and says that is what “I believe” should say, not that any sin is fine and you can still go to heaven.
What does “I believe” mean in the Bible?

But so, the adulterers. John 11:27, the statement of “I believe”: “I believe you are the Christ, the Son of God, who is to come into the world.” Okay. “I believe” is used four times, and every time it’s used this way. All right: I believe Jesus Christ is the Son of God, the only begotten Son of God. Lucifer is not a begotten Son of God. Lucifer was a created being. Jesus was birthed in the flesh by God. Amen. John 9:35: “Do you believe on the Son of God?” Jesus asked the man. He said, “Who is he, Lord, that I might believe on him?” Jesus said, “You have seen him, and it is he that talks with you.” I’m him, Jesus said. The man quickly says, “I believe.” I believe what? That you are the Son of God, that Jesus is the Son of God. How many believe that Jesus is the only begotten Son of God? Yeah. See, that’s what “I believe” should say: not “I believe homos can go to heaven,” and, “Oh, you know, I can get intoxicated and still go to heaven,” and all the rest. No. Acts 8:37: Philip said, “If you believe with all your heart, you may get baptized,” and the eunuch said, “I believe Jesus Christ is the Son of God.” He said it again. Paul, in Acts 27:25, on the island— or before he got to the island, on the boat: “Be of good cheer, I believe God.” What’s the statement? “I believe God that it shall be as it was told me.” Now, that sums it up: I believe that God will do what he said he would do. Amen. I can’t come up with my own little gizmo doctrines, my feel-good doctrines.
What does “I believe” mean in the Bible?

John 11:27: She said to Him, “Yes, Lord, I believe that You are the Christ, the Son of God, who is to come into the world.” John 9:35-37: Jesus heard that they had cast him out; and when He had found him, He said to him, “Do you believe in the Son of God?” He answered and said, “Who is He, Lord, that I may believe in Him?” And Jesus said to him, “You have both seen Him and it is He who is talking with you.” Acts 8:37: Then Philip said, “If you believe with all your heart, you may.” And he answered and said, “I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.” Acts 27:25: Therefore take heart, men, for I believe God that it will be just as it was told me.
Does the Bible say we should not judge anyone?

He says ministers are supposed to preach the Bible, and the Bible already judges, so telling people they are going to hell is telling them what the Bible said, not judging them himself. He compares it to a doctor who will not tell a patient with cancer he is going to die, and says Paul boldly told the Jews who rejected the word that they had judged themselves unworthy of eternal life.
Does the Bible say we should not judge anyone?

The Bible, in judging: you hear them all say they wouldn’t judge. You hear that? I’m not going to judge anybody. Well, no, all sinned. T. D. Jakes, all not going to judge: I’m not going to judge. Well, the Bible already judges it. And ministers are supposed to be preaching the Bible. See, I’m not judging people when I, you know, when I tell people you’re going to hell. I’m telling them what the Bible said. God’s judgment is you’re going to hell. And I told you people last year said nobody talks like that. I said, the Bible talks like that. And can you imagine going in for cancer, and the doctors don’t want to make a judgment? They don’t want to tell you that you’re going to die, and they just say, oh, you’re just fine, you’re just fine, you’re not going to die, you don’t need treatment, you’re just— you don’t need any kind of treatment, you don’t need any kind of medicine or anything else, you know. And in the end you what? Die, when you could have got some treatment and lived. And these preachers don’t want to tell people they’re going to die. See, the lake of fire we read is the second death. You’re going to die for eternity. The Jews opposed things spoken by Paul, in Acts 13:45. So Paul boldly said— Paul what? Boldly said. He didn’t sit there silently and, well, I’m not going to judge. Well, you know, I haven’t read into that, I don’t have knowledge. No, he boldly said, “It was necessary the word of God be spoken to you first, you Jews, but since you reject it and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, we’re going to the Gentiles.” See, they judged themselves. They made a decision themselves to miss out on eternal life.
Does the Bible say we should not judge anyone?

Acts 13:45-46: But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with envy; and contradicting and blaspheming, they opposed the things spoken by Paul. Then Paul and Barnabas grew bold and said, “It was necessary that the word of God should be spoken to you first; but since you reject it, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, behold, we turn to the Gentiles.
Are Christians supposed to make judgments, according to 1 Corinthians 6 and Acts 15?

He says 1 Corinthians 6 asks whether the saints will judge the world and angels, so they are not unworthy to judge the smallest matters of this life. He reads Acts 15:19, where the decision is to write to the Gentiles to abstain from idols, sexual immorality, things strangled and blood, and he says ministers should make that judgment today.
Are Christians supposed to make judgments, according to 1 Corinthians 6 and Acts 15?

1 Corinthians 6:2: “Do you not know that the saints would judge the world?” Whoo! Are you out there, church? “If the world will be judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters?” You can’t make decisions on the least little thing! You got these homosexuals and these Oprah telling you that— “Judge not, lest you be not judged. For what judgment you judge you shall be judged.” Come on! “Do you not know that we shall judge angels? How much more things that pertain to this life?” Are we supposed to make judgments concerning this life? Yeah. Are we to make judgment on the very smallest matters, whether we buy a car we can’t afford, or will we buy a car we can’t afford? Are we supposed to make judgments? Yeah. Good grief. Raise your child up in the way they should go, or raise them up the way Dr. Spock said they should go? We got to make— we’re to make judgment. They’re lying to you, people out there. Acts 15:19: “I judge.” What did he say? “I judge.” [Editor’s note: in Acts 15:19 the speaker is James, not Paul.] Oh my gosh, [unclear] is going to fall off his chair. Oprah and T. D. Jakes and Warren, what’s this? What are they going to do with this scripture? Paul’s judging. He’s making a decision. What’s his decision? “That we should not trouble the Gentiles who are turning to God, but that we write to them to abstain from things polluted by idols, sexual immorality, things strangled, and from blood.” Sexual immorality: no homosexuality, no adultery, no incest, no sex with kids, all sex in the marriage. That’s it. And he made that judgment. Don’t you think ministers should be making that judgment today? Absolutely.
Are Christians supposed to make judgments, according to 1 Corinthians 6 and Acts 15?

1 Corinthians 6:2-3: Do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world will be judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters? Do you not know that we shall judge angels? How much more, things that pertain to this life? Matthew 7:1-2: “Judge not, that you be not judged. For with what judgment you judge, you will be judged; and with the measure you use, it will be measured back to you. Acts 15:19-20: Therefore I judge that we should not trouble those from among the Gentiles who are turning to God, but that we write to them to abstain from things polluted by idols, from sexual immorality, from things strangled, and from blood.
Why are so many Christians weak, and what should they do?

He says God’s people are weak because they listen to weak preachers and do not have enough discipline to read the Bible themselves every day. He says Christians in trouble are non-readers who go to Bible studies mostly to associate with a group, and that they should get a connection with Jesus and his word, since we go to church to spiritualize, not socialize.
Why are so many Christians weak, and what should they do?

God’s people are wimps because they’re listening to wimpy ministers. That’s right. They’re weak because they listen to weak preachers, and they ain’t got enough discipline to get on their knees and open that Bible up themselves and read a proverb a day and read [unclear] a day and read the Bible every day. I guarantee you, Christians that are in trouble are non-readers, and they don’t go to Bible studies where they actually hear somebody expound and open up the scriptures to them. They go to Bible studies mostly to associate, you know, they’re associating with this group, they got a connection with the group. You better get a connection with Jesus and his word. Yeah, that’s worth a clap. We don’t go to church to socialize. These churches, America’s churches, have got it wrong. We go to church to spiritualize. We need to become better spiritual people. Hallelujah.
Should a church put out a member who is living in sexual sin?

He reads 1 Corinthians 5 and says Paul told the church not to keep company with the sexually immoral and others in the list, and that those inside the church are to be judged while God judges those outside. He says the man there was committing incest, and Paul passed a judgment to kick him out of the church.
Should a church put out a member who is living in sexual sin?

1 Corinthians 5:9: “I wrote to you not to keep company with sexually immoral brethren, or greedy people, extortioners”— and revilers, they that blast people with their mouth— “drunkard, or idolaters. Not to eat with such a person. What have I to do with judging outsiders? Do you not judge those who are inside?” Did you hear that? “But those outside God judges. For this reason, put away yourselves from that evil person.” This guy was committing incest. He was having sex with his father’s wife, and Paul passed a judgment to kick this guy out of the church, and he told the Corinthian church, you got to make decisions.
Should a church put out a member who is living in sexual sin?

1 Corinthians 5:9-13: I wrote to you in my epistle not to keep company with sexually immoral people. Yet I certainly did not mean with the sexually immoral people of this world, or with the covetous, or extortioners, or idolaters, since then you would need to go out of the world. But now I have written to you not to keep company with anyone named a brother, who is sexually immoral, or covetous, or an idolater, or a reviler, or a drunkard, or an extortioner—not even to eat with such a person. For what have I to do with judging those also who are outside? Do you not judge those who are inside? But those who are outside God judges. Therefore “put away from yourselves the evil person.”
What does it mean to live for Christ instead of for yourself?

He reads 2 Corinthians 5:14 and calls it basic kindergarten Christianity: if Christ died for you, you should live not for yourself but for him. He says selfishness is why churches have problems, and that following Jesus’s example means laying down our life, working, getting married, staying married and raising children right.
What does it mean to live for Christ instead of for yourself?

2 Corinthians 5:14: “The love of Christ compels, because we judge this: if one died for all, then all died, and he died for all, that those who live should live no longer for themselves.” Good Lord, that’s so simple. That’s basic kindergarten Christianity: that if Christ died for you, you should be living not for yourself but for him who died for you and rose again. Can I hear an amen? I don’t have to live to please Rick Warren or T. D. Jakes or Joel Osteen. I’ve got to please Jesus Christ. Amen. And let me tell you something, church: selfishness is why you got your problems. You’re only thinking about yourself and your feelings and what you want, and it creates problems. You just want your own way because you feel it’s right. Jesus, our example, laid down his life for us. If we’re going to follow his example, we’re going to what? Lay down our life. We’re not going to do what we want to do; we’re going to do what he wants us to do. Amen. We’re going to work, we’re going to get married, we’re going to stay married, we’re going to raise children, we’re going to raise them right. We judge this way. Are we to judge? Yes.
What does it mean to live for Christ instead of for yourself?

2 Corinthians 5:14-15: For the love of Christ compels us, because we judge thus: that if One died for all, then all died; and He died for all, that those who live should live no longer for themselves, but for Him who died for them and rose again.
Should preaching and prophecy be tested against the Bible?

He reads 1 Corinthians 14:29, let two or three prophets speak and let the others judge, and says he has a right to decide whether what ministers say is scripturally correct. He says personal prophecy has no one to verify it and that prophets should not be wrong, and that people must depend on the scriptures. He also says we are to judge ourselves, and that the Sermon on the Mount means start with yourself before helping a brother with a splinter.
Should preaching and prophecy be tested against the Bible?

1 Corinthians 14:29: “Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others”— what? Judge. See, I have a right to take what Joel Osteen, Rick Warren, T. D. Jakes and Oprah and all these guys say. I have a right to make a decision if they’re scripturally correct. And I’m not out to lambaste the brethren or to divide the church. I am out to speak the truth so people can know the truth and the truth can set them free. Is that an amen? I mean, it plainly says when somebody’s talking, there’s got to be somebody checking out whether they’re saying it right or not. Hallelujah. And that’s where personal prophecy goes right out the tube. There’s no one there to verify you’re speaking right. And let me tell you, I’ve heard a lot of lousy personal prophecies, and I just flat out— to him, you’re wrong, you missed it, bud. I mean, no, I can prophesy too. I mean, they act like they’re the only ones that’s got the gift, but let me tell you, I can prophesy. And when these prophets come in and they said this, that and the other, I said, you’re wrong. And they go, no way. I said, I got the proof, you’re wrong. I know that person, and this is why you’re wrong. They got mad at me. But prophets should not be wrong. Can I hear an amen? And getting people dependent on your personal prophecies, that’s not scriptural. People have got to get dependent on the scriptures. Amen. And prophecies are good when they confirm and all that, but when they don’t, and they’re out of line, it’s destructive. 1 Corinthians 11:30: “Many are weak and sick among you, many are dead already, for if you would judge yourselves you would not be judged.” So we are to what? Judge ourselves. And that’s what the Sermon on the Mount is talking about when he says, “Judge not, lest you be judged. For with what judgment you judge you shall be judged,” and what you give out you’ll get given back to you. You better first get the 2x4 out of your eye, he said, so that you can see clearly to help the brother get a splinter out of his eye. All it’s saying is you start with yourself.
Should preaching and prophecy be tested against the Bible?

1 Corinthians 14:29: Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others judge. John 8:32: And you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.” 1 Corinthians 11:30-31: For this reason many are weak and sick among you, and many sleep. For if we would judge ourselves, we would not be judged. Matthew 7:1-5: “Judge not, that you be not judged. For with what judgment you judge, you will be judged; and with the measure you use, it will be measured back to you. And why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye, but do not consider the plank in your own eye? Or how can you say to your brother, ‘Let me remove the speck from your eye’; and look, a plank is in your own eye? Hypocrite! First remove the plank from your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.
What is God’s solution for deflective, defective ministers?

He reads Jeremiah 3:15, where God promises shepherds after his heart who feed with knowledge and understanding, and says people are destroyed for lack of knowledge because preachers in America are making them feel good instead of helping them grow and change. He says Christian divorce, children out of marriage and single-parent homes are as high as in the secular world, and that something is wrong.
What is God’s solution for deflective, defective ministers?

God’s solution for defective, deflective disciples and ministers: here’s his solution. Are you ready? Jeremiah 3:15: “I will give you shepherds according to my heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.” The Bible says, “For lack of knowledge my people are destroyed,” and gone into captivity. They lack knowledge. And why? Because preachers in America aren’t giving them the knowledge to make decisions during the week. They’re making them feel good where they’re at. They’re not growing, they’re not changing, and they wind up destroying themselves. Christian divorce is just as high as secular divorce. Christians having kids out of marriage is just as high as the secular. Christians in a single-parent home is just as high as the secular. Something’s wrong, church. Yes. The results aren’t there. At that time— I love this— he says he’s going to do it, and he tells us what’s going to happen at that time. Jerusalem— Hebrews 12 tells us Jerusalem is the church. Okay. At that time the church shall be called the Throne of the Lord. He is Lord; he’s ruling. We are following him. I love that. Do you see that? He’s not in a lot of churches. The throne is not in a lot of churches. The pastor is on the throne, because these people are worshiping pastors and ministers.
What is God’s solution for deflective, defective ministers?

Jeremiah 3:15: And I will give you shepherds according to My heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding. Hosea 4:6: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I also will reject you from being priest for Me; Because you have forgotten the law of your God, I also will forget your children. Hebrews 12:22: But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, to an innumerable company of angels, Jeremiah 3:17: “At that time Jerusalem shall be called The Throne of the LORD, and all the nations shall be gathered to it, to the name of the LORD, to Jerusalem. No more shall they follow the dictates of their evil hearts.
What does it mean for the church to be called the Throne of the Lord?

He says Jerusalem is the church and that at that time it shall be called the Throne of the Lord, with all nations gathered to the name of the Lord, which is Jesus. He says in a lot of churches the pastor is on the throne instead, and that we gather to the King, not a minister or a group. He says we know the time we are in when we are doing what he wants, not what we want.
What does it mean for the church to be called the Throne of the Lord?

“And all nations shall be gathered to the throne” that’s in the church now. Is that Bible? We don’t gather to a minister or a group. We gather to the King on the throne in the church. Wow. “To the name of the Lord.” What’s his name? Jesus. Don’t give me no Buddha stuff. Don’t give me no Joseph Smith stuff. Don’t give me no [unclear]— I mean, Moroni, some angel that’s supposed to give— don’t give me that garbage. Give me Jesus. p: In this session of “Clarity on Crucial Choices,” Pastor David G. Kincer compares the conservative and moderate platforms in America with what it means to be a believer, follower and Christian. He tests their positions against Scripture on abortion, sexual immorality, alcohol and drugs, legislating morals and the role of government, and says self-control is the way to go and followers of Jesus must not be Christians or conservatives in name only.

items.ser: Clarity on Crucial Choices · Full sermon

After defining faith from the dictionary and Hebrews 11 / Romans 4 / John 8 / James 2, he surveys humanist, evolutionist, homosexual, liberal and religionist groups that treat some harm as moral if consensual, then details humanism’s requirements (reject Jesus, accept evolution-based morals) and consequences (STDs, abuse, forced compliance). tg: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors
p: Continuing the series on adding patience to faith, the speaker says patience is essential for diplomats of Bible morality. He points to the prophets and Job (James 5:10), rewards for patiently doing good (Romans 2:6), waiting for Christ’s return (James 5:7), recognizing true Christians (Revelation 2–3; 14:12), and a gentle, teaching response to humanism (2 Timothy 2:24), then argues Congress has established secular humanism and that Johnson’s 501(c)(3) gag order violates the First Amendment.

And James 5:10, the Bible says that the prophets are an example of patience and suffering, and they’re counted blessed because they endured the patience and suffering without complaining and without losing their temper. Yeah. And then he says, you have heard of the patience of Job and the end result of the Lord. Now, Job is a perfect and upright man, and in Job 31 it tells us Job had no deceit, no sexual immorality, no going astray, no greed, no abusers of his employees. He didn’t mistreat orphans or the poor. He didn’t mistreat those that hated him. He had no secret sin. He was not afraid of the crowd. He lodged travelers. He was not silent about wrong. And yet he lost his children, his wealth, and his health.
What do the prophets and Job teach about patience?

James 5:10: My brethren, take the prophets, who spoke in the name of the Lord, as an example of suffering and patience. Job 31:1-40: “I have made a covenant with my eyes; Why then should I look upon a young woman? For what is the allotment of God from above, And the inheritance of the Almighty from on high? Is it not destruction for the wicked, And disaster for the workers of iniquity? Does He not see my ways, And count all my steps? “If I have walked with falsehood, Or if my foot has hastened to deceit, Let me be weighed on honest scales, That God may know my integrity. If my step has turned from the way, Or my heart walked after my eyes, Or if any spot adheres to my hands, Then let me sow, and another eat; Yes, let my harvest be rooted out. “If my heart has been enticed by a woman, Or if I have lurked at my neighbor’s door, Then let my wife grind for another, And let others bow down over her. For that would be wickedness; Yes, it would be iniquity deserving of judgment. For that would be a fire that consumes to destruction, And would root out all my increase. “If I have despised the cause of my male or female servant When they complained against me, What then shall I do when God rises up? When He punishes, how shall I answer Him? Did not He who made me in the womb make them? Did not the same One fashion us in the womb? “If I have kept the poor from their desire, Or caused the eyes of the widow to fail, Or eaten my morsel by myself, So that the fatherless could not eat of it (But from my youth I reared him as a father, And from my mother’s womb I guided the widow); If I have seen anyone perish for lack of clothing, Or any poor man without covering; If his heart has not blessed me, And if he was not warmed with the fleece of my sheep; If I have raised my hand against the fatherless, When I saw I had help in the gate; Then let my arm fall from my shoulder, Let my arm be torn from the socket. For destruction from God is a terror to me, And because of His magnificence I cannot endure. “If I have made gold my hope, Or said to fine gold, ‘You are my confidence’; If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, And because my hand had gained much; If I have observed the sun when it shines, Or the moon moving in brightness, So that my heart has been secretly enticed, And my mouth has kissed my hand; This also would be an iniquity deserving of judgment, For I would have denied God who is above. “If I have rejoiced at the destruction of him who hated me, Or lifted myself up when evil found him (Indeed I have not allowed my mouth to sin By asking for a curse on his soul); If the men of my tent have not said, ‘Who is there that has not been satisfied with his meat?’ (But no sojourner had to lodge in the street, For I have opened my doors to the traveler); If I have covered my transgressions as Adam, By hiding my iniquity in my bosom, Because I feared the great multitude, And dreaded the contempt of families, So that I kept silence And did not go out of the door— Oh, that I had one to hear me! Here is my mark. Oh, that the Almighty would answer me, That my Prosecutor had written a book! Surely I would carry it on my shoulder, And bind it on me like a crown; I would declare to Him the number of my steps; Like a prince I would approach Him. “If my land cries out against me, And its furrows weep together; If I have eaten its fruit without money, Or caused its owners to lose their lives; Then let thistles grow instead of wheat, And weeds instead of barley.” The words of Job are ended.
Why does he say humanists are impatient with God and Christians?

He says humanists are impatient with the Bible, Jesus, and their followers, asking why a God would allow violence and suffering. They see some Christians living in sin mixed with humanism and do not see that believers have to grow and that God gave mankind responsibility to correct criminals.
Why does he say humanists are impatient with God and Christians?

Humanists are impatient with Bible and Jesus and their followers. They say, if there’s a God, why has he allowed violence and suffering in the earth? They see some Christians mistreat their family, their self, and living in sin and mixed with humanism and Christianity, and they don’t see believers have to grow and that God gave mankind the responsibility to correct criminals. Believers have to grow and work and provide.
What present and eternal rewards does he say come from patient good works?

He reads Romans 2:6 that God will render to each according to his deeds: eternal life to those who continue patiently in doing good, and anger and wrath to the self-seeking who do not obey truth. He says humanist faith denies God, hell, and eternal life, and that their policies have not solved America’s problems.
What present and eternal rewards does he say come from patient good works?

Patience also leads us to the present and eternal rewards based on moral deeds, not dead faith. Romans 2:6, God will render to each one according to his deeds. Number one, eternal life to all who continue patiently in doing good. Number two, anger and wrath to those who are self-seeking, do not obey truth, but obey and follow unrighteousness. Humanists—their self-seeking faith is: there is no God, no hell, no eternal life; the Bible is a myth full of errors; and human reasoning solves all human problems. Yet in the 200 years of United States existence, 50 years controlling America, their 20 percent of the population have not solved the wars, the poverty, the plagues, the famines, the acts of God, the drugs, the intolerance of one group over another, the dysfunctional families, divorce rate, education, or crime. In fact, if they were honest, their policies and their faith have made matters worse.
What present and eternal rewards does he say come from patient good works?

Romans 2:6-8: who “will render to each one according to his deeds”: eternal life to those who by patient continuance in doing good seek for glory, honor, and immortality; but to those who are self-seeking and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness—indignation and wrath,
Why should Christians be patient while waiting for Jesus’ return?
