He says God is looking for righteous people, not apples and oranges, and that humanists mock Jesus returning to judge; he names Hitler and Stalin as humanist bullies who did terrible atrocities.
Why should Christians be patient while waiting for Jesus’ return?

Patience is needed in waiting for the second return of Jesus Christ. In James 5:7, be patient unto the coming of the Lord. Farmers—and he gives this illustration—number one, wait for the precious fruit; number two, they wait for the fruit of the earth and they have long patience for it; number three, they’re patient until they receive the early, the spring rain, and the late summer rain. Be also patient and establish your hearts, for the coming of the Lord draws nigh. We need to be patient and we need to understand God’s looking for a fruit in the earth, and not apples and oranges, but righteous people. Humanists mock Jesus returning to judge humans for their deeds. Hitler, Stalin, and many other bullies—they were all humanists, by the way, and they did terrible atrocities.
Why should Christians be patient while waiting for Jesus’ return?

James 5:7-8: Therefore be patient, brethren, until the coming of the Lord. See how the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, waiting patiently for it until it receives the early and latter rain. You also be patient. Establish your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is at hand.
What does he say about the latter rain and when Jesus returns?

He says history confirms four great spiritual awakenings in the USA, but the latter rain is a future global event greater than the book of Acts before Jesus returns for a glorious, mature church that prevails over the gates of hell. He says Jesus is not coming today because we are not prevailing yet.
What does he say about the latter rain and when Jesus returns?

History confirms there were four great spiritual awakenings in the USA, but the latter rain is a global future event greater than the book of Acts before Jesus returns for his glorious church, his mature church, and his church that prevails over the gates of hell. That is the promise of God. Hallelujah. So he isn’t coming today because we’re not prevailing yet.
How does he say to recognize true Christians and true ministers?

He reads Revelation 2:2 that Ephesus tested those who claimed to be apostles and found them liars, and Revelation 3:9 that Philadelphia kept the word of his patience. He says God will deal with those who pretend to be Christians and show that those who kept the word of his patience were on the right track.
How does he say to recognize true Christians and true ministers?

Revelation 2:2, to the flawed church of Ephesus he writes, I know your patience and how you can’t bear them which are evil, and you’ve tested them which say they’re ministers, they’re apostles, and are not, and found them liars. Verse 9, to the unflawed Smyrna church, I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews and are not. Revelation 3:9, to the Philadelphia church, them which say they are Jews and are not but lie, I will make to come and worship and know that I have loved you, because you kept my word of patience. I will keep you from the hour of temptation coming upon the earth. God will still deal with those who pretend to be Christians and bring them in to worship him and let them know that these people who followed me and kept the word of my patience were on the right track. Hallelujah.
How does he say to recognize true Christians and true ministers?

Revelation 2:2: “I know your works, your labor, your patience, and that you cannot bear those who are evil. And you have tested those who say they are apostles and are not, and have found them liars; Revelation 2:9: “I know your works, tribulation, and poverty (but you are rich); and I know the blasphemy of those who say they are Jews and are not, but are a synagogue of Satan. Revelation 3:9: Indeed I will make those of the synagogue of Satan, who say they are Jews and are not, but lie—indeed I will make them come and worship before your feet, and to know that I have loved you.
What is “the word of my patience,” and who is a true Christian?

He lists humanist followers who say they are Christians yet legalize same-sex conduct and marriage, women’s health over baby’s health, welfare over work, and divorce and adultery over the strong family. He reads Revelation 14:12: the patience of the saints is keeping the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus.

Many humanist followers—homosexuals, evolutionists, religionists, liberals, Democrats, Republicans, and just basic American citizens—say they’re Christians and even ministers of the gospel, and yet they legalize same-sex conduct, same-sex marriage, women’s health over baby’s health, welfare over work, divorce and adultery over the strong family unit.
What is “the word of my patience,” and who is a true Christian?
Revelation 14:12: Here is the patience of the saints; here are those who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus.

He reads that he who leads into captivity shall go into captivity, and who kills with the sword must be killed with the sword—here is the patience and faith of the saints. He says those who bring people into captivity and those who use violence must themselves be restrained.
What does Revelation 13:10 say about captivity and the sword?

What is the word of my patience, and what is the true Christian? Revelation 14:12, here is the patience of the saints: they that keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus. That is the word of his patience. You patiently do it. In Revelation it’s going to talk about the true Christian and the true minister. In 13:10, he who leads into captivity shall go into captivity; who kills with the sword must be killed with the sword. Here is the patience and faith of the saints. We’ve got to understand that these people that bring people into captivity, they’ve got to be restrained themselves, and these that use violence to get what they want—by violence they got to be restrained.
What does Revelation 13:10 say about captivity and the sword?
Revelation 13:10: He who leads into captivity shall go into captivity; he who kills with the sword must be killed with the sword. Here is the patience and the faith of the saints.
How should civil leaders and Christians respond to evildoers and humanism?

He says obeying and teaching Bible morality in Jesus is the patience of the true Christian and minister. Civil leaders in Romans 13:1 and Genesis 9:6 are to use the sword to punish and correct evildoers; bullies who use the sword will perish by it.
How should civil leaders and Christians respond to evildoers and humanism?

All right, we got to obey and teach Bible morality in Jesus. That is the patience of the true Christian and the true minister. Christian humanists promoting bad behavior lead people into the captivity of sin and crime, and they must go into captivity themselves—be restrained. Remember, civil leaders in Romans 13:1 and Genesis 9:6 are to use the sword to punish and correct evildoers. Bullies use the sword, Jesus said, and they will perish by the sword.
How should civil leaders and Christians respond to evildoers and humanism?

Romans 13:1: Let every soul be subject to the governing authorities. For there is no authority except from God, and the authorities that exist are appointed by God. Genesis 9:6: “Whoever sheds man’s blood, By man his blood shall be shed; For in the image of God He made man.
What is a responsible, patient response to humanism?

He reads 2 Timothy 2:24 that the servant of the Lord must not quarrel but be gentle to all, able to teach, patient, instructing opponents in meekness so God may give them repentance and they recover from the Devil’s captivity. He says it is our responsibility to teach humanists who oppose Jesus and Bible morality with a right attitude.

Second Timothy 2:24, the servant of the Lord must not quarrel for any reason and debate just to be debating, but be gentle unto all men, teach, patient, in meekness instructing those that oppose themselves, so God will give them repentance and the acknowledging of the truth, and recover themselves out of the captivity of the Devil. And so it is our responsibility to teach and instruct with a right attitude these humanists that are opposing Jesus and Bible morality.

2 Timothy 2:24-26: And a servant of the Lord must not quarrel but be gentle to all, able to teach, patient, in humility correcting those who are in opposition, if God perhaps will grant them repentance, so that they may know the truth, and that they may come to their senses and escape the snare of the devil, having been taken captive by him to do his will.

He calls humanists to admit their policies do not work, repent, acknowledge Bible truths, recover from the Devil’s snare, and stop promoting harmful behavior that destroys children, families, and America.
What does he say humanists must admit and do?

All of these are the results of humanist policies and their faith. Criminals are not being rehabilitated like they said decades ago. 43 nations in the world are in wars and conflicts; forty thousand suicides in America per year; and lying is an acceptable behavior from the president down to children down to school teachers. We just lie. We lie in teaching at the textbook. We just lie everywhere. Humanists distort truth and they snub—they avoid—their failed faith and policies. They will not take accountability for their failed faith and their failed policies that they’ve had for reign in America for the last 50 years. Admit your policies as a humanist. Admit that they don’t work. Repent and acknowledge Bible truths. Recover yourself out of the snare of the Devil—a liar that you do not believe in but intimidate or imitate. And humanists, stop promoting harmful behavior that is destroying children, destroying families, and destroying America.
Has Congress established secular humanism, according to the sermon?

He reads the First Amendment’s religion, speech, press, assembly, and petition clauses, then says Congress has established the religion of secular humanism—no God—by taking God out of schools and public places and restricting Jesus’ name, thereby prohibiting free exercise for Bible Christians while restricting their speech and press.

Now we’re going to look at the Second—or the First—Amendment to the Constitution. They say we don’t have a right to speak, that the Bible is a book of faith and we got to shut up, but their religion is a religion of faith. And the First Amendment to the Constitution says Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion or prohibiting the free exercise thereof, or abridging the freedom of speech, or censoring the freedom of speech or the press, or the right of the people peaceably to assemble and to petition government for a redress or remedies of our grievances, our objections. And yet this First Amendment gives us the right to speak and print our values, our truths, and our morals, and they restrict the speech and press of Bible-morality citizens. And our Congress has violated through the pressure of the religion of humanism, secular humanism.

Does he say the 501(c)(3) gag order violates the First Amendment?

I submit to you today the churches have a right to peacefully assemble. They have a right to petition and request a remedy for our objections, and we have a right to speak out on our objections. He says Job had no deceit, no sexual immorality, no going astray, no greed, did not mistreat employees, orphans, the poor, or those who hated him, had no secret sin, lodged travelers, and was not silent about wrong.
What does he say humanist faith believes?
He says their self-seeking faith is that there is no God, no hell, no eternal life; the Bible is a myth full of errors; and human reasoning solves all human problems.

items.t: Except You Become as Little Children
items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer continues his series on stages of Christian growth and explains the child stage: those who are born again and now obey the Word. He reads Matthew 18:3, the disciples…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer continues his series on stages of Christian growth and explains the child stage: those who are born again and now obey the Word. He reads Matthew 18:3, the disciples called “children” who still needed the meat of the Word, and 1 John 2 on the last time and the many antichrists. He then describes what a spiritual person looks like and what he believes the “little child shall lead them” of Isaiah 11 points to: a coming move of God led by grown, obedient believers.
What are the embryo and newborn stages of growth in the Christian life?

He says in the embryo stage people respond to hearing the Word: some reject or mock it and say it is “an inconvenient time,” while others believe, repent and follow Christ, “not a church, not an author, not an apostle.” In the newborn stage “their sins are forgiven” and they “desire the sincere milk of the Word.”
What are the embryo and newborn stages of growth in the Christian life?

So today we’re going to look at the child stage of growth from the Bible. Okay, remember the embryo stage is when they hear the Word. It’s how they responded when they heard the Word. And they rejected the Word, they mocked when they heard the Word and rejected the Word. They not only mocked, but some of them abused the Bible, Jesus, and His followers, mistreated, lambasted, put down, persecuted others. Said, “It’s not a convenient time, it’s an inconvenient time. Wait, I’m out to high school. Wait, I’m out of college. Wait till I’m done raising my family,” whatever. It’s an inconvenient time for me to follow God. “Okay, we’ll hear you again. I’ll hear you again, but you know, I’m not ready to make that decision.” And then others believed, repented, and followed Christ. The important word there is “follow.” They followed who? Christ. Not a church, not an author, not an apostle, but they followed Christ. The newborn stage, you remember, their sins are forgiven. They come to Jesus to learn from Him. So this is their growing effort: they desire the sincere milk of the Word, the Scriptures, to grow, which is repentance from dead works, faith toward God, not toward a denomination, not toward a minister, faith toward who? God. Repentance from works that brings the second death, destruction, the lake of fire. Baptisms: how many baptisms are there? Three: baptism of the Holy Ghost, baptism in water, and baptism into the body, and He chooses where you fit into the body, not you. He chooses.
What are the embryo and newborn stages of growth in the Christian life?

Hebrews 6:1-2: Therefore, leaving the discussion of the elementary principles of Christ, let us go on to perfection, not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works and of faith toward God, of the doctrine of baptisms, of laying on of hands, of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment. 1 Peter 2:2: as newborn babes, desire the pure milk of the word, that you may grow thereby,
What do baby Christians do: praise, doing good, and partnership?

He says babies are being built into “a spiritual house” looking for the presence of Jesus, and their main weapon is “the sacrifice of praise.” They also offer “the sacrifice of doing good” and “the sacrifice of partnership,” going to church “not to be entertained” but to reach the unbeliever and grow the unlearned, and they offer their bodies as a living sacrifice.
What do baby Christians do: praise, doing good, and partnership?

Okay, and then we have the resurrection of the dead and eternal judgment, after laying on of hands, and that is the second coming, resurrection and the eternal judgment is the second coming. And it’s baby doctrine. It’s kindergarten doctrine. It’s not mature doctrine and sound doctrine at all. They are also being built a spiritual house, inhabited by who? Jesus. Not a rock concert, not a dance company, not mimes. Those are all tools we can use, but these people are looking for the presence of Jesus. And presence of who? Jesus. Not Allah, not Joseph Smith, Jesus Christ. It’s very important that people understand this stuff. We read it, we don’t get it, but we got to get it. Okay, that’s their effort of growth. Their main weapon is the sacrifice of praise to still the enemy and avenger. They boast about Jesus, they sing about Him, they shout unto Him, they speak of His greatness, and that is the weapon that destroys the devouring enemy and the avenger. Hallelujah. So the babies are very strong in praising God, boasting of God, because that destroys their enemy. They have a tremendous tool. They also offer the sacrifice of doing good. They don’t want to do good. They may not want to get up on Monday morning and go to work, but it’s good. See, they might not want to clean the toilet in the house, but it’s good. It’s good. They may not want to love the lousiest member of the body of Christ, but it’s a good thing to do, so they do it. It’s a sacrifice. A sacrifice is something you don’t want to do. So see, babies go to church by a sacrifice, not a compelling. They’d rather sleep in on Sunday, they’d rather, you know, relax on Friday night or whenever their church services are, but it’s a good thing, so they do what is good. It’s a sacrifice. Partnership. The sacrifice of partnership, fellowship, koinonia. They go to church, not to be entertained, not to get a man and a woman to marry them, but that’s a good place to find one. They go to church for a partnership. Partnership to what? To reach the unbeliever and to grow the unlearned. Are you there? They don’t come to church just to get something. They come to church to get and to give, and they’re there to help the unlearned grow up. They’re there to help the unbeliever become a believer. That’s the partnership. And sadly, in America we don’t have a lot of partners. Why? We haven’t passed the newborn stage yet. You see, going to church is just something convenient for them, going to a Bible study is something convenient for them, or whatever. They do everything out of convenience. But a real born again person will hear the Word and respond to the Word in that area of growth. Could that be an amen? You see, we have a responsibility to the unlearned and the unbeliever. We have that responsibility. And then they offer their physical body a living sacrifice unto God. So they do get up in the morning, they tell that body what to do, they do lift their hands and praise God, they do get involved. See, they offer their bodies, their physical body, a living sacrifice for Christ.
What do baby Christians do: praise, doing good, and partnership?

1 Peter 2:5: you also, as living stones, are being built up a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ. Hebrews 13:15-16: Therefore by Him let us continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name. But do not forget to do good and to share, for with such sacrifices God is well pleased. Romans 12:1: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your reasonable service.
What weaknesses do baby Christians have, and how should the church treat them?

He says babies are “jealous, they argue and quarrel, they’re sectarian, they divide” because “they haven’t learned the Word yet,” and still struggle with the works of the flesh. He says “we don’t throw babies out of the house because they haven’t grown up yet,” that “our job is to help them grow up,” and that they are “tossed about by every wind of deceptive doctrine.”
What weaknesses do baby Christians have, and how should the church treat them?

Now, they have a weakness. Their weaknesses are they’re jealous, they argue and quarrel, they’re sectarian, they divide. “I’m a Baptist, I’m a Pentecostal, I’m a Catholic, I’m a this, I’m a that.” You see, they’re very sectarian. They’re weak in that. Why? Because they haven’t learned the Word yet. They haven’t developed spiritually yet. And we don’t throw babies out of the house because they haven’t grown up yet, have we? Yeah. Our job is to help them grow up. And so when a baby needs you, you give them attention that they need. They have problems in the flesh, the carnal, with sexual immorality, anger, hatred, intoxication, partying, profanity, heresies, selfishness, and rebellion.
