What is a spiritual person? (1 Corinthians 14:37; Galatians 6:1; Colossians 1:9)

1 Corinthians 14:37: If anyone thinks himself to be a prophet or spiritual, let him acknowledge that the things which I write to you are the commandments of the Lord. Acts 17:11: These were more fair-minded than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness, and searched the Scriptures daily to find out whether these things were so. Galatians 6:1: Brethren, if a man is overtaken in any trespass, you who are spiritual restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness, considering yourself lest you also be tempted. Colossians 1:9-11: For this reason we also, since the day we heard it, do not cease to pray for you, and to ask that you may be filled with the knowledge of His will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding; that you may walk worthy of the Lord, fully pleasing Him, being fruitful in every good work and increasing in the knowledge of God; strengthened with all might, according to His glorious power, for all patience and longsuffering with joy;
Who is the “little child” who leads in Isaiah 11, and what is the “second” visitation? (Isaiah 11; Romans 11)

He says the “little child shall lead them” is not a kid in a utopia but “a level of growth of believers” leading “something that’s going to happen at the second return of Christ.” He reads Isaiah 11:11 as the Lord setting His hand again, “second time,” to recover a remnant, and says Romans 11 points to a second visitation for the Jews, brought back in “through His church.”
Who is the “little child” who leads in Isaiah 11, and what is the “second” visitation? (Isaiah 11; Romans 11)

Hallelujah. And you don’t need a birthday party or birthday gift to have this joy. This is a spiritual joy. Isaiah 11:6: “The wolf shall lay down with the lamb, the calf and the young lion will lay down together.” How many of you know those are opponents? Lions eat calves, wolves eat lambs. Now we know a little wolf is what? A believer in sheep’s clothing. They just got on the outward form. We know what a wolf is. They’re there acting like sheep, but they are not. Ain’t that right? But this Scripture says the lamb and the wolf are going to lay down together, “and a little child shall lead them.” Now, as a young minister, I just pictured this little kid in some kind of utopia and I’m leading the people. But when enlightenment came, I understood it was a level of growth of believers that are leading something that’s going to happen at the second return of Christ. Something is going to happen a second time. Are you there? And these believers are leading the pack. Not baby believers, these children believers are leading the way. Isn’t that exciting? Yes. “They shall not hurt nor destroy in My holy mountain.” We know from other lessons we’ve taught that the mountain of the Lord is the church, Zion. See, they shall not hurt and destroy in “My holy mountain.” Folks, we haven’t had that since Jesus ascended. They have been hurting and destroying in God’s church. They have bashed God’s church. “For the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord as the waters cover the sea.” So see, knowledge is coming, and who’s leading this knowledge? These children, these Christians that have grown past the newborn stage into understanding and obeying God’s Word, they’re leading this move of God. “And in that day,” verse 11, “the Lord shall set His hand again,” the what? Second time, “to recover the remnant of His people.” Jesus came the first time to recover, restore, bring back the remnant. The remnant are those that what? Have the testimony of Jesus, Revelation 12, and obey His Word. That’s the remnant. So there’s a second gathering, there’s a second visitation of God coming before this rapture takes place and all this. There’s a second visitation promise, and it’s the children that have grown up to obey the Word that are leading this move of God. Isn’t that beautiful? So see, there’s something going to happen. And that’s what I keep telling these people that argue with me. Jesus’s death on the cross is too powerful for Him to come now when we got billions of people that have not heard the Word of God yet and don’t believe in God. That’s right. Okay, second time. Romans 11:23: “If Israel abide not still in unbelief, they shall be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.” He’s talking about the olive tree, the kingdom of God. The Jews were cut off, and Paul is saying they’re going to be grafted back in again, and they can be grafted back in again. So there is a what? Second visitation coming for the Jews. These Scriptures just suddenly open up when you understand these definitions. Look, Romans 11:26, just a few verses down from it: “And so all Israel shall be saved, as it is written, there shall come out of Zion the Deliverer, and turn away ungodliness from Jacob.” Now, who’s Zion? We’ve learned, the church. Who’s the Deliverer? Jesus. So Jesus is going to rise in this last day church before the second coming, and He is going to bring in again the Israel, the people, the Jews. He’s going to bring them back in again, and He’s going to do it through His church.
Who is the “little child” who leads in Isaiah 11, and what is the “second” visitation? (Isaiah 11; Romans 11)

Isaiah 11:6-9: “The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, The leopard shall lie down with the young goat, The calf and the young lion and the fatling together; And a little child shall lead them. The cow and the bear shall graze; Their young ones shall lie down together; And the lion shall eat straw like the ox. The nursing child shall play by the cobra’s hole, And the weaned child shall put his hand in the viper’s den. They shall not hurt nor destroy in all My holy mountain, For the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the LORD As the waters cover the sea. Isaiah 11:11: It shall come to pass in that day That the Lord shall set His hand again the second time To recover the remnant of His people who are left, From Assyria and Egypt, From Pathros and Cush, From Elam and Shinar, From Hamath and the islands of the sea. Revelation 12:17: And the dragon was enraged with the woman, and he went to make war with the rest of her offspring, who keep the commandments of God and have the testimony of Jesus Christ. Romans 11:23: And they also, if they do not continue in unbelief, will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again. Romans 11:26: And so all Israel will be saved, as it is written: “The Deliverer will come out of Zion, And He will turn away ungodliness from Jacob;
What does 2 Thessalonians 1:7-10 say about Christ coming “in His saints”?

He reads that Jesus will be revealed “taking vengeance on them that know not God,” and says there is a lake of fire and “we need to tremble at that word.” He adds that the verse says He is “coming in His saints,” as He came into the apostles at Pentecost, and that “there is a move of God coming in His church” leading to “a great harvest.”
What does 2 Thessalonians 1:7-10 say about Christ coming “in His saints”?

2 Thessalonians 1:7: “When the Lord Jesus shall be revealed from heaven with His mighty angels, in flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not God, that obey not the gospel, who shall be punished with everlasting destruction.” You young people, there is a second coming of Christ. He is coming to punish the wicked. There is a lake of fire. There is an eternal punishment, and we need to tremble at that word. But there’s also the message that something powerful is going to happen before that day arise. And look at this: “when He shall come to be glorified in His saints, and be admired in them that believe, in that day.” Now, we’re always talking about the God is coming for His saints, but folks, this verse says He’s coming in His saints. Did He come in His saints the first time He came? Yes. The day of Pentecost, out of their innermost being these rivers of life-giving water flowed. You see, He came, He died on the cross, and He came in. He said the Holy Spirit is with you but shall be what? In you. So He’s coming in them. And when He came in the apostles, they were transformed from people that were weak and quarreling and denying Christ and all the rest to a group of people that nothing could move them. He came in them, and so He is coming in His people in that end time period. There is a move of God coming in His church that will cause the Jews and the Muslims and other people to recognize the truth and come in, and there will be a great harvest. Hallelujah. Now that’s exciting.
What does 2 Thessalonians 1:7-10 say about Christ coming “in His saints”?

2 Thessalonians 1:7-10: and to give you who are troubled rest with us when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with His mighty angels, in flaming fire taking vengeance on those who do not know God, and on those who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ. These shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of His power, when He comes, in that Day, to be glorified in His saints and to be admired among all those who believe, because our testimony among you was believed. John 7:38: He who believes in Me, as the Scripture has said, out of his heart will flow rivers of living water.”
What does Jeremiah 33:7-9 promise, and what must believers do now?

He reads “I will build them as at the first,” says “the church is the Israel of God,” and that God’s people are believing lies, so “it’s somebody’s job to speak up and restore and recover God’s people.” He says “if He did it at the first, He is going to do it a second time,” and “we need God, and we need to grow,” with the Holy Ghost active in the church.
What does Jeremiah 33:7-9 promise, and what must believers do now?

Jeremiah 33:7: “I will cause the captivity of Judah and Israel to return.” We know that Judah, in the Scriptures, the real Jew is not one outwardly, and circumcision is not in the flesh, but a real Jew, Paul said, was one inwardly, and circumcision of the spirit, and that’s the church. Amen. And Israel, Paul said, we are the Israel of God. The church is the Israel of God. “I will cause the captivity of Judah.” Is God’s people in captivity right now? Yeah. They’re believing lies, and it’s somebody’s job to speak up and restore and recover God’s people. “I will build them as at the first.” You see, He came and He started building, and the apostles did a great job, and then, as the Bible says, there was a falling away. But in these last days we started seeing the restoration when Luther came on the scene, and it’s been going on, this restoration, for quite a few, long time. Are you there? Now listen to this. The church, Judah and Israel, this thing’s going to be built, this house that’s being built. “It will be a name of joy, praise, and honor before all nations, which shall hear all the good that I do unto them, and the nations shall fear and tremble.” Now I submit to you, has that ever happened since Jesus ascended, where the nations shook and was in fear because of what God was doing in His church? No. There’s no history of it. Did Jesus say every Scripture will be fulfilled? Yeah. So does there have to be something going to take place at this end of the age? Yes. If He did it at the first, He is going to do it a second time. And that’s what we got to be believing for, folks. We need God, and we need to grow. “The enemy comes in like a flood, the Spirit of the Lord will lift up a standard against him.” We need the Holy Ghost active in the church and in our lives. We can’t do this on human thinking, we can’t do this in human power. And God promised that the Holy Ghost would come and empower us and give us things to edify and build the church. That’s why tongues and interpretation are important, prophecy is important, healing and miracles are important, faith, discerning of spirits, wisdom and knowledge is important, coming from the Holy Ghost. It builds, it edifies, it never draws attention to itself, it always points toward Jesus.
What does Jeremiah 33:7-9 promise, and what must believers do now?

Jeremiah 33:7-9: And I will cause the captives of Judah and the captives of Israel to return, and will rebuild those places as at the first. I will cleanse them from all their iniquity by which they have sinned against Me, and I will pardon all their iniquities by which they have sinned and by which they have transgressed against Me. Then it shall be to Me a name of joy, a praise, and an honor before all nations of the earth, who shall hear all the good that I do to them; they shall fear and tremble for all the goodness and all the prosperity that I provide for it.’ Romans 2:28-29: For he is not a Jew who is one outwardly, nor is circumcision that which is outward in the flesh; but he is a Jew who is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the Spirit, not in the letter; whose praise is not from men but from God. Galatians 6:16: And as many as walk according to this rule, peace and mercy be upon them, and upon the Israel of God. Isaiah 59:19: So shall they fear The name of the LORD from the west, And His glory from the rising of the sun; When the enemy comes in like a flood, The Spirit of the LORD will lift up a standard against him.
What three baptisms does he list?
He lists “baptism of the Holy Ghost, baptism in water, and baptism into the body,” and says “He chooses where you fit into the body, not you.”
Why does he say babies in Christ go to church?

He says they go “not to be entertained,” but for partnership: “to reach the unbeliever and to grow the unlearned.” He says “they come to church to get and to give,” and that “sadly in America we don’t have a lot of partners.”
Why does he say baby Christians divide into groups?

He says they say “I’m a Baptist, I’m a Pentecostal, I’m a Catholic, I’m a this, I’m a that,” and are weak in that “because they haven’t learned the Word yet.” He says the church’s job is to help them grow up, not put them down.
What age does he say “little children” refers to in the New Testament?
He says the word is used from infants to 12 years old, so “it’s basically used from age two and up.”
Does he say Christians know what stage of growth they are at?
No. He says “American Christians do not know what stage they’re at, and most of them are at baby stage, and they haven’t even conquered the baby doctrines yet, and it’s sad.”
Is there anything wrong with being in the embryo or newborn stage?
No. He says “there’s nothing wrong with being in the embryo stage if that’s where you’re at,” or a newborn Christian, but “we just got to help them” get born again and grow.
What is the difference between the milk and the meat of the Word?

He says “there is the milk of the Word and there is the meat of the Word,” and that the disciples were called children because they could not yet handle the meat. He says meat starts in the child stage and goes on to the next stages.
Why does he call the baptism of the Holy Ghost “baby doctrine”?
He says, “We’ve been baptized in the Holy Ghost, hallelujah. Okay, grow up. Say baptism of Holy Ghost is baby doctrine. Grow up. It’s there to help you grow up.”
Does he say one Antichrist is coming?
No. He says “there are many antichrists, many opponents,” that “the last time” began long ago, and that there is “no big superhuman like that movie.”
How does he say you can tell who is an antichrist?
He reads, “Who is a liar but he that denies that Jesus is the Christ?” and says “the person that denies that Jesus is the Christ is antichrist,” a “very plain definition.”
Does he say he hates people who deny Jesus is God?
No. He says “I’m not preaching hatred, I’m preaching truth” and “I don’t hate anybody. My job is to tell the truth.”
Can anyone know how long this age will last?
No. He says “nobody knows how long this age is going to go on,” and that people who say they know are lying because “the Bible says nobody knows.”
What does he say grace is?
He says “we’ve taken this grace thing and just distorted it horribly. Grace is the divine enablement of God,” which was upon Jesus, empowering Him as He grew in grace, wisdom and spirit.
What does he say it means that Christ is coming “in His saints”?

He says we are always told that He is coming for His saints, but the verse says He is coming in them. He says He came into the apostles at Pentecost and transformed them, and “so He is coming in His people in that end time period.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer walks through Ezekiel 18, the “laws of life and death,” and answers the charge that “the way of the Lord is not fair.” He teaches that each person is judged by his own…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer walks through Ezekiel 18, the “laws of life and death,” and answers the charge that “the way of the Lord is not fair.” He teaches that each person is judged by his own ways, that God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked, and that God offers a new heart, mind and spirit. He then turns to Ezekiel 33 and the watchman, and calls the church to speak what God said to speak.
What are the laws of life and death in Ezekiel 18?

He says he is going to Ezekiel 18 and 33 to look at “the laws of life and the laws of death.” He reads Ezekiel 18:20, “the soul that sins it shall die,” and says “A law is a statement that has a punishment,” adding that “the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father.”
What are the laws of life and death in Ezekiel 18?

And today we’re going to be going to Ezekiel chapters 18 and chapters 33 and we’re going to be looking at the laws of life and the laws of death. Now Ezekiel was a prophet after the first captivity. He was carried away captive about 25 years of age and uh in the in the sixth year of captivity, 31 years of age, he started prophesying. Now he’s several hundred miles away from Jeremiah who is speaking the same things. And that’s very important for you to know. These two are not connected with each other at all. Ezekiel was not even called to prophesy. Until the sixth year of the captivity. Jeremiah had already been prophesying for quite a while. All right? And though Ezekiel is hundreds of miles away in Babylon, he is saying the same thing that Jeremiah is talking about. And it’s very important for you to know that. You see, God is a supernatural God and he does supernatural things. All right? Uh in Ezekiel 18:20 he starts out saying the soul that sins it shall die. Now that’s a law. The soul that sins it shall die. A law is a statement that has a punishment. All right? If you violate that law, there is a payment to pay. And so the person that sins, soul is just a person that sins, it shall die. All right? Now, that’s the first thing. Number two, the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father. He says you can’t blame the son or punish the son for the father’s bad doing. Okay. Number three, nor shall the father bear the iniquity of the son. You see, my sons go out in sin and they’re of age. You know, you can’t blame me. I did my job. They just didn’t listen.
What are the laws of life and death in Ezekiel 18?

Ezekiel 18:20: The soul who sins shall die. The son shall not bear the guilt of the father, nor the father bear the guilt of the son. The righteousness of the righteous shall be upon himself, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon himself.
Is a sinful thought the same as a sin?

He says the wicked who turn from “committed sin” will live, and stresses “It’s not sins in your mind.” He says “Nowhere in the Bible was anyone stoned for thinking sexual immorality,” and that “You have to commit it.”
Is a sinful thought the same as a sin?

Number four, the righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him. Now, that sounds logical. If a guy does right, that he’s going to get the rewards of right. If the guy does wrong, he’s going to get the rewards of wrong. Amen. But if the wicked will turn, repent, turn from all his committed sins. Now, it’s important you understand that it’s committed sin. It’s not sins in your mind. It’s not, you know, everybody uses this thing. In fact, I just heard it this morning. Whosoever looketh a woman to lust after her has committed adultery already within his heart. So the Piers Morgan says, “You got to stone that person.” These people on TV and these radio and TV host and and anchor people, they they they get into areas they know nothing about. Nowhere in the Bible was anyone stoned for thinking sexual immorality. Never. No one was ever stoned for thinking about stealing something. You have to commit it. You have to do it. All right. But if the wicked see the evil person will turn from those committed sins, keep my statutes. Do that which is lawful and right, he shall live.
Is a sinful thought the same as a sin?

Ezekiel 18:21: “But if a wicked man turns from all his sins which he has committed, keeps all My statutes, and does what is lawful and right, he shall surely live; he shall not die. Matthew 5:28: But I say to you that whoever looks at a woman to lust for her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
What two lives does the Bible promise?

He says the law of life is “doing what’s right,” and “Even if I’ve messed up, I can turn.” He says the Bible promises “two lives,” eternal life and “the life that now is,” and that he doesn’t “want to wait to go to heaven to enjoy life.”
What two lives does the Bible promise?

Truly live. He shall not die. That’s the laws of sin and death. Even if I’ve messed up, I can turn and I will not be remembered for my past sins anymore. It’s just doing what’s right is the law of life. The law of life is doing what’s right. And when you go to the New Testament, the New Testament backs it up. Jesus backs it up. So that’s the laws of life and death. There are two lives in the Bible. Eternal life and the life that now is 2 Timothy 4:8. Godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is and that which is to come. I don’t know about you, but I don’t want to wait to go to heaven to enjoy life. And the Bible promises two lives. You will be blessed here on this earth. Say the laws of life and when you die, you will inherit eternal life. How many want God to bless you in this life? Yes. And how many are thankful there’s nowhere to go but eternity when you die? Hallelujah. With him. Now we’re going to move on here in Ezekiel 18 14-18 number six. If he a wicked father, he’s talking about a wicked father a son.
What two lives does the Bible promise?
1 Timothy 4:8: For bodily exercise profits a little, but godliness is profitable for all things, having promise of the life that now is and of that which is to come.
Do children pay for their parents’ sins?

He says “the children pay a big price for sinning parents,” but the son who sees his father’s sins and repents “shall not die for the iniquity of his father. He shall live.” He adds that God is not “up there” eager to condemn anyone, and asks whether the wicked should die and not “return from his wicked ways and live.”
Do children pay for their parents’ sins?

Oh, that’s cut off. Wow. That sees all his father’s sins. Okay. This son sees dad being bad, mom being bad, and the son is paying a big price. How many know the children pay a big price for sinning parents? Absolutely. They do. We put kids through hell on earth because us adults act like kids and we do bad things. Okay. He sees all that the parents have done. He considers it. He [unclear] it. He rationalizes it and does not [unclear] such like, but executes God’s judgments, walks in God’s statutes. He shall not die for the iniquity of his father. He shall live. See it. Instead of blaming or following the bad parents, these guys are repenting from their bad behavior. And it works. The one that repents and turns and does right shall live. God will bless you in this life and in the life to come. Now verse 23, number seven. Have I any pleasure delight in the wicked that they should die and not return from his wicked ways and live? God is just reminding us. He’s not up there saying, “Oh boy, I get to get that one. That one’s a Oh, hallelujah. Boy, get to put that one in hell. Okay, who’s next here?” No.
Do children pay for their parents’ sins?

Ezekiel 18:14-18: “If, however, he begets a son Who sees all the sins which his father has done, And considers but does not do likewise; Who has not eaten on the mountains, Nor lifted his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, Nor defiled his neighbor’s wife; Has not oppressed anyone, Nor withheld a pledge, Nor robbed by violence, But has given his bread to the hungry And covered the naked with clothing; Who has withdrawn his hand from the poor And not received usury or increase, But has executed My judgments And walked in My statutes— He shall not die for the iniquity of his father; He shall surely live! “As for his father, Because he cruelly oppressed, Robbed his brother by violence, And did what is not good among his people, Behold, he shall die for his iniquity. Ezekiel 18:23: Do I have any pleasure at all that the wicked should die?” says the Lord GOD, “and not that he should turn from his ways and live?
Does God want the wicked to die, and will he still judge them?

He says God “gets no delight in you dying. It’s totally your choice,” but that does not mean he will not judge sin: “He is a just God and he is a judge.” He says that if you do wrong, “You know what you’re doing,” whether by conscience or God’s word.
Does God want the wicked to die, and will he still judge them?

God has no pleasure. He gets no delight in you dying. It’s totally your choice. But because just because he doesn’t delight in the death of the wicked does not mean he will not judge you and put you in an eternal lake of fire for your sins. He will do that. He is a just God and he is a judge. Number eight verse 24. When the righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits iniquities of the wicked man, shall he live? Whoa. All his righteousness he has done shall not be mentioned. Won’t even be brought up in court.
If a righteous person turns back to sin, do his past good works count?

He reads Ezekiel 18:24 and says “All his righteousness he has done shall not be mentioned.” He uses Judas as his example: he preached, laid hands on the sick and cast out demons, but when he turned and betrayed Christ “all those goodies were forgotten.”
If a righteous person turns back to sin, do his past good works count?

The heaven’s court won’t even be brought up. And I told you, I’ve seen a vision of that judgment and nobody’s saying anything because they knew they were wrong when they did it. They have no answer. You know what you’re doing when you do wrong, whether it’s by the conscience or God’s word. In his trespass, violation of the law, and sin, shall he die. Now, a good example of that is Judas. You see, Judas followed Christ. Judas preached the gospel. People got saved. Judas laid hands on people and they got healed. Judas cast out demons. All those are right good works, aren’t they? But when Judas turned and let Satan enter into him and betrayed Christ, all those goodies were forgotten. And he’s burning in hell today. Are you there? What’s fair? What’s not fair? I’m always hearing people, well, this isn’t fair, fair, fair, fair, fair. Ezekiel 18:29. Yet the house of Israel says, the way of the Lord is not fair. It’s not fair. I was good for 60 years my life, and I turned bad for the last three, and I’m going to hell.
If a righteous person turns back to sin, do his past good works count?

Ezekiel 18:24: “But when a righteous man turns away from his righteousness and commits iniquity, and does according to all the abominations that the wicked man does, shall he live? All the righteousness which he has done shall not be remembered; because of the unfaithfulness of which he is guilty and the sin which he has committed, because of them he shall die. Ezekiel 18:29: Yet the house of Israel says, ‘The way of the Lord is not fair.’ O house of Israel, is it not My ways which are fair, and your ways which are not fair?
Does God weigh good deeds against bad deeds, and is his way fair?

He says some think “my good things should have outweighed my bad things,” but God says “I will judge you … Everyone according to his ways.” He says “Not grace, not faith, not the church I attend, not helping the poor, not tithing, none of those things even come into the equation.”
Does God weigh good deeds against bad deeds, and is his way fair?

That’s not fair. I should be weighed in a balance and my good things should have outweighed my bad things like some people believe. How many of you know that? Therefore, what does therefore mean? For this reason. So, when we see the word therefore, we got to consider what it’s there for. Okay. Why is the word therefore therefore? For this reason, I will judge you, oh house of Israel. What reason? Everyone according to his ways, says the Lord God. Not grace, not faith, not the church I attend, not helping the poor, not tithing, none of those things even come into the equation.
Does God weigh good deeds against bad deeds, and is his way fair?

Ezekiel 18:30: “Therefore I will judge you, O house of Israel, every one according to his ways,” says the Lord GOD. “Repent, and turn from all your transgressions, so that iniquity will not be your ruin.
What does it mean to repent and cast away transgressions?

He says what’s fair is to “repent,” and “Turn from your evil ways so that iniquity would not be your ruin.” He says to cast away “all committed transgressions,” and if you pick one up again, “Cast it away again.”
What does it mean to repent and cast away transgressions?

What’s fair? Number three, repent. That’s what’s fair. Turn from your evil ways so that iniquity would not be your ruin. Verse 31, cast from you. Number four, all committed transgressions. There’s that word again. Say that word. So I cast away my iniquities, you know, and then I mess up and pick up one here and there, and then I got to what? Cast it away again. Get yourselves a new heart. Here is a tremendous part of this new covenant. We’re going to show you it’s in the new covenant next week. And then we’re going to show you how to get a part of the new covenant that you deserve in this life. All right? Get yourselves a new heart.
What does it mean to repent and cast away transgressions?

Ezekiel 18:30-31: “Therefore I will judge you, O house of Israel, every one according to his ways,” says the Lord GOD. “Repent, and turn from all your transgressions, so that iniquity will not be your ruin. Cast away from you all the transgressions which you have committed, and get yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. For why should you die, O house of Israel?
What does it mean to get a new heart, a new mind and a new spirit?

He says the heart is “Mind, will, and the emotions,” so a new heart is “a new way of thinking” and responding to emotions. He says that if you only accept salvation, grace and faith “you’re missing out on one of the most important parts of the new covenant,” and that you also need “a spirit that connects with God’s spirit.”
What does it mean to get a new heart, a new mind and a new spirit?

Now, what’s the heart? Mind, will, and the emotions. That’s the center part of man, the mind, the intellect. Get yourself a new way of thinking. Get yourself a new way of responding to emotions. How many can say, “Boy, I I need some help in my emotions.” A new heart. And so he’s telling us to what? Get it. So if you only accept salvation and grace and faith, you’re missing out on one of the most important parts of the new covenant. He promised you, as we will see next week, a new mind. Doesn’t the New Testament say, “If any man be in Christ, he’s a new creature.” Well, what do you think that means? Old things are what? Passed away. Behold, all things are new. What do you think that starts? A new mind. And if preachers don’t preach the word, how you going to get a new mind? If you don’t write, read, and study the word, how you going to get a new mind? And a new spirit. How many of you know you’re a three-part being? Yeah. Body, soul, and spirit. You have a physical body, you have a soul. Again, the word soul there is, the emotions, the intellect, and the will. And then you have a spirit. There is a spirit living in you. That when this body dies, the spirit continues. And so, you need a new spirit. You need a spirit that connects with God’s spirit.
What does it mean to get a new heart, a new mind and a new spirit?

Ezekiel 18:31: Cast away from you all the transgressions which you have committed, and get yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. For why should you die, O house of Israel? 2 Corinthians 5:17: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.
Can God’s people die? Is “once saved always saved” true?

He says “house of Israel” is not Babylon or sinners but “God’s people,” and asks “Can God’s people die? Yeah.” He says of “once saved always saved,” “Come on. Common sense tells you,” and that God “takes no pleasure in punishing people. It’s just he has to do it because it’s the law.”
Can God’s people die? Is “once saved always saved” true?

Isn’t this good? See, these are tremendous promises. And and we fool around with nonsense when we got tremendous, exceedingly great and precious promises. For why should you die, oh house of Israel? Now, house of Israel is not talking about Babylon. It’s not talking about sinners and wicked people. It’s talking about what? God’s people. Can God’s people die? Yeah. This once saved always saved. Come on. Common sense tells you. For I have not no pleasure again in the death of the one who dies, says the Lord. Therefore, turn and live. He reminds us again. He takes no pleasure in punishing people. It’s just he has to do it because it’s the law. Now, we’re going to go to Ezekiel 33 and Ezekiel 3 and we’re going to look at the law of the watchman.
Can God’s people die? Is “once saved always saved” true?

Ezekiel 18:31-32: Cast away from you all the transgressions which you have committed, and get yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. For why should you die, O house of Israel? For I have no pleasure in the death of one who dies,” says the Lord GOD. “Therefore turn and live!”
What is the law of the watchman in Ezekiel 33?

He says the watchman stood on the wall and “would blow the horn” if enemies were coming. He says God made Ezekiel a watchman “to alert people, warn people,” that the message was “Repent,” and that “This church has a responsibility.”
What is the law of the watchman in Ezekiel 33?

The law of the watchman. The watchman was the guy that they put up on the wall and he was to look out and make sure that no enemies were coming, no armies were coming. And if they did, then he would blow the horn. I was going to bring my ram’s horn and do that and I forgot. We’re going to look at the law of the watchman. Now, you better listen closely. All right? Because you have a responsibility. This church has a responsibility. Christianity isn’t just Disneyland. I’ve made you a watchman to the house of Israel. Now he’s talking to Ezekiel. I’ve made you a watchman. Okay. You’re to alert people. I’ve chosen you to alert people, warn people, you know, of the coming destruction. You shall hear a word from what? My mouth. And warn them for me. Tell them what I’m saying. And what was the message to Ezekiel? Repent. He’s telling the people to repent. That is the message. What was Jesus’s first message? Repent and believe the gospel. Repent. What was John the Baptist’s message? Repent. What was the apostles message on the day of Pentecost? Repent. Duh. Turn from your sins. When I say to the wicked, “You shall surely die.” All right.
What is the law of the watchman in Ezekiel 33?

Ezekiel 33:7-9: “So you, son of man: I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel; therefore you shall hear a word from My mouth and warn them for Me. When I say to the wicked, ‘O wicked man, you shall surely die!’ and you do not speak to warn the wicked from his way, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood I will require at your hand. Nevertheless if you warn the wicked to turn from his way, and he does not turn from his way, he shall die in his iniquity; but you have delivered your soul.
What happens if we stay silent and do not warn people?

He says if you don’t speak to warn the wicked, “that wicked man shall die in his iniquity,” and says “Most American Christians just don’t care if the guy next door is going to hell or not.” On “his blood will I require at your hand,” he says the Hebrew is “seek” and “inquire,” and God will ask, “Why didn’t you speak up?”
What happens if we stay silent and do not warn people?

And that’s what exactly we heard in Ezekiel, wasn’t it? Isn’t that what John the Baptist said? Isn’t that what Jesus said? Yeah. You’re going to die. You’re going to pay a price for your sins, for being wicked if you do not speak. See the these these people say, “Well, I don’t wear my Christianity on my sleeve.” Well, you better be wearing it somewhere where people can see it. If you don’t speak silent, silent saints to warn the wicked from his wicked way, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity. That guy’s going to die. You don’t care. Most American Christians just don’t care if the guy next door is going to hell or not. They’re just concerned about themselves. I’m not going to speak up and rock the boat. Somebody better be rocking some boats because that boat’s going to sink. And if you’re not rocking it and get their attention, they’re just going to sink. They’re going to die. But listen to this. His blood will I require at your hand. Now that’s a strong word. The only problem is in the Hebrew it’s not require, it’s seek, it’s inquire. You can’t find anywhere in the Bible that honest, ignorant followers were punished in any way for being silent. What God is saying, he’s looking for you to get the message out. He’s seeking for you and he’s going to inquire of you. Why didn’t you speak up? Why didn’t you live up? So that that family member could have been convicted and had a chance for eternal life. That neighbor, that fellow worker. See, America’s got us being politically correct that Christianity has no place in the public. Well, where does secularism have a place in the public? Secular means non-spiritual and spiritual things don’t. It’s not in the constitution and it’s not in common sense. Okay, the watchmen.
What happens if we stay silent and do not warn people?

Ezekiel 33:8: When I say to the wicked, ‘O wicked man, you shall surely die!’ and you do not speak to warn the wicked from his way, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood I will require at your hand.
What is the difference between a wise watchman and a worthless one?

He says the wise watchman says “eternal life is by faith and keeping Bible laws, good works,” and speaks God’s laws. The worthless one says “eternal life by my faith” and lives “any way they want,” stays silent or speaks his own opinions, and does not “take personal responsibility.”
What is the difference between a wise watchman and a worthless one?

We’re going to look at the wise watchmen and then we’re going to look at the worthless watchmen and then you can decide which watchmen you are. Here are the wise. The wise say eternal life is by faith and keeping Bible laws, good works. Okay, that’s the wise watchman. The wicked, worthless watchman, eternal life by my faith. And then they live any way they want. Well, I’m saved by faith. I can just do what I want. Hallelujah. Going to heaven. Nowhere else to go. Worthless watchmen. They speak God laws. Worthless watchmen. They are silent or speak their own opinions. Well, I believe. Watch when people say I believe. Watch when people say my faith. It should be what Jesus said to believe. What Jesus would do. Yes. Personal accountability. Blame society. Blame your parents. Yeah. Blame the schools. Blame somebody. Don’t take personal responsibility for your actions. Speaks repentance speaks positive only. Repent is negative. And like Oprah Winfrey who is the expert on religion, you know, she says, “Nobody’s going to come to your church.” That’s why churches aren’t growing because, you know, they don’t want to hear their sin and you got to repent.
How should Christians warn people about sin?

He says “We are to warn the people, teach the people, and never do it in a prince peasant attitude that I’m better than you.” He says to do it in “a Moses attitude, the meekest man in the world,” who spoke what God told him “regardless of what the crowd did.”
How should Christians warn people about sin?

They want to hear that. They want to hear positive things. Got no respect for the Ten Commandments saying not to commit sexual immorality. Now, she don’t want to hear she’s wrong. She don’t want to hear she’s going to hell. So she goes to Joel Osteen’s church so she won’t hear it. Are you there? Yeah. She walk in here, she’ll hear it. Why? Because we don’t want people going to hell. We don’t want people ruining their life now and spending an eternity in the lake of fire. And we are to warn the people, teach the people, and never do it in a prince peasant attitude that I’m better than you. You do it in a Moses attitude, the meekest man in the world. He did what God told him to do. Spoke what God told him to speak regardless of what the crowd did. That’s why he was the meekest man on earth outside of Christ.
Is there a real hell, or is God too loving to punish anyone?

He says some teach “God is love. He won’t harm anybody” and “There’s no real hell. There’s no real punishment.” His answer is “We got a lot of lies out there,” and he says “somebody’s got to be a wise watchman.”
Is there a real hell, or is God too loving to punish anyone?

Fair is doing right. Fair is eternal life [unclear] works. Worthless doesn’t help my family. Doesn’t help anybody. Punishment now and in the eternal lake of fire. God is love. He won’t harm anybody. Remember we taught you that the liberal church, God is love. He wouldn’t hurt anybody. Those are just allegories. There’s no real hell. There’s no real punishment. You know, the Catholic Church, they got their people convinced because they’re Catholics, everything’s cool, man. You know, you have a auto accident, we come and give you the death [unclear] at the end. You’re going to [unclear]. You’re going to hell. We got a lot of lies out there.
Will we be a wise church or a worthless one?

He says “We got to make a choice to be a wise Christian or a worthless one,” and the wise one is “concerned about other people and their end result in this life and in the life to come.” He says he wants “a watchman church that is hearing from God and telling the world,” expects opposition, and says “God will prevail.”
Will we be a wise church or a worthless one?

Protestants, Catholics, but somebody’s got to be a wise watchman. Can I hear an amen? Somebody’s got to decide to do it God’s way. Somebody’s got to decide to be humble, not follow the crowd, and speak what God said to speak. And that’s the way we want this church to be. We got to make a choice to be a wise Christian or a worthless one. The wise one will be concerned about other people and their end result in this life and in the life to come. You see, I don’t want to see my homosexual acquaintances die from AIDS. It’s not just eternity. They’re dying now. They’re suffering horribly now. And all they got to do is admit they’re wrong. Ask Christ to come in and he can change that lifestyle just like he can change the drug addict, the alcoholic, the liar, the thief. So we got to decide. Are we going to be silent? Are we going to learn the word for ourselves? Are we going to not rock the boat or are we going to rock the boat so people wake up? Are we going to speak Jesus is the only way? Are we going to give in to all roads lead to the same God? That’s ridiculous. Are we going to speak up for Bible morality and withstand our adversaries? Don’t uh diminish yourself or think lowly of yourself. God will keep adding. He knows when to add and how to add. Are you with me? The bottom line is we can be a church who is really a watchman church that is hearing from God and telling the world. And yes, we will have enemies. Yes, we will have an opponent. Yes, we will have people opposing us. But in the end, God will prevail because a people was faithful to hear his word and speak it and we will see a great harvest in America and throughout the world. Amen. So, we got to ask God this morning for that new heart and that new spirit.
What is a “law” according to this message?
He says “A law is a statement that has a punishment.” If you violate it, “there is a payment to pay.”

He says Ezekiel was carried away captive at about 25 and began prophesying in the sixth year of captivity, “several hundred miles away from Jeremiah who is speaking the same things.” He says “These two are not connected with each other at all,” and that God “is a supernatural God.”
Can a father be blamed for his grown son’s sin?

He says “the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father,” and “nor shall the father bear the iniquity of the son.” Of his own sons he says if they go out in sin and are of age, “you can’t blame me. I did my job. They just didn’t listen.”
Does a person get what his own life earns?
He says “If a guy does right, that he’s going to get the rewards of right. If the guy does wrong, he’s going to get the rewards of wrong.”
He says God is “not up there saying, ‘Oh boy, I get to get that one.’” He says God asks, “Have I any pleasure delight in the wicked that they should die,” and that “He gets no delight in you dying.”
What good things does he say Judas did?

He says Judas “followed Christ,” “preached the gospel,” “laid hands on people and they got healed,” and “cast out demons.” He says these were “right good works,” but they were forgotten when Judas betrayed Christ.
What does he say does not come into the equation of God’s judgment?
He says God judges “Everyone according to his ways,” and that “Not grace, not faith, not the church I attend, not helping the poor, not tithing, none of those things even come into the equation.”
Are we a three-part being, according to this message?
He says “you’re a three-part being … Body, soul, and spirit.” He says the soul is “the emotions, the intellect, and the will,” and that when the body dies “the spirit continues.”
How does he say you get a new mind?
He asks, “if preachers don’t preach the word, how you going to get a new mind? If you don’t write, read, and study the word, how you going to get a new mind?”
What responsibility does he say the church has?
He says “you have a responsibility. This church has a responsibility,” and that “Christianity isn’t just Disneyland.” The watchman’s job is to warn people of coming destruction.
What message was the watchman to give?
He says the message to Ezekiel was “Repent,” and that it was also Jesus’s first message, “Repent and believe the gospel,” John the Baptist’s message and the apostles’ message on the day of Pentecost.
Is it enough to keep your faith private?
He says people say “I don’t wear my Christianity on my sleeve,” and answers “you better be wearing it somewhere where people can see it.”
What does he say about Christianity having a place in public life?

He says “America’s got us being politically correct that Christianity has no place in the public,” and asks “where does secularism have a place in the public?” He says secular means non-spiritual, and that it is “not in the constitution and it’s not in common sense.”
What does he say about blaming others for our actions?
He lists among the marks of the worthless watchman: “Blame society. Blame your parents. … Don’t take personal responsibility for your actions.”
What kind of church does he want this to be?

He says “we can be a church who is really a watchman church that is hearing from God and telling the world.” He says there will be opposition, “But in the end, God will prevail because a people was faithful to hear his word and speak it.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Jeremiah 23 that God judges false shepherds who destroy and scatter His sheep, gathers a remnant, and raises up the righteous Branch of David. He explains…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Jeremiah 23 that God judges false shepherds who destroy and scatter His sheep, gathers a remnant, and raises up the righteous Branch of David. He explains how Jesus can be both the Branch and the root, calls the church His body, and ends with a call to balance judgment with hope.
What is happening in Jeremiah’s day, and why preach hope?

He says Jeremiah preached when God was judging and correcting His people, with wars, captivity, famines, sickness and economic crisis. In the middle of it Jeremiah also speaks “a tremendous word of hope,” and he titles the message about the Messiah: false shepherds run and the sheep run to Jesus.
What is happening in Jeremiah’s day, and why preach hope?

Jeremiah is preaching at a time when God is judging and punishing, correcting his people. There are wars. There’s a captivity. There are famines and sicknesses. You know, economic crisis is going on all around Jeremiah. And he brings this message just a few years before the first captivity happened. He’s bringing these messages. And in the middle of these messages of punishment, of correction, of wars, of plagues, Jeremiah is also speaking a tremendous word of hope for those who will listen and hear it. Don’t we need hope in the midst of crisis? Yes. And so we’re going to call this when the Messiah comes, false shepherds run and the sheep run to Jesus.
Who are the false shepherds who destroy and scatter? (Jeremiah 23:1)

He says Jeremiah 23:1 describes pastors who are destroying and scattering God’s sheep, “the sheep of his pasture.” He says false preachers do not feed people God’s word, do not lead them to Jesus, and “bring them to themselves.” You can tell them, he says, because “they demand that you follow them.”
Who are the false shepherds who destroy and scatter? (Jeremiah 23:1)

Hallelujah. We need the Messiah rising, Jesus Christ. And Jeremiah 23:1: “Woe to the pastors that destroy.” Number one, these pastors, these shepherds are destroying. Number two, they are scattering. Number three, they’re destroying and scattering God’s sheep. And number four, these sheep are the sheep of his pasture. You see the pasture is the place where they are sheep are fed. And these false pro— these false teachers, he deals with prophets in the same chapter, speaks of them in the same way: adulterous men, teaching their own ideas and their own doctrines instead of God’s. [unclear] chapter 6, it says that we are destroyed for lack of knowledge. And in the New Testament, it says we’re destroyed when we don’t believe in Christ. We’re condemned already because we haven’t believed on the only begotten son of God. It is imperative that the people of the world hear that message that without Jesus that rules out Muhammad and every other source. Without Jesus we will be destroyed, and without his word, the knowledge of his word, we will be destroyed. And that’s what these false preachers do they do not feed the people with the knowledge of God’s word, and God’s people end up being destroyed. They don’t lead them to Jesus and bring them to Jesus. They bring them to themselves and they wind up being destroyed. Number two, they scatter the flock. These false preachers scatter the flock, and they’re scattering them from Jesus and his word. See, they don’t want them— they bring them to themselves. And it says over in the book of Acts that there will be grievous wolves coming in among you who will draw disciples after themselves. And this is what false shepherds, false pastors do, false so-called evangelists, or whatever title they got. You can tell who they are because they demand that you follow them.
Who are the false shepherds who destroy and scatter? (Jeremiah 23:1)

Jeremiah 23:1: “Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of My pasture!” says the LORD. Hosea 4:6: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I also will reject you from being priest for Me; Because you have forgotten the law of your God, I also will forget your children. John 3:18: “He who believes in Him is not condemned; but he who does not believe is condemned already, because he has not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God. Acts 20:29-30: For I know this, that after my departure savage wolves will come in among you, not sparing the flock. Also from among yourselves men will rise up, speaking perverse things, to draw away the disciples after themselves.
Who do the sheep belong to, and what is the pasture? (John 10, John 6)

He says the sheep belong to Jesus, who said “I am the good shepherd,” and Psalms 100 calls us “the sheep of his pasture.” He says the pasture is Jesus: in John 6 He is the bread of life, and His word is spirit, truth and life.
Who do the sheep belong to, and what is the pasture? (John 10, John 6)

And they teach things that distract you from Jesus Christ. And his word of righteousness. Amen. This is what these guys do. And we need Jesus. We need his word. And so they scatter from Jesus and his word. Third there, the sheep belong to Jesus. John 10, Jesus said, “I am the good shepherd. My sheep know my voice and I am known of them.” And in Psalms 100, it says, “We are his people and the sheep of his pasture.” And number four, the pasture is Jesus. In John 6:48, Jesus is the bread of life. And in verse 63 of John 6, his word is spirit, his word is truth, his word is life. And so Jesus feeds us with his word and with himself. How many enjoy feeling and participating in the presence of God when he comes? And then the word. Don’t you love it when somebody preaches the word and that Holy Spirit just penetrates your heart and makes that word alive and you go home feeling like you’ve been fed a meal. How many enjoy the word like that? Yes. And that’s what we need. And so Jeremiah is calling out these false pastors. And later in the chapter, it’s the false prophets. In John 9:22, it says, “If any man that could confess that Jesus is Christ, he would be put out of the synagogue.” See, they don’t want people coming to Christ. They want to bring him to their leader. Maybe Joseph Smith, maybe [unclear], Mary Baker [unclear].
Who do the sheep belong to, and what is the pasture? (John 10, John 6)

John 10:14: I am the good shepherd; and I know My sheep, and am known by My own. Psalm 100:3: Know that the LORD, He is God; It is He who has made us, and not we ourselves; We are His people and the sheep of His pasture. John 6:48: I am the bread of life. John 6:63: It is the Spirit who gives life; the flesh profits nothing. The words that I speak to you are spirit, and they are life.
What will God do to pastors who harm His flock? (Jeremiah 23:2-3)

He cites Jeremiah 23:2, “I will visit upon them the evil, the harm of their doing,” because they are hurting God’s people. He says there is “no salvation in any other” than Jesus, and that Jesus Himself will gather “the remnant of my flock” back into His fold.
What will God do to pastors who harm His flock? (Jeremiah 23:2-3)

You know, we bring people to somebody and to somebody’s doctrine instead of Jesus and his doctrine. Amen. And we don’t need those kind of pastors. And God says he’s going to deal with those kind of pastors. Going on in Jeremiah chapter 23:2. Thus saith the Lord against the pastors. I am speaking against the pastors. These pastors that scatter the flock. I will visit upon them the evil, the harm of their doing. See, they’re hurting God’s people. They’re hurting people that don’t even know God because there’s no salvation in any other than who? Jesus Christ. And the foolishness of preaching is what God has chosen to what? Save those that believe. And so, we got to have the preaching of God’s word. And we got to have Jesus involved. And he says, “I’m against these pastors that hurt and do harm.” Then he goes on to say, “I will gather the remnant of my flock.” He says, “I’m going to gather the remnant of my flock from where I have driven them.” Now, it isn’t the false shepherds that’s scattering them now. It’s Jesus Christ. He has driven them into countries, into areas, and he is going to bring them back out into his fold. It says there. And so Jesus is going to come and he is going to drive these people that really want him away from these false shepherds, away from these false pastors, these false teachers, and he’s going to bring them where? Into his fold. Hallelujah. And so in the midst of this big mess that Jeremiah is preaching in, there is a tremendous message of hope. And he says this remnant will be fruitful and increase. You see, when we get into God’s pasture where he feeds us with Jesus, the living bread, and his word, the living bread, that word of life, we become fruitful.
What will God do to pastors who harm His flock? (Jeremiah 23:2-3)

Jeremiah 23:2: Therefore thus says the LORD God of Israel against the shepherds who feed My people: “You have scattered My flock, driven them away, and not attended to them. Behold, I will attend to you for the evil of your doings,” says the LORD. Acts 4:12: Nor is there salvation in any other, for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved.” 1 Corinthians 1:21: For since, in the wisdom of God, the world through wisdom did not know God, it pleased God through the foolishness of the message preached to save those who believe. Jeremiah 23:3: “But I will gather the remnant of My flock out of all countries where I have driven them, and bring them back to their folds; and they shall be fruitful and increase.
Who is the remnant? (Romans 9:27, Romans 11:5, Revelation 12:17)

He says the remnant are the saved, delivered and “set free from sin,” and that “the real followers of Christ are delivered. We’re not just forgiven.” He cites Revelation 12:17, “the remnant which keep the commandments of God and have the testimony of Jesus,” and says they “continued in the apostles’ doctrine,” and not the doctrine of any human teacher.
Who is the remnant? (Romans 9:27, Romans 11:5, Revelation 12:17)

That’s where we get the power to be fruitful, to do what’s right, and we will increase. We will get enlarged. And this is the proof of the remnant. Okay? In Romans 9:27, a remnant shall be saved in the New Testament. So the remnant are people that are saved. They’re delivered. They’re set free from sin. They’re they’re saved from eternal damnation in the lake of fire. They’re saved from the kingdom of darkness and the power of Satan in the kingdom of darkness. They’re delivered. They’re set free from them. A remnant shall be what? Saved. You see, the real followers of Christ are delivered. We’re not just forgiven. We are what? Delivered. Set free. The kingdom of darkness has no power over us. Sin has no power over us. Romans 6 says— Romans 11:5: “At this present time there is a remnant. You see there is people when that book was written that were delivered they were saved by the power of Jesus and the power of his word. And Jeremiah preached this hundreds of years before it happened in the New Testament. Revelation 12:17 plainly tells us who’s the remnant is. It describes the remnant in clear detail. Satan makes war with the remnant of her seed. The remnant which keep the commandments of God and have the testimony of Jesus. You see these people that put their trust in Jesus and they follow Jesus and they keep the commandments of God. They keep the apostles doctrine as it says in that they continued in the apostles doctrine. Not Joel Osteen’s doctrine, not Martin Luther’s doctrine, not Calvin’s doctrine, not St. Augustine’s doctrine. They continued in the apostles doctrine. These are the remnant. Hallelujah. These are the people that are saved. These are the people that Jeremiah said God is going to gather. See, he’s getting them away from false prophets. The false prophets are dragging them from him, but he’s going to come and drag them from the false prophets unto himself, and they’re going to be fruitful, and they’re going to be increased.
Who is the remnant? (Romans 9:27, Romans 11:5, Revelation 12:17)

Romans 9:27: Isaiah also cries out concerning Israel: “Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, The remnant will be saved. Romans 11:5: Even so then, at this present time there is a remnant according to the election of grace. Revelation 12:17: And the dragon was enraged with the woman, and he went to make war with the rest of her offspring, who keep the commandments of God and have the testimony of Jesus Christ. Acts 2:42: And they continued steadfastly in the apostles’ doctrine and fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and in prayers.
What is the message of hope in the midst of crisis? (Jeremiah 23:4-5)

He says “we have a message of hope for all Americans” because Jesus is “still Lord in the midst of the judgments.” He says if you are discouraged or fearful, “throw it away,” because Jesus “still has a plan, and nothing can stop him from fulfilling it.”
What is the message of hope in the midst of crisis? (Jeremiah 23:4-5)

Hallelujah. We got a message, church. We have a message in the midst of the darkness that’s in the earth. In the midst of the conflicts that are in the earth, in the midst of the mess that’s in America, we have a message of hope for all Americans. See, he’s still Lord in the midst of the judgments, in the midst of the crisis. He’s still Jesus, the King, the Lord. Then he says, “I will set up shepherds which shall feed them, and they shall no more fear nor be dismayed or be discouraged.” I trust this morning you’re not discouraged because of the message of Christ, the message of how powerful Jesus is keeps you courageous in the midst of very difficult times which we are in in America. He says the Spirit must be involved to change you “from a fleshly creature to a new spiritual creature,” and that “It’s not in the letter. It’s not in book learning.”
Did people question the virgin birth in Jesus’ day?
He says yes, and that people still do: “Do they question it today? Absolutely.” He says Luke 3:23 shows people “supposed” Jesus was the son of Joseph.
What does he say happens when you know the word and have scriptural answers?
He says that when God gives you scriptural answers in the midst of a multitude, “They don’t know what to say.”
What does he mean when he says Jesus is the root?
He says “the root is the source of the rest of the plant,” and Jesus says “I’m the source. I’m the origin of David,” as well as David’s descendant.
Can Christians do anything without Jesus?
He says no: “Without me, you’ll do nothing.” He says “You won’t even live.”
What does he mean when he says the king is in me?
He says, “I’m not just a child of the king. The king is in me.” He says we are the branches and the body and temple of Jesus Christ.

p: In this Father’s Day message a guest speaker compares the birth of a baby with being born again, saying a baby has only two options, to be born and live or to die, and the same is true spiritually. He then follows Israel out of Egypt: Satan going after new believers through Pharaoh and the midwives, the lamb’s blood on the doorposts, and the hindrances after deliverance, including complaining, the flesh, emotions and fear. He closes with Jonah 2:9, “Salvation is of the Lord.”
What can the birth of a baby teach about the spiritual life?
He tells of his wife’s pregnancy and says “they really only have two options. They’re either going to be born and live or they’re going to die.” He says the same is true in the spiritual realm.
What can the birth of a baby teach about the spiritual life?

All the fathers this morning, fathers that break their backs for their family, they sacrifice themselves in their lives. It’s a wonderful thing. This morning we want to talk about the father and what he does for his children. When my wife became pregnant, I just want to tell a quick story. When Lara was pregnant, we made an appointment with the OB, the [unclear]. First thing she pulls out the monitor and she checks the heartbeat. Five, six weeks into it, the baby’s heart is beating. We were there three months and the baby’s heart, boom boom boom boom boom. That’s the first thing you check when you walk in. Uh, as we got closer to the due date, we visited the doctor more and more and more, and a week, every week. First it was every month, then every two weeks, then every month, every week, and uh, and then labor came, and that was just an awful experience for Lara. Me, you know, I was just, I was just kicking back, and uh, she had the baby after a bloody mess, and it’s just, it’s just an interesting experience. I’m not going to say it’s like the best thing in the whole world, cuz it’s just pretty nuts, all right. It’s, it’s crazy. Best thing in the whole world, it’s the best thing in the whole world. And uh, you know, I got to hold a leg and it’s like, “Oh gosh.” Praise God. Anyway, at the end of it all, I had, I got a little emotional with both my kids because I was just glad they came out okay after all that, after all the nine months of, “Are they okay?” or this or that, you know, complications, are they turned the right way, you know, is it [unclear], is it this, is it that, you know, it could be all these things. There could be a miscarriage. Finally, at birth, the baby’s okay. Praise God. So they give you a picture like this, and there, there it is, baby in the womb. And of course, you know, the TV shows, they explain it. You kids over here, you teenagers, you just have no idea unless you’re there seeing it all happen. Babies don’t come out clean, they’re all messy and ugly, you know. Beckham had the cord wrapped around his neck when he came out. He was blue. I was like, “Who is this kid?” And I was like, “Is that supposed to happen?” You know, in my mind I’m, “Oh, he’s like, oh, it’s blue, it’s, it’s baby blue.” You know, it’s okay, you know, he was trying to brush it off. Of course, the, you know, come on. But really, when it comes down to it, a baby, the, the, the thing that you care about, they really only have two options. They’re either going to be born and live or they’re going to die. I mean, it’s awful, but really the only option for that baby in the womb is to come out, or the other option is that they’re going to die. And it’s the same way in the spiritual

realm. They’ve been conceived, they’re being formed. You see, some people, when God’s word comes, it triggers something in their spiritual man. When they hear the word, it triggers a conception, and they begin to grow. And if, and people, as they keep getting reached by the church, they begin to grow, and the church does their job to continue that growth process. And finally, when they decide to accept Christ, it doesn’t take, it doesn’t have to take nine months like it does with, you know, natural pregnancy, but it takes time. We’ve got to understand those who have not been birthed, those who don’t know Christ, there’s only two options. We are going to live with our Father in heaven, or we are going to go and die and go in the lake of fire. And it’s a horrible thing, just like in the natural world, it’s a horrible thing when a, a baby dies. It’s awful. And no, and God doesn’t want any babies dying. pattern. And of course, God had taken them all this way to the Promised Land. And we know that an evil report came in Numbers 13:32 regarding the Promised Land.
