items.ser: Four Difficult Issues to Understand · Part 1
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer begins a look at four difficult issues in Revelation 20: the bottomless pit, Satan bound and loosed, the thousand years, and the first resurrection. He first questions the pre-tribulation rapture picture, then shows from Luke, Romans and Revelation what the bottomless pit is. He argues that Satan has been bound and loosed before, citing 1 Chronicles 21, Job and Luke 10, and that Satan was cast out of the earth when Jesus was lifted up.
What does he say about the picture of the pre-tribulation rapture?

He shows a picture of the pre-tribulation rapture theory and says he is “shocked that they have Jesus up there in the sky being seen.” He argues that if Jesus really appeared, “the world’s going to know what’s going on,” and that “that’s exactly what the Bible says when he comes, every eye shall” see him.
What does he say about the picture of the pre-tribulation rapture?

And today we’re going to hit a topic that I, I have titled “Four Difficult Issues to Understand” in Revelations chapter 20, and we’re going to try and give you some clear understanding of these things, so when you hear things on the radio and TV, you have a mind that can filter it and organize it and make sense out of it. Uh, here is a picture of the pre-tribulation rapture theory, where the church is raptured out, and I’m shocked that they have Jesus up there in the sky being seen. Because, you know, uh, in the movie Left Behind and these end-time pre-tribulation rapture movies, they have the saints being called up, and the world not knowing what went on. But if Jesus really appeared, how many you know, the world’s going to know what’s going on. Yeah, there ain’t going to be nobody, “What’s happening? Where’d everybody go?” So I’m shocked that Jesus is shown here, but uh, that’s exactly what the Bible says when he comes, every eye shall what? See him. So there’s no, uh, lack of knowledge. And you see the people coming out of the graves over here, you see these two people coming out of the car, this guy already left, and uh, that car accidents, airplanes hitting buildings and crashing because the pilot went to heaven, and all kinds of, of catastrophic problems because the saints went, in auto accidents and car, planes falling and crashing, and so
What does he say about the picture of the pre-tribulation rapture?
Revelation 1:7: Behold, He is coming with clouds, and every eye will see Him, even they who pierced Him. And all the tribes of the earth will mourn because of Him. Even so, Amen.
What are the four difficult things to understand in Revelation 20?

He calls the rapture picture “a great theory, but it is a theory.” The four things in Revelation 20 are “the bottomless pit,” Satan bound and chained in the bottomless pit and then loosed, a thousand years where Satan is bound and the martyrs reign with Christ, and “the first resurrection.”
What are the four difficult things to understand in Revelation 20?

forth. Uh, it’s a great theory, but it is a theory. And in Revelations chapter 20, there are four difficult things that we are going to, to discuss this morning. Number one, the bottomless pit. Number two, Satan bound, chained in the bottomless pit, and then loosed. And a thousand years, where Satan is bound and the martyrs reign with Christ. And then the fourth one is this topic called the first resurrection. Okay, fair enough. Hallelujah. Revelations 20 is going to be discussing these four areas. Now, last week we saw in the war of the word that God dealt with
Does he say Jesus returns with a literal army and swords?

He says “He didn’t come down with an army literally and war with swords and bows and arrows.” He says God dealt with nations with his word, backed up by plagues, famine and wars between tribes and nations, and “God’s power is in his word.”
Does he say Jesus returns with a literal army and swords?

nations with his word, and he backed up his word by using plagues and acts of God and famine and wars between tribes and nations to fulfill his word. He didn’t come down with an army literally and war with swords and bows and arrows. You remember the sword that came out of Jesus’s mouth was what? The word of God. See, God’s power is in his word, and those carcasses and all that is not going to be from God’s army annihilating the people of the earth in a real war. It’s going to be God’s word causes it to happen. Are you with me? All right, somebody said I didn’t make that clear last week, so I’m trying to clarify
Does he say Jesus returns with a literal army and swords?

Revelation 19:15: Now out of His mouth goes a sharp sword, that with it He should strike the nations. And He Himself will rule them with a rod of iron. He Himself treads the winepress of the fierceness and wrath of Almighty God.
How does he illustrate the bottomless pit with a whirlpool and a black hole?

He shows a lake draining through a dam outlet and a NASA black hole photo as natural pictures of the pit, and says “God doesn’t use natural things to chain, he just uses his word.” He says science cannot explain gravity: “Try to get science to really show you and clearly explain what gravity is, and they can’t.”
How does he illustrate the bottomless pit with a whirlpool and a black hole?

it. Now, the first area we’re going to hit is this bottomless pit. Got a picture here of a lake that’s going down the dam outlet, and this big, I’ve been there, and there’s a big tornado, uh, water tornado, water tunnel, funnel, and man, this water is moving fast and going down and so forth, [unclear] me, and I like to get as close as I can, and the rangers, I said, “Don’t you go another step.” I’m very [unclear], but it’s a great noise and it’s a great sight to see. Here at the bottom we have an artist with Satan chained, and uh, I, I get a kick out of this stuff, because God doesn’t use natural things to chain, he just uses his word. When he speaks, you can’t move, you’re not going to move, he doesn’t have to come down. But the chain is given to us so we understand in the natural, uh, in the spiritual what happens, in natural illustrations. And then we got the NASA black hole photo up here, and uh, I love the way science tries to explain this stuff, and I love the way you people fall for it. If a scientist says it, it must be right. Uh, they say this black hole is through the, uh, relativity, uh, the science of relativity, that’s the, and I know you guys know all this stuff, that’s the power of gravity and light and motion in the universe and time, see, and none of them work together, you know. They say that Einstein’s theory was proven, but it’s not proven, cuz they don’t work together. Did you guys know that? See, we just accept a lot of stuff, and so they try to explain this black, black hole by saying a star died, and when the star died it caused a big force of gravity that just drew in everything around, and light could not pass through that area because gravity was so strong. Now, folks, you get science to prove that, and I’ll throw away my Bible. Light is its own character, how many of you know that? Yes. And darkness is the absence of light. There is no thing, such thing as darkness, it’s the absence of light, and we call it darkness. Are you there? Try to get science to really show you and clearly explain what gravity is, and they can’t. They can just tell you what it
What do Revelation 20:1–3 and Luke 8:31 say about the bottomless pit?

He reads Revelation 20:1–3, where an angel with the key and a great chain binds the dragon for a thousand years. He turns to Luke 8:31, where the demons say “don’t cast us into the bottomless pit, because we don’t want to be tormented before our time.”
What do Revelation 20:1–3 and Luke 8:31 say about the bottomless pit?

does. See, I went to school once, and my mind thinks this way: you tell me something, you better be able to back it up, because my mind thinks in a manner, okay, what about this, what about that, what about this, and if you don’t have answers, then shut up and just admit you don’t have this kind of knowledge. So it’s very interesting, and actually when they really show a real photo of a black hole, there’s no black hole at all, there’s actually light there. How many have you seen real pictures of black holes? Yeah. See, but somewhere in the middle of that light there’s supposed to be a black hole. Anyway, I use these illustrations to illustrate the bottomless pit, the abyss. “An angel,” Revelations 20:1, “having the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand, laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil and Satan, and bound him a thousand years, and cast him into the bottomless pit, he shut him up and put a seal up on him, that that he should not deceive the nations anymore till the thousand years be fulfilled, and after that he must be loosed a little season.” Okay, now let’s talk about the bottomless pit in Luke 8:31. You remember the story there of the demon-possessed man that had thousands of demons, because they called him Legion, and when Jesus came to Legion, and he had these demons, and he was strong and he could do certain supernatural things. They spoke to him and said, “Hey, Son of God,” they knew who he was, “Have you come to torment us before our time?” See, they knew who Jesus was, they knew his power. Are you there, church? And so Jesus is going to command them to come out, and, and they said, “Listen, don’t cast us into the bottomless pit, because we don’t want to be tormented before our time.” And so he put them in a herd of swine, a herd of pigs, and the pigs went nuts and ran down the cliff, and these people’s, uh, income was
What do Revelation 20:1–3 and Luke 8:31 say about the bottomless pit?

Revelation 20:1-3: Then I saw an angel coming down from heaven, having the key to the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand. He laid hold of the dragon, that serpent of old, who is the Devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years; and he cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up, and set a seal on him, so that he should deceive the nations no more till the thousand years were finished. But after these things he must be released for a little while. Luke 8:31: And they begged Him that He would not command them to go out into the abyss.
What does he conclude the bottomless pit is?

He says “the bottomless pit is a place where spiritual wicked beings are tormented and imprisoned,” and in Romans 10:7 the abyss is used as “an illustration of the abiding place of the dead.” He says Satan is its king, but the kingdom of God “is more powerful than the kingdom of darkness.”
What does he conclude the bottomless pit is?

destroyed by these demons. And so, the bottomless pit is a place where spiritual wicked beings are tormented and imprisoned. Amen. Now, you also remember the story in Romans 10:7. He quotes in Romans 10:7 out of Deuteronomy, and he says, “Will we ascend into heaven to bring Christ down, or will we go into the abyss,” the bottomless pit, “to bring Christ up,” that is, from the dead. So Romans, the writer of Romans is using it as an illustration of the abiding place of the dead. Well, Christ wasn’t there anymore, but in Deuteronomy it actually says the sea, “Will you go across the sea?” And in many places in the Bible the sea, the ocean, is described as the deep, you know, a deep thing. So then in Revelations 9:11, which we’ve already covered, that there was an angel that was king over it, called Apollyon, or Destroyer, and so he is the king, and that is Satan himself, he’s the king of the bottomless pit, this kingdom of evil. The beast also came from the bottomless pit, seven heads and ten horns, and the beast that warred with the two prophets and finally killed them came from the bottomless pit, with seven heads and ten horns. An angel of God has the key to the bottomless pit. The angel, he released the, the, uh, dragon, the, uh, locust to come out, and he bounds Satan in it. So an angel up in heaven has more power than the king of the bottomless pit. Hallelujah. And that’s the kingdom we’re serving, the kingdom of God, the kingdom of light, the kingdom of righteousness is more powerful than the kingdom of darkness. Hallelujah. So the conclusion of the whole matter is the bottomless pit is a place of imprisonment and torment for powers of darkness, and it is a source of spiritual evil. Now, let’s take a look
What does he conclude the bottomless pit is?

Romans 10:7: or, “ ‘Who will descend into the abyss?’ ” (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead). Deuteronomy 30:12-13: It is not in heaven, that you should say, ‘Who will ascend into heaven for us and bring it to us, that we may hear it and do it?’ Nor is it beyond the sea, that you should say, ‘Who will go over the sea for us and bring it to us, that we may hear it and do it?’ Revelation 9:11: And they had as king over them the angel of the bottomless pit, whose name in Hebrew is Abaddon, but in Greek he has the name Apollyon.
Do angels or Satan have wings?

He says “angels don’t have wings, and neither does Satan have wings.” He says seraphim and cherubim have wings but not angels, that we put angels with wings on trees because “it’s handed down to us,” and “Angels are spirits, they don’t need wings to fly.”
Do angels or Satan have wings?

again at this Revelations 20. Here I got a picture again of Satan being thrown into the bottomless pit. I love these renditions of artists, they put wings on everybody, and angels don’t have wings, and neither does Satan have wings. We know he has a tail, and we know that he’s described as seven heads and ten horns, but never, heard, does Satan have wings, nor does an angel have wings. Seraphim have wings, cherubim have wings, but not angels. Are you there? I just keep bringing that out because, you know, we put angels with wings on our Christmas trees, and we just do things because it’s handed down to us, and we don’t even think about what is the real source here. Angels are spirits, they don’t need wings to fly, they just fly by the word of God.
What problem does he see in taking Revelation 20 literally?
He rereads Revelation 20:1–3 and says that if we take it literally, “Satan is not, never been bound, and never will be bound until this time, so he has free reign in the earth.”
What problem does he see in taking Revelation 20 literally?

Hallelujah. Uh, actually they don’t fly, they just transport themselves, they move by the word of God. Again, “An angel having the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand, laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil and Satan, and bound him a thousand years, and he cast him into the bottomless pit, shut him up and put a seal on him, that he should not deceive the nations anymore till the thousand years be fulfilled, and after that he must be loosed a little season.” Now, the problem we got here is this: if we take this scripture literally, see, that means Satan is not, never been bound, and never will be bound until this time, so he has free reign in the earth. Are you there? If we take this scripture
What problem does he see in taking Revelation 20 literally?

Revelation 20:1-3: Then I saw an angel coming down from heaven, having the key to the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand. He laid hold of the dragon, that serpent of old, who is the Devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years; and he cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up, and set a seal on him, so that he should deceive the nations no more till the thousand years were finished. But after these things he must be released for a little while.
What do 1 Chronicles 21:1 and 2 Samuel 24:1 show about Satan being bound and loosed?

He says Satan “has been bound and loosed, and bound and loosed since the beginning.” He puts 1 Chronicles 21:1 (Satan moved David to number Israel) beside 2 Samuel 24:1 (the Lord’s anger) and says this is “God needing to deal with Israel because of their sins,” with Satan as God’s “enforcer, because God can’t do evil.”
What do 1 Chronicles 21:1 and 2 Samuel 24:1 show about Satan being bound and loosed?

literally. But when we go to the Scriptures, we’re going to find that Satan has been bound and loosed before. Okay, we’re going to tell you in the Scriptures that Satan not only is going to be bound and loosed in that generation of the end, but he has been bound and loosed, and bound and loosed since the beginning. Are you ready? 1 Chronicles 21:1, “Satan stood up against Israel and provoked David to number Israel,” and we know that when they did it, they didn’t do it according to the law and take the census taxes, so the plague came. Okay, and who stirred up David to do it? Satan. Okay, now look at this nice little clear expansion of this verse, same story, same incident, 2 Samuel 24:1, “The Lord’s anger was kindled against,” who? Israel, ‘cause they were living bad, they were sinning. You see, a lot of people don’t think God is involved in people’s lives today, but he is. And you young people, you can rest assured, if you choose the road of wrong, God’s going to get you, bad things are going to come in your life. Why? ‘Cause he wants you to repent, turn, and live and do right. And so we justify and say, “Well, there is no God, there’s no power, it’s a bunch of bull.” Well, you’ll find out, like those before you, that big problems are going to come in your life. All right. And so he moved David to number Israel in Judah. And so when we mix the two scriptures together, what we have is God needing to deal with Israel because of their sins, and God can’t do evil. There’s certain things God cannot do, and they’re all good. So he gets Satan, he releases Satan, who was bound to not hurt Israel before, now he releases Satan to go and what? Move David to number Israel, so that a plague can come and bring discipline to them. And Satan, of course, is the source of the plague. Are you there? Hallelujah. See, Satan is God’s, uh, what do you call it, enforcer, because God can’t do evil. See,
What do 1 Chronicles 21:1 and 2 Samuel 24:1 show about Satan being bound and loosed?

1 Chronicles 21:1: Now Satan stood up against Israel, and moved David to number Israel. 2 Samuel 24:1: Again the anger of the LORD was aroused against Israel, and He moved David against them to say, “Go, number Israel and Judah.”
What does Job show about Satan needing God’s permission?

He says in Job that Satan could not touch Job because God had a hedge, and “Satan cannot do this till God gave permission.” He says God “will never let Satan or anything tempt you above what you can endure,” and “He doesn’t always remove it, but he empowers me to handle it.”
What does Job show about Satan needing God’s permission?

hallelujah. So he was bound, and then what? Loosed, and then he’s bound again. He can’t touch Israel anymore after that until God, what? Gives him permission. Satan cannot do this till God gave permission, and here we have the binding and the loosening of Satan to deceive. Let’s go to Job. The Lord said to Job, Satan comes up before God up in heaven, and, and God says, “Where you been, Satan?” He said, “I’ve been walking to and fro throughout the earth, just trying to find somebody like you that I can deceive.” And then God says, “What if you consider Job? He’s righteous, he’s mature, he’s upright, he won’t change his faith in me no matter what happens.” And Job said, said, “Oh yeah, but you got a hedge around about him, nobody can touch him, but you let me touch him.” Was he bound? Was Satan bound? Yes. Why? God had a hedge, Satan could not touch Job. And God brought up the issue, and I don’t want God doing that up there on me. I’m [unclear] no Job, so, you know, leave me alone here. But see, God will never bring, the Bible says he will never bring any temptation that you cannot have victory over. That there’s a way of escape that you can bear up under. He will never let Satan or anything tempt you above what you can endure. If you fall, it was your decision, because you had the power to what? Bear up under it. Hallelujah. So I’m not worried about tomorrow, and I’m not worried about temptations and all that, because God empowers me to get through them. He doesn’t always remove it, but he empowers me to handle it. Amen. So then Satan goes and he touches his children, kills his children, took his finances, took his wealth, and Job still wouldn’t do anything. Then Satan comes back and says, “Well, touch his body personally,” and, see, Satan could not touch his body personally until God says you can. And then he plagued him with what some people think was elephantiasis, these boils where the skin gets real tough and real thick and just very painful and ugly, and uh, still Job would not denounce God. Hallelujah. So Satan was what? Bound, and he was what? Loosed. Hallelujah. Luke 10, verse 18, we’re going to show you examples of
What does Job show about Satan needing God’s permission?

Job 1:6-12: Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came among them. And the LORD said to Satan, “From where do you come?” So Satan answered the LORD and said, “From going to and fro on the earth, and from walking back and forth on it.” Then the LORD said to Satan, “Have you considered My servant Job, that there is none like him on the earth, a blameless and upright man, one who fears God and shuns evil?” So Satan answered the LORD and said, “Does Job fear God for nothing? Have You not made a hedge around him, around his household, and around all that he has on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his possessions have increased in the land. But now, stretch out Your hand and touch all that he has, and he will surely curse You to Your face!” And the LORD said to Satan, “Behold, all that he has is in your power; only do not lay a hand on his person.” So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD. Job 2:4-7: So Satan answered the LORD and said, “Skin for skin! Yes, all that a man has he will give for his life. But stretch out Your hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will surely curse You to Your face!” And the LORD said to Satan, “Behold, he is in your hand, but spare his life.” So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD, and struck Job with painful boils from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head. 1 Corinthians 10:13: No temptation has overtaken you except such as is common to man; but God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you are able, but with the temptation will also make the way of escape, that you may be able to bear it.
What does Luke 10:18 teach about Satan’s fall and our authority?

He reads “I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven” and says it happened “when these apostles went out and used the power of his word.” He says this is the first record that the apostles, and all believers, have authority over Satan.
What does Luke 10:18 teach about Satan’s fall and our authority?

Satan being cast out of heaven. “I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven.” See, the apostles went out and they preached the gospel, and they healed the sick, demons were cast out, people were saved, and they came back reporting to Jesus, and Jesus said, “I saw Satan as lightning fall from heaven” when, when these apostles went out and used the power of his word. “I give you power to tread on serpents and scorpions and over all the power of the enemy.” This is our first record that not only did the apostles have authority over Satan, but all of us believers have authority over
What does Luke 10:18 teach about Satan’s fall and our authority?

Luke 10:18-19: And He said to them, “I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven. Behold, I give you the authority to trample on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall by any means hurt you.
When does he say Satan was judged and cast out of the earth?

He cites Revelation 12:7 and John 12:31, and says Satan was judged “when Jesus died on the cross.” He says “Satan was loose, now he’s bound,” that “You are a conqueror in the mess,” and that Satan “can do nothing without the big guy’s permission.”
When does he say Satan was judged and cast out of the earth?

Satan. Hallelujah. It’s important for you to know this. See, so not only was he cast out, he was cast out by the preaching of God’s word from believers. Revelations 12:7, “War broke out in heaven, Michael and his angels fought with the dragon and his angels, that old great serpent, the great dragon, the serpent, the Devil.” Satan was cast out of heaven to the earth, and so, see, we have another, before the end of the world, when we, in, in Revelations 20, we have an account that Satan’s been cast down before. Amen. From heaven. John 12:31, we’re going to show you Scriptures where he was cast out of the earth. Okay, cast down from heaven to, to earth, now he’s cast out of the earth. “Now is the judgment of this world, now shall the prince of this world be cast out, and if I be lifted up from the earth I will draw all men to,” who? Me. So when was Satan judged and cast out of the earth? When Jesus died on the cross, when he was lifted up to draw all men to him, he cast the prince of this world out. See, Satan was loose, now he’s bound. Are you there? See, it’s important for you to know that these things have been going on through the Bible. It’s very important, because this gives you the knowledge to live powerfully for Jesus Christ right now on earth. You’re not waiting for some, you know, magical thing at the end of the world to get you out of this mess. You are a conqueror in the mess. That’s right. That’s how powerful the blood, the cross, is. Again, in John 16:1, talking about the Holy Spirit that was going to come and convict us of sin, of righteousness, and of judgment, and he explains them. When he comes, to the judgment, he says, “of judgment because the prince of this world is” what? Judged. He sentenced, and we found in the Scripture before what was his sentence: he was cast out of the earth, so he couldn’t deceive people. You say, “Well, you’re in trouble, because he’s still doing, well...” We’ll get there, we’ll get there. Remember, he’s been bound and loosed all throughout the Bible. Hallelujah. He can do nothing without the big guy’s permission.
When does he say Satan was judged and cast out of the earth?

Revelation 12:7-9: And war broke out in heaven: Michael and his angels fought with the dragon; and the dragon and his angels fought, but they did not prevail, nor was a place found for them in heaven any longer. So the great dragon was cast out, that serpent of old, called the Devil and Satan, who deceives the whole world; he was cast to the earth, and his angels were cast out with him. John 12:31-32: Now is the judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world will be cast out. And I, if I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all peoples to Myself.” John 16:8-11: And when He has come, He will convict the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment: of sin, because they do not believe in Me; of righteousness, because I go to My Father and you see Me no more; of judgment, because the ruler of this world is judged.
What does he say the sword out of Jesus’s mouth is?
He says “the sword that came out of Jesus’s mouth was what? The word of God.”
Why does he say God does not chain Satan with natural things?
He says “God doesn’t use natural things to chain, he just uses his word. When he speaks, you can’t move.” The chain is given “so we understand in the natural, uh, in the spiritual what happens.”
What does he say darkness is?
He says “darkness is the absence of light. There is no thing, such thing as darkness,” and “Light is its own character.”
What does he say about real photos of black holes?
He says “when they really show a real photo of a black hole, there’s no black hole at all, there’s actually light there.”
What does he say happened to the demons in Luke 8?
He says Jesus put them in a herd of pigs and “the pigs went nuts and ran down the cliff.” He says the demons asked not to be cast into the bottomless pit.
Who does he say is the king of the bottomless pit?
He says the angel king called Apollyon, or Destroyer, “is Satan himself, he’s the king of the bottomless pit.”
Why does he say people put wings on angels?
He says “we put angels with wings on our Christmas trees, and we just do things because it’s handed down to us, and we don’t even think about what is the real source here.”
Why does he say God let Satan move David to number Israel?
He says it was “God needing to deal with Israel because of their sins,” and that God “wants you to repent, turn, and live and do right.”
Does he say God will let Satan tempt me beyond what I can bear?
No. He says “He will never let Satan or anything tempt you above what you can endure. If you fall, it was your decision.”
What does he say happened to Job’s body?
He says “Satan could not touch his body personally until God says you can,” and that “still Job would not denounce God.”
Does he say we have to wait for the end of the world to be free?
No. He says “You’re not waiting for some, you know, magical thing at the end of the world to get you out of this mess. You are a conqueror in the mess.”
What does he say the Holy Spirit convicts of?
He says the Holy Spirit would “convict us of sin, of righteousness, and of judgment,” and the judgment is “because the prince of this world is” judged.

items.t: Four Difficult Issues to Understand Part 2
items.d: In this second part of the series Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the death, burial and resurrection of Jesus destroyed the Devil’s power, and that a born-again believer’s new nature is not to sin. He says…
items.ser: Four Difficult Issues to Understand · Part 2
p: In this second part of the series Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the death, burial and resurrection of Jesus destroyed the Devil’s power, and that a born-again believer’s new nature is not to sin. He says Satan is still released and bound to influence the world, but is limited by God, using Paul’s thorn in the flesh, pride, marriage and sexual relationships as examples. He closes by saying we do not have to wait for the rapture to experience God’s power.
How does he say the cross destroyed the Devil’s power?

He reads Hebrews 2:14 and says “through the cross the Devil was destroyed, his power was reduced to zero.” He calls the death, burial and resurrection of Jesus Christ “the key to our victorious living.”
How does he say the cross destroyed the Devil’s power?

Hebrews 2:14, we’re going to show you that through the cross the Devil was destroyed, his power was reduced to zero. Hebrews 2:14, “Through death he,” Jesus, “might destroy him,” Satan, “that had the power of death, that is the Devil.” You see, so when Jesus died on the cross, this cross, this death, burial, and resurrection of Jesus Christ is the power of God and the salvation. Folks, this death, this burial, and this resurrection is the key to our victorious living. That was a good place for an amen, just in case you didn’t know, amens mean so be it, I [unclear] agree to that.
How does he say the cross destroyed the Devil’s power?

Hebrews 2:14: Inasmuch then as the children have partaken of flesh and blood, He Himself likewise shared in the same, that through death He might destroy him who had the power of death, that is, the devil,
What does 1 John 3 say about sin and being born again?

He says Satan’s power is “rendered powerless,” and reads 1 John 3:8 and 3:9: Jesus came “to destroy the works of Satan,” and “whoever is born of God does not” sin. He says being born again is “not just repeating a sinner’s prayer” or “getting on a church roll book,” but God putting himself in us by his Spirit and his word.
What does 1 John 3 say about sin and being born again?

All. And so his power is rendered powerless, and people say, “Satan’s been bugging me.” Well, have you read the Scriptures lately? He’s rendered what? Powerless. Hallelujah. Now, again, 1 John 3:8, “He that commits sin is of the Devil,” that’s habitual, consistent sin. “For this purpose the Son of God was manifest,” made plain, “that he might,” what? “Destroy the works of the Devil.” What’s the works of the Devil? Him getting you to sin. Isn’t that just plain and clear? You see, so Jesus came and died on the cross and rose again to destroy the works of Satan, to get you to sin, and not only that, but finish the scripture, it’s very important: “Whoever is born of God does not,” what? Sin, “for his seed,” Jesus’s seed, “remains in him, and he cannot sin because he’s been born of God.” And see, the Baptists and the Pentecostals and the charismatics, one of the things they really gave to us is this born-again thing. And the Bible says we’re born of the Spirit in John, and again it says we’re born of the word, and so the word and the Spirit come and work something in us, they birth us, we’re connected to a spiritual kingdom. It’s not just repeating a sinner’s prayer, it’s not just getting on a church roll book. This salvation thing, like the Baptists and, and the Pentecostals and the charismatics have emphasized, is a real Bible principle, where God comes and puts himself in us by his Spirit, we start living for Christ, by his word we start living, we get birth, we’re a, we’re now a spiritual being that’s connected
What does 1 John 3 say about sin and being born again?

1 John 3:8-9: He who sins is of the devil, for the devil has sinned from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that He might destroy the works of the devil. Whoever has been born of God does not sin, for His seed remains in him; and he cannot sin, because he has been born of God.
What does he say about denominations and our new nature?

He says every denomination “have given us something to hold tangibly onto, and we need to quit quarreling with one another and just serve the same Jesus.” He says a born-again person’s “new nature now is not to sin,” and that some so-called Christians sin because “they haven’t been born again.”
What does he say about denominations and our new nature?

spiritually. And I like to bring out some of these sources because denominations are fighting with each other and all that, and every one of the denominations and religious groups have given us something to hold tangibly onto, and we need to quit quarreling with one another and just serve the same Jesus. Could you say amen to that? Now, that’s a very powerful scripture. See, God’s active in your life to keep you from sin. Your nature, your new nature now, is not to sin. Oh, you might make some mistakes, but you’re not going to live habitually in sin when you’ve been born again. You’re going to correct that. Why? It’s your new nature. See, and that’s why a lot of Christians sin, they so-called Christians sin, they haven’t been born again. There is no motivation in, there’s no power in them moving them forward to grow in spiritual things and live righteously. They just said a little sinner’s prayer, they joined a church, or they got baptized without knowing anything, and a lot of churches love numbers, so they just love, “Okay, you believe, you’re one of us,” but we need to what? Get born
What does he say about overcoming the wicked one and 1 John 2:14?

He reads 1 John 2:14, “You young men, you are strong because the word of God abides in you,” and says he wants us to grow from the baby stage to a strong Christian who overcomes “his temptations, his seductions, his, his deceits.” He says we do it by the word, not by “people’s opinion and your feelings and your circumstances.”
What does he say about overcoming the wicked one and 1 John 2:14?

again. “They overcame Satan,” this is the believers, “by the blood of the Lamb, the word of their testimony, and they loved not their lives unto death.” Again, 1 John 2:14, “I have written unto you, young men.” He gives us the four areas of Christian growth there, and then this young man area of Christian growth, he says, “You young men, you are strong because the word of God abides in you, and because the word of God abides in you, you have overcome,” what? The wicked one. You see, we don’t want to stay in the baby stage too long, we don’t want to stay in the child stage too long, we want to get up there and become a strong Christian, who through the word of God we overcome the wicked one, his temptations, his seductions, his, his deceits.
What does he say about overcoming the wicked one and 1 John 2:14?

1 John 2:14: I have written to you, fathers, Because you have known Him who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, Because you are strong, and the word of God abides in you, And you have overcome the wicked one.
What does Romans 16:20 say about Satan under our feet?

He reads Romans 16:20 and says “You don’t have to dilly-dally along. You need to grow, and you need to start growing quickly, and you grow by the word of God.” He says Proverbs shows how to live in this life, Psalms how to live in the kingdom, and the New Testament illustrates the Old.
What does Romans 16:20 say about Satan under our feet?

Amen. And how did they do it? By the word of God. That’s why it’s important you’re in Bible studies and you’re in the word, that’s why it’s important that you speak the word to yourself, as we heard this morning and utterances, you use the word, you don’t use people’s opinion and your feelings and your circumstances, you use the word. Amen. Now, Romans 16:20, “The God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet,” after you’re 70 years old? “He shall bruise Satan on your feet shortly.” You don’t have to dilly-dally along. You need to grow, and you need to start growing quickly, and you grow by the word of God. And so you need, the young Christians needed, again, in the Bible studies, they need to be reading Proverbs and singing Psalms and studying the New Testament all the time. Proverbs tells you how to live in this life, Psalms tells you how to live in the kingdom, and the New Testament illustrates, gives us the illustration, the final illustration of everything in the Old Testament, so when you read the Old Testament you understand it. Now,
What does Romans 16:20 say about Satan under our feet?
Romans 16:20: And the God of peace will crush Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.
What does Acts 26:18 say about turning from the power of Satan?

He reads Acts 26:18 and says Jesus “didn’t just come to forgive you,” but to get you “out of the kingdom of darkness” and into the kingdom of light. He says that when the second coming is taught wrongly, “we get people distracted from the power of the church that we have in our lifetime.”
What does Acts 26:18 say about turning from the power of Satan?

hallelujah, and you will put Satan under your feet shortly. Acts 26:18, “Paul, I’m sending you to open their eyes, to turn them from,” what? Darkness to light, “and from the power of Satan to the power of God.” Now, see, Jesus didn’t just come to forgive you, he come to turn you, get you out of the kingdom of darkness and put you into the kingdom of light, and the power of the King of the kingdom of light. And see, when we teach the second coming wrong, we get people distracted from the power of the church that we have in our lifetime. Hallelujah. And a lot of preachers preach that you really can’t be perfect, you can’t be like Jesus, you can’t get his image or anything, you know, we just got to hang on till he comes. That is not
What does Acts 26:18 say about turning from the power of Satan?

Acts 26:18: to open their eyes, in order to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those who are sanctified by faith in Me.’
How does he say Satan is released and bound to influence the world?

He says the church is “a victorious church,” and that Satan, even after being cast out of the earth, “is released and bound, released and bound, to influence those in the world.” He cites Ephesians 2 and says God is in charge and Satan is “totally limited” and “always used for your good.”
How does he say Satan is released and bound to influence the world?

Bible. The church is a victorious church, it’s a victorious army, it’s a victorious family, they’re not hanging on to anything until the second coming, they are influencing the world for Jesus Christ, and denomination has nothing to do with it, it’s the person. Now, we want to show you that even after Satan was cast out of the earth, he is released and bound, released and bound, to influence those in the world. “In times past you walked according to the course of the world, according to the prince of the power of the air,” that we just heard was cast out, “the spirit now works in the children of disobedience.” Now, why do we need to know this stuff? Because we got to understand God’s in charge of everything, and he’s not going to let Satan come and just totally have possession of your life. He is totally limited to the God, God and Jesus Christ who created him, and what he can do, and he’s always used for your good. In the end it’s for your good. And yes, you can give into his limited power and commit sexual immorality and steal and use profanity and get mad and beat up people and act cocky and, and all the rest, and, and you’ll pay the price for it. Why? Because he wants you to turn, and if there’s no price to pay, you won’t
How does he say Satan is released and bound to influence the world?

Ephesians 2:1-3: And you He made alive, who were dead in trespasses and sins, in which you once walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit who now works in the sons of disobedience, among whom also we all once conducted ourselves in the lusts of our flesh, fulfilling the desires of the flesh and of the mind, and were by nature children of wrath, just as the others.
Why does he say God lets Satan do his handiwork?

He compares God’s discipline to his own parenting: “if I don’t discipline my kids, they’re not going to turn.” He says “God can’t do evil, so he has Satan over there doing his handiwork for him,” and reads 2 Corinthians 4:3, that the god of this world “has blinded the minds of them that believe not.”
Why does he say God lets Satan do his handiwork?

turn. See, if I don’t discipline my kids, they’re not going to turn, so I have to bring punishment on them, so one form or another, so they know, man, if I do this, it’s going to hurt. And that’s the way God is, both with the unbeliever and the believer. Is this making sense to you? Hallelujah. And remember, God can’t do evil, so he has Satan over there doing his handiwork for him, because that’s all Satan knows how to do, is rob, steal, kill, destroy, seduce, lie, that’s what he does. 2 Chron— uh, Corinthians 4:3, “If our gospel is hid, it is hid to them that are lost, whom the god of this world has blinded the minds of them that believe not.” See, you can accept Satan coming and telling you, “This is a bunch of baloney,” that’s what he’ll do, said, “Ah, God don’t know what he’s talking about, that Bible, it isn’t even authentic, book, and, you know, I can’t see God, and so how do I know there is one?” Yeah, he can, and you can accept it, he has that kind of
Why does he say God lets Satan do his handiwork?

2 Corinthians 4:3-4: But even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled to those who are perishing, whose minds the god of this age has blinded, who do not believe, lest the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine on them.
What does he say we must do to find Christ and see the light?

He says it is Satan, not God, who deceives: “come to Christ, pray to him, get in the book, and he will take the veil of Satan off of your eyes.” He says that Ephesians 2 speaks of being saved “for righteous and good works,” so “we’ve got to do something.” He says “I do something, he does something, and this thing works.”
What does he say we must do to find Christ and see the light?

influence. But see, once you’re blind and the light comes, like Jesus said, you know, when the light comes then the whole body is full of light, so you got to, not you got to experience and understand darkness before you can re, uh, uh, understand the light and accept the light and accept the change. Are you there? And it’s Satan that’s doing it, it isn’t God. “Well, God doesn’t show himself to me.” No, it’s Satan deceiving you, knucklehead. Come to Christ, pray to him, get in the book, and he will take the veil of Satan off of your eyes, and you will see him and you will experience him and you will know scripture. See, there’s something you got to do. These preachers are wrong when they say, “By grace are you saved through faith, and not of works, not of itself, lest any man should boast.” If they read the next verse, the next part of that context, that said that you were saved for righteous and good works. We’ve got to apply ourself, we’ve got to seek him, that’s our part, we’ve got to call on him, that’s what he asked us to do, we’ve got to do something, and yes, it’s not giving money and it’s not in the natural, it’s in the spiritual things. If I humble myself and pray, he will what? Hear. If I read that book, he will what? Open my
What does he say we must do to find Christ and see the light?

Ephesians 2:8-10: For by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, lest anyone should boast. For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand that we should walk in them.
What does he say Paul’s thorn in the flesh was?

To show that Satan’s influence over believers is limited, he cites 2 Corinthians 2:11, 1 Thessalonians 2:18 and the “messenger of Satan to buffet me.” He says the thorn “wasn’t a physical thing” but “an angel of Satan” sent to buffet Paul so he would not be lifted up in pride. The captions give the reference as “2 Chronicles 12:7.”
What does he say Paul’s thorn in the flesh was?

understanding. If I come to him, he will what? Draw nigh to me. I do something, he does something, and this thing works. Now, to show you that he has limited influence over believers, 2 Corinthians 2:11, “Lest Satan get an advantage of us.” 1 Thessalonians 2:18, “We wanted to come to you, but Satan,” what? Hindered us. 2 Chronicles 12:7, “God sent a messenger of Satan to buffet me.” See, that wasn’t a physical thing in Paul, that they believe, it plainly tells us what his thorn in the flesh was, it was an angel of Satan to what? Buffet him, give him some opposition, so he doesn’t get lifted up in pride.
What does he say Paul’s thorn in the flesh was?

2 Corinthians 2:11: lest Satan should take advantage of us; for we are not ignorant of his devices. 1 Thessalonians 2:18: Therefore we wanted to come to you—even I, Paul, time and again—but Satan hindered us. 2 Corinthians 12:7: And lest I should be exalted above measure by the abundance of the revelations, a thorn in the flesh was given to me, a messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I be exalted above measure.
How does he say God humbles us, and what does he say about marriage?

He says “some of you that God visits in a way that humbles you, relax, he’s doing you good,” and jokes about pride over a haircut or a brand-name shirt. He then turns to 1 Corinthians 7:5 and the marriage relationship: “Wives and husbands, do not hinder sexual relationships.”
How does he say God humbles us, and what does he say about marriage?

Are you out there? You know, we take the scripture, we do dumb things, and really, he couldn’t see, or, you know, he had a hearing problem, it wasn’t a physical thing, it was an angel that opposed him so he didn’t get lifted up with pride because of all the things he saw and he experienced. How many know that’s a good thing? Hallelujah. So some of you that God visits in a way that humbles you, relax, he’s doing you good. It’s the humble heart that God responds to. So yes, he knows to bring things in your life that humbles you, embarrasses you, so you don’t stay in that proud, cocky way of yours. Ain’t that right? I mean, we get proud over our haircut, that, that’s how lame we are. “My haircut better than your haircut, my haircut’s better than your, I’m the latest, man.” We get pride over clothing, you know, back ten years ago was an alligator on your shirt, man, if you didn’t have the alligator you weren’t cool, and when we had the alligator, we strutted. Yeah, “Man, I’m cool.” You see, and what does God come? He comes and brings things to humble you. You’re laughing because you’re guilty, and I haven’t, I haven’t even brought up the issue that you’re guilty of yet. In 1 Corinthians 7:5, God is, or Paul is, the Scriptures are talking about the marriage, and this is important, and he says, “Wives and husbands, do not hinder sexual
How does he say God humbles us, and what does he say about marriage?

1 Corinthians 7:5: Do not deprive one another except with consent for a time, that you may give yourselves to fasting and prayer; and come together again so that Satan does not tempt you because of your lack of self-control.
What does he say about sexual desire, marriage and homosexuality?

He says marriage keeps “that healthy principle of God in a healthy environment,” and says “there’s no such thing as a bisexual or a homosexual” and that “you have to learn those habits.” He calls that a lie from the Devil. These are his words and his claims, not established by this site.
What does he say about sexual desire, marriage and homosexuality?

relationships.” Don’t give me the headache excuse, and I’m working twelve hours a day excuse, there is no excuse, that’s fact. And I know people twist the scripture and say, “No, the Bible is trying, trying to tell us all through the Bible that we are sexually created people, we have a normal, healthy appetite for sex with the opposite sex, and there’s nothing wrong with it. There’s no such thing as a bisexual or a homosexual or a [unclear] or whatever. You have to learn those habits, you’re not created with that. That’s a lie from the Devil, absolutely deceiving people. And a lot of people are believing the lie. You have a normal sexual desire and a release in that for the opposite sex, and you get married so that you can keep that healthy principle of God in a healthy environment and avoid sexually transmitted diseases and destroying kids and having kids you don’t even, you know, have any parenthood over, you know, you just hit and impregnate and leave, and, see, it stops all that. Kids are the biggest sufferers of permissive sexual habits. And so he tells them plainly, and so does the Old Testament, don’t stop having sexual relationships in your marriage. And what’s the first thing people do when they get mad at each
What does he say about self-control and anger in marriage?

He says Satan takes advantage of “our lack of what? Self-control,” describes how eye contact starts temptation, and says anger comes when “you are so set on your way.” He says withholding sex or work in anger shows how important sexual relationships are in the home, because Satan can use it to distract.
What does he say about self-control and anger in marriage?

other? You sleeping on the couch. See, that’s a deception of Satan. Why? Because he says Satan will take advantage of us for our lack of what? Self-control. You’re opening the door for Satan to come in and tempt you to do, and women are always looking for men and men are always looking for women, and it starts with the eye contact. That’s why, when a woman, and when I was younger, looked at me with that eye contact, I never looked at him again in the eye. That’s a fact. It wasn’t going any further than that. Once I know what you’re up to, I’m not looking at you. That’s true, and believe it or not, I have to use it sometimes in my old age, I don’t understand why. I mean, look at me. You know, it would be just like this, okay, you know, there a, well, you know, okay, it’d be like the woman get mad and say, “I’m not cooking anymore, because things aren’t going my way.” You, you know, that’s why we get mad, don’t you? Because we don’t get our way. Hallelujah. That’s why we get mad, cuz when you’re trying to direct someone the right way, you got no reason to get mad, you’re just trying to direct, there’s a big difference. But when you are so set on your way, he’s being right, you don’t get your way, that’s when you throw a tantrum and say, “Okay, buddy, no sex, I’ll teach you, you’ll submit one way or another, or you’re not going to get any.” Oh, I’ve heard it as a pastor all my life. him, because you got to use the principle of seeking him. I don’t understand the word. Well, you’re telling me you never read the book, because if you read the book, he promised to what? He says “how did they do it? By the word of God,” and that you speak the word to yourself instead of using “people’s opinion and your feelings and your circumstances.”

He asks how many Christians “are shacking up,” and says “they’re using grace and faith to justify it.” He says clear Bible direction, when not followed, lets Satan entice us to sin.

items.ser: Four Difficult Issues to Understand · Part 3
p: In this third part Pastor David G. Kincer argues from Revelation 20, Psalm 90, 1 Corinthians 15 and 2 Peter 3 that the thousand years is a period of time in which Christ and his people already reign, that the first resurrection was the resurrection of Jesus and the saints of old, and that Gog and Magog stand for the deceived nations of the earth. He rejects the pre-tribulation rapture and says there is one second coming, with fire, and that believers should live holy lives now.
What problems does he see with the pre-tribulation rapture chart, and what is amillennialism?

He returns to the pre-tribulation rapture chart and says “this is just one of the problems of pre-tribulation rapture theory.” He says there are about eight theories of the second coming, and that “the biggest doctrine on the second coming is amillennialism,” meaning “no millennial.” He says the Catholic Church holds that view and that a church cannot get you to heaven: “you and Christ is what get you to heaven.”
What problems does he see with the pre-tribulation rapture chart, and what is amillennialism?

We’re going to go into the thousand years, so I got to show you the pre-tribulation rapture theory again. Here’s the rapture over here, seven years of tribulation, and then the second return, uh, they don’t call this the second return, they call it a rapture, and then the second return, and the first resurrection, and then the millennium. You see this fire here, I put that there because at the second coming the earth and the universe is renovated by fire. We got a real problem. This is just one of the problems of pre-tribulation rapture theory, it’s just one of the problems, there are many other problems. Now, how, even, you know, there’s about eight theories on the second coming. Okay, you know, now, how you know three of them are prominent: pre-tribulation rapture, post, I mean, pre-tribulation rapture, post-tribulation coming of Christ, no rapture but both believe in a seven-year tribulation, and then you got the millennial people. Okay, and do you know what the biggest doctrine on the second coming is? Amillennialism. Do you know what amillennialism is? No millennial. That’s the biggest accepted theory in the Christian world on the second coming, and the Catholic Church believes that there’s no millennium, and I’m going to show you some evidence. You know, the Catholic Church may have some bad things, but that doesn’t make them all bad. I get a lot of good information off of their website, I tell you, uh, they’ve got some historical documents and stuff that’s just powerful. And Left Behind, uh, [unclear], the Catholic people, they, they beat up the Catholic Church in the movie Left Behind, implying that if you’re a Catholic you’re doomed. How many know no church can get you to heaven, you and Christ is what get you to heaven, and to go beat up any area of Christian [unclear] is really trying to use scare tactics to build your [unclear], when we just should use Jesus and his word. Amen.
What does he say about the beheaded souls in Revelation 20:4?

He reads Revelation 20:4 and asks how people who would not worship the beast and were killed could be on earth at the last day. He says “this is a problem of pre-tribulation rapture” and “that’s why it’s a theory, because it doesn’t work every time.” In the same section he also argues that there is no homosexual gene and that it is “a learned habit,” which is his claim and not established by this site.
What does he say about the beheaded souls in Revelation 20:4?

So, uh, the thousand years is talking about this thousand-year period here between the second return, the first resurrection, and the second resurrection, okay, that is the pre-tribulation rapture theory. Verse four of Revelations 20, “I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them. I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus,” beheaded for the word of God, beheaded for not worshiping the beast. Remember back there when we talked about this beast that they worshiped, everybody that wouldn’t worship was what? Killed. Now, if that was literal at the last day, then there’s no one on earth that’s serving Christ, because they would all be killed, and this is a problem of pre-tribulation rapture. Okay, “they wouldn’t worship his image or they wouldn’t receive his mark on their foreheads or in their hands, and they lived and reigned with Christ” what? A thousand years. Now, your pre-tribulation rapture people say the saints are reigning, but the rapture says the saints are gone already. Okay, so this second, this what they call the first resurrection has to be just a resurrection of people that somehow believed in this tribulation time, and somehow they didn’t get beheaded, when if you didn’t worship the beast you’re killed, and that’s got a lot of problems. Do you see the problems? That’s why it’s a theory, because it doesn’t work every time, just like the atomic theory doesn’t work every time, the evolution theory doesn’t work every time. It’s a theory, it’s not a proven fact or proven law. Homosexuals having a homosexual gene, born that way, is ridiculous. There’s no homosexual gene, there’s no bisexual gene, there’s no DNA for that, it is a learned

Revelation 20:4: And I saw thrones, and they sat on them, and judgment was committed to them. Then I saw the souls of those who had been beheaded for their witness to Jesus and for the word of God, who had not worshiped the beast or his image, and had not received his mark on their foreheads or on their hands. And they lived and reigned with Christ for a thousand years.

He reads Psalm 90:4 and says “a thousand years to God is what? One day or a four-hour period,” so “it is a period of time.” He says the only place that says reigning for a thousand years is Revelation and “we need another verse.” He then applies a day-as-a-thousand-years rule to the 1,260 days of the two witnesses in Revelation 11:3 and says numerology “just accept numbers when it’s convenient to them.”

habit. You have to acquire the habit. You weren’t born into this world to be an alcoholic, you acquired the taste to be an alcoholic by starting. Amen. We need another verse to back up that there is a literal thousand-year reign in Christ. We need another verse, and there isn’t one. One day. Now, let’s take this principle of numerology and let’s apply it to other scriptures. He reads Revelation 20:5–6, “Blessed and holy is he that has part in the first resurrection,” and says “the second death has no power over you, period. theory. Okay, again, we’re going to be talking about the first resurrection. generation. Hallelujah. All. When are they hearing it? At the same time.
