He says the army comes against “the church, it’s the bride, it’s the heavenly Jerusalem,” and “we are all over the earth.” He says if the saints had already been raptured, “what are they doing down here?” He adds that whether you are “a Catholic, a Protestant, or Jew or whatever,” Christ will come to anyone who comes to him.
What does he say the camp of the saints and beloved city are?

raptured, what are they doing down here? See, that’s another big problem. And it’s not Jerusalem they’re coming against, it’s the church, it’s the bride, it’s the heavenly Jerusalem that they’re coming against, and we are all over the earth. Wow, that was good. And the saints are still here, those that haven’t been resurrected yet are still here. Why? Because Christ’s death on the cross is powerful and his promises are powerful, and he will fulfill them to anyone who listens, believes it, receives it, and acts upon it. I don’t care if you’re a Catholic, a Protestant, or Jew or whatever, he will come to you when you come to him, and he’ll make you a victorious overcomer in this earth. Amen.
How does he explain the fire from heaven in Revelation 20:9?

He says the fire is not tanks or bombs: “God speaks a word and zip.” He cites Ezekiel 39:6, where fire falls on Magog and on those who live carelessly in the isles, and 2 Thessalonians 1:7–9 about “a flaming fire taking vengeance.” He says God “deals with fire at this second coming.”
How does he explain the fire from heaven in Revelation 20:9?

Hallelujah, and listen to this. You know, they talk about the blood at the bridle, you know, and all the carcasses, and all this. “Fire came down from God out of heaven and devoured them.” Ain’t no sword, no tanks, no atomic bombs. God speaks a word and zip, they ain’t circling the camp of the saints anymore, they’re gone. And this is backed up by scripture. What’s this? Oh, Ezekiel 39:6, “I will send fire on Magog,” this is where they get Russia and all that from, “and among those who dwell carelessly in the isles.” So what’s the problem with Magog? They’re dwelling carelessly, just like the people in the islands were dwelling carelessly. You say Magog is also the careless people in the islands. Maybe that, an island sometimes is not a nation, it’s just a bunch of people living on an island, “and they shall know that I am the Lord.” Now, when Jesus shall be revealed from heaven, 2 Thessalonians 1:7, “with his mighty angels.” Hallelujah. “And a flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not God.” Does that back up Revelations 20? God, what? Fire from heaven devoured them. “Taking vengeance with a flaming fire on them that know not God and obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ, who shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the” what? “Presence of the Lord.” And so we see, yes, God deals with fire at this second coming. 2 Peter 3:10, “The day of the Lord will come as a” what? “Thief in the
How does he explain the fire from heaven in Revelation 20:9?

Ezekiel 39:6: “And I will send fire on Magog and on those who live in security in the coastlands. Then they shall know that I am the LORD. 2 Thessalonians 1:7-9: and to give you who are troubled rest with us when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with His mighty angels, in flaming fire taking vengeance on those who do not know God, and on those who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ. These shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of His power,
What does he say 2 Peter 3:10 teaches about the second coming?

He reads 2 Peter 3:10, that the day of the Lord will come as a “thief in the night,” and says “that’s the only second coming Jesus talked about in Matthew 24.” He says “there’s no rapture and then a second coming. There is a second coming,” and ties the heavens passing away to the sixth seal.
What does he say 2 Peter 3:10 teaches about the second coming?

night.” And that’s the only second coming Jesus talked about in Matthew 24, he will happen as a thief in the night. That’s the second coming, there’s no rapture and then a second coming. There is a second coming, there’s no third coming or fourth coming, there is a second coming, and the thief in the night is explaining exactly what Jesus talked about in Matthew 24 and in Luke and in Mark. Can I hear an amen? “The heavens shall pass away with a great noise” when he comes. The heavens are what? Going to pass away with a great noise. And that’s what we heard in the seals, the heavens passing away, the sixth seal. “And the elements will melt with fervent heat, the earth and the works therein shall be” what? “Burned up,” and all what?
What does he say 2 Peter 3:10 teaches about the second coming?

2 Peter 3:10-12: But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night, in which the heavens will pass away with a great noise, and the elements will melt with fervent heat; both the earth and the works that are in it will be burned up. Therefore, since all these things will be dissolved, what manner of persons ought you to be in holy conduct and godliness, looking for and hastening the coming of the day of God, because of which the heavens will be dissolved, being on fire, and the elements will melt with fervent heat?
What does he say happens to the saints when the earth is dissolved?

He says the wicked will be raised to burn in that fire, and the saints are safe: “the fire has no power over the saints,” as with “three Hebrew children” in Daniel. He warns that if you love your house and possessions and “turn back,” like Lot’s wife, “you’re going to burn.”
What does he say happens to the saints when the earth is dissolved?

Dissolved. So when he comes, yes, they’re going to be attacking us in that end day, just like they are now, they’re going to be belittling us and mocking us and mistreating us, but in that day when he comes, he’s going to bring fire, and the dead that are wicked are going to be raised to burn in that fire. These barns and all these buildings and all these cars are going to be switched, gone, just like that. Why? By the word of his mouth. He speaks it and fire comes, and this earth and the trees and the ocean and everything is gone. Are you there? You say, “Well, what about the saints that are down here?” Listen, didn’t you ever read the story in Daniel, that three Hebrew children went into the, the fire and not even a smell of smoke was on them? See, it depends on which side of Jesus you’re on. The fire has no power over the saints, it’s only the unbeliever and the wicked, they burn and they are moved, they are dissolved, they are destroyed. And if you’re Lot’s wife, that you love your house and your family and all your do-goodies in your house, and you [unclear] Silver Shadow in your car, and you turn back, you’re going to burn
What does he say happens to the saints when the earth is dissolved?

Daniel 3:27: And the satraps, administrators, governors, and the king’s counselors gathered together, and they saw these men on whose bodies the fire had no power; the hair of their head was not singed nor were their garments affected, and the smell of fire was not on them.
How does he sum up the thousand years and how we should live now?

He sums up that the thousand years is “some kind of time period,” that Satan is limited by Christ “every generation,” and “the time period when we rule with Christ on earth is now.” He says he submits “that the Catholics are right” on this point, and closes by asking “what kind of people should you be” in godliness, “because, folks, you can die any day.”
How does he sum up the thousand years and how we should live now?

because all that’s going to be burned up, and if that’s what you’re going to hold on to, you’re going to burn with it. Okay, bottomless pit, place of torment, prison, and a source of the kingdom of darkness is evil, and Satan is his king. We got it. Satan is bound and loosed till the end, all, every generation, he is limited what he can do by Jesus Christ himself in his power, and it will happen at the end also, and the saints shall rule over him. When? Now. Saints are priests unto God. When? Now. And we rule over Satan in his kingdom now. A thousand years is a time period of a day, a watch, or a year, in other words it’s some kind of time period, and it can be in our time period, and it is in our time period. I submit to you that the Catholics are right: the time period when we rule with Christ on earth is now. Hallelujah. Because there’s a new heaven and earth coming, and there’s no sickness, no disease, no wicked people there, no, no deception there. And so we need to rule when, when we have something, we got to rule over wickedness, sin. Amen. The first, first resurrection is Jesus Christ and the saints of old, the second death has no power over believers and those baptized in Jesus. And I didn’t read that part, but it says if this is true, that everything’s going to be dissolved, what kind of people should you be, in godliness and holiness and good conversation? What kind of people should you be? That’s what the Bible says. If all this is going to happen, then what kind of people should you be now? And paying attention to how you talk and how you live, because God is coming to punish those who reject him and don’t obey the word, and so we should be what? Not looking for something special up there at the end, we should what? Now be focusing on living for God and speaking rightly, because, folks, you can die any day, and you’re going to stand before Christ. You may never make the end-time generation, but when you die, you’re judged, and that’s what people should be concerned about: when is my time to die? And if I lived in, in that generation and everything is burned up, then I should be ready, with holiness and proper talk and a proper lifestyle.
What does he say amillennialism is?
He says it means “no millennial,” and calls it “the biggest accepted theory in the Christian world on the second coming.”
Does he say a church can get you to heaven?
No. He says “no church can get you to heaven, you and Christ is what get you to heaven.”
What problem does he see with the rapture theory and the beheaded saints?
He says if people who would not worship the beast were killed at the last day, “there’s no one on earth that’s serving Christ,” and “this is a problem of pre-tribulation rapture.”
Does he say there is a second verse for a literal thousand-year reign?
No. He says “we need another verse to back up that there is a literal thousand-year reign in Christ… and there isn’t one.”
What is his point about numerology?
He says “numerology just accept numbers when it’s convenient to them,” and that applying one rule to every scripture gives “a problem.”
Does he say the second death has power over believers?
No. He says “the second death has no power over you, period.”
Who does he say rose when Jesus rose?
He says “the saints of old” rose with him, “went into Jerusalem and appeared to many people,” and then ascended with him.
What does he say the first resurrection is?
He says it was “when Jesus rose from the grave, and the saints in the Old Testament rose with him,” and that faith in it “is what gives us power over the second death.”
Is Jesus ruling now, according to him?
Yes. He says “he is king now” and “he reigns now until all enemies has been put under his feet.”
In short, who does he say Gog and Magog are?
He says “it’s the nations of the earth that are deceived,” meaning “Gentiles, unbelievers.”
Does he say there is a rapture before the second coming?
No. He says “there’s no rapture and then a second coming. There is a second coming.”
What does he say we should focus on instead of the end time?
He says “not looking for something special up there at the end,” but “now be focusing on living for God and speaking rightly.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer walks through Isaiah 36–39 and four dilemmas Hezekiah faced: the Assyrian army, the word from God that he would die, a sickness, and the prophecy that his sons would be…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer walks through Isaiah 36–39 and four dilemmas Hezekiah faced: the Assyrian army, the word from God that he would die, a sickness, and the prophecy that his sons would be taken. He teaches that prayer, humility and repentance act as a “higher law” that can change even a God-given prophecy, and that Hezekiah’s failure to pray about the fourth dilemma left it to his son Manasseh. He closes with the power of the gospel and standing in the gap in prayer.
What are the four dilemmas in Isaiah 36–39, and what is the first one?

He says Isaiah 36–39 shows “four dilemmas, four serious problems” and “four solutions.” He starts from John 16:33 and says “God has solutions for your pollutions.” The first dilemma is war: Assyria has captured every city of Judah but Jerusalem, and its army is coming against it.
What are the four dilemmas in Isaiah 36–39, and what is the first one?

Today we’re going to look at chapters 36 to 39. We’re going to see four dilemmas, four serious problems, four serious issues that are going to be encountered, and there are four solutions. Remember in John 16:33, Jesus said, “In the world you will have tribulation, but be of good cheer, I have overcome the world.” And so God has solutions for your pollutions. Amen. Okay, we’re going to pick up the story with Hezekiah is 39 years of age, he has reigned for 14 years, starting at age 25, and we see dilemma number one is war. In Isaiah 36:1, Assyria had come in and attacked all of Judah and captured every other city but Jerusalem, and now we find the Assyrian army coming against
What are the four dilemmas in Isaiah 36–39, and what is the first one?

John 16:33: These things I have spoken to you, that in Me you may have peace. In the world you will have tribulation; but be of good cheer, I have overcome the world.” Isaiah 36:1: Now it came to pass in the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah that Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and took them.
Why does he say the Assyrian ambassador was not lying?

He says Judah’s military was weak, and that the Assyrian ambassador claimed the Lord had sent him. He says that was “a fact” because Isaiah had prophesied it 30 years earlier in Isaiah 7:17. He also cites Numbers 23:19, that God does not lie, and adds that “our enemy knows, gets enough out of the Bible to try to get you on the defensive.”
Why does he say the Assyrian ambassador was not lying?

Jerusalem, and with a great army. And you got to remember, just a few years back, 15 or so years before, in his father [unclear]’s day, Israel alone killed 120,000 Judeans in one day, and so their military isn’t too strong now. Besides that, Edom and the Philistines come and attack Judah and killed their military, and so their military is weak here. He inherited a weak military, and now the Assyrians have come and they’ve got every city of Judah but Jerusalem, the capital, and when they negotiate, when their ambassador talks to the king of Judah, Hezekiah, the Assyrian ambassadors, the Assyrian, uh, delegate that came to talk to Hezekiah said this: “Have I now come up without the Lord against this land to destroy it? The Lord said to me,” Jesus said to me, “go up against this land and destroy it. The Lord will bring the king of Assyria upon you and your people and your father’s house, days that have not come since the day that Ephraim departed from Judah.” And so Judah’s attackers are saying the Lord God sent them, the God that Judah worshiped sent them to destroy them. Okay, and right quick, if you don’t know your Bible, you will say, “Well, he’s just lying, you know, he don’t, he’s worshiping another God.” He is not lying. Okay, he is stating a fact. Isaiah chapter 7:17, Isaiah prophesied it 30 years before. In chapter 7:17, same wording: “The Lord will bring the king of Assyria upon you and your people and your father’s house, days that have not come since the day that Ephraim departed from Judah.” And see, the king of Assyria, the delegation of Assyria knew that prophecy, and they’re saying, “Hey, your God sent us to straighten you guys out, to conquer you.” See, they weren’t lying. Now, we know that in Numbers 23:19, “God is not a man, that he should lie, nor the son of man, that he should repent. Has he said, and will he not do it? Has he spoken, and will he not make it good?” You see, and in Daniel it says that the law of the Medes and the Persians cannot be altered. So here, here you got a prophetic
Why does he say the Assyrian ambassador was not lying?

Isaiah 36:10: Have I now come up without the LORD against this land to destroy it? The LORD said to me, ‘Go up against this land, and destroy it.’ ” Isaiah 7:17: The LORD will bring the king of Assyria upon you and your people and your father’s house—days that have not come since the day that Ephraim departed from Judah.” Numbers 23:19: “God is not a man, that He should lie, Nor a son of man, that He should repent. Has He said, and will He not do? Or has He spoken, and will He not make it good?
How does he say Hezekiah responded to the dilemma of war?

He says “Hezekiah’s approach to this dilemma should be all of our approach.” Hezekiah tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, went to the house of God, and prayed. He asks how many people did the same after 9/11, and defines prayer simply as “talk to God.”
How does he say Hezekiah responded to the dilemma of war?

appointment from God that Israel, Judah, is to be destroyed, the whole nation. All right, and our enemy knows that, and listen, folks, our enemy knows, gets enough out of the Bible to try to get you on the defensive. You really need to know your Bible, and some of these things they tell us is true. All right, so here Isaiah, I mean Hezekiah, is faced with a dilemma. The Assyrian army is there, it’s more powerful than they are, they can’t beat him, and God said 30 years before that they were coming. So what does Hezekiah do? Hezekiah’s approach to this dilemma should be all of our approach to these dilemmas. Isaiah 37:1, “King Hezekiah tore his clothes.” That would be a novelty if we really humbled our, and tore our designer clothes that cost 200 bucks. That would be something. “He covered himself with sackcloth,” burlap, “and he went to the house of God.” My goodness, he went to the house of God. How many know at 9/11 the churches for two or three months was flooded with people coming to the house of God because of the aggression that we experienced back there. And he prayed. He prayed. Prayed means to talk to God. Okay, talk to God. Now, all right, and then in verse 15, the delegation had said, you know, we, we got to leave because we, we got another enemy coming in, but we’re going to be back and we’re going to destroy you. So
How does he say Hezekiah responded to the dilemma of war?
Isaiah 37:1: And so it was, when King Hezekiah heard it, that he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the house of the LORD.
Can God-given prophecies and laws be changed by a higher law?

He says Hezekiah’s simple prayer was “Save us from Assyria, that all kingdoms of the earth may know that you are the Lord.” He argues that “God-given oaths, God-given laws, God-given prophecies can be changed by God’s higher laws,” such as the gift of Jesus Christ, God’s patience that leads to repentance, prayer, praise and confession.
Can God-given prophecies and laws be changed by a higher law?

Hezekiah went back into the house of God again and prayed to the Lord, and this was his simple prayer: “Save us from Assyria, that all kingdoms of the earth may know that you are the Lord, you alone.” Okay, now, God prophesied that this was supposed to happen, but Hezekiah prayed and said, “Lord, I’m not worthy of this, the nation’s not worthy of this, but you do it, so that the whole world will know that you are God, God alone.” Isn’t that a good, humble attitude? Yeah. So God-given oaths, God-given laws, God-given prophecies can be changed by God’s higher laws. Okay, the wages of sin is death, can be changed by the gift of God, Jesus Christ, given us life, confessing our sin. Okay, a higher law. Uh, when Jesus told the person, “You go and sin no more, lest worse things come upon you,” and that person, if he went back and sinned some more, there’s a higher law in Romans that the long patience of God before he judges, before he brings bad things, will lead you to repentance. So he’s trying to be patient with you to lead you, there’s a higher law. All right, plus prayer, as we saw here, at Hezekiah, his prayer is a higher law. Praise is a higher law. Confessing, admitting your wrong is a higher law. Humbling yourself, kneeling before God, raising your hand, lifting your voice, those, those acts of humility that God asked us to do is a higher law that will counteract the other law that God spoke. That’s right. I’m going to give you proof of that. All right, Jeremiah 18:7. The instant. How long will it take? Instant. It’s not even popcorn, it’s faster than popcorn. Popcorn takes two
Can God-given prophecies and laws be changed by a higher law?

Isaiah 37:15-20: Then Hezekiah prayed to the LORD, saying: “O LORD of hosts, God of Israel, the One who dwells between the cherubim, You are God, You alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth. You have made heaven and earth. Incline Your ear, O LORD, and hear; open Your eyes, O LORD, and see; and hear all the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to reproach the living God. Truly, LORD, the kings of Assyria have laid waste all the nations and their lands, and have cast their gods into the fire; for they were not gods, but the work of men’s hands—wood and stone. Therefore they destroyed them. Now therefore, O LORD our God, save us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You are the LORD, You alone.”
What does Jeremiah 18:7 say about God relenting, and why did Jonah run?

He reads Jeremiah 18:7–8 and says God relents “the instant we turn.” He says Jonah ran because he knew God was merciful and that if Nineveh repented, “Jonah would look like a false prophet.” He says preachers can look bad “because God has a higher law.”
What does Jeremiah 18:7 say about God relenting, and why did Jonah run?

minutes. This is instant. All right, “The instant I speak concerning a nation,” and remember, remember, the nation is Gentiles, heathen, humanist, religionist, so forth, “and concerning a kingdom,” a kingdom is an area ruled over by a king, a kingdom is like America, we were ruled over by a republic of laws, supposed to be anyway, and, uh, “if a kingdom,” or an individual, a heathen, a religionist, “when I pronounce judgment to pluck up, to pull down, and destroy it, if that nation against whom I have pronounced the judgment, if he turns from their evil,” see, turns from its evil, confess our sin, repent, if it turns, what will happen? “I will relent.” And when will he relent? The instant we turn. Folks, that’s a powerful God. And this, this idea that I got to wait three months to get delivered, or three months or whatever, a year or whatever, a rehab program of seven weeks, and no. The instant, “he will relent of the disaster that he thought to bring upon them.” And see, this is why Jonah ran from God. He knew that if he went to Nineveh and preach, “In 40 days God’s going to destroy this city, in 40 days you guys are going to pay the price, you’re going to be destroyed,” Jonah knew that God was merciful, God would change his mind if they repented, and then Jonah would look like a false
What does Jeremiah 18:7 say about God relenting, and why did Jonah run?

Jeremiah 18:7-8: The instant I speak concerning a nation and concerning a kingdom, to pluck up, to pull down, and to destroy it, if that nation against whom I have spoken turns from its evil, I will relent of the disaster that I thought to bring upon it. Jonah 4:1-2: But it displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he became angry. So he prayed to the LORD, and said, “Ah, LORD, was not this what I said when I was still in my country? Therefore I fled previously to Tarshish; for I know that You are a gracious and merciful God, slow to anger and abundant in lovingkindness, One who relents from doing harm.
What does he say the office of a prophet is?

He says the office of a prophet is “the position” of authority, and that people who “edify, encourage, and exhort” are not by that fact prophets. He says “a prophet is never wrong.” He then reads Isaiah 37:21 and says God answered “because you have prayed,” and that a house of God “should be called a house of prayer.”
What does he say the office of a prophet is?

prophet. See, that’s why he got mad at the end. After they repented, he wasn’t glad, he was mad, and he sat out there waiting for the destruction, the destruction didn’t come. Then God comes along, he said, “I told you, I told you you’d do this.” See, that’s why he ran from God. See, sometimes preachers can look bad because God has a higher law. We can, we can give you the law of God and the word of God, but if you humble yourself and repent, we look bad, because God has a higher law. Amen. And all we got to do is humble ourselves and pray and repent. Okay, the next dilemma, there, these two dilemmas, the office of a real prophet. A real prophet is the position, okay, of authority. Prophets that edify, encourage, and exhort the body of Christ is not the office of a prophet. You got to understand that, all right. And these people that say they are prophets and they are wrong, they are not a prophet. A prophet is never wrong. Never. All right, but Isaiah has the office of a prophet, okay, he has the authority to speak by the Spirit of God, and this, we’re going to find dilemmas number one and two resolved. Okay, then in, uh, Isaiah 37:21, “Then Isaiah sent to Hezekiah, saying, ‘Thus says the Lord, because you have,’” what? Prayed. “Because you have prayed,” you’re still a rascal. You haven’t even had time to show me you really meant it, you know. “Because you have prayed.” Folks, his house should be called a house of prayer, it’s very important. We’ve got to have time to pray in God’s house, talk to God. All right.
What does he say the office of a prophet is?
Isaiah 37:21: Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, “Thus says the LORD God of Israel, ‘Because you have prayed to Me against Sennacherib king of Assyria,
How does God defend Jerusalem in Isaiah 37, and what does he say about America?

He reads Isaiah 37:33–35, where the king of Assyria will not shoot an arrow in Jerusalem, and God says he “will defend this city to save it.” He says “righteousness exalts a nation” and that if Americans “stand up for righteousness” God will defend America, not because we are worthy but “for his sake.”
How does God defend Jerusalem in Isaiah 37, and what does he say about America?

“You prayed to me,” not to Buddha, not to Allah, you prayed to Jesus, “against [unclear] the king of Israel. This is the word which the Lord has spoken concerning him.” All right, see, the instant that Jeremiah said, and Jeremiah wasn’t even born yet, Jeremiah brought out this truth, that when God assigns a disaster upon us, we humble our self and pray and turn, God will turn from his judgment. Isaiah 37:33, “Assyria will not come into this city or shoot an arrow there,” won’t even shoot an arrow, “nor come with shield, nor build a siege against Jerusalem. By the way that he came, the same way he will return.” Verse 35, “For I, the Lord God, will defend this city to save it.” Man, you see, that’s why it pays for a nation to be righteous. For a nation to have a righteousness, “righteousness exalts a nation.” You see, a kingdom, and if we will stand up for righteousness, even in an ungodly nation, God will defend us. That’s his word. And if we in America, who have the freedom to make righteous laws, will stand up and not let these people push us around, we can turn this nation back around to righteous laws, and God will defend America from all of its enemies. And I’m telling you, when he defends it, it’s defended. Okay, and he’s going to do it for his own sake. Are we worthy? No. You look, look at, look around you, you’re looking at a bunch of, come on, we really coming short, but he’s going to do it for his sake, all right, so that the world knows that it is God that is building the house of God. God is building a kingdom, it’s not human beings.
How does God defend Jerusalem in Isaiah 37, and what does he say about America?

Isaiah 37:33-35: “Therefore thus says the LORD concerning the king of Assyria: ‘He shall not come into this city, Nor shoot an arrow there, Nor come before it with shield, Nor build a siege mound against it. By the way that he came, By the same shall he return; And he shall not come into this city,’ Says the LORD. ‘For I will defend this city, to save it For My own sake and for My servant David’s sake.’ ” Proverbs 14:34: Righteousness exalts a nation, But sin is a reproach to any people.
What does he say about signs, end-time prophets and the 185,000?

He says “a real prophet gives a sign” and criticizes end-time prophets who set dates and “gave no sign.” He reads Isaiah 37:36, where an angel killed 185,000, and says it happened “because one man prayed.” He also says to confess specific sins to God, not to a crowd, because “the gossip train will go.”
What does he say about signs, end-time prophets and the 185,000?

Okay, “and for my servant David’s sake.” That’s important, because God gave David a covenant that his seed would reign forever. All right, and God keeps his covenants. Isaiah 37:7, a sign was given. You see, a real prophet gives a sign, so that we know that this is from God. We don’t have to wait ten years for the prophecy to come to pass, or 40 years, or whatever, like all these end-time prophets do. You know, they thought that when they prophesied that Jesus would come in 1982 and 1992 and so forth, that was 10, 12, 13, 15 years before. They gave no sign. They were just lying to us, and we bought their books and believed their, their foolishness. Are you there? Yeah, we all got disappointed. If these guys cannot give you a sign, forget it, get to the Bible and just be practical with the Bible, believe it all. Right, chapter 37:36, “An angel came and killed in the camp of the Assyrian army 185,000.” Bang! How many know that’s better than an atomic bomb? Yeah, they just woke up dead. Because one man prayed. items.d: In “Four Heavyweights,” Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Matthew 23:23 that the weightier matters of the law that people omit are judgment, mercy, faith and love, and that the Bible is easier to understand…
p: In “Four Heavyweights,” Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Matthew 23:23 that the weightier matters of the law that people omit are judgment, mercy, faith and love, and that the Bible is easier to understand when we look for them. He then explains three kinds of God’s law — spiritual, civil and shadow (ceremonial) laws — using Jonah and Nineveh, Solomon’s judgment and the bond woman of Leviticus 19, and walks through Romans 6 and 8 to show which law we are not under and what each law is still for.

He defines it as the decision for or against anything, and says you can be for it or against it but you are making a judgment.
What did Jesus do with the woman caught in adultery?
He says Jesus told them, “Any of you without sin, go ahead and cast the first stone,” and then made a judgment not to stone her, but told her to go and sin no more.
He says mercy is a lot like love, an outward expression of compassion to a person afflicted.
Does Jesus only forgive, or does He also set us free?
He says Jesus wants to forgive you and also loose, free and liberate you, rather than leave you in your sin.
How does he say we are to love our enemies?
He says we love our enemies in a different way, such as helping with a donkey in a ditch or a broken-down car, without having to invite them into our home to influence our kids for evil.
What is the simplest summary of the law?
He says the whole law can be understood by not doing anything that hurts others or yourself, because love does no harm to his neighbor.
What does love not do, according to 1 Corinthians 13?
He lists that love is not jealous, proud, rude, demanding of its own way, or easily angered, and keeps no record of wrongs.
What does he say faith simply means?
He says faith simply means persuasion: being persuaded and convinced of moral truths in the Bible.
What good is knowledge without application?
He says knowledge, understanding and education do no good if there is no application, and that faith should stand in the power of God and not the wisdom of men.
What are statutes, commandments and spiritual laws?

He says statutes are usually connected with religious ceremonies and rituals, commandments are the civil laws including the Ten Commandments, and spiritual laws bring me into relationship and connection with God.
What did Nineveh do when Jonah preached?
He says all 120,000 believed God, proclaimed a fast by the king’s decree, prayed to God Jehovah and turned from their evil ways and violence, and God did not destroy them.
Does being saved by grace mean sin has no control over me?
He says when I am under grace’s control, grace is power and sin doesn’t have control over me, and Romans 6 says “God forbid” to sinning because of grace.
Are we still under civil and spiritual laws?
He says yes, we still have no right to break civil laws and we still pray, fast, go to church and worship, but those laws will not free us from sin.

p: In this message Pastor David G. He then gives Bible examples of censoring God’s word, judicial injustice, murder by government and removing arms, and says God can use a moral generation to change evil laws.

items.ser: Clarity on Crucial Choices · Full sermon
p: In “Gears of Judgment,” Pastor David G. Kincer defines judgment as deciding right and wrong from forensic facts, not circumstantial evidence, citing John 7:24 and Deuteronomy 17:6. He contrasts three groups from a prior session, then argues that the Humanist Manifesto’s rights to abortion, divorce and sexual lifestyles fail its own “short of harming others” rule. He cites AVERT and CDC-linked figures on AIDS and abuse and calls for laws that protect children rather than compel lifestyles he calls harmful.
What three choices does he say people can make?

From the last session (Matthew 13:30 and Malachi 3:18) he says people can serve Christ and do right, or be humanists/atheists who reject Jesus and don’t harm others (leave them alone—blind leaders of the blind), or do criminal acts that hurt themselves and others.
What three choices does he say people can make?

Thank you for joining with us today on our topic of clarity on crucial choices. And today we’ll be talking about the gears or components of judgment. The components of judgment: we can make bad decisions, bad judgments; we can make better judgment; and we can make very good judgments. Remember in our last chapter, last session, Matthew 13:30 and Malachi 3:18, we found that there were three choices that people could make. They could choose to serve Christ and do right and don’t harm others, and if they do that the judgment would be: you shall know the truth and the truth will set you free. You go to court and they find nothing but truth in you, they’re going to free you. The other one is the humanist, the atheist and so forth that reject Jesus and the Bible and don’t harm others. They won’t serve God but they really don’t go around harming people. And what is the solution there? Jesus said they’re blind leaders of the blind. When blind lead the blind they will both fall into the ditch. They’re not hurting anyone directly, so just leave them alone. If they want to go to hell, let them go to hell. John 8:32: And you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.” Matthew 15:14: Let them alone. They are blind leaders of the blind. He says join Bible followers to pass laws protecting Americans and kids from lifestyles he calls harmful, put them “back in the closet,” and support marrying one man and one woman for life—or else they are blind hypocrites.
What does he ask humanists to do?

anybody. And that’s not forensic judgment. Humanist, your manifesto says you are for good laws and lifestyles that don’t hurt others. And why don’t you join Bible followers to pass laws protecting Americans and innocent kids from harmful homosexuality, transsexual and transvestite lifestyles? Let’s put them back in the closet, not on public display. And what is the harm in persuading people to marry, then have sex, one woman, one man for life, and raise kids morally? Where is the harm in that? If humanists and followers don’t support good laws, they’re blind leaders of the blind. They’re hypocrites, because they say and do not.
What does he ask humanists to do?
Matthew 15:14: Let them alone. They are blind leaders of the blind. And if the blind leads the blind, both will fall into a ditch.”
Can Bible followers be hypocrites too?

Yes. He says followers who believe in Jesus but won’t stand up against harmful behavior that hurts children are hypocrites. He cites CDC July 2014 that homosexuals are 1.6% of the population, not 10%.
Can Bible followers be hypocrites too?

You can say you’re good without God, but if you are living a harmful lifestyle and promoting a harmful lifestyle you are a hypocrite—the same with followers of Jesus and the Bible. So they believe in Jesus, so they believe in the Bible—they don’t stand up for preventing deaths and harmful behavior traits that hurt the innocent people, especially children in America. What good is your belief in Jesus? And blind homosexuals, which are 1.6% of the population, not 10%, according to Center for Disease Control just this year, July of 2014—they won’t admit the harm, they won’t admit that they were not born that way, they won’t admit that it was a choice, they won’t admit that there’s no homosexual animals, they won’t admit that they are
What decision does he leave with the hearer?

He says naive Americans accept and promote what he calls preventable disease and death and poison students’ minds; you’ve been given forensic facts and must make a right judgment—the decision is yours.
What decision does he leave with the hearer?

liars. And the fact is naive Americans accept and promote homosexual lives, legalizing preventable diseases, deaths, and poisoning the minds of our innocent students. And folks, you’ve been presented with alarming forensic facts today. Now you must make the decision to make a right judgment. The decision is yours.
Should you beat harmless unbelievers over the head with a Bible?
No. He says if they reject Christ but don’t harm others, leave them alone; God will deal with them when they fall into the ditch.
Does “judge not” mean you should never judge?
He says people misuse that line; Jesus in John 7:24 said judge righteous judgment—you better make correct decisions.
How many witnesses does Deuteronomy require?
He says at the mouth of two or three examined witnesses; you’ve got to have two witnesses, not one.
What does Humanist Manifesto II section 6 say?
He quotes that short of harming others or compelling them to do likewise, individuals should express their sexual appetites and lifestyles as they desire.
Why does he mention seatbelts and helmets?
He says civil leaders ticket seatbelt and helmet violators to save thousands of lives a year but never ticket homosexuals.
What lifestyle does he say has no harm?
He asks what harm there is in persuading people to marry, then have sex, one woman and one man for life, and raise kids morally.
What does “back in the closet” mean here?
He says put homosexuality, transsexual and transvestite lifestyles back in the closet, not on public display.
What percent of the population does he say is homosexual?
He says 1.6%, not 10%, according to the CDC in July 2014.
Does he say homosexuality is inborn?
He says they won’t admit they were not born that way, that it was a choice, or that there are no homosexual animals.
Who must make the final judgment?
He says you’ve been presented with alarming forensic facts; now you must make the decision to make a right judgment—the decision is yours.

items.d: In “God Destroys Nations,” Pastor David G. Kincer says the Old Testament events are real and written for our learning, and uses Sodom and Lot to say what God judges a nation for. He reads Jude 7 and Ezekiel…
p: In “God Destroys Nations,” Pastor David G. Kincer says the Old Testament events are real and written for our learning, and uses Sodom and Lot to say what God judges a nation for. He reads Jude 7 and Ezekiel 16:49 to list Sodom’s sins, including sexual immorality, pride, idleness and not strengthening the poor, and compares them to America. He closes with what he says the church must do and why the judgment message has to be preached.
Did the events in the Bible really happen, or are they just allegories?

Pastor Kincer says the things written in the Old Testament happened: the six-day creation, the flood, Noah’s ark, Jonah’s great fish and the virgin birth all occurred. He says science can only explain natural things, not supernatural ones, and that these real events were written for our learning, as illustrations.
Did the events in the Bible really happen, or are they just allegories?

And when God decides to destroy a nation, it’s just going to fall. That’s the bottom line. “Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for” what? Our learning. So what we want to learn something, where do we go? The Bible, the Old Testament, the New Testament. They’re written for us to learn. 1 Corinthians 10:11: “All these things happened”— they what? Happened. They occurred. Bill O’Reilly on Fox News is wrong. The homosexuals are wrong, the atheists are wrong, the humanists are wrong, that say the Bible is a book of myths and allegories and so forth. “These things happened.” They occurred. They took place. God created the world in six days: it happened. God flooded the world: it happened. God had Noah to build an ark: it happened. God prepared a great fish to swallow Jonah: it happened. Are you with me? Jesus was born of a virgin: it happened. It occurred. And Bill O’Reilly’s wrong when he says he proves that the Bible is a book of allegories by using science. Science can never explain supernatural things. Science only explains natural things that any bird brain can look into and figure out how it worked. God is the one that created the working.
Did the events in the Bible really happen, or are they just allegories?
1 Corinthians 10:11: Now all these things happened to them as examples, and they were written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the ages have come.
Is all Scripture inspired by God, and what is it for?

He says all scripture is given by the inspiration of God and you cannot take anything out, such as the virgin birth or the atonement, as liberal churches do. He says the purpose of the Bible is teaching us how to live right, and that we were saved by Jesus to live right, and if we are not living right we are not saved.
Is all Scripture inspired by God, and what is it for?

“And it happened to them for examples”— illustrations. This is the allegorical part: these real occurrences happened to teach us, illustrations, so we can learn by, and “written for our admonition”— our warning, our encouragement, correction— “upon whom the ends of the world are come.” “All scripture is given by the inspiration of God.” How many scriptures? All of it. You can’t take it out. You can’t take the virgin birth out. You can’t take the atonement, the blood of Christ, out of the Bible like the liberal churches do. You can’t do that. “All scripture is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness.” Instruction in what? Righteousness. The purpose of the Bible: teaching us how to live right, “that the man of God might be perfect, thoroughly furnished unto all” what? Good works. These people that say that, you know, we don’t have works— we do. We have good works. “Let your light so shine before men that they may see your” what? Good works. You were saved by Jesus to live right, and if you’re not living right, you’re not saved.
Is all Scripture inspired by God, and what is it for?

2 Timothy 3:16-17: All Scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness, that the man of God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work. Matthew 5:16: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven.
Why was Sodom destroyed: was it a lack of hospitality?

He calls the claim that Sodom was destroyed for a lack of hospitality ridiculous and says it comes from a self-appointed Bible scholar, since the Bible interprets itself. He says Jude 7 explains why Sodom and the cities about them fell: they gave themselves over to sexual immorality and went after strange flesh, which he says means same-sex, unnatural, and that they are set forth as an example.
Why was Sodom destroyed: was it a lack of hospitality?

Jude 7. The humanist, the atheist, the homosexuals are saying that Sodom was not destroyed because of homosexual sin; it was destroyed because of a lack of hospitality. That’s the most ridiculous thing I ever heard in my life. And they quoted— I found out where they got it from— they quoted it from some self-appointed Bible scholar that interpreted that way. And when you hear the word interpret, run, because the Bible doesn’t need to be interpreted; it interprets itself. And here is Jude explaining why Sodom fell: “Even as Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities about them”— it wasn’t just one or two cities, it was several cities, it was a group— “were doing these things in like manner, giving themselves over to” what? Fornication, sexual immorality, “and going after strange flesh.” Now guess what strange flesh is: same-sex, unnatural, like Romans uses “unnatural.” All right, “set forth as an example.” Remember, they are an example. Didn’t we just read it in Corinthians? Yeah. Well, here’s the example of the destruction of people. Sodom is the example, “suffering the vengeance of eternal fire.” See, people that live that way, that reject God, reject the message, they’re going to go to the lake of fire.
Why was Sodom destroyed: was it a lack of hospitality?

Jude 1:7: as Sodom and Gomorrah, and the cities around them in a similar manner to these, having given themselves over to sexual immorality and gone after strange flesh, are set forth as an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire. Romans 1:26-27: For this reason God gave them up to vile passions. For even their women exchanged the natural use for what is against nature. Likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust for one another, men with men committing what is shameful, and receiving in themselves the penalty of their error which was due.
What happened when the men of Sodom surrounded Lot’s house?

He says the men of the city surrounded Lot’s house and demanded the two visitors, who were angels, so they could have sex with them. He says angels do not have sex organs and do not procreate with humans, calls the men’s demand an attempt to force their behavior on others, and says Lot lost his common sense when he offered his two virgin daughters.
What happened when the men of Sodom surrounded Lot’s house?

So people remove the lake of fire. There’s no lake of fire. Liberal churches remove hell; they remove the lake of fire. Isn’t that nice? And this is what they say: God is love, he would never do anything to harm his people. Genesis 19:5: “Where are the men?” Here’s the angels come into Lot’s house. They go into Lot’s house; the men of the city, the males of the city, come and surround the house, and they’re crying out to Lot and saying, “Where are these men?” These men happen to be two angels. They’re not men at all; they are two angels. They don’t even have sex organs. Angels don’t have sex organs. Don’t you believe that nonsense that angels procreate with humans and all that. It’s a bunch of baloney. “Where are these men which came into you this night? Bring them out to us that we may know them,” that we may have sex with them. All right, here they are forcing their ideas, their behavior standards on others. They’re forcing them. “Bring them out.” Genesis 19:8: “I have two daughters.” Look at this one. Lot says, “Wait a minute, guys, don’t mess with these two guys.” Ain’t nobody going to be messing with these two guys anyway; they’re angels. You can’t mess with an angel. But Lot got so, you know, worked up he lost his common sense here for a while. “I will bring out my two virgin daughters to you”— see, here’s that fornication, here’s that sexual immorality— “and do to them what is good in your eyes.” We got to understand there was more sins in these cities than sexual immorality and homosexuality. There was conditions. Okay, we need to know the conditions. We need to know the other sins.
What happened when the men of Sodom surrounded Lot’s house?

Genesis 19:4-5: Now before they lay down, the men of the city, the men of Sodom, both old and young, all the people from every quarter, surrounded the house. And they called to Lot and said to him, “Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us that we may know them carnally.” Genesis 19:8: See now, I have two daughters who have not known a man; please, let me bring them out to you, and you may do to them as you wish; only do nothing to these men, since this is the reason they have come under the shadow of my roof.”
What were Sodom’s other sins besides sexual immorality?

Reading Ezekiel 16:49, he says Sodom’s iniquity included pride, fullness of bread, abundance of idleness and not strengthening the hand of the poor and needy, besides homosexuality and sexual immorality. He says Sodom was prosperous and nobody went hungry, and that strengthening the poor means teaching them a job skill rather than giving them things, because giving makes them lose ambition and drive.
What were Sodom’s other sins besides sexual immorality?

Ezekiel 16:49: “This was the iniquity of your sister Sodom.” Now, he’s likening Israel and Judah to Sodom and Gomorrah, but in doing this he is expanding the condition and the sins of Sodom and Gomorrah. See, he’s revealing it and expanding it. Okay, and he’s going to tell us what the iniquity of Sodom was besides sexual immorality. They had pride, number three. They had pride. First one was homosexuality, the second was sexual immorality, number three is pride. They thought of themselves more highly than they ought. You feel you’re superior. Okay, “fullness of bread.” They didn’t lack food, and that’s why Lot went there. He went there because it was an economic, prosperous area. That’s why Lot went there. Sound like America? Fullness of bread: nobody goes hungry, we feed them all. Is America proud? Yeah. I don’t care what people’s beliefs are, they’re proud of it. “Abundance of idleness.” Man, in America we’ve got abundance of idleness. We Americans spend more time watching TV and playing video games than anything. Abundance of idleness. Two days off instead of working six days, and it gets us in trouble. And number six: “neither did she strengthen the hand of the poor and needy.” Now, you got to understand, there was fullness of bread, no one’s going hungry, but the scripture doesn’t say that is strengthening the poor. If you want to strengthen the poor, teach them a job skill so they can support themselves. That’s strengthening the poor. See, when you give somebody something, they expect it, and they lose their ambition, their drive. The poor had no problem. There were food places to go to get food. Nobody lacked in Sodom and Gomorrah and the surrounding cities. Everybody was taken care of. Sound like America today?
What were Sodom’s other sins besides sexual immorality?

Ezekiel 16:49: Look, this was the iniquity of your sister Sodom: She and her daughter had pride, fullness of food, and abundance of idleness; neither did she strengthen the hand of the poor and needy.
Was Sodom’s sin open and prosperous, and does he compare it to America?

He says Sodom also did abominations, was a prosperous well-watered plain before it was destroyed, and had open sin: they did not hide it or feel any shame. He says he sees the same in America today, where homosexuality is talked about as acceptable, sexual immorality is abundant and abortion is discussed without hesitation. He adds that God honors the righteous, and that you will be rewarded by how you live and talk.
Was Sodom’s sin open and prosperous, and does he compare it to America?

“And they did abominations.” Abominations are things that are detestable to God. Idolatry is listed as an abomination. Okay, homosexuality and adultery is listed as abominations. Sodom and Gomorrah obviously did these other things that were sins. In Genesis 13:10 we find confirmation of this in abundance. “Lot lifted up his eyes and beheld all the plain of Jordan, that it was well watered”: the area was prosperous everywhere before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah. After God got through with Sodom and Gomorrah, in that region, it was just a bunch of salt flats. “Even as the garden of the Lord”: the Garden of Eden, a prosperous place. Yeah, you see, like the land of Egypt— wasn’t Egypt a prosperous place when Israel went down there? Yeah. “As you come into Zoar.” Zoar is the city that Lot fled into, and because he went into it, the Lord spared the city, or else it would have been destroyed. All right, number eight: they had open and outspoken sin. They weren’t embarrassed at all to say they were homosexuals. They weren’t embarrassed at all to say they committed adultery. There was no shame in these people. “They declare their sin as Sodom; they hide it not.” Isaiah 3:9 through 11. Is that what we got in America today? People openly talking about homosexuality as an acceptable lifestyle. Sexual immorality is abundant, isn’t that true? Yeah. And openly talking about killing kids in the womb without even batting an eye, abortion on demand, just openly, blatantly. “Say to the righteous it will be well with him.” What’s the key to being well? Righteousness. Yeah. God honors the righteous. You might make some mistakes, but your heart is focused and your goal is righteousness, as we will see in Lot here. “For they will eat the fruit of their doings”— the fruit of their faith, the fruit of their grace? No, the fruit of their doings. All right: “Woe unto the wicked! It shall be ill with him, for the reward of his hand shall be given him.” You’re going to be rewarded by how you live and how you talk.
Was Sodom’s sin open and prosperous, and does he compare it to America?

Ezekiel 16:50: And they were haughty and committed abomination before Me; therefore I took them away as I saw fit. Genesis 13:10: And Lot lifted his eyes and saw all the plain of Jordan, that it was well watered everywhere (before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah) like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt as you go toward Zoar. Isaiah 3:9-11: The look on their countenance witnesses against them, And they declare their sin as Sodom; They do not hide it. Woe to their soul! For they have brought evil upon themselves. “Say to the righteous that it shall be well with them, For they shall eat the fruit of their doings. Woe to the wicked! It shall be ill with him, For the reward of his hands shall be given him.
How many righteous people would God have needed to spare Sodom?

He says Abraham interceded and bargained from fifty righteous people down to ten, and God said he would not destroy the city for ten righteous people’s sake. He says the righteous people in America are what is holding it together and that light judgments are coming because of the righteous population that stands for Bible morality. He then says Lot lingered when the angels told him to flee, and they literally dragged him out.
How many righteous people would God have needed to spare Sodom?

Genesis 18:32. Abraham is talking to God. Three spirit beings came and visited Abraham. Two of them went on to Sodom and Gomorrah; one of them stayed back, which the Bible says was the Lord, Jesus Christ. He was in the Old Testament before he came in the body; he was there. All right, and so Abraham is interceding for the city. Should we be interceding for our nation and the wicked people and the judgment of God that’s going to come on them? Yes. And so he starts out with fifty: “Well, if there’s fifty righteous, will you spare the city?” Yeah, yeah, yeah. It gets down to ten. It gets all the way down to ten, and God says, “Okay, that’s enough, I’ll spare it if I can find ten. That’s as low as I’m going. I will not destroy it for ten righteous’ sake.” Folks, one of the things that’s holding America together is the righteous people in America. Okay? We’re having light judgments because of the righteous population of America that stands for Bible morality. Genesis 19:5 [Editor’s note: the passage he reads here is Genesis 19:15.]: The angels speak to Lot and said, “Lot, take your wife, your two daughters, and whomever that you— there is in the city that is righteous like you, believes like you,” and so forth, “lest you be consumed in the punishment of the city.” And while he lingered— here he is lingering— “Well, you know, I got to think about this. I got to pray.” How many you know that’s a big thing with us Christians: “Well, let me think on that. Let me process that. Let me— I don’t know if I’m quite ready for that.” So he’s lingering. I mean, God’s got on his calendar a timetable: this city’s going down, and he’s hauling around. Does that sound like the church today? “The Lord being merciful to Lot” brought him out of the city. They took hold of him and literally dragged him out of the city.
How many righteous people would God have needed to spare Sodom?

Genesis 18:23-32: And Abraham came near and said, “Would You also destroy the righteous with the wicked? Suppose there were fifty righteous within the city; would You also destroy the place and not spare it for the fifty righteous that were in it? Far be it from You to do such a thing as this, to slay the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous should be as the wicked; far be it from You! Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?” So the LORD said, “If I find in Sodom fifty righteous within the city, then I will spare all the place for their sakes.” Then Abraham answered and said, “Indeed now, I who am but dust and ashes have taken it upon myself to speak to the Lord: Suppose there were five less than the fifty righteous; would You destroy all of the city for lack of five?” So He said, “If I find there forty-five, I will not destroy it.” And he spoke to Him yet again and said, “Suppose there should be forty found there?” So He said, “I will not do it for the sake of forty.” Then he said, “Let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak: Suppose thirty should be found there?” So He said, “I will not do it if I find thirty there.” And he said, “Indeed now, I have taken it upon myself to speak to the Lord: Suppose twenty should be found there?” So He said, “I will not destroy it for the sake of twenty.” Then he said, “Let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak but once more: Suppose ten should be found there?” And He said, “I will not destroy it for the sake of ten.” Genesis 19:15-16: When the morning dawned, the angels urged Lot to hurry, saying, “Arise, take your wife and your two daughters who are here, lest you be consumed in the punishment of the city.” And while he lingered, the men took hold of his hand, his wife’s hand, and the hands of his two daughters, the LORD being merciful to him, and they brought him out and set him outside the city.
What mistakes did Lot make, and what does the Bible show about drinking?

He lists that Lot quarreled with and divided from Abraham, lived among the wicked for prosperity, lost two daughters who married wicked men, offered his daughters to the men of the city, lingered, lost his wife, and got drunk twice. He says alcohol is the biggest problem in every nation he is researching and asks anyone to show him in the Bible where anybody handled it. He says Lot’s incest with his daughters carried on for generations.
What mistakes did Lot make, and what does the Bible show about drinking?

How righteous was Lot? Well, let me give you a breakdown on Lot. Number one: he quarreled with and divided from Abraham, the patriarch of the Bible. Wow. And the Bible says God hates those that sow discord among the brethren. The Bible says mark those that cause division among you, and he caused the division, because he wanted to go live where the economic system was prosperous. Are you there? Do you know people that cause division today? I know all kinds. Man, America’s church is filled with dividers, and God hates it. Number two: Lot lived with the wicked city dwellers for prosperity when he was a shepherd. You know, shepherds, they need room to feed their sheep. Number three: he lost two daughters who married wicked men in the city, and when Lot went to them to say, “Hey, the city’s going down, daughters, sons-in-law, you got to come out,” they thought he was joking. How many you know there’s some good Christians that lose children to the wickedness? Yeah. And a lot of it— some of it’s got to do with the fact we put them in public schools where they get brainwashed, or we live in communities where the pressure, the pure pressure, is so strong it sways them away. So if we can avoid things as much as possible, that would help, wouldn’t you say? Amen. Yeah. Number four: he offered his two virgin daughters to the militant homosexuals of the city. Number five: he lingered after the angels told him to flee the city. He also lost his wife, who turned back to Sodom; we covered that. Number six: he got drunk twice. You know, I’m doing a research on the nations of the world, and guess what their biggest problem is in every nation? Alcohol. In Russia, the number one cause of death in Russia is alcohol, number one. And these preachers got to preach Jesus drank. We all can drink, you know, we can handle it, we’re mature. Oh man, show me in the Bible where anybody handled it. And because he got drunk, he had sex— committed incest with his two daughters and had children with them. The wrong relationship. Now, some of us don’t have sex with our kids; we just lord over them, and our kids grow up wimps, because they can’t even think without Mom or Dad saying think. Or we want to be our kids’ friend, so we raise our kids as our friend instead of our child. It’s got to grow up and be independent. His descendants, in Psalm 83, became enemies of God, joined Assyria and Tyre against God’s purposes and God’s people.
What mistakes did Lot make, and what does the Bible show about drinking?

Romans 16:17: Now I urge you, brethren, note those who cause divisions and offenses, contrary to the doctrine which you learned, and avoid them. Psalm 83:5-8: For they have consulted together with one consent; They form a confederacy against You: The tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites; Moab and the Hagrites; Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek; Philistia with the inhabitants of Tyre; Assyria also has joined with them; They have helped the children of Lot. Selah
Why does the Bible call Lot righteous when he made so many mistakes?

He points to 1 John, where if we sin we have an advocate with the Father, and says we can mess up and clean up. He says 2 Peter calls Lot righteous because he was distressed in his spirit by the lives of lawless men, and that his spirit was focused on righteousness, though some mistakes carry on to other generations. He says Lot was perplexed and troubled and was a light, speaking up to the people.
Why does the Bible call Lot righteous when he made so many mistakes?

Now, why was he righteous when he did all these things? How many you know, 1 John says, “My little children, I would that you not sin, but if you do sin, you have an advocate with the Father, even Jesus Christ the righteous,” the atonement. So see, we mess up, we can clean up. Hallelujah. And so there’s something in Lot that’s different, and we find it in 2 Peter. 2 Peter 2:7 says God delivered Lot, a righteous man, “distressed in his soul, spirit, by the lives of lawless men.” See, he was distressed by people breaking God’s laws. It affected his spirit. And yes, he made some blunders. This blunder with his virgin daughter is a pretty big blunder, but the angels saved him from that blunder. This blunder with his two daughters, with incest, was a blunder that carried on for generations. And yes, we can get saved because our spirit is focused on righteousness; we are born again; we are pursuing righteousness. But we make some mistakes, and some of those mistakes carry on to other generations. Even though we can be forgiven, we can be restored, it still causes problems for those that we led astray. And that’s why Lot was righteous. You see, he had a commitment to God’s scriptures, even though he messed up sometimes. He was perplexed, [unclear] and troubled. Are we perplexed and troubled by the way our nation is going? At least Lot had a drive, a trouble in his spirit, and obviously he was being a light to those people and preaching to them, because they answered him as though they did, when those guys— “Who is this stranger coming amongst us and telling us what to do?” Obviously Lot was speaking up. Are you there?
Why does the Bible call Lot righteous when he made so many mistakes?

1 John 2:1: My little children, these things I write to you, so that you may not sin. And if anyone sins, we have an Advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous. 2 Peter 2:7-8: and delivered righteous Lot, who was oppressed by the filthy conduct of the wicked (for that righteous man, dwelling among them, tormented his righteous soul from day to day by seeing and hearing their lawless deeds)—
Does God send miracles and warnings before judgment?

He says that neither a miracle nor a message of the coming destruction converted the people of Sodom, but Lot spoke and told them of the coming judgment and they thought he was joking, and that is where America is now. He says that before judgment God appeared in the flood, at the Exodus and with angels, so the world has no excuse, and he is shocked that no one preaches that a warning with a miracle comes first. He says not to be surprised when God starts moving.
Does God send miracles and warnings before judgment?

Are we speaking up? Are we living up? Or we just go to church and go home and stay in our four walls at church and stay in our four walls at home and never let anybody know about this great word of God and this great Jesus? [Neither] a miracle performed nor a message of the coming destruction converted the Sodomites. Genesis 19:11: the angels struck the men at the doorway of the house with blindness, both small and great. So we got a miracle there, and we have two supernatural beings there. Genesis 19:14: Lot went and spoke— he what? Spoke. Say the word: spoke. And he spoke to them and told them about the coming judgment, and they thought he was joking. And that’s where America is now. Listen: at the flood we had God himself there at the flood, talking to Noah, and in the ark God said, “Noah, come into the ark.” So where was God? Inside the ark. And Noah preached for a hundred years. You see, supernatural— the message. They had the angel when they came out of Egypt, in a pillar of cloud and a pillar of fire. They had angels at Jesus’s birth. They had angels at Jesus’s ministry. So when angels appear, look out, world, we’re coming to the end. And I’m shocked that no one preaches this. They just think Jesus can come any minute, when he has got to warn the world. He has got to back up the word of the gospel with a miracle, so when people reject God, they have no excuse. And right now we just got a bunch of preachers scaring everybody to death that the second coming could happen any time. But let me tell you, there’s got to be some things that warn the people, because he always did. I could go on. There were angels at the lion’s den, angels at the fiery furnace, and a God demonstrating himself. Now remember, there was nothing for hundreds of years before the flood. There was nothing for four hundred years when they were in Egypt. There was nothing going on for four hundred silent years before Jesus was born. And right now in America there’s nothing going on. Hebrews 13:2 says, “Be not forgetful to entertain strangers, for some have entertained angels unawares.” So don’t be surprised when God starts moving.
Does God send miracles and warnings before judgment?

Genesis 19:11: And they struck the men who were at the doorway of the house with blindness, both small and great, so that they became weary trying to find the door. Genesis 19:14: So Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law, who had married his daughters, and said, “Get up, get out of this place; for the LORD will destroy this city!” But to his sons-in-law he seemed to be joking. Genesis 7:1: Then the LORD said to Noah, “Come into the ark, you and all your household, because I have seen that you are righteous before Me in this generation. Hebrews 13:2: Do not forget to entertain strangers, for by so doing some have unwittingly entertained angels.
How is America like Sodom, according to this message?

He compares America to Sodom point by point: homosexuality and sexual immorality, pride, abundance of bread and idle time, not strengthening the poor, abominations, and sacrificing children. He says America is sacrificing children not only in abortion but to the dogma of the homosexual, humanist, atheist and liberal church movements, and that there is much more adultery and sexual immorality than homosexuality, and that incest and sex with kids are happening while nobody talks about them.
How is America like Sodom, according to this message?

America versus Sodom. Homosexuality, sexual immorality: we’re equal, right? Yeah. Pride, abundance of bread: is that America? Pride is that superiority, that immodest boasting, self-importance. Idle time. Not strengthening the poor: that we think giving to the poor is going to solve the problem, when we need to teach the poor a career and provide jobs for them. Besides, in America, America’s too proud to pick strawberries in the fields. They’re too proud to mow lawns and clean swimming pools, but they’re not too proud to take welfare. Abominations: idols, sexual immorality, abuse of kids. In Leviticus 18 he lists these things as abominations, and one of them was the sacrificing of children. Is America sacrificing children? Yes. Not only in abortion, but we’re sacrificing our kids to the dogma of the homosexual movement, the humanist movement, the atheist movement and the liberal church movement. We are killing that by letting their brains be fed with this nonsense. Homosexuals and adulterers don’t hide their sin, is it, you know? Everybody’s talking about homosexuality right now because President Obama just made it okay in the military, and, you know, he wants same-sex marriage now and all that. But how many we know sexual immorality, adultery, fornication, hooking up, and, yeah, is just publicly and just openly done. And there’s a lot more adultery going on than homosexuality, because the homosexuals are about 3% of the population. So there’s a lot more sexual immorality going on. Incest is going on. I never hear anything about it. I happen to know about it because I’m a pastor and I’m brought into homes where incest happens, and it’s getting worse every year, and no one talks about it. And pedophilia, sex with kids, they ignore. Miracles, they ignore. They ignore the fact that gays and sexual immoral people and pedophiles and addicts have turned to Jesus, got delivered and living a normal life. How mean? No, salvation is still the greatest miracle, and they won’t acknowledge that. Plus there are miracles, there’s physical healings going on, there’s supernatural things going on.
How is America like Sodom, according to this message?
Leviticus 18:21: And you shall not let any of your descendants pass through the fire to Molech, nor shall you profane the name of your God: I am the LORD.
Does he say miracles are still happening, and why do people mock God’s judgment?

He says salvation is still the greatest miracle and that physical healings and supernatural things are going on, abundantly in South America, Africa and Asia. He says people mock the idea that events like 9/11 or the economy could be God’s judgment, and he notes the time Americans spend on entertainment instead of improving their character. He says that until the 1960s homosexuals were kept in the closet, which he calls the darkness, and then came out with an agenda.
Does he say miracles are still happening, and why do people mock God’s judgment?

It’s not abundant in America, but it is abundant in South America, Africa and Asia: just tremendous miracles. I mean literal miracles, not just healing of physical bodies. And they laugh at God’s judgment message. I hear it on TV, I hear it on radio, I hear it in these talk shows and all that. They just mock at people that say, you know, 9/11 could be the intervention of God. You kidding me? You know, their economy could be the intervention of God. He said they laugh and mock, just like Job’s daughters and sons-in-law did. [Editor’s note: in Genesis 19:14 it was Lot’s sons-in-law who thought he was joking.] Like I said, idleness: Americans spend four and a half hours a day watching TV or playing video games, plus sixteen minutes a day on Facebook, and then you got sports. And you know how many minutes Americans listen to music every day? An hour and a half. So we’re feeding our minds all the time with a bunch of entertainment nonsense instead of feeding our minds with things that will improve our job, improve our character, and improve us as a human being. From 1776 in America— actually from the 1600s when the Pilgrims came over— homosexuals were in the closet. See, you put things in the closet you don’t want guests to see: an ironing board, you put it in the closet. Okay, well, you want to come in and people see an ironing board. All right, they were in the closet where they should have been, in the darkness. The Bible calls that the darkness: do those things in darkness, do those things in secret, not openly. So until the 1960s they were in the closet. In the sixties and eighties they come out, and they came out with their agenda.
What does he say the “homosexual agenda” is?

He reads out a numbered list that he says was written in 1972 and added to in 1984, and says its goals have largely been achieved. The first points are rejecting the Bible and Christian morals, legislating same-sex marriage, promoting different genders under First Amendment rights, convincing the public that people are born that way while censoring evidence against a gay gene, which he says does not exist, branding speech against homosexuality as hate speech, and lobbying for job protection and federal aid. He says they got most of these.
What does he say the “homosexual agenda” is?

This is the homosexual agenda, written in 1972, added to in 1984, that they publicly declared they were going to pursue until they got them all. Number one: reject the Bible and Christian morals and discourage religiously based laws that homosexuality is a sin. Did they get that one? Absolutely. Even Christians will agree that the Bible says nothing against it. It’s amazing; they got Christians believing it. Number two: they are going to get involved in politics and get marriage legislated as, and used as, a legal term, not a spiritual term. Marriage is not a biblical term. It’s not a spiritual term. It is a legal term, and we’re going to legislate same-sex marriages. They just caught that. Number three: First Amendment rights allow them to exercise and publicly promote not only homosexuality but different sexual genders: transsexuals, bisexual, all these other things, and they’re going to repeal all anti-gay laws. Number four: they’re going to convince the public that genders cannot change, they were born that way, that there’s a gay gene, and they’re going to censor any evidence that the gay gene is a hoax, which it is, folks. That is ridiculous. If you had any biology, if you had any chemistry, you know there’s no gay gene. Number five: censoring speech and Bible statements against homosexuality by branding it to be hate speech, bashing, and a crime against homosexuals. And they did it. And I turn it back on them when I go and protest their protest. I call them haters, bashers, and that’s what they are. They bash Jesus, they bash the Bible, they hate Christians. Number six: lobbying for equal employment rights and protection from job discrimination and federal aid for gay activist groups. And they got it. They got federal aid to promote homosexuality. Number seven: end in the military and the Boy Scouts restrictions on homosexuality. How many you know the Boy Scouts have got a lot of pressure on them now? Yeah. And they almost caved in last month, and enough people rose up and they put it off, so it’s questionable now.
What else does he say is on that list, and why does he say it happened?

He continues the list with the Boy Scouts and military restrictions, therapy for children, teaching tolerance in public schools, adoption, elected office, lowering the age of consent and legalizing polygamy, which he says same-sex marriage is a cover for. He says it happened because the church stayed in its walls, content with the status quo, and by its removal allowed liberals, homosexuals, atheists and humanists to change the nation’s laws.
What else does he say is on that list, and why does he say it happened?

I mean, you know, it’s just stupid to have homosexual men leading boys, huh? Just like it would be stupid to have a sexual addict leading girls, male addict. Number eight: stopping children as young as five years old from attending therapy to repair their sexual preference. If a kid is confused, they don’t want anyone telling them that they need to change their thinking. Number nine: teach homosexual tolerance as an acceptable lifestyle in public schools so students support their agenda. And they’ve been doing that since the nineties, and a lot of public school students think bisexual, homosexual is okay. They want to legalize adoption— number ten— by gay individuals, genders and couples, and they got that in the nineties. They want to get homosexuals elected to offices, civil offices, and become judges to change the laws and promote the gay agenda. They did that in the nineties and still doing it. They want to lower the age of sexual consent and legalize polygamy. See, this move for same-sex marriage is just a cover. See, they want to keep breaking down the moral understanding of America. What they really want is they want to have as many partners as they want, and they want to keep lowering the sexual consent. They like young boys. I can testify to that: I was approached three times as a teenager by homosexuals trying to recruit me. They want free birth control and medical treatment for sexually transmitted diseases to all genders regardless of age, and they’ve won almost every one of them in a [unclear] year period.
