And I got to deal with it there. There was Baptist people, they invited me to come and preach at their Baptist church, and I got to address all these issues and preach there and baptize this family. God, yes, He does allow suffering. He allows it because He deals with the wickedness and the sin in this world now. So there is suffering, there is wars, there is genocide, through plagues and so forth. He allows the killing of women and kids because of unjust living and unjust violence. He comes, and yes, He sentences the women and the kids of Canaan land to death. He’s the Judge. They had been sinning for hundreds of years, their sin come to maturity, and God said, “Okay, the time for accountability is here. It’s going to cost you everything.” Folks, He has the right to do that. So don’t go twisting things around like our God is some kind of nitwit. He will deal with a whole nation. “God forbid” that He’s unrighteous because He’s doing His job. That’s what God does. “For how shall God judge the world?” If He can’t take vengeance, if He can’t punish the wicked doer, how’s He going to judge? How’s He going to correct things, how’s He going to deal with things? And He’s not unrighteous when He deals even with a whole nation and has women and kids killed. That’s His business, that’s His decision, and we need to fear God and avoid those kind of decisions. Hallelujah. The problem in America is we get sweet-talked every Sunday in most churches. It’s just a bunch of flattery, sweet talk, and we’re really focusing on worship and just touching Jesus, and we’re not getting the strength of God’s Word in us that will break the strongholds of the enemy. We living in a fairy-tale land where we think just our little prayer is going to change everything. Are you kidding me?
Is Jesus coming back as Savior or as Judge? (2 Timothy 4:1, Genesis 18:25)

He reads 2 Timothy 4:1, “Jesus Christ shall judge the living and the dead at His appearing,” and says “He’s coming as the Judge, not as the Savior.” He says God justifies the righteous, will judge sexual immorality, and deals with things now “to get our attention to repent.”
Is Jesus coming back as Savior or as Judge? (2 Timothy 4:1, Genesis 18:25)

Now, 2 Timothy 4:1: “Jesus Christ shall judge the living and the dead at His appearing.” See, there it is again. When He comes, He’s coming as the Judge, not as the Savior, He’s coming as the Judge. Hebrews 13:4: “Marriage is honorable, and the bed undefiled, but whoremongers,” sexual immorality people, “and adulterers God will judge.” And He won’t wait for the Judgment Day to do that, He’ll deal with it now. Genesis 18:25: “Be it far from You to slay the righteous with the wicked, and that the righteous should be as the wicked, be it far from You. Shall not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?” See, the God of all the earth will justify the righteous. Yes, we may make some mistakes, we may fall, get back up, repent, keep going, but God will justify the righteous, and He will deal now, and I’m going to show you proof of that, with the wicked, and He will deal with it when He comes for eternity. See, He’ll deal with it now to get our attention to repent, He’ll deal with it when He comes for eternity, and I don’t want God dealing with me then. How about you? I’d rather He deal with me now and get me turned around.
Is Jesus coming back as Savior or as Judge? (2 Timothy 4:1, Genesis 18:25)

2 Timothy 4:1: I charge you therefore before God and the Lord Jesus Christ, who will judge the living and the dead at His appearing and His kingdom: Hebrews 13:4: Marriage is honorable among all, and the bed undefiled; but fornicators and adulterers God will judge. Genesis 18:25: Far be it from You to do such a thing as this, to slay the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous should be as the wicked; far be it from You! Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?”
Will everyone stand before the judgment seat of Christ, and is there any debate? (Romans 14:10)

He reads Romans 14:10 that “we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ,” and says every knee shall bow. He says that in a vision of the judgment, “nobody was arguing,” that everyone admitted they knew they were wrong, and that “there’s no compromise when it comes to truth and right.”
Will everyone stand before the judgment seat of Christ, and is there any debate? (Romans 14:10)

All right, Romans 14:10: “Why do you judge or show contempt for your brother? For we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ.” How many? All. And it’s in this context that “every knee shall bow and every tongue shall confess to God.” I’ve told you many times from the pulpit that when God gave me a vision of the judgment, nobody was arguing. God was saying what was truth, and nobody answered back. They admitted that everything they did, they knew they were wrong when they did it. So don’t think there’s any debate going on up there. God is laying out truth, and you, when you hit His light, it’s exposed. Folks, God is a God of light, and everything you’ve done in darkness is exposed. Everything. And there’s no arguments up there, there’s no debate. You see, He is the Judge. Can I hear an amen? You know, we debate in America, we negotiate, we compromise. Obama’s wanting the Republicans to compromise and so forth. There’s no compromise when it comes to truth and right. We can’t do a little wrong so we can get a little right. Are you there?
Will everyone stand before the judgment seat of Christ, and is there any debate? (Romans 14:10)

Romans 14:10-11: But why do you judge your brother? Or why do you show contempt for your brother? For we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ. For it is written: “As I live, says the LORD, Every knee shall bow to Me, And every tongue shall confess to God.”
What does he say about Christians who don’t persuade people? (2 Corinthians 5:10-11)

He says that in God’s light everyone is exposed and “he ain’t going to say a word.” Reading 2 Corinthians 5:10-11, he says that because we know the terror of the Lord, “we persuade men,” and that Christians “that are not persuading people, you’re worthless.”
What does he say about Christians who don’t persuade people? (2 Corinthians 5:10-11)

This God is powerful, and I guarantee you, you’re going to bow. Hitler’s bowing right now. You see Hugh Hefner, he’s going to be dying pretty soon, and he’s going to be bowing to the Lord Jesus Christ. And he said in an interview that I saw last year that he is a righteous man, a man of character. I thought, my Lord, aren’t we really getting ridiculous in America? And when he stands before Christ, let me tell you, he ain’t going to say a word. In that light you’re exposed. “And we’re going to receive the things done in our body.” All of us must appear before the judgment seat, 2 Corinthians 5:10, “whether it be good or whether it be bad. Therefore, knowing the terror of the Lord,” we know what God is going to do to unjust people, wicked people, both now and eternity, because we know that “we persuade men.” Christians that are not persuading people, you’re worthless. You’re just like the other religions’ gods, their gods are worthless. And if you’re not persuading people by your lifestyle and by your word, you’re worthless, you’re not helping anybody.
What does he say about Christians who don’t persuade people? (2 Corinthians 5:10-11)

2 Corinthians 5:10-11: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive the things done in the body, according to what he has done, whether good or bad. Knowing, therefore, the terror of the Lord, we persuade men; but we are well known to God, and I also trust are well known in your consciences.
Does God care about the wicked, and what does Bible morality protect you from?

He says God does care about the wicked, and “he’s dealing with them so correction and get them to change,” but if they won’t change “they deserve what they’re getting.” He says “Bible morality is blessed and protected by God,” and “churches that refuse to preach this are worthless.”
Does God care about the wicked, and what does Bible morality protect you from?

Does God care about the wicked? Absolutely, yes. He’s going to judge them, yes. He’s going to deal with them, but He’s dealing with them so correction and get them to change, and if they won’t change, yes, they deserve what they’re getting. So Bible morality escapes the judgment, both now and eternal. Hallelujah. Bible morality is blessed and protected by God, and I wouldn’t be standing here before you today if that wasn’t true. I’ve had guns pulled on me, I’ve had, I’ve told you these stories. Okay, the Bible clearly states that God will punish all that do evil, both now and for eternity. Can I hear an amen? And churches that refuse to preach this are worthless. They’re just worthless.
How did God judge before the law was given? (Cain, Genesis 4:13)

He says the law did not come until over 2,000 years after creation, yet God personally judged Cain for killing Abel, banishing him and sentencing him to hard labor. He says Cain complained, “my punishment is greater than I can bear,” and that “you can’t get any more emotional than God,” yet He stood for right and truth.
How did God judge before the law was given? (Cain, Genesis 4:13)

Historical evidence of God’s judgment, God doing His job before the law came. We’re going to deal with it before the law. So the law didn’t come in till over 2,000 years after the creation. Genesis 4:13: Cain killed Abel. God came and personally judged Cain Himself, and Cain complained and said, “My punishment is greater than I can bear.” Oh, it’s okay to kill your brother, but God forbid that we do anything to you. Huh? Isn’t that the way the mentality is here? It’s inhumane to execute anyone. You know, women leaders are really getting me upset. They’re beginning to really irritate me, because they’re all for gun control, they’re all for stupid things, because they follow their emotions instead of truth. And folks, I have no problem with women leaders, the Bible has women leaders, but they got to be leaders. You can’t decide things on your feelings. You can only decide things with truth, and I don’t care how emotional you get about things, you’ve got to decide things by what’s right. And we’ve got a bunch of women in Congress, and we’ve had them for years, and they’ve done nothing to help America. If you’re going to be a leader, be one. Don’t give me your women stuff. Same way with minorities. We got all kinds of minorities now in governmental places, and they’re worthless. They’re not changing America. Why? Because they’re not turning America to Bible morality, they’re not standing up for Bible morality. Can I hear an amen? And the men leaders have been worthless for over 200 years, or 200 years, letting this nation go to where it is. It’s gone now. So his punishment was, he was banished. He was banished and he was sentenced to hard labor. “No, this is too much. This is inhumane. I got to spend my life in solitary confinement, and I got to work hard to eat, feed myself? You’re not even going to give me food?” That’s one of our problems. We put them in jail and we feed them, give them an exercise room, give a TV, all the comforts at home, and we pay for it. Are you hearing me today? Did God judge him? And you can’t get any more emotional than God. He has all the emotions that we have, and yet He stood for right and truth.
How did God judge before the law was given? (Cain, Genesis 4:13)
Genesis 4:13: And Cain said to the LORD, “My punishment is greater than I can bear!
What do Enoch and Noah show about God’s judgment? (Genesis 5:24, Genesis 6)

He says God judged Enoch and “justified him and took him,” showing a coming time when the righteous are taken and rewarded with heaven. He says Noah preached 100 years, God saved Noah’s family and three women who responded, and “they were all destroyed” in the flood, adults and children, and he says not to call God unjust “because He’s doing His job.”
What do Enoch and Noah show about God’s judgment? (Genesis 5:24, Genesis 6)

Genesis 5:24: “God took Enoch,” because he was righteous. See, He sentenced Enoch. When He judged Enoch, He justified him and took him. Enoch did not die, showing us there’s a time coming where all on the earth will be taken the same way, rewarded with heaven. How many want the reward of heaven? Yeah. Hallelujah. And there’s a generation that’s going to be taken, that righteous, this generation, and let me tell you, I’m one that doesn’t believe it’s a handful just surviving, just hanging on when Jesus comes. Genesis 6: God saved Noah plus seven. Okay, God saved Noah and those that heard his preaching, and those that heard his preaching were his three sons and his wife and three heathen women that responded to Noah’s message and his boys married them and watch their family destroyed in the flood. Hallelujah. You ever think of that? Ah, three. Most of us give up persuading men if we don’t get one soul saved in one week of effort, we just quit. Noah preached 100 years and only [unclear] his family and three women converted, and kept on preaching, and then He destroyed the wicked. Ever how many was there? They were destroyed. Children, babies, pregnant women, poor, rich, they were all destroyed. And don’t you call my God an unjust God because He’s doing His job. I’m going to get fiery and I’m going to get you with the Scriptures, so you better be ready to take the punches. You may talk to other people that way and get them all confused, but you ain’t confusing me. I know this God, He’s real.
What do Enoch and Noah show about God’s judgment? (Genesis 5:24, Genesis 6)

Genesis 5:24: And Enoch walked with God; and he was not, for God took him. Genesis 6:5-8: Then the LORD saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every intent of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually. And the LORD was sorry that He had made man on the earth, and He was grieved in His heart. So the LORD said, “I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth, both man and beast, creeping thing and birds of the air, for I am sorry that I have made them.” But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD.
Who has the responsibility to punish the wicked? (Genesis 9:6, Genesis 38:7)

He says after the flood God gave judgment to mankind, “capital punishment was instituted by God and given the responsibility to human beings.” He says that when men don’t do their job, as with Judah’s wicked sons, God steps in, and “it’s mankind’s fault” because they didn’t do their job.
Who has the responsibility to punish the wicked? (Genesis 9:6, Genesis 38:7)

Now, Genesis 9:6, after the flood, God gives judgment to mankind. You see, about 1,500 years ago by here, and God gives judgment to mankind, 15,700, somewhere in there. “Whosoever sheds man’s blood, by man’s blood shall he be shed.” Capital punishment was instituted by God and given the responsibility to human beings to do it. So this is what I tell them: you’re blaming my God for the suffering and the pain that’s in the earth when it’s your fault. You’re not doing your job. If you would be punishing the wicked and persuading them, we wouldn’t have this nonsense going on. Don’t you blame God for your lack of strength and guts to punish and correct wicked people. Good place for a clap. Yes. Hallelujah. Judgment is given to man. He doesn’t wait for the Judgment Day, folks, doesn’t wait for the Judgment Day. Genesis 38:7. All right, Judah had a couple of kids. The firstborn, [unclear], was wicked in the sight of the Lord, and no one did anything about it. See, they’re not doing their job, so God come down and slew him. His younger brother, not learning from it, messed up too, and God slew him. Judah wouldn’t correct it. “Oh, that’s my son.” Their mother wouldn’t correct it. “Oh, that’s my boy, he’s a good boy.” “Oh, mama’s kid, you’re a good boy.” So God came and dealt with it. Are you there? Now whose fault that God had to come down and do His job? Mankind’s job, because they didn’t do their job. It’s mankind’s fault, I’m sorry, because they didn’t do their job. Proverbs 10:27: “The wicked’s years shall be shortened.” Hallelujah. Hallelujah. Don’t ever forget that.
Who has the responsibility to punish the wicked? (Genesis 9:6, Genesis 38:7)

Genesis 9:6: “Whoever sheds man’s blood, By man his blood shall be shed; For in the image of God He made man. Genesis 38:7: But Er, Judah’s firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the LORD, and the LORD killed him. Proverbs 10:27: The fear of the LORD prolongs days, But the years of the wicked will be shortened.
What is the difference between shadow laws and civil laws? (Exodus 24:12)

He says God gave the Ten Commandments and the other laws, and that there are shadow laws, civil laws, spiritual laws and wise laws. He says shadow laws are “illustrations of what Christ was going to do” and ended in Christ, but “civil laws stay,” and it’s never okay to commit adultery or murder.
What is the difference between shadow laws and civil laws? (Exodus 24:12)

Now after the law, God is doing His job after delegating judgment to men, but He still does His job when men won’t do their job. Exodus 24:12: “I will give you tables of stone.” That’s the Ten Commandments. “I will give you a law.” That’s all the other laws and commandments, that’s the statutes, that’s everything. Remember, there are shadow laws, civil laws, there are spiritual laws, and there are wise laws that He gave him. Okay, civil laws have the punishment of eternal damnation. When you habitually hurt yourself and others, God will judge you eternally, and He will come and deal with you now. Shadow laws are illustrations of what Christ was going to do when He came, and that’s the law that was ended by the Christ. It’s not the civil law. It’s never okay to commit adultery, it’s never okay to murder. That is a civil law that stands firm for eternity. Amen. And when these people say, “You’re not under law, you’re under grace,” and they think that the whole law was banished, “Now I can commit adultery”? No, no, no, no. Civil laws stay. It’s the shadow laws that are fulfilled, is what’s ended, in Christ. See, the lamb being slain for sin back there was a shadow of Christ dying, and see, we don’t need shadows anymore, we got the real deal. Amen. You see, not eating, not eating catfish was a shadow law about righteousness and living rightly. You see, Christ comes, He was just, no sin, and we live rightly, that’s fulfilling it. You can eat catfish all you want to, and nobody got stoned for eating catfish. Are you there? They try to twist things around, you know, “He gets stoned for eating shrimp.” That’s what the homosexual say: “You get stoned for eating shrimp.” You don’t even know the Bible. Don’t. Only one person was ever stoned for a shadow law, and that was picking up sticks on the Sabbath day. God did it one time, never did it again. Okay, the illustration of the punishment for breaking the real law that was to come. Are you there? Does that make sense? If God goes around killing everybody, how’s He going to save them? Especially shadow laws, and you’re to teach them. So what is the church supposed to be doing? We supposed to be, you know, looking down on the wicked, or we supposed to be teaching them, teaching them, persuading them? “God’s going to get you.”
What is the difference between shadow laws and civil laws? (Exodus 24:12)

Exodus 24:12: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Come up to Me on the mountain and be there; and I will give you tablets of stone, and the law and commandments which I have written, that you may teach them.”
Does he say God judges the wicked now or only at the end?
He says both. He says God is Judge of “the righteous and the wicked both now and when He comes,” and that he will show historical evidence of God’s judgment before and after the law.
What does he say happened to the ruler in Acts who accepted being called a god?
He says “they exalted him as God, he did not renounce it, and so the Bible says God smote him with worms, that he died,” and that God dealt with it then and there.
What does he say the word “judge” includes?
He says “judge is a lawgiver, He is an executioner, He is a punisher, and He is a justifier of the innocent. That’s what a judge is.”
Does he say Christianity is just a philosophy?
No. He says it is “an entryway into the spiritual kingdom, the spiritual domain,” and that “we have a supernatural God that empowers us to live rightly.”
Can you hide sin from God?
No. He says “you might hide it from your mama, your daddy, or your wife or your husband, you ain’t hiding it from God, and God will judge you even though you’re doing it in secret.”
What does he say vengeance is?
He says vengeance is “making things right because someone has done something wrong, a day of reckoning, you hold them accountable.”
What does he say is the problem in churches in America?
He says “we get sweet-talked every Sunday in most churches,” focusing on worship and touching Jesus but “not getting the strength of God’s Word in us that will break the strongholds of the enemy.”
What does he say he saw in a vision of the judgment?
He says “nobody was arguing,” God “was saying what was truth,” and everyone “admitted that everything they did they knew they were wrong when they did it.”
Does he say you can do a little wrong to get a little right?
No. He says “there’s no compromise when it comes to truth and right. We can’t do a little wrong so we can get a little right.”
Whom does he blame for suffering in the earth?
He says to those who blame God for the suffering, “it’s your fault. You’re not doing your job,” and that if the wicked were punished and persuaded “we wouldn’t have this nonsense going on.”
What does he say happened to Judah’s two oldest sons?
He says the firstborn “was wicked in the sight of the Lord and no one did anything about it,” so God slew him, and the younger brother, “not learning from it,” was slain too.
Does he say grace ended the whole law?
No. He says “civil laws stay, it’s the shadow laws that are fulfilled,” so “it’s never okay to commit adultery, it’s never okay to murder.”
What does he say the church should be doing with the wicked?
He asks, “we supposed to be, you know, looking down on the wicked, or we supposed to be teaching them, teaching them, persuading them?”

p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer continues the series by listing the requirements of a judge from Exodus 18, Deuteronomy 1 and 2 Chronicles 19, and shows how God judged Judah when the people failed to correct their leaders. He then teaches how the righteous and the wicked grow together, using Proverbs, and calls Christians to stand for Bible morality, persuading, warning and teaching.
What requirements does the Bible give for a judge? (Exodus 18:21)

He says Exodus 18:21 and other passages give ten requirements of a judge, starting with “fear God,” which he defines as “depart from evil and hate evil.” He adds that judges must be men of truth, “not feelings, not emotions, not opinion,” and must hate covetousness.
What requirements does the Bible give for a judge? (Exodus 18:21)

Now 10 requirements of a judge. This is interesting. And this is where our constitution failed us. There’s no requirement of character to be a politician in our constitution. That’s where the constitution came up short. Number one, Exodus 18:21, fear God. Now, how many remember what fear God is? Depart from evil and hate evil. Say it. Hate evil. Depart from evil. The Bible says that’s the fear of God. Always use your Bible definitions. See, when I fear God, I will depart from evil. I not only will depart from it, but like Noah who hated evil and Job hated evil. They despised it. How many could use a little dose of hatred for sin? Yeah. So you don’t do it. Yeah. Now number two, they got to be men of truth. People of truth. See, not feelings, not emotions, not opinion, but truth. And they got to hate covetousness, the desire for something that’s not yours. To where you get it. You see, you desire somebody else’s spouse and you do whatever is necessary to get it. That’s covetousness. You desire your neighbor’s car. You don’t work, get an education to buy one, so you go steal it. That’s covetousness.
What requirements does the Bible give for a judge? (Exodus 18:21)

Exodus 18:21: Moreover you shall select from all the people able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness; and place such over them to be rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.
Must a judge treat everyone the same? (Deuteronomy 1:16-17)

He says a judge must “judge rightly” and treat everybody the same, “the small, the great, your brother, your family member, your church member, the stranger, the foreigner.” He says that means anyone who breaks the law is dealt with by it, and that laws should be made so people can come in legally with dignity and work.
Must a judge treat everyone the same? (Deuteronomy 1:16-17)

And judges cannot covet. In Deuteronomy 1:16. Number four, you got to judge rightly. All right? And you got to treat everybody the same. The small, the great, your brother, your family member, your church member, the stranger, the foreigner, they all got to abide by the same law. And that means if I live in Mexico and I come to America illegally, I have to be dealt with by the law. Just like if an American did something illegally, but not our Congress. Now, I know the Mexicans don’t appreciate this, but let me tell you, it’s the truth. And you go to Mexico illegally and see what happens. We just got a bunch of pansy congress people. That’s all. You know what they should do is make laws where these people can come in legally with dignity and work. Hallelujah. That’s just an example. No respecter of persons in judgment. And let me tell you something. When our chaplain in the military cannot stand up for the Bible because of the homosexuals, that’s respecter of persons.
Must a judge treat everyone the same? (Deuteronomy 1:16-17)

Deuteronomy 1:16-17: “Then I commanded your judges at that time, saying, ‘Hear the cases between your brethren, and judge righteously between a man and his brother or the stranger who is with him. You shall not show partiality in judgment; you shall hear the small as well as the great; you shall not be afraid in any man’s presence, for the judgment is God’s. The case that is too hard for you, bring to me, and I will hear it.’
Does he call it a culture war or a Bible war?
He says “it’s not a culture war,” it’s “a Bible war,” “a Jesus war,” because “they don’t like Jesus and they don’t like the Bible.” He says “we let them tame us with their thinking.”
Does he call it a culture war or a Bible war?

And that’s not a cultural war. Bill O’Reilly’s got that one wrong, too. It is a Bible and Jesus war. They’re trying to get rid of the Bible and they’re trying to get rid of Jesus. And O’Reilly uses it culture. I hate that. It’s not a culture war. They’re totally against the Bible and Jesus Christ who is for right Bible morality. Can I hear an amen? And see, we let them tame us with their thinking. A culture war. Cultural war. What’s a cultural war? It’s a Bible war. It’s a Jesus war. They don’t like Jesus and they don’t like the Bible. You will not be afraid of the face of men, these small and great, for the judgment is the Lord’s.
Does he call it a culture war or a Bible war?

Deuteronomy 1:17: You shall not show partiality in judgment; you shall hear the small as well as the great; you shall not be afraid in any man’s presence, for the judgment is God’s. The case that is too hard for you, bring to me, and I will hear it.’
Why must a judge not be afraid of the rich and powerful?

He says a judge “can’t be afraid of their stature,” their position or their money, and “has to be strong and do what’s right no matter what the threat or repercussions are.” He applies it to parents who water down discipline because they fear their child will not like them.
Why must a judge not be afraid of the rich and powerful?

And this is why a lot of people won’t judge. Like you get a rich man or a politician, they get away with things, don’t they? And a judge can’t be afraid of their stature. They can’t be afraid of their position. They can’t be afraid of their money. They can’t be afraid because they’re [unclear] and going to kill their family and everything else if we judge them. A judge has to be strong and do what’s right no matter what the threat or repercussions are. Wow. Well, if I correct my child, he won’t like me anymore. Well, it’s tough, isn’t it? So, I let my child be a bird brain because I don’t want him not liking me.
What did Jehoshaphat tell the judges he appointed? (2 Chronicles 19:5-7)

He says Jehoshaphat told the judges to “take heed,” be alert, know the laws, fear the Lord, and remember that “there’s no injustice with God.” He says there is no respect of persons and no taking bribes, and that “there’s one Bible,” not a Catholic, Protestant or Jewish one.
What did Jehoshaphat tell the judges he appointed? (2 Chronicles 19:5-7)

See, it’s in the family. Hallelujah. Well, if I really discipline him, he’ll run away. That’s his choice. I’m going to water down what he needs to learn because I’m afraid of him running away. Hallelujah. Are you there folks? You judge. See, parents have got to learn this stuff. We go to Jehoshaphat in 2 Chronicles 19:5. Jehoshaphat judges over the people and he gave him qualifications. Take heed. Be alert. Be attentive and get your homework done. Know the laws. Be cautious. All right. And then he repeats the fear of the Lord. He said, ‘There’s no injustice with God. God is never unfair. What’s good for men is good for women. What’s good for whites is good for blacks. What’s good for poor is good for rich. Judgment is never unfair. Hallelujah. See, Catholic or Protestant, you’re not excused because you’re a Catholic and they believe certain things that you can’t use that excuse. You go to heaven and tell them you worship Mary because the Catholic Church told you to. You’re not going to have a response. There’s no talking back up there. There’s no blaming anyone else. Are you there? There isn’t a Catholic Bible and a Protestant Bible and a Jewish Bible and a Mexican Bible and an African Bible. There’s one Bible. Amen. There’s that no respect of persons again. No taking bribes. I’ve been to court several times and I’ve saw lawyers giving judges cases of liquor tickets to uh you know sport events and so forth. How many you know that’s a bribe? Hallelujah. I’ve been in the business world and I watched it. Business giving people things to get them to buy their product and order their product. That’s a bribe. You should get a product because it’s the best on the market for the best price, not because someone is giving you something. Are you there? Disc jockeys on the radio are paid to play certain songs. That’s wrong. Now number 10.
What did Jehoshaphat tell the judges he appointed? (2 Chronicles 19:5-7)

2 Chronicles 19:5-7: Then he set judges in the land throughout all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city, and said to the judges, “Take heed to what you are doing, for you do not judge for man but for the LORD, who is with you in the judgment. Now therefore, let the fear of the LORD be upon you; take care and do it, for there is no iniquity with the LORD our God, no partiality, nor taking of bribes.”
What does it mean that a judge must warn the people? (2 Chronicles 19:10)

He says one requirement is to “warn them to trespass not against the Lord so wrath come upon you,” because if the judge doesn’t deal with sin, God will. He says that while we are to contend with those who oppose Bible morality, “Persuade them, warn them, and teach them to avoid that judgment of God.”
What does it mean that a judge must warn the people? (2 Chronicles 19:10)

Warn them. Warn them to trespass not against the Lord so wrath come upon you. Now let that soak in. One of the characteristic, one of the requirements for a judge is to warn the people to not sin against God because if the judge doesn’t deal with it, God’s going to deal with you. God’s wrath is going to come on. It was their job to warn the people. So, they were to persuade, teach, and warn, right? Amen. Hallelujah. Isn’t that interesting? You see, Jesus summed it up when he says, “Love your enemies.” Yes, there are people that oppose us. Yes, there’s people that oppose Bible morality. And we are to contend with them and fight with them, but at the same time, we are to what? Persuade them, warn them, and teach them to avoid that judgment of God. That’s the balance of it. Hallelujah. Now, illustration. David the king got caught up in pride, wanted to number Israel, didn’t get God’s permission. And this is a little sin. This is not a big one.
What does it mean that a judge must warn the people? (2 Chronicles 19:10)

2 Chronicles 19:10: Whatever case comes to you from your brethren who dwell in their cities, whether of bloodshed or offenses against law or commandment, against statutes or ordinances, you shall warn them, lest they trespass against the LORD and wrath come upon you and your brethren. Do this, and you will not be guilty.
What happened when David numbered Israel, and whose fault was the plague? (1 Chronicles 21)

He says David numbered Israel from pride without a census offering, Joab obeyed instead of persuading the people, and God sent a plague in which 70,000 died. He asks if God was unjust and answers, “No. They violated the law,” and says it was mankind’s fault for not doing their job to judge.
What happened when David numbered Israel, and whose fault was the plague? (1 Chronicles 21)

And so he had Joab to go take the census without the census offering. God told him when you take a census, you everybody has to pay a census offering. Okay? And Joab told David, “Don’t, you know, this is prideful. Don’t do it.” And Joab wasn’t a good man. But he knew this was wrong. How many you know, some some people can be wrong in other areas and be right in some areas. Yeah. And Joab tried to get David not to do it. And David wouldn’t listen. But instead of Joab going and trying to persuade the people, he just obeyed David and went and numbered the people. And about 3/4 of the way through, God decided this is it. And he sent a plague, an angel. And David, of course, repented and all that. And he had three choices. And David chose the plague because he knew God was merciful. But 70,000 people died by the plague. It was the first mad cows disease. It was a cow plague. Came from the cows. And the scientists would say, “God has nothing to do with this. It’s just, you know, these cows are carrying a disease. We got to kill all the cows and we got to cure the disease and all that.” No, no, no. God, them cows had that. Them cows were there before. But when God wants to do something, he can use anything he wants, can’t he? So 70,000 people died. Now, was God unjust? No. They violated the law.
What happened when David numbered Israel, and whose fault was the plague? (1 Chronicles 21)

1 Chronicles 21:1-14: Now Satan stood up against Israel, and moved David to number Israel. King Saul made a stupid law. Nobody eats any food until the enemy is destroyed. Till the sun goes down and the enemy is destroyed. Jonathan comes in, sees a honeycomb, and he dips his sword in honey and eats the honey and got strong. How many you know back then you didn’t shoot people. You had to sword fight with them and throw spears and and and you actually moved in a rank and the the guys behind were always pushing the guy in front of them forward and when he fell they just stepped on him and they were the front rank. So they were always using energy. Are you there? And the guy behind them was pushing him and the guy behind him was pushing him. And on the other side you got the other side doing the same thing. Now, how you know you need some food when you exercise that kind of sin. So Saul says, “Nobody can eat.” That’s dumb. So Jonathan ate and Saul’s going to have him executed and the people go, “Hey, Jonathan’s the one brought this great victory.” The people rescued Jonathan from Saul and his bad laws. And listen to me. I’ve been to court several times. I’ve been to court for religious liberties and personal liberties. The opposition will always use Romans 13. Obey them that have the rule over you. See, they want to disobey God. They want to violate Bible morals. They didn’t want to see Agag and all everybody killed and the and uh the spoils given to God and all this.

1 Samuel 14:24-45: And the men of Israel were distressed that day, for Saul had placed the people under oath, saying, “Cursed is the man who eats any food until evening, before I have taken vengeance on my enemies.” So none of the people tasted food. Now all the people of the land came to a forest; and there was honey on the ground. And when the people had come into the woods, there was the honey, dripping; but no one put his hand to his mouth, for the people feared the oath. Am I talking to the right people today? Hallelujah. You young believers, are you learning something? This is important stuff.

Matthew 21:46: But when they sought to lay hands on Him, they feared the multitudes, because they took Him for a prophet. Mark 15:15: So Pilate, wanting to gratify the crowd, released Barabbas to them; and he delivered Jesus, after he had scourged Him, to be crucified.

He says we must live from Monday to Saturday and be “making an impact on the world around me.” He says when the righteous are in authority the people rejoice, so “we need righteous leaders” who stand for justice and what is right.

I can’t just be in a utopia on Sunday morning in the presence of God and the word of God and be satisfied. I’ve got to be making an impact on the world around me. Now, the people’s underlined in white. What people are they? The people for Jesus and Bible morality. Are you listening to me out there? All right, the people rejoice. So when the foundations are removed, the Bible says, “What shall the righteous do?” The righteous has to find a way to get rid of the wicked. But I pray about that. I don’t care what you pray about. And if you know why, you would never allow arm control. In the Declaration of Independence, we are given arms, the freedom of arm to overthrow a bad government. What does Isaiah 5:20 say about calling evil good and good evil?

They cast away the law of the Lord and despise his word. Isn’t that what they’re doing? The anger of the Lord is kindled against these people. He stretches forth his hand against them and smites them. Bible morality persuades, warns, and teaches immoral people.

Isaiah 5:20-25: Woe to those who call evil good, and good evil; Who put darkness for light, and light for darkness; Who put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter! Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes, And prudent in their own sight! Woe to men mighty at drinking wine, Woe to men valiant for mixing intoxicating drink, Who justify the wicked for a bribe, And take away justice from the righteous man! What does he say it means to fear God?
He says “always use your Bible definitions,” and the Bible says the fear of God is “depart from evil and hate evil.” He says “when I fear God, I will depart from evil.”
What does he say covetousness is?
He defines it as “the desire for something that’s not yours, to where you get it,” such as desiring a neighbor’s car and stealing it instead of working to buy one.
What does he say “no respecter of persons” means in judgment?
He says everyone “got to abide by the same law,” including a stranger or foreigner, and that “no respecter of persons in judgment” means treating everybody the same.
Why does he say a lot of people won’t judge?
He says some are afraid of a rich man or a politician’s “stature,” position or money, but “a judge has to be strong and do what’s right no matter what the threat or repercussions are.”
Can anyone use their denomination as an excuse before God?
No. He says “there’s no blaming anyone else” and “there isn’t a Catholic Bible and a Protestant Bible and a Jewish Bible,” there is “one Bible.”
What does he say a bribe is?

He says it is anything given to influence a decision, giving examples from courts and business, and says you should get a product “because it’s the best on the market for the best price, not because someone is giving you something.”
How does he say we should treat people who oppose Bible morality?
He says “we are to contend with them and fight with them, but at the same time, we are to what? Persuade them, warn them, and teach them to avoid that judgment of God. That’s the balance of it.”
How many does he say died in the plague after David’s census?
He says “70,000 people died by the plague,” and that God was not unjust, because “they violated the law” and the people did not correct David.
How long does he say God waited before judging Judah?
He says “He waited 400 years to do this,” sending prophets “and everything else” but the people would not listen.

He says the people in white are those for Christ and Bible morality, and the people in red are those who “want to sin,” “want to disobey God,” and want to violate Bible morals. The slides are not shown in the transcript.

He says “when who perishes? The wicked. The righteous increase,” and that if the foundations are removed, “the righteous has to find a way to get rid of the wicked.”
What does he say is wrong with the church in America?
He says the church “has been dumbed down by faith and grace and a lot of other stuff distracting us from Bible morality to where we allow people to live in open sin without even challenging them.”
What does he say about legislating Bible morality?
He says “they say you can’t legislate Bible morality, but it’s okay for the atheists and the homosexuals to legislate their morality,” and asks, “are we that dumb?”

p: In this short message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that God judges and punishes His people when they behave worse than Sodom. He uses Jude 1:7 and Luke 17:28 to show Sodom as an example and argues that the Bible, not science, tells us what is an allegory. He then begins Ezekiel 16, where God lists abominations His people commit, starting with trusting in your own beauty and playing the harlot because of your fame.
Does God judge and punish His own people?
He says “God judges, and He punishes His people when His people behave worse than Sodom did.” He asks “what can be worse than that city of Sodom?” and says they will find out in this message.
Does God judge and punish His own people?

But today we’re going to look at the fact is, God judges, and He punishes His people when His people behave worse than Sodom did. Did you say, God’s people behave worse than Sodom? Sodom and Gomorrah, yes, we’re going to find out today. And what is worse than Sodom? What can be worse than that city of Sodom?
Why is Sodom a biblical example of God’s vengeance? (Jude 1:7)

He says Sodom is “a biblical illustration of God punishing people.” He cites Jude 1:7, that Sodom and Gomorrah gave themselves over to “sexual immorality and strange flesh,” and says sexual immorality includes adultery and sex before marriage.
Why is Sodom a biblical example of God’s vengeance? (Jude 1:7)

Sodom, we’re going to make a statement that Sodom is a biblical illustration of God’s vengeance. Okay, it’s a biblical illustration of God punishing people. In Jude’s chapter 1:7, the only chapter in Jude: “Sodom and Gomorrah, and the cities round about them, having given themselves over to sexual immorality and strange flesh.” Homosexuality. Two things he mentions is what? Sexual immorality. That’s adultery, sex before marriage, sex in marriage with somebody outside your marriage, marriage.
Why is Sodom a biblical example of God’s vengeance? (Jude 1:7)

Jude 1:7: as Sodom and Gomorrah, and the cities around them in a similar manner to these, having given themselves over to sexual immorality and gone after strange flesh, are set forth as an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire.
What does it mean that Sodom is “an example, an illustration”?

He says incest, orgies, bestiality and homosexuality are included and are “set forth as an example, an illustration, suffering the vengeance of God.” Because the Bible calls it an example, he says, “we want to use illustrations, we want to use the right one.”
What does it mean that Sodom is “an example, an illustration”?

Uh, uh, incest, orgies, bestiality, all these things are included, and homosexuality, are set forth as an example, an illustration, “suffering the vengeance of God.” You see, the Bible said it was an example, it was an illustration, and we want to use illustrations, we want to use the right one.
Who decides what is an allegory or an example in the Bible?

He says “we cannot use examples unless the Bible uses them. The Bible is the one that’s got to tell us what the examples, the allegories, and the metaphors are.” Those who say the Bible is a book of allegories and myths “by using science for their reason” are wrong, he says.
Who decides what is an allegory or an example in the Bible?

We cannot use examples unless the Bible uses them. The Bible is the one that’s got to tell us what the examples, the allegories, and the metaphors are. So Bill O’Reilly, homosexual atheists, humanists, and liberal activists are wrong when they say the Bible is a book of allegories and myths, by using science for their reason. They say--
Does science prove the Bible’s accounts are only allegory?

He says science is used to claim that the ark, the flood and Jonah’s fish are allegories, but “science can’t prove that they could happen.” He says “God is supernatural, and He can do anything He chooses when He chooses.”
Does science prove the Bible’s accounts are only allegory?

See, science says you can’t get all the animals on the ark, so it’s an allegory. Science says the earth wasn’t flooded, so it’s an allegory. Science says that there’s no fish that could swallow a human being and the human being live, because of the stomach acids and so forth and the lack of oxygen. Because science says you can’t go to the Bible and say these things are allegories and examples, they never happened, because science can’t prove that they could happen. God is supernatural, and He can do anything He chooses when He chooses.
When does the Bible itself use a parable, symbol or illustration?

He says the Bible becomes an allegory, parable or symbol when Jesus says so, such as “I’m telling you a parable.” Jesus then used natural truth, like sowers sowing seed and mustard trees growing from seed, to give spiritual illustrations.
When does the Bible itself use a parable, symbol or illustration?

The only time the Bible becomes an allegory, a parable, a symbol: Jesus said, “I’m telling you a parable.” He says, “I’m giving you a symbol, I’m giving you an illustration,” and then He used the natural truth to give us spiritual what? Illustrations. See, sowers did sow seed, mustard trees did grow from seed. Are you there?
What does Jesus say about the days of Lot and His return? (Luke 17:28)

He says we can use something as an example only when the Bible states it, as in Jude 1:7 and Luke 17:28, where Jesus speaks of “the days of Lot.” So when Jesus comes a second time, he says, “we have the example of what Sodom and Gomorrah, to go back to and figure out what’s going to happen there.”
What does Jesus say about the days of Lot and His return? (Luke 17:28)

We can only do this when it states that it’s an example and an illustration, as in Jude 1:7 that we just quoted you. Luke 17:28, where Jesus said, “Likewise the coming of the Son of Man shall it be in the days of Lot.” So see, when Jesus comes the second time, we have the example of what Sodom and Gomorrah, to go back to and figure out what’s going to happen there.
What does Jesus say about the days of Lot and His return? (Luke 17:28)

Luke 17:28-30: Likewise as it was also in the days of Lot: They ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they built; but on the day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven and destroyed them all. Even so will it be in the day when the Son of Man is revealed.
What does Ezekiel 16 say God’s people are judged for?
Reading Ezekiel 16:2, he says “God judges His people for abominations,” and “an abomination is something God hates.” He says God will give six abominations that His people do.
What does Ezekiel 16 say God’s people are judged for?

Ezekiel 16:2. We’re going to find that God judges His people for abominations. His people do abominations, yes. He’s going to give us six abominations that God’s people do. How many? Six. An abomination is something God hates, and see, we think that the homosexual last week was abominable, that’s just an abomination.
What does Ezekiel 16 say God’s people are judged for?
Ezekiel 16:2: “Son of man, cause Jerusalem to know her abominations,
What does “you trusted in your own beauty” mean? (Ezekiel 16:15)

He says the first abomination in Ezekiel 16:15 is “You trusted in your own beauty,” and that God hates it. He says you must understand the biblical definition of beauty, which is “not how good your hair looks” or the latest fashion designer clothes, and he gives 1 Chronicles 16:29, to worship the Lord in the beauty of “right living.”
What does “you trusted in your own beauty” mean? (Ezekiel 16:15)

Well, God’s going to give us six more abominations. And homosexuality is abomination, sexual immorality is abomination. God hates it, He detests it, and He’s given us six that His people do that He hates. Has he got your attention? Number one, Ezekiel 16:15: “You trusted in your own beauty.” It’s abomination. Well, how do I trust in my own beauty? Well, you got to understand the biblical definition of beauty, and it’s not how good your hair looks, and if you got the latest fashion designer clothes on. 1 Chronicles 16:29: “Worship the Lord in the beauty of” what? Oh, right.
What does “you trusted in your own beauty” mean? (Ezekiel 16:15)

Ezekiel 16:15: “But you trusted in your own beauty, played the harlot because of your fame, and poured out your harlotry on everyone passing by who would have it. 1 Chronicles 16:29: Give to the LORD the glory due His name; Bring an offering, and come before Him. Oh, worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness!
What happens when a righteous man trusts in his own righteousness? (Ezekiel 33:13)

He says trusting in your own beauty means trusting “what you determined was right in your own eyes. That’s an abomination. We got to trust in what the Bible says is right.” Citing Ezekiel 33:13, he says that if the righteous man trusts in his own righteousness and commits iniquity, “die for it, just like the Sodomites.”
What happens when a righteous man trusts in his own righteousness? (Ezekiel 33:13)

Living. He said, “You trusted in your own beauty,” what you determined was right in your own eyes. That’s an abomination. We got to trust in what the Bible says is right. Is that a good amen or an old me? Uh, is that a place where you slap yourself and go, “Wake up,” silly? Ezekiel 33:13: “If the righteous man”--he’s talking about the righteous man--“if the righteous man turns from his righteousness and begins to trust in his own righteousness,” his own beauty, all right, “and he commits iniquity,” he will what? Die for it, just like the Sodomites.
What happens when a righteous man trusts in his own righteousness? (Ezekiel 33:13)

Ezekiel 33:13: When I say to the righteous that he shall surely live, but he trusts in his own righteousness and commits iniquity, none of his righteous works shall be remembered; but because of the iniquity that he has committed, he shall die.
What does “you played the harlot because of your fame” mean? (Ezekiel 16:15)

He says Ezekiel is speaking to God’s people: “He’s not talking to sinners, he’s talking to his people.” The second abomination, he says, is “You played the harlot because of your fame,” trusting in being famous and popular throughout the world.
What does “you played the harlot because of your fame” mean? (Ezekiel 16:15)

Did. And he’s talking to his people now. He’s not talking to sinners, he’s talking to his people. Hallelujah. Number two abomination, number two: “You played the harlot because of your fame.” You know, you’re famous throughout the world. You go to Joel Osteen’s church, man, you’re popular. You go to Crystal Cathedral, you’re popular. You’re a Catholic, you got a pope, a new pope over there in, in, uh, the Vatican who believes in civil marriages, unions, same-sex unions. I checked up on this old boy, he’s not this little humble Jesuit priest that they want to exalt. He’s got some beliefs that are anti-Bible.
What does “you played the harlot because of your fame” mean? (Ezekiel 16:15)
Ezekiel 16:15: “But you trusted in your own beauty, played the harlot because of your fame, and poured out your harlotry on everyone passing by who would have it.
What is a harlot in the Bible?

He says a harlot is one who hires herself out, and “a harlot in the Bible is also one that just has intimate relationships with people outside the marriage,” wanting to be satisfied by someone outside their family, home, spouse or marriage.
What is a harlot in the Bible?

A harlot is one that hires herself out, as we heard Friday night here in the [unclear], they sell themselves. A harlot in the Bible is also one that just has intimate relationships with people outside the marriage. Don’t have to hire themselves out, they just want to be satisfied by someone outside their family, their home, their spouse, their marriage. Okay.
What does chasing popularity cost your relationship with Jesus?

He says that when you are so popular that everybody likes you, “you have broken your relationship with Jesus Christ and His Word to let these people satisfy you and indoctrinate you.” He moves on to the third abomination, that you “poured out your harlotry on everyone passing by.”
What does chasing popularity cost your relationship with Jesus?

He says, “And you’ve played the harlot because of your fame.” You are so popular, everybody likes you, everybody thinks that you’re great. You have broken your relationship with Jesus Christ and His Word to let these people satisfy you and indoctrinate you. He goes on to say, number three, not only did you do this, but “you poured out your harlotry on everyone passing by who would have”--
What does chasing popularity cost your relationship with Jesus?
Ezekiel 16:15: “But you trusted in your own beauty, played the harlot because of your fame, and poured out your harlotry on everyone passing by who would have it.
What does he say is worse than Sodom?
He says God’s people can behave worse than Sodom did, and that God “judges, and He punishes His people” when they do.
What does he say sexual immorality includes?
He says it is “adultery, sex before marriage, sex in marriage with somebody outside your marriage,” and that incest, orgies, bestiality and homosexuality are also included.
Does he say the Bible is a book of allegories and myths?
No. He says the Bible must tell us which are the examples, allegories and metaphors, and that those who call it “a book of allegories and myths” are wrong.
Can science disprove the ark, the flood or the fish that swallowed a man?
He says science says these cannot have happened, but “science can’t prove that they could happen. God is supernatural, and He can do anything He chooses when He chooses.”
When does he say the Bible is a parable?
He says the Bible becomes a parable or symbol when it says so, such as Jesus saying “I’m telling you a parable.”
What does he say an abomination is?
He says “an abomination is something God hates.”
What does he say is the biblical definition of beauty?
He says it is “not how good your hair looks” or the latest fashion designer clothes. He points to 1 Chronicles 16:29, worshiping the Lord in the beauty of right living.
What does he say it means to trust in your own beauty or righteousness?
He says it means trusting “what you determined was right in your own eyes,” rather than “what the Bible says is right.”
Is Ezekiel 16 speaking to sinners or to God’s people?
He says “he’s not talking to sinners, he’s talking to his people.”
Does “harlot” only mean someone who sells themselves?

No. He says a harlot is one who hires herself out, but in the Bible it also means someone who has intimate relationships with people outside the marriage and just wants “to be satisfied by someone outside their family, their home, their spouse, their marriage.”

items.d: In “God’s Correction Tactics Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer says God is slow to judge, yet he does involve himself in the lives of believers, correcting them because he loves them. He explains the difference…
p: In “God’s Correction Tactics Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer says God is slow to judge, yet he does involve himself in the lives of believers, correcting them because he loves them. He explains the difference between rebuke and chastening and how God speaks through parents, friends, the church, the Bible and civil authorities. He then presses the church to reach troubled homes and children, citing statistics on runaway youth.
Does God still judge and interfere in the affairs of people?

He says that because God is slow to judge, people begin to think he does not judge or interfere in the affairs of men, and he points to Jeremiah 5:12 where the people say evil will not come on them. He says God’s words become fire to those who speak that way.
Does God still judge and interfere in the affairs of people?

Because God is slow in judging a people, a nation, dealing with them, believers and unbelievers alike begin to think God does not judge nor interfere in the affairs of men. In fact, some of our founding fathers believe that that God does not involve himself in the affairs of men, and today they even mock at that statement. I’ve seen it on the Fox News and other news channels where they actually mock the idea of God doing anything to punish people for sin. In Jeremiah 5:12 it says, they have lied about the Lord. They said it is not he, neither will evil come upon us, nor shall we see sword or famine. The prophets, the preachers, are but wind.
Does God still judge and interfere in the affairs of people?

Jeremiah 5:12-18: They have lied about the LORD, And said, “It is not He. Neither will evil come upon us, Nor shall we see sword or famine. And the prophets become wind, For the word is not in them. Thus shall it be done to them.” Therefore thus says the LORD God of hosts: “Because you speak this word, Behold, I will make My words in your mouth fire, And this people wood, And it shall devour them. Behold, I will bring a nation against you from afar, O house of Israel,” says the LORD. “It is a mighty nation, It is an ancient nation, A nation whose language you do not know, Nor can you understand what they say. Their quiver is like an open tomb; They are all mighty men. And they shall eat up your harvest and your bread, Which your sons and daughters should eat. They shall eat up your flocks and your herds; They shall eat up your vines and your fig trees; They shall destroy your fortified cities, In which you trust, with the sword. “Nevertheless in those days,” says the LORD, “I will not make a complete end of you.
Why doesn’t God destroy people completely?
He says God does not destroy people completely because his ultimate plan is to restore them. He compares it to a parent who corrects a child rather than throwing the child out.
Why doesn’t God destroy people completely?

The word is not in them, so let what they say be done to them. For this reason, says the Lord, because you speak this kind of word, I will make my words in the prophet’s mouth fire, and the people wood, and devour them. I will bring a nation against you from [unclear], and they will devour your harvest, your food, your sons and your daughters, your flocks, your herds, your vines and your fig trees. With a sword they will destroy the fortified cities in which you trust. Yes, even in those days, declared declared the Lord, I will not destroy you completely. Why doesn’t he destroy people completely? Because his ultimate plan, we found last week, was to what? Restore. See, and if I want my children to grow up to be mannerly and well behaved, I have to correct them when they’re wrong, isn’t that right? See, I don’t throw my kid out because they’ve been bad. I correct the problem so that we can go on, and that’s the way God is. God does involve himself in Christians’ lives. He does bring things to punish and to correct us, and so.
Does God punish Christians who turn away from him?

He says God does involve himself in Christians’ lives, and that after he has done you good he will do you harm if you forsake him. He says God brings these things to get our attention, as a parent corrects a child.
Does God punish Christians who turn away from him?

In Joshua 24:20, if you forsake the Lord and serve foreign gods, then he will turn and do you harm and consume you after he has done you good. We get saved, he blesses our life, we get changed, and then we, you know, go back and start doing things we shouldn’t do. The Bible says after he’s done you good, he’ll do you harm if you forsake, if you turn your back on God. And so God brings these things to get our attention, this like a parent corrects the child to get their attention, to make their behavior and their speech and so forth better.
Does God punish Christians who turn away from him?
Joshua 24:20: If you forsake the LORD and serve foreign gods, then He will turn and do you harm and consume you, after He has done you good.”
Why do wicked people seem to get away with sin?

He says that when sin is not corrected quickly, evil becomes the new norm, and that a sinner who never repents can seem blessed. He tells listeners not to compare themselves to the sinner who seems to get away with it, because God has saved such people for the end time destruction, and those who fear God will have it well.
Why do wicked people seem to get away with sin?

Ecclesiastes 8:11, if the sentence against evil, or those that do evil, is not executed speedily, the heart of men is fully set in them to do evil. You see, if there is no correction, then what we’re doing becomes the new norm, the new law. Though a sinner, now listen to this, this is a powerful statement, though a sinner, a flagrant sinner, doesn’t repent, never repents, though he does evil a hundred times and his days are prolonged, and as it says in Psalms, nothing happens to his herds, nothing happens to his flock, he never gets sick, uh, you know, everything just seems to be working right for him. Though a sinner does evil a hundred times and his days are prolonged, and his life seems to be blessed, yet I surely know that it will be well with those who fear God. Isn’t that beautiful? You see, don’t compare yourself to the sinner out there that seems to be getting away with it. Because if you know the Scriptures in Psalms, Asaph said, I, Lord, I, I don’t understand why these evil people are just seemingly nothing bad is happening to them, until he went into the house of the Lord. It says in Psalms, and then his eyes were open that God had saved them for the end time destruction. How many don’t want to be saved for the end time destruction? You’d rather God correct you now. Let me see, show God your hand: Lord, correct me now. I don’t want to be pushed aside and just inherit eternal fire. And so this is a very powerful statement. So do not measure yourself by unbelievers, but realize what is the fear of the Lord: to depart from evil. If I live a life of righteousness, M, repent when I do things wrong, God is going to do good to me and going to do well for me, and in my in days I’ll look back on a blessed life. Amen, hallelujah. Very powerful.
Why do wicked people seem to get away with sin?

Ecclesiastes 8:11: Because the sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil. Ecclesiastes 8:12-13: Though a sinner does evil a hundred times, and his days are prolonged, yet I surely know that it will be well with those who fear God, who fear before Him. But it will not be well with the wicked; nor will he prolong his days, which are as a shadow, because he does not fear before God. Psalm 73:17: Until I went into the sanctuary of God; Then I understood their end.
Why does God correct his people?
He says God corrects his people because he loves them, just as parents correct children and a husband and wife correct each other. He says love is the reason for correction.
Why does God correct his people?

Okay, and so correction is important, and we dealt with correction of sin last week. And here in Revelations 3:19 it tells us why God corrects us, what kind of attitude he has. As many as I love, Jesus said, I rebuke and chasten, I, I correct. Be zealous therefore and repent. As many as I love. Why does he correct his people? Because he loves them. Why does a parent correct their children? Because they love them. If you don’t correct them, you’re what? Not loving them. Why does a husband and wife correct each other? Because they love each other, and they want the marriage to be solid and strong and the family to be strong. So love is the reason for correction. You see, do we get this?
Why does God correct his people?
Revelation 3:19: As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten. Therefore be zealous and repent.
What is the difference between God rebuking and chastening us?

He says rebuke is verbal, telling a fault to convince, and God comes verbally first. Chasten means to train up and educate by discipline or punishment. He says God’s Word can correct us so that we do not need to be punished.
What is the difference between God rebuking and chastening us?

Now, rebuke. He says, I rebuke. Rebuke is to tell a fault, to convince. So the first source of his correction is to verbally come and say you’re messing up. He’s going to verb... that’s what parents do. Son, you can’t do that. You cannot stick your finger in an electric socket. It’s going to straighten your hair. It’s going to knock you 15 feet. It’s verbal. Son, you cannot go out and play in the street. The cars are going to smash you. You know, it’s verbal. And so God comes, comes verbally first. How many are glad of that? Yeah. How many would like a hearing ear to hear God verbally? Yeah, yeah. And then he says, I will chasten, I will correct you. The word chasten is to train up, educate by discipline or punishment. Let me say it again. Chasten here is different than rebuke. Rebuke is verbal. Chasten is to train up and educate by discipline, by punishment. Say I do something that makes your life uncomfortable, and then you will straighten up. So in this verse we see there are two ways God corrects his people, besides, as we taught last week, our sin corrects us and our backslidings correct, correct us. Here God gets involved and corrects us verbally. He tells us we’re wrong, and this is why we need to assemble in Bible studies and, and church. Uh, we need to forget about the miracles and the flattering prophecies and the tongues and interpretation, and we need to go for the Word, because his Word will correct us. And I would rather be corrected by the Word of God than having him to come and punish me in some way, amen, because when God punish me, it also has a tendency to affect other members of my family or those around me. So it’d be better just to listen to the Word.
What is the difference between God rebuking and chastening us?
Revelation 3:19: As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten. Therefore be zealous and repent.
How can God correct us when we ignore his Word?

He says God can remove his presence and correct by things like disease, war, famine, floods, earthquakes and fire. He gives depression as an example, saying King Saul had a depressed, angry spirit come upon him because of his sins and God was correcting him.
How can God correct us when we ignore his Word?

Physical punishment. The Bible says he gives you what you want, but he’ll send leanness to your soul. He can remove his presence, like King David said, not, don’t take your presence from me. If you haven’t touched his presence in a while, it could be, and it obviously is, God is saying you need to correct something in your life. He can correct by disease, war, famine, acts of God, acts of God, or floods, earthquakes, fire, hell from heaven and all that stuff. Depression. King Saul was a, had a depressed, angry spirit come upon him because, because of his sins, and God was correcting him. And I know Christians that are depressed all the time. They never know how to smile. They’re grumpy, they’re grouchy, and they’re angry and they’re violent. King Saul tried to kill his own son because his son disagreed with him, the anger, the lashing out. You can’t stand yourself. Saul couldn’t stand it, and he would, would bring in a musician to bring peace to himself, and people around him couldn’t stand it. And so God uses these things to correct us. Are you out there? We just need to what? Recognize it, get the problem solved and move on.
Who does God use to correct us?

He says God will not use an audible voice from heaven but will use people: the parent, a friend, the church, the Bible and civil authorities. He says God gave parents the responsibility to train up a child, and quotes Colossians 3:20 about obeying parents in the Lord.
Who does God use to correct us?

Now, how does God carry these things out? Well, he’s going to speak to you through the parent, through a friend, through a church. The Bible is not going to be an audible voice from heaven: David, stop it. He’s going to come and he’s going to use people. So we have the parent, the friend, the church, the Bible, and civil authorities that are verbally going to correct us. Now, if you’re a child this morning and listening to this lesson, God gave parents the responsibility to train up the child in the nurture and the admonition of the Lord, including punishment. Even a grown-up child may need verbal correction or advice from a parent. The sad thing is that some parents never let their kids grow up. They’re 30 years old and the parents are still telling them what to do, and uh, God help you if you got one of those parents. The Bible says in Colossians 3:20, to obey your parents in the Lord.
Who does God use to correct us?
Colossians 3:20: Children, obey your parents in all things, for this is well pleasing to the Lord.
What if my parent is not a good parent?
He says that not every parent is a good example, and gives 2 Chronicles 22:3 where a mother was her son’s counselor to do wickedly. He says the child is then at the mercy of that parent until grown.
What if my parent is not a good parent?

In 2 Chronicles 22:3, what if the parent is not a good parent? You see, it’s great that parents are given the responsibility to train up and be an example to the children. It’s great. Man, I wish it was that easy, but what if the parent isn’t a good example? What if the parent aren’t good parents? And in 2 Chronicles 22:3 it says, his mother was his counselor to do wickedly. See, his own parent gave him bad advice and was a bad example. You see, the child in this case is at the mercy of the [unclear] till they grow up and can think [unclear].
What if my parent is not a good parent?
2 Chronicles 22:3: He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother advised him to do wickedly.
How does the Lord take up children whose parents forsake them?

He says the Lord takes them up through the church: the church gets the message out to children, brings them in, and teaches them what is right and wrong. He tells of a time he dealt with two sisters, where the one who took her children to church had children who knew what was wrong.
How does the Lord take up children whose parents forsake them?

But the Bible says in Psalms 27:10, when my parents forsake me, when they turn their back on me, the Lord will take me up. Now, how does the Lord take them up? The parent, the church. See, the church has got to wake up to what it really is. You know, we are here to get the message out that there’s a better way to live, and we’re here to get the message out to children that there’s a better way to live. And so when the children hear, they come to church, you go out and you bring them in, and they come to church and they hear what is right and wrong, and then they go home and they know something’s wrong here. There was a, some years back I dealt with two sisters. They married two brothers, and both brothers were bad brothers. They were drinkers and horrible sexual permissiveness and everything else. But one of the sisters went to church and took the children to church, so when this father approached the 16-year-old daughter of his in the kitchen and grabbed her, and she knew that that was wrong and fought off, that. But the other sister, who didn’t go to church, and of course neither of the men went to church, they didn’t know what was right and wrong, and they just thought, you know, well, this is this is life, and they gave in and had a child by the father and didn’t learn the years later that that’s wrong. You see, the church is important. Church, you are important to get the word out what is right and what is wrong, to save children from bad homes and to give parents in bad homes an opportunity to change their life. Amen. Are you with me? And if we, and, and it’s the Word that’s going to do that. We got to get the Word out. You got to be able to, you guys have got to learn, you are a witness of God’s Word. You can share the Word with people, and we’ve got to go out to the highways and the hedges and compel them to come in. They’re not going to come knocking on the door.
How does the Lord take up children whose parents forsake them?

Psalm 27:10: When my father and my mother forsake me, Then the LORD will take care of me. Luke 14:23: Then the master said to the servant, ‘Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.
Why must Christians go out and find people instead of waiting for them to come?

He says people are not going to come knocking on your door, so we must go find them where they are and invite them to hear the Word of God. He says that Word will change their life if they want change and receive it.
Why must Christians go out and find people instead of waiting for them to come?

They’re not going to come knocking on your house and go, hey, hey, hey, uh, can you tell me how to find Jesus or improve my life or whatever? No, you got to go knock on their door. You got to go find them where they’re at. You got to invite them to hear the Word of God and touch God, and that Word then will change their life if they want change and receive it. It’s amazing how we help the homeless, how we help the addicts, the dropouts, and defend the rights of adults in America to live as they please, but won’t stand up for the rights of innocent children that these same adults are hurting, abusing, sexing, neglecting and raising up wrongly. And the church has lost its fight in America.
What does he say about runaway youth in America?

He says the church used to speak out on righteousness and sin but now offers psychology and feel-good messages. He cites figures on teenage runaways being abused and says 1.6 million young people 18 and under run away every year in America.
What does he say about runaway youth in America?

In the ‘90s the church spoke out openly for righteousness and justice, but after the ‘90s you don’t hear the church speaking out on righteousness and sin. You hear psychology and feel-good messages, and God, you know, want you, you self-esteem, God wants you to have self-esteem. Well, my, you know, come on, church, we need the teaching of God’s Word, amen, in right and wrong. The United States Department of Health and Human Services said 46% of teenage runaways 18 and under are physically abused, [unclear]% were sexually abused, that’s why they ran away, 38% was emotionally abused: you’re no good, you’re worth, you’ll never amount to anything, uh, no interaction, the kid just left alone. 60%, 66% of runaways had an alcohol parent, two-thirds of runaways were running from alcohol and the abuse and the problems that come with it. 25% are running from those parents who abuse drugs. That’s 91% of runaways in America, or throwaways, are drug and alcohol related. Are you there? And the church wants to argue about whether Jesus drank or didn’t drink. Folks, there’s something wrong in America. Now listen. You say, well, so what? Well, there’s 1.6 million 18 and under running away every year in America.
Where is the church when young people are on the streets?

He asks whether the church cares or only wants to enjoy the presence of God, and says no one is addressing the problem. He says these young people are exposed to sex trafficking and survival sex, and says the church is silent.
Where is the church when young people are on the streets?

In 10 years that’s 16 million. Obama never addresses it, the Democrats never address it, the Republicans aren’t addressing it, no one is addressing it, and the church is silent. And yet we worry about the war in Iraq, and we worry about the border, and we worry about all a lot of these things, abortion and so forth, and yet 1.6 million of our young people are out on the streets every year. Does the church care, or do we just want to come in and enjoy the presence of God and hear an inspirational message and hear about us sending mission money to the mission field and feeding the [unclear] down here and the [unclear] that drops out and [unclear] and everything we are? Where is the church in this thing? These kids are exposed to sex trafficking. They’re actually being sold for sex, sex for survival. They have sex just so somebody will give them a roof to be under and some food. And we’re talking about kids from 10, 11 up to 18 years old. One mother sold her own child for sex in South Carolina. All this sexual promotion in America, and if it feels good, do it. The mentality is, you know, sex is the thing, and sex is okay, and we, and we sell our kids. There’s some wrong when a mother who has a God-given protection button in her, you touch that kid, man, you just caught a tail of a wild cat, and that is changed and neutralized to where have my daughter, have my son, give me a hundred bucks. Are you there? And what is the church saying? We’re saying nothing. Either they get HIV and they get viral diseases and they go into prostitution, and it’s just embarrassing. It’s shameful what is happening to 1.6 million youth every year. And some of these kids are thrown out by their parent. They don’t want them anymore, they’re just in the way, and other ones are running away.
What does he say is the source of America’s problems?

He says the source of America’s problems right now is the home, and that no one is addressing it. He says the church is here to be a source to straighten out troubled homes and to comfort and encourage neglected children and youth.
What does he say is the source of America’s problems?

Matthew 10:36, Jesus said, a man’s enemies will be those of his own household, and that is exactly what’s happening in America.
