The source of America’s problems right now is the home, and no one is addressing it, and the church, in my research, including this one, has not stood up publicly and declared that this is wrong. What politician running for office hammers about these issues? None. See, they want the right for women to have abortion, they’ll hammer, you know, environmental issues, they hammer all kinds of things, and no one is going to the rescue of these innocent kids being thrown out or running away from abusive homes. The church is there. We are here. We’re not just people here to come in and sing songs and enjoy the blessings of God, but we’re here to be a source to straighten out troubled homes and comfort and encourage [unclear] neglected children, neglected youth, and we should be going out of our way to do that. We should have time to do that. Can I hear an amen?
What does he say is the source of America’s problems?
Matthew 10:36: and ‘a man’s enemies will be those of his own household.’
How can a church work together as a team?

Using a football team as his picture, he says every player must know the role, the part and the goal, and that the church must agree to work as a team to get the Word of God out to homes and children. He says it is nothing for God to save by many or by few.
How can a church work together as a team?

You see, to do that we got to become a team. They’ve been talking about teams on Friday, you got to join the team. We’re having Super Bowl today, and every player has to play as this team player. They got to know their role, they got to know their part, they got to know the goal. The goal is to get that football in the end zone, and whatever it takes to get it there, we got to work as a team to do it. We got to protect our quarterback, we got to block for our runner. Are you there? The quarterback can’t go out there and hack the ball to himself and then throw it to himself. And church, look at you. You can decide today to be a team, because the Bible says it’s nothing for God to say by many or by few. But the key is we got to agree to work as a team and set a goal to get the Word of God out to these homes and get these, the Word out to these children and bring them in. That bus should be full of kids, because in no area have I been that there is such a high percentage of troubled homes in [unclear]. And I’ve ministered in a lot of areas in California. There’s a lot of troubled homes out there, messed up homes, parents who don’t know what they’re doing, they’re just self-centered, selfish, and accidentally had kids.
How can a church work together as a team?

1 Samuel 14:6: Then Jonathan said to the young man who bore his armor, “Come, let us go over to the garrison of these uncircumcised; it may be that the LORD will work for us. For nothing restrains the LORD from saving by many or by few.”
How can a friend correct us, and what about bad friends?
He says a good friend will correct you when you are wrong, and a Bible friend will verbally correct you. A worldly friend who seduces you into things against God’s word will lead you astray.
How can a friend correct us, and what about bad friends?

Now then, we got the friend, a friend, a close acquaintance, they can correct us. A man sharpens the countenance of his friend, Proverbs 27:17. See, as iron sharpens iron, we sharpen the countenance, the conscience, see, the person of our friend, and a good friend will do that. A good friend will correct you when you’re wrong. But what if that friend is not a good friend? Psalms 41:9, my own familiar friend in whom I trust, who ate my bread with me, has lifted up his heel against me. And a lot of your acquaintances are trying to lure you and seduce you into doing things that are against God’s word. We don’t have to go to church, it’s okay to drink and [unclear], they are seducing it. These kind of friends aren’t Bible friends. A Bible friend will verbally correct you. A worldly friend will lead you astray.
How can a friend correct us, and what about bad friends?
Proverbs 27:17: As iron sharpens iron, So a man sharpens the countenance of his friend. Psalm 41:9: Even my own familiar friend in whom I trusted, Who ate my bread, Has lifted up his heel against me.
What does Jeremiah 5 say God will not do?
In the passage he reads, God says that even in those days of judgment, “I will not destroy you completely.” He says that is because God’s ultimate plan is to restore.
What is the goal of God’s correction?
He says God’s ultimate plan is to restore, and that God corrects so that we can go on, just as a parent corrects the problem rather than throwing the child out.
Should we measure ourselves by unbelievers?

He says no: do not measure yourself by unbelievers, but realize the fear of the Lord is to depart from evil. He says if we live a life of righteousness and repent when we do wrong, God will do good to us.
Why do a husband and wife correct each other?
He says a husband and wife correct each other because they love each other and want the marriage and the family to be strong.
What two ways of correction does he find in Revelation 3:19?
He says that in this verse there are two ways God corrects his people: rebuke, which is verbal, and chastening, which is to train up and educate by discipline or punishment.
Why would he rather be corrected by God’s Word than by punishment?
He says he would rather be corrected by the Word of God than have God punish him, because when God punishes, it also has a tendency to affect other members of his family or those around him.
What does he say we need instead of miracles, flattering prophecies and tongues?
He says we need to forget about the miracles and the flattering prophecies and the tongues and interpretation and go for the Word, because his Word will correct us.
What does he say about depression and correction?

He says King Saul had a depressed, angry spirit come upon him because of his sins and God was correcting him. He says he knows Christians who are depressed all the time and recommends that we recognize the problem, get it solved and move on.
Does God speak to us with an audible voice from heaven?
He says it is not going to be an audible voice from heaven. He says God will come and use people to correct us verbally.
What does he say about parents and grown children?
He says even a grown-up child may need verbal correction or advice from a parent, but that some parents never let their kids grow up.
What does he say about the church speaking out in America?

He says that in the ’90s the church spoke out openly for righteousness and justice but after that you hear psychology and feel-good messages. He says the church needs the teaching of God’s Word in right and wrong.
What does he say the church is here for?

He says we are not just people here to come in and sing songs and enjoy the blessings of God, but are here to be a source to straighten out troubled homes and comfort and encourage neglected children and youth.
What makes a friend a Bible friend?
He says a Bible friend will verbally correct you, while a worldly friend will lead you astray.

items.d: In “God’s Correction Tactics Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer says God’s correction comes by his Word and, when it is ignored, by punishment, and that the goal is the peaceable fruit of righteousness (Hebrews…
p: In “God’s Correction Tactics Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer says God’s correction comes by his Word and, when it is ignored, by punishment, and that the goal is the peaceable fruit of righteousness (Hebrews 12). He uses Ezekiel 14, Isaiah 29:6 and 1 Corinthians 11:30, and Ezra’s request to God as a pattern for accepting correction and asking God to keep his promises. He closes with Proverbs 13:24 and 19:18 on prompt discipline.
Why is it important to find a good moral church?

He says preachers and churches are not always good, and that a church which stands for morality is the church that will have an effect for good on homes, the community and the world. He says a church that flatters you and lets you live the way you want is not a good church.
Why is it important to find a good moral church?

And then you got the church. But we know from the newspapers and the Bible that preachers and churches aren’t always good. Churches have been caught molesting children, taking the money, preaching bad doctrines, both in the Bible and in our everyday newspapers. So, finding a good moral church is important, isn’t it? A church that stands for morality. You may not like to hear the preaching, but let me tell you, that’s the church that is going to have an effect for good on the homes and the community and in the world. Could that be true?
Why can we always trust the Bible when we cannot always trust people?

He says you cannot always trust a friend, a spouse, church leaders or a parent, but you can always trust the Bible because it does not change. He says the Bible will keep you sound, keep correcting you and keep making you wiser, and that it is the foundation of correction.
Why can we always trust the Bible when we cannot always trust people?

Amen. A church that flatters you and lets you live the way you want is not a good church. And so when the ministers goes a muck, what does a person do? Well, then they go to the Bible. You can’t... the Bible stands strong. It’s our standard. And if you don’t twist it and turn it to your own convenience, that word will always keep you sound. Hallelujah. It will always be correcting you. It will always keep making you wiser. And do you realize that only 15%, 15% of Christians read their word? And that is the foundation of correction. You can’t always trust your friend. You can’t always trust your spouse. You can’t always trust the church leaders. You can’t always trust a parent. But you can always trust the Bible. Hallelujah. It doesn’t change. And it is sad when we do not read that seriously and objectively every day. How many of you read your Bible through last year? You see what I mean? And we’re in a church that pushes reading the word all the time, and we can’t find time to read the word. And we can find time to watch TV, go to movies, and do all kinds of things, but we can’t find time to read the book that is a sound source for us to be corrected by God.
What saves a person when God sends judgment?

Reading Ezekiel 14, he says Noah, Daniel and Job would only save themselves by their righteousness, not by faith, grace, miracles, worship, prayer, the ark or prosperity. He says you can have miracles and not be righteous.
What saves a person when God sends judgment?

Hallelujah. How do you know preachers are preaching the right thing if you don’t get to the book and find out? And that’s what the Bible said. The acts of God were also used to correct, and punishment. Correction by punishment in Ezekiel 14:21 sums it up. When I send my painful judgments upon Jerusalem, war, famine, beast, and epidemic diseases, if Noah, Daniel, and Job were there, they would only save themselves by their what? You notice the word faith is not there. You will notice the word grace is not there. Hello, are you out there? Do you notice the word miracles are not there? We got miracles in our church. You can have miracles and not be righteous. Hallelujah. Worship is not there. Some people, that’s all they want to do is just focus in on worship. That’s just one aspect. The word prayer is not there. Are you getting the message? Daniel was a prayer. Daniel had miracles. Daniel had visions. But it wasn’t his prayers, his visions, and his miracles that would save him. What was it? What was it? His righteousness. Noah built a boat. My goodness, what a feat he did. He had a huge building. Miraculous. Oh man, how awesome. But it wasn’t the ark that saved him. Are you there, church? It wasn’t his faith that saved him. It was his righteousness. Hallelujah. Job was wealthy, prosperous. So was Daniel. But it wasn’t their prosperity that saved him. It was their righteousness. Do you get it? Correction by punishment. God can bring a war. And I don’t care how great we are right now in, in the world, in our arms.
What saves a person when God sends judgment?

Ezekiel 14:14-21: Even if these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they would deliver only themselves by their righteousness,” says the Lord GOD. “If I cause wild beasts to pass through the land, and they empty it, and make it so desolate that no man may pass through because of the beasts, even though these three men were in it, as I live,” says the Lord GOD, “they would deliver neither sons nor daughters; only they would be delivered, and the land would be desolate. “Or if I bring a sword on that land, and say, ‘Sword, go through the land,’ and I cut off man and beast from it, even though these three men were in it, as I live,” says the Lord GOD, “they would deliver neither sons nor daughters, but only they themselves would be delivered. “Or if I send a pestilence into that land and pour out My fury on it in blood, and cut off from it man and beast, even though Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it, as I live,” says the Lord GOD, “they would deliver neither son nor daughter; they would deliver only themselves by their righteousness.” For thus says the Lord GOD: “How much more it shall be when I send My four severe judgments on Jerusalem—the sword and famine and wild beasts and pestilence—to cut off man and beast from it?
Does God use war and disease to correct a nation?

He says God can bring a war, and that if God decides this nation is going down, it will go down. He says “this HIV thing is obviously a visitation from God” and that new sexually transmitted diseases are God saying the sexual revolution is not the way to go.
Does God use war and disease to correct a nation?

If God decides this nation’s going down, folks, we’re going down. See, the Bible says, “Some trust in chariots, some in horses, armaments, but we will remember the name of the Lord our God.” Now, we got to have arms, but let me tell you, we got to have God. And this HIV thing is obviously a visitation from God. We didn’t have it before, before. It came from a source of sin. It’s obvious God is trying to adjust. All these new sexually transmitted diseases that we never heard of before, 30-some new ones, are God saying sexual revolution is not the way to go.
Does God use war and disease to correct a nation?
Psalm 20:7: Some trust in chariots, and some in horses; But we will remember the name of the LORD our God.
What are the acts of God that correct people?

He says acts of God are flood, fire from heaven and hell, and reads Isaiah 29:6, where the Lord of hosts visits with thunder, earthquake, a great noise, storm, tempest and devouring fire. He says the reason is to get you to correct yourself.
What are the acts of God that correct people?

And America just keeps pumping medicine into them and hanging on to these ideas and not recognizing, even mocking when somebody, and I heard ministers get on TV at these news, uh, talk shows and say that’s God’s judgment, and they were laughed at and mocked at. And one was a woman pastor that did an excellent job, and they just ridiculed her. And that was on Fox News. Did one of the best jobs I ever heard. Acts of God are flood, fire from heaven, and hell. In Isaiah 29:6 it says, “You shall be visited of the Lord of hosts with thunder and earthquake and a great noise, and a storm and a temp, tempest, and a flame of devouring fire.” Why?
What are the acts of God that correct people?
Isaiah 29:6: You will be punished by the LORD of hosts With thunder and earthquake and great noise, With storm and tempest And the flame of devouring fire.
Does 1 Corinthians 11:30 say believers are sick because of God’s correction?

He reads that many are weak and sick among you, and many asleep, and says God is talking to the church. He says some believers are weak, sick or dead before their time because they did not discern the Lord’s body, and that God corrects by punishment.
Does 1 Corinthians 11:30 say believers are sick because of God’s correction?

To get you to correct yourself. Colossian, 1 Corinthians 11:30, for this reason, many are weak and sick among you, and many asleep. He’s talking to the church. Some of you believers are weak, weak in your mind, weak in your emotion, weak in your spirit. Some of you are sick and some of you are dead before your time because you did not discern the Lord’s body. You are the body of Christ. His body died for our sins. We are the body of Christ. And so God corrects by punishment. What’s the goal of correction? Hebrews 12:9, our fathers of our flesh corrected us and we gave them respect.
Does 1 Corinthians 11:30 say believers are sick because of God’s correction?
1 Corinthians 11:30: For this reason many are weak and sick among you, and many sleep.
What is the goal of God’s correction according to Hebrews 12?

He says fathers of the flesh corrected us and we respected them, so it is common sense that God our Father will correct us, for our profit that we might be partakers of his holiness. He says no chastening seems joyous at the time, but afterward it yields the peaceable fruit of righteousness.
What is the goal of God’s correction according to Hebrews 12?

Shall we not much rather be in submission unto the father of spirits and live? In other words, if natural fathers correct us and we respected them, we responded. Isn’t it just common sense that God our father will correct us? For fathers of the flesh, for a few days corrected us after their own pleasure. But God for our profit, that we might be partakers of what? His holiness, his righteousness. See, God has a goal. No chastening, no correction for the present seems to be joyous, but it’s grievious. Now, we understand that in the natural, when I’d go to discipline my kids, you know, they’d put a book behind their bottom and, you know, pad whatever. It wasn’t a, it wasn’t an enjoyable time. They weren’t going, “Oh, great. Dad’s going to spank us. Hallelujah. Man, I can’t wait.” And neither do adults in the church. We don’t like it, and we try to ignore it and say it isn’t God. Like I read at the beginning, they say it’s not God, but afterward it yields the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised, trained thereby.
What is the goal of God’s correction according to Hebrews 12?

Hebrews 12:9-11: Furthermore, we have had human fathers who corrected us, and we paid them respect. Shall we not much more readily be in subjection to the Father of spirits and live? For they indeed for a few days chastened us as seemed best to them, but He for our profit, that we may be partakers of His holiness. Now no chastening seems to be joyful for the present, but painful; nevertheless, afterward it yields the peaceable fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.
Why would a loving father correct instead of letting a child keep doing harm?

Using the picture of a child who sniffs model-airplane glue, he says he would be a bad father if he neglected to teach the boy and do what is necessary to stop it. He says he is the adult, the one supposed to know better, protect and guide.
Why would a loving father correct instead of letting a child keep doing harm?

Hallelujah. You see, correction is part of the training, part of the exercise to make you a righteous person. Wouldn’t it be foolish for me? My kid gets an airplane model and he puts this airplane model together with glue. And in doing that, building this airplane model, he gets the smell of that and he gets a, a rise from it, a high from it. And so instead of building the airplane model, he just sniffs the glue. Now, wouldn’t it, wouldn’t I be a bad father if I neglect it to teach this boy and do what’s necessary physically to get him not to do that? Absolutely. See, he’s the child. I’m the adult. I’m the one that’s supposed to know better. I’m the one that’s supposed to be protecting. I’m the one that’s supposed to be guiding. And yes, in that issue, we all go, “Yeah, it’s a bad day. Yeah, he needs to correct it.” Well, church people are using profanity. Parents are using profanity. Church people lie. Church people lose their temper. They verbally abuse people. They slander people.
Why doesn’t God just say "I love you" and let us keep doing wrong?

He says if the child keeps sniffing the glue the mind burns out, and if we as Christians keep doing wrong things we destroy our life and the lives of those around us. He asks whether God should correct parents who drop their kids off at church and go home.
Why doesn’t God just say "I love you" and let us keep doing wrong?

Now, is God a good God when he just say, “Oh, I love you. You just keep sniffing the glue.” You know, it’s really not the best way for you, but I love you. You know, you just keep sniffing the glue. What happens if the kid keeps sniffing the glue? The mind burns out. Yes. What happens if we as Christians just keep doing these things that are wrong? We destroy our life and we destroy those around us. Hallelujah. Parents drop their kids off to babysit at church and go home.
How can God use trouble in our homes to correct us?

He says once you accept Christ God will correct you and you will have troubles, and that your own kids may come against you because of your neglect and because you ask them to do one thing while you do another. He says we need to go to the Bible to get our life, and then our home, straightened out.
How can God use trouble in our homes to correct us?

Shouldn’t God correct that? Shouldn’t a parent come as an example to the child? Church is not just good for you, it’s good for the whole family. Isn’t that right? So God’s got to come and deal with this stuff. Once you say you’re a believer and you accept Christ, God’s going to spank your fanny, and you’re going to have troubles. Your own kids will come against you. That’s one of his ways. He’ll turn your kids right against you. And he doesn’t have to do it directly. He does it because of your neglect. And you’re asking them to do one thing and you are doing another. And then we go to psychologists and psychiatry and we spend 50 bucks for a half hour to try to straighten out our home, when we just need to go to the Bible and get our life straightened out and our home would get straightened out.
How can the church have an effect on homes in America?

He says if he wants his children corrected, he has to let God correct him, and if the church is going to have an effect on homes and lives in America for good, we have to get our own home and life together. He says the purpose of correction is the peaceable fruit of righteousness.
How can the church have an effect on homes in America?

And that’s an amen. Hallelujah. But the correction, I got to let God correct me. If I want my children corrected, I got to let God correct me. If the church is going to have an effect on the homes in America, we got to get our home together. Is that true? If we’re going to have an effect on the lives of people in America for good, we got to get our life together. And the purpose of correction is what? The peaceable fruit of righteousness. Peaceable, lack of war, lack of opposition.
Why does he say America is becoming a weak nation?

He says America is becoming a weak nation because it will not listen to God’s corrective word. He says that when God deals seriously with America, beyond economic downturns and plagues such as AIDS and other diseases, the nation will be in anguish.
Why does he say America is becoming a weak nation?

Righteousness produces that peaceable fruit of righteousness. Hallelujah. We are becoming a weak nation because America will not listen to God’s corre... corrective word. And when God decides to deal seriously with America, and not these little things that he’s bringing, like an e... economical downturns and plagues such as AIDS and the STD diseases, when he really gets serious, this nation is going to be in anguish. Ultimatum. Now this is powerful. Ezra is in captivity for the sins of Israel.
What does Ezra’s ultimatum to the king of Persia teach?

He says Ezra was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers because he had told the king that the hand of God is upon all for good that seek him, and his power and wrath is against all that forsake him. He calls this an ultimatum and says the Persian Empire went down.
What does Ezra’s ultimatum to the king of Persia teach?

Several thousand went into captivity. In that captivity, God blessed them. They live for God and they serve God. And they came out of that captivity very wealthy. They had to leave homes behind to go back to Israel, their promised land. And so Ezra is talking to the king of Persia. And the king of Persia is offering him a military escort and everything else to go back. But Ezra says this, “I was ashamed to ask of the king a band of soldiers to help us against the enemy in the journey. I was ashamed to go for government for help. Is that getting into your cranial vacuum? I was embarrassed to go to government and ask for help for protection, food, clothing, so forth. Because we had told the king, ‘The hand of our God is upon all for good that seek him.’” Did you hear that? He had went to the king and said, “Listen, the hand of God, he had been preaching the gospel, is for good on all that seek him.” Is protection good? Is having a job good? Yeah. Having clothes good? Having a place to live good? Yes. Having children under control, is that good? Yeah. Having a day for recreation to watch the Super Bowl, is that good? Yes. That’s good. But his power and wrath is against all that forsake him, all that turn their back on him, renounce him. You know, they don’t verbally do it always. They can just neglect God’s word, neglect God, neglect prayer. Are you there? Neglect the house of God. They turn their back. And some can denounce and say, “Oh, you know, I don’t have to do this.” And they can verbally say that, but most of us just turn our back. See, his power and wrath is against those. Now, folks, this is two ultimatums. Are you listening to me? An ultimatum is a proclamation that something, there’s a penalty if something isn’t done. There’s a punishment if something isn’t done. And Ezra has given an ultimatum to the king. Are you there? He’s telling, “King, you’re going to lose your nation if you don’t turn to God.” And he did. The Persian Empire went down. Because when you forsake God, in the end, God’s going to come and deal with you. Amen.
What does Ezra’s ultimatum to the king of Persia teach?

Ezra 8:22: For I was ashamed to request of the king an escort of soldiers and horsemen to help us against the enemy on the road, because we had spoken to the king, saying, “The hand of our God is upon all those for good who seek Him, but His power and His wrath are against all those who forsake Him.”
What is Ezra’s proclamation to God, and how does it apply to us?

He says Ezra was effectively telling God that we are seekers and followers of you and you must do us good, and he calls this faith exercised. He says we must first give ourselves to righteousness and accept correction before we ask God to keep his promises.
What is Ezra’s proclamation to God, and how does it apply to us?

But listen to this. Watch this. He’s also making an ultimate proclamation to God himself. And what he’s saying is, God, we’re seekers of you. We’re followers of you. And you must do us good. Are you there? Now this is faith exercised. God, you promised to protect my home. You promised to give me a job and, and provisions for my home. You promised to give me health and a strong mind and all. God, you’ve got to produce. This king of Persia needs to see you are God. These people in Persia needs to see you are God. And we need to see you are God. Hallelujah. Now, isn’t that powerful? He didn’t go up there wimpy. Well, you know, uh, no. He made an ultimatum, an ultimate proclamation. We have set our lives apart to follow you, to seek you, to serve you, and you’ve got to back up your word and bless us with God. Wow. Didn’t God say he would give us the nations for our inheritance? Didn’t Jesus say, “Look on the harvest. They are ripe for the harvest. The fields are ripe for the harvest.” God, we are going to [unclear] with the word. You got to show you are God and back up your word by pricking their hearts and changing their thinkings and saving them and, and, and changing these families. Could that be an amen? See, of the works of my hand command you me. Not that we can go, God, do a miracle here and, you know, snap. No, this is the attitude of that. I gave you promises. Demand that I keep them. But you first got to what? Give yourself to righteousness. You got to accept correction. You’re not going to have much authority in this statement if you don’t let God deal with you and correct you.
What is Ezra’s proclamation to God, and how does it apply to us?
Isaiah 45:11: Thus says the LORD, The Holy One of Israel, and his Maker: “Ask Me of things to come concerning My sons; And concerning the work of My hands, you command Me.
What attitude toward correction does God bless?

He says that when you say you will accept God’s correction, discipline and verbal correction, then God starts blessing, progressively, not overnight like popcorn. He says people around you may copy the change or get mad at you, and either way you are great.
What attitude toward correction does God bless?

Come on, God. Correct me. Bring it on. But you go to God without an attitude of righteousness and correction and pray that, and he’s just going to go, “Who are you?” But when you say, “God, I’ll accept your correction. I’ll accept your discipline. I’ll accept your verbal correction. I’ll accept God. Just bless my life with good.” And that’s the attitude. Then he starts blessing. And it isn’t popcorn where it’s overnight. It’s progressive. Hallelujah. And then you see a change in you. Or no, you don’t see it at first. People do. And then you see a pe... a change in the people that are around you, because they saw a change in you and liked it and so they copied it, or they get mad at you and start just lambasting you up and down.
What does Proverbs 13:24 teach about prompt correction?

He says God corrects out of love, first verbally, and third by punishment, and reads Proverbs 13:24 that he who loves his child disciplines him promptly. He says God wants to correct us now because he wants to bless our life now, and reads Proverbs 19:18.
What does Proverbs 13:24 teach about prompt correction?

Either way, you’re great. If they’re changing, you’re great. If they hate you for being righteous, you’re still great according to the sermon on the mount. Ain’t that right? Recognize that God corrects us out of love because he loves us. And that first correction is verbal. You just got it this morning. How many will raise your hand to Jesus and said, “Lord, I got some things in my life I need correcting.” Yes. And that’s all he’s looking for is a good, honest heart. The verbal correction is the way to go. And then the third is punishment. Proverbs 13:24, “He who spares his rod hates his son, but he who loves his child disciplines him promptly.” Now, switching that back to God, will God want to correct us promptly, or does he want to do it three years from now? No, he wants to do it now. Why? Because he wants to bless your life now. Proverbs 19:18, “Correct your son while there is hope, and let not your soul spare for his crying.” They look at you with those beautiful eyes, and mommy, don’t give in.
What does Proverbs 13:24 teach about prompt correction?
Proverbs 13:24: He who spares his rod hates his son, But he who loves him disciplines him promptly. Proverbs 19:18: Chasten your son while there is hope, And do not set your heart on his destruction.
What does he say about how many Christians read their Bible?
He says “only 15%, 15% of Christians read their word,” calls that sad, and says the Bible is the foundation of correction.
How does he say you can know whether preachers are preaching the right thing?
He asks how you know preachers are preaching the right thing if you do not get to the book and find out for yourself.
Can you have miracles and not be righteous?
He says “You can have miracles and not be righteous,” and that Daniel had prayers, visions and miracles, but it was his righteousness that would save him.
What does he say saved Noah, Daniel and Job?
He says it was not the ark, not Noah’s faith, and not the prosperity of Job and Daniel that would save them; it was their righteousness.
What does he say about trusting in armaments?
He says some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we will remember the name of the Lord our God, and that “we got to have arms, but let me tell you, we got to have God.”
What does he say it means to discern the Lord’s body?
He says believers are the body of Christ, whose body died for our sins, and that some are weak, sick or dead before their time because they did not discern the Lord’s body.

He says no chastening seems joyous for the present, and he did not enjoy disciplining his kids and they were not glad about it either. He says afterward it yields the peaceable fruit of righteousness to those trained by it.
What does he say about psychologists and straightening out the home?
He says we go to psychologists and psychiatry and spend 50 bucks for a half hour to straighten out our home, when we just need to go to the Bible and get our life straightened out.
What does he say peaceable fruit of righteousness means?
He says peaceable means lack of war, lack of opposition, and that righteousness produces that peaceable fruit.
What does he say it looks like to forsake God?
He says people do not always forsake God verbally; they can neglect God’s word, neglect God, neglect prayer and neglect the house of God, and most of us just turn our back.
What does he say an ultimatum is?
He says an ultimatum is a proclamation that there is a penalty or punishment if something is not done, and that Ezra gave one to the king.
Does God bless right away when we accept correction?
He says it is not like popcorn where it happens overnight; it is progressive, and others may notice the change before you do.
Why does he say God wants to correct us now rather than later?
He asks whether God wants to correct us promptly or three years from now and answers “No, he wants to do it now. Why? Because he wants to bless your life now.”

items.d: In Part IV of “God’s Magnifical House,” Pastor David G. Kincer says the church must be built by the Bible pattern so the fame and glory of Jesus fill the nations, and that every believer is invited to be a…
p: In Part IV of “God’s Magnifical House,” Pastor David G. Kincer says the church must be built by the Bible pattern so the fame and glory of Jesus fill the nations, and that every believer is invited to be a priest. He gives four responsibilities of a priest from Deuteronomy 10:8, Numbers 16:9 and Hebrews 9, and says that through the blood of Jesus every believer can enter the holy of holies, minister to the Lord, hear his voice and have the Scriptures opened.
What does “the Lord’s house shall be exceedingly magnifical” mean?

He reads 1 Chronicles 22:5 that the Lord’s house would be magnifical, of fame and of glory throughout all countries, at a time when people did not know about other continents but God did. He says the fame was fulfilled in Luke 5:15, when great multitudes came to hear Jesus and be healed.
What does “the Lord’s house shall be exceedingly magnifical” mean?

We’re going to be talking about the magnifical church this morning and just a brief review. First Chronicles 22:5. The Lord’s house shall be exceedingly magnifical. Of fame. And of glory throughout all countries all nations. Now you’ve got to remember at this time they didn’t know there was nations in South America South Africa North America. They didn’t know that as human beings God did and God had a big plan way back there. The fame was fulfilled we saw in Luke chapter 5 verse 15 so much the more went there a fame abroad of Jesus great multitudes came together to hear him and to be healed of their infirmities they came to hear his word not just for a miracle not everybody needs a healing but they need to hear the word and so we see it fulfilled then we must remember.
What does “the Lord’s house shall be exceedingly magnifical” mean?

1 Chronicles 22:5: Now David said, “Solomon my son is young and inexperienced, and the house to be built for the LORD must be exceedingly magnificent, famous and glorious throughout all countries. I will now make preparation for it.” So David made abundant preparations before his death. Luke 5:15: However, the report went around concerning Him all the more; and great multitudes came together to hear, and to be healed by Him of their infirmities.
Must the church be built by the Bible pattern?

He says David gave Solomon the pattern by the Spirit, and “we cannot build the church our own way we’ve got to follow the Bible pattern.” He says the apostles turned their known world upside down, and Haggai 2:9 says the glory of the latter house shall be greater than the former.
Must the church be built by the Bible pattern?

And First Chronicles 28:11 David gave to Solomon the pattern of all he had by the spirit we cannot build the church our own way we’ve got to follow the Bible pattern and if we follow the Bible pattern then the fame will go to all nations Acts 17:6 these that have turned the world upside down are come here. Speaking of the apostles. Who went out preaching to the known world at that time the known world these like I said they didn’t know there was islands in the sea they didn’t know north and South America were around and they didn’t know anything about South Africa the southern part of africa and so they turned their known world upside down just like God said the glory and the fame would go to all countries now Haggai 2:9 says the glory of this latter house this last day house shall be greater than the former now if God through Jesus and the apostles could turn that world that known world upside down manifest his glory manifest his fame.
Must the church be built by the Bible pattern?

1 Chronicles 28:11: Then David gave his son Solomon the plans for the vestibule, its houses, its treasuries, its upper chambers, its inner chambers, and the place of the mercy seat; Acts 17:6: But when they did not find them, they dragged Jason and some brethren to the rulers of the city, crying out, “These who have turned the world upside down have come here too. Haggai 2:9: ‘The glory of this latter temple shall be greater than the former,’ says the LORD of hosts. ‘And in this place I will give peace,’ says the LORD of hosts.”
Is he looking for a rapture or for a move of God?

He says he is not looking for a rapture to get out of here but for a move of God that will stir the nations and show the fame of Jesus Christ. He says Numbers 14:21 promises all the earth will be filled with the glory of the Lord, which has not happened yet, and every jot and tittle will be fulfilled.
Is he looking for a rapture or for a move of God?

Haggai prophesied hundreds of years before that God’s going to do a greater thing in the last day church. So I don’t know about you but I’m not looking for a rapture to get out of here I’m looking for a move of God that’s going to stir the nations of the world and show his glory and the fame of Jesus Christ it says in Numbers 14:21 as truly as I live all the earth how much of the earth all the years shall be filled with the glory of the Lord I submit to you has that happened. If you know your history you know it hasn’t happened we know it happened in the book of acts to the known world. But we have not seen it. Filling every nation in the now known world hallelujah so that we have something very powerful to look forward to than just getting raptured out of this world could that be an amen. Is Jesus that big is his death burial and resurrection that powerful I submit to you it is and the Bible says every jot and tittle. Every little commandment will no wise pass from the law until all is fulfilled. Hallelujah so we got something great to look forward to Ephesians 5:27. Jesus gave himself for the church the Bible says that he might present the church to himself.
Is he looking for a rapture or for a move of God?

Numbers 14:21: but truly, as I live, all the earth shall be filled with the glory of the LORD— Matthew 5:18: For assuredly, I say to you, till heaven and earth pass away, one jot or one tittle will by no means pass from the law till all is fulfilled.
What kind of church is Jesus coming back for?

He reads Ephesians 5:27 and asks whether Jesus will present to himself a weak, divided, sickly, humanistic church or a glorious church, holy and without blemish. He says much of the church in America just goes along with public opinion, so we look forward to a powerful visitation of God.
What kind of church is Jesus coming back for?

Now who’s he coming back for when he comes the second time the church and he’s going to present it to himself a weak. Divided. Sickly. Humanistic church. Or a glorious church. See didn’t he say the church would be. Magnifical and fame and glory see and in Ephesians they picked up the same thing holy without blemish is the church in America holy and without blemish. No we’re legalizing sin because public opinion and public policy right now is everything’s okay the church just goes much of the church not all of it but much of the church just goes along with it and so we’ve got something to look forward to a powerful visitation of God fulfilling this prophetic word now.
What kind of church is Jesus coming back for?
Ephesians 5:27: that He might present her to Himself a glorious church, not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but that she should be holy and without blemish.

He says God invited all of Israel to be a kingdom of priests if they obeyed his voice, and Peter applies the same promise to the New Testament church. He says when you believe in Christ and follow Christ “you are a priest every one of us,” made kings and priests to reign on the earth.

God made a promise that all Israel would be priests to minister in this house that he was going to build. Exodus 19:5 if you obey my voice and keep my covenant that really helps when we obey and keep then when we obey and keep you shall be a special treasure to me above all people. For all the earth is mine and you shall be to me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. He’s inviting all of Israel to be priests to minister in his house. Everyone in Israel. Isn’t that beautiful. But. The same priestly promises to us of the New Testament. Peter quotes that verse in first Peter 2:9 you are a chosen generation a royal priesthood a holy nation of special people and said you when you believe in Christ and you accept Christ and follow Christ you are a priest every one of us. Revelations 5:10 Jesus has made us unto our God kings and what priests and we shall reign on the earth why are we so anxious to get raptured when he said we can rule and reign now. On the earth. Can he just write a book and he can’t back it up or can he back up the book he wrote I submit to you folks Jesus is a big powerful God and he can back up what he promised.

Exodus 19:5-6: Now therefore, if you will indeed obey My voice and keep My covenant, then you shall be a special treasure to Me above all people; for all the earth is Mine. And you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.’ These are the words which you shall speak to the children of Israel.” 1 Peter 2:9: But you are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, His own special people, that you may proclaim the praises of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light; Revelation 5:10: And have made us kings and priests to our God; And we shall reign on the earth.”
Why did God choose the tribe of Levi as priests?

He says after Aaron gave in to public opinion and Israel worshiped the golden calf, God separated the tribe of Levi, who stood for God when Moses asked who was on the Lord’s side. He says the church in America needs to draw a line and stand for Jesus no matter what the crowd does.
Why did God choose the tribe of Levi as priests?

Hallelujah so all of us in the new covenant in the New Testament are invited to be priests after making and worshiping a golden calf going back to Israel they were all given a promise to be priests then they worship the golden calf they made the thing. The leader Aaron gave in to the people gave in to public opinion and made a golden calf and they worshiped it and got their music out where playing music to it and everything else after that. Deuteronomy 10:18 at that time what time the making and worshiping of the golden calf the Lord separated the tribe of Levi to bear the ark of the covenant to stand before the Lord to minister unto him and to bless in his name God left the promise that all of Israel could be priests and he picked the tribe of Levi who stood up for God at that time remember Moses said who’s on the Lord’s side they draw the line and the tribe of Levi stood for God how many know the church in America needs to draw a line and say hey I’m standing for Jesus I don’t care what the crowd does I’m going to stand for Jesus so Levi now got the promise of the priesthood but you got to understand Israel had already rejected God’s presence once before they rejected him here and they rejected him before.
Why did God choose the tribe of Levi as priests?
Deuteronomy 10:8: At that time the LORD separated the tribe of Levi to bear the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to stand before the LORD to minister to Him and to bless in His name, to this day.
Why did Israel refuse to meet God at Mount Sinai, and why do people avoid Jesus today?

He says Israel stood afar off because they had worshiped idols all the way from Egypt and knew God would expose them. He says the same is true today from John 3:20: people make excuses about hypocrites, but the real reason is that touching Jesus and his word will expose them and they must repent and change.
Why did Israel refuse to meet God at Mount Sinai, and why do people avoid Jesus today?

Exodus 20:18 when all the people saw the thunderings, lightnings noise of the trumpet and the mountain smoking see God came on Mount Sinai with all these visual expressions. The people removed and stood afar off. And they said to Moses speak with us we will hear you go hear from God and come down and tell us but let not God speak with us least we die. See they already rejected God invited all of Israel to come up to the mountain to come into the presence of God with that smoke and that fire and that shaking and trembling. And they rejected it why do you think they said they would die do you ever you ever think about those things when you’re reading that book because. In Amos chapter 5 verse 25. Idols was why they did not go up to God’s presence these people were worshiping idols all the time the pillar of fire and the pillar of the cloud and the audible voice and the miracles were happening they were worshiping idols Amos tells us about it have you offered unto me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness 40 years o house of Israel but you have borne the tabernacle of Moloch and [unclear] your images the star of your God which you made to yourselves. And see they already had gotten the ten commandments. And it says the Lord thy God is one Lord thou shalt not make unto thee any graven images in heaven or in earth or in the sea or below the sea or whatever below the earth and they had these idols. They were worshiping all the way from Egypt. For 40 years in the wilderness and so they knew if they went up there God would expose them. And they would die do you understand that church. See they already rejected God then they made a calf that was two out of two or three witnesses let everything be established so now they are people that really don’t want to meet with God they want to come out of slavery and they want the land of promise of crops and fields and houses and everything else but they don’t want a personal encounter with God why because they knew God would expose them. And they didn’t want to be exposed same thing in the New Testament. John 3:20. Everyone practice in evil hates the light who’s the light Jesus and his word. See they hate the Bible and they hate Jesus because Jesus lived the Bible. And they won’t come to the light they won’t come to Jesus they won’t come to his word. Lest their deeds should be exposed. And they can attack the church and say well the church is a bunch of hypocrites filled with hypocrites and I don’t or I don’t want to go to church and be a hypocrite they got all these excuses but the real reason is if they really come in and touch Jesus Christ and they really touch that living word it’s going to expose them and they’ve got to repent and change that’s the reason.
Why did Israel refuse to meet God at Mount Sinai, and why do people avoid Jesus today?

Exodus 20:18-19: Now all the people witnessed the thunderings, the lightning flashes, the sound of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking; and when the people saw it, they trembled and stood afar off. Then they said to Moses, “You speak with us, and we will hear; but let not God speak with us, lest we die.” Amos 5:25-26: “Did you offer Me sacrifices and offerings In the wilderness forty years, O house of Israel? You also carried Sikkuth your king And Chiun, your idols, The star of your gods, Which you made for yourselves. John 3:20: For everyone practicing evil hates the light and does not come to the light, lest his deeds should be exposed.
Is worship music the same as meeting with God?

He says many believers would rather meet with music than meet with Jesus, and that music has power but having praise and worship does not mean we are meeting with God. He reads Ezekiel 44:10 that the Levites who went along with Israel’s idols could not come near as priests but became keepers of the house.
Is worship music the same as meeting with God?

Hallelujah. Right now a most American believers or a lot of them would rather meet with music than meet with Jesus and there’s a big difference. Music has power and you can go to a rock concert or any a country concert or whatever there is power in the air that that music affects you. And just because we got music and praise and worship in the church does not mean we’re meeting with God we could be meeting with music. Could that be true we must avoid following the crowd to do evil. Ezekiel 44 10 the Levites they’re the ones that God chose to be priests and they. Messed up. And here they messed up again. The Levites that went astray for me when Israel went astray after their idols they shall not come near to me to do the office of a priest unto me. Here God is rejecting the priest that he chose because. They accepted Israel serving God in a different way than God said we could serve him they weren’t following the pattern and the priest just went along with the people so God says they’re not going to be a priest. In an office unto me yet I will make them keepers of the house to serve the house and the people now. He’s not going to kill us.
Is worship music the same as meeting with God?

Ezekiel 44:10-11: “And the Levites who went far from Me, when Israel went astray, who strayed away from Me after their idols, they shall bear their iniquity. Yet they shall be ministers in My sanctuary, as gatekeepers of the house and ministers of the house; they shall slay the burnt offering and the sacrifice for the people, and they shall stand before them to minister to them.
What does it mean to minister to the Lord?

He gives Deuteronomy 10:8 as the first responsibility of a priest: to stand before the Lord to minister to him and to bless in his name. He says minister means to serve or wait on, like a waiter at a table, and bless means to kneel, to praise or brag about God, and to adore him.
What does it mean to minister to the Lord?

But how do you know you can have a very lean [unclear] when you don’t have meetings with God and meetings with the living word. Hallelujah. God’s magnifical house. Four responsibilities of the priest number one. Deuteronomy 10:8. They are to stand before the Lord to minister unto him minister unto him minister means to serve wait on like a waiter waiting on a table doing a slave waiting on his master doing what the master wants them to do ministering to the Lord and to bless and this word blessed has a three-fold. Understanding our application it means to kneel get down on your knees it means to praise brag about God. It would be nice if we bragged about Jesus and his word instead of ourself wouldn’t it we brag about ourselves so much and adore love him adore him it’s even [unclear] you know you have an infatuation you have an addiction. To Jesus Christ. All right and the kicker here is in his name now this is what separates us one of the things that separates us from the rest of the religions is we do things because Jesus said to do them we do it in his name. Are you hearing me you say we don’t get out a carpet and bow to the east three times a day because Jesus didn’t say to do that Muhammad said to do that we’re not followers of Muhammad we’re followers of Jesus.
What does it mean to minister to the Lord?
Deuteronomy 10:8: At that time the LORD separated the tribe of Levi to bear the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to stand before the LORD to minister to Him and to bless in His name, to this day.
Why do Christians lift their hands, dance and sing in Jesus’ name?

He says we kneel, lift our hands, rejoice, dance and sing praises because he said to do it, and we do it in his name. He says the house of God should be a place of joy, because there is nothing sad about Jesus dying on the cross and giving us eternal life.
Why do Christians lift their hands, dance and sing in Jesus’ name?

Amen so we do things in his name you see Psalm 63:4 thus I will bless there’s that word again kneel praise and adore you while I live it ain’t no good to wait till you’re dead. The Bible says the dead praise not the Lord. You got to do it now while you’re alive I will lift up my hands why. In thy name because you told me to lift my hand see so lifting my hands kneeling is what ministering unto him. Hallelujah. These humble little things Christians really trip over. Let’s continue. Psalms 89:16 in your name shall they rejoice the house of God should be a place of joy. Joy unspeakable and full of glory oh yeah. There is nothing sad about Jesus dying on the cross taking the shame taking the pain taking the blame for us and giving us eternal life and giving us a relationship with him that is just something to be excited about we are free. Amen. And we do it what in his name why he said to do it. Psalms 149:3 let them praise his name in the dance why do we dance before the Lord because he said to do it so we do it unto him as ministry and we do it because he Jesus said this is how you minister to me.
Why do Christians lift their hands, dance and sing in Jesus’ name?

Psalm 63:4: Thus I will bless You while I live; I will lift up my hands in Your name. Psalm 89:16: In Your name they rejoice all day long, And in Your righteousness they are exalted. Psalm 149:3: Let them praise His name with the dance; Let them sing praises to Him with the timbrel and harp. Psalm 9:2: I will be glad and rejoice in You; I will sing praise to Your name, O Most High.
How did the early church minister to the Lord in Acts 13?

He says in Acts 13 they ministered to the Lord and fasted, and the Holy Ghost spoke. He says we need to hear what the Spirit is saying to the church rather than copying a method from a book, and that it is not the songs you pick but the attitude you sing them in.
How did the early church minister to the Lord in Acts 13?

Are you out there. Psalms 9:2 I will sing. Praises bragging. Honoring to his name. Hallelujah. And you get songs that directly address Jesus and they’re very powerful he just touched God. Why because he said to do it and he said to do it in his name and when you have songs with his name in it it is really a double whammy now. How do we minister to God in the new covenant Acts 13:1-3 there were in the church certain apostles prophets teachers. And then he names them and as they minister to the Lord and fasted so fasting is part of what. Ministering to the Lord the Holy Ghost said boy that would be nice if we could hear what the spirit said to the church instead of what people are saying to the church doesn’t Revelation say several times he that hath the ear let him hear what the spirit says to the church yeah. It’s not some book you read you passing on information it’s not some tape or YouTube thing that you read wow it’s what the spirit is saying it’s what’s going to help you and that’s what’s going to help others are you there and what God is saying in one church because of the people that are there and their level would be entirely different than what God is saying to another church because again the level is different and the kind of people are different see you can have educated and babies. And you can have uneducated and mature. And to approach each one is a different approach. Are you hearing me but we try like the public schools to have one method for everybody. So God does something at some church and we read a book and we want to try. And it doesn’t work. Hallelujah we need to hear what the spirit’s saying. And so and to do that you’ve got to open up heaven by ministering unto him. You see and it’s really not the songs you pick for worship it’s the attitude that you sing them in. Are you singing them with expectation are you singing them as as Mike pointed out with the with the atmosphere of the song if it’s strong you sing strong.
How did the early church minister to the Lord in Acts 13?

Acts 13:1-3: Now in the church that was at Antioch there were certain prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon who was called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen who had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul. As they ministered to the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, “Now separate to Me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.” Then, having fasted and prayed, and laid hands on them, they sent them away. Revelation 2:7: “He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To him who overcomes I will give to eat from the tree of life, which is in the midst of the Paradise of God.” ’
Should laying on of hands be dramatic or theatrical?

He says praying is part of ministering to the Lord, and corporate prayer is more powerful than individual prayer. He says the apostles and Jesus never got theatrical; they just spoke and touched, and there is nothing wrong with simply touching someone on the shoulder and blessing them.
Should laying on of hands be dramatic or theatrical?

If it’s loving you sin you sing with an adoring spirit and attitude you see separate me Paul and Barnabas for the work we’re into I have called them when they fasted again and prayed so praying is what part of ministering to the Lord and you don’t have to wait to get to church to do that but the corporate prayer and the corporate ministering is more powerful than the individual at home and God’s designed it that way and he laid their hands on them and sent them away by the Holy Ghost and laid their hands on them and nowhere in the Bible do you find Jesus. In the name of the father now we get that from TV ministers. You know when we don’t have confidence we. We. Dramatize see when we don’t know we dramatize we get theatrical so we ooh or. Now all this theatrical you never find the apostles or Jesus doing that they just simply spoke and when they touched they just touched they didn’t have to you know somebody said well you got to get where the pain is well the woman’s got a pain in their breasts going what are you to do. Literally I’ve been in these circles. You know. And this. That’s all [unclear] and that other lady that’s what they promoted. That was that’s not a Bible thing. That that’s somebody that used a method and everybody copied it. Are you there. And as a young Christian I had to wade through this mess you know there’s people who don’t believe on laying on of hands because they see all the mess with it well. [unclear] said lay hands on and what’s wrong with reaching over and touching someone on their shoulder and just blessing them is there anything wrong with that you’re not bringing attention to yourself you’re not you know acting like you’re some superior it’s just obeying a principle that God honors and heals and imparts. Are you with me. Hallelujah. And they sent them away by the Holy Ghost it would be nice if ministers were sent out by the Holy Ghost instead of by seminars and Bible colleges and they’re out there just to make it a an occupation.
Should laying on of hands be dramatic or theatrical?

Acts 13:2-3: As they ministered to the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, “Now separate to Me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.” Then, having fasted and prayed, and laid hands on them, they sent them away.

He reads Hebrews 13:15-16 that we offer the sacrifice of praise continually, do good and communicate, which he says means to participate and partner with God’s church. He says women ministered to Jesus of their substance, and giving to the church to get the word out is part of ministering to the Lord.

Hebrews 13:15 by him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually how often continually you just keep praying you just keep praising you just keep doing what Jesus said to do you do it in his name. That is the fruit of our lips giving thanks to who his name. His name is above every name. Do good is there anything wrong with doing good. Is that a good ministry unto the Lord. Talking nice to your spouse and loving your kids and getting them educated and bringing them up in the way they should go that’s good stuff and that’s ministry under the Lord when you do good. And to communicate remember we told you that communicate is participate. It’s a partnership you you get involved with God’s church you get involved with the priestly ministry. For such with such sacrifices God as well as pleased Luke 8:3 many others ministered unto Jesus unto him of their substance you see do you ever figure out Jesus is out there sleeping on the ground wandering from town to town. How did he get his clothes washed. How did he take a bath. How did he eat. The women brought him food if women brought him. Drink. The women washed his clothes. Are you there. The women brought a pillow for his head instead of the rock. And people want to tell me women don’t have a place in the kingdom. Both accounts he’s talking about women ministering to Jesus. Hallelujah. Substance. Have you got to the place where you can really trust God with his 10 percent. See giving to Jesus giving to the church to get the word out and to help people grow in God is part of ministering to the Lord that’s why I tried to change the way we took an offering around here where we’re ministering to the Lord gosh.

Hebrews 13:15-16: Therefore by Him let us continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name. But do not forget to do good and to share, for with such sacrifices God is well pleased. Luke 8:3: and Joanna the wife of Chuza, Herod’s steward, and Susanna, and many others who provided for Him from their substance.

He says the second responsibility in Numbers 16:9 is to do the work of the tabernacle, cleaning, sweeping and financial accountability, and the third is to stand before the congregation to serve them. He says it is not all about you, and though some people are tough to deal with, God invites them all in.

That mentality will change how you do it and the attitude that you do it with okay. Second responsibility of a priest Numbers 16:9 is it a small thing to you that God that the God of Israel has separated you from the congregation of Israel to bring you near to himself. And number two see first the ministry now to do the work of the tabernacle. Do you realize these priests. And the people that came they had to have a bathroom. And somebody had to clean that bathroom.
