Financial accountability. Amen. Yeah and so there’s there’s. Taking care of the natural facilities and all of us are priests and all of us have that responsibility. Someone stopped me a couple of weeks ago and said you’re the pastor what are you doing out here working like this. Priests also take care of God’s house the natural part. Amen. If you know what a priest did it involves the natural part also. Okay. Third one Numbers 16:9 it is a small thing that God of Israel has separated you from the congregation to bring you near to himself to do the work of the tabernacle and number three to stand before the congregation to serve them. It’s not all about you. It’s also about the people that come in they need to be showed where the bathrooms are see they need to be told what to expect when they get to that altar and how that lamb is to be sacrificed they have to be instructed they have to be in order they have to be take a number who’s next yeah. Only one lamb could be sacrificed at a time on that altar are you there. And so you know they had to take care of the people when they come sick babies what are they going to do just say well you know it’s your problem no they had to have a first aid station had to take care of sick people sick babies whatever.
Do priests also take care of God’s house and the people who come?

Numbers 16:9: Is it a small thing to you that the God of Israel has separated you from the congregation of Israel, to bring you near to Himself, to do the work of the tabernacle of the LORD, and to stand before the congregation to serve them;
Can every believer enter the holy of holies?

He says only the high priest went into the holy of holies once a year, but Jesus is our high priest, entered once by his own blood, and the veil was torn from top to bottom. He says from Hebrews 10:19 that now we all can go in by the blood of Jesus, hear him speaking to us, have the Scriptures opened and see the change in our lives.
Can every believer enter the holy of holies?

And some of these people that come to God’s house are tough to deal with they are tough. But God invites them all in so what are you going to do is the priest. The fourth one Hebrews 9:7. Unto the second part of the temple went the high priest alone. Once every year. Not without blood which he offered for himself his own sins and for the sins of the people the mistakes of the people one time a year and I have the diagram of Solomon’s temple Moses’s tabernacle Herod’s temple they’re all the same you have the holy place and I don’t have anything there because I don’t want you focusing in on the holy place it’s a holy of holies once a year the priest you see these fancy clothes he wears. Those clothes every one of them has a meaning speaks of a truth speaks of a doctrine he would come in once a year. And there was the. Ark of the covenant with the mercy seat on top and the cloud of his presence visible presence of God at night a cloud turned to a fire. Visible. Audible. Presence of God in that holy place but only the high priest could go in not the other priests and he could only go in once a year. Now beside that ark of the covenant. Is a scroll with the scriptures God told Moses to put the scroll the scriptures beside the ark of the covenant and let me tell you folks there is nothing more illuminating. In the scriptures than reading it in the presence of God. That’s when you get illuminated Jesus Christ of course is our high priest for our sin Hebrews 9:11 Christ the high priest of good things to come by a greater and more perfect tabernacle. Not made with hands God is not interested in natural buildings he’s interested in living people. By his own blood he entered one time into the holy place. Having obtained. Eternal redemption for us he didn’t have to keep offering himself every year one time he gave us eternal redemption. Wow wow that is so powerful okay. Now. When Jesus died you see this little lightning bolt here. He rent the veil separating the holy place from the holy of holies he rented in two from top to bottom so that people knew it wasn’t a man or human that did it because this curtain was way up there they couldn’t reach it but when Jesus died God rent the curtain in two from top to bottom signifying that now not just the high priest can go in we all can go in. Now this is a powerful understanding. If you can catch it. Hebrews 10:19 having therefore for this reason brethren boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus by a new and living way so I can come in. To the presence of God hear his voice and see the result not just the cloud but I can see the fruit in my life I can see the fruit in your life you see. The visible results of the presence of God you see the change in the attitude you see the change in the talk how many you know we need that more than we need walking on water. And see this isn’t just for J.B. Fireball that’s the name I use for the mighty man of God full of faith and power the hour and everybody’s following him and whatever he says they do no. You can go in to Jesus Christ yourself in the holy of holies and hear him talking to you and have the scriptures. Open to you. Yeah give God a clap offering that’s powerful. But we have been so brainwashed that we look for some superwoman or some superman to lead us and guide us and hand walk us and feed us and give us a bottle and you know psychoanalyze our emotional levels and whatever when we have been invited in as priests to come into Jesus by the blood of Jesus and by his blood alone. And there he will speak to us and he will change us and we will see the change.
Can every believer enter the holy of holies?

Hebrews 9:7: But into the second part the high priest went alone once a year, not without blood, which he offered for himself and for the people’s sins committed in ignorance; Hebrews 9:11-12: But Christ came as High Priest of the good things to come, with the greater and more perfect tabernacle not made with hands, that is, not of this creation. Not with the blood of goats and calves, but with His own blood He entered the Most Holy Place once for all, having obtained eternal redemption. Hebrews 10:19: Therefore, brethren, having boldness to enter the Holiest by the blood of Jesus,
Can a priest or minister forgive sins?

He says we do not go into the holy of holies to redeem sin, because nobody can forgive sin but Jesus Christ, no matter what mighty man of God you follow. He says we go in to minister directly to him, hear his voice and have the Scriptures opened in his presence.
Can a priest or minister forgive sins?

Hallelujah very powerful. So ministering into him really becomes important lifting your hands singing praying kneeling doing these things is what he asked us to do to come into his presence that’s the protocol see it’s humbling. Now we don’t go into the holy of holies to redeem sin. Nobody can forgive sin but who Jesus Christ I don’t care what kind of mighty man of God you’re following he can do nothing for you let me tell you only Jesus can do anything. And he does them through ministries and he does them through the goofiest ministries because he loves people but it’s Jesus that does this stuff we can go into the holy of holies not to forgive sins the Catholics are all wrong that priest cannot absolve you from sin only Jesus can. Yeah I have to call it like it is I love the Catholics I love the people but let me tell you you can’t violate God’s word you’ve got to build it by the pattern you got to go to Jesus he is the only one on that has authority to forgive sin on earth that’s what the Bible says. I mean we can forgive other people’s offenses toward us but he can wash the sin away deliver you from that sin set you free and give you life. Not to redeem sins but to minister directly unto him hear his voice and have the scriptures open to us in his presence remember. The scroll of the scriptures was right beside the ark and the Bible says spiritual things are revealed by the spirit if you really want to get the word opened up to you come into his presence. Open that book and he will open your understanding he’ll speak to you in a still small voice.
Did the apostles fulfill the fame of God’s house?
He says the apostles turned their known world upside down, but they did not know about North and South America or the southern part of Africa, so the glory has not yet filled every nation.
Has the whole earth been filled with the glory of the Lord yet?
He says if you know your history it has not happened; it happened in the book of Acts to the known world, but we have not seen it fill every nation, so we have something powerful to look forward to.
Is the church in America holy and without blemish?
He says no, because public opinion and public policy say everything is okay and much of the church, not all of it, just goes along with it.
Why did Israel say they would die if God spoke to them?

He says Amos shows they carried idols for forty years in the wilderness, so they knew that if they went up God would expose them; they wanted the land of promise but not a personal encounter with God.
What does the word “bless” mean when priests bless the Lord?
He says it has a threefold meaning: to kneel, to praise or brag about God, and to adore him.
What does he say separates Christians from other religions?
He says we do things because Jesus said to do them and we do them in his name; we follow Jesus, not other religious founders.
Why does he say to praise God now while you are alive?
He says it is no good to wait till you’re dead, because the Bible says the dead praise not the Lord.
Does God say the same thing to every church?
He says what God is saying in one church would be entirely different from another because the people and their level are different, so we should not try one method for everybody.
How does he say ministers should be sent out?
He says it would be nice if ministers were sent out by the Holy Ghost instead of by seminars and Bible colleges, and not just to make it an occupation.
Do women have a place in the kingdom?
He says the women brought Jesus food and drink, washed his clothes and ministered to him of their substance, so he questions people who say women don’t have a place in the kingdom.
Is giving part of ministering to the Lord?
He says giving to Jesus and to the church to get the word out and help people grow is part of ministering to the Lord, and that mentality changes the attitude you give with.
What happened when the veil of the temple was torn?
He says when Jesus died God tore the curtain from top to bottom, too high for a man to reach, signifying that now not just the high priest but all of us can go in.
Where does he say the Scriptures are opened to us?

He says the scroll of the Scriptures was beside the ark, and if you really want the word opened to you, come into his presence, open the book and he will open your understanding in a still small voice.

items.d: In Part III of “God’s Magnifical House,” the speaker takes 1 Chronicles 22:5 and says the church must be built by God’s pattern. He says the glory came into the temple when the people praised God, that God’s…
p: In Part III of “God’s Magnifical House,” the speaker takes 1 Chronicles 22:5 and says the church must be built by God’s pattern. He says the glory came into the temple when the people praised God, that God’s house is now people as living stones, and that music, thanksgiving and participation are sacrifices to him. He closes with the power of the gospel over human intellect and the claim that miracles are for the church today.
What does 1 Chronicles 22:5 say the Lord’s house will be?

He reads that “the lord’s house shall be exceedingly” magnifical, “of fame and glory throughout all countries,” and recalls that earlier parts covered the fame of Jesus and the apostles. He says “miracles should be a normal part of the magnifical church,” pointing to Noah, the fiery furnace and Daniel.
What does 1 Chronicles 22:5 say the Lord’s house will be?

Follow in the Bible we’re going to 1 Chronicles 22:5. Now remember we talked about the fame and the honor of Jesus fulfilling this prophecy. We talked about the fame and the honor of the twelve apostles and the early church fulfilling this prophecy. It says the lord’s house shall be exceedingly magnifical. Of fame and glory throughout all countries throughout all countries not just the Jewish nation but every nation and I will therefore now make preparation for it we saw how miracles should be a normal part of the magnifical church. See God created everything out of nothing Enoch didn’t die miracles have been going on ever since God began creation Noah and seven others were saved from the flood with the animals the [unclear] swam in the Bible the fiery furnace didn’t burn the three Hebrew Hebrew children need the neither did the lions eat Daniel Jesus and his apostles did miracles and healings consistently.
What does 1 Chronicles 22:5 say the Lord’s house will be?

1 Chronicles 22:5: Now David said, “Solomon my son is young and inexperienced, and the house to be built for the LORD must be exceedingly magnificent, famous and glorious throughout all countries. I will now make preparation for it.” So David made abundant preparations before his death.
Why does he say the Bible can’t be reduced to the one word “faith”?

He says many Christians “have reduced the Bible to one word and that word is faith,” but “we can’t reduce the Bible down to one word of faith it’s just part of God’s word.” He says believing without repenting, confessing and being water baptized is “something for nothing,” which he calls “a welfare mentality” that “cripples the power of the Bible.”
Why does he say the Bible can’t be reduced to the one word “faith”?

We also found that it is built by foreigners aliens illegals or other words not so perfect individuals. [unclear] Being we’re not so perfect along with God’s chosen people. Now many Christians and denominations today. Have reduced the Bible to one word and that word is faith basically it is their faith but like the Muslims the Hindus the Confucius the Buddhas the animus and all the other religions. When we only have to believe and get all the rewards we’re getting something for nothing. When I don’t have to straighten my life out when I don’t have to repent when I don’t have to confess my sins and confess Jesus as God and Jesus is the savior and I don’t have to be water baptized.
Why must God’s house be built according to the pattern?

He says the temple “had to be built according to the pattern shown you on the mount,” and that David gave Solomon the pattern “by the spirit,” so “they couldn’t just do what they wanted to do.” He says “the magnifical house that God is building must be done his way.”
Why must God’s house be built according to the pattern?

What we’re saying is I’m getting something for nothing and that’s exactly what all the man-made religions offer something for nothing you just follow them and you’re in. We can’t reduce the Bible down to one word of faith it’s just part of God’s word. That’s a welfare mentality. When we want something for nothing and it cripples the power of the Bible. Now. This temple that God is talking about in first Chronicles had to be built according to the pattern shown you on the mount that’s Moses’s tabernacle and Solomon’s temple in 1 Chronicles 28:11 David gave to Solomon the pattern of all that he had by the spirit both Moses and tabernacle Solomon’s temple had to be built by the pattern that God gave they couldn’t just do what they wanted to do and we got to understand that.
Why must God’s house be built according to the pattern?

1 Chronicles 28:11-12: Then David gave his son Solomon the plans for the vestibule, its houses, its treasuries, its upper chambers, its inner chambers, and the place of the mercy seat; and the plans for all that he had by the Spirit, of the courts of the house of the LORD, of all the chambers all around, of the treasuries of the house of God, and of the treasuries for the dedicated things;
What does he say about the First Amendment and the Bible in early America?

He says the First Amendment bars Congress from setting up a religion or “prohibiting the free exercise thereof,” so “the church has a right to preach the gospel.” He says Congress “passed the law that the Bible would be printed,” sent Bibles to soldiers, and that “people are twisting the constitution to their own benefit.”
What does he say about the First Amendment and the Bible in early America?

The magnifical house that God is building must be done his way the Bible. Is twisted like our Constitution by people let’s look at the First Amendment of the Constitution all right Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion they can’t set up a religion. They can’t respect one religion over another neither. Can they make a law prohibiting the free exercise thereof. Or a bridge in the freedom of speech so not only as we as united states citizen have the right to speak freely. But the church has a right to preach the gospel. Now people say that this nation was not built on christianity. But let me just remind you. That Congress. It was Congress. That passed the law that the Bible would be printed. And suggested that it be taught in schools. It was Congress that decided to pass out ten thousand bibles to the soldiers in the revolutionary war they didn’t pass out ten thousand hindu books. Or any other religious books it was the Bible it was Congress that passed a law at the same time that said we’ve got to have chaplains for every two regiment it’s got to be a chaplain those chaplains were Methodists Quakers Presbyterians Baptists. They were Muslim Buddhists. Are you there church. See we’ve got to understand people are twisting the Constitution. To their own benefit and America’s destruction just like they twist the Bible. And we have got to wake up to these things. It was Congress and and the Bible wasn’t taken out of public school and prayer wasn’t taken out of public school when I was a boy we prayed in public school and we were taught scriptures in public school and we sang songs Christian songs in public school down south in Kentucky in the Appalachian mountains. The Bible and prayer wasn’t taken out until 1962.
What does he say happened in 1962, and what does he say about “separation of church and state”?

He says “up to 1962 the Bible was an accepted book,” and that then “congress made a new religion” of secular humanism and atheism, and that “they prohibited the Bible.” He says “the church is protected from government,” and that “when you repeat a lie enough people start believing it,” as people also twist the Bible.
What does he say happened in 1962, and what does he say about “separation of church and state”?

So up to 1962. The Bible was an accepted book. And remember lawyers in the beginning of our nation up into Abraham Lincoln they had to know the Bible to become a lawyer I don’t know if you’re aware of that. And so these people that say that you know it wasn’t founded on the Bible it wasn’t founded on christianity they’re lying to you these people are lying to you. Now in 1962 Congress. Made a new religion they recognized and respected a new religion and that religion was the religion of secular humanism. And the religion of atheism the Supreme Court back then said that atheism was a religion. And the humanists say they have the new religion of secular humanism and our government which is not supposed to identify any religion they respected the atheists and the humanists and in doing so they prohibited the Bible. And those who followed the Bible. In America they threw out Jesus and the Bible do you understand that. They violated this Constitution but what did they do they twisted it they started in about 1948 twisting it and saying separation of church and state separation of church and state we got to be a government’s got to be protected from the church no it’s the opposite the church is protected from government. That’s the truth but see when you repeat a lie enough people start believing it and just like they twist the Constitution people are twisting the Bible around and we don’t have magnificent churches anymore as the prophecy said last week you go to one church and it’s different than the next church every church is different when we should be like the Toyota car when you buy it in China or you buy it in Africa or where you buy it in America it’s the same product.
What happened in 2 Chronicles 5:13 when the musicians praised God?

He says they had built the temple with the door, altar, laver, lampstand, table and ark, “but nothing had happened” until “they started praising God with musical instruments.” He says then “the house of the Lord was filled with a cloud,” and “the glory of the Lord had filled the house.”
What happened in 2 Chronicles 5:13 when the musicians praised God?

Are you with me but we have got to get the vision for God’s way God’s pattern and do it his way whether we like it or not we got to change this thing 2 Chronicles 5:13. Now remember. The temple had a door which is Jesus it had an altar. Where the blood was shed for the cleansing of sin that’s the cross it had a labor water baptism it had a lampstand it had a table communion and it had alder of incense prayer and praise and it had a holy of holies where God dwelt. But they had built all this and they put everything together. The lampstand was there the communion table was there the altar of incense was there the ark of the covenant was there the mercy seat was there the temple was built beautiful everything was great they had a magnificent natural building but nothing had happened. Nothing spiritual had happened. Then we get the 2 Chronicles 5:13 it came to pass. As the musicians and singers were as one to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking the Lord you see it came to pass when this happened not the natural part of the building not the symbolic part of the building but when they started praising God with musical instruments. When they lifted little boys with the trumpets and the symbols and instruments of music and praise the Lord saying for he is good for his mercy endures forever then. Then. The house of the Lord was filled with a cloud so the priest could not stand to minister by reason of the cloud for the glory of the Lord had filled the house of God the presence of God came and filled the house of God and the ministers. Could minister anymore because God himself was ministering. And that really intimidates a lot of ministers and a lot of song leaders. When God shows up. It intimidates them it threatens them because they got to do their show you know they got to put on their their finest.
What happened in 2 Chronicles 5:13 when the musicians praised God?

2 Chronicles 5:13-14: indeed it came to pass, when the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking the LORD, and when they lifted up their voice with the trumpets and cymbals and instruments of music, and praised the LORD, saying: “For He is good, For His mercy endures forever,” that the house, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud, so that the priests could not continue ministering because of the cloud; for the glory of the LORD filled the house of God.
Why does he say ministers must step aside when God shows up?

He says that when God filled the temple “the priest could not stand to minister” and “God himself was ministering,” which “intimidates a lot of ministers and a lot of song leaders” and “ministers won’t step aside for God to touch people today.” He says “you can build crystal cathedrals… but that thing is nothing until God shows up.”
Why does he say ministers must step aside when God shows up?

Presentation but when God comes up we don’t need you my friend. And ministers won’t step aside for God to touch people today. But the key here they had everything the door the labor the water baptism Jesus is the way the truth and the life the door they had everything in the tabernacle but the glory but the presence and when they begin to praise and sing and minister unto him then God came and filled the temple. And the ministers had to step aside. Hallelujah. Now folks that’s when it became a magnifical house when the magnifical one came. You can have nice furnishings all you want you can build crystal cathedrals and all kinds of fancy buildings but that thing is nothing until God shows up he’s the magnificent one of the magnificent house.
Is God’s house a building or people? (Romans 15:4, Acts 17:24, Hebrews 3:6, 1 Peter 2:5)

He says the tabernacle “built and written about so we could learn from it,” and that God “does not dwell in temples made with hands.” He says “we are the house of God we are the temple of God… human beings not mortar but people,” and “living stones” in “spiritual house.”
Is God’s house a building or people? (Romans 15:4, Acts 17:24, Hebrews 3:6, 1 Peter 2:5)

Hallelujah. Very powerful. After. Following the pattern God came including. Praise and worship unto him. Romans 15:4 says things written the fourth time were written for our learning who’s learning hours. This tabernacle was built and written about so we could learn from it. First Corinthians 10:11 these things happen to them as examples. And they were written for our admonition upon whom the ends of the ages have come are we in the end of the ages yeah acts tells us we’re in the end of the last days we’re in the last days we’ve been in the last days since that day. So we got to learn God’s magnifical house. In Acts 17:24 is not a natural building at all. God as the scriptures say does not dwell in temples made with hands he’s quoting out of Isaiah. God never intended to dwell in a man-made building. Do you understand that. When he did this in Solomon’s temple he never intended. For that to be his dwelling place or Moses’s tabernacle. In Hebrews 3:6 Christ the son over his own house whose house are who we are the house of God we are the temple of God that’s what God was trying to teach us how to be a magnifical house of God human beings not mortar but people that’s all we see in first Peter 2:5 you as living stones are built up a what spiritual house a spiritual temple God is interested in people and he wants us to be magnifical.
Is God’s house a building or people? (Romans 15:4, Acts 17:24, Hebrews 3:6, 1 Peter 2:5)

Romans 15:4: For whatever things were written before were written for our learning, that we through the patience and comfort of the Scriptures might have hope. 1 Corinthians 10:11: Now all these things happened to them as examples, and they were written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the ages have come. Acts 17:24: God, who made the world and everything in it, since He is Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in temples made with hands. Hebrews 3:6: but Christ as a Son over His own house, whose house we are if we hold fast the confidence and the rejoicing of the hope firm to the end. 1 Peter 2:5: you also, as living stones, are being built up a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
What does “magnifical” mean, and why can’t the church do anything without Jesus?

He says “magnifica means excellence superior,” and the church is “supposed to be superior to every man-made ideal.” He says quoting Jesus that apart from him you can do nothing, and that “without Jesus folks we can’t do anything,” and a church isn’t built on a good worship leader, team or speaker: “Jesus is more important than the pastor… than anything.”
What does “magnifical” mean, and why can’t the church do anything without Jesus?

Magnifica means excellence superior. The church is supposed to be superior to every man-made ideal in this world. John chapter 15 verse 5 I am the vine you are the branches. If you abide in me and I abide in you. You’ll bear much fruit for without me you can do what. Nothing. You think a church is built on a good worship leader or a good worship team or a good orator. The church isn’t built on that without Jesus folks we can’t do anything. We need his glory to come and it comes when he comes it doesn’t come because you believe it came it can’t comes because it comes and you know it. Hallelujah. See Jesus is more important than the pastor than the youth leader then the church secretary then the clerk. He’s more important than anything. And without him we’re not going to excel and that’s what it says back there the glory of the Lord filled the house Jesus filled the house John 7:38 he that believes on me out of his belly shall flow rivers of life-giving water this [unclear] of the Holy Spirit which they that believe on him should receive. Same statement in John 3:16 he that believes on me shall not perish but have everlasting life same statement he that believes on me out of his belly shall flow the spirit of God the presence of God out of our innermost being so we are the temple as an individual as well as corporate. But if we don’t allow Jesus to show up we don’t allow Jesus to express himself and fill our being. We miss out on his glory. First Corinthians 6:9 your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost. Now who’s the Holy Ghost. God Jesus they’re all the same God the father God the son God the Holy Spirit it’s all God how many gods are there in christianity. One God okay. He manifested himself in that fleshly body called Jesus and you’ll see that flesh of the body when you go to heaven but it’s still God the Holy Spirit is God John 17:3 this is eternal life now everybody thinks that eternal life is just living forever but Jesus describes and gives us another definition of eternal life this is eternal life that they may what no you the only true God and Jesus Christ whom you have sent now this word no is used in the Bible as a sexual relationship all through the Bible Joseph did not know mary till after Jesus was born he didn’t have sex with mary to after Jesus was born and we are to have an intimate relationship with God he is to live in a it’s a real thing it’s not just head knowledge.

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Isaiah 29 and 30 about God punishing His people and their opponents, and says believers must confront opposition to the Bible, drawing examples from Moses…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Isaiah 29 and 30 about God punishing His people and their opponents, and says believers must confront opposition to the Bible, drawing examples from Moses, Joshua, Daniel, Jesus and Paul and from church history and the Humanist Manifesto. He closes with God’s promise “in that day” to rebels who repent: He opens ears and eyes, answers their cry, and says “weep no more.”
What does Isaiah 29 say about God punishing His people and their opponents, and honoring Him with lips only? (Isaiah 29:1-13)

He says Isaiah 29 gives “a word about God punishing the city of God, the people of God, Jerusalem, and her opponents,” both those God used to correct His people and those who just oppose God and His people. He says those who fight God and His church are like a man who dreams he eats but wakes up still hungry, and that we can say we are believers while “the heart, the mind, the will, our actions, our attitude is removed far from God.”
What does Isaiah 29 say about God punishing His people and their opponents, and honoring Him with lips only? (Isaiah 29:1-13)

Okay, in Isaiah 29:1-17 we find God, through Isaiah, giving a word about God punishing the city of God, the people of God, Jerusalem, and her opponents: those that God used to correct his people, and those that just oppose God and his people. It says in verse one, “Woe to Ariel, the city where David dwelt.” That’s Jerusalem. Woe to Jerusalem, you will be brought down. He said in verse 7, “The multitude of the nations that fight against Jerusalem, Ariel, shall be as a dream of a night.” When a man dreams and he’s hungry and he eats, he’s thirsty and he drinks, but he wakes up, he’s still hungry and he’s still thirsty. It’s just a dream. So people that think they can fight against God and his church, they’re just it’s just a dream. It says you will be punished by the Lord who fight against Mount Zion, the church. Isaiah 29:10, “The Lord has closed your eyes, and the eyes of the prophets, and the eyes of your rulers and the seers has he covered. The vision is like words of a sealed book delivered to one who’s learned, saying, ‘Read this,’ and he says, ‘I can’t read it because it’s sealed.’ Delivered to another that’s not learned, and he says, ‘I can’t read it because I’m not learned.’” For this reason the Lord says, “As the people draw nigh to me with their mouth and their lips do honor me, but they have removed their heart far from me.” You see, yeah, we say we’re believers, yeah, we say we’re Christians, but the heart, the mind, the will, our actions, our attitude is removed far from God. “Their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men.” You see, and do we have that today, where we just teach our own doctrines, man-made doctrines, much like the Constitution of America’s interpreted for their own personal gain, so is the Bible in a generation we live in. it’s just And when people use the word “interpret,” watch out, because the Bible doesn’t need to be interpreted. The Bible interprets itself. It explains itself. You don’t have to psychoanalyze it.

Isaiah 29:1-10: “Woe to Ariel, to Ariel, the city where David dwelt! Add year to year; Let feasts come around. Yet I will distress Ariel; There shall be heaviness and sorrow, And it shall be to Me as Ariel. You shall be brought down, You shall speak out of the ground; Your speech shall be low, out of the dust; Your voice shall be like a medium’s, out of the ground; And your speech shall whisper out of the dust. “Moreover the multitude of your foes Shall be like fine dust, And the multitude of the terrible ones Like chaff that passes away; Yes, it shall be in an instant, suddenly. You will be punished by the LORD of hosts With thunder and earthquake and great noise, With storm and tempest And the flame of devouring fire. The multitude of all the nations who fight against Ariel, Even all who fight against her and her fortress, And distress her, Shall be as a dream of a night vision. It shall even be as when a hungry man dreams, And look—he eats; But he awakes, and his soul is still empty; Or as when a thirsty man dreams, And look—he drinks; But he awakes, and indeed he is faint, And his soul still craves: So the multitude of all the nations shall be, Who fight against Mount Zion.” Pause and wonder! Blind yourselves and be blind! They are drunk, but not with wine; They stagger, but not with intoxicating drink. For the LORD has poured out on you The spirit of deep sleep, And has closed your eyes, namely, the prophets; And He has covered your heads, namely, the seers. Isaiah 29:13: Therefore the Lord said: “Inasmuch as these people draw near with their mouths And honor Me with their lips, But have removed their hearts far from Me, And their fear toward Me is taught by the commandment of men,

People say, “If there is a God, why he allow this wars and all this stuff in the earth?” It’s not him allowing it, it’s us. We’re not dealing with evil people like God told us to. It’s our fault. Now, God punishing the city of God and her opponents. her

Isaiah 29:14: Therefore, behold, I will again do a marvelous work Among this people, A marvelous work and a wonder; For the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, And the understanding of their prudent men shall be hidden.”
Is there a time to confront civil leaders? What did Moses do with Pharaoh? (Exodus 7-14)

He says “there is a time for confronting civil opponents” and gives Moses as the example: Moses did not just bring the people out of Egypt, he confronted Pharaoh, his sorcerers, his parliament and the religion of that day, saying “Let my people go.” He says Moses confronted the military, the civil government and the religious leaders of Egypt.
Is there a time to confront civil leaders? What did Moses do with Pharaoh? (Exodus 7-14)

Opponents. There is a time for confronting civil opponents, civil laws, and their army or their police department or whatever backs up the authority that backs it up. There is a time. For instance, Moses, when he went down to get the people of God out of Egypt, did he just go down and bring them out, or did he go to Pharaoh and confront Pharaoh? He confronted him. See, he dealt with Pharaoh. He said, “Let my people go.” So Pharaoh called his wise men, you know, his sorcerers and all that, together, and you know Moses threw down his rod to show the power of God, and then the sorcerers threw down their rod and it became a snake. Now, those sorcerers were not turning rods into snakes until Moses came down and God allowed it to happen. And Moses’s snake swallowed up the rest of the snakes. You see, they didn’t need more snakes, they needed to get rid of the snake that God caused to appear. And so the sorcerers, they turned the water also, like Moses did, to blood. Well, they were down there turning the water to blood before Moses came down. See, Moses was confronting Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, and his parliament. Here what they didn’t need: they didn’t need more blood. They needed the water that was turned to blood back to water, but they couldn’t do that because God didn’t allow them to. They only could bring more disaster. So when the frogs came along, “Yeah, we can do that.” Well, they didn’t need more frogs, they needed to get rid of the frogs that Moses brought up by the power of God, amen. So Moses was dealing with the king, of Pharaoh, and his his congress, his parliament, and the religion of that day, and just totally bringing it to an embarrassment, are you there, until Pharaoh finally said, “Let them go.” God brought 10 judgments, actually 11. I know your Bible says 10, but the Bible left out one. When they crossed the Red Sea and the Red Sea closed up on them, that was the last judgment. Pharaoh’s army was destroyed. See, Moses confronted the military might of Egypt, the civil government of Egypt, and the religious leaders of Egypt.

We don’t want to hear Bible things, we want to hear men’s philosophies. “Speak to us smooth things,” easy things, don’t rock the boat, bud, and we’ll get a new preacher. “Prophesy what deceits.” Prophesy deception. And when people say that homosexuals were born that way, they are, what, deceiving the homosexual. “Cause the Holy One of Israel to cease from before us.” We don’t want no presence of God to come, we just want a little church service, make ourselves feel good and go home. Chapter 30:2, “Because you have rejected this message,” what message? The law of the Lord and right things. “You’ve relied on oppression and dependent on deceit.” That’s what we said down here. That’s what he said, you want people to teach you lies, teach you deceits. Verse 15, “In repentance and rest you shall be saved.” So what’s the message? Repent. Feel bad about being your sins, feel bad about disobeying God’s word, and turn from disobeying God’s word to doing right, and rest. Jesus said what? “Come unto me, all you that labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.” See, we got to come to Jesus. There’s three things we have to unite around. That the Bible is God’s word and it’s the authority. Could you raise your hand, say “I believe that”? Yeah. Our opinions is nothing. The Bible. Secondly, Jesus, he’s not only God in the flesh, he is the Savior, he’s the only way to God and to eternal life. Could you raise your hand and say amen to that? Yeah. See, and then the third one is we are supposed to bring forth good fruit and live righteous. we Can you raise your hand to that? Yes, hallelujah. And repent as we’re growing in it. Don’t give up when you fail, get up.
Who are the rebellious people in Isaiah 30, and what is God’s message to them: repent and rest? (Isaiah 30:8-15)

Isaiah 30:8-11: Now go, write it before them on a tablet, And note it on a scroll, That it may be for time to come, Forever and ever: That this is a rebellious people, Lying children, Children who will not hear the law of the LORD; Who say to the seers, “Do not see,” And to the prophets, “Do not prophesy to us right things; Speak to us smooth things, prophesy deceits. Get out of the way, Turn aside from the path, Cause the Holy One of Israel To cease from before us.” Isaiah 30:15: For thus says the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel: “In returning and rest you shall be saved; In quietness and confidence shall be your strength.” But you would not, Matthew 11:28: Come to Me, all you who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
Will God answer the rebellious who cry to Him? (Isaiah 30:19-21)

He says that after putting them down, God gives “a powerful word”: “You rebels shall weep no more,” and “when he hears the cry he will answer.” He says all we have to do is say “Lord, I’ve been wrong, I need your help.” He says Satan says you are not worthy, but God sees a responsive heart and says “I’m going to lift you out of this mess.”
Will God answer the rebellious who cry to Him? (Isaiah 30:19-21)

So repentance and rest. Jesus, we got to come to Jesus. “In quietness and trust shall be your strength, but you would have none of it.” Because you’re a rebel, you want to do it your way. Okay, he’s showing them the message they rejected, he’s showing them how to get turned around, and he said you don’t want to even change. How many you met, people don’t want to change? They want to go to heaven but they don’t want to change. Yeah, I’ve done a lot of witness, I can’t believe it. Isaiah 30:19, “You rebels shall weep no more.” Here is, this this is God’s style with Isaiah: puts him down and then turns around and gives them a powerful word. You’re going to weep no more. “He will be very gracious to you at the sound of your cry.” If you just cry out to him for help, weep no more, here comes Jesus. Ain’t that beautiful? Powerful. When he hears the cry, he will answer you. All we got to do is say, “Lord, I’ve been wrong, I need your help,” and here comes Jesus on his white horse with his armor, charging in to take care of your problem. “Though the Lord gives you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, yet your teachers shall not be moved to a corner anymore, but your eyes shall see your teachers.” Though he corrects you, he’s only correcting you so you will get a ear to hear and eyes to see and be blessed by his promise of the inheritance that he promised you. Isn’t that beautiful? So see, Satan comes along and says you’re not worthy, and people will come along and say you’re not worthy, you’re a rebel, yeah, you’re a bad Christian, but God comes along and sees your responsive heart and says, “Hey, I’m going to lift you out of this mess. I’m going to change you and give you my blessings and my glory.” Isn’t that beautiful? Powerful. “Your ears will hear a word behind you saying, ‘This is the way, walk you in it.’” That’s his word to the rebels. “This is the way, walk you in it.”
Will God answer the rebellious who cry to Him? (Isaiah 30:19-21)

Isaiah 30:19-21: For the people shall dwell in Zion at Jerusalem; You shall weep no more. He will be very gracious to you at the sound of your cry; When He hears it, He will answer you. And though the Lord gives you The bread of adversity and the water of affliction, Yet your teachers will not be moved into a corner anymore, But your eyes shall see your teachers. Your ears shall hear a word behind you, saying, “This is the way, walk in it,” Whenever you turn to the right hand Or whenever you turn to the left.
What is rebellion, and how does he say Christians should stand up? (1 Samuel 15:23)

He says “the Bible says that rebellion is the sin of witchcraft,” and that rebellion is “ignoring the laws of God, doing your own thing instead of what God said to do.” He says if we cry out and admit we are wrong, God will open our eyes and ears. He says we must stand up for the Bible, for Jesus and for righteousness and Bible morality, and not let ourselves be shoved into a corner.
What is rebellion, and how does he say Christians should stand up? (1 Samuel 15:23)

A rebel. The Bible says that rebellion is the sin of witchcraft, and if we think witchcraft is bad, then rebellion is bad. Rebellion is just ignoring the laws of God, doing your own thing instead of what God said to do, just rebelling against God’s word, God’s laws. And he says if you’ll just cry out to me, if you’ll just admit you’re wrong, weep no more. I will come, I will open your eyes, I’ll open your ears, you’ll hear your teachers, I’ll show you the way to walk in. All I’m waiting for is to hear from you. Now, folks, we’ve seen today that there’s an enemy in America and the world trying to change God’s established family and God’s established church, and it’s called humanism. We’ve saw that we must confront these things for our children’s sake. As parents we’re responsible to make sure our children have a chance to grow up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord and not have their brain captured, yes, into the philosophies as of men. Ain’t that right? As Christians we’ve got to stand up for the Bible, for Jesus and for righteousness, Bible morality. We’ve got to stand up. We can’t let him shove us into some corner. The Bible is just as an authentic book as any book they bring out, more authentic, by the way. We got to stand up for it.
What is rebellion, and how does he say Christians should stand up? (1 Samuel 15:23)

1 Samuel 15:23: For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, And stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. Because you have rejected the word of the LORD, He also has rejected you from being king.” Ephesians 6:4: And you, fathers, do not provoke your children to wrath, but bring them up in the training and admonition of the Lord.
What does God promise those who respond to His voice? (Isaiah 30:26-31)

He says God promises to bless us with food, clothing and shelter and health, to bind up the bruise of His people, and to fight our battles with us. He says we need to hear “what the Spirit is saying to the church in our day,” and the first thing He asks is to admit we are wrong, feel bad about it, and turn from it.
What does God promise those who respond to His voice? (Isaiah 30:26-31)

And the key to this promise to live holy and righteous before him all the days of our life is we need to get holy and righteous. Isaiah 30 says he’ll bless us financially. He wants to bless you financially with food, clothing and shelter, whether you drive a [unclear] God could care the least about, but he promised to give you health, he promised to give you food and shelter and clothing. Are you with me? That’s the promise to the rebel, the the rebellious. And he says in that day there that day, that day you respond, that day you cry, “the Lord will bind up the bruise of his people heal their wound.” “You shall have a song as in the night, and gladness of heart, to come to the mountain of the Lord,” that’s where God is, “to the Mighty One of Israel.” He’ll fight our battles with us. “The Lord will cause his glorious voice to be heard.” How many, you know, in Revelations it says, “He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the church.” We don’t mean need men’s doctrines, we need to hear what the Spirit is saying to the church in our day, our hour, for our family and our time. Could that be an amen? See, we need the Spirit. The Spirit’s what opens the scriptures up to us. “For through the voice of the Lord Assyria will be beaten down.” See, Assyria was the nation that God used to correct his people that that time. And what everything he’s using to correct you, the voice of the Lord will beat it down. And he’s just asking you to respond to his voice. The first thing he’s asking us to do is admit we’re wrong where we’re wrong, feel bad about being wrong and being rebellious against God and breaking his word, and turn from those wrongs. And out of Leviticus he says, “You shall be holy unto me, for I the Lord I have separated you from other people, that you should be mine.” I’ve separated you to be righteous. I’ve separated you to live right.
What does God promise those who respond to His voice? (Isaiah 30:26-31)

Isaiah 30:26: Moreover the light of the moon will be as the light of the sun, And the light of the sun will be sevenfold, As the light of seven days, In the day that the LORD binds up the bruise of His people And heals the stroke of their wound. Revelation 2:7: “He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To him who overcomes I will give to eat from the tree of life, which is in the midst of the Paradise of God.” ’ Leviticus 20:26: And you shall be holy to Me, for I the LORD am holy, and have separated you from the peoples, that you should be Mine.
Which chapters of Isaiah does he preach from?

He preaches from Isaiah 29:1-17 and 29:18-24 on God punishing His people and her opponents, and Isaiah 30 on God’s word to rebellious people. He says Isaiah is “always talking about punishing God’s people and then the next statement is… how glorious God’s going to move upon his people.”
Why does he say the Bible does not need to be interpreted?

He says that when people use the word “interpret,” “watch out, because the Bible doesn’t need to be interpreted. The Bible interprets itself.” He says it explains itself and “you don’t have to psychoanalyze it.”
Why does he say the sorcerers in Egypt were no help?

He says they “didn’t need more snakes,” more blood or more frogs; they needed to be rid of what God had caused. He says they could only “bring more disaster,” because God did not allow them to undo it.
How many judgments does he say God brought on Egypt?
He says it was actually 11, not 10: “when they crossed the Red Sea and the Red Sea closed up on them, that was the last judgment.” He says that is when Pharaoh’s army was destroyed.
Why does he say God had to wait for David to be king?

He says it was prophesied in Genesis that the king would come out of Judah, and that David was part Moabite, and “a Moabite could not come into the congregation until the 10th generation.” He says David “just happened to be the 10th generation.”
Why does he say Christians have been silent?

He says the church in America has been told for about 20-some years “to keep silent. Do your little thing just in your church, don’t get up in public, don’t say anything in public.” He says “there’s too many Christians silent” who have “been brainwashed into saying nothing.”
Does he say Christians keep repenting?

He says “we’re going to spend our life repenting, going from salvation to salvation, if we want to bring forth the fruit of the kingdom.” He says that making a mistake does not mean you have to stay down.
Why does he say we should know our opponents?
He says it is important to “know your opponents,” and that although God said He would punish the church’s opponents, we cannot “just sit back and go okay God lightning bolt or something.”
Can being in error keep God from visiting you?
He says “your error will not keep God from visiting you.” He says that as a young Christian he had to change many of his beliefs over time, “but God still loved me and kept building me.”
What does he say will happen to those who complain?
He says that in that day God will open your ears and eyes, and “those who complain will learn doctrine.” He says God says “I’m going to change you.”
What does he say about people who want to be told smooth things?

He says they do not want Bible things but men’s philosophies, “smooth things, easy things, don’t rock the boat.” He says they just want a little church service to feel good instead of the presence of God.
What three things does he say believers must unite around?

He lists that the Bible is God’s word and the authority, that Jesus is God in the flesh and the only way to God and eternal life, and that we are supposed to bring forth good fruit and live righteous.
What does “weep no more” mean in his message?
He says it is God’s answer when we cry out to Him for help: “when he hears the cry he will answer you.” He says all we have to do is say, “Lord, I’ve been wrong, I need your help.”
What does he say rebellion is?
He says “the Bible says that rebellion is the sin of witchcraft,” and that rebellion is “just ignoring the laws of God, doing your own thing instead of what God said to do.”
What does he say God promises to give us?
He says God promised to give us “food and shelter and clothing” and health, and that the kind of car you drive is not what concerns Him. He says the key is that we need to get holy and righteous.

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Isaiah 34 and Revelation 6 about God’s dealing with the Gentiles: the ungodly and secular humanists. He argues that the stars falling and the sun darkening…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Isaiah 34 and Revelation 6 about God’s dealing with the Gentiles: the ungodly and secular humanists. He argues that the stars falling and the sun darkening are not allegory, that Esau and the ten virgins show a door that closes, and that God’s purpose in judgment is to win the nations to Christ. He closes with two family stories to show how far parents go for their children, and says God wants even his opponents to live.
Who are the Gentiles in Isaiah 34, and what does God ask of them?

He says Isaiah 34 is “God’s word to the Gentiles,” meaning “the ungodly, the heathen, the nations, the people that don’t believe in Jesus.” He says God asks two things of them, “hear, number one, and heed, number two,” and that the church has the responsibility to speak because “without a preacher” they cannot hear.
Who are the Gentiles in Isaiah 34, and what does God ask of them?

In Isaiah 34, he’s going to directly deal with the Gentiles. This session is entitled “God’s Word to the Gentiles,” the ungodly, the heathen, the nations, the people that don’t believe in Jesus, don’t believe that the Bible is God’s word and truth, they don’t follow Jesus. So Isaiah 34:1, “Come near, you Gentiles,” this is how Isaiah starts out. Now, he’s been hitting the church pretty hard for the last 30 chapters, but now Isaiah has focused his attention on the unchurched, the ungodly. “Come near, you Gentiles, come near,” and that’s what Jesus, “Come unto me, all you that labor and are heavy laden, I will give you rest.” And there’s two things that God asked for the Gentiles to do: hear, number one, and heed, number two. If we don’t obey the word, it doesn’t do us any good to have heard the word. And how are they going to hear? The Bible says, without a preacher, and so the church has the responsibility of speaking up for truth. Could that be an amen? And it isn’t like God’s going to speak from heaven, “You Gentiles,” he’s going to send you to speak to them and to get them to obey the word of God. The people is the Gentiles that he’s talking to. “Let the earth hear, and all that is in it.” Now, the earth is a specific
Who are the Gentiles in Isaiah 34, and what does God ask of them?

Isaiah 34:1-2: Come near, you nations, to hear; And heed, you people! Let the earth hear, and all that is in it, The world and all things that come forth from it. For the indignation of the LORD is against all nations, And His fury against all their armies; He has utterly destroyed them, He has given them over to the slaughter. Matthew 11:28: Come to Me, all you who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
What does he say about life in space and God’s anger at the nations?

He says “there’s only one Earth,” that “there is no life out there in space,” and that “science fiction is exactly what it is, fiction.” He says God’s “fury is against all their armies,” and that an army can also be the word, used to convince people of a philosophy.
What does he say about life in space and God’s anger at the nations?

planet. It’s not Mars, it’s not Jupiter, it’s not some earthlike planet ultra light years away. There’s only one Earth, there’s only one civilization that God made, there is no life out there in space, the Bible never says there is, he always speaks to the planet Earth. Can I hear an amen? Hallelujah. Science fiction is exactly what it is, fiction, all right, I love it, but it’s fiction. “The world,” or mankind, the world is mankind and all things that come from mankind, “come near and hear.” So he’s directly addressing those that are not his people. Verse 2, “For the indignation,” or anger, “the wrath of the Lord is against all the Gentiles.” Okay, he’s angry. None of you have ever been angry, you wouldn’t understand that, but God’s angry. “His fury is against all their armies.” The army is the authority, the might that a people, uh, use to force their propaganda on others or defend their philosophies from others, and an army that we forget about is the word. A lot of people use the word, and they convince people with the army of the word, speaking information, knowledge, to convince people, and we forget that it’s not always swords and spears and, and, uh, atomic bombs and so
What does he mean by “past tense,” and what is secular humanism?

He says Isaiah speaks of the Gentiles’ destruction in the past tense because “God has ordained it and it’s going to happen,” as Jesus “died before the foundation of the world.” He reads Psalm 9:19 and then says secular humanism is a group of Gentiles in our day, and quotes the humanist manifesto as saying there is no God and that the Bible is a book of myths.
What does he mean by “past tense,” and what is secular humanism?

forth. “He’s utterly destroyed,” past tense, he’s utterly destroyed them, “he has given them over to slaughter,” past tense. You see, it’s just like the Bible says that Jesus died before the foundation of the world, God, and the Bible also says in Revelation that Jesus was the beginning of creation, before anything else, God the Son, Jesus was the plan, he died, all right, past tense, before he said, “Let there be light.” Jesus had died, past tense, and then he came in the flesh and died for the sins of the world and caused it to happen. This is the same terminology here, past tense. God has ordained it and it’s going to happen, whether you like it or not, whether you believe in it or not, it’s as good as done, past tense. Amen. Psalm 9:19, “Let not man prevail, put them in fear, oh Lord, that the Gentiles may know themselves to be but men.” See, this is the cry of the Holy Spirit: Lord, put them in fear, so that mankind comes to the understanding that they’re just humans and you are the supernatural God. Hallelujah. So we just happen to have a group of people in our day that are Gentiles, ungodly, they’re called the religion of secular humanism. This is the global icon of the secular humanist movement all over the world, trying to spread their propaganda, trying to spread their philosophy and their doctrine. This is the icon for the American Humanist Association: “Good without God.” Don’t need no God. The humanist manifesto, as we shared earlier, the humanist manifesto created in [unclear] and 30s says there is no God, the, the universe always existed, it was not created, prayer will not help anyone, the Bible is just a book of myths with a lot of errors in it, a lot of, uh, erroneous things in it, contradictory things. They said all this in the manifesto. In the manifesto they said that the institutes and the associations, the families and the churches have to be converted, they have to be rebuilt, and they got to be rebuilt and converted to what we say that will help humanity and mankind. That’s right in their manifesto, okay. They also said that the present financial system of America, which was capitalism, is obsolete, and we
What does he mean by “past tense,” and what is secular humanism?

Psalm 9:19-20: Arise, O LORD, Do not let man prevail; Let the nations be judged in Your sight. Put them in fear, O LORD, That the nations may know themselves to be but men. Selah Isaiah 34:1-2: Come near, you nations, to hear; And heed, you people! Let the earth hear, and all that is in it, The world and all things that come forth from it. For the indignation of the LORD is against all nations, And His fury against all their armies; He has utterly destroyed them, He has given them over to the slaughter.
What does he say the propaganda war in the schools is, and what does he say about charity?

He says “we are in a propaganda war, we are in a war of philosophy,” and says humanists declared they would win in the public schools and universities. He says that charitable giving is used to argue that “you don’t need God to be good,” and that churches that focus on social programs have fallen into that, while “the gospel of Jesus Christ for salvation is the highest level.” He names wealthy donors in the transcript; those names are not repeated here.
What does he say the propaganda war in the schools is, and what does he say about charity?

must give everybody their fair share. We need social programs, social programs is the answer to America and mankind’s problems, right in their manifesto. And most Christians do not understand that we are in a propaganda war, we are in a war of philosophy, a war of speech, not always with guns and tanks and airplanes, but speech. And they said publicly, and they declared it emphatically, that the war they were going to wage was going to be in the public school classrooms and the universities of America, and they said, “We will win this war because we have them five days a week and the church only has a fraction of them for one hour on Sunday.” And, folks, 80 years have gone by, they pretty much won this battle. They got Christians dumbed down that we can’t even think right anymore, and this is people that publicly declare there is no God, the Gentiles, the ungodly, no Jesus, no Bible, they publicly declare it. Here is a advertisement for the, uh, humanistic religion, put out by the Secular Student Alliance. Secular Student Alliance, Billy Gates, we all know him, the second richest person in the world, they said donated 26 billion to charity. Billy Gates is good without God, they said. The third richest person, Warren Buffett, pledged to give 90%, of, 99% of his wealth to charity when he dies. Warren Buffett is good, they said, without God. What’s their emphasis? If you have a social program, you are good. You don’t need God to be good, and what’s their good? Helping somebody. Helping somebody. And the church has fallen into that. Many of the churches in America are centered now on social programs, and they think because they help people that they have attained the highest level of Christianity, and it’s not true. The gospel of Jesus Christ for salvation is the highest level, and to grow in him, that is the goal of God.
What does Isaiah 34:4 say about the heavens being rolled up?

He says it is unfair that humanists can teach in classrooms while believers cannot. He reads Isaiah 34:4, that “all the host of heaven shall be dissolved,” and says that is the “when” of God’s dealing with the nations. He says it “takes a supernatural God to perform something like this” and that people who call it an allegory will find out.
What does Isaiah 34:4 say about the heavens being rolled up?

Amen, amen. You can’t substitute that, but they’ve got us dumbed down. The religion of secular humanism, clergy in the classroom, this book. You see, they said, say there has to be a separation of church and state, but it’s okay for humanists to go into the classrooms and teach their religion in the classrooms, but no one that believes the Bible, no one that believes in Christ has a right to go in, it’s, it’s, it’s bigoted, it’s not fair, it’s not the American way. Could that be an amen? Hallelujah. And we let them get away with it. So we’re going to go on in Isaiah 34, and we’re going to see clarity of God dealing with the Gentiles. This is very powerful. When will he deal with them? Isaiah 34:4, “All the host of heaven shall be dissolved,” they will decay. Now, folks, that’s a big undertaking. The universe is huge, and God says there’s going to be a time when it’s going to decay, it’s going to rot away, it’s going to be dissolved. That’s the when, okay. “The heavens shall be rolled up like a scroll.” Now, that’s a big undertaking, this universe is huge, and God say he going to roll it up as a scroll. You roll a scroll up, you still have part of the scroll there. “All their host,” all the stars, all the planets, “shall fall down as a leaf from the vine,” and the [unclear].
What does Isaiah 34:4 say about the heavens being rolled up?

Isaiah 34:4-6: All the host of heaven shall be dissolved, And the heavens shall be rolled up like a scroll; All their host shall fall down As the leaf falls from the vine, And as fruit falling from a fig tree. “For My sword shall be bathed in heaven; Indeed it shall come down on Edom, And on the people of My curse, for judgment. The sword of the LORD is filled with blood, It is made overflowing with fatness, With the blood of lambs and goats, With the fat of the kidneys of rams. For the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah, And a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
Why does he say Edom and Esau picture the Gentile humanist?

He says God speaks of “Edom, the people of my curse,” and links it to Hebrews 12, where Esau “for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.” He calls that “your social program,” and says the birthright to us today is “being born again, born of the word, born of the Spirit.”
Why does he say Edom and Esau picture the Gentile humanist?

Folks, a sun, our sun is 100 times bigger than our earth, and there’s all kinds of suns out there. A sun, a star is one that radiates light, planets and other things reflect light. Okay, now, it takes a supernatural God to perform something like this. People say, “Well, it’s just an allegory,” like, uh, uh, Fox News guy Bill [unclear], “Yeah, it’s just a book, it’s an allegory.” We’ll see, we’ll see if it’s an allegory. All right, you know, they got us so dumbed down, we just think like they tell us to think. Now, “my sword shall be bathed in heaven, indeed it shall come down on Edom.” So now he’s talking about the who, he’s talking about the when, “I show wonders in the heavens,” and who is going to be influenced at that time? “I’m going to come down on Edom, the people of my curse.” A curse is something that is put on someone that they can’t change, something bad’s going to happen to them. And he used the word Edom, why? Because in Hebrews 12:6, “lest there be any fornicator or godless person,” Gentile, humanist, “as Esau.” Esau is Edom, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. There’s your social program. The guy, you know, he was cocky and arrogant, and he always went out and hunted deer and brought things on, but he didn’t get anything this week, every time he went out he didn’t bring back any meat, and he got hungry, and instead of going to Mom and Dad’s house and getting something to eat, he went to his brother, and his brother said, “Hey, you know, in my social program you got to sell your soul. I’ll give you a bowl of soup if you’ll give me your birthright.” See, the birthright was to the firstborn, and he got the spiritual inherited blessing, and Esau didn’t care anything about spiritual things. Yeah, he said, “Sure, you’re going to have the birthright, give me the b— man, give me the social program.” Birthright to us today is being born again, born of the word, born of the Spirit, God actually coming and birthing us in his truth and in his presence, in his Spirit. He goes on to say, “For you know that afterward, when Esau would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected, for he found no place of repentance.” Now, you get that? “He found no place of repentance, though he sought repentance carefully with tears.” There was no repentance, and this really bothered me when I was a young Christian, and I didn’t understand the full knowledge of God, but later I understood, and you’re going to understand it
Why does he say Edom and Esau picture the Gentile humanist?

Hebrews 12:16-17: lest there be any fornicator or profane person like Esau, who for one morsel of food sold his birthright. For you know that afterward, when he wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected, for he found no place for repentance, though he sought it diligently with tears.
What do the ten virgins and Esau show about repentance?

He says Esau “found no place of repentance,” and compares it to the ten virgins in Matthew 25, five wise and five foolish. He says “when you die, you can’t repent after that,” and when Jesus comes for final judgment “there’s no repentance, you had your chance, the door’s shut.”
