items.t: Has the U.S. Government Made Just Choices and Equal Choices?
items.d: In “Has the U.S. Government Made Just Choices and Equal Choices?”, Pastor David G. Kincer reads the Declaration of Independence and the Preamble of the Constitution and says government is to protect moral…
p: In “Has the U.S. Government Made Just Choices and Equal Choices?”, Pastor David G. Kincer reads the Declaration of Independence and the Preamble of the Constitution and says government is to protect moral rights and promote, not provide, the general welfare. He teaches that the Bible’s purposes include moving us from bad government to good, equal rights for all peoples in Christ, and a just judicial system. He then lists unjust and unequal choices past and present and calls government to repent or be replaced.
What does the Declaration of Independence say about rights?

He reads that all men are created equal and endowed by their Creator with rights, and says the Bible Creator is the standard of justice, and rights are the freedom to do moral things: “not the pursuit of crime.”
What does the Declaration of Independence say about rights?

Okay, we appreciate you joining us in our pursuit of clarity on crucial choices. Today we will address the question: has the United States of America’s government made just and equal choices? And we will start with the Declaration of Independence. We hold these truths to be self-evident. The Declaration of Independence is the purpose for changing a government. “We hold these truths to be self-evident, that all men are created equal,” then, “they are provided by their Creator,” you notice they refer to the Bible and God, created, Creator, “with certain unchangeable rights.” So the Bible Creator is the standard of just and rights, and rights are the freedom to do moral things. “And among these rights are life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness,” not the pursuit of crime, not the pursuit of immorality, but the pursuit of happiness. “And to protect these rights, governments are instituted among men, deriving their just powers from the consent of the governed.”
Did the founders use the Bible as a reason to change government?
He says they used the Bible as a purpose for changing government and referred to the Creator who gives rights people cannot change, including the right to life of a newborn baby.
Did the founders use the Bible as a reason to change government?

So we see that they use the Bible as a purpose for changing government. They wanted their own government rather than Britain ruling over them, and they referred to the Bible and its Creator that gives us unchangeable, inalienable rights. People cannot change that. That gives us freedom to do moral things, not immoral things. And we have a right to life, to live, and so does that little baby that just came into the world; they have a right to live. They have the right of freedom to pursue happiness, to pursue, uh, work, and, and provide for their family, and do moral things. And, uh,
What is the Preamble of the Constitution for?
He calls the Preamble an introduction and explanation of the Constitution’s purpose, and reads “We the People … to form a more perfect union” and “establish justice.”
What is the Preamble of the Constitution for?

the, the Declaration of Independence declares why we need a change of government and the purpose for changing a government. Now we’re going to look at the Constitution, and we’re going to look at the Preamble of the Constitution, which is an introductory to the Constitution and an explanation of the Constitution, and see what the purpose of the Constitution is for this new government. “We the People of the United States of America, in order to form a more perfect union,” in order to “establish justice,”
Is government supposed to promote or provide the general welfare?
He stresses that the Constitution says government is to “promote,” not provide, the general welfare, and to secure the blessings of liberty.
Is government supposed to promote or provide the general welfare?

in order to “insure domestic tranquility,” in order to “provide for the common defense,” and in order to “promote,” not provide, “the general welfare.” See, the explanation of the Constitution is not for government to provide the welfare; it’s to promote the welfare. “And secure,” or protect, “the blessings of liberty to ourselves and our” offspring. And so we see here that we, they wanted a perfect union in the Constitution,
What kind of union did the founders want?
He says they wanted a unity around impartial moral behavior, a moral judicial system, and an army and police to protect moral people from the immoral and from foreign nations.
What kind of union did the founders want?

a union, a unity, around moral behavior, impartial moral behavior. They wanted to, in the Constitution, established a moral judicial system that ruled in favor of right behavior, morality. They wanted an army to ensure the domestic peace, and a police force, whatever is necessary to protect the moral people from the immoral people, or a nation that would want to come and take away our freedom and our rights. And number five, which is very important, they wanted to let the American people know
What does the Bible say about good government?

He says one purpose of the Bible is to move us from bad government to good, as God delivered us from the power of darkness into the kingdom of His Son, and from the power of Satan unto God (Acts 26:18).
What does the Bible say about good government?

that the established government is there to promote, not provide, the general welfare, the happiness, the prosperity. They are there to promote it and protect it and ensure it, not provide it, and to protect the blessings of our freedom, to have a judicial system based on morality. Now, when we look at the purpose of the Bible, one of the purposes is to change bad government from a good one, to a good one rather, whether it’s spiritual or secular. God delivered us, the Bible says, from the power of darkness and translated us into the kingdom, the rulership, of his dear Son Jesus. From the power of Satan unto God, Acts 26:18 says. So the Bible’s purpose is to teach us and to transfer us from bad government to good.
What does the Bible say about good government?

Colossians 1:13: He has delivered us from the power of darkness and conveyed us into the kingdom of the Son of His love, Acts 26:18: to open their eyes, in order to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those who are sanctified by faith in Me.’
Does the Bible teach equal rights for all races?

From Acts 17:26 he says God made all nations of one blood, and from Galatians 3:28 and Colossians 3:11 that all, even the Scythian, are one in Christ, so even the dirty man beside him in church has equal rights.
Does the Bible teach equal rights for all races?

Another purpose of the Bible is equal rights in unity. Acts 17:26: God has made of one blood all nations. All races of people, all cultures, all languages have been made of one blood, and we have, as his creation, the right. In Galatians 3:28 and Colossians 3:11, there is neither Jew nor Greek, bond or free, male nor female, foreigner, which is a person that speaks a different language, it has a different culture and a skin color, or a savage. A foreigner or a savage, the savages, the Scythian, who never washed, they drank blood, they used skulls for drinking vessels, they were just a very, uh, you know, deep, uh, horrible, nasty people. But he says all of them are one in Christ Jesus, and as God’s chosen people, put on good behavior. So this dirty, stinking guy in the church sitting beside me has equal rights when he comes to Christ. He don’t know how to wash himself, he don’t know how to do things properly, but he has equal rights in the church.
Does the Bible teach equal rights for all races?

Acts 17:26: And He has made from one blood every nation of men to dwell on all the face of the earth, and has determined their preappointed times and the boundaries of their dwellings, Galatians 3:28: There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free, there is neither male nor female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus. Colossians 3:11: where there is neither Greek nor Jew, circumcised nor uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave nor free, but Christ is all and in all.
How has the U.S. government treated women unjustly?
Citing 1 Peter 2:14 on a just judicial system, he says women in the past could not vote, sit on a jury, own property if married, get higher education, or get their children in a divorce.
How has the U.S. government treated women unjustly?

Another purpose of the Bible: to choose a just judicial system to protect our rights. First Peter 2:14: governors are for the punishment of evildoers and for the praise of them that do well. And so the Bible tells us to choose a judicial system that will protect the rights of the moral people. Our government’s unjust and unequal choices: in the past, women could not vote, could not be on a jury, could not own property if they were married, they couldn’t get higher education, and they couldn’t get their kids in a divorce.
How has the U.S. government treated women unjustly?
1 Peter 2:14: or to governors, as to those who are sent by him for the punishment of evildoers and for the praise of those who do good.
How were Native Americans and slaves treated?

He says Indians had no rights or religious freedom, were sterilized and had their children taken, and were made citizens only in 1924. He says slaves had no freedom of religion and worshiped in hush harbors.
How were Native Americans and slaves treated?

As bad as that is, the Indians had no rights at all. They had none of the rights of the women, plus they couldn’t worship their religion, they had no religious freedom. They st-, they were sterilized to keep from reproducing. Their kids were taken from of them and put in parochial schools to brainwash them. And in 1924 they finally were allowed to be a citizen of the United States of America. And as bad as that is, slavery. Both Indians and blacks were in slavery, and they had no, the blacks had no freedom of religion, the African-American. They had to use hush harbors; they put wet quilts and stuff around an area so the sound wouldn’t go out, to worship the Lord Jesus Christ. Other than that, they had to do it in the white men’s church. And the Supreme Court and Darwin backs up this inferiority of the dark-skinned people,
What other unjust and unequal choices does he name?

He names separate-but-equal laws and limits on Chinese immigration and property, and says today Christians are censored when they speak about Bible morals, sin and hell, and marriage has been redefined.
What other unjust and unequal choices does he name?

and they were not allowed to be citizens until 1870, and then it was equal but separate; they weren’t allowed to mix with white folks. But the Chinese, Asians, they were not allowed to migrate after 1882 until 1943, when they were allowed to migrate again back to America and become a citizen, and they could not own property till 1965. Now, folks, that’s unjust and that’s unequal. Today we got Jesus and the Bible and Christians censored in speech and press. If we want to talk about homosexuals, or executions of a murderer, uh, we want to talk about hell and Bible morals and sin, we are censored. We are forbidden by government, frowned on by government, to do these things. The family and marriage has been redefined.
How does he say government choices have hurt families?

He cites family breakdown and abuse figures, and says printing money and inflation forced both parents to work: his father earned one dollar an hour in the ’50s and could buy a home and a new Chevrolet.
How does he say government choices have hurt families?

Less than 50 percent of Americans now get married. 44 percent of kids are in a one-parent home. 5 million children are abused every year, 450,000 of them sexually, and one-third of those by same-sex attackers. 500 a week in the military are sexually abused, and 500 a year in public schools are abused by the teacher, and just getting a slap on the hand. The banking system: since the institution of the Federal Reserve Bank, where America, our government, could just print money without any value, and especially since the 1965 War on Poverty, inflation and deflation has led to both mother and dad having to work to support the family. My dad in the ‘50s worked for one dollar an hour, bought a home, bought a new Chevrolet, fed, clothed and provided the medical attention for a seven-member family. Today ten dollars per hour will not buy a home, a new Chevy, pay a normal rent or medical insurance,
What is the solution for unjust government?
He says government must admit it is wrong, repent, and enforce constitutional and Bible morality, or be replaced, as the Declaration says the people may alter or abolish it.
What is the solution for unjust government?

leaving only food and clothing and whatever. So the parent, both parents have to work to provide a normal middle-class lifestyle, and thus the children are left alone till the parents get home. We have 1.1 trillion a year federal and state welfare expenditures. Since 1965 we have three times more spent on welfare than all the wars that we’ve been in put together. The federal debt is at 18 trillion and growing. 50 percent is our tax revenue when you add all the taxes. So what is the solution? Government must, government must admit they are wrong. They need to repent from that wrong, turn from that wrong, enforce constitutional and Bible morality, or be replaced. As the Declaration of Independence says, it is the right of the people to alter or to abolish it and to institute a new government. Moral citizens, what are we going to do and doing to address this problem?
What does he say rights are?
He says rights are the freedom to do moral things.
Does a newborn baby have a right to life?
He says yes: that little baby that just came into the world has a right to live.
Why does he emphasize the word “promote”?
He says the Constitution’s purpose is not for government to provide the welfare but to promote, protect and ensure it.
Why did the founders want an army and police?
He says to protect the moral people from the immoral people and from nations that would take away our freedom.
What does “made of one blood all nations” mean?
He says all races, cultures and languages have been made of one blood.
Who were the Scythians mentioned in Colossians 3:11?
He describes them as savages who never washed, drank blood and used skulls as drinking cups, yet says all are one in Christ.
What are governors for, according to 1 Peter 2:14?
He says governors are for the punishment of evildoers and the praise of those who do well.
He says slaves put wet quilts around an area so the sound wouldn’t go out, to worship the Lord Jesus Christ.
He says Christians are censored and frowned on by government when they speak about homosexuality, executions, hell, Bible morals and sin.
Why does he say both parents now have to work?
He blames printed money, inflation and deflation since the Federal Reserve and the War on Poverty, so that ten dollars an hour won’t buy a home or pay normal rent.
What right does the Declaration give the people?
He says it is the right of the people to alter or abolish an unjust government and institute a new one.

items.d: In “Heirs of the Kingdom,” Pastor David G. Kincer continues the series on God’s promises with the sixth promise, that believers will be heirs of the kingdom. He explains James 2’s definition of the poor who…
p: In “Heirs of the Kingdom,” Pastor David G. Kincer continues the series on God’s promises with the sixth promise, that believers will be heirs of the kingdom. He explains James 2’s definition of the poor who are rich in faith, the prerequisites of repentance, conditional righteousness and being converted, and being born of the Word and the Spirit, and then calls the church to demonstrate the kingdom’s power through healing, deliverance and prayer.
How can we escape the corruption of the world and share the divine nature? (2 Peter 1:4)

He reads 2 Peter 1:4 about “exceedingly great and precious promises” and reasons that if the Bible is God’s Word and God cannot lie, then “we are who the Bible says we are,” including “taking on the divine nature of God and escaping the lust of this world.”
How can we escape the corruption of the world and share the divine nature? (2 Peter 1:4)

We have been taking the Scripture in 2 Peter 1:4: “Whereby are given unto us exceedingly great and precious promises, that by these you might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.” It’s a powerful verse. And I gave you a little quotation that I use when I witness to people, and I’m going to give it to you again. I start out with, “If there is a God, can he lie?” They go, “No.” “If there is a God, he can’t lie.” Okay, God says the Bible is his Word. So the Bible is God’s Word, and God can’t lie. So God is who the Bible says he is, he’ll do what the Bible says he will do, we are who the Bible says we are, and we can do and be what the Bible says we can do and be, including taking on the divine nature of God and escaping the lust of this world.
How can we escape the corruption of the world and share the divine nature? (2 Peter 1:4)

2 Peter 1:4: by which have been given to us exceedingly great and precious promises, that through these you may be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.
Who are the poor who are “heirs of the kingdom” in James 2:5-8?

He says the kingdom is one kingdom however it is named and that James defines the “poor” as people who are “rich in faith,” “heirs, recipients, of the kingdom,” who love Jesus, who do not dishonor others and do not oppress. He says it is “not just any old poor; it’s a special kind of poor person,” and that the believers had “dishonored the poor man.”
Who are the poor who are “heirs of the kingdom” in James 2:5-8?

He says the church “should be delivering people from possession and oppression of demons.”
What are the signs of possessing the kingdom, and can a cross or a Bible drive out demons? (Matthew 12:28)

Now let’s look at the signs of possessing the kingdom. Now, this is important, and this is what I’ve been trying to get the church to understand for 40 years. I got this revelation in my bedroom on Warner Street in Santa Ana when I was just a couple of years old in God, and I said, “God, whatever it takes, whatever you got to do to me to reach this goal, I’m open to it.” Boy, I didn’t know what I said then, and I went through hell on earth. But this is the high mark of the calling of God, along with God’s character. Matthew 12:28: “If I cast out demons by the Spirit of God, surely the kingdom of God has come upon you.” Wow. This guy says he’s down on the church. Why? American churches don’t even believe in demons. Bill O’Reilly said there was a demon somewhere back in Ohio or someplace, and they had the priest on, and the priest said, “Yeah, I put the cross on him and, you know, he went crazy.” Church, demons are spirits. They could care the least if you touch that person with a cross, wooden, metal, plastic or whatever. In the Pentecostal realms, if you put the Bible on them, they, or they can’t say the Lord, and they go through the torch; that’s a bunch of baloney. Demons are spirits. And also in the Pentecostal world they vomit up demons; it’s really the phlegm coming out of their throat, and that’s a demon? That ain’t no demon; that’s your phlegm, you idiot. Down in Mexico they were casting out demons that came out as frogs. I said, “I don’t know what church you people are going to, but ain’t no frogs.” You read some scripture out of Revelation. Demons are spirits. Are you there? Hallelujah. You need some of these side issues sometimes. Somebody told me they took a picture of the Adam family. I immediately went home and looked on the Internet for this picture of the Adam; it’s a joke. Ain’t no picture, no Adam. Do you guys ever check things out? My goodness.
What are the signs of possessing the kingdom, and can a cross or a Bible drive out demons? (Matthew 12:28)
Matthew 12:28: But if I cast out demons by the Spirit of God, surely the kingdom of God has come upon you.
Is the kingdom in words or in power? (Luke 10:9, 1 Corinthians 4:20, 2:5)

He says the church should “heal the sick” and that “the kingdom of God is not in word but in power,” so we do not need “a lot of theology.” He tells how he led a young man of another religion to Christ in about five minutes by pointing to sin, the cross and that Jesus laid down his life, and says faith should “not stand in the intellect of men … but in the power of God.”
Is the kingdom in words or in power? (Luke 10:9, 1 Corinthians 4:20, 2:5)

Anyway, the church should be delivering people from possession and oppression of demons. Power! The church should be powerful, and this why this young person said, “I’m down on the church.” You know, he went to it, and it’s just a bunch of theology, just a bunch of rituals and routines, and no power. And yes, church, we should be people of power. Amen. Right, Luke 10:9: “Heal the sick there, and say to them, ‘The kingdom of God has come near to you.’” Heal the sick: physically sick, mentally sick, spiritually sick, emotionally sick. Jesus heals people. And people come in and we use psychology and we got these 12-step programs and seven-step programs, when the Bible says that the church can have power to heal. Are you there? And this is what we got to attain to, this is what we got to pursue: being a church that has the power. 1 Corinthians 4:20: “The kingdom of God is not in word but in power.” It’s not in speech, it’s not in words, it’s not all these words. When I led a young Muslim to Christ Friday night, I didn’t need a lot of theology. It took about five minutes. “Are you a sinner?” “No.” I said, “Well, let’s check this out. Have you murdered anybody?” “No.” I said, “Well, you’re looking good there.” I said, “Have you stole anything?” “Yep.” “Oh, really?” I said, “Have you told a lie?” “Yep.” I go, “Oh, two witnesses; you’re lying, you stole. What does that make you?” He looks at me, and someone beside me goes, “A sinner.” And then I told him the wages of sin is eternal death, eternal punishment, but there’s a higher law: Jesus Christ died on the cross. I says, “You Muslim, believe he’s just a prophet?” He said, “Yep, that’s right, we believe he was a prophet.” I said, “They’re lying to you. He’s not only the Son of God, he was God. And the Muslims are right, you can’t kill God. He had to lay down his life; that’s what Jesus said: ‘I lay down my life, ‘cause no one has authority to take it.’” And he laid it down so you could be forgiven, set free and so forth. We prayed the sinner’s prayer. Bam! Are you there? Hallelujah. And I, they don’t need to know where Cain’s wife come from and what the horns on the altar mean. Come on, they need this power of Christ touching them. God has chosen the foolishness of what? Preaching to save those that believe, and the gospel is the power of God. The gospel is Jesus’ birth, ministry, death and resurrection for you, and any of us can share that. Hallelujah. Not in words. 1 Corinthians 2:5: “Your faith should not stand in the intellect of men” (they use the word wisdom, really means intellect) “but in the power of God.” See, Calvin, St. Augustine, Wesley, the popes, Joseph Smith, Muhammad, I could care the least. I’ve read the Book of Mormon; man, I got one-third through it, and there’s so many mistakes, I go, “Any idiot can see that this just can’t be an angel. Angels don’t make mistakes like this.” Are you there? I mean, ridiculous mistakes. And I am shocked that people will read Christian books and not the Bible. I’m just shocked that authors today are better than Paul, better than Peter; it just amazing me, when these guys were connected with Christ in person. Are you there?
Is the kingdom in words or in power? (Luke 10:9, 1 Corinthians 4:20, 2:5)

Luke 10:9: And heal the sick there, and say to them, ‘The kingdom of God has come near to you.’ 1 Corinthians 4:20: For the kingdom of God is not in word but in power. 1 Corinthians 1:21: For since, in the wisdom of God, the world through wisdom did not know God, it pleased God through the foolishness of the message preached to save those who believe. 1 Corinthians 2:5: that your faith should not be in the wisdom of men but in the power of God. John 10:18: No one takes it from Me, but I lay it down of Myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. This command I have received from My Father.”
Why do Christians need to know the Scriptures, and what does “the power of the Lord was present to heal” mean? (Luke 5:17)

He says Jesus told the religious leaders “you are mistaken” because they didn’t know the Scriptures, and that today Christians “are passing on what these people are saying” instead of reading the Word. He says “the power of the Lord was present to heal” means it “wasn’t always there,” so “when it’s not there, we should not try to fake it.”
Why do Christians need to know the Scriptures, and what does “the power of the Lord was present to heal” mean? (Luke 5:17)

Matthew 22:29: “You are mistaken,” why? Because you don’t know the Scriptures. And this is the big problem in America: Christians are passing on what these people are saying. I try to get people to read the Word; they just won’t do it. They’ll go to a church where they don’t tell them to read the Word. “You’re going to harp on reading the Word? I’ll just leave.” What do I do? The Bible says, “Seek out of the book of the law and read,” “study to show thyself approved.” What do you want me to preach? You young people, you need to know the Scriptures. You need to start early. Remember this: we’re born by the Word and the Spirit, and the Word, his Spirit, by the way. Okay, the second reason we make [unclear] is we don’t have the power of God: the power of the name of Jesus, the power of the Holy Ghost, and the power of the Word. Luke 5:17. Okay, let me set the picture here. The lawyers, the religious leaders will come down to trap Jesus. They’re always trying to trap him, all right. And they come down, and Jesus is there, and the Bible says “the power of the Lord was” (they added this word “present”) “to heal.” All right, the power was there. So that means it wasn’t always there. And, folks, when it’s not there, we should not try to fake it, all right? So they brought in a man that was paralyzed, he couldn’t walk, four people brought him in on a stretcher, and Jesus said, “Your sins are forgiven you.” And these religious leaders and lawyers: “Hey, hey, nobody can forgive sins but God.” Well, duh! If you really knew your Bible, you’re looking at him; that’s God right there, Jesus. And so Jesus said these famous words: “Which is easier, to forgive sins or heal the sick?” Huh? Folks, both of them are supernatural. We can’t forgive sin and we can’t heal the sick, but he can do both. And so “the power of the Lord was present to heal.” That’s why we worship: to get the presence that will touch people’s minds, people’s souls, people’s spirit and change them. That’s why we want a living word, not some word from [unclear] or somebody, some book, you know. All these home Bible studies are using somebody’s book instead of the Bible book. We need the power of the Word; we need the power of the presence. And we can’t settle for anything less. And Jesus healed that paralytic man.
Why do Christians need to know the Scriptures, and what does “the power of the Lord was present to heal” mean? (Luke 5:17)

Matthew 22:29: Jesus answered and said to them, “You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God. Isaiah 34:16: “Search from the book of the LORD, and read: Not one of these shall fail; Not one shall lack her mate. For My mouth has commanded it, and His Spirit has gathered them. 2 Timothy 2:15: Be diligent to present yourself approved to God, a worker who does not need to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth. Luke 5:17: Now it happened on a certain day, as He was teaching, that there were Pharisees and teachers of the law sitting by, who had come out of every town of Galilee, Judea, and Jerusalem. And the power of the Lord was present to heal them.
Why did crowds travel 60 miles to touch Jesus? (Luke 6:17-19)

He says the crowds came “to hear him” and “to be healed,” with no advertising, because “when the powers in the church, they didn’t need to advertise.” He says they “just came up and touched him,” with no healing line or fanfare, and that we can touch him today through “worship and prayer, seeking his face, fasting.”
Why did crowds travel 60 miles to touch Jesus? (Luke 6:17-19)

Now look at this powerful scripture, Luke 6:17. “A great multitude from all Judea” (60 miles away from where Jesus is at; he’s at the Sea of Galilee) “and from the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon” (these are heathen nations, heathen cities; they’re on the coast of the Mediterranean; they are 60 miles away) “came to hear him.” Folks, if they walked, it would take them two days to get there, and how did they find out where he was at? They had no TV and radio. Word of mouth, that’s right. When you got the power, when the power’s in the church, they didn’t need to advertise. God did his own advertising by healing the sick, casting out demons, saving souls, strengthening spirits, delivering minds. Amen. See, they didn’t need to sell you a Bible autographed by [unclear], or some trinket that you could put there and pray on, or some prayer cloth that cost you a hundred bucks. You could just bring a hanky out of the drawer and it works without the $100. If God’s in it, God only did that one time, and we make a rule out of it. He did it one time. A great multitude 60 miles away, folks. No air conditioning; they either walked or they rode donkeys or they rode in chariots. Most of these people are poor; they walked, it’s hot, they sat in the hot sun to what? No nursery, no children’s program, no youth program, and the multitude will sit there all day and listen to him teach. All day they came. Number one, to hear him: Jesus had something to say. Jesus had a life-changing message. He had the living Word. And to be healed of their diseases, their torments by unclean spirits, not even necessarily possessed, just oppressed and tormented, and they were what? Healed. “The whole multitude sought to touch Him, for power went out from Him and healed them all.” See, he didn’t have a healing line. He didn’t have to go through these big dramatics: “In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ of Nazareth, I pronounce your healing.” No, they just came up and touched him, touched him, touched him. No cameras, no fanfare, and the magic word is “touch.” Say “touch.” Folks, we can touch him today through worship and prayer, seeking his face, fasting. We can touch him today.
Why did crowds travel 60 miles to touch Jesus? (Luke 6:17-19)

Luke 6:17-19: And He came down with them and stood on a level place with a crowd of His disciples and a great multitude of people from all Judea and Jerusalem, and from the seacoast of Tyre and Sidon, who came to hear Him and be healed of their diseases, as well as those who were tormented with unclean spirits. And they were healed. And the whole multitude sought to touch Him, for power went out from Him and healed them all. Luke 6:19: And the whole multitude sought to touch Him, for power went out from Him and healed them all. Acts 19:11-12: Now God worked unusual miracles by the hands of Paul, so that even handkerchiefs or aprons were brought from his body to the sick, and the diseases left them and the evil spirits went out of them.
What power did the early church demonstrate, and what do we need today?

He criticizes ministers who “take credit for healings” that Jesus did, and says we are “vessels to bring God and people together.” He lists the early church’s power (a ruler struck down, deception judged, prison doors opening, a shadow healing) and says “you don’t need a lot of theology, you don’t need a lot of psychology.”
What power did the early church demonstrate, and what do we need today?

And these ministers that take credit for healings, I’ve been in a lot of healing ministers’ meetings. They take credit for something that Jesus came and did. He came and touched them and healed people, and the mighty man of God raised money saying he had the ability. Are you there? I loved it how God worked in Africa. My first visit to Africa, I’m preaching the gospel out in the church and all that, and I get done, and, you know, 15 or 30 people came up front saying, “God healed this, and God healed that, and God did this, and God did that.” And I go, “Hold it.” You know me, I’m a doubter. I go down, I start questioning. “All right, now you say God did this. Now who, who knows this was, who knows?” “Oh, I know, over here, over here.” It’s really happening. Yeah, no fanfare, no nothing. While you’re preaching, while the worship is going on, God comes and touches people, and amazing things happen. No healing line, nobody getting credit, the elders didn’t get up and put on theatrics: “Oh, hallelujah, I’m praying for you.” You know, “call the elders of the church.” Yeah, man, I’m one of them guys. Check me out, man. “De Lord!” and they’d get worse. You see, we need to touch him. And like [unclear] said, “I am a vessel that brings God and people together.” And when people touch him, things happen. I liked what he said, and that’s what we are: we are vessels to bring God and people together, and God does his work. Hallelujah. Isn’t that powerful? So we can touch him. Now, young people, I want you to know, the early church, there was a big demonstration of power. All right, Herod was killed with worms; Ananias and Sapphira died because they lied to the [unclear]. Herod, because he took the title of being a god, took the worship of being a god. The sorcerer was blinded. Philip was transported 30, 40 miles; just beam me up, beam me down. Prison doors did open all by themselves. Peter’s shadow was healing people. The fear: the outsiders feared the church, that they would not say anything against it or do anything against it. That’s the power of God. You young ones hearing this, this is what you need. You don’t need a lot of theology, you don’t need a lot of psychology, you don’t need a lot of words. We need the living Word, and we need that Holy Ghost working in the church and touching people’s lives. And we’ve gotten away from that, and this is my point to this guy. See, the church has gotten away from that, and we just do things that will bring the people in. We go to some kind of survey company and they do a survey how to build a church, and so we do these things to get people into the church, and we have 10,000 in the congregation, and they can’t handle life at all. I know, ‘cause I have to deal with them. They got no power in their life at all. They can’t even stay married. Remember Paul reasoned to Felix, the [unclear], self-control, righteousness and a judgment to come, and Felix trembled. He shook just hearing that simple message. Are you there?
What power did the early church demonstrate, and what do we need today?

Acts 12:23: Then immediately an angel of the Lord struck him, because he did not give glory to God. And he was eaten by worms and died. Acts 5:1-10: But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession. And he kept back part of the proceeds, his wife also being aware of it, and brought a certain part and laid it at the apostles’ feet. But Peter said, “Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and keep back part of the price of the land for yourself? While it remained, was it not your own? And after it was sold, was it not in your own control? Why have you conceived this thing in your heart? You have not lied to men but to God.” Then Ananias, hearing these words, fell down and breathed his last. So great fear came upon all those who heard these things. And the young men arose and wrapped him up, carried him out, and buried him. Now it was about three hours later when his wife came in, not knowing what had happened. And Peter answered her, “Tell me whether you sold the land for so much?” She said, “Yes, for so much.” Then Peter said to her, “How is it that you have agreed together to test the Spirit of the Lord? Look, the feet of those who have buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out.” Then immediately she fell down at his feet and breathed her last. And the young men came in and found her dead, and carrying her out, buried her by her husband. Acts 8:39-40: Now when they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught Philip away, so that the eunuch saw him no more; and he went on his way rejoicing. But Philip was found at Azotus. And passing through, he preached in all the cities till he came to Caesarea. Acts 16:26: Suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken; and immediately all the doors were opened and everyone’s chains were loosed. Acts 5:15: so that they brought the sick out into the streets and laid them on beds and couches, that at least the shadow of Peter passing by might fall on some of them.
Is the church a one-man show? Why does he say you are important? (Acts 4, Acts 12)

He says Pentecost was “not a one-man show” but happened because “120 prayed and worshiped him,” and that in Acts 4 the whole church prayed. He says “you are important,” should make prayer and worship a priority, and should give God “one hour a day.” He ends by urging people to come to the altar “to touch Jesus.”
Is the church a one-man show? Why does he say you are important? (Acts 4, Acts 12)

And listen to this, this is what you got to get in your cranial vacuum, you ready? This is not a one-man show. God moved on the day of Pentecost because 120 prayed and worshiped him, not just Peter. God called Peter out to do the message, but it was the 120 that ushered in the baptism of the Holy Ghost. Acts chapter 4: the whole church was gathered together praying and saying, “Lord, grant unto us that signs and wonders would be done,” and God came and shook the place and granted unto them signs and wonders would be done, and they spoke the Word of God with power. You see, first the whole group prayed. See, this is a group. Are you getting this? You are important. We’re in America, we’re looking for the mighty man of God in the Baptist circles, the fundamentalist circles, the Catholics are looking for the pope and the priest, and, you know, we’re all looking for this one-man ministry thing. And all through the Bible it was the group. When Peter was in prison, he went to sleep, but the church didn’t. The church what? Prayed for him, and God came and rescued Peter. This is a corporate thing, and you are important. If you want the church to be more than just a bunch of word and a bunch of rituals and ceremonies, then you have to decide to get involved. You have to decide to make prayer a priority in your life, worship and praise a priority in your life, the Word. You need to give one hour a day to God; that’s what Jesus asked for, one hour. There’s 24; that leaves you 23. You say, “Well, I’m busy all day.” Then get up at 3:00 in the morning, seek God for an hour and go back to bed. Nobody can bother you, kids are sleeping. There is solutions for every problem that you give me. The reason I know that’s what I had to do: sometimes I had to get up in the middle of the night to get the real time in and go back to bed sometime. Hallelujah. Church, are you getting this? Do we want to be just another wordy church, rituals, routine? We got our little ceremony; we dance, we lift our hands, we shout unto God with the voice of triumph, and we have no hope in it at all. Hope is his expectation. These are scriptural things to do, but when we don’t do them with a purpose, it becomes a ceremony. Ain’t that right? It just becomes a ceremony. Now, these people traveled 60 miles to touch Jesus. Some of you only have to travel six feet to come down to the altar, humble yourself, get out of your safe zone, separate yourself from everybody around you, to touch Jesus.
Is the church a one-man show? Why does he say you are important? (Acts 4, Acts 12)

Acts 24:25: Now as he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was afraid and answered, “Go away for now; when I have a convenient time I will call for you.” Acts 4:24-31: So when they heard that, they raised their voice to God with one accord and said: “Lord, You are God, who made heaven and earth and the sea, and all that is in them, who by the mouth of Your servant David have said: ‘Why did the nations rage, And the people plot vain things? The kings of the earth took their stand, And the rulers were gathered together Against the LORD and against His Christ.’ “For truly against Your holy Servant Jesus, whom You anointed, both Herod and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles and the people of Israel, were gathered together to do whatever Your hand and Your purpose determined before to be done. Now, Lord, look on their threats, and grant to Your servants that with all boldness they may speak Your word, by stretching out Your hand to heal, and that signs and wonders may be done through the name of Your holy Servant Jesus.” And when they had prayed, the place where they were assembled together was shaken; and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they spoke the word of God with boldness. Acts 12:5: Peter was therefore kept in prison, but constant prayer was offered to God for him by the church.
What line does he use when witnessing about the Bible?
He asks, “If there is a God, can he lie?” and when they answer no, he says the Bible is God’s Word and God can’t lie, so “God is who the Bible says he is, he’ll do what the Bible says he will do.”
Does he say James is describing something the church actually did?
No. He says James uses “if” as “an allegory, an illustration of a truth,” and “he didn’t say the church was doing this at all.”
Does he say every poor person is an heir of the kingdom?
No. He says “you’re not poor unless you meet the definition of the Bible poor,” meaning rich in faith and loving Jesus. He says “I’ve been in churches where poverty is spirituality.”
What does he say about being taken to court over your faith?

He says he has “been to court four times because of my faith” and “won all four times.” He says people with money and position oppress because the gospel “threaten them” by telling them they have to change their lifestyle.
Which name does he say to use rather than just “God”?
He says the noble name is “Jesus,” and to “be careful about using God in this generation; everybody takes God as anybody’s God,” while “that name of Jesus” separates it from all other gods.
What does he mean by positional and conditional righteousness?

He says being “righteous by the blood” is positional, and asks what good it does your family and community “if you just stay positionally righteous and you live wrong in this world.” He says “I need a God that can change my brain, change my actions, change my talk.”
What does he say the word “converted” means?

He says “it literally means to turn and change your beliefs to the one you’re turning to,” so “turn from the erroneous beliefs over who you’re following and turn to God, turn to Jesus and get his beliefs.”
What two things does he say the church needs to birth and change people?
He says “the living presence of God, the Spirit of God, and the living Word of God.”
Does he say tongues or preaching pricked hearts at Pentecost?
He says “no one got their heart pricked when they heard him speaking in tongues in their language,” but when Peter “stood up and preached Christ and crucified, then the Word pricked their heart.”
What test does he give for a spiritual experience?
He says “when it doesn’t line up to the Word, I know it’s not the Spirit of God,” and that the Word and the Spirit “agree.”
Does he say a cross or the Bible on a person drives out a demon?

No. He says “demons are spirits. They could care the least if you touch that person with a cross, wooden, metal, plastic or whatever,” and he also says putting the Bible on a person is “a bunch of baloney.”
How does he describe sharing the gospel in about five minutes?

He says he asked simple questions about murder, stealing and lying, showed that the person was “a sinner,” then said the wages of sin is eternal death “but there’s a higher law: Jesus Christ died on the cross.” He says “they need this power of Christ touching them.”
What does he say about healing lines and credit for healings?

He says Jesus did the healing and ministers who “take credit” are taking credit for something Jesus did. He says in Africa God touched people during preaching and worship with “no healing line, nobody getting credit.”
How much time does he say to give God each day?
He says to “give one hour a day to God; that’s what Jesus asked for,” and if you’re busy, “get up at 3:00 in the morning, seek God for an hour and go back to bed.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the baptism of the Holy Ghost with power is a real experience separate from salvation and water baptism. He starts with John 7:38-39 and Jesus as the…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the baptism of the Holy Ghost with power is a real experience separate from salvation and water baptism. He starts with John 7:38-39 and Jesus as the baptizer, covers prophecy, visions and the names of the Holy Spirit, then walks through the accounts in Acts of Pentecost, the believers in Samaria, Cornelius’s household and the disciples at Ephesus. He also speaks about unity in worship, mistakes in Spirit-filled churches, and the purpose of the Spirit’s power.
What is the baptism of the Holy Ghost, and what does John 7:38-39 promise?

He says there is “an experience in God called the baptism of the Holy Ghost with power,” not just something at Pentecost, at salvation or at water baptism. He reads John 7:38-39 as a promise to believers, and says the criteria for having the Holy Ghost is “Believe. Okay, it’s not complicated.” The Spirit flows from “your belly, innermost being,” and “it’s not a ceremony, it’s not a ritual, it’s a real experience.”
What is the baptism of the Holy Ghost, and what does John 7:38-39 promise?

They told me that Holy Spirit baptism was one time on the day of Pentecost, or it was when you get saved, or it was when you got water baptized. And you people need to know how to answer this stuff, and you also need to know that there is an experience in God called the baptism of the Holy Ghost with power that is vitally important to your life, to the church life, and what God is doing in the earth. Okay, and I’m going to give you biology this morning. Are you ready? John 7:38-39. It is a promise to believers. Now, the Holy Spirit is called the Holy Ghost, Holy Spirit, Spirit of Truth, Comforter, My Spirit, and we’re going to give you the facts of the Holy Spirit. All right, nothing but facts. “He that believes on Me.” Okay, how many of you believe on Jesus? Where’s the rest of you? Huh, now. Okay, John 3:16 says, “He that believes on Me shall not perish but have everlasting life.” Same statement here, but instead of everlasting life, He says, “As the Scripture has said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.” And this spake He of the Spirit, which they that believe on Him should receive, for the Holy Ghost was not yet given because Jesus was not yet glorified. He hadn’t died and risen again, and so the Holy Spirit hadn’t been poured out on all flesh yet. But what’s the criteria for having the Holy Ghost? Believe. Okay, it’s not complicated. All right, and where will we experience this Holy Ghost? Out of your belly, innermost being. You’re going to experience it in that inner man that you really are, that spirit that’s really inside that body. Let me just share with you here a minute. It said, “As the Scripture has said” in the Old Testament. In Job 32:18, Elihu said, “I am full of the matter, the spirit within me constrains me. Behold, my belly is as wine which hath no vent, it is ready to burst like new wine bottles.” See, in the Old Testament Scriptures God already said He was going to do this. All right, and it’s going to pour out of our innermost being. It’s not a ceremony, it’s not a ritual, it’s a real experience. In Isaiah 58:11: “You shall be like a watered garden and like a spring of water whose waters fail not.” Hallelujah. And so this is the promise of that in John 7:38.
What is the baptism of the Holy Ghost, and what does John 7:38-39 promise?
