Paul already had been filled with the Holy Spirit, had his eyes open, met Jesus on the road to Damascus, but here in 13:9, Paul was filled with the Holy Ghost, set his eyes on the sorcerer, and smote him with blindness. The sorcerer was trying to distract the people from hearing the Word, and Paul just looked at it and said, “God smite you with blindness.” Bam, the guy went blind. You see, it gives us power to smite our enemies, cast out demons. There’s power in the Holy Ghost. It gives us power to embarrass the enemy. Verse 52: the disciples were filled with joy and with the what? Holy Ghost. They already been filled twice, and here they are filled again. So it is a what? Continual experience. So that means they weren’t always filled with the Holy Ghost, but when the Holy Ghost wanted to do something, He come upon them, and out of their innermost being these words flow out and things happened. And this is what us Pentecostals have got to get together. I don’t know, you know this, but your pastor is a Spirit-filled person. He has spoken in tongues. When I spoke in Third World countries, I interpreted a lot of tongues. All right, it is a sign for the unbeliever. Doesn’t happen so much in America. And this happened in Iconium, and they so spoke that a great multitude believed. They so spoke by the Holy Ghost that a great multitude believed. How many would like to see [unclear] really get a word from the Spirit of God? Amen, yes. See, that’s our cry, that’s my cry, that we get past the form and into the force. Yes, see, we get past the fear and into the force.
Is being filled a one-time experience, and what does he mean by “great grace”? (Acts 4:33; 13:9, 52; 14:1)

Acts 4:33: And with great power the apostles gave witness to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus. And great grace was upon them all. Acts 13:9: Then Saul, who also is called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked intently at him Acts 13:52: And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit. Acts 14:1: Now it happened in Iconium that they went together to the synagogue of the Jews, and so spoke that a great multitude both of the Jews and of the Greeks believed.
What does Samaria show about Holy Spirit baptism being separate from believing and water baptism? (Acts 8:12-17)

He says the Samaritans believed and were baptized in water, yet when Peter and John came “as yet He was fallen upon none of them,” and then “they laid their hands on them and they received the Holy Ghost.” He says “it didn’t happen at water baptism, it didn’t happen when they believe, it happened when God made it happen,” and calls it “a different experience from salvation, a different experience from water baptism.”
What does Samaria show about Holy Spirit baptism being separate from believing and water baptism? (Acts 8:12-17)

Okay, are they already believers? Yep. Have they been water baptized? Yeah. See, it didn’t happen at water baptism, it didn’t happen when they believe, it happened when God made it happen. It happens when it happens. Acts 8:12: “When they believed Philip preaching the things of the kingdom of God,” he went down to Samaria, and the name of Jesus Christ, and miracles, “they were all baptized, both men and women.” Okay, so they believed. Okay, are they filled with the Holy Ghost? Not yet. Are they baptized in water? Yes. Are they filled with the Holy Ghost yet? No. Verse 14: Peter and John came down and prayed for them to receive the Holy Ghost, “as yet He was fallen upon none of them.” Now here they use the word “fallen.” See, come upon. “Only they were baptized in the name of the Lord.” Had they been water baptized? Had they been water baptized? The story is the story, church. Do you get it? Then they laid their hands on them and they received the Holy Ghost. A different experience from salvation, a different experience from water baptism. Already believers, they were already baptized. Okay, now separate event. You agree? Is that what the Scripture says? Yes. Say amen if you got it. Amen. All right, say it with fortitude. Amen. All right, now I believe you.
What does Samaria show about Holy Spirit baptism being separate from believing and water baptism? (Acts 8:12-17)

Acts 8:12: But when they believed Philip as he preached the things concerning the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, both men and women were baptized. Acts 8:14-17: Now when the apostles who were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them, who, when they had come down, prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Spirit. For as yet He had fallen upon none of them. They had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. Then they laid hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
What does Cornelius’s household show about the order of salvation, the Holy Ghost and water baptism? (Acts 10:44-48)

He says “everything is backwards here”: the Holy Ghost fell on people who “were unbelievers,” and “before he could have an altar call for salvation, God just filled them with the Holy Ghost.” He says the Jews with Peter “were astonished,” and that the Gentiles “spoke with tongues again and magnified God.” He gives the order: “First you got the Holy Ghost, then you got them believing, and then you got them water baptized,” and calls it “separate experience from water baptism and the salvation of your soul.” He says God did it “because He knew these dumbbells in the future would twist the Scriptures and rob people of a real experience in God.”
What does Cornelius’s household show about the order of salvation, the Holy Ghost and water baptism? (Acts 10:44-48)

Now, this one is really interesting. God really dazzles you when you come to Cornelius. All right, I mean, everything is backwards here. God just don’t fall into our little pattern all the time, and He does have a pattern, but He’s God, He can go outside His pattern. We’re not allowed to, but He’s God, He can do anything He wants when He wants. Okay, Cornelius is a Roman soldier, praying and fasting. An angel came, told him go down and get Peter to come up and preach to him. So he went down and got Peter, Peter come up and spoke, and as Peter spoke the Word of God, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the Word. All these people came to Cornelius’s house. They were unbelievers. Peter had to come and preach the gospel to them. These were unbelievers, and before he could have an altar call for salvation, God just filled them with the Holy Ghost. How could He do such a thing? Because He knew these dumbbells in the future would twist the Scriptures and rob people of a real experience in God, a powerful experience in God, by their theological interpretations. And so here He really just messes everything up. They were filled with the Holy Ghost before a salvation call and before their water baptism, and they of the circumcision, the Jews that came with Peter, were astonished because on the Gentiles was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost. They were just astonished. How can this be? You know, it’s us [unclear], no more. You know, it’s just us people, with the, we’re the people. Hallelujah. And God said He would pour out His Spirit on how many flesh? All flesh. You are a candidate for the Holy Ghost. “For they heard them speak with tongues.” Oh, tongues again. My gosh, how could God do such a thing? They spoke with tongues again and magnified God, or praised God. Remember, on the day of Pentecost they spoke the mighty works of God. Here they praise and enlarged, magnified God. Then commanded Peter that they be baptized in water in the name of the Lord. Amen. First you got the Holy Ghost, then you got them believing, and then you got them water baptized. He’s God. He had definitely, this is a what? Separate experience from water baptism and the salvation of your soul. Unbelievers, not baptized, they got the Holy Ghost.
What does Cornelius’s household show about the order of salvation, the Holy Ghost and water baptism? (Acts 10:44-48)

Acts 10:44-48: While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all those who heard the word. And those of the circumcision who believed were astonished, as many as came with Peter, because the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out on the Gentiles also. For they heard them speak with tongues and magnify God. Then Peter answered, “Can anyone forbid water, that these should not be baptized who have received the Holy Spirit just as we have?” And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord. Then they asked him to stay a few days.
What happened in Ephesus in Acts 19, and what does he say about churches that do not teach the baptism of the Holy Ghost?

He says Paul asked, “Have you people received the Holy Ghost since you believed?” and they were “in a group that didn’t teach the Holy Ghost.” He says “when you don’t teach the baptism of the Holy Ghost, you are robbing the people of a powerful experience in God that will help them in daily life.” After Paul laid hands on them, “they spoke in languages again, and they prophesied.” He says tongues are “a sign for the unbeliever, prophecy is for the believer.”
What happened in Ephesus in Acts 19, and what does he say about churches that do not teach the baptism of the Holy Ghost?

All right, now we go to Acts 19. Here Paul comes to Ephesus, and Paul says, “Have you people received the Holy Ghost since you believed?” And of course they were in a group that didn’t teach the Holy Ghost. And see, when you don’t teach the baptism of the Holy Ghost, you are robbing the people of a powerful experience in God that will help them in daily life and help us reach the world for Christ. You got that? And here’s a group that wasn’t teaching. They said, “We never heard of it.” So when Paul preached to them, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. Paul laid his hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came upon them, and they spoke with tongues. Oh my God, that tongue again. That tongue just drives people nuts. They spoke in languages again, and they prophesied. They spoke by the inspiration, they did both of them. All right, so three out of five times they spoke with tongues, and we don’t know one of those times if they did or not because he didn’t say. He just didn’t say. And tongues are a sign for who? The unbeliever. Don’t forget that. Tongues are a sign for the unbeliever, prophecy is for the believer. Hallelujah.
What happened in Ephesus in Acts 19, and what does he say about churches that do not teach the baptism of the Holy Ghost?

Acts 19:1-7: And it happened, while Apollos was at Corinth, that Paul, having passed through the upper regions, came to Ephesus. And finding some disciples he said to them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?” So they said to him, “We have not so much as heard whether there is a Holy Spirit.” And he said to them, “Into what then were you baptized?” So they said, “Into John’s baptism.” Then Paul said, “John indeed baptized with a baptism of repentance, saying to the people that they should believe on Him who would come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.” When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. And when Paul had laid hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke with tongues and prophesied. Now the men were about twelve in all.
What does he say about excesses and “funny things” in Spirit-filled churches, and the claim that the Holy Ghost is not for today?

He admits “us Pentecostals, we do make mistakes,” and that “babies in Christ” may “speak some silly things,” but compares them to children: “we don’t kick them out of the house and condemn them.” He says “these things hurt no one,” and asks “how does tongues hurt you?” He says teaching that the Holy Ghost “isn’t for today” hurts people because “you’re robbing them of a tremendous experience and truth in God,” and that being offended by it is “called pride.” He says “I would rather be in a Spirit-filled church with some funny things going on.”
What does he say about excesses and “funny things” in Spirit-filled churches, and the claim that the Holy Ghost is not for today?

Now, I tell these brethren, you know, us Pentecostals, we do make mistakes. Okay, we get too shaken, we slain in the Spirit, we fall for this stuff, and we even have babies in Christ that speak some silly things. Okay, me and Mr. Barnes heard some of that in one of the services. Didn’t bother us any, we just knew they were babies in Christ. And you know, children, they say strange things, and we just laugh and we don’t kick them out of the house and condemn them. These things hurt no one. I asked them, “How does tongues hurt you?” It doesn’t hurt you. There’s no physical harm, there’s no spiritual harm because somebody speaks in tongues. If somebody shakes and falls down on the ground, how does that hurt you? Why are you offended at that? That does no personal harm to you, does it? You’re only hurt because they’re not believing what you believe. That’s why you’re hurt. It’s called pride. But I said, “Now, let’s get to your end. You’re telling people that the Holy Ghost isn’t for today. That hurts them because you’re robbing them of a tremendous experience and truth in God. I said, are you over here, you’re telling them that they get the Holy Ghost when they were water baptized and they didn’t get anything. You’re robbing them. I said, who’s really doing the hurting here? You’re robbing people of an experience in God.” Amen. So we have a few funny things going on. I would, listen, I would rather be in a Spirit-filled church with some funny things going on, and believe me, I have the authority to control things. You don’t believe me, you watch funny things happen. Yeah, we don’t have to hurt people and step on them, we can just guide them. We can grow in this thing. How many, when you first got on a bicycle, didn’t crash it? Most of us wrecked the bike, don’t we? Okay, so we do some funny things with the Holy Ghost. They’re babies, we’re babies, we’re learning. Could that be an amen? Amen, yes. What we need is that power. We need that power that changes people’s life in our services.
What is Holy Spirit baptism for, and what does he challenge the church to do? (John 3:30; 1 Corinthians 14:26; John 16:13)

He concludes that the baptism of the Holy Ghost “is another spiritual miracle like salvation,” and that “you have to believe above your experience before you’re going to experience it.” He says it is “for a purpose,” not “for you to feel good,” and people need “power, freeing them from sin, Satan, and self.” He says “everything we do should be to build up the people of God,” and the church must “decrease and let God increase.” He says the Spirit “will drive you to the Word,” and “politicians need to hear the Word of God” too.
What is Holy Spirit baptism for, and what does he challenge the church to do? (John 3:30; 1 Corinthians 14:26; John 16:13)

Okay, they are believers, they are baptized. Clearly the Holy Ghost baptism is another separate experience. Amen. Now, conclusion: “Clothed with power,” “receive power,” “witnesses unto Me.” The baptism of the Holy Ghost is another spiritual miracle like salvation. Okay, the Bible says that, I don’t care what you believe, the Bible say you have to preach above your experience before you’re going to experience it. You have to believe above your experience before you’re going to experience it. Don’t take your experience and bring the Bible down to your lack of experience. You speak the Bible and He will bring your experience up to what you’re speaking and believing. Separate from water baptism and salvation, we saw it clearly, didn’t we? There’s nothing to interpret, is there? Power to speak, smite your enemies, do miracles, and win souls. Do we need that in the church at Mountainside? Yes. As John says, “I must decrease and He must increase.” How many of you realize we got to decrease and let God increase in this church? We got to get out of our opinions, we got to get out of our cultural antics, and we got to say, “God, arise,” if we want to see a visitation. And I guarantee you, when God starts moving, people will come. The Holy Ghost baptism is for a purpose, either in the assembly or individually, whether they’re filled, baptized, or the Spirit comes upon them. All right, it’s for a purpose. It’s not for you to feel good, and that’s not totally true. There are times of refreshing, you need to be refreshed, but not to where you have to roll around on the floor and shake and bake. And just that refreshing on the inner man, that strengthening in the inner man. You see, it’s for a purpose. He’s a Comforter, He’s a Spirit of Truth that teaches us all things. So I challenge this church today. People need power, freeing them from sin, Satan, and self, and they need refreshing from God. This is what I liked about the Spirit-filled churches when I went to them. You could feel God. He would penetrate your being. He would convict you that you’re wrong. I was always wrong. I hadn’t given my heart to Christ yet. I believed in God, but I wasn’t about to serve Him because I had plans, man, I had plans. But that presence comes, you can feel Him. It’s like putting gas in your tank. You know, we run out of gas, we run out of spiritual gas, we get refilled. It’s a refreshing, and people need that. And people need the Holy Ghost to convict them of sin, forgive them of sin, and cleanse them of sin, and encourage them. Remember, prophecy is for edification, exhortation, and comfort. People need that comfort, people need that building up. See, and Paul said in 1 Corinthians 14, “Let all things be done to edify.” Everything we do should be to build up the people of God, make them better people, and that’s what the ministry of the Holy Ghost is for. We’ve got to get the word out. They told me over there they send us to go to politicians, politicians is of the devil, you know, and all this stuff. I go, man, this world is still believing the lies of Satan in the garden when Satan told Jesus that all these kingdoms are given to me and I can give them to who I want. He’s lying through his teeth. The Bible plainly tells us over and over that the nations, the kingdoms, belong to the Lord. Amen. He was lying. Politicians need to hear the Word of God. Unbelievers need to hear the Word of God. Unlearned people, unlearned people, they’re believers but they’re unlearned, they need to hear this Word that God has given this church. And to whom much is given, much is required. Folks, we got to get this word out. We’ve got to buck up, we’ve got to get together and get this word out: printed, Internet, radio, TV, CD. You know, Christine and Mike were really good on a camera, I’ve noticed. They really have camera appeal. Me and Mr. Barnes, we don’t, you know, we don’t look so good on camera. And remember, the Holy Ghost will guide you into all truth. When you really get filled with the Holy Ghost, you will not only know because of the feeling. He will not allow you to be lazy in the Word of God, because it’s the Word that set you free. He will drive you to the Word, He will drive you to church to learn the Word. You will have a motivational factor in your life.
What is Holy Spirit baptism for, and what does he challenge the church to do? (John 3:30; 1 Corinthians 14:26; John 16:13)

John 3:30: He must increase, but I must decrease. 1 Corinthians 14:26: How is it then, brethren? Whenever you come together, each of you has a psalm, has a teaching, has a tongue, has a revelation, has an interpretation. Let all things be done for edification. Luke 4:5-7: Then the devil, taking Him up on a high mountain, showed Him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said to Him, “All this authority I will give You, and their glory; for this has been delivered to me, and I give it to whomever I wish. Therefore, if You will worship before me, all will be Yours.” Luke 12:48: But he who did not know, yet committed things deserving of stripes, shall be beaten with few. For everyone to whom much is given, from him much will be required; and to whom much has been committed, of him they will ask the more. John 16:13: However, when He, the Spirit of truth, has come, He will guide you into all truth; for He will not speak on His own authority, but whatever He hears He will speak; and He will tell you things to come.
What teachings does he say he was told about Holy Spirit baptism?

He says, “They told me that Holy Spirit baptism was one time on the day of Pentecost, or it was when you get saved, or it was when you got water baptized.” He says “you people need to know how to answer this stuff.”
What does he say is the criteria for having the Holy Ghost?
He asks, “But what’s the criteria for having the Holy Ghost? Believe. Okay, it’s not complicated.” He says you will experience it in “that inner man that you really are.”
Who does he say baptizes in the Holy Ghost?
He says, “Jesus is the baptizer in the Holy Ghost,” and “Jesus is the sender,” reading Luke 3:16 and Luke 24:49.
Does he say prophesying and predicting are the same thing?
No. He says “there’s a big difference when you go into predicting,” and that “prophesying for edification, exhortation, and comfort is totally different.”
What does he say the Holy Ghost is not out to do?
He says, “He’s not out to condemn you, He’s not out to punish you, He is out to change you and help you in your time of need.”
What does he say about resisting the Holy Ghost as a young man?

He says, “I believed in God, but I had plans and I had purposes, and I would just shove that Holy Ghost away. I didn’t want to be convicted.” He says that “until finally He got my attention, and it’s been a great life ever since.”
What does he say about following the song leader in worship?
He says, “If the song leader claps their hands, you clap your hands. Song leader raises the hand, you raise your hand.” He also says, “if you don’t want to lift your hands, you don’t have to.”
What does he say about faking tongues?
He says of Pentecost, “They didn’t fake it, they didn’t pretend it,” and of his early experience in Pentecostal churches that “you don’t manufacture, God does it.”
How does he say you know you have been filled with the Holy Ghost?
He says, “Believe me, you will know. It comes from your innermost being. It is a visitation of power, supernatural ability.” He adds “tongues or no tongues, you will know.”
What does he say about speaking God’s Word with confidence?
He says, “speak like it’s God’s Word. It’s truth. Don’t speak like it’s a suggestion, it’s your opinion. Speak like it is.”
What does he say grace is?
He says, “grace isn’t just favor from God,” and “grace is divine enablement. There’s power in grace.”
What order does he give for Cornelius’s household?
He says, “First you got the Holy Ghost, then you got them believing, and then you got them water baptized.”
What bicycle illustration does he use?

He asks, “when you first got on a bicycle didn’t crash it? Most of us wrecked the bike, don’t we?” and says, “we do some funny things with the Holy Ghost. They’re babies, we’re babies, we’re learning.”
What does he say about politicians and the Word of God?
He says the Bible “plainly tells us over and over that the nations, the kingdoms, belong to the Lord,” and “politicians need to hear the Word of God. Unbelievers need to hear the Word of God.”

items.d: From Philippians 3:13–14 the speaker calls hearers to forget what is behind and press to God’s top goal—loving God and neighbor (Matthew 22) and the church—by adding virtue, knowledge, self-control, patience…
items.ser: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors · Part 15
tg: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors
p: From Philippians 3:13–14 the speaker calls hearers to forget what is behind and press to God’s top goal—loving God and neighbor (Matthew 22) and the church—by adding virtue, knowledge, self-control, patience, godliness, brotherly love, and love (2 Peter 1). Love leads to knowing God (John 17:3). He urges correcting criminal sinners, says humanists reject God’s rule, judges movements by fruit (Matthew 7) and sowing (Galatians 6:7), cites abortion, STD, work, and family statistics against humanist policy, and calls Christians out of the closet as warriors who admit wrong, repent, and unite to make America righteous again.
What is real hope and change from Philippians 3:13?

He reads Paul forgetting what is behind and pressing toward what is ahead—get over old mistakes God forgave, forgive yourself, and go forward forcefully toward the goal, not only being saved and going to heaven.
What is real hope and change from Philippians 3:13?

Real hope and real change. Philippians 3:13. I Paul said I forget those things which are behind folks there’s a place where you’ve got to just get over your old life your mistakes your failures God forgave you you got to forgive yourselves and you got to go forward can I be an amen you can’t go through life condemning yourself for the flaws you have until you can correct them and so Paul says I forget those things which are behind I reach for those things which are ahead I press I forcefully move forward to the goal see God has a goal. Of the high calling the top invitation of God yes he invited us to be forgiven for our sins he invited us to be the temple of God he invited us to come into his kingdom and but he says there’s other invitations and there is a top invitation.
What is real hope and change from Philippians 3:13?

Philippians 3:13-14: Brethren, I do not count myself to have apprehended; but one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind and reaching forward to those things which are ahead, I press toward the goal for the prize of the upward call of God in Christ Jesus.
What is the top calling or goal he says God invites us to?
Paul was the world’s worst sinner yet moved toward the goal. The top invitation is to reach the top commandment—Matthew 22:37, love God—with a prize/reward for pressing toward it.
What is the top calling or goal he says God invites us to?

And with that top invitation comes a prize a reward. And Paul says I press toward those things Paul was the world’s worst sinner and he laid that stuff he he put it behind him and he moved toward the goal the goal is not just being saved from your sins and going to heaven God has a higher goal involved. What is the goal of the top calling of God the top invitation. Here we have hope. The top goal the top invitation would be to reach the top commandment. Isaiah 20 I mean Matthew 22:37 love God. And remember we learn that God is love so you love love can you say that love love you know for people who don’t believe in God then love love.
What is the top calling or goal he says God invites us to?

Matthew 22:37: Jesus said to him, “‘You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’ Philippians 3:14: I press toward the goal for the prize of the upward call of God in Christ Jesus.
What does loving God with heart, soul, and mind mean here?

He says if you don’t have a problem with love you don’t have a problem with God—love God with every part of you. Love does nothing to hurt himself or his neighbor; it is the first and great law. God invited you to be forgiven so you could reach that.
What does loving God with heart, soul, and mind mean here?

I mean who’s going to have a problem with love. If you don’t have a problem with love you don’t have a problem with God. Love God with all your heart with all your soul with all your mind your spiritual man your intellectual man and and and your physical man love God with every part of you love love and remember love does nothing to hurt. Himself or his neighbor. All right it is the first and the great law so that is the high invitation of God he had to invite you to be forgiven for your sins he had to invite you to come to him for forgiveness confessing your sins get water baptized but his higher invitation is his first commandment.
What does loving God with heart, soul, and mind mean here?
Matthew 22:37-38: Jesus said to him, “‘You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’ This is the first and great commandment.
What do loving neighbor and loving the church require?

Love your neighbor as yourself—don’t hurt those around you or yourself. Jesus’ new commandment is love one another, the true church pursuing Bible morality—don’t talk against or hurt them. People who won’t go to church miss that.
What do loving neighbor and loving the church require?

To love. The second one it says is like an into it love your neighbor as yourself don’t hurt those around you don’t hurt yourself don’t do things that bring problems and distress and pain in your life and others life the third one is a new commandment Jesus gave us to love one another or love the true church don’t talk about don’t hurt those people that are pursuing Bible morality the genuine church we’re supposed to love and that’s why the church is so important people that don’t go to church they don’t get it you’re supposed to go to church to provoke one another to love and to good works and when you don’t go to church you’re not a promoter of people’s lives growing and reaching this goal and you’re not going to grow yourself.
What do loving neighbor and loving the church require?
Matthew 22:39: And the second is like it: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’
Why must you add qualities to faith after being planted in God’s house?
Those planted in the Lord’s house flourish. He says God saved you to get you on the road to the goal—saved and brought in so you grow. Faith alone is not the end; you add the sequence of qualities.
Why must you add qualities to faith after being planted in God’s house?

Because they that are planted in the house of the Lord shall flourish and grow in the courts of their God that’s the promise of God so the coming together is very important not to hear contemporary music or hillbilly music or jazz music or whatever music. But to be a part of the body of Christ that is contributing for others to love and to do good works. It’s not an entertaining place in a socializing place that’s the goal of the top calling of God first Timothy 1:5 the end the goal the last in sequence. Of the law is love out of a pure heart you see it’s not faith the goal is love. To love God love yourself love your neighbor and love your enemy that’s the goal of God that’s the whole purpose and we stop at salvation. He had to save you to get you on the road to the goal. He had to save you and bring you into the stadium where the track is so you can get in the race. Amen. And just because you’re saved it isn’t the goal the top goal is to love love and some have swerved they’ve deviated. They’ve strayed from that goal of God. How to sequentially reach the top goal step by step. All right second Peter one we’ve covered it chapter one verses four starting with verse four add to your faith whether you’re a humanist or whether you are a Christian no matter what you are if you’re an atheist if you’re a homosexual if you’re a liberal you have a faith in something you are persuaded in something.
What is faith as he defines it for humanists and believers?

Faith is being persuaded that something is right—whether humanist or Bible follower. You need Bible knowledge of moral excellence and must add self-control: you controlling yourself, not waiting for a phone call from God or a Holy Ghost meeting to stop wrong.
What is faith as he defines it for humanists and believers?

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer sets Jeremiah 31 and 32 in the middle of Israel’s captivity and shows the hope God gave there: a new, everlasting covenant in which God puts His Word in our hearts…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer sets Jeremiah 31 and 32 in the middle of Israel’s captivity and shows the hope God gave there: a new, everlasting covenant in which God puts His Word in our hearts, forgives, and promises to do us good. He then lays out our part, to repent, believe the gospel, confess Jesus as Lord and receive Him, and uses the butterfly and 1 John 2 to describe growing from baby to child to young man to father in Christ.
What was happening in Israel when Jeremiah 31 and 32 were written?

He says Josiah was the last good king, but his son “burned the Scriptures” and did evil before God, the first captivity came, and later the king of Babylon burned Jerusalem and destroyed the temple. He says Jeremiah 32 was written about ten years after that, and asks, “If Israel had hope, do we have hope?”
What was happening in Israel when Jeremiah 31 and 32 were written?

Okay, we’re going to go to Jeremiah chapter 31 and 32, but we want you to understand and remember when these chapters were written. Okay? You remember a few lessons ago we showed you that Josiah was the last good king of Israel. All right, looks like Israel was going to avoid the captivity and everything, because Josiah really turned to God, got the nation to turn to God, reinstituted the feast and the things of God. But then his son came on the throne. How many of you had children that didn’t follow your ways? Jehoiakim came up. He reigned 11 years, and he burned the Scriptures, just burned them, and he did evil before God. He shed innocent blood. He committed abominations. Abominations is sexual immorality, homosexuality, idolatry, stealing, murder. In Proverbs 6:17, you remember, there’s seven things that the Lord, it’s called abominations: a lying tongue, a proud look, hands that shed innocent blood, he that devises wicked imaginations, feet that are swift to running to do evil, a false witness that repeats lies and speaks lies, and he that sows division among the brethren, and there’s many others. Okay? And he committed them. He committed them all. All right, he had wars, there were famine, there were plagues, and the first captivity came at the end of his term. Then [unclear] arose, and he was king, made king by the king of Babylon, and he only lasted three months, but the Bible just summed him up and said he did evil like [unclear] did. Now it was in this condition that chapter 31 was written. Hallelujah. I mean, we got serious calamity. America’s got calamities, but nothing this bad yet. So if Israel had hope, do we have hope? If Israel would have listened to Jeremiah, 31 and 32 could have saved them a lot of pain, and so can we. Hallelujah. Then we go down to Zedekiah. He reigned 11 years, and the second captivity came in the 11th year, and this time the king of Babylon destroyed and burned the city of Jerusalem, destroyed the temple. He imprisoned the preacher of righteousness, Jeremiah, and this is when Jeremiah 32 was written, okay, about 10 years later.

He says fathers know Jesus from the beginning of the Bible to the end, love Him, and “can birth others” through the gospel, while “children can’t birth.” He says too many rely on the Savior stage, but “we got to have Jesus the rabbi, Jesus the teacher, and then Jesus the Lord.”
What is a spiritual “father” in Christ, and why must Jesus be Lord and Teacher, not only Savior?

You know the Bible and you overcome the wicked one. He can’t tempt you, test you, lead you astray. You’re just immune to it now. Satan is no problem. He just, “Get away from me, Satan. Get back. Get back off.” Not even a struggle for you. See, something’s going on inside of you, deep inside of you. See, that’s God working His work in you. And then the fathers. You see, fathers, you know Him. That’s Jesus from the beginning. You see, now they know God is Jesus. Now they know that Jesus was there at the beginning, to the end of the Bible, and they love Jesus, and they can birth others. See, fathers can birth others through Christ’s gospel. Children can’t birth. See, the father is married. The Bible says that Jesus is our Savior. That’s what babies rely on. But the Bible also says that He’s your Lord. See, are you there? He also says He is your rabbi, your teacher. These guys need to be taught the Word of God. Am I getting this across to you? See, too many people rely on the Savior stage. The Savior stage is the stage we got to go through. The caterpillar had to be hatched from the egg. It had to be done, but that wasn’t the goal. What was the goal of the egg? A beautiful butterfly. And so we got to have Jesus the rabbi, Jesus the teacher, and then Jesus the Lord. And these young men made Him Lord, so they studied the Word, they took time out for God, they did what God said to do, and they overcame the wicked one. They overcame the world, you see, by the Word of God, and a work was going on in them, transferring them to young adulthood, to fatherhood, into the image of Christ.
Can most Christians say what the new covenant is?

He says fathers make beautiful Christians out of non-believers, baby Christians and children by bringing them into the image of Christ. He says over 90% of Christians he asks cannot say what the new covenant is, and asks how you can live in or inherit something you have no knowledge of, then summarizes the steps: turn from sin, confess it, trust Jesus’s death, burial and resurrection, confess Him as Lord, accept Him, and “I will do all these things.”
Can most Christians say what the new covenant is?

Fathers, you know Him, and you can birth others. And this is the image: they birth people in the image of Christ. They make beautiful Christians out of non-believers, out of baby Christians, out of children. They nourish them and they bring them into the image of Christ. Isn’t that powerful? Hallelujah. And that’s the covenant. That’s it, it’s that simple. Most Christians cannot tell me the covenant. Over 90% of them, if I ask them what is the new covenant, they have no idea. How can you live in something that you don’t have knowledge of? How can you inherit things that you have no knowledge of? How can you just be satisfied with just being a saved Christian and not know the promise of the covenant that God promised to you, if you would do these simple things: turn from your sin, confess your sin, put your trust in Jesus’s death, burial, and resurrection, confessing Him as Lord, accept Him in your life? Then He said, “I will do all these things.”
What does he say Israel’s kings did that led up to the captivities?

He says Josiah turned the nation to God, but his son “burned the Scriptures,” shed innocent blood and committed abominations, listing the seven things the Lord hates from Proverbs 6:17. He says the first captivity came at the end of that king’s term.
What is a covenant, according to this message?

He says “a covenant is a contract.” He compares it to buying a house, where you promise the lender and the government to pay, “they do their part, I have to do my part,” and says the new covenant is God’s contract with God’s part and ours.
Does he say God forgives and forgets sin?
He says God says, “I’ll forgive it, I’ll render it zero, I’ll look at it like it never happened, and I will remember your sin no more.” He asks, “If God forgives us, shouldn’t we forgive ourselves?”
What does he say the fear of the Lord is?
He says, “depart from evil and hate evil. That’s the Bible definition of the fear of the Lord.”
What does he say about denominational names on churches?

He says Paul “plainly says there is one Lord, one Savior, one body, one baptism, one church,” and that putting a name on your church building and saying what you believe “doesn’t count.” He says all of us have the responsibility to line up to Him.
Is there another covenant coming after the new covenant?
No. He says it is the “everlasting” covenant and lists the Adamic, Noah, David and Moses covenants before it: “there ain’t no other covenant coming. This is it, and this is a good one.”
Why does he say God blesses those who obey His covenant?
He says God wants to bless your finances, health and life “because He wants to get the attention of your neighbor,” so they see it pays to serve God.
He says “repent: turn from your evil ways, adultery, stealing, and turn to right ways,” leave sin behind, and “believe the gospel.”
What does he say Luke 13:5 tells us we must do?
He reads, “Except you repent, you shall all likewise perish,” and says it doesn’t say “except you get baptized” or “except you witness”; “it says except you what? Repent. You turn.”
How does he say we confess our sins?
He says “I have to admit it with my mouth” and name what is wrong, and then, citing 1 John 1:9, “He is faithful to forgive, and not only forgive, but wash it off, cleanse me of the contamination.”
Does he say a Christian becomes mature right away?
No. He says “I’m not going to be zapped,” and says old Pentecostals thought “I’m totally mature now,” but “no, no, no,” you go from glory to glory, faith to faith, and salvation to salvation.
How can you tell which stage of Christian growth you are at?

He says, “you can identify where you’re at today.” If you have habitual sin you are a baby; if you don’t know the doctrines of Christ or believe in your own doctrines, you are a child; if you know the Bible and overcome the wicked one, you are a young man; fathers know Him and can birth others.
What does he say about relying only on Jesus as Savior?

He says “the Savior stage is the stage we got to go through,” like the caterpillar hatching from the egg, “but that wasn’t the goal.” The goal is “a beautiful butterfly,” so we need Jesus as teacher and then as Lord.
How many Christians does he say can tell him what the new covenant is?
He says “most Christians cannot tell me the covenant,” and over 90% have no idea when he asks, then asks how you can live in or inherit something you have no knowledge of.

items.t: How a Tax Exempt, New Testament Church Benefits Americans
items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer contrasts the federal 501(c)(3) definition of church—building, community aid, public-policy limits and no lobbying—with the Bible’s assembly of living stones focused on Jesus’ presence…
items.ser: Clarity on Crucial Choices · Full sermon
p: Pastor David G. Kincer contrasts the federal 501(c)(3) definition of church—building, community aid, public-policy limits and no lobbying—with the Bible’s assembly of living stones focused on Jesus’ presence, prayer, praise and truth. He argues public policy that silences the church while allowing other lobbies yields destroyed lives, and that a real New Testament gathering where each brings Spirit-led speech convicts unbelievers and benefits America more than welfare programs—while tax exemption keeps government from fighting God.
How does the federal government define a church?

He says they define it as a building where people congregate for worship, marriage, burial, communion and rites, with religious history and ordained ministers, and—most importantly—people congregated to give aid to the community via 501(c)(3).
How does the federal government define a church?

I want to thank you again and offer my appreciation for joining us on another session of clarity on crucial choices. Today we’re going to discuss how a tax-exempt New Testament church benefits America and Americans. What benefit does the New Testament church have for the people of America? We’re going to take a look first at the federal government’s definition of a church—how they define it, how they see it. First of all they say it is a building where people congregate to worship, marry, bury, serve communion, do other religious rites. Is this group must have a religious history, and this congregation of people ordained ministers such as priests, rabbis or so forth. But most importantly, as I have accented, it is a people congregated to give aid to the community. Now this is found in your 501(c)(3) instructions that almost every church gets a tax exemption by filling out this tax exemption form 501(c)(3). The second thing they define a church as is a
Why did a 1938 bill say churches get tax exemption?
H.R. 1860 argued government is compensated for lost tax by benefits from promoting general welfare—community aid saves the government money.
Why did a 1938 bill say churches get tax exemption?

House of Representatives bill—H.R. 1860, 75th Congress, third session in 1938—said the exemption from taxation of money or property devoted to charitable and other purposes, the church is based on the theory that the government is compensated for the loss of tax revenue by the benefits resulting from the promotion of the general welfare. The aid that the church gives to the community saves the government taxes, and therefore the government is compensated and can give a tax exemption.

He says a tax-exempt church must serve a public purpose for all the community and not be contrary to public policy, with no political lobbying or campaign involvement under separation of church and state.

Now that’s 501(c)(3) and this bill in the 1930s give us two of the definitions. The third one is there are restrictions, controls put upon the church by the federal government. Again quoting from the 501(c)(3) application and instruction in the IRS manual: an institution is a society or organization founded for religious, educational or social purposes. So an institution, a church seeking tax exemption, must serve a public purpose—in other words it’s got to serve all the people in the community
Who does he say can lobby when the church cannot?

He lists homosexuals, transvestites, transsexuals, pedophiles, NEA, feminists, NAACP, seniors, NRA and gun-control side, pro-Israel, pro-choice and Wicca—while the church (78% of America in his figure) is silenced.
Who does he say can lobby when the church cannot?

and not be contrary to public policy. In our generation we can’t be contrary to homosexuals, the unborn, illegal aliens, the capital punishment, right to bear arms, over-taxation, witchcraft—if the community and its public policy, we cannot contest it. All right. And it says absolutely no political lobbying or no involvement in campaign, and they use the excuse of the separation of church and state with the definition of church that they have. Now who can lobby and campaign? Well, homosexuals can, transvestites—those that dress like the opposite sex—transsexuals—those that change their sex—pedophiles—those that have sex with children—the National Education Association, the feminists, the NAACP, the seniors, the NRA and the other side wanting gun control. They can lobby. Pro-Israel or Jews can lobby. Pro-choice can lobby. Wicca or witchcraft can lobby. But not the church. These other people can be involved in campaign, speak about their candidates, but not the church, who is 78% of the population of America, and they are silenced by the restriction and controls of the 501(c)(3). Now we’re going to take a look at government policy, public policy benefits. What are the benefits of this public policy that the government puts upon the community? Well, it gives freedom to make harmful choices.
What results of harmful public policy does he cite?

Destroyed lives: 50% with STDs, 26,000 homosexual AIDS deaths a year, 450,000 tobacco deaths, 88,000 alcohol deaths and millions injured—policies putting birth control and abortion above self-control.
What results of harmful public policy does he cite?

And of course the results of these kind of public policies is destroyed lives. 50% of people in America have a sexually transmitted disease. 26,000 homosexuals are killed by AIDS every year. 450,000 people die from tobacco, and only 18% of Americans smoke. 88,000 people die from alcohol-related deaths and 4 million from alcohol-related injuries are hurt, and yet only 50% of Americans drink alcohol. So the public policy and the results are disastrous. They put abortion, birth control, above self-control. Birth control—
How does he contrast same-sex marriage with science?

He says science knows marriage is man-woman producing and raising kids; homosexuals cannot have kids naturally; no homosexual gene; AIDS stats versus civil-rights framing; evolution taught, creation censored.
How does he contrast same-sex marriage with science?

we just need to control ourselves. They put women’s rights over the scientific babies’ rights. Science has declared life begins at conception, but they don’t care. They put same-sex marriage above the Bible and science marriage. Even science knows that marriage is between a man and a woman because they can produce kids and they commit to a lifetime commitment to raise those kids and protect those kids. Homosexuals cannot have kids naturally; they have to take your kids. That’s science. But who cares about science or the Bible in America today? Same-sex lifestyle instead of a scientific fact they were not born that way—science has found there’s no homosexual gene. Homosexual civil rights versus science stats: AIDS kill 26,000 a year as we said before. And they put the unprovable evolution
What is the Bible’s definition of church?

Called-out assembly of Jesus’ followers—not a building or corporation. Acts 7:48 / Isaiah 66:1: God does not dwell in temples made with hands; 1 Corinthians 3:9 and 1 Peter 2:5: people are God’s building and living stones.
What is the Bible’s definition of church?

with Bible creation censored. They don’t like any opposition. Now let’s go and look at the Bible’s definition of the church and see how the Bible defines the church. First of all the word used in the Bible for church just simply means assembling—called out to assemble together. So a church is followers of Jesus and His word that come together, that congregate together. Church has nothing to do with a physical building. It has nothing to do with a corporation. A corporation is a company or group of people authorized to act as a single unit and recognized in civil law. The church is not a corporation. It is not a physical building. Acts 7:48 says, and is quoting from Isaiah 66:1, the Most High God does not dwell in temples, buildings made with hands. In Isaiah He explains that heaven is My throne, earth is My footstool—where are you going to put Me? I’m big. And so the Bible doesn’t back up our government’s definition of a church as a building where people congregate together. People can congregate for Christ anywhere—in the park, at a home or wherever—not some special building. 1 Corinthians 3:9 makes it plain: you, the followers of Christ, are God’s building. 1 Peter 2:5: you as living stones are built up a spiritual house to offer spiritual sacrifices. It is the people coming together that God is working with to build His spiritual house. He lives in the congregation of His people, and the people come together to offer up spiritual sacrifices—
What is the Bible’s definition of church?

Acts 7:48: “However, the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands, as the prophet says: Isaiah 66:1: Thus says the LORD: “Heaven is My throne, And earth is My footstool. Where is the house that you will build Me? And where is the place of My rest? 1 Corinthians 3:9: For we are God’s fellow workers; you are God’s field, you are God’s building. 1 Peter 2:5: you also, as living stones, are being built up a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
Is the church mainly a charitable welfare organization?
No. From Mark 14:6 Jesus prioritized the woman’s anointing over selling perfume for the poor—Jesus is the primary focus; aid has criteria (1 Timothy 5), not just handing out stuff.
Is the church mainly a charitable welfare organization?

not carnal, not fleshly offerings to God but spiritual ones. Continuing with the Bible definition of a church: the church is not a charitable or welfare organization. And Jesus made this clear when the woman with the alabaster box came—very expensive perfume—and anointed Jesus, and Judas and some others there go, this is ridiculous, this is a waste of money, this could have been sold and given to the poor and help the poor. And what was Jesus’ reply to these people? Leave her alone. Mark 14:6: leave this woman alone; she’s done a good work for Me to anoint My body for burial. You always have the poor with you, and whenever you want to you can do them good, you can help them, but Me you don’t always have with you. So in the church Jesus is the primary and high-ranking focus of the church. The first priority of spiritual sacrifices is ministering unto the presence of Jesus—not giving medical, food or clothing to the poor. Matthew 18:20 makes it very clear: where two or three are gathered in My name—see, the gathering of the people that follow Christ and His word—I am there in the midst. The important factor, the high priority factor when a church comes together is to bring the presence of Jesus Christ. The criteria for church aid by the way is found in 1 Timothy 5:8: if anyone does not provide for his own and especially for his immediate family he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever. No widow may be put on the list of widows unless she is over 60 years of age, had been faithful to her husband while he was alive and known for good deeds such as bringing up children, helping those that were in trouble and so forth. There were qualifications—not just handing out stuff. The church—continuing with the Bible’s definition of a church—we found that the church is an assembly of followers, and when they assemble together they assemble together to pray, to worship, to bless or speak good of God and one another, to thank—tell God that we appreciate Him—and to praise Jesus. So prayer, as the Bible says according to His will, is another spiritual sacrifice that we do in the church.
Is the church mainly a charitable welfare organization?

Mark 14:6: But Jesus said, “Let her alone. Why do you trouble her? She has done a good work for Me. Matthew 18:20: For where two or three are gathered together in My name, I am there in the midst of them.” 1 Timothy 5:8: But if anyone does not provide for his own, and especially for those of his household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
What is the house of God for?
Mark 11:17: house of prayer for all nations, not merchandise. Hebrews 13:15 and John 4:23: continual praise and true worship; Psalm 22:3: He inhabits praises.
What is the house of God for?

Mark 11:17: My house shall be called a house of prayer for all nations—Chinese, Australia, Russians, whoever, homosexuals, humanists, atheists, all nations, all people—but you have made it a den of thieves. And to America, just like then in the New Testament time they made the house a house of merchandise. The house of God is not for making money and merchandising; it’s for prayer— very limited in American churches. Hebrews 13:15: by Jesus let us offer continually the sacrifice of praise to God, that is the fruit of our lips giving thanks to His name. See, the New Testament church is a church that comes together to boast and brag and honor Jesus Christ and thank Him for His blood and His goodness. John 4:23: true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father is seeking such to worship Him. So when the church comes together they adore Him—not only praise Him but they adore Him, they love Him. Psalm 34:1: I will bless the Lord at all times—no matter what condition I’m in I’ll speak good of the Lord, I’ll speak good of His word, I’ll speak good of the church. His praise shall continually be in my mouth. And Psalm 22:3 says He inhabits the praises of His people.
What is the house of God for?

Mark 11:17: Then He taught, saying to them, “Is it not written, ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer for all nations’? But you have made it a ‘den of thieves.’ ” Hebrews 13:15: Therefore by Him let us continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name. John 4:23: But the hour is coming, and now is, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth; for the Father is seeking such to worship Him. Psalm 22:3: But You are holy, Enthroned in the praises of Israel.
How is the church the pillar of truth and a disciple-maker?

John 8:32 and 17:17: continue in the word; 1 Timothy 3:15: pillar of truth. Matthew 28:19 and Luke 24:47: make disciples of all nations and preach repentance and forgiveness—including to atheists and humanists.
How is the church the pillar of truth and a disciple-maker?

Continuing with the Bible’s definition of a church: the fourth description of God’s church—an assembly of followers of the Bible and Jesus that speaks and lives truth. John 8:32: Jesus said if you continue in My word you are My disciples indeed, and you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free. Chapter 17 verse 17 of John: God’s word is truth. So the followers speak the truth—not their opinions, not psychology and philosophies but the truth. 1 Timothy 3:15: these things I write to you so you may know how to conduct yourself in the house of God. He just gave us what we’re to do when we come together. The house of God which is the church—they’re synonymous terms—the church of the living God. His presence is there when we congregate together, and the church is the pillar and support of truth. We back up truth, not opinions. We back up truth, not lies. Matthew 28:19: Jesus said go make disciples of all nations, teaching them to observe all things that I have commanded you—not only to teach them but emphasize that they practice them. And all nations includes the atheists, the humanists, the homosexuals, the hedonists, the religionists, and any nationality that you can think of. Luke 24:47: Jesus said repentance and remission, forgiveness of sins, should be preached in His name among all nations. That is a primary message of the church: that people need to turn from sin and that’s how you give forgiveness.
How is the church the pillar of truth and a disciple-maker?

John 8:32: And you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.” 1 Timothy 3:15: but if I am delayed, I write so that you may know how you ought to conduct yourself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth. Matthew 28:19: Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, Luke 24:47: and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in His name to all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.
What speech gifts should build the church?

From 1 Corinthians 12–14 and Ephesians 5:19 he lists wisdom, knowledge, prophecy (edify/exhort/comfort), tongues with interpretation, revelation, teaching, psalms, hymns and spiritual songs—by the Spirit, not intellect.
What speech gifts should build the church?

Humanists, their followers and humanist churches don’t preach Jesus’s truth to turn immoral people to morality. Instead they teach immoral behavior is acceptable and they sentence people to preventable deaths, physical harm such as sexually transmitted diseases and other harms. And we need to preach repentance for forgiveness of sin every church. There are eight sources of speaking—and I left out prayer because most prayer is us talking to our God personally. 1 Corinthians 12:8: a gift is given to one by the Spirit the word of wisdom—it’s an ability to speak the word of wisdom. You hardly ever hear that in the church world today. Hasn’t been restored yet in my opinion. To another by the Spirit is given the word of knowledge—they actually get into the word and God opens the word up and they have knowledge of the word. To another, prophecy—and this word prophecy is edification, exhortation, comfort. It is not the office of a prophet to predict the future and it comes to pass. He’s using prophecy—speaking by the inspiration of God—to build the church. Tongues: to another tongues. And this is a big argument in America today, but tongues are Bible languages whether they are earthly or whether they’re heavenly. And Paul said if there’s no interpretation you can’t do it in the church because there’s no understanding. So he says to another’s given interpretation. Then in 14:6 he says what shall I profit you unless I speak to you either by revelation or teaching. Revelation is the uncovering of a truth revealed to you. Ephesians 5:19: speaking to yourselves in psalms, hymns and spiritual songs. See, music: hymns. Psalms is singing—singing Scripture. Hymns is a song of truth put together. And music and singing is very important. They carry a heavy weight in the New Testament church. And all this is to be done by the Spirit, not human intellect. You can’t go and get these things by human intellect. Teaching is basically what most of the church world is doing. You hardly ever hear a word of wisdom, a word of knowledge. I know what they call knowledge, but that’s not what this is. Teaching is basically what we’re doing—and they don’t even have the credentials of a teacher, they just teach. So to answer our question at the beginning: what are the benefits of a New Testament tax-exempt church service?
What speech gifts should build the church?

1 Corinthians 12:8: for to one is given the word of wisdom through the Spirit, to another the word of knowledge through the same Spirit, Ephesians 5:19: speaking to one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord,
What should each person bring when the church gathers?
1 Corinthians 14:26: each contributes song, teaching, tongue, revelation or interpretation for edification—not primarily food, clothing, medicine or 12-step programs.
What should each person bring when the church gathers?

1 Corinthians 14:26: when you come together—see, here we are, the church comes together—each of you, see, all of us, come with something to contribute: a song, song music, maybe your instrument play, maybe you’re a singer, whatever, maybe you’re just in the congregation and you lift up your voice and sing; a teaching; a tongue, a language; a revelation. He’s given five of the eight things listed here. And the other has an interpretation—come be ready to interpret a language. And let all things be done to edification—building, encouraging the people of God. Not when you come have food for the hungry, clothing for the naked, medicine for the sick and a 12-step recovery program for those who have gone through traumatic things.
What should each person bring when the church gathers?

1 Corinthians 14:26: How is it then, brethren? Whenever you come together, each of you has a psalm, has a teaching, has a tongue, has a revelation, has an interpretation. Let all things be done for edification.
How does that kind of service benefit America?

If all prophesy, an unbeliever is convinced and convicted, secrets revealed, falls and worships—encounter with Jesus. That spiritual awakening benefits community higher than anything else; tax exemption matters because it’s Jesus’s church.
How does that kind of service benefit America?

He didn’t say to bring that. 1 Corinthians 14:24: if all prophesy—speak and sing by the inspiration of the Spirit—and an unbeliever, unlearned, comes into the service, he is convinced by all of these things, he is convicted by all of these things—the songs, the prophecies, everything that’s going on. The secrets of his heart are revealed to him, and falling down on his face without being told to he will worship God and report God is truly in the midst of that church. Why? Because this unbeliever or unlearned person had an encounter with Him and God spoke to him what needed to be changed in his life. And that benefits America and a community higher than anything can—a spiritual awakening, a spiritual encounter with the person of Jesus Christ because God’s people come to bring something to contribute. New Testament church tax exempt benefits. All right, there’s an argument whether the church should be tax exempt or not. And the church is going to be a church whether we get tax exemption or not. But why is it important that our founding fathers and up to this present time gave a tax exemption to the church? Well, first of all it’s Jesus’s church
How does that kind of service benefit America?

1 Corinthians 14:24-25: But if all prophesy, and an unbeliever or an uninformed person comes in, he is convinced by all, he is convicted by all. And thus the secrets of his heart are revealed; and so, falling down on his face, he will worship God and report that God is truly among you.
Why tax exemption and the First Amendment?

Acts 5:39: if of God you cannot overthrow it lest you fight God—regulating by tax fights God. Separation was to keep government out of the church, not Christians out of government. Truth saves costs and gives eternal life; helping the poor is on the side.
Why tax exemption and the First Amendment?

and He can’t be restrained by tax or immoral laws. Acts 5:39: if it be of God, if anything be of God, you cannot overthrow it lest you be found fighting against God. And it’s God’s church, and if you try to regulate the church by taxation or tax benefits you’re going to be fighting against God directly Himself. And the separation of church and state was instituted by our government—the First Amendment—to keep government out of the affairs of the church. It wasn’t to keep Christians out of the affairs of government. It teaches Bible truths. A New Testament tax-exempt church—a real New Testament—there’s a lot of not-real New Testament churches—and truths protect people from preventable deaths, physical harm, mental harm, prevent emotional harm, thus saving families and government billions of dollars in medical, legal costs, police costs, criminal and immorality of all kinds of costs every year, every year. So besides that we give people eternal life, which is to know Jesus and God, and on the side we do help the poor.
Why tax exemption and the First Amendment?
Acts 5:39: but if it is of God, you cannot overthrow it—lest you even be found to fight against God.”
What does 501(c)(3) emphasize about a church?
He stresses people congregated to give aid to the community as the key federal accent.
May a 501(c)(3) church lobby or campaign?
He says absolutely no political lobbying or campaign involvement under their rules.
What percent of Americans does he say are the church?
He says 78% of the population, silenced by 501(c)(3) controls.
When does he say science says life begins?
At conception—yet he says women’s rights are put over the baby’s rights.
Is the church a physical building?
No. God does not dwell in temples made with hands; people are God’s building and living stones.
Did Jesus dismiss helping the poor?
No—He said you always have the poor and can help them whenever you want, but prioritized anointing Him then.
Who could be on the widow list in 1 Timothy 5?
Over 60, faithful to her husband, known for good deeds—not just handing out aid.
When may tongues be used in church?
He says if there’s no interpretation you can’t do it in church because there’s no understanding.
What happens if an unbeliever enters a prophesying service?
Convinced and convicted, heart secrets revealed, falls and worships, reporting God is truly among them.
What was separation of church and state for, in his view?
To keep government out of the church’s affairs—not to keep Christians out of government’s affairs.

items.t: How Do We Know That We Know God?
items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from John 17:1–4 that eternal life is knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ, that only God gives it, and that we receive it in proportion to a hearing ear.…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from John 17:1–4 that eternal life is knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ, that only God gives it, and that we receive it in proportion to a hearing ear. He explains how to know that we know God: the Spirit within us, keeping His commandments, being born again, and growing in the word.
What does “the hour has come” mean in John 17:1-4?
