If you gather together and you acknowledge Christ, his presence will come. That doesn’t mean your doctrine’s right. I said, “Father Fred, Jesus said that the spirit would pour out of us.” I said, ‘You haven’t got the baptism of the Holy Spirit. You just experienced the first time the presence of God. And there’s a big difference. Hallelujah. And that’s what Jesus is telling his apostles. Now, there is some spirit-filled churches that believe if you don’t have the baptism of the Holy Spirit with speaking in tongues, you’re not saved and you’re going to hell.
What is the difference between God’s presence with us and the baptism of the Holy Spirit?
Matthew 18:20: For where two or three are gathered together in My name, I am there in the midst of them.”
Do you have to speak in tongues to be saved?

He says some spirit-filled churches believe if you don’t speak in tongues you’re not saved, and tells of parents who told a daughter she was going to hell for that. He says “the Bible says not all speak in tongues,” and that in Acts 2 they spoke in languages while in Acts 4 they “spoke in their own language.” He says the parents stuck with their church doctrine over Scripture because they didn’t take time to find out.
Do you have to speak in tongues to be saved?

And I’ve had to deal with these people. I’ve had to deal with parents, good parents, that told their child, they had two children. One got filled with the Holy Ghost and spoke in tongues, the other one didn’t. And they told this other daughter that she was going to hell. And I knew that girl. She was a fine Christian girl. And I’m pretty sure Mr. Barnes knows who I’m talking about. And I had to— you know, I had to deal with this thing. I can’t have this girl going through life thinking she’s going to hell because she don’t speak in tongues when the Bible says not all speak in tongues. My God, church. It doesn’t take a genius to figure this out, does it? Amen. In Acts chapter 2, yes, they spoke in languages. In Acts 4, they didn’t. They spoke in their own language. They didn’t speak in other languages. Are you with me? And that couple, as tremendous a couple as they was, and the guy was a successful businessman and they were very educated and knowledgeable, they stuck with their church doctrine over scripture because they didn’t take time to find out and get the understanding. See, that’s what Paul meant when he— or Peter meant when he said, “Unstable and unlearned people, twist the scriptures and bring destruction.” But I finally got to the young lady. Hallelujah. And she’s the one that needed to hear.
Do you have to speak in tongues to be saved?

1 Corinthians 12:30: Do all have gifts of healings? Do all speak with tongues? Do all interpret? Acts 2:4: And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance. Acts 4:31: And when they had prayed, the place where they were assembled together was shaken; and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they spoke the word of God with boldness. 2 Peter 3:16: as also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things, in which are some things hard to understand, which untaught and unstable people twist to their own destruction, as they do also the rest of the Scriptures.
What does it mean to be born again? (John 3:5, John 1:12)

He says evangelicals, fundamentalists and spirit-filled churches agree God must be involved in salvation, not “head knowledge” or “getting your name on a church,” citing “you must be born again.” He says God is involved as you respond: if we confess our sins He is faithful to forgive and cleanse us, and John 1:12 gives power to “as many as receive him.” He says you must admit you’re wrong: “That’s the formula.”
What does it mean to be born again? (John 3:5, John 1:12)

And when mom and dad’s wrong, they’re just what? Wrong. Now this is what evangelicals, fundamentalists, spirit-filled churches, they all believe that God must be involved in your salvation. Can’t just be head knowledge. Can’t just be, you know, getting your name on a church and joining some group. God has to be involved. And we all use this scripture that Jesus said, you must be born again. Unless a man is born of water and of the spirit, he can’t enter the kingdom of God. You see, this is what separates Protestants from other Protestants. And this really separates the Protestants from other Protestants from Catholics because Catholics have the tendency to believe because they join that church and they do the rituals. They’re going to heaven. And folks, you got to be born again. That’s what the scripture says. And that born again, you got to be born of the spirit. See, God’s got to be involved in your salvation. And he’s involved as you what? Respond. See, if we confess our sins, he’s what? Faithful and just to forgive our sins and cleanse us from all unrighteousness. Not just forgive us, but cleanse us, wash the sin away. He will set us free from sin. And John 1:12 says, “To as many as receive him, to them gave he power.” Now, this is God coming and dwelling with us. This is not the baptism of the Holy Ghost. He will give them power that receive him to become sons of God. See, sons of God, when you know the interpretation of the sons of God in the Bible, the sons of God live right. They live holy. And so he empowers us to keep the word is what he’s saying. So when you invite Jesus, that initial presence of God comes. Hallelujah. And so this is what being born again is. You admit you’re a sinner. If you [unclear] admit you’re a sinner, God can’t cleanse you. He can’t forgive you. You got to admit you’re wrong. Even Christians that need areas of their life straighten out have to admit they’re wrong. That’s the formula. Hallelujah. Then after we get saved, if we seek him and we seek the word, we will grow in the word.
What does it mean to be born again? (John 3:5, John 1:12)

John 3:5: Jesus answered, “Most assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God. 1 John 1:9: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. John 1:12: But as many as received Him, to them He gave the right to become children of God, to those who believe in His name:
What is the conclusion? How do we know God?

He says a time and season has come: Jesus has already died for the sins of the world, we must confess we are sinners and come to Him for cleansing, and “No one can save you but Jesus.” He says this is the season to possess eternal life and to know God, in proportion to our hearing ear: “You have out of God what you put into God.” He says we know God by the Spirit in us and our hearing ear to keep His word.
What is the conclusion? How do we know God?

See, desire the sincere milk of the word that you may grow by that. You’ve got to have the word to grow and you got to have the water, the spirit to grow. And unless you go to church and get in Bible studies and you’re not going to grow. So, you got to take heed what you hear. 1 Peter 1:23, born again by the word of God, which lives and abides forever. You see, we’re born again by the word of God. Remember Jesus said, “My word is spirit. The spirit is spirit. The word is spirit. All this is spirit.” All this is God’s involvement with us, folks. And he promised this is the season. You live in it. And if you’ll respond to me, I will respond to you. And if you respond more, I will respond more. So what’s the conclusion? There’s a time and season that has come. Jesus has already died on the cross for the sins of the world. But we have to confess we are sinners and come to him for cleansing. No one can save you but Jesus. All right? And if you will admit and come to him, invite him into your life, he will back it up and he’ll come to you, forgive you, cleanse you, and live in you. He will give you eternal life. This is the season to possess eternal life. Not only to live with him forever when you die, but to know him. This is the season you can know God. And we are given these promises and other promises in proportion to our hearing ear. That’s the conclusion. You have out of God what you put into God. That’s what Jesus said. We know. We know God by the spirit in us and our hearing ear to keep his word. We know we should be honest. We know we should be truthful. We know we should not be doing wrong. So, we know God is in us cuz he’s putting that in us. He’s compelling us. He is causing us to rise up. Rise up, son. We heard it Friday night. Rise up, son. And finish the race.
What is the conclusion? How do we know God?

1 Peter 2:2: as newborn babes, desire the pure milk of the word, that you may grow thereby, 1 Peter 1:23: having been born again, not of corruptible seed but incorruptible, through the word of God which lives and abides forever,
He says “Glorify means honored.” He says God honored the Son with the ability to give His life, and no one could take it.
What authority does he say Jesus was given before creation?

He says Jesus has authority over everybody and every nation and every language on the earth: “He is the one running the kingdoms.” He says this was given to Him before creation, and He created everything.
Can anyone on earth give you eternal life?
He says no: “There is no one on earth that can give you eternal life.” He says “Only Jesus Christ can give you eternal life.”
What is the difference between enlightenment and eternal life?
He says “we’re not looking for enlightenment. We’re looking for eternal life.” He says eternal life is defined as knowing the only true God.
What does he say the Lord of the harvest can do?

He says the Lord of the harvest has the knowledge and authority to plant the seed and make it grow, cut it down, thresh it and bake it for the master’s table. He says “He’s the one that can do the job. We are just messengers.”
What was the can illustration about?

He opens a can labeled “Organic pumpkin” that looks like tomatoes, and says “too many of us do not dig deeper and find out if what preachers are telling us is the truth.” He says we need to put time into what we hear.
Who does he say gets more from God?
He says it is not faith, grace, a big church or a little church: “Whosoever has ears to hear, more will be given.”
Is obeying God just my own effort?
He says no: “It’s him providing the empowerment, the desire, the compelling to please him.” He says when he makes a mistake, that compelling picks him up and “I don’t stay in my mistake.”
What does he say happens when a Christian keeps messing up in an area?
He says the Spirit “compels me to repent” and ask God to cleanse and free him, and he gets back up and tackles the sin again. He says one day “the spirit has given me authority over it.”
Are the Comforter and the Spirit of truth the same?
He says “The comforter and the spirit of truth, the Holy Ghost, the Holy Spirit’s all the same thing.”
Does he say Christians believe in three gods?
He says no: “Us Christians do not believe in three gods. We believe in one.” He says “Make no mistake, we worship one God.”
How does he say we grow after we are saved?

He says we “desire the sincere milk of the word that you may grow,” and you’ve got to have the word and the Spirit. He says “unless you go to church and get in Bible studies and you’re not going to grow.”

items.t: How Supreme is the U.S. Supreme Court?
items.d: In “How Supreme is the U.S. Supreme Court?”, Pastor David G. Kincer reviews Article III and the Judiciary Act of 1789, then walks through landmark reversals—Fugitive Slave Laws, Dred Scott, and…
items.ser: Clarity on Crucial Choices · Full sermon
p: In “How Supreme is the U.S. Supreme Court?”, Pastor David G. Kincer reviews Article III and the Judiciary Act of 1789, then walks through landmark reversals—Fugitive Slave Laws, Dred Scott, and separate-but-equal—as decisions that were not so supreme. He argues religious sects became their own worst enemy in Bible-in-schools fights, cites Stone v. Graham (1980) that the Bible may be studied in history and ethics and that the state may not establish secularism, and calls Catholics, Protestants, Jews and humanists to unite and teach Bible morality.
What is the U.S. Supreme Court’s purpose under the Constitution?

From Article III he says all judicial power and justice are given to the Supreme Court, crimes are tried by jury in the state committed, and treason requires two witnesses—which he calls a Bible statement.
What is the U.S. Supreme Court’s purpose under the Constitution?

We welcome you in our continued search for clarity on crucial choices. Remember we can make bad choices, we can make better choices, or we can make the best choices. And today we’re going to ask ourselves: how supreme is the United States Supreme Court? How supreme is the United States Supreme Court? We’re going to look at its purpose. Article III, sections one through three of the United States Constitution. All judicial power has been given to the Supreme Court. All legal, all justice has been given into the hands of the Supreme Court of the United States. It also says there that the trial of all crimes will be by jury in the state committed, so everyone has a right to a jury trial. Treason conviction has to be on the testimony of two witnesses. That is a Bible statement.
What is the U.S. Supreme Court’s purpose under the Constitution?
Deuteronomy 17:6: Whoever is deserving of death shall be put to death on the testimony of two or three witnesses; he shall not be put to death on the testimony of one witness.
What did the Judiciary Act of 1789 give the Court?
He says Congress gave the Court power to judge whether a law or executive action is constitutional, under a system of 13 circuit and 94 district courts, as the highest authority on legality.
What did the Judiciary Act of 1789 give the Court?

The Judiciary Act of 1789: two witnesses, not circumstantial evidence. Circumstantial evidence is not a witness. In the Judiciary Act in 1789, Congress gave the Supreme Court power to judge a law or an executive action whether it is constitutional or not. They have that authority. Now you must understand that under the Supreme Court there are 13 circuit courts, and there are 94 district courts. And so the Supreme Court—supreme means the highest in authority—the Supreme Court holds the power of legality in the United States of America and the Constitution
What does he say about Fugitive Slave Laws and Dred Scott?

He calls them not-too-supreme reversals: citizens had to return fugitive slaves, helpers were jailed and fined, then the 14th Amendment reversed that; Dred Scott held African Americans could not be citizens.
What does he say about Fugitive Slave Laws and Dred Scott?

that backs it up. Now we’re going to look at some not-too-supreme court landmark reversals. We find here that the Supreme Court made some decision that wasn’t so supreme, like the Fugitive Slave Laws 1789 and 1850, where fugitive slaves—citizens were forced to return the slaves. People that helped runaways would be in prison and jailed and fined, and policemen were rewarded monetarily for capturing them. And then it was reversed by the 14th Amendment. Dred Scott was an ex-slave who was freed and they tried to put him back into slavery, and so he went to the Supreme Court, and the Supreme Court said African Americans, both free and slave, could not be citizens.
What was “equal but separate,” and was it reversed?

He says in 1896 the Court approved separate-but-equal for buses, trains, neighborhoods and restaurants; about 60 years later in 1954 the Court disapproved it—an embarrassment that it both approved and reversed.
What was “equal but separate,” and was it reversed?

And they defined blacks as a subordinate and inferior class of being, and slaves were property with no rights. Then in 1896—and that also was overthrown by the 14th Amendment—in 1896, equal but separate was approved by the Supreme Court. Blacks could not ride in the same area on the bus, the train; they couldn’t live in the same neighborhood, couldn’t eat in the same restaurants and all that, but they had freedom and they were equal but they were separate. And then we’ll move on—that was reversed, by the way, 60 years later in 1954 by the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court approved it; the Supreme Court disapproved it—an embarrassment to the Supreme Court. 1840s: public education came in, tax-supported, and they taught a Protestant
How does he say Bible morality left public schools?

He says 1840s tax-supported schools taught Protestant morality by Bible, hymns and McGuffey Readers; Ohio’s 1872 court said “religion” did not mean Christian and barred Bible and hymns; an 1875 Protestant amendment to block tax money to religious schools barely failed.
How does he say Bible morality left public schools?

morality by way of the Bible, hymns and McGuffey Readers till ten years later the New York board of educators rejected it. In the 1850s in Ohio, the state Supreme Court in 1872 declared that the word “religion” in the Constitution did not mean Christian, and they declared that no Bible reading, no hymns or sectarian exercises were allowed in public schools. In 1875 they tried to pass an amendment to the Constitution—and these were Protestants that presented this amendment—that no tax money could go to support a religious school, a religious sect of any kind. And the reason they did that is the Protestants didn’t like the Catholics at the time. They wanted the Catholics to be in public school to where they could give them the Protestant view of morality. And so they tried to pass this amendment and it barely, barely failed.
What is a “sect,” and why does the word matter?
He says a sect is a group within a group; many states still barred tax money to any religious sect or parochial school, and religious sects became their own worst enemy.
What is a “sect,” and why does the word matter?

But it did fail. But a lot of states still picked up the amendment and put it in their state constitution, that no tax money could go to any religious sect. And they used the word “sect,” and that’s an important word, because a sect is a group within a group. And they couldn’t use any tax money for the support of parochial or religious private schools anywhere. And so we have given you some Supreme Court decisions that were not supreme, and we’re going to work more on this school one. And we’re going to find that religious sects are their own worst enemy. The group within religion are really our own worst enemy. For instance, in Wisconsin in 1890,
How did Catholics get the King James Bible out of public schools?

He says after Protestant persecution in Wisconsin around 1890, Catholics went to court against the KJV and got it out, wanting the Catholic Bible; Mormons and Jews wanted theirs—groups fighting over non-essentials, followed by other states into 1910.
How did Catholics get the King James Bible out of public schools?

the Catholics had been persecuted by the Protestants—their churches burned, their properties burned, violently and brutally bullied around. And so the Catholics, they went to the Supreme Court and said we don’t want the King James Bible in public schools. All right. And they got the King James Bible out of public schools. They wanted the Catholic Bible in. The Mormons of course want in the Mormon Bible. The Jews wanted the Jewish Bible. So here we are, a group in a group fighting over some non-essential things. Nebraska followed 1903, Kansas 1904, South Dakota, Washington, Louisiana, Iowa. Illinois is in 1910. Then we move up to 1947,
When does he say “separation of church and state” entered school cases?

He points to a 1947 ruling upholding public transport reimbursements to parents, where that phrase came in, then 1962–63 rulings making Bible, prayer, hymns and sectarian exercises in public schools unconstitutional.
When does he say “separation of church and state” entered school cases?

when the Supreme Court ruled that the state bill to give public transportation of all students was constitutional and permissible because the reimbursements were given to the parents and not to the schools. And this is where they brought in the statement of separation of church and state. And then in 1962, as you know, and in 1963, the Supreme Court declared that the Bible, prayer, hymns, tax support, any sectarian exercise in public schools was unconstitutional. So they overruled something that had been going on for a long time.
How are religious people their own worst enemy in court?

Between 1800 and 1920 he counts Sabbath, church-property, prayer/Bible, aid-to-schools and blasphemy cases, and says the biggest fights were Catholics versus Protestants carrying Europe’s war into American courts.
How are religious people their own worst enemy in court?

But as I said, us religious people are our own worst enemy. Between 1800 and 1920 there were 87 recorded Sabbath closing work law cases. They went to court over whether you could work on the Sabbath or not, and if you could really make a legal agreement on the Sabbath or not, and such ridiculous details. There were 112 church property cases. There were 18 public school prayer and Bible reading cases. There were 15 public aid to religious school cases, and 22 blasphemy cases. And the biggest cases is the Catholics versus the Protestants—they’re carrying their war from Europe over to here in the courts.
What sectarian issues does he say hit the courts?

He names plural marriage, Sabbath, blasphemy, Southern denominations splitting over slavery, speaking in tongues, once-saved-always-saved, flag salute, and bans on dating or marrying outside your race—then turns to Stone v. Graham (1980).
What sectarian issues does he say hit the courts?

Some of the issues were plural marriages, Sabbath violations, blasphemies. Remember the Southern Baptist was started because they approved of slavery—so was the Southern Methodist, and so did the Southern Catholics. Most of the southern states were predominantly Catholic or Anglican at that time, and they separated from the northern denominations on the side of slavery. There was also speaking in tongues, once saved you’re all set always saved, don’t salute the flag, you can’t date or marry another person out of your race. And so the courts have all these sectarian issues hitting them. But you need to understand that the Supreme Court approves the Bible in public schools and public places. 1980 court case, Supreme Court case between Stone and Graham.
What did Stone v. Graham say about using the Bible?
Quoting a 1963 case, he says the 1980 Court declared the Bible may constitutionally be used in appropriate study of history, civilization, ethics/Bible morality and comparative religion.
What did Stone v. Graham say about using the Bible?

And they quoted out of a previous Supreme Court case in 1963, that the Bible may constitutionally be used in an appropriate study of history, used in the study of civilization, used in the study of ethics, Bible morality, used in the study of comparative religion, or such like. The Supreme Court declared that in the 1980 Stone versus Graham Supreme Court case. And they also made a statement from another court case.
May the state establish a religion of secularism?

He reads that the state may not establish secularism by showing hostility to religion and preferring unbelievers over believers, and says the 1980 case confirmed Bible study is approved in public schools and places.
May the state establish a religion of secularism?

The statement they made was this, and it’s very important for us to understand: the state may not establish a religion of secularism in the sense of favorably opposing or showing hostility to religion, thus preferring those who believe in no religion over those who do believe in a religion. This is the Supreme Court, the highest court, the highest authority in America over legal issues, speaking. And in that 1980 court case they confirmed that the Bible has approval to be studied and taught in public school and in public places
Is the Bible still “separate” like Plessy’s equal-but-separate?

He compares allowed-but-separated Bible teaching to African Americans under separate-but-equal, and says the Bible must be integrated back into public schools if the Court is the high authority; he asks all groups to unite on Bible morality.
Is the Bible still “separate” like Plessy’s equal-but-separate?

on the subject of history and on the subject of ethics or morality. But like African Americans with their free and equal but separate issue—the Supreme Court said they were free and equal but separate—the Bible is allowed by the Supreme Court but the Supreme Court still separates it, and it must be integrated back into the public school system if it is the high authority in the land. All Catholics, Protestants, Jews and humanists and their followers: will you agree with the Supreme Court and unite and teach America to turn back to Bible morality? The destructive facts of immoral behavior are shouting out: America,
What is his closing call to America?

He says get back to Bible morality and save people, especially children, from preventable deaths and harms, because the Supreme Court agrees Bible morality ethics can be taught publicly and in public schools.
What is his closing call to America?

get back to Bible morality. Save people, especially children, from preventable deaths and preventable harms, because the Supreme Court agrees that Bible morality ethics can be taught publicly and in public schools.
What does he say about jury trial and treason?
He says all crimes are tried by jury in the state committed, and treason conviction needs two witnesses—a Bible statement.
How many circuit and district courts does he name?
He says there are 13 circuit courts and 94 district courts under the Supreme Court.
What did Dred Scott hold, according to him?
He says the Court held African Americans, free and slave, could not be citizens, and defined blacks as a subordinate inferior class and slaves as property.
When does he say separate-but-equal was reversed?
He says about 60 years after 1896, in 1954, the Supreme Court disapproved what it had approved.
What were McGuffey Readers used for?
He says early tax-supported schools taught Protestant morality by the Bible, hymns and McGuffey Readers.
Why did Protestants try an 1875 constitutional amendment?
He says they didn’t like Catholics and wanted them in public school under a Protestant view of morality, barring tax money to religious schools; it barely failed.
Why was student transportation upheld in 1947?
He says reimbursements went to parents, not schools, and that case brought in “separation of church and state.”
How many religious court cases does he count from 1800–1920?
He cites 87 Sabbath cases, 112 church property, 18 prayer/Bible, 15 aid to religious schools, and 22 blasphemy cases.
In what subjects may the Bible be used, per Stone v. Graham as he reads it?
He lists history, civilization, ethics/Bible morality and comparative religion.
What hostility to religion does the Court forbid?
He says the state may not establish secularism by opposing or showing hostility to religion and preferring those who believe in no religion.

items.t: How to Have No Fail Success
items.d: In “How to Have No Fail Success,” Pastor David G. Kincer walks through the new covenant promises in Ezekiel 11, 36 and 37 — one heart, a new spirit, a heart of flesh, cleansing by the word, and the covenant of…
p: In “How to Have No Fail Success,” Pastor David G. Kincer walks through the new covenant promises in Ezekiel 11, 36 and 37 — one heart, a new spirit, a heart of flesh, cleansing by the word, and the covenant of peace that makes believers priests — and shows where the New Testament says the same. He teaches that God says “I will” and does the changing, while we must respond, seek Him and apply ourselves. He closes with accounts of early martyrs and the deathbed words of well-known unbelievers.
What is the new covenant promise in Ezekiel 11, and why should we know it?

He says we should know the covenant, even have it memorized, because “this is powerful.” In Ezekiel 11 God says “I will gather you,” and he ties this to the church being the called-out ones, brought out of the power of Satan into a spiritual land, not a natural one.
What is the new covenant promise in Ezekiel 11, and why should we know it?

So this is a very important thing. You got to know the covenant. You really do. You should have this memorized, basically. You need to pray about the covenant, you need to get this in your brain, because this is powerful. Okay, the new covenant, Ezekiel 11:16-21. First of all, He introduces the topic like Jeremiah does: “I will gather you from the people.” And in the New Testament we actually find that the church, the word church, means the called-out ones. Okay, and in Acts 26:18 the Bible says that Jesus came to turn people from darkness to light, from the power of Satan to the power of God. So He’s bringing us out from under the authority and the power, the kingdom of darkness and Satan, and placing us in, He isn’t bringing us into a natural land, He’s bringing us into a spiritual land. Got it?
What is the new covenant promise in Ezekiel 11, and why should we know it?

Ezekiel 11:16-21: Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD: “Although I have cast them far off among the Gentiles, and although I have scattered them among the countries, yet I shall be a little sanctuary for them in the countries where they have gone.” ’ Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD: “I will gather you from the peoples, assemble you from the countries where you have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel.” ’ And they will go there, and they will take away all its detestable things and all its abominations from there. Then I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within them, and take the stony heart out of their flesh, and give them a heart of flesh, that they may walk in My statutes and keep My judgments and do them; and they shall be My people, and I will be their God. But as for those whose hearts follow the desire for their detestable things and their abominations, I will recompense their deeds on their own heads,” says the Lord GOD. Acts 26:18: to open their eyes, in order to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those who are sanctified by faith in Me.’
Why does he say there is only one pastor and one church?

He says Ezekiel’s “one heart” matches Jesus saying there will be one fold and one shepherd, and that no pastor on earth can be your pastor because there is only one, Jesus Christ. He says that following one shepherd in one direction impresses unbelievers, and he points to the one accord of Pentecost.
Why does he say there is only one pastor and one church?

Number two, He said, “I will give them one heart.” Same thing Jeremiah said. If you see the italics up here, it’s exactly what Jeremiah said. “I will give them one heart.” Now in John 10:18 Jesus said there will be one fold and one shepherd. Hallelujah. There is no pastor on earth that can be your pastor. We are strictly delegated ministers of the gospel. There is only one pastor, one shepherd, and that is Jesus Christ. Do we understand that? And you better be under Him. You know, don’t go around saying, “My pastor is Dave Kinzer.” No, your pastor is the Lord Jesus Christ. He better be. In John 17:21 Jesus prayed this prayer: “Father, make them one, that the world may believe and know that You have sent Me.” See, us having one pastor, following one direction, impresses the unbeliever so much that they will believe and know, and it’s imperative that we strive to be one in God. Can I hear an amen? And in America we got so many denominations and so many voices and so many books and so many ways of doing things. There’s only one shepherd, one way, one truth, one baptism, one church in the Bible. Can I hear an amen? And we need to remember that. And that’s our promise from the Old Testament and in the New. And remember, in Acts one, on the day of Pentecost they were in one accord.
Why does he say there is only one pastor and one church?

Ezekiel 11:19: Then I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within them, and take the stony heart out of their flesh, and give them a heart of flesh, John 10:16: And other sheep I have which are not of this fold; them also I must bring, and they will hear My voice; and there will be one flock and one shepherd. He says no: he says we are “strictly delegated ministers of the gospel” and there is only one pastor, one shepherd, Jesus Christ.
What does Jesus pray about being one?
He reads Jesus praying, “Father, make them one, that the world may believe and know that You have sent Me,” and says having one direction impresses the unbeliever.
Does he connect John 3:16 and John 7:38?

He says both promise something to whoever believes, eternal life in one and rivers of living water in the other, and that “they both come as a package.” He says John 7:38 speaks of the Holy Ghost, who would be in us.
Is there more to the Holy Ghost than receiving Christ?
He says that when you accept Christ, He comes in you, but there is an infilling of the Holy Ghost of power, and they are two different things.
Why does he say we are not robots when we obey?
He says Jesus gives us a heart to fall in love with Him, so we obey because we care, love and appreciate Him, not because of “thou shalt not.” He says His word also brings rewards.
Does God hold believers accountable for doing detestable things?
He says that if you do the things God detests, He will come and hold you accountable, bringing problems and pain to correct you.
What does he mean by “God’s soap”?

He means the word of God, which he says keeps washing and cleansing us. He points to Ephesians 5:26, the washing of the water by the word, and says we need to read it, study it and listen to Bible studies.
What does God promise about daily needs in Ezekiel 36?
He says that in the verse about calling for the corn and laying no famine on them, God is saying He will bless your daily life, income, food, clothing and shelter.
What are the two sides of repentance?
He says one is turning and the other is feeling sorry or bad for what you have done, and that we need both.
Why does he say God blesses us?
He says God’s ultimate goal is the unbeliever, and God blesses us so He can reach our neighbors, parents and other people.
What could priests do under the covenant of peace?
He says they had authority to come into the very presence of God and minister to God, and to minister to the people, and could go in and talk to God directly.
Who does the changing: God or me?
He says “the ‘I will’ will do it” and not to try to do it on our own, but also, near the end, that we have to put some effort into it.
Can I have these promises here on earth?
He says you don’t have to wait for the rapture. If you give God time, he says, He will transform you into a priest who can minister to Him and to people and possess His promises.

items.t: How to Understand the Old Testament
items.d: In “How to Understand the Old Testament,” Pastor David G. Kincer reads Isaiah 2:1-3 and says the Old Testament is understood by the Spirit, through records, parables and shadows of things to come that were…
p: In “How to Understand the Old Testament,” Pastor David G. Kincer reads Isaiah 2:1-3 and says the Old Testament is understood by the Spirit, through records, parables and shadows of things to come that were written for us. He argues that Judah, Jerusalem and Mount Zion in Isaiah’s prophecy describe the church, that God does not dwell in temples made with hands, and that every member of the church is a living stone.
What does Isaiah 2:1-3 promise for the last days?

He says Isaiah 2:1 and Micah 4:1 have identical wording, so it is a prophetic word from God concerning Judah and Jerusalem. In the last days the mountain of the Lord’s house will be established above the mountains and hills, all nations will flow into it, and out of Zion will go forth the law.
What does Isaiah 2:1-3 promise for the last days?

You’re going to learn this morning how to understand Old Testament scripture. And this lesson is really imperative for people who really want to understand the Bible. Okay? This is a pivotal message that will illuminate the whole Bible and you remember God cannot lie. The Bible is God’s word of truth. God is who the Bible says he is. God did and will do what the Bible says he did and will do. We are who the Bible says we are. And we can do and be what the Bible says we can do and be. But for us to do and be, we got to understand what the Bible says for us to do and for what we can be. And so this morning, last week, we showed you a fantastic promise of God to God’s rebellious people. Now, he jumps right in to an extraordinary prophecy. Okay? Just jumps right in. And Isaiah says in Isaiah 2:1, “The same thing in Micah 4:1, Micah, remember prophesying at the same time Isaiah is.” And both of them said the identical wording, identical. Out of the mouth of two or three witnesses, let everything be established. And so this is definitely a prophetic word from God. And uh it’s a word concerning Judah and Jerusalem. Okay. Concerning Judah and Jerusalem. Now when is this word about Judah and Jerusalem going to happen? It shall come to pass in the last days. So this word concerning Judah and Jerusalem is going to happen in the last days. All right. What is going to happen in the last days concerning Judah and Jerusalem? The mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains. We all know what a mountain is, right? And we all know what a house is. So here’s a mountain with a house on it established in the top of the mountain. So there’s other mountains all around it. And be exalted of the hills. Hills is not as high elevated as mountains. This is what’s going to happen in the last days. And all nations are going to flow into this mountain of the Lord’s house that’s going to be established at the top of all the other mountains and all the other hills. And many people are going to say, “Let us go to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of Jacob’s God. Let’s go to the mountain with the house on it. Now, why are they saying it? Because he Jesus will teach us his ways and we his people will walk in his paths. A profound promise by God. All right. Very profound. If God said it, he can what? Perform it. Do it. Perform it. Yeah, that’s a better word. Perform it. He has the power to perform what he spoke also. Why? For out of Zion shall go forth the law. This is the word concerning Judah and Jerusalem. Out of Zion shall go forth the law. The law is a rule that has a punishment if you break it, has a reward if you keep it. And the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. So this is the word of the Lord concerning Judah and Jerusalem. And I know it’s all clear to you now. I don’t have to preach another thing. Now, if this is going to happen in the last days, then let’s look and see what all these things are. All right? Let’s see what the Bible says all of these things are concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
What does Isaiah 2:1-3 promise for the last days?

Isaiah 2:1-3: The word that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem. Now it shall come to pass in the latter days That the mountain of the LORD’s house Shall be established on the top of the mountains, And shall be exalted above the hills; And all nations shall flow to it. Many people shall come and say, “Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, To the house of the God of Jacob; He will teach us His ways, And we shall walk in His paths.” For out of Zion shall go forth the law, And the word of the LORD from Jerusalem. Micah 4:1-2: Now it shall come to pass in the latter days That the mountain of the LORD’s house Shall be established on the top of the mountains, And shall be exalted above the hills; And peoples shall flow to it. Many nations shall come and say, “Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, To the house of the God of Jacob; He will teach us His ways, And we shall walk in His paths.” For out of Zion the law shall go forth, And the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
How do we understand Scripture, and what are parables and records?

He says only the Spirit can give you understanding, not intellect, and quotes Mark 4:11 that it is given to you to know the mystery of the kingdom. He says a parable or metaphor illustrates a truth, while a record such as Noah and Lot or the six-day creation is not a myth or a parable but a historical record that speaks of a truth.
How do we understand Scripture, and what are parables and records?

We’re going to teach you how to understand scripture this morning. And if you can get this in your cranial vacuum, you don’t need me anymore. This will open up the Bible to you. But remember, only the spirit can give you understanding. You don’t get things intellectually. This is what the church has got to learn. You get things spiritually. Yeah. And you can have all the intellectual debate you want to, but you tell you you and until you let God touch your spirit, you’re just not going to get it. God’s got to be involved in this. All right. Our faith should not be in the intellect of men, but in the what? Power of God. And too many people are trying to figure this stuff out intellectually, and it has to be birthed spiritually. Could that be an amen? Oh, that was weak. That was weak. And you know, that’s the problem in America is we intellectually try to approach God. And don’t get me wrong, the intellect is part of it, but it is not the resulting power that gives us the answer. How to understand scriptures? Here we go. Mark 4:11. To you it is given to know the mystery. A mystery is something secret, something hidden until you get enough evidence to know what the secret is. It’s given to you to know the mystery of the kingdom of God. But unto them that are without, all these things are done in parables. Okay? Parables is a story or a record illustrating a truth. Allegory, metaphor, parable. They’re stories or a record, okay, that illustrate a truth. What is right? Now we all know a metaphor in the book of Samuel that said the olive the trees said to the olive tree reign over us. The fig tree reign over us. The vine tree reign over us and the bramble reign over us. And of course none of them have the height or the power to reign over the big trees. It was a metaphor, a parable, an illustration that Abimelech was a bad choice to be the king. All right, that’s an illustration. A record is Noah and Lot are recorded historical records of two judgments of God that illustrate the final judgment that’s coming. Okay, that’s a record. That’s not a parable. Like Schuler said and a lot of other people that that’s just a myth. No, that is a record. It happened and it illustrates the third judgment, the coming judgment of God. Jesus himself plainly said that. Are you with me? All right. It’s not a myth, not a parable. It is a record that speaks of a truth. Six day creation recorded in history. How the world came into being is another record of truth.
How do we understand Scripture, and what are parables and records?

Mark 4:11: And He said to them, “To you it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God; but to those who are outside, all things come in parables, Judges 9:8-15: “The trees once went forth to anoint a king over them. And they said to the olive tree, ‘Reign over us!’ But the olive tree said to them, ‘Should I cease giving my oil, With which they honor God and men, And go to sway over trees?’ “Then the trees said to the fig tree, ‘You come and reign over us!’ But the fig tree said to them, ‘Should I cease my sweetness and my good fruit, And go to sway over trees?’ “Then the trees said to the vine, ‘You come and reign over us!’ But the vine said to them, ‘Should I cease my new wine, Which cheers both God and men, And go to sway over trees?’ “Then all the trees said to the bramble, ‘You come and reign over us!’ And the bramble said to the trees, ‘If in truth you anoint me as king over you, Then come and take shelter in my shade; But if not, let fire come out of the bramble And devour the cedars of Lebanon!’

If you’re going to go to origins the start, then let tell me where they came from and tell me why there was only one little group of heat and gas. Why wasn’t there three or four or five that exploded? And we had three or four or five univer universes universes and or a thickening of this one. Are you out there? See, the evolutionist can never give you the origin cuz if they did, they would be talking about a God, something out of nothing. Genesis said God made something out of nothing. See, not proving that hot gas come from nothing is not using the scientific method. If he’s going to use the scientific method, then he should use it and show us how this gas and this heat, where did heat come from? Who created heat? You see, they’re not using the scientific method except at their particulars. All right. Now, they got to also answer this. Why not more than one big bang instead of one hot gas explosions? And where is the mutation link between an animal and humans and a fish and a bird? Where is it? And why did evolution stop? Why aren’t we still evolving into something more fitting? And if you’re going to use the scientific method, then use it like it was intended to be used. And don’t cheat. Don’t give me a lot of words that mean nothing. That’s all they do. They just give you a lot of words that mean nothing. Isn’t it funny how evolutionists cannot change or answer the following questions? Why does man live an average of 70 plus years as ignorant Bible authors stated and then return to earthly dust? Why is it these ignorant Bible authors gave us answers that are still prominent today and scientists can’t do a thing about it? Are you out there? Are you hearing me? Surely there’s a better way. Why aren’t we evolving to where we don’t eat, where we don’t have to go to the bathroom, where we, you know, come on. Why did evolution stop where God said it started? Romans 16:25, the revelation of the mystery which was kept secret. Since the world began since when the world began I we we know in the scriptures Jesus died before the foundation of the world. Now please listen. These mysteries kept secret since the world began, but now is made clear and by the scriptures of what? The prophets are made known to all nations. So if we want to learn the secret, where do we go to find the secrets? The prophets. Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Joel, all of these prophets. So these people that don’t believe in the Old Testament, they’re just in looney. They’re just, you know, the New Testament did not nullify the Old Testament. There are still truths to be revealed to us in the Old Testament. Are you with me so far? Hallelujah. Now, I told you, you get this, the Bible will open up to you. Really open up to you. Revelations 10:7, in the days of the seventh angel, when he begins to sound his trumpet, the mystery of God should be finished as declared to his servants, who? The prophets. Okay. Why was the Old Testament written, and what does it mean that it is a shadow?

That Old Testament was written for you to be encouraged and have expectation and be and to be comforted what God says he will do. 1 Corinthians 10:11. All these things happened to Israel for example. What do the mountain and the hills mean, and where did God choose to dwell?

He reads Deuteronomy 12:2 that the nations worshiped on mountains and hills, which he calls the wrong way, and says God chose a place to put his name. Deuteronomy 12:2, “Destroy all places for the nations serve their gods on the high mountains and on the hills and under every green tree. Destroy the altars, the pillars, the images, everything. So, the word of the Lord concerning Judah and Jerusalem is about a mountain of Zion where God’s house would be. Are you there? That’s what Isaiah is saying. 2 Chronicles 5:2, Solomon assembled the elders. Now, he just built a temple to Jerusalem. The word of the Lord concerning Judah and Jerusalem to bring up the ark of the covenant. That’s where God dwelt out of the city of David, which is what? The city of David is which is in which is in Judah. Now, this is where your fundamentalist, your literal interpretation of the Bible without revelation get messed up.

Deuteronomy 12:2-5: You shall utterly destroy all the places where the nations which you shall dispossess served their gods, on the high mountains and on the hills and under every green tree. And you shall destroy their altars, break their sacred pillars, and burn their wooden images with fire; you shall cut down the carved images of their gods and destroy their names from that place. Psalm 78:68: But chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion which He loved. 1 Chronicles 15:1: David built houses for himself in the City of David; and he prepared a place for the ark of God, and pitched a tent for it. 2 Chronicles 1:4: But David had brought up the ark of God from Kirjath Jearim to the place David had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it at Jerusalem. 2 Chronicles 5:2: Now Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the chief fathers of the children of Israel, in Jerusalem, that they might bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD up from the City of David, which is Zion.

What is Mount Zion according to Hebrews 12:22?

They actually think he’s talking about a mountain in Jerusalem, in Judah, in Israel. And that’s their big hangup. And we’re going to clear that up for you this morning. Are you ready? Hallelujah. I’m so glad you’re excited. The church is the mystery, the parable, the example, and the shadow that is revealed. What is it? Church. Church. Okay, we’re going to back it up. Hebrews 12:22. You are you a part of God’s body, the church? Yes. Yeah. All right. You are come to where? Mount Zion. Did you really come to Mount Zion? How many of you been to Mount Zion? Not a one of you. One. In Jerusalem. He put it in a parable. All right, we come to Mount Zion. Then he describes who Mount Zion is. The city of the living God. What is Mount Zion? The city of the living God. The heavenly Jerusalem. Mount Zion is the church. Jerusalem. The church. Yeah. The church of the firstborn. Now, are you a member of the church? I’m not talking about this church. I’m talking about his church. A lot of people are members of a church, but not a member of his church. And there’s a big difference. Hebrews 12:22-24: But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, to an innumerable company of angels, to the general assembly and church of the firstborn who are registered in heaven, to God the Judge of all, to the spirits of just men made perfect, to Jesus the Mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling that speaks better things than that of Abel.

Judah is the church. Flesh and blood has not revealed this unto you, Peter, but my father. You see, intellect. You didn’t get this through intellect, Peter. That I am the Christ, the son of the living God. You got it because my father opened your understanding. You responded. You young onions getting this? This is a powerful message. This really changes everything how you read and learn from the Bible. Galatians 6:15. In Christ Jesus, circumcision nor uncircumcision avails anything but a what? New creature. As many as walk according to this rule, this standard of behavior. Philippians 3:3: For we are the circumcision, who worship God in the Spirit, rejoice in Christ Jesus, and have no confidence in the flesh, Galatians 6:15-16: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision avails anything, but a new creation. Genesis 49:10: The scepter shall not depart from Judah, Nor a lawgiver from between his feet, Until Shiloh comes; And to Him shall be the obedience of the people.

Does God dwell in temples made with hands?

Hebrews 3:6, Christ his son over his own house. Whose house are? We. Acts 7:47-48, Acts 17:24, Isaiah 66:1. The Most High dwells not in temples made with hands. Why are we so set on a temple being rebuilt over there in Jerusalem when God said over and over, “I don’t dwell in temples made with hands. I dwell in a temple made without hands, the church of the living God. Are you out there folks? But you see, we read books out of the Christian bookstore. We watch and we listen to radio and TV propaganda until we believe stupid thing. Even in Genesis when they wanted to build a tower and God came down and destroyed it. See, God, why? God’s not interested in a physical thing to worship him. He’s interested in you. He’s interested in the people. Amen. And see, God doesn’t dwell in the Baptist, in the Catholics, in the Pentecostals. He dwells in his people. He doesn’t dwell in this building. He dwells in us as individuals and as the corporation coming together, the body of Christ coming together. Are you there? And what are we lacking in many churches in America? That powerful presence of God dwelling among this people.

Hebrews 3:6: but Christ as a Son over His own house, whose house we are if we hold fast the confidence and the rejoicing of the hope firm to the end. Acts 7:47-48: But Solomon built Him a house. “However, the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands, as the prophet says: Acts 17:24: God, who made the world and everything in it, since He is Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in temples made with hands. Isaiah 66:1: Thus says the LORD: “Heaven is My throne, And earth is My footstool. Where is the house that you will build Me? And where is the place of My rest?
Has Isaiah 2 been fulfilled, and what kind of church is Christ returning for?

He says Isaiah is prophesying about the church, which will be above all religions in the last days, and asks if the church rules over its enemies now. He says he has said for 40 years that Jesus Christ is not coming in his lifetime, because he is coming back for a glorious church without spot, and that the gates of hell shall not prevail against the church.
Has Isaiah 2 been fulfilled, and what kind of church is Christ returning for?

Now let’s go back and look at this in the light of the records and the parables. The word concerning Judah and Jerusalem. Isaiah’s prophesying about who? The church. When will the church be active? In the last days. Okay. And what’s going to happen to the church? The church will be above all religions. Now, let me ask you, is it We’re really dumb if we think this scripture has been fulfilled. They step on us. They mock us. They laugh at us. They rule over us when the Bible plainly says that the righteous will rule over the wicked. Are you out there? And I’ve been saying for 40 years, Jesus Christ is not coming in my generation, in my lifetime. I was called a cult. I was called all kinds of names because if you go against the status quo, oh my God, they how can you be right and everybody wrong? I didn’t say I was right. I’m telling you what the Bible said. He’s coming back for what kind of church? A glorious church without spot. Do we have spots and wrinkles? Yeah. You see, did Jesus say, “Rule thou in the midst of your enemies?” Are we? No. But we have been so brainwashed by these pre-tribulation rapture people, post-tribulation rapture people, our millennials, postmillennials, and all these other things that we failed to see the church and the promise that God promised the church until the last day. And we’re just waiting for the rapture to come. People are just hanging on. I’m just going to hang on. God don’t want you hanging on. The Bible says he will build his church and the gates of hell shall not what? Yeah. The gates of hell prevailing. Yes. Any idiot can see that the homosexuals who are 2% of America’s population are prevailing. Why? Because most of God’s people don’t even know this promise in Isaiah. These churches don’t preach it. These churches don’t teach it. And most of God’s people aren’t even interested. Just tell me I’m going to be prosperous and everything’s going to be okay and God’s going to keep sickness away. Yeah, man. Just don’t tell me I got to do something to be a active part of this thing.
Has Isaiah 2 been fulfilled, and what kind of church is Christ returning for?

Psalm 110:2: The LORD shall send the rod of Your strength out of Zion. Rule in the midst of Your enemies! Ephesians 5:27: that He might present her to Himself a glorious church, not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but that she should be holy and without blemish. Matthew 16:18: And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it.
Are all nations flowing into the church yet, and will people walk in his ways?

He says all nations are flowing in but not enough, and that tribes were discovered only in recent years, so Christ could not have come before they had a chance. He says that in the new covenant God will cause us to follow his way, yet even half of the church in America is not walking in his ways.
Are all nations flowing into the church yet, and will people walk in his ways?

I got to actually read my Bible and follow it. Are you out there? And yes, I have borne the attack of many people, but it’s 2014 and who was right. Who was right? The Bible. And they keep changing their theories. Church, this ought to excite you. Will God do what he said he will do? Yes. Yes. All nations shall flow into it. Now, we do have all nations flowing into the church. But remember this, before the 1400s, they didn’t know there was islands out there with people of South and North America. Okay? They didn’t know that and they were looking for the second coming. All right. We discovered North and South America and some islands and oh boy, now we and we thought we had reached all the ethnic groups, all the languages, and then just a few years ago, they discovered a tribe in South America that had they had never known before. And then over in Indonesia, they discovered another tribe of people we had never known before. See, we don’t know what else is going to be revealed. Now, could Christ have come before these people had a chance? He said, “Out of every nation.” And my gospel will be preached in what? Every nation. And we didn’t know there was two groups that still in this technology age was hidden from us until just a few years ago. Are you hearing what I’m saying? But we do see all nations flowing into it now. But not enough cuz he’s got a harvest up there that can’t be numbered. Okay, this thing is a big thing he’s working on. Many will say, “Let us go to the mountain of the house of the Lord,” which is his church. Let’s go to church. You don’t have to drag them out of bed. You don’t have to call them on the phone. You don’t have to send them an email message. Hey, church time. They’re going to be up and at him, man. Why? Because God is teaching us his ways and he is causing us to walk in his path. And that’s new covenant. I will cause you to follow my way. That’s the promise in the new covenant. God’s going to do something to us that inspires us, drives us. We’re not going to be struggling with sin and debauchery. Amen. Isn’t that what he’s saying? Is even 50% of the church world in America walking in his ways? No. They just pick and choose what commandments they want to keep and don’t keep. And if they’re going to a church and they pick a commandment or so that they don’t want to keep and they keep harping on it, then they are getting led by the spirit to go to another church that allows them. And how many know the church is like McDonald’s? It’s the same everywhere you go. But in America, the church isn’t like McDonald’s. It’s a smorgasbord. Whatever you want, we’ll appease your appetite. And that’s wrong. And America has to be woken up. And God promised he’s going to do something big. You getting it, church? Powerful.
Are all nations flowing into the church yet, and will people walk in his ways?

Matthew 24:14: And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world as a witness to all the nations, and then the end will come. Ezekiel 36:27: I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My statutes, and you will keep My judgments and do them.
What do the Psalms say about Zion, which he says is the church?

He says Zion, Jerusalem and Judah are all the church, and reads Psalm 125:1, 48:2, 74:2, 46:4 and 87:3 and Joel 2:32 about Mount Zion being immovable, joyful, redeemed, a place of deliverance and a city with glorious things spoken of it. He says every member of the church participates, with no mighty man of God mentality.
What do the Psalms say about Zion, which he says is the church?

For out of Zion, what’s Zion? The church. Out of the church shall go forth the law. And the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. What is Jerusalem? The church. What is Zion? The church. What is Judah? The church. And all those things written and recorded is so we could understand the church. Hallelujah. Now look at these powerful scriptures. Psalms 125, they that trust in the Lord shall be as mount Zion, which cannot be removed, but abides forever. They that what? Trust in the Lord. How many people you know that they say they trust in Jesus and they backslide 60 days? Why? Because they don’t understand. People aren’t teaching them how powerful the church is and where that power comes from. It doesn’t come from human intellect. See, I don’t have to work up faith. I don’t have to work up anything. The spirit reveals. The spirit empowers. God’s involved. Psalms 48:2, the joy of the whole earth is Mount Zion. So what should be abundant in the church? Joy. What should be abundant in God’s people? Joy. And joy is one of the fruits of the spirit. Psalm 74:2, you’ve been redeemed this Mount Zion wherein you dwell. So, did he buy us and purchase us the church? Yeah, he purchased us. See, it was there before he ever did it. Joel 2:32 in Mount Zion in Jerusalem shall be what? Deliverance. Folks, the church is supposed to be a place of of deliverance, setting free. And we are all supposed to be a part of that. Yes. Amen. See, that’s why we need to pray as a unit. Worship as a unit. Worship is not a preliminary. Worship is a source of the power of God to deliver and heal. Psalms 46, there is a river that streams make glad the city of God. The streams plural. See, out of your innermost being, everybody flows out. We get a big river. Psalms 87:3, “Glorious things are spoken of you, oh city of God.” What kind of things? Glorious things. Honorable things. The church is an honorable place. This man and that man was born in her. You can’t get into this church by a baptism certificate or a uh some ritual you go through or or uh uh what’s that thing the Catholics do? What? Confirmation. Confirmation. Yeah. Yeah. You got to be birthed by the spirit into this church. And this is where the Protestants have it. Almost every Protestant believes in being born again. Except your liberal ones. I don’t know why they even believe in God. Everything they believe reduces God down to no power. But every Protestant I know believes in being born again. That God has to be active in our life. And that is true. And he he said it about his church back there in Psalms. The singers as players on instruments shall be there. The music is a part of what God is doing in his church. And all my springs, how many? All of these streams, all of these rivers are in us. We’ve got to we’ve got to to see this is a every member participation thing.
What do the Psalms say about Zion, which he says is the church?

Psalm 125:1: Those who trust in the LORD Are like Mount Zion, Which cannot be moved, but abides forever. Psalm 48:2: Beautiful in elevation, The joy of the whole earth, Is Mount Zion on the sides of the north, The city of the great King. Psalm 74:2: Remember Your congregation, which You have purchased of old, The tribe of Your inheritance, which You have redeemed— This Mount Zion where You have dwelt. Joel 2:32: And it shall come to pass That whoever calls on the name of the LORD Shall be saved. For in Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there shall be deliverance, As the LORD has said, Among the remnant whom the LORD calls. Psalm 46:4: There is a river whose streams shall make glad the city of God, The holy place of the tabernacle of the Most High. Psalm 87:3: Glorious things are spoken of you, O city of God! Selah Psalm 87:7: Both the singers and the players on instruments say, “All my springs are in you.”
What does it mean that believers are living stones in a spiritual house?

He reads 1 Peter 2:5-10 that believers are living stones built up as a spiritual house and a holy priesthood, with Jesus as the chief cornerstone. He says Isaiah is talking to you, and you must ask whether God can pour out from you healing and deliverance, and then become a prayer, a worshiper and a Bible student.
What does it mean that believers are living stones in a spiritual house?

It isn’t the mighty man of God doing something. It’s the church pouring out of their innermost being these rivers of life that heal the nations, deliver them, and set them free. Man, that was good. See, you are important. We got to get rid of this mighty man of God mentality. The church is a many membered body and all of us are important. Yes, he uses certain people to speak and so forth, but it’s got to be the body. Amen. No, mighty man of God. No popes. First Peter 2:5, you also as living stones are built up a spiritual house, a holy priesthood to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ our Lord. Therefore, it is also contained in the scriptures. Behold, I lay in Zion a chief cornerstone, an elect precious cornerstone. And he who believes on him will by no means be put to shame. Therefore, to you who believe, he is precious. But to those who disobey, the stone which the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone, a stone of stumbling. Who is that? Jesus. You see, the New Testament tells us, see, we are the house of God, a spiritual house being built up. You are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, his own special people, that you pro you may proclaim the praises of him who hath brought you out of darkness into his marvelous light. Who once were not people, but now are the people of God. See, once you weren’t a person of God, now you are. And you are the living house to offer up spiritual sacrifices, not lambs and all that. The fruit of our lips, giving thanks and praise unto his name. So, who’s Isaiah talking to in Isaiah 2? You. Can God do it? That’s what you got to ask yourself. Can God really do this in me? See, we’re always looking for somebody else. But the church is that many membered body of Christ. Can God actually make me part of this manifestation of God pouring out of me, touching my life, and bringing healing and deliverance and salvation to the nations? That’s the question you got to ask yourself. And if so, you got to become involved. You got to become a prayer. You got to become a worshiper and a praiser. You got to become a Bible reader, a Bible student. And you got to become involved to release it. See, water’s no good while it’s in the ground. It doesn’t help anybody. It’s when it comes out, springs come out of the ground. That’s when it’s profitable to people. Hallelujah. And listen, if you think that Jesus’s sacrifice in the cross, that he would come today and that’s all he could do on this earth is what he’s done, you’re missing the big picture of the Bible.
What does it mean that believers are living stones in a spiritual house?

1 Peter 2:5-10: you also, as living stones, are being built up a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ. Therefore it is also contained in the Scripture, “Behold, I lay in Zion A chief cornerstone, elect, precious, And he who believes on Him will by no means be put to shame.” Therefore, to you who believe, He is precious; but to those who are disobedient, “The stone which the builders rejected Has become the chief cornerstone,” and “A stone of stumbling And a rock of offense.” They stumble, being disobedient to the word, to which they also were appointed. But you are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, His own special people, that you may proclaim the praises of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light; who once were not a people but are now the people of God, who had not obtained mercy but now have obtained mercy.
Did the New Testament cancel the Old Testament?
He says the New Testament did not nullify the Old Testament, and there are still truths to be revealed to us in the Old Testament, so where we find the secrets is in the prophets.
What does he say about end-times charts?

He says there are mysteries that will be revealed as God reveals them, and he will not reveal them until we need the revelation. He says people make charts because they sell books and get a following, and then they are wrong.
What does he say happens when Christians read the Bible only to say they read it through?

He says if Christians could get this vision, you couldn’t keep them from getting up in the morning to read their Bible, because there is comfort, hope and understanding there, but many read it only so they can say they read it through last year.
What does he say about the stonings in the Old Testament?

He says they are shadows, illustrations of the truth to come, and that God only did a handful of stonings. He says there were more stonings by evil people killing innocent people, and that you don’t get stoned for breaking a shadow law but for breaking the law the shadow reveals.
Does he say speaking in tongues is for today?

He says tongues by the inspiration of God are a prophecy in an earthly or heavenly language, that Paul said not to forbid speaking in tongues, and that he doesn’t understand how someone reads the Bible and concludes tongues stopped in the book of Acts.
What does he say about worshiping God by our own ideas?
He says too many Americans come up with their own ideas of how to worship God and do what is right in their own eyes, and asks who cares what you believe or see, when what matters is how God sees.
What does he say it means to be a member of "his church"?
He says a lot of people are members of a church but not a member of his church, which is the church of the firstborn, and that there is a big difference.
What does he say about rebuilding a temple in Jerusalem?
He asks why we are so set on a temple being rebuilt in Jerusalem when God said over and over that he doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands but in the church of the living God.
How does he compare the church to McDonald’s?
He says the church should be the same everywhere you go, like McDonald’s, but in America it is a smorgasbord where people pick the commandments they want to keep and go to a church that allows them.
Why does he say people backslide?

He says they say they trust in Jesus and backslide in 60 days because people aren’t teaching them how powerful the church is and where that power comes from. He says the Spirit reveals and empowers, and joy should be abundant in God’s people.
Does he say the church depends on a mighty man of God?

He says it isn’t the mighty man of God doing something but the church pouring out their innermost being, rivers of life that heal the nations. He says the church is a many-membered body, all of us are important, and every member participates.
What does he say we must do to release what God wants to pour out?
He says we must become a prayer, a worshiper and praiser, and a Bible reader and student, because water is no good while it’s in the ground and only profitable when it comes out.

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer says America has its own idols in entertainment and compares them with the gods of ancient Corinth. He walks through 1 Corinthians 8, where Paul answers those who rely on…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer says America has its own idols in entertainment and compares them with the gods of ancient Corinth. He walks through 1 Corinthians 8, where Paul answers those who rely on human knowledge about food offered to idols, and explains the weak conscience and the stumbling block. He then connects idolatry to spiritual adultery and to 1 Corinthians 10, where Paul says to flee from idolatry and uses communion as an illustration.
Do we have idols in America today?

He says in America “we do not have a tradition or custom to really worship” carved images, “but we do have our own idols.” He points to American Idol, where someone is made into a musical idol whom teenagers “adore,” and says music and TV develop the minds of most young people, who “imitate their idol.”
Do we have idols in America today?

Today in America, we do not have a tradition or custom to really worship and--and uh--follow idols, images created into gods. But we do have our own idols. American Idol is called American Idol. Why? Because they’re trying to make someone into a musical idol where the teenagers especially will adore them, wear the clothes that they wear, wear the hairstyle that they wear, and embrace the message that they’re trying to get across. These three judges, Steve Tyler, claims to be a Catholic, but he lives with women, and he aborted a five-month-old son and all kinds of other debauchery, drugs, sex, and everything else. You think he cares about the moral condition of these people coming to be the next American Idol? No, he doesn’t care about the moral condition. He can call himself a Catholic all he wants. The Bible says, “You know them by their fruits.” Jennifer Lopez. She was raised in a Catholic home. She was a Buddhist a few years ago and now she switched over to Scientology. She’s just, you know, smorgasbord. She has no problem playing nude scenes in movies and uh all kinds of other uh immoral things. Randy Jackson is from a Catholic family, but on the show he wears voodoo beads. He is from Louisiana and voodoo is big down there. Are you there? You think these judges care about whether these people wind up good or not? Or what they told him about this [unclear] fella, this young teenage rapper. They said, “Boy, you you you you win and you’re going to get all the girls you want.” This is what the judges told this young teenager. See, the focus is on sex, pleasure, partying, drinking, just a loose life. See, it’s idolatry. And they got the show pegged right. American Idol. Now, that’s not the only reality show. There’s other ones. The Kardashians is one, and I’ve never seen it, but wouldn’t want to see it, but I read about in the newspapers all the time, and other things. You see, we don’t have idols. We have living people that are idols. We have entertainment that we idolize. You know what develops the minds of most young people in America today? Music. You know what the second development of minds of most young people today? TV. The media. Absolutely. And that’s why kids dress like they dress, wear their hair like they do, and so forth. They imitate their idol. So idolatry in America is very prevalent, but we don’t have these images and stuff like Corinth had. Here is just a few of their idols, their gods. Okay. Now, all of these idols were served with sacrifices, whether plants or meat, incense, music, prayers. They were common to all.
Do we have idols in America today?
Matthew 7:16: You will know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes from thornbushes or figs from thistles?
What gods did people worship in ancient Corinth?

He lists gods such as Aphrodite, Poseidon, Apollo, Hermes, Fortuna and Isis, and the Pantheon where “any God you wanted to worship was there.” He says all idols were served with sacrifices, incense, music and prayers, and that Paul faced this “along with all the other debauchery going on,” including temple prostitution.
What gods did people worship in ancient Corinth?

And the participators got to eat the best part of the sacrifice. Both Rome and Greek religions had a view of the afterlife after you’re dead. The Rome you went, if you were good, you went to the Milky Way. Now, I don’t know what you’re going to do up the Milky Way, dance from star to star or whatever. And the Greek, you went to Hades.
