Church, this is the key. You got to admit you’re wrong when you know God says it’s wrong. Just admit it. Good Lord, stop justifying. Many of us spend hours justifying our failures to others instead of just humbly saying, “I’m wrong, I got to change this.” It’s not, “My husband made me do it,” or “my wife made me do it,” or “my children drive me crazy,” or “my parents are driving me crazy,” or “the community is driving me crazy,” or “the school’s driving me crazy.” Stop justifying your error. Just admit you’re wrong. And a lot of us, “Well, the way I was raised,” oh, cut it out. The power of the blood of Christ is higher than the way you were raised. “Oh, it’s my daddy was that way, and my mama was that way, and I’m that way, and the grandpa was that way, all of us are that way.” Oh, get off of it. You’re just making excuses for staying dumb. Repentance. What was the first message John the Baptist preached? What was the only message John the Baptist preached in the coming of Christ? Yeah. What was the first message Jesus preached? Repentance. What do these mega churches and everybody tell you? Faith and grace, you don’t have to repent. And yet Jesus said, “Unless you repent, you will all likewise perish.” Jesus said that. Unless you repent, unless you turn from your sin, unless you admit you’re wrong and turn from it, and if you mess up, you get up and you admit it and turn from it again, you’re going to be destroyed. Repentance is the main message. Turning from wrong to what? Right. Turning from the kingdom of darkness to the kingdom of light, turning from Satan to Jesus Christ. That’s what it is, it’s that simple. And the key to it is admitting you’re wrong and turning from the wrong, and God will cleanse you, forgive you, erase the record. Isn’t that powerful? “Woe to me!” Isaiah cried. “Woe to me, I’m in trouble, I am ruined, I’m a man of unclean lips, and I’ve lived among a people of unclean lips, and my eyes have seen the King, the Lord God Almighty.” I’m in big trouble. See, he hadn’t committed adultery, he hadn’t stolen anything, he hadn’t dishonored his parents, he hadn’t worshiped idols, but he had talked wrong. And if Isaiah needed to confess and repent, don’t we?
What was Isaiah’s response to the glory, and why does he say repentance is the main message? (Isaiah 6:5)

Isaiah 6:5: So I said: “Woe is me, for I am undone! Because I am a man of unclean lips, And I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips; For my eyes have seen the King, The LORD of hosts.” Luke 13:3: I tell you, no; but unless you repent you will all likewise perish. Matthew 4:17: From that time Jesus began to preach and to say, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.”
How does he say a person is cleansed and sent? (Isaiah 6:6-8)

He says “there’s only one church anyway, and that’s the church of the Lord Jesus Christ,” and that the coal touching Isaiah’s lip shows you repent “until heaven comes and touches you and cleanses you, and that’s what we call being born again.” When God asks whom to send, he says we can’t be “non-involved Christians,” and the prayer to pray is “Here I am, use me.”
How does he say a person is cleansed and sent? (Isaiah 6:6-8)

And this is the foundation of having the glory of God come to you and having your eyes open to see Jesus: you got to admit you’re wrong. And a lot of us have a lot more to confess than the way we talk, and the way we talk isn’t good. The Bible says let everything be done to edifying, and we tear everybody down. Ain’t that right? Bible tells us to bridle our tongue, and we just tell everybody off. “Take that! That’s it, the way I am.” We commit idolatry by greed, we get drunk, intoxicated, we have sexual relationships outside of our marriage, we do all this stuff, and we think we’re going to go to heaven because of faith and grace, and, and these ministers have lied to you. I’m just going to tell you, they’re lying to you. You go to the Bible, it was repentance, turning from wrong to right. I don’t care if you’re Catholic, Baptist, Pentecost, I don’t care what you are. I don’t care about the tag outside, or you’re just a non-church person. Nobody can be a non-church person, by the way. God has ordained that we assemble together to provoke one another to love and to good works and to exhort one another. We need to be reminded to live right. Isn’t that right? We don’t need to be told, “You’re okay the way you are.” No, the church is supposed to assemble together to build character and maintain character. I don’t care what group you’re in, there’s only one church anyway, and that’s the church of the Lord Jesus Christ. And that’s not the Latter-day Saints, that’s the church of the Lord Jesus Christ. You’re born into it, you’re birthed into it. I don’t care what the title is out on the door. Throw away the titles. And then what? The angel brought a coal from the fire, the altar of heaven, touched his lip, took away the guilt, cleansed his lip, and atoned for his sin. See, you repent until God births repentance, forgiveness in you. Till heaven touches you, you can’t get a baptismal certificate, or a church membership card, or whatever, I ain’t going to do anything, but you repent, you confess your wrong until heaven comes and touches you and cleanses you, and that’s what we call being born again. Are you there? Hallelujah. Now, so now we’re delivered from captivity. After being delivered from captivity, what’s next on God’s agenda? Hallelujah. “Whom shall I send to these people in captivity?” See, he is free now. He’s not going into captivity, he’s not in captivity, he’s free, and now God says, “Whom am I going to send to these people in captivity?” Does God always care for the people in captivity? Yes. Yes, church, he does. He’s always interested in them, but he has principles. Somebody’s got to go and talk to them. See, we can’t sit back and be non-involved Christians. We can’t be so worried about offending people that we are silenced by public opinion: keep your religion to yourself. Why is it that every subject’s okay to talk about but Jesus Christ? Because Jesus Christ brings conviction, and you either get mad or you get glad, one of the two. There’s no neutral reaction here. It’s always, they are mad because they don’t want to change their ways and they don’t want to hear you, or they’re glad because, “Hey, thank you for showing me the way.” The response of Isaiah, who is now cleansed, delivered, atoned for, says, “Here I am. I’m atoned for, I’m clean, I’m forgiven. Here I am, use me. I don’t know what to do, but here I am, use me.” Do you ever pray that prayer? Prayer in America, the, the prayers I hear, I hear this all the time: “God help me, God help me, God help me, God help me.” For 30 years people have been praying the same prayer. “God help me, God help me, God help me, help me to be a prayer, help me to be a worshiper.” Is God the hindrance here? No. We need to respond and say, “Here I am, use me. Make me a prayer, make me a worshiper, make me one that can speak the word of God with confidence.” But that requires responsibility to speak the word, you got to read the word. “Oh my gosh, I got to miss the soap operas, that’s a, that’s a big price. I’m going to miss my kid’s soccer game.” “Here I am.” What can you say? “Here I am, send me.” Let me hear it: “Here I am, send me.” Yes.
How does he say a person is cleansed and sent? (Isaiah 6:6-8)

Hebrews 10:24-25: And let us consider one another in order to stir up love and good works, not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as is the manner of some, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching. Isaiah 6:6-7: Then one of the seraphim flew to me, having in his hand a live coal which he had taken with the tongs from the altar. And he touched my mouth with it, and said: “Behold, this has touched your lips; Your iniquity is taken away, And your sin purged.” Isaiah 6:8: Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying: “Whom shall I send, And who will go for Us?” Then I said, “Here am I! Send me.”
What message did God give Isaiah to preach, and for how long? (Isaiah 6:9-12)

He says God’s message was “be ever hearing” but “never understanding,” and that “it’s not your responsibility whether they listen or not, it’s your responsibility to speak the word of God.” When Isaiah asks how long, God says until the cities lie ruined, which he takes to mean the Babylonian captivity, “then he gives an exception.” He attributes this message to Ezekiel; see the editor note.
What message did God give Isaiah to preach, and for how long? (Isaiah 6:9-12)

Don’t be afraid to speak with fortitude, church. Guys, we sing some of our songs so wimpy. “I’m a child of the King” isn’t a wimpy song, that is a prophetic song. “I am his, royal blood flows.” Sing it like that. Could that be an amen? “Go and tell these people.” “Okay, here I am, use me.” You got to go and you got to do something. “But Lord, it’s embarrassing to tell people about God Almighty, and the public opinion is keep your religion to yourself.” That’s America. Isn’t that America? Oh yeah. And look at the message he’s going to give him now. I don’t know if you remember this or not, but Ezekiel was given a message to take to the people, and God said, “They’re not going to listen to you.” You want me to go preach to people that are not going to listen? Yeah, church, it’s not your responsibility whether they listen or not, it’s your responsibility to speak the word of God. Here’s the message: “Be ever hearing, but never understanding. Be ever seeing, but never perceiving.” Aren’t you just excited about this message? “I’m going to make your heart callous and your ears dull and close your eyes.” That’s the message I was given: the message, “[unclear] your heart, close your eyes, you can’t see, you can’t hear.” Oh man, can you just see the crowds coming to hear that one? Are you getting this? I would not want to go with this message. Give me the signs and wonders, man. “Otherwise you might see with your eyes and hear with your ears, understand with your heart, and turn and be healed.” Man, what kind of message is that? See, this is where you need revelation. Let me raise your hand right now and say, “Boy, this makes no sense right now.” The rest of you lying through your teeth. Wow. How many want to take this message to the [unclear]? Nobody. Yeah. What is he saying? And then Isaiah responds and said, “Well, how long am I to preach this message?” How long? I mean, I hope it’s just one day or five minutes. And God replies and said, “Until the cities lie ruined without inhabitant, houses deserted, fields ruined and ravaged, until the Lord has sent everyone far away.” Now you begin to understand that he’s going to take them into Babylonian captivity, and he’s going to give them a message where they can’t see and hear, unless something else is done. Are you there? “The land is utterly forsaken.” Then he gives an exception. Praise God for the exception. He always gives an exception.
What message did God give Isaiah to preach, and for how long? (Isaiah 6:9-12)

Isaiah 6:9-10: And He said, “Go, and tell this people: ‘Keep on hearing, but do not understand; Keep on seeing, but do not perceive.’ “Make the heart of this people dull, And their ears heavy, And shut their eyes; Lest they see with their eyes, And hear with their ears, And understand with their heart, And return and be healed.” Isaiah 6:11-12: Then I said, “Lord, how long?” And He answered: “Until the cities are laid waste and without inhabitant, The houses are without a man, The land is utterly desolate, The LORD has removed men far away, And the forsaken places are many in the midst of the land.
Who are the tenth, the holy seed that escape captivity? (Isaiah 6:13)

He says “though a tenth remain in the land,” and to be in that tenth you must die to the old, get in the new, become a worshiper and seek Jesus. He says “it’s righteousness that will protect you in any judgment or visitation of God,” that “repentance to do right, not faith in grace” escapes captivity, and that “the key is the word repent.” He says God “cuts us down to size, and then he starts growing us again.”
Who are the tenth, the holy seed that escape captivity? (Isaiah 6:13)

Church, everyone’s supposed to go far away, and everybody wants to take the word of God literally without balancing it out with the whole word of God. He’s going to give us an exception, all right. “Though a tenth remain in the land, it will be laid waste, but as trees leave stumps when cut down, so” how many is going to be left in the land? 10%. How many want to be part of the 10 [unclear]? Well, to be that part, you got to follow what we just taught, what Isaiah was revealed. You need to die to the old, get in the new, hallelujah, become a worshiper, look for Jesus, seek him. Now the tenth, the tenth, so the holy seed will be the stump in the land. I told you in the last message, it’s righteousness. It’s not being a Catholic, a Baptist, or Pentecostal or whatever, it’s righteousness that will protect you in any judgment or visitation of God. You don’t have to be a preacher, you don’t have to speak in tongues, you don’t have to prophesy, you don’t have to lead one soul to Christ. If you’re living righteous, God’s going to honor you, and by the way, if you are living righteous, he’s going to make you a fisher of men. The two go together. The holy seed. So repentance to do right, not faith in grace, that’s the one that’s going to escape the captivity. And when God judges America, and the road America’s on, on, I’m speaking this prophetically, by history and by the Bible, the road America’s on, God’s going to intervene. And I told you, Mexico can beat us militarily when God intervenes. Nobody and no army can protect you when God decides that a nation needs to be humbled. Are you there? Remember, Jeremiah said, “When the Lord has determined judgment upon a nation, upon a people, if they will turn and repent, he will turn from the judgment.” So we can, what? Change this road we’re on, and the key is the word repent. Say it: repent. People in America need to turn from their wrong and do right. 1 Corinthians 13. You know that us Pentecostals, because we speak in tongues and prophesy and get a word of knowledge sometimes, and, you know, we see, go, God healed the sick and all that. 1 Corinthians 13 is very clear, though: “Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels and have not love, I’m nothing. Though I can prophesy and have faith to move mountains and do miracles and have not love, I’m nothing. Though I give my body to be burned, and though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor,” all these social programs that we’re into, drug rehabilitation, alcohol rehabilitation, prostitute rehabilitation, divorce rehab, all these social programs, “without love it profits me nothing.” And then he describes love very clear, in great detail. “Love is patient.” There went 50% of us. “Love is kind.” There went another 50% of the 50%. “Love doesn’t boast of itself.” We all went. We want people to brag on us, and if they don’t, we brag about ourselves. Are you there? See, the tree was a stump, and it grew into a tree. The stump, yes. God will cut us down, God will trim us, God will correct us, but any stump left will start growing into a tree again. Hallelujah. See, when the tree is wrong and the fruit’s wrong, God cuts it down. He doesn’t cut us out, he cuts us down to size, and then he starts growing us again. How many could use a regrowth? Yeah, yeah. Isn’t this powerful?
Who are the tenth, the holy seed that escape captivity? (Isaiah 6:13)

Isaiah 6:13: But yet a tenth will be in it, And will return and be for consuming, As a terebinth tree or as an oak, Whose stump remains when it is cut down. So the holy seed shall be its stump.” Jeremiah 18:7-8: The instant I speak concerning a nation and concerning a kingdom, to pluck up, to pull down, and to destroy it, if that nation against whom I have spoken turns from its evil, I will relent of the disaster that I thought to bring upon it. 1 Corinthians 13:1-5: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal. And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing. And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, but have not love, it profits me nothing. Love suffers long and is kind; love does not envy; love does not parade itself, is not puffed up; does not behave rudely, does not seek its own, is not provoked, thinks no evil;
What does he say about end-time prophets and blood moons?

He says God “doesn’t need blood moons or anything to consummate the end time,” only “Jesus coming through that cloud.” He tells hearers “don’t believe that garbage,” calls it “salesmanship,” and says he told a Pentecostal in China that people following such prophets were following “false prophets.” These are his opinions about unnamed groups and have not been verified here.
What does he say about end-time prophets and blood moons?

See, I don’t care what God’s going to do, these Kansas City prophets and all these people with the blood moons and all this junk coming up, you know, scaring everybody to death. God doesn’t need blood moons or anything to consummate the end time. All he needs is Jesus coming through that cloud, and bam! Woo! Everybody is going to see. Are you there? And he’ll do it. He don’t need any planets lining up, he don’t need atomic bombs to renovate this earth, he’s going to do it on his own way and in his own time. So don’t believe that garbage, that’s just a, that’s just salesmanship. They make millions off of you guys, and when they’re wrong, they start all over again and make millions off the next bunch. Are you there? And in China, I told him, when one person told me, a Pentecostal, that they were following these prophets, I said, “Those are false prophets.” He goes, “They’re the nice people.” I don’t care if they’re nice people or not, they’re false prophets. I said, “You better be following James and John and Matthew and Luke.” Amen. Somebody’s got to say something.
Why did Jesus speak in parables? (Matthew 13:10-17)

He says the disciples asked why Jesus spoke in parables, and the answer is “it has been given you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given.” He says “whoever has, to him more will be given,” and that what the disciples had was “a response of heart”: they repented, believed and followed, so they got more.
Why did Jesus speak in parables? (Matthew 13:10-17)

Now, in conclusion, we’re going to give you the message that Isaiah was given. All right, and you can line up your interpretation that you gave at the beginning with the real answer. We find it in the New Testament. Okay, New Testament use of Isaiah chapter 6. “Why do you speak to them in” what? Say the word: parables. Remember, he speaks through shadow, laws, parables, metaphors, allegories, you know, uh, a historical report of Israel. He speaks to us through all these things. And so the disciples are saying, “Why do you speak to the people in parables? Why don’t you just say directly what you want to say?” Are you there? Are you with me so far? Yeah. Why did God use parables? Why did he just say what he wanted to say? “Because it has been given you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given.” Okay, he says, “You apostles, it’s been given to you to know the mysteries.” So are there secrets and mysteries hidden in the Bible? Yeah, the Bible says that, we taught you that before. Okay, why would God hide these things in the word? Why would he do that? Is that a good question? Why can’t I just open the book and, bang, I just get it? And, may, read Leviticus the first time and go, “Oh man, this is boring.” That was me. I couldn’t wait to get through it, it was torture going through Leviticus, just torture. Now when I go through Leviticus, bam! “For whoever has,” what’s the word? Has. What, what do these apostles have, these disciples have, that the other people didn’t have? You see, “whoever has, to him more will be given, and he will have” what? “Abundance. But whoever does not have,” what, don’t they have? “Even that which he has will be taken away from him.” So the one who has keeps having more, and the one who doesn’t have loses even that which he had. So he’s below zero. What did they have? First of all, Isaiah was sent to speak to the people in what? In what? In parables. Say it: parables. He was sent to speak to the people in parables. Why? Why would God do that, and not knowing that the parables they would not understand? Folks, what they had was a response of heart. When Jesus came to the apostles and said, “Follow me,” they just dropped everything and followed him. They responded. See, they didn’t have authority over sicknesses and demons at that time, they had a responsive heart. See, when Jesus preached “Repent and believe the gospel,” they responded, they repented, they believed. When he said “Follow me,” they just dropped everything and followed him. See, they had a response of heart, and every time Christ came with something new, they responded, so they got more. Are you there? And they that don’t have a responsive heart, you even lose the little bit you had. You might have knowledge of Christ, you might have knowledge of the Bible, you even lose that. Are you there? So why does God do this? Because parables have to be revealed by the Spirit, by Jesus himself, and unless you come to him, you can’t understand and be healed and be delivered, because only he and the Holy Ghost can open up the Bible to you.
Why did Jesus speak in parables? (Matthew 13:10-17)

Matthew 13:10-11: And the disciples came and said to Him, “Why do You speak to them in parables?” He answered and said to them, “Because it has been given to you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given. Matthew 13:12: For whoever has, to him more will be given, and he will have abundance; but whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
How does he say we can understand the Bible? (John 6:44, Matthew 13:13-15)

He says “the word of God is beyond human intellect,” and that the answer is to come to Jesus, humble yourself and say “Lord, open my eyes, open my understanding.” He says “the Holy Ghost is what opens your eyes,” that American people lack knowledge of the scriptures “because they don’t humble themselves, come to Jesus,” and he urges listening to messages “on your knees.”
How does he say we can understand the Bible? (John 6:44, Matthew 13:13-15)

Didn’t Jesus say, “No man comes to me except the Father draw him, and no man comes to the Father but by me”? You can’t skirt, see, the revelation of God’s word, the drawing of his Spirit, by human intellect. And God knows that those that come to him, then they are candidates to be revealed the parables and healed and set free. Are you there? See, the word of God is beyond human intellect. If you keep it in the human intellect, you’re not going to understand that Bible. But when you come to Jesus and humble yourself and say, “God, open my understanding, open my eyes,” he will. I can remember when parables of the New Testament were opened to me. I can remember the day, bam, God came, because I didn’t understand those parables, things didn’t make sense to me, and bam, and once I understood the key parable, I understood them all, and then the New Testament just opened up tremendously, just like the Old Testament, in shadow, laws, and, and, uh, historical events of Israel, just revelation came. Are you there? See, why did he want Isaiah to talk in parables? Because the people must come to God to get the understanding, the knowledge, and that’s why American people don’t have knowledge of the scriptures, is because they don’t humble themselves, come to Jesus, come to God, let the Holy Spirit, let Jesus reveal the truth to them. You see it? Do you see it? Yes. See, that’s why you can’t get understanding just hearing me preach on Sunday morning. You need to get those messages and listen to them, like Mr. Barnes is trying to, been prodding you guys to do. You need to listen to them two or three times. You need to listen to them on your knees. You need to open that book on your knees, and you need to say, “Lord, open my eyes, open my understanding,” and he will. There’s no preacher has the authority and power to open your eyes and give you understanding. They are vehicles, they are vessels. The Holy Ghost is what opens your eyes. Amen. And see, if your heart’s not right, you’re not going to understand, and God’s going to discipline you. Are we here, church? Hallelujah. Now, did you get it? Well, at the beginning you had it all figured out. Yeah, yeah, yeah. Isaiah spoke to them in parables so those who were really genuine in God would understand and be healed and delivered, and those not, the religious people, didn’t get it. “Therefore I speak to them in parables, for they see not.” Now he’s quoting Isaiah: “and hearing they do not hear, seeing they do not see, nor do they understand.” And this is where the American church is. In them the prophecy of Isaiah’s fulfilled: “Hearing you will hear and shall not understand, seeing you will see and not perceive, for the hearts of these people have grown dull, their ears are hard of hearing, their eyes they have closed, lest they should see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts,” their mind, the heart is the mind, the intellect, “turn,” what’s another word for turn? Repent. “So that I should heal them.” And so God has all these mysteries and all these parables so that people have to come to him. And that’s the message Isaiah had. He had a message of parables, that if people weren’t genuine, they didn’t get the message, and people who were the tenth, they got the message, and they were saved from the captivity.
How does he say we can understand the Bible? (John 6:44, Matthew 13:13-15)

John 6:44: No one can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him; and I will raise him up at the last day. Matthew 13:13-15: Therefore I speak to them in parables, because seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear, nor do they understand. And in them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled, which says: ‘Hearing you will hear and shall not understand, And seeing you will see and not perceive; For the hearts of this people have grown dull. Their ears are hard of hearing, And their eyes they have closed, Lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears, Lest they should understand with their hearts and turn, So that I should heal them.’
What does he say the vineyard represents in the Bible?

He says Isaiah 5 shows “we, the people of God, are his vineyard,” and that when the Bible mentions the vineyard “he’s talking about what? The church,” unless it specifically says “a wild vineyard,” which is about sin.
What does he say it means that we know people by their fruit?
He says Jesus said “you know them by their fruit,” so “your works are important, what you do and what you say is important.”
Who does he say the real leader and shepherd is?
He says it is Jesus Christ, and that “all the rest of us are under-shepherds, we’re just delegated people” who need to “get off our high horse” and point people to him.
What does he say matters without righteousness?

He says “without righteousness you’re not beans,” and that “justice and righteousness are high principles in God’s word.” He says the church’s “priority job” is preaching the gospel and turning people to righteousness and justice.
What does he say “the year King Uzziah died” has to do with us?
He says “all things were written for our learning,” and that the king’s death shows “there has to be a death of the old thing before the bringing in of the new thing.”
What examples does he give of the old dying before the new?

He gives Saul and David (“David was a man after God’s own heart”), Moses and Joshua, and Jesus, who “had to die before the church was raised up.” He adds that “we got to die to ourself,” and quotes “if any man be in Christ” as being a new creation.
Does he say angels have wings?
He says no: “angels don’t have wings. Seraphim and cherubim have wings.” He says he has been trying to correct this for 40 years.
What does he say about praying in secret during corporate worship?
He says “worship isn’t the time to be secret, and corporate prayer is not a time to be in your closet. It’s an attitude.” He says “I’m not praying for people to hear, I’m praying to my God.”
How much time with God does he say we should give each day?
He asks people to give God “one hour a day,” and says “the word, prayer, and worship, the three work together,” with the Spirit giving “revelation of what you read.”
What does he say about making excuses for our failures?
He says “stop justifying your error. Just admit you’re wrong,” and that “the power of the blood of Christ is higher than the way you were raised.”
Does he say a person can be a “non-church person”?

He says “nobody can be a non-church person,” because God has ordained that we “assemble together to provoke one another to love and to good works.” He says “there’s only one church anyway, and that’s the church of the Lord Jesus Christ.”
Why does he say people avoid talking about Jesus?
He says every subject is okay to talk about but Jesus Christ “because Jesus Christ brings conviction and you either get mad or you get glad, one of the two.”
What does he say about the prayer “God help me”?
He says people have prayed “God help me” for 30 years, and asks “is God the hindrance here? No.” He says we need to respond, “Here I am, use me.”
What does he say 1 Corinthians 13 teaches about works without love?

Reading 1 Corinthians 13, he says that even tongues, prophecy, faith that moves mountains and giving to the poor are nothing “without love it profits me nothing.” He applies it to social programs and rehabilitation work.
What does he say about a tree that God cuts down to a stump?

He says “God will cut us down, God will trim us, God will correct us, but any stump left will start growing into a tree again.” He says God “doesn’t cut us out, he cuts us down to size, and then he starts growing us again.”
