And when we unite with the word of God and with Jesus—a three-fold cord—we become a group that the gates of hell cannot prevail against. And so God wants the church to be strong, He wants it to be great, and He wants it to be large, and it is—it spread throughout all the earth today.
What is the three-fold cord for the church?

Ecclesiastes 4:12: Though one may be overpowered by another, two can withstand him. And a threefold cord is not quickly broken. Matthew 16:18: And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it.
Why must churches unite and people come prepared?

A sectarian church that won’t fellowship can’t be strong. The house needs God’s glory-presence in every place, and musicians, preachers, workers and the congregation must come prepared to add something.
Why must churches unite and people come prepared?

But a church that’s sectarian and won’t fellowship with anyone else—they can’t be a strong church either that destroys the gates of hell. We need to unite. We need to come together with other churches, come together around the word, come together around Jesus, to be that magnifical church that God has destined us to be—and not just be people that are a fiber out there and never go to church. They are not contributing and they are weak and the enemy destroys them really easy. He goes on to say that this exceeding magnifical house of the Lord has got to be magnificent of fame and of glory. In both of these tabernacles of Moses and Solomon, God’s presence came down, and the Bible calls it the glory of God came. And so this house of God needs the presence of the Lord, and this house is to go throughout all countries—not just big cities but little towns and out in the suburbs—and we need to make preparation for it. And I asked you today: when you come to church today or when you went to church last week, did you go prepared to add anything to that service, or did you just get up and go? Musicians have to prepare, preachers have to prepare, children’s workers have to
What are living stones in 1 Peter 2:5?
Believers are living stones built into a spiritual house and holy priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices of prayer, praise, worship and singing—not secular things.
What are living stones in 1 Peter 2:5?

prepare, youth workers have to prepare, and the congregation must come prepared if we’re going to have a magnifical church. 1 Peter 2:5: you as living stones are being built up a spiritual house, a holy priesthood. The priests ministered to God and they ministered to the people, and we’re to offer spiritual sacrifices—not secular but spiritual things that God accepts. And we are the stones, we are the house, and our house is for the Lord to live in. And every one of us can minister to Him and we can minister to others, and we’re to come into the house prepared to offer up spiritual sacrifices of prayer, praise, worship,
What are living stones in 1 Peter 2:5?
1 Peter 2:5: you also, as living stones, are being built up a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
How should we behave in the house of God?
From 1 Timothy 3:15 the house of God is the church of the living God, pillar of the truth. Where two or three gather He is in the midst; opinions and philosophies must go—only Jesus and His word.
How should we behave in the house of God?

singing—all these things that God asked us to do in church. In 1 Timothy 3:15 Paul said, I write so you may know how to conduct yourself, how to behave in the house of God, which is the church. The house of God and the church are synonymous, and it’s the church of the living God—His presence lives in the midst of His people. Jesus said where two or three are gathered together I will be in the midst. And the church is the pillar and the support of the truth. We back up the truth, not our opinions. We’ve got to get rid of this opinion thing. The church must only support and back up truth. Jesus is truth and His word is truth, and our opinions and our ideas and our philosophies have got to go. And we are destined before Christ comes back to be built into a house, a temple for the Lord,
How should we behave in the house of God?

1 Timothy 3:15: but if I am delayed, I write so that you may know how you ought to conduct yourself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth. Matthew 18:20: For where two or three are gathered together in My name, I am there in the midst of them.”
Can imperfect people and “strangers” help build?
Yes. Solomon used strangers—“illegal aliens”—to cut stone, and a half-Israelite, half-Tyrian craftsman solved every device. You don’t have to be perfect to be involved.
Can imperfect people and “strangers” help build?

exceeding magnifical, that will be famous throughout the earth and literally have the presence of Jesus, the Holy Ghost, in its midst. So that you know, you don’t have to be perfect to be involved in this house. 2 Chronicles reminds us in chapter 2 verse 17 that Solomon numbered all the strangers in Israel—the illegal aliens—and these labored and hewed and they managed, they cut stone, and they had leaders over these workers. And they were not the people of God. They weren’t the great believers. They were strangers. In fact, 2 Chronicles 2:14, the son of a woman of Dan which was of the tribe of Israel and a father of Tyre which was a pagan nation was skillful to work in gold, silver, brass, iron, etc.,
Can imperfect people and “strangers” help build?

2 Chronicles 2:17: Then Solomon numbered all the aliens who were in the land of Israel, after the census in which David his father had numbered them; and there were found to be one hundred and fifty-three thousand six hundred. 2 Chronicles 2:14: (the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tyre), skilled to work in gold and silver, bronze and iron, stone and wood, purple and blue, fine linen and crimson, and to make any engraving and to accomplish any plan which may be given to him, with your skillful men and with the skillful men of my lord David your father.
How did David use imperfect musicians?
1 Chronicles 25: Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun’s sons prophesied with harps by the Spirit—288 in choir, 4,000 in orchestra. Many imperfect people build the magnifical house.
How did David use imperfect musicians?

and any gray engravings, and to find out every device which was put to him. This guy could solve any problem that was brought to him, and he worked with Israel’s skillful workers. So if you ever feel like a half-breed, you’re a candidate to be involved. 1 Chronicles 25:1: David separated the sons of Asaph and Heman and Jeduthun who prophesied with the harp—that means they played on their musical instrument by the inspiration of the Spirit of God. They had a choir of 288 and they had an orchestra of 4,000. It wasn’t an electric guitar, electric piano, bass and a drum. The singers were there. It takes many imperfect people working together to build the magnifical house of God.
How did David use imperfect musicians?

1 Chronicles 25:1: Moreover David and the captains of the army separated for the service some of the sons of Asaph, of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who should prophesy with harps, stringed instruments, and cymbals. And the number of the skilled men performing their service was:
Were Peter, Paul and Thomas still used after failure?
Peter denied, others fled and fished; Paul was chief sinner yet built the church; critical Thomas still was used. God chooses the foolish and weak to shame the wise (1 Corinthians 1:26).
Were Peter, Paul and Thomas still used after failure?

That restrains folks. In the New Testament, Peter cursed and denied God and still was used of God. The rest ran when Jesus was crucified and still were used of God. All went fishing. Paul didn’t marry; he killed innocent blood; he blasphemed the Holy Ghost and persecuted the church. The Bible says he was the world’s chiefest sinner—number uno sinner, number one—and God saved him and he became a part to build the church. Thomas was a discourager. Jesus said I’m going to go and raise Lazarus from the dead, and they said what’s the matter with you, don’t you know they tried to kill you when we were there last time? And He says, well, I’m going. And Thomas turns to the rest of the apostles and says, well, let’s go and die with him. We have so many people that criticize the church and speak discouragingly that it’s a wonder we can get anything done. But I want to tell you something: Thomas was used of God in spite of his discouraging critical talk. 1 Corinthians 1:26: you see your calling, brethren, your invitation. God chose the foolish, the weak, the inferior, the despised things of this world and the things that are not. I’m not mature yet. I haven’t got my tongue bridled yet. I’m not in control of myself yet. He chose these kind of people to shame the wise and the intellectual of this world—New Testament church.
Were Peter, Paul and Thomas still used after failure?
1 Corinthians 1:26: For you see your calling, brethren, that not many wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called.
What is the Old Testament temple pattern for?
Exodus 25:22: God meets and speaks from the mercy seat. 1 Corinthians 10:11: written for our example. Acts 2’s wind and fire show He still meets and speaks through people.
What is the Old Testament temple pattern for?

Exodus 25:22: we’re reminded that God dwelt between the cherubims in the holy of holies, and He says there I will—number one—meet with you, I will have an encounter with you, and number two, I will speak with you from above the mercy seat between the two cherubims on the ark of the testimony. 1 Corinthians 10:11 says these things were written for our example and our admonition, our learning, on whom the ends of the ages are come. So the Old Testament temple pattern was really an illustration of the magnifical house made of living stones—the church that God was really going to build. And if He met with them back there in the pattern and He spoke with them in the pattern, then He is going to meet with us and speak with us. And that’s what the church service is about: touching God and hearing His voice. All right. In the New Testament the encounter: they had a mighty wind in Acts chapter 2, they saw cloven tongues as of fire, and they spoke the mighty works of God as the Spirit gave them utterance. The presence of God came and moved on them and they spoke the mighty works of God—not God speaking
What is the Old Testament temple pattern for?

Exodus 25:22: And there I will meet with you, and I will speak with you from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim which are on the ark of the Testimony, about everything which I will give you in commandment to the children of Israel. 1 Corinthians 10:11: Now all these things happened to them as examples, and they were written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the ages have come. Acts 2:2-4: And suddenly there came a sound from heaven, as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting. Then there appeared to them divided tongues, as of fire, and one sat upon each of them. And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.
Why is God’s presence top priority in services?
Acts 4 shaking, Paul’s Damascus encounter, and John 16:8 conviction show His presence convinces of sin, righteousness and judgment—and Luke 6:19 virtue healed all who touched Jesus.
Why is God’s presence top priority in services?

Himself but through people. In Acts 4 the place was shaken where they were gathered together to pray and they spoke the word of God with boldness. Paul on the road to Damascus saw a light and heard a voice. He had an encounter with God. It blinded him. Then his blinded eyes were opened and he became the chief apostle to build this magnifical church that God had prophesied thousands of years before that He would do. The encounter also convicts us. John 16:8: when the Holy Spirit, the Comforter, has come, He will convict the world of sin, righteousness and judgment. That presence of God, when it touches you, will convince you of right and wrong and that there’s a judgment coming. We need the presence of God in our services—top priority, top priority. Then we find also in the Bible that the virtue, the power of God—that power of His presence—did tremendous things. In Luke 6:19 the whole multitude sought to touch Jesus, and there went virtue out of Him and healed them all—physically, mentally, spiritually, their sin. Power went out and healed them. Folks, that’s what people need to touch when they come to church: the power of His presence. That’s what does the job.
Why is God’s presence top priority in services?

Acts 4:31: And when they had prayed, the place where they were assembled together was shaken; and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they spoke the word of God with boldness. John 16:8: And when He has come, He will convict the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment: Luke 6:19: And the whole multitude sought to touch Him, for power went out from Him and healed them all.
Are healings and miracles for today?

He says people who deny them haven’t read their Bible. Felix trembled under Paul’s word (Acts 24:25); God still backs the gospel so presence can change people. He also speaks through gifts when people prepare and bring something (1 Corinthians 12).
Are healings and miracles for today?

And so He healed them and He did miracles. Now God is a supernatural God. It’s nothing for Him to do miracles. And people that say that healings and miracles aren’t for today just haven’t read their Bible. Acts 24:25: as Paul reasoned of righteousness, self-control and the judgment to come, Felix the governor, the secular leader, trembled. He’s literally shocked when Jesus backed up the word Paul was preaching and met with Felix and touched him. But Felix wouldn’t give in. He wouldn’t make a commitment to Jesus Christ. But God did His part and Paul did His part—he preached the gospel—and the Holy Ghost came and did His part and backed it up. And so we see in the New Testament that God kept His word. They encountered Him back there and they encountered Him in the New Testament church. And folks, it’s still the same plan today. We can have the power of His presence touching people and can change them and convince them and make them new creatures like He has made many of us who have been following Christ for some time. Secondly, we see that God spoke. But He didn’t speak in an audible voice like He did in the Old Testament. He spoke through His people. In 1 Corinthians 12 the Spirit gives to one a word of wisdom, to another a word of knowledge, to another a prophecy, faith, tongues, teaching, a revelation of psalms and hymns and spiritual songs. When you come together you bring something to the house of God. David said I’ve got to prepare. We need to prepare through the week and we need to get up on Sunday morning and prepare ourselves to come to the house of God. Could that be true? That is very true. We can’t rely on the past. We can’t rely on a song leader. Us, all of us, have got to prepare ourselves to come in and let the power of God move in the church and speak and touch people and change their life. And He’s the only one that can do it—the only one. And He gives us these venues of speaking. In 1 Corinthians 2:4 Paul said my speech and my preaching wasn’t with enticing words of men’s wisdom or intellect,
Are healings and miracles for today?

Acts 24:25: Now as he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was afraid and answered, “Go away for now; when I have a convenient time I will call for you.” 1 Corinthians 12:8-10: for to one is given the word of wisdom through the Spirit, to another the word of knowledge through the same Spirit, to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healings by the same Spirit, to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another discerning of spirits, to another different kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of tongues.
What four things belong in the house of God?

Edifying speech in Spirit-power (1 Corinthians 2:4; 14:26); change by the Spirit not programs (2 Corinthians 3:18); house of prayer with His presence via praise (Matthew 21:13; Psalm 100; 22:3); and preaching repentance (Luke 24:47) plus making disciples (Matthew 28:19).
What four things belong in the house of God?

but in power and demonstration of the Spirit, that your faith should not stand in the wisdom of men but in the power of God. 1 Corinthians 14:26: that all things be done unto edifying—to build, to encourage, to make the house of God strong and magnifical like God prophesied it would be. We’re going to go and take a look at four things that’s got to be done in the house of God. 2 Corinthians 3:18 says we are all changed—how many of us?—all are changed into the same image of Christ from glory to glory by the what? Inspirational preaching?
What four things belong in the house of God?

1 Corinthians 2:4: And my speech and my preaching were not with persuasive words of human wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power, 2 Corinthians 3:18: But we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, just as by the Spirit of the Lord. Matthew 21:13: And He said to them, “It is written, ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer,’ but you have made it a ‘den of thieves.’ ” Luke 24:47: and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in His name to all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.
What does he say destroyed past awakenings in America?

About 30 years after the last awakening, he says music-group idolatry, making gods of faith and prosperity, and psychology/psychiatry replaced what only Spirit and word can do—crowds without change into His image.
What does he say destroyed past awakenings in America?

By a 12-step program? No—by the Spirit of the Lord. Folks, that’s why we need Him. That’s why worship and praise is so necessary. These people that say what kind of God’s up there wanting everybody to praise Him and thank Him—it’s a principle that releases the power. He’s not up there with an ego. It’s a principle that works. And so when we do our part He will come by His Holy Spirit and do His part. But if we’re not looking for the Holy Ghost and we’re not looking for the presence of God, we’re just going to have a social gathering. There’s not going to be any power. We’ll have a meeting with music, we’ll have a meeting with people, we’ll fellowship with our friends, we’re going to go home unchanged, because it’s the Spirit that changes us into His image, and it’s His image that we’re after—not the popular author of the day. Matthew 21:13: My house shall be called the house of prayer, but you made it a den of thieves. We are in a 30th year after the last spiritual awakening in America, and we destroyed that awakening—the Jesus movement and the charismatic movement before that and the healing movement before that. We destroyed that by turning to music groups, making a god out of faith, making a god out of prosperity, and then bringing in psychology and psychiatry into the church to do what only the Spirit and the word can do. And we brought this on ourselves. But we’re trusting God will move again. How many people will come to church if all you do is pray for an hour? But you get a music group or a mime or a drama or something and they’ll come—“oh we got a thousand people out there”—but did they get changed when they were there into His image? That’s the bottom line. Psalm 100 says serve the Lord with gladness and come before His presence. After prayer we need His presence. We don’t need the presence of the song leader and a preacher and the ushers and so forth. The main ingredient in a church service, a New Testament, is He’s there. And He tells us how to come into His presence with praise and worship and singing and clapping and so forth. Psalm 100 verse 4: enter His gates—number three—with thanksgiving, His courts with praise; be thankful unto Him and bless His name. Speak good of His name, exalt His name, exalt Jesus, thank Jesus, glorify Jesus, build up Jesus, brag about Jesus. That’s how we’re supposed to come to the house of God—not “oh I wonder who the server is going to pick me up today.” I wonder—how we’re supposed to come: on fire, prepared. And when we do, His presence will come, because Psalm 22:3 says He inhabits the praises of His people. It’s a principle of praise. It’s not an egotistical God that the atheists try to say—what kind of God wants to be—but it is a principle He’s ordained that works, and when we operate it He will back it up. Luke 24:47: repentance and remission of sins should be preached in His name among the nations. So the fourth thing is we’ve got to have the word of God—the rhema word of God, the living word of God—and repentance and forgiveness and cleansing and freedom of sin should be preached. And it’s not being preached very much in America today because the church in America don’t want to hear they’re wrong. But they’re wrong whether they like to hear it or not. And we’ve got to get back to letting people know what sin is and they can repent from it and they can be forgiven, set free and cleansed from it. And that makes a magnifical church. And it should be done to all nations. No one is eliminated from this. They need to hear that message. Still on number four, the second part: Matthew 28:19, go and make disciples of all nations, teaching them to observe all things that I have commanded you—what He’s commanded, not what psychologists commanded, what theologians command. It’s what He commands, what He told us to teach. And every expression of speech—whether it’s songs, prophecy, revelation, tongues, interpretation, wisdom, knowledge, teaching, prayer—is to build and change the people that are in that service unto His image. Our songs have got to be songs that build, construct and strengthen people. Our messages, our prophecies, everything is to build and make people a strong magnifical person for Jesus Christ so we can be changed into His image. Now Isaiah prophesied this years before, hundreds of years before. Isaiah 2:3: many shall go and say, come, let us go up to the house of the God of Jacob.
Has Isaiah 2’s peace among nations been fulfilled?

He says no—swords into plowshares has not happened—and rejects treating the rapture as a magical answer. When the church becomes magnifical with His presence teaching His paths, Jesus can bring it to pass; without Him the American church tries in vain.
Has Isaiah 2’s peace among nations been fulfilled?

He will teach us His ways and we will walk in His paths. There’s that word again: He will teach us. The Holy Ghost would teach us. The presence of Jesus would teach us. And we will walk in His paths. Why? Because the Holy Ghost would convict us. The Holy Ghost will empower us to obey the word, not just hear it. For out of Zion—and Hebrews 12 tells us Zion is the church, and Zion is the new city of Jerusalem, the church—out of the church will go forth the law—[unclear] law, [unclear] law, and spiritual law—and the word of the Lord, what He commanded us to teach, from Jerusalem, from the church. So the word is supposed to go from the church, is supposed to be in the church—a living word, a powerful word from the Holy Spirit. And then look at the results when we do these things: He will judge among the nations, He will correct many people, they will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war anymore. And I submit to you: has this ever been fulfilled? No. Well, why do you think the rapture is some kind of magical answer when this is just one of the things in the Bible that has not been fulfilled? But when we get our act together and become a magnifical church that He’s building in these last days, He will have no problem bringing this to pass. He is Jesus and He is powerful. Hallelujah. And so it pays us to let the Holy Spirit come, the presence of God come, and teach us His ways so that we also have that presence of God motivating us to walk in His paths. These four things are necessary. And we don’t have a church service without any of them. But the most important part of these four things of prayer, praise and worship and thanksgiving and blessing and teaching the word—the most important part is His presence. The Bible says without Him we can do nothing, and the American church on the most part is trying to do this thing without Him.
Has Isaiah 2’s peace among nations been fulfilled?

Isaiah 2:3-4: Many people shall come and say, “Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, To the house of the God of Jacob; He will teach us His ways, And we shall walk in His paths.” For out of Zion shall go forth the law, And the word of the LORD from Jerusalem. He shall judge between the nations, And rebuke many people; They shall beat their swords into plowshares, And their spears into pruning hooks; Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, Neither shall they learn war anymore. Hebrews 12:22: But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, to an innumerable company of angels,
From 1 Chronicles 22:5 he says the house for the Lord must be exceeding magnifical—top quality fame and glory.
Can the gates of hell prevail against a united church?
He says when fibers unite with word and Jesus as a three-fold cord, they become a group the gates of hell cannot prevail against.
What is the church the pillar of?
He says the church is the pillar and support of the truth—not opinions.
If you feel like a “half-breed,” can you serve?
Yes. He says the Tyrian craftsman’s son worked with Israel’s skillful men, so you’re a candidate to be involved.
How large were David’s choir and orchestra?
He says a choir of 288 and an orchestra of 4,000 prophesying with instruments by the Spirit.
Who does he call the world’s chiefest sinner?
Paul—who killed, blasphemed and persecuted—yet God saved him to help build the church.
What two things did God promise at the mercy seat?
Meet with you (encounter) and speak with you from above the mercy seat.
What happened when Paul reasoned with Felix?
Felix trembled under righteousness, self-control and judgment to come, but would not commit to Christ.
What changes us into Christ’s image?
Not inspirational preaching alone or a 12-step program—by the Spirit of the Lord, from glory to glory.
What is the most important part of a church service?
His presence. Without Him we can do nothing, and he says much of the American church tries to do it without Him.

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from 1 Corinthians 16 on the first day of the week and why Saturday or Sunday is a “silly” argument, then on Paul’s “great door” with “many adversaries.” He lists…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from 1 Corinthians 16 on the first day of the week and why Saturday or Sunday is a “silly” argument, then on Paul’s “great door” with “many adversaries.” He lists nine kinds of opposition believers face, then answers critics who say the Bible is wrong about slavery, shellfish and other things.
Why did the early church meet on the first day of the week?

He cites Luke 24:1, Acts 20:7 and Revelation 1:10 to show the disciples met on the first day of the week because Jesus rose from the grave on that day. He says history shows Roman reports that Christians “meet on the first day of the week,” though Acts also shows them in the synagogue on Saturday.
Why did the early church meet on the first day of the week?

We are in chapter 16 of 1 Corinthians, in verses 1-4. He talks about collecting for the saints that are in Jerusalem on the first day of the week: take up the collection, so when I come there’s no collections to be taken up. And, uh, there’s a big argument in America and throughout the world on what day we should serve Jesus, what day we should come to church, Saturday or Sunday. In Luke 24:1 we find that on the first day of the week Jesus rose from the grave, on Easter Sunday, the first day of the week. So see, they met on Sunday, the first day of the week, because Jesus rose from the grave. We find in Acts 20:7 that on the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached to them until one guy fell out of the window. See, they say I’m a long-winded preacher here, but let me tell you, Paul has got me beat by a long shot. But anyway, they met together on the first day of the week. When you study history, you will find that Roman rulers, lower ranks in authority, would have to report to higher ranks, and they would say, “These Christians meet on the first day of the week, and they take communion, and they make a vow that they will not commit adultery and, and, uh, steal and, and do these bad things, on the first day of the week.” So there’s plenty of evidence that the early church met on the first day of the week. But also, if you read Acts, you’ll find them coming into the synagogue on Saturday also. They were there Saturday and Sunday if they could be. Revelations 1:10, John the apostle was in the Spirit on the Lord’s Day. Now, what’s the Lord’s Day? The first day of the week, Sunday. So do we meet together on Sunday, or do we meet together on Saturday? And let me tell you, there’s a big argument out there. I debated out at the college with a bunch of college students about this thing. They, they just get young Christians wrapped up in silly things like Saturday or Sunday. It’s just a, a silly thing.
Why did the early church meet on the first day of the week?

1 Corinthians 16:1-4: Now concerning the collection for the saints, as I have given orders to the churches of Galatia, so you must do also: On the first day of the week let each one of you lay something aside, storing up as he may prosper, that there be no collections when I come. And when I come, whomever you approve by your letters I will send to bear your gift to Jerusalem. But if it is fitting that I go also, they will go with me. Luke 24:1: Now on the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they, and certain other women with them, came to the tomb bringing the spices which they had prepared. Acts 20:7: Now on the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul, ready to depart the next day, spoke to them and continued his message until midnight. Revelation 1:10: I was in the Spirit on the Lord’s Day, and I heard behind me a loud voice, as of a trumpet,
Does it matter whether we meet on Saturday or Sunday? (Colossians 2:16)

He calls the Saturday-or-Sunday argument “a silly thing” and cites Colossians 2:16, “Let no man judge you in food or drink or in respect of a holiday or the new moon,” saying these are “shadow of things to come.” He cites Acts 1:3 and 1:14 to show Jesus was seen on any day, and says God “don’t care what day of the week it is.”
Does it matter whether we meet on Saturday or Sunday? (Colossians 2:16)

As we see, Colossians 2:16 sums it up this way: “Let no man judge you in food or drink or in respect of a holiday or the new moon or the” what? “Sabbath days. Let no man judge you.” These are a what? “Shadow of things to come.” Say that with me: shadow of things to come. So you know the shadow isn’t the real thing, right? You know, your shadow isn’t the real thing. It brings you to the real thing. And so the Sabbath day was just an example of something God wanted to teach us. All right, let’s, in Acts chapter 1:3, after Jesus rose from the grave, He was seen of them 40 days. Was He only seen of them on Sunday? Was He only seen of them on Saturday? No. He was seen of them anytime that they would accept seeing Him: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, and Saturday. Acts 1:14, the 120 people in the upper room continued 10 days in prayer. The Bible says in one place. So did they leave on Monday? Did they leave on Tuesday? Would God turn His back on them if they met on Monday? No. Oh, come on, church. God’s so excited about you coming before Him, He don’t care what day of the week it is. And so it’s important that you understand that whether we meet on Saturday, Sunday, Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday, God accepts you coming together and seeking Him. Can I hear an amen? And we need to get rid of these silly little things that we argue and fight about and get on the real thing.
Does it matter whether we meet on Saturday or Sunday? (Colossians 2:16)

Colossians 2:16-17: So let no one judge you in food or in drink, or regarding a festival or a new moon or sabbaths, which are a shadow of things to come, but the substance is of Christ. Acts 1:3: to whom He also presented Himself alive after His suffering by many infallible proofs, being seen by them during forty days and speaking of the things pertaining to the kingdom of God. Acts 1:14: These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with His brothers.
Why does Paul say a great door has opened but there are many adversaries? (1 Corinthians 16:5-9)

He says Paul will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost, a populated city where 12 people were filled with the Holy Ghost and bodies were healed through pieces of his garment, so that “All Asia has heard the word of God.” Paul says “a great and effective door has opened,” but there are many adversaries, or opponents.
Why does Paul say a great door has opened but there are many adversaries? (1 Corinthians 16:5-9)

Now he goes on to say in verses 5-8 that he’s going to stay in Ephesus till Pentecost, then he’s going to leave and pass through Corinth. And Ephesus, as you probably know by your history, is a populated city of 300,000 when Paul was there. And Paul went there, and 12 people were filled with the Holy Ghost in Ephesus to start his ministry there. And then parts of his clothing was sent out all through Asia, and bodies were healed and demons were cast out with just little pieces of his garment. And Paul said, “All Asia has heard the word of God,” and he’s writing to the Corinthians, and he says, “From Ephesus a great and effective door has opened for me here in Ephesus.” A powerful door. All these things are happening. The word of God is going out through all Asia, and talking about the Middle East, Asia Minor. But he says there are many what? Adversaries. There’s many opponents.
Why does Paul say a great door has opened but there are many adversaries? (1 Corinthians 16:5-9)

1 Corinthians 16:5-9: Now I will come to you when I pass through Macedonia (for I am passing through Macedonia). And it may be that I will remain, or even spend the winter with you, that you may send me on my journey, wherever I go. For I do not wish to see you now on the way; but I hope to stay a while with you, if the Lord permits. But I will tarry in Ephesus until Pentecost. For a great and effective door has opened to me, and there are many adversaries.
Who is our biggest opponent? (we oppose ourselves)

He starts a list of opponents by saying the first is ourselves: “We are our big, worst enemy,” thinking we’re not good enough, or too good, or that God can’t change our life. The second is those in the church who oppose with false teaching, such as saying there is no resurrection or that incest is okay.
Who is our biggest opponent? (we oppose ourselves)

Now let me give you a quick list of some opponents. You ready? Number one: we are the biggest opponent. Opponent means opposer. Opposer of the Scriptures, opposer of truth, opposer of God. He says, “in meekness instruct those who” what? “Oppose themselves.” We are our big, worst enemy. “We’re not good enough,” “we’re too good,” you know, “we’ve done the unpardonable sin,” you know, uh, we are our own worst enemy. “I’m so bad I can’t come to God now, God can’t change my life.” Number two, 1 Corinthians 15:12: “Some among you say there is no resurrection of the dead.” Then you got the problem with opposing in the church. Some among you say there’s no resurrection of the dead. Some among you say incest is okay. See, some among you are saying it’s okay to eat food sacrificed to idols and go into the idol temple and eat. Some of you have got these weird doctrines. But none of you. Right? Nobody in here. See, we oppose ourselves in the church, and we could go on and on. I taught, I taught on that; you can get the series.
Who is our biggest opponent? (we oppose ourselves)

2 Timothy 2:25: in humility correcting those who are in opposition, if God perhaps will grant them repentance, so that they may know the truth, 1 Corinthians 15:12: Now if Christ is preached that He has been raised from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
Do governments, religious leaders and Satan oppose believers?

He lists Jewish religious leaders commanding the disciples not to speak in Jesus’ name (Acts 4:18), a violent attempt to stone them (Acts 14:5), and the king who killed James with the sword (Acts 12:1). He says “government opposes us, church leaders oppose us,” and Satan hindered Paul (1 Thessalonians 2:18).
Do governments, religious leaders and Satan oppose believers?

Number three, Acts 4:18: Jewish religious leaders commanded them to not speak or teach in the name of Jesus. Number four, a violent attempt was made by both the Gentile and the Jews, with their rulers, to abuse and stone the disciples, Acts 14:5. Number five, Acts 12:1, Herod the king, direct from Rome, his connection was straight to Rome, “stretched forth his hands to pain some of the church.” He killed James, the brother of John, with the sword. See, government opposes us, church leaders oppose us, we oppose ourself, and our believing brothers oppose. There’s a lot of opposition. Number six, 1 Thessalonians 2:18: “We would have come unto you, but Satan hindered us.” Then we got Satan, our adversary, the Devil, as a roaring lion. He’s always trying to seduce us away from what’s right.
Do governments, religious leaders and Satan oppose believers?

Acts 4:18: So they called them and commanded them not to speak at all nor teach in the name of Jesus. Acts 14:5: And when a violent attempt was made by both the Gentiles and Jews, with their rulers, to abuse and stone them, Acts 12:1-2: Now about that time Herod the king stretched out his hand to harass some from the church. Then he killed James the brother of John with the sword. 1 Thessalonians 2:18: Therefore we wanted to come to you—even I, Paul, time and again—but Satan hindered us. 1 Peter 5:8: Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil walks about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.
Do witchcraft and science falsely so-called oppose the faith?

He cites Acts 16:16, a young woman possessed with a spirit of divination, as opposition from people into witchcraft and sorcery. He cites 1 Timothy 6:20 on “oppositions of science” and “falsely so-called,” says science is just knowledge, and asks if people try to use science to nullify the word of God: “Absolutely.”
Do witchcraft and science falsely so-called oppose the faith?

[unclear] 16:16, “the children of the wicked one.” “We went to prayer, and a certain lady, a certain young woman, was possessed with a spirit of divination, met us.” You see, opposition from people who don’t believe in God, people that are into witchcraft and wickedness and sorcery and so forth. Number eight, 1 Timothy 6:20: “Avoid profane and vain babblings and oppositions of science.” Say the word: science. “Falsely so-called, which some professing have erred concerning the faith.” See, what’s another word for science? Knowledge. It’s just knowledge. You know, get off of it. Do we have that today? Do they try to use science to, uh, nullify the word of God? Absolutely. We got the same opposition today he had it back there. It’s nothing new going on, nothing new at all.
Do witchcraft and science falsely so-called oppose the faith?

Acts 16:16: Now it happened, as we went to prayer, that a certain slave girl possessed with a spirit of divination met us, who brought her masters much profit by fortune-telling. 1 Timothy 6:20-21: O Timothy! Guard what was committed to your trust, avoiding the profane and idle babblings and contradictions of what is falsely called knowledge— by professing it some have strayed concerning the faith. Grace be with you. Amen.
What about opposition from family, race and false brethren? (2 Corinthians 11:26)

He cites 2 Corinthians 11:26, “perils of waters, robbers, countrymen,” and says countrymen means your race or your family, so the more you want to serve God the more some of your own household may oppose you. He also says false brethren fool Christians who don’t know their Bible, and that Scripture “is the high authority of God.”
What about opposition from family, race and false brethren? (2 Corinthians 11:26)

Then number nine, 2 Corinthians 11:26: “I was in perils of waters, robbers, countrymen.” Countrymen means your race, your family. Remember, in Psalms it says your enemies will be those of your own household. You know, you want to serve God, you really want to serve Him, and your, you know, your family starts opposing you, and the more you want to serve God and follow the Bible, um, the more some of them will, what? Oppose you. And [unclear], when I was in Ghana, Africa, while I was there preaching, the southern tribe got in a war with the northern tribe. See, black on black, killing each other, ripping the women that were pregnant open and taking the baby out of the womb and killing it, because of the hatred and the opposition from one tribe to another. See, racial problems, our own, our own nationality can reject us. Are you there? See, these, far, these problems aren’t new. Every generation thinks they’re new. They’ve been around forever. All right, then you got “problems in the city, in the wilderness, in the sea, with false brethren.” My gosh, these false brethren. A lot of, a lot of Christians, because they don’t know their Bible, really get fooled by false brethren and deviate from the Scriptures. And nobody has the authority to get you to deviate from Scriptures. Scriptures is the high authority of God. Can I hear an amen?
What about opposition from family, race and false brethren? (2 Corinthians 11:26)

2 Corinthians 11:26: in journeys often, in perils of waters, in perils of robbers, in perils of my own countrymen, in perils of the Gentiles, in perils in the city, in perils in the wilderness, in perils in the sea, in perils among false brethren; Micah 7:6: For son dishonors father, Daughter rises against her mother, Daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; A man’s enemies are the men of his own household.
What hardships did the apostles endure to preach the gospel?

He says the apostles “went without food,” worked and went without sleep trying to preach the gospel. He says “it takes work to serve God,” but that Paul says all these adversaries are there alongside a great door of opportunity.
What hardships did the apostles endure to preach the gospel?

Hallelujah. And then you got to work, you got hunger. You think you got it tough? These apostles had it tough. They went without food, they worked, and they went without sleep, trying to preach the gospel. Now, they’re not like a lot of American pastors who play golf five days a week and then come in, give their bell-ringing message, and then go back and [unclear]. These guys worked hard. Are you there? And it takes work to serve God. And so he says all these adversaries are there, but there’s a great door of opportunity, great door.
What hardships did the apostles endure to preach the gospel?
2 Corinthians 11:27: in weariness and toil, in sleeplessness often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness—
What do critics say the Bible is wrong about, such as slavery and shellfish?

He reads a speaker’s claim that people ignore what the Bible says about gay people the same way they ignore what it says about shellfish, slavery and other things, and that the Bible is “radically pro-slavery.” He says the speaker is a homosexual activist who told a high school the Bible is wrong, and that some students walked out while many applauded.
What do critics say the Bible is wrong about, such as slavery and shellfish?

The Bible, we’ll just talk about the Bible for a second. Uh, people often point out that they can’t help it, they can’t help with the anti-gay bullying. It says right there in Leviticus, it says right there in Timothy, it says right there in Romans that being gay is from— can you hear? We can learn to ignore the [unclear] in the Bible about gay people the same way, the same way we have learned to ignore the [unclear] in the Bible about shellfish, about slavery, about dinner, about farming, about ministration, about virginity, about masturbation. We ignore [unclear] in the body about all sorts of things. The Bible is a radically pro-slavery document. Slave owners waved Bibles over their heads during the Civil War and justified it. The shortest book in the New Testament is a letter from Paul to a Christian slave owner about owning his Christian slave, and Paul doesn’t say Christians don’t own people. Paul talks about how Christians own people. We ignore what the Bible says about slavery because the Bible got slavery wrong. Now, that guy’s name is Dan Savage. Dan Savage went to speak at a high school in America, and this is what he told the students. Dan Savage is a homosexual activist who promotes transsexualism, uh, homosexuality, trans sites, and all the rest, and tells them in a descriptive way how it’s done, okay? And they invite this guy in to speak to a high school student body. You’ve seen a lot of them walk out. Let’s give them a hand. They walked out. Yeah, but did you hear a lot of them applaud what he was saying? He was saying the Bible is just full, full of nonsense, only he used the worst word. All right, he says the Bible is wrong about slavery, wrong about shellfish, wrong about food, wrong about farming, ministration, virginity, and masturbation.
Are people in high places teaching that the Bible should not guide public policy?

He says homosexuals have been teaching this message since the ’70s to undermine the Bible’s influence, and that it has reached “people in high places.” He then reads a quote saying America is not just a Christian nation and asking which passages of Scripture should guide public policy, and says, “let’s read our Bibles.”
Are people in high places teaching that the Bible should not guide public policy?

Okay. Now, the homosexuals have been teaching this message since the ‘70s, trying to rip the Bible apart and, and undermine it and destroy its influence in America, and it has influenced people in high places. Okay, I want to show you some of these influential people that have picked up this bashing of the Bible, this opposition of the Bible. “Whatever we once were, we are no longer a Christian nation, at least not just. We are also a Jewish nation and a Muslim nation and a Buddhist nation and a Hindu nation and a nation of non-believers. And even if we did have only Christians in our midst, if we expelled every non-Christian from the United States of America, whose Christianity would we teach in the schools? Would it be James [unclear] or Al [unclear]? “Which passages of Scripture should guide our public policy? Should we go with the Leviticus, which suggests slavery is okay and that eating shellfish is an abomination? Or we could go with the Deuteronomy, which suggests stoning your child if he strays from the faith? Or should we just stick to the Sermon on the Mount, a passage that is so radical that it’s doubtful that our own Defense Department would survive its application?” We— so before we get carried away, let’s read our Bibles. Now, folks haven’t been reading their Bible. I [unclear] have been reading my Bible. See, this message has gone up to high places in America, influential people. Let’s continue.
Is there only one way to God?

He plays a clip in which a speaker says there are many paths to what you call God, then responds, “There is one way and only one way, and that is true, Jesus.” He says the speaker is influential all over the world and “has accepted this doctrine,” and he plays another clip on whether Christians and Muslims worship the same God and whether the Bible is literally true.
Is there only one way to God?

“One of the mistakes that human beings make is believing that there is only one way to live, and that we don’t accept that there are diverse ways of being in the world, that there are millions of ways to be a human being, and many ways— no, but many paths to what you call God. And her path might be something else, and when she gets there she might call it the light, but her loving and her kindness and her generosity brings her— if it brings her to the same point that it brings you, it doesn’t matter whether she called it God along the way or not. And I guess the danger that could be on that, I mean, it sounds great on the onset, but if you really look at both, besides, there couldn’t possibly be just one way. What? What about Jesus? What about Jesus?” And you say there isn’t only one way? There is one way and only one way, and that is true, Jesus. “There couldn’t possibly be—“ “With, yay for that lady!” Yeah, there’s only one way. Now, see, Oprah is worth over $2.5 million; she makes 250 million— $2.5 billion dollar; she makes 250 million a year. She’s very influential all over the world, and she has accepted this doctrine. Let’s continue. Influential people. “Do we all worship the same God, Christian and Muslim?” “I think we do.” “Does we have different routes of getting to the Almighty? Do Christians and non-Christians, do Muslims go to heaven in your mind?” “Yes, they do. We have different routes of getting there. But I— I want you to understand, I want your listeners to understand, I don’t get to decide who goes to heaven. I, the Almighty God, decides who goes to heaven. Uh, I— the Bible is an amazing book. Is it literally true, the Bible? I, you know, I probably not. You know, I mean, the idea that I know I’m not a literalist.”
Is the Bible factual or literal?

He says critics make “literal” sound like a bad word, but “literal means factual,” and answers that the Bible is factual: “Yes, it is.” He says these are influential people who have embraced these doctrines, and he will answer the claims that the Bible is wrong.
Is the Bible factual or literal?

Now they make “literal” sound like a bad word, but literal means factual. See, is the Bible factual? Yes, it is. Amen. Now, these are people in high places, influential places in America, that have embraced these doctrines.

He cites Exodus 21:16, that he who kidnaps or sells a man shall be put to death, and says “you can’t sell human beings, you can’t kidnap human beings.” He asks how there can be slavery “when you can’t force someone against their will.”

Now, Mr. Obama said we weren’t reading our Bible well. This guy happens to read his Bible and study it and knows this Book, and this guy is going to answer the questions that these Bible adversaries say the Bible is wrong on. Are you ready? Are you interested? See, is the Bible wrong on slavery, food, ministration, farming, uh, homosexuality, and all the rest? Is it wrong? Okay, should [we] ignore the Bible? All right, here we go. We’ll start with slavery. Exodus 21:16: “He who kidnaps, takes someone by force, a man, or he who sells a man”— maybe the guy volunteered to be a slave, doesn’t matter— you can’t sell human beings, you can’t kidnap human beings, or you will be put to death. Now let me ask Mr. Savage, how can there be slavery when you can’t force someone against their will? Are you there? See, they lie through their teeth. It was really talking about servanthood.
Exodus 21:16: “He who kidnaps a man and sells him, or if he is found in his hand, shall surely be put to death.
What does the Bible mean by servants, and did Paul approve of slavery?

He says the Old Testament word for servant meant servanthood: you got into debt and worked it off, and “at the end of every seven years, all servants were free,” like indentured servants coming to America. He cites Matthew 19:19, says Paul’s words to submit to masters were “just telling them to keep a good attitude,” and says “the Bible never, from Genesis to Revelation, promotes slavery.”
What does the Bible mean by servants, and did Paul approve of slavery?

When the, the word servant or slave in the Old Testament really is a word that means servanthood. You got into debt and you couldn’t pay off your debt, so you had to become a servant of somebody that would pay your debt, and then you worked it off, and you couldn’t work any more than seven years. At the end of every seven years, all servants were free. See, people came from Europe to America on being indentured servants. The businessmen in America would pay their way, and then they worked off their way over, the price it cost to get over there, by serving that guy for so many years. See, it wasn’t slavery, it was a mutual agreement. Are you there, church? Matthew 19:19: “Love your neighbor as yourself.” Now, how am I going to believe in slavery if I’m not willing to be a slave? You see, the Bible plainly says slavery was not accepted, and because they don’t understand the Bible, they twist these things around. Is that clear to you? The Bible never, from Genesis to Revelation, promotes slavery, never. When Paul wrote about slavery and told them to submit to their masters, he was just telling them to keep a good attitude, a right attitude, because there’s nothing you can do about it anyway. The government had passed a law for slaves, and just, he’s trying to tell them, you know, keep a good attitude in it. Ain’t that right? Not saying that slavery is okay. Now, how many raise your hand, said Mr. Savage is wrong? Yes. And people are believing this nonsense. They are believing this nonsense that these people are saying.
What does the Bible mean by servants, and did Paul approve of slavery?
Matthew 19:19: ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ ”
Is eating shellfish a sin? (Deuteronomy 14:21 and 1 Timothy 4:4)

He cites Deuteronomy 14:21 and asks whether eating shellfish, catfish or shark would put you in hell, answering that the food laws were there “to remind them to live holy.” He cites 1 Timothy 4:4 that every creature of God is good and nothing is to be refused if it is received with thanksgiving.
Is eating shellfish a sin? (Deuteronomy 14:21 and 1 Timothy 4:4)

Now let’s go to food, clothing, uh, farming, and these other things that he said the Bible is wrong on, and let’s take a close look at them. Are you ready? Deuteronomy 14:21: “You shall not eat anything that dies of itself. Give it to the stranger, the foreigner in the gates, or sell it to the alien, that he may eat it, for you are a holy people unto the Lord.” Now, why did God make these kind of laws? Was shellfish bad for anybody? Was eating shellfish going to put you into hell? Catfish was forbidden. If you eat catfish, you’re going to go to hell? Sharks were forbidden ‘cause they didn’t have scales. If you eat a shark, you’re going to go to hell? It wasn’t there for that. It was there to remind them to live holy. It says it right there, and the foreigners could eat it. Does God love the world? Does God love all nations? Is He going to allow one people to eat something that’s going to hurt them and another people, no? No. What’s He doing? He’s trying to teach the people and remind them to live holy, to live for God, to live right. That’s— continue. 1 Timothy 4:4: “Every creature”— how many creatures? Every creature, every animal— “of God is good, and nothing is to be refused for food if it is received with thanksgiving.” Now, is that plain? Yeah, you see—
Is eating shellfish a sin? (Deuteronomy 14:21 and 1 Timothy 4:4)

Deuteronomy 14:21: “You shall not eat anything that dies of itself; you may give it to the alien who is within your gates, that he may eat it, or you may sell it to a foreigner; for you are a holy people to the LORD your God. “You shall not boil a young goat in its mother’s milk. 1 Timothy 4:4-5: For every creature of God is good, and nothing is to be refused if it is received with thanksgiving; for it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.
What does 1 Corinthians 16:1-4 say about collecting for the saints?
He says Paul talks about collecting for the saints in Jerusalem on the first day of the week, so that when he comes “there’s no collections to be taken up.”
Did the early Christians meet only on Sunday?

He says no: they also came into the synagogue on Saturday, and “they were there Saturday and Sunday if they could be.” He says the early church met on the first day of the week, and John was in the Spirit on the Lord’s Day.
Would God turn His back on people who meet on a Monday?
He says no: “God’s so excited about you coming before Him, He don’t care what day of the week it is.” He points to the 120 in the upper room who continued 10 days in prayer.
How big was Ephesus, and what happened there?

He says Ephesus was “a populated city of 300,000” when Paul was there. He says 12 people were filled with the Holy Ghost to start Paul’s ministry there, and pieces of his garment were sent out and bodies were healed and demons cast out.
What does he say about thinking “I’m so bad I can’t come to God”?

He says that is one way we oppose ourselves: “I’m so bad I can’t come to God now, God can’t change my life.” He says the opposite error is “we’re too good,” and that either way “we are our own worst enemy.”
Who does he say killed James, the brother of John?
He says Herod the king, “direct from Rome,” stretched forth his hands to pain some of the church and killed James, the brother of John, with the sword.
What does he say Satan is always trying to do?
He says Satan, our adversary, is “as a roaring lion,” and he’s “always trying to seduce us away from what’s right.”
Does he say racial problems and family opposition are new?

He says no: “Every generation thinks they’re new. They’ve been around forever.” He says our own nationality can reject us and tells of a war between two tribes in Ghana as an example of racial hatred.
How does he compare Bible servanthood to indentured servants?

He says people came from Europe to America as indentured servants: businessmen paid their way and they worked off the price by serving that man for so many years. He says “it wasn’t slavery, it was a mutual agreement.”
What attitude does he say Paul told slaves to keep?

He says when Paul told them to submit to their masters, he was telling them to “keep a good attitude, a right attitude, because there’s nothing you can do about it anyway.” He says Paul was not saying slavery is okay.
Why does he say some foods were forbidden in the law?

He says the law was not there to send you to hell for eating shellfish or shark: “it was there to remind them to live holy.” He notes foreigners could eat it, and asks if God would allow one people to eat something that hurts them and not another.

items.d: In this second part Pastor David G. Kincer explains that the Old Testament has civil laws, spiritual laws and shadow laws that point to Jesus, using the shadow of a cross. He ties this to communion…
p: In this second part Pastor David G. Kincer explains that the Old Testament has civil laws, spiritual laws and shadow laws that point to Jesus, using the shadow of a cross. He ties this to communion, assembling, praise and baptism, explains why people were stoned, and says Jesus fulfilled the shadow laws and is the only way.
What are the three kinds of laws in the Old Testament?

He says there are civil laws (like “Thou shalt not murder”), which carry a punishment; spiritual laws (like seek the Lord and pray); and shadow laws. He says critics are “confused about the difference between civil, spiritual, and shadow laws.”
What are the three kinds of laws in the Old Testament?

What people don’t understand is there’s three kinds of laws in the Bible in the Old Testament. Are you ready? There’s civil laws. All right? Thou shalt not murder. That’s a civil law and it has a punishment if you break it. Then there are spiritual laws. Seek the Lord your God and you will find him. Pray, you know, come before him and sing. See that’s spiritual laws. And then there is shadow laws. As we heard earlier, shadow laws. Say the word shadow. Yeah. And this is what these people are confused about the difference between civil, spiritual, and shadow laws.
What does he mean by “shadow laws”? (Hebrews 10:1)

He cites Hebrews 10:1, the law is a “shadow of good things to come,” and uses a shadow of a cross: from the shadow alone you cannot tell its color or material, but following it leads you to the real cross. In the same way, shadow laws “point to the real thing, and that is Jesus Christ.”
What does he mean by “shadow laws”? (Hebrews 10:1)

Now don’t look at me like that. I’m telling you the truth. Hebrews 10:1: “For the law having a— what? Shadow of good things to come.” Say it. Shadow of good things to come. “And not the very image of the things can never with these sacrifices which they offer year by year make those who approach perfect.” But you see, they pointed to Jesus who can make you perfect. Now, you see up there on the screen a shadow of a cross. Now, because you’re an intelligent society, you know that’s a cross, isn’t it? But can you tell me the color of that cross? Can you tell me the dimensions of that cross? Can you tell me if it’s made of metal, wood, plastic, stone? No, all you can tell me is what? It’s a cross. And if I follow the shadow, I will get to what? The real cross. And I’ll see its color. I’ll know its dimensions. I’ll know its purpose. And so, you can’t understand the details of God’s words by following shadow laws. They point to the real thing, and that is Jesus Christ. Amen. Now, folks, that’s good stuff. And this is what Mr. Savage and Mr. Bush and Mr. Obama and Oprah has got all mixed up.
What does he mean by “shadow laws”? (Hebrews 10:1)

Hebrews 10:1-2: For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with these same sacrifices, which they offer continually year by year, make those who approach perfect. For then would they not have ceased to be offered? For the worshipers, once purified, would have had no more consciousness of sins.
What does he say happens when people bash the Bible?

He says Jesus came to make us new people, so “old things passed away,” and he lists adultery, homosexuality, stealing, murder and hatred as the old things. He says “when you bash the Bible who points to Christ, you are bashing Christ” and removing the force that can change your life.
What does he say happens when people bash the Bible?

They don’t know their Bible. And they’re trying to tell people what the Bible says when they don’t know their Bible. Mr. Obama, I read my Bible. I know my Bible. And I know you’re wrong. Do you guys see that clearly? Yeah, it’s very clear. Did Jesus come to make us new people? Old things passed away. Isn’t that right? What’s our old things? Adultery, homosexuality, stealing, murder, hatred. You see, Jesus came and he has the power to fulfill what God destiny is for us. And when you bash the Bible who points to Christ, you are bashing Christ and you’re eliminating the force in your life that can change your life and change society.
What does he say happens when people bash the Bible?
2 Corinthians 5:17: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.

He cites Isaiah 1:11 and says God did require the sacrifices, but “his goal wasn’t the shadow”; the people embraced the example and did not do what it said. He says the shadow laws were there “to remind them to treat people right, to live right, and to do right.”

So these are shadow laws, Mr. Savage. They have nothing to do with anything except to remind people in the Old Testament to live holy and right. Even in the Old Testament, Mr. Obama, God told him that he didn’t want these things. He told him that shadow laws were reminders to live right. Isaiah 1:11: “What purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices to me? I don’t delight in the blood of bulls and lambs and goats when you come to me. Who has required this?” Well, he required it. He’s the one said to offer lambs. He’s the one said to burn incense. He’s the one said to take the Sabbath day off and worship God and meet together and come into the— He said all that. But see, his goal wasn’t the shadow. His goal was good. And they were embracing the shadow, the example, and not doing what the example said to do. Are you with me? And we read on and we see it. Bring no more worthless sacrifices. Incense is an abomination to me. New moon, Sabbath, feast. My soul hates when you spread your hands and make many prayers. I will hide my eyes from you and I will not hear you. And then he says what those shadow laws are for. Wash yourselves. Make yourself clean. Put away the evil of your doings from my eyes. Cease to do evil and learn to do good. You see, the shadow laws were there to remind them to treat people right, to live right, and to do right. And they were caught up in the shadow laws.

Isaiah 1:11-13: “To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices to Me?” Says the LORD. “I have had enough of burnt offerings of rams And the fat of fed cattle. I do not delight in the blood of bulls, Or of lambs or goats. “When you come to appear before Me, Who has required this from your hand, To trample My courts? Bring no more futile sacrifices; Incense is an abomination to Me. The New Moons, the Sabbaths, and the calling of assemblies— I cannot endure iniquity and the sacred meeting. Isaiah 1:16-17: “Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean; Put away the evil of your doings from before My eyes. Cease to do evil, Learn to do good; Seek justice, Rebuke the oppressor; Defend the fatherless, Plead for the widow.
How do the Lord’s table and assembling together work as reminders?

He says the Lord’s table reminds us that Jesus died for our sins and gives new life, and we miss the point if we take communion but “don’t go to the real thing.” He says we assemble to be “stirred up to love one another” and do good when we leave, not for music or drama.
How do the Lord’s table and assembling together work as reminders?

See, they embraced the shadow. Is this clear to you? Now, watch this. Let’s bring it up to date. The Lord’s table. Jesus said, as of— do you do this in what? Remembrance of me. It reminds us that he died for our sins that we can get forgiveness even as a Christian. And he gives us that new life, that resurrection. That’s what the communion table’s for. But when we just take communion and embrace communion and don’t go to the real thing, we live any way we want, don’t we? Let’s take another one. Assembling together. The Bible says, “Assembling yourself together, even the more so as you see the day approaching, stirring up one another to love and to good works.” See, that’s why we come together is to remind ourselves that we are to go out and be a light to this world that they may see our good works. That’s the purpose of assembling. It’s not music. It’s not drama. It’s not some prophet or priest. It’s we are supposed to be stirred up to love one another, not hurt one another, and do good when we leave. It’s not having a bell ringing message and you know some athlete come in and give their testimony or whatever. We should come to church too like the old the New Testament church when the Roman leaders wrote to each other about the church.
How do the Lord’s table and assembling together work as reminders?

Luke 22:19: And He took bread, gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body which is given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.” Hebrews 10:24-25: And let us consider one another in order to stir up love and good works, not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as is the manner of some, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching.
How are praise and baptism reminders, not substitutes?

He says praise and worship is a sacrifice, citing the “sacrifice of praise, the fruit of your lips,” and that “if your worship isn’t stirring you to live good, then you’re not worshiping.” He says baptism “reminds you that Jesus died on the cross for your sins” and made you a new man.
How are praise and baptism reminders, not substitutes?

They get together on Sunday and they make a vow not to do wrong. Every Sunday they kept repeating the vow. Why? Because they messed up sometimes and they had to change and they had to recommit to doing right. Have any of you Christians ever messed up? Yeah. You see? Hallelujah. Praise and worship. My gosh. You know, when I got saved, praise and worship was taboo. Like the Holy Ghost baptism, man. If you were filled with the Holy Ghost, you were in a church on the other side of the street and everybody looked down on you. And if you praise and worship God, lifting your hands and dancing and, you know, being outwardly demonstrative, man, that’s horrible. Now everybody’s doing it. But folks, praise and worship is a sacrifice. In Hebrews, it says, “Bring therefore the sacrifice of praise, the fruit of your lips, giving thanks to his name.” That’s our sacrifices. But the sacrifice is not what we embrace. We embrace who the sacrifice brings us to. And that’s the presence of Jesus. And Jesus wants us to live right. Isn’t that right? So it reminds us again to what? Live right, do good. And if your worship isn’t stirring you to live good, then you’re not worshiping. You’re enjoying music. That’s all. Hallelujah. H2O means water baptism in case you didn’t know that. You know, people got their baptism or certificate. Baptism doesn’t mean a hill of beans. Baptism reminds you that Jesus died on the cross for your sins, rose from the grave and made you a new man and an overcomer of sin.
How are praise and baptism reminders, not substitutes?
Hebrews 13:15: Therefore by Him let us continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name.
Where do most American Christians put their confidence? (1 Samuel 15:22)

He asks whether Christians embrace the shadow or the reality, saying “We’re putting confidence in our church. We’re putting confidence in our baptism.” He cites 1 Samuel 15:22, “to obey is better than sacrifice,” and says God wants us to listen to Him, respond and live for Him.
Where do most American Christians put their confidence? (1 Samuel 15:22)

He put away sin. The old man is dead. So every time we see someone baptized, we are reminded that we’re new creatures. Sin no more has control over us. See, it’s a reminder. But what do most American Christians embrace? Do they embrace the shadow of the thing or do they really get the reality of the thing? See, we’re putting confidence in our church. We’re putting confidence in our baptism. We’re putting confidence and I take communion on Sunday when it should be pointing us to Jesus Christ and living for him. And that’s a good place for an amen. Now, these people are just wrong. Here it is again. 1st Samuel 15:22. Has the Lord a great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to listen better than the fat of rams. God wants us to listen to him and respond to him and live for him. And the sacrifices were there to direct us to that. Amen. Now I want to focus in on a very significant shadow law. This is important for you. You young Christians, you need to get this in your cranial vacuum. You old folks need to shake the cobwebs out of your head here and get this in there. Are you ready?
Where do most American Christians put their confidence? (1 Samuel 15:22)

1 Samuel 15:22: So Samuel said: “Has the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, As in obeying the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, And to heed than the fat of rams.
Why couldn’t they keep the shadow laws? (John 7:19)

He cites John 7:19, “Moses gave you the law, yet none of you keep it,” and says it was impossible because they were constantly unclean and “spent all their life trying to get clean.” He says the Jews embraced the shadow instead of what it pointed to, and warns we are in danger of doing the same.
Why couldn’t they keep the shadow laws? (John 7:19)

John 7:19, “Moses gave you the law, yet none of you keep it.” Why didn’t they keep it? Because it was impossible. Them guys were unclean every day. If they had sex with their spouse, they were unclean. If a bug landed on their— a bug landed on their plate or whatever, they were unclean. Every time you turn around, they’re unclean. They’re unclean. They spent all their life trying to get clean. The the shadow laws were impossible to keep. And yet the Jews embraced the shadow instead of what the shadow pointed to. And today we are embracing the shadow and to what the shadow points to. We’re in danger of that. Hallelujah.
Why couldn’t they keep the shadow laws? (John 7:19)
John 7:19: Did not Moses give you the law, yet none of you keeps the law? Why do you seek to kill Me?”
Why do some groups want you to follow them instead of Christ? (Galatians 6:13)

He cites Galatians 6:13 and says certain churches have you do certain things because “they glory in your flesh,” and that “they’re not wanting you to follow Christ.” He says the holy water that matters “is the baptism of the Holy Ghost and the word of the Lord.”
Why do some groups want you to follow them instead of Christ? (Galatians 6:13)

Galatians 6:13: “Neither they who are circumcised keep the law, but desire to have you circumcised so they may glory in your flesh.” Why does the Catholic Church have holy water there and all that and all this [unclear] and all this? So they can glory. That’s a Catholic. It does nothing. The holy water does nothing. The holy water is the baptism of the Holy Ghost and the word of the Lord. That’s the holy water. That’s the real thing. Can I hear an amen? Amen. See, why does certain churches have you do the certain thing? They glory in your flesh. Why does Dan Savage try to get you to believe the Bible’s full of BS so he can glory in your flesh turning from the Bible? Yeah. Yeah, I got through. See, they want you to follow them. They’re not wanting you to follow Christ. They want you to follow them, their group, their church. Now, that’s good preaching right there. And who are we to follow? And what word are we to follow? His word, right? Psalms 14 makes it even more clear. The Lord looked down from heaven to see if any understood who seek God. And his conclusion was they’ve all turned aside together. They’ve become corrupt. None does good. No, not one. You see, we mess up with these requirements of God. We mess up. But look at here. Us Christians make mistakes. Us believers make mistakes.
Why do some groups want you to follow them instead of Christ? (Galatians 6:13)

Galatians 6:13: For not even those who are circumcised keep the law, but they desire to have you circumcised that they may boast in your flesh. Psalm 14:2-3: The LORD looks down from heaven upon the children of men, To see if there are any who understand, who seek God. They have all turned aside, They have together become corrupt; There is none who does good, No, not one.
What is the importance of the shadow law, and why do we all make mistakes?

He says the shadow laws were impossible to keep because “they pointed to a requirement of God that was impossible without God for you to live up to.” He says believers make mistakes too, and that people who criticize the church can “always find” fault because we are “coming into maturity.”
What is the importance of the shadow law, and why do we all make mistakes?

I I’m a believer and I make mistakes. How many believers say, you know, I make mistakes? I made them in the past. I’ll probably make them tomorrow. Yeah. You see, this is the importance of the shadow law. The shadow laws were impossible to keep. Why? Because they pointed to a requirement of God that was impossible without God for you to live up to. It’s impossible. And this is the importance of the shadow law. The biggest biggest one. Now listen to this. Have all your workers of iniquity no knowledge? Who eat up my people as they eat bread and do not call on the Lord? See, this guy has the audacity to lambaste our Bible. A lot of these students walked out. When he started bashing the Bible, they walked out. Others applauded. And see, these people oppose us. Yes, they can find fault with us because we’re coming into maturity. We’re coming into his image. They can always find. You can’t be good enough for people that are trying to find something to criticize the church about. Ain’t I right? But see, us Christians know that Jesus is the answer for us and our mistakes. And you shouldn’t be messing around with this church. You should not be messing around with this church, even with their flaws. You don’t want to mess around with God’s people.
What is the importance of the shadow law, and why do we all make mistakes?
Psalm 14:4: Have all the workers of iniquity no knowledge, Who eat up my people as they eat bread, And do not call on the LORD?
Why weren’t people stoned for breaking the shadow laws?

He begins to address homosexuality by saying the food and clothing laws were “examples of living holy,” and that nobody was stoned in the Bible for the woman who lied about being a virgin: “Zero.” He says the one man stoned for working on Saturday was “an example of the judgment of God,” and that the real issue is an eternal price.
Why weren’t people stoned for breaking the shadow laws?

Now, let me address homosexuality. Now, we we address the food, the clothing, the different clothing. It was all examples of living holy. Okay? The virgin or the woman that wasn’t a virgin on her [unclear] night, she got stoned because she said she was a virgin. They didn’t put that in there and she wasn’t. She lied and and she went into a marriage with a lie and deception. And you know how many people were stoned for that in the Bible? Zero. Interesting, isn’t it? Why? It’s a shadow law. God didn’t put it there for us to go around killing people that sinned. It’s a shadow law. How many people were stoned for picking up sticks on the Saturday? One. One for working on Saturday and that was in in Exodus to give us an example of the judgment of God. You see there God is coming to judge and there is a judgment. But Jesus said, “I’ve not come to destroy sinners but to what? Save them.” See, God’s in his saving timetable right now. But when he comes again, folks, he’s going to judge. And stoning the people that messed up back there in the Bible is not the issue. It’s you are going to pay an eternal price.
Why weren’t people stoned for breaking the shadow laws?
