items.ser: No One Knows the Day · Part 1
p: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that no one knows the day or hour of Christ’s return, then walks through the pre-tribulation rapture teaching and a long history of failed end-time predictions, from 400 AD to Y2K and 2012. He warns that such predictions distract believers from the great commandment, make the church look foolish and confuse new Christians, and says God’s signs will be supernatural.
Why do Christians need present truth for their generation? (2 Peter 1:12; 1 Chronicles 12:32)

He says to be established in present truth, “truth for your time your generation your person.” He trusts that God’s people, like the children of Issachar, will have understanding of their present time and know what they ought to do.
Why do Christians need present truth for their generation? (2 Peter 1:12; 1 Chronicles 12:32)

Having a great life in Jesus Christ as we look into the scriptures in another session on present truth as 2 Peter 1:12 declares to us be established in present truth truth for your time your generation your person we want to remind you that Ecclesiastes chapter 3 tells us that God has a purpose under heaven he has a purpose on earth and he does those purposes in seasons and times also we want to remind you of 1 Chronicles 12:38 the children of Israel, of Issachar, I’m sorry had understanding of the times to know what Israel ought to do and we trust when we’re finished with this session you the Israel of God the spiritual Israel God’s people Christians will have understanding of your present generation your present time and know what you ought to do.
Why do Christians need present truth for their generation? (2 Peter 1:12; 1 Chronicles 12:32)

2 Peter 1:12: For this reason I will not be negligent to remind you always of these things, though you know and are established in the present truth. Ecclesiastes 3:1: To everything there is a season, A time for every purpose under heaven: 1 Chronicles 12:32: of the sons of Issachar who had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do, their chiefs were two hundred; and all their brethren were at their command;
Does anyone know the day or hour of Christ’s return? (Acts 1:7; Matthew 24:36; Mark 13:32)

He reads that it is not for us to know the times or seasons which the Father has put in His own authority, and that no one knows the day or hour. He says the Son of Man comes in an hour “you’re not even thinking about it.”
Does anyone know the day or hour of Christ’s return? (Acts 1:7; Matthew 24:36; Mark 13:32)

In this session we’re going to deal with no one knows the day or the hour and the times and the seasons which God has put in his own hands. Acts 1:6 says it’s not for you to know the times or seasons which the father has put in his own authority Matthew 24:36 and Mark 13:32 no one knows the day or hour. Matthew 25:13 you know neither the day nor the hour wherein the son of man comes. Matthew 24:44, Luke 12:40, and such an hour as you think not the son of mankind wow.
Does anyone know the day or hour of Christ’s return? (Acts 1:7; Matthew 24:36; Mark 13:32)

Acts 1:7: And He said to them, “It is not for you to know times or seasons which the Father has put in His own authority. Matthew 24:36: “But of that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels of heaven, but My Father only. Mark 13:32: “But of that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father. Matthew 25:13: “Watch therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour in which the Son of Man is coming. Matthew 24:44: Therefore you also be ready, for the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect. Luke 12:40: Therefore you also be ready, for the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect.”
Is “a thousand years as one day” a timeline for the end? (2 Peter 3:8)

He says that in spite of no one knowing the day, mankind has tried to predict it ever since Christ left the earth, including a 6,000-year timeline based on a thousand years as one day. He says “the Bible doesn’t say that but we presuppose that,” and when God tells us we don’t know, we say “yes we do we got a little chart here to prove it.”
Is “a thousand years as one day” a timeline for the end? (2 Peter 3:8)

As you think not you’re not even thinking about it, bingo, God comes. We’re going to look at in spite of the fact that no one knows the day or at the hour. Mankind has been trying to predict it ever since Christ left the earth. In the early church they come up with the earth timeline is similar to the seven days of creation God created the earth in seven 24-hour days but the earth’s historical chronology is a thousand years is one day 2 Peter 3:8. So we presuppose. Now the Bible doesn’t say that but we presuppose that. A thousand years as a day God created the earth and six days and then rested the seventh day so the seventh day would be the millennium the thousand year reign of Christ and there would be six thousand years up to when Christ’s return and as you know he has it right. But we come up with these numerology. These little things that we say open up when God tells us we don’t know we look back at him and say yes we do we got a little chart here to prove it. All right so the second coming would be before the seventh day millennial reign of Christ now.
Is “a thousand years as one day” a timeline for the end? (2 Peter 3:8)
2 Peter 3:8: But, beloved, do not forget this one thing, that with the Lord one day is as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.
What did some early church fathers believe about the second coming?

He says some believed in a pre-millennial second coming and a thousand-year reign, while others said Christ is ruling now and His kingdom is eternal: “We don’t have to wait we got victory from the at the cross.” He says they believed in one second coming, one resurrection, one judgment and one eternal kingdom, with tribulation but no seven years of tribulation.
What did some early church fathers believe about the second coming?

They believe that the gospel has to be preached to all nations they believed in the conversion of Israel before he comes the falling away the tribulation and the revealing of the man of sin the antichrist the antichrist has always been a focus on people predicting the end time and so some of our church fathers believed in the pre-millennial second coming of Jesus Christ then a thousand year reign others says no it’s not an actual thousand years Christ is ruling now his kingdom is now his kingdom is eternal his kingdom has always been and he’s always been a king and he always will be a king. We don’t have to wait we got victory from the at the cross see. And we know the king now and when he comes will recognize him who he is they believe that church is spiritual Israel that the old and new covenant uh is one covenant. And they believe that the kingdom is not temporary. They believed in one second coming, one resurrection, one judgment and one eternal kingdom okay. No seven years of tribulation but they did believe in tribulation. They just didn’t take Daniel’s 70th week and stretch it over two thousand years or more than that over two thousand years to the end time all right then you got.
What is the pre-tribulation rapture teaching?

He describes the popular teaching that Jesus can come any moment and rapture His church in a secret coming, followed by seven years of tribulation the saints do not go through. He says that has Christ coming back again and again: “Christ is up down up down up down up down.”
What is the pre-tribulation rapture teaching?

The tribulation people which is very popular today everywhere you go this is preach. Especially in fundamental circles spirit-filled circles and so forth okay so they believe here’s Jesus coming here’s the cross they believe that he can come any moment. Everything is ready he can pop through the sky at any time. All right they. Get the scriptures to say he’s going to come and rapture his church in a secret coming. You know two people are on a plane all sudden of a one’s gone the other remained two people are in a car the driver’s gone and the passenger wrecks you’ve seen all the pictures you’ve heard all the tales. Secret. Pre-tribulation rapture then seven years of tribulation but the saints are taken out so they don’t go through any trouble saints are taken out all right. Then. Christ is going to come back again to judge the nations so he’s coming back a third time. Came the first time as the savior came the second time to secretly take out his people and he’s coming a third time to judge the nations and then after the millennium. He’s gonna come another time. To lose Satan on the earth my gosh Christ is up down up down up down up down.
Where did the pre-trib teaching come from, and who profited from it?

He says the pre-trib teaching started with one man and spread to well-known preachers, seminaries and denominations. He says end-time authors kept rewriting books because their predictions were wrong, “and people keep buying these books and they just keep getting richer.”
Where did the pre-trib teaching come from, and who profited from it?

Pre-trib, mid-trib, post-trib mid-trib is really not I I don’t meet anybody with mid-trib anymore that just kind of went away but it’s pre-trib or post-trib. John Darby started this thing basically D.L. Moody bought into it Scofield bought into it the Dallas seminar, the spirit-filled seminar down there bought into it the Baptist bought into it Hal Lindsey wrote a book about it Late Great Planet Earth missed all over the place and just rewrote it and made another million dollars correcting his first mistake rewrote it again made another million dollars or more you know correcting his second mistake rewrote it he’s rewritten it about seven times. Because his predictions was wrong. And people keep buying these books and they just keep getting richer these people Tim LaHaye movies and books made a fortune of a God’s people.
Why are failed end-time predictions harmful?

He says people idolize those who claim end-time revelation instead of reading the Bible for themselves. He says failed prophecies distract followers of Christ from the great commandment, make the church look crazy to outsiders, and confuse baby Christians: “we lose a lot of baby Christian to cults from foolish prophecies.”
Why are failed end-time predictions harmful?

So in spite of the fact that we don’t know the day of the hour everybody. Is saying except me except me I’m the spiritual one I got revelation this is how it’s going to work out I got a chart and. I know and we worship them we idolize them buy their books listen to them instead of reading the Bible for ourselves. These failed end-time prophecies that by the way no one knows the specifics of the Bible says distracts followers of Christ from the great commandment that sum up and fulfills the prophecy, the prophets and the laws and it also makes the church look mad looks stupid look crazy like the word lunatics.
What end-time predictions failed in the church’s first thousand years?

He gives a history starting with a bishop who said the end would be in 400 AD and the antichrist was already born, then numerology predictions for 500 AD, 793 and 800 AD. He says as the millennium approached many preachers and Christians believed the world would end, “and they missed.”
What end-time predictions failed in the church’s first thousand years?

When we predict that nothing happens and we we just make another prediction. It’s impractical to outsiders. And it really confuses baby Christians and we lose a lot of baby Christian to cults from foolish prophecies. Now Christ’s second coming when predictions fail I’m going to give you a history of this. And we’re going to start at 400 AD the Bishop of Tours said the end time would be at 400 AD and the antichrist was already born focus on the antichrist the big bad antichrist the big bad beast. A Christian of Rome, of a renowned Christian of Rome, Julius, he through numerology calculated the dimensions of Noah’s ark to say that Christ and the world would come and the world would end in 500 AD okay here’s numerology. Spanish monk said it would come in 793 the Bishop Gregory said he would come in 800 AD Pope Sylvester the infallible popes. And many others see the millennium is coming. A thousand years and everybody’s focused on this millennium a thousand years thousand years of the day days of the thousand years you know Christ is going to reign thousand years everybody every time the thing clock turns over a thousand years he’s coming he’s coming and many people many preachers and many Christians believed that Christ would come in the world would end from his birth or at least his ascension unto heaven his death on the cross and ascending up to heaven and they missed the infallible pope goofed.
What end-time predictions failed from the Middle Ages to the 1600s?

He says one pope predicted 1284 AD as 666 years after the rise of Islam, showing “that infatuation with the number 666,” and the planets were predicted to bring the end in 1524 and 1624: “See none of this is new that you’re hearing today.” He says Anabaptist groups took over Münster by force and killed people waiting for Christ to come, “And he didn’t come,” and others predicted 1600, 1658 and 1666.
What end-time predictions failed from the Middle Ages to the 1600s?

Another pope Pope Innocent III said no Christ is going to come in 1284 AD because that’s exactly 666 years after the rise of Islam there’s that infatuation with the number 666 the antichrist numerology numbers. It all started way back there folks there’s nothing new and they’ve all missed ever since they started. Many during the black plague of 1346 and 51 many in Europe thought that the world was going to end. In 1524 and 1624 we’re getting knowledge of the heavens we can see into the clouds and we’re can figure out the planets and and everything up there and all there’s alignment of the planets as alignment of heavenly bodies it’s going to bring destruction of the earth and Jesus is going to come it’s going to be the end of the world. That was in 15 and 24. They missed so they started calculating the heavens again and they come up with another number in 1624. And they missed again. See none of this is new that you’re hearing today. In 1526 33 and 34 the Anabaptists three different groups at three different times said that the kingdom of God was coming down to the earth the city of God was coming down to the earth Münster was one of the cities supposed to be the city of God where Christ set up his rule and reign and they took an army in there invaded it and took it over waiting for Christ to come killed people. And he didn’t come. And the people raised up an army and took the city back. The new Jerusalem come out of heaven, Münster the city and then they picked two other cities. Luther predicted it would end in 1600 AD. Christopher Columbus got in on the act he calculated that the earth would be seven thousand years old in 1658 from the Jewish calendar and calculating the Bible and so the end would be then because that was his calculation numerology of seven thousand years. An explorer getting in on it everybody gets in on it Bishop of Tours to Christopher Columbus more famous failures of prof of end time prophecies interpretation. A black plague again in 1666 and because 666 was in the year 1666. They said Christ was coming there is that infatuation with 666 the antichrist numerology you get it the planets the heavens it’s been going on for centuries.
What end-time predictions failed in the 1700s and 1800s?

He lists a predicted comet in 1719 and 1736, the New England dark day of 1780, a predicted earth-destroying quake in 1805, and the 1833 meteor shower when people climbed on roofs waiting for the rapture. He describes the 1844 great disappointment, when people sold their properties and bought robes, and says “the Bible was plain that nobody knows what the day of the hour.”
What end-time predictions failed in the 1700s and 1800s?

In 17 and 19 and 1736 they predicted a comet would destroy the earth here’s the heavenly bodies again. In 1780 the New England states had a dark day created by a natural phenomena and they go oh the earth is this is a sign of the end of the time the Shakers, the Quakers predicted 1794. Some people predicted that there would be a quake in 1805 1805 that would destroy the whole earth that is some earthquake you know and and they’re they’re they’re infatuated with this wars and rumors of war of famines plagues on earth they’re just infatuated with that verse. 1780. The new england dark day the Shakers, the quake and then in 1833 there was a meteor shower during the middle of the night in America that literally lit up the night for about four hours so many meteors were falling from the sky that the people said you could read a newspaper it was written in the newspaper that you could read and everybody thought this is it this is it something climbed on top of the roof waiting for the rapture the second coming. In 1836 Wesley predicted, John Wesley, that the world would end 1884 the Millerites, Miller he had his numerology you ought to see that chart of his I’ve showed it to you before it’s amazing. How he got down to the day and the month in 18 and 44 he had missed before but this is his last prediction and people went they sold their properties as I’ve told you before they even bought a white robe so they could have resurrection robes to go up you know rapture robes to go up into the sky and they’re sitting there in the high places you know and they even had bathtubs so you could wash before he came and be clean. And then it didn’t come it’s called the great disappointment some people killed themselves other peoples it was so distant in such destitute because they sold their properties their means of of living they got that caught up into it and the Bible was plain that nobody knows what the day of the hour now anybody that knows their Bible would just overlook that because nobody knows.
Did cults and modern preachers predict the end too?

He says groups in the late 1800s and early 1900s predicted the end of time, then Halley’s comet in 1910 and nuclear war in the 1950s: “prediction after prediction after prediction. That did not happen.” He says after Israel took Jerusalem in 1967 prophets said the times of the Gentiles had ended, and he asked how He could have come any minute before that.
Did cults and modern preachers predict the end too?

Oh. The Seventh-day Adventists, the Mormons, the Jehovah Witnesses and other groups during these late 1800s. Early 1900s predicted the end of time Joseph Smith said Christ would come before he died he died and he came well he’s dead now they can’t point their finger at him. That’s nice if you’re going to predict something predict it after your death nobody can attack you. In 1910 Halley’s comet’s making its normal natural cycle but the tail is going to hit the earth and the gases are going to destroy everybody on the earth that’s the end time that’s it all right in the 50s which I lived through. I heard sermon after sermon on how the atomic bomb the atomic war the nuclear war was going to destroy the earth going to destroy you know the the earth by fire and I mean heard it all the time in the prediction after prediction after prediction. That did not happen. 1967 the Jews had a war in 1967 and they conquered all of Jerusalem and all of the West Bank to Jordan but the nations wouldn’t let them have it but now they have all of Jerusalem not just part of it so the prophets immediately rose up and said the times of the Gentile has ended the second coming is here. Now when I talked to them I said before 1967 you said he could come any minute now you’re telling me that in 1967 the fulfillment of the times of the Gentiles. Has been fulfilled and he can come so he couldn’t have come any minute before. And they look at me with daggers. Do you understand church. Yeah. Branham which was a tremendous man when he first started. Healing rose in the 48 as we showed you God moved again in 1948. And he would literally. Tell a person what was wrong with them literally. He didn’t just pray for the sick he told him what their problem was you know you have cancer you have cancer of the [unclear] you know whatever it was amazing. Oral Roberts had a line and he had a card and so he knew what was going on now.
Can faith in your faith corrupt the church?

He says after a period of real healings, some healers got corrupt and said if you don’t get healed “it’s your problem.” He asks whether Jesus ever healed people who had no belief and answers “Yes he did,” and says “when you have faith in your faith and not in the Bible and not in Jesus it doesn’t work.”
Can faith in your faith corrupt the church?

But God was healing there for a short period of time some some amazing things were reported I mean it’s in the newspapers and then as usual these guys get corrupt. And then they start saying you know you’re getting healed if you believe if you believe so if you don’t get healed it’s your problem. Did Jesus ever do that did he ever heal people that had no belief. Yes he did. Hallelujah. But God forbid we blame the mighty man of God it’s got to be the recipient not believing and faith literally corrupted the church because people started having faith in their faith and when you have faith in your faith and not in the Bible and not in Jesus it doesn’t work hallelujah.
Why do famous preachers’ predictions keep missing?

He says famous preachers all missed “because no one knows the day or the hour and the times of the seasons so stop acting like you’re something special.” He says he told ministers in Africa in the 1980s that Christ would not come before 2012, to prove the Mayan calendar wrong.
Why do famous preachers’ predictions keep missing?

Joe uh, Chuck Smith, Calvary Chapel, uh Gordon Lindsay, these famous people, Jerry Falwell, And I can go on on Pat Robinson, all predicted. They all miss and why did they miss because no one knows the day or the hour and the times of the seasons so stop acting like you’re something special. And troubling people’s minds and confusing baby Christians. Then the Y2K the second millennium came I was over in Africa preaching in 1985 86 and 87 and I happened to mention that Christ would not come before the year 2012 just to prove the Mayan calendar was wrong that God didn’t give truth to pagans and man when they went to lunch and those ministers were in there [unclear].
What about the 2012 and Y2K predictions?

He says people get hyped up on predictions and then keep silent or change them after they are wrong. Asked to teach on Y2K, he preached from the Bible, did his research with knowledgeable people and concluded nothing was going to happen, “and it didn’t.”
What about the 2012 and Y2K predictions?

And I simply kept my mouth shut and when they got done I said well we will know when 2012 comes who’s right. 2012 is the come and gone. See anybody can get hyped up on something. 15 years before they’re predicting it. To teach from the Bible on the Y2K problem the computer problem where computers were supposed to you know destroy the world here the computers are going to destroy the world floods and [unclear] lights traffic lights are not going to work right and people are going to be crashing into each other and all this stuff people were buying survival equipment survival food Christians. And I preach from the Bible and I happen to have been trained in computers by the National Cash Register company so I knew about the technology of computers it only can put out what you put into it. And I did my research and I talked to knowledgeable people in the field nothing was going to happen. And it didn’t and so my elders after I got through they said I hope you’re right gonna be embarrassing if you’re wrong well I was right and he didn’t come back and said nah he didn’t come back you know they thought they bought into it the elders of the church elders are some of your worst problems in the church is elders a title without the authority. Hallelujah.
Do scientists predict the end of the world too?

He says secular people get into it too, with theories of magnetic field reversal, gamma rays, solar flares, asteroids, alien attack, supernovas and black holes. He says scientists have theories and talk like they know, “but if you read the little words. You know it possibly could be.”
Do scientists predict the end of the world too?

So. The natural people get into it it’s not just the Bible people. The earth’s going to be destroyed by a magnetic field reversal north pole is going to become south pole and the earth’s going to be destroyed all right gamma rays yeah a proton emitted off of a nuclear reaction and it does. Blows up and expands going to destroy the air solar flare going to destroy the earth an asteroid there are asteroids up there as big as 500 miles over 500 miles wide and if one of them hits the earth you’ve seen the movies on it bingo there goes the earth uh alien attack. That’s really far-fetched. The supernova. Is an explosion that briefly outshines an entire galaxy. Radiating as much energy over the life of a sun just immediate bound gonna destroy the earth the black hole or a star collapsed and sucks supposedly everything into it light can’t even get out it is so strong that light can’t even get out and they saw stars disappear and at least they were honest they didn’t know if they went into the hole or they’re behind the hole if they’re behind the hole how many you know that black stuff is a substance. So see scientists have theories too. And and when they do it they talk like they know what they’re talking about but if you read the little words.
Will God’s end-time signs be supernatural?

He says end-time prophets and secular scientists forget “that God needs no help from nature nor mankind.” He points to the rod and the snake, water to blood, darkness that could be felt, the axe that swam, the dead raised and three hours of darkness at the cross, and says the signs will be supernatural, a miracle that “nature numerology nor mankind can do.”
Will God’s end-time signs be supernatural?

You know it possibly could be it’s a it’s a big difference so that the secular people are in on this also but both. End-time prophets and secular scientists forget that God needs no help from nature nor mankind. Member. Remember he turned the rod to a snake and the snake back to a rock that is supernatural he turned the water to blood and the blood backed the water he turned the darkness he brought darkness for three days that could be felt even a lit candle in a room could not be seen that is supernatural. You understand church. When God gives a sign it’s supernatural. Brimstone from heaven to destroy Sodom and Gomorrah, the axe that swam. How do you scientifically prove that iron doesn’t float but this axe swam. Right up to the top so the prophet could pick it up right at the surface of the water the dead were raised back to life. Including Jesus Christ who they could not find the body of if they could have they could have proved the Bible was wrong. And remember there was darkness at the cross for three hours and every account that I read about the death of Christ caused it an eclipse no eclipse lasts for three hours. It was a supernatural darkening of the day. I mean oh God says I want the earth to be dark it’s going to be dark and he doesn’t need our scientific laws to work through that’s what makes it a sign supernatural a miracle. It will be signs a supernatural a miracle that nature numerology nor mankind can do. These events are going to totally be God.
Will God’s end-time signs be supernatural?

Exodus 10:21-23: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward heaven, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, darkness which may even be felt.” So Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and there was thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days. They did not see one another; nor did anyone rise from his place for three days. But all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings. 2 Kings 6:5-7: But as one was cutting down a tree, the iron ax head fell into the water; and he cried out and said, “Alas, master! For it was borrowed.” So the man of God said, “Where did it fall?” And he showed him the place. So he cut off a stick, and threw it in there; and he made the iron float. Therefore he said, “Pick it up for yourself.” So he reached out his hand and took it. Luke 23:44-45: Now it was about the sixth hour, and there was darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour. Then the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn in two.
Have people always tried to predict Christ’s return?
He says mankind has been trying to predict it ever since Christ left the earth, beginning in the early church.
Is Christ king now, or only after He returns?
He says Christ is ruling now, His kingdom is eternal, “and he’s always been a king and he always will be a king.”
Is the mid-tribulation view still taught?
He says he doesn’t meet anybody with mid-trib anymore; it is pre-trib or post-trib.
Why does he warn against idolizing end-time teachers?
He says everybody claims, “I got revelation this is how it’s going to work out I got a chart,” and we idolize them and buy their books instead of reading the Bible for ourselves.
Why does he talk about an infatuation with 666?
He says predictions were tied to 666 years after the rise of Islam and to the year 1666, showing an infatuation with the antichrist and numerology that has gone on for centuries.
What happened in the 1833 meteor shower?
He says meteors lit up the night for about four hours so that you could read a newspaper, and everybody thought “this is it,” some even waiting on the roof for the rapture.
What happened after the 1844 prediction failed?
He says it was called the great disappointment; some people killed themselves and others were destitute because they had sold their properties and means of living.
What does he say about predicting the end after your death?
He jokes, “if you’re going to predict something predict it after your death nobody can attack you.”
Could Christ come any minute before 1967?
He says prophets taught He could come any minute, then said 1967 fulfilled the times of the Gentiles so He can come, which means “he couldn’t have come any minute before.”
Did Jesus heal people who had no belief?
He asks, “Did Jesus ever do that did he ever heal people that had no belief. Yes he did.”

He says we get distracted with end-time events, finances, prosperity and other “P’s” from Christ’s first message: repent and believe the gospel, for the kingdom of God is at hand.

Repent. What were Jesus’ final words on His coming? (Matthew 24:44)

What were Jesus’ final words on His coming? (Matthew 24:44)

Jesus final words on the issue Matthew 24:44 therefore be ready that’s his final word. After all of this he says be ready be prepared. Okay. He starts yielding to lust of the eyes lust of the flesh the pride of life the cares of this life the day of the Lord would come upon him. Unaware. He is not ready. And God’s saying to us in America are we ready. After all this teaching Jesus focused on be ready admit you’re wrong. Feel bad about being wrong when God convicts you you will feel bad about it that’s part of it when he is involved in this and turn he will urge you to turn from that don’t do that sexual immorality, [unclear], stealing and lying anymore and he will finish the good work line upon line, precept upon precept in your life you won’t start out a mature Christian but he will get you there that’s his promise and that’s his final word I submit to you that Bible morality may be unpopular but the results are indisputable.
What were Jesus’ final words on His coming? (Matthew 24:44)

There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
What does the word “sign” mean in Matthew 24?

Are wars and rumors of wars a sign of the end?

What does a good preacher say about who has the answer?

When does he say Jerusalem and the temple were destroyed?

How did he learn to check teaching by the Scriptures?

Will false prophets do miracles, and can the elect be deceived?

But he says it is impossible to deceive the followers of Christ: “they know him they know his book and they stand firm,” and they are still on earth: “No secret rapture.”
He says the elect cannot be deceived and they are still on earth: “No secret rapture.” He says nothing is secret about His coming, which everybody sees and hears.
Why is the coming of Jesus called supernatural?
He says it is supernatural because when Christ comes everybody everywhere on earth sees Him, while normally we do not see what happens on the other side of the earth.
What kind of church will be on earth when He comes?
He says the elect will be so strong that false prophets and miracles cannot move them from Jesus Christ, a glorious church without spot or wrinkle that overcomes the gates of hell.
How can you tell if a teaching about the end time is scriptural?
He says the scriptures always put everything in alignment, and “when it’s out of alignment. It’s not scripture.”
Is the seal of God the same as the baptism of the Holy Spirit?
He says no: anyone who accepts Christ receives His Spirit and becomes the temple of God, while the baptism of the Holy Spirit is a baptism of power with gifts.
Is the kingdom of God here now or coming?
He says Christ’s first message was that the kingdom of God is at hand: “it’s here it’s not coming it’s here,” and we are part of His kingdom with laws that protect and bless us.
Do we have to start out as mature Christians?
He says you won’t start out a mature Christian, but God will finish the good work in your life, line upon line, and get you there: “that’s his promise.”

items.d: In this message, Pastor David G. Kincer continues on the baptism of the Holy Ghost, teaching that it brings understanding of God’s word. He covers Proverbs 1:23 and Acts 2:38, why the apostles needed their…
p: In this message, Pastor David G. Kincer continues on the baptism of the Holy Ghost, teaching that it brings understanding of God’s word. He covers Proverbs 1:23 and Acts 2:38, why the apostles needed their understanding opened, the hardened heart, 1 Corinthians 14 on tongues, and why love and maturity are the greatest signs.
Where does he say the Holy Spirit is promised? (Ephesians 5:18, Proverbs 1:23, Joel 2:28, Acts 2:38)

He says he is “a firm promoter of the baptism of the Holy Ghost” and wants “everything that God offers to get me into the divine nature.” He says Proverbs 1:23, “turn at my reproof,” holds the same promise as Joel 2:28, “I will pour out my spirit unto you,” and as Acts 2:38, so “the same promise in the Old Testament is the same promise in the New.”
Where does he say the Holy Spirit is promised? (Ephesians 5:18, Proverbs 1:23, Joel 2:28, Acts 2:38)

Ephesians 5:8 says, “Be filled with the Spirit, be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess.” And that word “excess” does not mean where you get drunk to intoxicate you, you know, you’re stumbling around. It means the word means it leads to undisciplined behavior. Don’t get drunk with wine, because it brings you to undisciplined, uncontrollable behavior. That’s what alcohol does, and so does marijuana and other drugs. So we are going to continue on the baptism of the Holy Spirit and show you another one of its ministers, of ministries rather, to those who receive the baptism of the Holy Ghost. I am a firm promoter of the baptism of the Holy Ghost because the Bible promotes the baptism of the Holy Ghost, and I also experienced the baptism of the Holy Ghost, so I know what I’m talking about from both the Bible and my experience. Okay. Now, I’m going to be sharing with you some things that I didn’t know until the last few years, when God stepped back and waited for me to seek him to find out some new truth. Okay, now a further look at the Holy Spirit and its effect on us: partaking, participating in the divine nature. If I need something to empower me and help me partake of the divine nature, I don’t want to dismiss it, do you? I want everything that God offers to get me into the divine nature. Could that be an amen? And the Holy Spirit is one of these promises that he promised to give us, to bring us into the divine nature. Proverbs 1:23. Pentecostal has never used this scripture; they always use Joel 2:28. Charismatics, same way: Joel 2:28, Acts 2, Joel 2:28 and Acts 2, Joel 2:28, Acts 2, that’s it. But the Holy Ghost is mentioned all throughout the Old Testament, and the same words: “I will pour out.” “Turn at my reproof.” Okay, “turn” means repent. Repent at my reproof, when I come to you with the prophets, when I come to you with preachers preaching the word. If you will repent and turn from your sins, admit you’re wrong, does that sound like a New Testament principle? Absolutely. It wasn’t, that’s not a New Testament principle, it’s since the beginning principle. You know, so many Christians think the New Testament just obliterated, just ended the Old Testament. Folks, all this stuff is in the Old Testament, all of it. So here in Proverbs 1:23: “Turn at my reproof,” and he says if you will repent, I’ll do something for you: “Behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you.” Wow. Same word “pour” as Joel used: “I will pour out my spirit on all flesh.” Here it is in Proverbs, okay: “I will pour out my spirit unto you.” Now, we got to understand that this is the same statement in the New Testament, Acts 2:38: “Repent and be baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ for the remission, forgiveness, of sins, and you shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.” Okay, the same promise in the Old Testament is the same promise in the New. So when Dave Kincer heard the preaching of the gospel, and he confessed his sins and asked Jesus to forgive his sins, and I renounced those sins, knew they were wrong, and I purposed to turn from them. Now, I didn’t turn from all of them in one day; I just purposed to turn from them. It took me some time to get rid of some sins. How many took you a little time to get rid of? Yeah, yeah. But my goal, my heart, was to renounce these things and get rid of them. Then I became a candidate for the baptism of the Holy Ghost.
Where does he say the Holy Spirit is promised? (Ephesians 5:18, Proverbs 1:23, Joel 2:28, Acts 2:38)

Ephesians 5:18: And do not be drunk with wine, in which is dissipation; but be filled with the Spirit, Proverbs 1:23: Turn at my rebuke; Surely I will pour out my spirit on you; I will make my words known to you. Joel 2:28: “And it shall come to pass afterward That I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh; Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, Your old men shall dream dreams, Your young men shall see visions. Acts 2:38: Then Peter said to them, “Repent, and let every one of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins; and you shall receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
What does Philip in Samaria show about the baptism of the Holy Ghost? (Acts 8)

He says Philip preached in Samaria with healings, belief and water baptism, and that “days later Peter came down and laid hands on them and they got the Holy Ghost.” He says “the Holy Ghost was a different experience than water baptism, than salvation, than miracles and signs and wonders and hearing the preaching of the word. We need them all.” He calls the claim that you get it in water baptism “a bunch of baloney.”
What does Philip in Samaria show about the baptism of the Holy Ghost? (Acts 8)

Now, you find in Acts 8 a story of Philip going down and preaching the gospel to the Samaritans, okay, the city of Samaria. He preached the gospel, there were healings and miracles going on, the people believed. Great joy filled the city. The people repented, the people were baptized in water, tremendous thing. Now, folks, I have been trying for 40 years to get the church to see this. Philip went down and preached the gospel. Jesus said that he will work with the word, with signs following, if we would preach his gospel, preach his gospel, not man’s ideas, he would back it up with miracles and signs and wonders. And we don’t see that today, and one of the reasons we don’t see it in America. We’re seeing it overseas, whether people want to accept it or not, it’s happening overseas in South America, Central America, Africa, Asia. It’s happening. Okay, the Book of Acts is happening. The miracles happened, they were baptized in water, then days later Peter came down and laid hands on them and they got the Holy Ghost. The Holy Ghost was a different experience than water baptism, than salvation, than miracles and signs and wonders and hearing the preaching of the word. We need them all. Could that be an amen? And I’ve been trying for 40 years to get God’s people to get their spiritual minds opened up to this: that when God arises, his enemies are scattered; if he be lifted up, he’ll draw all men to him. And the key to this is the power of the word and the power of the Holy Ghost, and get the mechanics out, get the ritual out, get our opinions out, and stick to the word, and God will come and do his thing, and people will come. People will come when there’s real miracles going on. People will come when there’s a real move of God changing people’s lives. See a homosexual changing his life, that’s a miracle. An alcoholic changing his life, that’s a miracle, and the word’s going to get out. You know, advertisement, you can’t get better advertisement than that. But we have gotten distracted in America, and we’ve been distracted for decades. And today I want to make sure that you know what I’m trying to get across to you. Amen. What the Holy Ghost is trying to get across to you. All right, so these people that say, “I got baptized in the Holy Ghost when I got baptized in water,” that’s a bunch of baloney. These people that say there’s no indication or sign that you are filled with the Holy Ghost, that’s a bunch of baloney. They are different experiences, and we need them all. And this Holy Ghost is a promise given to us to be partakers of the divine nature, and the Bible says without him we can do what? Nothing.
What does Philip in Samaria show about the baptism of the Holy Ghost? (Acts 8)

Acts 8:5-17: Then Philip went down to the city of Samaria and preached Christ to them. And the multitudes with one accord heeded the things spoken by Philip, hearing and seeing the miracles which he did. For unclean spirits, crying with a loud voice, came out of many who were possessed; and many who were paralyzed and lame were healed. And there was great joy in that city. But there was a certain man called Simon, who previously practiced sorcery in the city and astonished the people of Samaria, claiming that he was someone great, to whom they all gave heed, from the least to the greatest, saying, “This man is the great power of God.” And they heeded him because he had astonished them with his sorceries for a long time. But when they believed Philip as he preached the things concerning the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, both men and women were baptized. Then Simon himself also believed; and when he was baptized he continued with Philip, and was amazed, seeing the miracles and signs which were done. Now when the apostles who were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them, who, when they had come down, prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Spirit. For as yet He had fallen upon none of them. They had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. Then they laid hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
Does the baptism do it all? (Proverbs 1:23, 2 Timothy 2:15, John 14:26)

He says “there’s no magical baptism, water or Holy Ghost,” and “you got to put some effort into this.” He says “the Holy Ghost will drive you into the word,” citing John 14:26, and that the Holy Ghost “will only reveal to you what Jesus Christ himself taught and the disciples passed on,” not any minister’s opinions.
Does the baptism do it all? (Proverbs 1:23, 2 Timothy 2:15, John 14:26)

Folks, we need Jesus, we need the Holy Ghost. Amen. Now then, he says what he will do when he poured out his spirit unto you: “I will make known my words unto you.” Boy, that would be nice if God’s people really understood the Bible, and you can raise your hand and actually say, “I understand from Genesis to Revelation the whole Bible.” You’re a wise people. And you know, one of the reasons is you haven’t really read it consistently or studied it. The Bible says, “Study to show yourself approved.” Put some time into this book. We just want, you know, water baptism does it all, or the Holy Ghost baptism does it all. No, you got to put some effort into this. I mean, will you raise your hand and say, “Yeah, I agree with that, I got to put some effort into this”? There’s no magical baptism, water or Holy Ghost. The Holy Ghost will drive you into the word. Okay, how many would like for the Holy Ghost to come and give you understanding of his word? It’s important that you respond, because God is looking, and you can respond mechanically, or you can be distracted like some of these teens over here giggling and so forth, writing notes between each other and distracting the other guy, or you can get serious and you can attain these things. Huh? So publicly responding, I found as a young Christian, was a very important part of my growth in God. John 14:26: “The Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, shall teach you all things.” See, the New Testament confirms and verifies what God said he would do in Proverbs. The Holy Ghost will teach you all things and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you. We got to get away from [unclear] and [unclear] and [unclear] and whatever, and we got to get back to Jesus Christ and the apostles’ doctrine. And I’m not trying to knock that, I’m just telling you people are worshiping ministers, and they’re looking to ministers to tell them what to do, when they need to go to that Bible and get their understanding open to what Jesus Christ himself said. And that’s all the Holy Ghost will reveal to you. He won’t reveal to you [unclear]’s opinions, he won’t reveal to you [unclear]’s opinions or Billy Graham’s opinions. The Holy Ghost will only reveal to you what Jesus Christ himself taught and the disciples passed on. Amen. And I told you before, I read many books when I was a young Christian, 30, 35 books a year, but nothing surpassed the Bible. I finally realized I don’t need human books, I need the Holy Spirit revealing this Bible to me.
Does the baptism do it all? (Proverbs 1:23, 2 Timothy 2:15, John 14:26)

Proverbs 1:23: Turn at my rebuke; Surely I will pour out my spirit on you; I will make my words known to you. 2 Timothy 2:15: Be diligent to present yourself approved to God, a worker who does not need to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth. John 14:26: But the Helper, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in My name, He will teach you all things, and bring to your remembrance all things that I said to you.
Why does he say books should never replace the Bible? (1 Corinthians 2:13)

He says “books should never replace the Bible” and that you “come to the level of the real author, the Holy Spirit and Jesus Christ.” Citing 1 Corinthians 2:13, he says the apostles spoke “not in words which man’s intellect teaches, but which the Holy Spirit teaches,” and says he has “heard a lot of human intellect” and repents of passing it on.
Why does he say books should never replace the Bible? (1 Corinthians 2:13)

Amen. A lot of those books were wrong, they were just flat-out wrong. You cannot write a book on your experience in God; you must write a book on Jesus’s experience in God, because he is the fullness, and the apostles are the fullness, they had it. Are you there? Because all you’re going to do is come to the level of the author. When you go to the Bible, you’ll come to the level of the real author, the Holy Spirit and Jesus Christ. Hallelujah. I’m not against books, but books should never replace the Bible. New Testament verification, 1 Corinthians 2:13: “These things we speak, not in words which man’s intellect teaches, but which the Holy Spirit teaches.” And that seems to be lacking in America today. We have intellect, and I watched a bunch of shows on TV this week, and I just heard a lot of human intellect, that’s all I heard. And I, I repent. Did I go, “God, am I like that? Am I just going to the Bible with human intellect and passing on human intellect?” Forgive me if I am; that is horrible. He said we don’t teach with our intellect but with the Holy Spirit, what the Holy Spirit teaches. See, the apostles only taught what the Holy Spirit gave them to say.
Why does he say books should never replace the Bible? (1 Corinthians 2:13)
1 Corinthians 2:13: These things we also speak, not in words which man’s wisdom teaches but which the Holy Spirit teaches, comparing spiritual things with spiritual.
Why did the apostles need their understanding opened? (Luke 24:45, Isaiah 28:10)

He says the apostles had walked with Jesus “three and a half years,” seen miracles and preached, “and yet they didn’t understand until he came and opened their understanding.” He says “you got to realize you don’t know everything just because you accepted Christ,” and compares growth to school: “God isn’t like American public schools that just pass you because you attend church.”
Why did the apostles need their understanding opened? (Luke 24:45, Isaiah 28:10)

Wouldn’t that be good if our ministers would do that? Wouldn’t it be good if the congregation would do that? Good Lord, we have so many opinions and we all think we’re right. So I want you to know the New Testament backs up this Old Testament promise, and so we go back to the divine nature of Christ. Luke 24:45: “Then Jesus opened their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures.” Now listen, those apostles had been walking with him for three and a half years. They had heard the Sermon on the Mount over and over and over and over and over. You see, they had heard his teachings of the kingdom over and over and over and over and over. They had heard him say he was going to die on the cross and rise again, over and over and over and over, for three and a half years. They had seen the miracles, they were participators in miracles and casting out demons and healing the sick and preaching the gospel and people saved, they were ministers of the gospel, and yet they didn’t understand until he came and opened their understanding. And this is step number one: you got to realize you don’t know everything just because you accepted Christ. And you don’t know everything because your church has some articles of faith. You don’t even know their articles of faith. I guarantee you right now this congregation cannot tell me 10% of the truths in our articles of faith, and our articles of faith covers the Bible. Are you there? So we need Christ to, what, come along and open our understanding, and he does it. The Bible says little by little, line upon line, precept on precept. You got to get kindergarten passed before you go to first grade, second grade, third grade, high school, college in God. So if you don’t respond to the kindergarten message, you’re not going to move on. God isn’t like American public schools that just pass you because you attend church. He only passes you to the next level when you are participators in the first one, in the previous one you got. That, I mean, you can hear high messages and it doesn’t matter; only Jesus can reveal it to you, I don’t care who’s preaching. Okay, now if Bible characters needed more understanding, so may we need more understanding. Joseph and Mary: now remember, Joseph and Mary had angels coming and visited them. Mary had an angel coming and visit her and told her she was going to have Jesus, the Messiah, the Savior of the world.
Why did the apostles need their understanding opened? (Luke 24:45, Isaiah 28:10)

Luke 24:45: And He opened their understanding, that they might comprehend the Scriptures. Isaiah 28:10: For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept, Line upon line, line upon line, Here a little, there a little.”
What does he say about Mary, Joseph and “delegated ministers”? (Luke 2:49)

He says Mary and Joseph both had angelic visits, yet when Jesus was 12 he “had more understanding than the priests in the temple.” He says Joseph was not a stepfather but “a delegated minister,” and that “the Pope is a delegated minister, mainly by the Catholic Church, not God,” while a pastor “better be from God himself.” These are his own views.
What does he say about Mary, Joseph and “delegated ministers”? (Luke 2:49)

I mean, man, she got the message straight, and she had the Holy Ghost overshadowing her, and that which was birthed in her was conceived by God himself. She experienced high, powerful spiritual experiences; she experienced a word of revelation from the angel himself.
