They say there’s no sign, there’s no indication of being filled with the Holy Ghost. Yes, there is. You’re going to have a compelling for the word of God so you can get understanding. Your understanding is going to keep increasing, your behavior is going to change, the way you approach God is going to change. You may not have raised your hand before, you may not have clapped before, but as I tell the fundamentalist, the Bible says, “Clap your hands, all ye people,” that includes fundamentalists, “and shout to God with a voice of triumph.” Are you there? “I would that men, all men everywhere, raise up holy hands without wrath or doubt,” and that includes fundamentalists. Who gave you the right to disobey God’s word because you were raised a certain way? You got to break away and follow God’s word, and God honors the principle of response. Wow, that was good. Amen. That’s what I tell the Catholics. Oh, I love them and I share with them, but I am direct with them. Understanding we need from the Holy Spirit. Okay, this is what we got to get in our cranial vacuum: “Though I have the gift of prophecy, understand all mysteries, have all knowledge, have all faith,” the faith camp, the prophecy camps, they’re all in here, “though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor,” the focus on the poor, it’s all in here, “and though I give my body to be burned,” a martyr for Jesus, a martyr for my church, martyr for my opinions, “and have not love, I am nothing, and it profits me nothing.” See, we can experience, and this is what the Catholics and the other Protestant churches don’t understand, is that God can move in Pentecostals and charismatics and gifts and all these things, and they not have understanding, and they behave in a manner and do things that any idiot of the Bible knows is not Bible. And there’s no Bible for “slain in the Spirit,” falling backwards, and there’s no Bible for that, and anybody with any common sense is going to go, “You guys are nuts.” And that’s what Paul said. He said they’re going to think you’re crazy. But I tell my Protestant friends that are non-Pentecostals and Catholics, you don’t throw out a truth because someone shipwrecks it. It’s still a truth. You don’t stop flying airplanes because one crashed. You don’t stop driving a car because one crashed. It’s the drivers that crash, it’s the people. The baptism of the Holy Ghost is for us, it’s a key to turning America around back to God, and anybody can have it. This church can have it. Amen. And the Bible says, say at the end of this, “Let all things be done decently and in order.” You see, and when we get out of order, we look stupid, but we need to do it right. Amen.
What does he tell Pentecostals and non-Pentecostals? (1 Corinthians 13:1–3, 14:40)

Psalm 47:1: Oh, clap your hands, all you peoples! Shout to God with the voice of triumph! 1 Timothy 2:8: I desire therefore that the men pray everywhere, lifting up holy hands, without wrath and doubting; 1 Corinthians 13:1-3: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal. And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing. And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, but have not love, it profits me nothing. 1 Corinthians 14:40: Let all things be done decently and in order.
How does he end? Love and growing up (1 Corinthians 14:20, 13:11)

He says “love is the result of the Spirit” and “pride and division is the result of human intellect,” and that “the greatest sign is the greatest commandment.” He urges bringing a woman who had an abortion to “forgiveness and change and reconciliation in her life.” Citing “be not children in understanding,” he asks, “Can we grow out of Christian childhood and into a responsible, mature Christian?”
How does he end? Love and growing up (1 Corinthians 14:20, 13:11)

We need to do it right. Love is the result of the Spirit, the Holy Spirit’s impartation of understanding. Pride and division is the result of human intellect. That’s my statement. The baptism of the Holy Ghost, the greatest sign is the greatest commandment: to love God. The great commission, the great commandment is to love God, love your neighbor, love yourself, love your wife, love your husband, love your children. That’s the greatest sign of the Holy Ghost baptism that I know of, is when he brings you to that dimension of love. And this is what the Holy Ghost will do for you, and he’ll give you a heart to love the Catholics, knowing they’re wrong, to love the homosexual. How are you going to reach them if you don’t love them? To love the lady who had an abortion and bring her to the place where she can find forgiveness and change and reconciliation in her life. How are you going to do it? For God so loved the world, he didn’t tongue the world, he didn’t [unclear] the world, he loved the world, and came and taught us in the condition we are in. And that is my high recommendation to this church: we need this baptism of the Holy Ghost, we need its expressions in our services, so unbelievers and believers can grow in God. “When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I understood as a child, and I thought as a child. When I became a mature man, I put away childish things.” Did you get that? Is your understanding Christian childishness? Is that the level you’re at? God wants you to know you can grow up. Doesn’t that sound exciting? I mean, who wants to stay a baby all their life? “Be not children in understanding, but in understanding be” what? Mature. Isn’t that a powerful challenge from God to us? Can we grow out of Christian childhood and into a responsible, mature Christian that not only believes the things of God and sees the things of God but possesses the things of God? Absolutely you can, and you will be a powerful, effective force in the earth when you do this. All claim to have the Holy Ghost, yet we argue over baby doctrines, support lifestyles that the Holy Ghost opposes and support doctrines that the Holy Ghost opposes, and everybody claims to be filled with the Holy Ghost.
How does he end? Love and growing up (1 Corinthians 14:20, 13:11)

John 3:16: For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life. 1 Corinthians 13:11: When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child; but when I became a man, I put away childish things. 1 Corinthians 14:20: Brethren, do not be children in understanding; however, in malice be babes, but in understanding be mature.
Which Old Testament verse does he say speaks of the Holy Spirit being poured out?
He says Pentecostals “always use Joel 2:28,” but that “the Holy Ghost is mentioned all throughout the Old Testament,” including Proverbs 1:23.
What does he say it takes to be a candidate for the baptism of the Holy Ghost?
Citing Acts 2:38, he says you repent and are baptized, and that “I just purposed to turn from them” (his sins), adding “it took me some time to get rid of some sins.”
Where does he say miracles are happening today?
He says it is “happening overseas in South America, Central America, Africa, Asia,” and that in America “we don’t see that today.”
Does he say water baptism or Holy Ghost baptism does it all?
No. He says “there’s no magical baptism, water or Holy Ghost,” and “you got to put some effort into this.”
Whose opinions does he say the Holy Ghost will reveal?
He says the Holy Ghost “will only reveal to you what Jesus Christ himself taught and the disciples passed on.”
Why does he compare spiritual growth to school?
He says “you got to get kindergarten passed before you go to first grade,” and that God “only passes you to the next level when you are participators in the first one.”
Why does he say Joseph can’t be called a stepfather?

He says a stepfather marries a child’s mother when the other parent is divorced, died or irresponsible, but “God is not irresponsible, God did not divorce Mary, and God’s not dead,” so Joseph is “a delegated minister.”
What does he say the word “afraid” means in Luke 9:44?
He says “the word ‘afraid’ is a reverence fear,” and that he found “I don’t have to be afraid of God.”
What was wrong with building three temples at the Transfiguration?
He says it shows how “our human intellect comes in” when people build a separate place for each leader.
He says “hardened” means “to be completely unwilling to learn or accept new truth.”
What does he say the word “tongue” means?
He says it means a language “acquired by a supernatural means,” and that this is what “the quarrel is about in the church world in America and Europe.”
Does he say miracles prove God approves of a person’s life?
He says “it’s not his approval of your lifestyle,” and that you can experience miracles and gifts, “that doesn’t mean you have understanding.”
Does he say Paul used an interpreter?
He says “there’s no record of him having an interpreter on his ministry team,” and that Paul spoke in the languages of the nations he visited.
Is there a sign of being filled with the Holy Ghost, according to him?
He says “yes, there is,” and that “you’re going to have a compelling for the word of God so you can get understanding.”
What does he say about growing up in Christ?
He says “God wants you to know you can grow up,” and asks, “Can we grow out of Christian childhood and into a responsible, mature Christian?”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from 2 Peter 1:3-4 that believers are called to be partakers of the divine nature. He traces the first promise in Genesis 3:15, the woman’s seed bruising Satan’s…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from 2 Peter 1:3-4 that believers are called to be partakers of the divine nature. He traces the first promise in Genesis 3:15, the woman’s seed bruising Satan’s head, and says Jesus and His church have rendered Satan powerless. He then uses the parable of the wheat and the tares in Matthew 13 to explain why the good and bad seed grow together, and how behavior shows who are children of God and who are children of the devil.
What does it mean to be a partaker of the divine nature? (2 Peter 1:3-4)

He says 2 Peter 1:3-4 gives “exceedingly great and precious promises, that through these you may be partakers of the divine nature.” “We’re not a fan sitting in the stand watching the Super Bowl game; we are out there on the field playing the game.” He says Christians tend to look elsewhere, but being participators in God’s nature “needs to be a high priority in our life.”
What does it mean to be a partaker of the divine nature? (2 Peter 1:3-4)

In 2 Peter 1:3-4: “As Jesus the divine power has given us all things,” “whereby by these things are given us exceedingly great and precious promises, that through these you may be partakers of the divine nature.” Okay, participators of the divine nature. We’re not a fan sitting in the stand watching the Super Bowl game; we are out there on the field playing the game. We’re participants. Okay, now American Christians have a tendency to look for the second coming, a prosperity, purpose, positive confessions, focusing on the poor instead of the divine nature, or phenomenal-- Miracles and so forth. We have a tendency to look for gifts and all that, and a lot of groups focus on different areas, uh, some on soul-winning and so forth, but God very strongly puts in His Word that there are promises that we can be participators in the divine nature, God’s nature, and so that needs to be a high priority in our life. Could that be true? Okay, now we have to ask ourself, what are these promises that I through them can become a participator of God’s divine--
What does it mean to be a partaker of the divine nature? (2 Peter 1:3-4)

2 Peter 1:3-4: as His divine power has given to us all things that pertain to life and godliness, through the knowledge of Him who called us by glory and virtue, by which have been given to us exceedingly great and precious promises, that through these you may be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.
What is the first promise in the Bible? (Genesis 3:15)

He says the first promise was “to declare war on Satan and Satan’s seed.” In Genesis 3:15, “I will put war between you and the woman, between your seed and her seed,” and her seed “shall bruise your head,” your chief part, your authority. Read with “he,” he says, it is Jesus who bruises Satan’s head and Satan who bruises His heel.
What is the first promise in the Bible? (Genesis 3:15)

Nature? You have to ask yourself some questions when you read the Bible, not just read it to say, “I read it through for the year.” You have to--you have to inquire of God and ask Him questions, and/or let the Holy Spirit ask you questions. The first promise we find in order in the Bible is back in Genesis, and the first promise was to declare war on Satan and Satan’s seed. Okay, we find that in Genesis 3:15, the Lord said to Satan--okay, God’s talking to Satan himself. Satan is a created being by God, the Bible says that the, uh, he was created to-- Destroy. And, uh, He says to Satan, “I’m going to put war, enmity, opposition, but between you and the woman.” Now, He didn’t say Eve, but He’s talking about Eve, but He said “woman.” Okay, that woman has a name, but there’s a reason, I think, why it says “woman.” Okay, “between your seed and her seed.” Now, this next word is a third-person word, all right, can be used as “it,” can be used as “he,” can be used as “she,” according to the subject of the sentence or the paragraph. All right, third-person singular word, so we’ll use the word-- “It.” “I will put war between you and the woman, between your seed and her seed. It, her seed, shall bruise your head,” your chief part, your authority, “and you, Satan, shall bruise its heel.” That’s the woman’s seed’s heel, the lowest, farthest part of the body or the rear of an army. Heel means the, the rear part, the rear of an army, the, the farthest part back. Now let’s read it with the masculine singular word: “Between your seed and her seed, He,” Jesus, “shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise His heel.” “His” is put in there to give us clarity, because the people that put this book together realized that it was Jesus that bruised Satan’s heel, so they use the word “He,” but it can be either one of these third-person singular words. Now let’s read it: “Between your seed and her seed,”
What is the first promise in the Bible? (Genesis 3:15)
Genesis 3:15: And I will put enmity Between you and the woman, And between your seed and her Seed; He shall bruise your head, And you shall bruise His heel.”
Who is the “she” who bruises Satan’s head, and what does “bruise the heel” mean? (Genesis 49:17)

He reads the word as “she,” the church, the bride of Christ, “always referred to in the Bible as feminine,” and says Satan bruises the church’s heel, the rear of an army. “God promised that, and God can’t lie.” From Genesis 49:17, “an adder in the path that bites the horse’s heels,” he says “Satan is always out trying to get you to go backwards.”
Who is the “she” who bruises Satan’s head, and what does “bruise the heel” mean? (Genesis 49:17)

“She.” Where does “she” come in? The church, the bride of Christ, always referred to in the Bible as feminine. Okay, “she,” the church, “shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise her”--the church’s--heel, the rear part of the army. Okay, now God promised that, and God can’t lie, He has to fulfill things. So in Genesis 49:17, we have a verse here that shines some light on “bruise the heel,” the rear of the army, the heel itself. Genesis 49:17: “Dan shall be a serpent by the way,” by the pathway, the way traveled, “an adder in the path that bites the horse’s heels.” And what is the result of biting the horse’s heels? So that his rider will fall backwards. And see, Satan is always out trying to get you to go backwards.
Who is the “she” who bruises Satan’s head, and what does “bruise the heel” mean? (Genesis 49:17)
Genesis 49:17: Dan shall be a serpent by the way, A viper by the path, That bites the horse’s heels So that its rider shall fall backward.
Why does Satan go after the weak and the stragglers? (Deuteronomy 25:18)

He cites Deuteronomy 25:18, where Amalek attacked the rear of Israel, “the feeble ones, the weary ones, the weak ones that were behind.” He says we become weak when we do not feed on the Word, since “the Word of God is our food,” and “the stragglers are the ones that don’t nourish themselves.” It is imperative, he says, that newborn Christians “not stay weak, but grow quickly to the young man’s stage.”
Why does Satan go after the weak and the stragglers? (Deuteronomy 25:18)

To get you to backslide, you see, and the only thing he can’t touch you, so he touches the direction you’re going, get you distracted. In this case the horse reared up and you fell off, and so forth. So this helps us understand “bruising the heel.” In Deuteronomy 25:18, remember Amalek? Amalek is the, the tribe of people that came while Israel was in the wilderness and attacked the rear part of Israel. Okay, “Remember Amalek, how he met you by the way and smote the rear most of you.” You see, the heel, the rear most. And what people make up the rear most? “All that were feeble behind-- You,” “and when you was--was faint and weary,” he came and smote the feeble ones, the weary ones, the weak ones that were behind. Now, how do we become weak? Well, you become weak in the natural if you don’t eat. Try not eating for 30 days and see how good you can travel. Try not eating for seven days and just see how good you can travel. You’re back there dragging your feet. Try not drinking for seven days and see how you travel. You’re going to be crawling. And see, the Word of God is our food, the Bible says, and when we don’t feed on the Word of God, we get what? Weak. The Holy Spirit is the water. The Word is the water too, but--and when we don’t get into His presence, we get weak and we drag behind. Everybody’s four miles ahead and here we are, “Oh, I will bless the Lord at all times.” Oh yeah. Why? Because we haven’t fed ourselves, we haven’t taken care of ourselves. Another way you get weak is no exercise. You sit on the couch all day, your joints don’t move right, things get weak, the muscles don’t work right. And so we have to exercise the Bible, we have to feed on the Bible, and we got to drink. Could that be an amen? And the stragglers are the ones that don’t nourish themselves, and Satan comes and gets them, fights with them. Okay, he bruises the weak. Christian, it’s imperative that newborn Christians not stay weak, but grow quickly to the young man’s stage. Remember, in the last session we showed you the five areas of growing in God. The young man stage not only keeps the Word, but the Word abides in him, the Scripture abides in him, and he overcomes the evil one and overcomes evil. So we need to grow to that stage so we’re not stragglers and Satan can come and bruise us and crush us. Are you with me? Did God keep His promise? These are questions I ask God: “God, did You back this up? Did You really do--
Why does Satan go after the weak and the stragglers? (Deuteronomy 25:18)
Deuteronomy 25:18: how he met you on the way and attacked your rear ranks, all the stragglers at your rear, when you were tired and weary; and he did not fear God.
Did Jesus destroy Satan’s power and the works of the devil? (Hebrews 2:14, 1 John 3:8, Romans 8:3)

He says through death Jesus “rendered Satan powerless over people who believe in that cross.” He says “he can tempt you, he can suggest things, but he has no power over Christians.” From 1 John 3:8 he says Jesus came “to destroy the works of the devil, which is sin,” and from Romans 8:3 that God condemned sin in the flesh through His Son.
Did Jesus destroy Satan’s power and the works of the devil? (Hebrews 2:14, 1 John 3:8, Romans 8:3)

This?” Hebrews 2:14: “Through death He,” here is that third-person singular, “He,” Jesus, “may destroy him that had the power of death, that is the devil.” So Jesus on the cross destroyed--He rendered Satan powerless over people who believe in that cross and believe in Him and accept Him. And when I grew up in church, the devil was chasing everybody. In fact, the minister would get up and cast demons out of the church, literally. “Well, we want to get the devil out of here. The devil, in the name of Jesus--“ There’s no Bible for that. Satan is rendered-- Powerless when we come to Christ. He is rendered powerless to the cross. Amen. See, now I don’t have Satan hindering me from being a partaker of His divine nature. Allelujah. And too many churches are given too much credit to Satan. Jesus’s cross has rendered him powerless over Christians. He can tempt you, he can suggest things, but he has no power over Christians. Jesus fulfilled that Word. Amen. Now, 1 John 3:8: “He that commits sin is of the devil, for the devil sinned from the beginning.” He was a murderer from the beginning, he was a liar from the beginning, and he doesn’t know how to tell the truth, the Bible says. “For this purpose the Son of God was manifest, that He might destroy the works of Satan,” the devil. So the purpose of Jesus coming, God in the-- Flesh, was to destroy the works of the devil, which is sin. See, he wants you to sin, he wants you to violate God’s Word, he wants you to commit sexual immorality, he wants you to get drunk, he wants you to lose your temper and be a violent person, he wants you to break God’s Word, and Jesus on the cross destroyed the works of the devil, which was sin. Okay, to make it more clear, Romans 8:3: “God sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh,” “God sending His own Son for sin, condemns sin in the flesh.” See, He put to death sin in the--
Did Jesus destroy Satan’s power and the works of the devil? (Hebrews 2:14, 1 John 3:8, Romans 8:3)

Hebrews 2:14: Inasmuch then as the children have partaken of flesh and blood, He Himself likewise shared in the same, that through death He might destroy him who had the power of death, that is, the devil, 1 John 3:8: He who sins is of the devil, for the devil has sinned from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that He might destroy the works of the devil. Romans 8:3: For what the law could not do in that it was weak through the flesh, God did by sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, on account of sin: He condemned sin in the flesh,
What does it mean that God will bruise Satan under your feet? (Romans 16:20)

He says Romans 16:20, “The God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly,” is spoken to the church, not only about Jesus, and “the very thing that he can attack is the very thing you crush him with.” Citing Luke 10, “nothing shall by any means hurt you,” he says “we step on Satan and his demonic powers with the weakest part of our body, our heel.”
What does it mean that God will bruise Satan under your feet? (Romans 16:20)

Flesh. So you see, it is fulfilled. The seed not only bruised Satan, but he [unclear] bruised the works of Satan, which is sin. Jesus didn’t come to condemn people, He come to condemn Satan and sin. Hallelujah. So now I can become a partaker of the divine nature. Satan doesn’t have any control over me, and sin doesn’t have any control over me, according to Romans chapter 6, Romans 16:20: “The God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.” Oh, now who’s your-- Here, the feminine, the church, “she,” the church. He’s talking to the church. Not just Jesus destroyed Satan now, but His church. Uses the same word, “bruise Satan under your feet shortly.” See, and when you are stepping on Satan, the serpent, the only place he can attack you is your heel. The very thing that he can attack is the very thing you crush him with. Isn’t that something? Are you guys out there this morning? Hallelujah. Luke 10:17: “I give you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall by any means hurt you.” Nothing--
What does it mean that God will bruise Satan under your feet? (Romans 16:20)

Romans 16:20: And the God of peace will crush Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen. Luke 10:19: Behold, I give you the authority to trample on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall by any means hurt you.
How much power does Satan really have?

He says “the church out there has given way too much credit to Satan.” Even in Job’s story Satan “had to get permission from God to do it.” He says Satan can suggest and roar, but is “a lion that has no teeth and no claws,” and God’s promise is to “destroy sin and Satan, not destroy you.”
How much power does Satan really have?

Means nothing. See, we don’t pick up serpents, we don’t pick up scorpions, we step on Satan and his demonic powers with the weakest part of our body, our heel. Hallelujah. See, you say, “Well, that was to the apostles.” Well, God is no respecter of persons. He’s going to give that to the apostles, and He’s not going to give that to His church? Come on. You see, so it’s a very powerful thing, and see, the church needs to understand that Satan has been rendered powerless. The church out there has given way too much credit to Satan, way too much. Now, don’t get me wrong, even in the Old Testament, Satan, you know, he came and he took Job’s wealth, he took his health and killed his kids and so forth, but he had to get permission from God to do it. You see, everybody thinks Satan is just a loose goose out here doing what he want. He can’t do anything, and never could, without his Creator saying, “Okay,” and the Creator always has a what? Purpose in letting Satan do what he can-- Do. And in the New Testament it’s the same way. See, when Paul said, “We wanted to go to another city, but Satan hinders us,” okay, and, and if you really study and read it, it wasn’t really Satan, it was the people there hindering them going over there. And so, yes, he can come and suggest you do wrong and all that. He can roar, basically he can roar, but he’s a lion that has no teeth and no claws, and that makes him a kitten. When a lion doesn’t have any teeth and no claws, they’re just a kitten. Okay, and they can roar like a lion, but it has no authority over you. Do you understand that? Because God destroyed it. And that you become a partaker of His divine nature. So God’s promise then is to--to destroy sin and Satan, not destroy you. We need to get off this mentality that, you know, every time we do something bad, you know, God’s going to, or Satan’s going to come and bring horrible things on us. You know, we’re going to lose our job, we’re going to get sick, and if something happens, we get in the car wreck, “Oh, it’s because I, you know, tell a little white lie, or I had a bad attitude last week.” Come on, church. He’s not out to condemn you and destroy you. He’s out, and His promise was, to do Satan and sin in your life and make you a partaker of the divine nature. Do we got it? Now, let’s look at the seed, her seed, his seed. Okay, the good seed, the bad seed. I got this from Burpee and Gerber seed, showing the difference between a good seed and a bad seed. All right, in the natural, this bad seed, as you notice, the bottom part is not full like this seed of--
How much power does Satan really have?

Job 1:12: And the LORD said to Satan, “Behold, all that he has is in your power; only do not lay a hand on his person.” So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD. 1 Thessalonians 2:18: Therefore we wanted to come to you—even I, Paul, time and again—but Satan hindered us.
What do the wheat and tares teach about a good seed and a bad seed?

He compares a good seed with a bad seed that will not produce fruit, then shows wheat and tares, which look alike. As a young minister he used it for hypocritical Christians, but he now says “it’s got nothing to do with that.” Tares “grow taller than the wheat,” their roots entangle the wheat, and that is why Jesus said, “Let them both grow together.”
What do the wheat and tares teach about a good seed and a bad seed?

Wheat. Okay, and Gerber says these seeds will not produce fruit, they will not grow, and they only give you growing seed, so they get rid of the bad seed. Why is it bad? According to science, it has not been pollinated, so what we call the sperm has not come in contact with the feminine side of the plant so that a seed is formed, embryo can be produced. It hasn’t happened, or it hasn’t reached maturity. It may be fertilized, it may be pollinated, but it hasn’t--the seed itself has not grown into an embryo seed yet where it can get sunlight and water and grow. So these seeds, you can give water all you want and you can put sunlight out there and everything else and nothing’s going to come up, because it does not have the potential to germ-- to germinate, I should say, and bear fruit. So that’s the-- Natural. Now, here we have a picture. On the left side here of wheat, this is wheat, and on the right side, darnel wheat, or tare, is what we call weeds. A picture, see how they look alike? Now, as a young minister I would always use that as the hypocritical Christians versus the real ones, but becoming more enlightened, as we’re supposed to, it’s got nothing to do with that. It can be Christians, it can be believers, but it doesn’t have to be, and we’ll see why. Hallelujah. So I attacked the poor Christians back there as a young-- Minister, and left the children of Satan out of the whole picture, but they’re not left out of this picture. Okay, the tares, for one thing, grow taller than the wheat. So when you look out on the wheat field, and the, and the tares grow faster, and isn’t that true in the spiritual? Wicked people just get wicked quick. I mean, even at a young age. Yeah, and they’re noticeable. The tares are noticeable. You know, you look out over the wheat field and there’s the tare about this much higher than the wheat, and it keeps going like that until it’s like this above the wheat, and so you can see the tares. They’re obvious. How--me, you know, wicked people are like that. You can just tell, there’s nothing hidden there at all. Yeah, they may look like us, they may resemble us, but their lifestyle sets them apart. You notice them very quickly. Also, these weeds, the root grows quickly also and entangles itself with the root of the wheat, so if you try to pull up the weed, you pull up what? Some of the wheat with it. That’s why Jesus said, “Let them both grow together,” because they wanted to pull up the weeds out of the field, and He said, “Don’t do that.” He doesn’t want you pulled up, because you have to live in association with the wicked people, people of this world. Okay, they might have had an impact on you for a while down inside, and He don’t want you being rooted up before you have a chance to produce fruit. Hallelujah. Ain’t that good? Yes.
What does eating darnel show, and who are the wheat and tares in Matthew 13:38?

He says eating darnel causes someone to get “drowsy, you want to sleep,” and compares it to Christians “asleep in the Kingdom” and young believers following the crowd. “Because the source of that seed is Satan, so you take on the nature of the source.” From Matthew 13:38 he reads that “the good seed are the children of the kingdom.”
What does eating darnel show, and who are the wheat and tares in Matthew 13:38?

Now, if a human being eats the darnel wheat, they can give it to animals in portions, but for human consumption this is the result you will get: drowsy, you want to sleep. Isn’t that the way a lot of Christians are? They’re just asleep in the Kingdom. Oh, you get into hypnotic episodes, that means you get temporarily under the control of someone else. Isn’t that the way young believers are, and young people, period? They have the herding instinct: whatever the other young people are doing, they want to do it. They wear the certain clothes, I wear the certain clothes; they have the certain hairstyle, I want the certain hairstyle; you know, they’re smoking marijuana, I want to smoke-- Marijuana. See, convulsions and trembling, drunkenness and intoxication that leads to the inability to walk, and what’s the “walk” referred to in the Bible? Our what? Behavior. You see, it affects their walk and it affects their talk. Why? Because the source of that seed is Satan, so you take on the nature of the source. Now we go to Matthew 13:38, in this famous Sunday school lesson in the Bible: “The field is the world, the good seed are the children of the kingdom,
What does eating darnel show, and who are the wheat and tares in Matthew 13:38?
Matthew 13:38: The field is the world, the good seeds are the sons of the kingdom, but the tares are the sons of the wicked one.
When are the tares gathered, and why must wheat and tares grow together? (Matthew 13:30)

He says “the enemy that sowed them is the devil,” and the effect “comes out in our behavior, our talk, and our walk.” The harvest is at the end of the world, when “the tares are gathered and burned in the fire.” When he first read Matthew 13:30, he says, he asked why he must “put up with them the rest of my life.”
When are the tares gathered, and why must wheat and tares grow together? (Matthew 13:30)

But the tares are the children of the wicked one.” So we have her seed, and his, and Satan’s seed, right here. Don’t we? Okay, so the tares were sold as a seed and the wheat was sold as a seed, and as it begins to grow it’s referred to as the children of God, and the tares are the children of Satan, the wicked one. The enemy that sowed them is the devil. Okay, we let him come into our life, have an effect on our life, and that effect comes out in our behavior, our talk, and our walk. The harvest, when things are reaped, is at the end of the world, because Jesus is going to let them both grow together. “The reapers are the-- Angels. As the tares are gathered and burned in the fire, so shall it be at the end of the world.” You see, the Jewish weed, with this effect it had on human beings, was just burned so it wouldn’t have a chance to seed and grow back. They tried to get rid of it. Matthew 13:30: “Let both grow together.” Oh man, the first time I read that, I go, “God, why does this have to be? If I didn’t have all these wicked people around me tempting me and testing me and pushing me and abusing me and, and, uh, persecuting me and making fun of me, and boy, life would be a lot easier. And here You’re telling me I got to put up with them the rest of my life? I got to grow with
When are the tares gathered, and why must wheat and tares grow together? (Matthew 13:30)

Matthew 13:39-40: The enemy who sowed them is the devil, the harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are the angels. Therefore as the tares are gathered and burned in the fire, so it will be at the end of this age. Matthew 13:30: Let both grow together until the harvest, and at the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, “First gather together the tares and bind them in bundles to burn them, but gather the wheat into my barn.” ’ ”
Who is gathered first at the end of the age? (Matthew 13:30)

He says the reapers are told to “gather first the” tares, “not the saints,” and tells those into a pre-tribulation rapture, “you got a serious problem.” The tares are bound to burn and the wheat gathered into the barn, and God has them grow together because “a lot of these tares can be converted.”
Who is gathered first at the end of the age? (Matthew 13:30)

Them until the harvest.” When’s the harvest? At the end of the age, the end of the time. “Then I’ll say to the reapers, gather together first”--now, for those of you who are really into pre-tribulation rapture, you got a problem here. And you can explain it away all you want, but you got a serious problem. “Gather first the” what? Tares, not the saints. Just throw that out of your mind. You know, we just believe things we hear on the radio, we read in books, without even researching them out to see if they’re true. So who’s gathered first when Christ comes? The bad seed. Yeah, the tares, “and bind them in bundles to burn them.” Is that what’s going to happen at the end day? They’re going to be gathered together and they’re going to go to the lake of fire, isn’t that right? All right, “but gather the wheat, the good seed, into My barn.” See, why does God want us to go together? Because a lot of these tares can be converted and change their nature and become wheat. So if you pull out the tare, you’re not only in danger of pulling out a fellow believer because the roots entangled, but you may be pulling out someone that can be converted and changed into a wheat
Who is gathered first at the end of the age? (Matthew 13:30)

Matthew 13:30: Let both grow together until the harvest, and at the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, “First gather together the tares and bind them in bundles to burn them, but gather the wheat into my barn.” ’ ”
Should the church come down hard on sinners, and how are the good and bad seed at war? (Proverbs 28:4)

He says “I was once one of those tares,” and the church can “come down hard on sin and sinners without the compassion to realize that many of these can be converted like you were converted.” The seeds are at war “by their behavior,” and from Proverbs 28:4 he says when we keep the Word “we’re at war with the wicked.”
Should the church come down hard on sinners, and how are the good and bad seed at war? (Proverbs 28:4)

And take on the nature of God. And I was once one of those tares. How many were once a tare? Yeah. Aren’t you glad God didn’t pull you out? But the church has the tendency to overlook this, and we can come down hard on sin and sinners without the compassion to realize that many of these can be converted like you were converted, because conversion means you were changed from one thing to another. So once, whether you raised your hand or not, you were a tare. Now, the good and bad seed are at war by their behavior. Remember, He said there’s going to be war Between Satan’s seed and the woman’s seed, the church, and Satan’s seed and Satan’s children, God’s children and Satan’s children. It’s going to be war. Okay, I want to show you that we are at war by our behavior. Proverbs 28:4: “They that forsake the law praise” who? The wicked. You see, when we don’t follow God’s righteous word, we’re giving honor to the atheist, to the humanist, and all these people that oppose the righteous Word of God, but when we keep the Word, we contend with the wicked. We’re at war with the wicked. Just our lifestyle drives them crazy. You see, they don’t like Christmas Because it refers to Christ. They don’t like Easter because it refers to Christ, His death and His birth and His resurrection, so they bring in the Easter bunny to distract. Here comes Peter Cottontail hopping down the bunny trail, you know, they make it all nice and, and warm and fuzzy. Ah, man. But we celebrate Easter because of His resurrection, which He put Satan under His feet then, and we celebrate His birth because He come in for the purpose to destroy Satan and sin and bring us to the nature of God. Amen. Hallelujah. So yes, they hate
Should the church come down hard on sinners, and how are the good and bad seed at war? (Proverbs 28:4)
Proverbs 28:4: Those who forsake the law praise the wicked, But such as keep the law contend with them.
Does keeping God’s Word put you at war, and is the war cultural?

He says when you keep the Word and everything that points to Christ, “you’re at war with them,” and “when you do right, you shine like a light.” “It’s more powerful when you speak and you obey the Word than it is when you speak and disobey the Word.” He says it is “a right and wrong war,” “not a cultural war at all,” and “there is nothing wrong with being born with any skin color in the Bible, but there is something wrong with your behavior.”
Does keeping God’s Word put you at war, and is the war cultural?

It. And when you keep the Word and you keep the holidays that we have and you keep everything that points to Christ, you’re at war with them. When they get drunk and you don’t, you’re at war with them. When they commit sexual immorality and you stay faithful to your marriage, you’re at war with them, and they don’t like it. It bugs them. See, it exposes them. When you do right, you shine like a light. That’s what the Bible says: “Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works.” You see, your, your, your behavior is just as powerful as you speaking the Word. In fact, it’s more powerful when you speak and you obey the Word than it is when you speak and disobey the Word. That’s right, because you neutralize exactly what you’re trying to tell People. Ain’t that beautiful? See, you just choosing to do right, and we’re at war in America right now. We’ve been at war for 40 years, right and wrong. It’s a, it’s a, it’s a battle of morality, that’s exactly what it is. It’s not a cultural war at all. I disagree with [unclear] about the cultural war. It’s a right and wrong war. It’s got nothing to do with blacks and whites and Mexicans and Chinese and homosexuals and, and pedophiles and all the rest. It’s right and wrong. There is nothing wrong with being born with any skin color in the Bible, but there is something wrong with your behavior. Yes, amen. Hallelujah. And I don’t want to leave out the men and women war. You know, women are trying to make themselves to be something they weren’t created to be because they want to be equal with men. You’ll never be equal with a man. You ever look at us both naked?
Does keeping God’s Word put you at war, and is the war cultural?
Matthew 5:16: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven.
How do we know who is of God and who is of the devil? (John 8:44, Acts 13:10)

He says positive identification is whether you stand for truth: from John 8:44, “he does not stand in the truth.” “When you stand up for truth, that shows you’re God’s seed, and when you don’t stand up for truth, it shows that you’re of Satan.” Of the people in Acts 13:10 he says wicked people aren’t always against everything right: “they’re just against the source of all that is right: God, the Bible.”
How do we know who is of God and who is of the devil? (John 8:44, Acts 13:10)

There’s a big difference. There. Except who you are. Could that be an amen? Yeah. Jeez. So we want to give you, in closing, positive identification of the good seed and the bad seed. Now here from good old Gerber, I have the weed seed. Okay, and here is the weed seed, and unless you were trained, you wouldn’t know beans about what’s what. You just see seed, but the truth is this seed has been impregnated with evil, Harmful, and it’s going to produce harmful fruit. This seed has been impregnated with good nourishment, and it will produce nourishing fruit. Okay, John 8:44: “You are of your father the devil.” You see, “he does not stand in the truth.” That is positive identification. When people don’t stand up for truth, they are the seed of who? Satan. It’s not saying, “I’m a Christian, I got a baptismal certificate.” When you stand up for truth, that shows you’re God’s seed, and when you don’t stand up for Truth, it shows that you’re of Satan. Is that positive identification? Yeah, okay. Let’s go again. Acts 13:10: “You are a child of the devil.” Paul is talking to the sorcerer, and he says, “You’re a child of the devil,” okay, a seed of the devil, “an enemy of everything that is right.” You see, now, wicked people aren’t always against everything that is right, they’re just against the source of all that is right: God, the Bible. And when you embrace all of it, you expose them in maybe five areas that they don’t see anything wrong with. Okay, “You are full of all kinds of deceit.” Deceit
How do we know who is of God and who is of the devil? (John 8:44, Acts 13:10)

John 8:44: You are of your father the devil, and the desires of your father you want to do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and does not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks from his own resources, for he is a liar and the father of it. Acts 13:10: and said, “O full of all deceit and all fraud, you son of the devil, you enemy of all righteousness, will you not cease perverting the straight ways of the Lord?
What is deceit, and how does 1 John 3:10 tell who the children of God are?

He describes deceit as “sly lying. You don’t actually lie, you just don’t tell the truth.” He says “it’s got nothing to do with your baptismal certificate,” your time at the altar, or saying the sinner’s prayer: “anyone who doesn’t do what is right is not a child of God.” He distinguishes this from stumbling: “we sin and we get up, we make mistakes and we get up,” but “when I consistently sin, I am not a God.”
What is deceit, and how does 1 John 3:10 tell who the children of God are?

Is, is, uh, sly lying. You don’t actually lie, you just don’t tell the truth. You see, I come home, my wife asked me where I’m at. “Oh, I was just out.” Well, that didn’t tell her where I was at. “Well, where were you out?” “Oh, I just stopped by the gas station to put gas in the car.” I didn’t tell her where I was before I stopped at the gas station to put gas in the car. “Well, what did you do before you put gas?” “I was talking to someone that I met.” Well, that didn’t tell you who you were talking to. You see, it’s just--it’s deceit. We like to cover our bad actions with deceit, indirect Lying and trickery. “You will never stop perverting the right ways of God.” They pervert, they distort, they make evil of the ways of God, you see. And here’s the real kicker, John 3:10. This is how we know who the children of God are. It just plain says it. This is how we know, positive identification, who the children of God are and who the children of the devil are, and it’s got nothing to do with your baptismal certificate, it’s got nothing to do with your time at the altar getting saved, it’s got nothing to do with you say the sinner’s prayer, it’s got nothing to do with you being raised a Baptist or a Catholic all your life, got nothing to do with It. “All anyone who doesn’t do what is right is not a child of God.” See, when I habitually, habitually--see, we sin and we get up, we make mistakes and we get up--but when habitually, when I consistently sin, I am not a God. I may say I am, and that’s the way the Pharisees and the Sadducees and the scribes were. They believed in God, they could quote Scriptures, they could teach Scriptures, but they didn’t live Scripture, and that’s why Jesus said, “You are of the seed of your father the devil,” because their behavior. Amen. So, see, we
What is deceit, and how does 1 John 3:10 tell who the children of God are?
1 John 3:10: In this the children of God and the children of the devil are manifest: Whoever does not practice righteousness is not of God, nor is he who does not love his brother.
How do we put Satan under our feet and share in God’s nature?

He says “Jesus destroyed Satan through his death on the cross, he has no control over us. We ourselves put Satan under our feet, and now we can become a partaker, a participant, of the divine nature.” He lists God’s attributes, righteous, holy, wise, knowledgeable and good, that “we can have and shine like a light in this darkened world.”
How do we put Satan under our feet and share in God’s nature?

Know what the good seed is and the bad seed. Now we know Jesus destroyed Satan through his death on the cross, he has no control over us. We ourselves put Satan under our feet, and now we can become a partaker, a participant, of the divine nature. God is righteous, God is holy, God is wise, God is knowledgeable, God is good, all these attributes of God we can have, and shine like a light in this darkened world and hopefully bring many tares to be converted to Christ. Amen.
What does he say American Christians tend to focus on instead of the divine nature?
He says they “have a tendency to look for the second coming,” prosperity, purpose, positive confessions, miracles and gifts, and that groups focus on different areas such as soul-winning.
How does he say we should read the Bible?
He says not just to read it through for the year: “you have to inquire of God and ask Him questions, and/or let the Holy Spirit ask you questions.”
Can the word in Genesis 3:15 be read as “it,” “he” or “she”?
He says it is a third-person singular word that can be used as “it,” “he” or “she” depending on the sentence. With “he” it refers to Jesus, and with “she” he says it refers to the church.
Why does he say the church is the “she”?
He says the church, the bride of Christ, is “always referred to in the Bible as feminine,” so “she” the church shall bruise Satan’s head.
How does he say believers keep from being weak?
He says “we have to exercise the Bible, we have to feed on the Bible, and we got to drink.” Not exercising or feeding leaves us weak and dragging behind.
Does he say the devil is chasing every Christian?
No. He says that when he grew up in church ministers tried to cast the devil out of the church, but “there’s no Bible for that. Satan is rendered powerless when we come to Christ.”
Was it really Satan who hindered Paul?
He says when Paul said Satan hindered them, “if you really study and read it, it wasn’t really Satan, it was the people there hindering them going over there.”
If something bad happens, is God or Satan punishing me?
He says we need to “get off this mentality” that a car wreck or lost job comes because of a little white lie or a bad attitude. “He’s not out to condemn you and destroy you.”
Why does he say the tares should not be pulled up?
He says the tare’s root “entangles itself with the root of the wheat,” so pulling it up pulls up wheat too. “He don’t want you being rooted up before you have a chance to produce fruit.”
What does he mean by the “herding instinct” in young believers?
He says young believers and young people “have the herding instinct”: whatever the other young people are doing, they want to do it, such as wearing certain clothes or hairstyles.
Can a tare be converted into wheat?
He says yes: “a lot of these tares can be converted and change their nature and become wheat,” so pulling one out may remove “someone that can be converted.”
Why does he say people dislike Christmas and Easter?
He says they “don’t like Christmas because it refers to Christ” and don’t like Easter because it refers to His death and resurrection, so they bring in the Easter bunny to distract.
Does he say a baptismal certificate or the sinner’s prayer proves you are a child of God?

He says no: “it’s got nothing to do with your baptismal certificate,” your time at the altar, saying the sinner’s prayer, or being raised a Baptist or a Catholic. “Anyone who doesn’t do what is right is not a child of God.”

items.d: In “Overlooked Future Intervention,” Pastor David G. Kincer teaches Isaiah 2:4 and Micah 4 and says a future global intervention by God will end war through the terror of the Lord, as seen on a smaller scale…
p: In “Overlooked Future Intervention,” Pastor David G. Kincer teaches Isaiah 2:4 and Micah 4 and says a future global intervention by God will end war through the terror of the Lord, as seen on a smaller scale with Jehoshaphat, Jacob and Solomon. He reads Isaiah 2:5-22 on the proud being humbled in that day, and Hebrews 12:26-28 on the shaking of created things, and says man-made doctrines and lifestyles need to be shaken.
What does Isaiah 2 say about God teaching his ways in the last days?

He says it is about the last days, the mountain of the Lord’s house is Zion, which is the church, and all nations will flow into it. He says God has to open your understanding to learn his ways, and that Americans are not yet walking in them, with psychology and sympathy coming out of the church more than the word.
What does Isaiah 2 say about God teaching his ways in the last days?

Last week we learned that this is about the last days. It will come to pass in the last days that the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established at the top of the mountains which we found the mountain of the Lord’s house was Zion. Zion is the church and be exalted above all the hills. All religions and all nations shall flow into it. And we have seen that many nations have come into the church and many people will come and say let us go up to the house of the mountain of the Lord and he will teach us his ways. He will teach us his ways. You can’t get this through personal intellect. God has got to open your understanding. He will teach us his ways and we shall walk in his path. Now, we have seen the revelation of teachers being raised up in these last 50 years like never before bringing us the word of God, but we haven’t seen walking in his ways. Is America believers walking in the ways of God? No. Come on. Out of Zion the church shall go forth the law and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. 50 years ago, there was a word pouring out. Today, we got psychology, we got sympathy pouring out of the church and not the word of God. Now, there are groups that are preaching the word, but not overall in America. And so we come to verse four and he is going to make a tremendous statement here.
What does Isaiah 2 say about God teaching his ways in the last days?

Isaiah 2:2-3: Now it shall come to pass in the latter days That the mountain of the LORD’s house Shall be established on the top of the mountains, And shall be exalted above the hills; And all nations shall flow to it. Many people shall come and say, “Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, To the house of the God of Jacob; He will teach us His ways, And we shall walk in His paths.” For out of Zion shall go forth the law, And the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
What does Isaiah 2:4, "He shall judge among the nations," mean?

He says "he" is Jesus, and that "shall" in the Hebrew is a word where it is impossible to stop it, and that rebuke is almost like judgment: to address an issue, condemn it and bring punishment. He reads that the nations will beat their swords into plowshares and not learn war anymore, and says we should not rubber band the verse to fit a millennium reign.
What does Isaiah 2:4, "He shall judge among the nations," mean?

Okay. He and we know he is Jesus. The one that will teach us his ways and the path that we’re to walk in is his paths. All right. He Jesus will judge among the nations. Shall judge. Shall in the Hebrew is a word that it’s impossible to stop it. It’s a very powerful word and rebuke many people. And the word rebuke is almost like the word judgment. Okay? He’s going to try. He’s going to address an issue. He’s going to condemn it. He’s going to bring punishment. All right? Then and and He says they they are the nations and the people that he’s rebuking that he is judging. Got it? They these nations he’s rebuking and judging will beat their swords into plowshares or plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. And this awesome statement, nation shall not lift up sword against nation, nor shall they learn war anymore. Now, most people just really conveniently put this into what they call the millennium reign of Christ, but we’re just going to bring it as the scripture stated. Okay? We’re not going to rubber band anything. Rubber band means you take a verse over here and you stretch it to fit into something that you want to accomplish. All right. Now, we know that the church part has been fulfilled and we know that many nations are coming into the church. I also shared last week that there were two tribes of people, one in South America and one in Indonesia just a few years back that were discovered that they never knew was on this earth before. And how many nations must hear the gospel before Jesus comes? Every one of them. So these people in the ‘50s, [unclear], ‘80s, ‘60s, ‘90s that were saying Jesus is going to come, he couldn’t come because there were people that still haven’t even been discovered that need to hear the gospel. Are you there? You see, we get all worked up about some things that the radio and TV and and the books and the Christian bookstores pass on and we don’t take time to really research the Bible and get understanding of it.
What does Isaiah 2:4, "He shall judge among the nations," mean?

Isaiah 2:4: He shall judge between the nations, And rebuke many people; They shall beat their swords into plowshares, And their spears into pruning hooks; Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, Neither shall they learn war anymore.
Has the end of war in Isaiah 2:4 already been fulfilled?

He says there was never a time on earth when God globally intervened and there were no wars, so this is a future thing. He reads Micah 4:5 that every man will sit under his vine and fig tree and none will make them afraid, and says less than half of the church in America is walking in the ways of its God.
Has the end of war in Isaiah 2:4 already been fulfilled?

So, we just accept nonsense and we get caught up in a gospel of nonsense. This, my friend, has not been fulfilled. I know my history. I’ve done a lot of research and there was never a time on earth where there was a global intervention of God where there were no wars. So this is a future thing. It’s got to happen. Can I hear that? Could be true. That could be true. Hallelujah. See, I’ve told you for 40 years, I’ve been telling people, Jesus Christ is not going to come in my lifetime because there’s so many things to be fulfilled before he can come. And I’ve been branded as a cult leader. I’ve been branded as a weirdo and everything else. But 40 years have gone by and Jesus hasn’t come. Why didn’t he come? Because everything has to be fulfilled. And he’s got some tremendous work to do in the earth. And Isaiah is going to open our understanding to that. Are you ready? In Micah 4:5, now we know that Micah prophesied the same identical words about the last days, the house of the Lord being established at top the mountains and all nations flowing in it and so forth. Then Micah in verse five after this statement says, “They shall sit every man under his vine and fig tree and none shall make them afraid.” You see what’s he talking about? No wars. He confirms it. Micah confirms it and backs it up. And when is all this going to happen? In the last days. All right. He’s talking about the last days. All right. Micah also goes on to say, “For all people will walk everyone in the name of his God. And we will walk in the name of the Lord our God.” Now, I would say less than 50% of the church in America are even coming close to walking in the ways of the God they believe in. Could that be true? Yes, folks, it’s true. We can we can dream and fantasize all we want, but there is so much preaching on faith that Christians just believe they’re going to heaven no matter what they believe and do. In America and that’s a fact they are so addicted to the message of faith they fail to even consider when the rich man came to Jesus and said what must I do to have eternal life Jesus said keep the commandments he didn’t say believe on me now we’re supposed to believe on him that’s one of the of the for parts of the formula, but keeping his commandment is the second part. And America has been so drugged in the church world on just faith that they have no performance at all. And we find that this part has not been fulfilled in our generation. Are people walking in the name of their God? Absolutely. Without shame, without conviction, without a challenge. And many Christians have contrived their own God out of Jesus. They just kind of make Jesus what they want him to be. And we’re not walking in the way Jesus walked at all, are we? So, is Isaiah hitting this thing on the head for our generation? Yeah, absolutely. And this is, you know, hundreds and hundreds of years ago. So, I proclaim to you that this is not fulfilled globally. Could that be an amen? Now, let’s look at some truths we know about judgment.
Has the end of war in Isaiah 2:4 already been fulfilled?

Micah 4:1-5: Now it shall come to pass in the latter days That the mountain of the LORD’s house Shall be established on the top of the mountains, And shall be exalted above the hills; And peoples shall flow to it. Many nations shall come and say, “Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, To the house of the God of Jacob; He will teach us His ways, And we shall walk in His paths.” For out of Zion the law shall go forth, And the word of the LORD from Jerusalem. He shall judge between many peoples, And rebuke strong nations afar off; They shall beat their swords into plowshares, And their spears into pruning hooks; Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, Neither shall they learn war anymore. But everyone shall sit under his vine and under his fig tree, And no one shall make them afraid; For the mouth of the LORD of hosts has spoken. For all people walk each in the name of his god, But we will walk in the name of the LORD our God Forever and ever. Matthew 19:16-17: Now behold, one came and said to Him, “Good Teacher, what good thing shall I do that I may have eternal life?” So He said to him, “Why do you call Me good? No one is good but One, that is, God. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.”

But see, we’re looking so much for Jesus to come for us. There’s hardly any Christian in America looking for him to show forth his glory in us. And what’s the glory? Demonstration of the presence of his power. 2 Thessalonians 1:10. When he shall come to be glorified where? In his saints. When and that day. Now, is there something spectacular going to be happening before Christ comes? Absolutely, folks. You can believe that nonsense that he’s coming any minute and he’s going to come in your lifetime and he’s going to come because the stars are lining up again and all that baloney. Those stars have been lining up ever so many years for thousands of years and he hadn’t come. But people who want to make money, they sell books and all that to get you who are too lazy to read your Bible to believe stuff and make them rich. Is this something that we should be looking forward to and believing for? Yes.
What does it mean that God "arises to shake the earth"?

Isaiah 2:19: They shall go into the holes of the rocks, And into the caves of the earth, From the terror of the LORD And the glory of His majesty, When He arises to shake the earth mightily. Romans 8:18: For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us. 2 Thessalonians 1:10: when He comes, in that Day, to be glorified in His saints and to be admired among all those who believe, because our testimony among you was believed.
What does Isaiah 2:22, "Stop trusting in man," mean?

He says to stop exalting ministers and start looking to Jesus alone, which takes time in prayer, worship and reading your Bible. He says the Lord alone shall be exalted, and that no minister, evangelist or pastor will be, as ministers are just delegated workers.
What does Isaiah 2:22, "Stop trusting in man," mean?

He arises to shake terrible of the earth. We’ll go into the shaking in a minute. All right. Then verse 22, he simply says, “Stop trusting in man. The Lord alone will be exalted in that day. Stop putting your trust in man. Stop exalting the Jake and all these ministers. Stop it and start looking to Jesus alone. And for you to do that, you’re going to have to put a little time into it in prayer and worship and so forth, reading your Bible. The Lord alone shall be exalted in this day. Who else is going to be exalted? No one. No minister, no evangelist, no pastor. Who is the only one going to be exalted during this time? Jesus Christ. How many you know that’s the key? Amen. How many you know we’ve been wrong for years looking to ministers to solve our problems? They’re just delegated workers. That’s all they are. They ain’t nothing like they say they are. And Jesus is the man. Now shake and explained. All right. He’s going to shake terrible of the earth. Thank God for the book of Hebrews. That really explains this shaking. Hebrews 12:26, whose voice then shook the earth.
What does Isaiah 2:22, "Stop trusting in man," mean?
Isaiah 2:22: Sever yourselves from such a man, Whose breath is in his nostrils; For of what account is he?
What does Hebrews 12:26-28 say about the shaking?

He says Hebrews explains the shaking: the things that can be shaken are removed, the created things, so that what cannot be shaken remains. He says the kingdom that cannot be shaken is righteousness, peace and joy in the Holy Ghost, along with the gospel of the kingdom, the king and its citizens.
What does Hebrews 12:26-28 say about the shaking?

Talking about when God was on Mount Sinai spoke, his voice shook the earth. But now he has promised yet once more I will shake not only the earth but also heaven. And why is he going to shake? Indicating the removal of things that can be shaken. He’s going to remove things that can be shaken. Ain’t that why you I don’t know, but we used to have an apple tree in our front yard and you could shake that limb and the apples that were mature and ripe would fall off. Yes. And in fact, if they were overripe and rotten, they would fall off and the young apples would be left on. And so you could shake it and you could pick up your apple and you could eat it. All The right. Things that can be removed is what’s going to be removed. And the things that cannot be removed are going to remain. Does that sound like a good visitation of God? Yes. A divine intervention that we need. Then he tells us what things can be removed as of things that are what? Made. Created. Things that are created. Whoa. Whoa. Whoa. That the things which cannot be shaken may what? Remain. So the created thing can be shaken and the noncreated thing will remain. Are you there? Yes. So what’s the created thing? Verse 28. We are receiving a kingdom which cannot be shaken. What cannot be shaken? The kingdom. Okay. The kingdom is not meat nor drink but righteousness, peace and joy and the Holy Ghost. The kingdom is in power. See, the supernatural power of God cannot be shaken. Righteousness cannot be shaken. Peace cannot be shaken. Joy cannot be shaken. The gospel of the kingdom cannot be shaken. Is there a gospel of the kingdom? A word of the kingdom. Yeah. That word cannot be shaken. Is there a king of that kingdom? Yeah. Who is he? Yeah. Yeah. He can’t be shaken. Is there a citizenry of that kingdom?
What does Hebrews 12:26-28 say about the shaking?

Hebrews 12:26-28: whose voice then shook the earth; but now He has promised, saying, “Yet once more I shake not only the earth, but also heaven.” Now this, “Yet once more,” indicates the removal of those things that are being shaken, as of things that are made, that the things which cannot be shaken may remain. Therefore, since we are receiving a kingdom which cannot be shaken, let us have grace, by which we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear. Romans 14:17: for the kingdom of God is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.
What man-made doctrines and behaviors does he say need to be shaken?

He says things that mankind makes, such as the commandments of men and fables, turn people from the truth and need to be shaken, and gives examples such as idols and certain church practices, faith-only salvation, once saved always saved, predestination and dispensationalism. He says the Bible gives no right to your own faith, only his, and that Jesus alone should be exalted.
What man-made doctrines and behaviors does he say need to be shaken?

Yeah. They cannot be shaken. Isn’t that powerful? Folks, this is really good stuff. Okay, so things that are made can be shaken. Well, what are these things that are made? Things that mankind make, things that mankind create, they’re shaken. Matthew 7:7, “In vain they worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of who?” Men, they created them. They made them. And they have to be shaken. And that’s what we need in America. Titus 1:14, not giving heed to Jewish fables, myths, fairy tales. The Jews are God’s chosen people. That’s a lie. He’s chosen the poor of this earth, rich in faith, heirs of the kingdom. Are you there? Are you there? Oh, if I’m the bloodline of Judah, man, I got it made. He ain’t got nothing made. He’s made out of one blood all nations. And he wants to bring all nations to him. He has chosen all nations. Yes. Wow. And the commandments of men. And what is the result of these men things created? They turn people from the truth. Who is the truth? Jesus. What is the truth? His word. And when we say this is what I believe, honey, it doesn’t matter what you believe. It’s what God said to believe is what you need to believe and put your trust in. Amen. And these things need to be shaken. And we need a good shaking in America. For instance, the Catholic Church, they got to own up to their problems. Idols, come on. Any kindergartener that goes and reads the Bible knows that idols are out. Can I hear an amen? That needs to be shaken. Celibate, pedophile, homosexual priest. Come on. That’s just that’s got to be shaken. That just can’t be. Can I hear an amen? Nuns that have sex with the priest and abort the babies and all this stuff that have been happening for decades and hundreds of years. The Catholic Church needs to own up to it. They need to be shaken. Can I hear an amen? Yeah. Holy water, baby baptism, all lighting candles, and all this nonsense that takes us away from the real truth. It needs to be shaken. Isn’t that true? And you guys know I have no problem with the Catholic Church. They they need Jesus. I fellowship with them and all the rest. And I found genuine Christians in the Catholic Church because they decided to follow Christ and follow truth, not because they’re Catholic. So, we’re not attacking the Catholic Church. We’re just saying the Catholic Church needs to own up to their man-made doctrines. Is that an amen? Us Protestants, we got a lot of them. You know, we think we’re the elite because we came out of Catholicism. But Protestants, as I said before, create these doctrines of faith for salvation only. And they got so many of people in America believing they’re going to heaven because of faith and no works involved. They just threw James right out of the book and other things that Jesus taught right out of the book. This doctrine of once saved, always saved, that needs to be shaken. That’s not true. Predestination needs to be shaken. Calvin [unclear] needs to be shaken. Dispensationalism is a man-made doctrine. No medicine. The Pentecostals. And I’m a spiritfilled person, but I tell you, a lot of spiritfilled people give us a bad name. It’s it’s it’s sad. No medicine. You just believe God, the faith camp. And just in the last few months, a seven-month old baby and an eight-month old baby died because the parents believe God. You’re not supposed to take medicine. And the child died when the child could have lived. Folks, that doctor needs to be shaken. Amen. And just because you speak in tongues does not elevate you to a place where you can ignore the rest of the word of God. Can I hear an amen? I don’t care if you feel his presence and you speak in tongues and you can interpret him. You can’t preach this kind of doctrine. Handling of snakes is all Pentecostals. And two people died just recently. A 28-year-old woman and a 40-year-old pastor from a snake bite. That is stupid. And we can’t I’ve preached to them till I’m blue in the face. It they’re just so set in their ways. How many know we need a divine intervention where God shakes them loose? See, this nonsense has to be shaken. This is man-made stuff that kills and brings destruction and keeps us from the truth. Intoxication and getting high on drugs, that’s got to be shaken, folks. Adultery and homosexuals are okay. They’re going to heaven. No, that’s got to be shaken. All of these claim my faith. This is my faith. In the Bible, you don’t have a right to your faith. You only have a right to his faith. Can I hear an amen? See, my religion, they’ll say, my religion. Your religion. There is no your religion. There is no your faith in the Bible. It’s him and him only that should be exalted in our doctrines and in our lifestyle. Is that an amen? The liberal church who does not believe that Jesus was born of a virgin. That does not believe that there is a hell that a loving God would send anybody to. And a lot of other dumb doctrines of the liberal church. And they brag about it. We’re liberal. They literally brag about it. That’s got to be shaken, folks. Is that an amen? That’s got to be shaken. Somewhere we’re not getting the job done. So somewhere we need Jesus to come and shake loose these things that are causing people to roam from the truth. These behaviors and these doctrines so that Jesus alone is what? Exalted. And we don’t have to wait for that global visitation. We can what? Seek him now and have him shake us and have him shake our community and free people from these man-made lifestyles, acceptable lifestyles and man-made doctrines. And Isaiah spoke about it thousands of years before our generation. And we are in that kind of generation.
What man-made doctrines and behaviors does he say need to be shaken?
Mark 7:7: And in vain they worship Me, Teaching as doctrines the commandments of men.’ Titus 1:14: not giving heed to Jewish fables and commandments of men who turn from the truth.
What does he mean by "rubber band" a verse?
He says rubber band means you take a verse over here and stretch it to fit into something you want to accomplish, and that he wants to bring the scripture as it was stated.
How many nations does he say must hear the gospel before Jesus comes?
He says every one of them, and that two tribes were discovered only a few years back in South America and Indonesia, so people saying Jesus would come in earlier decades could not have been right.
What has he said for 40 years about when Jesus will come?

He says he has been telling people for 40 years that Jesus Christ is not going to come in his lifetime because there are so many things to be fulfilled, and that he has been branded a cult leader and a weirdo for it.
Does he say faith alone is enough?

He says America is so addicted to the message of faith that people fail to consider that Jesus told the rich man to keep the commandments. He says believing on him is one part of the formula and keeping his commandments is the second part.
What are the two types of the fear of the Lord?

He says the first is a moral respect for God where we hate sin and flee from it, and the second is the terror of the Lord, a tremendous feeling of fear that changes your metabolism, which kept the nations from making war against Judah.
What does he say about prosperity and greed in America?

He says even the poor in America drive a car and have a TV and a cell phone, and that greed is idolatry, with the poor wanting welfare without work and the rich wanting to make as much as they can without being taxed.
What does he say about "Forgive them not" in Isaiah 2:9?
He says Isaiah says not to forgive them when they are acting like this, but that God gives a solution every time: come to Jesus and you can be forgiven.
Why does God always give a solution along with judgment?

He says right at the same time as a thick judgment, he gives a solution every time because his whole goal is to save the world, and that people who are extreme on judgment need to balance it with the solution: come to Jesus.
Does he say we can move God now instead of waiting for that day?

He says that through seeking God we can get it done locally, and that you can move heaven by humbling yourself and doing what God said to do. He says it is a church movement God is interested in, not a man or woman of God.
What does he say about looking for Jesus to come for us versus in us?
He says everybody is looking for Jesus to come for us, but he also said he would come in us, and that hardly any Christian in America is looking for him to show forth his glory in us.
What does he say the kingdom that cannot be shaken includes?
He says the kingdom is righteousness, peace and joy in the Holy Ghost, and that the supernatural power of God, the gospel of the kingdom, the king and the citizens of that kingdom cannot be shaken.
What does he say about "my faith" and "my religion"?
He says in the Bible you don’t have a right to your faith, only to his faith, and there is no "your religion," because it is him and him only who should be exalted in our doctrines and lifestyle.

items.d: In this first lesson, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Revelation 2:1 that the seven stars are in the right hand of Jesus, who holds his ministers and keeps believers by John 10:28. He then teaches that…
p: In this first lesson, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Revelation 2:1 that the seven stars are in the right hand of Jesus, who holds his ministers and keeps believers by John 10:28. He then teaches that Jesus walks in the midst of the churches, so his presence, not music, rituals or special speakers, is the center of the assembly.
What does it mean that the seven stars are in his right hand? (Revelation 2:1, Romans 10:14–15, Matthew 10:1)

He says “the seven stars are the seven messengers of the seven churches of Asia,” and that all of us must be in the Lord’s hands, “not in a denomination’s hands, not in a religious group, not our own opinions and our own ideas, not self-appointed.” He cites Romans 10:14–15, that “no man takes the priesthood upon himself, he has to be selected by God,” and Matthew 10:1, where Jesus “called unto him his 12 disciples.”
What does it mean that the seven stars are in his right hand? (Revelation 2:1, Romans 10:14–15, Matthew 10:1)

We’re studying the book of Revelation, and, uh, this morning we’re going to look at the powerful revelations of Jesus Christ. Last week we talked about the revelation of the church. There’s more to come. I got emails and input from people saying how great that message was, because God’s word is great, amen, and we need to know who we are. Well, this morning we’re going to see more about Jesus Christ. First we’re going to look at the revelation of the keeping power of Jesus Christ. Revelations 2:1, when he addressed all these churches, I skipped over it last week, because they were, every one of them began with a revelation of Jesus Christ when he spoke to the churches, and this morning we’re going to go back through that and pick up the revelation of Jesus Christ: “He who holds the seven stars in his right hand, he who walks in the midst of the golden lampstands.” Remember, the seven stars are the seven messengers of the seven churches of Asia, a church leader. Now, a church leader must be in the hands, and not only church leaders, all of us must be in the hands of the Lord Jesus Christ, not in a denomination’s hands, not in a religious group, not our own opinions and our own ideas, not self-appointed. Romans 10:14 says, “How shall they believe in him whom they have not heard? And how shall they hear without a preacher?
