And how shall that preacher preach unless he is sent?” He’s set apart on a mission by God. In Hebrews it says no man takes the priesthood upon himself, he has to be selected by God. Could that be an amen? And see, when we just go and we just anoint people, and [unclear] anointing, and just pick people, people without God’s hand upon them, we open them up for disasters in the church. Are you there? Now, the seven stars are in his right hand. It’s important that the messengers of God are in the hand of the Lord Jesus Christ. Matthew 10:1: “He called unto him his 12 disciples.”
What does it mean that the seven stars are in his right hand? (Revelation 2:1, Romans 10:14–15, Matthew 10:1)

Revelation 2:1: “To the angel of the church of Ephesus write, ‘These things says He who holds the seven stars in His right hand, who walks in the midst of the seven golden lampstands: Romans 10:14-15: How then shall they call on Him in whom they have not believed? And how shall they believe in Him of whom they have not heard? And how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach unless they are sent? As it is written: “How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the gospel of peace, Who bring glad tidings of good things!” Hebrews 5:4: And no man takes this honor to himself, but he who is called by God, just as Aaron was. Matthew 10:1: And when He had called His twelve disciples to Him, He gave them power over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all kinds of sickness and all kinds of disease.
Does he say a minister must be called by Jesus himself? (Matthew 10:1–22)

He says “until Jesus Christ invites you to be a messenger of the gospel of Christ… you don’t qualify,” however much seminary or Bible college you have. He says opposition will come, and “that’s why ministers have nervous breakdowns” and “quit the ministry,” because “they were never called in the first place.” He adds that “when you’re in his hand, he’s responsible for you.”
Does he say a minister must be called by Jesus himself? (Matthew 10:1–22)

See, first he called unto him his 12 disciples, then it says he gave them power against unclean spirits to cast them out and to heal all manner of sickness and diseases, and these 12 he sent forth and told them, “Freely you receive, freely give.” First he, what? Called them to himself. Folks, you can go to seminary all you want, Bible college all you want, but until Jesus Christ invites you to be a messenger of the gospel of Christ, a minister, a leader in the church of the living God, you don’t qualify. You got to be in his hand, and we’re going to see why. Here it goes on to say in that verse, for they are going to reject you, they’re going to persecute you, your own family is going to rise up against you, and with all of this opposition you’re not going to handle it if you’re not in his hand. Can I hear an amen? That’s why ministers have nervous breakdowns and they take sabbatical and they quit the ministry. Why? They were never called in the first place. Hallelujah. See, your own opinion only lasts until you go through a conflict, and then you’re going to fall apart, but when you’re in his hand, he’s responsible for you. Wow. And remember, these churches had some flaws in them, and yet the ministers of those churches were still in his hands and his presence was still in their midst. Don’t eliminate yourself because you’re not perfect yet. You understand that? Amen. And don’t eliminate a young minister or something because they’re not perfect. Forget it, if they’re in his hand, let me tell you, God is going to take the responsibility to back them up and get them through these things. Amen.
Does he say a minister must be called by Jesus himself? (Matthew 10:1–22)

Matthew 10:1-8: And when He had called His twelve disciples to Him, He gave them power over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all kinds of sickness and all kinds of disease. Now the names of the twelve apostles are these: first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother; Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James the son of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus; Simon the Cananite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed Him. These twelve Jesus sent out and commanded them, saying: “Do not go into the way of the Gentiles, and do not enter a city of the Samaritans. But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. And as you go, preach, saying, ‘The kingdom of heaven is at hand.’ Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out demons. Freely you have received, freely give. Matthew 10:16-22: “Behold, I send you out as sheep in the midst of wolves. Therefore be wise as serpents and harmless as doves. But beware of men, for they will deliver you up to councils and scourge you in their synagogues. You will be brought before governors and kings for My sake, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles. But when they deliver you up, do not worry about how or what you should speak. For it will be given to you in that hour what you should speak; for it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you. “Now brother will deliver up brother to death, and a father his child; and children will rise up against parents and cause them to be put to death. And you will be hated by all for My name’s sake. But he who endures to the end will be saved.
Can anything take believers out of his hand? (Deuteronomy 32:39)

He says “there’s nothing going to be able to get you off track… when you’re in the hands of Jesus,” and that Satan, demons and “the people that follow evil cannot distract us.” He says “we have the freedom to walk out of his hand, but no one, no power can come in and take us out of his hand,” and that “he’ll finish the good work he began in us.”
Can anything take believers out of his hand? (Deuteronomy 32:39)

Very powerful, very powerful. In Deuteronomy 32:39: “There is no God besides me; I kill, I make alive; I wound, I heal; nor is there any who can deliver out of my hand.” There’s nothing going to be able to get you off track, to get you distracted, when you’re in the hands of Jesus. The problem is we get in our own hand, we start taking responsibility for our own life and we can’t handle things. We got to get back into the hand of what? Jesus Christ. Amen. He’s got these stars in his right hand, and nobody, Satan, demons, Satan’s children, the people that follow evil, cannot distract us, cannot disrupt us. Why? Because we’re in his hand, nobody can touch us. We can walk away, but nobody can come in and snatch us away. We have the freedom to walk out of his hand, but no one, no power can come in and take us out of his hand. Amen. And he’ll finish the good work he began in us. Hallelujah. Yeah.
Can anything take believers out of his hand? (Deuteronomy 32:39)

Deuteronomy 32:39: ‘Now see that I, even I, am He, And there is no God besides Me; I kill and I make alive; I wound and I heal; Nor is there any who can deliver from My hand. Philippians 1:6: being confident of this very thing, that He who has begun a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ;
What does he say is missing in the American church? (Isaiah 43:13, John 10:28)

He says “this is not a little religion we’re going through, this is an identity with a real person, the Lord Jesus Christ.” He cites Isaiah 43:13 and John 10:28, and says that “almost all New Testament scripture is found in the Old Testament.” He says “America is going backwards, the other ones are going forward, because they depend on Jesus and they’re focused on Jesus.”
What does he say is missing in the American church? (Isaiah 43:13, John 10:28)

That’s a powerful revelation of Jesus Christ. This is not a little religion we’re going through, this is an identity with a real person, the Lord Jesus Christ, and he has power to work in our life. It says in Isaiah 43:13, “There is no one who can deliver out of my hand.” Do you get the message? I told you before over and over, almost all New Testament scripture is found in the Old Testament. Why? Because God just keeps repeating himself, trying to get us to get the message. Hallelujah. And it confirms that the prophets in the Old and New Testament are all saying the same thing. Keeping power of Jesus Christ, John 10:28: “I give unto them eternal life, and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand.” How many of you have eternal life through Jesus Christ? Come on. All right, with that comes this. You see, this is what the American church is missing, and I told you before, I’ve preached all over the world, and America is going backwards, the other ones are going forward, because they depend on Jesus and they’re focused on Jesus, and we get focused on religion and our own opinions and what [unclear] say and [unclear] say. “I don’t only give them eternal life, but they shall never perish.” You’re never going to be bothered about the lake of fire and eternal damnation. Why? Because you came to him, he gave you eternal life, he saved you from that punishment, and he put you in his hand that Satan and the evil people and no one can come and touch you.
What does he say is missing in the American church? (Isaiah 43:13, John 10:28)

Isaiah 43:13: Indeed before the day was, I am He; And there is no one who can deliver out of My hand; I work, and who will reverse it?” John 10:28: And I give them eternal life, and they shall never perish; neither shall anyone snatch them out of My hand.
What does he say about witchcraft and his time in Africa?

He says that in Africa he told people, “bring on these witch doctors, I’ll take them on, I’m not afraid of them,” and that “the name of Jesus has power and authority over the highest one.” He says “I’m in the hands of Jesus,” and that we cannot be content with the rapture but “got to be a mighty force in the earth to be reckoned with today.” This is his own account and is not verified here.
What does he say about witchcraft and his time in Africa?

Are you there? You can give in, you can give up, but nobody can touch you. Hallelujah. So see, our choices are important. I’m in his hand. Bring on the world, bring on Satan, bring on the kingdom. When I was in Africa, I told them, “Bring on these witch doctors, I’ll take them on, I’m not afraid of them.” The pastors of the local churches were afraid, the people were afraid, because they didn’t understand the three areas of witchcraft that’s in the Bible, and they didn’t understand that the name of Jesus has power and authority over the highest one, and that’s demonic witchcraft, and the word has authority over the fleshly and the chemical witchcraft. Yes, yeah, they look good till somebody comes along that knows Jesus Christ. And I told you before, I told them, “Do something to me, come on, show me your stuff, kill me, put a [unclear] on my nose, do something. You got no power over Christ, you got no power over, I’m in the hands of Jesus.” Man. Are you out there, church? See, this is the revelation of the power of Jesus Christ in our lives today, and it’s given to all of us who have eternal life. Hallelujah, hallelujah. We need to start focusing on these other issues. We can’t just be thankful we’re going to go to heaven when the rapture comes and all that.
What does he say about the Father, Jesus and the Holy Ghost? (John 10:29–30)

He says “there is a Father, there is Jesus Christ, and there’s a Holy Ghost,” and that although “the Trinity was a created word,” it “really explains how the Bible describes God.” Citing John 10:29–30, he says “there’s three beings in one,” and that “these Jesus-only people are missing it.”
What does he say about the Father, Jesus and the Holy Ghost? (John 10:29–30)

No, you got to be a mighty force in the earth to be reckoned with today in this hour. Hallelujah. “My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all.” Now, here is part of the Trinity thing. You know, people can say, you know, the Trinity was a created word, and, you know, it is, somebody created it, but it really explains how the Bible describes God. There is a Father, there is Jesus Christ, and there’s a Holy Ghost, and the Father has superpower over Jesus Christ, and Jesus Christ has superpower over everything else, and then the Holy Ghost is sent to us to empower us to live for him. And this scripture brings it out, and these Jesus-only people are missing it, totally missing it. He says, “My Father, which gave them me,” who brought the people to Jesus? The Father is greater than all. Who has the most authority? The Father. “No man is able to pluck them out of my Father’s hand, and I and my Father are” what? One. He is the Father and he is the Son, and yet there’s three beings in one. Jesus plainly said it. Amen. So if you don’t want to believe in Jesus and you believe in God, he’s still Jesus, and you’re still in his hand. Man, get off your hobby horse and get with the program. Amen.
What does he say about the Father, Jesus and the Holy Ghost? (John 10:29–30)
John 10:29-30: My Father, who has given them to Me, is greater than all; and no one is able to snatch them out of My Father’s hand. I and My Father are one.”
Does he say Jesus’s presence in the church means approval? (Revelation 2:1)

He says though the churches “had problems,” Jesus was still in their midst: “His presence is not his approval. His presence is his faithfulness to back up his word, to finish the good work he began in you.” He says “the most important person in the church is the one that’s in the midst,” and not “the pastor or the Pope or the priest or the evangelist.”
Does he say Jesus’s presence in the church means approval? (Revelation 2:1)

You know, we like to just discuss doctrine, we don’t like to be empowered by doctrine, just discuss it, show everybody what we know. We need to possess it. Hallelujah. Now, how many of you glad you’re in the hands of Jesus? Yes. And because of him, see, his camp is great because he’s great, he’s strong. Jesus Christ in the assembly. Revelations 2:1: “He who holds the seven stars in his right hand, who walks in the midst of the seven golden candlesticks.” He’s in the midst of the churches. Though they had problems, they left their first love, they had sexual immorality going on, they had idolatry going on, they had unrestrained people living an unrestrained life, you remember what was happening in the church, and yet his presence was where? In the church. His presence is not his approval. His presence is his faithfulness to back up his word, to finish the good work he began in you. He’s always trying to change you into someone that is a light to the world, a likeness of him, that is his goal, and to get you to that goal he had to forgive you your sins and save you from eternal damnation, and all we dwell on is what? Being saved from my sins and eternal, you know, life, and we don’t think about the objective. The objective is to reach the goal. Now, we need Jesus in the church, and the most important person in the church is not the pastor or the Pope or the priest or the evangelist; the most important person in the church is the one that’s in the midst, and that’s who? Jesus Christ. And in America we get distracted from that by good speakers, by music groups coming in, and music and all the rest.
Does he say Jesus’s presence in the church means approval? (Revelation 2:1)

Revelation 2:1: “To the angel of the church of Ephesus write, ‘These things says He who holds the seven stars in His right hand, who walks in the midst of the seven golden lampstands: Philippians 1:6: being confident of this very thing, that He who has begun a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ;
What does he say the assembly should focus on?

He says the focus should be on Jesus, “not distributing food to the poor,” not the youth group, the children’s church, senior citizens or addicts, “and certainly not psychology.” He says in a board meeting he said, “all I hear is humans talking,” and “we need a transition from our mental and our physical and our human capabilities into his capabilities.”
What does he say the assembly should focus on?

We get distracted from him who is the essential ingredient when we assemble together. Isn’t that true? Or we come for a socializing, social club, to see our friend or to find a woman or a man or whatever. We should be coming because Jesus, when we come together, is there, and the focus should be on him, not distributing food to the poor. It should be on him. He is the most important thing, not the youth group, not the children’s church, not senior citizens, not the addicts of drugs and alcohol and sex, and certainly not psychology, how the human mind works, and that’s what’s creeping into the American church. And that’s why a church must worship and pray and praise and wait on Jesus and preach and prophesy the [unclear] living word of God, because he’s in our midst and we need to hear from him. Hallelujah. King David in the Old Testament said, “The Spirit spake by my mouth,” and that’s what we need to do. I was in a board meeting once, and they were covering some really heavy issues, and I finally stopped and I said, “You know, all I hear is humans talking. I never hear the, I’m not hearing the Spirit anywhere.” And we need to hear what the Spirit’s saying in things. We need a transition from our mental and our physical and our human capabilities into his capabilities. Could that be an amen? And preachers preach without that. Remember, these seven churches were doing these disappointing things, and he was there, and remember he walked in the midst. He promised to be in the midst without music.
What does he say the assembly should focus on?
2 Samuel 23:2: “The Spirit of the LORD spoke by me, And His word was on my tongue.
Does he say the church needs music, rituals, or certain clothes? (Matthew 18:20)

He says “there’s no requirement of music, no singing, no special speaker,” and that Christians who choose a church for casual clothes ask, “where is that in the Bible?” He tells of Africans who “dressed their best” because “if we go before our kings here on earth dressed our best, then we’re going to dress our best for Jesus Christ.” He cites Matthew 18:20, “where two or three are gathered together in my name.”
Does he say the church needs music, rituals, or certain clothes? (Matthew 18:20)

There’s no requirement of music, no singing, no special speaker, no miracle worker, no miracles, no rituals, no casual clothes or suits and ties. I just, it just really agitates me when Christians say, “Well, I go to that church because I can wear casual clothes.” Well, where is that in the Bible? That’s not even mentioned. I mean, you go to church because you can look like a dud? You should go because he’s in the midst. Yes. And Africa had the best outlook on dressing to the house of God that I’ve ever run across. These people were dirt poor, and yet they came to church dressed their best, and this is what they told me every time: “If we go before our king,” they have little chiefs everywhere, you know, kings and all that, “if we go before our kings here on earth dressed our best, then we’re going to dress our best for Jesus Christ.” And I go, wow, that is a good attitude. Hallelujah. But not in America. We got to build up, “I don’t have to shave, I don’t have to comb my hair, I don’t have to, you know, blow the snot out of my nose or anything, I can just go.” I tell you, Africa has the best idea. It’s just a gathering together, no rituals, just the gathering together. In Matthew 18:20: “Where two or three are gathered together in my name,” no music, no concerts, no dramas, no [unclear], no candles burning, just assembling together unto him. He said, “I’ll be there.” Now, and Friday night, as I watched these young people gather together as that service started, I just said, “God, they have no concept yet of how powerful you are.” Just because they’re here, they’re waiting for the music to start, and they’re waiting for [unclear] to run up and down, these things, you know, they’re waiting for the ritual. They have no concept to know how powerful you are here. Your presence is here because they showed up.
Does he say the church needs music, rituals, or certain clothes? (Matthew 18:20)

Revelation 2:1: “To the angel of the church of Ephesus write, ‘These things says He who holds the seven stars in His right hand, who walks in the midst of the seven golden lampstands: Matthew 18:20: For where two or three are gathered together in My name, I am there in the midst of them.”
What does he say about church attendance, repentance and hypocrites? (Acts 3:19)

He says “the American church is the only one dwindling in church attendance; the other nations are increasing,” and that people will go to “a concert” but not simply because Jesus is there. Citing Acts 3:19, “repent therefore and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out,” he says “the church is not hypocrites,” because “a hypocrite says one thing and does another purposely,” while others “are pursuing the goal.”
What does he say about church attendance, repentance and hypocrites? (Acts 3:19)

Amen. Yes. And you got Christians that won’t even show up. They don’t have to sing, they don’t have to do anything, they just show up, and Jesus said, “I’ll be there.” And the American church is the only one dwindling in church attendance; the other nations are increasing, as I showed you, millions worship him at a time in other nations. You can’t get 10 people out to worship God in America. Oh, you can get them to a concert, you can get them to a popular singer or popular speaker, but just to come because Jesus is there? How boring. No, he is everything. Church without him, we can what? Do nothing. Acts 3:19: “Repent therefore and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out.” See, we’ve all done that, “that the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord.” Oh, see, I have to repent, I have to change my life, but that’s so I can reach the objective and Jesus can come and touch my life and make me into his likeness, into his image. Now, isn’t that a good Bible? Amen. He does the changing, he’s promised it, and he has the power to back up what he promised, if I’ll just come and join with the ones I don’t even like, they irritate me, they drive me nuts, these hypocrites in the church. Yeah, come on, hypocrite, join them. How many’s heard that statement? “I go to church, go to the hypocrites.” Well, come on, hypocrite, you’re one of them. Actually, the church is not hypocrites. A hypocrite says one thing and does another purposely. Uh, many of God’s people just haven’t attained to things yet, and yes, they may look like hypocrites, but they are pursuing the goal, and that makes a difference. Amen. They have some flaws and they have some weakness and they have some sins they overcome, but they’re not justifying it, they’re pursuing the goal.
What does he say about church attendance, repentance and hypocrites? (Acts 3:19)
Acts 3:19: Repent therefore and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, so that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord,
What does he say about music in church?

He says “God chose to use music, God chose to do miracles so that people would believe,” but “when we get distracted by these things… our focus isn’t on him, now it’s on the music.” He says of music, “it’s not a neutral vehicle,” and that “they think they’re experiencing the power of God” when it is the music. These are his views on styles of music and large churches.
What does he say about music in church?

That’s not a hypocrite. Hallelujah. See, we need him to come in our midst and refresh us, inspire us, renew us. God chose to use music, God chose to do miracles so that people would believe, God chose these things, but when we get distracted by these things and we just go with miracles or the promises of them, or where we just go where there’s good music, we have lost the whole concept of Jesus in the midst of his church. Our focus isn’t on him, now it’s on the music. Could that be true? “I go to this church because they play country music.” Well, you poor little thing, God is limited to one kind of music. “I go to this church because they play contemporary rock music.” That is, that’s not even in the Bible. God never said, “Hey, I’ll give you the music of your choice.” No, he said, “I’ll give you the music of the kingdom.” Are you there, church? Hallelujah. And we’re filling the big churches, one of the reasons they have a lot of members is they have rock music, they have the music that people listen to through the radio during the day, and they come into church and, and I’ve watched them, they’re worshiping music and don’t even know it. I sit there in amazement, because music has a high, music has a, it inspires you, it does something to you, it’s not a neutral vehicle, it does something to you, and because they’re experiencing the power of the music they think they’re experiencing the power of God, and I sit there in amazement, and I can prove it by saying, “Don’t play the music now. Worship.” And they’re dead on their feet.
What does he say the seven stars are?
He says “the seven stars are the seven messengers of the seven churches of Asia,” meaning church leaders.
Does he say seminary makes someone a minister?
No. He says “you can go to seminary all you want, Bible college all you want, but until Jesus Christ invites you… you don’t qualify.”
Why does he say ministers have nervous breakdowns?
He says it is “why ministers have nervous breakdowns and they take sabbatical and they quit the ministry,” because “they were never called in the first place.”
Does he say anyone can take a believer out of Jesus’s hand?
No. He says “no power can come in and take us out of his hand,” though “we have the freedom to walk out of his hand.”
What does he say about the Trinity?
He says “the Trinity was a created word,” but “it really explains how the Bible describes God,” and “there’s three beings in one.”
Does he say Jesus’s presence in a church is his approval?
No. He says “his presence is not his approval,” but “his faithfulness to back up his word.”
What does he say a gathering needs?
He says “there’s no requirement of music, no singing, no special speaker, no miracle worker,” and “you should go because he’s in the midst.”
Why does he say Christians in Africa dressed their best?
He says they told him “if we go before our kings here on earth dressed our best, then we’re going to dress our best for Jesus Christ.”
How does he define a hypocrite?
He says “a hypocrite says one thing and does another purposely,” while many of God’s people “just haven’t attained to things yet.”
Does he say music is neutral?
No. He says of music, “it’s not a neutral vehicle,” and “it does something to you.”

items.d: In this second lesson, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Revelation 2:8 through 3:14 about the first and last, the word as the sword of the Spirit, the seven spirits of God from Isaiah 11:2, the key of…
p: In this second lesson, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Revelation 2:8 through 3:14 about the first and last, the word as the sword of the Spirit, the seven spirits of God from Isaiah 11:2, the key of David, and Jesus as the beginning of the creation of God. He closes with the throne room of Revelation 4:1–8.
What does he teach from “the first and the last”? (Revelation 2:8)

He reads “I am the first and the last, who was dead and I came to life again,” and says “Jesus is the beginning of everything and the ending of everything.” He says “he had to give up his life, and he picked it back up again, that takes deity.”
What does he teach from “the first and the last”? (Revelation 2:8)

Next, the revelation of the eternal Jesus and his word. Revelations 2:8: “The first, that I am the first and the last, who was dead and I came to life again.” So Jesus is the beginning of everything and the ending of everything. He’s the first in rank, and yet he lowered himself to become one of us, lay down his life for us, and take it back up again. Now, that is a deity. That just makes Allah and Muhammad and Joseph Smith and all them, they’re just nothing. This is real deity, are you with me? Nobody could kill him. He had to give up his life, and he picked it back up again, that takes deity. You try killing yourself and picking yourself back up. Yeah, you’re going to, you’re going to be in the grave. See, that’s God. He’s eternal, he was before he became flesh.
What does he teach from “the first and the last”? (Revelation 2:8)

Revelation 2:8: “And to the angel of the church in Smyrna write, ‘These things says the First and the Last, who was dead, and came to life: John 10:18: No one takes it from Me, but I lay it down of Myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. This command I have received from My Father.”
What does he say about the sword of the Spirit and the spoken word? (Revelation 2:12, Ephesians 6:17, Hebrews 4:12)

He says “the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God” will “separate your fleshly things from your spiritual things,” and that Jesus “created the world by his word.” He says “the Bible says the word will set you free,” and that “prayer will bring you in tune with God, and he will tell you what to do, and then you have to respond to the word.”
What does he say about the sword of the Spirit and the spoken word? (Revelation 2:12, Ephesians 6:17, Hebrews 4:12)

He was God when he was here in the flesh, he was God when he laid down his life on that cross, he was God when he resurrected himself from the dead, and he was God when he ascended back to heaven, and he’s God when he comes the next time. Amen. Revelations 2:12: “He who has the sharp two-edged sword.” We know that this word of the Lord is called the sword, the sword of the Spirit in the Bible. In Ephesians 6:17, “the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.” Hebrews 4:12: “The word of God is quick and powerful and sharper than any two-edged sword,” but we don’t read any further, “piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit.” See, that word will separate your fleshly things from your spiritual things, so that you know there’s a distinct difference and not follow the flesh. The Bible says the spirit is willing, but the flesh is what? Weak. Well, the word comes and separates the two so you can make the choice, and he is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart. He knows why you’re doing what you’re doing, that word exposes your motives. Is that powerful? Yes. And he chose the foolishness of preaching to save, what? All that believe. That word is very powerful. He created the world by his word, his spoken word. When he said, “Lazarus, come forth,” out of the grave, guess what? Lazarus came forth. That’s how powerful his word is, and it’s the spoken word that’s powerful. That’s why you need to [unclear] it, sing it, you need to speak it, you need to memorize it. That word is what sets you free. You got a flaw you want to work on, you want to cure, get into the word on that problem, and that word will set you free. But in a Pentecostal, that’s Spirit-filled people, we want the man of God to [unclear] over us and get us free; in the Catholic church we want the priest to sprinkle water over us and get us free; but the Bible says the word will set you free. Amen. And so you got to be in the word, and you got to speak that word. We’re looking for some prayer, oh, we go to a prayer meeting and I’ll get free. No, prayer will bring you in tune with God, and he will tell you what to do, and then you have to respond to the word. Are you there? That’s the revelation. Isn’t that powerful? Isn’t this powerful? If we get our eyes on Jesus, it will revolutionize our life. Now, here are some of Christ’s powerful possessions. This is what Christ possesses. Are you ready for this?
What does he say about the sword of the Spirit and the spoken word? (Revelation 2:12, Ephesians 6:17, Hebrews 4:12)

Revelation 2:12: “And to the angel of the church in Pergamos write, ‘These things says He who has the sharp two-edged sword: Ephesians 6:17: And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God; Hebrews 4:12: For the word of God is living and powerful, and sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing even to the division of soul and spirit, and of joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart. 1 Corinthians 1:21: For since, in the wisdom of God, the world through wisdom did not know God, it pleased God through the foolishness of the message preached to save those who believe. John 11:43: Now when He had said these things, He cried with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come forth!”
What does he say we inherit from Christ? (Revelation 2:18, Revelation 3:1, Romans 8:17)

He says “we are joint heirs with Jesus Christ, what he inherits we inherit,” but that “we will never be God, but we will take on his nature.” On Revelation 2:18 he says that “darkness is the absence of light” and “a Christian should never be in what? Darkness. Why? Because Jesus is there.”
What does he say we inherit from Christ? (Revelation 2:18, Revelation 3:1, Romans 8:17)

No, you want to go home? And remember, if Christ possesses it, the Bible says we are joint heirs with Jesus Christ, what he inherits we inherit. Wow. Now, we can’t be God, let’s don’t be ridiculous here, you know, we never will be creators, we will never be God, but we will take on his nature and possess the things that he possessed while he was here in the flesh. Revelations 2:18: “I am the Son of God,” or he is the Son of God, God, Jesus is the Son of God, “I’m the one who has eyes like a flame of fire.” You know, I don’t care what kind of darkness is in you, I’m going to come and see right through it, and when light comes, what happens to darkness? Yeah, it’s gone. See, darkness is the absence of light. Darkness is nothing, light is everything, and the absence of light, you got what? Darkness. So a Christian should never be in what? Darkness. Why? Because Jesus is there. “And his feet like fine brass.” Revelations 3:1: “He who has the seven spirits of God and the seven stars.” The seven spirits of God are best described in Isaiah 11:2.
What does he say we inherit from Christ? (Revelation 2:18, Revelation 3:1, Romans 8:17)

Romans 8:17: and if children, then heirs—heirs of God and joint heirs with Christ, if indeed we suffer with Him, that we may also be glorified together. Revelation 2:18: “And to the angel of the church in Thyatira write, ‘These things says the Son of God, who has eyes like a flame of fire, and His feet like fine brass: Revelation 3:1: “And to the angel of the church in Sardis write, ‘These things says He who has the seven Spirits of God and the seven stars: “I know your works, that you have a name that you are alive, but you are dead.
What does he say the Spirit of the Lord and the Spirit of wisdom give us? (Isaiah 11:2, Luke 24:49)

He says “the Holy Ghost has got a lot more to it than tongues, and greater things than tongues,” and that “that Spirit will cause us to rule on earth,” meaning “we rule over sin.” He says “wisdom is the principal thing,” and “the wise man foresees the evil and avoids it.”
What does he say the Spirit of the Lord and the Spirit of wisdom give us? (Isaiah 11:2, Luke 24:49)

“The Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him.” Spirit of the Lord, Lord is all controlling, all powerful ruler. “The Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him.” The Holy Ghost comes upon us. He said, “You go in and tarry in Jerusalem till you be endued with” what? Power from on high. Well, one of the attributes of that Holy Ghost, and us Pentecostals, we mess it up because we, you know, have promoted for years of charismatics that tongues is the initial sign of the Holy Ghost, and, no, let me tell you, the Holy Ghost has got a lot more to it than tongues, and greater things than tongues. And the Bible says don’t forbid to, what? Speak in tongues. But, folks, there’s bigger things than tongues right here. That Spirit will cause us to rule on earth, as we will see later. Spirit of the Lord, the rulership part of the Spirit. When a guy rules, that means things are under his control, right? Your tongue. Hallelujah. Your sexual desires. See, we rule over sin, the Spirit of the Lord, very important. I don’t know about you, but I’d rather have that part of the Spirit than tongues, and I speak in tongues, but this is much more powerful. The Spirit of wisdom: wisdom is the principal thing, and in all your getting, get understanding. Wisdom makes you wiser, the word of God makes you wiser than the heathen. Are you there? The wise man foresees the evil and avoids it. See, Christians see where this decision is going to lead to, and they don’t make it. See, how many would like wisdom? How many read in James about the wisdom from above?
What does he say the Spirit of the Lord and the Spirit of wisdom give us? (Isaiah 11:2, Luke 24:49)

Isaiah 11:2: The Spirit of the LORD shall rest upon Him, The Spirit of wisdom and understanding, The Spirit of counsel and might, The Spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the LORD. Luke 24:49: Behold, I send the Promise of My Father upon you; but tarry in the city of Jerusalem until you are endued with power from on high.” 1 Corinthians 14:39: Therefore, brethren, desire earnestly to prophesy, and do not forbid to speak with tongues. Proverbs 4:7: Wisdom is the principal thing; Therefore get wisdom. And in all your getting, get understanding. Proverbs 22:3: A prudent man foresees evil and hides himself, But the simple pass on and are punished.
What does he say about wisdom from above, might, and the tractor? (James 3:17, 2 Timothy 1:7)

He says the wisdom from above is “first pure, then peaceable,” and quotes “I have not given you a spirit of fear but of power and love and a sound mind.” He says “Christians are wimps” because “they don’t ask God for these things,” and illustrates with a tractor: “The Christians have got the tractor and they don’t have the attachments.”
What does he say about wisdom from above, might, and the tractor? (James 3:17, 2 Timothy 1:7)

Yes, that’s the wisdom you need to be asking for, and he says ask wisdom and God will give it liberally. The wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable. It’s first, what? Pure, then peaceable, it’s easy to get along with. See, it’s kind and it’s, uh, quick to submit and cooperate, it doesn’t have to be in charge. Hallelujah. Has no partiality, no hypocrisy. The wisdom from above is beautiful, church. Understanding: “My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge,” and understanding. The Spirit of counsel, the Spirit of might, strong. “I have not given you a spirit of fear but of power and love and a sound mind.” I have given you a spirit of strength, and yet Christians are wimps. Why? Because they don’t ask God for these things. Most of them don’t even know these things are available. It’s like this tractor we have out here, you know, the tractor is great, but without the attachments it’s worthless. Without the attachment you’re just riding around, but you put a grabber on there and you can move big rocks, you put a bucket on there and you can move lots of dirt, you put a [unclear] on there and, man, you can level things that are rough and uneven, you put a plow on there and you can have a harvest. The Christians have got the tractor and they don’t have the attachments. Could that be an amen? They’re worthless, they can’t do anything but just run up and down saying, “I’m a Christian, I’m a believer.” Boy, that was good. Even has a horn on it, we’re good at that, “Hey, come, I can’t do anything but here I am.”
What does he say about wisdom from above, might, and the tractor? (James 3:17, 2 Timothy 1:7)

James 3:17: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, willing to yield, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality and without hypocrisy. James 1:5: If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach, and it will be given to him. Hosea 4:6: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I also will reject you from being priest for Me; Because you have forgotten the law of your God, I also will forget your children. 2 Timothy 1:7: For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind.
What does he say about the key of David and the keys of hell and death? (Revelation 3:7, Revelation 5:5, Revelation 1:18)

He says “the fear of the Lord is to depart from evil,” and that Jesus is the one “who opens and no man shuts.” He says “when he does something, nobody can come against it and change it,” that “he has the keys of hell and death,” and that “Jesus has been given the responsibility to build a church.”
What does he say about the key of David and the keys of hell and death? (Revelation 3:7, Revelation 5:5, Revelation 1:18)

You see, Jesus possessed these things and we can possess them. The Spirit of knowledge and the Spirit of the fear of the Lord. Boy, the Spirit of counsel is a good one too, you ought to hear the advice you guys give each other. We need that Spirit of counsel, believe me. The fear of the Lord is to depart from evil. How many need the Spirit of the fear of the Lord? You struggle with evil, you struggle with sin? Yeah, we need that, it’s promised to us, hallelujah, to empower us. Revelations 3:7: “He who is holy, he who is true, he who has the key of David, he who opens and no man shuts, and shuts and no man opens.” That’s Jesus. When he does something, nobody can come against it and change it. Revelations 5:5: “Weep not. Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, has prevailed to open the book and loose the seals thereof.” You see, he has the key of David, he came of the root and offspring of David, that’s how we know he’s the real Messiah, that was what was promised in the Old Testament. In Revelations 1:18 we read that he has the keys of hell and death. Hallelujah. Hell and death: my going to hell and dying in the second death, it’s totally in the authority of Jesus Christ, not the Catholic church, not the Protestant church, not Muhammad or anybody else, it’s totally in the hands of the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. So shut up, this thing’s been solved. David was given permission to build a temple for God and prepare for it, but Jesus has been given the responsibility to build a church. He is the key to the building of the church, do you understand that? That’s the key of David. David was an example, a type of Jesus. Jesus is the real deal.
What does he say about the key of David and the keys of hell and death? (Revelation 3:7, Revelation 5:5, Revelation 1:18)

Proverbs 8:13: The fear of the LORD is to hate evil; Pride and arrogance and the evil way And the perverse mouth I hate. Revelation 3:7: “And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia write, ‘These things says He who is holy, He who is true, “He who has the key of David, He who opens and no one shuts, and shuts and no one opens”: Revelation 5:5: But one of the elders said to me, “Do not weep. Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has prevailed to open the scroll and to loose its seven seals.” Revelation 1:18: I am He who lives, and was dead, and behold, I am alive forevermore. Amen. And I have the keys of Hades and of Death.
Does he say Jesus can come back any minute?

He says “he’s not coming back until it’s fulfilled, every jot and every tittle of the word has to be fulfilled.” He says earlier predictions that Jesus would come before 1960, 1962, 1964 and 1972 all passed, and that “Jesus has a lot of things to do,” including “the great harvest that he promised.”
Does he say Jesus can come back any minute?

Hallelujah. And if he is out to build you up, and he is out to build a church in this earth, and I tell you he’s not coming back until it’s fulfilled, every jot and every tittle of the word has to be fulfilled, isn’t that right? And so with these people, Jesus said that he can come any minute? No, he can’t, because there’s some things he’s got to do, and one of them is his church. Hallelujah. When I was a kid they scared us to death because Jesus was going to come before 1960, and I’m still here. Then it was 1962, then it was 1964, then it was 1972, then it’s this year, it’s that year, the 11th hour, the second hand’s ticking, we’re almost there, I’m still here. Why? Because Jesus has a lot of things to do. Another is the great harvest that he promised, to fill heaven with people, and there’s no greater population on earth right now of all time than in our generation, and you think Jesus wants to come and put millions of billions of people to hell because the church wants to get raptured? No, he wants to bring in the harvest. He said, “Get your eyes on the field, they are ripe for the harvest.”
Does he say Jesus can come back any minute?

Matthew 5:18: For assuredly, I say to you, till heaven and earth pass away, one jot or one tittle will by no means pass from the law till all is fulfilled. John 4:35: Do you not say, ‘There are still four months and then comes the harvest’? Behold, I say to you, lift up your eyes and look at the fields, for they are already white for harvest!
How does he explain “the beginning of the creation of God”? (Revelation 3:14, John 1:1)

He reads “the beginning of the creation of God” and says “people laugh at me when I teach this,” yet “he’s eternal, he was, he is, and he will be.” Turning to John 1:1 he says “we can’t limit him to our human thinking.”
How does he explain “the beginning of the creation of God”? (Revelation 3:14, John 1:1)

We got our eyes on the heavens, “Come, oh come, Lord, rapture, fit into our theory.” Amen. These are distractions from Jesus. Revelations 3:14: “I am the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God.” Wow. And people laugh at me when I teach this because they go, “Well, how can he be created when he was the Creator and he always was?” Well, you got to understand it, you got to read it like it is: Jesus was what? The beginning of the creation of God. Is that what it says? The start, the first. Okay, and yet he is what? God. He’s eternal, he was, he is, and he will be, he’s eternal. Now, watch how simple it is to understand this. John 1:1: “In the beginning was the” what? Word. At the start of everything was the word, “and the word was with God.” And the word, wow. Now, you explain that in your little human mentality: the word was with God. I’m with Rebecca, and “the word was God,” I am Rebecca. Duh. Yeah. You see, he’s supernatural, folks, we can’t limit him to our human thinking. Jesus is God, Jesus is the Son of God, Jesus is the Lamb of God, he is everything. Now look, “and the word became” what? Flesh, “and dwelt among us.” Okay, this is how Jesus was created at the very beginning, before anything else, before the foundation of the earth was laid, before the sun, the light, the moon, the stars, and all the rest, God said, “I’m going to have to go and dwell in the flesh and die for the world if they make the wrong choice.” That was his first, that’s his plan. People say he had a plan A and then he made a mistake and he got a plan B.
How does he explain “the beginning of the creation of God”? (Revelation 3:14, John 1:1)

Revelation 3:14: “And to the angel of the church of the Laodiceans write, ‘These things says the Amen, the Faithful and True Witness, the Beginning of the creation of God: John 1:1: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. John 1:14: And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld His glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth.
What does he say about Jesus being foreordained before the world began? (Revelation 13:8, Titus 1:2, 1 Peter 1:18–20)

He says “God don’t make mistakes. He had one plan, plan A,” and that “when God speaks something, it’s as good as what? Done.” He cites Revelation 13:8, the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world, and says “this was God’s creation to save the world from sin.”
What does he say about Jesus being foreordained before the world began? (Revelation 13:8, Titus 1:2, 1 Peter 1:18–20)

God don’t make mistakes. He had one plan, plan A. They could have ate of the tree of life and live forever and still replenish the earth and so forth, but they made the wrong choice, and God prepared for that, and so when Jesus came 4,000 years later and was birthed, then that creation happened, when he was created in that womb, birthed in that flesh, then that he is the first. He was, it was done before anything else, and then it was fulfilled, do you get that? And I’m going to show it to you again, you see, when God speaks something, it’s as good as what? Done. Now, Revelations 13:8, “the Lamb slain from the” what? Foundation of the world. But he wasn’t slain until when? 4,000 years later. Yes, but God said this is what’s going to happen, he created Jesus to come in the flesh and die on the cross before anything else, and he was God, but it did not take place till he came in the flesh and dwelt amongst us. Do you see that? Do you? Hallelujah. Okay, Titus 1:2: “He gave us the hope of eternal life, which God, that cannot lie, promised before the world began.” When did we have eternal life? Before the world began. See, it was in his plan, and we can appropriate it today. Why? Because he ordained it before the world began. See, he ordained Jesus to come in the flesh and die before the world began, the first of the creation, the first in his plan, with Jesus dying, his blood was shed before the world, before the foundation of the world was laid, before “let there be light,” before there was water covering the earth, Jesus was destined to die. Do you get it, church? And that’s why it has to happen. 1 Peter 1:18: “We are redeemed with the precious blood of Christ as a lamb without blemish and without spot, who truly was foreordained,” determined beforehand, “before the foundation of the world.” Amen. See, that’s why he was the first of creation. It wasn’t that he was a created, a new being, this was God’s creation to save the world from sin. That was his first act. Aren’t you glad of that? Aren’t you glad that he had a plan already prepared if we made a wrong choice? Hallelujah.
What does he say about Jesus being foreordained before the world began? (Revelation 13:8, Titus 1:2, 1 Peter 1:18–20)

Genesis 3:22: Then the LORD God said, “Behold, the man has become like one of Us, to know good and evil. And now, lest he put out his hand and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever”— Revelation 13:8: All who dwell on the earth will worship him, whose names have not been written in the Book of Life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world. Titus 1:2: in hope of eternal life which God, who cannot lie, promised before time began, 1 Peter 1:18-20: knowing that you were not redeemed with corruptible things, like silver or gold, from your aimless conduct received by tradition from your fathers, but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot. He indeed was foreordained before the foundation of the world, but was manifest in these last times for you
What does he say about the throne room? (Revelation 4:1–8)

He reads “a door standing open in heaven” and “come up here, and I will show you things which must take place after this,” and says the “seven lamps of fire burning before the throne… are the seven spirits of God.” He says “an elder is an overseer in the church,” and that angels “don’t have wings,” adding “we believe that because it’s been passed on for generations.”
What does he say about the throne room? (Revelation 4:1–8)

Yes, slain before the foundation of the world, the first of the creation of God. That’s why he can be eternal and yet the first of creation. Now we go to Revelations 4:1-8: “After these things,” after the seven churches, in the seven attributes of Jesus Christ, “I looked, and behold, a door standing open in heaven, and the first voice which I heard was like a trumpet speaking with me, saying, ‘Come up here, and I will show you things which must take place after this.’” After what? The seven churches, the seven attributes of Christ. “Immediately I was in the Spirit, and behold, a throne set in heaven, and one sat on the throne.” And here’s a picture of all this, and, uh, we got the elders sitting around the throne, we got the four beasts here with a cow head and a lion head and a human head and so forth. Here’s the elders on both sides with their little crowns, just thinking how great they are, man. Hallelujah, they arrived. Then you got all these angels, and look at that throne, the lightning bolts coming out of it. “And he who sat on the throne was like a jasper,” that’s the upper left-hand corner, it’s a couple of jasper stones I put up there, “and a sardius stone in appearance,” sardius is over on your right, and of course the light and the lightning bolts block out this image in this illustration. Uh, “and there was a rainbow around the throne, in appearance like an emerald.” It’s a wonder the church don’t have emerald in the church, you know, we always make idols out of everything, I’m surprised we haven’t brought in the emerald thing yet. “Around the throne were 24 elders sitting on their thrones, clothed in white robes, and they had crowns of gold on their heads.” They’re feeling pretty good right now. “And from the throne proceeded lightnings.” An elder is an overseer in the church, like the Sanhedrin and Jews and so forth. “Before the throne, or from the throne, proceeded lightnings, thunderings, and voices.” We sing about it this morning in the revelation song. “Seven lamps of fire burning before the throne, which are the seven spirits of God. And before the throne was a sea of glass, and in the midst of the throne and around the throne were four living creatures full of eyes in front and back. The first had a head of a lion, the second like a calf, the third the face of a man, and the fourth was like a flying eagle. And the four living creatures each having six wings, full of eyes round about within.” Now, see, the seraphim, the creatures, the cherubims, have wings, but angels, what? Don’t have wings. Hallelujah. But we believe that because it’s been passed on for generations.
What does he say about the throne room? (Revelation 4:1–8)

Revelation 4:1-8: After these things I looked, and behold, a door standing open in heaven. And the first voice which I heard was like a trumpet speaking with me, saying, “Come up here, and I will show you things which must take place after this.” Immediately I was in the Spirit; and behold, a throne set in heaven, and One sat on the throne. And He who sat there was like a jasper and a sardius stone in appearance; and there was a rainbow around the throne, in appearance like an emerald. Around the throne were twenty-four thrones, and on the thrones I saw twenty-four elders sitting, clothed in white robes; and they had crowns of gold on their heads. And from the throne proceeded lightnings, thunderings, and voices. Seven lamps of fire were burning before the throne, which are the seven Spirits of God. Before the throne there was a sea of glass, like crystal. And in the midst of the throne, and around the throne, were four living creatures full of eyes in front and in back. The first living creature was like a lion, the second living creature like a calf, the third living creature had a face like a man, and the fourth living creature was like a flying eagle. The four living creatures, each having six wings, were full of eyes around and within. And they do not rest day or night, saying: “Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, Who was and is and is to come!” Revelation 4:1: After these things I looked, and behold, a door standing open in heaven. And the first voice which I heard was like a trumpet speaking with me, saying, “Come up here, and I will show you things which must take place after this.”
Why does he say Jesus is real deity?
He says “nobody could kill him. He had to give up his life, and he picked it back up again, that takes deity.”
What does he say the sword of the Spirit is?
He says it is “the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God,” and that the word “will separate your fleshly things from your spiritual things.”
What does he say sets a believer free?
He says “that word is what sets you free,” and tells listeners to “get into the word on that problem.”
Does he say prayer alone sets you free?
No. He says “prayer will bring you in tune with God, and he will tell you what to do, and then you have to respond to the word.”
Does he say believers can become God?
No. He says “we never will be creators, we will never be God, but we will take on his nature.”
What does he say about tongues as the initial sign?
He says the Holy Ghost “has got a lot more to it than tongues, and greater things than tongues,” and that he would “rather have that part of the Spirit than tongues, and I speak in tongues.”
How does he describe the wisdom from above?
He says it is “first pure, then peaceable,” and tells hearers to ask for it because God “will give it liberally.”
He says a tractor “without the attachments it’s worthless,” and that “the Christians have got the tractor and they don’t have the attachments.”
What does he say the key of David means?
He says Jesus “came of the root and offspring of David,” which is “how we know he’s the real Messiah,” and that “he is the key to the building of the church.”
Does he say Jesus can return at any minute?
No. He says “he’s not coming back until it’s fulfilled,” and that “Jesus has a lot of things to do.”
Does he say Jesus was created?
He reads “the beginning of the creation of God,” and says Jesus is “the start, the first,” and yet “he’s eternal, he was, he is, and he will be.”
Does he say God had a plan B?
No. He says “God don’t make mistakes. He had one plan, plan A.”
What does he say about angels having wings?
He says the seraphim, the creatures and the cherubims “have wings, but angels, what? Don’t have wings,” and “we believe that because it’s been passed on for generations.”

items.d: In this third lesson, Pastor David G. Kincer continues through Revelation 4 and 5: the elders bowing before the throne, the sealed scroll that only the Lamb is worthy to open, and the heavenly worship of Jesus…
p: In this third lesson, Pastor David G. Kincer continues through Revelation 4 and 5: the elders bowing before the throne, the sealed scroll that only the Lamb is worthy to open, and the heavenly worship of Jesus Christ. He teaches that believers are made kings and priests to rule over sin, that praise reminds us who God is, and that the sevens of Revelation point to what is coming.
What does he say is happening in heaven around the throne? (Revelation 4:8–11)

He says the elders fall down and cast their crowns because “he is the king. He’s the crown of crowns,” and “you’re getting a picture of” what goes on in heaven. He says “America refuses to bow before the king.”
What does he say is happening in heaven around the throne? (Revelation 4:8–11)

And they cry, they saying, “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God Almighty, who was and is to come.” And whenever the living creatures give glory and honor and thanks to him that sits on the throne, who lives forever and ever, the [unclear] elders fall down on their face, casting their crowns, ‘cause he is the king. He’s the crown of crowns. Anything you got is really unworthy of what he’s done. So here they are bowing. So you want to know what’s going on in heaven? You’re getting a picture of it. And yet America refuses to bow before the king. Refuses to worship and sing “Holy, holy, holy.” Then these elders sing, “You are worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honor and power, for you have created all things, and for your pleasure they are and were created. Thou art worthy. Thou art worthy. Thou art worthy, oh Lord, to receive glory, glory and honor, glory and honor and power.” Remember them songs, [unclear]? You remember that song right out of, I loved it. That’s why I went to Living Faith. They sing out of the scriptures. The scriptures are powerful. “For thou hast created, hast all things created.
What does he say is happening in heaven around the throne? (Revelation 4:8–11)

Revelation 4:8: The four living creatures, each having six wings, were full of eyes around and within. And they do not rest day or night, saying: “Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, Who was and is and is to come!” Revelation 4:10-11: the twenty-four elders fall down before Him who sits on the throne and worship Him who lives forever and ever, and cast their crowns before the throne, saying: “You are worthy, O Lord, To receive glory and honor and power; For You created all things, And by Your will they exist and were created.”
What does he say about creation “for thy pleasure”? (Revelation 4:11)

He says that when the scripture was opened to him, “evolution is out. This thing didn’t happen by accident,” and “God created this whole thing for his pleasure.” He says “he wants to fill heaven with people that love him.”
What does he say about creation “for thy pleasure”? (Revelation 4:11)

For thou hast created all things.” And here’s the reason: “And for thy pleasure they are created,” for thou art worthy, oh Lord. Man, when I learned that song and I, that scripture was opened up to me, evolution is out. This thing didn’t happen by accident. God created this whole thing for his pleasure. He wants to fill heaven with people that love him, and he did everything to get them there. Hallelujah. He did all this thing for him, not for you. And he wants me to be a part of eternity. Man, that’s exciting. Isn’t that a beautiful song when you sing the scriptures?
What does he say about creation “for thy pleasure”? (Revelation 4:11)
Revelation 4:11: “You are worthy, O Lord, To receive glory and honor and power; For You created all things, And by Your will they exist and were created.”
What does he say the sealed scroll shows about messengers? (Revelation 5:1–4)

He explains that “a seal, young people, was just a wax thing that was melted and put on a book,” and that “the messenger who took it could open it, but he wasn’t what? Worthy.” He says “we are messengers. Only Jesus can open the book to people.”
What does he say the sealed scroll shows about messengers? (Revelation 5:1–4)

Whoa. “I saw in the right hand of him that sat on the throne a scroll written inside and out, sealed with seven seals.” See, there’s that scroll. Now, a seal, young people, was just a wax thing that was melted and put on a book and had the symbol of the one who sent the message. And no one could open it but the one, the one who sent the message gave authority to open it. You understand that it wasn’t locks on there, you know, wasn’t chains. It was just a seal. Anybody could open it. The messenger who took it could open it, but he wasn’t what? Worthy. He didn’t have the authority. The messenger, and that’s what pastors and priests and ministers got to understand. We are messengers. Only Jesus can open the book to people. Only Jesus can open their understanding. Only Jesus can do this stuff. Amen. That’s good. So, we see the one on the throne and we see that sardius and jasper, an emerald rainbow there, and another artist’s drawing of it. “Then I saw a strong [unclear] proclaiming with a loud voice, ‘Who is worthy to open the scroll and to loose its seals?’ And no one in heaven or on earth or under the earth was able to open the scroll or to look at it. So I wept much because no one was found worthy to open and read the scroll or to look in it.”
What does he say the sealed scroll shows about messengers? (Revelation 5:1–4)

Revelation 5:1: And I saw in the right hand of Him who sat on the throne a scroll written inside and on the back, sealed with seven seals. Revelation 5:2-4: Then I saw a strong angel proclaiming with a loud voice, “Who is worthy to open the scroll and to loose its seals?” And no one in heaven or on the earth or under the earth was able to open the scroll, or to look at it. So I wept much, because no one was found worthy to open and read the scroll, or to look at it.
What does he say about the Lion and the Lamb who open the scroll? (Revelation 5:5–10)

He reads “the lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, has prevailed to open the scroll,” and “a lamb as though it had been slain, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God.” He says “if they’re worshiping in heaven, don’t you think we ought to get warmed up here on earth?”
What does he say about the Lion and the Lamb who open the scroll? (Revelation 5:5–10)

“But one of the elders,” hey, hallelujah, the elders are coming through here, “one of the elders said to me, ‘Don’t weep. The lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, has prevailed to open the scroll and to loose its seven seals.’” So, we got a scroll with seven seals. We got a lamb slain that was worthy to open the scroll. “And then I looked, and in the midst of the throne, the four living creatures, and in the midst of the elders stood a lamb as though it had been slain, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God.” He keeps talking about these seven spirits of God. “And he came and took the scroll out of the right hand of him who sat on the throne. And when he had taken the scroll, the four living creatures and the 24 elders fell down before the lamb. Here they are again, each having a harp and golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints. And they sang a new song, saying, ‘You are worthy to take the scroll and to open its seals. For you were slain and have redeemed us to God by your blood, out of every tribe, tongue, people, and nation.’” Hallelujah. If they’re worshiping in heaven, don’t you think we ought to get warmed up here on earth? If elders, leaders are bowing before him in heaven and casting their rewards before him, don’t you think we need to start now? Am I talking to the wrong people?
What does he say about the Lion and the Lamb who open the scroll? (Revelation 5:5–10)

Revelation 5:5-6: But one of the elders said to me, “Do not weep. Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has prevailed to open the scroll and to loose its seven seals.” And I looked, and behold, in the midst of the throne and of the four living creatures, and in the midst of the elders, stood a Lamb as though it had been slain, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven Spirits of God sent out into all the earth. Revelation 5:8-10: Now when He had taken the scroll, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb, each having a harp, and golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints. And they sang a new song, saying: “You are worthy to take the scroll, And to open its seals; For You were slain, And have redeemed us to God by Your blood Out of every tribe and tongue and people and nation, And have made us kings and priests to our God; And we shall reign on the earth.”
What does he say believers were made to do? (Revelation 5:10, Ephesians 2:8–9)

He says “I was made by Jesus to rule and reign here on earth over the kingdom of darkness, over sin. That is his objective.” He adds “you got to pursue Christ and he will work these things in you,” and asks “how many want to rule over sex and drugs and sin and alcohol.”
What does he say believers were made to do? (Revelation 5:10, Ephesians 2:8–9)

But see, we’ve been taught to come and let the preacher do everything for us, or the priest, or whatever. But we are to come and be partakers of these things. And look at this: “You have made us” what? “Kings and priests to reign” where? “To reign” where? See, drugs don’t get me down. Alcohol doesn’t get me down. Sexual permissive does. Why? I was made by Jesus not to be just a fisher of men. Not to be just a believer. Not just to be a person of faith. I was made by Jesus to rule and reign here on earth over the kingdom of darkness, over sin. That is his objective. Are you with me, church? But you see, when we get bombarded, well, we’re saved by grace through faith and not of works, lest any man should boast. We don’t, we, we, we just get, uh, uh, pleased with where we’re at. “I don’t have to do nothing.” Yes, you got to pursue Christ and he will work these things in you. Amen. How many want to rule over sex and drugs and sin and alcohol and all that stuff that destroys homes and families and lives? Amen. Yes, Jesus promised to make you a ruler. Alcoholics Anonymous, they got some kind of, you know, uh, what do they call that? What? Higher power. Higher power. Listen, don’t call Jesus a higher power. Call him who he is: Jesus Christ. Amen. He’s the one that has the power to cause you to be a ruler here on earth.
What does he say believers were made to do? (Revelation 5:10, Ephesians 2:8–9)

Revelation 5:10: And have made us kings and priests to our God; And we shall reign on the earth.” Ephesians 2:8-9: For by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, lest anyone should boast.
What does he say about calling Jesus a “higher power”? (Matthew 28:18)

He says “don’t call Jesus a higher power. Call him who he is: Jesus Christ,” because “all authority in heaven and earth been given unto who? Jesus Christ.” He says people “will go to counseling and seven-step procedures and 12-step procedures… and won’t go to Jesus and his word.”
What does he say about calling Jesus a “higher power”? (Matthew 28:18)

Yes. Amen. That’s your promise, church. But if we don’t know it and we don’t pursue it and we don’t ask for it, we never possess it. Hallelujah. Yeah. We don’t have to call him a higher power though. Baby steps. Jesus is the only high power. That’s what the Bible says. All authority in heaven and earth been given unto who? Jesus Christ. I can’t call a higher power something else. I got to call it what it is: Jesus Christ. And so I need to go to Jesus, and I need to worship him, and I need to seek him, and I need to get in the book, and he will what? Set me free and bring to pass these things he promised in me. And who gets the credit? Jesus. Hallelujah. And it works. And it amazes me how people will go to counseling and seven-step procedures and 12-step procedures and all the rest and won’t go to Jesus and his word. They’ll give those groups years to help them and they won’t give Jesus one week. They try it for one day and, well, nothing happened. Are you with me? Hallelujah. Now, how many ready to be a ruler on earth? Now, you can overcome. I don’t care where you’re at in your sins and your play. I’m telling you, Jesus promised this.
What does he say about calling Jesus a “higher power”? (Matthew 28:18)
Matthew 28:18: And Jesus came and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to Me in heaven and on earth.
Who does he say is praised in heaven? (Revelation 5:11–13)

He reads “worthy is the lamb who was slain to receive power and riches and wisdom and strength and glory and honor and blessing,” and says that in heaven it is Jesus Christ who is honored, not any founder or religious leader. He says “remember, the book of Revelations is the revelation of Jesus Christ.”
Who does he say is praised in heaven? (Revelation 5:11–13)

It worked in my life. It worked in a slew of others that I grew up with, and they’re here today and still serving God. And it will work for you. And his name is Jesus, and the book is the Bible. Hallelujah. This stuff works. Now, he goes on to say, uh, I think I just passed up something. “Then I looked and heard the voice of many angels around the throne, the living creatures, and the elders. And the number of them was 10,000 times 10 thousands and thousands of thousands.” In other words, over a 100 million angels are up there. Plus “saying with a loud voice, ‘Worthy is the lamb who was slain to receive power and riches and wisdom and strength and glory and honor and blessing.’” You notice it’s not Allah. It’s not Muhammad. It’s not Joseph Smith. They’re up there honoring. Who is it? Jesus Christ. Is not Mary Baker Eddy or any Pope Benedict or a pope of any kind or Billy Graham or some evangelist in a Protestant church. It is Jesus Christ. And folks, if it is Jesus Christ in the eternities, then we need to start what? Worshiping him, seeking him and acknowledging him now. Amen. Remember, the book of Revelations is the revelation of Jesus Christ. Hallelujah. Verse 13: “Every creature which is in heaven and on the earth and under the earth, and such as in the sea, and all that is in them, I heard saying, ‘Blessing and honor and glory and power be to him who sits on the throne and to the Lamb forever and ever.’ And the four living creatures said, ‘Amen.’ And the elders said, ‘Amen.’ And bowed down again and worshiped him.”
Who does he say is praised in heaven? (Revelation 5:11–13)

Revelation 5:11-12: Then I looked, and I heard the voice of many angels around the throne, the living creatures, and the elders; and the number of them was ten thousand times ten thousand, and thousands of thousands, saying with a loud voice: “Worthy is the Lamb who was slain To receive power and riches and wisdom, And strength and honor and glory and blessing!” Revelation 5:13: And every creature which is in heaven and on the earth and under the earth and such as are in the sea, and all that are in them, I heard saying: “Blessing and honor and glory and power Be to Him who sits on the throne, And to the Lamb, forever and ever!”
Why does he say bowing and worship matter now?

He says “up there, the very power of his presence is going to put you on your face,” and that God uses bowing because “in the world, in the earth, subpowers always bow to the higher power.” He says of bowing, “it’s not unhealthy… your spirit is going to be strengthened.”
Why does he say bowing and worship matter now?

Man, they’re just up and down. That’s one thing I like about the Catholic Church. They bow a lot. And Protestants could use some of that. They get on their knees and it’s scriptural. So now it’s not just the elders, but everyone on earth, under the earth, are dead people up there. We’re all going to be what? Worshiping him. And you’re not going to say, “Well, I didn’t grow up that way. Well, I was timid. I, I can’t do this. I’m [unclear].” No. Up there, the very power of his presence is going to put you on your face. And why does, why does the Bible give us the bowing thing? Because in the world, in the earth, subpowers always bow to the higher power. When people would go into a natural king, they would what? Bow. A given recognition that you are a higher power than I am. And so God used it. He speaks to us in natural things so we can understand spiritual things. And does it hurt us to humble ourselves and bow and lift up our voice? No, it doesn’t do anything. It’s not unhealthy. You’re not going to have a heart attack. You know, uh, it’s not going to affect you in any way except your spirit is going to be strengthened. See, he chose the humble way. We humble ourselves and do these things. See, you want to, this is a little picture of what you’ve been doing in heaven. This is not the total picture, but there’s a little glimpse. There’s more. Remember, Jesus didn’t make us just fishers of men. Not just believers, not just people of faith, but kings and priests to rule on earth, to rule over the kingdom of darkness, to rule over Satan and Satan’s children who follow evil.
Why does he say bowing and worship matter now?
Revelation 5:14: Then the four living creatures said, “Amen!” And the twenty-four elders fell down and worshiped Him who lives forever and ever.
Does he say God needs to be told how great he is?

He says “he don’t want to be told. He already knows who he is,” and “you’re not telling God anything.” He says “he ordained praise and worship for you to give to him so you are reminded who he is,” and “then your faith is built up to possess the things that he told you you could have.”
Does he say God needs to be told how great he is?

Even family members who want to lead us astray. You see, now let me explain. Some people say, “Well, what kind of God is up there with a big ego? He wants to be told how great he is.” He don’t want to be told. He already knows who he is. You’re not telling God anything. Get off your hobby horse. But you see, you need to remember who he is. See, this is what affects your thinking. This is what affects your spirit. You need to remember who he is. And so he ordained praise and worship for you to give to him so you are reminded who he is. And then your faith is built up to possess the things that he told you you could have. Does that make sense? And it brings his presence. He comes and touches us and refreshes us in that, and we get our mind changed and we get our spirit refreshed when we worship and praise and seek the Lord our God. That make sense? Yeah. He’s not up there wanting, “Come on, praise me. Come on, praise.” No. Ministers like that. Preachers like people to slap him on the back and say, “What a good message.” [unclear]. “Oh man, what, what a man you are, a woman you are.” No, no, no. Jesus is in my, he already knows who he is. He doesn’t have to be told. But you need to know. See, I can’t get into praise and say anything bad about Jesus. When I start lifting up his name, I have to start saying, “Lord, you’re the creator of the world.
How does he describe praise changing a believer’s day? (Matthew 1:23, 1 Corinthians 6:19, Romans 8:31)

He says “I’m not telling him anything he doesn’t know. I’m reminding myself of what I need to know. And then my faith rises. And then my mind gets changed.” He says “I have an empowerment in me to say no,” and “he’s Emmanuel. He’s God with us.”
How does he describe praise changing a believer’s day? (Matthew 1:23, 1 Corinthians 6:19, Romans 8:31)

You are God. There is no one but you. You died to save the world from sin.” See, I’m remembering who I am now. “You rose again to give us life.” Now I’m remembering I’m to live in life, newness of life. “You ascended [unclear] the heavens and you poured out your spirit back on your church. You are the wise God. Wisdom is in you. Knowledge is in you. You’re the all powerful and the all authority. You have authority over all the earth. All the principalities and powers of darkness.” See, then what am I doing? I’m not telling him anything he doesn’t know. I’m reminding myself of what I need to know. And then my faith rises. And then my mind gets changed. And when I go through the day, I make decisions. Why? Because I’ve been empowered by that praise and worship that I gave to him. And remember who he is. And I can say no to drugs and no to sexual immorality and no to alcoholism and no to these things that are bad. No to gangs. I have an empowerment in me to say no. Amen. And his name is Jesus. That’s why praise and worship is so powerful. You see, he’s Emmanuel. He’s God with us. I’m not looking to heaven. He’s in me. I’m the temple of God. Jesus is right here with me. And “if God [unclear] me,” the Bible says what? Who can stand against me? God is with me. He’s on my side, man. It says in Psalms, he doesn’t remember the sins of our youth.
How does he describe praise changing a believer’s day? (Matthew 1:23, 1 Corinthians 6:19, Romans 8:31)
