Matthew 1:23: “Behold, the virgin shall be with child, and bear a Son, and they shall call His name Immanuel,” which is translated, “God with us.” 1 Corinthians 6:19: Or do you not know that your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God, and you are not your own? Romans 8:31: What then shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?
What does he say about the past and about boasting? (Psalm 25:7, 2 Corinthians 5:17)

He says “the blood of Jesus healed my past. He does not remember the sins of my youth,” and “I’m a new creature.” He says “praise means to boast about,” and that “even if I attain something in God, I have to recognize it was him who did it.”
What does he say about the past and about boasting? (Psalm 25:7, 2 Corinthians 5:17)

I don’t have to go back to the past and try to get cleansed of some kind of stupid healing thing that they have. The blood of Jesus healed my past. He does not remember the sins of my youth. Don’t talk about my past. It’s dead. I’m a new creature. Are you with me? See, this is what praise: praise means to boast about. You can’t boast about yourself. The Bible says if you boast of yourself, your boasting is wrong. Let others boast of you. And there’s nothing in me to boast about. You’ve seen these elders casting their crowns before him. Even if I attain something in God, I have to recognize it was him who did it. And just give it back. Amen. Are you with me? Now, isn’t that powerful?
What does he say about the past and about boasting? (Psalm 25:7, 2 Corinthians 5:17)

Psalm 25:7: Do not remember the sins of my youth, nor my transgressions; According to Your mercy remember me, For Your goodness’ sake, O LORD. 2 Corinthians 5:17: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new. Proverbs 27:2: Let another man praise you, and not your own mouth; A stranger, and not your own lips.
What does he say about seeking Jesus instead of paying for counseling? (Matthew 7:7)

He says “this is not a religion. This is a reality. Jesus is real,” and that people “will pay 50 bucks an hour for counseling from some psychologist and won’t get on their knees for that half hour with the Bible.” He says “I started at age 20 and haven’t stopped yet. I never backslid, never had a nervous breakdown.”
What does he say about seeking Jesus instead of paying for counseling? (Matthew 7:7)

And this is the Jesus that we have. There’s no other religion on earth that promises you these things, folks, because they’re man-made religions. This is not a religion. This is a reality. Jesus is real. And the Bible says if you will seek and keep seeking and ask and keep asking and knock and keep knocking. I am just amazed at how people will pay 50 bucks an hour for counseling from some psychologist and won’t get on their knees for that half hour with the Bible and seek him who has the power to change their thinking, to change their emotions, to change their spirit. I’m just shocked, and it worked for me.
What does he say about seeking Jesus instead of paying for counseling? (Matthew 7:7)
Matthew 7:7: “Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
What does he say about church splits and Christ being formed in us? (Galatians 4:19, Luke 1:45)

He says he “didn’t fall apart when the church split because it wasn’t my church. It’s his church.” He says “Christ is still wanting to form himself in his church,” and that Jesus “come to give us a sound mind, strong emotions, a strong spirit.”
What does he say about church splits and Christ being formed in us? (Galatians 4:19, Luke 1:45)

I started at age 20 and haven’t stopped yet. I never backslid, never had a nervous breakdown. I didn’t fall apart when the church split because it wasn’t my church. It’s his church. If people want to leave Christ in his church, then Christ can deal with them. It’s not my problem. Are you out there? But shouldn’t you feel bad? No. It’s not my church. It’s not my problem. If people want to go, I say bye. I go on following Christ. Isn’t that what Jesus said to do? Just keep following him. Isn’t it shocking in America that people are going from church to church and can’t handle the least adversity and flaw in a church, and we’ve been offered this Jesus who is so powerful and so great. Are you with me? Don’t you think it’s time that we go God like Mary of old: “Let there be a performance of that which was spoken.” You know she birthed Jesus, and the Bible says, Paul says, we travail in Christ, we travail again that Christ would be formed in you. See it, we, Christ is still wanting to form himself in his church. And Christians have mental breakdowns and mental problems and emotional problems when Jesus did not come to leave us in that condition. And he come to give us a sound mind, strong emotions, a strong spirit. And so don’t give up on yourself. Yes, you’ve made mistakes in the past, but the Bible says he won’t remember the sins of your youth.
What does he say about church splits and Christ being formed in us? (Galatians 4:19, Luke 1:45)

Luke 1:45: Blessed is she who believed, for there will be a fulfillment of those things which were told her from the Lord.” Galatians 4:19: My little children, for whom I labor in birth again until Christ is formed in you,
What does he say about the sevens in Revelation and “7777”?

He says “let the blood shut the door,” and “give God some time. He can’t lie. He has to do what he said he would do.” He closes by listing seven churches, seven candlesticks, seven spirits and more, and says “that’s what’s coming. 7777, not 666.”
What does he say about the sevens in Revelation and “7777”?

Let the blood shut the door. They’re done. If you’ve asked for repentance, it’s done. You’re a new creature. Let’s start a fresh and a new and give God time to work his image and his inheritance in you. Now, that’s a good place for an amen. Give God some time. He can’t lie. He has to do what he said he would do. Seven churches, seven candlesticks, seven spirits, seven lamps, seven horns, seven eyes, seven stars, seven messengers, seven angels, seven seals, seven trumpets, seven thunders, seven plagues. That’s what’s coming. 7777, not 666.
Why does he say the elders cast their crowns?
He says it is because “he is the king. He’s the crown of crowns,” and that “anything you got is really unworthy of what he’s done.”
What does he say about evolution?
He says “evolution is out. This thing didn’t happen by accident.”
What does he say a seal was?
He says “a seal, young people, was just a wax thing that was melted and put on a book and had the symbol of the one who sent the message.”
Who does he say is worthy to open the scroll?
He reads that “the lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, has prevailed to open the scroll and to loose its seven seals,” and that a lamb “was worthy to open the scroll.”
What does he say believers were made to do?
He says “I was made by Jesus to rule and reign here on earth over the kingdom of darkness, over sin.”
Does he say Jesus should be called a “higher power”?
No. He says “don’t call Jesus a higher power. Call him who he is: Jesus Christ.”
What does he say about counseling and step programs?
He says “it amazes me how people will go to counseling and seven-step procedures and 12-step procedures and all the rest and won’t go to Jesus and his word.”
Who does he say is honored in heaven?
He says it is Jesus Christ, and “remember, the book of Revelations is the revelation of Jesus Christ.”
Why does he say the Bible gives us bowing?
He says “in the world, in the earth, subpowers always bow to the higher power,” and “he speaks to us in natural things so we can understand spiritual things.”
Does he say God needs praise to feel great?
No. He says “he don’t want to be told. He already knows who he is,” but “you need to remember who he is.”
Does he say God remembers the sins of our youth?
No. He says “he does not remember the sins of my youth,” and “the blood of Jesus healed my past.”
How does he say he handled a church split?
He says “I didn’t fall apart when the church split because it wasn’t my church. It’s his church,” and “I go on following Christ.”
What does he mean by “7777, not 666”?
After listing the sevens of Revelation, including seven seals, seven trumpets, seven thunders and seven plagues, he says “that’s what’s coming. 7777, not 666.”

items.t: Prelude to the Last Seven Plagues
items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Revelation 15 that the seven last plagues come out of the temple in heaven, and that the people on the sea of glass conquered the beast. He contrasts the…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Revelation 15 that the seven last plagues come out of the temple in heaven, and that the people on the sea of glass conquered the beast. He contrasts the song of Moses with the song of the Lamb and says Jesus is interceding for believers.
What are the seven last plagues, and where do the angels come from? (Revelation 15:1)

He says Revelation 15:1 shows seven angels with the seven last plagues, “filled with God’s wrath, God’s anger, God’s punishment,” coming out of the temple in heaven. He says it is important to understand “there is a temple in heaven,” and the earthly temples were given so we could understand how the heavenly one works.
What are the seven last plagues, and where do the angels come from? (Revelation 15:1)

In Revelation 15:1: “I saw another sign in heaven, great and marvelous: seven angels having the seven last plagues, for in them the wrath of God is complete.” And so all the other things before are also plagues. These are the seven last plagues, and, uh, he says there are seven angels with seven bowls of the seven last plagues, filled with God’s wrath, God’s anger, God’s punishment. So we have a nice little picture there for you to see, these angels coming out of the temple in heaven with the seven last plagues. It’s important for us to understand they’re coming out of the temple in heaven. It’s important for you to understand that there is a temple in heaven, and the natural temples that God gave us on earth was just so we could understand how the heavenly temple works. Are you with me? You know, we don’t want to worship natural temples like the Jews wound up doing. Uh, the temple that God gave them, He only gave them to show them how the heavenly temple worked, and even today we got to be careful of not getting so into a natural building.
What are the seven last plagues, and where do the angels come from? (Revelation 15:1)
Revelation 15:1: Then I saw another sign in heaven, great and marvelous: seven angels having the seven last plagues, for in them the wrath of God is complete.
Why does he say the earthly temple was only a shadow of the heavenly one? (Hebrews 8:4-5, 9:23)

He says the Old Testament priests, sacrifices and rituals were “an example of the end result,” serving “unto the example and shadow of heavenly things,” and the natural sacrifices “pointed to the real sacrifice, Jesus Christ.” He says we should not get so wrapped up in natural things, and that “we need to come out to see Jesus glorified.”
Why does he say the earthly temple was only a shadow of the heavenly one? (Hebrews 8:4-5, 9:23)

The way we like it and so forth, and getting away from the fact that there is a spiritual temple in heaven, and that is the pattern to follow. Are you with me? Uh, I want to give you some Scriptures on that, if I can. Here it says in Hebrews chapter 8:4, “the earthly priests offer gifts, who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things.” See, God never intended for those priests in the Old Testament, uh, and the sacrifices and the rituals they went through, to be the end result. They were an example of the end result. And that’s why the Catholic Church today, you know, they beautified a dead pope. You don’t beautify dead popes or dead people. That stuff is nonsense. What we need is to hear from God and meet with God. Can I hear an amen? Amen. And over a million people come out to see some dead person beautified. Listen, we need to come out to see Jesus glorified. Isn’t that true? Isn’t that what the Bible’s all about? Uh, you know, we get so wrapped up (and I’m not just picking on the Catholic Church, they were doing something this weekend along with the royalty and all this junk that we get into). What we need to do is just humble ourself and touch God. Could that be true? Yeah. Not get distracted. He says all these things “serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things.” See, that heavenly temple. Hebrews 9:23: “the patterns of heavenly things should be purified with these,” animal bloods, “but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than” God gave for the natural temple. And the natural sacrifices pointed to the real sacrifice, Jesus Christ. Amen. And that’s why they’re there. That’s when I go to third world countries and they’re still offering animals and shedding blood, I go, “Whoa, you guys are missing this thing that was only an example.” And, uh, the normal churches wouldn’t have anything to do with these churches. Well, how you going to help them if you won’t have anything to do with them? You know, they’re ignorantly still, you know, slicing animals’ throats and shedding blood, thinking they’re doing God a favor, and they don’t get that that was just an example of Christ’s coming and dying on the cross, and now we don’t do that anymore.
Why does he say the earthly temple was only a shadow of the heavenly one? (Hebrews 8:4-5, 9:23)

Hebrews 8:4-5: For if He were on earth, He would not be a priest, since there are priests who offer the gifts according to the law; who serve the copy and shadow of the heavenly things, as Moses was divinely instructed when he was about to make the tabernacle. For He said, “See that you make all things according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.” Hebrews 9:23: Therefore it was necessary that the copies of the things in the heavens should be purified with these, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
What is Jesus doing in the heavenly temple for us? (Hebrews 9:24)

He says Jesus “is up there right now interceding and mediating for you personally,” and that this is why he can “get up in the morning with confidence.” He says it is nice that we pray for one another, but “when Jesus goes to the Father, the Father hears,” so you go to Jesus.
What is Jesus doing in the heavenly temple for us? (Hebrews 9:24)

“For Christ has not entered the holy places made with hands,” that natural Jewish temple, “which are the figures of the true,” the true temple, where? In heaven. Okay. “But into heaven itself, Christ ascended, into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us.” See, Jesus is up there right now, interceding and mediating for you personally, you, me. See, that’s why I can get up in the morning with confidence. I have someone in the heavenly temple saying, “God, he believes in me. Father, he believes in me, you know, he’s pursuing me. You’ve got to be merciful, you’ve got to strengthen him, you’ve got to help this boy.” Hallelujah. I mean, Him up there praying for me and interceding for me is the big difference in you praying for me. Amen. You know, it’s nice that we pray one for another, but I tell you, when Jesus goes to the Father, the Father hears. And, I, you know, Mary is another thing. You don’t go to Mary, you don’t go to, uh, Joseph Smith, and none of these distractions. You go to Jesus. Why? He’s in the temple of God in heaven interceding, talking to God for you. Amen. Hallelujah. That’s powerful. So do we, we don’t want to get distracted. We got to understand there is a temple in heaven. Now it goes on to say that in this sea of glass.
What is Jesus doing in the heavenly temple for us? (Hebrews 9:24)
Hebrews 9:24: For Christ has not entered the holy places made with hands, which are copies of the true, but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us;
Who stands on the sea of glass and conquers the beast? (Revelation 15:2)

He says there is “a group of people that got victory over the beast,” and “the beast didn’t conquer them.” He says that as a young Christian he got sick of hearing how bad things would get when “there’s another slant to this whole thing” in the Bible.
Who stands on the sea of glass and conquers the beast? (Revelation 15:2)

Standing on the sea of glass up there in heaven, mingled with fire, this sea of glass, there’s a group of people that got victory over the beast. Now, I don’t know about you, but I, as a young Christian, I got sick and tired of hearing about the beast and the antichrist and the son of perdition and how bad things were going to be and everything else. When I read the Bible, there’s another slant to this whole thing. I don’t care what the beast is, you can call it what you want to, but there are some people that got victory over it. They conquered the beast. The beast didn’t conquer them. Are you there? Isn’t that what it says in Revelation 15? Yes. See, Christians aren’t wimps. I sent out a weekly Bible study this week. If you’re not on that and you’d like to be, just let one of us know and we’ll get you on it. I mean, Paul just plainly said we’re not wimps. He plainly said we could attain things, and in our generation in America there are so many books and tapes just make us out to be wimps, and we are a powerful people because Jesus is a powerful King. Amen.
Who stands on the sea of glass and conquers the beast? (Revelation 15:2)

Revelation 15:2: And I saw something like a sea of glass mingled with fire, and those who have the victory over the beast, over his image and over his mark and over the number of his name, standing on the sea of glass, having harps of God.
Do Christians need to be raptured out to overcome the beast?

He says the people on the sea of glass got victory over the beast, “over his image,” and “over the mark,” and “we don’t have to be afraid, we don’t have to be raptured out to conquer this beast.” He asks, “how do you conquer something that you’re not around?” and says they conquered it “while it was going on.”
Do Christians need to be raptured out to overcome the beast?

Look at this: these people got victory over the beast, over his image (they didn’t worship it), over the mark (they didn’t take the mark so they could buy and sell). If God has to, He’ll bring the ravens to feed you. God will take care of His people, folks. Amen. We don’t have to be afraid, we don’t have to be raptured out to conquer this beast. And how do you conquer something that you’re not around? I mean, we conquered Germany because we confronted Germany and had war with them and won, ain’t that right? We didn’t conquer them by, you know, digging a hole in the ground and sheltering us from their bombs. And so these people, they conquered the beast, they conquered the mark, they conquered the image. Why? Right here, while it was going on. Hallelujah. And this is a problem they got, the [unclear] people have got a real problem here. I submit to you that the cross, the blood of Christ, is the most powerful thing. It’s the basic thing, and it’s the most powerful thing for the Christian, because it not only forgives us, it delivers us. It makes us, and the number of his name, 666. These people stood on the glass mingled with fire.
Do Christians need to be raptured out to overcome the beast?

Revelation 15:2: And I saw something like a sea of glass mingled with fire, and those who have the victory over the beast, over his image and over his mark and over the number of his name, standing on the sea of glass, having harps of God. 1 Kings 17:4-6: And it will be that you shall drink from the brook, and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.” So he went and did according to the word of the LORD, for he went and stayed by the Brook Cherith, which flows into the Jordan. The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening; and he drank from the brook.
Can anything separate us from the love of God, even the beast? (Romans 8:35-39)

He reads Romans 8:35-39 and says that includes the beast and the mark: “Why am I afraid of this beast and this mark? The Bible promises me that nothing’s going to separate me.” He says “I don’t need to be taken out of this world. God will empower me at that time to be victorious.”
Can anything separate us from the love of God, even the beast? (Romans 8:35-39)

Now, Romans 8:35 says, “Who shall separate us from Christ’s love? Shall tribulation, distress, famine, persecution, nakedness, peril, or sword?” No. “And in all these things we are more than conquerors.” See, it’s all through the Bible. You know, we’re going through an economic time. Does that depress the Christian? No way. We have a [unclear] way beyond that. We got promises higher than that. People mistreat us, and robbers want to rob us, and all the rest, and people want to threaten us, persecution comes, or whatever, that doesn’t move us. Why? We have a fellowship with Jesus that’s above all that, and that’s what these people were. “I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities nor powers, nor things present nor things to come, nor height nor depth, nor any other creature.” Any other what? Creature. That includes the beast, beast numero uno and beast numero dos, both of them. The little bit of Spanish I know. “Shall be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord.” So why am I afraid of this beast and this mark? The Bible promises me that nothing’s going to separate me. When it comes, I’m going to stand for Christ. I don’t need to be taken out of this world. God will empower me at that time to be victorious. Amen.
Can anything separate us from the love of God, even the beast? (Romans 8:35-39)

Romans 8:35-39: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword? As it is written: “For Your sake we are killed all day long; We are accounted as sheep for the slaughter.” Yet in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us. For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities nor powers, nor things present nor things to come, nor height nor depth, nor any other created thing, shall be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

He cites Revelation 5:10, “He has made us kings and priests, and we shall rule,” and asks, “how are you going to rule on earth if you got to be raptured out?” He says these things have been happening for 2,000 years, and “Christians since Christ came have overcame these things.”

It’s powerful. This is powerful, as you’ve seen in the book of Revelation. The church is approached as a very powerful people. Revelation 5:10: “He has made us kings and priests, and we shall rule.” Where? Now, how are you going to rule on earth if you got to be raptured out? Rule means you have power over. You’re the one in control. So we are in control of the beast when he comes. We are in control of whether we worship his image or not, and here it says that we are a people that conquered it. So obviously we have to be here when it happens, and obviously we showed you these things have been happening for 2,000 years, and we showed you that Revelation, twice, at the beginning and at the end, says these things will happen “shortly.” See, people are being persecuted, been persecuted for 2,000 years. They’ve been going through economic problems and famine and plagues and sicknesses for 2,000 years. What’s the big deal here? Why do we got to have some super duper thing up here at the end time to get all egotistical about? I submit to you that Christians since Christ came have overcame these things.
Revelation 5:10: And have made us kings and priests to our God; And we shall reign on the earth.”
Who is on the defense: the church or the gates of hell? (Matthew 16:18)

He says he has found conquerors in many denominations: “it’s not the group you belong to, it’s the King that you believe in.” From Matthew 16:18 he says gates are the entry to a fortress, so hell is on the defense, and “we can bring people out of the captivity of hell by preaching the Word and bringing them Jesus Christ.”
Who is on the defense: the church or the gates of hell? (Matthew 16:18)

And I’ll tell you, I’ve preached all over the world. I preached in South America, Africa, Europe, and, uh, over in Asia and all, and I found people of all denominations and walks of life, because I cross over borders. It doesn’t bother me what people do. I just go in and worship God with them. I found people in those groups that are conquerors. They love Jesus, they live right, they are beautiful people. That includes Catholics and Presbyterians and Baptists. It’s not the group you belong to, it’s the King that you believe in. Hallelujah. So I found people in all these denominations that are more than conquerors. The Bible says in Matthew 16:18, He says, “I will build My church, and the gates of hell will not” what? “Prevail against it.” Gates are the entry to a fortress. Okay, so who’s on the defense here? Huh? Hell is the gates of hell. See, the entrance to hell. Who is on the defense? Hell is not us. Hallelujah. Gosh. See, we’re a powerful people. People, why are we, you know, so the homosexuals and the sinners and everybody out there is promoting it, what do we care? Why are we so shaky? We prevail against it by living for Christ and preaching the Word. We can bring people out of that fortress, isn’t that right? We can bring people out of the captivity of hell by preaching the Word and bringing them Jesus Christ. Hallelujah. And we can be around the forces of hell, the sin and the kingdom of darkness, without being affected by it. Why? Because we’re more than conquerors. Man, we’re those people that stand on the sea of glass that overcome, and not only we overcome, we are conquering. There it is, that verse, Matthew 16:18: “I will build My church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail,” overpower or succeed “against it.” The kingdom of darkness cannot succeed against the kingdom of Christ. Amen. The people of darkness cannot have success over the people of Christ. That’s the Bible, and we see in Revelation that it worked. Amen. Isn’t that powerful?
Who is on the defense: the church or the gates of hell? (Matthew 16:18)
Matthew 16:18: And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it.
What is “the song of Moses,” and why is it not a victory song? (Deuteronomy 31:19-21; 32)

He says Revelation speaks of the song of Moses and the song of the Lamb, and that there literally is a song of Moses. He says God told Moses to write a song to be evidence against Israel, predicting they would serve other gods and break the covenant, and he says, “how many know that’s not a very edifying song?”
What is “the song of Moses,” and why is it not a victory song? (Deuteronomy 31:19-21; 32)

And listen to this: “They sang the song of Moses and the song of the Lamb.” Now, just like you need to know that there’s a temple on the earth, then there’s a temple in heaven, you need to know that there’s a song that God gave Moses, and there’s a song about the Lamb, and we’re going to look into these two songs and show you the difference. Are you ready? See, most of us don’t even know there was a song of Moses. There literally is a song of Moses, and there literally is a song of the Lamb, and if we know these, then we can understand what’s going on. Are you ready? All right. Deuteronomy 31:19, God told Moses, “Write this song and teach it” as a witness to Israel, okay, as evidence. And this song says they will serve other gods, they will break My covenant, and they’ll turn aside from My commandment. Wow. Did you hear that? Before they ever did it, God said this is what they’re going to do. They’re going to turn aside, they’re going to break My covenant, and they’re going to serve other gods. Well, they were already serving other gods, if you know your Bible. Even when they were there in the wilderness, they were serving other gods, and I don’t have time to go into that. So in verse 21 God says this song will testify against them. This song will be evidence against them when they do these things that I told them what they’re going to do. “Their hearts were this way. I know their imagination, their fantasies and their thinking. I know their rebellion. I know that they’re void of counsel and understanding.” I mean, how would you like God to bring you that song? Huh? You’re void of understanding, you’re void of counsel, you’re a dumb, stupid people. “Oh, that they were wise, that they would consider their latter end.” Famines, plagues, and the sword, or wars, will destroy them. Deuteronomy 32:43, “God will provide atonement for them.” He’s going to bring them back, but they are going to go away. Are you there? That’s the song of Moses. How many know that’s not a very edifying song? I’ll bet you Israel didn’t sing that very often. I bet they didn’t come in, you know, with this song on their lips.
What is “the song of Moses,” and why is it not a victory song? (Deuteronomy 31:19-21; 32)

Revelation 15:3: They sing the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying: “Great and marvelous are Your works, Lord God Almighty! Just and true are Your ways, O King of the saints! Deuteronomy 31:19-21: “Now therefore, write down this song for yourselves, and teach it to the children of Israel; put it in their mouths, that this song may be a witness for Me against the children of Israel. When I have brought them to the land flowing with milk and honey, of which I swore to their fathers, and they have eaten and filled themselves and grown fat, then they will turn to other gods and serve them; and they will provoke Me and break My covenant. Then it shall be, when many evils and troubles have come upon them, that this song will testify against them as a witness; for it will not be forgotten in the mouths of their descendants, for I know the inclination of their behavior today, even before I have brought them to the land of which I swore to give them.” Deuteronomy 32:28-29: “For they are a nation void of counsel, Nor is there any understanding in them. Oh, that they were wise, that they understood this, That they would consider their latter end! Deuteronomy 32:43: “Rejoice, O Gentiles, with His people; For He will avenge the blood of His servants, And render vengeance to His adversaries; He will provide atonement for His land and His people.”
What is the song of the Lamb? (Revelation 5:9-10)

He says everything in the song of Moses “came to pass,” and God atoned for them and brought them out of captivity, showing that “the blood of Christ can bring us out.” The song of the Lamb says “You are worthy to open the seals of the book. You were slain,” and that He made us “kings and priests,” and “we shall reign.”
What is the song of the Lamb? (Revelation 5:9-10)

Huh. But it happened. It came to pass, didn’t it? Everything in here came to pass. Plagues came, wars came, they went into captivity, and God, what? Atoned for them and brought them out of captivity, showing us the example that if we go into captivity, the blood of Christ can bring us out. And all they had to do was admit they were wrong in captivity and ask for forgiveness, and God said, “I will turn their captivity and bring them back.” Hallelujah. So that’s all for an example, but that’s the song of Moses. I don’t know about you, but he can keep that song. Here’s the song of the Lamb. Now look at this big difference. The elders fell down before the Lamb singing a what? New song. “You are worthy.” Who is worthy? The Lamb, Jesus. This is the song of the Lamb: “You are worthy to open the seals of the book. You were slain, and You redeemed us to God by Your blood out of every kind and tribe, tongue, people, and nations, and You have made us unto our God kings and priests, and we shall reign.”
What is the song of the Lamb? (Revelation 5:9-10)

Revelation 5:9-10: And they sang a new song, saying: “You are worthy to take the scroll, And to open its seals; For You were slain, And have redeemed us to God by Your blood Out of every tribe and tongue and people and nation, And have made us kings and priests to our God; And we shall reign on the earth.”
Why is the song of the Lamb better than the song of Moses? (Hebrews 8:6)

He says the song of the Lamb has “nothing about backsliding… nothing about breaking the covenant,” but “a song of victory… a song of strength, a song of power.” From Hebrews 8:6 he says it is better because “the old covenant wasn’t the final covenant,” and Jesus is “a Mediator of a better covenant.”
Why is the song of the Lamb better than the song of Moses? (Hebrews 8:6)

Where? Where? Nothing about backsliding. Amen. Nothing about going astray. Nothing about turning away. Nothing about breaking the covenant. He says, “Man, you’re going to rule on earth.” Hallelujah. I mean, which one would you rather be, a weak [unclear] people, or you would like to be this people? This is the promise to us. It isn’t the promise that we’re going to backslide, and we’ve got to hang on to the rapture, and, you know, we just got to go through life sinning and all the rest. This is a song of victory. This is a song of accomplishment, a song of strength, a song of power, where? Right now, in this earth. Hebrews 8:6: “Jesus has obtained a more excellent ministry as a Mediator of a better covenant, established on better promises.” See, why can this be? Why is the Moses song so not victorious, and the song of the Lamb is? Because the old covenant wasn’t the final covenant. The Old Testament was not the final. It only pointed to the final one, and all the saints of old who were looking forward to the final one lived victorious. Are you there? But now we’re in the new covenant, and Jesus is a Mediator of what? A better covenant. That’s why the song is better. Does that make sense to you? Yes. “Established on better promises.” So we have better things than the Old Testament, uh, covenant.
Why is the song of the Lamb better than the song of Moses? (Hebrews 8:6)
Hebrews 8:6: But now He has obtained a more excellent ministry, inasmuch as He is also Mediator of a better covenant, which was established on better promises.
Does Jesus lose any of His people? (John 17:12, 18:9)

He says Jesus “lost how many? None,” and he quotes the verse, “While I was with them in the world, I kept them in Your name, and none of them is lost.” He says “a person only gets born again one time,” so you don’t keep getting saved over and over, but he needs to “keep changing.”
Does Jesus lose any of His people? (John 17:12, 18:9)

John 17:21: “While I was with them in the world, I kept them in Your name, and none of them is lost.” How many? Wow. Wow. See, and people that I know, these people where I go to visit all over the world and meet, that are conquerors, they actually met with Christ, they actually got born again, they actually are living for Christ, regardless of the denomination they’re in. It is very, very encouraging to see Catholics and Presbyterians and Methodists and Baptists living for Christ, living a strong life, overcoming the things of this world and living for Christ here on earth now. Amen. And a lot of times they got to overcome their church. Jesus said, “I’ve lost how many? None.” Wow. Now, how many Christians you know been saved about 10 times? Yeah, I, you, I used to meet them at the altar. I said, “What are you doing up here?” “Well, I got to get saved again.” I go, “A person’s only born one time, and a person only gets born again one time. Now, either your birth was lousy, no good, or you just need to let Jesus be Lord of your life and grow in Christ. Now, which is it?” He said, “Man, I need to buck up.” “Okay, then let’s buck up.” Isn’t that a difference? I don’t keep getting saved and over saved and saved and saved and saved again, but I do need to, what? Keep changing. “I lost how many?” Hallelujah. And, you know, that’s what happened in my life. I never thought about backsliding. I didn’t even know that that was an alternative. Christ was so good and the Word was so powerful, it was always just pursuing. Did I make mistakes? Yes, but I could correct them. Aren’t you glad every one of us has erasers on your pencils? Yeah, you know, we can correct. Aren’t you glad that God has an eraser? Yes, it’s called repentance: admitting you’re wrong and asking forgiveness. He erases. John 18:9: “Of those whom You gave Me I have lost” how many? None. Now, is this a better covenant? Are these better promises? This is powerful, church, and this is in the book of Revelation, and it’s all through the Bible. Luke 22:31: “Satan has desired to have you, Peter, and sift you as wheat, but I have prayed for you that your faith fail not.” See, what’s He up there in heaven doing for us? Interceding for us that our faith fails not. I have a powerful lawyer up there pleading my case and a King that has power to perform in my life what He promised when you’re converted, see, when you’re changed.
Does Jesus lose any of His people? (John 17:12, 18:9)

John 17:12: While I was with them in the world, I kept them in Your name. Those whom You gave Me I have kept; and none of them is lost except the son of perdition, that the Scripture might be fulfilled. John 18:9: that the saying might be fulfilled which He spoke, “Of those whom You gave Me I have lost none.” Luke 22:31-32: And the Lord said, “Simon, Simon! Indeed, Satan has asked for you, that he may sift you as wheat. But I have prayed for you, that your faith should not fail; and when you have returned to Me, strengthen your brethren.”
What does Peter’s story show about Jesus’s prayer for him? (Luke 22:31-32)

He says Peter was a strong apostle who still denied Christ, rebuked Jesus, and went fishing, yet was first out of the boat when Jesus appeared. He says “Jesus prayed for him that his faith fail not, and it didn’t fail,” and Peter “wound up being a conqueror.”
What does Peter’s story show about Jesus’s prayer for him? (Luke 22:31-32)

Now, Peter was a pretty strong apostle, but he did deny Christ. He did tell Jesus (he rebuked Jesus, the Bible says) and says, “You can’t die, you can’t die on the cross.” You know how many Christians I hear rebuking God? They don’t say they’re rebuking Him, but when you tell God He can’t do certain things, and you tell God what His Word should be, that’s exactly what you’re doing. You’re rebuking God. And, uh, Peter was the one that went fishing. He said, “Well, Jesus is dead, I’m going fishing.” He’s the one that, and the whole group followed him. And a lot of you are like that: one person gets cold and said, “Hey, I’m just going to stay home,” well, 10 of you just stay home. It’s true. But who was the first one out of the boat when Jesus came to the seashore and said, “Children, do you have any meat?” Peter. Man, he said, “It’s the Master!” Jumped out of that boat, made it, he split, got to shore. You see, see, Jesus prayed for him that his faith fail not, and it didn’t fail. He made some errors, but he wound up being a conqueror. Amen.
What does Peter’s story show about Jesus’s prayer for him? (Luke 22:31-32)

Luke 22:31-32: And the Lord said, “Simon, Simon! Indeed, Satan has asked for you, that he may sift you as wheat. But I have prayed for you, that your faith should not fail; and when you have returned to Me, strengthen your brethren.”
How can I change and strengthen others, and what does Jesus’s intercession do for me?

He says “you’re not going to be able to strengthen people until you got strength yourself,” and that when you are not changing “you have no clout to tell anyone else to change.” He says Jesus is up there interceding for us to change, and “when we bring people to Christ, then Christ maintains and keeps them.”
How can I change and strengthen others, and what does Jesus’s intercession do for me?

And that same Jesus is interceding for us, folks. That’s what makes the difference. And He says, “When you do get changed, strengthen your brethren.” Now, how many know you’re not going to be able to strengthen people until you got strength yourself? Does that make sense? Yeah. You’re not going to be able to change people till you change yourself, and in marriages and in raising kids, you know, we want our kids to change and we want our spouse to change, and we’re not changing. And when you’re not changing, you have no clout to tell anyone else to change. You have nothing to give them, you have no example before them. You’re just a clanging drum and a clanging symbol, [unclear] irritating. You’re just shooting your mouth off when you need to shut up and change and show them the way they should go. Boy, that was good. Amen. And Jesus said we could change. He’s interceding for us to change. So He said, “Father, don’t leave him in that state. Don’t leave that guy with a temper. Don’t leave that guy with a lustful desire for sexual [unclear]. Father, come on, do Your thing.” Father. Is that beautiful? And see, that’s encouraging. So I don’t have to get down, I don’t have to get depressed, and I don’t have to feel rejected, and I don’t have to quit. Why? I got somebody that can do something about my situation up there in heaven, appearing before the throne of God for me, and I’m going to wind up being a victorious, victorious person. Why? Because the Victorious One is pleading my cause. So bring on the beast, and bring on the mark, and bring on these things. We are more than conquerors in Him. I’m going to wind up what? Worshiping before Him in heaven. Why? Because I am a part of a better covenant, better promises. He lost how many? None, and I’m not going to let Him lose me. He keeps what comes to Him. Isn’t that powerful? But see, when we bring people to a church, then the church has to maintain and keep them. When we bring people to a minister, that minister has to maintain and keep them. But when we bring people to Christ, then Christ maintains and keeps them.
How can I change and strengthen others, and what does Jesus’s intercession do for me?
Luke 22:32: But I have prayed for you, that your faith should not fail; and when you have returned to Me, strengthen your brethren.”
Where do the seven angels with the last plagues come from?
He says they come “out of the temple in heaven,” holding seven bowls “filled with God’s wrath, God’s anger, God’s punishment.”
What does he say about honoring dead church leaders?
He says, “You don’t beautify dead popes or dead people. That stuff is nonsense. What we need is to hear from God and meet with God.” He says “we need to come out to see Jesus glorified.”
Why does he say animal sacrifices are no longer needed?

He says the natural sacrifices “pointed to the real sacrifice, Jesus Christ,” and that people still shedding blood are “thinking they’re doing God a favor” and miss that “that was just an example of Christ’s coming and dying on the cross.”
Why does he say you go to Jesus and not to Mary?
He says “you don’t go to Mary… and none of these distractions. You go to Jesus. Why? He’s in the temple of God in heaven interceding, talking to God for you.”
Does the Bible say believers can conquer the beast?
He says yes: “there are some people that got victory over it. They conquered the beast. The beast didn’t conquer them.”
Does he say Christians should be afraid or weak?
He says no: “Christians aren’t wimps,” and “we are a powerful people because Jesus is a powerful King.” He says “if God has to, He’ll bring the ravens to feed you.”
What does “more than conquerors” mean to him?

He says an economic downturn or persecution “doesn’t move us” because “we have a fellowship with Jesus that’s above all that,” and quotes that nothing “shall be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord.”
How long does he say these trials have been happening?
He says “these things have been happening for 2,000 years,” with persecution, economic problems, famine, plagues and sicknesses, and asks, “what’s the big deal here?”
Does he say only one denomination has real Christians?
He says no: he found “people in all these denominations that are more than conquerors,” and “it’s not the group you belong to, it’s the King that you believe in.”
Who is on the defense in Matthew 16:18?
He says gates are “the entrance to hell,” so “who is on the defense? Hell is not us.” He says “the kingdom of darkness cannot succeed against the kingdom of Christ.”
What does he say the song of Moses said would happen to Israel?

He says it said Israel would serve other gods, break the covenant and turn aside, and that “famines, plagues, and the sword, or wars, will destroy them.” He says it also said “God will provide atonement for them.”
What is different about the song of the Lamb?
He says it has “nothing about backsliding… nothing about going astray, nothing about turning away, nothing about breaking the covenant,” but promises “you’re going to rule on earth.”
Can a person be born again more than once?
He says no: “a person’s only born one time, and a person only gets born again one time.” He says you need to “let Jesus be Lord of your life and grow in Christ,” and keep changing.
What does he mean by God having an eraser?
He says, “Aren’t you glad that God has an eraser? Yes, it’s called repentance: admitting you’re wrong and asking forgiveness. He erases.”
What did Jesus pray for Peter?
He says Jesus prayed “that his faith fail not,” and “it didn’t fail.” He says Peter made some errors “but he wound up being a conqueror.”

items.d: In “Proof of Bad Judgments,” Pastor David G. Kincer compares America before and after the sexual revolution that began in 1960 and says the results prove it was a bad judgment. He says the groups that promoted…
p: In “Proof of Bad Judgments,” Pastor David G. Kincer compares America before and after the sexual revolution that began in 1960 and says the results prove it was a bad judgment. He says the groups that promoted it have not admitted it was wrong, and he calls for confession and repentance (1 John 1:9, Luke 13:3). He closes with a Bible solution drawn from 2 Peter 1: moral excellence, knowledge, self-control, patience, respect for God and brotherly love.
What is the sermon “Proof of Bad Judgments” about?

He says we can make bad, better and best choices, and in this session he shows the proof of bad judgments by comparing life before and after the sexual revolution that started in 1960 when the pill was introduced.
What is the sermon “Proof of Bad Judgments” about?

We can make bad choices, we can make better choices than bad choices, and then we can make the best choices. In this session we’re going to be talking about the proof, and showing you the proof, of bad judgments. We’re going to take a look at the sexual revolution that started in 1960, when the pill was introduced, up to the present. We’re going to look at things, uh, before the sexual revolution, and then we’re going to look at things after the sexual revolution.
How many sexually transmitted diseases were there before and after the sexual revolution?

He says there were only two before 1960 and that now there are over 30, costing Americans $16 billion a year to treat. He says the share of people who have had one went from less than 2% to greater than 50%, citing the Center for Disease Control.
How many sexually transmitted diseases were there before and after the sexual revolution?

Before the sexual re- revolution happened in 1960, there were only two sexually transmitted diseases. Uh, we call them STDs, and these two sexually transmitted diseases were gonorrhea and syphilis. After the sexual revolution, and progressively so, new types of sexually transmitted diseases came up on the scene, and now we have over 30 sexually transmitted diseases. It cost American $16 billion a year to treat them, and this is from the Center of Disease and Control. Before the sexual revolution there were less than 2% that had a sexually transmitted disease; now it is greater than 50% of Americans have had or have now a sexually transmitted disease, where six of them kill and four are incurable.
How did the sexual revolution affect children and families?
He says one-parent homes rose from 10% to 44% of children, that 85% of youth in prison come from single-parent homes, and that unplanned births rose from 10% to 40%.
How did the sexual revolution affect children and families?

Before the sexual revolution, 10% of children lived in a one-parent home. Now 44% live in a one-parent home, and these children have a high percent of behavioral disorders, such as 85% of youth in prison come from single-parent homes; 85% that have been behavioral disorders come from single-parent homes. Before the sexual revolution, 10% were unplanned births; now 40% are unplanned births, according again to the Center for Disease Control.

He says the numbers mean that safe sex education and Planned Parenthood’s idea “did not work,” and he lists what came out of the closet after 1960, along with figures on sexual abuse in the military and in schools.

This means that safe sex, safe sex education, and Planned Parenthood’s idea did not work. Again, the sexual revolution from 1960, things that came out of the closet: local sex shops in the community where kids can walk by, nude bars, adult theaters, where you couldn’t drive your kid into town without it going by one of these things; public expression of homosexuality, transvestite and transsexuality; divorce came out of the closet; abortion on demand and divorce on demand; and being a virgin was no longer popular, you were, something wrong with you, or, if you were still a virgin. 45,000 military men were raped in the past 30 years, and increasingly so, according to the United States Department of Veteran Affairs, up to the place where today 500 military men and women are sexually abused in the military, according to the USA Today, 2012, and 14% of those military are men. 1/3 of 460,000 children that are sexually abused, uh, are the same-sex attacker. 500 per year of public school teachers sexually abused students.
What does he say about media bias?

He says media bias “has come out of the closet” and contrasts how widely one killing was promoted as a hate crime while a 13-year-old boy’s death got no big fuss. He says forensic facts prove this judgment was harmful.
What does he say about media bias?

And the media bias has come out of the closet, and they’re just flat-out bias on the left. You see Matthew Shepard, who was killed in Texas, and the homosexual activist promoted it, and so did the media, as a hate crime. At the same time, a young kid aged 13 by the name of Jesse [unclear] was lured up into an apartment by two homosexuals, tied up, and raped until the boy died, and yet the media made no big fuss over that at all. Forensic facts prove that this judgment was harmful.
What are the four heartbreaks he says science has exposed?

He names evolution, abortion, the claim that homosexuals were born that way, and safe sex education. He says science has exposed the first three, yet humanists, the media and other groups still promote them.
What are the four heartbreaks he says science has exposed?

Now, there are four heartbreaks that science has exposed, but humanists, the media and other groups still promote, even though they’ve been scientifically exposed as a lie. Number one is evolution. There is no missing link, part ape and part man; there is no present mutation; and the big bang, why did it happen only once, and where did the first matter come from? You see, there is no scientific evidence. The second one is abortion. Science has declared that the baby is a human at conception, with all the DNA to become a human being, and yet they still abort babies. The third heartbreak is homosexuals. They were not born that way. Science said there is no homo- homosexual gene; it is a choice. And the heartbreak is that both homosexuals and people are saying they cannot change.
Why does he say safe sex education failed?

He points to STD rates, 1.2 million abortions a year and 40% unplanned births as proof that it “just promoted loose sexual activity.” He asks those who say science is the solution to admit the mistake and make changes that protect innocent children.
Why does he say safe sex education failed?

The fourth one that’s a heartbreak is this safe sex education that was promoted by Planned Parenthood and the teachers unions of America and so forth. And 50% of Americans having a sexually transmitted disease, 1.2 million abortions per year, unplanned, 40% kids are unplanned births, are the proof that safe sex education didn’t work; it just promoted loose sexual activity. The humanist and followers say science, not the Bible or God, is the solution for man. If the humanist and their followers really believe that, then I submit to them: why don’t we unite, admit that this was wrong, we made a mistake, and make changes that protect people and innocent children from harm?
Which groups does he say promoted the sexual revolution?

He lists homosexual rights groups, Planned Parenthood, both political parties, the Supreme Court and the American Humanist Association, along with atheists, liberals and others. He says none have admitted it was a bad judgment and reads 1 John 1:9 on confessing sin.
Which groups does he say promoted the sexual revolution?

Now we’re going to look at some groups that was responsible for the legalization of the sexual revolution. At the top I have several icons: the homosexual rights icon, with the lady kissing the Statue of Liberty; Planned Parenthood icon; Republican; Democ- Democrat; Supreme Court; and the American Humanist Association; along with atheists, liberals, religionist, hedonist and freethinkers. All promoted and supported the sexual revolution. None have admitted it was a bad judgment. None. 1 John 1:9 tells us, if we confess our sin, our crime, God is faithful and just to forgive our sin and our crime and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. I have not heard anyone from these groups admitting they were wrong, their group was wrong, and asking America to forgive them.
Which groups does he say promoted the sexual revolution?
1 John 1:9: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
What does it mean to repent?

Quoting Luke 13:3, he says repent is to turn my thinking from bad, harmful thinking to good, right thinking, and to turn my bad behavior to right behavior. He says the Bible idea of hope and change includes repentance.
What does it mean to repent?

None of these groups are calling for a change. Yet in Luke 13:3 the Bible says, unless you repent you shall all likewise perish. Repent is to turn my thinking from bad thinking, harmful thinking, to good thinking, right thinking, and turn my bad behavior to right behavior. And I’ve heard no group. Obama talked about hope, change, but he never mentioned and admitted that these judgments back there were wrong and we need to repent, and asked America to forgive us. His ideal of hope and change was not the Bible ideal of hope and change. But we need to get back to the Bible idea, the Bible principle, of hope and expectation and change. And I’m going to present to you some principles that will bring a solution to this pollution of the sexual revolution.
What does it mean to repent?
Luke 13:3: I tell you, no; but unless you repent you will all likewise perish.
What is the Bible solution to the sexual revolution?

He proposes adding the pursuit of moral excellence to our faith, teaching Bible morals (including in public schools), requiring self-control over sexual desires, and using patience to wait and marry one man to one woman for life.
What is the Bible solution to the sexual revolution?

Propose solutions to the sexual revolution, and I submit to these groups, you need to listen and respond to the Bible solution to these things. Number one, we need to add the pursuit of moral excellence to our faith. Whether you have the faith of humanist, there is no God, you’re a Christian, there is a God, or whatever, you need to add the pursuit. We’re not there yet, but we need to say we need to pursue moral excellent, right behavior. Number two, we need to teach the citizens of America the knowledge of Bible moral. We need to get the Bible back into public schools, teaching the principles of moral character. Number three, we need to require people use self-control over sexual desires, and a penalty if they don’t. Number four, we need to use patience to wait and marry one man to one woman for life, and we need to wait pr- through premarital sex and this free sex ideal and sexual revolution, and wait and save sex for marriage.
What is the Bible solution to the sexual revolution?

2 Peter 1:5-7: But also for this very reason, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue, to virtue knowledge, to knowledge self-control, to self-control perseverance, to perseverance godliness, to godliness brotherly kindness, and to brotherly kindness love.
How does Bible morality save lives?

He says to respect God, who is love, and obey love’s moral laws, because love does no harm to his neighbor. His bottom line: “Bible morality saves lives,” saves medical cost, saves marriages and saves the future of innocent children.
How does Bible morality save lives?

Number five, we need to teach respect for God, and remember God is love, and obey love’s moral laws. Whether you believe in God or not, you must believe in love, and love does no harm to his neighbor. So we need to respect love, and we don’t prohibit the free exercise of brotherly love. Brotherly love are those that do exercise moral principles. And we need to honor the Bible love, to do no harm to anyone, and punish those that do. The bottom line is, Bible morality saves lives, it saves medical cost, it saves marriages. Bible morality saves the life and the future of innocent children.
What does 2 Peter 1 teach about the solution?

He says Second Peter chapter 1 gives the principles of a solution: admit we are wrong, repent, and change laws. He says whether you are a humanist or a Christian you have no excuse to harm others, so Americans must make the right judgment.
What does 2 Peter 1 teach about the solution?

And I submit to you that Second Peter chapter 1 gives us the principles of a solution. We must admit we are wrong, we must repent from that wrong, and change laws that promote right. The naive and not-so-naive accept and promote harmful sexual behavior. They promote its lies and legalize its preventable diseases, deaths and monetary harm, and especially harm to innocent children. I’ve given you alarming forensic facts, and the Bible has given us a solution. Whether you are a humanist or whether you are a Christian, you have no excuse, no excuse to harm others. So, Americans, we presented to you the facts; now you must make the right judgment.
What does 2 Peter 1 teach about the solution?

2 Peter 1:5-7: But also for this very reason, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue, to virtue knowledge, to knowledge self-control, to self-control perseverance, to perseverance godliness, to godliness brotherly kindness, and to brotherly kindness love.
When does he say the sexual revolution started?
He says it started in 1960, when the pill was introduced.
Which two STDs does he say existed before 1960?
How many STDs does he say can kill or are incurable?
He says six of them kill and four are incurable.
What does he say came out of the closet after 1960?
He lists sex shops, nude bars and adult theaters, public expression of homosexuality, divorce, abortion on demand and divorce on demand, and says being a virgin was no longer popular.
Does he say people are born homosexual?
He says they were not born that way, that science said there is no homosexual gene and that it is a choice; the heartbreak, he says, is that people say they cannot change.
When does he say a baby is human?
He says science has declared that the baby is a human at conception, with all the DNA to become a human being.
He says if we confess our sin, God is faithful and just to forgive our sin and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
What does he say about “hope and change”?
He says a political call for hope and change never admitted these judgments were wrong, and that it was not the Bible ideal of hope and change, which includes repentance.
Should the Bible be taught in public schools?
He says we need to get the Bible back into public schools, teaching the principles of moral character.
What does he say about sex before marriage?
He says to use patience to wait and marry one man to one woman for life, and to wait and save sex for marriage.
What if someone does not believe in God?
He says whether you believe in God or not, you must believe in love, and love does no harm to his neighbor.
What does he ask Americans to do?
He asks them to admit we are wrong, repent, change laws, and make the right judgment, because no one has an excuse to harm others.
