p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer walks through Isaiah’s prophecies against nine cities and nations (Isaiah 13–23) and shows how Babylon, Moab, Egypt and Tyre were fulfilled, then looks at the hidden “day of the Lord” passages in them. He says God will show mercy and bring in the heathen as well as His people who have given up their inheritance, and ends with Isaiah 26 on desiring Jesus and God’s judgments teaching righteousness.
What are the nine prophecies in Isaiah 13–23, and did Babylon become uninhabited as foretold? (Isaiah 13:17-20)

He lists the nine cities or nations Isaiah addresses (Babylon, Moab, Damascus, Egypt, “the desert of the sea,” the valley of vision, Tyre and Sidon, and others) and says Babylon was “a tremendous city” that God said would never be inhabited again. He shows a picture of its ruins today and says “this Bible is a very powerful book” whose prophecies were fulfilled just as spoken, which only a supernatural God can do.
What are the nine prophecies in Isaiah 13–23, and did Babylon become uninhabited as foretold? (Isaiah 13:17-20)

First he talks about, in Isaiah 13, chapters 13 23, he talks about Babylon. Okay, then he talks about Moab. Moab is the incestuous offspring of Lot and his two daughters that got him drunk, all right, and had sex with their father. Then he is going to talk about Damascus, the capital of Syria, the N the nation or empire of Syria. And then he’s going to talk about Egypt, number four. And then he’s going to call something “the desert of the sea,” and this threw me for a for a loop for quite a few years, “the desert of the sea.” And commentaries and all that said that’s the wind blowing in from this sea and destruction of Babylon. You know, when we don’t know something, we just contrive anything. But there’s some key words that he’s given us and we will see that later. It’s really going to be Persia and the Medes. All right. Then you have the valley of vision. That didn’t throw me at all, because he’s talking about Jerusalem and Judea here. And then number nine, Tyre and Sidon over here on the coast. Okay, he’s going to talk about the these nine cities or nations. Now he says in Isaiah 13:17, Babylon shall never be inhabited. Now, our opponents are always saying that, you know, God said he would do things and then in the New Testament people just made it happen because they already wrote it, so they just acted on it and said it was fulfilled. But how do you say a tremendous city like Babylon, it was a tremendous city if you know your history, and God says will never be inhabited again. And folks, here’s a picture of it today. Looks pretty in uninhabited, doesn’t it? And there’s many things you see. You can say that God’s going to come in the flesh, give his life, die and resurrect himself again. But how do you cover that up when he did come and die and resurrected himself again? You see, and the Roman Empire tried their best to distort and destroy that story, but they couldn’t find the evidence. There was nobody. He did rise from the grave, and so forth. So anyway, you young in the Lord, this Bible is a very powerful book. He spoke things in the natural, prophetic nation and so forth, that were fulfilled just as he spoke. In the spiritual realm that are being fulfilled, you understand? And only God can do that. This God is a supernatural God, okay? He’s real. Jesus is real. Okay, he also says at the same time Assyria, that’s right here, and Philistine, that’s over here by the coast, we’ll see it when I get rid of this picture. Will be broken. All right, and Assyria was broken, and Palestine right here down in Canaan was also broken. None of these nations ever amounted to anything after God spoke and said they weren’t.
What are the nine prophecies in Isaiah 13–23, and did Babylon become uninhabited as foretold? (Isaiah 13:17-20)

Isaiah 13:17-20: “Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them, Who will not regard silver; And as for gold, they will not delight in it. Also their bows will dash the young men to pieces, And they will have no pity on the fruit of the womb; Their eye will not spare children. And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, The beauty of the Chaldeans’ pride, Will be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah. It will never be inhabited, Nor will it be settled from generation to generation; Nor will the Arabian pitch tents there, Nor will the shepherds make their sheepfolds there.
Did God’s prophecies about Moab, Egypt and “the desert of the sea” come true? (Isaiah 16:14, 19:4, 21:2)

He says Moab’s survivors were “few and feeble,” Egypt was ruled in turn by Assyria, Babylon, Greece and Rome and “never rose to a prominence in the earth,” and “the desert of the sea” turned out to be Persia and the Medes who destroyed Babylon. He says atheists and those who attack the Bible “got to be confronted with these facts.”
Did God’s prophecies about Moab, Egypt and “the desert of the sea” come true? (Isaiah 16:14, 19:4, 21:2)

Okay, Isaiah 16:14, “Within 3 years Moab’s splendor and all her many people will be despised, and her survivors will be few and feeble.” And how many have ever met a Moabite? I didn’t think so. I haven’t either. There are few. All right. Isaiah 19:4, “The Egyptians shall be given over unto a hand of a cruel lord, and a fierce king shall rule over them.” And if you know your history, Assyria came in and ruled over Egypt, Babylon came in and ruled over Egypt, Greece came and ruled over Egypt, and then Rome did. And the Egyptians never rose to a prominence in the earth, okay, just like God said. And these atheists and these people that attack the Bible, you know, they got to be confronted with these facts. Are you there? Hallelujah. The desert of the sea. Okay, and here’s where I get the desert of the sea. He says, “Go up,” or attack, “O Elam.” You know, we say, “Oh, God, come.” Okay, he said, “Elam, go up and attack. Media, go up and besiege,” and then he keeps talking about it, and then it says Babylon has fallen. So Persia, the Medes and the Persians are the ones that rose up and destroyed the kingdom of Babylon, if you know your history, right? And we’ve taught you this before, it’s just a a remembrance session. And so this powerful God, when he says a nation in the natural is going to fall, it’s going to fall, okay? But that also means when he says something in the spiritual is going to happen, it’s going to happen.
Did God’s prophecies about Moab, Egypt and “the desert of the sea” come true? (Isaiah 16:14, 19:4, 21:2)

Isaiah 16:14: But now the LORD has spoken, saying, “Within three years, as the years of a hired man, the glory of Moab will be despised with all that great multitude, and the remnant will be very small and feeble.” Isaiah 19:4: And the Egyptians I will give Into the hand of a cruel master, And a fierce king will rule over them,” Says the Lord, the LORD of hosts. Isaiah 21:2: A distressing vision is declared to me; The treacherous dealer deals treacherously, And the plunderer plunders. Go up, O Elam! Besiege, O Media! All its sighing I have made to cease.
What does Edom’s lost birthright mean, and why does God say “return”? (Isaiah 21:11-12)

He says Edom, the offspring of Esau, gave up the birthright, which was the right to the inheritance, and that many Christians do the same by just wanting to go to heaven and not inheriting “love, joy, peace, self-control.” He says God’s message to Edom is positive: “inquire,” “return,” which he equates with repent, and “come on back, I’ll give you inheritance.”
What does Edom’s lost birthright mean, and why does God say “return”? (Isaiah 21:11-12)

Now, Isaiah 21:11. Dumah is a city down here. Now I, in my research, have a hard time believing that. Edom, Edom is the offspring of Esau, who gave up his birthright. The birthright was the right to the inheritance. Okay, and many Christians give up their inheritance. They just want to believe God and go to heaven, get taken up in the rapture, and they don’t inherit love, joy, peace, self-control, meekness, kindness, faith. they They don’t inherit these things. They give up their birthright. But Edom, from my study, is right in this area, but they could have reached down into this far at one time or another. So anyway, he calls to me out of Seir. Seir is Edom, it’s another name for Edom, okay? “If you will inquire, inquire.” Now, this is what he says to the ones, the offspring who rejected the inheritance. Okay, he says, “Inquire,” ask. Ask. And then the reply is what? “Return, come back.” And what’s another word for return? Repent, you know? Okay, turn from your giving up your birthright. Turn and come back to me. Now, this is a positive prophecy to Edom. Hallelujah. He didn’t say there were going to be few and all this and that and the other. He said you need to turn and come back and I’ll give you your inheritance. Ain’t that beautiful? How many of you know Christians, or maybe you’re one, that hadn’t bothered about the inheritance? Well, God can says, “Come on back, come on back, I’ll give you inheritance.”
What does Edom’s lost birthright mean, and why does God say “return”? (Isaiah 21:11-12)

Isaiah 21:11-12: The burden against Dumah. He calls to me out of Seir, “Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?” The watchman said, “The morning comes, and also the night. If you will inquire, inquire; Return! Come back!”
What happens when we make our own plans instead of waiting for God’s plan? (Isaiah 21:16-17, Isaiah 22)

He says Ishmael came from Abraham and Sarah trying to get God’s promise done themselves, which is “what a lot of Christians do”: they come up with their own plan and wind up with a mess. He says “your own plans are always going to fail,” and that Judah was carried into captivity just as God said, because “they didn’t pursue God.”
What happens when we make our own plans instead of waiting for God’s plan? (Isaiah 21:16-17, Isaiah 22)

Okay, Isaiah 21:16. Arabia. “Within a year all the glory of Kedar,” Ishmael, it’s another word for Ishmael and his offspring. Ishmael was the offspring of Abraham through Sarah’s handmaiden. Okay, when ab Abraham and Sarah tried to get God’s promise done themselves, and this is what a lot of Christians do, they come up with their own plan instead of waiting for God’s plan and following God’s plan. Come up with our own plan and then we have a mess on our hands, all right? You’re going to fail. And yeah, your own plans are always going to fail, folks, and you’re going to have to do what Edom did. You’re going to have to come back. Could that have be an amen? Amen. You can’t dream up your own plan plans, and America’s filled with people with their own plans, they got got all figured out their way. You better find out how he says his way is. Then Isaiah 22:7, the valley of vision. Shebna, he says, talks about Shebna, a specific man that was an official in Hezekiah’s kingdom, and he said you’re going to be carried away with a mighty captivity. And Babylon came and carried away Judah into captivity just like God said. Amen. So we have a powerful God, and what you guys got to remember, he’s the same yesterday, today and forever. And if he can do things like this in the old days, he can do things like this today. But we need to pursue him. See, they didn’t pursue God. God raised up prophets to tell them and all the rest, and they just hold hum and on, and aren’t we kind of like that in America?
What happens when we make our own plans instead of waiting for God’s plan? (Isaiah 21:16-17, Isaiah 22)

Isaiah 21:16-17: For thus the LORD has said to me: “Within a year, according to the year of a hired man, all the glory of Kedar will fail; and the remainder of the number of archers, the mighty men of the people of Kedar, will be diminished; for the LORD God of Israel has spoken it.” Isaiah 22:7: It shall come to pass that your choicest valleys Shall be full of chariots, And the horsemen shall set themselves in array at the gate. Isaiah 22:15: Thus says the Lord GOD of hosts: “Go, proceed to this steward, To Shebna, who is over the house, and say: Hebrews 13:8: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.
What happened to Tyre and Sidon, and what does he say must happen before we are caught up? (Isaiah 23:1)

He says Tyre and Sidon were a strong fortress on an island that “they thought they were impregnable” until a conqueror built a causeway and destroyed it, and “they never rose again.” He says “there are so much going to happen before we’re caught up in the air to be with Christ,” and that God is going to raise up a generation to initiate these things.
What happened to Tyre and Sidon, and what does he say must happen before we are caught up? (Isaiah 23:1)

Yeah, the most exciting things in America, Christians, is are waiting for the rapture that’s supposed to come any minute. Folks, there are so much going to happen before we’re caught up in the air to be with Christ, so much powerful things, powerful things. But when you’re... ham and long as you know you’re going to die and go to heaven, you’re okay. But God’s going to raise up a generation that’s going to initiate these things, and I want to be a part of it. How about you? Hallelujah. Tyre. Isaiah 23:1, “It is laid waste, and be ashamed, Of Sidon.” So he hits Tyre and Sidon at the same time, and most of you know, you know, that was a strong fortress on an island and they thought they were impregnable, and they were for centuries. And then Alexander the Great come along, build a causeway, attacked it, destroyed it, and they never rose again. Hallelujah, just like God said. All right, it’s going to be laid waste, and Alexander the Great did it.
What happened to Tyre and Sidon, and what does he say must happen before we are caught up? (Isaiah 23:1)
Isaiah 23:1: The burden against Tyre. Wail, you ships of Tarshish! For it is laid waste, So that there is no house, no harbor; From the land of Cyprus it is revealed to them.
What is “the day of the Lord,” and what does he say will happen in it? (Isaiah 13:6-13)

He says the “burden” means divine utterance, and that in the middle of the prophecies about natural cities Isaiah switches to the prophetic day of the Lord, the time before and when He comes. He lists that it is a day of destruction from God, that men’s hearts will melt, that sinners will be destroyed for the evil they do, and that the stars, sun and moon will be darkened, so that “you’re going to look up and it’s going to be black.”
What is “the day of the Lord,” and what does he say will happen in it? (Isaiah 13:6-13)

Now, that is the prophecies, the utterances. The burden means utterance, divine utterances, prophetic utterances to these natural cities and kingdoms. But in the middle of all this he speaks of something else, and this is what God does. That’s how he hides things in his scriptures, that’s how he makes them a mystery. is He’ll be speaking directly to, like, Egypt, now all of a sudden he switches. He’ll be talking directly to the Back kingdom, of Babylon, all of a sudden he switches. All right, we’re going to go back and look at the switch. Hallelujah. Here it is: the prophetic day of the Lord. Now, remember, the day of the Lord is the time of the Lord when he comes, and also the day of the Lord is the period before he comes, and the day of the Lord is a period of what he’s doing at the time he’s doing it. So you can individually experience your day in the Lord in different aspects. We, as a generation in the present time, can experience what God is doing throughout the world in this time of the Lord, day of the Lord, and then you got him appearing. All right, so there’s several things. He’s directly going to, it it’s just clear as a bell. Okay, number one, it’s a day of destruction from God. You know, back in the ‘50s everybody was preaching that God was going to use the atomic bomb to destroy the world. Russia and America was going to get atomic warfare and they were just going to blow up each other, and they and the radiation was going to wipe out the rest of the world. Listen, God don’t need man’s help when he is going to do something. You understand that? See, this destruction comes from God and people are going to know it’s from God. All right, number two: men’s hearts will melt, they’ll be afraid and in pain in this day of the Lord. Number three: sinners will be destroyed for their... what? Evil. Not their thoughts of doing evil, but the evil that they’re doing, they evil deeds. Sinners are going to be destroyed. And that destruction, we found out, is from who? God. Number four: the stars, the sun and moon will be darkened. Interesting, very interesting. And this is where Bill O’Reilly missed it in his book, The Killing of Jesus. They look for a natural fulfillment of this when it’s supernatural. Okay, and I’ll get into it a little more.
What is “the day of the Lord,” and what does he say will happen in it? (Isaiah 13:6-13)

Isaiah 13:6-13: Wail, for the day of the LORD is at hand! It will come as destruction from the Almighty. Therefore all hands will be limp, Every man’s heart will melt, And they will be afraid. Pangs and sorrows will take hold of them; They will be in pain as a woman in childbirth; They will be amazed at one another; Their faces will be like flames. Behold, the day of the LORD comes, Cruel, with both wrath and fierce anger, To lay the land desolate; And He will destroy its sinners from it. For the stars of heaven and their constellations Will not give their light; The sun will be darkened in its going forth, And the moon will not cause its light to shine. “I will punish the world for its evil, And the wicked for their iniquity; I will halt the arrogance of the proud, And will lay low the haughtiness of the terrible. I will make a mortal more rare than fine gold, A man more than the golden wedge of Ophir. Therefore I will shake the heavens, And the earth will move out of her place, In the wrath of the LORD of hosts And in the day of His fierce anger.
Does God show mercy to His people in the day of the Lord, even those who devised their own way? (Isaiah 14:1, Romans 10:9-10)

He says Isaiah promises “mercy to Jacob and Israel,” the church, even those who “devised their own way of serving and worshiping God,” and that God “is going to be merciful to us during it,” which means “we’re not going to be destroyed.” He says strangers are joined to them as sinners wake up, admit they are wrong, and that “with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.”
Does God show mercy to His people in the day of the Lord, even those who devised their own way? (Isaiah 14:1, Romans 10:9-10)

Sun, moon and stars. In other words, the heavens are going to be what? Dark. It’s the sun that gives off light, the stars, the sun is a star, right, gives off light. The moon is a reflector of light, and if there’s no light to reflect, it goes out. So the heavens are going to be dark. You’re going to look up and it’s going to be black. Are you there? I mean, there’s some big stuff going to happen, folks, before Jesus appears, big stuff. He’s going to make his power and greatness known in the earth before he appears in the sky. Hallelujah. mercy to Jacob and Israel. Whoa, all right, now, like that, who’s Jacob? All the 12 tribes of Israel, right? The church. Who’s Israel? The church. But in this part he’s saying Jacob, the whole church, and then he uses Israel. Israel is the one that’s separated from the 10 tribes, separated from the 12, and became the northern kingdom, and the Bible says they worship God with things they devised in their own heart. And they never had one good king. They just served God the way they thought was appropriate for their mind, the heart is the mind, they made up their own way of serving and worshiping God. Do we have Christians like that today? Absolutely. One of their famous statements is, “Well, I don’t see it that way.” “Well, I believe, I I believe,” and that’s supposed to justify everything because you believe it, and that’s a tip-off that you’re talking to an Israelite Christian. Israelite. Hallelujah. But there’s mercy to the church, even to the ones who have devised their own way of serving and worshiping God. God’s going to be merciful. Oh, all right, I can handle that, hallelujah. So I don’t have to be worried about this day of destruction, do I? Do I? I don’t have to hope that Jesus going to snatch me out of it, because here it says he’s going to be merciful and kind to me in it. Are you out there? But see, people that don’t really know God and people that really don’t know the Bible, they think we got to escape this great time of the Lord where there’s destruction and God showing his power in the earth. No, folks, he is going to be merciful to us during it. That means we’re not going to be destroyed. Hallelujah, it’s going to pay to serve Jesus in that day. Number six: strangers will be joined unto them, Jacob and Israel, the ones that he’s being merciful to. Now watch. Up here, sinners are destroyed for their evil, but down here some of these sinners wake up and go, “Hey, I got to change my way.” So they admit their wrong. If we confess our sins, say with the mouth, confession is made unto salvation. You guys understand that? With the heart man believeth unto righteousness, Romans 9:10 through 11, but with the mouth confession is made into what? Salvation. Confession is made into what? Salvation. You got to admit you’re wrong. You can believe for righteousness, but until you admit you’re wrong and you repent and turn, you’re not saved. You can grace and faith said all you want to, hallelujah, you better read Romans 9:10, 11:12. It’s very powerful. He goes on to say, “How will they hear without a preacher?” How they going to believe if they don’t hear, and how they going to hear without somebody speaking it? You should be sharing the gospel of Jesus Christ to people.
Does God show mercy to His people in the day of the Lord, even those who devised their own way? (Isaiah 14:1, Romans 10:9-10)

Isaiah 14:1: For the LORD will have mercy on Jacob, and will still choose Israel, and settle them in their own land. The strangers will be joined with them, and they will cling to the house of Jacob. Romans 10:9-10: that if you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus and believe in your heart that God has raised Him from the dead, you will be saved. For with the heart one believes unto righteousness, and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation. Romans 10:14: How then shall they call on Him in whom they have not believed? And how shall they believe in Him of whom they have not heard? And how shall they hear without a preacher?
Will people still be saved in that day, and who rules over their oppressors? (Isaiah 14:2, Daniel 7)

He says many of those “destined to be destroyed” will be getting saved in that day, and that he has seen people try to kill themselves because they were afraid they could not make it through the tribulation if they missed the rapture. He says “that pre-tribulation rapture thing is very destructive,” and that the saints will rule over their oppressors, which is why we are not in heaven when that happens.
Will people still be saved in that day, and who rules over their oppressors? (Isaiah 14:2, Daniel 7)

Anyway, strangers are joined to them, but that when they admit their wrong, they repent from the wrong, they turn, these people that are destined to be destroyed, many of them are getting saved in that day. And your pre-tribulation rapture people say, “Boy, if you don’t get saved before the rapture, you’re just, you know, you’re just not going to make it, cuz it’s going to be so bad.” And I’ve had to, and I’ve seen people try to kill themselves because they’re afraid they couldn’t make it through the tribulation period if they didn’t, you know, get caught up with God and, you know, make it in a rapture. Literally, I’ve dealt with people that tried to commit suicide, that uh that pre-tribulation rapture thing is very destructive. You know, I deal with people all the time and I know the destruction in it. Anyway, I’m just throwing that out. they rule over their oppressors. Now, how you going to rule over your oppressors if you’re up in heaven? Oppressors is the tyrant. Okay, and remember Daniel said that we would be under our enemy for a season, and then then we get to rule over. The saints of the Most High will rule. Are you there? You can go back to the Daniel lessons and learn all this. So the bottom line is the scriptures are uniform throughout. All right, you don’t have to rubber band scriptures and bend them and stretch them, they’re uniform throughout. So these are seven things that are going to happen. All right, now we’re going to deal with men’s hearts and the stars. I’m going to expand on it.
Will people still be saved in that day, and who rules over their oppressors? (Isaiah 14:2, Daniel 7)

Isaiah 14:2: Then people will take them and bring them to their place, and the house of Israel will possess them for servants and maids in the land of the LORD; they will take them captive whose captives they were, and rule over their oppressors. Daniel 7:18: But the saints of the Most High shall receive the kingdom, and possess the kingdom forever, even forever and ever.’
Was the star the wise men followed a supernatural event, and what does it say about signs in the sun, moon and stars? (Luke 21:25, Matthew 2)

He says Luke 21:25 speaks of “signs in the sun, moon and stars,” and that the star the wise men followed could not have been the sun or a normal star because it appeared, disappeared and reappeared over a specific house and “only the wise men saw it.” He says “it’s a supernatural event,” so God can do a separate supernatural thing with the sun, moon and stars before Christ comes, and “this stuff’s got to happen before Christ comes.”
Was the star the wise men followed a supernatural event, and what does it say about signs in the sun, moon and stars? (Luke 21:25, Matthew 2)

Luke 21:25, “There will be signs in the sun, moon and stars.” Okay, Jesus said, Jesus is talking here. Okay, the wise men followed a star. He says a big key is letting the Holy Ghost put in us a desire for Jesus, not for what we can get from Him. He says “it’s not faith that causes people to live right, it’s not grace… it’s the judgment,” quotes “let grace be shown to the wicked” and “yet he will not learn righteousness,” and says “this flattering gospel of just grace and faith has destroyed the church in America.” He closes with “your dead shall live” and a restoration of the church and the nations.
What does desire for Jesus have to do with worship, and why do God’s judgments teach righteousness? (Isaiah 26:8-19)

Now here is a very important part. they they That’s what worship was about this morning. “I desire you in the night, by my spirit I seek you early.” Morning and night, I desire you, I desire you. I’m not looking for a better job, I’m not looking for a ministry in the church, Jesus, I desire you. Powerful. Most people have never experienced what the woman with the alabaster box experience. People that desire Jesus, they have a drive to come to church, they have a drive to read the Bible, they have a drive to pray. Why? They have a desire that compels them and motivates them, and who is that desire about? Jesus. Not what I can get from him, not my prayer petition, but just him. And so we need, and this is where the American Christian has really blown it since I came into the kingdom, is we haven’t maintained an authoritative position in our government for Bible morality. Because because it’s the judgments that teach righteousness. And folks, that’s the way it is in the kingdom. God wants to correct us, and this this flattering gospel of just grace and faith has destroyed the church in America and weakened it tremendously. Are you out there? “You’re dead shall live and they shall arise.” And it says a lot of good stuff. I just took some excerpts out of this, it’s very powerful. “Your dead shall live and they shall arise.” See, these people in the world, they going to live and they will arise. As Christians, are going to live and we’re going to arise. The whole purpose of God is for us to, what, live and arise out of trespasses and sin and live a life for Christ. Can I hear an amen? Now, is there a big thing coming up here according to Isaiah? Yes. And you younger ones have a chance to be in part of this. I’ve been in part of this, but it’s obvious I’m going to miss out on some of this good stuff here. But you young people have a tremendous thing to look forward to: the the restoration of the church in America, the restoration of the nation in America, the restoration of the nations of the world, God showing himself that he’s God in a powerful way. You may get to see, and you will see, a lot more of that, and I’ve seen, and I’ve showed you that we’ve be we’ve been able to see it since Azusa, in fact since Luther put his thesis on the wall. Isaiah 26:9: With my soul I have desired You in the night, Yes, by my spirit within me I will seek You early; For when Your judgments are in the earth, The inhabitants of the world will learn righteousness. Luke 7:37-38: And behold, a woman in the city who was a sinner, when she knew that Jesus sat at the table in the Pharisee’s house, brought an alabaster flask of fragrant oil, and stood at His feet behind Him weeping; and she began to wash His feet with her tears, and wiped them with the hair of her head; and she kissed His feet and anointed them with the fragrant oil.
What does he say a “burden” is in the prophets?

He says “the burden means utterance, divine utterances, prophetic utterances” to natural cities and kingdoms. He says God sometimes hides a second message in them: “that’s how he makes them a mystery.”
Why does he say prophecy switches from nations to the day of the Lord?
He says God will be “speaking directly to like Egypt” and then “all of a sudden he switches.” He says “that’s how he hides things in his scriptures, that’s how he makes them a mystery.”
What does he say “the day of the Lord” means?

He says it is the time when the Lord comes, “the period before he comes,” and “a period of what he’s doing at the time he’s doing it.” He says each generation can experience what God is doing in its day of the Lord.
Does he say man will destroy the world with weapons?

He says that back in the 1950s everyone preached God would use the atomic bomb to destroy the world, and answers “God don’t need man’s help when he is going to do something.” He says this destruction “comes from God and people are going to know it’s from God.”
What does he mean by an “Israelite Christian”?

He says Israel was the northern kingdom that “worship God with things they devised in their own heart,” never had a good king, and served God “the way they thought was appropriate for their mind.” He says a tip-off is the statement “well, I believe,” as if believing justifies everything.
Does he say believers must escape the great day of the Lord?

He says people who don’t know the Bible “think we got to escape this great time of the Lord,” but “he is going to be merciful to us during it, that means we’re not going to be destroyed.” He says “it’s going to pay to serve Jesus in that day.”
Why does he say we must admit we are wrong?
He says “you can believe for righteousness, but until you admit you’re wrong and you repent and turn, you’re not saved.” He cites that with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.
What does he say about the pre-tribulation rapture teaching?

He says people tell others they will not make it if they are not saved before the rapture, and that he has dealt with people who tried to commit suicide because of it. He says “that pre-tribulation rapture thing is very destructive.”
Why does he say you do not have to bend the scriptures?
He says “the scriptures are uniform throughout,” so “you don’t have to rubber band scriptures and bend them and stretch them.” He says there are seven things that will happen in that day.
Why does he say the wise men’s star could not be a normal star?

He says the nearest star is the sun and if it were moved closer we would boil, so they could not follow it to a specific house, and it disappeared and reappeared. He says it could have been an angel or “a little sun” God made, and that “it’s a supernatural event.”
What does he say about the word of knowledge?

He says it was added in the late 1940s: people “actually could foretell people’s lives, tell them about themselves accurately,” and God would heal or transform them. He says it brought a powerful presence and worship, with churches praising God for an hour.
What does he say about the 1960s outpouring in the denominations?

He says God poured out His Spirit on Episcopalians, Anglicans, Presbyterians, Lutherans, Methodists and Baptists, and in 1967 on the Catholic Church, and “he didn’t ask the Pope’s permission or anybody’s permission.” He says the Jesus people came along in the 1970s.
Does he say God loves people of every nation?
He says “God loves everybody in the earth. He created them and wants to bring them in,” and lists Eskimos, Mongolians and the people of the islands of the sea. He also says God loves Muslims.
What does he say about ministers in that day?

He says “ministers are going to be nothing” and “we need to learn to be like John the Baptist: we must decrease and he must increase.” He says too many ministers are letting people worship them and put their trust in them.
How does he sum up the gospel?

He says Jesus was born of a virgin, did signs and wonders, preached the kingdom of God, laid down His life, rose from the grave and ascended for the sins of the world, and “if you call on him he will forgive you, cleanse you and empower you to become a son of God.”

p: In “Resurrection Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from 1 Corinthians 15:35 on, where Paul answers how the dead are raised and with what body. He follows Paul’s common-sense examples of seeds, flesh and the sun, moon and stars, then describes the supernatural body raised in power, and Jesus as the last Adam who gives life now. He ends with the change at the last trumpet, Jesus’ return, and letting God be God about the end times.
How are the dead raised, and with what body do they come?

He says Paul explains the resurrection of the dead in great detail starting at 1 Corinthians 15:35, and that Paul saw Jesus personally after He ascended. The two questions are honest ones from people with common sense, he says, like the Sadducees, who knew the body decayed, and Paul answers by calling them “fool,” which means stupid or without reason, and by arguing from common sense and then Scripture.
How are the dead raised, and with what body do they come?

We are in 1 Corinthians 15:35. He’s going to explain the resurrection of the dead in great detail here. He saw Jesus personally after Jesus had ascended. I know that he has much more clout, much more understanding, much more truth than any author in this present day. Could that be an amen? And we need to get what Paul is saying in the depths of our heart. Here he starts out in verse 35 by saying, “But some will say, ‘How are the dead raised? And with what body do they come?’” These are two good questions. Now this [unclear] is not like some among you that didn’t believe in truth. This [unclear] are people that have common sense questions about biblical matters that they cannot seem to embrace because they just don’t fit into the natural understanding of the human mind. All right, so they’re saying, “Okay, we get resurrected. What do we look like when we come out? What kind of form do we have, and what is this?” See, it’s a good question: “How are the dead raised, and with what body do they come?” Excellent question. Just like when the Sadducees and these people that could not understand how you could have life after death. You see, they know the body decayed and went into the grave, and back in those days there were no caskets; you went into the grave and the worms ate you and the body consumed itself and you wound up dust. And so they challenged Jesus by saying, you know, “How can there be a resurrection of the dead when this woman had seven husbands? You know, which husband is going to be her husband up in heaven?” See, they lacked understanding in spiritual things, but they didn’t lack understanding in natural things, and it created questions in them. Are some of you like that? Yeah. So some of us have questions, and they’re honest questions, but watch how Paul answers. Okay. “Fool.” Fool. Now the word “fool” means several things. It means you’re stupid, you know, and that’s how I feel when I get in the presence of God and He’s talking to me. I feel real stupid, ignorant, same thing. Egotistical: you exaggerate your selfish, self-centered intellect, your own importance, above what is common sense around you. Now that’s good stuff. Now that fits in, you know; we exaggerate our intellect above. And Paul is saying you’re foolish, but also part of the definition of “fool” is without reason or without common sense. He said you guys are missing common sense here. Let’s look at this through common sense. And remember, Paul approaches everything through common sense and then Scriptures. You noticed that in 1 Corinthians, right? And that’s what threw me off for a while. I thought his common sense were Scriptures, when he’s just illustrating things in life, and they may not be in Scripture at all, but they work because they are common sense. Yeah. Okay, how many can say, “Well, okay, I could be without common sense in some of these areas, I could be a fool”? You’re halfway there. See, when we think of ourselves more highly than we ought, we open ourself up to a fall.
How are the dead raised, and with what body do they come?

1 Corinthians 15:35: But someone will say, “How are the dead raised up? And with what body do they come?” Matthew 22:23-28: The same day the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Him and asked Him, saying: “Teacher, Moses said that if a man dies, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother. Now there were with us seven brothers. The first died after he had married, and having no offspring, left his wife to his brother. Likewise the second also, and the third, even to the seventh. Last of all the woman died also. Therefore, in the resurrection, whose wife of the seven will she be? For they all had her.” 1 Corinthians 15:36: Foolish one, what you sow is not made alive unless it dies.
What does a seed teach us about the resurrection?

He says Paul’s first example is plants: a seed has to die before it can live again and produce a body and fruit. He says the seed germinates and comes alive on the inside first, and that is how we start, “on the inside first,” then comes the outward fruit, and every seed gets its own body.
What does a seed teach us about the resurrection?

So now let’s listen to Paul. He’s going to explain the resurrection, how it’s happening and what body do they come up with. “That which you sow is not made alive except it dies.” Now he’s talking about plant seeds. Okay, example number one, he’s going to use plants. He’s going to use human, uh, fleshly bodies, and he’s going to use the celestial bodies, the universe. Example number one: “What you sow, you do not sow that living body that shall be, but bare grain,” naked grain, just the grain, just the seed, “perhaps wheat or some other.” Now you see pictures up here. I have a tomato plant. That’s the body right here, that’s the living body, and it has a stalk and it holds these tomatoes and it produces tomatoes. But to the left of that is a living seed. That seed’s not dead yet. And see, he’s using common sense. The seed has to die before it can live again and produce a body and fruit, isn’t that right? See, he’s approaching it from a very common-sense approach. Over here on the left is a dead tomato seed that if you put it in the ground, and the right temperature and the right moisture, it will germinate, come alive on the inside first, and that’s how we start, on the inside first. Then comes forth the outward fruit and the body. “But God gives it a body as it pleased Him, and to every seed his own body.” And this is where the evolutionist just can’t figure this out. God made it at the beginning that like kinds produce like kinds; they don’t produce half and half. All right, you mate a snake with a bird, you won’t come up with a flying snake. You won’t come up with anything. It won’t germinate, it won’t work. Got it?
What does a seed teach us about the resurrection?

1 Corinthians 15:36-38: Foolish one, what you sow is not made alive unless it dies. And what you sow, you do not sow that body that shall be, but mere grain—perhaps wheat or some other grain. But God gives it a body as He pleases, and to each seed its own body.
What do the different kinds of flesh and the sun, moon and stars show about the resurrection?

He says Paul’s second and third common-sense examples are that all flesh is not the same, and that celestial and earthly bodies each have their own glory. He says the sun, the moon and the stars each have a different look, glory and purpose, and that Paul is using common sense before he has quoted a Scripture, and he applies the first example to evolution and the age of the earth.
What do the different kinds of flesh and the sun, moon and stars show about the resurrection?

Now, example number two: “All flesh is not the same flesh, but one of flesh of men, of beast, fish, and birds.” Okay, that’s just common sense. We know that horses have flesh, but they’re not human beings; fish have flesh, but they’re not horses. Okay, and if the evolutionist would just use some common sense, they wouldn’t come up with these ridiculous billions-of-years-old nonsense. Every time they come into a problem, they have to make the earth older to solve it. You ever notice that? See, when I was in school, the earth was a million years old, and they made movies on it: 1 million B.C., 1 million B.C. Then they run into problems, so they went to 2 million, 5 million, 10 million, now we’re at 4 billion. Every time they run into a problem, just solve it by extending the age of creation. “There is also celestial, heavenly bodies, and terrestrial, earthly bodies, but the glory of this celestial is one, and the glory of the terrestrial is another.” Okay, we got the universe up there, we got the earth, the planets, everything, and he goes on to talk about the sun, the moon and the stars have all a different structure, a different look, a different way. All right. He’s just using what? Common sense. See, to these people who have these questions, he’s approaching them first with just common sense. Hadn’t he quoted a Scripture yet? I love this guy. Any educated person that really learned in school could understand this stuff. Any uneducated person who dropped out of school can understand this stuff, isn’t that right? It’s just common sense; you can’t argue with it. Yeah, they’re all different. They’re all different. Now he’s going to, there’s the sun, the moon, the stars, all in one, there’s the moon, the sun behind it, and so forth. They all have a different look, a different glory, a different purpose.
What do the different kinds of flesh and the sun, moon and stars show about the resurrection?

1 Corinthians 15:39-41: All flesh is not the same flesh, but there is one kind of flesh of men, another flesh of animals, another of fish, and another of birds. There are also celestial bodies and terrestrial bodies; but the glory of the celestial is one, and the glory of the terrestrial is another. There is one glory of the sun, another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for one star differs from another star in glory.
What kind of body will we have in the resurrection?

He says the body is sown in corruption and raised in incorruption, sown in dishonor and raised in honor, sown in weakness and raised in power, and sown a natural body and raised a spiritual body. “Spiritual,” he says, means supernatural, so the body comes out of the grave a supernatural body that does not decay anymore and lives forever.
What kind of body will we have in the resurrection?

And then he plainly says, “So also is the resurrection of the dead.” You see, he made his three common-sense examples, and then he says this is the way the resurrection of the dead is. “The body is sown in corruption”: decay. We all know that when you take your last breath, you start rotting. I don’t care how beautiful you kept yourself while you were alive, you start rotting immediately. In three days no one wants to be around you. We’re a decaying people. “It is raised in incorruption,” or eternal, or perpetual, never-ending. You see, “it is sown in dishonor, it is raised in honor; it is sown in weakness, it is raised in power.” Supernatural power is how it’s raised. “It is sown a natural body, it is raised a spiritual body.” The word “spiritual” means not human, not natural, not of the natural things of this universe; it’s supernatural. So the body comes out of the grave a what? Supernatural body that doesn’t decay anymore, that lives forever.
What kind of body will we have in the resurrection?

1 Corinthians 15:42-44: So also is the resurrection of the dead. The body is sown in corruption, it is raised in incorruption. It is sown in dishonor, it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness, it is raised in power. It is sown a natural body, it is raised a spiritual body. There is a natural body, and there is a spiritual body.
Did Jesus have blood in His body after He rose from the dead?

He says Jesus’ blood drained out when He died, and when He came out of the grave the holes were still in His hands and side but no blood dripped, because He has a supernatural, spiritual body and does not need blood. He says the saints of old who rose with Him came out the same way, since God can get wherever the dust is.
Did Jesus have blood in His body after He rose from the dead?

Now here’s Jesus Christ. I used Him because He came out of the grave. His blood drained out, He died, He had no blood in Him. Now He was dead, He comes out of the grave, and lo and behold, the holes are still in His hands and in His side. They’re still there, but there’s no blood dripping out. Why? Because He has a supernatural body now, a spiritual body. He don’t need blood. See, us natural people need blood. The Bible says blood is the life of the flesh. We need that blood circulating through us to get the oxygen and the minerals and the vitamins where they should be so our body functions. But when Jesus rose, see, He didn’t have any blood, and He didn’t have a decaying body anymore. There was a transition in that resurrection, and the saints of old that rose with Him at that same time, they came out the same way. Well, you say, “How in the world? Those saints of old, you know, they went to dust, the worms ate them and pooped them out, and, you know, how does God, how’s that work?” Listen, He can get wherever that dust is. We go back to just a handful of dust. You know, I mean, as big as you are, after a year or so you’re just a handful of nothing. That’s it. Are you there?
Did Jesus have blood in His body after He rose from the dead?

John 20:27: Then He said to Thomas, “Reach your finger here, and look at My hands; and reach your hand here, and put it into My side. Do not be unbelieving, but believing.” Leviticus 17:11: For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you upon the altar to make atonement for your souls; for it is the blood that makes atonement for the soul.’
Will a sick or frail body be raised as a spiritual body?

He says no matter how frail or sick this body is, it is going to be raised a spiritual body, and a person who accepted Christ and wasted away will be glad, “because certainly you don’t want to come back with that old body.” He uses a person in the last stage of AIDS as his example, and in this section he also makes his own statements about homosexuality, AIDS statistics and government policy.
Will a sick or frail body be raised as a spiritual body?

Now, He came out with a supernatural body, so did the saints of old who rose with Him. Here is a guy dying of AIDS in the last stage of AIDS. You know, the immunity system’s broken down, they’re just wasting away, sores come upon them, it’s a horrible death, and anyone promoting homosexuality is sentencing people to a horrible death. 91% of all people that have AIDS are homosexuals or bisexuals. The rest just happen to get it because their parents, their children and their parents pass it on to them somehow, and blood transfusions and so forth, dirty needles and whatever. But 91%, when you agree that homosexuality is an acceptable lifestyle, you are sentencing people to this kind of death right here, and there is no plague on earth that our government does not quarantine you from except AIDS. Are you looking at me? Yeah, it is sad that 2% of the people in America can have that big an influence on America’s thinking. But anyway, this guy, let’s say he accepted Christ, and I know some that did, and they wasted away. God didn’t heal them and they died. But as frail as this body is, as sick as it is, it’s going to be raised a spiritual body, and he’s going to be glad, because certainly you don’t want to come back with that old body. Amen. You see?
Who is the last Adam, and what is the tree of life?

He says Paul writes that the first Adam became a living being and the last Adam became a life-giving spirit, which means Jesus is more than a prophet or a good man: He gives life. He says Adam’s mistake was embracing the tree of knowledge of good and evil over the tree of life, that Jesus is that tree of life, and that you can have knowledge with life.
Who is the last Adam, and what is the tree of life?

Now he’s going to go into the spiritual, the Scriptures. This is his style: “And so it is written.” Now where is it written in the Bible, the Scriptures, that “the first Adam became a living being” and “the last Adam became a life-giving spirit”? A life-giving spirit. Wow. Jesus is more than a prophet. Jesus is more than a good man. Jesus gives you life. And you can accept religion if you want to, but I like the life. Adam made his mistake by embracing the tree of knowledge of good and evil over the tree of life. Jesus is that tree of life. And you can get so into the knowledge of God’s Word that you are worthless; you’re just a proud person throwing Scriptures out that you don’t even know. But you can get that knowledge with life, and that life comes from Jesus Christ. All right, the Scripture, Genesis 2:7, “God formed man out of the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living soul,” or living being. It says here in Corinthians, you see, that’s the first Adam. Now the last Adam, Jesus, is a life-giving Spirit.
Who is the last Adam, and what is the tree of life?

1 Corinthians 15:45: And so it is written, “The first man Adam became a living being.” The last Adam became a life-giving spirit. Genesis 2:7: And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living being.
Do we have to wait for the end time to be resurrected and have life?

He says no: there are two kinds of deaths, so “I don’t have to wait to die and be resurrected at the end time to find life.” We were dead in trespasses and sin, and when we come to Jesus He resurrects us and makes us alive, forgiving all trespasses, which is why anyone in Christ is a new creature.
Do we have to wait for the end time to be resurrected and have life?

For as the Father, in John 5:21, raises the dead. Who raises the dead? The Father. See, you can’t get away from this plurality, Godhead, that is one, all through the Scriptures. You can’t get away from the fact that there’s a plurality in the Godhead, yet that the God is what? One God. “Raised us from the dead, and even so the Son gives life to whom He will.” The Father raises the dead and gives those dead life, and Jesus raises the dead and gives life to whom He wills. So we’re talking about two kinds of deaths here. Do you see that? See, I don’t have to wait to die and be resurrected at the end time to find life. I can die now, and Jesus will resurrect me and give me what? Life. Okay, are you watching this? Are you ready for this? Colossians 2:13, Paul said, “You being dead in your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, He has” what? Made alive. See, He gave you life. “He has made alive together with Him, having forgiven you” what? Of a few sins? All sins, all trespass, all break. Trespass means you violated the law. Doesn’t matter if it’s one or 100, He forgives you of all. You see, so Jesus, so we were dead in what? Trespasses and sin. We come to Jesus and He what? Resurrects us. That’s why the Bible says, “If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature; old things are passed away, behold, all things are made new.” Why? He resurrected us out of trespasses and sin, which we were dead in. Got it? It’s powerful. See.
Do we have to wait for the end time to be resurrected and have life?

John 5:21: For as the Father raises the dead and gives life to them, even so the Son gives life to whom He will. Colossians 2:13: And you, being dead in your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, He has made alive together with Him, having forgiven you all trespasses, 2 Corinthians 5:17: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.
What does it mean to bear the image of the heavenly Man?

He says the spiritual is not first but the natural, and afterward the spiritual: the first man was of the earth, made of dust, and the second man is from heaven. He says the second Adam is God Himself, to give us life, and as we have borne the image of the man of dust we shall also bear the image of the heavenly Man, and that Jesus’ character is not what we were brought out of.
What does it mean to bear the image of the heavenly Man?

Now “however, the spiritual is not first, but the natural, and afterward the spiritual. The first man was of the earth,” made of dust. “The second man is from heaven,” Jesus. God, the second Adam, is God Himself to give us life. Powerful. “As we have borne the image of the man of dust, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly Man.” Now, would Jesus be a homosexual? Would Jesus be an adulterer? Would He commit incest? Would He rob? No. See, that’s not His character, and we were brought out of trespasses and sin to become a new creature like Him. Now, not at the resurrection, isn’t that good? Powerful. Does He have the power to back it up? Absolutely. If we can get past religion and our own beliefs and our own shortcomings of common sense, we can experience this stuff.
What does it mean to bear the image of the heavenly Man?

1 Corinthians 15:46-49: However, the spiritual is not first, but the natural, and afterward the spiritual. The first man was of the earth, made of dust; the second Man is the Lord from heaven. As was the man of dust, so also are those who are made of dust; and as is the heavenly Man, so also are those who are heavenly. And as we have borne the image of the man of dust, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly Man.
Can flesh and blood inherit the kingdom of God?

He says 2 Corinthians 3:18 says we are changed into the same image by this life-giving Jesus, and that Jesus is in heaven but His Spirit is on earth, so His presence is still with us. He then turns to the mystery of the resurrection, where Paul says in 1 Corinthians 15:50 that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God.
Can flesh and blood inherit the kingdom of God?

2 Corinthians 3:18, “We all,” how many of us, “with an open face beholding it as in a glass the glory of the Lord,” the Word of God, “are changed into the same image.” Now look at this, this is tremendous. We are changed into the same image. How are we changed? By this life-giving Jesus. See, we’re changed the same, “even as by the Spirit of the Lord.” There’s that third part of the plurality, Godhead. Yes, Jesus is in heaven, but His Spirit is on earth. He poured His Spirit back upon the earth, so His presence is what? Still with us. Now he’s going to give us the mystery of the resurrection. “Flesh and blood,” he says in verse 50, 1 Corinthians 15, “cannot inherit the kingdom of God.” You see, you can’t inherit the kingdom of God if you got flesh and blood.
Can flesh and blood inherit the kingdom of God?

2 Corinthians 3:18: But we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, just as by the Spirit of the Lord. 1 Corinthians 15:50: Now this I say, brethren, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God; nor does corruption inherit incorruption.
What does “we shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed” mean?

He says we are in the kingdom now, but there is a time when it will be a real thing ruling the earth, and flesh and blood cannot inherit that. “Sleep” means die, and the Bible uses it because we do not stay in the grave: whether sinner or saint it is a temporary period. Those in the grave will come out with a new spiritual body, and those alive will be changed “in a moment and a twinkling of an eye at the last trumpet.”
What does “we shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed” mean?

In this revealed kingdom that’s coming, we are in the kingdom, don’t get me wrong. We are in the kingdom, but there is a time when that kingdom is going to be a real thing in the earth and not just in our hearts. It’s going to be ruling the earth. Okay, so flesh and blood can’t inherit that, “nor does corruption, decay, inherit incorruption,” or eternity. I’m going to tell you a secret, Paul says, a hidden secret. I’m going to tell you something nobody else knows. I was called to the third heaven, and I know something you don’t know. Well, he got my attention when I read that: “We shall not all sleep.” What’s the other word for sleep? Die. Why does he use the word “sleep”? Because we don’t stay in that grave, folks. Whether you are a sinner or a saint, that’s a temporary period of time. You’re going to come out, just like people wake out of their sleep. So the Bible uses the word “sleep” for death a lot, because it explains that we are in the ground temporarily; we’re only dead physically temporarily. Got it? Now, “but we shall all be changed”: those that are in the grave come out, spiritual body, a new body, no flesh, no blood, no decaying flesh, I should say. “We who are alive”: there’s a group of people going to be alive. Now let me tell you, we who are alive are going to be changed just like those in the grave came out of the grave. We’re going to be, only we’re not going to die, we’re going to be changed just like that, faster than I can snap my finger, bam, your blood’s gone, your skin is changed, you have an eternal body now. Just like that, pow. Hallelujah. “In a moment and a twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet, for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be” what? Changed. And that’s why Christ came in the first place. He wants to change us from a sinner to one living righteous, and when we get resurrected in that last day, He wants to change us into an everlasting body that will never die again and will live with Him forever. Hallelujah. So Jesus, when He came out of the grave, did not have this decaying flesh anymore, neither did He have blood. He had a supernatural body. I can handle that.
What does “we shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed” mean?

2 Corinthians 12:2: I know a man in Christ who fourteen years ago—whether in the body I do not know, or whether out of the body I do not know, God knows—such a one was caught up to the third heaven. 1 Corinthians 15:51-52: Behold, I tell you a mystery: We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed— in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed.
What will we be like when Jesus appears?

He says 1 John 3:2 tells us we are sons of God now, and it does not yet appear what we shall be, “but we know this, that when He shall appear, we shall be like Him.” He says that means we will have a supernatural body like His, with no more blood and an eternal body.
What will we be like when Jesus appears?

Hallelujah. Now we understand what 1 John 3:2 says: “Beloved, now we are sons of God,” we get an inheritance now, “and it does not yet appear what we shall be,” or we don’t know yet what we shall be, “but we know this, that when He shall appear, we shall be like Him, for we shall see Him as He is.” We’re going to be what? Like Him. We’re going to have that [unclear] body now. No more blood. We got an eternal body, and we are going to see the same body coming out of heaven. Isn’t that beautiful? Oh, I think it’s tremendous. Hallelujah. We’re going to be like Him. What? We’re going to have a supernatural body like He has.
What will we be like when Jesus appears?
1 John 3:2: Beloved, now we are children of God; and it has not yet been revealed what we shall be, but we know that when He is revealed, we shall be like Him, for we shall see Him as He is.
What does the Bible say about Jesus’ return, the trumpet and the judgment?

He reads 1 Thessalonians 4:16, Matthew 16:27 and 24:31 and 2 Thessalonians 1:7, saying the Lord will descend with a shout and the trumpet of God, the dead in Christ will rise first, and the Son of Man will reward every man according to his works. He says the sheep and the goats will be separated, and that the goats who mistreated people, especially God’s people, will go into the fire reserved for Satan and his angels, so “you better be treating people good.”
What does the Bible say about Jesus’ return, the trumpet and the judgment?

Speaking of the resurrection, the Lord Himself, in 1 Thessalonians 4:16, “shall descend from heaven with a shout, and with the voice of the archangel, and the trumpet of God, and the dead in Christ shall rise first. Then we who are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air, and so shall we ever be with the Lord.” Matthew 16:27, “For the Son of Man shall come in the glory of His Father with His angels, and then at that time He shall reward every man according to his works.” Matthew 24:31, “He shall send His angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together His elect from the four winds, from the four corners of the earth.” It’s going to happen. “When the Son of Man shall come in His glory, and all the holy angels with Him, then shall He sit on the throne of His glory, and before Him shall be gathered all nations, and He will separate them one from another, as a shepherd divides his sheep from the goats.” And it goes on to say that the goats, they that have mistreated people, especially God’s people, will go into the fire that’s reserved for Satan and his angels. That’s what it says. So you better be treating people good, especially God’s people. I’m telling you, they may be young believers and got a lot of flaws; love them. Hallelujah. The rewards are worth it. Could I hear an amen? 2 Thessalonians 1:7, “The Lord Jesus shall be revealed from heaven with His mighty angels, in flaming fire, taking vengeance on them that know not God and that do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Wow. “Who shall be punished with everlasting destruction.” Is it possible I can be a believer and not an obeyer?
What does the Bible say about Jesus’ return, the trumpet and the judgment?

1 Thessalonians 4:16-17: For the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God. And the dead in Christ will rise first. Then we who are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air. And thus we shall always be with the Lord. Matthew 16:27: For the Son of Man will come in the glory of His Father with His angels, and then He will reward each according to his works. Matthew 24:31: And He will send His angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they will gather together His elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other. Matthew 25:31-33: “When the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the holy angels with Him, then He will sit on the throne of His glory. All the nations will be gathered before Him, and He will separate them one from another, as a shepherd divides his sheep from the goats. And He will set the sheep on His right hand, but the goats on the left. 2 Thessalonians 1:7-9: and to give you who are troubled rest with us when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with His mighty angels, in flaming fire taking vengeance on those who do not know God, and on those who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ. These shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of His power,
When will death be swallowed up in victory?

He says it is possible to be a believer and not an obeyer, as with the Pharisees and Sadducees, who could quote Scripture and preach yet would not obey. He then reads that when this corruptible puts on incorruption and this mortal puts on immortality, death is swallowed up in victory, which he says is quoted from Isaiah 25:8.
When will death be swallowed up in victory?

Yeah. Is there an example in the Bible of that? Yeah. What’s the big one? The Pharisees and the Sadducees, the Jews during Jesus’s day. He looked at them and said, “You’re the children of the Devil, because you do the deeds of Satan.” And yet they were believers. They could quote Scripture, they preached, and they made converts, and yet they would not obey, and He says you’re going to be punished too. Revelation 1:7, “He is coming with clouds, and every eye will see Him.” “For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.” Mortal is a dying body; immortality is a non-dying body. “And when this corruptible has put on incorruption, and this mortal has put on immortality, then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, ‘Death is swallowed up in victory,’” which he is quoting from Isaiah 25:8, where Jesus is talking Himself through the prophet and says, “I will swallow death up in victory, and I will wipe all tears from their eyes.” There in Isaiah, hallelujah. Jesus is going to do it all.
When will death be swallowed up in victory?

John 8:44: You are of your father the devil, and the desires of your father you want to do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and does not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks from his own resources, for he is a liar and the father of it. Revelation 1:7: Behold, He is coming with clouds, and every eye will see Him, even they who pierced Him. And all the tribes of the earth will mourn because of Him. Even so, Amen. 1 Corinthians 15:53-54: For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality. So when this corruptible has put on incorruption, and this mortal has put on immortality, then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written: “Death is swallowed up in victory.” Isaiah 25:8: He will swallow up death forever, And the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from all faces; The rebuke of His people He will take away from all the earth; For the LORD has spoken.
What is the last enemy overcome, and can we chart the end times?

He says there is something that transpires before God manifests His kingdom and puts enemies under, and “these people that try to put all their little charts together are way off.” He says nobody understood the procedure when Jesus came the first time until it happened, so “we need to let God be God,” and if we love Him we will be like Him when He comes.
What is the last enemy overcome, and can we chart the end times?

Right now, what’s the last enemy that is overcome? So all the other enemies now are what? Overcome. Common sense: is Satan an enemy? Yeah. So see, there’s something that transpires before this. God’s going to manifest His kingdom and enemies are going to be put under. Are the children of the wicked one our enemy, according to Matthew, the parables? Yeah. See, something’s going to transpire that we don’t understand yet, and these people that try to put all their little charts together are way off. And how do I know? I try to put my chart together, ain’t no chart. He’s going to do His thing, and He’s going to reveal it when He does it. Ain’t that right? See, and I can prove it. When Jesus came the first time, did they have any understanding of the procedure and the sequence that was going to happen? When Jesus was here for 33 and a half years, they understood beans. It’s as He did it, they go, “Oh, that was written. Oh, this is that which was. Oh, this is that which was written.” I mean, we need to let God be God and stop playing these little God things that we do down here like we have some knowledge. How, you know, He’s capable of wrapping this end time up just perfectly. Hallelujah. Yeah, and if we love Him, we’re going to be like Him when He comes, and everything’s going to be fine.
What is the last enemy overcome, and can we chart the end times?
1 Corinthians 15:26: The last enemy that will be destroyed is death. Matthew 13:38: The field is the world, the good seeds are the sons of the kingdom, but the tares are the sons of the wicked one.
Why does he trust Paul’s explanation of the resurrection?
He says Paul saw Jesus personally after Jesus had ascended, so he has “much more clout, much more understanding, much more truth than any author in this present day.”
Why did the Sadducees question the resurrection?

He says they knew the body decayed and went into the grave, so they asked Jesus whose husband a woman with seven husbands would be in heaven. “They lacked understanding in spiritual things, but they didn’t lack understanding in natural things.”

He says it can mean stupid or ignorant, egotistical (exaggerating your selfish, self-centered intellect and your own importance), and without reason or common sense. He adds that when we think of ourselves more highly than we ought, “we open ourself up to a fall.”
Does Paul argue from common sense or from Scripture?

He says Paul approaches everything through common sense and then Scriptures, and that it threw him for a while because he thought Paul’s common sense were Scriptures when Paul was just illustrating things in life that work.
Why does he say a seed has to die?

He says the seed has to die before it can live again and produce a body and fruit, and that a dead seed put in the ground with the right temperature and moisture will germinate and come alive on the inside first.
What does he say about evolution and the age of the earth?

He says evolutionists keep extending the age of the earth every time they run into a problem, from a million years when he was in school to “4 billion” now, and that if they used common sense they would not come up with it. He also says God made like kinds produce like kinds.
He says the word “spiritual” means not human, not natural, not of the natural things of this universe; it is supernatural.
How can God raise people whose bodies turned to dust?
He says God can get wherever that dust is, and that the saints of old who rose with Jesus came out with a supernatural body the same way He did.
He says Adam embraced the tree of knowledge of good and evil over the tree of life, and that Jesus is that tree of life.

He says you cannot get away from the plurality in the Godhead all through the Scriptures, “yet that the God is what? One God.” He points to the Father raising the dead and the Son giving life to whom He will.
What does it mean that Jesus resurrects us out of trespasses and sin?

He says we were dead in trespasses and sin, and when we come to Jesus He resurrects us and makes us alive, forgiving all trespasses, whether it is one or 100. That is why anyone in Christ is a new creature.
Why does the Bible call death “sleep”?
He says it is because we do not stay in the grave: whether you are a sinner or a saint, it is a temporary period, and we come out just like people wake out of their sleep.
Can a person be a believer and not an obeyer?

He says yes, and that the biggest example in the Bible is the Pharisees and the Sadducees, who could quote Scripture, preach and make converts yet would not obey, and Jesus told them they would be punished too.
Can we put the end-time events on a chart?
He says no: “these people that try to put all their little charts together are way off,” and when he tried to put his chart together, “ain’t no chart.” God will reveal it when He does it.

items.d: In “Resurrection Pt. 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer continues from 1 Corinthians 15, explaining why the sting of death is sin and the strength of sin is the law, and what the first resurrection and second death…
p: In “Resurrection Pt. 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer continues from 1 Corinthians 15, explaining why the sting of death is sin and the strength of sin is the law, and what the first resurrection and second death are. He then walks through Romans 7 and 8, teaching that Paul separates sin from the believer so Jesus can put it to death without destroying us. He closes with putting off the old man, working and disciplining ourselves, and reigning in life now through Jesus Christ.
Why is the sting of death sin?

He says the sting of death is sin because the wages of sin is death, and James 1:15 shows that lust gives birth to sin and sin brings forth death. Sin starts with lust, he says, but the desire “doesn’t mean a hill of beans” until you act upon it, and that is when you violate God’s word and death sets in.
Why is the sting of death sin?

“Death, where is your sting? Death, where is your victory?” Where is your conquest? Quoting out of Scripture again. “The sting of death is sin, and the strength of sin is the law.” Why is the sting of death sin? Well, Romans 6:23, “The wages of sin is” what? Death. You see, when lust has conceived, in James 1:15, it gives birth to sin, and sin, when it is full grown, brings forth death. See, so sin starts with lust, but that lust does not mean anything till you act upon it. See, I can desire a woman outside my marriage, but it doesn’t mean a hill of beans until I what? Act upon it. That’s when I violate God’s word, and that’s when death sets in. I can want to kill somebody, “Oh, they got me so upset.” See, my desire, but if I don’t activate it, it doesn’t produce sin. Are you there?
Why is the sting of death sin?

1 Corinthians 15:55-56: “O Death, where is your sting? O Hades, where is your victory?” The sting of death is sin, and the strength of sin is the law. Romans 6:23: For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord. James 1:15: Then, when desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full-grown, brings forth death.
Is having a bad thought the same as sinning?

He says no: “the thought isn’t the sin, the wrong desire isn’t the sin; the sin is when you activate that wrong desire.” If you are not activating the thought, he says, don’t beat yourself up. He then says there is another death everyone must confront, the lake of fire, by our deeds and how we treated other people.
Is having a bad thought the same as sinning?

And the point is this: just because you have a bad thought or something, don’t beat yourself up if you’re not activating the thought. Relax. Hallelujah. The thought isn’t the sin, the wrong desire isn’t the sin; the sin is when you activate that wrong desire and you commit incest, and you commit, you know, stealing, and so forth. Romans 20:14, “Death and hell were cast into the lake of fire.” This is the second death. Now, you got to understand that we’re not just talking about the body dying. There is another death that everyone must confront, and that is the lake of fire. By our deeds, not our faith. It doesn’t say you’re judged out of the books by your faith, does it? By your what? Deeds, your actions, how you behave, how you treated other people. “Whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.” And the lake of fire is what? The second death. That’s the eternal death. That’s when that eternal body will be eternally punished forever and ever and ever; he can’t die.
Is having a bad thought the same as sinning?
Revelation 20:14-15: Then Death and Hades were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death. And anyone not found written in the Book of Life was cast into the lake of fire.
What is the first resurrection, and do we reign with Christ now?

He says the first resurrection is Jesus Christ and the saints of old coming out of the grave, and that it matters to believe in the resurrection as well as the cross, because in the resurrection “I am a new creature.” If we have part in it, the second death has no power over us, and he says the key is not the thousand years but reigning with Christ, who is in us now: “I reign now because He reigns now.”
What is the first resurrection, and do we reign with Christ now?

Now Revelation 20:6, “Blessed and holy is he that has part in the first resurrection.” What’s the first resurrection? Jesus Christ, and those saints of old coming out of the grave when He came out of the grave, Jesus Christ. See, He died for us and He rose again. It’s important that we not just believe in the cross and the blood but also in the resurrection, because in the resurrection is the example of life. On the cross is the death to sin, but in the resurrection I am a new creature; I live because He lives in me. Now that’s good stuff. So when I have part in the first resurrection, remember I was dead in trespasses and sins, but I come to Christ and He resurrects me. I’m free from all those; He’s forgiven me. Hallelujah. I take part in that, then the second death has what? No power over me. Why? Because I’m a partaker of Christ and His first resurrection. I let Him resurrect me out of trespasses and sin, make me a new creature, and He says, “Don’t sweat it, kid, the lake of fire has no power over you.” “But they shall be priests of God and of Christ and shall reign with Him a thousand years.” Now you can get into the thousand years all you want. I would be careful about bringing that to a real thousand years, because other things in the Scriptures did not happen in the time period that God said, but if it’s a thousand years, that’s fine either way. The key here is not the thousand years. What’s the key? Reign and ruling with Christ. And where is Christ right now? In us. I reign now because He reigns now. Hallelujah. And when He comes, ever what happens, I’m going to be part of it, whether it’s 10 years, a thousand years, or 10,000 years. I’m going to be reigning with Him for eternity.
What is the first resurrection, and do we reign with Christ now?

Revelation 20:6: Blessed and holy is he who has part in the first resurrection. Over such the second death has no power, but they shall be priests of God and of Christ, and shall reign with Him a thousand years.
Why is the law the strength of sin?
