You go get the milk, you go do that.” “I know your love, your service, your faith and your patience.” Wow, this is the church of Thyatira over here. Look at them. Wow, they’re feeling pretty good about themselves right now. Look at them, man, they’re looking cocky. Their heads are getting big. But you allow Jezebel. You see the, those women at that table, you all?
Does God still correct and punish, and what is the “new name” on the stone? (Revelation 2:16-19)

Revelation 2:16: Repent, or else I will come to you quickly and will fight against them with the sword of My mouth. Revelation 2:17: “He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To him who overcomes I will give some of the hidden manna to eat. And I will give him a white stone, and on the stone a new name written which no one knows except him who receives it.” ’ Revelation 2:19: “I know your works, love, service, faith, and your patience; and as for your works, the last are more than the first.
Who is the “Jezebel” in Thyatira, and what does Jesus say he will do? (Revelation 2:20-23)

He says Thyatira had great works but let a woman who “says she’s a prophetess” teach and lead others into “sexual immorality and worship idols.” He says “you can tell everything by the results,” that Jesus gave her time to repent, and that those who “refuse to repent” are known by their “lifestyle” and “fruit.”
Who is the “Jezebel” in Thyatira, and what does Jesus say he will do? (Revelation 2:20-23)

“You allow Jezebel to come in and teach and seduce my servants to commit sexual immorality and worship idols.” Wow. After this great stuff, they let the feminist come in. She says she’s a prophetess, and she’s not. She, she, she gave herself the title. How many, not a lot of ministers give themselves the title. And you can tell by the results. You can tell everything by the results, the fruit. He says, “I gave her time to repent.” I told her to repent. I told these people, “Do you stop it?” The people that are following her, the one that’s teaching, repent, and they wouldn’t repent. And you know that is the message to God’s church, church: that we can repent and we should repent. And how many, you know, there’s people that just refuse to repent. They justify their wrong, ain’t that right? And you know it by their lifestyle, by their fruit. “So I’m going to put her in a sick bed of tribulation. I’m going to bring sickness, I’m going to bring tribulation on her for her works.” Her what? What’s the word? Works. Not her faith, her what? Works. “And I’m going to kill their children.” God’s going to kill innocent people, folks. You got to remember, God’s an eternal being. Death is part of the program. When he had David’s child that was conceived in sexual immorality die, he is God. Yes, that child is innocent, but that’s part of God’s program. Don’t believe this liberal thinking that, “Well, if there’s a God, why does he allow these problems in the earth?” We create the problem. Don’t blame God. The Bible says God can do no evil. See, David and Bathsheba was the one that caused this child to die, not God.
Who is the “Jezebel” in Thyatira, and what does Jesus say he will do? (Revelation 2:20-23)

Revelation 2:20: Nevertheless I have a few things against you, because you allow that woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess, to teach and seduce My servants to commit sexual immorality and eat things sacrificed to idols. Revelation 2:22-23: Indeed I will cast her into a sickbed, and those who commit adultery with her into great tribulation, unless they repent of their deeds. I will kill her children with death, and all the churches shall know that I am He who searches the minds and hearts. And I will give to each one of you according to your works.
Does God kill innocent people, or do we wrongly blame him? (Revelation 2:23)

He says “death is part of the program” for an eternal God, but “we create the problem. Don’t blame God,” and “God can do no evil.” He tells atheists they cannot blame someone they say doesn’t exist, and says that when innocent people suffer it is “people” who are responsible, not God.
Does God kill innocent people, or do we wrongly blame him? (Revelation 2:23)

You teenagers, you getting this? This is very important for you, because these atheists who don’t believe in God always blame God for everything on the earth, and my response to them: how can you blame someone you don’t believe in? Number one, you say he doesn’t exist, and now you’re blaming him. I says, if you really knew the book, he gave us authority, he gave us the responsibility to deal with bad things in the earth and to do right and raise our children right, and when the problems come and the payment comes, it’s our fault, not God’s. Can I hear an amen? And innocent people dying, from Genesis to Revelation, God’s people, innocent, died. Stephen died, they killed him. Prophets were stoned and killed in the Old Testament. They were innocent people. God wasn’t responsible for that death, people was. You understand that? Please tell me you understand that. They try to turn things around and put us on the defensive. And yes, things happen to innocent people when we make bad decisions. Don’t blame God. Blame the one that made the bad decision. Could that be an amen? Now, folks, I don’t know, this is good stuff. This is the revelation of the church. You need to get this in your mind. “To the rest, the people that aren’t following Jezebel, keep what you have till I come.” Isn’t that beautiful? See, he always encourages, always encouraging. And “to they that overcome, I will give you power over the nations.” Does the church have power over the nations? And we’re diminishing. You know, we had America when I was a child (I was sharing with people yesterday) was a moral nation.
Does God kill innocent people, or do we wrongly blame him? (Revelation 2:23)

Revelation 2:23: I will kill her children with death, and all the churches shall know that I am He who searches the minds and hearts. And I will give to each one of you according to your works. Acts 7:59: And they stoned Stephen as he was calling on God and saying, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.”
Should the church have power over the nations, and what is the “morning star”? (Revelation 2:24-28)

He says Jesus promises “power over the nations,” and that America used to be “a moral nation” where “even bad people knew what was right and wrong.” He says we are to “overcome and get it back,” and that “the morning star” is Jesus Christ.
Should the church have power over the nations, and what is the “morning star”? (Revelation 2:24-28)

Even bad people knew what was right and wrong. Now bad people feel they’re okay, they believe they’re okay. That’s how we’ve declined. Before the sixties, America’s impact from the religious area was very powerful. We didn’t even have supermarkets opened on Sunday. I can still remember the first time they opened up a supermarket on Sunday in Detroit, Michigan. Why? Because of the impact of the church upon the nation. And we’ve lost it in fifty years. We have lost it. But we can what? Overcome and get it back. We’re supposed to be the ones that have impact and influence over the nations. Amen. Do you get this? See, this is the revelation of the church. This is the revelation that God has for you. But they got us thinking we got to hang on to the rapture, and we got, us, you know, the church age and the, and, uh, dispensationalism. It’s not even in the Bible. They make up this stuff and we hear it and we believe it. And this is the real dispensation, this is the real church age: we are supposed to be a force in the earth, growing into his image and becoming a, a, an element in the earth to be reckoned with. Hallelujah! And he says, “I will not only give you power over the nations, I will give you the morning star.” Who’s the morning star? Jesus Christ.
Should the church have power over the nations, and what is the “morning star”? (Revelation 2:24-28)

Revelation 2:26-28: And he who overcomes, and keeps My works until the end, to him I will give power over the nations— ‘He shall rule them with a rod of iron; They shall be dashed to pieces like the potter’s vessels’— as I also have received from My Father; and I will give him the morning star. Revelation 2:28: and I will give him the morning star.
What does Jesus say to Sardis, and who are “the worthy”? (Revelation 3:1-6)

He says Sardis had “a name that you’re alive” but was dead, and was told to “strengthen the remaining things.” He says “I will come” does not mean the second coming but “coming and taking care of business,” and that “some are worthy,” including people he has met across denominations.
What does Jesus say to Sardis, and who are “the worthy”? (Revelation 3:1-6)

Now here’s the church of Sardis right here. This group right here, one with the hood on his hat, and that group right there. Hallelujah! And the old man that just come from the Arctic Circle here, up there where it’s so cold, my goodness, just hearing about it I got chills running up and down my spine. But he’s so important, they can’t do without him up there. “I know your works. You are not perfect.” Well, yeah, you got me there. “You have a name that you’re alive, yeah, but you’re dead.” Woo, that’s not nice, that’s not edifying, that’s not kind, that you’re dead. You just think you’re alive. “Be watchful, be alert, strengthen the remaining things that are ready to die.” You got some good in you, you got some things in you. Come on, strengthen those things and let’s get out of this. Amen. You see how he encourages? “Repent, and remember those things which you received and heard. Remember those things that are dying that you have. If not, if you don’t watch, I will come.” And he says “I will come” to six of the seven churches. He’s not talking about the second coming here. He’s talking about coming and taking care of business. See, we got our eyes on the second coming, we can’t see that he can come now and he can deal with us. Are you there? “Some are worthy, they’re not defiled.” Hallelujah! And you’ll find this almost everywhere you go: there are some people. I’ve been all over the world, I’ve been in every denomination, I’ve preached in almost every denomination there is in America, including the Catholic Church. And you ask around, how many Protestants have preached in a Catholic church? But yeah, if you don’t mingle, you know, if you get this sectarian mentality where you got to be separate from everybody, how you going to impact people if you’re separated from them? And I have found that there were Catholics that loved Jesus. I was found there were Episcopalians that loved Jesus. Yeah, their church taught some weird stuff, goodness, but there were sincere, genuine, born-again people there. See, and that’s what it says here: “Some of you are worthy, you’re not defiled.” If you overcome, “I’ll give you white attire, [unclear], and I’ll put your name in the Book of Life.” Hallelujah!
What does Jesus say to Sardis, and who are “the worthy”? (Revelation 3:1-6)

Revelation 3:1-2: “And to the angel of the church in Sardis write, ‘These things says He who has the seven Spirits of God and the seven stars: “I know your works, that you have a name that you are alive, but you are dead. Be watchful, and strengthen the things which remain, that are ready to die, for I have not found your works perfect before God. Revelation 3:3: Remember therefore how you have received and heard; hold fast and repent. Therefore if you will not watch, I will come upon you as a thief, and you will not know what hour I will come upon you. Revelation 3:4-5: You have a few names even in Sardis who have not defiled their garments; and they shall walk with Me in white, for they are worthy. He who overcomes shall be clothed in white garments, and I will not blot out his name from the Book of Life; but I will confess his name before My Father and before His angels.
What is the “open door” that no one can shut for Philadelphia? (Revelation 3:7-8)

He says Philadelphia gets no rebuke and is told, “I’m going to open doors for you that nobody can shut.” He says not to worry about “the liberals … the atheists … the homosexuals and the sinners,” and that “it only takes a little strength in God” because he multiplies it.
What is the “open door” that no one can shut for Philadelphia? (Revelation 3:7-8)

Now here’s the angel of Philadelphia here, that row in the back, nothing but women. I should have made them the Jezebel church. Huh? I wasn’t thinking good enough there. Look at him back there. Man. “I know your works. I have set before you an open door, and no man can shut it.” This is to the church of Philadelphia. He says nothing bad about this church. He said, “Because of who you are, I’m going to open doors for you that nobody can shut.” Don’t you worry about the liberals, don’t you worry about the atheists, don’t you worry about the homosexuals and the sinners. I’m going to open doors and none of these groups can shut it. Do we need that in America? Yeah, yeah. Why? Because this church was everything that he said to the other church: faithful, persistent, serving God. “You have a little strength.” How many of you know it only takes a little strength in God? He multiplies the strength. You say, “I’m not very strong.” Well, you’re a candidate. You know, when you realize you got some strength but you’re not the total strength, then you’re a great candidate for God to do something. Now, hallelujah! When we get too confident in our strength, we eliminate ourselves, because it’s got to be him. But when we have a little strength that he is working in me, then nothing is limited. Hallelujah! How many are glad for a little strength? Amen. You know, don’t put yourself down because you feel a little strong. “You’ve obeyed my word.” Wow, did you hear that? “You’ve obeyed my word, and you have not denied my name.” “Some of them have come to you that are Jews, of Satan’s synagogue, and they lie,” and he says, “I’m going to deal with you so that they know I love you.”
What is the “open door” that no one can shut for Philadelphia? (Revelation 3:7-8)
Revelation 3:8: “I know your works. See, I have set before you an open door, and no one can shut it; for you have a little strength, have kept My word, and have not denied My name.
What are the promises to Philadelphia: the hour of testing and the pillar in the temple? (Revelation 3:9-12)

He says Jesus will make groups that oppose the church “know I love you,” and keep them “from the hour of testing.” He says the goal is for God to move “in us so greatly” that those groups see God’s love, and that overcomers will be “a pillar in my temple” with Jesus’s “new name.”
What are the promises to Philadelphia: the hour of testing and the pillar in the temple? (Revelation 3:9-12)

You see, this is where the church needs to get in America, where the liberals and the atheists and the humanists, these groups that are putting down the church, and these false apostles and these false prophets and all the rest, God moves in us so greatly that those groups know God loves us. Do you see? Not that we’re some great people, but what Jesus loves us. Oh, that’s good. Maybe raise your hand and say, “I really want to see that in America.” Yeah. You see, we got to understand the promise to the church before we can get this. Promises: “I’ll keep you from the hour of testing.” Okay, that ten days of tribulation coming back there, he said it’s not going to happen to you. “I don’t need, I don’t need to fool around with this area in your life, we’re moving on.” How many raise your hand, say, “Man, I can handle that, get out of this tribulation, we’ve had enough tribulation, we don’t need to keep having tribulation”? “The hour of testing. I come quickly. Hold fast to your crown.” See, he’s coming to do what he said he would do: open the door that no man could shut, to bring these groups that say they’re Christians and they’re not, they’re against the things of Christ, to your feet, where they know that God loves you. God’s doing it, not us. Now that’s good stuff, folks. Can he? Remember the faith of Abraham: can God perform? Does he have the power to do what he promised? See, that’s all the faith we need. We got to quit looking at our weak strength and our mistakes and our problems and start looking to him and let him come and move us up to this dominion, to this area. Amen. “They that overcome, I’ll make him a pillar in my temple, and I’m going to give him my new name.” Not them a new name, “I’m going to give them my new name,” Jesus’s new name. You see, and there’s a sermon on that. Moses, you know, was given these new names.
What are the promises to Philadelphia: the hour of testing and the pillar in the temple? (Revelation 3:9-12)

Revelation 3:10: Because you have kept My command to persevere, I also will keep you from the hour of trial which shall come upon the whole world, to test those who dwell on the earth. Revelation 3:12: He who overcomes, I will make him a pillar in the temple of My God, and he shall go out no more. I will write on him the name of My God and the name of the city of My God, the New Jerusalem, which comes down out of heaven from My God. And I will write on him My new name. Romans 4:21: and being fully convinced that what He had promised He was also able to perform.
What does it mean to be lukewarm, and how do we “buy” from Jesus? (Revelation 3:14-21)

He says Laodicea says “I don’t need anything else” but is “poor, blind and naked.” He says we “buy” from Jesus by “seeking him, praying, reading his word,” not by giving money to a minister, and that even this lukewarm church “still had the presence of Jesus,” who is “always knocking.”
What does it mean to be lukewarm, and how do we “buy” from Jesus? (Revelation 3:14-21)

And the last church, Paul back there all by himself, and Lou. Look at those two guys. Here we are, the Laodicean church. “I know your works. You’re neither cold nor hot. I wish that you were cold or hot, because you’re lukewarm and neither cold or hot, I’m going to vomit you out of my mouth.” Man, look at him. Hallelujah! Woo! Now, you got to remember John wrote these, wrote it seven times and sent it to the seven churches, and the seven churches are reading this, and this is the message to each church. They’re hearing what he said to the other churches, and they’re hearing what he said to us. My God, how many, you know, they can learn from all seven churches, and me, know those seven churches were written so all of us could learn. Yes, absolutely. All right. Now, “you say you’re rich and you have need of nothing.” Hallelujah! Have you met him? “Oh, I’m a believer in Jesus, I don’t need anything else. I don’t need maturity, you know, I don’t need wisdom, I don’t need nothing, and I’m just, I’m just fine.” I meet them all the time. And God says, “You don’t know that you’re poor, blind and naked.” You can’t even see that you don’t have garments of righteousness. You can’t see anything. You don’t know anything. You’re spiritually in poverty. And then he encourages him to “buy refined gold from me, white attire, and eye salve.” Now, how do we buy from Jesus? Do we get money out of our pocket and give it to the minister? No. How do we buy? Seeking him, praying, reading his word, coming to him. See, that’s how we purchase. We believe that his cross, his death on the cross, paid the price for everything, not just the payment for my sin, but the inheritance for my inheritance. Amen. “I love, and I chasten and I rebuke those whom I love, so repent.” See, remember this lukewarm church still had the presence of Jesus. See, he hangs in there. He hangs in there. Don’t you let people talk you into, “Well, I’m so lousy and I’m so lukewarm and I’m so messed up, God, no.” He hangs in there. The candle, the church was still in the presence of Jesus. Jesus would come when they assembled together and sought him. “Open the door, and I will come in.” He’s always knocking. Paul, open the door. Lou, open the door. Come on. Have to knock a little louder. Lose a little heart of hearing. He’s always trying to get into your life to encourage you and strengthen you and change you. Are you with me? He, Jesus said, “I will never leave you nor what? Forsake you.” He just wants you to recognize your condition and what? Buck up, step up. “He overcomes, he will sit with me on my throne, as I sit with my Father on his throne.” There’s that rulership again. Common to all or common to most: “I know your works.” Was that common all? Yeah. Are works important? Yes. “He who overcomes.” Can we overcome? Yeah. He, he not only brought the weakness in our life, but he said, “Come on, we can conquer this, and I’ll reward you.” Did he encourage every church? Absolutely, absolutely he encouraged. Did they all hear what the Spirit said unto the churches?
What does it mean to be lukewarm, and how do we “buy” from Jesus? (Revelation 3:14-21)

Revelation 3:15-16: “I know your works, that you are neither cold nor hot. I could wish you were cold or hot. So then, because you are lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will vomit you out of My mouth. Revelation 3:20: Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears My voice and opens the door, I will come in to him and dine with him, and he with Me. Hebrews 13:5: Let your conduct be without covetousness; be content with such things as you have. For He Himself has said, “I will never leave you nor forsake you.”
What do all seven letters have in common, and what is the challenge? (Revelation 2–3)

He says every letter says “I know your works,” every church gets “come on, we can conquer this,” and “hear what the Spirit is saying to the churches.” He says Jesus corrected six and told five to repent, that “I will come” appears six times, and that God points things out “so he can … make us better,” not to throw us out.
What do all seven letters have in common, and what is the challenge? (Revelation 2–3)

Yeah, every church. He said, “Hear what the Spirit is saying to the churches.” He corrected six of them. Only Philadelphia did not need correction, but they were challenged to move up. Told five of them to repent. Told three of them, those of you who haven’t done these other things, you keep what you have, you maintain what you have. And so these are common. He says, “I will come” six times. “I will come, I’ll take care of business, I’ll come to make you an overcomer, I’ll come to fulfill my promises in your life.” You know, we only tell our kids things wrong in their life so that they can be straightened out. We don’t point out things in our kids wrong so we can throw them out. “Okay, I got a reason to get rid of you, James. Out!” No. And God, he comes to point things in our life so he can what? Make us better. So get out of the guilt-trip thing and get into the conquering, overcoming mentality that you were chosen by God to become a conqueror. And he said to the angel of the seven churches to preach those things and teach those things that only Jesus allows us to teach. Could that be an amen? And we should go to churches where they teach the Bible so we can grow and become a conqueror church. This is a tremendous promise to us. This is the revelation part of it. There’s more to come. He’s not done revealing his church, but this is powerful. So you can see some weaknesses in your life and you can repent and turn from them and get up, and you can see some promises and possess them. Hallelujah! You can be encouraged that God isn’t finished with the work that he started in you, if you’ll accept that challenge today and say, “Jesus, I’m going to spend some time like John did in spiritual things. I’m going to repent from the things that I need to repent from. If I have to do it ninety-nine times, I’m going to do it till it’s done. And Lord, I’m going to bow before you and submit to you, and I want you to touch me and empower me to possess these things.”
What do all seven letters have in common, and what is the challenge? (Revelation 2–3)

Revelation 3:22: “He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.” ’ ” Revelation 3:21: To him who overcomes I will grant to sit with Me on My throne, as I also overcame and sat down with My Father on His throne.
Why does he say some Christians grow weary?
He says some serve God “for a couple of years” and then you “don’t see them anymore,” because “they don’t feed themselves. You can’t give if you don’t receive.”
What does he say the Ephesians’ “first love” was?
He says it is the first commandment: loving God with all your heart, soul, might and strength, so that when you “go and labor” you have something to give.
Does he say God’s presence means he approves of what a church is doing?
No. He says “the presence of God is not his approval,” and that “helping the poor and visiting the sick” means “nothing without him.”
What does he say is known about the Nicolaitans?
He says “the only place we can find a source on them is from the early church fathers,” who said they were “an unrestrained group that shared wives.”
What does he say the second death is?
He says “the second death is the lake of fire,” which “burns for eternity” for those who “reject Christ and his word,” and that overcomers “will not be hurt by the second death.”
What does he say the doctrine of Balaam looks like today?
He says it is preachers who “just want the money” and “just want to tell you how good you are,” and “don’t care” about sin “as long as you’re sending in the money.”
Does he say Jesus only does good and never corrects?
No. He says “he also corrects, and he corrects with his word,” and that if God “cannot be involved in the earth and correct me and punish people, he’s a worthless God.”
What does he say the Jezebel figure represents?
He says it is a woman who “gave herself the title” of prophetess and leads others astray, and that you can know such people “by their lifestyle, by their fruit.”
Does he say God kills innocent people?
He says “God’s going to kill innocent people, folks,” but “God’s an eternal being,” “death is part of the program,” and “we create the problem. Don’t blame God. The Bible says God can do no evil.”
What does he say to atheists who blame God for suffering?
He says “how can you blame someone you don’t believe in? Number one, you say he doesn’t exist, and now you’re blaming him,” and that “it’s our fault, not God’s.”
What does he say about the rapture and dispensationalism?
He says “it’s not even in the Bible. They make up this stuff and we hear it and we believe it,” and that “the real church age” is that “we are supposed to be a force in the earth.”
Does he say “I will come” in the letters is the second coming?

No. He says “I will come” to six of the seven churches means “coming and taking care of business,” and that “we got our eyes on the second coming, we can’t see that he can come now and he can deal with us.”
What does he say about believers in other denominations?

He says he has preached “in almost every denomination there is in America” and found “sincere, genuine, born-again people” among Catholics and Episcopalians, and that a “sectarian mentality” keeps you from impacting people.
How does he say we “buy” from Jesus?
He says it is not “money out of our pocket” to a minister but “seeking him, praying, reading his word, coming to him,” because “his cross, his death on the cross, paid the price for everything.”
Why does he say God points out faults in our lives?

He says we tell our kids what’s wrong so they can be “straightened out,” not “throw them out,” and God points things out “so he can … make us better,” so “get out of the guilt-trip thing” and into “the conquering, overcoming mentality.”

items.d: In “Seven Last Plagues Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer works through the seven bowls of wrath in Revelation 15-16, arguing that the plagues are spiritual illustrations of something that happens before Jesus…
p: In “Seven Last Plagues Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer works through the seven bowls of wrath in Revelation 15-16, arguing that the plagues are spiritual illustrations of something that happens before Jesus returns. He covers the kings of the east and the Euphrates, Armageddon and “I come as a thief,” why Jesus comes after the tribulation, and the powers of heaven being shaken.
What are the seven last plagues in Revelation 15:1, and have they happened?

He says the seven last plagues “concludes the wrath of God,” and that there is “no historical Bible evidence” that they have literally taken place. His conclusion is that something will happen before Jesus returns that gets the world’s attention and leaves people “a choice to repent and serve Jesus Christ or not repent.”
What are the seven last plagues in Revelation 15:1, and have they happened?

Today we’re going to be talking about what the Bible calls the seven last plagues in the book of Revelation. That concludes the wrath of God; it finishes it, brings it to an end. It says in Revelation 15:1, “I saw another sign in heaven, great and marvelous: seven angels having the seven last plagues, for in them the wrath of God is complete.” So these last seven are the end of these things. Now, here’s a little picture of the seven. There is no historical Bible evidence that any of these last plagues have literally taken place, so that only leaves one conclusion: there’s something going to happen before Jesus returns that will get the world’s population’s attention and leave them with a choice to repent and serve Jesus Christ or not repent. So something very influential is going to be happening in these last days to separate the good from the bad and give people a chance to accept Christ.
What are the seven last plagues in Revelation 15:1, and have they happened?
Revelation 15:1: Then I saw another sign in heaven, great and marvelous: seven angels having the seven last plagues, for in them the wrath of God is complete.
What do the first four bowls of wrath do? (Revelation 16:2-9)

He walks through the first four bowls: painful sores on those with the mark of the beast, the sea becoming blood, the fresh water turned to blood “for the martyrs,” and scorching heat, after which people still “blasphemed God.” He says he is not sure how humans live in the sea and that “it could be an allegory.”
What do the first four bowls of wrath do? (Revelation 16:2-9)

So the first angel poured out his bowl upon the earth, and there were painful sores on the people with the mark of the beast and those that worship the beast. In the book of Revelation, have you seen it? It didn’t pay to worship the beast; it didn’t pay to get his mark. They’re always being tormented; something’s always bad happening to them. The second angel poured out his bowl, and the sea became dead men’s blood, and all living souls in the sea die. Now, I don’t know how humans live in the sea, unless somewhere in the future we build cities underneath the ocean, but it could be on boats, could be those beside the sea, the oceans, and it could be an allegory. But anyway, the only place where men are dying in these seven last plagues is here in the sea, or things are dying; could be just the creatures of the sea. Then he turns all the fresh water to blood for the martyrs. You remember back in the seals, there had to be a number of martyrs, people that had died for Jesus’ name, for Jesus’ way, for his book, for his truth. They had to be a certain number that were martyred, killed because they loved Jesus and served Jesus, before Jesus would return. And here we find it again in these last plagues: he gives these people that murder God’s people the blood to drink, and the angel said, “This is just, because they shed your people’s blood, and you’ve given them blood to drink.” Then the fourth angel poured out his bowl, and he had power to scorch people on earth with severe heat, and they blasphemed God; they spoke evil of God and they blasphemed God’s name. They would not give God any glory, would not give God any honor, after all the other plagues before and now this one. So you know, there’s a hardness in people’s hearts somewhere that even these things cannot turn around.
What do the first four bowls of wrath do? (Revelation 16:2-9)

Revelation 16:2-9: So the first went and poured out his bowl upon the earth, and a foul and loathsome sore came upon the men who had the mark of the beast and those who worshiped his image. Then the second angel poured out his bowl on the sea, and it became blood as of a dead man; and every living creature in the sea died. Then the third angel poured out his bowl on the rivers and springs of water, and they became blood. And I heard the angel of the waters saying: “You are righteous, O Lord, The One who is and who was and who is to be, Because You have judged these things. For they have shed the blood of saints and prophets, And You have given them blood to drink. For it is their just due.” And I heard another from the altar saying, “Even so, Lord God Almighty, true and righteous are Your judgments.” Then the fourth angel poured out his bowl on the sun, and power was given to him to scorch men with fire. And men were scorched with great heat, and they blasphemed the name of God who has power over these plagues; and they did not repent and give Him glory.
Why do people refuse to repent in the fifth bowl, and what judges us? (Revelation 16:10-11)

He says that under the fifth bowl people bit their tongues in pain and “repented not of their deeds,” and that “it’s our deeds that we’re going to be judged by, not what church you go to.” He says people cannot repent unless the Word is preached, so “the saints are still here,” preaching “both by example and by their mouth.”
Why do people refuse to repent in the fifth bowl, and what judges us? (Revelation 16:10-11)

And then the fifth angel poured out his bowl on the seat of the beast, and the kingdom was full of darkness. The people of his kingdom gnawed (they chewed their tongues for pain); they were in such pain that they bit their tongues to find relief, and they blasphemed God because of the pains and the sores. See, they still got the sores of the first plague, and they talked bad about God and evil about God for these pains and the sores, and who, recognizing that God is the one who had the authority over these plagues. And it says they repented not of their deeds. And it’s our deeds that we’re going to be judged by, not what church you go to, not your baptismal certificate. And you got to remember, people cannot repent unless the Word is preached. See, and how can they hear the Word unless there’s a preacher? So the saints are still here, preaching, both by example and by their mouth, speaking the Word of God, and they won’t repent, just like in the days of Noah, just like in the days of Lot.
Why do people refuse to repent in the fifth bowl, and what judges us? (Revelation 16:10-11)

Revelation 16:10-11: Then the fifth angel poured out his bowl on the throne of the beast, and his kingdom became full of darkness; and they gnawed their tongues because of the pain. They blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and their sores, and did not repent of their deeds. Romans 10:14: How then shall they call on Him in whom they have not believed? And how shall they believe in Him of whom they have not heard? And how shall they hear without a preacher? Luke 17:26-29: And as it was in the days of Noah, so it will be also in the days of the Son of Man: They ate, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noah entered the ark, and the flood came and destroyed them all. Likewise as it was also in the days of Lot: They ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they built; but on the day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven and destroyed them all.
Who are the kings of the east in Revelation 16:12?

He says the Bible “doesn’t tell us who the kings of the east are,” though “kings came from the east when Jesus died.” He says it “doesn’t have to be China” or India, as “these theory people” say, merely because they are east of Jerusalem.
Who are the kings of the east in Revelation 16:12?

Then the sixth angel poured out his bowl, and the Euphrates River became dry; the kings of the east were going to cross over the river. It made the way for the kings of the east to come, and I’m sure you know who the kings of the east are; everybody knows that Sunday school story. Huh? Yeah, you’re looking at me like, “Yeah, really?” It doesn’t tell us who the kings of the east are, but we know that kings came from the east when Jesus died. So it doesn’t have to be China, it doesn’t have to be India, as these theory people tell us, because they’re east of Jerusalem. Anyway, the kings of the east. The demons come out of Satan, the mouth of Satan, the mouth of the beast and the mouth of the false prophet, and they come out as frogs.
Who are the kings of the east in Revelation 16:12?
Revelation 16:12: Then the sixth angel poured out his bowl on the great river Euphrates, and its water was dried up, so that the way of the kings from the east might be prepared.
Do demons come out of people as frogs or spiders? (Revelation 16:13-14)

He says “demons are spirit; they don’t come out as anything,” and that you cannot take a metaphor in Revelation and say demons come out of people in some fashion. He says the frogs came out of the dragon, the beast and the false prophet, and that Satan already has “an army of demon men” to influence the earth, so “he’s illustrating.”
Do demons come out of people as frogs or spiders? (Revelation 16:13-14)

Now, when I traveled to third world countries and we’re ministering down there, they tell me, you know, that they cast a demon out and it came out as a spider, and it came out... I go, “Folks, that is not Bible. Demons are spirit; they don’t come out as anything. They come out the way they went in: a spirit.” You can’t take a verse in Revelation that’s metaphoric, illustrating something, and then say demons come out of us in some kind of fashion. Are you with me? But see, we have these extreme things going on all over the world in the church world because we don’t know our Bible. Now, you got to remember, this frog came out of Satan himself. Can we see Satan? No. The frog came out of the beast. It’s possible that we can’t see this beast that everybody is so sure is going to be a group of nations and a group of kings, and it came out of the false prophet. Just getting your mind to think.
Do demons come out of people as frogs or spiders? (Revelation 16:13-14)

Revelation 16:13-14: And I saw three unclean spirits like frogs coming out of the mouth of the dragon, out of the mouth of the beast, and out of the mouth of the false prophet. For they are spirits of demons, performing signs, which go out to the kings of the earth and of the whole world, to gather them to the battle of that great day of God Almighty.
What does “I come as a thief” mean, and what is Armageddon? (Revelation 16:14-16)

He says the nations are gathered “for war at the place of Armageddon,” and Jesus says “I come as a thief,” which he explains is because “no one knows when the thief is coming.” He says “nobody knows when he’s coming” and “we just don’t know.”
What does “I come as a thief” mean, and what is Armageddon? (Revelation 16:14-16)

You know, we read books in the Christian bookstore, and when we read the Bible we just read it right in, but if we just use a little common sense, we can get real Bible truths here. Okay, hallelujah. Does Satan need something coming out of his mouth to influence the earth with demonic power? No, because he already has an army of demon men doing that. Ain’t that right? So see, he’s illustrating. He’s illustrating now. And so they come for war; he gets all the nations to come for war at the place of Armageddon (Armageddon, as I’ll show it to you in a minute). And then he says, “Behold, I come as a thief in the night.” Now, have we heard that statement before? Yeah, Jesus said, “I come as a thief.” The apostles said it. And so, he says, you know, that’s because no one knows when the thief is coming. The thief doesn’t announce himself, because if he did, you’d be ready to blow his head off. So Jesus is coming; nobody knows when he’s coming, and this is where the [unclear] really miss it, folks. We just don’t know. Can’t we get it? But anyway, now he says this is the place where he’s coming as a thief. This is it. Are you there?
What does “I come as a thief” mean, and what is Armageddon? (Revelation 16:14-16)

Revelation 16:14-16: For they are spirits of demons, performing signs, which go out to the kings of the earth and of the whole world, to gather them to the battle of that great day of God Almighty. “Behold, I am coming as a thief. Blessed is he who watches, and keeps his garments, lest he walk naked and they see his shame.” And they gathered them together to the place called in Hebrew, Armageddon. Revelation 16:15: “Behold, I am coming as a thief. Blessed is he who watches, and keeps his garments, lest he walk naked and they see his shame.”
Where are the saints during the plagues, and what does he say about the rapture? (Revelation 16:15)

He says Jesus promises to bless those whose garments are white, so “the saints” are “still here on earth,” “preaching” and “walking in righteousness,” and God is “blessing us in the middle of all these plagues.” He says “righteousness is our garment and unrighteousness is our shame.”
Where are the saints during the plagues, and what does he say about the rapture? (Revelation 16:15)

And he also says he’s going to bless those whose garments are white and righteous. He’s going to bless those that are living for him. And so, where are the saints? Still here on earth. And what’s with this rapture thing? They’re still here. These are the seven last plagues, and we’re still here; we’re preaching, and we’re walking in righteousness, and God is blessing us in the middle of all these plagues. Now that’s a God, amen. That is a God. He’s worth something; he can do things for his people, those who serve him. He can do something for them. “He that watches and keeps his garment, blessed are they,” he says, “lest you walk naked and they see his shame.” See, righteousness is our garment and unrighteousness is our shame, and that’s all through the Bible. Isn’t that right? Hallelujah.
Where are the saints during the plagues, and what does he say about the rapture? (Revelation 16:15)

Revelation 16:15: “Behold, I am coming as a thief. Blessed is he who watches, and keeps his garments, lest he walk naked and they see his shame.” Revelation 16:15: “Behold, I am coming as a thief. Blessed is he who watches, and keeps his garments, lest he walk naked and they see his shame.”
What does the Euphrates River drying up mean? (Revelation 16:12)

He says the Euphrates begins in the area of the Garden of Eden, and that the “dry river” made sense to those who 150 years ago thought of horses crossing, but today troops could simply be dropped “out of the air.” He concludes the dry Euphrates “has nothing to do with anything except in the spiritual.”
What does the Euphrates River drying up mean? (Revelation 16:12)

Now, here is a picture, or map, of a map with the Euphrates River right here. As you follow it north, it goes into where the Garden of Eden used to be. How many already knew where the Garden of Eden was? All right, now the rest of you just found out where the Garden of Eden was. The Euphrates was found its head in the Garden of Eden, along with four other rivers. Okay, now let me ask you something. 150 years ago, when the rapture theory came out, we didn’t have airplanes, amphibious vehicles and so forth. So the Euphrates River drying up, yeah, we could get across the Euphrates. Well, they got to get across the Tigris first. The Tigris is another big river. Why wouldn’t it dry up? Have I got your brain thinking? But see, back then it was horses, and yeah, the river dry, man, they can come right across. Well, they got a lot of mountains and they got a lot of rivers to cross, if the Chinese and the Indians and all these eastern nations are going to come over and destroy and fight a battle at Armageddon there in Israel. All right, are you with me? Do we need a dry river to get across today? No, we just drop them out of the air. Amphibious vehicles could land here, and our troops are just running up there with their Humvees and all these vehicles, and, man, we’re right there. We don’t need no Euphrates River dried up. But see, they didn’t know that back then. Their little human minds were trying to figure this out with the knowledge that they had then. Are you there? So obviously this dry river Euphrates has nothing to do with anything except in the spiritual. Amen. And these are spiritual illustrations, as we will see.
What does the Euphrates River drying up mean? (Revelation 16:12)

Genesis 2:10-14: Now a river went out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it parted and became four riverheads. The name of the first is Pishon; it is the one which skirts the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold. And the gold of that land is good. Bdellium and the onyx stone are there. The name of the second river is Gihon; it is the one which goes around the whole land of Cush. The name of the third river is Hiddekel; it is the one which goes toward the east of Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates. Revelation 16:12: Then the sixth angel poured out his bowl on the great river Euphrates, and its water was dried up, so that the way of the kings from the east might be prepared.
Are the “kings of the east” really China and India? What does he say about end-time theories?

He says the eastern kings are tagged as China and India “because they’re east of Israel,” but other nations in the south do not follow Jesus either, so “he’s not talking about really eastern nations.” He says a theory “can’t be proven as a fact,” and when people say they know when Jesus is coming, “the Bible plainly says what we don’t know.”
Are the “kings of the east” really China and India? What does he say about end-time theories?

Now, here’s Israel, and this is where all the theory people have all the armies congregating down here at Armageddon. It’s a series of mountains in southern Israel, and this is where they have the whole big war going on. Now, folks, let’s use some common sense. The eastern kings: we are tagging China, India and all those eastern nations with a tag because they’re east of Israel. Now, do you think they’re the only nations that don’t like God? You know, south of that is Africa, and there’s a lot of nations that, you know, there they still worship the devil and demons and stuff like that in there, and Muslim has a big hold in Africa. You got Australia, farther south than that, you got South America. Now, you think all those nations are for Jesus? Come on. You know that’s not true. Ain’t that right? So see, he’s not talking about really eastern nations, China and all that. These theory people just don’t get it. And something is a theory because what? It can’t be proven as a fact; it doesn’t work every time. That’s why, when I was witnessing to a couple of young men, I told them evolution is a theory. They said, “No, it’s a fact.” I said, “No, it’s a theory; they can’t prove it.” They teach it like it’s a fact, but it’s a theory because they have no evidence to prove what they’re saying. None. I said, “Did you know the scientific method?” “No.” I said, “Well, how can you stand on science and not know how science works?” So I told them the scientific method. It’s a good method, but scientists need to use it. Ain’t that right? They need to use it themselves. And anyway, these theories we have about the second coming is, number one, a theory, when they say they know when he’s coming and the Bible plainly says what we don’t know. We just know he’s coming, and that’s good enough for me. How about you?
Are the “kings of the east” really China and India? What does he say about end-time theories?
Revelation 16:16: And they gathered them together to the place called in Hebrew, Armageddon.
What happens at the seventh bowl, and can Revelation be in chronological order? (Revelation 16:17-21)

He says that at the seventh bowl God says “It is done,” the end of the wrath, with a great earthquake and the cities of the nations falling. He says since the islands and mountains were already gone at the sixth seal, “this cannot be literally and in chronological order.”
What happens at the seventh bowl, and can Revelation be in chronological order? (Revelation 16:17-21)

Now, let’s get back to the seventh plague. He poured out his bowl, and God said, “It is done.” This is it. This is the end of the wrath, the end of the plagues. There was a great earthquake, and the great city was divided into three parts; the cities of the nations fell. New York just went down, just like that. Aren’t you glad you’re living in [unclear], not LA? How many, you know, if you’re serving God in LA, if that nation falls, God’s going to... what? He’s going to protect you. He’s God, folks. There’s no islands and no mountains; they’re gone. Now, that’s a big thing, but we already found back there at the sixth seal that the islands and mountains were gone. When did they reappear? Are you guys out there, do you ever think this way? I’m going to show you a little later, we’re going to go back to the sixth seal: the islands and the mountains were gone back then; how did they appear again? You see, in other words, this cannot be literally and in chronological order, because there’s the several clashes here, as we will see in a minute. Are you interested?
What happens at the seventh bowl, and can Revelation be in chronological order? (Revelation 16:17-21)

Revelation 16:17-21: Then the seventh angel poured out his bowl into the air, and a loud voice came out of the temple of heaven, from the throne, saying, “It is done!” And there were noises and thunderings and lightnings; and there was a great earthquake, such a mighty and great earthquake as had not occurred since men were on the earth. Now the great city was divided into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell. And great Babylon was remembered before God, to give her the cup of the wine of the fierceness of His wrath. Then every island fled away, and the mountains were not found. And great hail from heaven fell upon men, each hailstone about the weight of a talent. Men blasphemed God because of the plague of the hail, since that plague was exceedingly great. Revelation 6:12-14: I looked when He opened the sixth seal, and behold, there was a great earthquake; and the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the moon became like blood. And the stars of heaven fell to the earth, as a fig tree drops its late figs when it is shaken by a mighty wind. Then the sky receded as a scroll when it is rolled up, and every mountain and island was moved out of its place.
Can anyone know the day or hour of Jesus’ return?

He says Christians “literally fight over their belief in the end times, when Jesus plainly said nobody knows the day or the hour.” He says when someone predicts it for a certain month “he’ll be wrong again,” and that God “wouldn’t come just because he wanted to show him wrong.”
Can anyone know the day or hour of Jesus’ return?

You see, these people can write books and all this, and we read their books and we get all hyped up and we don’t go check the book, and then we fight over (the Christians literally fight over) their belief in the end times, when Jesus plainly said nobody knows the day or the hour. We act like we got it down. Somebody’s predicting it to happen this month, and he’ll be wrong again. I told the church when I was in my 20s that I would not see the return of Jesus Christ. Why? Everybody just thought I was a heretic, but I’d read enough of the book to know there’s some things has to be done, and also read enough of the book to know that God wouldn’t come just because he wanted to show him wrong, even... he just, you know, like this 2012. Yeah, there’s going to be a big embarrassment next year. God’s got this stuff on his calendar anyway. Hail came down; they blaspheme God again, they speak evil of God.
Can anyone know the day or hour of Jesus’ return?
Matthew 24:36: “But of that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels of heaven, but My Father only.
Does Jesus return before or after the tribulation? (Matthew 24:29)

He reads “immediately after the tribulation” and says Jesus comes after, not before, the tribulation, so “every eye shall … see him,” not a quiet return. He says the “the powers of the heaven shall be shaken” means “the supernatural rulers in heaven,” tied to wrestling “against principalities and powers.”
Does Jesus return before or after the tribulation? (Matthew 24:29)

Now, let’s take a look at some interesting Scriptures here. Here we go. I just listened to [unclear] Lindsay last week on TV. I was channel surfing there, and he was, and sure enough, he went here and he quoted this verse, and then talked about all the wars going on and all the rest, and I sat there and, gosh, Almighty, this guy’s making millions of bucks lying to people. Read this verse with me: “Immediately after the tribulation” (what’s this, “before tribulation” stuff?) “of those days shall the sun and moon be darkened.” Is that what we have over in Revelation, the sun and moon darkening? Isn’t that what we saw? “The stars shall fall from heaven.” Is that what Revelation said? I mean, John is just writing what was already written. “The powers of the heaven shall be shaken.” Two things here. Number one, when is he coming, before or after tribulation? After. It plainly says it, doesn’t it? So they got to have the rapture, a “many return”: he doesn’t really come and everybody see him; he just kind of comes and we get caught up, and then everybody sees our clothes laying around and our car just drives off and hits a telephone pole, and, you know, and then they go, “What’s going on? What’s going on?” But the scripture says every eye shall what? See him. So number one, he’s coming after tribulation. Number two, all these stars, all these moon and sun being darkened, the powers of heaven shall be what? Shaken. The powers, the supernatural rulers in heaven, shall be shaken. Are you hearing me? So what’s this moon and stuff got to do with it? It’s got to do with the powers. Remember, we wrestle not against flesh and blood but against principalities and powers and spiritual wickedness in high places, heavenly places. See, there’s a war going on in the spirit realm, and he’s illustrating to us with natural things what’s happening in spiritual things. Now that was good, church.
Does Jesus return before or after the tribulation? (Matthew 24:29)

Matthew 24:29: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light; the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken. Ephesians 6:12: For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this age, against spiritual hosts of wickedness in the heavenly places. Revelation 1:7: Behold, He is coming with clouds, and every eye will see Him, even they who pierced Him. And all the tribes of the earth will mourn because of Him. Even so, Amen.
What is the sign of Christ’s coming? (Matthew 24:30-31)

He says “wars and rumors of wars” and “earthquakes and famines and plagues are not the sign of his coming,” but “his sign of his coming is him coming.” He quotes that they shall see the Son of Man coming in the clouds and the angels will gather his elect.
What is the sign of Christ’s coming? (Matthew 24:30-31)

“And then they shall see the sign of the Son of Man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. All the earth shall mourn. Angels will gather together his elect from one end of heaven to the other.” So see, wars and rumors of wars aren’t the sign of his coming; earthquakes and famines and plagues are not the sign of his coming. His sign of his coming is him coming. Are you there? See, it’s just like Pentecostals and charismatics, of which I got saved in, said that tongues were evidence, a sign, of the baptism of the Holy Ghost. The Bible never says that. We just made a statement because that’s how we got the ghost, and so we just made a new law; we wrote our own law that you had to speak in tongues to be filled with the Holy Ghost, and the Bible doesn’t say that at all. Are you there?
What is the sign of Christ’s coming? (Matthew 24:30-31)

Matthew 24:30-31: Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. And He will send His angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they will gather together His elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other. Matthew 24:6: And you will hear of wars and rumors of wars. See that you are not troubled; for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet.
Does the Bible say speaking in tongues is the sign of the baptism of the Holy Ghost?

He says the Bible “never says” tongues is the evidence, that Pentecostals “wrote our own law,” and that “there’s nothing wrong with speaking in tongues,” but condemning someone who doesn’t is “a real problem.” He says the word of wisdom is first among the nine gifts and tongues is “way down at the bottom.”
Does the Bible say speaking in tongues is the sign of the baptism of the Holy Ghost?

And Pentecostals and charismatics just believe that without going and searching the Scriptures. Now, there’s nothing wrong with speaking in tongues; the Bible says, “Forbid not to speak in tongues.” But when you condemn somebody because they don’t speak in tongues, that’s a real problem, because if God doesn’t give them tongues, they’re never going to get it. But there’s a lot of other things that are expressions of the Holy Ghost, isn’t there? And what’s the top one? Wisdom. The nine gifts of the Spirit: what’s the first one? The word of wisdom. Where’s tongues? Way down at the bottom. Are you there? And he said, “Do all speak with tongues?” No. “Do all prophesy?” No. We just got to let God be God in us. Could that be an amen? Hallelujah. We don’t need to fight and quarrel with one another because one of us don’t have something another does. We just need to flow together to the goodness of the Lord and let God be God in us.
Does the Bible say speaking in tongues is the sign of the baptism of the Holy Ghost?

1 Corinthians 14:39: Therefore, brethren, desire earnestly to prophesy, and do not forbid to speak with tongues. 1 Corinthians 12:8-10: for to one is given the word of wisdom through the Spirit, to another the word of knowledge through the same Spirit, to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healings by the same Spirit, to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another discerning of spirits, to another different kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of tongues. 1 Corinthians 12:29-30: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all workers of miracles? Do all have gifts of healings? Do all speak with tongues? Do all interpret?
What does Luke 21:25 say about signs in the sun, moon, stars and the sea?

He reads Luke 21:25 about signs in the sun, moon and stars and the sea and waves roaring, and says that is “a lot more clear” than the sea turning to blood. He says people will have hearts “failing them for fear” and “they’re still going to not repent, and they’re going to blaspheme God.”
What does Luke 21:25 say about signs in the sun, moon, stars and the sea?

Anyway, let’s continue. Luke 21:25: “There will be signs in the sun, moon and stars, and on earth distress of nations and perplexity; the sea and the waves roaring.” Now, that sounds a lot more clear to me than the blood, that sea turning to blood. I can understand how people can die when the sea starts roaring: tsunamis and all that, that creates problems for us humans, doesn’t it? And, yes, our blood is shed. “Men’s hearts failing them for fear and expectation of those things which are coming on the earth.” I mean, these people are going to be shaken in their shoes and their knees are going to be knocking, and they’re still going to not repent, and they’re going to blaspheme God. This is what Revelation is trying to illustrate for the powers of heaven. What? The powers of heaven will be shaken; they will be destroyed.
What does Luke 21:25 say about signs in the sun, moon, stars and the sea?

Luke 21:25-26: “And there will be signs in the sun, in the moon, and in the stars; and on the earth distress of nations, with perplexity, the sea and the waves roaring; men’s hearts failing them from fear and the expectation of those things which are coming on the earth, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
Does the Bible say the beast or the son of perdition is the antichrist?

He says the beast, Satan and the false prophet are “powers in heavenly places, spiritual wickedness in spiritual places,” and that “the Bible never says” the son of perdition or the beast is the antichrist. He says the theorists “can never find a verse that says that those three people are the same.”
Does the Bible say the beast or the son of perdition is the antichrist?

So the beast, Satan and the false prophet are what? Powers in heavenly places, spiritual wickedness in spiritual places. Amen. And we try to reduce it down to some antichrist. The Bible never says that the son of perdition is the antichrist, or that the beast is the antichrist. The theorists say that; they can never find a verse that says that those three people are the same, and I can show you verses where they’re not. The powers of heaven; don’t forget that. Then they will see Jesus, what? Coming in the clouds with power.
Does the Bible say the beast or the son of perdition is the antichrist?

2 Thessalonians 2:3: Let no one deceive you by any means; for that Day will not come unless the falling away comes first, and the man of sin is revealed, the son of perdition, Matthew 24:30: Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
What does he conclude since the plagues have not literally happened?
He says it “leaves one conclusion”: something “very influential” will happen in the last days “to separate the good from the bad and give people a chance to accept Christ.”
Why does he connect the rivers turning to blood with the martyrs?

He recalls from the seals that “there had to be a number of martyrs,” killed because they loved Jesus, and says that in these plagues those who murdered God’s people are given “the blood to drink,” because “they shed your people’s blood.”
What does he say we are judged by?
He says “it’s our deeds that we’re going to be judged by, not what church you go to, not your baptismal certificate.”
Does he say demons come out of people as animals?

No. About reports of demons leaving as a spider, he says “that is not Bible,” because “demons are spirit; they don’t come out as anything. They come out the way they went in: a spirit.” He says such extreme ideas happen “because we don’t know our Bible.”
Why does he say the frogs are illustration?

He asks whether Satan needs something coming out of his mouth “to influence the earth with demonic power” and answers “no, because he already has an army of demon men doing that,” so “he’s illustrating.”
Why does he say Jesus comes “as a thief”?
He says “the thief doesn’t announce himself,” and “nobody knows when he’s coming,” and he adds that “we just know he’s coming, and that’s good enough for me.”
What does he say the garment of the saints is?
He says “righteousness is our garment and unrighteousness is our shame, and that’s all through the Bible.”
Where does he say the Euphrates begins?
He says that following the Euphrates north it “goes into where the Garden of Eden used to be,” and that it “found its head in the Garden of Eden, along with four other rivers.”
What problem does he raise about the islands and mountains disappearing?
He says they were already gone at the sixth seal, so “when did they reappear?” and concludes the passages “cannot be literally and in chronological order.”
What does he say he told his church about Jesus’ return when he was in his twenties?

He says he told them he “would not see the return of Jesus Christ,” because he had “read enough of the book to know there’s some things has to be done” first, and that “God’s got this stuff on his calendar anyway.”
Does he say Christians should fight over end-time beliefs?

No. He says people “get all hyped up” from books and “we don’t go check the book,” and that Christians “literally fight over their belief in the end times” even though Jesus said nobody knows the day or hour.
What does he say is the sign of Christ’s coming?
He says “his sign of his coming is him coming,” not wars, earthquakes, famines or plagues.
What does he say we should do instead of quarreling over spiritual gifts?

He says “we just got to let God be God in us” and that “we don’t need to fight and quarrel with one another because one of us don’t have something another does.” We should “flow together to the goodness of the Lord.”
What does he say the powers of heaven are?
He says the powers of heaven shaken are the beast, Satan and the false prophet, “powers in heavenly places, spiritual wickedness in spiritual places,” and that “they will be destroyed.”

items.d: In “Seven Last Plagues Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer begins with the believer’s security in Romans 8 and authority in Luke 10:19, then compares the plagues of Egypt with the plagues of Revelation, including…
p: In “Seven Last Plagues Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer begins with the believer’s security in Romans 8 and authority in Luke 10:19, then compares the plagues of Egypt with the plagues of Revelation, including the sorcerers’ limited power and the two witnesses. He ends with the three sources of deception in Revelation: religion, secular reasoning (science) and Satan himself.
Can spiritual powers separate a born-again believer from God’s love? (Romans 8:38-39)

He says no: when you are born again and really committed to Christ, “you’re not going to backslide.” You might “fall and you might fail and goof up,” but “that spirit that you’ve been born with is going to pick you back up,” which he calls “the difference between religion and reality.”
Can spiritual powers separate a born-again believer from God’s love? (Romans 8:38-39)

Romans 8:38: “I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities nor powers shall separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.” So is there spiritual powers? Are they trying to separate us? Can they? No. When you’re born again and you’re really committed to Christ, you’re not going to backslide. You might fall and you might fail and goof up and go through a cold season or a dumb time, but that Spirit that you’ve been born with is going to pick you back up. It’s going to convict you, it’s going to agitate you until you get back to being a son of the living God. See, that’s the difference between religion and reality. Does he say God is asleep to his people’s needs?
No. He says “aren’t you glad you got a God that isn’t sitting up there asleep?” and that “we got a lot more promises from God than we really understand.”
Does he say any culture or race is above another?
No. He says “no culture or race or whatever is above another in God’s eyes. He loves and cares for them all, and he’s speaking to them all.”
What does he say about people who have limited supernatural power?
He says they use “limited supernatural power to make people think he’s God,” as Simon did in Acts and as the woman does by her sorceries.
What does he say about asking God to prove himself with a sign?
He tells of a preacher who asked God to move a statue on his mantle, and says that is “testing, tempting God, and the Bible tells us not to do that.”
What does he say about trusting God if everything goes bad?

He says that “if everything goes bad for us, it doesn’t matter; we know in ourself that Jesus is God and we love him and we’re going to serve him no matter what,” and that without that “you’re going to fall for his tricks.”
What does he call “the big lie”?

He calls the big lie that you can “live what you want” and “still go to heaven” with no requirement and no accountability, and says “it’s big in America.” He also says religion that offers eternal life without requirements is “false.”
He says “the word science means the study of physical things; it’s knowledge,” and “knowledge has made the airplane, the computer, the internet. Knowledge exposed superstition.”
What does he say is not a sign of the last days?
He says “wars and rumors of wars” are not the sign, because “those things will always be.” The sign he points to is the increase of knowledge, citing Daniel.
What does he say about the melting of the ice caps?

He says there will not be a melting of the ice caps “because it would flood the world, and the Bible says that Jesus would never flood the world again.” He says secular reasoning “forgets that God’s in control of things.”

items.d: In “Seven Last Plagues Part 3,” Pastor David G. Kincer concludes the series by saying wars and plagues are not the sign of Jesus’ coming, that Daniel’s delayed answer shows spiritual warfare in the heavenlies…
p: In “Seven Last Plagues Part 3,” Pastor David G. Kincer concludes the series by saying wars and plagues are not the sign of Jesus’ coming, that Daniel’s delayed answer shows spiritual warfare in the heavenlies, and that the seals, trumpets and bowls describe one big event. He also warns about date-setting and the history of the rapture theory, and says God loves all nations.
Are wars, rumors of wars and earthquakes the sign of the end?

He says Jesus told us not to be troubled by wars and rumors of wars, because “such things must be” and “they’ve been happening since creation.” He says we don’t have to “stretch anything” because Scripture “just says what it says.”
Are wars, rumors of wars and earthquakes the sign of the end?

“Watch. Be alert, lest any man deceive you.” And the first thing he says: “False Christs will come and false prophets, and when you hear of wars and rumors of wars, be not” what? Now here’s [unclear] Lindsay telling the people, “Oh, look at all these wars going on and all these volcanoes and all that just this week.” And yet Jesus said, what? “Be not” what? Don’t even pay any attention to it. “For such things must be.” They’ve been happening since creation, and they’re going to keep happening. Yes. See, if we just read what it says, we get it. And he says, “For as a result, nations shall rise against nation, there’ll be earthquakes, famine and pestilence,” that’s the [unclear] there, “heavenly signs and troubles, and brother will betray brother to death, father and son, children their parents.” Don’t be troubled; “these things must be” has nothing to do with this end time. Just letting it sink in. I’m amazed that we got to interpret a scripture that needs no interpretation. It just plainly says it.
Are wars, rumors of wars and earthquakes the sign of the end?

Mark 13:5-13: And Jesus, answering them, began to say: “Take heed that no one deceives you. For many will come in My name, saying, ‘I am He,’ and will deceive many. But when you hear of wars and rumors of wars, do not be troubled; for such things must happen, but the end is not yet. For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. And there will be earthquakes in various places, and there will be famines and troubles. These are the beginnings of sorrows. “But watch out for yourselves, for they will deliver you up to councils, and you will be beaten in the synagogues. You will be brought before rulers and kings for My sake, for a testimony to them. And the gospel must first be preached to all the nations. But when they arrest you and deliver you up, do not worry beforehand, or premeditate what you will speak. But whatever is given you in that hour, speak that; for it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit. Now brother will betray brother to death, and a father his child; and children will rise up against parents and cause them to be put to death. And you will be hated by all for My name’s sake. But he who endures to the end shall be saved.
Is there salvation at the end, and what is the sign of Jesus’ coming?

He says “there’s preaching at the end, and there’s saints preaching at the end,” because God chose “the foolishness of the preaching” to save the lost, “not miracles.” He says the sign of Jesus is not wars or plagues but his coming, and “the end is when he comes.”
Is there salvation at the end, and what is the sign of Jesus’ coming?

“You’ll be hated of all men for My name’s sake, but he that endures to the end” (that’s what Revelation is talking about) “shall be saved.” Is there salvation at the end? Is there salvation at the end? So there’s preaching at the end, and there’s saints preaching at the end, because God’s chosen the foolishness of the preaching to what? Save the lost, not miracles. Preaching. “After the tribulation in those days the sun and moon dark, stars”; we already read that the heavenly powers are shaken, and then the sign of Jesus. So when’s the sign of Jesus down here? When he comes. What is not the sign of Jesus? Wars, rumors of war, earthquakes, pestilence, plagues. Have Christians been hated ever since Jesus brought the message? Oh, absolutely. Your own family members will hate you if you really serve Christ, and that’s what it says here, and that’s happened what? Through every generation. He says don’t be bothered; these things will happen, the end is what? Not yet. The end is when he comes. Are you there? Now, isn’t that clear? You don’t have to stretch anything, you don’t have to fumble anything; it just says what it says, doesn’t it? Hallelujah.
Is there salvation at the end, and what is the sign of Jesus’ coming?

Mark 13:13: And you will be hated by all for My name’s sake. But he who endures to the end shall be saved. 1 Corinthians 1:21: For since, in the wisdom of God, the world through wisdom did not know God, it pleased God through the foolishness of the message preached to save those who believe. Matthew 24:29-30: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light; the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken. Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
Why did Daniel wait 21 days for an answer to his prayer? (Daniel 10:12-13)

He says the angel told Daniel his words were heard, but “the prince of the kingdom of Persia” withstood the angel for 21 days. He says it was “wasn’t a human being” but “a prince in the spiritual heavenlies,” so “there was a war going on in the spiritual arena.”
Why did Daniel wait 21 days for an answer to his prayer? (Daniel 10:12-13)

“Fear not, Daniel, from the first day you set your heart to understand, your words were heard before God, and I am come for your words.” This is the angel Michael. Okay, “But the prince of the kingdom of Persia,” there was like 21 days. Daniel was praying and no answer, because what? “The prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood.” Yeah, it’s 21 days, because it’s written right there. If I would have read it, I... okay: the prince of the kingdom of what? Persia withstood who? Michael, one of the chief angels, for how many days? 21 days. So Michael couldn’t get to who? Daniel, to give him his prayer request. Now, was Cyrus or, not, Darius, the king of Persia at that time, is that who was withstanding Michael? No, no, wasn’t a human being. It was a prince in the spiritual heavenlies, in wicked places, that was withstanding Michael. There was a war going on in the spiritual arena. Are you there? Hallelujah. I’m sorry, that’s the angel. “Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, and I remained there with the” what? “Kings of Persia.” Kings, seven heads, 10 horns, had nothing to do with the human king of Persia; had to do with what? The spiritual kingdom who was influencing the kingdom on earth of Persia. Now, folks, you can’t get any plainer than that. Hallelujah. And John is showing us the spiritual powers being destroyed in Revelation, just as Jesus said they would be. “On My servants and handmaidens,” Acts 2:18, “I will pour out in those days of My Spirit, and they shall prophesy. And I will show wonders in the heaven above and signs in the earth beneath: blood and fire and vapor of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness and the moon into blood, before that great and notable day of the Lord. And it will come to pass that whosoever calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.”
Why did Daniel wait 21 days for an answer to his prayer? (Daniel 10:12-13)

Daniel 10:12-13: Then he said to me, “Do not fear, Daniel, for from the first day that you set your heart to understand, and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard; and I have come because of your words. But the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me twenty-one days; and behold, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, for I had been left alone there with the kings of Persia. Daniel 10:20-21: Then he said, “Do you know why I have come to you? And now I must return to fight with the prince of Persia; and when I have gone forth, indeed the prince of Greece will come. But I will tell you what is noted in the Scripture of Truth. (No one upholds me against these, except Michael your prince.
What does Acts 2:18-21 say about the sun and moon turned to blood?

He says Acts 2 uses “the same terminology” as the signs in Revelation, to say that God is “filling people with his Spirit,” using young people “both male and female” to prophesy, and that people are getting saved. He says it is “the same illustration,” and “we got a real God, and he’s in charge of this earth.”
What does Acts 2:18-21 say about the sun and moon turned to blood?

You see, he uses the same terminology to say God is doing great things. When this moon and sun are turned to blood, God is filling people with his Spirit, God is using his young people, both male and female, to speak the Word of the Lord through prophecy, God is doing things in the earth, and people are what? Getting saved. And he uses what illustration? The moon, the blood, the moon, the sun, signs in the earth, signs in the heavens. He uses the same illustration, but do they ever quote this? No. Hallelujah. I don’t know about you, folks, but we got a real God, and he’s in charge of this earth.
What does Acts 2:18-21 say about the sun and moon turned to blood?

Acts 2:18-21: And on My menservants and on My maidservants I will pour out My Spirit in those days; And they shall prophesy. I will show wonders in heaven above And signs in the earth beneath: Blood and fire and vapor of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness, And the moon into blood, Before the coming of the great and awesome day of the LORD. And it shall come to pass That whoever calls on the name of the LORD Shall be saved.’
