Is the first seal the antichrist, and what does he say about the famine in the seals?

He says “the seal is not the antichrist,” because “the Bible says it’s a conqueror on the horse” and “you can’t put in the word antichrist when the Bible doesn’t put it in.” He says killing each other is “not new,” and that the price of barley and wheat shows “plenty,” not famine.
Is the first seal the antichrist, and what does he say about the famine in the seals?

Now, here it is, the great tribulation, that blinking thing says what? Great deception. See, Jesus said, first thing he said: do not be what? Deceived. Now watch closely here. Here’s the seven seals, here’s the seven trumpets and here is the seven bowls, from their theory, one of their theories. Okay, first of all, the seal is not the antichrist. The Bible says it’s a conqueror on the horse, not an antichrist. You can’t put in the word antichrist when the Bible doesn’t put it in. Isn’t that right? Okay, secondly, they got anarchy, chaos going on, lawlessness, and it doesn’t say that; it says that they kill each other. Have we been killing each other since Cain killed? Yeah, that’s not new. You see how? And then they got a famine, and remember when we search the Scriptures, the price of barley and wheat, we found that there was no famine at all. In fact, there was what? Plenty. You could eat for a month on a day’s wages. Remember when we search the Scripture? Are you there?
Is the first seal the antichrist, and what does he say about the famine in the seals?

Revelation 6:1-8: Now I saw when the Lamb opened one of the seals; and I heard one of the four living creatures saying with a voice like thunder, “Come and see.” And I looked, and behold, a white horse. He who sat on it had a bow; and a crown was given to him, and he went out conquering and to conquer. When He opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature saying, “Come and see.” Another horse, fiery red, went out. And it was granted to the one who sat on it to take peace from the earth, and that people should kill one another; and there was given to him a great sword. When He opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature say, “Come and see.” So I looked, and behold, a black horse, and he who sat on it had a pair of scales in his hand. And I heard a voice in the midst of the four living creatures saying, “A quart of wheat for a denarius, and three quarts of barley for a denarius; and do not harm the oil and the wine.” When He opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature saying, “Come and see.” So I looked, and behold, a pale horse. And the name of him who sat on it was Death, and Hades followed with him. And power was given to them over a fourth of the earth, to kill with sword, with hunger, with death, and by the beasts of the earth.
As it was in the days of Noah and Lot, was there a famine?

He says Jesus’ comparison to Noah’s and Lot’s days shows life “going on as normal,” with people “getting married,” “buying,” “selling,” and “violence was in the earth, but not famine.” He says Sodom had “abundance of bread, abundance of idleness.”
As it was in the days of Noah and Lot, was there a famine?

But boy, you know, we just interpret it; that’s when you get into trouble, it’s when you start interpreting, especially because you want it to fit into your idea. Now, to prove this, Jesus said, “As it was in the days of Noah and the days of Lot, so shall it be at the coming of the Son of Man.” Was there any famine in the days of Noah? No, life was going on as normal. They were getting married, they were buying, they were selling, they were just living there. There was no big thing. Violence was in the earth, but not famine. They were killing each other, but not famine. So was as in Sodom and Gomorrah: abundance of bread, abundance of idleness, and they committed sexual immorality and worshiped false gods and all the rest.
As it was in the days of Noah and Lot, was there a famine?

Luke 17:26-30: And as it was in the days of Noah, so it will be also in the days of the Son of Man: They ate, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noah entered the ark, and the flood came and destroyed them all. Likewise as it was also in the days of Lot: They ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they built; but on the day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven and destroyed them all. Even so will it be in the day when the Son of Man is revealed.
Are the seals, trumpets and bowls one big event? (the sixth seal and the day of wrath)

He says the sun, moon and stars cannot be both gone at the sixth seal and still there, so “this is one big event.” He says the sixth seal and the seventh trumpet both say “the day of the wrath has come,” so “how can you have two days of wrath coming?” and the seven last plagues are “summing up the one big event.”
Are the seals, trumpets and bowls one big event? (the sixth seal and the day of wrath)

Now, a quarter of the people slain. All these red things is where people are dying. The rivers, here, all these red illustrate over here; a third of the people are dying. So people are dying one way or another, and it says the martyrs, and then over here you got the martyrs drinking blood, the people that killed the martyrs. And then you got the earthquake, which is in a gray area here. You got the sun darkened, the abyss opens and darkens the sun again, and over here darkness. You got darkness in all three areas, probably because it’s all one big thing. Are you with me? All right, then you got the sixth seal, where he says the sun and moon are turned to blood, darkened and turned to blood. And how, you know, if the sun’s gone, the moon don’t have light either; that’s a no-brainer. The moon gets its light from the sun. Okay, but it says that the heavens are rolled away like a scroll, just like it says in Isaiah that the heavens are going to be rolled away like a scroll. Well, how many know the sun and the moon are in the heavens? How many know the stars are there? Now, how many know if this is literal, if this is actual what happened, we can’t have any more sun, moon and stars? They’re gone, and yet we have them. See, the sun’s hot, the sun’s dark and the sun’s gone. So this tells us what? This is one big event. Hallelujah. I tell you, it pays to read the book instead of all those books, but all those books drove me to find the real truth in the book. Now, it says right here at the sixth seal, “the day of the wrath has come.” At the sixth seal, the day of the wrath has what? Come. Well, what’s all this other stuff here? That’s all one big thing; this is part of the day of wrath. Down here at the seventh trumpet he says the day of the wrath has come, same statement. Well, how can you have two days of wrath coming? It’s obvious it’s what? One big event. And the seven last plagues are summing up the one big event, and it means the other events are taking place all the time, and these things are going to be a great crescendo at the end, a great ending.
Are the seals, trumpets and bowls one big event? (the sixth seal and the day of wrath)

Revelation 6:12-17: I looked when He opened the sixth seal, and behold, there was a great earthquake; and the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the moon became like blood. And the stars of heaven fell to the earth, as a fig tree drops its late figs when it is shaken by a mighty wind. Then the sky receded as a scroll when it is rolled up, and every mountain and island was moved out of its place. And the kings of the earth, the great men, the rich men, the commanders, the mighty men, every slave and every free man, hid themselves in the caves and in the rocks of the mountains, and said to the mountains and rocks, “Fall on us and hide us from the face of Him who sits on the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb! For the great day of His wrath has come, and who is able to stand?” Isaiah 34:4: All the host of heaven shall be dissolved, And the heavens shall be rolled up like a scroll; All their host shall fall down As the leaf falls from the vine, And as fruit falling from a fig tree. Revelation 11:18: The nations were angry, and Your wrath has come, And the time of the dead, that they should be judged, And that You should reward Your servants the prophets and the saints, And those who fear Your name, small and great, And should destroy those who destroy the earth.”
Who has victory over the beast, and what will things be like when Jesus appears?

He says the people have “victory over the beast” and over Satan, and “if we got victory, we’re still here.” He says it will be like Noah’s and Lot’s days, with normal life, and “all of a sudden Jesus appears,” coming as a thief.
Who has victory over the beast, and what will things be like when Jesus appears?

Now, here it says that the people have victory over who? The beast, and victory over who? Satan. Where are we at? If we got victory, we’re still here. Are we giving in anything? Are we quitting? No, we have victory; we’re conquering. And there’s those voices at each one that I told you about. And remember, as it was in the days of Noah, it says they were buying, they were selling, they were marrying and giving in marriage. Is that a normal life, working, marrying? Yes. “And as it was in the days of Noah, and it was in the days of Lot, so shall it be at the coming of the Son of Man.” And that’s why it’s a thief: things are going to be normal, and all of a sudden Jesus appears. Whoo! All of a sudden something starts happening in the earth from the battles in the heavenlies, that humans can make a decision to serve God or not. Are you with me? Isn’t this a lot of stuff? I warned you it was a lot of stuff.
Who has victory over the beast, and what will things be like when Jesus appears?

Revelation 15:2: And I saw something like a sea of glass mingled with fire, and those who have the victory over the beast, over his image and over his mark and over the number of his name, standing on the sea of glass, having harps of God. Luke 17:26-30: And as it was in the days of Noah, so it will be also in the days of the Son of Man: They ate, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noah entered the ark, and the flood came and destroyed them all. Likewise as it was also in the days of Lot: They ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they built; but on the day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven and destroyed them all. Even so will it be in the day when the Son of Man is revealed.
What does he say about the 1833 sky event and where the rapture theory came from?

He says on November 13th, 1833 the sky lit up for four hours and people thought the end was here. He says the rapture theory was invented “back in the 1800s” and “wasn’t heard of before that,” and that groups then began to set dates, including 1843, called “the Great Disappointment.”
What does he say about the 1833 sky event and where the rapture theory came from?

On November 13th, 1833, the sky lit up for four hours. You could read a newspaper on the streets of New York at 2:00 in the morning. Billions of stars come buzzing through the atmosphere, one right after another. It was seen from Canada down to Florida and across the United States. Nighttime was daytime. Okay, so what did the people think? The end was here. This guy here created the rapture theory back in the 1800s, John Darby. He invented this theory. It’s very new; wasn’t heard of before that. No church taught it in their creed, it wasn’t in a catechism class, no statement of faith. You can’t find it anywhere till this guy come up with it. And then the Seventh-day Adventists, the Jehovah’s Witnesses, the Mormons, the Baptists, the fundamentalists all grabbed a hold of it, and they began to set dates. And this guy here set a date in 1843: Jesus was going to come, the end of the world was going to happen. It was called the Great Disappointment. People actually sold their houses, they took a vacation from their job, and they went to watch the end of it all, and then it didn’t happen.
What happens when people set dates for the end?

He says when the dates failed some “committed suicide, some went into great depression,” and that “all these little cults appeared at that time.” He says modern predictions like “the world’s going to end May the 21st” are wrong, and “he’ll come up with a new one.”
What happens when people set dates for the end?

Some committed suicide, some went into great depression. They had been, and there were preachers preaching it was a why, but the people would not believe it. The Baptists were strong in it, and it didn’t happen. Then the Mormons predicted it. The Seventh-day Adventists, that’s where they kept their name from, the advent, and all these little cults appeared at that time, the Mormons and Jehovah’s Witnesses and all this. Man, the whole focus of... was on the second coming. Did you guys know that these groups sprung out of this second coming nonsense? Mary [unclear] Eddy and all these so-called prophets: false prophecy. Well, now you know, and you can check it out, it’s in all history books, you can read it, it’s not hard to find. Okay, then we come to the modern world. There’s [unclear] Lindsay and that guy up there is Camp, the top guy. He’s saying the world’s going to end May the 21st, I think it is, of this month. Yeah, May the 21st. That’s after May the 14th; that was yesterday. A great catastrophic thing was going to happen throughout the world, and we just went along our merry way, but they’re still, they’re still saying he’s coming the 21st. And guess what? On the 22nd he’s going to be wrong, and he’ll come up with a new one. He’s come up with them before, and he’s got people believing it.
Why should you read the Bible for yourself and confirm it with someone living it?

He says “you go to the book for yourself,” and then “confirm what you’re reading in the book with somebody that knows the book and living the life.” He says to get somebody “strong in God because they’ve been walking with God” rather than a writer whose “changed prophecies” earn “millions of bucks.”
Why should you read the Bible for yourself and confirm it with someone living it?

You see, that’s why it’s important that you go to the book for yourself. Could that be an amen? And not just for yourself, but you confirm what you’re reading in the book with somebody that knows the book and living the life, the book is working for them. Amen. Don’t get somebody that’s wimpy and weak-hearted and can’t handle the slightest little problem and all this; get somebody that’s strong in God because they’ve been walking with God, and they walk with a buck, and confirm your truths and your beliefs by them. [Unclear] Lindsay said the rapture would come before 1990, in The Late Great Planet Earth. Well, 1990 came, and he quietly took the book off the shelf and brought in a new one, and he said it will come by the year 2000. Well, the year 2000 came and went, and he quietly took off that book and brought in a new one, and the guy makes millions of bucks from Christians reading his changed prophecies.
Does God condemn a whole nation because of its government?

He says “God loves everybody in the world” and “is not picking on any particular race or culture,” and that “a nation is just simply a form of government under which a bunch of people live.” He says God “isn’t going to condemn a nation” because its government is communist, “he loves those people.”
Does God condemn a whole nation because of its government?

Now, I stopped reading them after the first time they’re wrong. How about you? And that’s what the Bible says to do. These guys do make a lot of money; they live in big homes from ignorant Christians sending in money and believing in this nonsense. Folks, God loves everybody in the world. He’s coming to everybody in the world, he’s wanting everybody in the world to come to him. He is not picking on any particular race or culture or whatever; he’s after the whole world. Can that be an amen? And he doesn’t hate one nation above another. No, he loves all the nations. A nation is just simply a form of government under which a bunch of people live, and he isn’t going to condemn a nation in people in China because their government is communist, is he? Why? He loves those people. And we saw him bring down Russia, and he can bring down China. He’s gone.
Why might an answer to prayer be delayed, and do science and the Bible conflict?

He says answers may take a while “like Daniel because of things in the heavenlies,” so “pray a little harder.” He says “science and the Bible never contradict each other,” and conflicts only come from “extreme science or people in the Bible going extreme ways.”
Why might an answer to prayer be delayed, and do science and the Bible conflict?

We see the people get victory over the beast and over Satan. We see that God protects his people, that God answers their prayer. It may take a while, like Daniel, because of things in the heavenlies, but he shows up. And if you’re going through things and you want God to move a little faster, just pray a little harder, because there could be warfare going on in the heavenlies so that the answer can be released to you. And it’s worth the wait, ‘cause when he comes, nothing can replace it. And this secular reasoning: don’t be fooled by it. Science and the Bible never contradict each other. Never. It was the Bible that said the earth is hung on nothing before scientists even knew that. Ain’t that right? Yes. It was the Bible that said the earth was a sphere, a round, before scientists, in just the last couple hundred years, came up with the fact that it’s a round ball, or 500 years. So science and the Bible never conflict, if it’s reasonable science and reasonable Bible. But when you have extreme science, or people in the Bible going extreme ways, then yes, you got a conflict. Why? Because they’re being ridiculous, they’re being extreme.
Why might an answer to prayer be delayed, and do science and the Bible conflict?

Daniel 10:12-13: Then he said to me, “Do not fear, Daniel, for from the first day that you set your heart to understand, and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard; and I have come because of your words. But the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me twenty-one days; and behold, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, for I had been left alone there with the kings of Persia. Job 26:7: He stretches out the north over empty space; He hangs the earth on nothing.
What was the mixed multitude that left Egypt, and why do some harden their hearts?

He says God “separated the people of Egypt from God’s people” and “the plagues didn’t touch God’s people,” and a mixed multitude of Egyptians and others joined them, so “nations in the last days” will join “our ranks.” He says those who choose to do wicked “harden yourself” because they “don’t want to live right.”
What was the mixed multitude that left Egypt, and why do some harden their hearts?

Jesus is on your side, folks, and the Bible says that he will finish the good work he began in you. And there’s coming a day, just like in Egypt, where God separated the people of Egypt from God’s people. Egypt had darkness in their dwelling; God’s people had what? Light. The plagues didn’t touch God’s people after the frogs; God’s people were kept. And then there was a mixed multitude. I forgot to bring that out there. There was a harvest. A mixed multitude came out of Egypt with God’s people. There were Egyptians and other nationalities living there that joined God’s people’s ranks, and they went out of Egypt with God’s people. And we’re going to have that: nations in the last days joining our ranks, and there’s a great harvest coming. Amen. We are going to be honored in the earth when God starts moving in this realm of revelation, and the people that choose to do wicked, their hearts are going to be hardened, because it’s the foolishness of preaching that saves. If you’re not going to believe the Word of God, you’re not going to believe, even if these things come. You’re going to justify him, ‘cause you don’t want to live right, you don’t want to choose right, you want your own way, and so you’re going to harden yourself. We see it in Revelation, we’ve seen it in Sodom and Gomorrah and Noah’s flood and in Egypt, didn’t we? Aren’t you glad you’re on the side of Jesus? How many of this morning are on Jesus’s side? Yes.
What was the mixed multitude that left Egypt, and why do some harden their hearts?

Philippians 1:6: being confident of this very thing, that He who has begun a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ; Exodus 12:38: A mixed multitude went up with them also, and flocks and herds—a great deal of livestock. Exodus 10:23: They did not see one another; nor did anyone rise from his place for three days. But all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings.
What does he say not to pay attention to?
He says wars, volcanoes and rumors of wars: “don’t even pay any attention to it,” since “they’ve been happening since creation and they’re going to keep happening.”
Does he say Christians have always been hated?
Yes. He says it has “happened” through “every generation,” and that “your own family members will hate you if you really serve Christ.”
Who does he say withstood the angel in Daniel 10?
He says it was not the human king of Persia but “a prince in the spiritual heavenlies, in wicked places,” and the “spiritual kingdom who was influencing the kingdom on earth of Persia.”
What does he say John is showing in Revelation?
He says that “you can’t get any plainer” and that “John is showing us the spiritual powers being destroyed in Revelation just as Jesus said they would be.”
What does he say God is doing when the moon turns to blood in Acts?
He says “God is filling people with his Spirit, God is using his young people, both male and female, to speak the word of the Lord through prophecy,” and people are getting saved.
What does he say about the famine in the seals?
He says that when they searched the Scriptures, the price of barley and wheat meant “there was no famine at all,” in fact “plenty,” and you “could eat for a month on a day’s wages.”
What does he say gets people into trouble when interpreting prophecy?
He says “that’s when you get into trouble, it’s when you start interpreting, especially because you want it to fit into your idea.”
How does he relate the sixth seal and the seventh trumpet?
He says both say “the day of the wrath has come,” and that “it’s obvious” it’s “one big event,” with the other events “taking place all the time” and a “great crescendo at the end.”
What does he say about normal life before Jesus appears?

He says “things are going to be normal, and all of a sudden Jesus appears,” and that something will start happening in the earth “from the battles in the heavenlies,” so that people can decide to serve God or not.
How old does he say the rapture theory is?
He says it is “very new,” was created “back in the 1800s,” “wasn’t heard of before that,” and that no church taught it in a creed, catechism or statement of faith.
What does he say about teachers whose predictions keep changing?

He says he stopped reading them “after the first time they’re wrong,” and that people send money and believe “nonsense” from teachers who “quietly took the book off the shelf and brought in a new one.”
Does he say God loves all nations?
Yes. He says “God loves everybody in the world,” is “not picking on any particular race or culture,” and “doesn’t hate one nation above another.”
What does he say to do if God seems slow to answer?
He says “just pray a little harder, because there could be warfare going on in the heavenlies so that the answer can be released to you,” and that “it’s worth the wait.”
What does he say the Bible said before scientists knew?
He says it was the Bible “that said the earth is hung on nothing before scientists even knew,” and that the earth was a sphere before scientists “came up with the fact that it’s a round ball.”

items.d: In this first message on six of the seven seals, Pastor David G. Kincer begins from the idea that people with charts and predictions missed Jesus’ first coming and may be wrong about the second. He asks what…
p: In this first message on six of the seven seals, Pastor David G. Kincer begins from the idea that people with charts and predictions missed Jesus’ first coming and may be wrong about the second. He asks what the book with seven seals in Revelation 5:5 is, then starts the four horsemen: the white horse and whether it is the Antichrist, what the Bible says about “antichrist,” the rider of Revelation 19:11, and the red horse, closing with Mark 13:7 on wars and the end.
Why does he say we can be wrong about the second coming the way people were wrong about the first?

He says the Jews and the preachers who had “their charts” at Jesus’ first coming “missed every point,” because they looked for a son of David to restore the kingdom from Rome, and “the Messiah wasn’t coming to restore the natural kingdom from Rome to them. He was coming to put a kingdom in people’s lives.” He says “we can be wrong today,” and “they did not know the Messiah was God Himself when He came the first time.”
Why does he say we can be wrong about the second coming the way people were wrong about the first?

Seriously, okay, we’re going to get into the Bible this morning, and we are talking about the book of Revelation, and today we’re going to be talking about six of the seven seals. Now, the approach to Revelation is strictly from the book of Revelation, and you’ve got to remember this, please. Get this in your cranial vacuum what I’m going to say. The Jews and the preachers, when Jesus came, had their charts. They had it all figured out what was going to happen, how it was going to happen, and they missed every point. Do you realize that? You see, the Jews had it wrong the first time Jesus came. They were looking for a son of David to restore the kingdom to them from Rome, and the Messiah wasn’t coming to restore the natural kingdom from Rome to them. He was coming to put a kingdom in people’s lives. See, they were totally wrong, and we can be wrong today. They did not know the Messiah was God Himself when He came the first time. They didn’t have that in their charts and their predictions. They did not know.
What does he say defiles us, and what did the religious teachers of Jesus’ day miss? (Mark 7:15; Matthew 11:14)

He says “it is things within that defile us, and not what we eat or what we wear,” and “it’s what comes out, those words and those actions, that’s what defiles us and condemns us.” He says they “had doctrines of clothing, Sabbath day’s journey,” and “the washing of hands and dishes,” and of the Sabbath rule says “it’s not in the Bible, they made it up.” He says they “didn’t know that John the Baptist was Elijah that was to come in the spirit,” and “they wanted and tried to kill Jesus, God Himself.”
What does he say defiles us, and what did the religious teachers of Jesus’ day miss? (Mark 7:15; Matthew 11:14)

It is things within that defile us, and not what we eat or what we wear. See, Seventh Day Adventists, they’re still into the food program. The holiness people are into no jewelry and no makeup, and you know, look pale and don’t go to hell. You know, and it’s not what we eat. We can eat pork, we can eat what, it has nothing to do with our character and nothing to do with our spiritual man and nothing to do with sin. See, it’s what comes out, those words and those actions, that’s what defiles us and condemns us. They had doctrines of clothing, Sabbath day’s journey, you can only go so far on the Sabbath day, it’s not in the Bible, they made it up, the washing of hands and dishes and all this stuff. You see, they had all of these doctrines, and when Jesus came, they missed it totally. They didn’t know that John the Baptist was Elijah that was to come in the spirit, the forerunner of Jesus, and they cut off his head. They wanted and tried to kill Jesus, God Himself, which violated the Ten Commandments they claim to believe in. Amen. And a lot of these theoretical people about the second coming, they don’t balance their checkbook, they don’t stay married, they violate the very book that they say that they believe in, but yet they got this second coming all figured out.
What does he say defiles us, and what did the religious teachers of Jesus’ day miss? (Mark 7:15; Matthew 11:14)

Mark 7:15: There is nothing that enters a man from outside which can defile him; but the things which come out of him, those are the things that defile a man. Matthew 11:14: And if you are willing to receive it, he is Elijah who is to come.
What does he say about preachers who predict the end time and the day or hour? (Matthew 24:36)

He says preachers “have made millions of dollars selling you a bill of goods, claiming to know the inside of the end time, when Jesus Himself and God Himself said twice, no man knows the day or the hour.” He says they “still predict the day,” yet “Nobody knows but God Himself.” He says some in Jesus’ day thought He was an old prophet risen from the dead, and “this is what happens with the second coming teaching. We wind up leaving Jesus Himself, the most important person in the Bible, the goal of the Bible, and get into our petty little doctrines that mean nothing.”
What does he say about preachers who predict the end time and the day or hour? (Matthew 24:36)

And let me tell you something: preachers have made millions of dollars selling you a bill of goods, claiming to know the inside of the end time, when Jesus Himself and God Himself said twice, no man knows the day or the hour. They still predict the day, they still, still, still predict the year and the month and everything else, and it says plainly, what? Nobody knows but God Himself. And you buy their books, and you got the book to read yourself, and they’re making a fortune. Literally, some believed Jesus was an old prophet risen from the dead. Look at that doctrine they conjured up. Well, this is one of them old prophets, I don’t know which one, but it’s one of them that raised from the dead. And they believed Jesus was a sinner. They called Him a sinner, and He’s God, and God cannot what? Sin. The Bible says there was no sin in Him. And this is what they said: if we leave Jesus alone, all will believe on Him. Well, duh, that’s the whole point. We’re supposed to be believing and trusting in and following Jesus Christ, but they wanted people to believe in their group, their doctrine, and leave Jesus. And this is what happens with the second coming teaching. We wind up leaving Jesus Himself, the most important person in the Bible, the goal of the Bible, and get into our petty little doctrines that mean nothing.
What does he say about preachers who predict the end time and the day or hour? (Matthew 24:36)
Matthew 24:36: “But of that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels of heaven, but My Father only.
What did the apostles and John the Baptist misunderstand about Jesus? (Matthew 16:22; 17:4; 11:2-3)

He asks, “if they missed the first time, could it be possible we don’t know beans about the second time?” He says “even the apostles did not understand that Jesus was going to die,” that Peter said “you can’t die,” that they “wanted to be number one,” and wanted to build three tabernacles at the transfiguration: “these are the apostles, the chosen twelve.” He adds that John the Baptist later sent his disciples to ask “Are You the One?” and asks, “just because we hear something, does that mean we got it?”
What did the apostles and John the Baptist misunderstand about Jesus? (Matthew 16:22; 17:4; 11:2-3)

Are you with me now? My point is this: if they missed the first time, could it be possible we don’t know beans about the second time? See, they knew the Messiah was coming, just as we know Jesus is what? Coming again. We know that it says over and over He’s coming the second time. And so with that introduction, we’re going to be studying this book of Revelation. Even the apostles did not understand that Jesus was going to die. He told them He’s going to die, and they still didn’t get it. Isn’t that right? So just because we hear something, does that mean we got it? No. No, in fact, Peter said, “Well, you can’t die. We’re not going to let you die.” They wanted to be in charge of others, the first, you know, they wanted to be number one. They wanted to build three tabernacles when Jesus was transfigured. They wanted to build one for Jesus, one for Moses, and one for Elijah. See, they got it all wrong, and these are the apostles, the chosen twelve. John the Baptist, after declaring that Jesus was the One to come and take away the sins of the world, check this out. After John the Baptist declared and baptized Jesus, then a little bit later he sends his disciples to Jesus and said, “Are You the One?” And yet in this day and hour, these guys are proclaiming they got all this knowledge.
What did the apostles and John the Baptist misunderstand about Jesus? (Matthew 16:22; 17:4; 11:2-3)

Matthew 16:22: Then Peter took Him aside and began to rebuke Him, saying, “Far be it from You, Lord; this shall not happen to You!” Matthew 17:4: Then Peter answered and said to Jesus, “Lord, it is good for us to be here; if You wish, let us make here three tabernacles: one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” Matthew 11:2-3: And when John had heard in prison about the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples and said to Him, “Are You the Coming One, or do we look for another?”
What does he say about prophecy writers who keep revising their predictions?

He says the author of a popular end-time book “has changed his theory twelve times that I know of, because he predicted some things that did not happen, so he had to rewrite his book, and people bought it again.” He then introduces today’s topic, “six of the seven seals,” and notes that Daniel “was told to shut up the words and seal the book.”
What does he say about prophecy writers who keep revising their predictions?

And the guy that wrote The Late Great Planet Earth, Hal Lindsay, has changed his theory twelve times that I know of, because he predicted some things that did not happen, so he had to rewrite his book, and people bought it again. And they just keep buying it, like Hal Lindsay got some kind of personal insight that no one else has. Are you with me? So with that in our cranial vacuum, we don’t have a cranial vacuum anymore, we got something in there, you know, let’s just keep this thing simple. All right, what are we teaching on today? Six of the seven seals. You remember in the book of Daniel, Daniel himself, that they use to twist Scriptures and get these ideas, was told to shut up the words and seal the book.
What does he say about prophecy writers who keep revising their predictions?
Daniel 12:4: “But you, Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book until the time of the end; many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall increase.”
Could we be hearing Revelation without understanding it, like Daniel? (Daniel 12:8)

He says Daniel said, “I heard, but I understood not,” and asks, “could it be possible, when we read the book of Revelation, we are hearing but we’re not getting much understanding out of it?” He says “we don’t always understand things, and there’s nothing wrong with it.” When Jesus came the first time, “they started understanding as things happened,” and “all their charts didn’t amount to anything,” so at His second coming “we may be totally wrong in saying how He’s going to do it.”
Could we be hearing Revelation without understanding it, like Daniel? (Daniel 12:8)

Are you there? And in the last chapter, when the angel is talking to Daniel, Daniel says, “I heard, but I understood not.” Could it be possible, when we read the book of Revelation, we are hearing but we’re not getting much understanding out of it? And Daniel, who was one of the three heroes of the Old Testament, did not understand what the angel was saying. Could it be possible we don’t always understand things, and there’s nothing wrong with it? And this is the point: when Jesus came the first time, they started understanding as things happened, the virgin conceiving and having a child. See, then as it was preached and as it happened, then they started what? Getting understanding. All their charts didn’t amount to anything, all their programs and all their ideas they come up with had to be thrown out when it started happening. And it could be the same way when Jesus comes the second time. When He starts doing something, we’re going to go, “Oh, that’s what that is! Oh, that’s what that is!” Because God is doing something again, and we can identify it as He does it, and we may be totally wrong in saying how He’s going to do it. Could that be a good amen? Hallelujah.
Could we be hearing Revelation without understanding it, like Daniel? (Daniel 12:8)
Daniel 12:8: Although I heard, I did not understand. Then I said, “My lord, what shall be the end of these things?”
What is the book with seven seals in Revelation 5:5, and what other books does the Bible mention? (Revelation 5:5; 20:12; Isaiah 29:11)

He calls this “a college course. This isn’t for wimps. This is serious teaching.” He reads Revelation 5:5 about the Lion of the tribe of Judah who “hath prevailed to open the book and to loose the seven seals thereof,” and says the Bible tells us “about eight books in the Bible itself,” including the Book of Life and the book of our works in Revelation 20:12, where “everything we did, everything we say is written there.” He then rules out the Scriptures themselves and the judgment book of Israel and Babylon, and raises the sealed book Isaiah saw.
What is the book with seven seals in Revelation 5:5, and what other books does the Bible mention? (Revelation 5:5; 20:12; Isaiah 29:11)

And with that in your head, I told you this is a college course. This isn’t for wimps. This is serious teaching. You know, in college you listen to the professor and then you got to go home and study for hours to get it. Are you there? So we got a bunch of non-wimps in here this morning. You came to hear this tough teaching, hard to sit there. Okay, we got a picture of the Lamb, and the seven seals are open, there, of the book in Revelation 5:5: “The Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book and to loose the seven seals thereof.” What book? The Bible tells us about eight books in the Bible itself. The Book of Life, you know, if our name’s in there, we go to heaven, if it’s not, we’re in trouble. The book of our works, in Revelation 20:12, everything we did, everything we say is written there, and if we’re in the Book of Life, we’re not judged out of the things in the book of works. Hallelujah. Anyway, we know it’s not that book. We certainly know it’s not the Scriptures, the Bible itself, because Jesus opened understanding to them. We know it’s not the judgment book of Israel and Babylon and Jeremiah, because that was to them. We know that the sealed book that Isaiah saw could be it. This is a sealed book. Isaiah saw a sealed book, but it was sealed, it wasn’t opened, and so it just goes on. He saw a sealed book and that’s it.
What is the book with seven seals in Revelation 5:5, and what other books does the Bible mention? (Revelation 5:5; 20:12; Isaiah 29:11)

Revelation 5:5: But one of the elders said to me, “Do not weep. Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has prevailed to open the scroll and to loose its seven seals.” Revelation 20:12: And I saw the dead, small and great, standing before God, and books were opened. And another book was opened, which is the Book of Life. And the dead were judged according to their works, by the things which were written in the books. Isaiah 29:11: The whole vision has become to you like the words of a book that is sealed, which men deliver to one who is literate, saying, “Read this, please.” And he says, “I cannot, for it is sealed.”
Could the book be Isaiah’s, Ezekiel’s or Daniel’s sealed book, or the book of remembrance? (Ezekiel 2:9-10; Daniel 12:4; Luke 21:20; Exodus 17:14)

He considers whether it is the sealed book Isaiah saw, the book of woe in Ezekiel, or Daniel’s sealed book, and says “there’s a lot of woes when this book starts getting opened.” He says that in Luke, “when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh,” so “the destruction of Jerusalem in 70 AD was the fulfillment of Daniel,” and “some of Daniel’s book was open, so I doubt it’s Daniel’s book.” He also considers the book of remembrance in Exodus 17:14 and says, “I doubt it’s that book, because people have been sinning ever since.”
Could the book be Isaiah’s, Ezekiel’s or Daniel’s sealed book, or the book of remembrance? (Ezekiel 2:9-10; Daniel 12:4; Luke 21:20; Exodus 17:14)

The book was locked up and stayed locked up, so maybe that could be it. The book of woe in Ezekiel that Ezekiel saw could be, because there’s a lot of woes when this book starts getting opened, there’s a lot of woes. And then the sealed book of Daniel that I told you about earlier, seal the book, all those things he saw, he said seal it up until the last days, but we got some revelation of Daniel’s sealed book. When Jesus came, Jesus said that the abomination of desolation, when you see that, you know that the time is nigh, in Matthew 13:14 and in Mark. But in Luke it says, “When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.” So we know that the destruction of Jerusalem in 70 AD was the fulfillment of Daniel. We know that, so at least part of Daniel’s sealed book was opened up, if not all of it, then. And so Daniel’s book could have been fulfilled during Jesus’s birth, death, and resurrection, and the church period, the early church period. Are you with me? Because we have some insight that some of Daniel’s book was open, so I doubt it’s Daniel’s book. Hallelujah. And we also know that Jesus came and all that in that book of Daniel. And then you got the book of remembrance. In Exodus 17:14, Amalek came and attacked Israel and picked on the stragglers and the weak ones, and God says, “I’m going to have a book of remembrance for him.” And a few hundred years later, sure enough, God says, “Okay, it’s time to judge Amalek for what he did back there to Israel and the weak ones and the straggling.” He picked on the stragglers and the weak ones, and He had Saul to rise up and destroy that nation and that king. Are you there? And so I doubt it’s that book, because people have been sinning ever since
Could the book be Isaiah’s, Ezekiel’s or Daniel’s sealed book, or the book of remembrance? (Ezekiel 2:9-10; Daniel 12:4; Luke 21:20; Exodus 17:14)

Ezekiel 2:9-10: Now when I looked, there was a hand stretched out to me; and behold, a scroll of a book was in it. Then He spread it before me; and there was writing on the inside and on the outside, and written on it were lamentations and mourning and woe. Matthew 24:15: “Therefore when you see the ‘abomination of desolation,’ spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place” (whoever reads, let him understand), Luke 21:20: “But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation is near. Exodus 17:14: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Write this for a memorial in the book and recount it in the hearing of Joshua, that I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.”
What does he say the book in Revelation is, and how can a record in the book of remembrance be erased?

He says “most likely the book in Revelation is its own book. It’s the book of wrath. It’s a book that explains God’s day of wrath that already has been explained throughout the Scriptures. It’s not a fresh new revelation.” He says “when you do things, God remembers,” but you can get it erased by repenting: “That’s the power of the blood. The power of the blood is endless, and there is nothing it can’t cleanse.”
What does he say the book in Revelation is, and how can a record in the book of remembrance be erased?

Eve. And yes, there’s a book of remembrance, and He does come to correct and deal with that. Most likely the book in Revelation is its own book. It’s the book of wrath. It’s a book that explains God’s day of wrath that already has been explained throughout the Scriptures. It’s not a fresh new revelation. Are you with me? I wanted you to know there’s eight books in the Bible. See, there is a book of remembrance. When you do things, God remembers. All right, you can get it erased by what? Repenting. Absolutely. “I was wrong.” That’s the power of the blood. The power of the blood is endless, and there is nothing it can’t cleanse. Don’t ever forget that. And a simple humbling yourself and admitting you’re wrong and asking forgiveness and cleansing gets it done.
Who rides the first horse in the seven seals, and does the Bible say it is the Antichrist? (Revelation 6:1-2)

He says “we feel like we got to interpret the stuff, and this is where we get into our problem.” The first horse is “a white horse with a rider that has a crown and a bow,” going “conquering and to conquer.” He says most interpreters say it is the Antichrist, but “it never says in the Bible that the Antichrist rides a white horse.”
Who rides the first horse in the seven seals, and does the Bible say it is the Antichrist? (Revelation 6:1-2)

Hallelujah, that’s the bottom line. Now, let’s go. Okay, here we are, the four horsemen. The seven seals are going to be opened here. And here comes the interpretations of all these things. We feel like we got to interpret the stuff, and this is where we get into our problem. All right, we get four horses. The first one is a white horse with a rider that has a crown and a bow, and this horse and rider, they go conquering and to conquer. See, now they say that this is a war horse and rider, or most of them say this is the Antichrist. It never says in the Bible that the Antichrist rides a white horse.
Who rides the first horse in the seven seals, and does the Bible say it is the Antichrist? (Revelation 6:1-2)

Revelation 6:1-2: Now I saw when the Lamb opened one of the seals; and I heard one of the four living creatures saying with a voice like thunder, “Come and see.” And I looked, and behold, a white horse. He who sat on it had a bow; and a crown was given to him, and he went out conquering and to conquer.
What does he say the Bible teaches about “antichrist”? (1 John 2:18; 4:2-3)

He says “it never says that the Antichrist is some one person that’s going to rise up in the earth,” and “we conjure up these things and then we go to the Scripture to fit them in, and this is our problem.” He says the apostle John “said there are many antichrists” because “they oppose Christ,” saying “Christ hasn’t come in the flesh, He wasn’t the Word that came in the flesh, He wasn’t God.” He says “the Jews who do not believe Jesus has come the first time, they are what? Antichrist,” and adds, “That’s the truth. They oppose Jesus.”
What does he say the Bible teaches about “antichrist”? (1 John 2:18; 4:2-3)

Never. It never says that the Antichrist is some one person that’s going to rise up in the earth. Never says that anywhere. We conjure up these things and then we go to the Scripture to fit them in, and this is our problem. You see, John, the apostle John himself, said there are many antichrists. You see why? Because they oppose Christ. They say Christ hasn’t come in the flesh, He wasn’t the Word that came in the flesh, He wasn’t God. That’s antichrist. That’s opposing Christ. And so the Jews who do not believe Jesus has come the first time, they are what? Antichrist. Oh, you can’t say that, that’s intolerance. That’s the truth. They oppose Jesus, and God was
What does he say the Bible teaches about “antichrist”? (1 John 2:18; 4:2-3)

1 John 2:18: Little children, it is the last hour; and as you have heard that the Antichrist is coming, even now many antichrists have come, by which we know that it is the last hour. 1 John 4:2-3: By this you know the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is of God, and every spirit that does not confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is not of God. And this is the spirit of the Antichrist, which you have heard was coming, and is now already in the world.
Who is the rider on the white horse in Revelation 19:11, and what about the crowns and the bow? (Revelation 19:11-15; 4:10)

Reading Revelation 19:11, he says “now we got somebody on a white horse,” called “Faithful and True,” and answers the objection about one crown versus many: “when the elders bow before Him, they cast their crowns. He put them back on His head.” He says “you find Jesus came also with a bow and with an arrow,” and “the bottom line is it doesn’t tell us who this white horse rider is.” He says the messages to the seven churches tell them to “be overcomers.”
Who is the rider on the white horse in Revelation 19:11, and what about the crowns and the bow? (Revelation 19:11-15; 4:10)

Jesus. Amen. That’s what the Scripture says, and that’s all the authority we have to preach, is what the Scripture says. But now we do have a Scripture in Revelation that tells us about a white horse. In Revelation 19:11, there was a white horse, and “he that sat on him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war. And on his head were many crowns, and out of his mouth goes a sharp sword, with it he shall smite the nations that war against him and his army.” Now we got somebody on a white horse, but they say, “Well, the one here is one crown, and over there it’s many crowns.” Well, dummy, when the elders bow before Him, they cast their crowns. He put them back on His head. That’s as good a theory as yours. You think you’re going to get any honor when you stand before Jesus Himself? You’re going to give it back to Him. Why? You wouldn’t have any honor if it wasn’t for Him. So yeah, He’s going to wear your crown, because He’s the one empowered you to get your crown. Hallelujah. He says, “Well, He’s got a bow and not a sword.” Yes, but if you go through the Scriptures, you find Jesus came also with a bow and with an arrow. All right, so He can use the sword, the bow and arrow, they’re both the Word of God. But the bottom line is it doesn’t tell us who this white horse rider is. That’s the bottom line, it just says this guy. Now, does Jesus, is Jesus conquering? Yes. Is He going to conquer? Absolutely. It describes Him in the messages to the seven churches. Did He tell all of them to rise up and be conquerors? Yeah, be overcomers.
Who is the rider on the white horse in Revelation 19:11, and what about the crowns and the bow? (Revelation 19:11-15; 4:10)

Revelation 19:11-15: Now I saw heaven opened, and behold, a white horse. And He who sat on him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness He judges and makes war. His eyes were like a flame of fire, and on His head were many crowns. He had a name written that no one knew except Himself. He was clothed with a robe dipped in blood, and His name is called The Word of God. And the armies in heaven, clothed in fine linen, white and clean, followed Him on white horses. Now out of His mouth goes a sharp sword, that with it He should strike the nations. And He Himself will rule them with a rod of iron. He Himself treads the winepress of the fierceness and wrath of Almighty God. Revelation 4:10: the twenty-four elders fall down before Him who sits on the throne and worship Him who lives forever and ever, and cast their crowns before the throne, saying: Revelation 2:7: “He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To him who overcomes I will give to eat from the tree of life, which is in the midst of the Paradise of God.” ’
What does he say about conquering and overcoming through Christ?

He says “how do we overcome? Through Jesus Christ,” and asks how many “have conquered things in your life through Christ.” He says “that’s the King of kings and the Lord of lords riding on His white horse. He is conquering, He is going to conquer, and He has conquered.” He says “the Bible never says the Antichrist rides a white horse, or the Antichrist has a crown, or the Antichrist has power to conquer people for God and win people to Christ.”
What does he say about conquering and overcoming through Christ?

Hallelujah. And how do we overcome? Through Jesus Christ. Amen. How many of you are conquering? Have conquered things in your life through Christ? How many things are being conquered right now? They’re not quite down, but they’re being conquered, and how many of you go looking tomorrow for some other things to be conquered in your life? Yeah, that’s the King of kings and the Lord of lords riding on His white horse. He is conquering, He is going to conquer, and He has conquered. Amen. That’s as good a theory as them things that the Antichrist, where do you get that from? Because you’re wanting to build a theory you already wanted to reach, and so you’re grabbing for things, and you just say it means that. You cannot just say it means that when the Bible doesn’t say that. And the Bible never says the Antichrist rides a white horse, or the Antichrist has a crown, or the Antichrist has power to conquer people for God and win people to Christ. Are you with me?
What does he say about the red horse and God “smiting” the nations? (Revelation 6:3-4; Acts 2:37)

He asks, “Is God wanting to smite the nations, the people? Isn’t that what He did on the day of Pentecost? Their hearts were smitten.” He describes the second horse as “a red horse with a huge sword” given “power to take peace from the earth so that men slaughter one another,” and says “He isn’t slaughtering anyone, they’re slaughtering what? One another.” The theory people, he says, “call this anarchy, the absence of government.”
What does he say about the red horse and God “smiting” the nations? (Revelation 6:3-4; Acts 2:37)

Now, hallelujah. Is God wanting to smite the nations, the people? Isn’t that what He did on the day of Pentecost? Their hearts were smitten. Amen. How many of you had your heart smitten? Yeah, about Christ. Yeah, a change of heart. Absolutely. That fits way more into this Antichrist thing. Can I hear an amen? Amen. Now, the second horse is a red horse with a huge sword. Empowered, he’s been given power to take peace from the earth so that men slaughter one another. He isn’t slaughtering anyone, they’re slaughtering what? One another. The theory people call this anarchy, the absence of government, the disorder and the lawlessness that’s coming.
What does he say about the red horse and God “smiting” the nations? (Revelation 6:3-4; Acts 2:37)

Revelation 6:3-4: When He opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature saying, “Come and see.” Another horse, fiery red, went out. And it was granted to the one who sat on it to take peace from the earth, and that people should kill one another; and there was given to him a great sword. Acts 2:37: Now when they heard this, they were cut to the heart, and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles, “Men and brethren, what shall we do?”
Does he say wars and earthquakes are signs that the end has come? (Mark 13:7-8)

He says wars and killing have been “going on since the beginning,” and reads Mark 13:7 that such things “must needs be, but the end is not yet.” He says people call wars, earthquakes, volcanoes and hurricanes “the sign of the end,” but “Jesus said just the opposite.” In his words, “that’s no indication of the second coming,” and when people tell us what to believe, “we interpret the Bible to believe what they told us to believe, and yet Jesus Himself said just the opposite.”
Does he say wars and earthquakes are signs that the end has come? (Mark 13:7-8)

But let me submit to you, this has been going on since the beginning. People killing one another, hurting one another, it’s been going on ever since the earth started. In Mark 13:7 it says, “When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, be not troubled. Such things must needs be, but the end is not yet. For a nation will rise against nation, kingdom against kingdom, and there will be earthquakes in different places, and there will be famines and troubles. And these are the beginning of sorrows.” But the what? End is not yet. Did you hear that? And what do they say? “Oh, all these wars and earthquakes and volcanoes exploding and hurricanes, that’s the sign of the end.” Jesus said just the opposite. He said, [unclear], wars and rumors of war were going to happen, but what? The end, the second coming, is not yet. In other words, that’s no indication of the second coming. Are you out there? But see, when they tell us what to believe, and when we read the Bible, we interpret the Bible to believe what they told us to believe, and yet Jesus Himself said just the opposite. Are you there? You see, and so people have been killing people ever since.
Does he say wars and earthquakes are signs that the end has come? (Mark 13:7-8)

Mark 13:7-8: But when you hear of wars and rumors of wars, do not be troubled; for such things must happen, but the end is not yet. For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. And there will be earthquakes in various places, and there will be famines and troubles. These are the beginnings of sorrows.
What does he say people got wrong at Jesus’ first coming?

He says “the Jews had it wrong the first time Jesus came,” looking for “a son of David to restore the kingdom to them from Rome,” and “they did not know the Messiah was God Himself when He came the first time.”
Does he say anyone can know the day or hour of the second coming?
No. He says Jesus and God “said twice, no man knows the day or the hour,” and “it says plainly what? Nobody knows but God Himself.”
What does he say Peter said when Jesus spoke of dying?
He says, “Peter said, ‘Well, you can’t die. We’re not going to let you die.’” He says the disciples “wanted to be number one.”
Does he say Daniel understood what he heard from the angel?
No. He says that in the last chapter Daniel says, “I heard, but I understood not,” and that Daniel “did not understand what the angel was saying.”
What does he expect people to say when Jesus begins acting at the second coming?

He says, “When He starts doing something, we’re going to go, ‘Oh, that’s what that is! Oh, that’s what that is!’” and that “we can identify it as He does it, and we may be totally wrong in saying how He’s going to do it.”
How does he describe this teaching?
He says, “I told you this is a college course. This isn’t for wimps. This is serious teaching,” and that in college “you got to go home and study for hours to get it.”
What does he say the Book of Life and the book of works are?

He says, “The Book of Life, you know, if our name’s in there, we go to heaven, if it’s not, we’re in trouble. The book of our works, in Revelation 20:12, everything we did, everything we say is written there.”
How does he say what God remembers can be erased?
He asks, “You can get it erased by what? Repenting.” He says “a simple humbling yourself and admitting you’re wrong and asking forgiveness and cleansing gets it done.”
Does he say the Bible describes the Antichrist as one person?
No. He says, “It never says that the Antichrist is some one person that’s going to rise up in the earth,” and that John “said there are many antichrists.”
What does he say about honor when we stand before Jesus?
He says, “You think you’re going to get any honor when you stand before Jesus Himself? You’re going to give it back to Him. Why? You wouldn’t have any honor if it wasn’t for Him.”
Does he say wars and earthquakes are the sign of the end?
No. He says people say “that’s the sign of the end,” but “Jesus said just the opposite,” that “the end, the second coming, is not yet.”
What does he say about letting others tell us what to believe from the Bible?
He says, “when they tell us what to believe, and when we read the Bible, we interpret the Bible to believe what they told us to believe, and yet Jesus Himself said just the opposite.”

items.d: In this second message on six of the seven seals, Pastor David G. Kincer works through the third horse, the black horse with scales and the price of wheat and barley, and argues from Mark 6:37 that it does not…
p: In this second message on six of the seven seals, Pastor David G. Kincer works through the third horse, the black horse with scales and the price of wheat and barley, and argues from Mark 6:37 that it does not describe a famine. He then covers the fourth seal and the pale horse named Death, Satan’s limited authority, the fifth seal martyrs and the martyred number, and the sixth seal with its earthquake, darkened sun, blood-red moon and rolled-up sky.
How does he open this message, and how does he introduce the black horse? (Revelation 6:5-6)

He says Chicago and Washington, D.C., “are the murder capitals of the United States of America,” that “it’s not the gun that kills people, it’s the one pulling the trigger,” and “if you change the heart of a person, you have control.” He then moves on: “the third horse is a black horse, and its rider has a pair of scales.”
How does he open this message, and how does he introduce the black horse? (Revelation 6:5-6)

Chicago, by the way, and Washington, D.C., are the murder capitals of the United States of America. In Washington, D.C., you’re not allowed to have a gun, and in Chicago there’s strict gun controls, and guess what? They have the highest murder rate in America, and they just don’t get it. You see, it’s not the gun that kills people, it’s the one pulling the trigger. Are you there? So if you change the heart of a person, you have control. Amen. Anyway, just thought I’d throw that out. Okay, the third horse is a black horse, and its rider has a pair of scales. Wow. And there’s a voice saying, “A measure of wheat for a denarius, and three measures of barley for a denarius, but don’t hurt the oil and wine.”
How does he open this message, and how does he introduce the black horse? (Revelation 6:5-6)

Revelation 6:5-6: When He opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature say, “Come and see.” So I looked, and behold, a black horse, and he who sat on it had a pair of scales in his hand. And I heard a voice in the midst of the four living creatures saying, “A quart of wheat for a denarius, and three quarts of barley for a denarius; and do not harm the oil and the wine.”
What do others say the black horse is, and why does he say “wine and oil” does not fit a famine?

He says, “What do they say this horse is? Famine. Yes, that’s exactly what they say it is.” He then argues that when God says “don’t touch things, don’t touch My people, it means you don’t bother them,” so “don’t touch the wine and oil” means those are not bothered: “We got plenty of wine and oil. That doesn’t sound like a famine, does it?”
What do others say the black horse is, and why does he say “wine and oil” does not fit a famine?

Now, what do you think they say this horse is? Come on, you know, you’ve read the books, don’t play dumb with me, you’re just afraid I’m going to expose you. What do they say this horse is? Famine. Yes, that’s exactly what they say it is. And boy, it sure sounds like that when they told us it’s famine. Oh yeah, a pair of scales, you know, a measure of wheat for a denarius and three measures of barley, and don’t touch the wine and oil. Okay, but when you go into the Bible and God says don’t touch things, don’t touch My people, it means you don’t bother them. Isn’t that right? So taking the Bible’s expression, don’t touch the wine and oil, the wine and oil is what? Not bothered. We got plenty of wine and oil. That doesn’t sound like a famine, does it?
How does he use Mark 6:37 and the feeding of the 5,000 to work out the price of wheat? (Mark 6:37)

He says the feeding of the 5,000 was “actually about 15,000 when you count the women and the children,” and reads Mark 6:37, where the apostle says, “Shall we go and buy 200 denarii of bread and give them to eat?” He reasons that “one measure feeds one person,” and that “if we buy barley instead of wheat, we can eat three times.”
How does he use Mark 6:37 and the feeding of the 5,000 to work out the price of wheat? (Mark 6:37)

Second problem they got is Jesus feeding the 5,000, which is actually about 15,000 when you count the women and the children. Okay, you ready for this? Mark 6:37, the apostle says, “Shall we go and buy 200 denarii of bread and give them to eat?” Oh, now we got a monetary amount. Jesus said feed these people, there’s 5,000 men plus women and children. Women always outnumber men in this generation anyway. I mean, look around you. When it comes to God, the women are there, their men are off golfing and watching football and doing their thing, except these men. Hallelujah. And of course you at least got the same number of children, so there’s about 15,000 people there. Okay, we know then by this story that one measure feeds one person, ain’t that right? Are you following me? Is this simple arithmetic over your head, college kids? We got in the story of the loaves and the fishes that one measure feeds what? One person. One measure of wheat feeds one person, and we can get three measures of barley, so if we buy barley instead of wheat, we can eat three times.
How does he use Mark 6:37 and the feeding of the 5,000 to work out the price of wheat? (Mark 6:37)
Mark 6:37: But He answered and said to them, “You give them something to eat.” And they said to Him, “Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give them something to eat?”
What does he conclude about the cost of wheat and barley, and whether this is a famine?

He says 200 denarii for 15,000 people comes to “0.013 denarii per person,” that “you can buy a hundred measures of wheat for one denarius,” and “folks, that’s not famine.” He says with barley “you can feed yourself for 300 days, a whole year almost,” and “so we don’t have a famine here.” He adds that people “like bad news” and “trouble gets our attention.”
What does he conclude about the cost of wheat and barley, and whether this is a famine?

Right, now let’s find out what it cost for one measure of wheat, then we’ll know we got a famine or not. Hallelujah. Okay, we take the 15,000 people for 200 denarii, and we come up with 0.013 denarii per person. It doesn’t even take one denarius to get one measure of wheat. You can buy a hundred measures of wheat for one denarius, you can feed yourself for almost a hundred days with one denarius. Folks, that’s not famine. Are you out there? You see, and where do we go to find out things? The book. And so you can feed yourself for 300 days, a whole year almost, if you buy the barley. So we don’t have a famine here. They want it to look bad because people like bad news. You know, we say anything good’s happening at the end time, big deal, we don’t like that, we want trouble. Man, trouble gets our attention. Are you out there? I told you this is a college course, you’re going to have to hear this several times, and that math was really deep, you know, that math was simple percentages and decimals, you know, but that’s real deep stuff. Hallelujah.
What do Revelation 7:3, Revelation 9:4 and the days of Noah add to his argument? (Revelation 7:3; 9:4; Matthew 24:37-38)

He reads Revelation 7:3 and 9:4 about not hurting the earth, the grass or any tree, and says “the oil is used for cooking and a lot of other things, and they can sell it and make money, that’s a good investment.” He concludes “things aren’t famine here, things are looking pretty good,” and recalls Jesus’ words, “As it was in the days of Noah, so shall it be in the coming of the Son of Man,” when people were “buying, they were selling,” “marrying, giving in marriage,” and “life is normal.”
What do Revelation 7:3, Revelation 9:4 and the days of Noah add to his argument? (Revelation 7:3; 9:4; Matthew 24:37-38)

Church, Revelation 7:3 says, “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees.” Revelation 9:4 says, don’t hurt the grass of the earth, neither any green thing nor any tree. And so the wine and the oil, the oil is used for cooking and a lot of other things, and they can sell it and make money, that’s a good investment. The fig tree, the oil was a great investment to have in your yard. Amen. And so things aren’t famine here, things are looking pretty good. Didn’t Jesus say, “As it was in the days of Noah, so shall it be in the coming of the Son of Man”? Isn’t that right? They were buying, they were selling, duh, they were marrying, giving in marriage, duh, they ate, they drank, duh. Isn’t that what we do in normal life? Duh, life is normal. Are you with me so far? Up with the Bible and down with The Late Great Planet Earth.
What do Revelation 7:3, Revelation 9:4 and the days of Noah add to his argument? (Revelation 7:3; 9:4; Matthew 24:37-38)

Revelation 7:3: saying, “Do not harm the earth, the sea, or the trees till we have sealed the servants of our God on their foreheads.” Revelation 9:4: They were commanded not to harm the grass of the earth, or any green thing, or any tree, but only those men who do not have the seal of God on their foreheads. Matthew 24:37-38: But as the days of Noah were, so also will the coming of the Son of Man be. For as in the days before the flood, they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noah entered the ark,
How does he answer the charge that he thinks he is right, and what does he say about popular prophecy writers?

He says, “I’m not thinking anything, I’m just telling you what the Bible says,” and “God forbid that I say I’m right.” He says those who attack him offer “justification for your laziness and not getting into the book and finding truth,” while “I did study for hours and I did find things out by God revealing them to me.” Of popular prophecy writers he says, “who says they know? They’re making their millions, they ride fancy cars, live in fancy homes, and you drive a Volkswagen because you buy their books.”
How does he answer the charge that he thinks he is right, and what does he say about popular prophecy writers?

And people say this to me, “Well, you just think you’re right.” I’m not thinking anything, I’m just telling you what the Bible says. “How do you know that you’re right and they’re not right?” I’m just telling you what the Bible says. God forbid that I say I’m right. You think you know everything, that’s just justification for your laziness and not getting into the book and finding truth. You’re attacking me because I did get into the book and I did study for hours and I did find things out by God revealing them to me, and then you just want to attack because you’re too lazy to read the Bible. You read Hal Lindsay and the guy up here in Riverside, he’s got one, what’s his name, Calvary Chapel guy, [unclear], you know, and you think, “Oh man, they know.” Well, who says they know? They’re making their millions, they ride fancy cars, live in fancy homes, and you drive a Volkswagen because you buy their books. Or a used car, or whatever. Hallelujah.
What does he say the fourth horse is, and how much authority does it have? (Revelation 6:7-8; Hebrews 2:14)

He says the rider on the pale horse “is Death,” with “Hades, the abiding place of the dead,” following, and that he is “given authority and power over one-fourth of the earth to kill with the sword, with famine, with plagues, and with wild beasts.” He says “this devil isn’t the big bad guy you claim he is, and he has no authority if God doesn’t what? Give it to him,” and “we know that this Death is Satan,” citing Hebrews 2:14 on Jesus destroying “him who had the power of death.”
What does he say the fourth horse is, and how much authority does it have? (Revelation 6:7-8; Hebrews 2:14)

Okay, now here we come to the fourth rider. All right, he’s on a pale horse, and the rider is Death. It explains exactly what this rider is. The rider is Death, Hades, the abiding place of the dead, follows right behind. He’s given authority and power over one-fourth of the earth to kill with the sword, with famine, with plagues, and with wild beasts. Acts of God, these are acts of God. The sword is war, but these other things are acts of God, and it explains very clearly that this guy is out through war and famine and other things. What they’re trying to say, the other things, say that this one says it, so we know what this guy’s producing: famine and acts of God, volcanoes and deaths by all this. But he’s only got authority over what? Twenty-five percent of the earth. This devil isn’t the big bad guy you claim he is, and he has no authority if God doesn’t what? Give it to him. And we know that this Death is Satan. Jesus destroyed him in Hebrews 2:14, “him who had the power of death, that is, the devil.” Satan, we know in Revelation that his name is Apollyon,
What does he say the fourth horse is, and how much authority does it have? (Revelation 6:7-8; Hebrews 2:14)

Revelation 6:7-8: When He opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature saying, “Come and see.” So I looked, and behold, a pale horse. And the name of him who sat on it was Death, and Hades followed with him. And power was given to them over a fourth of the earth, to kill with sword, with hunger, with death, and by the beasts of the earth. Hebrews 2:14: Inasmuch then as the children have partaken of flesh and blood, He Himself likewise shared in the same, that through death He might destroy him who had the power of death, that is, the devil,
What does he say about the Destroyer, Satan’s limited power, and who has the real power? (Exodus 12:23; Revelation 9:11; 12:9; John 10:10)

He says the angel at the Passover was “called the destroyer, so we know that was Satan coming, and he had permission to kill the firstborn,” and “he can’t do beans without God giving him permission.” He says Satan “only has power over one-fourth of your life. Don’t give him that much credit.” Asked who has the real power: “Jesus Christ.” He says “he came to kill, steal, and destroy,” and “this is Satan getting people to follow him and die eternally.”
What does he say about the Destroyer, Satan’s limited power, and who has the real power? (Exodus 12:23; Revelation 9:11; 12:9; John 10:10)

Destroyer, or in the Greek, the Destroyer. And so the angel over there in Israel that came through at the Passover and was killing the firstborn was called the destroyer, so we know that was Satan coming, and he had permission to kill the firstborn. He can’t do beans without God giving him permission, and see, God can’t do bad things, so He has what? Satan doing it. Satan’s ready and willing any time God will let him, but he only has power over one-fourth, so he only has power over one-fourth of your life. Don’t give him that much credit, any more credit than it’s due him. Could that be an amen? Who has the real power? Jesus Christ. Hallelujah. Now, Revelation 12:9 says that great dragon was cast out, we know the dragon, that old serpent in the garden, called the Devil and Satan, which deceives the whole world. We know who he is. “They had a king over them, which is the angel of the bottomless pit.” Revelation 9:11 called Abaddon, the destroying angel, but in the Greek, Apollyon, the Destroyer. Hebrews 2:12, as I said before, Jesus destroyed him who had the power of death, that is the devil. So we know the rider on this horse is who? Satan himself. And we know that he came to kill, steal, and destroy. Isn’t that what he does? Isn’t that what Jesus said, he comes to steal, kill, and destroy? When you follow Satan, he’s just out to destroy you, he’s out to take what you got, and he’s out to kill you in the eternal lake of fire. That’s his goal. And people, this has been going on since the beginning of the world. And remember the rich man in the parable of the prodigal, of the parable of the rich man and Lazarus, was in hell, the abiding place of the dead. You see, so this is Satan getting people to follow him and die eternally.
What does he say about the Destroyer, Satan’s limited power, and who has the real power? (Exodus 12:23; Revelation 9:11; 12:9; John 10:10)

Exodus 12:23: For the LORD will pass through to strike the Egyptians; and when He sees the blood on the lintel and on the two doorposts, the LORD will pass over the door and not allow the destroyer to come into your houses to strike you. Revelation 12:9: So the great dragon was cast out, that serpent of old, called the Devil and Satan, who deceives the whole world; he was cast to the earth, and his angels were cast out with him. Revelation 9:11: And they had as king over them the angel of the bottomless pit, whose name in Hebrew is Abaddon, but in Greek he has the name Apollyon. John 10:10: The thief does not come except to steal, and to kill, and to destroy. I have come that they may have life, and that they may have it more abundantly. Luke 16:19-31: “There was a certain rich man who was clothed in purple and fine linen and fared sumptuously every day. But there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, full of sores, who was laid at his gate, desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table. Moreover the dogs came and licked his sores. So it was that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels to Abraham’s bosom. The rich man also died and was buried. And being in torments in Hades, he lifted up his eyes and saw Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom. “Then he cried and said, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.’ But Abraham said, ‘Son, remember that in your lifetime you received your good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things; but now he is comforted and you are tormented. And besides all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed, so that those who want to pass from here to you cannot, nor can those from there pass to us.’ “Then he said, ‘I beg you therefore, father, that you would send him to my father’s house, for I have five brothers, that he may testify to them, lest they also come to this place of torment.’ Abraham said to him, ‘They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.’ And he said, ‘No, father Abraham; but if one goes to them from the dead, they will repent.’ But he said to him, ‘If they do not hear Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded though one rise from the dead.’ ”
What does he say about how many people will be saved? (Romans 3:23)

He says that if Satan gets one-fourth, “that means that a lot of people are going to go to heaven,” and “that means that the blood of Christ has that much power.” He cites that “all have sinned and come short of the glory of God” and asks how many sinners there are in the world: “One hundred percent.”
What does he say about how many people will be saved? (Romans 3:23)

Are you out there? Now, that means that a lot of people are going to go to heaven. Oh, well, that means that the blood of Christ has that much power. Hallelujah. A great harvest, including you. Now, the Bible says all have sinned and come short of the glory of God. Satan is getting one-fourth of them, but how many sinners is there in the world? One hundred percent.
