Is this arithmetic too tough on you?
What does he say about how many people will be saved? (Romans 3:23)
Romans 3:23: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,
What does he say about giving Satan too much credit, and hope despite our flaws? (Romans 3:10)

He says “we have given Satan much more credit than he deserves, and we’ve diminished the power of Christ’s death on the cross way below what it really can do.” When people see flaws in themselves and think there is no hope, he says, “Yes, there is hope, because right here we see you have a 75 percent chance of making it in spite of your flaws.” He also says, “there’s none righteous, no, not one. We’re working on righteousness, but we still have some flaws.”
What does he say about giving Satan too much credit, and hope despite our flaws? (Romans 3:10)

You see, we have given Satan much more credit than he deserves, and we’ve diminished the power of Christ’s death on the cross way below what it really can do. And you measure that by a few Scriptures and your life, you see flaws in yourself and you go, “Oh man, there’s no hope.” Yes, there is hope, because right here we see you have a 75 percent chance of making it in spite of your flaws. Hallelujah. Now that’s good news. That is really good news. Amen. Hallelujah. Now, there’s none righteous, no, not one. We’re working on righteousness, but we still have some flaws, and I think we’d all raise your hand if I said raise your hand, think we may be a little good, but we still got some things in us. Woo.
What does he say about giving Satan too much credit, and hope despite our flaws? (Romans 3:10)
Romans 3:10: As it is written: “There is none righteous, no, not one;
Who are the martyrs of the fifth seal, and what does he say about renouncing the Bible by our works? (Revelation 6:9-11)

He says the fifth seal shows “white-robed souls, martyred for the Word and the testimony,” who “died because they would not renounce Jesus Christ and they would not renounce the Bible.” He says “in America we don’t verbally renounce Jesus Christ. The Bible says by our works we renounce Him,” and that “when we say that homosexuality is an acceptable lifestyle, we have renounced the Bible, because the Bible says it’s not,” and “when we say that it’s okay for Christians to divorce, we just renounce the Bible.” He adds that “you may not have power over it, the other person may want to divorce you.” He says those martyred “would not budge, like John the Baptist,” and “you stand up for truth and you’re going to get abuse.”
Who are the martyrs of the fifth seal, and what does he say about renouncing the Bible by our works? (Revelation 6:9-11)

Now comes the fifth seal. Now we see white-robed souls, martyred for the Word and the testimony. Okay, and here I got it in a little picture here, the only picture I could find. These guys, you know, they’re clothed in white, and they’re martyred. That martyr means they were killed because they followed Jesus and served Jesus and served His Word. That’s a martyr. They died because they would not renounce Jesus Christ and they would not renounce the Bible. In America we don’t verbally renounce Jesus Christ. The Bible says by our works we renounce Him. You see, when we say that homosexuality is an acceptable lifestyle, we have renounced the Bible, because the Bible says it’s not. When we say that [unclear] and sexual immorality are okay, and that’s the way it is in this generation, we just renounce the Bible, because the Bible says no sex should be saved for marriage, and married one person and stay married for life, ain’t that right? When we say that it’s okay for Christians to divorce, we just renounce the Bible. Now, you may not have power over it, the other person may want to divorce you, now it’s not a thing you can do, but when we say it’s okay to do it, we just renounce it, and that’s what Christians are doing. So see, we deny Him and renounce Him by our what? Actions. But these are martyred because they would not budge, like John the Baptist. He told Herod, “You can’t have your brother’s wife. What you did is unscriptural. You divorced your wife and you went and took your brother’s wife and had an affair and married her.” John the Baptist said that is wrong, and they cut off his head for it. You stand up for truth and you’re going to get abuse. Wow, that was good. Let’s say it: stand up for truth, you’ll get abused. You don’t stand up for truth, nobody’s going to care. Hallelujah.
Who are the martyrs of the fifth seal, and what does he say about renouncing the Bible by our works? (Revelation 6:9-11)

Revelation 6:9-11: When He opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of those who had been slain for the word of God and for the testimony which they held. And they cried with a loud voice, saying, “How long, O Lord, holy and true, until You judge and avenge our blood on those who dwell on the earth?” Then a white robe was given to each of them; and it was said to them that they should rest a little while longer, until both the number of their fellow servants and their brethren, who would be killed as they were, was completed. Mark 6:17-18: For Herod himself had sent and laid hold of John, and bound him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife; for he had married her. Because John had said to Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.”
What does he say about the number of martyrs and why Christ has not yet returned? (Revelation 6:11)

He says the voice tells them “you’re to rest here till the martyred number is complete,” and “there’s going to be more martyrs.” He says “it’s very clear it isn’t the end yet, and this proves it’s not the end.” He says “He has a number, and when that number is reached, guess what? Jesus is coming,” which is why “He can’t come today, and He didn’t come yesterday, because the martyrs haven’t reached the number.” He says “there is no any-minute return of Christ, there is a special time, an appointed time.”
What does he say about the number of martyrs and why Christ has not yet returned? (Revelation 6:11)

Now, he also says that you’re to rest here till the martyred number is complete. Wow. Not only were there martyrs when John saw, but he says there’s going to be more martyrs. So see, this is not a one-action thing. This is saying things are going to happen in the future, it didn’t just happen at that time. There are martyrs, and there’s going to be what? More martyrs. There was famines and plagues and wars and so forth, and there will be what? Famines, plagues, and wars. Are you with me? Amen. People turn on one another, they’re in the future, they’re turning on one another now, and they have what? Turned on one another in days past and slaughtered and killed and hurt one another. He’s declaring a statement. Can you see that? It’s very clear it isn’t the end yet, and this proves it’s not the end. There’s more martyrs to come, we don’t know how many, He didn’t give us the number. He has a number, and when that number is reached, guess what? Jesus is coming. That’s one of the reasons why He can’t come today, and He didn’t come yesterday, because the martyrs haven’t reached the number. There is no any-minute return of Christ, there is a special time, an appointed time. Things will happen and things fulfilled, and then He will what? Come. And one of them is the martyrs.
What does he say about the number of martyrs and why Christ has not yet returned? (Revelation 6:11)

Revelation 6:11: Then a white robe was given to each of them; and it was said to them that they should rest a little while longer, until both the number of their fellow servants and their brethren, who would be killed as they were, was completed.
What does he say the sixth seal’s blood-red moon, falling stars and rolled-up sky mean? (Revelation 6:12-14; Isaiah 34:4)

He says an eclipse can make “the moon turns to blood because of the red coloration of the eclipse,” and that “we have meteorites falling out of the sky and they light up the sky.” Of the sixth seal he says there was “a great earthquake,” the sun “was black,” the moon “like blood,” and the sky “rolled up like a scroll.” He adds, “Isaiah said the same thing: the heavens will roll like a scroll, talking about the end times, the stars will fall. It’s all through the Bible, this is nothing new.”
What does he say the sixth seal’s blood-red moon, falling stars and rolled-up sky mean? (Revelation 6:12-14; Isaiah 34:4)

Okay, we see nothing happening or going to happen that has not already happened and is happening. Correct? Correct. Yes. Okay, now let’s continue. The sixth seal. Woo. How many of you know when we have an eclipse of the sun, certain places in the earth, the moon turns to blood because of the red coloration of the eclipse? You’re looking at me like you didn’t know that. I have pictures. These are actual pictures. This is an actual picture of the moon during an eclipse of the sun where it is red. Well, we learned something today. Very interesting. Hallelujah. And here I thought you read the almanac and all these good books, but now you’re telling me you’ve been watching TV. Isn’t that beautiful? The moon turned to blood, folks, I give you. And the stars falling from heaven, how many, you know, we have meteorites falling out of the sky and they light up the sky, and there’s periods where a bunch of them have done it. Okay, now getting back to the sixth seal, there was a great earthquake, the sun was black, it went out, the moon like blood, and we just give you an illustration of that. But here this moon, sun is gone, and the moon is like blood, it’s red, the stars dropped, the sky rolled up like a scroll. Now, how many even know the sky has the sun in it, the moon in it, am I right? The stars. And it’s what? Rolled up like a scroll. It’s gone. First it’s black and red, then it’s gone, and stars drop, then it’s gone. Are you there? This is what John said. It’s gone, it’s rolled up, a scroll, you roll it up. Done. Isaiah said the same thing: the heavens will roll like a scroll, talking about the end times, the stars will fall. It’s all through the Bible, this is nothing new.
What does he say the sixth seal’s blood-red moon, falling stars and rolled-up sky mean? (Revelation 6:12-14; Isaiah 34:4)

Revelation 6:12-14: I looked when He opened the sixth seal, and behold, there was a great earthquake; and the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the moon became like blood. And the stars of heaven fell to the earth, as a fig tree drops its late figs when it is shaken by a mighty wind. Then the sky receded as a scroll when it is rolled up, and every mountain and island was moved out of its place. Isaiah 34:4: All the host of heaven shall be dissolved, And the heavens shall be rolled up like a scroll; All their host shall fall down As the leaf falls from the vine, And as fruit falling from a fig tree.
What point does he make with his opening statement about guns and murder?
He says, “it’s not the gun that kills people, it’s the one pulling the trigger,” and “if you change the heart of a person, you have control.”
What does he say people claim the black horse is?
He says, “What do they say this horse is? Famine. Yes, that’s exactly what they say it is.”
How many people does he say were fed in the feeding of the 5,000?
He says it was “actually about 15,000 when you count the women and the children.”
How long does he say one denarius would feed a person?
He says, “you can feed yourself for almost a hundred days with one denarius,” and with barley, “for 300 days, a whole year almost.”
What does he say about the days of Noah and normal life?

He says, “Didn’t Jesus say, ‘As it was in the days of Noah, so shall it be in the coming of the Son of Man’?” and that they were “buying, they were selling, duh, they were marrying, giving in marriage, duh, they ate, they drank, duh. Isn’t that what we do in normal life?”
Who does he say the rider of the pale horse is?
He says, “the rider is Death,” and “we know that this Death is Satan.”
How much power does he say Satan has?
He says Satan is “ready and willing any time God will let him, but he only has power over one-fourth.” He says, “Don’t give him that much credit.”
What does he say about hope despite our flaws?
He says, “Yes, there is hope, because right here we see you have a 75 percent chance of making it in spite of your flaws.”
What does he say a martyr is?
He says, “That martyr means they were killed because they followed Jesus and served Jesus and served His Word. That’s a martyr.”
Why does he say Jesus has not yet returned?

He says, “He has a number, and when that number is reached, guess what? Jesus is coming. That’s one of the reasons why He can’t come today, and He didn’t come yesterday, because the martyrs haven’t reached the number.”
What does he say happens to the sky in the sixth seal?
He says, “there was a great earthquake, the sun was black,” and “the moon like blood,” and that the sky is “rolled up like a scroll.”

items.d: In this third message on six of the seven seals, Pastor David G. Kincer finishes the sixth seal, connecting it to Joel in Acts 2:16, Matthew 24:29 and Isaiah 34:4. He then previews the seventh seal with the…
p: In this third message on six of the seven seals, Pastor David G. Kincer finishes the sixth seal, connecting it to Joel in Acts 2:16, Matthew 24:29 and Isaiah 34:4. He then previews the seventh seal with the sealing of God’s servants in Revelation 7, teaches that believers are sealed by the Holy Spirit, and gives reasons for a delay in the second coming: the martyr number, the sealing, and the great harvest of the multitude no one could count.
What does he say the sixth seal does to the earth, and why does everyone hide? (Revelation 6:14-17)

He says, “Every mountain and island was dislodged, removed out of its place,” and ties it to the Bible’s promise that “He’s going to renovate the earth.” He says “everybody’s hiding. Why? They see Him.” He then challenges the rapture idea: “These people that say, you know, Jesus comes and raptures the church and people are wondering what happened. Well, good grief, even in your theory the graves were open and they’re wondering what happened.”
What does he say the sixth seal does to the earth, and why does everyone hide? (Revelation 6:14-17)

Every mountain and island was dislodged, removed out of its place. Hawaii is at the Antarctica, Tahiti is in the Arctic, everything’s moved around. Boy, that sure messes up the evolution science theories. Huh? Mount St. Helens is in the ocean now, we don’t know where it is, it’s removed, it’s moved. There’s a drastic change here, isn’t that right? All right, which the Bible talks about, He’s going to renovate the earth. Okay, all hid from Him on the throne and the wrath of the Lamb. Everybody’s hiding. Why? They see Him. These people that say, you know, Jesus comes and raptures the church and people are wondering what happened. Well, good grief, even in your theory the graves were open and they’re wondering what happened.
What does he say the sixth seal does to the earth, and why does everyone hide? (Revelation 6:14-17)

Revelation 6:14-17: Then the sky receded as a scroll when it is rolled up, and every mountain and island was moved out of its place. And the kings of the earth, the great men, the rich men, the commanders, the mighty men, every slave and every free man, hid themselves in the caves and in the rocks of the mountains, and said to the mountains and rocks, “Fall on us and hide us from the face of Him who sits on the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb! For the great day of His wrath has come, and who is able to stand?”
What does he say popular rapture stories have done to the church’s reputation? (Revelation 6:13; Matthew 24:32)

He says “we just believe these little movie stories and these little books that they give us,” and that “this second coming thing is really given us a black eye in the world. People with any intelligence know something’s wrong here.” He says, “It’s made us look bad, we need to get this thing right.”
What does he say popular rapture stories have done to the church’s reputation? (Revelation 6:13; Matthew 24:32)

Are you there? But see, we just believe these little movie stories and these little books that they give us, you know, there are plane pilots flying and one goes and the other’s left, you know, or somebody’s driving a car down the freeway and he’s gone and his car wrecks. How many of you seen those pictures? Yeah. Oh, that really, you know, this second coming thing is really given us a black eye in the world. People with any intelligence know something’s wrong here. Are you there? Hallelujah. It’s made us look bad, we need to get this thing right. Stars drop like shaking figs, and Jesus said, “Behold the fig tree.” Anyway, just thought I’d pass that out. May not be all hid from Him on the throne and the wrath of the Lamb.
What does he say popular rapture stories have done to the church’s reputation? (Revelation 6:13; Matthew 24:32)

Revelation 6:13: And the stars of heaven fell to the earth, as a fig tree drops its late figs when it is shaken by a mighty wind. Matthew 24:32: “Now learn this parable from the fig tree: When its branch has already become tender and puts forth leaves, you know that summer is near.
Has the great day of His wrath already happened? (Revelation 6:16-17)

He says the people hide “Because they’re seeing Him. They’re afraid, they know they’ve messed up.” He asks about “the great day of His wrath” and who can stand, and says the verse is “talking about a day when it will happen,” so as with the conquering, slaughter, famines and plagues, “this is a promise of something going to happen. It hasn’t happened yet.” He says he will show why next week “when we get to the seven trumpets and the seven bowls.”
Has the great day of His wrath already happened? (Revelation 6:16-17)

Why? Because they’re seeing Him. They’re afraid, they know they’ve messed up. “For the great day of His wrath has” what? The great day of His wrath is what? Come, “and who is able to stand?” Before the day of His wrath, and stand before Jesus Christ. Now, according to this verse, it has what? Happened. But we know these statements were made throughout the Bible, and it hasn’t happened, it’s talking about a day when it will happen. Amen. And I submit to you, just like the conquering and the slaughtering of men and the famines and the plagues and all that are happening, will happen, that this is a promise of something going to happen. It hasn’t happened yet, and I’m going to prove it to you next week why it hasn’t happened when we get to the seven trumpets and the seven bowls.
Has the great day of His wrath already happened? (Revelation 6:16-17)

Revelation 6:16-17: and said to the mountains and rocks, “Fall on us and hide us from the face of Him who sits on the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb! For the great day of His wrath has come, and who is able to stand?”
What do Acts 2:16 and Joel say about the last days? (Acts 2:16-21; Joel 2:28-32)

He reads Acts 2:16, “This is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel,” and says it was “addressed before” on Pentecost when “they spoke the wonderful works of God.” He reads Joel’s words, including “The sun shall be turned into darkness and the moon into blood before the great and notable day of the Lord.” He says, “He is saving people to the day He comes. Prophesying and preaching the Word of God is going to happen to the day He comes.”
What do Acts 2:16 and Joel say about the last days? (Acts 2:16-21; Joel 2:28-32)

Fair enough, it’s just simple. Acts 2:16, “This is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel.” Are you with me? See, this has been addressed before. On the day of Pentecost the Holy Ghost moved, and they spoke the wonderful works of God, they spoke in languages, and they were filled with power and everything else. And the Bible says this is what the prophet Joel prophesied: “It will come to pass in the last days that I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh. Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your young men will see visions, and your old men will dream dreams. On My servants and on My handmaidens I’ll pour out My Spirit, and they will prophesy. I will show wonders in the heaven above, signs in the earth beneath, blood, fire, and vapor of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness and the moon into blood before the great and notable day of the Lord. And it shall come to pass that whosoever shall call on the Lord shall be” what? Saved. Folks, He is saving people to the day He comes. Prophesying and preaching the Word of God is going to happen to the day He comes. Amen.
What do Acts 2:16 and Joel say about the last days? (Acts 2:16-21; Joel 2:28-32)

Acts 2:16-21: But this is what was spoken by the prophet Joel: ‘And it shall come to pass in the last days, says God, That I will pour out of My Spirit on all flesh; Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, Your young men shall see visions, Your old men shall dream dreams. And on My menservants and on My maidservants I will pour out My Spirit in those days; And they shall prophesy. I will show wonders in heaven above And signs in the earth beneath: Blood and fire and vapor of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness, And the moon into blood, Before the coming of the great and awesome day of the LORD. And it shall come to pass That whoever calls on the name of the LORD Shall be saved.’ Joel 2:28-32: “And it shall come to pass afterward That I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh; Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, Your old men shall dream dreams, Your young men shall see visions. And also on My menservants and on My maidservants I will pour out My Spirit in those days. “And I will show wonders in the heavens and in the earth: Blood and fire and pillars of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness, And the moon into blood, Before the coming of the great and awesome day of the LORD. And it shall come to pass That whoever calls on the name of the LORD Shall be saved. For in Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there shall be deliverance, As the LORD has said, Among the remnant whom the LORD calls.
What does he say about a seven-year tribulation? (Matthew 24:29)

He says good and powerful things go on “till the day He comes. But we turn this into some kind of great seven-year tribulation period, which is ridiculous nonsense.” He says, “Nowhere in the Bible does it say there’s seven years of tribulation, nowhere. They have to manufacture it out of Daniel.” He reads Matthew 24:29 and says, “Immediately after what? The great tribulation, these things are going to happen, along with the prophesying and the preaching.”
What does he say about a seven-year tribulation? (Matthew 24:29)

Aren’t you glad good things are going on until the day He comes? Powerful things are going on till the day He comes. But we turn this into some kind of great seven-year tribulation period, which is ridiculous nonsense. Are you with me? Nowhere in the Bible does it say there’s seven years of tribulation, nowhere. They have to manufacture it out of Daniel. Hallelujah. Jesus spoke the same thing in Matthew 24:29: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of heaven will be” what? Shaken. Immediately after what? The great tribulation, these things are going to happen, along with the prophesying and the preaching and great things happening, God doing great things in the earth.
What does he say about a seven-year tribulation? (Matthew 24:29)

Matthew 24:29: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light; the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
What does Isaiah 34:4 add, and what does he say about the seals being thousand-year periods? (Isaiah 34:4; 2 Peter 3:10)

He reads Isaiah 34:4 and says, “it was Isaiah spoke it way before John said it,” and “it is something that’s going to happen, it didn’t happen.” He criticizes a timeline that “starts with the first seal”: “The Bible doesn’t say each seal is a thousand-year period. The Bible says this seal is about a book proclaiming the day of wrath, ain’t that right? A one-time period.” He reads 2 Peter 3:10 and says, “It’s not happened yet, but will happen in the future.”
What does Isaiah 34:4 add, and what does he say about the seals being thousand-year periods? (Isaiah 34:4; 2 Peter 3:10)

Isaiah 34:4: “All the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll, and all their host shall fall down as the leaf falls from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree.” See, it was Isaiah spoke it way before John said it. Are you with me? It is something that’s going to happen, it didn’t happen. Here is my point, do you get it? Because they got a timeline, and this timeline starts with the first seal, and they got an Antichrist, you know, the [unclear] have the seven seals as seven 1,000-year periods. We get so ridiculous. The Bible doesn’t say each seal is a thousand-year period. The Bible says this seal is about a book proclaiming the day of wrath, ain’t that right? A one-time period. 2 Peter 3:10: “The day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night, in which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, the earth also and the works that are therein shall be” what? Burned up. Just as many other Scriptures talk of something coming to pass ahead of us, so is John. It’s not happened yet, but will happen in the future. Okay, I’m going to save this for next week.
What does Isaiah 34:4 add, and what does he say about the seals being thousand-year periods? (Isaiah 34:4; 2 Peter 3:10)

Isaiah 34:4: All the host of heaven shall be dissolved, And the heavens shall be rolled up like a scroll; All their host shall fall down As the leaf falls from the vine, And as fruit falling from a fig tree. 2 Peter 3:10: But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night, in which the heavens will pass away with a great noise, and the elements will melt with fervent heat; both the earth and the works that are in it will be burned up.
What does he say about a rebuilt temple, and how does he introduce the seventh seal? (Acts 7:48; Revelation 7:3)

He says of a built temple, “the Bible plainly says God doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands, and yet they got to have a temple built because it’s got to fit into their theory.” He introduces the seventh seal: “This is the last one, and the last one is a long one, as we will see next week.”
What does he say about a rebuilt temple, and how does he introduce the seventh seal? (Acts 7:48; Revelation 7:3)

This is their chart. They got to have a temple built, and the Bible plainly says God doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands, and yet they got to have a temple built because it’s got to fit into their theory. All right. Okay. Now we come to the seventh seal. How many seals are there? Seven. This is the last one, and the last one is a long one, as we will see next week. All right, previews of coming attractions. Revelation 7:3, the seventh seal is coming, but before the seventh seal comes, he says,
What does he say about a rebuilt temple, and how does he introduce the seventh seal? (Acts 7:48; Revelation 7:3)

Acts 7:48: “However, the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands, as the prophet says: Revelation 7:3: saying, “Do not harm the earth, the sea, or the trees till we have sealed the servants of our God on their foreheads.”
What does the sealing of God’s servants before any harm mean? (Revelation 7:1-3; Ezekiel 9:4-6)

He reads that no harm is to be done to the earth, the sea or the trees “until we have sealed the bond servants of our God on their forehead,” and says, “you never hear preaching on that. It’s always 666.” He says God says to “delay everything until I’m done sealing My people.” He connects it to Ezekiel 9:4-6: “Put a mark on the foreheads of the men who sigh and cry over all the abominations.”
What does the sealing of God’s servants before any harm mean? (Revelation 7:1-3; Ezekiel 9:4-6)

“Don’t harm the earth, the sea, nor the trees until we have sealed the bond servants of our God on their forehead.” Don’t do any destruction until the people of God are sealed by God. Now, you never hear preaching on that. It’s always 666, can’t buy and sell, 666, number of men, tick, tick, tick. We think Revelation was a revelation of 666. Well, here God seals His people, and He says delay everything. Say it: delay everything until I’m done sealing My people. Woo, woo. “After this I saw four angels stationed at the four corners of the earth, firmly holding back the four winds of the earth so that no wind could blow on the earth, on the sea, or on any tree. Then I saw a second angel coming up from the east, carrying a seal of the living God, and with a loud voice he cried out to the four angels who had been given authority and power to hurt the earth and the sea.” And he says, “Don’t you hurt anything till we have sealed the bond servants of our God in their foreheads.” Ezekiel 9:4-6, Ezekiel saw it: “Put a mark on the foreheads of the men who sigh and cry over all the abominations that are done in My temple.” And to the others He said in my hearing, “Go after him through the city and kill, and do not let your eyes spare nor have any pity. Utterly slay all the young men and the maidens and the little children and the women. Do not come near anyone on whom is the mark of God.”
What does the sealing of God’s servants before any harm mean? (Revelation 7:1-3; Ezekiel 9:4-6)

Revelation 7:1-3: After these things I saw four angels standing at the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow on the earth, on the sea, or on any tree. Then I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God. And he cried with a loud voice to the four angels to whom it was granted to harm the earth and the sea, saying, “Do not harm the earth, the sea, or the trees till we have sealed the servants of our God on their foreheads.” Ezekiel 9:4-6: and the LORD said to him, “Go through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem, and put a mark on the foreheads of the men who sigh and cry over all the abominations that are done within it.” To the others He said in my hearing, “Go after him through the city and kill; do not let your eye spare, nor have any pity. Utterly slay old and young men, maidens and little children and women; but do not come near anyone on whom is the mark; and begin at My sanctuary.” So they began with the elders who were before the temple.
What does it mean to be sealed by God, and does he say believers must be raptured out of tribulation? (Ephesians 1:13; 2 Corinthians 1:22)

He says, “if God has given me a seal, I don’t have to be raptured out of the tribulation period. Man, I can handle it. Why? He’s sealed me.” He reads Ephesians 1:13 and 2 Corinthians 1:22, that we are sealed and given the Spirit “as a guarantee,” a guarantee “that He will finish the good work He’s begun in us.” He says, “as long as I serve Him and seek Him, He’s going to get me there, and I don’t have to worry about my flaws now and my weaknesses and my problems now.”
What does it mean to be sealed by God, and does he say believers must be raptured out of tribulation? (Ephesians 1:13; 2 Corinthians 1:22)

Are you there? Now, if God has given me a seal, I don’t have to be raptured out of the tribulation period. Man, I can handle it. Why? He’s sealed me. Amen. Ephesians 1:13 says you were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise. 2 Corinthians 1:22: “You also He has sealed and given us the Spirit in our hearts as a guarantee,” a guarantee of what? That He will finish the good work He’s begun in us. Jeez, when I heard that, when God opened that to me as a young Christian, I just exploded. You’re looking at me like, so what? He guarantees me He will get me to my destiny. Now, folks, that takes it out of my hands. As long as I serve Him and seek Him, He’s going to get me there, and I don’t have to worry about my flaws now and my weaknesses and my problems now. He will heal those problems, get me out of those problems, and He will get me to the goal, because He guarantees that it’s His seal to me, and it’s that Holy Spirit that witnesses it in me.
What does it mean to be sealed by God, and does he say believers must be raptured out of tribulation? (Ephesians 1:13; 2 Corinthians 1:22)

Ephesians 1:13: In Him you also trusted, after you heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation; in whom also, having believed, you were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise, 2 Corinthians 1:22: who also has sealed us and given us the Spirit in our hearts as a guarantee. Philippians 1:6: being confident of this very thing, that He who has begun a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ;
Why does he say there is a delay in the second coming, and what is “the mark of God”?

He says “there are multitudes in this world that God wants to save and seal,” so there is a delay: “He is out to win people to Himself and seal them.” He says, “The real focus is on the mark of God, not the mark of the beast,” and “with the mark of God, nothing can touch me.”
Why does he say there is a delay in the second coming, and what is “the mark of God”?

Amen. So I can serve my God with all the zeal and the fortitude that I have in me. And just like the martyrs, He hadn’t finished the martyrs yet, and, you know, hasn’t finished sealing God’s people yet. There are multitudes in this world that God wants to save and seal. Could that be an amen? So there’s a delay. There’s the delay of this stuff, the heavens rolled back like a scroll and the moon turned to blood and the sun going down and all that. There’s a delay. Why? He is out to win people to Himself and seal them. Man, that’s good stuff. And so this second coming is a powerful thing, very powerful. The real focus is on the mark of God, not the mark of the beast. Can I hear an amen? With the mark of God, nothing can touch me, and without it, huh, I’m worthless.
What reasons for the delay does he give, and what is the great harvest? (Revelation 7:9)

He says, “First we find the delay because of the martyr quota hasn’t been reached. Second, we find there’s a delay because the saints of God have got to be sealed.” He gives another reason: “Remember I keep telling you that there’s going to be a great harvest in these last days? Right here it is.” He says of the multitude no one could count, “Give me a break,” rejecting the idea that it comes out of a seven-year period.
What reasons for the delay does he give, and what is the great harvest? (Revelation 7:9)

So there’s a delay. First we find the delay because of the martyr quota hasn’t been reached. Second, we find there’s a delay because the saints of God have got to be sealed. Okay. And here is another reason for the delay. Remember I keep telling you that there’s going to be a great harvest in these last days? Right here it is. Right here it is. “After this I saw a multitude no one could count.” Is this big? Yeah. They say, “Well, this is the one that comes out of the great tribulation period.” Give me a break. A multitude that no one could count coming out of seven years, and then you preach that’s going to be hard to get a, accept Christ, and, you know, you tell us it’s hard and the Spirit’s taken from the earth and all this, then you tell me, give me a break. Are you, you understand what I’m saying?
What reasons for the delay does he give, and what is the great harvest? (Revelation 7:9)

Revelation 7:9: After these things I looked, and behold, a great multitude which no one could number, of all nations, tribes, peoples, and tongues, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, with palm branches in their hands,
What does he say about predictions that Russia, China or others will attack, in light of Revelation 7:9?

He says, “if He’s bringing people out of every nation, kind, and tribe, and tongue,” then of those who predict a nation will destroy Israel, “they’re picking on a nation that God wants to save.” He says, “He’s out to bring out a people for Himself out of all these nations,” and “He doesn’t dislike Russians because they’re Russians.”
What does he say about predictions that Russia, China or others will attack, in light of Revelation 7:9?

Okay, a multitude no one could number come out of great tribulation, out of every nation, kind, and tribe, tongue, and people, and “there stood before the throne and before the Lamb.” Now listen, if He’s bringing people out of every nation, kind, and tribe, and tongue, these people that said Russia’s going to come down and destroy Israel and blah, blah, blah, they’re picking on a nation that God wants to save. When they say China’s going to do it, and the, you know, the Muslims are going to do it, the Arabs and all that, they’re picking on a nation that God wants to save. He’s out to bring out a people for Himself out of all these nations. Let’s stop picking this, let’s stop bringing this. You know, the symbol of Russia was the bear, and so it says over there in Ezekiel the bear, and so forth, so they connect the symbol with the, God didn’t need a symbol back there to tell us what the bear was. He didn’t need a symbol today that Russia has to tell us who the bear is. And He doesn’t dislike Russians because they’re Russians. You cannot judge of people to die and persecute the Jews because they’re born Russian. What if you were born in Russia? Would that be good news to you? You’re doomed to come down and be destroyed. Amen.
What does he say about predictions that Russia, China or others will attack, in light of Revelation 7:9?

Revelation 7:9-10: After these things I looked, and behold, a great multitude which no one could number, of all nations, tribes, peoples, and tongues, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, with palm branches in their hands, and crying out with a loud voice, saying, “Salvation belongs to our God who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!”
Who does he say the people in white robes are? (Revelation 7:11-14; John 16:33)

He reads Revelation 7:13-14 about those “clothed in long white robes” who “have washed their robes and made them white in the” blood of the Lamb. He says, “these people came from earth, and they were made white by what? The blood of the Lamb, not the persecution, not the tribulation.” He says, “we don’t have to be raptured out, we can handle this thing,” and quotes Jesus, “In this world you will have” tribulation.
Who does he say the people in white robes are? (Revelation 7:11-14; John 16:33)

Now these cried, saying, “Salvation to our God who is seated on the throne and to the Lamb.” Here they are worshiping again, and all the angels were standing around the throne and around the elders and the four living creatures, and they all fell prostrate before the throne and worship God. Here’s a lot of worship going on in Revelation, and they cried, “Blessing and glory and majesty and splendor and wisdom and thanksgiving and honor and power and might to our God forever and ever.” All right. Now, those people in white robes, this innumerable number of people that came out of the great tribulation. Verse 13 says one of the elders said to me, “Who are these clothed in long white robes, and from where have they come?” And I replied, “Sir, you know.” And he said to me, “These are they which have come out of the great tribulation, the great persecution, and have washed their robes and made them white in the” what? Blood of the Lamb. Jesus said, “In this world you will have” what? Tribulation. How many found that out? You know, if you’re twenty years old, you find you’re in a world that’s got a lot of conflict and trouble in it, and you are one of your biggest sources of trouble, aren’t you? Yeah, the guy you look at in the mirror. So these people came from earth, and they were made white by what? The blood of the Lamb, not the persecution, not the tribulation. You see, we don’t have to be raptured out, we can handle this thing. Are you with me? Are you with me? And it says “a number of,” so the blood of the Lamb is going to bring a powerful lot of people into the kingdom of God. Hallelujah, and you’re one of them.
Who does he say the people in white robes are? (Revelation 7:11-14; John 16:33)

Revelation 7:11-12: All the angels stood around the throne and the elders and the four living creatures, and fell on their faces before the throne and worshiped God, saying: “Amen! Blessing and glory and wisdom, Thanksgiving and honor and power and might, Be to our God forever and ever. Amen.” Revelation 7:13-14: Then one of the elders answered, saying to me, “Who are these arrayed in white robes, and where did they come from?” And I said to him, “Sir, you know.” So he said to me, “These are the ones who come out of the great tribulation, and washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb. John 16:33: These things I have spoken to you, that in Me you may have peace. In the world you will have tribulation; but be of good cheer, I have overcome the world.”
What does he say about the 144,000 and the twelve tribes? (Revelation 7:4-8)

He says, “He lists twelve tribes and 12,000 out of each one,” but “Joseph is listed as one of the twelve tribes,” Ephraim “is not even mentioned,” and “Dan, who was one of the original twelve tribes, is not mentioned.” He says, “it has nothing to do with anything,” and “there ain’t just 144,000 going to heaven like the Jehovah’s Witnesses said.” He says “there’s an innumerable group of people up there in heaven” and the twelve tribes “illustrate the sealing of God’s people.”
What does he say about the 144,000 and the twelve tribes? (Revelation 7:4-8)

Now, going back to the sealed people. Say, well, you know, there’s 144,000 people sealed. Well, give me a break. He lists twelve tribes and 12,000 out of each one. The problem here is Joseph is listed as one of the twelve tribes, but if you know your Bible, there’s really thirteen tribes now, because Ephraim was picked to be one of Jacob’s children and be one of the tribes, and so Ephraim got the birthright and everything, and Ephraim is not even mentioned in these twelve tribes. Dan, who was one of the original twelve tribes, is not mentioned. Hello? Now, God is so confused He don’t even know the names of His tribes. No, because it has nothing to do with anything. There ain’t just 144,000 going to heaven like the Jehovah’s Witnesses said, they’re a bunch of baloney. There’s an innumerable group of people up there in heaven. Amen. And He’s just using these twelve tribes to illustrate the sealing of God’s people. Hallelujah. So is there a delay? Why? The martyr quota hasn’t been reached.
What does he say about the 144,000 and the twelve tribes? (Revelation 7:4-8)

Revelation 7:4-8: And I heard the number of those who were sealed. One hundred and forty-four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel were sealed: of the tribe of Judah twelve thousand were sealed; of the tribe of Reuben twelve thousand were sealed; of the tribe of Gad twelve thousand were sealed; of the tribe of Asher twelve thousand were sealed; of the tribe of Naphtali twelve thousand were sealed; of the tribe of Manasseh twelve thousand were sealed; of the tribe of Simeon twelve thousand were sealed; of the tribe of Levi twelve thousand were sealed; of the tribe of Issachar twelve thousand were sealed; of the tribe of Zebulun twelve thousand were sealed; of the tribe of Joseph twelve thousand were sealed; of the tribe of Benjamin twelve thousand were sealed.
Why does he say we should want the harvest to come in before the Lord returns?

He says, “if you’re one of these that’s praying, ‘Oh, come, Lord Jesus, get me out of this mess,’ you don’t see the harvest,” and urges, “Stop being selfish and let’s get the vision of the harvest.” He asks whether Jesus’ blood is “big enough to save billions of people,” and says “what God wants to do is way beyond our capabilities.” He concludes, “it’s not about the beast and the troubles and the seven years of tribulation. It’s about the conquering Jesus and the harvest that His blood has power to bring in.”
Why does he say we should want the harvest to come in before the Lord returns?

God isn’t finished saving souls and sealing them, and the harvest hasn’t been brought in yet. Now, if you’re one of these that’s praying, “Oh, come, Lord Jesus, get me out of this mess,” you don’t see the harvest. If you put yourself in the shoes of someone in China that they won’t even allow him to hear the gospel, and it’s very hard to hear it, you wouldn’t want Him coming now. You would want to hear the gospel first, isn’t that right? Stop being selfish and let’s get the vision of the harvest. Hallelujah. Is the blood of Jesus, the sacrifice of Jesus, big enough to save billions of people in this last day? We got almost 7 billion people in this world. You talk about a harvest, we have a potential harvest, and that’s why we need to fast and pray and seek God, because what God wants to do is way beyond our capabilities. We need Him to arise in us, we need Him to arise in the world and accomplish what He promised to accomplish. Amen. And the second coming is about the power of Jesus Christ, the revelation of Jesus Christ, and what He can do in the earth. It’s not about the beast and the troubles and the seven years of tribulation. It’s about the conquering Jesus and the harvest that His blood has power to bring in. Now, I don’t know about you, but that’s good news.
What does he say happens to mountains and islands in the sixth seal?
He says, “Every mountain and island was dislodged, removed out of its place,” and “There’s a drastic change here, isn’t that right?”
What does he say about popular second-coming stories and books?
He says, “this second coming thing is really given us a black eye in the world,” and “It’s made us look bad, we need to get this thing right.”
Which prophet does he say Acts 2:16 points to?
He reads Acts 2:16, “This is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel,” and says it is what happened on the day of Pentecost.
Does he say the Bible mentions a seven-year tribulation?
No. He says, “Nowhere in the Bible does it say there’s seven years of tribulation, nowhere. They have to manufacture it out of Daniel.”
Does he say each seal is a thousand-year period?
No. He says, “The Bible doesn’t say each seal is a thousand-year period.”
What does he say about God dwelling in temples?
He says, “the Bible plainly says God doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands.”
What does he say is delayed until God’s servants are sealed?
He says, “Don’t do any destruction until the people of God are sealed by God,” and that God says, “delay everything until I’m done sealing My people.”
What does he say a seal from God guarantees?
He says it is “a guarantee of what? That He will finish the good work He’s begun in us,” and “He guarantees me He will get me to my destiny.”
What two reasons does he first give for the delay?
He says, “First we find the delay because of the martyr quota hasn’t been reached. Second, we find there’s a delay because the saints of God have got to be sealed.”
What does he say made the robes white?
He says, “they were made white by what? The blood of the Lamb, not the persecution, not the tribulation.”
Does he say only 144,000 people go to heaven?
No. He says, “there ain’t just 144,000 going to heaven,” and “there’s an innumerable group of people up there in heaven.”
What does he say about praying for Jesus to come and get us out of this mess?
He says, “if you’re one of these that’s praying, ‘Oh, come, Lord Jesus, get me out of this mess,’ you don’t see the harvest,” and “Stop being selfish and let’s get the vision of the harvest.”

items.d: In “Slavery Explained,” Pastor David G. Kincer links the curses in Deuteronomy 28 and Israel’s captivities to the “divine nature” promised in 2 Peter 1:4. He teaches a three-part path to freedom from the…
p: In “Slavery Explained,” Pastor David G. Kincer links the curses in Deuteronomy 28 and Israel’s captivities to the “divine nature” promised in 2 Peter 1:4. He teaches a three-part path to freedom from the slavery of sin and Satan: admit you are wrong, seek Jesus, and repent, including the role of water baptism and the preached word.
What curses does Deuteronomy 28 list, and what kinds of “slavery” does he warn about today?

He reads Deuteronomy 28:15 and says the curses include “famines,” “plagues,” “war” and “slavery.” He says people can be enslaved by communism, Islam and “humanism … by capturing your mind,” and that this is why “Christian schools are so important.”
What curses does Deuteronomy 28 list, and what kinds of “slavery” does he warn about today?

Okay, in Deuteronomy 28:15 God told them that if you do not obey the voice of God, to observe carefully all his commandments and all his statutes which I command you today, that all of these curses will come upon you and overtake you. All right: curses, misfortunes, calamities, things that are not pleasing to go through. And then he lists them. Famines: we call it an economical turndown. Plagues: that’s not just your common cold, that’s your bubonic plague, that’s your Asian influenza that kills just hundreds of thousands, millions of people. AIDS today is killing millions of people. War: you know, Jesus said you will always have wars and rumors of war, and everybody connects that as a sign of the end time, but it doesn’t say that. It says the end is not yet. You see, there are going to be wars because, when you violate God’s word, there’s going to be, like there was in the Old Testament, armies rising up against nations. Okay. And slavery. Slavery, in fact slavery where they would be taken from their homeland and into another nation. Now, today we have communism and we have Islam that want to enslave the world. It’s in the Communist Manifesto that they want to conquer the world, they want to make the world follow them, enslave the people. The Muslims are the same way. In their Quran they’re out by force to enslave the rest of the world, and you got to be aware of these things. And humanism is just as dangerous, because humanism is out to enslave the world by capturing your mind. You see, and so we got to be aware of these things, and this is why Christian education is so important. This is why Christian schools are so important. We need to get our kids out of public schools where they’re indoctrinated with humanism, atheism and all these other things, and get them in where their minds are not captured by the philosophies of the world today. Could that be true? And I was very impressed over in China that they start Christian schools. In Africa they’re not so [unclear] on that, and in South America they’re not so [unclear] on that, but the education level in China is way above Africa on the percentage. And so, you know, education really helps. See, knowledge really helps. And I saw a lot of just beautiful Christian schools over there that they took me to. It was just beautiful, and China’s being blessed with that movement, and we need that spread throughout the world and in America.
What curses does Deuteronomy 28 list, and what kinds of “slavery” does he warn about today?

Deuteronomy 28:15: “But it shall come to pass, if you do not obey the voice of the LORD your God, to observe carefully all His commandments and His statutes which I command you today, that all these curses will come upon you and overtake you: Matthew 24:6: And you will hear of wars and rumors of wars. See that you are not troubled; for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet.
How does he say Israel went into captivity, and what does that show?

He says Israel was enslaved several times in Judges “in their own homeland,” then taken by Assyria and Babylon, and later oppressed by Greece and Rome, with the temple destroyed in 70 AD. He says all of this happened “just like God said he would do,” and that God “doesn’t live in temples made with hands.”
How does he say Israel went into captivity, and what does that show?

So we find, as you know by reading the Bible, that these things were accomplished in Judges. Israel went into captivity several times, from seven years to forty years, in their own homeland. In their own homeland they went into captivity to Mesopotamia, Moab, Canaan, Midian and the Philistines, but they stayed in their homeland. It’s just God brought another nation to enslave them in their own homeland. But his promise was, his correction was, “I’m going to take you out of your homeland.” All right. And so we find that the Assyrian Empire, in about 720 AD, or BC, came and took Israel into captivity. Two captivities, all right. It actually happened. They took them out, and there’s no Bible that these ever came back, unless they came back in the captivity of Babylon. But then in about 604 or 605 we have the Babylonian captivity, you see, coming, taking the Jews and the remaining people there into Babylonian captivity. Now, Rome and Greece both enslaved the Jews while they were still in their own nation, all right, for four hundred years before Christ came. These nations came and enslaved the Jews in their own nation again, just like Judges. But in 70 AD the Roman army came, destroyed the temple in Jerusalem like Jesus said it would be. And I don’t know why they want to build it again, that’s nonsense. It’s totally against the Bible. But these end-time people have this temple being built again, and that’s foolish. God doesn’t live in temples made with hands. He is building a church, a spiritual house. Amen. That’s the building that we’re building today. But anyway, they took hundreds of thousands of Jews captive and made them slaves, all right, just like God said he would do. And the Jews still didn’t get it, many of them. Now, a lot of Jews came to Christ, you know. In fact, the first people that came to Christ were Jews. All right. And so in that, second, before the Second World War, Germany enslaved the Jews, killed six million of them, enslaved the rest, forcing them into slave labor, all because they were Jews, just like God said he would do. Are you there?
How does he say Israel went into captivity, and what does that show?

Acts 7:48: “However, the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands, as the prophet says: 1 Peter 2:5: you also, as living stones, are being built up a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
What is the “divine nature,” and why does he say the church lost sight of it? (2 Peter 1:4)

He reads 2 Peter 1:3-4, that through God’s promises “you may be a partaker of the divine nature.” He says people were “so focused on the second coming” and “who had the right chart” that “we lost sight of the divine nature,” and that Jesus came “not only to die on the cross but to give us his divine nature.”
What is the “divine nature,” and why does he say the church lost sight of it? (2 Peter 1:4)

Now, what’s that got to do with the Christmas message? Glad you asked. Ah, now we get into the divine nature. Ah, I love these clouds forming a heart here, to remind you. 2 Peter 1:3-4: “As Jesus’ divine power has given us all things... whereby are given unto us exceedingly great and precious promises.” Why did he give us these great promises? He answers the question: that through these you may be a partaker of the divine nature, a participator of the divine nature. Wow. When I got saved, everybody was so focused on the second coming they never even thought about the divine nature. They thought Jesus was coming any minute, coming in 1960, coming in 1972, coming, coming, coming, coming, come, come, come, come, come, and he hadn’t come yet. And, say, we were so looking and so focused on who had the right chart for the second coming that we lost sight of the divine nature. We forgot all about that Jesus was born of a virgin, and he came into the world for a purpose, not only to die on the cross but to give us his divine nature. Hallelujah. We got so focused on prosperity. There are so many groups that teach that prosperity is Christianity, it’s righteousness, and the Bible plainly says that’s wrong. Now, he wants to bless you, but remember, heathens are rich. But we focus on prosperity, and they do it today especially on TV and radio. It’s embarrassing. They focus on purpose, positive thinking, purpose-driven, positive thinking. Prophecy, especially in Pentecostal groups, they so focus on prophecy, giving everybody a private prophecy. It’s horrible, and I can talk about us tongue talkers because I am one. And when you make mistakes, you got to clear it up. Could that be an amen?
What is the “divine nature,” and why does he say the church lost sight of it? (2 Peter 1:4)

2 Peter 1:3-4: as His divine power has given to us all things that pertain to life and godliness, through the knowledge of Him who called us by glory and virtue, by which have been given to us exceedingly great and precious promises, that through these you may be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.
What makes a prophet false, and who does he say is the one prophet to listen to?

He says “when you say something’s going to happen and it doesn’t, then you’re a false prophet,” and mentions a failed prediction. He says Moses said “God will send a prophet like unto me,” and that this is Jesus: “Jesus is the one I listen to.”
What makes a prophet false, and who does he say is the one prophet to listen to?

Prophesying about the White House going to be blown up, the God going to blown up last year, and it didn’t happen, and all these false prophets. Just when a prophet doesn’t come to pass, they are what? False prophets. I got nothing to do with you. You need to get saved, you need to get with it. I don’t care how nice you are, I don’t care how well you can speak. When you say something’s going to happen and it doesn’t, then you’re a false prophet. Amen. Now, how many of you know there’s only one prophet the Bible tells us to listen to? God will send a prophet like unto me, Moses said, and to him you must listen. Who is that? Jesus. Jesus is the one I listen to. Muhammad is not the prophet of God. Jesus is. Amen. And these self-appointed prophets are not the prophets of God. Jesus says, and I must follow, follow Jesus, and if they prophesy according to Jesus and all that, that’s fine, but when they’re wrong, I got to follow Jesus. How about you? Yes.
What makes a prophet false, and who does he say is the one prophet to listen to?
Deuteronomy 18:15: “The LORD your God will raise up for you a Prophet like me from your midst, from your brethren. Him you shall hear,
What distractions does he say keep us from the divine nature: helping the poor, miracles and gifts?

He says the American church brags about “helping the poor,” but “we need to help the poor in spirit.” He says Jesus “only healed one person” at the pool of Bethesda, that he was healed of valley fever, and that filling out a spiritual-gifts “form” is not in the Bible: “a gift is an ability.”
What distractions does he say keep us from the divine nature: helping the poor, miracles and gifts?

And so we got all these distractions. Helping the poor is so big in the American church that they really think they’re great Christians because they help the addict and the poor and the homeless and all that the American government is giving money to and enabling them to be poor, and the church just gloats over and brags about how they’re helping the poor. And we need to help the poor in spirit. Are you there? “Blessed are the poor in spirit.” Why are they poor? They don’t know Jesus, they don’t know wisdom, they don’t have knowledge. That’s the riches they need. See, we’re distracted, and so we don’t see this nature of God. You don’t even hear it preached on hardly anywhere, that we can be partakers, and his purpose to come was for us to be partakers of his divine nature. Phenomena again in the Pentecostal Spirit-filled areas, man, they’re all into miracles. A miracle a day keeps unbelief away, or something like that, and if you don’t have a miracle every day, there’s something wrong. Well, how many of you know Jesus went to the pool of Bethesda and only healed one person? Walked right over all of them and healed one person, ain’t that right? He didn’t heal them all. And we love the healings. God healed me of, uh, valley fever. They told me I was going to die in thirty, sixty days, and God healed me, and it’s great. My wife loved me staying alive. She didn’t want me dying, she had kids to raise. And the doctor said, “You have a miracle.” The doctor right there in his office said it twice: “You got a miracle, man, you should be dead.” Are you there? But he, you know, it’s like he does it every day, but it’s nice when it happens. Amen. Gifts of the Spirit in America: you can take a little sheet to see what gifts you can have or something. There’s nothing like that in the Bible. “Let me fill out this form and see what gift I got.” If you got a gift, you got a gift. A gift is an ability. If you got an ability, you can use it. If you don’t have it, you can’t use it. I don’t care what kind of form you fill out. And we’re so focused on gifts that we miss the promise of the divine nature.

He says “no man can make us sin,” and “Satan cannot make me sin. He can accuse me, he can tempt me, but he cannot make me sin.” He says we “choose to die through sin” and can “come alive again by confessing, seeking and repenting,” and that this is “the Christian’s divine nature.”
Can Satan make us sin, and how do we live free from the slavery of sin? (1 John 2:1)

I give you this power. That’s my commandment to you.” Well, if that’s God’s commandment to him, and we’re partakers of the divine nature, what is God’s commandment to us who believe on him? That sound fair? We have the same natural power, only we choose to die through sin. See, no man can make us sin. We choose to die through sin, and we can choose to come alive again by confessing, seeking and repenting from our sins, and we can live. Watch how this works: sin kills the spirit, [unclear] makes alive. Here’s the commandment we received of our Father. Unlike Jesus, who had no sin (I’m sure you all agree with that), we messed up, didn’t we? In fact, you probably messed up yesterday. You might have messed up this morning with a bad attitude, saying things you shouldn’t have said. We are, we are good at this thing. Jesus had no sin. Unlike Jesus who had no sin, we become slaves of sin, Satan and spiritual death. But like Jesus, we have power to die by choosing to sin. “You are dead in trespasses and sin. Arise, you that sleepeth, arise from the dead, and Christ will give you life.” Arise from that sin. We also have power to live by choosing to be slaves of Jesus and righteousness. You see, I have the ability to go out here and sin today if I want to. I can go out and sin. I can choose that road, and I did as a young man. I didn’t follow God. I sinned really bad stuff. It doesn’t matter whether you’re a deep sinner or whether you’re a lightweight sinner, the punishment’s all the same, you know. So if you’re going to be a sinner, it might as well just be a heavyweight sinner. You know, you’re going to burn in hell forever, it might as well be a heavyweight sinner. But I chose that. But when I was twenty years old, I chose Christ. I chose to admit I was wrong, I chose to seek Christ, I chose to return, turn from my sin, renounce sin and live for him, and Christ came to me and gave me life. So our divine nature is to live free from the slavery of sin, the slavery of Satan and spiritual death, by Jesus’s death, by his resurrection, and obeying his word. Satan cannot make me sin. He can accuse me, he can tempt me, but he cannot make me sin. The sinners of this world can’t make me sin. It’s a choice I make. But if I confess my sin, and I seek Jesus, and repent, our divine nature is to do this anytime we find ourself a slave of sin. See, that is the Christian’s divine nature. If we do mess up, and 1 John 1 says, chapter 2, 1 John 2:1: “Beloved, I would that you not sin, but if you do sin, you have an advocate with the Father, even Jesus Christ the righteous.” See, I can go and I can be free from that slavery of sin by admitting I’m wrong, seeking Jesus, and repenting, and that’s the Christian nature. That’s what makes us different from the world. Yeah, we make mistakes, we do things we shouldn’t do, but the nature God’s given us through his commandment is: I admit I’m wrong, I seek Jesus for the cleansing, the forgiveness and the deliverance from sin, and I turn from that sin. That’s the nature of the Christian. So the Christian keeps growing upward. Amen. Are you there? See, we keep taking on the nature of God. God had no sin, we do, but we keep gaining ground, because the nature he’s put within us is to admit we’re wrong, seek Jesus, and repent from that wrong.
Can Satan make us sin, and how do we live free from the slavery of sin? (1 John 2:1)

Ephesians 5:14: Therefore He says: “Awake, you who sleep, Arise from the dead, And Christ will give you light.” 1 John 2:1: My little children, these things I write to you, so that you may not sin. And if anyone sins, we have an Advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous.
What curses does he list from Deuteronomy 28?
He lists “famines,” “plagues,” “war” and “slavery,” and says they come when “you violate God’s word.”
What does he say about communism, Islam and humanism?

He says communism and Islam “want to enslave the world,” and that “humanism is out to enslave the world by capturing your mind.” He says that is why he wants kids out of public schools “where they’re indoctrinated with humanism, atheism.”
What does he say the church focused on instead of the divine nature?
He says prosperity, “positive thinking,” “prophecy” and miracles: “we got so focused on prosperity,” and he adds that “heathens are rich.”
What does he say about prophecies that do not come true?
He says “when a prophet doesn’t come to pass, they are what? False prophets,” and “when you say something’s going to happen and it doesn’t, then you’re a false prophet.”
Does he say Jesus healed everyone?
No. He says Jesus “only healed one person” at the pool of Bethesda and “didn’t heal them all,” though “it’s nice when it happens.”
What does he say is the first thing we must do?
He says “you got to admit you’re wrong,” and that it is “wrong according to the Bible, not your friend’s opinion, not your opinion.”
What does he say about prayer and mega churches?
He says people say “a little two-minute prayer” but “don’t get down on their knees and seek God,” and that “there’s no mega church that can solve your problem. Only Jesus can.”
What is the difference between a song service and a worship service?
He says “in a worship service, in a praise service, you touch Jesus. In a song service, you touch the song. It’s all about the music.”
Why does he say we take on the nature of what we spend time with?
He says “you can’t have a meeting with God without taking on his nature,” and “what you spend time with, you become like. So when I spend time with Jesus, I become like Jesus.”
Does he say baptism is only an outward sign?
No. He says “water baptism is not an outward sign of an inward work. Man phrased that statement; it is not in the Bible,” and that “he does something in water baptism.”
What does he say Satan is?
He says Satan “is a spirit” and “doesn’t have horns and a long tail and all that garbage,” and that “God created Satan.”
Who does he say can save you?
He says “Jesus can only save you. Jesus can only forgive you. Jesus can only cleanse you of sin,” and that “your church can’t get you saved.”
Does he say the Jews or the Romans killed Jesus?
He says “none of them could kill Jesus. He laid down his life, and he picked it back up again,” so saying either group killed Jesus is “not total truth.”
Does he say sinning is a choice?
Yes. He says “we have power to die by choosing to sin,” and “we also have power to live by choosing to be slaves of Jesus and righteousness.”
What does he say a Christian does when they mess up?
He says “I admit I’m wrong, I seek Jesus for the cleansing, the forgiveness and the deliverance from sin, and I turn from that sin,” and “that’s what makes us different from the world.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer lays out a timeline of 400-year patterns of God’s judgments, then studies the three New Testament mentions of Sodom (Mark 6, Matthew 11, Luke 17), arguing that Sodom is…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer lays out a timeline of 400-year patterns of God’s judgments, then studies the three New Testament mentions of Sodom (Mark 6, Matthew 11, Luke 17), arguing that Sodom is the example for the end times, that the apostles preached repentance, and that Lot’s wife shows the danger of going back. He closes with his view of conditions in America.
What is the 400-year pattern between God’s judgments?

He lays out a timeline in which about 400 years separate the flood, the judgment of Sodom, the judgment of Egypt, the period of the judges, the era of the kings, and then 400 silent years before Jesus came. He says Jesus did not follow the pattern for His return “cuz we’re 2,000 years from that time,” but he says judgment is surely coming.
What is the 400-year pattern between God’s judgments?

First I’m going to give you a timeline. There, here’s the flood, okay. That’s God destroyed the earth because of violence and sin in the earth, sexual immorality and so forth. At the flood, there’s approximately 400 years between that judgment and the judgment of Sodom and Gomorrah, okay? When God destroyed Sodom, then we come over here to the Exodus. Israel was 400 years from Sodom. Abraham and had sons, and then they had sons, and they went down to Egypt for actually 430 years, but approximately 400 years between Sodom and God judging Egypt and literally destroying Egypt to set his people free. Are you with me so far? We find that the period of the judges was approximately 400 years. Everybody doing what’s right in their own eyes. The judges were brought up to judge God’s people. he would He would bring in armies or plagues to correct God’s people, and then he would raise up a judge to lead them out of the captivity, the judgment. All right, that was 400 years, approximately 400 years. Are you getting the picture? 400 years is all of a sudden a prominent figure in God’s judgments. All right. Then we come over here to where they have a king. They didn’t want to judge anymore, and so they wanted a king. They wanted to be like the nations. And this is during the era of the kings is when God, through Jeremiah and Ezekiel, said that his people was like Sodom and Gomorrah. They were sinning. Isaiah, all these, Hosea, all these prophets came and tried to turn God’s people back, to right back to Bible morality. Okay. And so, sure enough, it was about 400 years of the reigns of the kings, and then God took them into captivity, the Babylonian captivity. All right. Now we have 400 silent years from Nehemiah and Malachi, the last two prophets, Ezra, after the restoration of God’s people from captivity. There’s 400 silent years. God didn’t say anything till Jesus came. Interesting. Now when Jesus came, he himself said it will be like Sodom when I come the second time and judge the earth. But we don’t have a period of time, and obviously he didn’t follow the 400-year paradigm, did he? Cuz we’re 2,000 years from that time. But you can rest assured it’s what? Coming. Now notice this. That over here in the law, Moses, Deuteronomy, God told Israel that you’re going to fall away, you’re going to sin, you’re going to serve other gods, and you’re going to go into captivity. That was 800 years before they went into into captivity. God told them what was going to happen, because Deuteronomy also says they didn’t have a heart. He said, “Oh, that there was a heart in them to obey me and to know me.” You see, he was trying to save and trying to uh use a people, and a lot of them didn’t want to obey him and didn’t want to know him. Are you there? And he predicted this stuff 800 years before they went into captivity for their sin. Are you there? Now, see, that’s a supernatural God.
What is the 400-year pattern between God’s judgments?
Deuteronomy 5:29: Oh, that they had such a heart in them that they would fear Me and always keep all My commandments, that it might be well with them and with their children forever!
Why does he say end-time predictions are wrong when Jesus compared the end to Sodom?

He says Jesus Himself said there would be a falling away and that the second coming would be like Sodom, and that the pre-, mid- and post-tribulation and millennial views all “have a real problem, because no one is connecting it to what God said is the example of the end.” He says the next “Sodom example” comes at the return of Christ.
Why does he say end-time predictions are wrong when Jesus compared the end to Sodom?

Folks, supernatural gods can predict things before they ever happen. Nobody else. But it’s also coincidental that over here, Jesus himself said there would be a falling away, and we would be like Sodom at the second coming of Jesus Christ. And this is where all your second uh return, your your end time predictions are all wrong. I’ve studied them all. They all have a problem: pre-tribulation, post-tribulation, mid-tribulation, premillennium, postmillennium, amillennium. All these things have a real problem, because no one is connecting it to what God said is the example of the end. We do all this crazy stuff with weeks and Daniel and all this nonsense, and we get God’s people all, we lead them. Okay, now we got the picture of the timeline. When’s the next next Sodom example coming? At the second coming, the return of Christ. Okay, we don’t know how long, we don’t know how many years people try to predict it, but we know that one of the signs is things are going to be like Sodom and Gomorrah. Right? Yeah. Now, so we go to the New Testament now to get the clarification of Sodom judgment. Here we go. First, men of Sodom in the New Testament.
What does Jesus say in Mark 6:11 about those who reject the preachers? (Mark 6:11)

He says Jesus sent the apostles out and said that for people who would not receive or hear them, it “shall be more tolerable” for Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city. He says this shows “there’s levels of judgment” and that those who reject the message and the preachers get a greater judgment than Sodom.
What does Jesus say in Mark 6:11 about those who reject the preachers? (Mark 6:11)

Mark 6:11: “Whosoever shall not receive you.” Talking to the apostles, he sent them out to preach the gospel, and he says, “Whoever not receive you, accept you, nor hear you.” You see, you can reject the preacher, hate him, put him in prison or whatever, and you can also reject the message that the preacher is bringing. And he says whoever rejects the message and whoever rejects and mistreats the preacher preaching it, “I say it shall be more tolerable,” more bearable, it be a better word here, “for Sodom and Gomorrah in the” what? “Day of judgment than for that city.” Wow. Did you hear that, church? He sent the preachers out to preach, the apostles out to preach, and he said this statement that it’s going to be more tolerable, bearable in the day of judgment. In other words, there’s levels of judgment, and Sodom and Gomorrah’s people is going to have a lesser judgment than the people that reject the message and reject the preachers preaching it.
What does Jesus say in Mark 6:11 about those who reject the preachers? (Mark 6:11)

Mark 6:11: And whoever will not receive you nor hear you, when you depart from there, shake off the dust under your feet as a testimony against them. Assuredly, I say to you, it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city!”
What did the apostles preach: psychology, prosperity or repentance?

He says the apostles preached that men should repent, and he contrasts it with “psychology,” “prosperity” and “possibility thinking” in America today. He says what is rejected is repentance, “not grace and faith,” and that “if you don’t” stop sinning “you’re like Sodom and Gomorrah.”
What did the apostles preach: psychology, prosperity or repentance?

Wow. And so what did the apostles do? They went out and preached psychology. Right? No. Isn’t that what we’re hearing today in America, a lot of psychology? They would out preach prosperity. Right? No. Isn’t that what we’re hearing in America? “Boy, come to Christ, you’re going to be wealthy and rich.” Ain’t that right? Possibility thinking, purpose-driven thinking, all of this stuff. They preach none of that. What did they preach? That men should what? Repent. What’s the message they’re rejecting? Repentance, not grace and faith. And what do you hear prominently in every church and in every radio and TV minister? Grace and faith. “Come to Christ.” No. “You’re in, man. You believe in Christ, you in.” No repentance. But what was the apostles’ message? Repentance. Said repentance. You got to turn from your sin. You got to stop sinning. And if you don’t, you’re like Sodom and Gomorrah.
Why will it be more tolerable for Sodom than for cities that saw miracles? (Matthew 11:20-24)

He says Jesus rebuked the cities where most of His miracles were done because they did not repent, and that it would be “more tolerable” for Sodom in the day of judgment than for them. He says Sodom would have repented if it had seen those miracles, and says the city of Nineveh did repent when told it would be destroyed in 40 days.
Why will it be more tolerable for Sodom than for cities that saw miracles? (Matthew 11:20-24)

Hallelujah, hallelujah. Isn’t that clear? I mean, folks, you can’t get any more clear than that. You see, and we got to get it out of our mind that God’s just going to judge homosexuals and sexual immorality people because that’s what Sodom. We showed you in Jeremiah and Ezekiel that God referred to his people being like Sodom and Gomorrah when they did worse sins than Sodom and Gomorrah did. Matthews 11:20, second mention of Sodom. Jesus rebuked the cities in which most of his mighty works had been done, for they did not what? Repent. [unclear] Capernaum, they’re going to be brought down to what? Hell, Hades, the abiding place of the dead that don’t know God or don’t didn’t follow God. Why? Because God did a miracle there. He was born of a virgin. He opened blinded eyes. He, you know, multiplied the fish and the loaves and all kinds of things, and they would not repent even though he did all the miracles. You ever hear people say, “Boy, if I could see a miracle, I believe”? He again says it’s going to be more tolerable, they’re going to be more bearable for Sodom in the day of what? Judgment, the second coming, than for you. “For if I would have done the miracles in Sodom and Gomorrah that I did in you and preached the word that I preached in you to you, they would have remained. There would have been no judgment. They would have repented.” how many You know, the city of Nineveh was like that. God was going to destroy it.
