He went in with the message, “In 40 days God’s going to destroy it,” and the people what? Repented.
Why will it be more tolerable for Sodom than for cities that saw miracles? (Matthew 11:20-24)

Matthew 11:20-24: Then He began to rebuke the cities in which most of His mighty works had been done, because they did not repent: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works which were done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes. But I say to you, it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon in the day of judgment than for you. And you, Capernaum, who are exalted to heaven, will be brought down to Hades; for if the mighty works which were done in you had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day. But I say to you that it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment than for you.” Jonah 3:4: And Jonah began to enter the city on the first day’s walk. Then he cried out and said, “Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown!”
What is Sodom’s example for believers, and what does Luke 17:28 say about normal life? (Luke 17:28)

He says Sodom is “the example of God’s vengeance and judgment both on unbelievers and believers who reject” the message of repentance. He reads Luke 17:28, that in Lot’s day they ate, drank, bought, sold, planted and built, and says this sounds like “normal everyday life,” not the terrible days described by tribulation teachers.
What is Sodom’s example for believers, and what does Luke 17:28 say about normal life? (Luke 17:28)

Hallelujah. Now, isn’t this clear? God’s example of Sodom is the example of God’s vengeance and judgment both on unbelievers and believers who reject what the message of repentance, not the message of faith, not the message of water baptism, not the message of the Holy Ghost baptism, was speaking in tongues, not the message that everybody’s got a gift and God has got a purpose for you. Third time Sodom and Gomorrah is mentioned, third time, and it’s in procession, it’s in step by step. Luke 17:28: “Likewise,” similarly, in the same manner, “as it was in the days of Lot.” Where was Lot? In Sodom. Okay. “They ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted and built.” Now does that sound like days are terrible, like pre-tribulation rapture people talk about, like post-tribulation people talk about? Buying, selling, marrying, giving in the marriage. The other scripture says. Isn’t that just normal everyday life? Yeah. Eating, drinking, working, not working, still eating. Don’t have to work, you can still eat. Is America in this condition, in spite of our economy problems and everything else? Are we still buying, selling, marrying, giving in marriage, eating? Yeah, yeah. People that don’t work, do they get to eat free? Oh absolutely, no problem. Have five kids, we just raise your salary, raise your welfare.
What is Sodom’s example for believers, and what does Luke 17:28 say about normal life? (Luke 17:28)
Luke 17:28: Likewise as it was also in the days of Lot: They ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they built;
What happened the day Lot left Sodom, and what does it say about the end? (Luke 17:29-30)

He says that on the day Lot went out of Sodom “it rained fire and brimstone from heaven and destroyed” all of them, and that when Christ is revealed the world will be the same: with natural life going on and people sinning. He says God always protects the righteous, such as the seven thousand in Israel who had not bowed to Baal.
What happened the day Lot left Sodom, and what does it say about the end? (Luke 17:29-30)

But the day Lot went out of Sodom, it rained fire and brimstone from heaven and destroyed how many? All of them. You see, when God removed the righteous, and he always protects the righteous. Remember in Israel there were seven thousand that had not bowed their knee to Baal. No matter how much you read in the scriptures, there’s always that remnant that is there that God is blessing, people that are following God, which the next series will show you. In the midst of this stuff, God comes up with tremendous promises to his people. In the midst of this mess, God makes these promises. “Even so shall it be in the day when the Son of Man is revealed.” When Christ comes back, this is what is going to be happening, just like Sodom and Gomorrah. They were with natural life, but they were sinning, homosexuality, all these sins were going to go into them. Okay, so the condition of the earth is going to be like what? Sodom and Gomorrah. Okay.
What happened the day Lot left Sodom, and what does it say about the end? (Luke 17:29-30)

Luke 17:29-30: but on the day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven and destroyed them all. Even so will it be in the day when the Son of Man is revealed. 1 Kings 19:18: Yet I have reserved seven thousand in Israel, all whose knees have not bowed to Baal, and every mouth that has not kissed him.”
Does the Bible say the son of perdition is the antichrist, and why does Jesus say to remember Lot’s wife? (Luke 17:32)

He says “the Bible never says that the son of perdition is the antichrist,” and that anyone teaching a coming “big bad” antichrist is teaching a lie. He says Jesus’ statement “Remember Lot’s wife” matters because Lot’s wife did not just look back, “she went back.”
Does the Bible say the son of perdition is the antichrist, and why does Jesus say to remember Lot’s wife? (Luke 17:32)

There ain’t no big bad uh son of perdition, the antichrist, rising up, folks. Everyone who teaches you that teaching you a lie. It’s just not in the scriptures. The Bible never says that the son of perdition is the antichrist. Never says it. Then he says this powerful statement: “Remember Lot’s wife.” Oh, remember I told you that Lot’s wife didn’t just look back, as that word is, she went back. You wasn’t listening when I said that, huh? Yeah, well, right here: remember Lot’s wife. Why does he want us to remember Lot’s wife? Because the angels came. Her husband was a righteous man. He had two virgin daughters, and he had two daughters married to heathen men, probably had kids by them, probably had grandchildren, and they mocked and laughed when he said, when Lot said, “You know, God’s going to destroy the city.” They go, “You got to be kidding, man. Ain’t nothing like that going to happen. We’re buying, we’re selling, we’re marrying, giving, everything normal.”
Does the Bible say the son of perdition is the antichrist, and why does Jesus say to remember Lot’s wife? (Luke 17:32)
Why does he say Lot’s wife went back to Sodom?

He says the angels literally grabbed Lot, his wife and their two daughters and took them out of the city, but she decided “I’m not following the angels any further” because she had a home, grandchildren and money in the bank. He says this is exactly what was going on in Sodom: people could even live off welfare.
Why does he say Lot’s wife went back to Sodom?

And then the angels grab Lot, his wife, and the two virgin daughters, living still in their home, and took them out of the city, literally grabbed them and took them out of the city. Now the angels had the message, the angels had the authority. They start going down the road from Sodom and Gomorrah, leaving the town, and she decides, “I’m not following the angels any further. I’m not following my righteous husband any further. I’m going back. I got a home back there. I just bought a nice 60-inch widescreen TV. I got grandchildren back there. We got money in the bank, and besides that, I can live off welfare. I don’t even need a Lot.” If you read what we told you, that’s exactly what was going on in Sodom and Gomorrah. You didn’t even have to work. They’d feed you. Are you guys out there?
What does Jesus mean by saving your life and losing it? (Luke 17:33)

He says Lot’s wife was caught in the judgment and turned to a pillar of salt because she did it her own way, as in the flood, the judges and the captivity where everyone did what was right in their own eyes. He says “you go God’s way, you’ll live,” and “if you do it your way, you will die.”
What does Jesus mean by saving your life and losing it? (Luke 17:33)

He said, “Remember Lot’s wife.” What happened to her? She got caught in the judgment and turned to a pillar of salt, just like everything else was salt in that area, and it’s still salt. And this, he explains, “If you seek to save your life,” and that’s what she did, “I’m not going to follow them guys, I’m going to do it my way.” Isn’t that what happened in Judges? They did what was right in their own eyes. Isn’t that what happened at the flood? They did what was right in their own eyes. And that what happened, went into captivity, everybody was doing what was right in their own eyes. No repentance, no Bible morality. They all believed in God, but no Bible morality, no repentance. “And whoever loses his life,” you give up your way of doing things, “you will find it.” You will get life. Isn’t that right? You go God’s way, you’ll live. Repent, turn from your sins, accept Jesus’ sacrifice on the cross for the punishment for your sin, you will live. If you do it your way, you will die. Ain’t that clear? Did Lot’s wife die with two angels leading her out? Yeah.
What does Jesus mean by saving your life and losing it? (Luke 17:33)
Luke 17:33: Whoever seeks to save his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life will preserve it.
What does he say sin is, and what does he say about sexual immorality and homosexuality?

He says sin is “just a Bible word for crime,” a violation of a moral law with a punishment. He says sexual immorality is much bigger than homosexuality because more people commit it, that Sodom’s second sin was pride, “fullness of bread, abundance of idleness,” and that we are to strengthen the hand of the poor by getting them a job. He also says that AIDS is “a obvious judgment on the male homosexuals,” which is his own claim and not verified here.
What does he say sin is, and what does he say about sexual immorality and homosexuality?

Remember their sins. Sodom’s crimes. Sins is just a Bible word for crime. And so when you use sin, they say, “Well, we can’t use the word sin.” Sin is nothing but the same word as crime. You violated a moral law, it is a crime, there’s a punishment, there’s a hurt that’s going to be done. Are you with me? United States, in Europe today, and at the second coming. All right, sexual immorality is much bigger than homosexuality, because there’s more people committing sexual immorality than there is people committing homosexuality, and how’s he going to single out the homosexuals and just judge them, except for this AIDS thing? You know, that’s a obvious judgment on the male homosexuals, cuz, you know, 90% of the people who have it are male homosexuals, over 90%, 94 or something like that. Are you there? We need to correct our sexual immorality, also incest, adultery, fornication, sex with animals, and all that stuff. Sexual immorality, homosexuality was the second sin. Pride, of course. America has no pride. Right? Fullness of bread, abundance of idleness. Do we have abundance of idleness? We we went through all this. Yeah, we’re lining up. Boy, we’re we’re right there. We don’t strengthen the hand of the poor and the needy. And how do you strengthen the hand of the poor and the needy? Getting them a career, getting them a job, getting them work. That’s right.
What does he say sin is, and what does he say about sexual immorality and homosexuality?

Ezekiel 16:49: Look, this was the iniquity of your sister Sodom: She and her daughter had pride, fullness of food, and abundance of idleness; neither did she strengthen the hand of the poor and needy.
What does he say the Bible calls an abomination?

He lists sexual immorality, homosexuality, incest, pedophilia, sex with animals, witchcraft, all child abuse, desecrating God’s house, stealing and lying, and says failing to tell people to repent is also an abomination. He says an abomination is “something God detests” because it brings harm.
What does he say the Bible calls an abomination?

Abominations. Abominations include sexual immorality, homosexuality, incest, pedophilia, sex with children, sex with animals, witchcraft, all child abuse, including the murder of children. The Bible declares is an abomination. When you mistreat a child, whether it’s verbally, physically, sexually, emotionally or whatever, God says that’s an abomination. Not telling people to repent, we just learned, as an abomination. Okay. Desecrating God’s house is an abomination. Stealing, lying, all this stuff, that’s an abomination. Abomination is something God detests. God hates it because it brings harm. Now, they declared openly their sin. They didn’t hide it. And we just found that, as I said, no repentance to the gospel message is their sin. All right, and that’s the way it’s going to be at the coming of Christ.
Why does he say no one predicted these changes in America?

He says that in the circles he grew up in, no one predicted laws for same-sex marriage and acceptance of homosexuality, which he says gained “inroads” in churches and politics. He says no one predicted the fall of Russia “overnight,” and that if God can bring that down He can bring down America, quoting the warning not to trust in chariots or horses.
Why does he say no one predicted these changes in America?

Now let me just say, back in those years growing through all that, the people around me and I myself, who became a tongue-talking, spirit-filled believer, wound up in a circle of churches that believed in prophecy, setting people into the body of Christ. And nobody that I read books on, no preacher, no minister that I talked to, and no minister, big mega church on TV and radio, even gave an indication, even a thought, that America would be passing a law for same-sex marriage, homosexuality accepted, that these homosexuals would have infiltrated the churches, the politics, Congress, local city councils, mayors, state, and that one to two of people would gain inroads like they have today. No one predicted it, including us tongue talkers who supposed to be a notch above everybody else, man. You know, nobody. They were all saying, “Jesus is coming, Jesus is coming, Jesus is coming.” Oh man, no one predicted the fall of Russia overnight, just like that. And if God can bring down Russia overnight, can he bring down America? Oh yeah, he’s God, folks. That’s why the scriptures say don’t trust in chariots, don’t trust in horses. Back then, those days, that was the tremendous weapons, the cavalry, the armor was the chariots. He said, “Don’t trust in your army. When I decide to do something, armies don’t even get in my way.” Are you there?
Why does he say no one predicted these changes in America?
Psalm 20:7: Some trust in chariots, and some in horses; But we will remember the name of the LORD our God.
What does he say about sexually transmitted diseases?

He says no one predicted the sexual revolution would leave about half of Americans with a sexually transmitted disease or over 30 new ones, and he says over 30,000 Americans die of them a year. He says “if it feels good, do it” hurts others, and that accepting homosexuality sentences a man “to a horrible death of AIDS.” These statistics are as he gave them and have not been checked.
What does he say about sexually transmitted diseases?

None of these people were predicting these things. None of these were predicting when the sexual revolution came along. No one predicted that America would wind up with 50% of Americans with a sexually transmitted disease today. 50% of Americans have a sexually transmitted disease or had one, or got more than one, one-half, one and two. No one predicted there were to be 30 over 30 and new sexually transmitted diseases. No preacher was predicting that. No politician was predicting that. Just, you know, “if it feels good, do it.” That was the statement back there. Am I right, you older ones? “If it feels good, do it. I’m not hurting anybody else.” Yeah, you do hurt somebody else when you do these things, and it starts spreading through America. Uh, over 30,000 a year die from sexually transmitted diseases in America, and they make a big issue of a few kids getting gunned down in a school, and they make no issue of over 30,000 Americans dying every year from sexually transmitted diseases. 30,000. Over, and about 27, 28,000 of those, those are AIDS. They die from AIDS. When you say the homosexual is acceptable and they come, you are sentencing that man to a horrible death of AIDS. Nowhere else do we sentence people to a disease. Are we like Sodom and Gomorrah? Oh yeah, oh yeah.
What statistics does he give about single parents and rape?

He says 48% of children are born to single-parent mothers, 30% of Americans never marry, and that a high percentage of children born to single parents become criminals or abusers of drugs or alcohol, in his words from news sources. He also says 93,000 men and boys and 19,000 military women were raped in a year, and only 8% are punished; these figures are as he stated them and have not been checked.
What statistics does he give about single parents and rape?

48% of children are born to single-parent mothers. 30% of Americans never marry. 49% of women, young women today, live with a man on an average of 22 months, then they go live with another. is the NBC News. Of those 48% born to single parents, I mean uh to single moms, a high percentage of them become criminals, drug abusers, alcohol abusers, high school dropouts, sexually permissive, welfare, and sexually transmitted diseases. And they know this. Fox News, uh, you know, the Center for Disease and Control, all of these people know this. President Obama knows these statistics. Listen to this one. Are you ready for this one? You young ones, listen to this. You young males, listen to this. 93,000 United States men and boys were raped last year. Now is women raping them? This is from the Department of Justice, the Department of Defense and Fox News. 19,000 military women were raped last year, and more than once. 5,000 military men were raped last year, and only 8% are punished. And folks, if they have that many recorded, how many you think happened and no one said anything? Do we have a problem in America? And our Congress is not addressing or telling Americans about these situations.
What does he say about suicide, a sound mind and hope? (2 Timothy 1:7, Romans 8:24)

He says 105 people commit suicide every day, 8 and a half of them young people, and that “Bible moral people don’t commit suicide” because God has given a spirit of power, love and a sound mind. He ends by saying “we’re saved by hope,” and that we have hope for America, our youth and our families because God is not a man that He should lie.
What does he say about suicide, a sound mind and hope? (2 Timothy 1:7, Romans 8:24)

105 people commit suicide every day. You young hearing that? 105, a lot more than all the shootings in the schools. 8 and a half of them are young people every day, young people. Eight and a half are committing suicide. You see, Bible moral people don’t commit suicide. Are you there? The Bible says he hasn’t given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of what? Sound mind, a solid mind. Sound mind people don’t commit suicide, and they don’t hurt other people. That was good. See, Christians don’t have a confused mind. We’re not confused. We have a sound mind, a solid mind, a strong mind. 49% of the unemployed are under age 34. That’s really a disaster. That’s really hurting in America, that our young people are the highest of the unemployed. Is this clear? Are we lining up to Sodom and Gomorrah? How many know the Bible says we’re saved by hope? I just gave you that verse a couple weeks ago. Hallelujah. How many Christians have never heard that verse? They always heard you say by faith through grace and not of ourselves, not a work. We saved by hope. We have great hope in his name. Amen. We have hope for America. We have hope for our youth. We have hope for our family, because God is not a man that he should lie. What he says he will do. And he uses consistent, faithful people like you to reach the inconsistent, unfaithful people that need to be reached. Amen. Hallelujah. So Bible morality preaches repentance and repents.
What does he say about suicide, a sound mind and hope? (2 Timothy 1:7, Romans 8:24)

2 Timothy 1:7: For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind. Romans 8:24: For we were saved in this hope, but hope that is seen is not hope; for why does one still hope for what he sees? Numbers 23:19: “God is not a man, that He should lie, Nor a son of man, that He should repent. Has He said, and will He not do? Or has He spoken, and will He not make it good?
What did Jesus say would be like Sodom?
He says Jesus said that at the second coming of Jesus Christ “we would be like Sodom,” and that Luke 17 compares the days of the Son of Man to the days of Lot.
What does he say about end-time timelines and weeks of Daniel?

He says “we do all this crazy stuff with weeks and Daniel and all this nonsense,” and that all the pre-, mid- and post-tribulation and millennial views have a problem because they do not connect to the example of Sodom.
Does he say there are levels of judgment?
He says yes: “there’s levels of judgment,” and Sodom and Gomorrah’s people will have a lesser judgment than the people who reject the message and the preachers.
What message does he say people are rejecting today?
He says it is “repentance, not grace and faith,” and that “you got to turn from your sin, you got to stop sinning.”
Does he say Sodom was judged only for homosexuality?

He says “we got to get it out of our mind that God’s just going to judge homosexuals and sexual immorality people because that’s what Sodom” was, and says Jeremiah and Ezekiel referred to God’s own people as being like Sodom when they did worse sins.
Does he say miracles make people repent?
He says no: the cities where most of the miracles were done did not repent “even though he did all the miracles,” and he says Jesus said Sodom would have repented if it had seen them.
What does he say about welfare and work?

He says people who do not work still get to eat, with salary and welfare raised for more children, and compares it to Sodom, where “you didn’t even have to work. They’d feed you.” He says the way to help the poor is getting them “a career… a job.”
What does he say about the righteous in times of judgment?
He says God “always protects the righteous,” like the remnant in Israel, and that “in the midst of this mess God makes these promises” to His people.
What does he say about the antichrist?
He says “There ain’t no big bad uh son of perdition, the antichrist, rising up,” and that “the Bible never says that the son of perdition is the antichrist.”
Why does he say Lot’s wife turned to salt?
He says she “got caught in the judgment and turned to a pillar of salt,” because she chose to do it her own way instead of following the angels and her righteous husband.
He says “sin is nothing but the same word as crime,” a violation of a moral law that carries a punishment and a hurt.
What does he say about child abuse?
He says the Bible declares all child abuse, “including the murder of children,” an abomination, whether verbal, physical, sexual or emotional.
What does he say about suicide?

He says 105 people commit suicide every day, that “Bible moral people don’t commit suicide,” and that the Bible promises a spirit of power, love and a sound mind. Anyone struggling should reach out for help from a crisis line or a trusted person.
What does he say we are saved by?
He says “we’re saved by hope,” that many Christians have never heard that verse, and that we have great hope in His name.

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Jeremiah 3 that in the midst of God’s judgments there are promises for those who repent: God is married to His people, gives shepherds who feed with…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Jeremiah 3 that in the midst of God’s judgments there are promises for those who repent: God is married to His people, gives shepherds who feed with knowledge, increases the righteous, and gathers the Gentiles to Zion, the church. He ends with hope for America and the call to bow to Jesus now.
What does God promise in the midst of judgment?

He says he will look at “precious promises before, during, and after Sodom’s judgment,” and that in the midst of war, famine and captivity God has another message for people who will listen to the message of repentance. He says Jeremiah spoke shortly before the captivity while nations warred around Judah and false prophets said nothing would happen, and asks, “Does it sound like America today?”
What does God promise in the midst of judgment?

We’re going to take a look at precious promises before, during, and after Sodom’s judgment that God pronounced on the wicked, on the wicked believers and people that would reject the message of repentance. Okay? Now remember in the midst of these messages that we preached previously, the judgments, the war, the famines, the acts of God, the captivity where they lost their home, their family members, they lost their nation, they were taken away from their nation, everything that they knew. In the midst of these judgments, there’s another message that God has for the people that will listen to the message of repentance. Okay? And Jeremiah is speaking less than 20 year or less than 30 years before the captivity is going to happen. He is speaking 11 years. The Egyptian war, the Egyptian nation and the Assyrian nation and the Babylonian nation are warring, and Judah is right in the middle of it. And it’s happening all around them. And Jeremiah’s preaching what’s going to— the, these guys. Israel has already been carried away captive and destroyed by war and famine. And now we find Judah still even though all these things are going on around about them.
Is God still married to His people? (Jeremiah 3:14, 2 Corinthians 11:2)

He cites Jeremiah 3:14, “Return, repent, oh backsliding children, says the Lord, for I am married to you,” and says God hates divorce, so He is not wanting to divorce us. He says this applies to the church as well as Judah, citing 2 Corinthians 11:2, and that “Yes, he will punish us. Yes, he will correct us,” but He is married to us.
Is God still married to His people? (Jeremiah 3:14, 2 Corinthians 11:2)

They think and they believe and they speak. Their false prophets speak that nothing’s going to happen to Judah. Does it sound like America today? All these wars, all this sin going on in their nation, all this trouble around us. A lot of the nations I’ve preached in a lot of the nations in the world and they hate America. You know, America just don’t get it. Are you there? And in the midst of this, God comes with the other side of the message. Jeremiah 3:14: “Return, repent, oh backsliding children, says the Lord, for I am married to you.” Now, the Bible says that God hates what? Divorce. And he’s married to us. So, is he wanting to divorce us? Are you out there? See, this is pertinent stuff. It’s important. See, he is God was married to his Jews, his Jewish people back there. He’s married to his church. And he reminds even though he’s telling them all these judgments are coming, he reminds them that you’re my bride. You’re married to me. And so not only for that group back in Judah at that time, but also for the church. Jeremiah is prophesying. In 2 Corinthians 11:2: “I’ve espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.” Amen. So who is the wife of Christ? The church. Yes. You see, he’s married to us. Yes, he will punish us. Yes, he will correct us.
Is God still married to His people? (Jeremiah 3:14, 2 Corinthians 11:2)

Jeremiah 3:14: “Return, O backsliding children,” says the LORD; “for I am married to you. I will take you, one from a city and two from a family, and I will bring you to Zion. 2 Corinthians 11:2: For I am jealous for you with godly jealousy. For I have betrothed you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.
Is Christ coming back for a mature bride? (Revelation 19:7, Revelation 21:9)

He says God is not giving up on us “because we got some problems,” and cites Revelation 19:7 and 21:9, saying Christ will return for a mature, righteous bride, not “a baby church.” He says most end-time preachers bring only the seven years of tribulation and the antichrist, which he says “isn’t even in there,” and he gives David reclaiming his bride from another man as an illustration of Jesus taking us from Satan.
Is Christ coming back for a mature bride? (Revelation 19:7, Revelation 21:9)

But he’s married to us and he isn’t giving up on us because we got some problems. Amen. He’s just asking us to change our stupid ways. In Revelation 19:7, “the marriage of the Lamb has come and his wife has made herself ready.” Speaking of the second return of Christ, the church will be a mature, righteous dressed in white linen bride when Christ comes. And this is what most of the end time prophetic preachers aren’t bringing in. All they bring in is the seven years of tribulation and the antichrist, which isn’t even in there. You have to twist scriptures to get that out. One man being an antichrist and son of perdition and all that. But when Christ comes back, is he coming back for a baby church or a mature bride church? Yeah. Do men marry children? No. [unclear] that child has to grow up and mature and take on that shape that these women have to get these men’s attention. And in the spiritual, that’s exactly what’s going to happen. Jesus is going to build a glorious church. And he’s coming back for that glorious [unclear]. Also in Revelation 21:9: “I will show you the bride, the Lamb’s wife.” And he showed Jerusalem coming down out of the heaven as a bride prepared for her husband. Okay. Now again in Jeremiah 3:14-18: “I will take you from one city and two from a family, and I will bring you to Zion.” He said, “I’m married to you, and I’m going to go and get my bride.” Now, King David is an illustration of this. King David’s first wife was taken by her father. David had to go into the wilderness. Her father married her off to another man. And when King David got through his wilderness wanderings and God’s promise came to him and he was made king, he went and got his bride back from that husband that wasn’t his her real husband. You see, when we’re in sin, when we’re in the kingdom of darkness, we’re married to Satan. We have a relationship with Satan. But Jesus comes by his blood and the power of his resurrection and he takes us from that bad husband and he brings us unto himself.
Is Christ coming back for a mature bride? (Revelation 19:7, Revelation 21:9)

Revelation 19:7: Let us be glad and rejoice and give Him glory, for the marriage of the Lamb has come, and His wife has made herself ready.” Revelation 21:9: Then one of the seven angels who had the seven bowls filled with the seven last plagues came to me and talked with me, saying, “Come, I will show you the bride, the Lamb’s wife.” Jeremiah 3:14-18: “Return, O backsliding children,” says the LORD; “for I am married to you. I will take you, one from a city and two from a family, and I will bring you to Zion. And I will give you shepherds according to My heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding. “Then it shall come to pass, when you are multiplied and increased in the land in those days,” says the LORD, “that they will say no more, ‘The ark of the covenant of the LORD.’ It shall not come to mind, nor shall they remember it, nor shall they visit it, nor shall it be made anymore. “At that time Jerusalem shall be called The Throne of the LORD, and all the nations shall be gathered to it, to the name of the LORD, to Jerusalem. No more shall they follow the dictates of their evil hearts. “In those days the house of Judah shall walk with the house of Israel, and they shall come together out of the land of the north to the land that I have given as an inheritance to your fathers.

He says Zion is the church. He cites John 12:15, where Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a donkey’s colt, and Hebrews 12:22, “the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, the general assembly, the church of the firstborn.” He says God will take us “one from there and two from here” and bring us to His church where He is enthroned.

Are you there? Yes. And Jeremiah is speaking of all these things back then for those people and the future of the church that God is going to raise up in the earth. Now he says, “I’ll bring you to Zion.” And I’m going to remind you that Zion is the church. John 12:15. Jesus is coming into Jerusalem. And he quotes the scriptures: “Fear not, daughter of Zion, for your king is coming to you sitting on a donkey’s colt.” All right. Jesus is riding in Jerusalem on a donkey’s colt. And the scripture is quoted that your king is coming unto Zion. So where was Zion at that time Jesus was riding? In Jerusalem and that’s where the natural Zion was. It was a mountain in Jerusalem, a stronghold. All right. But your king is coming unto you. Was he really coming just for that natural city or was he coming to the people? The people, of course. And to make it clear in Hebrews 12:22, we’ve come to Mount Zion. We the church have come to Mount Zion. And then he explains what Mount Zion is. The city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, the general assembly, the church of the firstborn. So Zion is the what? Church of the firstborn. And it goes on to say to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant. Are you there? So Zion is Jesus making a stronghold in his church. You see, and he says he’s going to take us one from there and two from here and bring us to his church where he is enthroned. Ah man, that was good. Do you guys get that? See, this was hundreds of years before Christ came and died and built his church. And Jeremiah is speaking tremendous things during this bad stuff going on. What great stuff can happen while it’s going on and will happen in the future. All right. Then he says, “I will give you shepherds according to my heart who will feed you with knowledge and understanding. I will give you shepherds, pastors, feeders of the flock, and they will make you feel good.”

John 12:15: “Fear not, daughter of Zion; Behold, your King is coming, Sitting on a donkey’s colt.” Hebrews 12:22-24: But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, to an innumerable company of angels, to the general assembly and church of the firstborn who are registered in heaven, to God the Judge of all, to the spirits of just men made perfect, to Jesus the Mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling that speaks better things than that of Abel. Jeremiah 3:15: And I will give you shepherds according to My heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.
What does God promise about shepherds who feed us with knowledge? (Jeremiah 3:15)

He quotes “I will give you shepherds according to my heart who will feed you with knowledge and understanding,” and says we need knowledge and understanding. He cites Jesus as the good shepherd and Hebrews, that God now speaks to us through His Son.
What does God promise about shepherds who feed us with knowledge? (Jeremiah 3:15)

Now, what is these pastors that God is sending doing? Feeding us with what? Knowledge and understanding. Hallelujah. How many of you know that’s what we need? We need some knowledge and understanding. And the scriptures back it up. Number one, in John 10:1, Jesus said, “I am the good shepherd.” “I am the good shepherd.” Folks, in Hebrews it says God spoke in the old days to our forefathers by the prophets, but now he speaks to us through his son Jesus Christ. And let me tell you something.
What does God promise about shepherds who feed us with knowledge? (Jeremiah 3:15)

John 10:11: “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd gives His life for the sheep. Hebrews 1:1-2: God, who at various times and in various ways spoke in time past to the fathers by the prophets, has in these last days spoken to us by His Son, whom He has appointed heir of all things, through whom also He made the worlds;
Why isn’t zeal without knowledge enough? (Romans 10:2-3)

He says “no undershepherd has the right to give you their opinion,” only the truth from the Bible. He cites Romans 10:2–3, “a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge,” and says some Christians are stirred up for Jesus but don’t go to Sunday school or Bible studies or open their Bible through the week.
Why isn’t zeal without knowledge enough? (Romans 10:2-3)

Even though Jeremiah said, “I will send you shepherds plural,” no undershepherd has the right to teach anything but what the shepherd Jesus said to teach. No undershepherd has the right to give you their opinion. They must give you the truth from the Bible. Period. In Romans 10:2: “They have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge.” Here the Jews, he’s talking about the Jews. Yeah, they have a zeal of God. They’re stirred up for God, but they don’t have the knowledge. How many of you know Christians like that? You know, they’re stirred up for Jesus and they don’t even know him. Why? They have no knowledge. They don’t go to Sunday school. They don’t go to Bible studies where the word is being taught and they don’t open their book through the week. Got no time to study the Bible. Got time for everything, but can’t study the Bible, which is our new covenant promise that he would inscribe it in our minds and our hearts. But how can he inscribe when we’re not hearing it, listening to it, reading it, and studying it? Can I hear an amen? Amen. Also in Romans 10:3: “Being ignorant of God’s righteousness and going about to establish their own righteousness.” See, they don’t have the knowledge of God’s righteousness. And the Bible tells us in first John that “he that doeth righteous is righteous.” Duh. Amen. And so they’re ignorant of what God says is right. Jeremiah 4:22 says, “My people are foolish.
Why isn’t zeal without knowledge enough? (Romans 10:2-3)

Romans 10:2: For I bear them witness that they have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge. Romans 10:3: For they being ignorant of God’s righteousness, and seeking to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted to the righteousness of God. 1 John 3:7: Little children, let no one deceive you. He who practices righteousness is righteous, just as He is righteous. Hebrews 8:10: For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the LORD: I will put My laws in their mind and write them on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be My people. Jeremiah 4:22: “For My people are foolish, They have not known Me. They are silly children, And they have no understanding. They are wise to do evil, But to do good they have no knowledge.”
What are God’s people destroyed for lack of? (Hosea 4:6)

He applies Jeremiah’s words about people who “are wise to do evil” to the American church that talks about Jesus and the Bible but doesn’t know Him. He cites Hosea 4:6, “My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge,” and says it does not say lack of faith, grace, or the baptism of the Holy Ghost with speaking in tongues. He then reads that in the midst of warnings, “Jerusalem shall be called the throne of the Lord.”
What are God’s people destroyed for lack of? (Hosea 4:6)

They haven’t known me. They are stubborn children. They have no understanding. They are wise to do evil, but to do good, they have no knowledge.” And this is the American church. We talk about Jesus. We talk about the Bible, but we don’t know him. And we do evil because we don’t bother finding out what God says is right and what God says is wrong and avoid the wrong and do right. Can I hear an amen? In Hosea 4:6, “My people are destroyed for lack of faith.” No, you guys shaking your head. That’s right. It doesn’t say that. “My people are destroyed for lack of grace.” No, it doesn’t say that either. “My people are destroyed for the lack of the baptism of the Holy Ghost with speaking in tongues and prophecy.” No, it doesn’t say that. But these are the little eccentrics that the church groups get on. It says, “My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. And because you’ve rejected knowledge, I’ve rejected you to be priests unto me.” A priest is the minister. How can you be a minister when you don’t have the knowledge of God? Verse 16, then it shall come to pass when you are multiplied and increased in the land, Jerusalem shall be called the throne of the Lord. Wow. In the midst of this message that you know you’re going to die from famine, you’re going to die from war, you’re going to die from plagues, you know, and you’re going to be taken into captivity.
What are God’s people destroyed for lack of? (Hosea 4:6)

Hosea 4:6: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I also will reject you from being priest for Me; Because you have forgotten the law of your God, I also will forget your children. Jeremiah 3:16-17: “Then it shall come to pass, when you are multiplied and increased in the land in those days,” says the LORD, “that they will say no more, ‘The ark of the covenant of the LORD.’ It shall not come to mind, nor shall they remember it, nor shall they visit it, nor shall it be made anymore. “At that time Jerusalem shall be called The Throne of the LORD, and all the nations shall be gathered to it, to the name of the LORD, to Jerusalem. No more shall they follow the dictates of their evil hearts.
Does God promise increase in the midst of judgment?

He says that in the middle of a message of famine, war and captivity, God says, “I’m going to increase you,” a message to the righteous alongside the message to the wicked. He says there were 7,000 who never bowed to Baal, and people like Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego, Ezekiel, Jeremiah, Ezra and Esther who listened and were multiplied.
Does God promise increase in the midst of judgment?

Here he comes and says, “Hey, I’m going to increase you.” Totally the opposite of the other side of the prophecy. Are you hearing me? So, in the midst of the message to the wicked, he has a message to the righteous. In spite of these things coming, in spite of the wicked, continue to do wickedly. Believers that do wickedly, unbelievers that do wickedly, I’m going to increase you and I’m going to multiply you. And we found that he did. In Israel, there were 7,000 that never bowed their knee to Baal, nor kissed his feet. There were people in the northern kingdom that served God. We know there were people in the southern kingdom that came to God at this time. Daniel was one of them. Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego, Ezekiel, Jeremiah here.
Does God promise increase in the midst of judgment?
1 Kings 19:18: Yet I have reserved seven thousand in Israel, all whose knees have not bowed to Baal, and every mouth that has not kissed him.”
What does he say about church attendance statistics?

He says no one prophesied that only 25% of Catholics would be going to church in 2013, and that Catholics and Protestants (27%) are “voting by staying away” because of corruption in the churches. He says home Bible studies have the same problems as denominations, and “we need to get rid of these problems and get back to the book.”
What does he say about church attendance statistics?

There’s Ezra, Esther. I mean, these people listened to this message and God was what? Multiplying and increasing them and enthroning in them. And Jeremiah is also speaking to the church that is a far off several hundred years when Christ comes. Okay. Now, how does that relate to us today? Well, today, no one was prophesying, no one was speaking that only 25% of Catholics would be going to church in 2013. No one back there 50, 40, 30, 20 years ago. You see, the Catholic people are getting upset about their church allowing these homosexuals to come in and abuse their children, abuse their youth, and so forth. And so, they’re voting by staying away. Protestants, only 27% have been going for about 20 years. They got their little home Bible studies going and all that and they’re voting because of all the junk and the corruption in the Protestant church. Am I right? The only problem is when I looked into the home the home Bible study movement, they got the same problems as the denominational does. And we need to get rid of these problems and get back to the book. Can I hear an amen? Many of Americans youth, the news says today, vote liberal and they reject God’s promises of increase.
What happens to young people who grow up in church?

He says over 40 years of records show about 75% of young people whose parents take them to church fall away when they leave home, but in strong Christian homes with Christian schools about 75% stay with their faith. He says 50% of those who fell away come back, and “God is bigger than the statistics.”
What happens to young people who grow up in church?

They reject God’s word. But I submit to you, I’ve been keeping records for 40 years, over 40 years. And it’s been this way in every generation. 75% of the young people whose parents take them to church, okay? Fall away when they leave the house and go to college, go to school. The universities turn them all around and all that opportunity to sin is there. It’s always been that way. But let me tell you something. I also found that in strong Christian homes where they put their kids in a Christian school that 75% of them stay with their faith. Are you there? So in the midst of the bad news, there’s what? Good news. I also kept statistics that these that fell away, 50% of them come back somewhere down the road when they’ve been trained up in the way they should go. Somewhere they come to their senses like the prodigal in the pig pen, they come back and that puts the percentages in our favor. Are you there? So, don’t get so riled up about these statistics. God is bigger than the statistics and he has a message in the midst of the statistics that he is touching lives and gathering in people to him. Can I hear an amen? Hallelujah.
What happens to young people who grow up in church?

Proverbs 22:6: Train up a child in the way he should go, And when he is old he will not depart from it. Luke 15:17: “But when he came to himself, he said, ‘How many of my father’s hired servants have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!
Is God still reaching the unbeliever? (Jeremiah 3:17, Revelation 7:9)

He says “All nations, all Gentiles will be gathered to Jerusalem, the throne of the Lord,” and that Gentile means someone who doesn’t believe in God the Creator, so God is still reaching the unbeliever in the middle of judgment. He says “you got to preach the whole counsel of God,” the bad news and the good news, balanced. He cites Revelation 7:9, a great multitude “that no man could number.”
Is God still reaching the unbeliever? (Jeremiah 3:17, Revelation 7:9)

And that’s what we want him to do in this generation. Is that correct? Absolutely. All nations, all Gentiles will be gathered to Jerusalem, the throne of the Lord. All the Gentiles, he didn’t leave out the unbeliever. Gentile is someone that doesn’t believe in God, the creator. They believe in God’s, but they don’t believe in God the creator. They don’t believe in Jesus. Okay? That’s what the word nation is almost every time in your Bible. It’s Gentile. It’s those that don’t believe in God. That makes it easy to understand. So, is God in the middle of this judgment upon his people, judgment upon the wicked? Is he still reaching out to the unbeliever, the wicked sinner? Absolutely. And that’s what us Christians got to understand. You can’t get so wrapped up in the bad news that you forget there’s good news. In spite of God’s judgment, in spite of God’s vengeance, he is still married and he is still bringing people to Zion, his people. And he is still reaching out to the unbeliever and bringing them in. Wow. And you got to preach the whole counsel of God. If you’re going to preach the bad news, you got to preach the good news. If you’re going to preach the good news, you got to preach the bad news. It’s got to be balanced. Can I hear an amen? When we need to repent, we need to repent. Many of Americans, youth and Americans right now are voting liberal. They reject God’s promises of increase. They reject the Gentiles coming to God. They reject the message that believers are no more following their own ways and we’re just caving in and giving in to the news media around us. Now continuing, we go over to Revelation 7:9 and it says, “A great multitude that no man could number of all nations, all the Gentiles, all the kindreds, all the ethnic groups, all the people and all the languages stood before the throne and before the lamb clothed with white robes.” How many people when this thing is over is before Jesus Christ?
Is God still reaching the unbeliever? (Jeremiah 3:17, Revelation 7:9)

Jeremiah 3:17: “At that time Jerusalem shall be called The Throne of the LORD, and all the nations shall be gathered to it, to the name of the LORD, to Jerusalem. No more shall they follow the dictates of their evil hearts. Revelation 7:9: After these things I looked, and behold, a great multitude which no one could number, of all nations, tribes, peoples, and tongues, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, with palm branches in their hands,
Is the church big and powerful in God’s eyes?

He says Revelation shows an innumerable company of people, and “The church is big. The church is powerful. The church is strong in God’s eyes.” He says end-time preachers miss that “the Lord of the harvest is bringing in the harvest” of both His people who act like Sodom and those without Him. He cites Jeremiah 3, “no more shall they follow the dictates of their evil hearts.”
Is the church big and powerful in God’s eyes?

A number that cannot what? Be numbered. Jeremiah is talking about something God is doing in the earth. John over in Revelation is talking about the accomplishment of it. And it’s an innumerable company of people. Christianity is big in God’s eyes. Christianity is powerful in God’s eyes. The church is big. The church is powerful. The church is strong in God’s eyes. And he’s going to bring our eyes up to his eyes. He’s going to bring our knowledge up to his knowledge and he’s going to bring the performance of his word up to where it is going to come to pass. And this is what the end time preachers are missing. That there is a visitation the end time. In spite of the bad news, there is some tremendous news that God the Lord of the harvest is bringing in the harvest. Both of his people who act like Sodom and those who are acting like Sodom and without him. Ah church, Jeremiah is hot stuff here. And this is the part that should get you excited to keep on serving God and keep preaching the gospel and let God change America. And listen to this. Jeremiah, going back to Jeremiah 3, no more shall they follow the dictates of their evil hearts. Wow. Now, is God going to do something or not? Yes. I mean, this is God talking so strongly that he says, “Man, I’m not only bringing the Gentiles in and my people who were wicked in, but no more are they going to follow their own opinions, their own standard of morality.
Is the church big and powerful in God’s eyes?

Luke 10:2: Then He said to them, “The harvest truly is great, but the laborers are few; therefore pray the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into His harvest. Jeremiah 3:17: “At that time Jerusalem shall be called The Throne of the LORD, and all the nations shall be gathered to it, to the name of the LORD, to Jerusalem. No more shall they follow the dictates of their evil hearts.
Can God change America, and what is “the land of the north”? (Jeremiah 3:18)

He says God accomplished what He said in Jeremiah’s day, in Jesus’ day and in the apostles’ days, so “can he do that in the days of America? Absolutely.” He cites Jeremiah 3:18 and says “the land of the north” in the prophets is Bible terminology for opposition that invades God’s people. He says groups that oppose the Bible are “coming from the north,” and when the enemy comes in like a flood, the Lord will raise up a standard, “Bible morality.”
Can God change America, and what is “the land of the north”? (Jeremiah 3:18)

They’re going to follow me and my Bible morality. And he did it. When Jesus came, he did it. Multitudes followed him. When the apostles went out, the Bible says they turned the world upside down with the message of repentance. God accomplished what he said. And if he can accomplish it back in Jeremiah’s day, if he can accomplish in Jesus days, if he can accomplish in the apostles days, can he do that in the days of America? Absolutely. That’s the power of Jesus Christ. Again in verse 18, in those days the house of Judah shall walk with the house of Israel. They shall come together. The house of Judah shall walk with the house of Israel. And they shall come together out of the land of the north. The land of inherit to the land of inheritance. The land of the north throughout Ezekiel, throughout Jeremiah, throughout Daniel is referring to the opposition in the natural coming down and invading Judah and having war with his people. Started with Assyria. It says Assyria came out of the north when they really came out of the east. It said Babylon came out of the north when Babylon was directly east. You’re looking at me like, “Huh? Duh.” Yeah, you need to you need to examine these things. In Daniel, we know that Rome and Greece were from the north. He says they were from the north and finally they get somebody north. But see, it’s a Bible terminology of opposition. So when the homosexual activists, the atheist, the humanist, the religious, and all these groups that oppose the Bible, they are coming from the north. Why? Because they are opposing God’s people. They’re opposing Jesus. They’re opposing the word. And when the enemy comes in like a flood, the Lord will what? Raise up a standard against him. And that standard is Bible morality. Amen. They’re going to come out of the land of the north. So these people, Judah and Israel, these part of God’s people are what? Opposers of the very God and the very Bible that they believe in. Are you there? Now, how does that work for us today? Well, let me give you a little of kinser imagination today.
Can God change America, and what is “the land of the north”? (Jeremiah 3:18)

Jeremiah 3:18: “In those days the house of Judah shall walk with the house of Israel, and they shall come together out of the land of the north to the land that I have given as an inheritance to your fathers. Isaiah 59:19: So shall they fear The name of the LORD from the west, And His glory from the rising of the sun; When the enemy comes in like a flood, The Spirit of the LORD will lift up a standard against him.
What is his illustration of Israel and Judah in America today?

He imagines Israel as the liberal side of the Bible in America and Judah as the conservative side, saying Israel rejected the Scriptures and made its own way of worship while Judah had God’s way but broke the moral laws. He says Christians in America today also “know the right way” but sin, and that God says He will bring them out of that opposition to Himself.
What is his illustration of Israel and Judah in America today?

All right. I very seldom say this is me but today this is me. Let me give you a little illustration of this. Let’s imagine that Israel is the liberal side of the Bible in America today and Judah is the conservative side. Okay, you got it? Two groups both believe in God. But see, Israel, they rejected the scriptures and said there was other sources to reason and logically make decisions and they created other gods and other ways of worshiping God. Does that sound like the liberals in America today? Absolutely. You see, they rejected the atonement that was coming, just like the liberals in America today. They made their own form of worship and taught the people a different way of worship than God’s way. Isn’t that what liberals do today? The liberal churches. Israel not only broke the moral laws, adultery, stealing, and all them civil laws, but they had their own way and wrong way to worship God and serve Jesus. Okay? Judah, they had the right way. They had God’s way, but they sinned. They broke the moral laws of the Bible. Are you there? Isn’t that the way a lot of us Christians are in America today? Yes, we know the right way, but we commit adultery, homosexuality, incest, stealing, you know, we won’t work. We’re lazy bums. Are you there? And so, we’re in opposition to Jesus and his word. And he said, I’m going to bring them out of that opposition. I’m gonna bring them to myself. Folks, that is powerful.
Is there hope for backsliding Americans and Christians? (Jeremiah 3:22, Isaiah 2:2)

He asks whether there is hope for Americans, believers who don’t obey, and the liberal church, and answers “Absolutely,” citing Jeremiah 3:22, “I will heal your backslidings.” He says salvation is not found in “the hills and the multitude of mountains” but in the Lord, and cites Isaiah 2:2 and Micah 4, where the mountain of the Lord’s house is the church. He says Israel’s high places were worship outside the temple, and deliverance “isn’t in these religions. It is in you.”
Is there hope for backsliding Americans and Christians? (Jeremiah 3:22, Isaiah 2:2)

Is there hope for Americans today? Hope for Christians that believe and don’t obey? Hope for the liberal church that had really messed up everything. Can they be saved by the power of Christ, his blood, and resurrection? Absolutely. Jeremiah 3:22, “Return. Repent you backsiding children. I will heal your backslidings.” Does Jesus have the power to heal, not just forgive our backsidings? Yes. Can he heal them? Can he restore us, make us whole again? Absolutely. He can deliver us from the disease of sin. Now listen to this. Jeremiah suddenly goes to the first person of the people through the Holy Spirit. He starts talking from the first person of the people and he says indeed we will come to you the Lord our God. Now see he’s talking about the people now saying this we will come to you the Lord our God. Truly in vain is salvation hoped for from the hills and the multitude of mountains. Truly in the Lord our God is the salvation, the deliverance, the healing of Israel. Now you got to understand what the hills and the mountains are to get this. Isaiah 2:2, Micah 4 is very important verses for the church in this hour and in this day. Very important verses. Okay. And this is what he says. It shall come to pass in the last days. When is this going to come to pass? Are we living in the last days? Have we been living in the last days since Jesus died and started building his church? Absolutely. Okay. In the last days, the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains. Now, what is the who’s the Lord’s house? The church. Okay. It be established in the top of the mountains and exalted above the hills and all Gentiles shall flow into it. All many people shall go and say, “Come, let us go to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob. He will teach us his ways. We will walk in his paths. For out of Zion, the church shall go forth what? The law and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem, the church.” Now, see, this is our problem. Israel had high places up on the hills and the mountains all over Judah and Israel. You got that? They had these high places. These places where they went to do their little thing to worship God when only worship was supposed to be where? In the temple. The sacrifices, the gathering together was to be where? In the temple. Not on the hills and the high places in the mountains. We will come to you. They said we will come to you. For deliverance isn’t in the mountains. It isn’t in these religions. It is in you. Amen. And who is the Lord, by the way? Jesus.
Is there hope for backsliding Americans and Christians? (Jeremiah 3:22, Isaiah 2:2)

Jeremiah 3:22: “Return, you backsliding children, And I will heal your backslidings.” “Indeed we do come to You, For You are the LORD our God. Jeremiah 3:23: Truly, in vain is salvation hoped for from the hills, And from the multitude of mountains; Truly, in the LORD our God Is the salvation of Israel. Isaiah 2:2-3: Now it shall come to pass in the latter days That the mountain of the LORD’s house Shall be established on the top of the mountains, And shall be exalted above the hills; And all nations shall flow to it. Many people shall come and say, “Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, To the house of the God of Jacob; He will teach us His ways, And we shall walk in His paths.” For out of Zion shall go forth the law, And the word of the LORD from Jerusalem. Micah 4:1-2: Now it shall come to pass in the latter days That the mountain of the LORD’s house Shall be established on the top of the mountains, And shall be exalted above the hills; And peoples shall flow to it. Many nations shall come and say, “Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, To the house of the God of Jacob; He will teach us His ways, And we shall walk in His paths.” For out of Zion the law shall go forth, And the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
Will every knee bow? (Micah 4:5, Philippians 2:10, Romans 14:11)

He cites Micah 4:5, “we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and ever,” and says the name people hate is Jesus. He cites Philippians 2:10 and Romans 14:11, “Every knee shall bow to me.” He says at the judgment throne you will be “confessing you were wrong,” and asks, “Wouldn’t it be better to do that now?”
Will every knee bow? (Micah 4:5, Philippians 2:10, Romans 14:11)

Now Micah 4:5 goes on to say this. All people will walk everyone in the name of his God. But we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and ever. And what is his name? Say it like you mean it. Yes. What do they hate out there? Jesus. You can say God all day long, but you say Jesus, you get them riled up. And that’s the exact name God has given us in Philippians 2:10. At the name of Jesus, every knee will bow. If Jesus is your Lord, I guarantee you, you will bow. If Jesus is your king, I guarantee you he will bow because that is a biblical expression of a recognition of a power by bowing. Romans 14:11, it is written, “Every knee shall bow to me.” Whether you like it, one of these days, you’re going to bow. You might have missed out on it on earth, but boy, when you get to heaven and you stand before him, you’re going to bow. Ain’t no cockiness. Then you’re going to humble yourself immediately. Bowed down on the ground. When you see his majesty, when you see his glory, when you see his authority, you are puny. You’re nothing. And you’re going to bow. And every tongue shall confess. If we confess our sins, he’s what? Faithful and just to forgive us our sins. What do you think you’re going to be doing when you stand before the judgment throne? Defending your choices? No. You’re going to be admitting, confessing you were wrong. Wouldn’t it be better to do that now? Amen. You say, “I’m wrong, Lord.” Jesus is the one we’re [unclear] into. Jesus is the one that can deliver us. Jesus is the one that can save America. Jesus is the one that can change my life today.
Will every knee bow? (Micah 4:5, Philippians 2:10, Romans 14:11)

Micah 4:5: For all people walk each in the name of his god, But we will walk in the name of the LORD our God Forever and ever. Philippians 2:10: that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those in heaven, and of those on earth, and of those under the earth, Romans 14:11: For it is written: “As I live, says the LORD, Every knee shall bow to Me, And every tongue shall confess to God.” 1 John 1:9: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
When does he say Jeremiah was speaking?
He says Jeremiah spoke less than 30 years before the captivity, with the Egyptian, Assyrian and Babylonian nations at war around Judah, and Israel already carried away captive.
What does he say the false prophets told Judah?
He says they spoke that “nothing’s going to happen to Judah,” even with wars and sin all around. He asks whether that sounds like America today.
Who does he say is the wife of Christ?
He says “The church,” citing 2 Corinthians 11:2, and that God reminds even a disciplined people, “you’re my bride.”
Is Christ coming back for a baby church?
He asks, “is he coming back for a baby church or a mature bride church?” He says the church will be a mature, righteous bride dressed in white linen when Christ comes.
What is his illustration from King David?

He says David’s first wife was married off to another man by her father, and after David became king he went and got his bride back. He says Jesus likewise takes us from the “bad husband” by His blood and the power of His resurrection.
Why does he say some Christians lack knowledge?
He says some don’t go to Sunday school or Bible studies “and they don’t open their book through the week.” He says they have time for everything but studying the Bible.
How does he say God writes His word in us?
He says it is the new covenant promise that God would inscribe it in our minds and hearts, but asks “how can he inscribe when we’re not hearing it, listening to it, reading it, and studying it?”
Does he say young people who fall away come back?
He says 50% of those who fell away come back “like the prodigal in the pig pen,” which “puts the percentages in our favor.”
He says Gentile is someone who doesn’t believe in God the Creator or in Jesus. He says the word nation in your Bible is almost every time Gentile: “It’s those that don’t believe in God.”
Must we preach both the bad news and the good news?
He says “If you’re going to preach the bad news, you got to preach the good news. If you’re going to preach the good news, you got to preach the bad news.” He says, “It’s got to be balanced.”
What does he say we will be doing at the judgment throne?
He says we will not be defending our choices: “You’re going to be admitting, confessing you were wrong.” He says it would be better to do that now.

items.t: Stupid and Twisted on the Edge
items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from 2 Peter 3:16 and 2 Peter 2 about “untaught” and “unstable” people who twist the scriptures. He lists doctrines he says are twisted, including once saved…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from 2 Peter 3:16 and 2 Peter 2 about “untaught” and “unstable” people who twist the scriptures. He lists doctrines he says are twisted, including once saved always saved, the prosperity doctrine, purgatory and infant baptism, discusses who interprets scripture, and says believers should be like the Bereans and search the Bible daily.
What does it mean to twist the scriptures? (2 Peter 3:16, 2 Timothy 2:18)

He says 2 Peter 3:16 speaks of the “untaught and unstable” who twist the scriptures to their own destruction, and “twist means to distort, to explain falsely, to misinterpret.” He gives the early church teaching that the resurrection was already past (2 Timothy 2:18) as an example, and says “once saved always saved” is a distortion that is “not in the Bible anywhere.”
What does it mean to twist the scriptures? (2 Peter 3:16, 2 Timothy 2:18)

So we have been teaching on a disregard of Bible doctrines, and second Peter 3:16. “Untaught and unstable people twist the scriptures to their own destructions.” Twist means to distort, to explain falsely, to misinterpret. Okay, and to change the meaning of. They twist it, they change it, they distort it. Now this is a very important scripture in the Bible that most Christians don’t even bat an eye at, but it’s very important, and if you’ll listen this morning, you’re going to learn a lot. All right. I’m going to give you a list of things on the screen that the early church twisted. 2 Timothy 2:18: some people were teaching in the early church that the resurrection is passed already, there’s no more resurrection coming, and they overthrew, overthrown the faith of some. They’ve overthrown people’s faith. Why? Because if you have no hope after death, what’s the point? There’s no no judgment after death, there’s no reward after death, what the point? So people wouldn’t believe, and that was a New Testament distortion of scripture. I got two underneath that for today. “Once saved always saved” is not in the Bible anywhere, and I can prove that once saved always saved does not work. In the Old Testament, God told Moses, “He that sins will I blot out of my book.” Now if he blotted them out of the book, were they in the book? Yes. So were they believers? Were they followers? Could they be blotted out? And over in Revelation it says what? Only those in the book will go in to eternal life. Isin’t that right? Yeah. Hallelujah. There’s a lot more scriptures in that.
What does it mean to twist the scriptures? (2 Peter 3:16, 2 Timothy 2:18)

2 Peter 3:16: as also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things, in which are some things hard to understand, which untaught and unstable people twist to their own destruction, as they do also the rest of the Scriptures. 2 Timothy 2:18: who have strayed concerning the truth, saying that the resurrection is already past; and they overthrow the faith of some. Exodus 32:33: And the LORD said to Moses, “Whoever has sinned against Me, I will blot him out of My book.
What does he say about Jesus drinking wine, the prosperity doctrine, and grace without works? (1 Timothy 6:5)

He says nowhere does the Bible say Jesus drank wine, and he says the faith camp and prosperity camp are a doctrine Paul told us to withdraw from. He says “grace and faith without works” is also twisted, because laws such as honoring parents and not committing adultery still apply, and that the Bible is “a book of truth,” not just “a book of faith.”
What does he say about Jesus drinking wine, the prosperity doctrine, and grace without works? (1 Timothy 6:5)

One, “Jesus drank wine.” So I can, nowhere in the Bible does it say Jesus drank wine. Nowhere. They said, “Well, you know, he changed the water to wine in Cana.” Yeah, didn’t say he drank it. He said he changed the water to wine. “Well, at the communion table.” At the communion table he said, “I will not drink of this cup till I drink it with you in the kingdom.” He didn’t drink the cup. They did. Hallelujah. And these Christians that promote drinking and getting intoxicated when it’s destroying families, it’s destroying productivity on the jobs, it’s destroying kids, it’s very foolish, and it’s not Bible, and you can’t use Jesus for that. Okay, the second one. In the Old Testament, is 1 Timothy 6:5, “gain his godliness, from such withdraw yourself.” That’s still a doctrine today. That’s the uh prosperity camp and the faith camp, you know, name it, claim it, give and it’ll give back to you. Everybody’s going to be rich. In churches that, in churches I go to to preach, the more jewelry you have, the more spiritual you are, and it’s ridiculous. In the New Testament church, Paul frowned on it, and it’s still with us today. But underneath that is two doctrines: grace and faith without works. “All I need is grace and faith, I don’t need any works. You know, we’re not under the law, we’re under grace.” You’re telling me I’m not under honoring and obeying my parents? That’s a law. You’re telling me that I commit can commit adultery, when the Ten Commandments says “Thou shalt not commit adultery”? That’s a law. “Thou shalt not steal” is a law. And I’m so, what I’m to not do that, I work at doing good, honoring my parents, not committing adultery, sexual immorality, not stealing, and so forth. “The Bible is a book of faith.” Nowhere in the Bible does it say the Bible’s a book of faith. These liberal theologians have brainwashed us into that. the Bible The Bible says that faith comes by hearing God’s word. The Bible says that the Bible is a book of truth, ain’t that right? “My word is truth.” It’s a book of truth, and it can be used, truth can be used in any debate. But you see, these people won’t let us use the Bible in science or in politics, because they don’t want to hear moral standards, moral responsibility. So they say the book is a book of faith, it’s religious, you can’t use it. No, it’s a book of truth. Can I hear an amen? All right.
What does he say about Jesus drinking wine, the prosperity doctrine, and grace without works? (1 Timothy 6:5)

Luke 22:18: for I say to you, I will not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.” 1 Timothy 6:5: useless wranglings of men of corrupt minds and destitute of the truth, who suppose that godliness is a means of gain. From such withdraw yourself. Romans 10:17: So then faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God. John 17:17: Sanctify them by Your truth. Your word is truth.
What does 1 Timothy 6:20 mean by “science falsely so-called”? (1 Timothy 6:20)

He says “science” just means “knowledge,” and the Bible “never contradicts real science.” He says people once believed the earth was flat or the center of the universe, while the Bible says it hangs on nothing and is a sphere, and that falling for false science leads into error.
What does 1 Timothy 6:20 mean by “science falsely so-called”? (1 Timothy 6:20)

Next one is the same chapter of Timothy, 6:20: “Avoid oppositions of science falsely so-called, some professing have erred concerning the faith.” Now remember, at this time people believed that the earth was flat, that the earth was held up by something, and the Bible says that the earth was hung on nothing, and the Bible says that the earth is a sphere. Remember, science at this time thought the earth was the center of the universe and the sun rotated around it. Are you there? And so people given into knowledge and science from Plato and all these guys would fall into error, cuz the Bible never contradicts real science. And what is the word for science? Knowledge. it Science just means knowledge. That’s all. It’s not some magic word that makes a scientist a guru.
What does 1 Timothy 6:20 mean by “science falsely so-called”? (1 Timothy 6:20)

1 Timothy 6:20: O Timothy! Guard what was committed to your trust, avoiding the profane and idle babblings and contradictions of what is falsely called knowledge— Job 26:7: He stretches out the north over empty space; He hangs the earth on nothing.
What does he say about claims that homosexuals go to heaven, that the Bible was written by men, and that Jesus is not God? (John 14:6, John 1:1)
