And these kind of people buy their books, it isn’t working for them, and they buy their books, and it won’t work for the purchaser either. And verse two, or verse three of chapter 2 tells us that by greed they will will sell you with deceptive false words. They want the money. They don’t give you their books free. They don’t give you their tapes for it, they want you to buy them, so they can live in a mansion. They want you to come to their conferences, and they want to charge you a fortune, so now they not only pay for the conference room, they can live a year off the income that they made off that conference. And we go like, “Matthew, John, Peter and Paul are insufficient to teach us, and the Holy Ghost is insufficient, and gathering together in a church and seeking God for truth is insufficient. We got to somehow purchase enough books.” And we don’t even realize the books that they bought in the ‘60s they don’t buy today, the books they bought in the ‘70s they don’t buy today, the books they bought in the ‘80s and ‘90s they don’t buy today. It’s fresh books come out, in the same garbage, and the next generation just goes and buys them. Are you there? And so we pay these guys to tell us lies.
How do lifestyle and greed cause the way of truth to be blasphemed? (2 Peter 2:2-3, John 20:30-31)

2 Peter 2:2: And many will follow their destructive ways, because of whom the way of truth will be blasphemed. John 20:31: but these are written that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing you may have life in His name. 2 Peter 2:3: By covetousness they will exploit you with deceptive words; for a long time their judgment has not been idle, and their destruction does not slumber.
How do false teachers entice people, and what is “liberty” that enslaves? (2 Peter 2:14, 2 Peter 2:19)

He says false teachers tell people “they can sin and still have eternal life,” which is what “seducing” and “entice” means, to “make sin look attractive and make sin look approved and okay.” He says God does not make anyone a homosexual or a thief: “you chose to do that,” and describes visiting a church in Paraguay that stopped bringing the Bible and waited for the Holy Ghost, which he calls “their own imagination.”
How do false teachers entice people, and what is “liberty” that enslaves? (2 Peter 2:14, 2 Peter 2:19)

Number four, they want to hear that they can sin and still have eternal life. That’s the bottom line. Okay, “they speak evil of things they do not understand, they will utterly perish in their own corruption, they’ll receive the wages of unrighteousness, having eyes full of adultery,” verse 14, “that cannot cease from sin, enticing unstable souls.” Seducing. Now here it is. Who are these people following false prophets and buying false information and and wanting to live in sin? what How does he title them? Unstable. The very scripture he says, “unlearned and unstable people twist the scriptures to their own destruction.” So this, the word “entice” means to seduce, make sin look attractive and make sin look approved and okay. Yeah, and that’s what ministers are telling the homosexuals, “Oh, it’s okay, God made you that way.” That’s a lie. God didn’t make a pedophile a pedophile, a thief a thief, or a homosexual a homosexual. You chose to do that. Number five, “they boast of having liberty, but they are the slave slaves of destruction.” “Oh, I’m mature now. I used to believe like you, but I’m mature now.” Oh, I was down in a church in Paraguay where they didn’t even bring the Bible to church anymore. They just let the Holy Spirit teach them. Us Spirit-filled people can be kooks. I tell you, we can be really kooks. The Bible says to study to show thyself approved. “Seek ye out of the book of the law and read.” The Bible says these things. And yes, yes, it does say the Holy Spirit will teach you as you study, as you read it, as you hear teachers teaching it. Really? No one brought, they just went in, waited for the Holy Ghost to talk, and wasn’t the Holy Ghost talking? I I’m not stupid. I was there. I got the same Holy Ghost. Holy Ghost wasn’t saying anything through these people. It was their own imagination. And my first message straightened that whole church out. Really, not my message, the first message I brought from the Bible just straighten, God came and just straightened that whole thing out.
How do false teachers entice people, and what is “liberty” that enslaves? (2 Peter 2:14, 2 Peter 2:19)

2 Peter 2:14: having eyes full of adultery and that cannot cease from sin, enticing unstable souls. They have a heart trained in covetous practices, and are accursed children. 2 Peter 2:19: While they promise them liberty, they themselves are slaves of corruption; for by whom a person is overcome, by him also he is brought into bondage. 2 Timothy 2:15: Be diligent to present yourself approved to God, a worker who does not need to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.
Which desires are okay, and what happens when people who knew the way go back? (2 Peter 2:18-21)

He says desires to eat, for sexual fulfillment and to relax are given by God, but “lewdness” means going overboard, and “you don’t have to be stupid” because you have a desire. He reads 2 Peter 2:20-21 that if they are again entangled and overcome “the latter end is worse for them than the beginning,” and says it is horrible for someone to think they are okay when they are not.
Which desires are okay, and what happens when people who knew the way go back? (2 Peter 2:18-21)

second Peter 2:18: “They speak great boastful words of emptiness, they entice to the lust of the flesh, lewdness.” It’s important that lewdness is there, because there are desires of the flesh that are okay. You’ll have a desire to eat, there’s nothing wrong with that. You’ll have a desire for sexual fulfillment, there’s nothing wrong with that. God put it there, you understand? You’ll have a desire to relax and enjoy, have a recreational time. God gave us that. But he put the word “lewd,” evil, in there, so you know that when you go overboard or you break away from what’s right, that’s the wrong desire. Okay, that’s very important. And a lot of people beat themselves up, you know, looking at a woman and lust after her. “Oh my my God, oh my God, oh my God.” Look, God created you a sexual being. Relax. Just control it, bridle it. You don’t have to drink arsenic, you can drink milk. You don’t have to eat poison or whatever, or poison ivy, you can eat wholesome food. You don’t have to be stupid. Just because you got a desire to eat doesn’t mean you don’t have the faculties to control what you eat, does it? Number six, they had escaped the way of righteousness, knew the way of right, but turned back and were entangled and overcome. And that’s what he says in verse 20, “after escaping the pollutions of the world by the knowledge of the Lord Jesus Christ.” See, that’s why we need to go a church where they’re teaching us knowledge, they’re teaching us wisdom, they’re giving us things that work. “They are again entangled in those things they were saved from and overcome, the latter end is worse for them than the beginning.” Why? Because now they think they’re going to heaven, and they’re not. And it’s horrible when somebody thinks they’re okay when they’re not okay. Verse 21: “It would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness.” So they see, they knew the way of righteousness, and they left it, and “after knowing it, to turn from that holy commandment delivered to them.” Now folks, I’ve watched a lot of people turn. I’ve watched them touch God, I’ve watched God save them, I watched them commit themselves to living for God and repenting from their sin and stopping sinning, and then somebody comes along and, that and uh you understand me, and we bond, we connect, and they teach them lies, and they get in a little clique, and they fall away. I’ve seen it over and over and over.
Which desires are okay, and what happens when people who knew the way go back? (2 Peter 2:18-21)

2 Peter 2:18: For when they speak great swelling words of emptiness, they allure through the lusts of the flesh, through lewdness, the ones who have actually escaped from those who live in error. 2 Peter 2:20: For if, after they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, they are again entangled in them and overcome, the latter end is worse for them than the beginning.
How should we respond? Be like the Bereans (Acts 17:11, Matthew 7:16, 2 Peter 2:22)

He quotes “a dog returns to his own vomit” for those who go back to sin, and says twisted doctrine destroys people and “all of us are guilty.” He says Peter wrote to genuine Christians to watch for unstable teachers, and we should search the scriptures daily like the Bereans, look for Jesus in every book, and know people by their fruit, since “denomination doesn’t save you.”
How should we respond? Be like the Bereans (Acts 17:11, Matthew 7:16, 2 Peter 2:22)

But it has happened to them according to the true proverb: “A dog returns to his own vomit, and a pig after being washed to her wallowing in the mire.” So the unstable go back to sin, or they never really come out. Hallelujah. I’ve seen a lot of things, church. Twisted doctrine destroys people. The Catholics, the Baptists, the Presbyterians, all of us are guilty. And it’s our fault that we believe a church doctrine of faith above the Bible and not know what the Bible says ourself. That’s our fault. Hallelujah. How many going to raise your hand and said, “Man, I’m going to watch out for twisted doctrine”? Yes. You know, it’s easy for us to do it. we want to say we want to We want the scripture so badly to back up what we believe that we twist it. It’s important for you to know who Peter wrote this to. Okay, who did Peter write these words to? He wrote him to those who obtain the same precious faith as him and others by Jesus Christ. The same faith we’re supposed to have. The same faith Jesus had, the same faith the apostles had, equal faith, you can’t change it. We got to have the same faith. Amen. And that’s who he wrote to. He said, you people, be careful of unstable and unlearned people that twist the scriptures. And he’s writing to you, if you’re a genuine Christian that wants to serve Christ. You may have problems in your life, but you’re working on him, you’re growing. He’s writing to you and say, watch out for these unlearned and unstable people that twist the scriptures, that give you liberty to stay in the sin you’re in or go back to the sin. This is the kind of people we got to be, the Bereans. They “receive the word with all readiness of mind and they search the scriptures.” How often? Daily. To see whether those things were true. Those things Paul and Peter and them were teaching them, they search the scriptures daily. You cannot be a Bible scholar going to church once or twice a week and just getting a message from your pastor. You got to get into the word daily. And God promised to open that word up to you, and let me tell you the key. The key is he wants to reveal Jesus. So when you start reading Genesis, who do you look for? Jesus. When you read Leviticus, that boring book, who you looking for? Jesus. Hallelujah. The truth. Matthew 7:16: “You shall know them by their” what? Fruit. Not by their mouth, by their lifestyle, by how they live. Anybody can say, “I believe in Jesus.” A disciple follows him. Amen. A disciple isn’t tripped up by these winds of doctrine, these twisted people. We must not disregard true Bible doctrines. We must not twist scriptures to our own and others’ destruction. I may will raise your right hand and say, “Yes, I agree with that. That’s truth. I mustn’t. I must be very careful.” Yes. Doesn’t matter what denomination we’re in, denomination doesn’t save you. Jesus and the word saves you. We must not leave the way of truth and right by inventing our own beliefs, using twisted scripture. Wow. How many’s been guilty of inventing your own doctrines in days past? Man, I’m I was guilty. What my biggest mistake as a young Christian, I believed everything they said on the radio, and boy, I found out the hard way they were lying. I mean really, they were lying. That’s flat out lies. They were just flat out lying. So I learned not to follow those people on the radio. I turned off the radio and turned on the Bible tapes. I started listening to Paul and Peter and these guys.
How should we respond? Be like the Bereans (Acts 17:11, Matthew 7:16, 2 Peter 2:22)

2 Peter 2:22: But it has happened to them according to the true proverb: “A dog returns to his own vomit,” and, “a sow, having washed, to her wallowing in the mire.” Acts 17:11: These were more fair-minded than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness, and searched the Scriptures daily to find out whether these things were so. Matthew 7:16: You will know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes from thornbushes or figs from thistles?
He says “twist means to distort, to explain falsely, to misinterpret,” and to change the meaning of scripture.
What does he say about “once saved always saved”?
He says it “is not in the Bible anywhere,” and cites God telling Moses “he that sins will I blot out of my book,” which he says shows those in the book could be blotted out.
Does he say Jesus drank wine?
He says “nowhere in the Bible does it say Jesus drank wine,” and that at the communion table Jesus said “I will not drink of this cup till I drink it with you in the kingdom.”
Is the Bible a book of faith or a book of truth?
He says “nowhere in the Bible does it say the Bible’s a book of faith,” and that it is “a book of truth” which can be used in any debate, including science and politics.
What does he say science means?
He says “science just means knowledge. That’s all. It’s not some magic word that makes a scientist a guru.”
What does he say he told a Jehovah’s Witness about Jesus being God?
He says he asked, “how do you account for John 1:1,” and that the Word is God and the Word became flesh, and that Jesus’ name Emmanuel means “God with us.”
Does he say the Bible has errors?
He says the rooster crowing twice or three times and a king being 8 or 18 years old “doesn’t take away from the truths of the Bible,” and says he can explain everything atheists call a contradiction.
What does he say about marriage in heaven?
He says the Bible “plainly” says that in the age to come people neither marry nor are given in marriage, and that Jesus said people err “not knowing the scriptures nor the power of God.”
What does he say about infant baptism?
He says “there is no infant baptism in the Bible” and that a baby cannot understand preaching or repent, since repentance comes before baptism.
What does he say to people who say “don’t judge”?
He says when they say homosexuality is okay they are making a judgment, “doing the very thing you’re telling me not to do,” and that he can decide “with the authority of the Bible.”
What does he say about turning the other cheek?
He says “ain’t no time to turn no cheek, it’s a time to talk,” and that these people “need to be told, because God wants to save them.”
Does he say grace is something we grow in?
He reads 2 Peter 3:17-18, that we should beware being led away by the error of the wicked and “grow in grace,” and says “grace is something you grow in.”
Does he say we can interpret scripture ourselves?
He says “nobody has the right to interpret scripture… the Bible interprets, explains itself,” and you should find where else the Bible says it.
What does he say about magic ceremonies?
He says “ain’t no magical ceremony,” and that “it’s the truth that sets you free… that causes you to grow… that heals you.”
What does he say about refusing medicine?
He says Jesus said the sick need a doctor, that children die when parents refuse medicine, and that faith in your faith is wrong: “our faith is to be in the Lord Jesus Christ.”

p: In “Terrorism: Cause and Cure,” Pastor David G. Kincer questions the FBI definition when laws or policies themselves harm, then names three sources: God’s appointed terror for breaking His covenant (Leviticus 26), government that uses the sword against good people (Romans 13 misused), and bullies/gangsters. He lists American examples—abortion, approved same-sex lifestyle, and Bible-bashing—and offers cures: obey God’s word, change bad laws or hide until change, and punish those who refuse correction (Genesis 9:6).
What FBI definition of terrorism does he start with?

Violent acts dangerous to human life that violate federal or state law, apparently intended to intimidate or coerce civilians or government—yet he asks what if the law or policy itself induces terror.
What FBI definition of terrorism does he start with?

So thank you for joining us. Again with Bible moralities and in this session we’re going to be discussing clarity on crucial choices today we will answer the question terrorism what are the causes of terrorism and what are if any the cures of terrorism. we’re going to look at the FBI definition of terrorists. and you can see pictures on the news on the internet of a FBI hit squad they’re terrifying. Themselves but their definition is an international or domestic violent acts dangerous to human life that violate federal or state.
Can government policy itself be a source of terrorism?
Yes. He cites Hitler killing Jews and enslaving other races as government policies that were terror, and asks whether those who tried to assassinate Hitler were the terrorists.
Can government policy itself be a source of terrorism?

Law and my question there is what if the law induces terrorism. they go on to say that terrorism appears to be intended to intimidate and coerce a civilian population number one a policy of a government. And my question there again is what if that policy itself is harmful like Hitler’s policy of killing the Jews because they were Jews or enslaving people because they were a different race government did those things and so government policies themselves can be a source of terrorism number three they said it appears and intend to be intended to intimidate or coerce the conduct of a government by mass destruction assassination or.
What is intimidation and coercion in his definition?
Bullying people to act against their will by psychological pressure, propaganda, physical force or threats to achieve a political goal—forcing others to behave and believe as you do.
What is intimidation and coercion in his definition?

Kidnapping but I submit to you were the people that tried to assassinate Hitler were they the terrorist or was Hitler the terrorist and so it just depends on the moral factor what is. Right intimidation and coercion is bullying people to act against their will. By the use of psychological. Pressure. Propaganda get their mind to think different physical force or threats now the dictionary definition of terrorism is the use of violent acts mental propaganda and verbal threats to frighten people to achieve a political. Goal or their goal people want to control other people that’s what a a terrorist is they want you to behave and act and believe the way they do and if you don’t they’re going to do everything.
How can God be a “source” of terrorism in his teaching?
From Leviticus 26: if you disobey and break the covenant, God appoints terror—disease, war, famine, beasts, faint heart, scattering—as consequences of violating moral absolutes.
How can God be a “source” of terrorism in his teaching?

To force. You to accept that and I submit to you this morning that it’s still terrorism if a federal or state law endangers human life using intimidation, coercion against one more moral will bullying and forcing people to go against their moral will now we’re going to look at three sources of terrorism and the first one is God himself God a predictor of sin’s source of terrorism Leviticus 26:14 if you do not obey me and all these commandments but break my covenant see if you don’t obey my word you break break my covenant Leviticus 26:16 I will appoint I will assign terror over you and he lists them disease war famine beast you have a faint heart a weak heart a cowardly heart and I’ll scatter you or you’ll be scattered because you sin you violate God’s law see he appointed it he assigned it he made a law that if you’re going to disobey.
How can God be a “source” of terrorism in his teaching?

Leviticus 26:14: ‘But if you do not obey Me, and do not observe all these commandments, Leviticus 26:16: I also will do this to you: I will even appoint terror over you, wasting disease and fever which shall consume the eyes and cause sorrow of heart. And you shall sow your seed in vain, for your enemies shall eat it.
How does your own wickedness correct you?
Jeremiah 2:19: your wickedness and backslidings correct you. Love God and neighbor (Matthew 22) means do no harm; violating that brings repercussions including disease and judgment.
How does your own wickedness correct you?

Moral absolutes moral standards then those sins that disobedience is going to bring problems in your. Life in Jeremiah 2:19 he backs it up your own wickedness and your backslidings will correct you you see if you’re going to decide to live immorally there’s going to be repercussions and the Bible says a backslider is filled with their only own ways a backslider someone just does what they want to do. Not what God says to do now we know in Matthew 22:36 that the whole prophets in the law is summed up in loving God and loving your neighbor as yourself in other words don’t do any harm to God and don’t do any harm anything that hurts people around you and so it’s easy then to.
How does your own wickedness correct you?

Jeremiah 2:19: Your own wickedness will correct you, And your backslidings will rebuke you. Know therefore and see that it is an evil and bitter thing That you have forsaken the LORD your God, And the fear of Me is not in you,” Says the Lord GOD of hosts. Matthew 22:37-39: Jesus said to him, “‘You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’ This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like it: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ 2 Corinthians 5:11: Knowing, therefore, the terror of the Lord, we persuade men; but we are well known to God, and I also trust are well known in your consciences.
When does government become the terrorist?
Romans 13: rulers are a terror to evil, not good. If government executes wrath on those practicing good—like Idi Amin killing pastors who submitted—it becomes terrorist; do not submit out of context.

Understand that if I violate that and hurt people then that violation is going to have repercussions diseases there were 10 10 million dead worldwide by infectious diseases in 1860 through 1890 smallpox killed 300 million people in the 1800s and I can go on and on the mass murderers and all these things that have happening in the world through war famine killing people natural disasters and 2 Corinthians 5:11 says knowing the terror of the Lord I persuade men and so that’s why preachers should be preaching the gospel and Christians should be sharing the gospel because there is repercussions for sin and there’s repercussions in eternal life eternal judgment now the second source of terrorism is government Romans 13:3-4 rulers are not a terror to good works if you do evil be afraid he doesn’t bear the sword in vain for he is God’s minister and avenger to execute wrath on him who practices. Evil but what if that. Government uses the sword uses his authority to execute wrath on those that are practicing good, then that government that political leader becomes a. Terrorist you see leaders you read about them in history Idi Amin killed hundreds of thousands of his own people his own citizens because they weren’t of his tribe and he killed the media and he killed the rich and he killed Christians in fact he invited Christians to come to meet with him back there when he took over Uganda and and the message of that time period from the church is submit to those in authority over you and so these pastors foolishly responded and came to meet with Amin and he had them killed every one of them thinking they were obeying God’s word we cannot take Romans 13 out of its context government must honor good people and punish bad people when they punish good people and honor bad people and immorality they are not doing their job and we are not to submit

Romans 13:3-4: For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to evil. Do you want to be unafraid of the authority? Do what is good, and you will have praise from the same. For he is God’s minister to you for good. But if you do evil, be afraid; for he does not bear the sword in vain; for he is God’s minister, an avenger to execute wrath on him who practices evil.
What does he say about Stalin and unrighteous decrees?
He cites Stalin’s mass killings and communist force, and Muslim Quran conquering by force as terrorism. Isaiah 10:1: woe to unrighteous decrees that turn aside the needy and moral from justice.
What does he say about Stalin and unrighteous decrees?

and many Christians foolishly think that we have to submit to government because of Romans and so Romans 13 and so does government they cited this in court they used it on me and I’m supposed to do whatever they say if I’m going to follow the Bible Stalin killed 50. Million and he said we must eradicate capitalism they a disease capitalism is a disease that disease that must be cleansed from the world and then the communist manifesto it says we got to eradicate capitalism by revolution and by force so both the communist and the Muslim Quran advocates conquering the world for their purposes by force that’s terrorism simply because you disagree with them they’re going to force you to live their way Isaiah 10:1 says woe to those who make unrighteous decrees and oppressive judgments oppressive decisions that turn aside the needy the moral from.

Isaiah 10:1: “Woe to those who decree unrighteous decrees, Who write misfortune, Which they have prescribed

1 Samuel 17: Israel feared Goliath’s threats. Bullies are in neighborhoods, schools, work, media, parties and families—including husbands terrifying families and wives using tears, nagging or withholding sex.

Justice see instead of giving the moral people justice they turn turn aside and they give immoral people the right to live and behave the way they behave and they hurt other people another source of terrorism is gangsters. Interrogation and I’m not going to have sex tonight if you don’t do what I. 1 Samuel 17:11: When Saul and all Israel heard these words of the Philistine, they were dismayed and greatly afraid.
What abortion example does he call terrorism in America?
He lists politicians, judges and activists who approve abortion and ignore self-control as terrorists; the terrorized is the baby in the womb, killed though science says life begins at conception.

Control whether it is in school, whether it is in the home or the community it’s still terrorism let me give you some examples of terrorism in America who are the terrorists democrats and republican party politicians supreme court judges state judges state governors city mayors liberals humanists homosexual activists religionists atheists hedonists freethinkers agnostics and anyone that approves abortion birth control and ignores self-control birth control and ignores the life of the baby. items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the final revelation in Revelation is the judgment of God, and that ministers must preach it because everyone will stand before Christ and be judged by their…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the final revelation in Revelation is the judgment of God, and that ministers must preach it because everyone will stand before Christ and be judged by their works. He covers the second death and lake of fire, the book of life, the sheep and goats of Matthew 25 and how we treat God’s people, and being ready to die.
What are the three revelations in the book of Revelation, and why can’t John add to the word?

He says there are three revelations in Revelation: the revelation of Jesus Christ, of His church, and of the judgment of God, “the same revelation that’s in the rest of the New Testament and the rest of the Old Testament.” He says John could not add to or take away from the word, so if something is not found in the rest of the scriptures “we’re missing the revelation of revelations.”
What are the three revelations in the book of Revelation, and why can’t John add to the word?

The end lesson of revelations is the end time judgment. I told you there were three revelations in revelations. First, it is the revelation of Jesus Christ. Wow. Jesus Christ. He knows it because he just taught it or he’d have forgot it too. The second revelation in Revelation is the revelation of his church. The third revelation is the revelation of the judgment of God. The same revelation that’s in the rest of the New Testament and the rest of the Old Testament. Same revelation. You see, John said, “You can’t add to the word or take away from it.” See, John could do nothing that didn’t already been spoken in the scriptures. And so when we go to Revelations and we take things out and twist it and make great fairy tales out of it, that’s not what John is doing.
What does the Bible say about the coming judgment? (Psalm 1:5, Psalm 98:9, Daniel 7:10, Daniel 12:2, Matthew 16:27, Acts 10:42)

He gives scriptures that the ungodly shall not stand in the judgment, that the Lord will judge the world with righteousness, that the books were opened, and that the Son of Man will reward “every man according to his… works, his behavior, his action.” He says Jesus commanded the apostles “to preach to the people and to testify that it is Jesus who was ordained by God to judge,” and that “you’re going to be judged.”
What does the Bible say about the coming judgment? (Psalm 1:5, Psalm 98:9, Daniel 7:10, Daniel 12:2, Matthew 16:27, Acts 10:42)

If it’s not found in the rest of the scriptures, we’re missing the revelation of revelations. Hallelujah. Did John have to keep his own principle, not adding to the word nor taking away? Absolutely. In fact, it wasn’t his words. It was Christ’s words he was given to. Hallelujah. Okay, I want to give you some scriptures about the judgment. Psalms 1:5, the ungodly shall not stand in the judgment. Psalms 98:9, the Lord is coming to judge the earth with righteousness. He will judge the world and the people, the flocks, the congregations with impartiality. Yes, you’re going to be judged. You’re quoting Jesus and believing in Jesus is not going to keep you from standing before Christ. Isaiah 39:11, “The day of the Lord comes. It’s going to be a cruel day with both wrath and fierce anger, and he will destroy the sinners in it. For the stars of heaven and their constellations will not give light. The sun will be darkened. The moon will will not shine. And I will punish the world for its evil and the wicked for their iniquity. And I will stop the arrogance of the proud. That’s Old Testament stuff. Daniel 7:10. 10,000 times 10,000 stood before him, and the judgment seat was set, and the books were open. The book of works, the book of your actions, the book of your behavior is opened. Daniel 12:2, “Many that sleep in the dust of your of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, t some to shame and everlasting contempt.” Matthew 16:27, “The Son of man shall come with his angels. Then he will reward every man according to his faith.” No. According to his grace? No. According to his saving of many souls, no. According to his works, his behavior, his action. The second coming is all about the judgment. Acts 10:42, he commanded us to preach to the people. Listen to this, church. He commanded us, the apostles. He commanded us, the apostles, to preach to the people and to testify that it is Jesus who was ordained by God to judge, to be the judge of the living and of the dead.
What does the Bible say about the coming judgment? (Psalm 1:5, Psalm 98:9, Daniel 7:10, Daniel 12:2, Matthew 16:27, Acts 10:42)

Psalm 1:5: Therefore the ungodly shall not stand in the judgment, Nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous. Psalm 98:9: before the LORD, For He is coming to judge the earth. With righteousness He shall judge the world, And the peoples with equity. Isaiah 13:9-11: Behold, the day of the LORD comes, Cruel, with both wrath and fierce anger, To lay the land desolate; And He will destroy its sinners from it. For the stars of heaven and their constellations Will not give their light; The sun will be darkened in its going forth, And the moon will not cause its light to shine. “I will punish the world for its evil, And the wicked for their iniquity; I will halt the arrogance of the proud, And will lay low the haughtiness of the terrible. Daniel 7:10: A fiery stream issued And came forth from before Him. A thousand thousands ministered to Him; Ten thousand times ten thousand stood before Him. The court was seated, And the books were opened. Daniel 12:2: And many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, Some to everlasting life, Some to shame and everlasting contempt. Matthew 16:27: For the Son of Man will come in the glory of His Father with His angels, and then He will reward each according to his works. Acts 10:42: And He commanded us to preach to the people, and to testify that it is He who was ordained by God to be Judge of the living and the dead.

He says yes: Jesus ordained it, and the apostles were commanded to tell people of the judgment. He says it was “the gospel that used to scare me to death,” coupled with the part that Jesus loves us, so he had a force pushing him away from hell and one drawing him to Christ, and that when you don’t tell people the truth “you are hurting them.”

Should ministers in every Christian church be preaching the judgment? Yes. Yes, he ordained it. And Paul said, “Us apostles, we are commanded to tell people of the judgment and they’re going to be judged by their works. And if they don’t repent, they don’t accept the sacrifice of Christ and his empowerment to live for him, they’re going to be judged.” See, that is the main part of the gospel. That’s the gospel that used to scare me to death. I didn’t want to go to hell. Coupled with the other part of the gospel that we’re the bride of Christ and Jesus loves us and we can all know him. Wow. He’ll make himself real to me. So you got I had a force pushing me away from hell and I had a force drawing me to Christ. Now you can’t beat that kind of power. Amen. And when you’re afraid to speak about the judgment and sinners being punished and all that, you’re missing the revelation of the judgment day of Christ and you’re hurting people. When you don’t tell people the truth, you are hurting them. You’re doing them harm. When you tell them they’re okay and they’re thinking and the way they believe and all that and you don’t tell them the truth, you are damaging them in the future because they are going to be judged. Romans 1:32, they know God’s righteousness degree, God’s righteous decree that those who do such thing deserve death. And he had that list of sins there and homosexuality is one of them. Adultery is another one and you know stealing and all that. A whole list there. He says, “They that do these things deserve to die. They not only continue to do these things, but approve of those who practice them.” So when you approve of the homosexual committing a homosexuality, you are joining in their judgment. When you approve of people getting high on drugs and medical marijuana and this nonsense that’s coming in America, you are guilty because you aren’t telling them that’s wrong. Are you out there?
Romans 1:32: who, knowing the righteous judgment of God, that those who practice such things are deserving of death, not only do the same but also approve of those who practice them.
Will believers escape the judgment because they believe in God? (Romans 2:3, 2 Corinthians 5:10)

He says the judgment is “an eternal judgment” and that God “doesn’t judge by emotions. He judges by truth.” He says being a believer, being baptized, in a Christian church, or saying “I love Jesus” does not let you escape if you commit sin, and cites 2 Corinthians 5:10, that we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ to receive what we have done, “whether it be good or whether it be bad.”
Will believers escape the judgment because they believe in God? (Romans 2:3, 2 Corinthians 5:10)

The judgment’s a serious thing. It’s an eternal judgment, folks. There’s no getting back out. Once the judgment is passed, there is no. And God isn’t like the judges today, as we’re going to see in this message. He doesn’t judge by emotions. He judges by truth. Hallelujah. This is a serious message. Romans 2:3. You who judge those practicing sinful things and you do the same. Do you think you’re going to escape the judgment of God? What is he saying? Because you’re a Jew and you believe in God and yet you’re doing what the sinners do. You think because you believe in God and you learned about God, that you’re going to escape the judgment just because you’ve accepted Christ and you’ve been baptized and you’re in a Christian church and you know, you say, “I love Jesus.” And yet you commit adultery. You lie. You steal and flagrantly break the word out. You think you’re going to escape the judgment? No way. Now I’m giving you the scriptures. This is not David Kincer. This is the author of the Bible. And the only thing I have permission to teach is what he taught. I don’t have permission to give you my opinion. I can’t say I believe unless I’m believing what he believes. Are you there? And do you know you can’t do that either? You know, you’re saying, “Well, I don’t see nothing wrong with it. Doesn’t matter if you see what’s wrong with it.” What does God see? Hallelujah. The judgment is serious. It’s very serious. Listen to this. 2 Corinthians 5:10. Parents, young people, you got to get this. 2 Corinthians 5:10. We must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ. That everyone may receive the things done in his body according to he what he has done. Whether it be good or whether it be bad. If you done bad, you’re going to be punished. If you dang good, you’re going to be rewarded. And listen to this. Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men. What compelled the apostles? What made them sacrifice their life? What made them, you know, do things where they were stoned and put in prison and beaten over and over?
Will believers escape the judgment because they believe in God? (Romans 2:3, 2 Corinthians 5:10)

Romans 2:3: And do you think this, O man, you who judge those practicing such things, and doing the same, that you will escape the judgment of God? 2 Corinthians 5:10: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive the things done in the body, according to what he has done, whether good or bad. 2 Corinthians 5:11: Knowing, therefore, the terror of the Lord, we persuade men; but we are well known to God, and I also trust are well known in your consciences.
Why are people who warn about the judgment mistreated? (2 Corinthians 5:11)

He says the apostles suffered because “they understood that there’s a judgment to come and we got to persuade men to escape that judgment.” He says when you have that concern you may be mocked or separated from, because you are disturbing their comfort zone, and that churches start in unity around mercy but divide over “doctrines of discipline.”
Why are people who warn about the judgment mistreated? (2 Corinthians 5:11)

And what made them act like that and put up with that? Because they understood that there’s a judgment to come and we got to persuade men to escape that judgment. Yes. Yes. Give the Lord a clap offering for the [unclear] word. Yes. See, and when you get that concern, you’re going to be mistreated. You’re going to have people separate from your company. You’re going to have them mocking and laughing at you. Why? You are disturbing their comfort zone. And they don’t care if Jesus said it, if God said it. They don’t want to hear it. Your family members can turn on you. Your friends can turn on you. Church members can turn on you. You see the church starts in unity around Jesus. We all like that message of mercy and forgiveness all of us. And then it starts dividing over other doctrine because people don’t want to embrace restraint doctrine, discipline, doctrines of discipline. And so they separate you and they laugh at you and they’ll call you a holy roller or a religious extremist or whatever. And all you’re doing is just expanding your faith in God’s word and exercising it and preaching it.
What is the second death, and will everyone be resurrected? (Revelation 20:14)

He says everyone dies once, then “you’re going to be resurrected” whether you believe in it or not, and stand before the white throne to give an account. He says those who rejected Jesus’ word “You’re going to be cast into the lake of fire” as the second death, while those who repent and don’t flagrantly sin, “We’re only going to die once.”
What is the second death, and will everyone be resurrected? (Revelation 20:14)

And the judgment is one of the top messages. Is that a good amen? And you young people, don’t you believe this nonsense from TV and what people are telling you. They’re telling you a bunch of lies. This Bible is the facts. This is the truth. It’s really going to happen. Now, the lake of fire, which is the second death. See, you die once and you go to the grave, young people. Then you’re going to be resurrected and ain’t a thing you can do about it. You don’t have any control over this. It’s going to happen whether you believe in it or not. And you’re going to be resurrected. Your body is going to come back to you. It’s going to materialize. And you’re going to stand before his white throne before the judgment and give an account of your life. It’s going to happen. Okay. You are resurrected. You might be 14. You might be 24. You might be 54. You might be 68. You might be 99 when you die, but you’re going to be resurrected. You’re going to die one time. And that’s all God intended for you to do is die one time. Physically die. But on that day, if your behavior wasn’t right, if you rejected Jesus, you say, “But I didn’t reject Jesus.” Yes. But see, Jesus said, “In works they disown me. With the mouth they profess to know me, but they don’t choose my word and live by my word.” So, that is a rejection of who? Jesus. See, you can’t separate Christ and his word. They’re the same. Isn’t that right? Yes. And then you’re going to die a second death. You’re going to be cast into the lake of fire. He said, “That’s the second death. You’re going to die twice. But those of us who live for God and we might make mistakes but not flagrant and we don’t flagrantly sin.
Who goes into the lake of fire, and how long does it last? (Revelation 19:20, Revelation 20:10, Revelation 20:14)

He says the beast and the false prophet were cast alive into the lake of fire, then the devil, who is “tormented… forever,” and then death and hell. He says “the last enemy” is death, and that we already have Satan “under our feet.”
Who goes into the lake of fire, and how long does it last? (Revelation 19:20, Revelation 20:10, Revelation 20:14)

We repent. We get back up and all the rest. We’re only going to die once. We’re not going to the lake of fire. You’re going to die twice. And your second death is eternal. Do you young people understand that? This is serious stuff. Who’s going to go to the lake of fire? Revelations 19:20, the beast and the false prophet are cast alive into the lake of fire. They’re already there. The Devil Revelation 20:10 that deceived the nations was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone where the beast and beast and false prophet are already there. The first two to go was the beast and the false prophet and then Satan. And they’re going to be tormented for a few days in purgatory and they can pray their way out. They’re going to be tormented how long, young people? Forever. Say it. Forever. Here forever. Revelations 20:14, death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. What’s the last enemy? What’s the last enemy? Death. See, that last enemy that God Jesus is going to destroy when he comes is death. See, we already have Satan under our feet. A lot of you don’t know that, but you do. If if I could just get it through your cranial vacuum, you are a powerful people. Death and hell were cast into the lake of fire.
Who goes into the lake of fire, and how long does it last? (Revelation 19:20, Revelation 20:10, Revelation 20:14)

Revelation 19:20: Then the beast was captured, and with him the false prophet who worked signs in his presence, by which he deceived those who received the mark of the beast and those who worshiped his image. These two were cast alive into the lake of fire burning with brimstone. Revelation 20:10: The devil, who deceived them, was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone where the beast and the false prophet are. And they will be tormented day and night forever and ever. Revelation 20:14: Then Death and Hades were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death. 1 Corinthians 15:26: The last enemy that will be destroyed is death.
How do we get our name written in the book of life? (Revelation 20:15, Luke 10:20)

He says it is by “embracing Jesus the life, his cross, his blood, cleansing us, forgiving us of sin.” He says when we confess our sins and ask Him into our life, He forgives and cleanses, our past is erased, and He writes our name in the book of life; so “rejoice because your names are written in heaven.”
How do we get our name written in the book of life? (Revelation 20:15, Luke 10:20)

Hell is the abiding place of the dead that has gone on before. Okay? And this is the second death. All not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire. How do we get our name in the book of life? By embracing Jesus the life, his cross, his blood, cleansing us, forgiving us of sin. See, when we confess our sins and ask him to come into our life, he forgives, he cleanses, and he because our past is erased by his blood. He writes our name in the book of life because we have accepted Jesus Christ, the lifegiver, and his word into our life. Hallelujah. And remember Jesus said, “Rejoice because your names are written in heaven in this book.” If you can’t praise him for anything else, man, just say, “Thank you, God, for getting me in a book.
How do we get our name written in the book of life? (Revelation 20:15, Luke 10:20)

Revelation 20:15: And anyone not found written in the Book of Life was cast into the lake of fire. Luke 10:20: Nevertheless do not rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rather rejoice because your names are written in heaven.”
What is the judgment of the sheep and the goats about? (Matthew 25:31-46)

He says that when the Son of Man comes, the nations are separated like sheep and goats, and those on the left are sent to everlasting fire for not feeding, clothing, visiting or taking in “the least of my brethren, the church, the Christian, the believer.” He says “how I treat the people of God is going to determine my destiny at the judgment.”
What is the judgment of the sheep and the goats about? (Matthew 25:31-46)

All not found, written in the book of life, was cast into the lake of fire.” Now look at this one. And I want you adults attention here. When the Son of Man comes in his glory and all his holy angels with him, he will sit on the throne of his glory. All nations are going to be gathered together before him and he will separate them as a shepherd divides his sheep from the goats. And he’ll say to them on the left hand, okay, some went to the right, some went to the left. Those on the left. He says, “Depart from me, you cursed and to everlasting fire prepared for the Devil and his angels.” And then they say, “Well, Lord, when did we, you know, what do we do that we deserve this?” And he says, “Well, I was hungry and you didn’t feed me. I was naked and you didn’t clothe me. I was in prison and you didn’t visit me. I was sick and you could care the least. I was a stranger and you wouldn’t take me in to your house and fellowship with me. He says, “Well, when did we see you?” He said, “When you didn’t do it to the least of my brethren, the church, the Christian, the believer. You didn’t do it to me. See, how I treat the people of God is going to determine my destiny at the judgment. Now, a lot of you think that this is only a natural illustration.
What is the judgment of the sheep and the goats about? (Matthew 25:31-46)

Matthew 25:31-46: “When the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the holy angels with Him, then He will sit on the throne of His glory. All the nations will be gathered before Him, and He will separate them one from another, as a shepherd divides his sheep from the goats. And He will set the sheep on His right hand, but the goats on the left. Then the King will say to those on His right hand, ‘Come, you blessed of My Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world: for I was hungry and you gave Me food; I was thirsty and you gave Me drink; I was a stranger and you took Me in; I was naked and you clothed Me; I was sick and you visited Me; I was in prison and you came to Me.’ “Then the righteous will answer Him, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You, or thirsty and give You drink? When did we see You a stranger and take You in, or naked and clothe You? Or when did we see You sick, or in prison, and come to You?’ And the King will answer and say to them, ‘Assuredly, I say to you, inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these My brethren, you did it to Me.’ “Then He will also say to those on the left hand, ‘Depart from Me, you cursed, into the everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels: for I was hungry and you gave Me no food; I was thirsty and you gave Me no drink; I was a stranger and you did not take Me in, naked and you did not clothe Me, sick and in prison and you did not visit Me.’ “Then they also will answer Him, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see You hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not minister to You?’ Then He will answer them, saying, ‘Assuredly, I say to you, inasmuch as you did not do it to one of the least of these, you did not do it to Me.’ And these will go away into everlasting punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”
What does he say “hungry,” “naked” and “in prison” mean in that judgment?

He says Jesus’ earthly illustration points to heavenly things, and that feeding the poor is good but “that is not the meat of this message.” He says the naked are those without the white linen of righteousness, the prisoners are those in bondage to drugs and witchcraft, and the hungry are people hungry for righteousness and truth who come to church and find “we have nothing to offer them. We just got religion.” He says we must feed them with the word.
What does he say “hungry,” “naked” and “in prison” mean in that judgment?

Well, I got to go out and I got to feed the poor and you know, I got to give my shirt to the ones that doesn’t have one and anybody in prison, I got to go visit them. You got to remember Jesus said, “If I speak to you heavenly things, you won’t understand them. So I speak to you of earthly things about heavenly things so you can what? Understand them.” Now, let’s get to the spiritual side of this. And don’t get me wrong, we’re still don’t visit the sick and all that, but that is not the meat of this message. Because you can be feeding the poor like Bill Gates does and Oprah. You can help orphans. You can do all this stuff and not know God and be teaching. Gates is a atheist. 1 Corinthians 16:22: If anyone does not love the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be accursed. O Lord, come! John 14:15: “If you love Me, keep My commandments.
Why did Jesus come the first time, and what is the condemnation? (John 3:17-20)

He says Jesus’ first coming “was not to condemn the world” but to warn that a judgment is coming and to forgive and cleanse sin. He says those who do not believe are already condemned because light has come into the world and men loved darkness, because their deeds were evil.
Why did Jesus come the first time, and what is the condemnation? (John 3:17-20)

Okay. Jesus’s first coming, as we know, was not to condemn the world. In John 3:17, but that the world through him might be saved. His first coming was not to judge the world. He come to warn the world there’s a judgment coming and, “My blood will forgive you your sins, clean you your sins, and you can correct all your wrongs. Your slate can be clean and you can be reconciled back to God.” That was his message. “He that believes on him is not condemned. He that believes not is condemned already, because he hasn’t believed on the name of the only begotten Son of God. And this is the condemnation: that light has come into the world, and men loved what? Darkness rather than light, because their deeds were what? Evil. For everyone that does evil hates the light.” Who’s the light? Jesus and his word. “Neither comes to the light.” Who’s the light? Jesus and his word. “Lest his deeds should what? Be exposed.”
Why did Jesus come the first time, and what is the condemnation? (John 3:17-20)

John 3:17-20: For God did not send His Son into the world to condemn the world, but that the world through Him might be saved. “He who believes in Him is not condemned; but he who does not believe is condemned already, because he has not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God. And this is the condemnation, that the light has come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. For everyone practicing evil hates the light and does not come to the light, lest his deeds should be exposed.
Why do people reject the message, and when will the word judge us? (John 12:48, Acts 17:31)

He says people who reject the message blame the preacher or the church, but the truth is “they want to sin and they don’t want anybody telling them they can’t.” He says the same word will judge us in the last day, that God has “an appointed day,” and that no one should rely on predicted dates.
Why do people reject the message, and when will the word judge us? (John 12:48, Acts 17:31)

You know, people that reject the message, they blame the preacher, they blame the church, they put the blame on everything. And the truth is, they want to sin and they don’t want anybody telling them they can’t. So they reject Christ because what? Christ is going to convict them of their sin so he can save them. And that’s why he came the first time. He didn’t come to back up that Old Testament law. But the second coming, John 12:48: “The word that I’ve have spoken to you, the same shall judge you” what? “In the last day.” Acts 17:31: he was a there was “He has appointed a day on which he will” what? Judge the world. It’s not an in-minute thing. There is an appointed day. This is going to happen. And when that day comes, it’s going to happen. And you can put out teaser dates and you can predict dates all you want, but the thing of it is, God has a design, a plan, and he has a day when he’s coming, and he’s going to judge the world. And you die before that, you’re still accountable. That’s your judgment day. And you’re going to be resurrected to this one.
Why do people reject the message, and when will the word judge us? (John 12:48, Acts 17:31)

John 12:48: He who rejects Me, and does not receive My words, has that which judges him—the word that I have spoken will judge him in the last day. Acts 17:31: because He has appointed a day on which He will judge the world in righteousness by the Man whom He has ordained. He has given assurance of this to all by raising Him from the dead.”
Will believers appear before Christ, and is God partial? (2 Corinthians 5:10)

He says “we will all appear before the judgment seat of Christ,” and that being a believer does not exempt you because Judas also believed, preached and cast out demons. He says many Christians think God would be partial to those who believe, and says that is “a lie.”
Will believers appear before Christ, and is God partial? (2 Corinthians 5:10)

Second Corinthians 5:10: “We will all appear before the judgment seat of Christ.” How many of us? “But I’m a believer of Christ.” So what what? Judas was a believer of Christ too, you know. Have I got you thinking? Yeah, he believed in Christ. Is he in the lake of fire? Yes, he’s in the lake of fire. We don’t know our Bible. Did Judas preach the gospel? Yes. Did he cast out demons? Yes. Did he heal the sick? I mean, God healed the sick through him. Yeah. Are you there, church? You see, this thing is the power. This is the message of the gospel of Christ. This judgment is strong and it’s powerful and it moves us forward. We’re going to all appear. And and see, a lot of Christians don’t think they’re going to appear before Christ. They think God is partial because we believe in him. “Believed in you, Lord. I’m committing sexual immorality and doing everything this guy over here did, but he didn’t believe in you.” And and and so God says, “Well, he didn’t believe in me, I’m going to I’m going to mess him up. But you, you believe, all right.” Is God partial, folks? We’re lying to the people, and the people love to believe a lie.
Will believers appear before Christ, and is God partial? (2 Corinthians 5:10)
2 Corinthians 5:10: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive the things done in the body, according to what he has done, whether good or bad.
What does it mean to be judged by works? (Revelation 20:13, 2 Corinthians 5:10)

He says they were judged each one according to their works, and that believing in Christ does not help a family if you abuse them, and does not help a sinner if you tell them they don’t have to turn. He says living for Christ helps our neighbors and families, and that grace and faith are not all there is to it.
What does it mean to be judged by works? (Revelation 20:13, 2 Corinthians 5:10)

“Anyway, that he may receive the things done when in this body according to what he has done, whether it be good or bad.” All right. “The sea gave up the dead who were in it. Death and Hades delivered up the dead who were in them. They were judged each one according to his” what? What’s the word? Works. See, it doesn’t do my wife and children any good I believe in Christ, and then I’m going out on my wife and I’m beating my kids to death because they do things that irritate me. And that doesn’t help them any. And I believe in Christ, and I tell the sinner, “You know, you just believe in Christ, you don’t have to turn from that.” Doesn’t help that sinner any or his home any. You see, us living for Christ is what helps our neighbor. That’s what helps our family. And now that’s a good place for a good amen. You may not agree with me, but that’s the key. And they got us thinking that this grace and faith is all there is to it. No, you can be a tremendous blessing in your home by following the word of God, and you can go to heaven.
What does it mean to be judged by works? (Revelation 20:13, 2 Corinthians 5:10)
Revelation 20:13: The sea gave up the dead who were in it, and Death and Hades delivered up the dead who were in them. And they were judged, each one according to his works.
Does Jesus come only once, and what is the new heaven and new earth? (Matthew 16:27, Revelation 21:1)

He says the Bible nowhere says Jesus comes “once, twice, and the third time”; He comes one time, judges the world, resurrects the people, and then comes eternity. He says everything now will be “renovated by fire” and replaced by “a much better” heaven and earth, not surfing or fishing.
Does Jesus come only once, and what is the new heaven and new earth? (Matthew 16:27, Revelation 21:1)

Matthew 16:20: “For the Son of Man shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and then he will reward every man according to his” what? Works. See, nowhere in the Bible does he say he’s coming once, twice, and the third time. It says he’s coming one time, and he’s going to judge the world, and he’s going to resurrect the people, and they’re going to stand before God, and then eternity. Revelations 21:1: “I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth [unclear] passed away. Also there was no more sea.” I love these young Christians when they say, “Boy, I can’t wait to catch that wave in heaven,” you know, surfing, or “Boy, just imagine the fishing in heaven.” and And I look at, I, you’re not getting this. Everything that you see here is going to be renovated by fire. It’s going to be burned up: buildings, everything’s gone, water gone, moon, stars, sun, everything’s gone, and a much better comes to replace it.
Does Jesus come only once, and what is the new heaven and new earth? (Matthew 16:27, Revelation 21:1)

Matthew 16:27: For the Son of Man will come in the glory of His Father with His angels, and then He will reward each according to his works. Revelation 21:1: Now I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away. Also there was no more sea.
What will eternity be like? (Revelation 21:4-5, 2 Peter 3)

He says God “will wipe every tear from their eyes,” there will be no more death, sorrow, crying or pain, because the former things have passed away, and God says “I make what? All things new.” He says the heavens will pass away with a great noise and a fervent heat, and that the new earth is “much better than what we know.”
What will eternity be like? (Revelation 21:4-5, 2 Peter 3)

Hallelujah. So get rid of those fairy tales. God has something much better than what we know. Now, “God will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death,” why? Cuz death is is conquered. Now, “no sorrow, no crying. There will be no more pain, for the former things have” what? Passed away. And remember, “with a fervent heat the heavens passed away with a great noise, the earth was burned up and everything in it.” And they want us down here on earth. Ain’t nothing to be down here for until he recreates the new earth. Hallelujah. I’m just throwing out some things to help you get through this nonsense out there. Then “he who sat on the throne said, ‘Behold, I make what? All things new.’” Wow. Fresh. Now I don’t know about you, but that sounds pretty good to me.
What will eternity be like? (Revelation 21:4-5, 2 Peter 3)

Revelation 21:4: And God will wipe away every tear from their eyes; there shall be no more death, nor sorrow, nor crying. There shall be no more pain, for the former things have passed away.” 2 Peter 3:10: But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night, in which the heavens will pass away with a great noise, and the elements will melt with fervent heat; both the earth and the works that are in it will be burned up. Revelation 21:5: Then He who sat on the throne said, “Behold, I make all things new.” And He said to me, “Write, for these words are true and faithful.”
Will everyone get the same reward in heaven?

He says there “are levels,” so what you do now depends on your reward; you will get eternal life, but people who do not pursue or grow in God will not get the same reward as those who do. He says the idea that everyone is treated equal is “the Disneyland gospel,” and that there are things to be rewarded up there.
Will everyone get the same reward in heaven?

Is it worth living for Christ for 70 to 80 years on this earth to inherit an eternity like that? And we we already talked about Christ, you know, we get to love him and know him up there, and he’s the focus of everything, plus we get all the new heaven and a new earth to live in. There are levels, uh, so it’s important what you do now. Depends on your reward. These people think they all get the same reward. See, that’s just like these lazy people. They don’t want to work and they think they should be able to be fed and everything and drive cars just like the workers. And the Christians are like that, you know. We don’t pursue God, we don’t grow in God, yet we want the same reward that those who applied God, and it’s not there in the Bible. Now, you will get eternal life, don’t get me wrong, but remember there’s a new heaven and new earth, things are going on there’s a order up there, and I don’t know about you, but you want to be as high as you can when you get there. Amen. You say, “Man, that sounds weird.” Yeah, I know, because we love the fair tale, the Disneyland gospel. We don’t want any responsibility or accountability to do anything, and we want everything handed to us, and it’s not that way. You will be judged according to your works. You see, Blake gets a very good paycheck because he has a good marketing uh skill to market, and see, you guys, want some of you want the same paycheck without putting the effort in, and it ain’t going to happen. Picking on Blake today. And all of you believe this fantasy from TV and radio that, “Oh man, your faith and gra, everybody’s treated equal, everybody get.” No, you didn’t do beans for Christ, you’re barely going to get in, and thank God you got in. But there’s things to be rewarded up there, and you want those rewards. Is that a good amen? Hallelujah.
What is the message of the cross, and how should we respond? (Proverbs 20:11)

He says Jesus wants to keep us from “that lake of fire, that second death,” by choosing Him for forgiveness and starting to “start walking on the right road,” and going back to the cross when we fall. He says the message is “a total package”: forgiveness and cleansing plus a commitment to obey His word, with growth over time until we shine “by your good works, giving glory to God.”
What is the message of the cross, and how should we respond? (Proverbs 20:11)

Young people, stop what you’re doing. Here, I love young people. They look at each other to see if this is cool or not. Young people, the Bible says, “Even a child is known by its ways, whether it is bad or whether it’s good.” And so we’ve got to choose to live the right way, and this is what the message is all about. Jesus wants to keep you from that lake of fire, that second death, and so he’s coming to tell you. You’re not looking at me. That’s it, sweetie, that beautiful face. I’d love to see those eyes. Do you understand when you do that you distract those around you? Yeah, they look to see what you’re doing. Adults do that. And see, a serious thing, our eternal life is on the line here, and we got to get enough respect to listen and soak it in and make a decision. And this is what I’m getting to. Jesus is telling us to choose him for forgiveness for wrong and to start walking on the right road and start living for him. And if you fall, you go back to him, back to that cross, asked him to forgive and get back up on that road and keep walking. And you can reject it today. You can want to please your friends around you. You want to be the cool crowd. You can believe the lie. Adults can believe the lie that’s preached on radio and TV. I told you over the weekend that if Jesus Christ preached the message that preachers are preaching today, he would never have been crucified, because they are not warning you to turn from evil and do right and serve the living God. That’s why they killed him. They didn’t want to change, and religious people didn’t want to change. And so young people and adults this morning, this is the message of the cross. Are you going to choose not only the forgiveness of Christ and the cleansing of sin that he offers, but a commitment to obey his word and live for him? It’s a total package. And let him slowly, you know, doesn’t have to be too slow now, but a lot of this doesn’t happen overnight. So when I’m telling you, some of you drag your feet way too long, but let him building. You keep getting back up. Keep letting him deal with it until that thing is gone. You just keep working on these things to finally you shine like a light in this world by your good works, giving glory to God.
What is the message of the cross, and how should we respond? (Proverbs 20:11)
Proverbs 20:11: Even a child is known by his deeds, Whether what he does is pure and right.
Who does he say goes to the lake of fire?

He says cowards who do not stand up for Jesus, the unbelieving, the sexually immoral, sorcerers, idolaters and liars, if they do it “flagrantly and consistently,” will have their part in the lake that burns with fire and brimstone, which is the second death.
What does he mean by “the cowardly” in Revelation 21:8?

He says it does not mean being afraid to drive on the freeway; it means not having “the courage of your faith” to stand up for what’s right and instead giving into the crowd, especially for teenagers who are peer pressured.
How does he say we grow spiritually?
He says “get with people that are up there above you,” because “we get influenced by who we’re around and the quality of life that they have.”
What does he say about work and laziness?

He says “no working, no eating” was the first law, and quotes the Proverb that a man’s stomach will drive him to work. He says letting people be lazy and still feeding them, or letting children stay at home to age 40, does not build self-esteem.
What does he say about eating blood?

He says the command not to eat meat with the life blood was a “shadow law” of the blood of Christ, with no punishment attached. He says you can actually eat blood “if you don’t overdo it,” and it is used in many nations, like other parts of the animal.
What does he say about marriage?

He says marriage is “a public declaration” before God and people that you will be faithful, love that person, treat them right and raise your kids right. He says many people are “just shacking up,” but “Christians get married.”
Whose fault does he say it is when evil happens?

He says it is not God’s fault but ours, because God gave human beings the responsibility to “take care of the criminal” and judge. He says he gets tired of people blaming God and “his perfect word when it is our fault.”
What does he say about immigrants and the law?

He says “we’re to allow immigrants into our nation, but they should come in the legal way,” because it is not fair to those who came legally. He says government leaders who do not back up the law are “wimps.”
Who does he say is supposed to punish criminals?

He says civil leaders, not the church, are supposed to deal with criminals and carry out punishment by death, and says “they’re not doing it.” He says the church’s greatest punishment is excommunication.
Why did Jesus not judge the world at His first coming?
He says Jesus came to warn that a judgment is coming and to offer forgiveness and a clean slate through His blood, and that those who do not believe “condemned already.”
What does he say about Judas?

He says Judas “believed in Christ,” preached, cast out demons and healed the sick through God’s power, yet “he’s in the lake of fire,” to show that believing alone does not exempt anyone from judgment.
What does he say about grace and faith being all there is to it?
He says “they got us thinking that this grace and faith is all there is to it,” and that following the word of God is what makes you a blessing to your home and takes you to heaven.
What does he say about surfing and fishing in heaven?
He says everything here “is going to be renovated by fire” and replaced by something “much better than what we know,” so people should get rid of those “fairy tales.”
Why does he say living for Christ is worth it?
He asks if it is “worth living for Christ for 70 to 80 years on this earth to inherit an eternity like that,” where we get to love and know Him and have a new heaven and new earth.
What does he say about preachers today?
He says if Jesus preached the message that preachers are preaching today “he would never have been crucified,” because they do not warn people to turn from evil.
