p: In this fourth session on present truth, Pastor David G. Kincer reviews eleven present truths about the last days and then examines the falling away. He describes how the medieval church fell away from the simplicity of Christ, the good news and godly living, and asks hearers to see how many of the same things are happening in Catholic and Protestant churches in America and Europe today, saying the remnant who keep God’s commandments are the hope.
What are the first present truths about the last days?

He recaps that we are in the last days, which started in 33 AD and run until the day of the Lord: the days of salvation and the outpouring of God’s Spirit in Acts 2:16, more than one outpouring, and all who call on the Lord shall be saved. Present truth number two is that Jesus the Messiah, God, has come in the flesh.
What are the first present truths about the last days?

Thank you for joining us in our fourth session of present truths out of second Peter 1:12. We are to be established in present truth. Ecclesiastes, you remember, says God has a purpose under heaven and he does it in certain seasons and certain times. And 1 Chronicles 12 tells us that the children of Issachar had understanding of the times to know what Israel ought to do. Today we’re going to be looking at the falling away. First of all of review so that this gets in your cranial structure. The first present truth that we talked about were is that we’re in the last days which started in 33 AD till the day of the Lord when he comes. That’s also the days of salvation and the days of the pouring out of God’s spirit in Acts 2:16. This is that which is spoken by the prophet Joel. Then in the last days I will pour out my spirit. Last days plural. There’ll be signs in heaven and in earth before the day singular one season of the Lord. I will pour out my spirit in those days. What days? The last day. So there’s more than one pouring out. And all who call on the Lord shall be saved. So the first present truth is we’re living in the last days. We don’t know how long they are. And these days are the days of salvation and the outpouring of the Holy Spirit. Present truth number two that we have taught Jesus the Messiah, the Christ, the prophet, the king and God has come in the flesh. 1 AD we’ll call it.
What are the first present truths about the last days?

2 Peter 1:12: For this reason I will not be negligent to remind you always of these things, though you know and are established in the present truth. 1 Chronicles 12:32: of the sons of Issachar who had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do, their chiefs were two hundred; and all their brethren were at their command; Acts 2:16-21: But this is what was spoken by the prophet Joel: ‘And it shall come to pass in the last days, says God, That I will pour out of My Spirit on all flesh; Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, Your young men shall see visions, Your old men shall dream dreams. And on My menservants and on My maidservants I will pour out My Spirit in those days; And they shall prophesy. I will show wonders in heaven above And signs in the earth beneath: Blood and fire and vapor of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness, And the moon into blood, Before the coming of the great and awesome day of the LORD. And it shall come to pass That whoever calls on the name of the LORD Shall be saved.’
Who are the false prophets and antichrists, and why are believers persecuted?

He says there are many false prophets and antichrists until Jesus returns, and false prophets are known mainly by saying sin is okay. He says Jesus’ followers are hated and persecuted till the end for three biblical reasons: preaching the kingdom of God and repentance, living godly, and simply believing in Jesus.
Who are the false prophets and antichrists, and why are believers persecuted?

We’re living in that season. Present truth number three. There are many false prophets and antichrist from 1 AD till Jesus returns. And we know that today some of our antichrists are Jews who don’t accept Christ coming in the flesh. Muslims who distort he didn’t die on the cross. Atheists, religionists, liberals, humanist, and communists are a few of the antichrists in the world today that we live in. False prophets, we know them mainly by them saying sin is okay. It’s okay that you sin for any reason, faith, grace, whatever. Present truth number four. Jesus followers are hated and persecuted till the end. Okay, they were persecuted back there when Christ was here after Christ and the apostles. They’ve been persecuted all through and they’ll be persecuted till Jesus returns. The three biblical reasons for persecution is for preaching the kingdom of God and repentance. The second one is living godly. So you threaten their lifestyle. And the third one is simply believing in Jesus. If you are persecuted for doing wrong, the Bible says there’s no profit in it. There’s no reward in it. But the Bible acceptance of persecution is one of these three things. Okay? And mainly if you go out talking about repentance, people aren’t going to like it.
Has the falling away happened, and is it happening again?

From Second Thessalonians 2:2-3 he says do not be shaken by claims that the day of Christ is at hand, because a falling away comes first. He says he will show that it has happened and give clues so you can decide whether it is happening again, and that false prophets troubling people with dates make a fortune off the church.
Has the falling away happened, and is it happening again?

Present truth number five, a season of falling away. We’re going to show you today that it has happened. We’re going to give you clues so you can decide, will it happen again or is it happening? Be not soon shaken. First 2 Thessalonians 2:2 in mind or troubled either by spirit or word nor by letter from us that the day of Christ is at hand. Let no man deceive you for there shall come a falling away first. Okay. And what are the people doing? Of prophets. They’re destroy they’re troubling us with this Jesus is coming in a minute and predicting days and all the rest.
Has the falling away happened, and is it happening again?

2 Thessalonians 2:2-3: not to be soon shaken in mind or troubled, either by spirit or by word or by letter, as if from us, as though the day of Christ had come. Let no one deceive you by any means; for that Day will not come unless the falling away comes first, and the man of sin is revealed, the son of perdition,

He says present truth number six is that times of refreshing and the restoration of all things must come, and Jesus is retained in the heavens until then. He says the reason he did not come yesterday or today is that all things have not been restored: “just simple logic.”

And God’s people fall for it. And these false prophets make a fortune off of people in the church thinking that they have some kind of Revelation that God says we don’t have. Present truth number six. Times of refreshing and the restoration of all things must come. Jesus retained into the heavens until the restoration of all things in the times of refreshing. We’re going to show you in our next session how that has happened and possibly more will happen. And we got to remember when all things are restored, Jesus won’t be retained in the heavens anymore. He will come. So the reason he didn’t come any minute and he didn’t come today and he didn’t come yesterday is all things haven’t been restored.

Acts 3:19-21: Repent therefore and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, so that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord, and that He may send Jesus Christ, who was preached to you before, whom heaven must receive until the times of restoration of all things, which God has spoken by the mouth of all His holy prophets since the world began.
Is knowledge increasing as Daniel said?

He says when you are down, get back up, because God will refresh and restore you. Present truth number seven is that knowledge will increase, beginning with the printing press in 1440, and Daniel was told the words are sealed until the time of the end, when the wise will understand.
Is knowledge increasing as Daniel said?

Just simple logic. Simple logic. Okay. So we are in the seasons of refreshing and restoration. Don’t you ever forget it. When you’re down, get back up. God will refresh you and he will restore you. Present truth number seven. Knowledge will increase. Daniel said in the time of the end. Uh knowledge has we’re going to show you and is still increasing beginning with the printing press in 1440. And he also tells us that the end time is shut up till the time of the end. See, Daniel said, I heard, but I understood not. And I asked, which shall be the end of these things?
Is knowledge increasing as Daniel said?

Daniel 12:4: “But you, Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book until the time of the end; many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall increase.” Daniel 12:8-10: Although I heard, I did not understand. Then I said, “My lord, what shall be the end of these things?” And he said, “Go your way, Daniel, for the words are closed up and sealed till the time of the end. Many shall be purified, made white, and refined, but the wicked shall do wickedly; and none of the wicked shall understand, but the wise shall understand.
Does anyone know the times and seasons of the end?

He says present truth number eight is that Israel became a nation again in 1948, and number nine is that no one knows the times and seasons: Jesus said it is not for you to know, and in Mark 13:32 “no one knows the day or the hour.” So when people trouble you about the second coming, wars and tsunamis, do not be troubled.
Does anyone know the times and seasons of the end?

And the man said, the words are closed up and sealed to the time of the end. Many shall be purified, made white, that’s that salvation season, and tested. But the wicked will do wickedly, and none of the wicked will understand, but the wise will understand. The children of Issachar had understanding of the time. Present truth number eight. Israel became a nation again in 1948 after 2600 years of not being a nation. Present truth number nine. No one knows the times and the seasons. Is a present truth. We showed you that in Daniel. We shown it here in Acts. Will you at this time restore the restore the kingdom to Israel? Jesus said, “It’s not for you to know the times of the seasons which the father has put in his own authority.” Mark 13:32, “No one knows the day or the hour.” So when these people are troubling you with the second coming of the Lord and all these things and wars and and uh tsunamis and whatever, don’t be troubled.
Does anyone know the times and seasons of the end?

Acts 1:6-7: Therefore, when they had come together, they asked Him, saying, “Lord, will You at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?” And He said to them, “It is not for you to know times or seasons which the Father has put in His own authority. Mark 13:32: “But of that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.
Has the gospel been preached to all nations as a witness?

He says present truth number ten is that the gospel as a witness to all nations has not been fulfilled, because if it had, Jesus would have come. He says all nations were not known until the 1500s, so those predicting the second coming before then did not understand God’s seasons.
Has the gospel been preached to all nations as a witness?

No one knows. We will know when it’s activated. When God activates it, we’ll start getting it. Present truth number 10, the gospel as a witness. Can’t leave that statement out. items.d: In this session on present truths Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the gospel of the kingdom and of repentance and remission of sins will be preached to all nations as a witness, confirmed by signs and…
p: In this session on present truths Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the gospel of the kingdom and of repentance and remission of sins will be preached to all nations as a witness, confirmed by signs and wonders. He walks through the signs that follow believers, the signs of an apostle and the results in Acts, and says a last-days visitation greater than the early church is coming, with the ministries of apostle and prophet restored.
What message will usher in the end time? (Matthew 24:14; Luke 24:47)

He says the gospel of the kingdom shall be preached to all nations “as a witness,” and Jesus said repentance and remission of sins should be preached in His name to all nations. He says that message, not prosperity, the second coming, positive thinking, personal prophecy or poverty, is what will usher in the end time.
What message will usher in the end time? (Matthew 24:14; Luke 24:47)

What does he say about the title “pastor”?
He says “putting a title on you as a pastor, that means nothing. Pastor is a job description.”
Does he say believers need a human priest?
He says “we’re all priests that can go in before God… We can go in Christ ourselves, we can hear from Him, and we can come out and we can be a blessing to others.”
Why does he say believers must speak?

He says “if you’re silent when you go out these doors, you’re not helping anybody,” and “Jesus was on earth for 30 years and never did anything, had no effect on the world, none, until He started speaking.”
Does he say America is special to God?
He says “America is no special child of God,” and “God loves the whole world.”
How does he say Assyria fell?
He says “Assyria shall fall by the sword, not of man,” and “185,000 died in one night of the Assyrian army. 185,000 by the sword of the angel.”
Do we have to wait for the rapture to reign?
He says “we shall reign in life. We don’t have to wait for the rapture. We don’t have to wait to go to heaven. We don’t have to wait to die.”

p: In this message a guest speaker at Vine Cluster Church continues his study of Esther in chapters 8–10 as a parable of the new covenant. He teaches that the new covenant has authority over the old, that the ceremonial “shadow laws” point to Jesus while the moral law stays, and that Jesus gives his church power. He closes with the judgment on Jerusalem in AD 70 and a call to stand like Mordecai today.
Why does God hide things from “the wise and learned” and reveal them to little children? (Matthew 11:25)

He says smart people can have “spiritual understanding” that “is not that great” because “God Jesus Christ has to reveal it to you,” and “it’s not something that you get because you’re smart.” He says you get it by submitting, reading, praying, and being like a child who is “seeking after the father… following the instructions… listening responding.”
Why does God hide things from “the wise and learned” and reveal them to little children? (Matthew 11:25)

With Esther starting in 8th through chapter 10. Their spiritual understanding is not that great because God Jesus Christ has to reveal it to you it’s not something that you get because you’re smart. It’s something you get because you submit because you allow God to speak to you you go to his word you read it you pray you follow his process. You know just like a Harvard graduate he went through schooling he did all the work he did all those projects he you know worked his butt off to get through college and we have to apply that same kind of effort in the word and allow Jesus to open up our understanding and it says he revealed them unto little children and we know because we’ve been taught that there are stages in our growth when you are born as a Christian you are a new believer you are a baby you start as a baby and then you grow into the child stage and the adolescent stage this is a teenager and then the young adult and the maturity stage. See a child. Is seeking after the father a child is following the instructions a child is. Listening responding and that’s what we need to be. p: In this message a guest speaker at Vine Cluster Church reads Esther 3–7 as a parable of the new covenant. He says Haman pictures the proud scribes and Pharisees and Mordecai pictures Jesus, who would not bow to them. He then follows Esther going before the king, her two banquets, and Haman’s end, and closes by urging believers to surrender old ways.
What is the parable of Haman and Mordecai in Esther 3, and was Mordecai the king’s employee?

He says parables are “a short allegorical story designed to illustrate or teach truth,” and that the Old Testament stories “not just historical events they are examples and illustrations.” He says he had assumed Mordecai worked for the king, but “mordecai wasn’t necessarily employed by the king,” while Haman was “promoted above all the princes.”

John 8:39: They answered and said to Him, “Abraham is our father.” Jesus said to them, “If you were Abraham’s children, you would do the works of Abraham. John 8:44: You are of your father the devil, and the desires of your father you want to do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and does not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks from his own resources, for he is a liar and the father of it.
What should Christians learn from the scribes and Pharisees, and what happened to Haman?

He says “we do not want to be like these people” and that Jesus said “listen to what they say but do not do what they do,” so Christians should be people others “can follow.” He says Haman was hanged on the gallows he built for Mordecai, and when Jesus died “the old covenant the old way stopped.”
What should Christians learn from the scribes and Pharisees, and what happened to Haman?

But some of them turned it is true. And you see just like these scribes and Pharisees they didn’t realize that they were killing the son of God. Even all of their lives these scribes and Pharisees they still believe that the messiah hasn’t come yet. They still believe that. You know Jesus Christ is not the son of God. And they think that they’re helping God they think that they’re helping the father. And we don’t want to be that way church amen we don’t want to go around thinking that I’m a Christian when you’re doing exactly the opposite of what Jesus would do now here you have these people that were bribing they were sinning they were. They were doing all these bad things you know they just circumvented the law they just said forget the moral law I’m just going to do what I want so that I can get rid of this man Jesus. They wanted to punch him they wanted to kill him you know Jesus knew her their thoughts. We’ve got to remember that we do not want to be like these people we don’t want to get into a state in our christianity where we become like the scribes and the Pharisees we become and he says it very plainly hypocrites. And Jesus said about the scribes and Pharisees he says listen to what they say but do not do what they do. And you see we do not want to be Christians. That where people cannot follow our example. You see when Christina is part of the youth group and she does something. You know on her mind I know honor her mind because it’s on my mind she thinks to herself how is this going to influence the youth group. You know should I be doing this and and it shouldn’t just be her we’ve all got to be take that responsibility as the church how are my actions influencing. The people around me. You know if if a child in the church saw me doing this would would that be a good example. Amen. You know I want Jesus to say about me that you can follow what he’s saying and you can follow what he does for the most part. Amen. Or you’re getting there you know you can follow his heart that would be a nice statement for God to say about you right you can follow he’s got a good heart well thanks God. I’m glad I got a good heart. In that Esther 7:10 it says they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. And then the king’s wrath was pacified you see here Haman. Was hanged. Haman as you learn in this story is an example of the scribes and Pharisees now in actuality. When Jesus came who died who died. Tell me Jesus Christ died. But in this story in the story of Esther here Haman died. So we got to understand what’s what’s the deal here you you see when Jesus died. The old covenant the old way stopped. The burnt offerings stopped. The ceremonies stopped. Amen. The old covenant the old way stopped. See when Jesus died on the cross the veil was rent in two that the the all those laws about the son of Aaron and all only certain people could go into the temple that all stopped. When Jesus died everyone now can come in everyone now has an opportunity everyone now that has a desire to please the king can come in. You see when Jesus died on the cross all of their pomp all of their pride all of their position that they have thought they had stopped. And you see. They had to come. To God. The new covenant way they had to get a desire for God they had to get a desire for Jesus Christ they had to come to him Jesus said I am the way I am the truth I am the life they had to surrender. Their old way. And come to Jesus Christ come to the cross. Give forgiveness from sin no longer going to the burnt offerings anymore that’s all ended. They had to come to Jesus Christ.
What should Christians learn from the scribes and Pharisees, and what happened to Haman?

Matthew 23:3: Therefore whatever they tell you to observe, that observe and do, but do not do according to their works; for they say, and do not do. Esther 7:10: So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then the king’s wrath subsided.
What old ways must we surrender, and what does it mean that we are the temple of the Holy Spirit?

He says the point is “not necessarily the old covenant that we’re following,” and that “old opinions old philosophies” must be surrendered “the new way… through Christ.” He says the scribes and Pharisees loved the temple building, but Jesus “always wanted to dwell in our hearts.”
What old ways must we surrender, and what does it mean that we are the temple of the Holy Spirit?

And there a lot of there were a lot of religious people there are a lot of scribes and Pharisees that never turn. That never turned to the new way. They never accepted Jesus Christ they never they all they they rejected him. And this morning we do not want to be a people that rejects. Jesus Christ and you see it’s not necessarily the old covenant that we’re following it’s our old our old ways our old life the Bible says that we’re a new creature old things have passed away amen. In our lives there could be old things that are keeping us down old opinions old philosophies that we used to follow you’ve got to surrender it. And we’ve got to come the new way we’ve got to come his way we’ve got to come through Christ. And lastly. There was so much there was so much love and there was so much uh. Desire for for the temple the actual building. They love that temple so much they they love to look at it and go into it and everybody see them go into the temple. I’m awesome. And they love the temple they love doing all the ceremonies and going in and all that and Jesus Christ he reminds us and he says that we. Are the temple of the Holy Spirit see Jesus Christ never wanted to dwell with temples made with hands he always wanted to dwell in our hearts. You.
What old ways must we surrender, and what does it mean that we are the temple of the Holy Spirit?

2 Corinthians 5:17: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new. John 14:6: Jesus said to him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me. 1 Corinthians 6:19: Or do you not know that your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God, and you are not your own?
Does he say Mordecai worked for the king?
No. He says “mordecai wasn’t necessarily employed by the king,” and that although he had always pictured him as a servant of the king, he went looking for where it says so and “it’s not there.”
What does he say about Haman’s pride?
He says Haman “loved the attention and the praise,” everyone was to bow, and he was so upset when Mordecai did not bow. He says Haman “was all about himself” and was “so prideful.”
What does he mean by the new covenant and “the new Israel”?
He says Esther was “the example of new the new Israel,” so “no longer is it only the nation of Israel it’s anyone who pleases the king,” and he thanks God “we’re part of the new covenant.”
What does he say happened when Jesus was twelve?

He says Jesus’ parents thought he was with them, went back to the temple and found him “asking questions” and talking with the priests. He says Jesus said “I’m supposed to be about my father’s business,” which was “to complete the new covenant.”
What law did Haman get the king to pass?

He says Haman “bribed the king” and was “willing to pay ten thousand talents of silver to get rid of all the Jews,” and that “the scribes wrote and sealed the law to destroy them.” He says “this is an actual historical event.”
What does he say about a Christian who feels like he is just following rules?

He says “you don’t want to get stuck in that mindset that God is just a bunch of rules,” and that it should be a desire “to please him” as when you first met your wife and ask “how can I make you happy.”
What does the golden scepter mean in his message?
He says it “meant that she was accepted,” and since “she’s the new covenant” and “the new church,” we can “go in to the inner court where the king is” and “speak to the king yourself.”
What does he say about Jesus and the Passover?
He says “Jesus Christ was killed on the 14th day of the first month the same day as the Passover,” and that “Jesus Christ is the Passover lamb.”
What does he say the scribes and Pharisees believed about the Messiah?
He says “they didn’t realize that they were killing the son of God” and that they “still believe that the messiah hasn’t come yet.” He then warns “we don’t want to be that way church.”
What does he say about being an example to others?
He says “we do not want to be Christians that where people cannot follow our example,” and asks “how are my actions influencing the people around me.”
What does he say stopped when Jesus died?
He says “the old covenant the old way stopped,” including “the burnt offerings” and “the ceremonies,” and that “everyone now can come in” and “has an opportunity.”
What does he say the scribes and Pharisees loved about the temple?

He says they loved “to look at it and go into it and everybody see them go into the temple,” while Jesus “never wanted to dwell with temples made with hands” and “always wanted to dwell in our hearts.”

items.d: In “The Lamb’s Wife Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Revelation 19–22 that the Lamb’s Wife, the New Jerusalem and the church are the same. He covers praise in heaven, the wife making herself ready…
p: In “The Lamb’s Wife Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Revelation 19–22 that the Lamb’s Wife, the New Jerusalem and the church are the same. He covers praise in heaven, the wife making herself ready, the bride in Paul’s letters, the four-square city, and why membership alone does not mean belonging to the church.
Can anyone predict when Jesus returns, and who is the “Lamb’s Wife”?

He says the pre-tribulation rapture theory “is not the most widely believed doctrine of the second coming” and that we should study “like the Bereans.” He says the Lamb’s Wife “is the New Jerusalem and is the church,” and that both date-setting and “teaser predictions” are “very destructive” because “nobody knows.”
Can anyone predict when Jesus returns, and who is the “Lamb’s Wife”?

And I also want to tell you that that pre-tribulation trap rapture theory that’s on radio and TV is not the most widely believed doctrine of the second coming. It’s just their own radio and TV. Are you hearing me? Most of the church world does not embrace that doctrine. Did you know that? Hallelujah, that’s true. That’s why we need to read and study like the Bereans. They studied the Scriptures to see if things were true, and we need to do that, amen. So this morning I want to give you another encouraging message out of Revelation. We’re going to be talking about this morning the Lamb’s Wife, which we’re going to find is the New Jerusalem and is the church. They’re all synonymous terms. Obviously the end of the world didn’t come yesterday. He has predicted it before, many people have predicted it, and this is the problem in the church world on the second coming. We either have people predicting it, when the Bible plainly says nobody knows, isn’t that right, and then we have teaser predictions. We got these [unclear] people, “Well, there’s wars and, you know, Jerusalem is surrounded by armies, so boy, it’s anytime.” It’s called teaser predictions. They won’t lock themselves into a day, but it’s like he can come right now, am I right? Both are very destructive. Hallelujah. How many you know Jesus came in the fullness of time the first time? That’s what the Bible says. He didn’t come at just any time, he came at the right time, he came at the time God had appointed for it to happen, and that’s exactly what’s going to happen at the end time. Now, this guy, by the way, I read, I looked up on him, he’s worth $78 million from followers who are given to donating to this nonsense, and he’s predicted wrong before. This is not his first wrong prediction. And a lot of these ministers are living in mansions and driving Rolls-Royces from God’s people so ignorant, so unknowledgeable to things, that they give money to this hyped-up doctrine that fails and it’s always failed. Jesus Christ has been predicted to come at least twenty to thirty times since I was a kid, and been hearing all this preaching, and every one of them’s missed. Nobody knows. Folks, how many believe the Bible and say yes, nobody knows? Hallelujah. And the reason he didn’t come at 10:00 is because something has to happen for him to come when he does come. Hallelujah.
Can anyone predict when Jesus returns, and who is the “Lamb’s Wife”?

Acts 17:11: These were more fair-minded than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness, and searched the Scriptures daily to find out whether these things were so. Galatians 4:4: But when the fullness of the time had come, God sent forth His Son, born of a woman, born under the law,
Why does Revelation show constant praise in heaven, and why should we start now? (Revelation 19:4-5)

He says “praise is going on in Revelation all the time,” so “you might as well start now,” and that “if nothing else,” we can praise because “your name’s written in the Book of Life.” He says the beast, false prophet and Satan are judged, and he mentions a Chinese church that has to worship secretly.
Why does Revelation show constant praise in heaven, and why should we start now? (Revelation 19:4-5)

Now let’s go to Revelation 19:4-5. “The twenty-four elders and the four beasts fell down and worshiped God, saying, Hallelujah! Amen!” “A voice out of the throne said, Praise our God, for all his servants.” How many of us see praise is going on in Revelation all the time? It’s going on in heaven, so you might as well start now. I’m serious. You need to start worshiping and praising him now, because it’s ordained that we praise and worship him now, and when we go to heaven it is going to continue. Amen. So get out of your [unclear], get out of your excuses, and do what the elders and the four and twenty beasts are doing up in heaven: worship and praise the Lord Jesus Christ. He says, “and all you that fear him, both small and great.” For the [unclear] has been judged. Here they’re praising him because the beast, the false prophet and Satan, and the [unclear] has been judged and defeated by the church and judged by Jesus Christ. And it’s like the guy that was healed at the gate, you know, he went walking and leaping and praising God because of what God has done. And if nothing else, the Bible says praise him and thank him because your name’s written in the Book of Life. If you’ve got nothing else, maybe you’re divorced, maybe your kids hate you and they’re off doing their own thing or whatever, listen, if your name’s written in the Book of Life and you’re going to heaven, that’s something to be excited and thankful about. Amen. And it’s going on in heaven, and that’s a great message of Revelation, is praise and worship. This is a Chinese church praising and worshiping God. They have to do it secretly. But praise and worship is going on in the earth.
Why does Revelation show constant praise in heaven, and why should we start now? (Revelation 19:4-5)

Revelation 19:4-5: And the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshiped God who sat on the throne, saying, “Amen! Alleluia!” Then a voice came from the throne, saying, “Praise our God, all you His servants and those who fear Him, both small and great!” Acts 3:8: So he, leaping up, stood and walked and entered the temple with them—walking, leaping, and praising God.
What does “his wife has made herself ready” mean? (Revelation 19:6-7)

He says heaven has “multitudes of people in it, not a few,” and that the wife “has made herself ready,” which means Christians “have to do something”: respond to God, seek the word. He says “Jesus isn’t coming back for a dumb church … an immature church.”
What does “his wife has made herself ready” mean? (Revelation 19:6-7)

Revelation 19:6: “I heard, as it were, the voice of a great multitude, and the voice of many waters, as the voice of a mighty thundering, saying, Alleluia! For the Lord God omnipotent” (all powerful) “reigns. Let us be rejoice and give honor to him.” First of all, we find that there are many. When I was a young minister, people were preaching that, you know, “Straight is the gate and narrow is the way that leads unto life, and few there be that find it.” But when I got over to Revelation, I found out there was a multitude that could not be numbered. I find here that there’s a multitude, many voices. What God’s sacrifice on the cross is so powerful, heaven has multitudes of people in it, not a few. Amen. Here they are giving honor to him “for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and the wife has made herself ready.” Not just Satan is defeated, not just the beast is defeated, not just the [unclear] is defeated, not that the church comes out of great tribulations with white [unclear], but here he says we are to praise him because not only does the time of judgment come and the time of defeat, but the time of the marriage of the Lamb. And his wife has what? Made herself ready. How many of you made yourself ready to come to church this morning? What about the rest of you? Did your husband do it, or your wife, or somebody else do it? Now, how many prepared yourself to come to church this morning? Yeah. Christians have to do something. You can’t just be sitting back, “Well, God, my phone number, you know where I live. If he wants me, if he wants to do something, just let him come.” Now, you’ve got to do something. You got to make yourself ready. You got to respond to God, you got to respond to the word, you got to seek God, you got to seek the word. Could I hear an amen on that? And it says here the wife has what? Made herself ready. Jesus isn’t coming back for a dumb church, he isn’t coming back for an immature church. He’s coming back for a church, through the power of the word and the power of the Spirit, has made themselves ready for that time at the end of the world. Hallelujah.
What does “his wife has made herself ready” mean? (Revelation 19:6-7)

Revelation 19:6-7: And I heard, as it were, the voice of a great multitude, as the sound of many waters and as the sound of mighty thunderings, saying, “Alleluia! For the Lord God Omnipotent reigns! Let us be glad and rejoice and give Him glory, for the marriage of the Lamb has come, and His wife has made herself ready.” Matthew 7:14: Because narrow is the gate and difficult is the way which leads to life, and there are few who find it. Revelation 7:9: After these things I looked, and behold, a great multitude which no one could number, of all nations, tribes, peoples, and tongues, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, with palm branches in their hands,
What does the parable of the wheat and tares say about the church’s maturity? (Matthew 13)

He says “wickedness is going to come to its full maturity, but righteousness is going to come to its full maturity,” and that “the church isn’t that mature right now.” He says the same blood that saved the worst sinner is “powerful enough for his people to grow up and be the mature bride.”
What does the parable of the wheat and tares say about the church’s maturity? (Matthew 13)

All right, look, some of you looking at me like, “I don’t know what I’m talking about.” The parable of the field: it was sown with wheat, right, and then some secret enemies came in and sowed tares among the wheat, and they went to the master, the Lord of the field, the Lord of the harvest. They said, “What are we going to do?” He said, “Let both grow together till the end of the age, the harvest.” See, wickedness is going to come to its full maturity, but righteousness is going to come to its full maturity. Are you there? And you know good and well the church isn’t that mature right now. So it’s obviously we’re not living right now and can expect him. There is some powerful things got to take place. Ah, hallelujah. At least think on it, give it some thought. “The marriage of the Lamb has come, his wife has made herself ready.” So the mystery of the church is made very clear here. Jesus said, “I will build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.” He come to build a church. He died for the church as well as for the sins of the world. Don’t ever forget that. And of his death for the sins of the world brought many into eternal life, so much more will his death bring many of those that came into eternal life into his church, his wife, a mature people, church. If the blood was powerful enough to save the worst sinner, Paul, then that same blood, the Bible says he gave himself for his church, that same blood is powerful enough for his people to grow up and be the mature bride that Christ said they would be. Now, that was a good statement. That’s good Scripture. Hallelujah.
What does the parable of the wheat and tares say about the church’s maturity? (Matthew 13)

Matthew 13:24-30: Another parable He put forth to them, saying: “The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field; but while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat and went his way. But when the grain had sprouted and produced a crop, then the tares also appeared. So the servants of the owner came and said to him, ‘Sir, did you not sow good seed in your field? How then does it have tares?’ He said to them, ‘An enemy has done this.’ The servants said to him, ‘Do you want us then to go and gather them up?’ But he said, ‘No, lest while you gather up the tares you also uproot the wheat with them. Let both grow together until the harvest, and at the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, “First gather together the tares and bind them in bundles to burn them, but gather the wheat into my barn.” ’ ” Matthew 16:18: And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it.
How does the New Testament describe the church as the bride of Christ? (Ephesians 5:25; 2 Corinthians 11:2; Romans 7:4)

He reads Ephesians 5:25-32, 2 Corinthians 11:2 (“Chaste virgin to Christ”) and Romans 7:4 to show the church is the bride, and that “it’s that intimate relationship now that causes us to bear fruit.” He says the word is going to do a work in the church “in these last days.”
How does the New Testament describe the church as the bride of Christ? (Ephesians 5:25; 2 Corinthians 11:2; Romans 7:4)

Ephesians 5:25: “Husbands, love your wife as Christ loved the church and gave himself for it.” He likens the church into the marriage, a husband and wife relationship, “to sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of the water by the word.” His word is going to do a work in the church, church, in these last days that’s going to be a sign and a beacon to the nations of the earth, “that he might present to himself a glorious, honorable church,” an honorable church, “not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing.” And then he says, “This is a great mystery, but I speak concerning Christ and the church.” So what’s the mystery? That the church is the bride, the wife of Christ. Hallelujah. 2 Corinthians 11:2: “I’ve espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a” what? “Chaste virgin to Christ.” There again, the church is likened as the bride. A bride prepares herself for that day of marriage. Romans 7:4: “You also have become dead to the law through the body of Christ, that you may be married to another,” who’s the other? “To him who was raised from the dead,” that’s Jesus Christ, “that we should bear fruit to God.” You see, it’s that intimate relationship now that causes us to bear fruit. Hallelujah. See, the marriage of the Lamb is coming, and the wife has made herself ready. Ephesians 3:9, look how powerful this is: “To make all see what is the fellowship of the mystery which from the beginning of the ages has been hidden in God, who created all things.” See, this thing has been secret until Christ came, “to the intent that now the many manifold different wisdoms of God might be made known by the, who, by the church, to who?
How does the New Testament describe the church as the bride of Christ? (Ephesians 5:25; 2 Corinthians 11:2; Romans 7:4)

Ephesians 5:25-32: Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the church and gave Himself for her, that He might sanctify and cleanse her with the washing of water by the word, that He might present her to Himself a glorious church, not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but that she should be holy and without blemish. So husbands ought to love their own wives as their own bodies; he who loves his wife loves himself. For no one ever hated his own flesh, but nourishes and cherishes it, just as the Lord does the church. For we are members of His body, of His flesh and of His bones. “For this reason a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh.” This is a great mystery, but I speak concerning Christ and the church. 2 Corinthians 11:2: For I am jealous for you with godly jealousy. For I have betrothed you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ. Romans 7:4: Therefore, my brethren, you also have become dead to the law through the body of Christ, that you may be married to another—to Him who was raised from the dead, that we should bear fruit to God.
What is the “mystery” of the church, and who learns from it? (Ephesians 3:9-10)

He says the church “is something more than a building and people in it,” and the secret kept from the beginning is now made known “by the church” to “principalities and powers in heavenly places.” He says Satan and his demons “learn things as God keeps moving and dealing with his church.”
What is the “mystery” of the church, and who learns from it? (Ephesians 3:9-10)

To principalities and powers in heavenly places.” You see, Satan and his demons and his kingdom of darkness get their knowledge when God gives it through the church. They learn things as God keeps moving and dealing with his church. So we are a valuable source on earth, not only to the people that don’t know God, but we living for God are coming against the principalities and powers of darkness. They learn from us. Hallelujah.
What is the “mystery” of the church, and who learns from it? (Ephesians 3:9-10)

Ephesians 3:9-10: and to make all see what is the fellowship of the mystery, which from the beginning of the ages has been hidden in God who created all things through Jesus Christ; to the intent that now the manifold wisdom of God might be made known by the church to the principalities and powers in the heavenly places,
What is the “fine linen,” and who is invited to the marriage supper? (Revelation 19:8-9)

He says the fine linen “is the righteousness of the saints,” and there are “two types of righteousness”: our position through the blood of Christ, and doing right. He says the invitation “went out to the whole world,” and “blessed are they which are called” who responded.
What is the “fine linen,” and who is invited to the marriage supper? (Revelation 19:8-9)

See, the church is something more than a building and people in it, and this was the secret that was kept from the beginning of time. And John, in his book of Revelation, is explaining in detail these things. Revelation 19:8, going back to Revelation, talking about the marriage, the wife has made herself ready: “To her was granted that she would be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white, for fine linen is the righteousness of the saints.” You see the thing this bride did is she put on righteousness. Now, there’s two types of righteousness. One, we are righteous through the blood of Christ. See, that’s our position. The second one, in John it says, “They that do righteous are righteous.” And so the bride, the mature ones in the church, are they that have grown to the place where they do right. And at the end of the age the church is going to be a manifested group through all the earth, as a people that do right. Hallelujah. You know, we have been so distracted with the beast and the antichrist and the false prophet and all that, we don’t see the power of the church that Jesus died for and is raising up in the earth. Verse 9: “Blessed are they which are called to the marriage supper of the Lamb.” Called, summoned, invited. And so didn’t Jesus invite all to come to him? So the invitation went out to how many? The whole world. Jesus said, “Come unto me.” The invitation went out to the whole world. “I want to marry you, I want to know you, I want to have an intimate relationship, I want to change your life.” And “blessed are they which are called.” So all of us are what? Blessed who heard the call and responded and accepted Christ. Amen. How many of you accepted Christ? Yeah. See, you responded to the invitation. Now he wants to make you his bride, a mature Christian, a mature woman in God. Hallelujah, and you’ve got to prepare yourself by responding.
What is the “fine linen,” and who is invited to the marriage supper? (Revelation 19:8-9)

Revelation 19:8-9: And to her it was granted to be arrayed in fine linen, clean and bright, for the fine linen is the righteous acts of the saints. Then he said to me, “Write: ‘Blessed are those who are called to the marriage supper of the Lamb!’ ” And he said to me, “These are the true sayings of God.” 1 John 3:7: Little children, let no one deceive you. He who practices righteousness is righteous, just as He is righteous. Matthew 11:28: Come to Me, all you who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
Why does he say the bride is the New Jerusalem, a “four-square city”? (Revelation 21:2, 9)

He says the bride “is likened unto this new city,” which is “a four-square building,” not a wedding dress. He says “this four-square city is the bride,” and that “we learn things from the marriage relationship, but we’re going to learn a lot more from the four-square city.”
Why does he say the bride is the New Jerusalem, a “four-square city”? (Revelation 21:2, 9)

Revelation 21:2: “Then I, John, saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.” Okay, I got a picture up there showing all the nations making up the bride. I love that picture, isn’t that a beautiful picture? At the top one, all these people, they just are flowing in. That’s the wide skirt down there, and then just getting right into where, you know, where the bride of Christ, all of us, are the bride of Christ. Well done, every who did this did a good job. Okay, but also this bride is likened unto this new city, Jerusalem. It’s a four-square building. It has nothing to do with a marriage dress and a wreath or whatever there and all that. We’re supposed to be a four-square city with three gates on each side and pillars that we’re supported on, and inside the city are things that are going on. Are you ready for this? Now, first you got to understand that this four-square city is the bride. It’s the wife. Is that through your cranial vacuum? You say, “I don’t understand how a bride can be a four-square city.” Because God said it was. All right. Now, we learn things from the marriage relationship, but we’re going to learn a lot more from the four-square city that the bride is. Are you ready? A bride prepared for her husband. Then in Revelation 21:9 he said again, “Come, and I will show you the bride, the Lamb’s wife.” Okay, we saw it once, now we’re going to see it again. Are you ready? “He showed me the great city, the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God, having the glory of God.”
Why does he say the bride is the New Jerusalem, a “four-square city”? (Revelation 21:2, 9)

Revelation 21:2: Then I, John, saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. Revelation 21:9-11: Then one of the seven angels who had the seven bowls filled with the seven last plagues came to me and talked with me, saying, “Come, I will show you the bride, the Lamb’s wife.” And he carried me away in the Spirit to a great and high mountain, and showed me the great city, the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God, having the glory of God. Her light was like a most precious stone, like a jasper stone, clear as crystal.
Is the New Jerusalem a natural thing like a star? (Revelation 21:10-11)

He says that when he was a young minister, prophets predicted the city based on a star that “was shaped different than any other star.” He says “it’s not a natural thing. The church is a spiritual building,” and that “these prophets hang on to any ridiculous thing to try to prove the ridiculous predictions.”
Is the New Jerusalem a natural thing like a star? (Revelation 21:10-11)

Now, when I was a young minister, these prophets, you know, were predicting, because the astronomers saw a star coming out of the north, and it was shaped different than any other star, didn’t have the five points and all this, and they conjured up this thing that this is the four-square city coming down out of heaven. Church, it’s not a natural thing. The church is a spiritual building. Paul said, “You are built up a” what? “Spiritual house.” Ain’t no star coming out of them. But see, these prophets hang on to any ridiculous thing to try to prove the ridiculous predictions. Just letting it sink in. Now, this city is also the bride of Christ. You got it? Okay. “He showed me the great city, the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God, having the glory of God.”
Is the New Jerusalem a natural thing like a star? (Revelation 21:10-11)
1 Peter 2:5: you also, as living stones, are being built up a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
Why is there no temple in the city, and who is the temple? (Revelation 21:22-23)

He says “I saw no temple in this city” because “God himself” and Jesus abide in it, meaning “us.” He says “who is the temple of God? We are,” and that this has “got nothing to do with the future, it’s got to do with now.” He says the Lamb is its light because Jesus “lives in us and he projects through us.”
Why is there no temple in the city, and who is the temple? (Revelation 21:22-23)

Revelation 21:22. Look at here, these people are wanting to build a temple over in Jerusalem. “I saw no temple in this city.” Are you there? Now, if there’s no temple in the city, what in the world we worried about a temple for? Okay, “for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its” what? Temple. Temple means an abiding place. See, so who’s abiding in this city? God himself. Amen. And Jesus Christ. Now, that’s us, church. Who abides in us when we come together? Who’s with us? Jesus and the Father himself. When we leave here as individuals, who is the temple of God? We are. Isn’t that what the Bible says? “You are the temple of the living God.” Spirit of God lives in you. Okay, got nothing to do with the future, it’s got to do with now. Giving you understanding of who you are and what the church is. Are you with me? “The city had no need of the sun or the moon,” no natural light, “for the glory of God” what? Illuminates it. You see, the real light of the church is God’s presence and God’s word. Amen. The Lamb is its light. Didn’t Jesus say, “I’m the light of the world,” and then he said, “I’m going to be leaving, and you are the light of the world”? Why are we the light of the world? Because he lives in us and he projects through us. Now, now see, he’s describing the church. Now, hallelujah.
Why is there no temple in the city, and who is the temple? (Revelation 21:22-23)

Revelation 21:22-23: But I saw no temple in it, for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple. The city had no need of the sun or of the moon to shine in it, for the glory of God illuminated it. The Lamb is its light. 2 Corinthians 6:16: And what agreement has the temple of God with idols? For you are the temple of the living God. As God has said: “I will dwell in them And walk among them. I will be their God, And they shall be My people.” John 8:12: Then Jesus spoke to them again, saying, “I am the light of the world. He who follows Me shall not walk in darkness, but have the light of life.”
Who enters the city, and what are the requirements? (Revelation 21:24-27)

He says the church brings in people from “every kind and tribe, tongue and nation,” and that “the whole ticket to this church is coming in through Jesus, repenting of your sins.” He says you can have a baptism certificate and a church role, but “if you haven’t repented, renounced your sins and work on changing them, you’re not in.”
Who enters the city, and what are the requirements? (Revelation 21:24-27)

“Nations of those who are saved shall walk in its light, and kings of the earth will bring their glory and honor into it. Its gates shall not be shut at all. They shall bring the glory and honor of the nations into it.” Didn’t Jesus say out of every kind and tribe, tongue and nation I will bring out a people for myself? And where is he bringing them to? The church. And who does he use to reach the nations? The church. And what is the glory of a nation? The people. Hallelujah. See, this is supposed to be us. Now, “there will by no means enter in anything that defiles or causes an abomination or a lie, but only those who are written in” what? “The Lamb’s Book of Life.” Didn’t Jesus say, “I am the way, the truth and the life”? Yes. See, the whole ticket to this church is coming in through Jesus, repenting of your sins. If you no repent, you know, become part of the bride, oh, your name can be on the church roll, you can have a baptism certificate, but if you haven’t repented, renounced your sins and work on changing them, you’re not in. Amen. Ain’t that right? And this is what’s duped a lot of people today. They become a member of a church, get a baptism certificate, they even become an elder, deacon in the church and all that, and they haven’t met the husband. They haven’t met Jesus, they haven’t been born again, they haven’t come through the right process. And he plainly says, “I don’t care.” You can’t get in if you’re going to live a sinful life, flagrant sinful life.
Who enters the city, and what are the requirements? (Revelation 21:24-27)

Revelation 21:24-27: And the nations of those who are saved shall walk in its light, and the kings of the earth bring their glory and honor into it. Its gates shall not be shut at all by day (there shall be no night there). And they shall bring the glory and the honor of the nations into it. But there shall by no means enter it anything that defiles, or causes an abomination or a lie, but only those who are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life. John 14:6: Jesus said to him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.
Is church membership the same as belonging to his church?

He says “although a church might put you on their membership roll, that doesn’t mean you belong to his church,” and “there’s only one church.” He says we should not “change the church to meet our condition,” but get our condition up to what he says we are.
Is church membership the same as belonging to his church?

And so then we change the church to meet our condition instead of seeing what the church is and getting our condition up to what he says we positionally are. Could that be an amen? See, right now all the churches in America just accept anybody. There is no requirements. But in the real church, in the real kingdom, in the thing that God is building, there are requirements. And although a church might put you on their membership roll, that doesn’t mean you belong to his church. There’s only one church. There isn’t a Baptist church, Presbyterian church, a Catholic church and a Pentecostal church. There is one church, and these are its characteristics, and he’s given us the qualifications. Now, this has nothing to do with the [unclear] thing, except we are going to be a mature church. We’re going to be this when he comes, so there’s a tremendous visitation of God coming.
What is the river of life that the church needs? (Revelation 22:1)

He says the nations “don’t need psychology, they don’t need philosophy, they need to touch this river of life that flows directly from God.” He says churches replace “spiritual understanding” with “human understanding,” and tells how he touched the river of life and it “changed my life.”
What is the river of life that the church needs? (Revelation 22:1)

Now look at this. In this city, in this church, in this bride, there “he showed me a pure river of water of life, [unclear] crystal, proceeding from the throne of God and of the Lamb.” Church, that’s what the nations need. They don’t need psychology, they don’t need philosophy, they need to touch this river of life that flows directly from God. Can I hear an amen on that? And instead of seeking God and fasting and praying till God moves this way, we start a church like the, you know, they go to these seminaries: how to multiply a church, how to grow a church. And we replace human, we take human understanding and replace it with spiritual understanding, and people aren’t touching the river of life that’s supposed to be in the church. Boy, that was good. I don’t know about you, but I touched that river of life. It changed my life back there. I didn’t know God was that real. I thought it was just something you thought about in your mind and just stubbornly did and mentally dead. But when I came to him, he came to me. I found that river of life. I drank from that river. I was a different person. I had different desires. Now, don’t get me wrong, my flesh still wanted to do things that were wrong, but my spirit wanted to please God now.
What is the river of life that the church needs? (Revelation 22:1)
Revelation 22:1: And he showed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding from the throne of God and of the Lamb.
What does he say about the pre-tribulation rapture theory?
He says it “is not the most widely believed doctrine of the second coming” and that “most of the church world does not embrace that doctrine.”
What does he mean by “teaser predictions”?
He says they are predictions that “won’t lock themselves into a day, but it’s like he can come right now,” and that both date predictions and teaser predictions “are very destructive.”
How many times does he say Jesus’s return has been predicted?
He says it “has been predicted to come at least twenty to thirty times since I was a kid,” and “every one of them’s missed. Nobody knows.”
Why does he say we should praise God now?
He says “it’s ordained that we praise and worship him now, and when we go to heaven it is going to continue,” and “get out of your excuses.”
What does he say if you have nothing else to be thankful for?
He says “if your name’s written in the Book of Life and you’re going to heaven, that’s something to be excited and thankful about.”
Does he say only a few people are saved?
He says he used to hear “few there be that find it,” but in Revelation “there was a multitude that could not be numbered,” so “heaven has multitudes of people in it, not a few.”
What does he say Christians must do to make themselves ready?
He says “you got to respond to God, you got to respond to the word, you got to seek God, you got to seek the word,” rather than sitting back and waiting.
What does he say will happen to wickedness and righteousness?
He says “wickedness is going to come to its full maturity, but righteousness is going to come to its full maturity,” and so “there is some powerful things got to take place.”
Did Jesus die only for the world, or for the church too?
He says “he died for the church as well as for the sins of the world,” and the same blood that saves is “powerful enough for his people to grow up and be the mature bride.”
What are the “two types of righteousness” he mentions?
He says one is “righteous through the blood of Christ. See, that’s our position,” and the other is “they that do righteous are righteous,” the mature who “do right.”
How can the bride be a four-square city?
He says “this four-square city is the bride,” and “I don’t understand how a bride can be a four-square city” is answered by “because God said it was.”
What does he say about people who want to rebuild a temple in Jerusalem?
He says “these people are wanting to build a temple over in Jerusalem,” but “I saw no temple in this city,” so “what in the world we worried about a temple for?”
What does he say about baptism certificates and church membership?
He says you can have “a baptism certificate” and even be “an elder, deacon,” but if “they haven’t met Jesus, they haven’t been born again,” they’re not in.
Does he say there are many churches or one?
He says “there is one church,” not “a Baptist church, Presbyterian church, a Catholic church and a Pentecostal church,” and that “in the real church … there are requirements.”
What does he say the nations need?
He says “they don’t need psychology, they don’t need philosophy, they need to touch this river of life that flows directly from God.”

items.d: In “The Lamb’s Wife Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Revelation 22 that the river of life and the tree of life are in the church now. He also covers who is outside the city, the Spirit and the…
p: In “The Lamb’s Wife Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Revelation 22 that the river of life and the tree of life are in the church now. He also covers who is outside the city, the Spirit and the bride saying “come,” the cost of accepting the invitation, and why he says Jesus wants to come to people quickly, not only at the second coming.
What is the river of life in the church, and how is knowledge different from the tree of life? (Revelation 22:1)

He says “you are the temple of the living God,” so “when we come together all of our streams come together and make one big river.” He says Adam and Eve’s mistake was thinking knowledge was enough: “the knowledge is got to bring us to the life,” and the church should be “known for the river of life flowing in it.”
What is the river of life in the church, and how is knowledge different from the tree of life? (Revelation 22:1)

And it proceeds straightly. And where does God live? Where’s his throne? You are the temple of the living God. He set up residence in you, so you have a source of God directly from God, and when we come together, all of our streams come together and make one big river, and people can drink out of it if they choose, and that’s what they need. They need to drink of this life. Remember in the Garden of Eden there was the tree of knowledge and the tree of what? The tree of life. We make the same mistake Adam and Eve made. We think because we got knowledge of God and knowledge of the Bible that we are in, but until we eat of the tree of life and get touched by God, and he is involved in us, that birthing, we’re not in. Knowledge isn’t it. The knowledge is got to bring us to the life. Hallelujah, and he’s inviting us. The church has this. The church should be known for the river of life flowing in it. See, that’s why God said, “They that worship the Father must worship him in spirit and truth.” Why? It’s that spirit and truth worship that produces that river of life that people can drink from. And that’s why he says you’ve got to preach the living word. Why? Because it’s the living word that pricks people’s hearts, that convinces them and convicts them to change their ways. So we got to have the living word and the living presence of God, amen. That’s the church. Now, we’re supposed to be that now, and there is a time coming on earth where this is going to happen, I mean overall. Now, don’t get me wrong, there are people who experience this, you understand that, but the major, the church is not experiencing this. They don’t even know this stuff. All they know is a big bad beast are coming and the antichrist and the [unclear] and all the rest, and they know nothing about the powerful church God is raising up in the earth.
What is the river of life in the church, and how is knowledge different from the tree of life? (Revelation 22:1)

Revelation 22:1: And he showed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding from the throne of God and of the Lamb. John 4:24: God is Spirit, and those who worship Him must worship in spirit and truth.” 1 Corinthians 3:16: Do you not know that you are the temple of God and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?
What is the tree of life in the church, and why are its leaves for the healing of the nations? (Revelation 22:2)

He says Jesus is “the tree of life,” “the river of life” and “everything,” and that it bears fruit “every month” so you can get “fresh joy, fresh peace, fresh wisdom.” He compares the leaves to photosynthesis: we absorb his light and then “release that word of God, that life that comes like oxygen.”
What is the tree of life in the church, and why are its leaves for the healing of the nations? (Revelation 22:2)

“In the middle of the street, and on either side of the river, was the tree of life, which bore twelve fruits, yielding fruit every month, and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.” In this city, in this bride, in this church, there’s not only the river of life but there is the tree of life. And I selected this picture because it illustrates it right, except for all this greenery. This is a spiritual thing, got nothing to do with grass and flowers. They should have had a paved street going down through there, but this is the only one that had the tree whose stump went on both sides of the river, and that’s exactly what Revelation says, the tree is on both sides of the river. Hallelujah. So the water’s flowing under it, doesn’t it? Oh, I love that illustration. Now, in the church, it’s supposed to be the tree of life. Now, who is obviously the tree of life? Jesus Christ, duh. Who’s the river of life? Jesus Christ, duh. Who’s everything? Jesus Christ, duh. He’s it, man. And there’s fruit, and it produces fruit. How often? Every month. Every month fruit is produced. When you need mercy, you need faith, you need joy, you need peace, every month you can get fresh joy, fresh peace, fresh wisdom. Are you there? And where is it found? In the church. But even if you don’t have any fruit, the leaves of the tree are the what? Healing of the nations. Church, we have the leaves of a tree, as you all know, through photosynthesis from the light mixing with the light, create an energy and a food for the tree and release oxygen into the air so people can breathe. Now isn’t it interesting that Jesus said its leaves are for the healing of the nations? See why? As we are in the presence of his light now, who’s the light of the church? Jesus. And see, through us being in his presence, we feed our spiritual man. Are you there? The photosynthesis, only this is the spiritual synthesis. See, so we need to recognize Jesus and absorb his presence, absorb his light, and then we get energy, spiritual energy for a spiritual man, and then we release that word of God, that life that comes like oxygen is released, that causes others to be able to, what? Have life, come to Christ and go through it, too. You see how, you see the big responsibility the church has in the earth. You see why it’s important for us to come together. You see why it’s important for us to grow. See, we are the key to the biggest harvest that God has ordained in this, in his creation that he has created, through the church. The principalities and powers know the wisdom of God, remember that, through the what? Church.
What is the tree of life in the church, and why are its leaves for the healing of the nations? (Revelation 22:2)

Revelation 22:2: In the middle of its street, and on either side of the river, was the tree of life, which bore twelve fruits, each tree yielding its fruit every month. The leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.
How do we get the right to the tree of life? (Revelation 22:14; John 1:12)

He says this requires repentance: admitting “he was a sinner,” renouncing sins, and asking Christ to forgive and cleanse. He says “as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God,” and that we get up after mistakes, but “when we want to justify our sin and just stay sinning, we don’t have a right.”
How do we get the right to the tree of life? (Revelation 22:14; John 1:12)

This is powerful, church. “Blessed are those who do his commandments, that they may have the right to the tree of life and may enter through the gates into the city.” See, Dave [unclear] had to repent. He had to admit he was a sinner, and he had to renounce those sins, ask Christ to forgive him of those sins and cleanse him from those sins, and then God was faithful to what? Cleanse and forgive, and then come to Dave [unclear]. See, the Bible says in 1 John, or John 1:12, “As many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God.” And that comes by me what? Agreeing that I’m a sinner, I need saved, and Jesus is that Savior and inviting me into my life, and then I have what? Power to be made into a son of God, into a mature bride, into the holy city, New Jerusalem.
How do we get the right to the tree of life? (Revelation 22:14; John 1:12)

Revelation 22:14: Blessed are those who do His commandments, that they may have the right to the tree of life, and may enter through the gates into the city. John 1:12: But as many as received Him, to them He gave the right to become children of God, to those who believe in His name:
Who does he say are the “dogs” outside the city, and what does he say about homosexuality? (Revelation 22:15)

He reads “outside the city are dogs” and says “what’s a dog in the Bible? Homosexuals,” along with sorcerers, sexual immorality and other flagrant sinners. He says “there’s no scripture for being bisexual” and that people are born in the sex they are created in, and that he has led many homosexuals to Jesus.
Who does he say are the “dogs” outside the city, and what does he say about homosexuality? (Revelation 22:15)

This is exciting stuff. And if I don’t keep his commandments, and you know, we make mistakes, but we got to still, the principle of repentance, we get up and what? Keep going, isn’t that right? We don’t quit. But when we want to justify our sin and just stay sinning, we don’t have a right to this tree of life or the river of life. “Outside the city are dogs.” Now, what’s a dog in the Bible? Homosexuals. Flagrant sinners, people that disdain God, sorcerers, witchcraft, people into, you know, the signs of the heavens and astrology and all that stuff, sexual immorality, whether it’s incest, adultery, fornication, homosexuality, bestiality. You. Uh, there’s a thing going through here about being bisexual. There’s no scripture for being bisexual. We are created in the sex we were created in, and that is a lie. You’re believing a lie out there when they say you can be bisexual, you can [unclear] either one. It’s a lie. When they say homosexuals are born that way, people that know the book aren’t deceived by the lie. It says in the last days he’ll bring them strong delusions that they believe a lie. One of the lies is they’re saying that homosexuals are created that way. That’s a lie, and they have proven that was a lie. Science have proven it, that there’s no homosexual gene. You have to learn the habit. Are you there? And so we got to stop this nonsense of bisexual and homosexual and all that. God knew what he was doing when he created us. Are you out there? Amen. And church, I have led many homosexuals to Jesus Christ, many. Some of them went back, just like drunkards went back and drug addicts went back.
Who does he say are the “dogs” outside the city, and what does he say about homosexuality? (Revelation 22:15)

Revelation 22:15: But outside are dogs and sorcerers and sexually immoral and murderers and idolaters, and whoever loves and practices a lie. 2 Thessalonians 2:11: And for this reason God will send them strong delusion, that they should believe the lie,
What does he say about murder, idolatry and “the lie”? (Revelation 22:15)

He says that if you hate a race or social status, “you’re a murderer,” and that “greed is idolatry.” He says “evolution is a lie. It is a theory, it’s not a fact,” that a child in the womb is not “just a piece of flesh” but “a real being,” and that the Bible is “a book of truth,” not “a book of faith.”
What does he say about murder, idolatry and “the lie”? (Revelation 22:15)

Sin is sin. Some of them went back and came back, and some of them came and stayed and are serving God today, and it’s been over thirty years. The cross works for anybody who will work it, amen, but we can’t believe the lie. “Murderers.” He says if you hate people you’re a murderer, when you, you know, hate a race or hate a social status, the rich or the poor or whatever. That’s, the Bible says in the New Testament, that’s the source of murder, and so you stop it at what? Hatred. You don’t look down on anybody. Amen. Now, that’s got nothing to do with criminals. Criminals need to be brought to justice, isn’t that right? “And idolaters.” And greed is idolatry. If your whole life is about money and that’s all you talk about, live for, and whatever you’ve got, you’re serving an idol, you’re worshiping something other than God. “And whoever loves and practices a lie.” You see, and we got a lot of lies going on in our generation. Evolution is a lie. It is a theory, it’s not a fact. They have no proof of any of it. They give you enough stuff to frustrate you and think, and they make these beautiful charts and all the rest, yet they have no tangible evidence to back it up. They still have not found one connection from one species turned into another. It absolutely isn’t there. Are you there? This child in the womb is just a pile of flesh, just a piece of flesh? No, it is a real being. See, people of the book, don’t believe the lie. These people that say the book, the Bible, is a book of faith, they’re lying to you, and many Christians believe the lie. They think the Bible is a book of faith. Nowhere in the Bible does it say it’s a book of faith. All through the Bible it says it’s a book of truth.
What does he say about murder, idolatry and “the lie”? (Revelation 22:15)

1 John 3:15: Whoever hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him. Revelation 22:15: But outside are dogs and sorcerers and sexually immoral and murderers and idolaters, and whoever loves and practices a lie.
How do “people of the book” know the lie from the truth?

He says people who “drink of this water, this river of life and this tree of life” “have met the life, they know his nature.” He says as a young Christian he could say, “I tell you that’s not the nature of the God that I met,” and later found in the word that the lie was wrong.
How do “people of the book” know the lie from the truth?

See, people of the book, people of Christ, people that drink of this water, this river of life and this tree of life, they don’t believe the lie. They have met the life, they know his nature. Maybe they don’t understand it all. When I was a young Christian I didn’t understand it all, but because I met God I knew his nature, and so I knew what was wrong when people would come to me. I said, “I don’t have an answer for you, but I tell you that’s not the nature of the God that I met.” And sure enough, as I learned the word more and all that, then I found in the word that they were wrong. Hallelujah.
Who is saying “come” in Revelation 22:17: the Spirit, the bride, and whoever hears?

He says “three people saying come”: the Spirit, the bride (“we are”), and “whosoever hears.” He says we are to tell people “come to Jesus,” not “come and join a church and get a baptism,” and that even a new Christian with flaws can “also have the right to say” come.
Who is saying “come” in Revelation 22:17: the Spirit, the bride, and whoever hears?

Revelation 22:17: “The Spirit and the bride say, Come! Let him who hears say, Come! Let him who thirsts come. Whosoever desires, let him take of the waters of life freely.” Now look at this: there’s three people saying come. The Spirit, which is Jesus, which is God, he’s saying, “Come.” Most of us has felt that voice pulling us, huh? Drawing us. But not only the Spirit is saying come. Who else is saying come? The bride. Who’s the bride? We are. See, we’re telling people, come to the tree of life, come to the river of life, come to Jesus. Man, your life can be transformed, it can be revolutionized, it can be totally changed. Come and drink of him. Don’t come and join a church and get a baptism or said to come to Jesus. Are we telling people to come? We’re supposed to be. “And whosoever hears says, Come.” Okay, this person isn’t the bride. Maybe they’re a new Christian and they got a lot of flaws in their life. They haven’t got on that righteous linen yet, except positionally through the blood. They still may curse and they still may lie and do some things that are not right, and they’re working on it, but Jesus said because they listen to the message, “come,” and they came, they also have the right to say what? Come. You know, I might be perfect yet, and I may have some faults, but come, man, this thing is real, come on in. Amen. “And then who is thirsty, and who desires, let them come and take of” what? A church membership? A help-the-poor program? A visit-to-sick program? No. What is the issue here?
Who is saying “come” in Revelation 22:17: the Spirit, the bride, and whoever hears?
Revelation 22:17: And the Spirit and the bride say, “Come!” And let him who hears say, “Come!” And let him who thirsts come. Whoever desires, let him take the water of life freely.
What is the “payment” for the free water of life? (Revelation 22:17)
