He says the water is free of money, but “there is a payment”: “the humbling of yourself to respond to this great invitation.” He says some are “too proud and they miss out,” but the church is still saying “come” to all, naming homosexuals, liberals and a magazine publisher.
What is the “payment” for the free water of life? (Revelation 22:17)

Come and take a drink of the waters of life freely. The only thing you have to do is just respond, accept his offer. It isn’t quite free, but you don’t have to pay any money for it. You don’t have to do [unclear] for it. You just have to believe, accept, admit you’re wrong and ask him to forgive you, cleanse you and do this work in you. That’s the payment. There is a payment. It’s the humbling of yourself to respond to this great invitation. Amen. And some people can’t pay that price. They can’t humble themselves, admit they’re wrong, admit they need Jesus and ask Jesus to come into their life and give him to drink of those waters. They’re too proud and they miss out. But the church is still saying what? Come. Homosexuals, come. Liberals, come. Uh, Hefner, come, publisher of Playboy, come. Come. Amen. And the Spirit saying, “Come.”
What is the “payment” for the free water of life? (Revelation 22:17)
Revelation 22:17: And the Spirit and the bride say, “Come!” And let him who hears say, “Come!” And let him who thirsts come. Whoever desires, let him take the water of life freely.
Is this for now or the future, and what does “quickly” mean? (Revelation 22:6-7)

He says “it’s not something in the future,” that “this needs to happen in every generation,” and that “this is not necessarily talking about his second coming.” He says Jesus wants to “do a quick work in the last days,” and “I don’t want to take all your lifetime.”
Is this for now or the future, and what does “quickly” mean? (Revelation 22:6-7)

Now, in closing, I want to show you that this is for, I want to show you that it’s for now. It’s not something in the future. The Lord, and I showed you this in earlier messages, “the Lord God of the holy prophets sent his angels to show his servants,” who his servants? Who’s his servants? Us, the church, the bride, the whole heavenly Jerusalem, “things which was what? Come to pass at the end of the world, or shortly come to pass.” Shortly come to pass. Why? Why? Because this needs to happen in every generation. The church needs to be saying come. The church needs to have the river of life and the tree of life in it. The church needs to be illuminated by the presence of God, Jesus Christ himself, in every generation. The church is the one that is the vehicle to bring in the nations on to God. And this is not necessarily talking about his second coming. “I want to come to you now. I want to come to you in your generation. I want to touch you with my tree of life, with my river of life. I want to make you a bride that’s prepared for her husband, that the world can look at and say, ‘Yes, that is a person who Jesus Christ rules and reigns in their life.’” Amen. And he wants to do it how long? Quickly. Say it: quickly. Now, I had a problem with this when I was a young Christian. Thought it was going to take me a lifetime to get anywhere. But Jesus said, “I will do a quick work in the last days.” The last days started when Jesus ascended into the heavens. He’s coming quickly to us. He wants to adjust us quickly. He wants us to grow quickly. He doesn’t want us to take a lifetime. Amen. And it says, “I am coming quickly. Blessed is he who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book.” “I am coming” what? Quickly. “And I want to bless people that hear and keep the words of this book, and I want to do it in your generation, and I don’t want to take all your lifetime. I want to move in your life in a short period of time and make something beautiful out of your life.” Now, isn’t that powerful?
Is this for now or the future, and what does “quickly” mean? (Revelation 22:6-7)

Revelation 22:6: Then he said to me, “These words are faithful and true.” And the Lord God of the holy prophets sent His angel to show His servants the things which must shortly take place. Revelation 22:7: “Behold, I am coming quickly! Blessed is he who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book.”
What is the reward and the work the bride must do? (Revelation 22:12)

He says the preparation of the bride means “I have got to humble myself, I got to seek him, I got to pray, I got to worship, I got to read the word, I got to assemble together,” so that Jesus can “reward me with himself … with maturity … with fruit.” He adds that it “doesn’t take a long time to get this if you start pursuing it.”
What is the reward and the work the bride must do? (Revelation 22:12)

Revelation 22:12: “I am coming” when? How often? How long? Quickly. “And my reward is” what? With me. “To give everyone according to his” what? Work. See, that preparation of the bride: I have to apply myself, I have got to humble myself, I got to seek him, I got to pray, I got to worship, I got to read the word, I got to assemble together. I got to do these things. That’s the work he wants me to do so he can reward me with himself, reward me with his life, reward me with maturity, reward me with fruit, so that the world can see the good works in me and give honor to who? Jesus Christ. Hallelujah. And he isn’t one to take very long to do this. In the Bible, you know, it showed a tree would bear fruit in three to four years. This doesn’t take a long time to get this if you start pursuing it. Now, that’s good, that’s good Scriptures. Revelation 20, all this is in Revelation 22: “Surely I am coming quickly.” Do we need Jesus to come to us now? Yeah, I need him now. The second coming is wonderful, but hey, I need him now. “If any man thirst, let him” what? “Come to me and drink.” Jesus said, “If any man love me,” John 14:23, “he will keep my words, my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our abode with him.” That’s what he’s talking about. “I want to come to you, man. Respond to my words. Me and Papa, we want to come, we want to live in your life, we want to make something great out of you.”
What is the reward and the work the bride must do? (Revelation 22:12)

Revelation 22:12: “And behold, I am coming quickly, and My reward is with Me, to give to every one according to his work. John 14:23: Jesus answered and said to him, “If anyone loves Me, he will keep My word; and My Father will love him, and We will come to him and make Our home with him.
Do we need Jesus now, or can we wait for the rapture? (Luke 19:10; Matthew 11:28)

He says “the second coming is wonderful, but hey, I need him now,” and that “he doesn’t want to wait for the rapture and for the end of the world.” He says “this rapture thing is distracting us from the thing that God wants to do in the church.”
Do we need Jesus now, or can we wait for the rapture? (Luke 19:10; Matthew 11:28)

Hallelujah. But we got all the comes and, in Revelation, there’s a second coming, but we can’t wait for the second coming to have Jesus and God. Could that be true? “The Son of Man has come to seek and save that which was” what? Lost. See, he wants to come to the sinful world. He doesn’t want to wait for the rapture and for the end of the world. He wants to do it when? Now. He wants to do it quickly. Are you with me? “Come unto me, all you that labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you” what? Rest. See, “my reward is with me.” I’ll take your depression and your distress and your troubles and your struggles, I’ll give you rest, I’ll give you life, I’ll give you peace, man, I’ll bless you, I’ll reward you. Come to me, I’ll reward you. How many don’t want to wait for the rapture to get rewarded? Yeah. We need things now, and this is why we’ve got to understand this rapture thing is distracting us from the thing that God wants to do in the church and make it a powerful church and do it quickly.
Do we need Jesus now, or can we wait for the rapture? (Luke 19:10; Matthew 11:28)
Luke 19:10: for the Son of Man has come to seek and to save that which was lost.” Matthew 11:28: Come to Me, all you who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
Why do people join a church instead of coming to Christ? (John 3:20-21)

He says people join a church because “the church doesn’t expose their evil sins,” so someone can be “beating his wife” and still say “he’s got the baptism certificate.” He says we avoid the living word because “it exposes us,” and that “we don’t want God touching us in our intimate places.”
Why do people join a church instead of coming to Christ? (John 3:20-21)

“All practicing evil hates the light and does not come to the light, lest their deeds should be exposed, but he who does the truth comes to the light, that his deeds may be clearly seen that they have been done in God.” Why will people join a church instead of coming to Christ? Because the church doesn’t expose their evil sins. “You’re okay. You got the blood, you got grace, you got faith, man, you’re in.” He’s beating his wife, he’s committing sexual immorality, [unclear] in his kids, but oh hallelujah, he’s got the baptism certificate. He says he’s a believer. This is why we don’t like Christ in the church and we don’t like the living word, because it exposes us. It exposes the intents of our heart, the purposes of our heart, and we don’t like it. But when we embrace him, we’re glad, because when he shines, I told the people Friday night the church told me my problems would be over when I come to Christ. Literally, man, you can just skate through life, and then I got Christ and I didn’t know I had so many problems. You know, when you get in his light, you see all the flaws. I was looking pretty good. I mean, even my neighbors named kids after me, they thought I was the greatest kid in the neighborhood. I mean, I graduated from school, that’s something everybody else wasn’t doing, and I was a good kid, I wasn’t part of a gang and all that. But boy, when I come into his light, Lord, how mercy, I didn’t know I had that many faults and problems. Are you there? And this is it: we don’t want God touching us in our intimate places that we try to keep secret. And so we rather have religion than life. But God says in the church there’s a tree of life and a water of life. “Search the Scriptures, for in them you” what? Think. See, people get intellect and knowledge of the Bible and they think they’re going to heaven. It’s exactly what Jesus is addressing. See, but he says, “These are they which testify of me,” and see, that’s what Revelation is written about. It’s written about the power of Christ in the church. “And you’re not willing to come to me that you might have” what? Life. The whole message of the church is come to Jesus and keep coming to Jesus. Touch him in prayer, touch him in worship, touch him in the living word.
Why do people join a church instead of coming to Christ? (John 3:20-21)

John 3:20-21: For everyone practicing evil hates the light and does not come to the light, lest his deeds should be exposed. But he who does the truth comes to the light, that his deeds may be clearly seen, that they have been done in God.”
Is Jesus better than prophecies and miracles, and what should we do? (John 5:39-40; Revelation 22:17)

He says “Jesus is better than prophecies, word of knowledge, word of wisdom,” and “better than signs and wonders and miracles.” He says “the whole message of the church is come to Jesus and keep coming,” and that “when we start touching him, our message will change.”
Is Jesus better than prophecies and miracles, and what should we do? (John 5:39-40; Revelation 22:17)

Keep touching him, keep letting that photosynthesis spiritual stuff putting energy and change into your life, amen, so you can grow and produce fruit. “If anyone thirst, let him come to the church. Let him come to the evangelist of the day. Let him come to the prophet and get another word from God.” If any man thirst, let him come to who? Me. Jesus is better than prophecies, word of knowledge, word of wisdom. Jesus is better than signs and wonders and miracles. Jesus is the key to your growth and becoming an effective Christian in your generation. Now that’s a good amen. I wished I could help you, man. I’d have done it a long time ago, man, if I could just go and lay hands on you and shake a little and you would just be transformed, man, I’d be doing it in a minute. Or like some of these churches, they just spray their people with water and they supposed to be all of a sudden holy and all that. Boy, I wish that worked. But they got to humble themselves and they got to come to Jesus. Christ Jesus wants to come to you quickly. He wants to come to you today. You’re wanting to go through the motions and think it’s going to take weeks and months and years. He’s wanting to come right now, and he’s wanting to do a work in you quickly. And he has told us today that the river of God and the tree of life, the river of life and the tree of life, is in the church, so all of us have that in us, and when we come together we have a full river flowing in the church. But he also told us that you got to admit you’re wrong, and you got to ask him to forgive you of that wrong, and you got to ask him to cleanse you of that wrong, and you got to ask him to come into your life and give you the power to become a child of God, a bride of Christ, the heavenly Jerusalem. Not very many Christians are on fire and telling other people to come to Jesus. We just go to church, we go home, we go through the routine of life, but when we start touching him, our message will change.
Is Jesus better than prophecies and miracles, and what should we do? (John 5:39-40; Revelation 22:17)

John 5:39-40: You search the Scriptures, for in them you think you have eternal life; and these are they which testify of Me. But you are not willing to come to Me that you may have life. Revelation 22:17: And the Spirit and the bride say, “Come!” And let him who hears say, “Come!” And let him who thirsts come. Whoever desires, let him take the water of life freely.
Why does he say knowledge of the Bible is not enough?

He says “we think because we got knowledge of God and knowledge of the Bible that we are in,” but “until we eat of the tree of life … we’re not in,” because “the knowledge is got to bring us to the life.”
Who does he say the tree of life and river of life are?
He says “who is obviously the tree of life? Jesus Christ, duh. Who’s the river of life? Jesus Christ, duh.”
He says the leaves feed the tree through light, so “as we are in the presence of his light … we feed our spiritual man,” then “release that word of God, that life that comes like oxygen.”
What does he say we must do to become a son of God?
He says it comes by “agreeing that I’m a sinner, I need saved, and Jesus is that Savior and inviting me into my life,” and then “power to be made into a son of God.”
What does he say about bisexuality?
He says “there’s no scripture for being bisexual,” that “we are created in the sex we were created in,” and “it’s a lie” to say people are born homosexual.
Does he say people can leave homosexuality?

Yes. He says “I have led many homosexuals to Jesus Christ,” that “some of them went back” while “some of them came and stayed and are serving God today,” and “the cross works for anybody who will work it.”
What does he say about hatred?
He says “if you hate people you’re a murderer” including “hate a race or hate a social status,” but adds “that’s got nothing to do with criminals. Criminals need to be brought to justice.”
What does he say about evolution?
He says “evolution is a lie. It is a theory, it’s not a fact,” and “they still have not found one connection from one species turned into another.”
Does he say the Bible is a book of faith or of truth?
He says “nowhere in the Bible does it say it’s a book of faith. All through the Bible it says it’s a book of truth.”
Can a new Christian with flaws invite others?
Yes. He says a new Christian who “may curse” or lie and is “working on it” still can “have the right to say” come, because the invitation is “come on in.”
Is the water of life free?
He says “it isn’t quite free, but you don’t have to pay any money for it,” and that “the payment” is “the humbling of yourself to respond to this great invitation.”
Does he say Revelation 22 is only about the second coming?
No. He says “this is not necessarily talking about his second coming,” but about Jesus wanting “to come to you now … in your generation.”
He says Jesus said “I will do a quick work in the last days,” and “he wants us to grow quickly. He doesn’t want us to take a lifetime.”
Why does he say the rapture is a distraction?
He says “we can’t wait for the second coming to have Jesus,” and “this rapture thing is distracting us from the thing that God wants to do in the church.”
Why does he say people avoid the living word?
He says “we don’t like Christ in the church and we don’t like the living word, because it exposes us. It exposes the intents of our heart.”

items.t: The Other Side of Eternal Life
items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that eternal life has two sides: believing in Christ and obeying Him. He reads John 17:3 and 1 John 2 on what it means to know God, and Matthew 7:21-27 on the…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that eternal life has two sides: believing in Christ and obeying Him. He reads John 17:3 and 1 John 2 on what it means to know God, and Matthew 7:21-27 on the many who say “Lord, Lord” but do not do the Father’s will.
What is the first side of eternal life, and do demons go to heaven? (John 3:16, James 2:19, John 3:36)

He says the first part of eternal life is “believing in Christ, putting your trust in Christ,” and that this is the one “we hear about.” He asks, “Do demons go to heaven? No, they don’t,” since “demons also believe, and they tremble.”
What is the first side of eternal life, and do demons go to heaven? (John 3:16, James 2:19, John 3:36)

Okay, when you talk about eternal life, most people, well, you’re going to live forever. But we’re going to talk about another side of eternal life. In John 3:16: “For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that whosoever, everyone that believes in Him, should not perish but have everlasting life.” So here we have the first part of eternal life: believing in Christ, putting your trust in Christ, His death on the cross, forgiveness of sins, cleansing of sins, and you will have everlasting life. And that’s the one we hear about. That’s the one that’s in the football games and all that, right? Okay, now let me ask you this question. James 2:19: “You believe that there’s one God. You do well. Very good. But demons also believe, and they tremble.” So my question is, does everyone that believes go to heaven? Do demons go to heaven? No, they don’t. We know that the lake of fire was made for Satan and his angels, the evil spirits and all that. Amen. Have I got your attention? Okay, that’s the first requirement, is believing in Christ. The second side of eternal life, all right, now watch this closely. “He who believes in the Son has everlasting life.” This is John 3:36, same chapter, just a few verses down. See, first requirement: believe in Christ. Amen. Then He says this statement:
What is the first side of eternal life, and do demons go to heaven? (John 3:16, James 2:19, John 3:36)

John 3:16: For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life. James 2:19: You believe that there is one God. You do well. Even the demons believe—and tremble! John 3:36: He who believes in the Son has everlasting life; and he who does not believe the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God abides on him.”
What does it mean to not “believe the Son”? (John 5:24, John 12:48)

He says “they believe on what He did, but they’re not believing and trusting in keeping what He said.” He reads John 5:24 and says the second requirement of eternal life is hearing and obeying: “listens to and obeys.”
What does it mean to not “believe the Son”? (John 5:24, John 12:48)

“He who does not believe the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God abides on him.” He who does not believe the Son. Not in the Son, not on the Son, not His virgin birth, not His death on the cross, not His resurrection from the dead, but they do not believe the Son. Now, that statement is pretty clear: they’re not believing what the Son is saying. They believe on what He did, but they’re not believing and trusting in keeping what He said. Are you there? Ah, and the wrath of God abides on them. God’s going to get mad and deal with it. All right. Now John 5:24 backs it up: “He who hears My words and believes in Him who sent Me.” And now He brings in God. You see, you’ve got to believe in God and Jesus Christ. The Bible’s very plain about that. These people cannot get rid of Jesus Christ in the name of worshiping a God, and we cannot get rid of God in the name of the Jesus Christ. They’re both very important. Okay, but “he who hears My word,” listens to and obeys, “and believes in Him who sent Me has everlasting life and shall not come into judgment, but has passed from death to life.” See, second requirement of eternal life. John 12:48: “He that rejects
What does it mean to not “believe the Son”? (John 5:24, John 12:48)

John 5:24: “Most assuredly, I say to you, he who hears My word and believes in Him who sent Me has everlasting life, and shall not come into judgment, but has passed from death into life. John 12:48: He who rejects Me, and does not receive My words, has that which judges him—the word that I have spoken will judge him in the last day.
What will judge people at the last day? (Acts 20:27, Daniel 12:2)

He says “What’s going to judge people? The word that He spoke,” and “the same word shall judge him in the last day.” He says “you don’t hear very much in America” this message, since “all you hear is the first part of eternal life.”
What will judge people at the last day? (Acts 20:27, Daniel 12:2)

Me,” they don’t even believe in Me, they don’t believe in the story, they don’t believe the Bible’s real, they don’t believe Jesus is God and died for our sins and rose again, “and receives not My words,” they reject Jesus’s teaching, reject everything Jesus said, “has one that judges him: the word that I have spoken.” What’s going to judge people? The word that He spoke. See, “he that believes not the Son,” the words that the Son spoke. Are you out there? Hallelujah. Now, this message, really, you don’t hear very much in America. All you hear is the first part of eternal life. Am I right? Absolutely. But Paul said this in Acts, he says, “I have not failed to declare unto you the whole counsel of God.” And how many know we need the whole counsel? Yes. “The same word shall judge him in the last day.” So that word that we reject, that word that we refuse to obey, is going to judge us, sentence us when He comes back. Now remember, in Daniel chapter 12:2: “Many who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life and some to everlasting shame and contempt.” See, it speaks about this in the Old Testament. Now why are some awakening to shame and contempt? Well, we go on with the verse: “Those who are
What will judge people at the last day? (Acts 20:27, Daniel 12:2)

Acts 20:27: For I have not shunned to declare to you the whole counsel of God. Daniel 12:2: And many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, Some to everlasting life, Some to shame and everlasting contempt.
Why are some resurrected to shame and contempt? (Daniel 12:3)
He says “they’re not turning to righteousness,” and “even back in the Old Testament, righteousness is going to determine whether you are resurrected for honor or shame and contempt.”
Why are some resurrected to shame and contempt? (Daniel 12:3)

wise, and those who turn many to righteousness.” Is it so? What? Why are some resurrected to shame and contempt? They’re not turning to righteousness. But those that are wise, I mean, you know, he that is wise wins souls. “He that winneth souls is wise.” Yeah, that communicates righteousness, the Bible, morality: “shall shine like the brightness of the firmament, like the stars forever.” And so even back in the Old Testament, righteousness is going to determine whether you are resurrected for honor or shame and contempt, everlasting life or shame and contempt. Now Matthew
Why are some resurrected to shame and contempt? (Daniel 12:3)

Daniel 12:3: Those who are wise shall shine Like the brightness of the firmament, And those who turn many to righteousness Like the stars forever and ever. Proverbs 11:30: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, And he who wins souls is wise.
What did Jesus tell the rich man who asked about eternal life? (Matthew 19:16-19)

He says Jesus replied, “If you want to enter into eternal life, keep the commandments,” and “Didn’t say a word about believing. Why? Because He’s dealing with the other side of eternal life.” He says Jesus named the last six commandments and “Love your neighbor as yourself.”
What did Jesus tell the rich man who asked about eternal life? (Matthew 19:16-19)

19:16. This is plain and clear. A rich man came up to Jesus and said, “What must I do to have eternal life?” That was his question. Jesus replied and says, “If you want to enter into eternal life, keep the commandments.” Didn’t say a word about believing. Why? Because He’s dealing with the other side of eternal life. Now, hallelujah, just letting it sink in. See, now the rich man, of course, being arrogant like rich people are and confident, the guy came up to Him so arrogant and confident, he says, “Which ones?” There’s a lot of commandments over there, you know. So Jesus
What did Jesus tell the rich man who asked about eternal life? (Matthew 19:16-19)

Matthew 19:16-19: Now behold, one came and said to Him, “Good Teacher, what good thing shall I do that I may have eternal life?” So He said to him, “Why do you call Me good? No one is good but One, that is, God. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.” He said to Him, “Which ones?” Jesus said, “‘You shall not murder,’ ‘You shall not commit adultery,’ ‘You shall not steal,’ ‘You shall not bear false witness,’ ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ ”
Does obeying mean we do not need to believe in Jesus?
He says “No. That’s the first step of eternal life, is believing in Jesus.” He adds, “The second part is what? Obeying Him, obeying what He said to do.”
Does obeying mean we do not need to believe in Jesus?

said, and He quoted the last six commandments of the Ten Commandments, only He replaced the last commandment, “Thou shalt not covet,” with “Love your neighbor as yourself.” Okay, the Ten Commandments, the last six, and He replaced the covet commandment with “Love your neighbor as yourself.” “Thou shalt not covet thy neighbor’s wife, thy neighbor’s house,” or whatever is thy neighbor’s, and Jesus just switched it over to “Love your neighbor as yourself.” All right, He says, “You shall not murder, commit adultery, steal, bear false witness, but you shall honor your parents and love your neighbor as yourself. If you do this, you will inherit eternal life.” Now, does that mean we don’t have to believe in Jesus? No. That’s the first step of eternal life, is believing in Jesus. You say trusting in Jesus. The second part is what? Obeying Him, obeying what He said to do. You got it? Hallelujah. All right.
Why does he say Bible morality has always been the goal?

He says “It wasn’t just to get you to believe. It wasn’t just to get you into heaven to live forever.” He says, “my belief in God does not help my family at all. It’s my obedience to God that blesses my children,” and “the demons believed, but they didn’t obey.”
Why does he say Bible morality has always been the goal?

Now, Bible morality has always been the goal. It wasn’t just to get you to believe. It wasn’t just to get you into heaven to live forever. Bible morality has always been the goal. We showed you that in the last four lessons, when we talked about the supernatural God and Bible that we have, when we talked about the mysteries hidden from the foundation of the world, and so forth. Bible morality has always been the goal, not you just believing. I’ve told you many a time, my belief in God does not help my family at all. It’s my obedience to God that blesses my
How does the Bible define eternal life? (John 17:3)

He says to understand a word you go “where the Bible defines how the Bible is using that word.” He reads “This is eternal life, that you may know God, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom God has sent,” and says “all they basically leave us with is eternal life as you die and you go to hell for eternity… or heaven for eternity.”
How does the Bible define eternal life? (John 17:3)

children. Okay, blessing is my merit, doing what is right. It is what’s going to help my community. Remember, the demons believed, but they didn’t obey. Now, the other side of eternal life. You can go to your Hebrew and Greek all day, and I do. I want to make sure I’m using the word in the right context and so forth, but I have to go to the Bible definition, where the Bible defines how the Bible is using that word. All right, now here is the Bible definition of eternal life. Are you ready for this? John 17:3: And this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent.
What does the demon’s answer in Acts 19 show? (Acts 19:15)

He says that “a lot of preachers” mimic other preachers, and “you can’t get it by pretending you got it.” He retells how the sons tried to cast out a demon in the name of Jesus that Paul preached and the demon answered, “Who in the world are you?”

this. Acts 19:15: “The evil spirit answered and said, ‘Jesus I know, and Paul I know, but who in the world are you?’” See, these sons of [unclear], who wanted to cast out demons, they were mimicking Paul. And that’s what a lot of preachers do. They go to channel 40, and they go to TV and radio, and they go to the Christian bookstore, and they mimic other preachers. Amen. And some of them don’t have anything to mimic, and the ones that do have something to mimic, you can’t get it by pretending you got it. Wow, that was a good statement. And we’ve got a lot of miming going on in the church world. We’re mimicking the real thing when we need to possess the real thing. Could that be an amen? Acts 19:15: And the evil spirit answered and said, “Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are you?”

So we’ve got to find out what the word “know” means. What does the Bible say the word “know” means? What’s the definition of the word “know” in the Bible? Your Hebrew and Greek won’t work here. All right, are you with me so far? Now 1 John 2:3: “By this we know that we know Him.” Now we have the definition of knowing God. It’s coming up. See, here’s God’s dictionary. He’s going to define what knowing God is. And remember, knowing God is what? Eternal life. Knowing God is eternal life. Say “eternal life.” Okay, so what is knowing God? “If we keep His commandments.” Oh, so this is eternal life, that we keep His commandments, God’s commandments and the commandments of Jesus Christ. Going back to John 17:3. Are you there? Hallelujah. John goes on to say this powerful statement: “He who says, ‘I know Him,’ and does not keep His commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in you.” He calls people a liar. That is just forbidden in America today. That’s just not politically correct. I get told quite a few times every year, nobody talks like that. When I tell people, you need to grow

1 John 2:3: Now by this we know that we know Him, if we keep His commandments. 1 John 2:4: He who says, “I know Him,” and does not keep His commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.

up, you’re going to hell, nobody talks like that. Well, the Bible talks that way. Okay, when you’re a liar, you are a liar. Ain’t that right? “He who says that Christ abides in him ought.” And the word “ought” is very powerful. Now here’s the Greek word they use. The word “ought” means very necessary, so necessary they use it as owing a debt. In other scriptures that word is used as owing a debt. I don’t walk like the ones on TV. I don’t walk after my parents and all that, only as they follow God. I am to walk after who? Jesus Christ. You see, and Jesus Christ became flesh. He was God in the flesh, and He walked, and He obeyed the commandments. Not one commandment did He break. So our example and our idol is who? Jesus Christ. And now, don’t get alarmed here, because immediately we can start condemning ourselves because we’re so short of Jesus. This is the difference between our opponents and us. We make mistakes, and we’re working on some flaws in our life, but we don’t justify it. We admit it’s wrong,
1 John 2:6: He who says he abides in Him ought himself also to walk just as He walked.

and we keep repenting and we keep confessing. They just say there’s nothing wrong with adultery, there’s nothing wrong with homosexuality, nothing wrong. You see, that’s the difference. So don’t go jumping on Christians that are growing in God. Christianity, the Bible says, starts at a baby stage, then we grow to a child stage, and to an adolescent stage, and then an adult stage, and into a fatherhood stage. And while we’re reaching the fatherhood stage, we’re still justified before God. We haven’t grown through some stages yet. Are you there? So see, that’s why the Bible says there’s no condemnation. Why? I am in the growing process. Yes, I’ve got some flaws, but I am pursuing the goal, and I’m not agreeing that wrong is right, even if I’m doing it.

Romans 8:1: There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus, who do not walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.

What do the two sides of eternal life look like in Matthew 7:21-23?

Amen. Yeah, don’t let that thing get you under guilt. Now, Bible morality is the other side of eternal life. That’s the bottom line. Doing what’s right is the other side of eternal life. What good does it do me to believe if I do not obey what Jesus said to do? Now, Matthew 7:21 really defines these two. The two sides are in Matthew 7:21: “Not all that say to Me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ shall enter into the kingdom of heaven.” They’re not going to get eternal life with Me, “but he that does the will of My Father, which is in heaven. Many will say unto Me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in Your name? Have we not cast out devils in Your name, and done miracles in Your name?’” You see, these people are believers, and God loves people, so He reaches people. God will, I’ve been in this thing, these uncalled, bad preachers seemingly get results when it’s just God honoring the faith and the seeking heart of those that are coming. How many of you know, if a miracle’s done, no minister gets credit for it? They can’t do it. And remember, Judas did miracles, and he was a

Matthew 7:21-22: “Not everyone who says to Me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ shall enter the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of My Father in heaven. Many will say to Me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in Your name, cast out demons in Your name, and done many wonders in Your name?’
Do miracles prove someone is right with God?

He says “you don’t measure them by whether they do miracles and cast out demons. You measure them by their fruit, their lifestyle, how they live.” He says those in Matthew 7 “believed, but they didn’t know God.”

betrayer. So you don’t measure them by whether they do miracles and cast out demons. You measure them by their fruit, their lifestyle, how they live. Are they obeying God’s Word? Hallelujah. So you have the two illustrations right here: they were believers, and they had results as believers. And this is what American Christians, because they haven’t been taught the Bible. See, they get the same junk whether in the bookstore or on TV, that American Christians can’t make common sense decisions about things. They don’t know how to answer things. Am I right? Yeah. idea. Therefore, and then He goes right into the parable of the wise man building his house on the rock. “For this reason, whosoever hears these sayings of Mine,” and what? And what? Matthew 7:24: “Therefore whoever hears these sayings of Mine, and does them, I will liken him to a wise man who built his house on the rock: Matthew 7:20: Therefore by their fruits you will know them.
