items.d: In “The Power of Restoration Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer compares God’s people to Pharaoh’s trained horses, then explains that everyone needs restoration because sin destroys. He covers the ashes of…
p: In “The Power of Restoration Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer compares God’s people to Pharaoh’s trained horses, then explains that everyone needs restoration because sin destroys. He covers the ashes of Ezekiel 28, “dishonest trade,” backsliding, and how he says sin corrects people through alcohol, sexual sin and disease.
Why does God compare his people to a filly among Pharaoh’s horses? (Song of Solomon 1:9)

He explains that Pharaoh’s horses were trained to pull the king’s chariot and to go to war, and “they never ran from adversity.” He says God likens us to them, so many of his people “are scared to death of a little problem,” but we are “new creatures” being fashioned to “lead the king down to the streets.”
Why does God compare his people to a filly among Pharaoh’s horses? (Song of Solomon 1:9)

Before we get into the topic of restoration, I want to show you in the Bible one of the things that God compares his people to. Song of Solomon 1:9, “I have compared you, my love, to a filly among Pharaoh’s horses.” Now, Pharaoh would go out and he would get horses. Horses ran around in the wild, and they learned to tame them and they learned to train them. And a chariot back in those days was like an automobile today, okay, and also they used them in war. It was like a tank in war. And so these horses were trained to pull the king in his golden chariot, and they were trained to go to war, and in war they would go in there with swords clashing, arrows flying all around, all the noise, all the racket, people dying, they’d get hit by arrows, they’d be wounded, and these horses would just keep doing what they’re supposed to do. They never ran from adversity, they never ran from being afraid of the enemy. Are you out there, church? Warfare was no problem to them, and when there was no war going on, they had no problem pulling the king, pulling the king, Alleluia, making a way for the king. And that’s what God likens us to here. And so many of God’s people are scared to death of a little problem. They’re scared to death of warfare. They’re scared to death of any kind of opposition, any kind of challenge or adversity in their life, and they shouldn’t be. We were born again, new creatures, old things are passed away. It doesn’t matter what we were, we are new people today that God is fashioning into a horse that can lead in battle and lead the king down to the streets where the people bow to the king. Don’t you want to be that kind of church where you bring the presence of the king and people bow before the king? And when war comes, you’re not afraid of war.
Why does God compare his people to a filly among Pharaoh’s horses? (Song of Solomon 1:9)
Song of Solomon 1:9: I have compared you, my love, To my filly among Pharaoh’s chariots.
Why is being in the king’s barn better than being independent?

He says wild horses were affected by parasites, disease and famine, while those in the king’s barn were groomed, medicated and fed. He says “being independent isn’t always the best way,” and the church, likened “as a female,” should submit to “the king’s bridle.”
Why is being in the king’s barn better than being independent?

Now, he would take these wild horses. When you’re a horse is wild, see, they can do what they want to do, and that’s what a lot of Christians are. They just still want to do what they want to do. But when you’re out in the wild and no one to take care of these horses, we’re affected by parasites: the fly, the tick, the flea, some other chickers, and these things would carry diseases, and horses would die from disease. But see, when you were brought into the king’s barn, the king had groomers to take care of those things, and these guys were kept from the parasites, and there was also inner parasites that they would drink water or whatever and get these little microorganisms in them and it would kill them. But when they were in the king’s barn, none of this happened. Out in the wild, when famine coming along and there was no rain and so forth and the springs dried up and there was no food to eat, the horses in Pharaoh’s barn ate well, they had plenty of water, but the independent horses, they starved, they got bony, they couldn’t find water. So see, being independent isn’t always the best way, is it? Hallelujah. And in Pharaoh’s barn he took care of them with medicine when they were sick. Those horses were his most prized possession, and those horses were always groomed, they always looked good, and they were trained, and they submitted to the king’s bridle. And church, that’s why he likened you to a filly. The church is illustrated in the Bible as a female. In Pharaoh’s army, Pharaoh was a king, Jesus is the King of kings. Are you with me? Hallelujah. Do you really want to be a church that brings the presence of the king where people worship him? Hallelujah. That’s what we’re likened to. But to attain to all these things, we’ve got to hear this message of restoration.
What is restoration, and why do even “good” people need it?

He says restoration “just simply means to remake a wreck like new,” and that God wants to make “that wreck better than new.” He says even good people need it because “there is none good but God,” and compares it to a car that needs fixing and cleaning “every once in a while.”
What is restoration, and why do even “good” people need it?

Restoration just simply means to remake a wreck like new. You know, you take an old car, and Mr. Barnes just had his car detailed and it looks like it just came off the assembly line, but also when he has bad brakes he has to fix it and so forth, he has to keep the repairs up. And when people don’t keep the repairs up, the car winds up being a piece of junk, it’s in the junkyard, and then somebody that likes that car will go and get it, the 1957 Chevrolet or something, you know, they would get and they would restore it back to like new. That’s what restoration is. And see, we, through our own independent decision and doing things, we destroy our life, but God wants to restore it. He wants to make that wreck better than new. This is the promise, this is what he wants to do. Now, why do all people need restoration, even good people? People say, “Well, I’m good, I don’t, you know, I don’t need restored.” But the Bible says that none, there is none good but God. Jesus said that when they called him good, he said, “Hold on, why do you call me good? There’s none good but the Father.” The God is the good one. And Jesus was God, but if he would have took recognition above God, then he would have sinned, and he can’t sin. Hallelujah. So us good people, what need restore? Mr. Barnes’s truck is not a wreck, but it needs fixing every once in a while. Amen. It needs cleaning.
What is restoration, and why do even “good” people need it?
Luke 18:19: So Jesus said to him, “Why do you call Me good? No one is good but One, that is, God.
Why do all people need restoration? (Romans 3:23; Ecclesiastes 7:6)

He says “all have violated God’s word,” and “the wages of sin is death or destruction or ruin.” He reads Ecclesiastes 7:6, saying the crackling thorns under a pot are “dying … destroying itself,” as fools do when they are “out there partying and doing their own thing.”
Why do all people need restoration? (Romans 3:23; Ecclesiastes 7:6)

Romans 3:23: “All have sinned.” How many? All have violated God’s word. Sin is the violation of God’s word. What? Sin. Yes, it’s the violation. All have violated God’s word. How many raise your hand and say, “Ah, that’s me, I’ve done it”? Now, the wages of sin is death, or destruction, or ruin, the payment for sinning. It’s going to destroy your life, okay, and so you need to be restored. Ecclesiastes 7:6: “For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of a fool.” We brought this Scripture last time we taught on this subject. The wood underneath the pot makes a noise. It’s the only time it makes noise, but it’s dying. It’s dying, it’s destroying itself, and that’s what fools do when they’re out there partying and doing their own thing. Oh yeah, they’re making all this joke and laughter and everything, but they’re dying, because sin destroys.
Why do all people need restoration? (Romans 3:23; Ecclesiastes 7:6)

Romans 3:23: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, Romans 6:23: For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord. Ecclesiastes 7:6: For like the crackling of thorns under a pot, So is the laughter of the fool. This also is vanity.
What do the “ashes” in Ezekiel 28:18 mean?

He says “ashes are worthless,” and “nobody wants anything to do with somebody that’s destroyed their life.” He says we should not wait to turn into total ashes: “you want to … restore your life at the small mistake,” and God “keeps fixing you just like new, not just forgiving you.”
What do the “ashes” in Ezekiel 28:18 mean?

Ezekiel 28:18: “By your many sins and dishonest trade you defile your sanctuaries, so I made a fire to come out from you and consume you, and I reduced you to ashes on the ground in the sight of all who were watching.” Now, ashes are worthless, and right quick some people are going to say, “No, I can put them in my garden.” Yeah, you just keep putting them in the garden, you just keep throwing them in the garden, let’s see what happens. Now, here’s some ashes. Now, how many like to fellowship with ashes? You want a handful? Oh, come on, come on, how about you, you want a handful of ashes? No? You want to paint your face with ashes? No. See, nobody wants ashes. Nobody wants anything to do with somebody that’s destroyed their life. They’re worthless. They just get blown with the wind. Whatever’s going on in the world, they just follow it, because they have no substance. Not all of us destroy our lives to where we’re ashes. We destroy part of our life as ashes, we get burned and we get scorched. But like Mr. Barnes’s car, you don’t want to wait to turn into total ashes. You want to what? Restore your life at the small mistake. So see, all of us need restoration, even us good people who think, and we are, we’re doing pretty good. We still need what? Some restoring in our lives. Maybe we didn’t say the right thing yesterday, maybe we had the wrong attitude two days ago, we got to what? Get that fixed. And God promised to fix it. And young people, please listen: don’t you ever listen to the enemy or anyone that tells you you’re too bad, you know, you’ve been up and down too many times.
What do the “ashes” in Ezekiel 28:18 mean?

Ezekiel 28:18: “You defiled your sanctuaries By the multitude of your iniquities, By the iniquity of your trading; Therefore I brought fire from your midst; It devoured you, And I turned you to ashes upon the earth In the sight of all who saw you.
How do we defile the sanctuary, which is us? (1 Corinthians 3:16)

He says when God says “your many sins have defiled your sanctuary,” “he’s talking about you. You’re the temple of God,” and “God doesn’t like to live in defiled temples.” He says God keeps “fixing you just like new.”
How do we defile the sanctuary, which is us? (1 Corinthians 3:16)

God keeps restoring, he keeps restoring, he keeps fixing you just like new, not just forgiving you, he fixes you. Are you with me now? You understand that? And so we destroy our life and God can restore it back. Now remember, we defiled our sanctuaries. The Bible says in 1 Corinthians 3:16, “You are the temple of God and the Spirit of God dwells in you. If anyone defiles the temple of God, God will destroy him, for the temple of God is holy, whose temple you are.” So when it says “your many sins have defiled your sanctuary,” he’s talking about you. You’re the temple of God, and you’re doing things that is defiling the sanctuary. God doesn’t like to live in defiled temples. Hallelujah. Now, “your dishonest trade.” Let me tell you what dishonest trade is. You’re thinking it’s somebody that’s charging you more for a loaf of bread than they should be. That isn’t the kind of trade God’s talking about. You see, he died on the cross for your sins. He took your sins to the cross, and in exchange for your sins he gave you eternal life, but he also asked you to do a few things.
How do we defile the sanctuary, which is us? (1 Corinthians 3:16)
1 Corinthians 3:16: Do you not know that you are the temple of God and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?
What is “dishonest trade,” and why assemble with other believers?

He says dishonest trade is saying, “I accept your death on the cross for my sins, but I’m going to live the way I want.” He says God asks us to “repent and not sin anymore” and to assemble, because “they that go grow,” and “you took his eternal life … but you didn’t give him back what he asked for.”
What is “dishonest trade,” and why assemble with other believers?

He asked you to repent and not sin anymore. Dishonest trade is saying, “Okay, I, God, I accept your death on the cross for my sins, but I’m going to live the way I want.” See, that’s dishonest trade, and it’s going to destroy you. You’re going to become ashes. Do you understand? God says to assemble in the house of God. “Well, I don’t have to go to church.” You won’t find that in the Bible, you know. Do you realize when you get up in the morning, all over America, all over the world, and you assemble in church, that you’re a sign saying to the nations, “I am a follower of Jesus Christ, I’m a follower of the Bible”? Do you realize that is expression of obedience that they see in you, let alone when you come and he inhabits the praises of his people? See, when we gather together and praise him, the new wine is found in the cluster, not one grape but a cluster of grapes. When we come together, God promises to do things, and it says that if you’re going to grow, in Psalms, you’re going to have to go to the house of God. They that go, grow. Say it: they that go grow. You see, that’s dishonest trade. He asked you, I mean, he gave you forgiveness of sin, eternal life, and he asked you to do some things so you can be a light to the world, and then you don’t do them. That’s dishonest trade. You took his eternal life, you took his forgiveness, you, you know, you took all the things you wanted, but you didn’t give him back what he asked for. That’s dishonest trade. Do you young people understand that a lot of Christians are living a life of dishonest trade? And so what happens? Destruction comes in their life.
What is “dishonest trade,” and why assemble with other believers?

Psalm 22:3: But You are holy, Enthroned in the praises of Israel. Isaiah 65:8: Thus says the LORD: “As the new wine is found in the cluster, And one says, ‘Do not destroy it, For a blessing is in it,’ So will I do for My servants’ sake, That I may not destroy them all.
What is a backslider, and why must we “exercise” righteousness? (Hebrews 11:25; Jeremiah 2:19; Galatians 6:7)

He says we can enjoy sin “for a season” but “you’re going to pay the price,” and that “standing still in the kingdom is still … going backwards, because he’s moving.” He says sowing to the flesh reaps corruption, and “exercise is spelled W-R-K, work,” because “you got to put some effort into it.”
What is a backslider, and why must we “exercise” righteousness? (Hebrews 11:25; Jeremiah 2:19; Galatians 6:7)

Hebrews 11:25: you can enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season. You know, you can get away with it, it’s, you know, there’s no payment for a while. You see, there’s no payment, but after a while, when the season’s over, you’re going to pay the price. Jeremiah 2:19: “Your own wickedness will” what? “Correct you, and your backslidings will” what? Now, the Bible tells us what a backslider is. The Bible says a backslider is filled with his own ways. Those independent people that do what they want to do, they come to Christ, they took his eternal life, they took his forgiveness, but then they do what they want to do. They backslid, they didn’t keep their word. Instead of going forward and following Jesus, they went backwards, or they just stood there and he’s moving forward, so what? They’re going backwards. Standing still in the kingdom is still what? Going backwards, because he’s moving. Are you with me now? Now, young people, if your sin corrects you and your backslidings rebuke you (is another word for correction), then how does that work? In Galatians 6:7 it says, “Whatsoever a man sows, that he will also reap, for he who sows to his flesh shall of the flesh reap corruption.” When a body dies, it decays, just like the ashes, the wood and the fire, it turns, the ashes, the body turns to ashes back to the dust through just natural decay. And so when we sow to our flesh, we’re going to reap corruption, but when we sow to the Spirit, we will reap everlasting life. And so, as we heard Friday night, we got to exercise the things of God to get strong in the things of God. You see, this message of “not of works, lest any man should boast” has been taken to an extreme, that God’s people in America think they don’t have to do anything. And yet if you don’t exercise righteousness, you’re not going to get strong in righteousness. If you don’t exercise godliness, you’re not going to get strong in godliness. And exercise is spelled W-R-K, work. You got to put some effort into it. You’ve got to apply yourself. Amen.
What is a backslider, and why must we “exercise” righteousness? (Hebrews 11:25; Jeremiah 2:19; Galatians 6:7)

Hebrews 11:25: choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God than to enjoy the passing pleasures of sin, Jeremiah 2:19: Your own wickedness will correct you, And your backslidings will rebuke you. Know therefore and see that it is an evil and bitter thing That you have forsaken the LORD your God, And the fear of Me is not in you,” Says the Lord GOD of hosts. Proverbs 14:14: The backslider in heart will be filled with his own ways, But a good man will be satisfied from above. Galatians 6:7: Do not be deceived, God is not mocked; for whatever a man sows, that he will also reap. Ephesians 2:9: not of works, lest anyone should boast.

He reads Proverbs 23:29-35 about misery, wounds and addiction from wine, and shows videos of a person being bitten by a snake as a picture of messing with dangerous things. He says “it’s addictive,” and “you’re going to mess around with dangerous things, you’re going to get destroyed.”

Now, Proverbs 23:29, let’s look at how sin corrects you: “Who has misery? Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has contention? Who has complaints? Who has wounds without a cause? Who has redness of eyes? Those who linger long at the wine, those who go in search of mixed wine.” See, sin’s self-exposure and self-correction. People that want to drink, they’re going to bring misery to their life and all these things, and we know it’s true. Somebody sent me a report from the federal government, the Department of Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services, that in 2006, 51% of Americans used alcohol. Only 51%. And we make it an issue in the church. My figures were 39% were not yet drinking alcohol, so I was glad for the, we just gained 10% by a different survey. So almost half of America is smart enough to what? Stay away from alcohol and drugs and those things. Why? Because they bring destruction. You can see what happens in people’s life that do it. Proverbs 23:32, look at this guy over here. He’s got a snake, and they’re having a birthday party for the snake, and he’s going to let this snake touch this little baby, okay, because he’s had this snake for like ten years and no problems, and he’s down there showing this snake off and letting people wrap it around them and all this stuff. Now, just a couple of minutes ago this snake was put right up in the face of a baby, but watch what happens right here. Get ready here it comes. Bam! Now, what if that would have happened to that baby? Watch him spit teeth out here. See them teeth fall? The snake’s teeth went right into his mouth. See, young people, you mess around with dangerous animals. A trainer just last week got killed by an elephant that turned on him. These are wild animals, they’re destructive, and you start messing around. Look at this guy over here, I kept him rolling, you know, he’s trying to show how big, bad, brave he is, and that snake just decided to take a hunk out of him. Are you there? You see, and this is what the Bible says. You know, you’re going to mess around with dangerous things, you’re going to get destroyed. And so he says, “At last it bites like a serpent and stings like a viper. Your eyes shall behold strange women, and your heart will utter perverse things.” That’s sin correcting you. Proverbs 23:34: “You will be like one who lies down in the midst of the sea, at the top of the mast, saying, They struck me, but I was not hurt. They beat me, but I felt it not. And when I wake, I’ll seek another drink.” It’s addictive.

Proverbs 23:29-30: Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has contentions? Who has complaints? Who has wounds without cause? Who has redness of eyes? Those who linger long at the wine, Those who go in search of mixed wine. Proverbs 23:32: At the last it bites like a serpent, And stings like a viper. Proverbs 23:34-35: Yes, you will be like one who lies down in the midst of the sea, Or like one who lies at the top of the mast, saying: “They have struck me, but I was not hurt; They have beaten me, but I did not feel it. When shall I awake, that I may seek another drink?”
What does he say about alcohol and sexual sin? (Proverbs 31:5; Proverbs 7:22-23)

He says “alcohol perverts justice,” that you “make bad decisions,” and that drinking makes casual sex easier. He reads Proverbs about a young man led “as a fool to the correction of the stocks,” “till a dart strikes through his liver,” and says his decision “is going to bring correction.”
What does he say about alcohol and sexual sin? (Proverbs 31:5; Proverbs 7:22-23)

Proverbs 31:5 says that alcohol perverts justice. You make bad decisions, you make bad judgments. Over here is a picture of a woman before you drink. Oh, hag. And here she is after a drink, she looks like the queen of [unclear]. Man. And I got that off a secular site talking about, you know, it’s easy to have sex once you got a few drinks in you, with anybody. That’s what they were talking about. Then you wake up the next morning and there’s a hag next to you. Ah, God. Okay, here’s another one: sex. Here’s the dumb guy, young, young guy, you know, flexing his muscles into bodybuilding, get to the gym, showing off, don’t wear shirts, because you want these girls to see your muscles and everything, you know, and these girls are showing their cleavage, you know, and they’re showing their thighs and moving around because they know that just gets guys, [unclear]. So Proverbs says, “Why, my son, be overcome and embraced by the bosom, the breast, of an immoral woman? She is loud, she is stubborn, her feet abide not in her house. She says, Let’s take our fill of love.” And then it says, “He goes as a fool to the correction of the stocks.” See, his decision is going to bring correction, “till a dart strikes through his liver. He knows not that it is for his life.” There are three venereal, sexually transmitted diseases that affect the liver. Syphilis is one, [unclear] is another, and, uh, I forgot the other one. Back in the old days people died from syphilis, okay. A lot of Christopher Columbus’s crew died from syphilis, just having sex, taking advantage of the natives and so forth, and you can read this stuff in history.
What does he say about alcohol and sexual sin? (Proverbs 31:5; Proverbs 7:22-23)

Proverbs 31:5: Lest they drink and forget the law, And pervert the justice of all the afflicted. Proverbs 7:22-23: Immediately he went after her, as an ox goes to the slaughter, Or as a fool to the correction of the stocks, Till an arrow struck his liver. As a bird hastens to the snare, He did not know it would cost his life.
What statistics and warnings does he give about sexually transmitted diseases, AIDS and the military?

He says one out of two people in America “have had a sexually transmitted disease or have one,” and that new diseases appeared as “almost a brand new venereal disease every year” after the sexual revolution. He says AIDS deaths come from “homosexual activities” (his claim), opposes homosexuals in the military, and says to “follow right and not compromise the word of God” even if “you’ll lose friends.”
What statistics and warnings does he give about sexually transmitted diseases, AIDS and the military?

But now, see, they have antibiotics for it and you can survive, now you just got to put up with it the rest of your life. As I said before, one out of two people in America have had a sexually transmitted disease or have one. 39% of those sexually transmitted diseases are incurable. They can never be cured, we don’t have the medicine to cure them yet, and so they have to live with, you see, the sexual revolution came on in the 1960s, but there’s been almost a brand new venereal disease every year from that date. Before the sixties there was only three basic sexually transmitted diseases. Now there’s almost forty, almost a new one every year, and some of them are incurable, there’s nothing you can do. And of course AIDS brings death, and our great President Obama wants homosexuals to go into the military. 600,000 people have died from AIDS and 75% of those is directly from homosexual activities, 20,000 new cases a year, and he wants to put these guys in our military. Our politicians aren’t thinking right, folks. And the Egyptians are rising up against their dictator and said, “We’ve had enough of you,” and somewhere in America, America’s got to rise up and say, “We’ve had enough, we got to change things.” So they’re going to go in, they’re going to spread, home, AIDS, and you’re going to be in a shower with a guy looking at you. I wouldn’t want that, and so they’d have to drag me into the military if I was a young man. Now, that’s blunt, but it’s important that you know this stuff. You know, remember Noah and them did not follow public policy, they followed right. And it doesn’t matter how many people are following right, it matters that you are. Amen. I don’t care, you’ll lose friends over this, you’ll lose family members, that’s their choice. But you got to follow right and not compromise the word of God.
What does he say Pharaoh’s horses did in war?
He says they were trained to pull the king and “to go to war,” and “these horses would just keep doing what they’re supposed to do.”
What does he say the church should be like?
He says “don’t you want to be that kind of church where you bring the presence of the king and people bow before the king?” and that “when war comes, you’re not afraid of war.”
What does he say happened to wild horses compared to Pharaoh’s horses?
He says in famine “the horses in Pharaoh’s barn ate well” but “the independent horses, they starved, they got bony,” so “being independent isn’t always the best way.”
What does restoration mean according to this message?
He says it “just simply means to remake a wreck like new,” and that God “wants to make that wreck better than new.”
Does he say anyone is good?
He says “there is none good but God,” and that Jesus said, “why do you call me good? There’s none good but the Father.”
What does he say the wages of sin are?
He says “the wages of sin is death or destruction or ruin, the payment for sinning,” and that “it’s going to destroy your life.”
What does “the crackling of thorns under a pot” mean?
He says the wood under the pot makes noise, “but it’s dying,” and that fools are “making all this joke and laughter and everything, but they’re dying, because sin destroys.”
Why does he use ashes as an illustration?
He says “nobody wants ashes. Nobody wants anything to do with somebody that’s destroyed their life,” and “they just get blown with the wind.”
Does he say God only forgives?
No. He says God keeps “fixing you just like new, not just forgiving you, he fixes you.”
Why does he say to go to church?
He says “when we come together, God promises to do things,” and “they that go grow,” and that assembling is “a sign saying to the nations, I am a follower of Jesus Christ.”
What does he say a backslider is?
He says “a backslider is filled with his own ways,” people who “took his forgiveness” and then “do what they want to do. They backslid, they didn’t keep their word.”
Does he say works are needed?
He says the “not of works, lest any man should boast” message “has been taken to an extreme,” and that “if you don’t exercise righteousness, you’re not going to get strong in righteousness.”
What alcohol statistic does he give?
He says a federal report said “in 2006, 51% of Americans used alcohol,” and that “almost half of America is smart enough to … stay away from alcohol and drugs.”
What does he say about sexually transmitted diseases?

He says “one out of two people in America have had a sexually transmitted disease or have one,” and that before the sixties “there was only three basic sexually transmitted diseases. Now there’s almost forty.”
What does he say we should do even if it costs us friends?
He says “Noah and them did not follow public policy, they followed right,” and “it doesn’t matter how many people are following right, it matters that you are,” even if “you’ll lose friends.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer says sin brings correction, then teaches from Isaiah 61 and Luke 4 on the process of restoration: good tidings to the poor, beauty for ashes, the oil of joy and the…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer says sin brings correction, then teaches from Isaiah 61 and Luke 4 on the process of restoration: good tidings to the poor, beauty for ashes, the oil of joy and the garment of praise. He says God’s plan is to restore people so they become trees of righteousness who bring honor to Christ, and he shares accounts of safety in Christ.
Does sin bring correction into our lives?

He says “a lot of things you do in life are going to bring correction,” not just sex and alcohol: steal or run with a gang and “you’re going to wind up in jail.” He says “that’s how sin corrects you,” and that most people don’t take the correction, “they just get harder.”
Does sin bring correction into our lives?

Now here it is: “a fool to the correction of the stocks.” A lot of things you do in life are going to bring correction, not just, not just sex and alcohol. You know, you’re going to wind up in jail if you go steal. You’re going to wind up in jail, that’s the bottom line. You want to hang out with a gang, you’re going to wind up in jail, you’re going to destroy your life. Are you with me? See, that’s how sin corrects you. And the amazing thing is that most people don’t [unclear] the correction, they just get harder.
Does sin bring correction into our lives?
Proverbs 7:22: Immediately he went after her, as an ox goes to the slaughter, Or as a fool to the correction of the stocks,
What does he say about people who have money but no self-control?

He lists a group of public figures and says “all these have one thing in common: they all have an incurable sexually transmitted disease.” He says “these people have the bucks and everything else, but they have no self-control.” These are his claims about named people and have not been verified here.
What does he say about people who have money but no self-control?

Here is Mike [unclear], Fred [unclear], Brad Pitt, Bill Clinton, Justin Timberlake, Britney Spears, Lindsay Lohan, Katie Holmes, [unclear] Jackson, and [unclear]. All these have one thing in common: they all have an incurable sexually transmitted disease. It’s incurable. This is just 10 of them, there’s whole kinds of them. Now these people have the bucks and everything else, but they have no self-control. Now, Katie Holmes just married Tom Cruise a few years ago, so guess what? Tom Cruise has joined the ranks. He should have stuck with his first wife.
What does Deuteronomy 21:20 teach about rebellious children and their parents?

He says the passage has parents taking a stubborn, rebellious son who “will not obey our voice” to the city officials, and tells young people that parents who are “any kind of parents at all” will draw the line and correct them. He tells parents that if they live a loose life and want their kids to do right, “they’re going to know you’re a hypocrite.”
What does Deuteronomy 21:20 teach about rebellious children and their parents?

Deuteronomy 21:20: parents take their child to the city officials, the police department, and say, “Our son is stubborn, rebellious, he will not obey our voice, he’s a glutton and he’s a drunkard. Deal with him, he won’t listen to us, maybe he’ll listen to you.” In other words, young people, you start making decisions in your young life to be independent, like these wild horses. Your parents, if they’re any kind of parents at all, are going to come to a place where they draw the line and say, “No, this isn’t going to happen in this house, and you’re going to be corrected.” And if parents were smart, they’d correct it way before it came to this. Can I hear an amen? And parents, it’s the same way. You want to live a loose life and everything else, and then want your kids to do what’s right? They’re going to know you’re a hypocrite. You’re telling me to do one thing and you’re doing another. They’re going to rebel. Your sin will correct you, it’s going to bring problems. In a lot of families, how many here live in a family where there’s dissension and division and separation in the home? Really? That’s... all you guys are lying. Maybe you don’t understand what it is yet.
What does Deuteronomy 21:20 teach about rebellious children and their parents?
Deuteronomy 21:20: And they shall say to the elders of his city, ‘This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious; he will not obey our voice; he is a glutton and a drunkard.’
Why does he warn against unsettling and dividing the church? (Acts 15:24)

Reading Acts 15:24, he says some who left the church at Jerusalem without permission “started saying things” and caused problems, and Paul brought them back to be confronted. He says people who “split the church, divide the church” will be dealt with, and that “God can bring things to correct you.”
Why does he warn against unsettling and dividing the church? (Acts 15:24)

Acts 15:24: “We have heard that some of you went out from us, have troubled you, some who went out from us have troubled you with words, unsettling your souls.” They were in the church there at Jerusalem, and they left without permission, went out and started saying things without permission, and it started causing problems wherever they went. And so Paul got them together and brought them right back down to the church in Jerusalem and confronted them. And folks, there’s people always want to get a hair in their nose, some kind of wind of doctrine, some kind of selfish doctrine, and split the church, divide the church, and make a mess of things and unsettle people and trouble them, and the church has to deal with it. So if you’re a church member and you want to do unsettling things, it’s going to bring destruction to you. I, I would never advise you to say anything about God’s church. He don’t mess around. You can die early, you can get sickly. God can bring things to correct you, and let me tell you, you don’t want that. Hallelujah. And remember, we all need restoration, right? Yes. So there’s people in there that we call hypocrites. They, well, they’re there hopefully because they want to change, and if you had any maturity you’d hang in there and be a source that added to the atmosphere of their change. Can I hear an amen? That was a good statement right there.
Why does he warn against unsettling and dividing the church? (Acts 15:24)

Acts 15:24: Since we have heard that some who went out from us have troubled you with words, unsettling your souls, saying, “You must be circumcised and keep the law”—to whom we gave no such commandment—
How should we treat hypocrites in the church, and who should we give to?

He says there are hypocrites in the church who are there “hopefully because they want to change,” and that a mature person would “hang in there and be a source that added to the atmosphere of their change.” He says people who want your money and possessions and want you to feel sorry for them should be handled by going “through church leadership to give anyone anything.”
How should we treat hypocrites in the church, and who should we give to?

Hallelujah. But when you got to stay home because there’s nothing but hypocrites in the church, and there’s some people down there that, that you’re one of those people we got to put up with. You, and they do it with words. Watch the words. And also, people want your money and they want possessions. They want you to feel sorry for them and give them things. You should always go through church leadership to give anyone anything. They are parasites that need changed. Hallelujah.
What is the process of restoration in Isaiah 61 (Luke 4)?

He says Jesus quoted this passage from Isaiah in Luke: He anointed me to “preach, teach, speak” good tidings to the poor, heal the brokenhearted, and proclaim liberty to the captives. He says “we preach restoration,” then “the word heals and sets free,” and “you don’t need a recovery group or a 12-step procedure,” because “the word and the Spirit will revolutionize your life.”
What is the process of restoration in Isaiah 61 (Luke 4)?

Now, the process of restoration. Here we go. “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me,” Jesus quoted this from Isaiah in the book of Luke, “for He has anointed me to preach.” What’s the word? Preach, teach, speak. “Good tidings to the poor.” What do the poor need more than money, more than food? The word. They need the word. The truth of God’s word is what they need, because it will change their life tomorrow and they won’t be poor. And beside that, it’s talking about poor spiritually, and I’m lacking spiritual stuff. “Heal the brokenhearted, proclaim,” say the word, proclaim is just like preach, teach, speak, “liberty to the captives.” He’s preaching, speaking, proclaiming, opening a prison to those who are bound, “to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of the vengeance of our God.” This is the process of restoration. We preach restoration. We preach God’s a healer. We preach God’s a liberator. We preach God as a mender of the brokenhearted. We preach this stuff, and then the word heals and sets free. Can I hear an amen? And you don’t need a recovery group or a 12-step procedure or anything. The word and the Spirit will revolutionize your life.
What is the process of restoration in Isaiah 61 (Luke 4)?

Luke 4:18-19: “The Spirit of the LORD is upon Me, Because He has anointed Me To preach the gospel to the poor; He has sent Me to heal the brokenhearted, To proclaim liberty to the captives And recovery of sight to the blind, To set at liberty those who are oppressed; To proclaim the acceptable year of the LORD.” Isaiah 61:1-3: “The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon Me, Because the LORD has anointed Me To preach good tidings to the poor; He has sent Me to heal the brokenhearted, To proclaim liberty to the captives, And the opening of the prison to those who are bound; To proclaim the acceptable year of the LORD, And the day of vengeance of our God; To comfort all who mourn, To console those who mourn in Zion, To give them beauty for ashes, The oil of joy for mourning, The garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; That they may be called trees of righteousness, The planting of the LORD, that He may be glorified.”

He says ashes can’t be made into anything, but God says “my restoration is so powerful” that even if you have destroyed your life and there is no sign of life in you, “I can make your life beautiful … but better than before.” He says “we don’t need psychology, we need the preaching of the word and the move of the Spirit,” and that the oil of joy means God gives joy “right where you’re at.”

“To comfort and console those who mourn, to give them beauty for ashes.” Now here we go. What can we make out of ashes? Nothing. There is nothing. There, there’s nothing we can do. Now, this partly burnt piece of wood, we could use it for something, even if it was just a stake in the ground, it’s usable. But the ashes are gone. And God says, what, my restoration is so powerful, young people, listen to me, my restoration is so powerful that if you have destroyed your life and there’s not a sign of life in you, I can make your life beautiful, not just like I, not just like it was before, because you weren’t beautiful before, but better than before. I’ll make your life look like mine. Beautiful. Hallelujah. Now, that’s our promise. We, we don’t need psychology, we need the preaching of the word and the move of the Spirit in His church. How many would like beauty for ashes? You know, maybe we’re just partly burned, but you want to be beautified back. Amen. “The oil of joy for mourning.” Oh, you had a rough home and a rough life, and oh man, your mom and dad were this and your mom and dad were that, and the neighborhood you lived in was this and the neighborhood you lived in was that, and it just depressed you and caused sorrow. God says, I’ll give you joy. I won’t even take you out of the thing, I’ll give you joy right where you’re at, then I’ll take you out. It’s easy to lead someone that can smile.

Isaiah 61:3: To console those who mourn in Zion, To give them beauty for ashes, The oil of joy for mourning, The garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; That they may be called trees of righteousness, The planting of the LORD, that He may be glorified.”
What does God give for the spirit of heaviness and depression?

He says God offers “the garment of praise” for the spirit of heaviness. He says people can mistreat you and, “if you don’t have that power of the Holy Ghost in you you can get depressed,” and God says “I’ll come along and I’ll restore you.” He says people go to psychologists to get rid of depression, but “God has that as part of His restoration.” These are his views and not medical advice.
What does God give for the spirit of heaviness and depression?

“The garment of praise, honor, for the spirit of heaviness.” See, all these people are going to psychologists and everything else trying to get rid of depression. God has that as part of His restoration. Yes, people can cause pain in your life. People can, they can mistreat you, and they can cause you, if you don’t have that oil of joy, if you don’t have that power of the Holy Ghost in you, you can get depressed, you can get cast down. God said, I’ll come along and I’ll restore you, I’ll give you praise, praise and honor for that spirit of heaviness.
What are the two purposes of becoming “trees of righteousness”? (1 Chronicles 16:29)

He says the beauty God gives is “a righteous life,” and names two purposes: God makes you a tree of righteousness, and people see it and bring honor to God. He says you couldn’t do it on your own, and when people see God working in you, “they’re going to want it.”
What are the two purposes of becoming “trees of righteousness”? (1 Chronicles 16:29)

“And they will be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the Lord, that He may be glorified.” 1 Chronicles 16:29: “Worship the Lord in the beauty of holiness.” So the beauty that He wants to give you is a righteous life, a life that’s doing what is right. And so there’s two high purposes here, all right. He wants to make you a tree of righteousness, and He wants people to see that and bring honor to God, not you. Are you out there? See, you couldn’t do it on your own, but when you came to Christ, He worked it in you, and your testimony is, “Jesus changed my life.” See, that gives honor to Christ, who then are directed to Him by the change in your life. See, that’s the purpose. And if we don’t get changed, do they want what we got? No, they already got what we got. We got, if we haven’t been changed. But when they see God working in your life and making you a righteous person, a beautiful person, they’re going to want it, and that brings honor to Christ, because they got to come to Christ to get it, like you did. The prophets of restoration.
What are the two purposes of becoming “trees of righteousness”? (1 Chronicles 16:29)

Isaiah 61:3: To console those who mourn in Zion, To give them beauty for ashes, The oil of joy for mourning, The garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; That they may be called trees of righteousness, The planting of the LORD, that He may be glorified.” 1 Chronicles 16:29: Give to the LORD the glory due His name; Bring an offering, and come before Him. Oh, worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness!
What does God gain from restoring us?

He says those who are restored “bring honor to Christ and are used by Christ to restore others.” Reading that they will build the old ruins and repair the desolations, he says God gets honor and “people that are really the light of the world, that bring people to Christ just by their life.”
What does God gain from restoring us?

Okay, what does God profit from this? Well, simple. It goes on to say, “They shall build the old ruins,” rebuild them, restore them, “they shall raise up the former desolations, and repair the ruined cities, they will repair the desolations of many generations.” Those that get restored bring honor to Christ and are used by Christ to restore others. Now, don’t you think, church, it’s about time we thought of the full picture, the long picture, that if we can grow in God, other people will want what we got, and we can be a source to bring their life to a place of restoration? That’s the profit God gets out of it. He not only gets honor, he gets people that are really the light of the world, that bring people to Christ just by their life and the way they speak. Isn’t that beautiful?
What does God gain from restoring us?
Isaiah 61:4: And they shall rebuild the old ruins, They shall raise up the former desolations, And they shall repair the ruined cities, The desolations of many generations.
Is God’s plan for correction always restoration? (Jeremiah 27:22)

Reading Jeremiah 27:22, he says God put them in Babylon and dealt with them “over and over,” but “his whole plan was to what? Correct them, get them to come to their senses, and restore them back to being better than they were before.” He says this means God has “something more for me than just waiting for Jesus to come.”
Is God’s plan for correction always restoration? (Jeremiah 27:22)

Jeremiah 27:22: “They shall be carried to Babylon, until the day that I visit them, then I will restore them to this place.” God’s ultimate plan is to what? Restore. He corrected, he put them in Babylon, he came and he dealt with them over and over and over again, but his whole plan was to what? Correct them, get them to come to their senses, and restore them back to being better than they were before. Now that’s a great message. Message that God has something more for me than just waiting for Jesus to come.
Is God’s plan for correction always restoration? (Jeremiah 27:22)
Jeremiah 27:22: ‘They shall be carried to Babylon, and there they shall be until the day that I visit them,’ says the LORD. ‘Then I will bring them up and restore them to this place.’ ”
Will God avenge those who mistreat us? (Ezekiel 28:25)

He reads Ezekiel 28:25 about God punishing neighbors who maligned and mistreated Israel, and says the Bible tells us not to avenge, “but God will come along and … he’ll deal with it.” He says “you don’t have to punch anybody out,” just “stay calm,” though “you got to stand and confront what’s wrong.”
Will God avenge those who mistreat us? (Ezekiel 28:25)

He will also avenge us. Ezekiel 28:25: “The sovereign Lord says, when I gather the people of Israel from the nations where they have been scattered, I will show myself holy among them in the sight of the nations, and they will live in their own land which I gave to my servant Jacob, and they will live there in safety, and they will build houses and plant vineyards, and they will live in safety, when I inflict punishment on all their neighbors who maligned,” mistreated them, slandered them, criticized them, did things to hurt them, “then they will know that I am the Lord.” You see, doesn’t the scripture say, “Vengeance is mine, saith the Lord”? And the Bible tells us not to avenge, but God will come along and, what, he’ll deal with it. See, that’s what, you don’t have to punch anybody out. You don’t have to poison anybody. You don’t have to verbally attack anybody. Just stay calm. God will get them, and let me tell you, he knows how to get them to bring them to him. We can get him, but we cause them to run from him. Man, if that’s Christianity... And don’t get me wrong, you got to stand and confront what’s wrong. Hallelujah. Avenge, pay back.
Will God avenge those who mistreat us? (Ezekiel 28:25)

Ezekiel 28:25-26: ‘Thus says the Lord GOD: “When I have gathered the house of Israel from the peoples among whom they are scattered, and am hallowed in them in the sight of the Gentiles, then they will dwell in their own land which I gave to My servant Jacob. And they will dwell safely there, build houses, and plant vineyards; yes, they will dwell securely, when I execute judgments on all those around them who despise them. Then they shall know that I am the LORD their God.” ’ ” Romans 12:19: Beloved, do not avenge yourselves, but rather give place to wrath; for it is written, “Vengeance is Mine, I will repay,” says the Lord.
What does he say happens to people who attack God’s church?

He says “don’t mess around with God’s church,” and that if you are “slandering and attacking and verbally doing things to harm his church,” things will come in your life, your children’s life or your finances “to get your attention.” He says God does it “so he corrects you so you can change.”
What does he say happens to people who attack God’s church?

And I want to tell you again, I would strongly advise you, don’t mess around with God’s church. God has some strong principles, and he will correct you. You might be able to brag and say, “I don’t commit adultery, I don’t steal, I don’t kill.” But if you are slandering and attacking and verbally doing things to harm his church, I’ll guarantee you he will deal with you, and things will come in your life, or in your children’s life, or in your finances, or something to get your attention. Why? So he corrects you so you can change. Amen. Hallelujah.
How did he answer a gang leader who said he could not leave? (safety in Christ)

He tells of a Mexican Mafia leader who wept on his lawn and said “I can’t live it.” He answered that “the Mexican Mafia is not greater than Jesus Christ,” and offered to walk through that neighborhood on a Friday night “because my Jesus will keep me safe.” This is his own account and has not been verified here.
How did he answer a gang leader who said he could not leave? (safety in Christ)

Now, young people, there is a place in God of safety like this that’s just unbelievable. I remember the Mexican Mafia leader in my area came to me one day, and he wanted to talk to me about Jesus and so forth. I mean, he was one, he, he looked like [unclear] Diamond here, only mean. Diamond’s got a great face here, but he was built like that. I mean, one sweep of his hand, my head’d be knocked off. And he had this tough countenance and tattoos, and that little Mexican Mafia tattoo that they put on there, and everything else. And I gave him the gospel. Most of you know I don’t mess around, I go straight for the jugular, I go straight for the cross. And he’s crying, this big tough guy sitting on my lawn crying, and one of my children were there, and they’re just, I mean, they were at first scared to death for Dad, and now they’re going, here’s this big gangster just weeping like a baby because of the word of God. And I’m asking him to repent and confess his sins, and he’s crying. He says, “But I can’t live it. You know, I can’t get out, the Mexican Mafia, you know, they just don’t let you go.” And I said, “Listen, the Mexican Mafia is not greater than Jesus Christ, and I’ll prove it to you. I will go to your neighborhood on Friday night, the worst day of the week, the worst time of the day, and I will walk from one end of your neighborhood to the other, and nothing will happen to me, because my Jesus will keep me safe. I said, I wouldn’t do this normally, but so you know that there’s power and safety in Christ, I will go down and do it.” Hallelujah.
Was he afraid preaching the gospel in El Salvador?

He says that when communists found they were preaching, they fired into the camp from a distance, so his group had to go back through the jungle to avoid guerrillas. He says “there was not one ounce of fear in me” because “my Jesus sent me there, and he has power to keep me while I’m there.” This is his own account and has not been verified here.
Was he afraid preaching the gospel in El Salvador?

We have a lot of things offered to us. When I was down in El Salvador and the communists found out we were there preaching the gospel, and they hate the gospel, and they would fire into the camp from a long distance of where you were preaching, because you had lanterns and stuff at night, and so we had to go back through the back jungle to try to avoid the guerrillas and being captured as Americans down there. There was not one ounce of fear in me. Why? Because my Jesus sent me there, and he has power to keep me while I’m there. Are you with me? We had to go over this terrain that’s unbelievable, there’s quite an experience, wade through rivers. We came down the road, but we had to go back the hard way.
Is forgiveness enough, or do we need restoration?

He says “restoration is powerful and it’s offered to every one of us,” and that he still needs it. He says “I don’t want just forgiveness” and that God doesn’t want you to be “a pile of ashes” but someone “powerful,” “well groomed,” who “draws people to him” and fights the enemy.
Is forgiveness enough, or do we need restoration?

And young people, you can experience this stuff. It’s not what they say on television and everything else. There is restoration in God to become like God. Is God afraid of anybody? No. Does God follow the crowd? No. Does God get depressed because people leave? No. Say it, no. Restoration is powerful and it’s offered to every one of us, and all of us need it in our life. I still need it. I get a burn spot in me, I need God to restore it. Amen. I start doing things that start decay in my life, I need God to restore. I don’t want just forgiveness. See, that’s our problem in America, is we just, “I’m forgiven.” But you’re a piece, or you’re a pile of ashes. “I’m forgiven.” Pile of ashes. No, God wants you to be something that draws people to him. He wants you to be powerful, like this Pharaoh’s horse. He wants you to be one that is well groomed, looks good, and leads people to the King, brings the presence of the King. And when there’s war, he wants you to stand up and fight the enemy and win the battles. That’s restoration, and you can have it all. It’s for you.
What does he say about “a fool to the correction of the stocks”?
He says a lot of things you do in life will bring correction: if you steal or hang out with a gang, “you’re going to wind up in jail.” He says “that’s how sin corrects you.”
What does he say about parents who live a loose life but want their kids to do right?
He says children “they’re going to know you’re a hypocrite,” because “you’re telling me to do one thing and you’re doing another.” He says “they’re going to rebel.”
What does he say about saying things against God’s church?
He says “I would never advise you to say anything about God’s church,” and warns “you can die early, you can get sickly.” He says God can bring things to correct you.
Why does he say to put up with hypocrites in the church?

He says “we all need restoration,” and that the people we call hypocrites are there “hopefully because they want to change.” He says if you had maturity you would hang in there and be part of their change.
Who does he say you should go through when giving to someone?
He says “you should always go through church leadership to give anyone anything,” and says people who just want your money and possessions “are parasites that need changed.”
What does he say the poor need more than money?
He says they need “the word,” because “the truth of God’s word … will change their life tomorrow.” He also says it is talking about being poor spiritually.
Does he say we need a recovery group or a 12-step program?
He says no: “you don’t need a recovery group or a 12-step procedure or anything, the word and the Spirit will revolutionize your life.”
What does he say God can do with a life that is ashes?
He says “my restoration is so powerful” that if you have destroyed your life, “I can make your life beautiful,” and “better than before.” He says “I’ll make your life look like mine.”
What does he say the oil of joy means?
He says even if you had a rough home and life, God says “I’ll give you joy right where you’re at, then I’ll take you out.”
Why does he say your testimony honors Christ?
He says you couldn’t change on your own, but “when you came to Christ, He worked it in you,” and your testimony is “Jesus changed my life.” He says that gives honor to Christ.
What does he say God gets out of restoring us?
He says God “not only gets honor, he gets people that are really the light of the world, that bring people to Christ just by their life and the way they speak.”
Does he say we should take revenge on people who hurt us?

He says the Bible tells us not to avenge, but God will deal with it: “you don’t have to punch anybody out. You don’t have to poison anybody. You don’t have to verbally attack anybody. Just stay calm.”
What does he say about power and safety in Christ?

He says to the gang leader, “there’s power and safety in Christ.” He says of El Salvador, “my Jesus sent me there and he has power to keep me while I’m there.” These are his accounts and have not been verified here.
What does he say is the problem with “I’m forgiven” in America?
He says “I don’t want just forgiveness,” and that people say “I’m forgiven” but are still “a pile of ashes.” He says God wants you to be something that “draws people to him.”

items.d: In this first session on present truth, Pastor David G. Kincer says God works in seasons and that the present season, the last days before Christ’s return, is a season of salvation. He separates present truth…
p: In this first session on present truth, Pastor David G. Kincer says God works in seasons and that the present season, the last days before Christ’s return, is a season of salvation. He separates present truth from future events no one can date, and walks through signs he says are already fulfilled or under way: antichrists and persecution, the falling away, restoration, the gospel to all nations, increased knowledge and Israel becoming a nation.
What is present truth, and does God work in seasons?

He says Second Peter 1:12 tells us to be established in present truth, truth at that time. From Ecclesiastes 3 he says to everything there is a season, and God has made everything beautiful in its time.
What is present truth, and does God work in seasons?

Thank you for joining us in our first session. Of present truth. In second Peter chapter 1 verse 12. The Bible tells us to be established. In present truth. Truth at that time. In Ecclesiastes 3:1-8. The Bible tells us to everything there is a season. And a time for every purpose under heaven and he goes on and lists the time of war a time of peace a time together a time to cast away a time to hate a time to love a time to be born a time to die and then he makes this awesome statement. In verse 11.
What is present truth, and does God work in seasons?

2 Peter 1:12: For this reason I will not be negligent to remind you always of these things, though you know and are established in the present truth. Ecclesiastes 3:1-8: To everything there is a season, A time for every purpose under heaven: A time to be born, And a time to die; A time to plant, And a time to pluck what is planted; A time to kill, And a time to heal; A time to break down, And a time to build up; A time to weep, And a time to laugh; A time to mourn, And a time to dance; A time to cast away stones, And a time to gather stones; A time to embrace, And a time to refrain from embracing; A time to gain, And a time to lose; A time to keep, And a time to throw away; A time to tear, And a time to sew; A time to keep silence, And a time to speak; A time to love, And a time to hate; A time of war, And a time of peace. Ecclesiastes 3:11: He has made everything beautiful in its time. Also He has put eternity in their hearts, except that no one can find out the work that God does from beginning to end.
Can we discern the signs of the times?

He says if you know the seasons of God you are at peace, even in what others call bad seasons. In Luke 12:56 and Matthew 16:3 Jesus told the religious critics they could discern the sky but not this time or the signs of the times; God has seasons and times in which he performs his purposes.
Can we discern the signs of the times?

He has made everything beautiful in its time so the end result is if you know the seasons of God you’re at peace even what other people would call bad seasons you have no problem with because you understand. That God is a purpose during that season. In Luke chapter 12 verse 56. Jesus turns to those who are following him and criticizing him and very religious group and says you hypocrites you that say and do nothing do the opposite you can discern the face of the sky and of the earth you can tell me when it’s going to rain you can tell me when it’s going to be a hot day when it’s going to be a cool day you can discern those natural signs but you can’t discern this time the time of the messiah the time of the church being built by him in Matthew 16:3 he makes it even more clear using the same verse the same statement but instead of saying you can’t discern this time he says you can’t discern the signs of the times in other words God has season and he has times that he’s going to perform purposes in.
Can we discern the signs of the times?

Luke 12:56: Hypocrites! You can discern the face of the sky and of the earth, but how is it you do not discern this time? Matthew 16:3: and in the morning, ‘It will be foul weather today, for the sky is red and threatening.’ Hypocrites! You know how to discern the face of the sky, but you cannot discern the signs of the times.
Does anyone know the day Jesus will return?

He says future truth is not present truth. From Mark 13:24-32 he says after the great tribulation the Son of man will come in the clouds, but no one knows the day or hour, not the angels, only the Father.
Does anyone know the day Jesus will return?

Now first you got to understand that future truth is not in the present season. No one knows for instance the day and the hour of these future seasons Mark 13:24 through 32 after the great tribulation. A future season the sun will be darkened the moon will not give its light the stars of heaven will fall then they will see the son of man coming in the clouds with great power and glory his second coming is a future event we don’t know when that is then he will send his angels and gather his elect from the four winds but the day and hour knows what no one not the angels in heaven nor the— but only the father and what is happening in.
Does anyone know the day Jesus will return?

Mark 13:24-32: “But in those days, after that tribulation, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light; the stars of heaven will fall, and the powers in the heavens will be shaken. Then they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds with great power and glory. And then He will send His angels, and gather together His elect from the four winds, from the farthest part of earth to the farthest part of heaven. “Now learn this parable from the fig tree: When its branch has already become tender, and puts forth leaves, you know that summer is near. So you also, when you see these things happening, know that it is near—at the doors! Assuredly, I say to you, this generation will by no means pass away till all these things take place. Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will by no means pass away. “But of that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.
What future events have not happened yet?

He says despite the constant bombardment that Jesus is coming any minute, nobody knows but God, and people predicting dates are dealing in future things. He lists future truths: the great tribulation, the seals, trumpets and bowls of Revelation, a glorious church, the heavens rolled up, the second coming, the resurrection and the renewed earth.
What future events have not happened yet?

The world today is a constant bombardment that we’re in the end times and Jesus is coming in a minute and he plainly says nobody knows but God himself not even Jesus who was God in the flesh knew. And yet we got all these people prophesying he’s coming and predicting dates and everything else that is future things that’s not present truth. Future things is the great tribulation the seals of Revelation the trumpets of Revelation the bowls of Revelation the thunderings of Revelation perplexities that come upon the nations and upon the people that is a future thing a time of peace is a future thing a glorious church where the gates of hell cannot prevail against we’re not there yet the heavens dissolved and rolled up like a scroll we’re not there yet Jesus second coming his second return to judge the world we’re not in that truth yet the dead resurrected from the graves and those alive caught up to meet the Lord in the air we’re not there yet and the fiery earth renovated and renewed those are future truths present truth is a basic one here we’re living in the last days that’s the basic.
Are we living in the last days?

He says the basic present truth is that we are living in the last days, which began when God poured out his Spirit in Acts 2, quoting Joel. He says this signified more outpourings of the Holy Ghost, which came in 1900, 1948 and 1968, and that whosoever calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.
Are we living in the last days?

Present truth and it is the season of a season of salvation in these last days Acts 2:16 makes it very clear quoting from Joel chapter 2 this is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel that it shall come to pass in the last days well so when God poured out his spirit in Acts 2 and they spoke in tongues the mighty works of God that was the beginning of the last days the beginning of the last days God says I will pour out my spirit on all flesh your sons and your daughters shall prophesy your young men will see visions and your old men will dream dreams on my servants and my handmaidens I will pour out in those days of my spirit and they shall prophesy signifying that there’s going to be more outpourings of the Holy Ghost which came in 1900. Which came again in 1948 which came again in 1968. God came and visited the mainline denominational churches in 1968 filled them with the Holy Ghost they spoke in tongues and and in 1948 was another outpouring of his spirit which we will hit later. And the Azusa Street revival which spread throughout the world. We are in the last days. He goes on to say I will show wonders in heaven above and signs in the earth beneath blood and fire and vapor of smoke the sun shall be turned into darkness and the moon unto blood before the great and notable day of the Lord the second coming of Christ is a future event and so now he’s talking about other future events before the second coming of Christ we’re not there yet but he says it shall come to pass that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be.
Are we living in the last days?

Acts 2:16-21: But this is what was spoken by the prophet Joel: ‘And it shall come to pass in the last days, says God, That I will pour out of My Spirit on all flesh; Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, Your young men shall see visions, Your old men shall dream dreams. And on My menservants and on My maidservants I will pour out My Spirit in those days; And they shall prophesy. I will show wonders in heaven above And signs in the earth beneath: Blood and fire and vapor of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness, And the moon into blood, Before the coming of the great and awesome day of the LORD. And it shall come to pass That whoever calls on the name of the LORD Shall be saved.’ Joel 2:28-32: “And it shall come to pass afterward That I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh; Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, Your old men shall dream dreams, Your young men shall see visions. And also on My menservants and on My maidservants I will pour out My Spirit in those days. “And I will show wonders in the heavens and in the earth: Blood and fire and pillars of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness, And the moon into blood, Before the coming of the great and awesome day of the LORD. And it shall come to pass That whoever calls on the name of the LORD Shall be saved. For in Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there shall be deliverance, As the LORD has said, Among the remnant whom the LORD calls.
What season are we in now?

He says the season before Christ’s second return is a season of salvation from sin. He builds on it: present truth number one is that Jesus, God in the flesh, has come, and number two that many antichrists and false prophets are in the world; from First John 4:1-3, every spirit that confesses Jesus has come in the flesh is of God.
What season are we in now?

Saved. During the last days before the second return is a season of salvation. Salvation from sin. It is the season no matter what people tell you that’s the season we are in and it started with the beginning of the last days now we’re going to look at some we’re going to build on the basic present truth number one Jesus God in the flesh has come number two many antichrists are in the world. In first John 4:1-3 many false prophets are going into the world they were there back then they’re here now that’s no big deal. By this you know the spirit of God every spirit that confesses that Jesus has come in the flesh is of God. You see. You can tell when a person is right but do they believe and do they preach and teach that Jesus Christ is the messiah God in the flesh who died on the cross for the sins of the world born of a virgin did miracles. Ascended back to heaven after he died and he’s coming back again after he builds a glorious church see you know that that is of God every spirit that confesses not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is not of God and not only is it not a God this is the spirit of antichrist the people that oppose God and even now it is in the world now the difference between the false prophet and the antichrist is the antichrist does not believe the messiah has come that Jesus is the messiah God in the flesh false prophets believe but they teach you things that lead you away from him you got it.
What season are we in now?

1 John 4:1-3: Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits, whether they are of God; because many false prophets have gone out into the world. By this you know the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is of God, and every spirit that does not confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is not of God. And this is the spirit of the Antichrist, which you have heard was coming, and is now already in the world.

He says there are many antichrists, not one big boogeyman, and lists groups he says oppose Christ because they do not believe he existed or was God in the flesh who died for the sins of the world. Present truth number three is that Christians are hated and persecuted.

Even now there are many how many many antichrist not one big boogeyman coming there are many opponents of Christ in the earth whereby we know that it is the last time and so we know that Jews who don’t accept Christ the Bible calls antichrist. We know that atheists are antichrists humanist or antichrist religionists are antichrists free thinkers homosexual activists liberals and so forth they are opposers of Christ simply because they don’t believe that he really existed or they don’t believe he was God in the flesh and died for the sins of the world they opposed Jesus Christ that’s one of the present truths we are living in number three Christians are hated and persecuted Luke 21:11 there will be wars earthquakes famines pestilences fearful sights.

1 John 2:18: Little children, it is the last hour; and as you have heard that the Antichrist is coming, even now many antichrists have come, by which we know that it is the last hour. Luke 21:11-12: And there will be great earthquakes in various places, and famines and pestilences; and there will be fearful sights and great signs from heaven. But before all these things, they will lay their hands on you and persecute you, delivering you up to the synagogues and prisons. You will be brought before kings and rulers for My name’s sake.
Are wars, earthquakes and famines signs of the end?

He says Jesus said these things come but the end is not yet, so do not be troubled; they have nothing to do with his return. From Matthew 24:9 he says believers will be hated of all nations, and since the nations were not all known until about 1500, there will be a later persecution in the last of the last days.
Are wars, earthquakes and famines signs of the end?

In heaven but the end is not yet the end is not yet these things have nothing to do with the signs of the end of the time and Jesus coming which these people promote plainly says and he doubles it he says don’t be troubled before all of these things they will persecute you and deliver you to synagogues prisons kings and rulers for my name which they did up to 313 a.d the early church was heavily persecuted heavily persecuted. They will afflict and kill you Matthew 24:9 and you’ll be hated of all nations for my name’s sake now they didn’t know that South America was there yet North America was there yet Australia was there yet the islands [unclear] they didn’t know there was other nations in the world yet so there has to be a later persecution. Because now we know all the nations of the earth. And until 1500 a.d we didn’t know there was other nations. And so Christians and people who taught that Christ was coming any time any time and picking dates they didn’t even realize that first we’ve got to be revealed that there are other nations other people in the earth so there will be a persecution. Also in the last of the last days after all nations have been revealed to us. And just remember. He says the end is not yet and don’t be troubled by people telling you there’s wars earthquakes famines pestilences plagues and so forth he says don’t be troubled by that that’s not anything to do with the return of Jesus Christ.
Are wars, earthquakes and famines signs of the end?

Matthew 24:9: “Then they will deliver you up to tribulation and kill you, and you will be hated by all nations for My name’s sake. Matthew 24:6: And you will hear of wars and rumors of wars. See that you are not troubled; for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet.
Has the falling away already happened?

From Second Thessalonians 2:2-3 he says that day will not come except there come a falling away first. He says after Rome fell in 476 A.D. came the dark ages, when the church went into real corruption and people could not read the Bible, and that we are living after the falling away, so it has already been fulfilled.
Has the falling away already happened?

Present truth number four there will be a falling away before Jesus returns. II Thessalonians 2:2-3. Be not soon shaken in mind or be troubled neither by spirit nor by the word nor by a letter from us apostles that the day of the Lord is at hand and what are people doing today in tv and radio and books troubling us that Jesus is coming anytime and uh Israel surrounded by armies and all this wicked sin in the world he said don’t be troubled by that I got a lot of things to do. Let no man deceive you for that day will not come except there come a falling away and we find as we read history when the Roman Empire fell here. That. In 476 A.D. That darkness we call them the dark ages and the church went into real corruption the Catholic church was grossly corrupt during this time. Everybody knows it it’s history from sexual immorality to homosexuality to selling people free eternal ticket to heaven because they could live any way they want if they just pay the church money and so for almost [unclear] A.D. we were in the dark ages there was a great falling away. The Bible was written by hand number one and people of poverty and people of of poor means could not even afford to read the Bible on their own and they were forbidden to read the Bible by the Catholic church because only the priests could tell you what the Bible said and when you can’t read the word there’s a great chance you’re going to fall away.
Has the falling away already happened?

2 Thessalonians 2:2-3: not to be soon shaken in mind or troubled, either by spirit or by word or by letter, as if from us, as though the day of Christ had come. Let no one deceive you by any means; for that Day will not come unless the falling away comes first, and the man of sin is revealed, the son of perdition,
What is the restoration of all things?

He says present truth number five is the restoration of all things and times of refreshing. From Acts 3:19-21 he says repent and be converted so times of refreshing may come, and Jesus cannot come until the restoration of all things spoken by the prophets is fulfilled.
What is the restoration of all things?

So the bottom line is we’re living in a season after the falling away. After he predicted the falling away. We’re on the other side of it so we know the falling away has already been fulfilled number five the restoration of all things and the times of refreshing that’s a season we’re in Acts 3:19 repent be converted that your sins may be blotted out so that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord that he may send Jesus Christ preached to you before whom the heavens must receive until the times of restoration he can’t come until the restoration of how many things all things. He can’t come until this is fulfilled.
What is the restoration of all things?

Romans 1:17: For in it the righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith; as it is written, “The just shall live by faith.”
