p: In this message, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that eternal life was promised before the world began and means knowing God, then walks through the seven people in John 10: the thief, the shepherd, the doorkeeper, the stranger, the hireling, the wolf, and the sheep, ending with Jesus as the one door and one flock.
What does he say about keeping the law and being saved? (Matthew 19:17)

He says Jesus told the man to “keep the commandments” for eternal life, “so we not only got to believe, but we got to, what, obey the word for eternal life.” He recounts telling a Southern Baptist that “if I can show you one person that was saved that later wasn’t saved, it destroys your doctrine,” and that he can show “at least five in the Bible.” His remarks about how that church began are his own claim and are not verified here.
What does he say about keeping the law and being saved? (Matthew 19:17)

This is the fourth promise that will cause you to be a participant in the divine nature. I have added to that check on your sheet: keep the law. Matthew 19:17. I was witnessing to a Southern Baptist this week, and, uh, I love to remind Southern Baptists how their church got started: slavery. It broke away from the traditional Baptist because they said the Bible approves of slavery. He said, “Oh my God,” he said, “I’ve never heard that before.” I said, “You need to do research, you need to know what, you where you’re going, what you need to know things.” Man. And then we had a great discussion, and of course, as you know, fundamentalists and Baptists believe in once saved always saved, who immediately asked me my stand on that, and I says, “If I can show you one person that was saved that later wasn’t saved, it destroys your doctrine,” and I can show you at least five in the Bible, and that got his attention. See, how many, you know, it helps to know the scriptures when you’re going to talk to people. See, it helps to kind of understand their background, where they’re coming from. Hallelujah, anyway. I trust you are witnesses for Jesus Christ every opportunity, you tell people about Jesus and about truths. Anyway, the Bible also says to keep the law. When he said, “What must I do to have eternal life?” Jesus said, “Keep the commandments.” The guy says, “Which ones?” And Jesus laid them out, seven of the Ten Commandments, laid them right out to him. And so we not only got to believe, but we got to, what, obey the word for eternal life. Okay, and then these scriptures are the scriptures I used to lead people to Christ, which I did Friday night.
What does he say about keeping the law and being saved? (Matthew 19:17)
Matthew 19:17: So He said to him, “Why do you call Me good? No one is good but One, that is, God. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.”
What is eternal life, and when was it promised? (Titus 1:2, Acts 15:18, John 17:24)

Using a cartoon of climbers asking for “the secret of eternal life,” he says the founders of other religions are dead but “Jesus is alive,” and “someone who died and came back to life can tell you exactly about eternal life.” From Titus 1:2 he says God “promised eternal life before the world began,” and “he didn’t have a plan B.”
What is eternal life, and when was it promised? (Titus 1:2, Acts 15:18, John 17:24)

Eternal life is very important, so we will give you the definition of eternal life. Over here in my little cartoon, these guys climb the mountain to the Hindu group, they get up there and there’s dry bones, and the guy behind says, “No, remember, ask him the secret of eternal life.” The guy’s dead. So is Muhammad, so is Buddha, so is the founders of Hindu, there’s many of them, just a bunch of stuff thrown together. So are the witches and sorcerers, so is Joseph Smith. Jesus is alive. Amen. And someone who died and came back to life can tell you exactly about eternal life. Can I hear an amen? There’s no other one. I don’t have to go anywhere. Titus 1:2: “In the hope of eternal life, which God, that cannot lie, promised before the world began.” Before we ever were created, before Adam was created, Eve was created, before the sphere of the earth was created, before there was any water, God promised eternal life. And that’s very important for you young people to know, because this stuff about “before the world began” shows you the Bible is powerful. And let’s talk about that before we talk about eternal life: other things initiated before the world was created. Acts 15:18: “Known unto God are all his works from the beginning of the world.” He didn’t have a plan B. He knew exactly what he was wanting to do. You know, these people said, “Well, God messed up, you know, Adam and Eve, you know, they sinned, you had to go to a plan B.” No, no plan B. God had promised eternal life before the world began. He knew his plans in the beginning of the world, and it wasn’t just to create a globe and a sphere and plants and animals. John 17:24: “Father, you loved me before the foundation of the world.” God loved Jesus when? Before the world was made. So Jesus was in God’s plan before anything was done. Now, young people, that is powerful. There is no book on earth that can back up these kinds of things but the Bible. Jesus, the beginning of the creation of God. See, it backs it up. He was loved before the foundation of the world. Jesus was in God’s plan before the foundation of the world. He was going to come, God was going to come live in the flesh, die for the sins of the world, rise again, and build a church in the earth and his kingdom. That was his plan.
What is eternal life, and when was it promised? (Titus 1:2, Acts 15:18, John 17:24)

Titus 1:2: in hope of eternal life which God, who cannot lie, promised before time began, Acts 15:18: “Known to God from eternity are all His works. John 17:24: “Father, I desire that they also whom You gave Me may be with Me where I am, that they may behold My glory which You have given Me; for You loved Me before the foundation of the world.
Was Jesus in God’s plan before the foundation of the world? (1 Peter 1:19, Matthew 25:34, Revelation 13:8, John 10:28)

He says Jesus was “foreordained before the foundation of the world,” and “God had Jesus dying before he ever said, ‘I create the heavens and the earth.’” On Revelation 13:8, “the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world,” he says “he’s talking about his plan.” He then gives John 10:28 and John 11:26 as a definition of eternal life: “they shall never perish.”
Was Jesus in God’s plan before the foundation of the world? (1 Peter 1:19, Matthew 25:34, Revelation 13:8, John 10:28)

1 Peter 1:19: “The blood of Christ, who was foreordained before the foundation of the world.” Foreordained, you know, arranged beforehand. God had Jesus dying before he ever said, “I create the heavens and the earth, I create light, I separate the waters.” Before he ever done any of that, Jesus was his plan. Matthew 25:34: “Inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.” When was the kingdom of God thought of? Before anything was done. God wanted you to enter into the kingdom of righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Ghost, a kingdom of power. Amen. That was foreordained. You see, this book is a powerful book, young people. This isn’t men’s intellect talking, this is God setting a plan out and had the power to carry out the plan from the beginning. Hallelujah. And you need to be reminded of these things. Now, in Revelations 13:8, “the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.” And so I asked people that argue with me, what, did Jesus really die before the foundation of the world was made, his blood shed back there before Adam and Eve were created? No. Well, what’s he talking about? He’s talking about his plan. Jesus had, God had planned for Jesus Christ, God in the flesh, to die before anything else was done. Hallelujah. And so Jesus is the big guy, he’s the important guy. Bible definition of eternal life, John 10:28: “I give unto them eternal life, and they shall never perish,” never die, “neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand.” John 11:26: “Whosoever lives and believes in me shall never die.”
Was Jesus in God’s plan before the foundation of the world? (1 Peter 1:19, Matthew 25:34, Revelation 13:8, John 10:28)

1 Peter 1:19: but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot. Matthew 25:34: Then the King will say to those on His right hand, ‘Come, you blessed of My Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world: Revelation 13:8: All who dwell on the earth will worship him, whose names have not been written in the Book of Life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world. John 10:28: And I give them eternal life, and they shall never perish; neither shall anyone snatch them out of My hand. John 11:26: And whoever lives and believes in Me shall never die. Do you believe this?”
Do people who die still live? (Matthew 22:32, Matthew 17:3)

He says Abraham, Isaac and Jacob “were still alive” because “their spirit did not die,” citing “God is not the God of the dead.” He says Moses and Elijah appeared with Jesus, that “when you die, your body dies, but you live,” and that at Christ’s coming “that body is going to be reunited with that spirit.”
Do people who die still live? (Matthew 22:32, Matthew 17:3)

Now, we know that people die, the body dies. But what is Jesus saying? Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob still lived. Okay, Matthew 22:32: “I am the God of Abraham, I am the God of Isaac, I am the God of Jacob.” God is not the God of the dead, but of the what? Living. These guys were still alive. Their bodies were dead, their bodies were in the grave, but they were still alive. See, their spirit did not die because they serve God. Are you there, church? Hallelujah. Now, when Christ comes, that body is going to be reunited with that spirit. Moses and Elijah still lived, Matthew 17:3: on the Mount of Transfiguration there appeared unto them Moses and Elijah talking with Jesus. Moses was taken into heaven without dying. Elijah was taken up without dying. Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, they all died, but all three of them were what? Still alive up in heaven. So whether we’re raptured or whether we come out of the grave, we’re still, when you die, your body dies, but you live. Yes, that’s eternal life. From the time I was conceived, [unclear] in the womb, I was destined for eternity. Wow. So mothers better take care of that baby in that womb; that is a child destined to live with Christ for eternity. Hallelujah. You young people need to understand you were born into eternity.
Do people who die still live? (Matthew 22:32, Matthew 17:3)

Matthew 22:32: ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.” Matthew 17:3: And behold, Moses and Elijah appeared to them, talking with Him.
What does it mean to know God? (John 17:3)

He says “you were born into eternity” and will “live forever one way or another.” Citing John 17:3, he says “eternal life is not only living forever, but it is knowing Jesus.” He describes his own conversion as “an encounter with God,” not “some intellectual thing,” and says people can do miracles in Jesus’s name and still hear “I never knew you.”
What does it mean to know God? (John 17:3)

You’re going to live forever one way or another. It isn’t like the atheist and the humanist say, you just go to the grave and life’s over. Uh-uh, honey, you got to stand before a judge that’s going to decide where you spend eternity that you were born into. Hallelujah, that is eternal life. Another definition of eternal life, John 17:3: “This is eternal life, that they might know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent,” that they might, what? Know God and know Jesus. And this is what I was telling the Southern Baptist guy. No one ever told me I could know God. My parents took me to church, but I never heard any preaching about knowing God. You can actually know God, or I missed it. One, I said, but when I went to that altar call at that Assembly of God church and asked Christ to forgive me my sins, I had an encounter with God. I go, “My gosh, this thing is real, God is real.” See, God came to take away my sin, it wasn’t some intellectual thing, it was a spiritual thing. And I went up to the altar on the scientific method; I finally decided, “I’m just going to go up and prove if this thing is real or not real,” and lo and behold, God was real. Next week I was water baptized, and the week after I got baptized in the Holy Ghost, and wow, did I know God was real. Wow, the power of his love was just tremendous. No one ever told me that. If they had told me that, I’d probably have been saved as a teenager. I didn’t get saved till I was 20, because I never seen anybody really hanging in there and living a Christian life. I just thought it was just, you know, believe and hang on and hope for the best until the end, because the church was just a bunch of mixed-up people, inconsistent, and I didn’t want that. And then I found Jesus was real, and folks, you have been promised the promise to know him. Amen. Not just hear about him, but encounter him, know him; he’s a real person. Now, let’s elaborate on this a little bit. We’ve showed you in lessons recently that by this you know that you know him, if you keep his commandments. Okay, we already taught you on that. We’ve showed you that people can do miracles, preach the gospel, cast out demons, and not know him. Jesus said, “I never knew you.” These people that prophesied, preached the gospel, did miracles, they said, “Lord, we did all this in your name.” See, they used his name, but they didn’t know him. He said, “I never knew you, depart from me, I never knew you.” See, eternal life is not only living forever, but it is knowing Jesus. You can’t have one without the other. I mean, you can have eternal life, you’re going to live forever, it’s just whether it’s in the lake of fire or heaven, and the lake of fire in the Bible is death. You say, so you do die, a spiritual death, if you don’t follow Christ. Are you with me? You understand? Now, we’re going to elaborate on this, knowing God. All right, so get your ears open, we’re going on a roller coaster ride.
What does it mean to know God? (John 17:3)

John 17:3: And this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent. Matthew 7:21-23: “Not everyone who says to Me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ shall enter the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of My Father in heaven. Many will say to Me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in Your name, cast out demons in Your name, and done many wonders in Your name?’ And then I will declare to them, ‘I never knew you; depart from Me, you who practice lawlessness!’
Who are the seven people in John 10, and what does he say about thieves? (John 10:1, Hebrews 6:4–6)

He says “the sheepfold is the church, the called-out ones,” and that Christ lists seven people who come into it, beginning with the thief. He says thieves come for “money, possessions, sex,” and that Judas “was a thief… he never knew Jesus.” Of those who fall away he says “you got to admit you were wrong, you got to go back to the cross.”
Who are the seven people in John 10, and what does he say about thieves? (John 10:1, Hebrews 6:4–6)

Here, John 10:1: “He who doesn’t enter the sheepfold by the door but climbs up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber.” Now, in this parable Christ is going to list seven people that come in to the sheepfold. Okay, he’s going to list seven people that come into the sheepfold. All right, the sheepfold is the church, the called-out ones. The church is very important. The church is not the Baptist, it’s not the Independent like us, it’s not the Catholics. The church is the body of Christ, the called-out ones, and when they meet together, that’s when they are the church, when they assemble together. All right, so it’s important for us to assemble. Now, how many people is he going to talk about coming into the church? Seven. All right, the first one is a thief. He starts out with a thief; they don’t enter the sheepfold by the door, they climb up some other way, as a thief. Okay, all they want is money, possessions, sex, you know, people come in to look for the opposite sex to take out of the church so they can have sex with them. I mean, I’ve been a pastor of a church, a leader of a church, for years, and, man, that’s one of the big things. These people come in, they want to get your women, they want to get your men, they’re not interested in getting Christ, or they want money, they want handouts, they want possessions. You see, they’re not interested in the [unclear] life, they want somebody to get intoxicated with. These are thieves; they come to rob the church. You know, they don’t want to repent or change, they just want what they can get from church members, mainly money, any kind of possession. They’ll get you to give them a car, they’ll get you to do all kinds of things. These are thieves, all right. They don’t come to give, they come to get. Judas was a thief. He did miracles, he preached the gospel, people were saved in his ministry, and, but he was a thief, and he betrayed Christ. See, he never knew Jesus. He knew the message, but he didn’t know Jesus. In Jesus’s life [unclear]. Hebrews says, once you taste of the heavenly gift, been partakers of the Holy Ghost and so forth, you fall away, it’s impossible to come back, because you got to crucify Christ again, you got to admit you were wrong, you got to go back to the cross, and they don’t want to admit they were wrong, they want to say, “I’m still saved, I’m still a believer.” You see, because nothing is impossible with God, it’s their problem. Hallelujah. And the Baptist boy just looked at me like, “Where did you get this stuff?” I said, “Your problem, sir, is you just listen to your circle, your inner circles, all you ever hear, so they keep telling you the same thing over and over. You never go out to find somebody else’s view on these truths to challenge you and get you to dig.”
Who are the seven people in John 10, and what does he say about thieves? (John 10:1, Hebrews 6:4–6)

John 10:1: “Most assuredly, I say to you, he who does not enter the sheepfold by the door, but climbs up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber. Hebrews 6:4-6: For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted the heavenly gift, and have become partakers of the Holy Spirit, and have tasted the good word of God and the powers of the age to come, if they fall away, to renew them again to repentance, since they crucify again for themselves the Son of God, and put Him to an open shame.
Who is the shepherd, and what is a doorkeeper? (John 10:2–4, 1 Samuel 17:34)

Does he say people in the Bible were saved and later fell away?
He says “if I can show you one person that was saved that later wasn’t saved, it destroys your doctrine,” and that he can show “at least five in the Bible.”
What difference does he draw between Jesus and the founders of other religions?
He says the founders are dead, but “Jesus is alive,” and “someone who died and came back to life can tell you exactly about eternal life.”
Does he say God had a plan B?
No. He says “no plan B,” and that God “had promised eternal life before the world began” and “knew his plans in the beginning of the world.”
When does he say Jesus’s death was planned?
He says it was “arranged beforehand,” and “God had Jesus dying before he ever said, ‘I create the heavens and the earth.’”
What does he say the verse “they shall never perish” means?
Citing John 10:28 and 11:26, he gives it as a definition of eternal life: “they shall never perish,” and “whosoever lives and believes in me shall never die.”
What does he say happens to the body and the spirit at death?
He says “the body dies,” but “their spirit did not die,” and that when Christ comes “that body is going to be reunited with that spirit.”
How does he say he came to know God?
He says at an altar call he asked Christ to forgive him and “had an encounter with God,” and “it wasn’t some intellectual thing, it was a spiritual thing.”
Does he say someone can do miracles and still not know Jesus?
Yes. He says people can “do miracles, preach the gospel, cast out demons, and not know him,” and Jesus says, “I never knew you.”
What does he say “the church” is?
He says “the church is the body of Christ, the called-out ones,” and that “it’s important for us to assemble.”
Does he say a minister has to be paid?
He says “you don’t have to give money to be a minister in God’s house; I ministered for years before they ever paid me.”
Who does he say the “stranger” in John 10:5 is?
He says “a stranger is from the kingdom of darkness” and “lives a sinful lifestyle,” and believes in “a government that is different from the Bible.”
What does he say about all religions leading to the same God?
He says it is “a lie according to the scriptures,” because “there is how many doors? One. And who is the door? Jesus.”
Does he say joining a church saves you?
He says “you joining Mountainside doesn’t do beans for you. You joining Jesus is powerful.”
What does he say a hireling is?
He says a hireling “is one that does it for money,” who “doesn’t own the sheep” and “only wants the paycheck.”
Does he say people are predestined to be saved or lost?
He says “anyone who comes through Jesus Christ, the gate, can be saved,” and calls predestination “a lie from hell.”

items.ser: Book of Revelation · The Seventh Seal
p: Continuing in Revelation, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches the seventh seal and the first six trumpets (Revelation 8-10), arguing the visions are not a chronological timeline and that the saints are still on earth, praying, sealed and protected. He stresses the power of the prayers of the saints, God’s delay so more can repent, and a glorious church preaching the gospel right up to Christ’s coming.

p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer opens the seventh seal at Revelation 8, arguing that the visions are not in sequence and that the prayers of the saints ascending to God show the church is still on earth. He reads Psalm 18, leads the church in prayer, and begins the first trumpets.
What is the seventh seal, and what is the silence in heaven? (Revelation 8:1)

He shows a chart of seven seals, seven trumpets and seven bowls and says “it’s all under the book.” He reads Revelation 8:1, “there was silence in heaven for one half an hour,” and says “Remember that.” He asks them to say “day of wrath.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer continues through the fourth, fifth and sixth trumpets, arguing they are not in sequence and that the saints remain on earth. He teaches that the delay is for repentance…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer continues through the fourth, fifth and sixth trumpets, arguing they are not in sequence and that the saints remain on earth. He teaches that the delay is for repentance, that the mystery of God is the church, and that believers must eat the whole book.

There’s always a fresh book coming off the printing press to cover up yesterday’s mistakes. But we can be born out of due time even if He’s coming back 10 years from now or 50. Can we have what He promised now? Absolutely.
What does he say Revelation is telling the church?
1 Corinthians 15:8: Then last of all He was seen by me also, as by one born out of due time.
What does he say about the one third of the day and night?
He says “the sun is light, the absence of light is dark, and yet we’ve got one third night,” and “this is not a sequential thing.”
What does he say the falling star with the key is?
He says “how many of those stars can’t use keys? So obviously he’s talking about a spirit being.”
What does he say about the star the wise men followed?
He says “this confirms that the star the wise men followed was a spirit being illuminating their way.”
How long does he say the fifth trumpet torment lasts?
He says “Five months. Not three and a half years.”
Who is the king of the locusts, according to him?
He says “Satan is the destroyer, so Satan is the king of the locusts that’s coming out of the smoke.”
Is the woe a woe for everyone?
He says “It depends on what side of the cloud you’re on,” like Israel, where “on their side of the cloud there was light and blessing in God.”
Does he say the 200 million horses are literal?
He says “that’s just an illustration so we can understand the vastness of it and the power of it.”
What does he say was the last reason for the delay?
He says “for people to repent,” and “giving people every possible chance to repent.”
Why does he say wanting Jesus to come any minute is selfish?
He says “there’s a lot of people that still need what? A chance to repent. So that’s why there’s a delay.”
What does he say “no further delay” means?
He says “What he’s really saying is, ‘there will be no further delay.’”
What does he say the mystery of God is?
He says “The mystery of God will be finished, and this mystery of the church, people being saved by the blood of the Lamb, the Gentiles and Jews coming together.”
What does he mean by sweet in the mouth and bitter in the belly?
He says “when that Word gets down into the belly… you’ve got to be responsible and you’ve got to be disciplined.”
What does he say the Son of Man will find on earth?
He says “He will find what? Faith on earth. What faith? That God has the power to do what He promised.”
What if Christ does not come for a thousand years?
He says “What if He wasn’t coming back for another thousand years?” and “we can be born out of due time even if He’s coming back 10 years from now or 50.”

p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer begins the seventh trumpet by critiquing popular prophecy charts, then teaches from Revelation 11 that the temple is the church, the new Jerusalem is the church, and the two witnesses cannot be anyone from history. He ends with the seventh trumpet and the reign of Christ.
Why does he say the end-time prophecy charts do not add up?

He shows charts of the premillennial view and says the seals, trumpets, two witnesses, the man-child’s mother and the beast each get “three and a half years,” which “adds up to about 14 years, not seven.” He asks what the authors’ end goal is, and says “the whole point is somehow the church gets taken up and everybody else gets punished.”
Why does he say the end-time prophecy charts do not add up?

We’re going to talk today about the seventh trumpet, but before we get into that, I want to show you just some basic charts. There’s so many of them, but here’s the premillennial view. You have here the rapture. They have somehow taken Thessalonians and turned it into an ambiguous Jesus coming in the heavenly, snatching up the church and leaving again without revealing Himself to the whole world, very ambiguous. But here is this, quote unquote, rapture. They got the energy crisis down here like that’s supposed to mean something. And they got the temple being built, good God, help us. They got the seals, three and a half years. They got the beast, the antichrist, coming up. Then you got the trumpets, and the seventh trumpet is when everything ends, and then they got the vials being poured out, three and a half more years, and then they got the millennium. The problem they got here is there’s two witnesses here, as you’ll see later, are doing some very powerful things, okay? That’s a real problem with this chart, as you will see. You got the man-child and the man-child’s mother with three and a half years, both of these are three and a half years, and then you got the beast rising up for three and a half years. Well, it adds up to about 14 years, not seven. Okay, here’s another chart, and, uh, you can see here’s three and a half years. Revelation 8:9 through 11:15, you got the seals, then you got the trumpet, then you got the seventh trumpet, and again you got this problem with the Gentiles treading the courts of the temple of God for three and a half years. All right, then you got the two witnesses bringing out fire from their mouth for three and a half years and tormenting the people on earth, and then you got the man-child’s mother in the wilderness for three and a half years, and then you got the beast for three and a half years. How many do that add up to? 14 years. Okay. Now, you know, people can write charts all they want to. What is their end goal? That’s what I want to know. And like an author who wrote this book, you know, when you read a book, you should know who the author is and what they’re trying to get across. See, what’s their point? The whole point is somehow the church gets taken up and everybody else gets punished. That’s their goal. Somehow we deserve to be raised up before the second coming.
What does Revelation 11:1-2 mean by measuring the temple and the Gentiles treading the city 42 months?

He says the angel’s command to measure the temple, altar and worshipers is not about a natural building, since “the natural temple was destroyed in 70 AD.” He says the holy city trodden by the Gentiles for 42 months is “Jerusalem has been trodden by the Gentiles for 2,000 years” and the church has been tried for 2,000 years “by civil laws and limiting what Christians can and cannot do.”
What does Revelation 11:1-2 mean by measuring the temple and the Gentiles treading the city 42 months?

Before the second coming. Then you got the vials being poured out and so forth, and here’s the Messiah, second coming, and then you have the premillennium people, we’re going to reign and rule with Christ a thousand years. Then we got the amillennium people who say we, the whole thing is we’re reigning and ruling ever since Christ came, and then you got, I’m sorry, the amillennium, there is no millennium, and then you got the postmillennium people, and then the pre-tribulation rapture and the post-tribulation rapture and the mid-tribulation rapture and the prewrath rapture. [unclear] All these charts. So these are your basic couple of them charts. All right, now we’re going to deal with some three-and-a-half-year periods here. Okay, before we get into this seventh trumpet, the first one in Revelation 11:1 and 2. “It was given me a reed like a measuring rod, and the angel said, ‘Rise and measure the temple of God, measure the altar, and measure the people who worship there.’” Okay, I’m 5’10” and three-quarters. Is that what he’s talking about? Okay, the altar is x amount of, is that what he’s talking about? The temple is so big? This is why they got to have the temple rebuilt, because they’re trying to reduce this down to a natural temple. Are you with me? Stick with me here, please. Stick with me. But it says don’t measure the outer court, because it’s going to be given to the Gentiles, the unbeliever, the nations of the world, the non-Christians, to tread for three and a half years. Okay, three and a half years, and they will, uh, tread the city of Jerusalem, the holy city, for three and a half years, or 42 months. Now, for your information, the natural temple was destroyed in 70 AD. Herod’s temple, the temple the Jews went to worship at, was destroyed already when this Revelation came. Got it? Are you with me? You have to use your brains today. Okay, that temple is not there, so he’s not talking about measuring that temple, is he? No. And then he says the holy city will be trodden by the Gentiles for three and a half years. Well, Jerusalem has been trodden by the Gentiles for 2,000 years. Yes, that’s a fact. We know that’s a fact. History has told us that they have been trying the church for 2,000 years by civil laws and limiting what Christians can and cannot do.
What does Revelation 11:1-2 mean by measuring the temple and the Gentiles treading the city 42 months?

Revelation 11:1-2: Then I was given a reed like a measuring rod. And the angel stood, saying, “Rise and measure the temple of God, the altar, and those who worship there. But leave out the court which is outside the temple, and do not measure it, for it has been given to the Gentiles. And they will tread the holy city underfoot for forty-two months.
Does God dwell in temples made with hands? (Acts 7:48, Acts 17:24, Isaiah 66:1)

He says “God does not dwell in temples made with hands,” citing Acts 7:48, Acts 17:24 and Isaiah 66:1. He says the Jewish temple was “a shadow of things to come” and “a pattern,” and God destroyed it because “the Jews couldn’t leave it,” just as we struggle to leave how we were raised to serve God.
Does God dwell in temples made with hands? (Acts 7:48, Acts 17:24, Isaiah 66:1)

Now, Acts 7, verse 48. This is what we know, we know this, ain’t no ifs and buts about it. We know this truth: God dwells not in temples made with hands. Says it in Acts 7:48, Acts 17:24, and Isaiah 66:1. God does not dwell in temples made with hands. Well, why do we want to build a temple if God is dwelling, and temples made with hands? He already destroyed the Jewish temple that pointed to the church, the real temple of God. He had the Roman army destroy it because the Jews couldn’t leave it. And aren’t we like that today? We can’t leave how we were raised to serve God to really enter in to the fullness of God. Don’t we struggle with that? Yeah. So did the Jews, man. They worshiped that natural temple, and that natural temple, the Bible says, was plainly a shadow of things to come, doesn’t it say that? A pattern of what was to come.
Does God dwell in temples made with hands? (Acts 7:48, Acts 17:24, Isaiah 66:1)

Acts 7:48: “However, the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands, as the prophet says: Acts 17:24: God, who made the world and everything in it, since He is Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in temples made with hands. Isaiah 66:1: Thus says the LORD: “Heaven is My throne, And earth is My footstool. Where is the house that you will build Me? And where is the place of My rest?

He reads Galatians 4 that the natural Jerusalem “is in bondage with her children, but the Jerusalem above is free, which is the mother of us all.” He adds Hebrews 12:22, “you are coming to Mount Zion, unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem,” and asks, “the church is the what? New Jerusalem.”

Galatians 4:25, the new Jerusalem from above. Galatians 4:25: “Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia and corresponds to Jerusalem which now is.” And for you Bible scholars, let me throw this out to you. If Sinai was in the peninsula that all the maps say, why does Paul say it was in Arabia? Could it be that the maps are wrong and Mount Sinai is actually in another place that the maps haven’t told us? Just giving you some tidbits, you Bible scholars that like to dig into things, and, you know, the Bible isn’t wrong, right? Yeah. Okay, just throwing that out. “And it corresponds to Jerusalem which now is,” that’s the natural city of Jerusalem, “and this natural city is in bondage with her children, but the Jerusalem above is free, which is the mother of us all.” Which is what? Which is what mother? Say the word “mother.” That word is going to come up again later in this message, okay? “The Jerusalem from above is free, and the mother of us all. We, like Isaac, are the children of promise,” not of the flesh, not the children of bondage but free, the free woman, the free Jerusalem. Are you with me? Hebrews 12:22: “You are coming to Mount Zion, unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, to an innumerable company of angels, to the general assembly and church of the firstborn, to Jesus the Mediator of the new covenant.”

Galatians 4:25-26: for this Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia, and corresponds to Jerusalem which now is, and is in bondage with her children— but the Jerusalem above is free, which is the mother of us all. Hebrews 12:22-24: But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, to an innumerable company of angels, to the general assembly and church of the firstborn who are registered in heaven, to God the Judge of all, to the spirits of just men made perfect, to Jesus the Mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling that speaks better things than that of Abel.
Is the church the new Jerusalem? (Revelation 3:12, 21:2)

He says “if God has got a new Jerusalem, what do I care about Jerusalem over in Israel?” and that God “could care the least about the natural Jerusalem” and is after “a new Jerusalem, the church.” He reads Revelation 3:12 and 21:2 and says “He’s not interested in a natural temple… He’s interested in you.”
Is the church the new Jerusalem? (Revelation 3:12, 21:2)

So we are come to what? The new Jerusalem. The church. The church is the what? New Jerusalem. Are you out there? Now, this is hot stuff. This can open this Bible up to you when you read it. Now, if God has got a new Jerusalem, what do I care about Jerusalem over in Israel? Could that be an amen? What’s all this nonsense about Jerusalem and a temple, when God doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands, and God could care the least about the natural Jerusalem? He’s after a what? A new Jerusalem, the church. Church, that’s powerful. He’s after you. He’s interested in you. Revelation 3:12: “I will write upon him the name of My God and the name of the city of My God, which is the new Jerusalem, which comes down out of heaven from My God.” Are you there? Isn’t this good? Revelation 21:2: “I, John, saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, ‘Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and He will dwell with them, and they shall be His people, and God Himself shall be with them and be their God.’” He’s not interested in a natural temple. He could care the least about this barn. He’s interested in you.
Is the church the new Jerusalem? (Revelation 3:12, 21:2)

Revelation 3:12: He who overcomes, I will make him a pillar in the temple of My God, and he shall go out no more. I will write on him the name of My God and the name of the city of My God, the New Jerusalem, which comes down out of heaven from My God. And I will write on him My new name. Revelation 21:2: Then I, John, saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.
Does God want to live in you rather than in a building? (Revelation 21:10, 1 Corinthians 3:16, 2 Corinthians 6:16)

He says “a temple is an abiding place,” and God “wants to take up residence in your life.” He cites Revelation 21:10, 1 Corinthians 3:16 and 2 Corinthians 6:16, and says “I don’t have to wait for some natural temple to be built,” since “We have been the temple of God that He’s interested in.”
Does God want to live in you rather than in a building? (Revelation 21:10, 1 Corinthians 3:16, 2 Corinthians 6:16)

He wants to live with you. A temple is an abiding place, a home is a place of residence, abiding place. He wants to take up residence in your life. Wow. Revelation 21:10: “He showed me the great city, the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God, having the glory of God.” “I saw no temple there, for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple of it.” See, they dwell there. “There will in no wise enter into it anything that defiles, neither whatsoever works an abomination or makes a lie, but they which are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life.” Folks, I don’t know about you, but the only way since Jesus came was to believe on Him for forgiveness of sin and get your name written in the Lamb’s Book of Life. This has been going on for 2,000 years, not three and a half. We have been the temple of God that He’s interested in. He got rid of the natural temple because He came and fulfilled what the natural temple pointed to and was a pattern of. 1 Corinthians 3:16: “You are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God dwells in you. If any man defiles the temple of God, God will destroy him, for the temple of God is holy, which temple you are.” So, see, I can’t defile my temple. I don’t have to wait for some natural temple to be built in some, and, I, Christ rise up and offer some kind of stupid sacrifice on it that they dream up. It’s not in the book. They dream this stuff up. 2 Corinthians 6:16: “You are the temple of the living God, as God has said: ‘I will dwell in them and walk in them, and I will be their God, and they shall be My people.’” Do we get it? See, we know God doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands. He dwells with human beings that believe on Him. Amen. And us human beings are not to defile the temple.
Does God want to live in you rather than in a building? (Revelation 21:10, 1 Corinthians 3:16, 2 Corinthians 6:16)

Revelation 21:10-27: And he carried me away in the Spirit to a great and high mountain, and showed me the great city, the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God, having the glory of God. Her light was like a most precious stone, like a jasper stone, clear as crystal. Also she had a great and high wall with twelve gates, and twelve angels at the gates, and names written on them, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel: three gates on the east, three gates on the north, three gates on the south, and three gates on the west. Now the wall of the city had twelve foundations, and on them were the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb. And he who talked with me had a gold reed to measure the city, its gates, and its wall. The city is laid out as a square; its length is as great as its breadth. And he measured the city with the reed: twelve thousand furlongs. Its length, breadth, and height are equal. Then he measured its wall: one hundred and forty-four cubits, according to the measure of a man, that is, of an angel. The construction of its wall was of jasper; and the city was pure gold, like clear glass. The foundations of the wall of the city were adorned with all kinds of precious stones: the first foundation was jasper, the second sapphire, the third chalcedony, the fourth emerald, the fifth sardonyx, the sixth sardius, the seventh chrysolite, the eighth beryl, the ninth topaz, the tenth chrysoprase, the eleventh jacinth, and the twelfth amethyst. The twelve gates were twelve pearls: each individual gate was of one pearl. And the street of the city was pure gold, like transparent glass. But I saw no temple in it, for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple. The city had no need of the sun or of the moon to shine in it, for the glory of God illuminated it. The Lamb is its light. And the nations of those who are saved shall walk in its light, and the kings of the earth bring their glory and honor into it. Its gates shall not be shut at all by day (there shall be no night there). And they shall bring the glory and the honor of the nations into it. But there shall by no means enter it anything that defiles, or causes an abomination or a lie, but only those who are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life. 1 Corinthians 3:16: Do you not know that you are the temple of God and that the Spirit of God dwells in you? 2 Corinthians 6:16: And what agreement has the temple of God with idols? For you are the temple of the living God. As God has said: “I will dwell in them And walk among them. I will be their God, And they shall be My people.”
Who are the two witnesses in Revelation 11? (Revelation 11:3-4)

He says the two witnesses prophesy for three and a half years, with fire coming out of their mouths. He lists guesses that they are Moses and Elijah, or John the Baptist and Jesus, or “two prophets to come,” and notes the two olive trees and two lampstands (Revelation 11:4, Zechariah 4:14), but says “all these are great speculations.”
Who are the two witnesses in Revelation 11? (Revelation 11:3-4)

Amen. Hallelujah. We are that new Jerusalem. We’re free, and there’s no temple in it because Christ, when He comes and dwells in us, is the temple. Hallelujah. Then in Revelation 11:3, there are two prophets, two witnesses, that rise up and begin to prophesy for three and a half years. Okay, fire comes out of their mouth, the Bible says, and destroys anybody that messes around with them. He says it kills them. I mean, these two guys are going around, you talk about a dragon. And the Bible says they tormented the people on earth for three and a half years. You young people, there is a time coming up the road where God’s going to manifest Himself, and you’re going to be glad you chose Christ when that happens. I mean, these two witnesses are something else. “I will give power unto my two witnesses for three and a half years.” Now, the Bible says in Acts 1:8 that we are the witnesses of God, “You shall be My witnesses.” In Isaiah 43:10 it says Israel was a witness for God. Some say Moses and Elijah are the two witnesses, and some of us just say these are two prophets to come, we’ve never seen anything like them. Some people say it’s John the Baptist and Jesus, which prophesied and spoke for three and a half years, and then John rose with Jesus when all the saints of old rose, and all these are great speculations. In verse 4 of Revelation 11, it says these are two olive trees and two lampstands standing before the God of the earth. Now, do you remember what the lampstand is? What’s the lampstand? The church. Okay, so two churches. Hm. The church of Israel in the wilderness, the church of Jesus Christ. Okay, the two olive trees are two anointed ones that stand beside the Lord of the whole earth. In Zechariah 4:14 it talks about one lampstand and two olive trees. Okay, so some say it’s one lampstand because the Jews and Gentiles are one church. Now, the problem with all the above, all that I said, is this.
Who are the two witnesses in Revelation 11? (Revelation 11:3-4)

Revelation 11:3-4: And I will give power to my two witnesses, and they will prophesy one thousand two hundred and sixty days, clothed in sackcloth.” These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands standing before the God of the earth. Acts 1:8: But you shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you shall be witnesses to Me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.” Isaiah 43:10: “You are My witnesses,” says the LORD, “And My servant whom I have chosen, That you may know and believe Me, And understand that I am He. Before Me there was no God formed, Nor shall there be after Me. Zechariah 4:14: So he said, “These are the two anointed ones, who stand beside the Lord of the whole earth.”
Could the two witnesses be Moses and Elijah, or Jesus and John the Baptist? (Revelation 11:5)

He says “Jesus didn’t spit fire out, neither did John the Baptist,” and “no man of God has ever gone through the earth spitting fire out and destroying those who oppose them.” He says “it’s definitely not Moses and Elijah, and it’s definitely not anyone that we have ever heard about in history.”
Could the two witnesses be Moses and Elijah, or Jesus and John the Baptist? (Revelation 11:5)

“If anyone wants to harm these two witnesses, fire proceeds from their mouth and destroys their enemies.” Jesus didn’t spit fire out, neither did John the Baptist. They let their enemies kill them, both of them did, so it’s definitely not them, is it? And it’s definitely not Moses and Elijah, and it’s definitely not anyone that we have ever heard about in history. Could that be an amen? Because no man of God has ever gone through the earth spitting fire out and destroying those who oppose them and tormenting people. These two prophets are tormenting the people of the world, torturing them. Okay, so that eliminates all the theories. Could that be an amen? Could that be an amen?
Could the two witnesses be Moses and Elijah, or Jesus and John the Baptist? (Revelation 11:5)
Revelation 11:5: And if anyone wants to harm them, fire proceeds from their mouth and devours their enemies. And if anyone wants to harm them, he must be killed in this manner.
What power do the two witnesses have, and is the beast the antichrist? (Revelation 11:6-7)

He says they have power to shut up heaven and turn waters to blood, like the seals and trumpets. He says “this leaves Israel and the church out,” since neither has done these things since Jesus left, and “nowhere does it say the beast and the antichrist are the same person.”
What power do the two witnesses have, and is the beast the antichrist? (Revelation 11:6-7)

Absolutely. “These have power to shut up heaven so that no rainfall falls in the days of their prophecy, and they have power over the waters to turn them into blood and strike the earth with all plagues as often as they desire.” And if you remember the seals and the trumpets, that’s what was going on: fire, blood, all this stuff. So it’s almost like a connection here. “As often as they want,” they bring these plagues. So this leaves Israel and the church out, unless the church is empowered in the last days to do these things, because neither Israel nor God’s church since Jesus left this earth has done these things. Am I right? Absolutely. “The beast that ascends out of the bottomless pit will make war with these and overcome them and kill them.” And nowhere in the Bible, church, does it say the beast is the antichrist. See, they have to connect it with their own human intellect. Nowhere does it say the beast and the antichrist are the same person.
What power do the two witnesses have, and is the beast the antichrist? (Revelation 11:6-7)

Revelation 11:6-7: These have power to shut heaven, so that no rain falls in the days of their prophecy; and they have power over waters to turn them to blood, and to strike the earth with all plagues, as often as they desire. When they finish their testimony, the beast that ascends out of the bottomless pit will make war against them, overcome them, and kill them.
Where do the two witnesses die, and how can everyone see them? (Revelation 11:7-12)

He says Sodom and Egypt are Old Testament metaphors for Jerusalem, and the bodies are seen by all peoples while the world rejoices. He asks how everyone could see them and says “trying to literally interpret it as natural things in sequence just doesn’t work,” just as “everybody on earth sees Jesus when He comes,” because “He just opens your eyes to see.”
Where do the two witnesses die, and how can everyone see them? (Revelation 11:7-12)

“He makes war against them and kills them, and they lay for three days in the streets of Jerusalem, called Sodom and Egypt.” That’s a metaphor in the Old Testament of Jerusalem, “where the Lord was crucified.” So these guys are supposed to actually lie in the natural city of Jerusalem somewhere? We’ve never read it in history, have we? No. For three and a half years? Hm, interesting. “Then those from the peoples, the tongues, the tribes, the nations will see their dead bodies three and a half days and not allow their dead bodies to be put into the grave, and all those who dwell on the earth will rejoice over them, make merry, and send gifts to one another” (Christmas time) “because these two prophets who tormented those on earth are dead.” They’re happy these guys are gone. Now let me ask you this question: how can everybody see these two prophets? You say, “Well, the satellite TV.” Yeah, but not everybody has one. “Well, we got Internet.” Not everybody has a computer. Let me ask you this: how did they see Jesus? Everybody on earth sees Jesus when He comes. Does God need a satellite TV to do that? No, He just opens your eyes to see. Am I giving you food for thought? See, trying to literally interpret it as natural things in sequence just doesn’t work, and when it doesn’t work, we just need to leave it alone until He, what? Opens our eyes and we understand. “After three and a half days, life comes back into them, they stood on their feet, and a great fear fell on those who saw them, and they heard a loud voice from heaven saying, ‘Come up here,’ and they ascended to heaven in a cloud, and their enemies saw them.” All their enemies saw them ascend. Now, to me, that’s not too hard to figure out, but I’m going to leave that for you. When Jesus comes, does everybody see Him? Will everybody see the graves open and the people arise? Yeah. Why? Because He’s going to, He’s going to open your eyes to see Him. Because see, in the natural mind, if Jesus came in America, how would China see Him? But see, He’s coming all over the earth. He’s God, and people are going to witness this event. It says every eye sees Him. It’s not some rapture where everybody’s going, “What happened? Huh? What happened?” No, we all, what? See. Amen. Hallelujah.
Where do the two witnesses die, and how can everyone see them? (Revelation 11:7-12)

Revelation 11:7-12: When they finish their testimony, the beast that ascends out of the bottomless pit will make war against them, overcome them, and kill them. And their dead bodies will lie in the street of the great city which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified. Then those from the peoples, tribes, tongues, and nations will see their dead bodies three-and-a-half days, and not allow their dead bodies to be put into graves. And those who dwell on the earth will rejoice over them, make merry, and send gifts to one another, because these two prophets tormented those who dwell on the earth. Now after the three-and-a-half days the breath of life from God entered them, and they stood on their feet, and great fear fell on those who saw them. And they heard a loud voice from heaven saying to them, “Come up here.” And they ascended to heaven in a cloud, and their enemies saw them.
Why were 7,000 killed, and who is the remnant? (Revelation 11:13-14)

He says it “doesn’t make sense” for 7,000 to be killed in a city of millions “unless you know the Scriptures about 7,000 in Israel that did not bow their knee.” He says the remnant “were afraid and gave glory to the God of heaven,” and “you’re going to see that we are the remnant.”
Why were 7,000 killed, and who is the remnant? (Revelation 11:13-14)

“Now there was a great earthquake the same hour, a tenth of the city fell in the earthquake, 7,000 people were killed.” Why 7,000? Why 7,000? A great earthquake, there’s millions of people in the city of Jerusalem, and 7,000 are killed. Doesn’t make sense unless you know the Scriptures about 7,000 in Israel that did not bow their knee. So these 7,000 were bowing their knee, but anyway, “and the remnant,” listen, the remnant, that’s coming up later, “were afraid and gave glory to the God of heaven.” The remnant, the remainder of the people, were afraid. They were in fear, respect, and they, what? Honor God. And you’re going to see that we are the remnant in a few minutes. Hallelujah. “The second woe is past, the third woe is coming.” Okay, are you with me so far? These are three and a half and three and a half. Is how many years? Seven. Now, we got the abomination of desolation, Daniel, that they stretch over 49 weeks. They take one week and stretch it over to the end time. They have it, and it fits right in. I’ve calculated it out from the carrying away to the building of the temple when Jesus came was about the years. It’s very close. Now, let me ask you this: when did the sacrifices cease, the abomination of desolation spoken by Daniel the prophet?
Why were 7,000 killed, and who is the remnant? (Revelation 11:13-14)

Revelation 11:13-14: In the same hour there was a great earthquake, and a tenth of the city fell. In the earthquake seven thousand people were killed, and the rest were afraid and gave glory to the God of heaven. The second woe is past. Behold, the third woe is coming quickly. 1 Kings 19:18: Yet I have reserved seven thousand in Israel, all whose knees have not bowed to Baal, and every mouth that has not kissed him.”
When did the sacrifices cease, and what is the abomination of desolation? (Daniel 9:27, Matthew 24:15, Luke 21:20)

He says the sacrifices ceased not when the temple was torn down but “when Jesus died on the cross… He fulfilled all the law, all those types and shadows and patterns.” He compares Matthew’s “abomination of desolation” with Luke’s “Jerusalem surrounded by armies,” says “the abomination of desolation has happened,” and says “nowhere does it say there’s seven years of tribulation.”
When did the sacrifices cease, and what is the abomination of desolation? (Daniel 9:27, Matthew 24:15, Luke 21:20)

See that the sacrifices will cease. Okay, now remember we told you, in Matthew it says, “When you see the abomination of desolation,” then flee to the mountains for the destruction of Jerusalem is coming. But in Luke, he doesn’t say, he does say “abomination of desolation,” he says, “When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, flee to the mountain, for its destruction is coming.” And so the abomination of desolation has happened. Right now, let me ask you this: when did the sacrifices cease? Was it when the temple was torn down? No, it’s when Jesus died on the cross. Right. When He died, there was no more sacrifices. He did it. See, He fulfilled all the prophecies, He fulfilled all the law, all those types and shadows and patterns. He did it all. And so when He died, and He said, “It is finished,” that’s when the sacrifices were finished. Did the Jews keep sacrificing? Yes. Did it mean they had any profit, any clout? No. Why? Because Jesus, the one and only sacrifice, was done now, and our faith was to be in Him, and all sacrifices were to, what? Cease. And so the Jews couldn’t get out of the natural, just like we can’t get out of the natural, and so God had the Roman army come in and destroy the temple, so now they can’t sacrifice. Why? And if you don’t want to get out of the natural and into the spiritual, God has ways to fix you. I tell you, take the faith way, take the believing way. Don’t take that other way. That’s a tough road to hoe. Hallelujah. Amen. What’s the one sacrifice left that we do? Praise. “The sacrifice of praise, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks unto His name,” which most Christians will not do. Why? Because of the way they were raised, the way they were taught. Are you with me? Now, let’s continue. Revelation 12:6, we’re going to get into this, but there’s a woman who has fled in the wilderness for three and a half years that birth the man-child. Okay, and then in Revelation 13:5 we got the dragon and the beast warring with the saints and winning, for how long? Three and a half years. Church, there’s a lot of three and a half years here, and nowhere does it say there’s seven years of tribulation. It’s not there. In one sentence, it’s not there. You have to add all this stuff up, twist Scriptures, rubber band them over here and there. Are you with me?
When did the sacrifices cease, and what is the abomination of desolation? (Daniel 9:27, Matthew 24:15, Luke 21:20)

Daniel 9:27: Then he shall confirm a covenant with many for one week; But in the middle of the week He shall bring an end to sacrifice and offering. And on the wing of abominations shall be one who makes desolate, Even until the consummation, which is determined, Is poured out on the desolate.” Matthew 24:15-16: “Therefore when you see the ‘abomination of desolation,’ spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place” (whoever reads, let him understand), “then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains. Luke 21:20-21: “But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation is near. Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains, let those who are in the midst of her depart, and let not those who are in the country enter her. Hebrews 13:15: Therefore by Him let us continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name. Revelation 12:6: Then the woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, that they should feed her there one thousand two hundred and sixty days. Revelation 13:5: And he was given a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies, and he was given authority to continue for forty-two months.
What happens at the seventh trumpet, and is Christ reigning now? (Revelation 11:15, Matthew 28:18)

He reads Revelation 11:15, “The kingdoms of this world have become the kingdoms of our Lord and His Christ, and He shall reign forever,” and asks, “is Christ reigning now? Yeah.” He cites Matthew 28:18, “All power is given to Me in heaven and in earth,” and says the 24 elders worship Jesus “every time you turn around.”
What happens at the seventh trumpet, and is Christ reigning now? (Revelation 11:15, Matthew 28:18)

Seventh trumpet, third woe. Revelation 11:15: “The seventh trumpet sounded, and the angel said, ‘The kingdoms of this world have become the kingdoms of our Lord and His Christ, and He shall reign forever.’” All right, well, let me ask you this question, uh: is Christ reigning now? Yeah. Is He the King of kings and Lord of lords of the nations now? Yeah. Duh. Hallelujah. Matthew 28:18: “All power is given to Me in heaven and in earth. Go you, for this reason, and teach all nations.” How much power does Jesus have? All of it. Amen. The 24 elders worship again. You don’t like worship, you don’t like getting on your knees, I don’t know what you’re going to do in heaven. All through Revelation these guys are worshiping Jesus every time you turn around, ain’t that right? Yeah. What are you going to do, get up there and say, “Hey, that’s not my nature, I wasn’t raised that way, that ain’t how we did it in our Baptist church. Where’s the candles, man? I’m a Catholic, where’s the candles? Where’s the incense?” No, you’re not going to argue, so we might as well do it now.
What happens at the seventh trumpet, and is Christ reigning now? (Revelation 11:15, Matthew 28:18)

Revelation 11:15: Then the seventh angel sounded: And there were loud voices in heaven, saying, “The kingdoms of this world have become the kingdoms of our Lord and of His Christ, and He shall reign forever and ever!” Matthew 28:18: And Jesus came and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to Me in heaven and on earth.
Is the third woe really a “woe” for the saints? (Revelation 11:17-18)

He says the nations being angry, the dead being judged and the saints being rewarded are “all happening at the same time.” He says “the third woe… doesn’t sound like much of a woe to me when you’re on the right side,” and that resurrection and judgment are described together in the passage.
Is the third woe really a “woe” for the saints? (Revelation 11:17-18)

He says, “You have taken Your great power and reign.” “The nations were angry, for Your wrath has come, and the time of the dead that are judged, and the rewards for the saints.” Look at this. Everything is happening at the same time. Watch this, just read it. The nations are what? Do they, a lot of the people, nations means people, are a lot of people mad at Jesus? They don’t like you saying that name. Is our government mad at Jesus? They don’t want the name said. Yeah. “Your wrath has come.” Okay, these plagues, these things that God does to get people’s attention and get them to repent, as we learn. “And the time of the dead being judged.” Oh, how does the dead get judged? They got to be what? Resurrected. See, this is all happening at the same time. “And the saints are rewarded.” Ooh, that don’t sound like a big woe to me. The third woe has come. Doesn’t sound like much of a woe to me when you’re on the right side, does it? Rewards, I can handle rewards. Are you with me? Hallelujah. But boy, they got it all complicated. And, you know, saints are resurrected, then later the dead in sin are resurrected, and all this stuff, but right here it says what? It’s all happening at the same time.
Is the third woe really a “woe” for the saints? (Revelation 11:17-18)

Revelation 11:17-18: saying: “We give You thanks, O Lord God Almighty, The One who is and who was and who is to come, Because You have taken Your great power and reigned. The nations were angry, and Your wrath has come, And the time of the dead, that they should be judged, And that You should reward Your servants the prophets and the saints, And those who fear Your name, small and great, And should destroy those who destroy the earth.”
What does he say is the problem with the prophecy charts?
He says each chart has several periods of three and a half years that “adds up to about 14 years, not seven,” and that the two witnesses are “a real problem with this chart.”
What does he say about a temple being rebuilt?

He says “the natural temple was destroyed in 70 AD,” so “he’s not talking about measuring that temple, is he? No.” He says people want a rebuilt temple “because they’re trying to reduce this down to a natural temple.”
Does God live in buildings made by people?
He says no: “God does not dwell in temples made with hands.” He says the real temple is the church and the Jewish temple “pointed to the church, the real temple of God.”
Why does he ask where Mount Sinai is?

He says Galatians says Hagar is Mount Sinai “in Arabia,” and asks Bible scholars, “could it be that the maps are wrong and Mount Sinai is actually in another place that the maps haven’t told us?” He says he is “just throwing that out.”
What does he mean by “the new Jerusalem”?
He says “we are come to… the new Jerusalem, the church,” and “He’s after you. He’s interested in you.”
What is a temple, according to him?
He says “a temple is an abiding place, a home is a place of residence, abiding place. He wants to take up residence in your life.”
Can a Christian defile the temple of God?
He says yes, in the sense that “us human beings are not to defile the temple,” since “you are the temple of God and the Spirit of God dwells in you.”
How long do the two witnesses prophesy?

He says “for three and a half years,” with fire coming out of their mouths, and they “tormented the people on earth.” He says to the young people that God is going to manifest Himself and “you’re going to be glad you chose Christ when that happens.”
Why does he say the two witnesses are not Moses and Elijah?
He says “no man of God has ever gone through the earth spitting fire out and destroying those who oppose them,” and “it’s definitely not Moses and Elijah.”
Does the Bible say the beast is the antichrist?
He says “nowhere in the Bible, church, does it say the beast is the antichrist.” He adds, “Nowhere does it say the beast and the antichrist are the same person.”
How can everyone on earth see the two witnesses?
He says it is the same as everyone seeing Jesus when He comes: “does God need a satellite TV to do that? No, He just opens your eyes to see.”
Why were 7,000 people killed in the earthquake?
He says it “doesn’t make sense” for “millions of people in the city” unless you know of “7,000 in Israel that did not bow their knee.”
When does he say the sacrifices ceased?
He says “it’s when Jesus died on the cross. Right. When He died, there was no more sacrifices.” and when He said “It is finished,” that is “when the sacrifices were finished.”
What sacrifice does he say is left for believers?
He says “the sacrifice of praise, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks unto His name,” which “most Christians will not do” because of the way they were raised.
He says yes: “Is He the King of kings and Lord of lords of the nations now? Yeah.” He cites “All power is given to Me in heaven and in earth.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Revelation 12 that the manchild is Jesus, the dragon is Satan the accuser, and the brethren overcome him by the blood of the Lamb and the word of their…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Revelation 12 that the manchild is Jesus, the dragon is Satan the accuser, and the brethren overcome him by the blood of the Lamb and the word of their testimony. He says the remnant lives on earth and is called to rule over sin now.
Who is the woman and the manchild in Revelation 12?

He describes the woman clothed with the sun, the manchild, and the dragon who persecutes her. He asks, “is the woman Israel?” and “Is it the church? Is it Mary?” He says of the manchild, “We know that Jesus is the manchild. There’s no question about it.”
Who is the woman and the manchild in Revelation 12?

Let’s go to Revelations 12. It talks about a woman with the moon under her feet, clothed with the sun, and delivering a manchild. Okay? She’s going to birth a manchild. And the dragon comes to keep the woman from birthing the manchild. And then the dragon comes to persecute the woman who birthed the manchild and her seed. Okay, let’s watch this. Now, is the woman Israel? You know, she’s got 12 stars in her crown, as we can see there. She’s got a crown up there. There’s 12 tribes. Actually, there’s 13. Is it the church? Is it Mary? We know Mary birthed what? Jesus Christ. We know that. We know that Jesus is the manchild. There’s no question about it. There ain’t no confusion here. But who’s this woman? Who is this woman? Is it Israel? Is it Mary? “The woman fled into the wilderness, prepared by God, that they would feed her 1,260 days,” or three and a half years. Here we are, another three and a half years. “And when the dragon saw he was cast to the earth, he persecuted the woman who gave birth to the male child.”
Who is the woman and the manchild in Revelation 12?

Revelation 12:1-6: Now a great sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet, and on her head a garland of twelve stars. Then being with child, she cried out in labor and in pain to give birth. And another sign appeared in heaven: behold, a great, fiery red dragon having seven heads and ten horns, and seven diadems on his heads. His tail drew a third of the stars of heaven and threw them to the earth. And the dragon stood before the woman who was ready to give birth, to devour her Child as soon as it was born. She bore a male Child who was to rule all nations with a rod of iron. And her Child was caught up to God and His throne. Then the woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, that they should feed her there one thousand two hundred and sixty days.
Can the woman be Mary or Israel?

He says there is “no record that she was persecuted by Satan, and obviously no flood,” and that Israel was persecuted yet “did not eliminate that nation.” He notes that “many of them, by the way, have accepted Christ.”
Can the woman be Mary or Israel?

“But the woman was given two wings like a great eagle to fly into the wilderness, where she is nourished for three and a half years. The serpent spit out water out of his mouth like a flood, trying to drown the woman and carry her away by a flood. But the earth opened up and helped the woman and swallowed up the flood.” Now, we know Mary birthed Jesus. We know that she fled into Egypt. We don’t know how many years, but she did go into Egypt. We have no record that she was persecuted by Satan, and obviously no flood. Israel is made up of 12 tribes, and one person out of Israel, Mary, birthed Jesus.
Can the woman be Mary or Israel?

Revelation 12:14-16: But the woman was given two wings of a great eagle, that she might fly into the wilderness to her place, where she is nourished for a time and times and half a time, from the presence of the serpent. So the serpent spewed water out of his mouth like a flood after the woman, that he might cause her to be carried away by the flood. But the earth helped the woman, and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed up the flood which the dragon had spewed out of his mouth.
Is the woman the church, and what is God’s goal for her? (Galatians 4:19, Colossians 1:27, Ephesians 4:13)

He reads “My little children, in whom I travail and birth again until Christ be formed in you,” and says God’s goal is “the fullness of the stature of… Jesus Christ,” not the preacher, the TV evangelist or the great book writer. He says, “God has a goal, a destiny, to birth Himself in you till you are like Him.”
Is the woman the church, and what is God’s goal for her? (Galatians 4:19, Colossians 1:27, Ephesians 4:13)

And Satan has persecuted Israel since Christ was here, and even before. Okay? Satan’s persecution of Israel did not eliminate that nation. They’re still with us today in spite of the persecution. And many of them, by the way, have accepted Christ. The church. Galatians 4:19. Are you ready for this? “My little children, in whom I travail and birth again until Christ be formed in you.” Oh, oh, Christ be formed in you. Ah, Colossians 1:27: “God would make known what is the riches of His glory of this mystery among the nations,” among the unbelievers, “which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.” Ephesians 4:13: “Till we all come into the unity of the faith, the knowledge of the Son of Man, unto a perfect man, unto the measure and the stature of the fullness of Christ.” Wow. Not only is He being formed in His church, but it tells us what the goal is: the fullness of the stature of the preacher? No. The TV evangelist? No. The great book writer? No. Of Jesus Christ.
Is the woman the church, and what is God’s goal for her? (Galatians 4:19, Colossians 1:27, Ephesians 4:13)

Galatians 4:19: My little children, for whom I labor in birth again until Christ is formed in you, Colossians 1:27: To them God willed to make known what are the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles: which is Christ in you, the hope of glory. Ephesians 4:13: till we all come to the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to a perfect man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ;
Has the church been persecuted since Jesus ascended?

He says “Satan has persecuted the church since Jesus ascended,” and gives figures from the Voice of the Martyrs and the International Bulletin of Missionary Research. He gives examples from different centuries and countries and asks, “That sounds big to me. How about you?”
Has the church been persecuted since Jesus ascended?

God has a goal, a destiny, to birth Himself in you till you are like Him. Wow. We know these things. Are you there? Satan has persecuted the church since Jesus ascended. More than 43 million Christians have been killed for their faith since the crucifixion of Jesus Christ. These statistics are from the 2004 Voice of the Martyrs and the International Bulletin of Missionary Research. Six to 12 million Christians were killed the first 250 years after Christ. And we’re looking for some great persecution up the road as the only one, as the big deal, as the big tribulation. That sounds big to me. How about you? That’s big time. The Catholic Church persecuted and killed many Protestant believers in Europe for leaving the Catholic Church. According to many resources, Hitler killed 3 million Christians and persecuted millions more during the Second World War. Leading up to it and during it, the Muslims have killed people in our day. October 2005, three teenagers were beheaded because they were going to a private Christian school in Indonesia. Three 12-year-old Indonesian Christian schoolgirls were beheaded by the Muslims. Again, in October 2010, a 14-year-old boy working in a factory was beheaded because he would not denounce Jesus Christ. Orphanage workers were beheaded in August of 2010, just last year. In 2008, they sliced off the head of a 25-year-old man in Kenya for converting to Christianity. China killed 30,000 Christians in 1900. In 1912, 40 had their eyes put out and they were beheaded because they wouldn’t denounce Christ. Thousands have died when the communists took over in China.
Is the great tribulation still in the future?

He recounts that believers behind the Iron Curtain told missionaries, “You told us we wouldn’t go through the tribulation. What do you think we’ve been in, man?” He gives more present-day figures, and says “this tribulation thing, it isn’t something we’ve got to wait for. It’s in the world right now.”
Is the great tribulation still in the future?

An estimated 250,000 Christians died in China from the 1950 takeover, that era, until the present. How many know that’s serious tribulation? In fact, when the Iron Curtain opened back up and we were allowed to go back in, the first thing the believers there told the missionaries that came is, “You told us that we would not go through the tribulation.” That was the first words out of their mouth: “You told us we wouldn’t go through the tribulation. What do you think we’ve been in, man?” Are you there? Is this making sense to you? Or am I confusing you? There’s a lot of persecution been going on, folks, for a long time. 270 Christian martyrs happen every 24 hours for the last 10 years. That’s over a million Christians that have died for Christ since 2001. That’s big-time stuff. There have been more than 26 [unclear] documented cases of martyrdom from 1900 to the year 2000. More than 200 million Christians in over 60 nations face persecution each day. 150,000 are martyred each year, and about one and a half million over a 10-year period. Christians today are the most persecuted group in the world. Persecution is on the rise because of communism and the expansion of Islamic and Hindu extremism. Literally hundreds of thousands of people today are being killed and brutalized, sold as slaves, tortured, imprisoned, threatened, discriminated against, and arrested solely because they are Christians. That’s some serious persecution, folks. That’s some serious tribulation times. Am I right? And you don’t have to be a Christian. You can be persecuted just because of your nationality or your race. Remember the blacks in the United States were persecuted for a long time. When I was a boy, they had to take shoeshine jobs and sweeping the floors, and they were terribly mistreated. I’ve seen it with my own eyes. And over in Africa right now, the whites are being persecuted by the blacks. Their property is taken, they’re killed. The blacks, which rose up and said, “The whites are mistreating us,” once they got in power, they reversed it. And whites in Africa are being tormented, tortured, and killed, and their property taken away. Why? Because they’re white. So this tribulation thing, it isn’t something we’ve got to wait for. It’s in the world right now. Could that be an amen? Yes. Religions have persecuted religions. Atheists have persecuted believers and killed them.
Who is the male child who rules with a rod of iron? (2 Timothy 3:12, Revelation 2:26, Acts 1:9, Psalm 2:9)

He says “all that live godly in Christ shall suffer” persecution, and that the male child is Jesus: “That part’s a no-brainer.” He reads Revelation 2:26 and says “we can overcome to what we rule… He will cause us to rule.”
Who is the male child who rules with a rod of iron? (2 Timothy 3:12, Revelation 2:26, Acts 1:9, Psalm 2:9)

Now, you’re going to tell these people that the great tribulation hasn’t come yet? Think about it. Are you with me? It’s something that’s been around for 2,000 years. The Bible says in 2 Timothy 3:12 that “all that live godly in Christ shall suffer” what? Persecution. You know, it’s not about being a believer. They don’t care if you believe in Christ. They just don’t want you living for Him. Now, the male child. You want to find out who the male child is? This is an easy one. Jesus. “She bore a male child who was to rule all nations with a rod of iron.” “And her child was caught up to God and His throne.” Okay. Revelations 2:26: “He that overcomes and keeps My works until the end, to him will I give power over the nations, and he will rule them with a rod of iron.
