As the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers, even as I received from My Father.” So who’s the person that rules with a rod of iron? Jesus. And we can what? Do the same. We can overcome to what we rule. See, we don’t have to sin like the nations sin. We don’t have to give in to things like the nations give into. He will cause us to rule. Amen. Because that’s what He is. He’s an overcomer. Acts 1:9. “While they watched, Jesus was taken up, and a cloud received Him out of their sight.” And the angel said in verse 11, “This same Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will so come in like manner as you saw Him go into heaven.” So who’s the one that’s the manchild that’s born and ascended back to the Father? Jesus Christ. That part’s a no-brainer. That’s an easy one. Psalms tells us that Jesus would rule the nations with a rod of iron. Psalms 2:9. Okay. Now, who’s this dragon? This persecutor. He hates our guts. Well, this same chapter tells us it’s Satan. “Another sign appeared in heaven: a fiery red dragon having seven heads and 10 horns and seven diadems on his head.
Who is the male child who rules with a rod of iron? (2 Timothy 3:12, Revelation 2:26, Acts 1:9, Psalm 2:9)

2 Timothy 3:12: Yes, and all who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution. Revelation 2:26: And he who overcomes, and keeps My works until the end, to him I will give power over the nations— Acts 1:9: Now when He had spoken these things, while they watched, He was taken up, and a cloud received Him out of their sight. Psalm 2:9: You shall break them with a rod of iron; You shall dash them to pieces like a potter’s vessel.’ ”
Who is the dragon in Revelation 12? (Revelation 12:3-9)
He reads that the dragon is “that old serpent called the Devil and Satan,” and asks, “what’s Satan’s job? To deceive the whole world.” He says Satan is on the earth, “He’s here, folks.”
Who is the dragon in Revelation 12? (Revelation 12:3-9)

“His tail threw a third of the stars from heaven to the earth. And the dragon stood before the woman who was ready to give birth, to devour her child as soon as it was born.” And Satan was thrown out of heaven. “And Michael and his angels fought with the dragon, and his angels, and they were cast down. That old serpent called the Devil and Satan,” verse 9, “who deceives the whole world. He was cast to the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.” So wait, what’s Satan’s job? To deceive the whole world. Okay? And where is he at? On earth. He’s here, folks. He’s the one that tested Jesus in the garden. Remember, I mean, in the wilderness, remember?
Who is the dragon in Revelation 12? (Revelation 12:3-9)

Revelation 12:3-9: And another sign appeared in heaven: behold, a great, fiery red dragon having seven heads and ten horns, and seven diadems on his heads. His tail drew a third of the stars of heaven and threw them to the earth. And the dragon stood before the woman who was ready to give birth, to devour her Child as soon as it was born. She bore a male Child who was to rule all nations with a rod of iron. And her Child was caught up to God and His throne. Then the woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, that they should feed her there one thousand two hundred and sixty days. And war broke out in heaven: Michael and his angels fought with the dragon; and the dragon and his angels fought, but they did not prevail, nor was a place found for them in heaven any longer. So the great dragon was cast out, that serpent of old, called the Devil and Satan, who deceives the whole world; he was cast to the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.
What does it mean that Satan is “the accuser of our brethren”? (Revelation 12:10, Luke 10:17-18)

He says Satan accuses you in your mind, “See, you’re no good. You’re a failure,” and “Christ isn’t finished with your life yet.” He ties Revelation 12 to the 70 who returned and Jesus saying, “I saw Satan as lightning fall from heaven.”
What does it mean that Satan is “the accuser of our brethren”? (Revelation 12:10, Luke 10:17-18)

He’s here. He’s already been thrown down. He’s been here for a long time. Ain’t that right? Don’t we know that? We know that. “Then I heard a voice saying in heaven, ‘Now salvation, strength, and the kingdom of our God and the power of Christ have come. For the accuser of our brethren, who accused them before our God day and night, has been cast down.’” So he’s called the serpent, Satan, the Devil, and the what? Accuser. And yes, he’ll come and accuse you. You make a mistake, he’s going to be right there talking in your mind, your subconscious, saying, “See, you’re no good. You’re a failure. Just quit pretending.” What’s he doing? He’s accusing you. That’s his job. That’s what he does. He lies. He accuses. He tries to deceive you. But see, Christ has a goal for you. Christ isn’t finished with your life yet. And he don’t want Christ finishing with your life yet. He don’t want you becoming an overcomer. He don’t want you overcoming sin and living rightly in this world and being a blessing to yourself and to your family. And so he is out to deceive you. Hallelujah. Now, in Luke 10:1, 17, it says the 70 returned after being sent out with Christ, and they said, “Lord, even the devils are subject to us through Your name.” And Jesus said, “I saw Satan as lightning fall from heaven.” Okay. These 70 went out, preached the gospel, people got saved, demons were cast out, and Jesus likened it to what?
What does it mean that Satan is “the accuser of our brethren”? (Revelation 12:10, Luke 10:17-18)

Revelation 12:10: Then I heard a loud voice saying in heaven, “Now salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of His Christ have come, for the accuser of our brethren, who accused them before our God day and night, has been cast down. Luke 10:17-18: Then the seventy returned with joy, saying, “Lord, even the demons are subject to us in Your name.” And He said to them, “I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven.
Have Satan and his angels already been cast down? (Jude 6, Job 1:9)

He says “this is a past tense thing” and “Has Satan and his angels already been cast down? Yeah.” He says “It isn’t some special time up the road. He’s working on us now,” and brings in Satan before the Lord in Job.
Have Satan and his angels already been cast down? (Jude 6, Job 1:9)

Satan falling. Hallelujah. So these things have been done and can be done. “If God spared not the angels that sinned, and cast them down to hell and delivered them into chains of darkness to be reserved unto judgment.” Have the angels that sinned already been cast down? Where are they reserved? In darkness till the judgment. See, this is a past tense thing. Jude 6: “The angels which kept not their first estate.” There’s only one chapter in Jude. Jude 1:6. “But left their own habitation, He has reserved in everlasting chains under darkness until the judgment of the great day.” Amen. So, has Satan and his angels already been cast down? Yeah. Is Satan trying to deceive us? Yeah. It isn’t some special time up the road. He’s working on us now. Job 1:9: Satan presented himself before the Lord after going to and fro upon the earth. So, was Satan going to and fro upon the earth in the Old Testament? Yes. To seek whom he may devour? To see who he could get to deceive and turn from God. And he accused Job before God. See, the accuser of our brethren, what does he do? Well, you know, “If Job wouldn’t serve You if You let some problems come in his life, You’ve got a hedge around him and he doesn’t have any problems. You let some problems come, You take his health, You take his kids, You take his wealth, and he’ll curse you to his face.”
Have Satan and his angels already been cast down? (Jude 6, Job 1:9)

2 Peter 2:4: For if God did not spare the angels who sinned, but cast them down to hell and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved for judgment; Jude 6: And the angels who did not keep their proper domain, but left their own abode, He has reserved in everlasting chains under darkness for the judgment of the great day; Job 1:9: So Satan answered the LORD and said, “Does Job fear God for nothing?
Will God raise up a church like Job?
He says “in these last days, God’s going to raise up a church like Job.” He says, “We serve Him because He deserves to be served.”
Will God raise up a church like Job?

And so God said, “Okay, go do your thing, Satan. You don’t know My servant Job.” And I’ll tell you, in these last days, God’s going to raise up a church like Job. We don’t serve God because He blesses us, because He gives us money and finances and health. We serve Him because He deserves to be served. We serve Him because He’s true. He’s righteous. He’s wisdom. He’s knowledge. He’s understanding. He’s everything. Amen. We know Him. We love Him. And so, Satan’s been doing this for quite a while now. Who are the brethren in Revelations 12? And who are the remnant? All right.
Who are the brethren who overcame Satan, and where are they? (Revelation 12:10-11, Matthew 12:48-50)

He says that if the brethren overcame Satan, they are “still where? On earth. They haven’t been raptured anywhere.” He cites Jesus saying those who do the Father’s will are His brethren, mother and brother.
Who are the brethren who overcame Satan, and where are they? (Revelation 12:10-11, Matthew 12:48-50)

Now, look at this. This is powerful. Very powerful. The big bad beast hadn’t even come along yet. We’ll deal with him next week. “The accuser of our brethren, who accused them before our God day and night, has been cast down.” Now, who are the brethren? The next verse, chapter 12, verse 11: “They overcome him,” which is who? Satan. Satan. They overcame. Where are they still? Where’s the saints? If they’re overcoming Satan, where are they? They’re still where? On earth. They haven’t been raptured anywhere. How are you going to get credit for overcoming Satan and up in heaven where Jesus is and God and all the angels? The credit is you overcoming where? Right here on earth. And these brethren, and the Bible throughout the New Testament, Jesus said to His disciples, “They that do the will of My Father are My brethren and My mother.” Are you aware of that? Matthew 12:48: “Who is My mother and who are My brothers?” And He stretched forth His hand toward His disciples and said, “These are My mother and My brother. For whosoever does the will of My Father, the same as My brother and My mother.” Remember that word I asked you to say earlier, “mother.” Say it again. Mother.
Who are the brethren who overcame Satan, and where are they? (Revelation 12:10-11, Matthew 12:48-50)

Revelation 12:10-11: Then I heard a loud voice saying in heaven, “Now salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of His Christ have come, for the accuser of our brethren, who accused them before our God day and night, has been cast down. And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, and they did not love their lives to the death. Matthew 12:48-50: But He answered and said to the one who told Him, “Who is My mother and who are My brothers?” And He stretched out His hand toward His disciples and said, “Here are My mother and My brothers! For whoever does the will of My Father in heaven is My brother and sister and mother.”
How do the brethren overcome Satan? (Revelation 12:11)
He says “We overcome Satan by the what? Blood of the Lamb,” and “There’s power in that blood to forgive and cleanse sin.” He adds, “You need to open your mouth. The word of their testimony.”
How do the brethren overcome Satan? (Revelation 12:11)

A mother produces something. See, in her womb is formed something, and she gives birth to something, and the church is to give birth to Jesus Christ and His righteousness. Are you with me now? Look how powerful you are. How many understand you’re the brethren? Yeah. I mean, the apostles when they wrote “brethren,” didn’t they use that word? We are the saints. We are the brethren. The brethren overcame Satan by the blood of the Lamb. And this is why I got upset last week at these two ministers. They put human counseling above the power of the blood. We overcome Satan by the what? Blood of the Lamb. There’s power in that blood to forgive and cleanse sin. “Man, by the word of their testimony.” That’s why you need to speak. You need to praise Him. You need to open your mouth. The word of their testimony. I’m a believer in Jesus. I’m a Jesus boy. See, you’ve got to speak the word. Can I hear an amen? “And they love not their life even unto death.” They put Jesus first. They overcame who? Look at that. Ain’t that cool? Now, the Bible says He will bruise Satan under your feet in [unclear]. Shortly. What are you waiting on? What’s the word? Shortly. This don’t take a lot of time. Why, man? He’s powerful. His blood’s powerful.
How do the brethren overcome Satan? (Revelation 12:11)
Revelation 12:11: And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, and they did not love their lives to the death.

He says “We don’t have to get raptured out to escape this stuff. Jesus is powerful in His church,” and reads Revelation 12:17. He asks, “Are you just a believer, or are you a remnant? Yes. Be a remnant.”

Get Satan under your feet. Don’t let that accuser open his yap about you. We know we’ve got some problems, but we know He’s the problem solver. We don’t need Satan pointing out our faults. Amen. And we don’t need to be cast down about our faults. We need to keep getting up till we don’t have those faults. Amen. And here the brethren are overcoming Satan. We don’t have to get raptured out to escape this stuff. Jesus is powerful in His church. Ah, now this is good stuff. You young ones need to understand this. Christians aren’t wimps in this world. The remnant. The remnant. Verse 17: “The dragon was enraged with the woman, and he went to make war with the remnant of her seed.” And then it explains who the remnant is: “They that have the testimony of Jesus and keep the commandments.” Are you just a believer, or are you a remnant? Yes. Be a remnant. Be the part of the crowd that keeps the testimony of Jesus and keeps His commandments. Amen. We have the testimony. That’s the covenant. We have the new covenant. He shed His blood that we could be free from sin and know Him. And He gave us great promises in this new covenant. Hallelujah. And it says that they war with Satan. He comes and wars with them. See, Satan don’t like you serving Christ. He could care the least if you’re a lukewarm, fuddy-duddy, nothing Christian, just word of mouth. What he doesn’t like, if you want to keep His commandments, man, he’s going to come after you. If you proclaim the new covenant, “I’m under the new covenant.”
Revelation 12:17: And the dragon was enraged with the woman, and he went to make war with the rest of her offspring, who keep the commandments of God and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.
Do believers have to be raptured out to escape this world’s trouble?
He says Satan “can’t stand” those who stand on the blood of Christ, and “all he can do is flap his mouth.” He says “He wants you to have an effect on this mess,” and “We rule over sin now.”
Do believers have to be raptured out to escape this world’s trouble?

If you stand on the blood of Christ, he can’t stand that. He’s going to come after you. And all he can do is flap his mouth. “You’re not good enough. You’re not worthy enough. You booed yesterday. You booed today. And you’re going to boo tomorrow. So why don’t you just get out of church and give up?” See, that’s what he does. He’s just over there, he’s a lion with no teeth. All he can do is roar. He can’t roar good. He just flaps his mouth. He just accuses, and he makes war with the remnant and persecutes them. So where is the remnant? Are they up in heaven? No. They’re on earth, church. This is powerful. Are you getting this? You know, these people got us thinking we’ve got to get raptured out of here to get any peace of mind. In fact, one of these ministers last week, I said, “You know what’s the next move of God?” He said, “It’s the second coming.” I said, “You’ve got to be kidding me.” I said, “There’s a billion people in China and most of them have not heard the word of the gospel yet, and you want Him to come?” That’s selfish. Are you out there? But that’s how they have us thinking. “Oh, come, Lord Jesus. Get me out of this mess.” No, He wants you to have an effect on this mess. So, we overcome Satan with all of his kingdom of darkness, the sins, his children that follow sin. We are what? Overcomers. We what? Overcome. When? Now. Doesn’t it say in Revelations that “I’ve made you kings and priests,” remember? And you shall reign when? On earth. Say it. On earth. We don’t have to be raptured out. We rule over sin now. We rule over things now. We rule over the kingdom of darkness now. We are rulers now. And Romans, it says what? Through death He destroyed them. And if we believe in His death, we shall what? Rule in this life.
Do believers have to be raptured out to escape this world’s trouble?

Revelation 1:6: and has made us kings and priests to His God and Father, to Him be glory and dominion forever and ever. Amen. Romans 5:17: For if by the one man’s offense death reigned through the one, much more those who receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness will reign in life through the One, Jesus Christ.)
What attitude should a believer take?

He compares a child born to a king, “destined to have the throne,” and says “We need to start taking on that attitude.” He closes, “I’m not afraid of the big bad beast. He’s afraid of me,” and says Satan is put under our feet “Shortly.”
What attitude should a believer take?

Say it. Rule in this life. Don’t you think we just need to square our shoulders back and go, “Man, hey, I’m a ruler”? May not look like much one today, but man, you know, a child born to an old-type king was destined to have the throne. And you know, he might only have been seven years old, but man, he walked around like, “Hey, man, I’m going to be the top dog one. I’m going to be the king one of these days, man.” Yeah. And he goes through all this indoctrination and training and all that. And he gets to be 12, 13, 14. You think he went around all tiny and whiny and everything? No, he was a little cocky. He was a little big-headed. “I’m going to be king one of these days. As soon as Dad moves over and the grave, I’m slipping into the throne, man. I’m going to rule and I’m going to reign.” We need to start taking on that attitude. Amen. Instead of “I’m not worthy” and “I’m this” and “I’m that,” we need to start saying, “Man, I’m getting groomed to be a king, to rule and reign in this earth, because I am a believer. I am a brethren. I am a remnant. I am His church.” Hallelujah. Yes. And I don’t have to get raptured out to get victory. I don’t have, you know, to have everything happen nice to me to serve my God. I’m going to serve my God. I’m going to serve Him with authority and power. Hallelujah. Yes. Hallelujah. And where are the saints? On earth. In Revelations 12, the saints are still where? On earth. Now, if you can figure out the two witnesses, you let me know. What scripture did I miss? And if you’re worried about the Antichrist and the beast, I’m not afraid of the big bad beast. The big bad beast. The big bad beast. I’m not afraid of the big bad beast. He’s afraid of me. How many raise your hand and say, “I accept this. I accept this, Lord. Train me. Train me overtime. Give me double time. I’m headed for rulership.” Hallelujah. People that put Satan under their feet how fast? Shortly.
Does he say the woman is Mary?
He says Mary “fled into Egypt,” but “We have no record that she was persecuted by Satan, and obviously no flood.”
What does he say is God’s goal for the church?
He says “God has a goal, a destiny, to birth Himself in you till you are like Him.”
What did believers behind the Iron Curtain tell the missionaries?
He says “the first thing the believers there told the missionaries that came is, ‘You told us that we would not go through the tribulation.’”
Does he say the great tribulation has not come yet?
He asks, “you’re going to tell these people that the great tribulation hasn’t come yet?” and says “It’s something that’s been around for 2,000 years.”
He says it is Jesus: “So who’s the person that rules with a rod of iron? Jesus. And we can what? Do the same.”
Who is the dragon, according to this sermon?
He says “this same chapter tells us it’s Satan,” the one who “deceives the whole world.”
What does he say is Satan’s job?
He says “He lies. He accuses. He tries to deceive you.” He adds, “But see, Christ has a goal for you.”
Does he say Satan has already been cast down?
He says “It isn’t some special time up the road. He’s working on us now.”
Why does he say we serve God?
He says “We don’t serve God because He blesses us… We serve Him because He deserves to be served.”
Where does he say the saints are who overcome Satan?
He says “They’re still where? On earth. They haven’t been raptured anywhere.”
What does he mean by “mother” for the church?
He says “A mother produces something,” and “the church is to give birth to Jesus Christ and His righteousness.”
How does he say we overcome Satan?
He says “That’s why you need to speak. You need to praise Him. You need to open your mouth. The word of their testimony.”
He reads “They that have the testimony of Jesus and keep the commandments,” and says “Be the part of the crowd that keeps the testimony of Jesus and keeps His commandments.”
Why does he say we should not wish to be taken out?
He says “these people got us thinking we’ve got to get raptured out of here to get any peace of mind,” and “He wants you to have an effect on this mess.”
What does he mean by “rule in this life”?
He says “Say it. Rule in this life,” and “I am a believer. I am a brethren. I am a remnant. I am His church.”

items.t: The Six Seals — Book of Revelation
items.d: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches on the first six seals of Revelation 6 and the sealing of God’s people in Revelation 7, warning that just as the Jews’ charts missed the first coming, end-time charts can miss…
items.ser: Book of Revelation · The Six Seals
p: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches on the first six seals of Revelation 6 and the sealing of God’s people in Revelation 7, warning that just as the Jews’ charts missed the first coming, end-time charts can miss the second. He reads the four horsemen from Scripture alone, argues the black horse is not famine and the pale horse’s power is limited, and says Christ’s return waits for the martyrs, the sealing of God’s people and a great harvest from every nation.
Why should we approach the book of Revelation humbly?

He says the Jews and preachers had their charts when Jesus came the first time “and they missed every point,” expecting a son of David to restore the natural kingdom from Rome. He says they had doctrines about food, clothes and the Sabbath, and missed Jesus totally, “and we can be wrong today.”
Why should we approach the book of Revelation humbly?

Seriously okay we’re going to get into the Bible this morning and we are talking about the book of Revelation and today we’re going to be talking about six of these seven seals. Now the approach to Revelation is strictly from the book of Revelation and you got to remember this please get this in your cranial vacuum what I’m going to say. The Jews and the preachers when Jesus came had their charts they had it all figured out. What was going to happen how it was going to happen and they missed every point. Do you realize that you see the Jews had it wrong the first time Jesus came they were looking for a son of David to restore the kingdom to them from Rome and the messiah wasn’t coming to restore the kingdom the natural kingdom from from Rome to them he was coming to put a kingdom in people’s lives see they were totally wrong and we can be wrong today they were they did not know the messiah was God himself when he come the first time they didn’t have that in their charts and their predictions they did not know it is things within that defile us and not what we eat or what we wear. The Seventh-day Adventists they’re still into the food program the holiness people are into no jewelry and no makeup and you know look paled and don’t go to hell you know. And it’s not what we eat we can eat pork we can eat what it has nothing to do with our character and nothing to do with our spiritual man and nothing to do a sin see it’s what comes out those words and those actions that’s what defiles us and condemns us they did not they had doctrines of clothes the Sabbath day journey you can only go so far on the Sabbath day that’s not in the Bible they made it up ah the washing of hands and dishes and all this stuff you see they had all of these doctrines and when Jesus came they missed it totally they didn’t know that John the Baptist was Elijah that was come in the spirit the forerunner of Jesus and they cut off his head they wanted and tried to kill Jesus God himself which violated the Ten Commandments they come to a claim to believe in amen and a lot of these theoretical people about the second coming they don’t balance their checkbook they don’t stay married they violate the very book that they say that they believe in but yet they got the second coming all figured out.
Should we trust preachers who claim to know the end time?

He says preachers have made millions selling “a bill of goods” claiming to know the end time, though Jesus said no man knows the day or the hour. He says end-time teaching often leads us to leave Jesus, “the most important person in the Bible,” for petty doctrines: “if they miss the first time could it be possible we don’t know beans about the second time.”
Should we trust preachers who claim to know the end time?

And let me tell you something preachers have made millions of dollars selling you a bill of goods claiming to know the inside of the end time when Jesus himself and God himself said twice no man knows the day or the hour they still predict the day they spill still still predict the year and the month and everything else and it says plainly what? Nobody knows but God himself. And you buy their books and you got the book to read yourself and they’re making a fortune literally. Some believe Jesus was an old prophet risen from the dead look at that doctrine they conjured up well this is one of the [unclear] I don’t know which one but it’s one of them that raised from the dead. And they believe Jesus was a sinner they called him a sinner and he’s God and God cannot what sin the Bible says there was no sin in him and this is what they said if we leave Jesus alone all will believe on him well duh. That’s the whole point. We’re supposed to be believing and trusting in and following Jesus Christ but they wanted people to believe in their group their doctrine and leave Jesus and this is what happens with the second coming teaching we wind up leaving Jesus himself the most important person in the Bible the goal of the Bible and get into our petty little doctrines that mean nothing are you with me now my point is this if they miss the first time could it be possible we don’t know beans about the second time see they knew the messiah was coming just as we know Jesus is what coming again we know that it says over and over he’s coming the second time and
Did even the apostles and John the Baptist misunderstand?

He says the apostles did not understand when Jesus told them He would die, and John the Baptist, after declaring Jesus the Lamb of God, later sent to ask, “are you the one.” He says a popular end-time author has changed his theory many times, and says “let’s just keep this thing simple.”
Did even the apostles and John the Baptist misunderstand?

so with that introduction we’re going to be read we’re going to be studying this book of Revelations even the apostles did not understand that Jesus was [unclear] he told him I’m going to die and they still didn’t get it, in that right? so just because we hear something does that mean we got it no. No in fact Peter says well you can’t die we’re not gonna let you die. They wanted to be in charge of others the first in you know they wanted to be number one they wanted to build three tabernacles when Jesus was transfigured they wanted to build one for Jesus one for Moses and one for Elijah see they got it all wrong and these are the apostles the chosen 12. John the Baptist after declaring that Jesus was the one to come and take away the sins of the world check this out after John the Baptist declared and baptized Jesus then a little bit later he sends his disciples to Jesus said are you the one. And yet in this day an hour and these guys are proclaiming they got all this knowledge. And the guy that wrote The Late Great Planet Earth, Hal Lindsey, has changed his theory 12 times that I know of because he predicted some things that did not happen so he had to rewrite his book and people bought it again. And they just keep buying it like Hal Lindsey’s got some kind of personal insight that no one else has are you with me so with that in our cranial vacuum we don’t have a cranial vacuum anymore we got something in there you know let’s just keep this thing simple all right what are we teaching on today six of the seven seals you remember in the book of Daniel Daniel himself that they use to twist scriptures and get these ideas was told to shut up the words and seal the book.
Is it okay not to understand everything in prophecy? (Daniel 12:4, 8)

He says Daniel was told to seal the book, and even Daniel said “I heard but I understood not.” He says when Jesus came the first time people understood as things happened, and it could be the same when He comes the second time: “we can identify it as he does it.”
Is it okay not to understand everything in prophecy? (Daniel 12:4, 8)

Are you there and in the last chapter when the angel is talking to Daniel Daniel says I heard but I understood not could it be possible when we read the book of Revelations we are hearing but we’re not getting much understanding out of it and of Daniel who was one of the the heroes the three heroes of the Old Testament. Did not understand what the angel was saying could it be possible we don’t always understand things and there’s nothing wrong with it and this is the point when Jesus came the first time they started understanding as things happened the virgin conceiving and having a child see then as it was preached and it has happened then they started what getting understanding all their charts didn’t amount to anything all their programs and other ideas they come up with had to be thrown out when it started happening and it could be the same way when Jesus comes the second time when he starts doing something we’re going to go oh that’s what daddy oh that’s what that is because what God is doing something again and we can identify it as he does it and we may be totally wrong in saying how he’s going to do it could that be a good amen hallelujah and
Is it okay not to understand everything in prophecy? (Daniel 12:4, 8)

Daniel 12:4: “But you, Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book until the time of the end; many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall increase.” Daniel 12:8: Although I heard, I did not understand. Then I said, “My lord, what shall be the end of these things?”
What is the sealed book that the Lamb opens, and can God’s book of remembrance be erased? (Revelation 5:5)

He says the Lion of the tribe of Judah has prevailed to open the book and loose its seven seals, and lists books in the Bible such as the book of life, the book of works and the book of remembrance. He concludes “most likely the book in revelation is its own book it’s the book of wrath,” explaining God’s day of wrath. He says what God remembers can be erased by repenting: “the power of the blood is endless and there is nothing it can’t cleanse.”
What is the sealed book that the Lamb opens, and can God’s book of remembrance be erased? (Revelation 5:5)

with that in your head I told you this is a college course this isn’t for wimps. This is serious teaching here. You know in college you listen to the professor and then you got to go home and study for hours to get it are you there. So we got a bunch of wimps a non wimps in here this morning you came to hear this tough teaching. Hard to sit there okay we got a picture of the lamb and the seven seals are open their the book. In Revelations 5:5 the lion of the tribe of Judah that root of David has prevailed to open the book and to loose the seven seals thereof. What book? The Bible tells us about eight books in the Bible itself. The book of life you know our names in there we go to heaven if it’s not we’re in trouble the book of our works and Revelations 20:12 everything we did everything we say is written there and if we’re in the book of life we’re not judged out of the things in the book of works hallelujah. Anyway we know it’s not that book we certainly know it’s not the scriptures the Bible itself because Jesus opened understanding to them we know it’s not the judgment book of Israel and Babylon and Jeremiah because that was to them we know that the sealed book that Isaiah Isaiah saw could be it this is a sealed book Isaiah saw a sealed book but Isaiah it was sealed about an open and so it just goes on he saw a sealed book and that’s it the book was locked up and stayed locked down so maybe that could be it the book of woe in Ezekiel that Ezekiel saw could be because there’s a lot of woes when this book starts getting open there’s a lot of woes and then the sealed book of Daniel that I told you about earlier seal the book all those things he saw said seal it up until the last days but we got some revelation on Daniel’s sealed book. When Jesus came Jesus said. That the abomination of desolation when you see that you know that the time is nigh in Matthew 13:14 and in Mark, but in Luke it says when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies then know that the desolation thereof is nigh so we know that the destruction of Jerusalem in 70 AD was the fulfillment of Daniel we know that so at least part of Daniel sealed book was opened up if not all of it then and so Daniel’s book could have been fulfilled. During Jesus’s birth death and resurrection and the church period there the early church period are you with me because we have some insight that some of Daniel’s book was open so I doubt it’s Daniel’s book. Now there and we also know that Jesus came and and all that in that book of Daniel and then you got the book of remembrance in Exodus 17:14 Amalek came and attacked Israel and picked on the stragglers and the weak ones and God says I’m going to have a book of remembrance for him and a few hundred years later sure enough God says okay it’s time to judge Amalek for what he did back there to Israel and the weak ones and the stragglers he picked on the stragglers in the weak ones and he had Saul to rise up and destroy that nation and that king are you there and so I doubt it’s that book because people have been sinning ever since Eve. And yes there’s a book of remembrance and he does come to correct and deal with that most likely the book in revelation is its own book it’s the book of wrath it’s a book that explains God’s day of wrath that already has been explained throughout the scriptures it’s not a fresh new revelation are you with me I wanted you to know there’s eight books in the Bible see there is a book of remembrance when you do things God remembers all right you can get it erased by what. Repenting absolutely I was wrong that’s the power of the blood the power of the blood is endless and there is nothing it can’t cleanse don’t ever forget that and a simple humbling yourself and admitting you’re wrong and asking forgiveness and cleansing gets it done hell yeah that’s the bottom line now. items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Revelation 19:10 that “the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy,” and that prophecy means speaking by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit within the…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Revelation 19:10 that “the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy,” and that prophecy means speaking by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit within the boundary of Scripture. He then lists marks of false prophets from Jeremiah 2 and 23.
What is “the testimony of Jesus” in Revelation 19:10?

He says the angel told John not to worship him but God, because the angel and the brethren “have the testimony of Jesus,” and that testimony “is the spirit of prophecy.” He says this angel had been speaking by the inspiration of the Spirit for 19 chapters.
What is “the testimony of Jesus” in Revelation 19:10?

We’re going to start in Revelation chapter 19:10. Remember, the angel has been talking to John for 19 chapters, and, uh, it’s the same angel that’s in Revelation 17:7. The angel said to me, it’s the same one talking. And, uh, John fell at his feet to worship this angel, and the angel said, “Don’t do that. Worship God. I am your fellow servant and of your brethren. I am the servant of the same master as you and your brethren.” See, worship God, and me, the angel, the fellow servant, and the brethren have the testimony of Jesus. What do they have? The testimony of Jesus. So there is a testimony of Jesus, and then he tells us what that testimony is: the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.
What is “the testimony of Jesus” in Revelation 19:10?

Revelation 19:10: And I fell at his feet to worship him. But he said to me, “See that you do not do that! I am your fellow servant, and of your brethren who have the testimony of Jesus. Worship God! For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.”
What does “the spirit of prophecy” mean, and why does the church need it?

He says prophecy “means speaking by the inspiration of the Spirit,” not human intellect, wishes or opinions, but “the Spirit’s truth and facts.” He says Jesus’s testimony, the evidence of who He is, is the spirit of prophecy, and the church needs the witness and proof of Jesus shown by it.
What does “the spirit of prophecy” mean, and why does the church need it?

Prophecy, and that’s what this angel had been doing for 19 chapters. He had been speaking by the inspiration. Prophecy means speaking by the inspiration of the Spirit. The Spirit’s involved, not your human intellect, not your human wishes, your human opinions, but it’s the Spirit’s truth and facts that is being spoken. And so the testimony, the witness of Jesus, is the spirit of prophecy. Now, if you’ve ever been in a courtroom (I’ve been there several times), a person gives their testimony. They’re giving the testimony, the evidence of what they experience, or what they are, or who they are, or whatever, you see. So Jesus’s testimony, the evidence of who He is, is the spirit of prophecy. When His presence comes, the proof that it’s Jesus’s presence is the spirit of prophecy. Are you out there? Now, I know this is new to a lot of people, but we have been religious for too long in America. We need to get into Bible doctrine and Bible experience. Is that an amen? Yes! We need to buck up and come up. So in the church, it is imperative that we have the witness, the proof, the evidence, the testimony of Jesus, and that would be shown by the spirit of prophecy. Hallelujah. See, Paul said in 1 Corinthians 14, “Desire spiritual gifts, but rather that you...” What? What? Prophesy: speak by the inspiration of the Holy Ghost. How many can say amen to that? You know, healing lasts for the time that you get healed, but tomorrow and the days after, in all your life, you’ve got to talk, and some of us don’t talk too well, do we? So we need that, the spirit of prophecy.
What does “the spirit of prophecy” mean, and why does the church need it?
1 Corinthians 14:1: Pursue love, and desire spiritual gifts, but especially that you may prophesy.
How did Jesus speak by the spirit of prophecy?

He says the temple soldiers sent to arrest Jesus came back empty-handed because they were so influenced by what came out of His mouth: “Never spake a man like this Man.” He says Jesus spoke what the Bible did say, with authority and power, and that it is “the living word of God that pierces and pricks men’s hearts.”
How did Jesus speak by the spirit of prophecy?

Now, just to show you that the angel knows what he’s talking about, going back to Jesus, John 7:46. The temple soldiers were sent down to get Jesus and arrest Him and bring Him back. Well, these soldiers went down there, and Jesus was teaching the people, and the soldiers were so influenced by what was coming out of His mouth, that spirit of prophecy, that they wouldn’t arrest Him. They came back empty-handed, and when the temple leaders said, “Well, where’s this man Jesus?” they said, “Never spake a man like this Man.” Why? He was speaking by the spirit of prophecy. See, He wasn’t speaking His opinions, He wasn’t speaking His feelings, He wasn’t speaking what He wished the Bible said; He spoke what the Bible did say, the spirit of prophecy. In Matthew 1:22, they were astonished at His teaching because He spoke with authority. See, that’s the spirit of prophecy. When the Spirit is involved, it comes across with power. It’s not psychology or philosophy; it is the living word of God that pierces and pricks men’s hearts. It has power in it. Amen. Second Peter 1:19. This is very important, because I’m telling you, I was saved in a Pentecostal church. I got filled with the baptism of the Holy Ghost in the Pentecostal church. [unclear] was the greatest thing that ever happened to me, but us Pentecostals did a lot of weird things, and we certainly didn’t focus on the spirit of prophecy.
How did Jesus speak by the spirit of prophecy?
John 7:46: The officers answered, “No man ever spoke like this Man!” Mark 1:22: And they were astonished at His teaching, for He taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
What boundaries keep prophecy safe? (2 Peter 1:19-21)

He says Peter gave the boundary: a “more sure word of prophecy,” which is not of private interpretation and did not come “by the will of man.” He says Isaiah and Jeremiah were only allowed to speak what the Spirit told them, and “when the Spirit speaks, He don’t care what you believe.”
What boundaries keep prophecy safe? (2 Peter 1:19-21)

And so we need boundaries for this, don’t we? And here’s the boundaries. Peter said, “We have a more sure word of prophecy. No prophecy of the Scripture is of any private interpretation,” any personal understanding. See, it’s not human ability. He said, “But the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man.” See, men’s opinions, men’s thinking, men’s deciding of what’s right and wrong had nothing to do with this. It was totally the Spirit. Doesn’t that make you feel safe? Yeah. Isaiah and Jeremiah, they weren’t allowed to throw in their opinions. They were only allowed to write and speak what the Spirit told them to. They didn’t say, “I believe.” Where did Isaiah and Jeremiah say, “Well, I believe it’s this way”? Is it in there? No. The Psalms: does the psalmist ever say, “Well, I believe this is what is truth”? No. Why? The Spirit’s talking, and the Spirit is a Spirit of what? Truth. And when the Spirit speaks, He don’t care what you believe. And I can prove it to you.
What boundaries keep prophecy safe? (2 Peter 1:19-21)

2 Peter 1:19-21: And so we have the prophetic word confirmed, which you do well to heed as a light that shines in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts; knowing this first, that no prophecy of Scripture is of any private interpretation, for prophecy never came by the will of man, but holy men of God spoke as they were moved by the Holy Spirit.
Can the Spirit speak through someone who does not believe? (Caiaphas)

He says the high priest Caiaphas hated Jesus, yet the Spirit came on him and he prophesied that Jesus was the Messiah come to die for the nation “and not only that nation but those everywhere.” He says “holy men of God spoke as they were” moved by the Holy Spirit.
Can the Spirit speak through someone who does not believe? (Caiaphas)

Caiaphas hated Jesus, didn’t he? Didn’t he? He wanted to kill Jesus, didn’t he? The high priest in Jerusalem when Jesus was there, didn’t he? Yeah. And one day the Spirit came upon Caiaphas, who hated Jesus, didn’t believe in Jesus, didn’t want Him to be the Messiah, and prophesied that Jesus was the Messiah, come to die for the sins of that nation, and not only that nation but those everywhere. Now, Caiaphas didn’t want to say that. He didn’t want to hear that. In fact, he didn’t even hear it after he spoke it. He still hated Jesus. But “holy men of God spoke as they were” what? Moved, stirred, initiated, stimulated by the Holy Spirit.
Can the Spirit speak through someone who does not believe? (Caiaphas)

John 11:49-52: And one of them, Caiaphas, being high priest that year, said to them, “You know nothing at all, nor do you consider that it is expedient for us that one man should die for the people, and not that the whole nation should perish.” Now this he did not say on his own authority; but being high priest that year he prophesied that Jesus would die for the nation, and not for that nation only, but also that He would gather together in one the children of God who were scattered abroad. 2 Peter 1:21: for prophecy never came by the will of man, but holy men of God spoke as they were moved by the Holy Spirit.
Should the church expect and seek the Holy Ghost to move?

He says he wants a church “where the Holy Ghost is stirring,” and that Pentecostals knew “the power of the Holy Ghost and what it could do.” He tells how he failed and got back up to seek God, and says God told him, “at least you’re laying before the Lord.”
Should the church expect and seek the Holy Ghost to move?

And, church, this is what we’ve got to get skillful at. See, a lot of you raised your hand a few weeks ago and said you would give one hour a day to God. I guarantee you, most of you felt guilty. Why? Because I was young once and made these promises. I had to get up many times from the failure and get back to my commitment. I didn’t stay in my failure. Hallelujah. In fact, I worked; I started work at 6:00, so I had to get up with enough time to seek God in the morning and all the rest and drive to work, and sometimes I would fall asleep seeking God, and I would feel so guilty. But God came to me and said, “Son, at least you’re laying before the Lord.” And that encouraged me. He didn’t come, “Well, you know, you’re goofed up, you’re off the map now, that’s it.” No. I had to get up the next morning and stay awake. Amen. Moved by the Holy Ghost, stirred by the Holy Ghost. How many of us want to be a church where the Holy Ghost is stirring? Yeah. This is what the Pentecostals were good at. Yes, we made mistakes, but let me tell you, we knew the power of the Holy Ghost and what it could do, and in every service we were looking for the Holy Ghost to move, and most of the time He would honor our desire. Hallelujah. Now, we did funny things when He came, but, you know, you get them corrected, you get them changed, and don’t act like these [unclear] people don’t make mistakes. I can give you a whole list of failures they do. All right, so when these people want to argue with me about the baptism of the Holy Ghost and the kooks in the Pentecostal circles, well, I can show you a lot of kooks in the fundamental circles. I’ve been there. In the Catholic circles, I can show you a lot of kooks. Hallelujah. So, you know, don’t go throw mud stones at the Pentecostals if your own house has glass. You get it?
Will the Holy Spirit ever tell you to do something that violates Scripture?

He says “the Holy Ghost will never ask you to say anything or do anything that violates Scriptures.” He says that when someone claims the Spirit told them to divorce, the Scripture is “if the unbelieving depart, let them depart,” and you stay faithful to your marriage and family.
Will the Holy Spirit ever tell you to do something that violates Scripture?

Now, so what’s the sure word? The Scriptures. The Holy Ghost will never ask you to say anything or do anything that violates Scriptures. Never. So when people tell me, you know, the Holy Spirit told them to divorce their spouse, or the Holy Spirit told them to, you know, divorce their parents, or whatever, I say, “That ain’t no Holy Ghost talking that violates Scripture.” The Scripture is, “If the unbelieving depart, let them depart.” Let them do the action; you stay faithful to your marriage, stay faithful to your family. You let them make the wrong decision; you don’t say, “In the name of the Holy Ghost, I’m going to violate the Bible.” Can I hear an amen?
Will the Holy Spirit ever tell you to do something that violates Scripture?
1 Corinthians 7:15: But if the unbeliever departs, let him depart; a brother or a sister is not under bondage in such cases. But God has called us to peace.
What is the purpose of prophecy, and can you believe whatever you want? (1 Corinthians 14:31)

He says “you’ve got to believe what Jesus told you to believe.” From 1 Corinthians 14:31 he says “all may prophesy one by one,” that this is the gift of speaking by the inspiration of the Holy Ghost, not the office of a prophet predicting the future, and that its purpose is to teach, comfort, encourage and strengthen people and bring them to Jesus.
What is the purpose of prophecy, and can you believe whatever you want? (1 Corinthians 14:31)

Amen. Then I witnessed to a lot of people, you know, and they tell me, “God said,” and they tell me, “This is what I believe.” I don’t care what you believe. You’ve got to believe what God told you to believe. You don’t have the freedom to believe what you want to believe. You’ve got to believe what Jesus told you to believe. Amen. And we need the move of the Holy Spirit, and if we will start spending this one hour a day, and we will come into our services with the goal to let the Holy Spirit move and stir us and speak through us and pray through us and sing through us, I want to show you what will happen. Now, 1 Corinthians 14:31: “Some of you will prophesy.” Is that what it says? No, it doesn’t. “All may” what? Prophesy. Now, this is not the office of a prophet predicting the future. This is the gift of speaking by the inspiration of the Holy Ghost. “All may prophesy one by one.” In other words, don’t two of you talk at the same time. And, uh, the purpose is that we may learn. The purpose of prophecy is to teach the people, and not just teach them but comfort them, encourage them, strengthen them, and call them alongside Jesus. If what we’re saying isn’t bringing them to Jesus, we’re off base. See, if what we’re saying isn’t clear enough to encourage and motivate them to turn from sin and live a better life and come to Jesus, we’re off base. See, prophecy is a teaching avenue, an instruction avenue. Hallelujah. And, and, and, church, I believe in this stuff, and I’ve experienced this stuff, and I’ve preached all over the world, and this stuff works. I’m 70 years old, I’ve been around. I’ve preached in the jungles of Paraguay, I’ve preached in the jungles of Africa, because “jungle” seems to think, “Wow!” I also preached in the capital of Paraguay. “Oh, really?” But I say “jungle,” “Oh man, you suffered for Christ.” Yes! You go to the jungles; you go wherever people are that want to hear the word of God. Amen. See, I preached out in the volcanoes of San Salvador.
What is the purpose of prophecy, and can you believe whatever you want? (1 Corinthians 14:31)
1 Corinthians 14:31: For you can all prophesy one by one, that all may learn and all may be encouraged.
Whose voice does the church need to hear: people or the Spirit?

He says seven times Revelation says to hear “what the Spirit is saying to the churches,” not what the philosophers or latest authors are saying. He says “what I need is what the Holy Spirit is saying to me,” and “I don’t need psychology,” but a word from the Holy Ghost that strengthens him on the inside.
Whose voice does the church need to hear: people or the Spirit?

God’s whole purpose in this church is to touch people’s lives, not to flatter you and make you feel good, but to get you to a place where you can be used by the Holy Spirit. Is that an amen? Now, remember, seven times it says in Revelation, “He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit is saying to the churches.” Not what the philosophers are saying to the church, what the latest authors are saying to the church. No: what the Spirit is saying to the church. I could care the least what Billy Graham has to say. I could care the least what Oral Roberts and Joyce Meyer and all them have to say. What I need is what the Holy Spirit is saying to me, for my family, my time, in my place. I need a word from the Spirit encouraging me, moving me, strengthening me. Can I hear an amen?
Whose voice does the church need to hear: people or the Spirit?
Revelation 2:7: “He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To him who overcomes I will give to eat from the tree of life, which is in the midst of the Paradise of God.” ’
How can you identify a false prophet? (Jeremiah 2:8)

He begins a list of marks of a false prophet from Jeremiah 2:8, the first being that they prophesy by Baal. He says the Bible shows Baal as an idol and that “some people do speak by the anointing of the demonic world,” in a spiritual world that is real.
How can you identify a false prophet? (Jeremiah 2:8)

Amen. And I don’t need psychology, and I don’t need you to pat me on the back to make me feel good. What I need is a word from the Holy Ghost that strengthens, quickens me on the inside. Hallelujah. I don’t need a 12-step program when I got a one-step program: Jesus Christ. Maybe two steps: His word. Jesus and His word heals you and sets you free, that Holy Spirit. Can I hear an amen? Now, I want to show you the marks of a false prophet. It’s easy to identify them. Jeremiah 2:8, number one: the prophets prophesy by Baal. All right, the Bible says Baal’s an idol, and Baal was many idols, and the Bible says when they talked about this that they sacrificed to devils. So some people do speak by the anointing of the demonic world. Now, I know scientists don’t believe in demons and all that, but, you know, they’re scientists. All they do, they just think we’re just a physical world and that’s it. We are also in a spiritual world.
How can you identify a false prophet? (Jeremiah 2:8)

Jeremiah 2:8: The priests did not say, ‘Where is the LORD?’ And those who handle the law did not know Me; The rulers also transgressed against Me; The prophets prophesied by Baal, And walked after things that do not profit.
Can people speak by a demonic spirit, even in the name of Jesus?

He says some people speak by a demonic spirit and that “Christians are so naive because they don’t know this.” He points to the woman with the familiar spirit in Acts, who “had a limited knowledge of things,” and says demons “can only do what God allows them to do.”
Can people speak by a demonic spirit, even in the name of Jesus?

Amen. And this is where the church comes in. Whether you like it or not, you’re in a spiritual world that’s influenced by principalities and powers of the spirit, and you have a spirit in you. Like the woman with the, uh, familiar spirit in Acts: she could tell the people that Paul and them were servants of the Most High God. She had a limited knowledge of things by the demonic spirit. Are you there? Limited. They do have limited power; they can only do what God allows them to do, number one. And so God didn’t care if she told them they were servants of the Most High God. God wanted them to know they were servants of the Most High God. See, her owners (she was a slave) and her owners made a lot of money with her fortune telling. Yeah, and Paul just said, “Bam, come out of here,” and that thing was gone, and there went their money, and they got mad and they wanted to kill Paul. Okay, some people speak by demonic spirit. I’ve been in churches, in meetings, where people are speaking by demonic sources, and Christians are so naive because they don’t know this. Christ, and they don’t know their Bible, they, you know, they don’t do it and say, “I’m a demon talking.” They do it in the name of Jesus. God and the Bible, are you there? I remember my first encounter was in Alabama. I went to this advertised meeting, and that woman up there was speaking by a demon, and she was telling people their addresses and, you know, “You got cigarettes in your pocket,” and all that. And I kept my eyes right on her. I dared her to come to me. I was daring her, and she knew it. I would have set her straight in a jiffy. And I was only a year and a half old in God, but I had read my Bible through a couple of times by now, and studied it, and been active in soul winning and all the rest. I had gotten strong in a year and a half. I didn’t mess around, you know. Three months after I was saved, I was going door-to-door witnessing. Are you there? I took a soul-winning class, I got with the program, I got up and sung special songs like they did today in church, at the missions, at the jails. I got my guitar, and I took it out there where the sinners were, and I would sing, then I would preach. Hello! People say, “What makes you different?” That’s one of the things that makes you different. I got involved very quickly. I didn’t use excuses. I worked six days a week; I worked 12 hours a day for five of them and a half a day for the other one, and yet I still found time for the kingdom. So you get strong. Amen.
Can people speak by a demonic spirit, even in the name of Jesus?

Acts 16:16-18: Now it happened, as we went to prayer, that a certain slave girl possessed with a spirit of divination met us, who brought her masters much profit by fortune-telling. This girl followed Paul and us, and cried out, saying, “These men are the servants of the Most High God, who proclaim to us the way of salvation.” And this she did for many days. But Paul, greatly annoyed, turned and said to the spirit, “I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her.” And he came out that very hour.
What do false prophets do that leads people astray? (Jeremiah 23)

He says they walk after things that do not profit you spiritually, they lead people astray from “Jesus and righteousness,” and they say sin is okay. He calls the idea that it doesn’t matter what you do “a lie from the pit of hell.”
What do false prophets do that leads people astray? (Jeremiah 23)

Church, now they walk after things that do not profit you. You can tell them by their lifestyle. See, they behave in things that do not profit you spiritually. They give themselves to things that don’t profit you spiritually and don’t profit the kingdom. Number three, the prophets of Samaria (that’s the capital of the northern kingdom, Israel). They prophesy in Baal, and they cause my people Israel to err. See, you lead people astray. You lead people astray from what? Jesus and righteousness. Number four, the prophets of Jerusalem (that’s the capital of the southern kingdom, Judah and Benjamin). They commit adultery. “Homosexuality is okay, adultery is okay, sex with children is okay, incest is okay, you know, hallelujah, you’re saved by grace through faith, and not of yourselves, it is the gift of God, not of works. It don’t matter what you do, you can just, you know, you believe in Jesus, you’re just going to heaven.” That is a lie from the pit of hell.
What do false prophets do that leads people astray? (Jeremiah 23)

Jeremiah 23:13-14: “And I have seen folly in the prophets of Samaria: They prophesied by Baal And caused My people Israel to err. Also I have seen a horrible thing in the prophets of Jerusalem: They commit adultery and walk in lies; They also strengthen the hands of evildoers, So that no one turns back from his wickedness. All of them are like Sodom to Me, And her inhabitants like Gomorrah. Ephesians 2:8-9: For by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, lest anyone should boast.
Is believing in Jesus enough, or must you also live right?

He asks whether the rich man who came to Jesus was told to believe or to keep the commandments. He says “salvation is a two-banked river: faith in Christ and His blood and death on the cross for forgiveness, and living right.”
Is believing in Jesus enough, or must you also live right?

When the rich man came to Jesus and said, “What must I do to have eternal life?” did He say believe, or did He say keep the commandments? See, salvation is a two-banked river: faith in Christ and His blood and death on the cross for forgiveness, and living right. Amen. See, it doesn’t help my wife (I’ve told you this many times), it doesn’t help my wife and my children if I believe in Christ. What helps them is when I live for Christ. See, I don’t go out on my wife, I don’t mistreat my children, I encourage them and I bring them up in the way. See, if I just believe, that doesn’t help them a hill of beans. They don’t do them any good if I’m a bad example to them. What good is my religion? They walk in lies.
Is believing in Jesus enough, or must you also live right?

Matthew 19:16-17: Now behold, one came and said to Him, “Good Teacher, what good thing shall I do that I may have eternal life?” So He said to him, “Why do you call Me good? No one is good but One, that is, God. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.”
What does it mean that false prophets “strengthen the hands of evildoers”?

He says it means calling sin acceptable and encouraging it, and that “preachers have got to stand up and blatantly tell them they are wrong.” He says false prophets would rather have a thousand in their church than preach anything that offends, and that real Bible prophecy turns people from doing wrong.
What does it mean that false prophets “strengthen the hands of evildoers”?

They strengthen the hands of evildoers. Now, I’m going to tell you something that’s going to hurt some of you, but you need to hear this. Obama has strengthened the hand of evildoers when he says homosexuality is an acceptable lifestyle and forcing it on us. He claims to be a Christian. His Democratic Party, which is 52% liberals, and if you ever read the Democratic platform, it has strengthened the hand of evildoers, you know, using abortion as a contraceptive. “Go ahead and commit adultery, make a mistake, we’ll pay you to have an abortion.” See, and they call it women’s health. And I’m sorry that this offends people, but, folks, I, as a preacher, have to hit the, the, the iron where it’s at, and when these people are blatantly disobeying and encouraging sin in the nation, preachers have got to stand up and blatantly tell them they are wrong. Can I hear an amen? He don’t even want chaplain to preach their conviction in the military. That’s horrible. And America elected him president, and he strengthens the hand of evildoers, “and none return from their wickedness.” Their prophesying does not result in people changing their life. That’s false prophets. See, they would rather have a thousand in their church than preach anything that would hurt anybody and cause them to be offended and leave. You know, we let them go to hell, we’ll let him suffer the judgment of God here on earth, but God forbid that we lose one member from preaching sin and getting them to change. And the spirit of prophecy is very important. See, it’s not hard to figure out a false prophet. They violate Scriptures all the time. Real Bible prophecy turns people from doing wrong. Can I hear an amen?
What does it mean that false prophets “strengthen the hands of evildoers”?

Jeremiah 23:14: Also I have seen a horrible thing in the prophets of Jerusalem: They commit adultery and walk in lies; They also strengthen the hands of evildoers, So that no one turns back from his wickedness. All of them are like Sodom to Me, And her inhabitants like Gomorrah.
Why does he say prophets who speak from their own heart make people worthless? (Jeremiah 23:16)

He says false prophets “make you vain,” and most of the American church world is “worthless” because they don’t pray, read their Bible or know how to lead anyone to Christ. He says they speak “a vision of their own heart,” while the only boundaries are what the Spirit and the Bible say, and that God says “I have not spoken to nor sent these prophets.”
Why does he say prophets who speak from their own heart make people worthless? (Jeremiah 23:16)

Adultery, homosexuality, theft, divorce, murder, drugs, deceit, laziness (they don’t even want to get out and work now; they just get stuff from the government). Real Bible prophecy will hit all these issues. Can I hear an amen? Jeremiah 23:16, number eight: the prophets make you vain. They make you worthless. Most of the American church world is worthless. They don’t know how to pray, they don’t read their Bible, they don’t know Scriptures, they don’t know how to lead anyone to Christ. They’re worthless. Are you there? Somebody asked them, “How do I find Christ?” “Oh, let me take you to the pastor.” Somebody asked them, “Well, what’s a baptism of the Holy Ghost?” “Well, I don’t know. I don’t know. Never heard of such a thing. Let me take you to the Pentecostal church.” These false prophets make us worthless. They’re worthless, and what you are, you pass on. Number nine: they speak a vision of their own heart, mind. They just say what they feel is truth. “I believe this, I believe that.” They say them words all the time. “Well, I believe, and the way I see it...” It doesn’t matter what you believe. It doesn’t matter the way you see it. What is the Spirit saying, and what is the Bible saying? Because I only have those boundaries to speak in, “not from the mouth of the Lord.” Number 10: “I have not spoken to nor sent these prophets.” I haven’t spoken to them, I didn’t anoint them and send them. They’re self-appointed, or their church group appointed them. I didn’t send them. See, if God would have sent them, He would have gave them the message that He gave Adam and Eve. See, we showed you at the beginning the whole gospel was there last week, right? The whole gospel is right there in Genesis, the first few chapters, the mysteries of God. Yet they ran and prophesied.
Why does he say prophets who speak from their own heart make people worthless? (Jeremiah 23:16)

Jeremiah 23:16: Thus says the LORD of hosts: “Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you. They make you worthless; They speak a vision of their own heart, Not from the mouth of the LORD. Jeremiah 23:21: “I have not sent these prophets, yet they ran. I have not spoken to them, yet they prophesied.
What do false prophets lack? (standing in God’s counsel, Jeremiah 23:22)

He says if they had stood in God’s counsel they “would have called my people to hear my word” and turned them from their evil way. He says because they are not in the Word they can’t teach it, and people who are not taught the Word do not turn and repent from their sin.
What do false prophets lack? (standing in God’s counsel, Jeremiah 23:22)

All right, number 11: “If they had stood in my counsel.” They didn’t stand in my counsel. David said, “Thy word has been my counselors all the days of my pilgrimage.” David was a reader and a studier of Scriptures, and, you know, why Christians have to go to counseling? Because they don’t read the book. “If they would have stood in my counsel, they would have called my people to hear my word.” So they do not cause the people to hear the word of God; it’s their own opinions. And the last one is, they “would have turned them from their evil way and from the evil of their doing.” See, because God didn’t send them, because they’re not in the Word, they can’t teach the Word to the people, and when you don’t teach the Word to the people, they’re not going to turn and repent from their sin. That’s false prophets. Now, you know as well as I do, the megachurches are filled with sinners. You know, when you stay in sin, there’s pain in sin. Eventually there’s pain in sin, isn’t there?
What do false prophets lack? (standing in God’s counsel, Jeremiah 23:22)

Jeremiah 23:22: But if they had stood in My counsel, And had caused My people to hear My words, Then they would have turned them from their evil way And from the evil of their doings. Psalm 119:24: Your testimonies also are my delight And my counselors.
Why did the angel tell John not to worship him?
He says John fell at the angel’s feet to worship, and the angel said, “Don’t do that. Worship God. I am your fellow servant and of your brethren.”
Why didn’t the temple soldiers arrest Jesus?
He says they were “so influenced by what was coming out of His mouth” that they came back empty-handed and said, “Never spake a man like this Man.”
Where does true prophecy not come from?
He says it is not from human ability or “the will of man,” and that men’s opinions, thinking and deciding of right and wrong “had nothing to do with this. It was totally the Spirit.”
Did a man who hated Jesus really prophesy?
He says yes: the Spirit came on the high priest, who “didn’t believe in Jesus, didn’t want Him to be the Messiah,” and he still prophesied that Jesus was the Messiah come to die for the nation.
What did God tell him when he fell asleep seeking Him?
He says he would fall asleep seeking God and feel guilty, but God said, “Son, at least you’re laying before the Lord,” and he got up the next morning and stayed awake.
Does the Holy Spirit tell people to divorce their spouse?
He says no: “That ain’t no Holy Ghost talking that violates Scripture.” He says to stay faithful to your marriage and family and let the unbelieving depart if they choose to.
Is the gift of prophecy the same as the office of a prophet predicting the future?
He says no: “this is not the office of a prophet predicting the future. This is the gift of speaking by the inspiration of the Holy Ghost.”
Can you believe whatever you want to believe?
He says no: “You don’t have the freedom to believe what you want to believe. You’ve got to believe what Jesus told you to believe.”
What does he say instead of a 12-step program or psychology?
He says, “I don’t need a 12-step program when I got a one-step program: Jesus Christ. Maybe two steps: His word.” He says Jesus and His word heal you and set you free.
What happened with the woman with the familiar spirit in Acts?

He says her owners made a lot of money from her fortune telling, and Paul told the spirit to come out. He says that “thing was gone, and there went their money, and they got mad and they wanted to kill Paul.”
How did he say he grew strong as a new Christian?
He says three months after he was saved he was going door-to-door witnessing, he took a soul-winning class, and sang and preached at missions and jails, and “I didn’t use excuses.”
What does he mean that salvation is “a two-banked river”?

He says the two banks are “faith in Christ and His blood and death on the cross for forgiveness,” and “living right.” He says it doesn’t help his family if he only believes; it helps them when he lives for Christ.
How can you tell a false prophet?

He says “they violate Scriptures all the time,” while “real Bible prophecy turns people from doing wrong.” He lists adultery, theft, divorce, murder, drugs and deceit as issues real Bible prophecy will hit.
Does God say He sent the false prophets?
He says God says, “I have not spoken to nor sent these prophets.” He says they are “self-appointed or their church group appointed them,” and God did not send them.
Why does he say Christians have to go to counseling?
He says David was “a reader and a studier of Scriptures,” and that Christians have to go to counseling “because they don’t read the book.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer gives the marks of a real prophet, who stands in God’s counsel and speaks what the Bible says, and then teaches from 1 Chronicles 25, 2 Chronicles 20, 2 Kings 3 and Acts…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer gives the marks of a real prophet, who stands in God’s counsel and speaks what the Bible says, and then teaches from 1 Chronicles 25, 2 Chronicles 20, 2 Kings 3 and Acts 16 about the anointing and the place of music and praise in prophecy and worship.
What are the marks of a real prophet, and does it matter what other preachers say?

He says the first mark is that “God did speak to them. God did send them,” and the second that “they did stand in His counsel”: they were people of the Word who read, studied and got into teaching where the Spirit revealed the Scriptures. He says they cause people to hear God’s words, and it does not matter what others say, “it’s what the Bible says.” When people say he thinks he is right and everyone else is wrong, he says, “I’m just telling you what the Bible says.”
What are the marks of a real prophet, and does it matter what other preachers say?

I want to give you the marks of a real prophet. They’re right here. Characteristic number one: God did speak to them. God did send them. Can I hear an amen? It’s right here, the opposite of the false. Characteristic number two: they did stand in His counsel. They were people of the Word. They found time to read and study the Word and get in teaching where the Word was being taught, not some book out of the Bible bookstore, but the Scriptures were being taught by the Holy Spirit revealing them. That’s the kind of people that are real prophets. “And they caused my people to hear my words,” not their words. See, it doesn’t matter what Copeland says, it doesn’t matter what the pope says, it’s what the Bible says. Hallelujah. And I hear this all the time: “Well, you think you’re right and everybody else is wrong.” I didn’t say that. I’m just telling you what the Bible says. I’m not telling you what I say, I’m not telling you what I believe, I’m telling you what the Bible says. They probably put you on a guilt trip. “Well, how can all these people...” I hear this too: “How can all these people be wrong and you’re right?” I’m not telling you I’m right, I’m telling you what the Bible says. You show me in the Bible where you are right, and they can’t. They just believe some book, some tape, some CD, some guy off the TV.
What are the marks of a real prophet, and does it matter what other preachers say?

Jeremiah 23:21-22: “I have not sent these prophets, yet they ran. I have not spoken to them, yet they prophesied. But if they had stood in My counsel, And had caused My people to hear My words, Then they would have turned them from their evil way And from the evil of their doings.
What does he say the church is for, and who convicts people?

He says the mark of a real prophet is that they “turn many people from their evil way,” and “that’s what the church is all about. It’s not about a social club.” He says no speaker has “the power to convict people”; a feel-good message is gone the next day, but “when they are touched by the Holy Ghost, He’s there the next morning.”
What does he say the church is for, and who convicts people?

And number, item, characteristic number four: “They turn many people from their evil way and from the evil of their doings.” Folks, that’s what the church is all about. It’s not about a social club. It’s about us having our act together, so when people come, they are convicted by the Holy Spirit. They can reject Him (I see people reject), but they’re convicted by the Holy Spirit to turn from the wrong. And, folks, I don’t care how good a speaker you are, you don’t have the power to convict people. Oh, you might speak so well that they feel good at the moment, but the Holy Ghost is lasting, and you’re not lasting. When they go home and they get up the next day, that feel-good, inspired message is gone, but when they are touched by the Holy Ghost, He’s there the next morning saying, “Come on, boy. Come on, boy.”
What does he say the church is for, and who convicts people?
Jeremiah 23:22: But if they had stood in My counsel, And had caused My people to hear My words, Then they would have turned them from their evil way And from the evil of their doings.
How should the gifts of the Spirit be used?

He says the Holy Spirit “needs a mouthpiece,” and “all of us can” prophesy one by one, speaking when you need to by the Holy Ghost, even one-on-one. He says the gifts are not a prize: “The gifts of the Spirit are weapons to use when we need them,” and the Holy Spirit will touch you at the time you need them.
How should the gifts of the Spirit be used?

Hallelujah. So us as a church, we need the Holy Spirit, don’t we? And we need the Holy Spirit speaking, and so that means He needs a mouthpiece, and all of us can, what? Prophesy one by one. In other words, you know, you can speak when you need to speak by the Holy Ghost. You might be talking to someone one-on-one, and the Holy Ghost will give you something to say, and you don’t have to say, “I got a word for you, for you,” that just puts a, that just makes you look good. That’s why you do that. “I have a word of God, God gave me a word for you.” Like the things of God are something that we go to the Olympics to win a prize about. “Oh boy, I got the prize of healing.” Oh, shut up. The gifts of the Spirit are weapons to use when we need them, and when you need them, the Holy Spirit will touch you and use that at the time. Can I hear an amen?
How should the gifts of the Spirit be used?
1 Corinthians 14:31: For you can all prophesy one by one, that all may learn and all may be encouraged.
Did Paul have the gifts of the Spirit every day, and why does America need real prophets?

He says Paul had all nine gifts but did not use them every day: in some cities God did no healing, and in others “God released the miraculous.” He says that when the Holy Ghost releases it, “you don’t get any credit,” and that God is bringing America low “so that we can get an ear to hear.”
Did Paul have the gifts of the Spirit every day, and why does America need real prophets?

Amen. Did Paul have all nine gifts of the Spirit? Yes, he did. Oh man, you’re looking at me like a “duh.” Did he use them every day? No. There were cities where he went into, God did no healing. He couldn’t turn that on: “Oh, I have the gift of healing.” He’d go from one city, he couldn’t do nothing in the miraculous; he’d go to another city, and God released the miraculous. And when the Holy Ghost releases, then you can do something, and you don’t get any credit. It’s the Holy Spirit. Hallelujah. Hallelujah. Now that’s the marks of a real prophet. Can I hear an amen? And, folks, we need in America some real prophets rising up. See, America’s, I mean, God is bringing us low in America so that we can get an ear to hear. You see His style all through the Bible.
