items.ser: The War of The Word · Part 2
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer finishes Revelation 19, arguing that the supper of the great God, the horses and the sword from His mouth show a spiritual war of the word rather than a natural war. He gives Bible examples of the war of the word, from the flood, Sodom, Egypt, Babylon and the ark, to angels fighting for believers, and then turns to present-day suffering, morality and the question of which side of the word you are on.
What is the “supper of the great God” in Revelation 19, and why do the birds gather?

He reads Revelation 19:17, the angel “standing in the sun” crying to the birds to gather “into the supper of the great God.” He says Jesus used eagles and vultures as an illustration of the coming at the end of the world, citing “wherever the carcass is, there the eagles will be gathered together.”
What is the “supper of the great God” in Revelation 19, and why do the birds gather?

And angels, verse 17, standing in the sun. Now you try standing in the sun, see how long you last. “Cried to all the birds, the fowls of heaven, gather yourselves together into the supper of the great God.” Now, we know that in the book of Daniel and in other books in the Bible, when there were national wars, physical people were killed, and the vultures actually would come and gather together and eat the dead flesh. Right? All right. We also know that angels— I mean, I’m sorry, we also know that eagles were used by Jesus to describe the second coming in Matthew 14 and in Luke and in John and Mark. Where one would be taken and the other left, and they said, “Where, Lord? Where are these people going to be taken?” And He says, “Wherever the carcass is, there the eagles will be gathered together.” So we know that Jesus used these fowl, these vultures, as an illustration of the coming at the end of the world. Are you there? Hallelujah. In Luke 17:36 it said, “Two men will be in the field; one shall be taken, the other left.” And they answered, “Where, Lord?” “Wherever the body is, there the eagles will be gathered together.” See, where the dead carcass is, the eagles, the vultures— the eagle is a vulture, he feeds on dead bodies and lights on [them].
What is the “supper of the great God” in Revelation 19, and why do the birds gather?

Revelation 19:17-18: Then I saw an angel standing in the sun; and he cried with a loud voice, saying to all the birds that fly in the midst of heaven, “Come and gather together for the supper of the great God, that you may eat the flesh of kings, the flesh of captains, the flesh of mighty men, the flesh of horses and of those who sit on them, and the flesh of all people, free and slave, both small and great.” Matthew 24:28: For wherever the carcass is, there the eagles will be gathered together. Luke 17:34-37: I tell you, in that night there will be two men in one bed: the one will be taken and the other will be left. Two women will be grinding together: the one will be taken and the other left. Two men will be in the field: the one will be taken and the other left.” And they answered and said to Him, “Where, Lord?” So He said to them, “Wherever the body is, there the eagles will be gathered together.”
Why does he say the horses in Revelation 19 show this is a spiritual war and not a natural one?

He says the birds eat the flesh of kings, captains, mighty men, horses and riders, “both free and bond, both small and great.” He says if this took place in our day, “we don’t use horses for war,” so “this is not a natural war. This is a spiritual war.”
Why does he say the horses in Revelation 19 show this is a spiritual war and not a natural one?

And so we know that this is illustrated as part of the second coming. Okay, and it’s the supper of the great God, and the birds were to eat the flesh of kings, the flesh of captains, the flesh of mighty men, the flesh of horses and the people that sat on the horses, and the flesh of all men, both free and bond, both small and great. So these fowls are going to what? Eat the dead carcasses of everybody, including the horses. Now, the horses here tell you something. That’s why it’s in red. If this takes place in our day, as these prophets claim is going to be, we don’t use horses for war. You don’t win wars with horses anymore. You got to have tanks, you got to have airplanes, you got to have, uh, uh, aircraft carriers, I mean. So that tells us what? This is not a natural war. This is a spiritual war.
Why does he say the horses in Revelation 19 show this is a spiritual war and not a natural one?

Revelation 19:18: that you may eat the flesh of kings, the flesh of captains, the flesh of mighty men, the flesh of horses and of those who sit on them, and the flesh of all people, free and slave, both small and great.”
Will armies of the earth really fight Jesus when He returns?

He says God’s war of the word is “with everyone on earth,” small and great, bond and free. Of Revelation 19:19 he says people on earth will hide in the rocks and caves from a spirit coming out of heaven with angels, and “you’re going to run” rather than fight them with atomic bombs and missiles.
Will armies of the earth really fight Jesus when He returns?

Amen. And the fact that it says small and great, both free and bond, he’s talking about all people. People not even in the war. And is God’s war dealing with all nations? His war of the word, is He dealing with the small and the great? The Bible tells us that, doesn’t it? See, the bond and the free, He’s dealing with everyone. God’s spiritual war is with everyone on earth. Verse 19: “The beast, the kings of the earth, and their armies gathered together to war against Him that sat on the horse and against His army.” And this, again, is just ridiculous. Jesus comes riding out of heaven on a white horse with angels behind Him. They, people on earth, are going to do exactly what it said before this: they’re going to hide in the rocks and the caves and the— from the one who’s what? Coming. You see a spirit coming out of heaven, and angels, spirits, coming out of heaven, and you’re going to get your atomic bombs and your missiles and try to fight them? Uh-huh, honey, you’re going to run, just like He told, said, they’re going to run. They’re going to want to hide from this one who’s coming out of the heavens. Are you there? So this is obviously what? A spiritual war. Amen. But they got us thinking Russia’s coming and China’s coming and all this natural stuff, and, you know, and we don’t read the Bible enough to even know if they’re telling us the truth or not.
Will armies of the earth really fight Jesus when He returns?

Revelation 19:19: And I saw the beast, the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered together to make war against Him who sat on the horse and against His army. Revelation 6:15-16: And the kings of the earth, the great men, the rich men, the commanders, the mighty men, every slave and every free man, hid themselves in the caves and in the rocks of the mountains, and said to the mountains and rocks, “Fall on us and hide us from the face of Him who sits on the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb!
What happens to the beast and the false prophet, and who is slain with the sword of His mouth?

He says the beast and false prophet were “cast alive into the lake of fire,” and since you take an enemy captive in battle, “the spiritual powers are captured.” He says the rest were slain “with the sword of His mouth”: when the word of God comes to us we can accept it and live forever, or reject it and be called “dead in trespasses and sins.”
What happens to the beast and the false prophet, and who is slain with the sword of His mouth?

Revelation’s verse 19, chapter 19:20: “The beast and the false prophet were taken.” See, this beast and false prophet is the, the spiritual realm. “And they were cast alive into the lake of fire burning with brimstone.” Now, you know, when you conquer an enemy, you take them captive, isn’t that right? Huh? Those who are alive and not dead, you take him captive. Who’s taken captive in this battle? The beast and the false prophet. See, it’s a spiritual war in the spiritual realm, and the spiritual powers are captured. Hallelujah. I got a picture here of these two dummies getting thrown into the pit. Now verse 21: “The remnant were slain with the sword of Him that sat on the horse, which sword proceeded out of His mouth, and all the fowls were gathered and filled with their flesh.” Now, the armies and these other people, the small and the great, how were they slain? With the sword of His mouth. See, the word of God comes to them. And how, you know, when the word of God comes to us, we can accept it or we can reject it. If we accept it, we live what? Forever. We’re given eternal life and we live forever. If we reject it, we are called dead in trespasses and sins.
What happens to the beast and the false prophet, and who is slain with the sword of His mouth?

Revelation 19:20-21: Then the beast was captured, and with him the false prophet who worked signs in his presence, by which he deceived those who received the mark of the beast and those who worshiped his image. These two were cast alive into the lake of fire burning with brimstone. And the rest were killed with the sword which proceeded from the mouth of Him who sat on the horse. And all the birds were filled with their flesh. Ephesians 2:1: And you He made alive, who were dead in trespasses and sins,
Is the war of the word only for the end times? (the flood)

He says “these wars have been going on since the beginning,” and the end-time prophets are wrong to make us think it is “just at the end of the age.” His first example is the flood: God spoke, Noah preached righteousness for a hundred years, only six or seven people listened, and the rest “died in the judgment.”
Is the war of the word only for the end times? (the flood)

Isn’t that what the Bible says? See, when we don’t believe in Christ and live for Him and accept His death on the cross, and we sin, the Bible says we are dead even though we’re alive, and trespasses in what? Sin. Hallelujah. Now, let me give you some Bible illustrations of the war of the word. Are you ready? You want to see some examples of this? They’ve been going on for quite some time. See, these end-time prophets try to make us think it’s just at the end of the age, but these wars have been going on since the beginning. You want to see some examples? Are you interested in this war of the word? All right, here we go. Let’s go to the flood. Did God come down and say by His word, “I’m going to destroy the earth with a flood”? Was that the word of God? Did He send Noah to preach righteousness and the judgment to the people for over a hundred years? For 100 years he preached right, and did anybody listen? Yeah, six people did, or seven people did: his wife, his boys and their wives that came out of sinful families of the world. The rest rejected it, and what? Died in the judgment. You see, the war of the word. He speaks it, it’s going to happen. Does He always give a way out? Absolutely. He’s God, He gives you a way out.
Is the war of the word only for the end times? (the flood)
2 Peter 2:5: and did not spare the ancient world, but saved Noah, one of eight people, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood on the world of the ungodly;
What does Sodom and Gomorrah show about the war of the word?

He says there was a righteous man in Sodom and Gomorrah as a witness, and God’s word was “I’m going to destroy Sodom by fire and brimstone.” He says Lot’s married daughters and their husbands laughed, and “they think that the end-time judgment is a big joke.” Lot was led out by the angels with his two daughters, and his wife turned back and got caught in the judgment.
What does Sodom and Gomorrah show about the war of the word?

Okay, next illustration is Sodom and Gomorrah. Was there a righteous man living in Sodom and Gomorrah? Say yes. As a witness to these people who were committing homosexual acts and idleness of bread and abundance of food. Two angels come, two angels, and they want to have sex with the angels. Now, how dumb can you get? Hallelujah. But see, the angels appeared as beings. They, as Star Wars says, materialized. “Beam me up, Scotty.” And the word was, “I’m going to destroy Sodom by fire and brimstone.” His own daughters that didn’t live with him and their husbands laughed at him and said, “You got to be joking, Lot. Fire and brimstone from heaven’s going to destroy Sodom and Gomorrah, just these two cit— give me a break. You got to be joking.” And that’s what a lot of people do today. They think that the end-time judgment is a big joke. So Lot was led out by the angels with his two daughters that lived at home. His wife turned back and got caught in the judgment.
What does Sodom and Gomorrah show about the war of the word?

Genesis 19:14: So Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law, who had married his daughters, and said, “Get up, get out of this place; for the LORD will destroy this city!” But to his sons-in-law he seemed to be joking. Genesis 19:26: But his wife looked back behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
What did the plagues of Egypt show about the limits of spiritual power?

He says Egypt’s sorcerers copied some of the signs, but “they can only do what God allowed them to do,” so “there is a limited spiritual authority and power in the world.” He says that after the frogs God’s people were separated and safe, and “they didn’t have to be raptured to be safe.”
What did the plagues of Egypt show about the limits of spiritual power?

Egypt. Now, here’s a good one. Egypt has two prophets, Moses and [unclear]. And they’re bringing plagues down. They bring 10 plagues down. Egypt had sorcerers there. They had people into witchcraft, and they were doing nothing to— Moses came along, and then they were turning sticks into snakes, and they were turning water into blood, and they were bringing frogs out of the river. When they didn’t need any more snakes, and they didn’t need any more frogs, and they didn’t need any more blood, they needed no frogs, clear water, and no snakes. But see, they can only do what God allowed them to do. Are you there? So there is a limited spiritual authority and power in the world. It’s very limited. Now the Israelites, they experienced the blood, the water, they experienced the frogs coming out. But after the frogs, the Bible says God’s people were separated. And so when the [unclear] and the fire from heaven and the plague on the cattle and all that came, God’s people were what? Safe. They didn’t have to be raptured to be safe. Hallelujah. God can keep us right here. Amen. See, God gave— God came with His word through His prophets and gave them a chance. Now, some people in Egypt did convert, because a mixed multitude came out, and that’s what happened since Jesus died, that a lot of people have came out. They’ve converted. And is that right?
What did the plagues of Egypt show about the limits of spiritual power?

Exodus 7:11-12: But Pharaoh also called the wise men and the sorcerers; so the magicians of Egypt, they also did in like manner with their enchantments. For every man threw down his rod, and they became serpents. But Aaron’s rod swallowed up their rods. Exodus 8:22-23: And in that day I will set apart the land of Goshen, in which My people dwell, that no swarms of flies shall be there, in order that you may know that I am the LORD in the midst of the land. I will make a difference between My people and your people. Tomorrow this sign shall be.” ’ ” Exodus 12:38: A mixed multitude went up with them also, and flocks and herds—a great deal of livestock.
How did the Passover blood and the Red Sea show a war of the word?

He says in the death of the firstborn, those with the blood on the door had “no death, no darkness,” while homes without it lost the firstborn. At the Red Sea there was “no sword fighting, no bombs,” just God doing things by His word, and “everything depends on what side of the word you’re on.”
How did the Passover blood and the Red Sea show a war of the word?

Hallelujah. Now, the death of the firstborn. They put the blood on the door, and the destroying angel came through, the death angel. If you had the mark of the heavens, the blood on the door, no death, no darkness, nothing. But if you didn’t have it, if you were the firstborn, you were dead, and everybody in your family that was firstborn died. So every home had somebody dead in it, some of them more than one, ‘cause if the papa was firstborn and the mother was firstborn and they had a child firstborn, three people in that family died. Are you there? But not with the mark on the door. Hallelujah. And see, Revelation talks about the people of God having a what? A seal on them, a mark on them. And I forgot to tell you, all these wars were defeating and tormenting and punishing the people that didn’t have the seal. They weren’t touching the righteous. It’s just that the beast overcame the righteous, like in the earth today, our rulers are usually unrighteous, isn’t that true? And a lot of people in authority unrighteous, and they give us problems. They have limited authority over God’s people. So they come to the Red Sea, the waters parted, the people of God passed through on dry land safely, and the army of Israel, what? Were drowned. See, a war of the word. No sword fighting, no bombs. It’s just God doing things by His what? Word. And then when the Egyptian army came up, they couldn’t see, so they couldn’t go on and overtake Israel, because on this side of the pillar of fire and the cloud was darkness, and on the other side there was what? Light. So Israel could see, and the Egyptians on the other side of the light couldn’t see. See, everything depends on what side of the light you’re on, just as everything depends on what side of the word you’re on. Now, that was good. When you’re on the right side of the word, you don’t have to worry about all these wars and things going on in the heavens, because the end result is going to be to bless you. If you’re on the wrong side of the word, you better watch out. Things are coming in your life that you’re not going to like. So in the war of the word, it depends on which side of the word you’re on.
How did the Passover blood and the Red Sea show a war of the word?

Exodus 12:13: Now the blood shall be a sign for you on the houses where you are. And when I see the blood, I will pass over you; and the plague shall not be on you to destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt. Revelation 9:4: They were commanded not to harm the grass of the earth, or any green thing, or any tree, but only those men who do not have the seal of God on their foreheads. Exodus 14:21-22: Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the LORD caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea into dry land, and the waters were divided. So the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea on the dry ground, and the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left. Exodus 14:19-20: And the Angel of God, who went before the camp of Israel, moved and went behind them; and the pillar of cloud went from before them and stood behind them. So it came between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel. Thus it was a cloud and darkness to the one, and it gave light by night to the other, so that the one did not come near the other all that night.
What did four men do in Babylon, and should talk of Russia and China distract us?

He says four men who would not worship idols “changed the laws of Babylon,” with no swords, guns or tanks, just standing “on the right side of the word.” He asks how much more a church could change the nations by knowing and living God’s word, and says not to let end-time prophets distract you about Russia and China: “the war is in heaven.” He says you are punished not for being born in the wrong nation but “because you live in the wrong kingdom, the kingdom of darkness.”
What did four men do in Babylon, and should talk of Russia and China distract us?

Okay, Israel that came out of Egypt, they came out serving idols, they committed sexual immorality, and they did things that were bad. What did God do? He said, “I’ll come and I’ll punish you for these things.” So He had to bring famine here in one place and another place, and He would bring armies against them, and He would try to correct them. Why? Because they were breaking His word. Finally they went into captivity in Babylon. So we go to Babylon. What did four men do in Babylon? The Bible says that four men changed the laws of Babylon because they would not worship idols, they would not defile themselves, they stood for Jesus Christ. They got no swords, they got no guns, they got no tanks, they just stood on the right side of the word of God, and the Bible says that the king of Babylon changed the whole law because of these four men. Now, folks, that’s powerful. See, it’s the war of the word, and four men can change a nation, a sinful nation, a corrupt nation, and rewrite their laws. How much more can a church in the earth today change the nations of the earth by getting God’s word in them, knowing God’s word, and living God’s word? Amen. Don’t you let these end-time prophets distract you about Russia coming down and China coming over. You realize that the war is in heaven, and we who use the word are going to win. Amen. And God’s for the Russians, He’s for Chinese, Jesus died for all the people of the earth. Could that be an amen? Amen. You’re not going to be punished because you’re born in the wrong nation. You’re only punished because you live in the wrong kingdom, the kingdom of darkness. Now that’s hot stuff.
What did four men do in Babylon, and should talk of Russia and China distract us?

Daniel 3:28-29: Nebuchadnezzar spoke, saying, “Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego, who sent His Angel and delivered His servants who trusted in Him, and they have frustrated the king’s word, and yielded their bodies, that they should not serve nor worship any god except their own God! Therefore I make a decree that any people, nation, or language which speaks anything amiss against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego shall be cut in pieces, and their houses shall be made an ash heap; because there is no other God who can deliver like this.”
What happened when Israel took the ark of the covenant into battle while sinning?

He says Israel was “sinning and not following God,” brought the ark, and “got beat up the next day.” When the enemy put the ark in the house of their god, that god fell on its face with its head cut off, and he says “your God is worthless” if he needs your help. He adds that Gideon’s father told the city to “let him defend himself,” and asks if Jesus is big enough to defend Himself: “Yes, He’s the all-powerful One.”
What happened when Israel took the ark of the covenant into battle while sinning?

Now let’s go to the ark of the covenant. The ark of the covenant is where God dwelt in the Old Testament. So Israel went to battle and they lost the battle, so they said, “We need the ark of the covenant. We need the presence of God.” And that’s true, we need the presence of God, and the word is right there with the ark. Remember that? Is that what the Bible says? Right beside the ark is the word. So they bring the ark of the covenant down, and man, Israel, who was sinning and not following God all through, was celebration, and they got beat up the next day in war. The enemy took the ark, took it back to their nation, put it in the house of their God without war, without hand-to-hand combat. The next morning their God Dagon was fallen on his face, his wrists were cut, his head was cut off. I mean, duh, you’d think they’d get the hint, but instead they propped Dagon back up. I mean, when you got to do something to help your God, your God is worthless. I mean, when your God needs your help, other than prayer, you know, the spiritual weapons that we come on. Amen. And this is what Gideon’s father told the people of the city when Gideon went and tore down the idol. They said, “Hey, you bring your son out, we got to kill him for destroying our idol.” He says, “Listen, if your idol is really a God, let him defend himself.” Isn’t that correct? Is Jesus big enough to defend Himself? Yes, He’s the all-powerful One. Hallelujah. So God didn’t finish there. He smoked them with a plague. They died. They started dying like flies, and boils come out on them, and oh man, they were a mess. And so these guys say, “What? We got to get rid of this ark. This God of Israel is going to kill us.” And so they sent the ark back, and when they did, God stopped the plague. You see, the word of God is powerful. It’s a war of the word, and when you’re on the right side of the word, you got no problem.
What happened when Israel took the ark of the covenant into battle while sinning?

1 Samuel 5:2-4: When the Philistines took the ark of God, they brought it into the house of Dagon and set it by Dagon. And when the people of Ashdod arose early in the morning, there was Dagon, fallen on its face to the earth before the ark of the LORD. So they took Dagon and set it in its place again. And when they arose early the next morning, there was Dagon, fallen on its face to the ground before the ark of the LORD. The head of Dagon and both the palms of its hands were broken off on the threshold; only Dagon’s torso was left of it. 1 Samuel 5:6: But the hand of the LORD was heavy on the people of Ashdod, and He ravaged them and struck them with tumors, both Ashdod and its territory. Judges 6:31: But Joash said to all who stood against him, “Would you plead for Baal? Would you save him? Let the one who would plead for him be put to death by morning! If he is a god, let him plead for himself, because his altar has been torn down!”
Do angels and the army of heaven fight for believers?

He says they tried to kill Jesus several times but “He just walked through their midst” because He was on the right side of the word, and an angel let Peter out of prison. He says “this army in heaven is on our side,” recalling the prophet who prayed that his servant’s eyes be opened to see angels and chariots encamped around God’s people, so “these angels are fighting for us.”
Do angels and the army of heaven fight for believers?

Jesus and His apostles, was Jesus and the apostles persecuted, tried to kill, and even killed by leaders and people around Him? Yes. They tried to kill Jesus several times, and the Bible says He just walked through their midst. See, He didn’t have to fight back, He didn’t have to use physical swords and physical fists. The Bible says He just walked right through. Why? ‘Cause He’s on the right side of the word. And yet they killed Him because they didn’t know, the Bible says, that He was God, or else they would not have fulfilled the work. And then the apostles come along and they killed the apostles. James was beheaded. All the apostles died a very tragic martyr death except for John. They were put in prison, and an angel came to Peter in prison and let him out. There’s that angel again. Amen. Angels came and ministered to Jesus when He [unclear], isn’t that right? Yes, angels came and ministered. Folks, this army in heaven is on our side, and though you can’t see them, remember the prophet Elijah said, “Lord, open the eyes of my servant that he can see what’s going on here.” And when He opened the eyes of the earth, angels and chariots were encamped all around the people of God. See, if your eyes were open, you’d see how powerful the kingdom of righteousness is, the kingdom of light, the kingdom of Jesus is. Hallelujah. But “blessed are they that have not seen and yet” what? “Believe.” How that we don’t have to see these angels. God says they’re there, and so we’ve got to live our life like we are connected to the heavenlies. These angels are fighting for us, and we are victorious people. Amen. How many of you need a little supernatural power to fight your battles? Oh, the rest of you are pretty strong. Huh.
Do angels and the army of heaven fight for believers?

Luke 4:30: Then passing through the midst of them, He went His way. Acts 12:7: Now behold, an angel of the Lord stood by him, and a light shone in the prison; and he struck Peter on the side and raised him up, saying, “Arise quickly!” And his chains fell off his hands. 2 Kings 6:17: And Elisha prayed, and said, “LORD, I pray, open his eyes that he may see.” Then the LORD opened the eyes of the young man, and he saw. And behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha. John 20:29: Jesus said to him, “Thomas, because you have seen Me, you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed.”
What does he say the next judgment will be?

He says the Bible says the earth will be destroyed by fire next time, with the heavens rolling back like a scroll and the elements melting with fervent heat, “because God’s word said so.” He says Jesus said those who didn’t follow Him would be cast into the lake of fire made for the Devil and his angels, and “those on the side of the word are going to be blessed” while those on the wrong side will be punished.
What does he say the next judgment will be?

Now, the Bible says that the earth’s going to be destroyed by fire next time. It says that the heavens are going to roll back like a scroll, the elements are going to melt with a fervent heat on that day of the coming of the Lord. You see, the next judgment is fire, and why is it going to happen? Because God’s word said so. So it’s the word, it’s the word. Jesus said that the people that didn’t follow Him and live right, and— Matthew— that they would be cast into the lake of fire made for the Devil and his angels. What was the lake of fire created for? To handle Satan and his angels, the wicked powers of the spiritual world, in that great clash at the last day. Amen, hallelujah. And so this thing is going to happen, folks. It is going to happen. Uh, those on the side of the word are going to be blessed. Those on the wrong side of the word are going to be punished. Now, if you think this thing is just for the end time, let me give you a few facts. Are you ready for some natural facts? 5 billion people, that’s 56% of the population of the earth today, live on $5 a day or less. In other words, 56% of the world’s population is in poverty.
What does he say the next judgment will be?

2 Peter 3:10: But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night, in which the heavens will pass away with a great noise, and the elements will melt with fervent heat; both the earth and the works that are in it will be burned up. Matthew 25:41: “Then He will also say to those on the left hand, ‘Depart from Me, you cursed, into the everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels:
Is the tribulation only coming, or are people suffering now?

He gives statistics he says show suffering now, such as poverty, hunger, wars and disease, and says if you tell those people about a coming seven-year tribulation they will say, “I’m living in it, and it’s moving.” He says “the Americans forget that not everybody lives like us, and yet God loves these people.”
Is the tribulation only coming, or are people suffering now?

25,000 people die a day from hunger. Now you go to those people and you tell them there’s some great big seven-year period of tribulation coming. “Man, I’m living in it, and it’s moving.” When you see these pictures of people in Africa and South America and Asia and just [unclear] and with orange hair and bloated bellies because they don’t have the food, and skinny, and finally just dying because they don’t have the nourishment. The Americans forget that not everybody lives like us, and yet God loves these people. More than 9 million per year are dying from hunger. There are 30 wars and conflicts in the world today. 1.8 million died last year from AIDS. Death, the number one death in the world, it is the number one source of death in the world is from AIDS. There are 16 million AIDS orphans in the world, and yet Arnold Schwarzenegger, Brown, and our legislators want us to honor a Harvey Milk Day and a Day of Silence for the homosexuals in our schools, when that is a lifestyle that will kill you. And Harvey Milk was a, a recruiter of young, frustrated boys that didn’t know what was going on in life, and he would have sex with them. He was not an honorable man. Can I hear an amen? And yet our legislators and Governor Schwarzenegger, who said he was a Republican, and the Republican platform does not stand for that, he promoted it, and then we find out why he’s doing things on the side. He’s not living for God at all. He’s saying one thing and living another. Are you there?
What does he say about children’s suffering and America’s moral problem?

He says children are neglected, abused and trafficked in every nation, and that “America is not great. We’re immorally bankrupt, and our children are paying the price for it.” He warns that sexual immorality “has a price to pay,” and says the real issue is “the heavenlies, morality.”
What does he say about children’s suffering and America’s moral problem?

Now you go to these 16 million kids and you tell them there’s a [unclear] and a half year period, man, of real trouble in the earth. They’re going to look at you and say, “What do you think I’m in? I got no mama, I got no daddy, my mama passed on AIDS to me, I’m doomed.” I just dealt with someone on the internet whose mother passed AIDS onto her. She’s 20 years old and she’s wasting away with the HIV virus, born with it. I mean, you know, that’s not fair. There are quakes and volcanoes and hurricanes and tornadoes and floods and landslides and avalanches that kill hundreds of thousands of people every year. There are crimes going on in every nation: criminals bullying people, stealing, raping, selling sex slaves, and abusing children and neglecting children. And 3 billion people in the earth today have a sexually transmitted disease. Do you realize that’s 50% of the earth’s population? And see, Jesus came, He says, “My word is not grievous, because My word will give you life.” I want to warn you, don’t commit sexual immorality. It has a price to pay. See, don’t do these things. It has a price to pay. And Obama and none of our federal government legislators will admit there is a morality problem in America, and there’s signs of it by sexually transmitted diseases, children are being neglected, children are being abused, and yet they stand up there and talk like America’s just great, we’re just in a little financial problem right now. America is not great. We’re immorally bankrupt, and our children are paying the price for it. Children all over the world are paying the price for it, and we’re not addressing the moral issue. But this is the issue: the heavenlies, morality.
Where should Christians look instead of Russia and China?

He says people are being led to look for Russia and China to move against Israel and across the Euphrates, but “we need to look into the heavenlies.” He says “through using spiritual principles we can move the heavenlies to move earth.”
Where should Christians look instead of Russia and China?

Hallelujah. And they got us looking for Russia to come down against Israel and China to come across the Euphrates, and, you know, some big guy, government, going to unite. All they got us looking in the wrong direction. We need to look into the heavenlies. Amen. We need to look where? To the heavenlies, and through using spiritual principles we can move the heavenlies to move earth. Hallelujah. So the conclusion, as I said, this is a war of the word, and it all depends on which side of the word you’re on, how you’re going to come out in this war.
What is the conclusion: which side of the word are you on?

He says the war of the word depends on “which side of the word you’re on,” and that in the last days a demonstration of the word will bring a harvest like the mixed multitude that left Egypt. He says God is “not out to kill them” but to put them to death to sin and alive to righteousness, and that Jesus used the word, not a sword or fist, for three and a half years.
What is the conclusion: which side of the word are you on?

And that’s why in the last days there’s going to be a demonstration of the word that’s going to bring a harvest in, just like Egypt. Remember, in Egypt there was a mixed multitude, there were people besides God’s people coming out of Egypt, so it’s going to be at the end time. There’s going to be a tremendous harvest. There is over 6 billion people today, and when God moves in these final days, He’s moving to win as many as He can to Himself. He’s not out to kill them, He’s out to re-kill them— as, as put them to death to sin and alive to righteousness. Amen. That’s what Romans says: we’re dead to sin and we’re alive to righteousness. And He needs to kill us with the word and kill that sinful nature in us and resurrect us into a man of what? Righteousness. Hallelujah. The war of the word. Did Jesus use the word when He came for three and a half years and preached? Absolutely. Did He take up a sword against anyone? Did He hit anyone, hit anyone with His fist? No. He used the word. And the word made people glad, or they made people mad, and that’s what’s going to go on in every generation. It’s the word, and in the last generation it’s the word. It’s the war of the word, destroying the principalities and powers in heavenly places and bringing release and victory on earth to human beings.
What is the conclusion: which side of the word are you on?
Romans 6:11: Likewise you also, reckon yourselves to be dead indeed to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus our Lord.
Why does he say the eagles in Jesus’ words are vultures?

He says Jesus used “these vultures, as an illustration of the coming at the end of the world.” He says “the eagle is a vulture, he feeds on dead bodies,” and so where the dead carcass is, the eagles gather.
What does he say about the idea that Russia and China are coming?
He says “they got us thinking Russia’s coming and China’s coming and all this natural stuff,” and that “we don’t read the Bible enough to even know if they’re telling us the truth or not.”
Who is taken captive in the battle of Revelation 19?
He says the beast and the false prophet are taken captive, and “it’s a spiritual war in the spiritual realm.” They are cast alive into the lake of fire burning with brimstone.
What happens when the word of God comes to us?
He says “we can accept it or we can reject it.” If we accept it we live forever and are given eternal life; if we reject it we are called dead in trespasses and sins, even though we are alive.
Does God always give people a way out?
He says yes: “He’s God, He gives you a way out.” He says God sent Noah to preach, and the rest of the world rejected it and died in the judgment.
What could Egypt’s sorcerers do compared to Moses?

He says Egypt had sorcerers and people into witchcraft who also turned sticks into snakes, water into blood and brought out frogs. He says they could only do what God allowed them to do, so spiritual power in the world is “very limited.”
Do Christians have to be raptured to be safe?
He says God’s people were separated in Egypt and were safe, and “they didn’t have to be raptured to be safe.” He says “God can keep us right here.”
What did Israel do after leaving Egypt, and how did God respond?

He says Israel came out of Egypt serving idols and committing sexual immorality, and God said, “I’ll come and I’ll punish you for these things.” He says God brought famine and armies against them to correct them because they were breaking His word, until they went into captivity in Babylon.
What did Gideon’s father say when people wanted to kill Gideon for tearing down the idol?

He says Gideon’s father told the people of the city, “if your idol is really a God, let him defend himself.” He asks if Jesus is big enough to defend Himself and answers, “Yes, He’s the all-powerful One.”
What happened to the people who kept the ark of the covenant?
He says God sent a plague and “they started dying like flies,” with boils coming out on them. They said they had to get rid of the ark, sent it back, and God stopped the plague.
What does he say the lake of fire was created for?

He says it was created to handle Satan and his angels, “the wicked powers of the spiritual world,” in that great clash at the last day. He says Jesus said those who did not follow Him and live right would be cast into it.
What does he say God is aiming for in the final days?

He says a demonstration of the word will bring a tremendous harvest, “just like Egypt” with its mixed multitude, and that God is “moving to win as many as He can to Himself.” He says God is not out to kill them but to put them to death to sin and alive to righteousness.
Did Jesus use a sword or his fists when He preached?

He says Jesus used the word for three and a half years and did not take up a sword or hit anyone, and that “the word made people glad.” He says it is the war of the word, “destroying the principalities and powers in heavenly places.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer looks at four New Testament recipients of the baptism of the Holy Ghost (Jesus, John the Baptist, Stephen and Saul), and says what they had in common was forgiveness. He…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer looks at four New Testament recipients of the baptism of the Holy Ghost (Jesus, John the Baptist, Stephen and Saul), and says what they had in common was forgiveness. He teaches that forgiveness is part of the divine nature and works through Mark 11:25, Matthew 6, Matthew 18 and Ephesians 4:32.
What does “be filled with the Spirit” mean, and who are the four recipients? (Ephesians 5:18)

He says the baptism of the Holy Spirit and being filled with the Holy Spirit are “synonymous terms,” and he will look at its effect on four recipients in the New Testament, going back to the Bible and not to a revival. From Ephesians 5:18 he says wine changes your personality, and the Holy Spirit “will change the way you behave, the way you speak.”
What does “be filled with the Spirit” mean, and who are the four recipients? (Ephesians 5:18)

We’re going to continue with the third promise. Remember, we showed you the first three promises, and the last one was the baptism of the Holy Ghost. God promised that, and it plays an integral part in us partaking of the divine nature. And this third promise is so vast and broad I have to bring it in segments, and so instead of this week showing you it was a promise and all that, we’re going to look a little further into this baptism of the Holy Ghost, and we’re going to look at it this way: the baptism of the Holy Spirit and its effect on four recipients. I’m going to bring you four recipients in the New Testament of the baptism of the Holy Ghost, which is the baptism of the Holy Spirit, which is being filled with the Holy Spirit. They’re all synonymous terms. Okay, and we’re not going to go back to Azusa Street, we’re not going to go back to the 1968 charismatic revival and get four recipients out of there. We’re going to go back to the Bible. Ephesians 5:18 says, “Do not be drunk with wine, wherein is excess, but be filled with the Spirit.” You know, if Christians would not twist that Scripture to say, “Well, what he means is, if I drink and I don’t get intoxicated, I’m fine.” It isn’t saying that at all. What it really says: “Be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess.” Excess means it will lead you to wrong behavior, loose behavior. Wine will distort your judgment, alcohol will, and so you can’t use that to justify drinking at all. But his comparison is with the wine because wine changes your personality, am I right? Yes. Yeah, it affects you. So he illustrates it with the wine because the Holy Spirit (be filled, be baptized with the Holy Spirit) will affect you. It will change the way you behave, the way you speak, and so all of us are supposed to be baptized with the Holy Ghost.
What does “be filled with the Spirit” mean, and who are the four recipients? (Ephesians 5:18)
Ephesians 5:18: And do not be drunk with wine, in which is dissipation; but be filled with the Spirit,
Why do Christians quarrel about the Holy Ghost, and what happened when Jesus was filled? (Luke 4:1)

He says Christians quarrel and argue over the baptism of the Holy Ghost, and he wants “to get rid of the argument” and show its power. The first recipient is Jesus, “full of the Holy Ghost,” who did not speak in tongues or get slain in the Spirit but “went immediately into the wilderness to be tested.”
Why do Christians quarrel about the Holy Ghost, and what happened when Jesus was filled? (Luke 4:1)

Now, in this generation, when I came to Christ, everybody is quarreling about the Holy Ghost. You know, in the ‘50s the Spirit-filled people were considered the church on the other side of the railroad tracks. You know, “You don’t go there, those people are weird, they’re a cult, man.” And then God came in ‘68, poured out His Spirit on the Catholics, Presbyterians, the Lutherans. He just did it, and they spoke in tongues, and they made all the same mistakes that the Pentecostals made, but they wouldn’t take the name Pentecost. They used the word charismatic. They didn’t want to identify with those across-the-track church, so they changed the name to charismatic, but it was the same thing. And, uh, then you’re fundamentalist and you’re Catholic, and everybody, they fight over this baptism of the Holy Ghost, quarrel and argue. And so through this we want to get rid of the argument, and we want to show you the power of the Holy Ghost. Okay, through these four, first we’re going to show you that there was four recipients. Number one, Jesus Christ Himself, in Luke 4:1: “Jesus being full of the Holy Ghost.” A dove came down in the form of the Holy Ghost, or the Holy Ghost came down in the form of the dove, and, uh, He didn’t speak in tongues, okay. He didn’t pass out in the water, He didn’t get slain in the Spirit, He didn’t even speak the mighty works of God. He went immediately into the wilderness to be tested. Wow. Nobody likes that sign of the Holy Ghost. “Give me the tongues, man. Give me the prophecy. Give me the good stuff. I don’t want no testing.” But anyway, that is one of our recipients of the baptism of the Holy Ghost when they got it.
Why do Christians quarrel about the Holy Ghost, and what happened when Jesus was filled? (Luke 4:1)
Luke 4:1: Then Jesus, being filled with the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness,
Did John the Baptist, Stephen and Saul speak in tongues when they were filled with the Holy Ghost?

He says John the Baptist was filled from his mother’s womb and “didn’t speak in tongues.” For Stephen, “there’s no record that he spoke in tongues… there’s no record that he didn’t,” and for Saul “there is no indication that Paul spoke in tongues when he got filled.” He says “we all like to justify our opinion instead of going to the Bible.”
Did John the Baptist, Stephen and Saul speak in tongues when they were filled with the Holy Ghost?

Okay, our next one is John the Baptist, Luke 1:15. “John shall drink neither wine nor strong drink.” Here again is wine and strong drink. John didn’t drink it. I wish people would line up with John instead of twisting the Scriptures, they do, to promote something that’s destroying families, destroying lives, and that is alcohol and drugs and marijuana and all that. It has a destructive end. You know, whether you like it or not, the Bible does not approve of intoxication of any kind, and that’s a big amen, because God isn’t for anything that destroys you and alters your personality to be bad. Okay, “he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost from his mother’s womb.” Okay, so when he was born, he’s filled with the Holy Ghost. Again, he didn’t speak in tongues, he didn’t get slain in the Spirit, he didn’t speak the mighty works of God. He just got filled with the Holy Ghost. And I know us Pentecostals, us charismatics, say, “Well, that’s because before the Holy Ghost was poured out.” Well, it’s still the same Spirit, and all through the Old Testament people were filled with the Holy Ghost. It’s just God in the last days was going to give it to all flesh, not just the select people. Are you there? It’s the same Holy Spirit. Now, the next person is Stephen, “a man full of faith and the Holy Ghost,” Acts 6:5. See, there’s no record that he spoke in tongues when he got the Holy Ghost. There’s no record that he didn’t. And this is the big argument right now: tongues, no tongues, and the news media makes fun of you if you speak in tongues and all the rest, and, uh, I mean, the natural people attack tongues, okay? People that don’t believe in God, what I mean. And then you have Saul, Acts 9:17, whose name was changed to Paul the apostle: “Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road as you came, has sent me that you may receive your sight,” God blinded him, “and be filled with the Holy Ghost.” Now, there is no indication that Paul spoke in tongues when he got filled with the Holy Ghost. The Pentecostals go, “He speaks in tongues more than y’all.” Yes, he does. He did. But that doesn’t mean he spoke in tongues when he first got it. You see, we all like to justify our opinion instead of going to the Bible and just rationally letting the Holy Ghost reveal truth to you. Amen.
Did John the Baptist, Stephen and Saul speak in tongues when they were filled with the Holy Ghost?

Luke 1:15: For he will be great in the sight of the Lord, and shall drink neither wine nor strong drink. He will also be filled with the Holy Spirit, even from his mother’s womb. Acts 6:5: And the saying pleased the whole multitude. And they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit, and Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas, a proselyte from Antioch, Acts 9:17: And Ananias went his way and entered the house; and laying his hands on him he said, “Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road as you came, has sent me that you may receive your sight and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”
What did the four recipients have in common?

He says regardless of when or how they were filled they had unity, and the thing they had in common was forgiveness: “the Holy Ghost empowered them to forgive.” He describes forgiveness as throwing the mistake away like a piece of paper in the trash and never bringing it back out: “forgiveness is forgiving and forgetting.”
What did the four recipients have in common?

Yes, so these four people were filled with the Holy Spirit. Okay, so let’s see what they had in common. These four recipients had one thing in common, regardless of when they were filled with the Holy Ghost or how they were filled with the Holy Ghost. They had one thing in common. And actually, they had another thing in common that I preached to you many times before: they had unity. Yes. On the day of Pentecost they were in unity; the new ones that come in were in unity. There was a strong effect of flowing together and unifying. And do we have unity in the church in America? No way. And everybody says they’re filled with the Holy Ghost. Everybody I meet says they’re filled with the Holy Ghost. Let’s see what these four recipients had in common. You’ll notice I got “forgiveness” up there with a piece of paper going into the trash bin. We throw a piece of paper into the trash bin because we made a mistake on it, it can’t be restored, so we wad up the paper and throw it away. It’s taken to the dump. That’s what forgiveness is. You throw away the mistake, you take it to the dump, and you never get it back again. Forgiveness is forgiving and forgetting. Pardoning, you know, no condemnation, no guilt. I pardon you, I pardon myself, and I’m not bringing that piece of paper back out of the trash. Can I get an amen? So, as you know by now, the common thing they had was forgiveness. The Holy Ghost empowered them to forgive, something that all the argument doesn’t even bring out. The fundamentalists don’t bring it out, the Pentecostals don’t bring it out, charismatics don’t bring it out, the Catholics don’t bring it out, but this Holy Ghost, all four of these people were empowered to forgive.

And how can I share with them if I have nothing to do with them? You see, I hate these Pentecostals that roll around on the floor and shake and quake and slaying out the p— and all these guys on TV. All okay, they are making some mistakes, but what is our responsibility? Give them space and address the issue, and how you going to do that if you won’t have anything to do with these Pentecostals and charismatics? So we had four witnesses in the Bible. I gave you my witness of the baptism of the Holy Ghost. Tongues was a small part of that baptism. That baptism of love, that baptism to respond right, that part of the Holy Ghost was the thing that really got my attention, the part that drove me to the Bible to learn it and not just depend on people from the pulpit teaching me. That part of the Holy Ghost to love people, to stay in unity, even with Catholics. I preached in Catholic churches, I preached in Baptist churches, I had no offenses even though I disagreed with them. And I wouldn’t go in there with my disagreements. I would go in there with other truths and get, let get them to know me. Are you with me? I have had a chance to witness to the number one guy of the American Baptist Association and the Southern Baptist Association in one meeting in California, because they saw in me something different than other Pentecostals and Spirit-filled people had, and that’s what they told me. “We’ve never met a Spirit person like you.” And my response was, “Well, you haven’t met any of them because you won’t have anything to do with them. I came to you, I got involved with you.” But I had the chance, from the Scriptures, they showed me their argument, and I had a chance, from the Scriptures, to show them their argument wasn’t Scriptural. Hallelujah. One of those Baptist leaders was in the Assembly of God church, sought for the baptism of the Holy Ghost, he told me, didn’t get to speak in tongues, so he just felt it was a bunch of nonsense, and he left and went into the fundamental church. And I told him that’s one of the mistakes Pentecostals and charismatics make. They say the tongues is the only sign of the baptism of the Holy Ghost, and it is not. The Bible doesn’t say it’s the only sign, and it’s not the only sign. And the real signs are the character, the divine nature of God. Can you honestly say amen to that? And all of us can have it. It’s poured out on all flesh, but you get it when you get it, and if you don’t have it, you’ve got to admit you don’t have it to get it. Now, how many would like the promise of God to have the baptism of the Holy Ghost that brings you into the divine nature? Let me see your hand. Yeah, you see, a lot of people are so scared of the Holy Ghost now because of big arguments, they won’t seek the very thing that can revolutionize their life, their marriage, their church.
How should we treat people we disagree with, and is tongues the only sign of the baptism of the Holy Ghost?

Acts 2:17: ‘And it shall come to pass in the last days, says God, That I will pour out of My Spirit on all flesh; Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, Your young men shall see visions, Your old men shall dream dreams.
Does he use “baptism of the Holy Spirit” and “filled with the Holy Spirit” for the same thing?
He says yes: the baptism of the Holy Ghost “is the baptism of the Holy Spirit, which is being filled with the Holy Spirit. They’re all synonymous terms.”
Does Ephesians 5:18 allow Christians to drink as long as they do not get drunk?
He says no: he says it isn’t saying “if I drink and I don’t get intoxicated, I’m fine,” and that wine “will distort your judgment, alcohol will, and so you can’t use that to justify drinking at all.”
Did Jesus speak in tongues when He was filled with the Holy Ghost?
He says no: “He didn’t speak in tongues… He didn’t pass out in the water, He didn’t get slain in the Spirit.” He says Jesus “went immediately into the wilderness to be tested.”
What does he say the Bible says about alcohol?
He says John the Baptist “shall drink neither wine nor strong drink,” and that “the Bible does not approve of intoxication of any kind,” because “God isn’t for anything that destroys you.”
Does the Bible record Stephen or Paul speaking in tongues when they were filled?

He says for Stephen “there’s no record that he spoke in tongues when he got the Holy Ghost. There’s no record that he didn’t.” For Paul he says “there is no indication,” though “he speaks in tongues more than y’all” later.
What is forgiveness, according to his piece-of-paper illustration?

He says you throw the mistake away like a wadded-up piece of paper, take it to the dump “and you never get it back again. Forgiveness is forgiving and forgetting. Pardoning, you know, no condemnation, no guilt.”
Who does he say is our example?
He says “the Bible plainly says Jesus Christ is our example. We’re to model after Him and Him only,” and quotes Paul, “follow me as I follow Christ.”
Can a pastor, priest or evangelist free you from sin?
He says no: “the pope can’t free you from sin, the priest can’t free you, I can’t free you from sin, the evangelist can’t free you from sin. We are all voices trying to bring you to Christ.”
Does he say he may hate people he thinks are wrong?
He says no: “I have a right to confront wrong, but I don’t have a right to hate Catholics and look down on Catholics and not fellowship with Catholics.” He says, “I have a right to address wrong.”
He says yes: “these people say unconditional love, unconditional love… The Bible has a condition on things, and here the condition is, you forgive and God will forgive you.”
What does he mean by “perception hurt”?
He says some people weren’t really hurt by the other person: “that person that was hurt perceived they did or said something that the people didn’t really do or say.”
Why does he say some people cannot forgive?

He says “they let themselves be hurt. They get hurt, they get emotionally affected, and when you get emotionally involved… truth goes out the door, the Scriptures go out the door, and your emotions start running your life.”
Should you wait for the person to change before you forgive?

He says no: “you forgive them, even if they don’t ask you to forgive them… Jesus died before we asked Him to forgive us.” He says “why are you waiting for the person to change before you forgive them?”
What is the parable of the unforgiving servant?

He says a king forgave a servant a $10,000 debt, but that servant demanded $10 from another and had him jailed. The king called him “wicked” and, he says, “delivered him to the tormentors till he should pay all that was due.”
Is tongues the only sign of the baptism of the Holy Ghost?
He says no: “They say the tongues is the only sign… and it is not. The Bible doesn’t say it’s the only sign.” He says “the real signs are the character, the divine nature of God.”

p: In “Three Revelations Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer introduces the book of Revelation through its opening verse, saying it gives three revelations: the revelation of Jesus Christ, the revelation of the righteous judgment of God, and the revelation of the church. He teaches that Revelation is written to all of God’s servants, uses Romans 2 and Revelation 20 to show judgment by works and the Book of Life, and begins the revelation of the church as the body of Christ from Romans 16 and Ephesians 3 and 5.
Why does he say we should listen to John, who wrote Revelation on Patmos?

He says John was banished to the isle of Patmos after being tarred and feathered for preaching the gospel, and that on the island, in that affliction, he received the book of Revelation. He says that when somebody pays a price like that, “we need to listen to them.”
Why does he say we should listen to John, who wrote Revelation on Patmos?

This John got this on the isle of Patmos. He was banished by the local authorities to the isle of Patmos after he had been tarred and feathered and somehow survived for preaching the gospel. I mean, if you really want to go out and preach the gospel, people aren’t going to like you. It is not like the church in America today where we flatter people. And this is what you’re going to find in the book of Revelations, these guys that really went out and preached the gospel, they were [unclear], they were in prison, they were beaten, I mean they were subject to abuse all the time. Today, not so, because we’re really not preaching the gospel. We’re preaching a very flattering message that doesn’t challenge anyone, doesn’t shake up anyone. Most, now not all the church, but the majority of the church, and the majority of the church is on TV and radio, because you want numbers and you want money, you have to water down the message. You don’t want to hurt anybody’s feelings. But John wasn’t like that. He preached the gospel, he was tarred and feathered, and they banished him, and on that island, in that kind of affliction, he got this book of Revelation. And so when somebody pays a price like that, we need to listen to them. Could that be an
What are the three revelations in the book of Revelation?

He says the book is the revelation of Jesus Christ, not of the beast or Satan, and that there are three revelations: of Jesus Christ, of the eternal judgment, and of the church. He says that if you read the Bible without looking for Jesus, “you’re going to miss the whole point of the Bible.”
What are the three revelations in the book of Revelation?

amen? Revelations 1:1, it starts out by saying “the revelation of Jesus Christ.” Not the beast, not the revelation of Satan, not the revelation of the [unclear] sitting on the seven mountains. Are you hearing me? It’s the revelation of who? Jesus Christ. This book is going to tell us about Jesus Christ. Revelation means to disclose, to reveal things, even things that have not been seen before. Okay, and so we’re going to have the revelation, the revealing, the disclosure of Jesus Christ. And we find that there’s three revelations in the New Testament. That’s the revelation of Jesus, the Lion, the Lamb, the Captain of the host, the Head of the church. I mean, He’s the big guy, He’s the chief honcho in the Bible, and when you read the Bible, if you’re not looking for Jesus, you’re going to miss the whole point of the Bible. Secondly, it’s the revelation of the judgment. The Bible tells us there’s a revelation of the eternal judgment, and you don’t hear this message much anymore, that you’re going to be held accountable for what you say and do, and God is going to sentence you by what you say and do. You don’t hear this much anymore. When I was a kid you heard it all the time. They scared the hell out of you. I mean, man, you wanted Jesus and you wanted to get to heaven. But then we got into the love thing, everybody’s okay. And then the revelation of the church. I meet very few American Christians that even understand the basic revelation of the church. They think it’s a building with people in it. And I’d submit to you today, you don’t know it.
What are the three revelations in the book of Revelation?
Revelation 1:1: The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to show His servants—things which must shortly take place. And He sent and signified it by His angel to His servant John,
Is the church just a building with people in it?

He says no: the Bible calls the church the body of Christ, each member with a particular function, and that it is also a flock, an army, and a house, a temple of God. He says that seeing what the church really is “should revolutionize” how you use your time and approach God.
Is the church just a building with people in it?

Because if you did, it would change your life. It would change the way you do things. When we get through with the book of Revelation and you see what the church really is, it should revolutionize the way you schedule your time and you approach your God. It will make all the difference in the world, because the church isn’t some building with people in it. The Bible refers to it as the body of Christ. You see all those heads? See, we are the body of Christ and each one a member in particular, with a particular function. We have a function. Your little finger has a function. The smallest in God’s church has a function, a purpose and an objective. We are a flock, we follow the Shepherd, we need His protection, but we’re also an army, and we’re also a house, a temple of God. But we will get into that later, and this is what the Bible speaks of, these three revelations.
What are the three points in Revelation 1:1, and how do we get understanding?

He says Revelation 1:1 gives the revelation of Jesus Christ from God, things shown to “his servants,” which is all believers and not only the seven churches in Asia, and things that must shortly come to pass. He says we must pray for understanding of the scriptures because the Spirit is the only one who can open them to us.
What are the three points in Revelation 1:1, and how do we get understanding?

Now Revelations 1:1 has three points in it. Number one, the revelation of Jesus Christ, as we talked about, which God gave to Him. Who gave this to Him? God. All right. It’s not like Muhammad, it’s not like Joseph Smith. Those are imitators, as we’ll show you a little later. And you got to be [unclear]. You got to know truth if you want to be free and you want others to be free. It’s the truth that sets you free. Free from what? Your traditions, your unbelief, your [unclear] doctrines, your doctrines of men. It sets you free from these things. Amen. And sin. Now number two, “to show unto His servants things.” Okay, He’s going to show us things, and it’s not just to the seven churches in Asia. To show unto His servants, all of us who accepted Christ. Christ is the King and we are His servants, and so He wants to show everybody, not just the seven churches of Asia. This is directed to everyone, isn’t that true? And He’s going to show us things. How many want your eyes open to the things He wants to show? Yeah. You got to pray. One of your main prayers is not only wisdom, but you need to pray that God gives you understanding of the scriptures, because the Spirit is the only one that can open the scriptures up to you. That’s what the Bible says, they are spiritually discerned. The Spirit has to do it. See, we can use our human intellect, but it is the Spirit that really bursts the truth in us.
What are the three points in Revelation 1:1, and how do we get understanding?

Revelation 1:1: The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to show His servants—things which must shortly take place. And He sent and signified it by His angel to His servant John, John 8:32: And you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.” 1 Corinthians 2:14: But the natural man does not receive the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to him; nor can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.
Do we need a special prophet or teacher to explain Revelation to us?

He says no, because it says it was written to God’s servants, all of us. He says we do need preachers and teachers, but “they’re not the ones to follow,” and our faith should be in Jesus Christ and His truth, not in any man or man’s teaching.
Do we need a special prophet or teacher to explain Revelation to us?

Amen. And number three, read this last one with me: “which must shortly come to pass.” Read it again: “which must shortly come to pass.” Now I submit to you, it’s 2,000 years. Shortly? It doesn’t sound very shortly, does it? Hallelujah. These words, Revelations 22, now we’re at the last chapter of the book, all right: “These words are faithful.” You can count on them. The words of Revelation, they are truth. They’re just like all the other books in the Bible. “The Lord God of the holy prophets sent His angel to show His servants.” There we are again, to show who? His servants, all of us. Do we need some special prophet opening the book of Revelation to us? No. Why? Because He wrote it for all of us. You see, only in America do we have this mentality, we need the gurus, we need Osteen, we need Joyce Meyer, we need somebody. Why? ’Cause that’s what they tell us, they preach we need them. But here it says this is to who? All of us. Is God partial? We just taught on it. Do you have every right to every inheritance just like anybody else? Absolutely. Do we need preachers and teachers? Yes, we do, but they’re not the ones to follow, and they’re not the ones to worship. They should be leading us to the One, and our faith should not be in any man or any man’s teaching. Our faith should be in the Jesus Christ and His truth.
Do we need a special prophet or teacher to explain Revelation to us?
Revelation 22:6: Then he said to me, “These words are faithful and true.” And the Lord God of the holy prophets sent His angel to show His servants the things which must shortly take place.
What does he say about “shortly come to pass” and end-time prophecy teachers?

He says the book plainly says these things must shortly come to pass, and that end-time prophets twist and stretch scriptures to make it fit our last days. He warns that what you believe determines your behavior, and says there are people making up their own doctrine today.
What does he say about “shortly come to pass” and end-time prophecy teachers?

Amen. The things which must what? Shortly come to pass. He emphasizes it again. And what do all these end-time prophets do with Revelation? They twist and stretch all kinds of scriptures to get it to fit into our last days. Am I right? I am right. And it says plainly, these things must what? Shortly come to pass. Wow, you youngins got that? He says you need to take heed. Jesus told him, take heed, beware of the doctrine of the scribes and the Pharisees. Why? What you believe is what will determine your behavior. And the Pharisees had made up their own doctrine, and the Sadducees had made up their own doctrine, and have, you know, there’s people today making up their own doctrine, and people will try to please a church group in their doctrines of faith rather than please Christ and His book of faith. Could that be true? Now you young people understand this now. This is good stuff. This is deep stuff. This is not for the weak-hearted.
What does he say about “shortly come to pass” and end-time prophecy teachers?
Revelation 1:1: The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to show His servants—things which must shortly take place. And He sent and signified it by His angel to His servant John,
How does he say we should study the book of Revelation?

He uses an illustration of being shipwrecked on an island with only the book of Revelation, and says to use other true scriptures to confirm it. He compares it to a book about aerodynamics that mentions turbulence: the book is about how airplanes fly, and Revelation is about the revelation of Jesus Christ, not the other things it mentions.
How does he say we should study the book of Revelation?

This stuff is meat. It will get into your innards and work powerful in your life. So these three things: revelation of Jesus, He’s going to show His servants things, and it’s going to be brought about what? Shortly. Shortly. Okay, let’s look at the revelation of the righteous judgment of God in Romans chapter 2. Now we’re going to use the book of Revelations as the book. We’re going to pretend that we’re on an island, we got shipwrecked, and we’re on an island, and we were just a dumb sinner before that, and then this book comes floating in on shore, somehow it got in the ocean and it washed up on shore, and we got one book and it’s the book of Revelation. We’re only going to use other true scriptures to confirm the book of Revelation. Is that fair enough? Are you with me? How many of you know, a book of aerodynamics, it states in the introduction and all the rest, this is a book on aerodynamics, how airplanes may fly. Okay, so what’s the book going to be about? How airplanes fly. Now in the book they talk about electric storms in the heavens, and they talk about, uh, what they call that when it plain shakes? Turbulence. Now is the book about storms and turbulence, or is it still about aerodynamics? Aerodynamics. Okay, this book is about the revelation of Jesus Christ, and if He talks about other things, the book isn’t about those other things. It’s about what? The revelation of Jesus
How does he say we should study the book of Revelation?
Romans 2:5: But in accordance with your hardness and your impenitent heart you are treasuring up for yourself wrath in the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God,
What is the revelation of the righteous judgment of God, and how will we be judged?

He says the New Testament gives three revelations, and the second is the judgment to come, “a day of wrath and the unveiling of the righteous judgment of God.” He says God renders to each one according to his deeds, not according to his faith, his grace, or the church he attends.
What is the revelation of the righteous judgment of God, and how will we be judged?

Christ. And so the New Testament gives us three revelations: the revelation of Jesus Christ, the revelation of the judgment to come. See, the book isn’t complicated, it’s not 20 revelations, it’s how many? Three. “With your hardness and unrepentant heart you’re treasuring up wrath in the day of wrath.” Is there a day of wrath? Yes. “And the revelation of the righteous judgment of God.” So the two are synonymous, the two are happening at the same time. There’s a day of wrath and the unveiling of the righteous judgment of God. Now isn’t that easy to see? See, it’s not complicated. You don’t need the Hebrew and Greek, and you don’t need somebody on TV telling you what it says. It says what it says. Amen. “Who renders to each one according to his”, faith? Is that what it says? No. According to his grace? No. According to the church he goes to? No. According to your deeds, your work, your lifestyle, how you speak and how you act. You young people got that? That’s why the Bible says in Ecclesiastes, remember the Lord thy God in the days of thy youth before the evil day comes. Obey God, live right in your youth, because there’s a penalty coming. Eternal life. Then He tells us what’s going to happen by our
What is the revelation of the righteous judgment of God, and how will we be judged?

Romans 2:5-6: But in accordance with your hardness and your impenitent heart you are treasuring up for yourself wrath in the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God, who “will render to each one according to his deeds”: Ecclesiastes 12:1: Remember now your Creator in the days of your youth, Before the difficult days come, And the years draw near when you say, “I have no pleasure in them”:
Did Judas believe in Jesus, and what does he say about believing and living right?

He says Judas believed, preached, healed and cast out demons, yet was a thief and, in his words, did not go to heaven or find repentance. He says the gospel works no matter who preaches it, and that you get eternal life by believing, but if you believe on Jesus and live like Judas did, “you’re going to hell.”
Did Judas believe in Jesus, and what does he say about believing and living right?

deeds. You say, did Judas believe in Jesus? You’re looking at me like you’re afraid to answer. Absolutely, he did. Did Judas preach the gospel? Yes. Did Judas heal the sick? Yes. Did Judas cast out demons? Yes. Was Judas a thief the whole time? Yes. Jesus said, “I’ve chose you 12 and one of you is a thief.” Jesus knew who Judas was when He picked him, and He picked him because He knew his heart, and he would fulfill what the scriptures had designated to be fulfilled, and there was a lot of Judases that day, He just picked this one. Are you out there, church? So because someone’s preaching the gospel and the gospel works, does that mean they’re great? No. It means the gospel’s great. Do you young ones get that? See, the gospel works no matter who’s preaching it. Because the gospel just works. Hallelujah. So He’s going to tell us what’s going to happen because of our works and our deeds. When our works are right, we get eternal life: “to those who by patience and continuing in doing good.” They patiently serve God whether things are good, whether things are bad, whether people serve God or whether the people don’t, they just stay faithful, they patiently serve God doing good things. Amen. And they get what? Eternal life. But I’m going to get eternal life because I believe on Jesus. That’s the step. But you believe on Jesus and you live like Judas did, you’re going to hell. Did Judas go to heaven? No. Did Judas find repentance, by the way? No. Are you there? See, it’s best to just serve God all the days of your life. And then there’s wrath to those who are self-seeking, who do what they want to do. They just do what they want to do. Their life’s about them. Everything they do is something to their advantage. What do I get out of it? Most of the church world in America have no compassion for the lost. They don’t weep in their prayers for the lost. You know, we got a lot of teenagers coming in here on Friday night who need our weapons of warfare exercised so that the kingdom of darkness’ hold on them is broken, but people don’t care. The kids are coming in, let them have fun, let them play games, you know, “I’ll just stay away.” Uh, you know, no. See, we don’t understand the
