p: In “UnBorn Again,” Pastor David G. Kincer uses the stages of a seed, an embryo and a baby to teach spiritual growth. He covers how hearing the word starts the process, why some “abort” it (mock it or put it off), the four soils, baptism, and what it means to grow up into Christ rather than a denomination.
What does natural growth from a seed teach about spiritual growth?

He says “the Bible always uses natural illustrations to help us understand the spiritual.” Every seed has an embryo that grows “into the image that God designed it to grow in,” and in the spirit “the word of God is what’s going to start that seed in us.”
What does natural growth from a seed teach about spiritual growth?

Today we are going to talk about spiritual growth. All right, as you can see up there, I have some photos illustrating the natural, spiritual growth. At the top, the baby in the womb, the baby born, and then toddler up to adulthood. And then in the second series, we have, again, the baby in the womb, the baby born, and then following Jesus, growing to maturity. And this is what this is about. And the Bible always uses natural illustrations to help us understand the spiritual. Here we have a seed. Inside every seed is an embryo, okay, that embryo contains life. All it has to do is have the water to hit that seed, after that seed is dead, and that embryo inside will start growing into the image that God designed it to grow in. A bean will not produce a tomato. It will grow into the image. As you can see, the roots start coming out, the root more, and then the plant starts growing out of the ground, and then the leaves start growing on the plant, and in the end you have the fruit of that plant, and that is the growing process. Also in the spirit, we need a seed. See, we need it watered, we need it in the right atmosphere, the right conditions, and the word of God is what’s going to start that seed in us. It’s going to be the embryo, all right.
What is the “unborn” stage of spiritual growth, and what happens when we hear the word? (Acts 17:32)

He says the unborn stage is when God’s word is planted “in your inner man.” Some who heard Paul “mocked,” some said “we’ll hear you again,” and “some believed and followed.” He says “when you mock and when you want to put it off, you have hindered the growth of the word.”
What is the “unborn” stage of spiritual growth, and what happens when we hear the word? (Acts 17:32)

Now we’re going to look at the unborn fetus stage of growth, okay, and how to recognize an unborn seed of God’s word. It’s in the fetus stage, all right. Acts 17:32, “when they heard of the resurrection of the dead.” Okay, they heard. God has chosen the foolishness of preaching to save all that would believe. You know, go out and preach the gospel, and so that is the sowing of the word. When you hear the word, that’s when God will come by his Spirit and try to plant that word in your inner man, in your spirit. We got it. You young ones over here, got it? See, hearing the word is vitally important. All right, “when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked.” See, they didn’t let the word take, get attached to the spiritual man and grow. “Others said, we’ll hear you again.” They put it off. Well, you know, I’m busy, you know, I’m getting a career, I’m going to college, I’m working, I’m raising kids, whatever. You know, I’ll listen another time. “But some believed and followed.” So which ones actually let the embryo grow and produce seed? The one who believed, and not just believed, but they followed. All right, when you mock, and when you want to put it off, you have hindered the growth of the word in your inner man. Acts 2:37: “When they heard this, they were pricked in their heart.” Again, they heard the preaching, they heard the message of the gospel, they were pricked, they were stirred in their heart, in their mind, in their emotional man, that’s the heart, and said, “What shall we do?” You see, now they responded to the word. They didn’t mock and they didn’t put it off. They said, “What must we do?”
What is the “unborn” stage of spiritual growth, and what happens when we hear the word? (Acts 17:32)

Acts 17:32: And when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked, while others said, “We will hear you again on this matter.” 1 Corinthians 1:21: For since, in the wisdom of God, the world through wisdom did not know God, it pleased God through the foolishness of the message preached to save those who believe.
How did the jailer respond to the word, and why does he say baptism should not be delayed? (Acts 2:37; 16:25-33)

He says the jailer “trembled,” asked “what must I do to be saved,” and was baptized “the same night.” He says he asked a nation that delays baptism six months to a year for “scripture for putting off baptism” and “there is none,” and that baptism is not “an outward sign of an inward work.”
How did the jailer respond to the word, and why does he say baptism should not be delayed? (Acts 2:37; 16:25-33)

And so the embryo is getting root and growing in. Acts 16:25-29: Paul and Silas were in jail, and they prayed and sang praises to God, the prisoners what? Heard them. They didn’t do silent prayers. They didn’t do silent praise and worship. The prisoners heard them. All right, then the keeper of the prison was going to kill himself, and Paul said, “Don’t do that. Don’t kill yourself. We’re all here. There’s no one escaped.” And so when the keeper heard, what did he do? He trembled. See, the word affected him. It shook him, it stirred him. He trembled at the word of the Lord, fell down and said, “What must I do to be saved?” See, we knew he heard the message because he’s asking, “What do I got to do to correct my problem, to get saved from sin? What do I got to do?” And the word pierced his heart. That embryo started, that seed started. He didn’t mock, he didn’t put it off. He let it bring forth that embryo fruit, the root starting and the fruit of salvation to be produced in his life. You got it? Acts 16:33: “The same hour of the night he was baptized in all his house, immediately, and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house.” I was just in a nation not too long ago where they put off baptism for six months to a year, and I asked them, “Give me scripture for putting off baptism.” There is none. You repent and you what? Get baptized. How long did it take for the jail keeper to get baptized in water? The same night. You see why? Because baptism is not a ceremony, which I heard recently, an outward sign of an inward work. That is not in the Bible. You cannot show me that statement in the Bible. It’s just something we hear and we hold on to it and we repeat it without really checking in the Bible. Baptism is putting to death of the old man of sin and coming up a new creature, and people need to know this stuff before they’re baptized so that they can experience baptism for what it’s for. Can I hear an amen? And a lot of people have been robbed of a great experience in water baptism because it’s an outward sign of an inward work, we’re just going through a ceremony, it’s just a ritual, there’s nothing in it. There is something in it. When you put to death the old man, there’s something powerful happening, and when you rise up a new creature that’s committed to righteousness, that is a tremendous work of God, and God chose water baptism to do that.
How did the jailer respond to the word, and why does he say baptism should not be delayed? (Acts 2:37; 16:25-33)

Acts 2:37: Now when they heard this, they were cut to the heart, and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles, “Men and brethren, what shall we do?” Acts 16:25-29: But at midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them. Suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken; and immediately all the doors were opened and everyone’s chains were loosed. And the keeper of the prison, awaking from sleep and seeing the prison doors open, supposing the prisoners had fled, drew his sword and was about to kill himself. But Paul called with a loud voice, saying, “Do yourself no harm, for we are all here.” Then he called for a light, ran in, and fell down trembling before Paul and Silas. Acts 16:33: And he took them the same hour of the night and washed their stripes. And immediately he and all his family were baptized.
What are the four kinds of ground in the parable of the sower, and what does he add about patience? (Matthew 13)

He describes hard-minded hearers who “mocked” and “put it off,” the skeptical who “have no root” and “fall away,” those “choked” by the cares of life, and the “honest and good heart” who “keep the word.” He says we need many seeds of the word, not just “grace and faith or water baptism,” and “patience for God to reveal … the truth.”
What are the four kinds of ground in the parable of the sower, and what does he add about patience? (Matthew 13)

Now we’re going to go to the old Sunday school lesson of the parable of the sower. The seeds fell on four different kinds of ground, four different kinds of hearers. This helps us to understand the embryo growth, the embryo, that initial inward growth of God. All right, the seed fell on the wayside here, or it fell on hard minds, okay. Their minds were hardened. They hear, then comes the Devil and takes away the word. They mocked, they put it off, see, like we already heard, “lest they should believe and be saved.” They never get to the believing stage, that never brings forth the fruit of trusting God. Believe is to trust. All right, that’s the first one. They’re hard-hearted, they’re hard-headed, they’re hard-minded, and they mock and they don’t listen to the word of God. The second one fell upon the rocks. They’re the skeptical ones, the doubters. They hear and receive the word with joy, but they have no root. And who’s the root? Jesus Christ is the root and offspring of David. They have no root in themselves, and in time of temptation they fall away. You see, time of testing they fall away. Now, a lot of churches preach that Christians don’t go through testing. Show me in the Bible. And no, don’t just preach stuff, show me, because I can show you from Adam to John the Revelator testings, and you’re going to go through testings, all right. They fall away. What do they fall away from? The only thing they had. What did they have? Belief. They fall away from the belief. Okay, and oh, these are the, I call them shooting stars. They get saved and they put on these great things. “Oh yeah, man, oh what, you know, I was in drugs and I was a prostitute and all this stuff and man, I got saved, Jesus saved me and old man,” and then poof, they’re gone, because there’s no root. The root can’t grow on rocks. The rocks are too hard, it can’t find a place to get into the soil and bring forth fruit. Number three, they fell among thorns. These people hear the word of God and they go forth and are choked. They go forth, they go out into the world, they live their life (and all of us have got to go out into the world and live our life), and they’re choked with the cares and the riches and pleasures of this life and bring no fruit to perfection or maturity. They got a little bit of faith, see, they got a little bit of grace, got a little bit of, you know, belief, but never brings it to maturity where it really can be seen in their life. And this is the embryo again. See, the embryo is not growing right. That inner seed is not growing right. And then some fell on good ground. These are they that hear the word in an honest and good heart. They’re not hiding any sins, they’re not hiding any pride, they’re not hiding anything. They have an honest heart. If they make a mistake, they admit it, and their heart, their mind is set to do good. You see, they repented because they were doing bad things, and they have a goal to do good things, and so out of that kind of mind, out of that kind of an emotion, the embryo seed can grow, get root and produce fruit. See, and they heard the word, they keep the word. They actually keep the word. They don’t just talk about faith and grace, they keep the word. Every word that they heard, they set a goal to keep. Isn’t that beautiful? And how many you know there’s more word in the Bible than just saved by grace through faith. That is the initial foundation that you must get started on, but there’s a lot of word seed. All of you, I’m sure, enjoy different vegetables, not just wheat. You don’t go through life just eating wheat all the time. You throw a little corn, beans in there, and potatoes and rice, and so it is in the word of God. There are many seeds of the word, and you need them all for nourishment. Wow, that was good. Did you guys get that? We can’t stop at grace and faith or water baptism. Okay, and they bring forth fruit with what? What’s that magic word? Patience. You know, they don’t give up because they’re not there yet. They don’t quit because they haven’t bridled the tongue yet. They don’t quit because they haven’t bridled their temper yet. They don’t quit because, you know, they haven’t figured out what the Holy Ghost baptism is all about. They don’t quit because they don’t know which way Christ is coming: [unclear] post-trib, mid-trib, [unclear] millennium, postmillennium, premillennium. You know, they don’t quit and give up, they just keep growing. They have patience for God to reveal to them the truth, and that’s the only way you’re going to get it anyway. There is no preacher that has the power to open your spiritual man to understand the word. Only the Holy Ghost can do that.
What are the four kinds of ground in the parable of the sower, and what does he add about patience? (Matthew 13)

Matthew 13:3-9: Then He spoke many things to them in parables, saying: “Behold, a sower went out to sow. And as he sowed, some seed fell by the wayside; and the birds came and devoured them. Some fell on stony places, where they did not have much earth; and they immediately sprang up because they had no depth of earth. But when the sun was up they were scorched, and because they had no root they withered away. And some fell among thorns, and the thorns sprang up and choked them. But others fell on good ground and yielded a crop: some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty. He who has ears to hear, let him hear!” Luke 8:12: Those by the wayside are the ones who hear; then the devil comes and takes away the word out of their hearts, lest they should believe and be saved. Luke 8:15: But the ones that fell on the good ground are those who, having heard the word with a noble and good heart, keep it and bear fruit with patience.
What does he mean by people who “abort the word”? (Acts 5:33; 7:54; 24:25)

He says some people in the Bible “aborted the word,” killing it “just like a baby,” and then tried “to shut up anybody that’s speaking the truth.” He gives the council that wanted to slay the apostles, those who stoned Stephen, and Felix, who trembled when Paul reasoned of righteousness, self-control and judgment.
What does he mean by people who “abort the word”? (Acts 5:33; 7:54; 24:25)

We’re going to look at people that abort the word and their reaction, their behavior. All right, these are people that are in the Bible that aborted the word. We’re going to Acts. We’ll start with Acts 5:33: “When they heard, they were cut to the heart and took counsel to slay” Peter and the apostles who spoke the word. See, they not only mock, they don’t even put it off for another day, they not only mock but they want to physically address the issue. And you got to understand why these people are the way they are. They aborted the word. The word came, they killed it, just like a baby. This baby has been killed and aborted by a saline solution. They just burn the baby to death. And this is what people do with the word. They just kill it, and then when they kill it, their outward behavior is to try to shut up anybody that’s speaking the truth of God’s word. Acts 7:54: “When they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed on him with their teeth” and stoned Stephen. You see, again, they aborted the word. He gave them a tremendous word. As you know, one of the greatest sermons ever. You talking about me preaching from Genesis to Revelation, this guy covered half of the Old Testament in one sermon, and instead of them going, “Yay for Jesus, yay for truth,” they aborted the word. The Bible says they put their hands over their ears, they hated it, and they stoned Stephen. Acts 24:5: as Paul reasoned to Felix, the civil leader, as he reasoned, that’s him preaching the word, he’s talking the word, he reasoned of righteousness, temperance or self-control, and the judgment to come. He said there’s a coming judgment if you don’t control yourself and do what’s right, and the word caused Felix to what? Tremble. I’ve told you before, I have witnessed to atheists. Atheists say, “You cannot prove there’s a God.” I tell them, “I can prove there’s a God.” They go, “Oh no, you can’t.” I said, “Oh yes, I can.” And I said, “If you obey the principles of this book, you admit you’re sinners, you ask Jesus to forgive you your sins, and you will find God showing up and making himself real.” And so they go through the motions, okay, and those of course, they don’t know how to pray, so I’ll say, “You know, just follow my prayer, just repeat after me,” and man, you know, I bring out the sin, and I’m specific with the sins, and they’re speaking, “I’m over there arrogant,” and all this stuff. Oh yeah, yeah. And then I asked them to ask Jesus to cleanse them for these sins, and man, when they start saying that part, they start shaking. They don’t want it to be real. They don’t want this presence to be there, and so they resisted. And this is what people in the baptized in the Holy Ghost do. The reason they shake is because they don’t know how to release the baptism of the Holy Ghost, and I was a shaker until I learned how to channel it. You know, this power comes on you and you go, “My goodness, whoa.” You like it but you’re afraid of it, and you kind of, oo. And this is what the atheists did. They tremble, and then they let go of my hand, “We got to get out of here.” And Mr. Barnes has been with me at least twice when I’ve done that, haven’t you? See, God honors his word. God shows up. Don’t tell me I can’t prove there’s a God. God will honor his word. Hallelujah.
What does he mean by people who “abort the word”? (Acts 5:33; 7:54; 24:25)

Acts 5:33: When they heard this, they were furious and plotted to kill them. Acts 7:54: When they heard these things they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed at him with their teeth. Acts 24:25: Now as he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was afraid and answered, “Go away for now; when I have a convenient time I will call for you.”
What happened with Felix and Agrippa, and what does “Christian” mean? (Acts 26:27-28)

He says Felix said “at a convenient time I will call for you” and so “aborted the word,” and that Agrippa said “almost you persuade me to be a Christian” but would not follow. He says “Christian” means to “come from,” “belong to,” and “follow” Christ, so “a Christian follows Christ, period.”
What happened with Felix and Agrippa, and what does “Christian” mean? (Acts 26:27-28)

And so then Felix said, “At a convenient time I will call for you.” So what did he do? He aborted the word after he shook and he trembled and he heard it all and he knew it was real. He didn’t want it, and so he aborted it, just like people abort babies today. They don’t want them, they’re inconvenient, and they abort them. So do people abort the word of God. Acts 26:27: now this is really good. This is a grip of the second. And Paul is talking to him, and see, for us to go to civil leaders is Bible. These people that believe that Satan’s in charge of the governments, and leave them alone, there’s nothing we can do. Satan’s a liar. He lied to Jesus, of all people. Jesus was the head of the nations, he is the King of kings and Lord of lords. See, growth is a stage, there, steps. End-time prophets look at Israel, they look at acts of God, they look at wickedness, instead of the glorious church overcoming the gates of hell. The Bible says in Revelation that he’s coming and his bride has what? Made herself ready. Ephesians says that he’s coming for a bride that is a glorious church without spot or wrinkle or any such thing. Are we there yet? No, we can’t even fellowship with people outside of our corral, our denomination, our beliefs. We’re not there. Are we destroying the gates of hell in America today as a corporate church? No way. The homosexuals, the atheists, everybody’s having free rein with us. You’re going to be sad that you were here this morning, because who much is given, much is required. Church, God has given this church a fantastic word, but if we don’t take it seriously and get it out to others and just live our life, grazing, kids, working a job, going through every day routine, we’re not going to help anybody. So I submit to you, we got to get the word out, and get them to hear the word and read the word. That word will set people free, that word will heal people, but we can’t keep putting it off. We can’t just stay at this place where, “Oh boy, we got a word, hallelujah, that was a good message.” No, we’ve got to get a hunger and desire and a compelling to get it out to others. Could that be an amen? Printed word, audio word, video word, any word, we need to get it out, because it’s the word that sets us free, and who much is given, much is required, and we need to get this word out. We need to challenge. I’m ready to get on radio and TV and challenge the leaders of our day, both political and church leaders. They are wimps when they deny the truth of the Bible just to have a big congregation and a lavish lifestyle. That is wrong. We need to preach truth no matter if it takes everything, every possession we got.
Are we the “glorious church” yet, and why must we get the word out? (Ezekiel 14:14)

Ezekiel 14:14: Even if these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they would deliver only themselves by their righteousness,” says the Lord GOD. Revelation 19:7: Let us be glad and rejoice and give Him glory, for the marriage of the Lamb has come, and His wife has made herself ready.” Luke 12:48: But he who did not know, yet committed things deserving of stripes, shall be beaten with few. For everyone to whom much is given, from him much will be required; and to whom much has been committed, of him they will ask the more.
What does he mean by the “unborn fetus stage” of growth?
He says it is when the word is planted: “when you hear the word, that’s when God will come by his Spirit and try to plant that word in your inner man, in your spirit.”
Does he say baptism should be delayed?
No. He says “give me scripture for putting off baptism. There is none,” and that the jailer was baptized “the same night.”
What does he say about baptism being “an outward sign of an inward work”?
He says “that is not in the Bible,” and that “a lot of people have been robbed of a great experience in water baptism” because they treat it as a ritual: “there is something in it.”
What does he call the “shooting stars” in the parable of the sower?

He calls the rocky-ground hearers “shooting stars”: they “get saved and they put on these great things,” and “then poof, they’re gone, because there’s no root.” He also says “a lot of churches preach that Christians don’t go through testing.”
What does he say “good ground” looks like?
He says they have “an honest heart,” “they’re not hiding any sins,” “if they make a mistake, they admit it,” and “they keep the word.”
What does he say happens when he witnesses to atheists?
He says he tells them “I can prove there’s a God” if they “obey the principles of this book,” and that when they pray about their sins “they start shaking” and “don’t want it to be real.”
Why does he compare rejecting the word to abortion?
He says Felix “aborted the word” after he “shook and he trembled,” “just like people abort babies today. They don’t want them, they’re inconvenient, and they abort them.”
What does he say the word “Christian” means?

He says the suffix “ian” means “to come from, belong to, or to follow,” so “a Christian follows Christ, period,” not “a Protestant denomination.” He says “I can be a Pentecostal, I can be a Baptist, I can be a Methodist, I can be a Catholic and follow Christ.”
What does he say happened in 1968?
He says “God poured out the Holy Ghost upon all the denominations,” and the denominations “kicked them out,” though the Catholics said “go ahead, do your thing in the back room.”
What does he mean by a “religionist”?
He says “religionist is someone that puts their opinions above the Scripture,” and “when you put your opinions or your denomination’s opinions above Scripture, you are a religionist.”
Does he say being a baby Christian is a problem?

No. He says “if you’re a baby, you’re a baby, there’s nothing wrong with that,” and “God looks at you and says that person is perfect” because “they’re right where they’re supposed to be at this time.”
Does he say Christians should see a doctor?
Yes. He says “God can heal, but if he doesn’t, you better get to a doctor,” citing Jesus: “They that are sick need a physician.”
What does he say about welfare?
He says “welfare is a bribe,” that it “should be connected with work,” and that “somebody has got to get this,” while saying “is there a time where people need help? Absolutely.”
What does he say it means to be a “baby Christian”?
He says “if you are number two … you are a born-again, probably a baby Christian, and there’s nothing wrong with being a baby Christian at all.”
How much time does he say God asks for each day?
He says “God asks for one hour of your day,” “in the Bible and in prayer,” and that people have “time to watch everything on TV” but are “busy satisfying your own agenda.”

p: In this session on present truth, Pastor David G. Kincer recaps the seasons of the last days and then turns to recognizing hatred and persecution. From John 15 and Second Timothy 3:12 he says believers are hated for following Jesus and living godly, shows that John the Baptist, Jesus and Stephen were killed for speaking morally, recounts early martyrs, the Inquisition and modern persecution, and urges American Christians to stand for Bible morality.
What does it mean to be established in present truth?

He says God accomplishes his purposes in times and seasons, the children of Issachar understood God’s times, and Second Peter 1:12 says to be established in present truth. He recaps that we are in the last days, the salvation season, plural days in which God poured out his Spirit in 1900, 1948 and 1968, and in a 2,000-year season of false prophets and antichrists.
What does it mean to be established in present truth?

Again I’d like to thank you for coming and join us in another session of present truths. Remember we have found that God has a purpose under heaven and he accomplishes that in a time and a season First Corinthians 12:38 tells us the children of Issachar had understanding of God’s times God’s seasons to know what Israel ought to do and so if we’re going to be established in present truth as II Peter 1:12 says we need to know what present truth is. Remember. We found that we are living in the last days we’re in the last day season. Which is the salvation season people can come to Christ and be saved from their sins in this season the last days is plural there’s more than one day one season one happening in these last days and we don’t know how long they are. And he says I’ll pour out my spirit in those days plural again before the day singular of the Lord comes. And so God did he poured out his Holy Spirit in 1900 1948 1968. The last days. We also found were in the false prophet and the antichrist season. Present truth the present truth is we are living and we have been living for 2,000 years in the false prophet season and the antichrist season from the time Jesus began to preach there was false prophets even before that when he began to preach they were antichrist they that opposed Christ or antichrist he didn’t come in the flesh wasn’t born of a virgin didn’t rise from the dead or whatever.
What does it mean to be established in present truth?

1 Chronicles 12:32: of the sons of Issachar who had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do, their chiefs were two hundred; and all their brethren were at their command; 2 Peter 1:12: For this reason I will not be negligent to remind you always of these things, though you know and are established in the present truth.
What are the clues of false prophets, and where does persecution start?

He recaps that false prophets say sin is okay, are in it for the money and behave immorally. He says Jesus’ followers are hated, and it starts in their own family: the more you want to serve God the more people separate from you, and it can branch out to persecution and martyrdom by all nations until the end.
What are the clues of false prophets, and where does persecution start?

And we found false prophet clues were they say sin is okay they’re in it for the money. They behave immorally. And we found that there’s a future projection. When some of these false prophets will do signs and wonders but we haven’t seen that yet. We found we’re in the season. The time where Jesus followers are hated they’re mistreated. And it starts in their own family. The more you want to serve God and do what’s right the more people want to separate from you your friends change and then it can branch out to persecution and even martyrdom. But. We found that all nations were going to persecute the church until the end.
Has the falling away already happened?

He says Christ could not have come before the 1500s because all nations were not yet known. He says the great falling away already happened in the dark ages, from 476 A.D. to around 1500, and end-time prophets troubling people that Jesus is coming any minute are doing what the Bible says not to be shaken by.
Has the falling away already happened?

And all nations were not discovered until the 1500s so God couldn’t have come before the 1500s because we didn’t know there was other nations out there and people who prophesied his coming before that missed it because they didn’t understand understand the scripture that we don’t know. That’s put in the hands of God and these things have to be fulfilled. We found we’re in the season of falling away. Has already happened. And will it happen again that’s up to God but we know in history there was a great falling away of the church of Christianity. Uh we call them the dark ages from 476 A.D. to around 1500 a little bit before. There was a tremendous falling away the church was very corrupt and it says don’t be troubled. By spirit or by word don’t be shaken in your mind that the day of the Lord is at hand let no man deceive you and this is what end time prophets are doing they’re just troubling the minds and the hearts of God’s people thinking that any minute Jesus is going to come when the Bible says don’t be shaken by these people don’t be shaken by these people. We also found that the gospel. Will be preached to all nations as a witness. And so we and then shall the end come so we know because of this scripture.
Has the falling away already happened?

2 Thessalonians 2:2-3: not to be soon shaken in mind or troubled, either by spirit or by word or by letter, as if from us, as though the day of Christ had come. Let no one deceive you by any means; for that Day will not come unless the falling away comes first, and the man of sin is revealed, the son of perdition,
Has the gospel been preached to all nations, and is knowledge increasing?

From Matthew 24:14 he says the gospel has not been preached to all nations as a witness, because if it had, the end would come. He says we are in the season of increasing knowledge since the printing press, and the book of Daniel was sealed until the time of the end, when the wise shall understand, so wisdom will be restored.
Has the gospel been preached to all nations, and is knowledge increasing?

The gospel has not been preached to all nations. Because if it has, the end comes. And that’s in Matthew 24:14. North and South America had not even been. Discovered till the 1500s Australia and the islands of the seas and so people who predicted the second coming before this time didn’t know what they were talking about because God has to fulfill these scriptures. Jesus said everything every jot and every tittle of the word will be fulfilled. We also found. That there will be an increase in knowledge. And we. Found that we are living in that season of increase in knowledge and technology industrial revolution the printing press being invented in 1440 just started changing everything where they used to hand write 40 pages a day now they could print 3600 pages a day books became cheap knowledge began to increase. And we’ve got to remember that the book was sealed until the time of the end even Daniel did not understand what God was talking about in Daniel 11 and 12. And he said I I hear you but I don’t understand it and he says this book is sealed up until the time of the end many will be purified made white and tried people are going to be saved people are going to be following God the wicked will do wickedly and none of the wicked shall understand but the wise shall understand so there’s going to be a restoration of wisdom so I’m going to be one of the things restored. We also found that restoration and refreshing times have come from the presence of the Lord in Acts 3. And there’s more to come. Till the end.
Has the gospel been preached to all nations, and is knowledge increasing?

Matthew 24:14: And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world as a witness to all the nations, and then the end will come. Matthew 5:18: For assuredly, I say to you, till heaven and earth pass away, one jot or one tittle will by no means pass from the law till all is fulfilled. Daniel 12:8-10: Although I heard, I did not understand. Then I said, “My lord, what shall be the end of these things?” And he said, “Go your way, Daniel, for the words are closed up and sealed till the time of the end. Many shall be purified, made white, and refined, but the wicked shall do wickedly; and none of the wicked shall understand, but the wise shall understand.
Why hasn’t Jesus come yet, and are disasters signs of the end?

He says Jesus has to remain in the heavens until all things are restored, so there is more to be done, and if you are dry and dead, let Jesus refresh you and restore the wasted years. He says wars, quakes, famines and plagues have been present since Jesus preached, but Jesus said “the end is not yet.”
Why hasn’t Jesus come yet, and are disasters signs of the end?

Because Jesus it says there and Acts 3:18 has to remain in the heavens until all things are restored. If all things were restored. Jesus would have come already. So obviously there’s more to be done. And so we’re in the seasons of refreshing from the presence of the Lord if you’re dry and dead let Jesus refresh you let Jesus build you up let Jesus restore the wasted years. We also found in Luke 21:11. That wars quakes. Famines plagues. Are present truths and have been present truth since Jesus started preaching himself. But we found it’s not a sign of the end. Jesus himself said. The end is not yet. Don’t be troubled for such things must happen they must needs be, the end shall not be yet and so many end time prophets put a focus and an importance on the fact that we have wars earthquakes famines and plagues and diseases throughout the earth and Jesus said that’s not a sign of the end that’s just going to happen and so we’re living in the season where wars and earthquakes and famines and hurricanes and all these things plagues are going to be happening that’s the season we’re living in. We also found we live in the present true season of Israel becoming a nation.
Why hasn’t Jesus come yet, and are disasters signs of the end?

Acts 3:19-21: Repent therefore and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, so that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord, and that He may send Jesus Christ, who was preached to you before, whom heaven must receive until the times of restoration of all things, which God has spoken by the mouth of all His holy prophets since the world began. Luke 21:9-11: But when you hear of wars and commotions, do not be terrified; for these things must come to pass first, but the end will not come immediately.” Then He said to them, “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. And there will be great earthquakes in various places, and famines and pestilences; and there will be fearful sights and great signs from heaven.
What does Israel becoming a nation tell us?

He says Jesus told those who asked about restoring the kingdom to Israel that it is not for us to know the times and seasons, yet end-time prophets claim to know. He notes Israel became a nation in 1948, the same year God poured out his Spirit on the church, but says that does not mean natural Israel is spiritual.
What does Israel becoming a nation tell us?

And Jesus said. To those who ask him will you at this time restore the kingdom of Israel Jesus said it’s not for you to know the times and the seasons which the father has put in his own authority. And all these end time prophets are trying to tell us they know. What Jesus said we couldn’t know. And Israel became a nation in 1948. Uh very interesting one of the times when he poured out his spirit was in 1948 and brought restoration back to the church he was moving in natural Israel at the same time doesn’t mean natural Israel is spiritual as we will find. Today we’re going to look at. Recognizing acknowledging.
What does Israel becoming a nation tell us?

Acts 1:6-7: Therefore, when they had come together, they asked Him, saying, “Lord, will You at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?” And He said to them, “It is not for you to know times or seasons which the Father has put in His own authority.
Why does the world hate followers of Jesus?

From John 15:19-20 he says Jesus chose us out of the world, so the world hates us, and if they persecuted him they will persecute us. He compares it to marriage, when old suitors stopped liking him, and from Second Timothy 3:12 and John 15:16 gives two reasons: having an encounter with Jesus to follow him, and living godly.
Why does the world hate followers of Jesus?

And perhaps having to flee from persecution and hatred. John 15:19 I chose you out of the world for this reason the world hates you see I chose you Jesus said I came and had an encounter with you I came to you. And he goes on to say the servant is not greater than his Lord if they have persecuted me they will persecute you ooh. Now. When I married my wife Rebecca she was a very beautiful woman who had many suitors. But when I married her those guys that were interested in her didn’t like me anymore. They hated me and girls that were interested in me didn’t like her anymore and that’s the way it is with Jesus we have an encounter with him things change. We come out of the world she come out of the single life we come out of the world and then the world hates us because we’re not part of that anymore second Timothy 3:12 says all that live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution so here’s two reasons when we have an encounter with Jesus to follow him and when we live godly in this present world people are going to mistreat us. And so these are two of the reasons. Christians get persecuted biblical reasons John 15:16 says you have not chosen me but I have chosen you and I’ve ordained appointed you that you should go and bear fruit and that your fruit should remain you’re not up and down you’re not in God and backslidden the next day you remain steadfast and you produce fruit those are the Bible.
Why does the world hate followers of Jesus?

John 15:19-20: If you were of the world, the world would love its own. Yet because you are not of the world, but I chose you out of the world, therefore the world hates you. Remember the word that I said to you, ‘A servant is not greater than his master.’ If they persecuted Me, they will also persecute you. If they kept My word, they will keep yours also. 2 Timothy 3:12: Yes, and all who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution. John 15:16: You did not choose Me, but I chose you and appointed you that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain, that whatever you ask the Father in My name He may give you.
When is persecution profitable, and why was John the Baptist martyred?

He says there is no profit in being persecuted for doing wrong, only for doing good and following Jesus. He says John the Baptist was martyred because he told the king, from Leviticus 20:21, that it was not lawful to have his brother’s wife; he told civil government that laws needed to be moral and it cost him his head.
When is persecution profitable, and why was John the Baptist martyred?

Accepted reasons for persecution when you do wrong and persecuted the Bible says what profit is in that it’s when you do good and when you follow me and you’re persecuted then there’s profit in it so we’re going to look at some recorded Bible martyrs and persecutions. John the Baptist Jesus Stephen and James were all martyred James in 44 A.D. Paul Peter John the apostles and the church which were scattered they fleed the persecution were all persecuted now why was John martyred in Mark 6:18 he told Herod the king the government of the land it’s not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife quoting out of Leviticus 20:21 if a man takes his brother’s wife it’s an unclean thing and John told civil government.
When is persecution profitable, and why was John the Baptist martyred?

1 Peter 2:20: For what credit is it if, when you are beaten for your faults, you take it patiently? But when you do good and suffer, if you take it patiently, this is commendable before God. Mark 6:18: Because John had said to Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.” Leviticus 20:21: If a man takes his brother’s wife, it is an unclean thing. He has uncovered his brother’s nakedness. They shall be childless.
Why were Jesus and Stephen killed?

He says Jesus was martyred for the same reason: he spoke publicly and morally challenged people, “unless you repent you will all likewise perish.” Stephen was killed for his speech to the religious leaders in Acts 7:51. He gives three motives for persecution: speaking Bible morality, choosing to follow Jesus, and living Bible morality, which exposes you as a Christian.
Why were Jesus and Stephen killed?

That they needed. To be moral and that laws needed to be moral and it cost him his head he was martyred for it why was Jesus martyred. Same reason John was martyred he spoke. Publicly and morally challenged the public unless you repent you will all likewise perish in Luke 13:3 you scribes Pharisees hypocrites you make a proselyte two times the child of hell as yourself you’re making religious members going to hell like you are Matthew 23:15. John 8:44 you are of your father the Devil because his lust you desire to do that’s the way Jesus spoke and they didn’t like it and they killed him. Why was Stephen martyred. Because of his speech to religious people he was brought before the Sanhedrin and those that were there the Jewish leaders he says you are a stubborn. Generation and uncircumcised in heart and ears Acts 7:51. You resist the Holy Ghost as your fathers did you’re just like your your predecessors persecuting and killing the prophets of Jesus the just one whom you betrayed and murdered and you received the law and you have not kept it and they got mad. By his speech and killed him so three spiritual motives for persecutions and martyrdom the Bible. Speaking morally about the Bible to people and to civil religious leaders choosing Jesus have an encounter with him to follow him is the second one speech is the top one they’re going to hate you and persecute you for that when you start talking and living Bible morality living Bible morality exposes your belief in the first two it’s like the Nazis in the World War II when they come up to a person they thought was a Jew a young man and he says no I’m not a Jew they would say well take down your pants and when he took down his pants if he was circumcised they knew he was a Jew.
Why were Jesus and Stephen killed?

Luke 13:3: I tell you, no; but unless you repent you will all likewise perish. Matthew 23:15: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you travel land and sea to win one proselyte, and when he is won, you make him twice as much a son of hell as yourselves. John 8:44: You are of your father the devil, and the desires of your father you want to do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and does not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks from his own resources, for he is a liar and the father of it. Acts 7:51-52: “You stiff-necked and uncircumcised in heart and ears! You always resist the Holy Spirit; as your fathers did, so do you. Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? And they killed those who foretold the coming of the Just One, of whom you now have become the betrayers and murderers,
How were the apostles and early Christians martyred?

He says Christians are exposed when they live morally. From Foxe’s Book of Martyrs he lists apostles and early believers who were crucified, beheaded, stoned, hanged, cut to pieces or exiled, as Jesus predicted.
How were the apostles and early Christians martyred?

See Christians. Are exposed. When they live morally you can’t hide the fact that you’re a Christian. Early church martyrs as Jesus predicted. Taken from Foxe’s Book of Martyrs. Those crucified were Peter in 68 A.D. they crucified him upside down. Jude. Was crucified in 76 A.D. Bartholomew. Simeon. Philip. Philip was crucified in 54 A.D. and Andrew. Who was killed by the [unclear]. And beheaded there are crucified there and those beheaded were Paul in 68 A.D. by Nero the emperor of Rome. Matthias was beheaded. They stoned him and then they beheaded him in Jerusalem he never left Jerusalem he was there preaching the gospel. Other means such as hanging quartering where they pull you apart. Stoning. Thomas. He died in Asia. Uh by [unclear] India’s pagan priest Luke was hanged by the pagan priests of Greece Matthew in 60 A.D. was cut into was pieces with a axe blade. Uh Barnabas in 73 A.D. was killed. James the author of the book of James was stoned by the Jews at age 94.
What does the story of the young martyr in the arena teach?

He tells of a 22-year-old new believer with a nursing infant whose father and husband urged her to renounce Christ; she would not, and was given to the wild beasts. He says she put modesty before her pain and wanted to die looking noble for Jesus Christ, though she was simply persecuted for believing in Christ.
What does the story of the young martyr in the arena teach?

Mark was dragged to pieces in Alexandria Egypt John was tarred and feathered and exiled to Patmos and Perpetua. Was a 22 year old lady that just got saved was going to catechism they raided the catechism in 2003 A.D. and they arrested her and some other ones to re study in the Bible she’s a young believer she’s got an infant child on the breast being breast fed she’s married she’s got an old aging father they beat her father her father tried to get her to renounce Christ her husband tried to get her to renounce Christ they took her baby away from her trying to get her to renounce Christ and she wouldn’t do it and they gave her to the wild beast in the arena as an amusement. For all these people to see. And when the beast attacked her they tore off her clothes and she grabbed him quickly and covered herself putting modesty before her pain she even put her hair back up after the beast attacked her because she didn’t want to die looking like one of the pagans who had given up she wanted to die looking noble for Jesus Christ very powerful story. And many nobodies like her see she wasn’t preaching the gospel she didn’t have time to live morally she just believed in Christ and was persecuted for it pagans persecuted and martyred Christians Persians which is Iraq and Iran today East German Goths and Vandals Africa India Muslims and the Catholic Inquisition from 1184 to 1800 A.D. for simply saying you believe the Bible is the only source of God’s truth.
Why did the Inquisition and later Protestants persecute people?

He says the Inquisition persecuted people for saying the Bible is the only source of God’s truth and rejecting the mass, penance, indulgences and the pope as God on earth. He says Protestants then persecuted Catholics, other Protestants and pagans over sacraments and baptisms, not for godly living but because they did not agree with one another.
Why did the Inquisition and later Protestants persecute people?

The cup and bread is not Jesus’s body and blood. Nor is penance necessary Jesus paid the price I don’t have to do anything to be forgiven except believe in him and confess my sin rejecting idols rejecting the pope as God on earth rejecting mass because it didn’t profit anything and indulgences would you do something to get forgiveness of sin if you said you read the Bible and if you said you were a Protestant. The Inquisition. Would come and question you and kill you take your property. And persecute your family after you. But then the Protestants turned around and did what the Catholics did to them they persecuted Protestants and Catholics and pagans. And they persecuted him over sacraments over baptisms water baptism Holy Spirit baptism baptism in the body of Christ infant baptism. They persecuted Catholics because they were afraid the pope’s authority over the civil. Nation and the church would destroy the nation and bring persecution and so they persecuted Catholics for believing that and follow it. And then they just persecuted for having different doctrines they weren’t persecuted for godly moral living for moral preaching or believing in and following Jesus it was simply they were persecuting one another because they didn’t agree with one another. Now. Why were these in modern day.
Why are Christians martyred in modern times?

He says the Christians in the picture of men about to be beheaded were not killed for preaching or for perfect moral lives; they were killed because they believed in and followed Jesus and would not deny him and become Muslim. He says communist nations have killed and mistreated Christians for decades.
Why are Christians martyred in modern times?

Times our time why were these Christians martyred we’ve all seen this picture these men were simply Christians they’re going to cut their heads off. In this nation you couldn’t preach. Bible morality or Jesus so it wasn’t because they were preaching it was against the law. And it wasn’t necessarily because they were living perfect moral lives they they weren’t. Killing them for that reason they just simply killed him because they believed in and followed Jesus they had an encounter with Jesus they would not deny Jesus and become a Muslim if they would have denied Christ and become a Muslim and accepted Allah they would have saved their life. But they weren’t preaching it was against the law and they weren’t arrested for their moral lifestyle they were simply arrested and butchered because they believed antichrist communist humanist Russia China North Korea Cambodia and other communist nations have killed and forbid and mistreated Christians.
How are American Christians mistreated, and what should they do?

He says American Christians who speak for Bible morals are hated and bullied, pressured to accept legalized sin and forced to pay for others’ risky lifestyles and the national debt. He quotes that the Constitution was made only for a moral and religious people, and says Christians need to flee the public opinion that legalizes sin and join a group that embraces morality: “when America is good America is great.”
How are American Christians mistreated, and what should they do?

For decades. The United States government embraces these nations and these Muslim nations. Who have committed tremendous atrocities not only against Christians but other people as well American Christians who speak for Bible morals and Bible moral laws are hated and bullied and mistreated by opponents and unlearned believers. Who believe these things that the humanist and atheists and liberals are telling us American Christians are bullied to accept legalization of homosexuality abortion drugs alcohol pornography illegal aliens military sex abuse and chaplain abuse they are forced to pay for the welfare and the high cost of health care of risky lifestyles and they’re forced to pay off our national debt which they don’t believe in. John Adams said it plainly our constitution was made only for a moral religious people it is wholly inadequate to the government of any other. Our government now legalizing evil instead of God is going to bring down the fall of America. And because of that American Christians need to flee this public opinion of of legalizing sin and legalizing crime and legalize immorality they need to flee it and embrace. Get in a group that embraces morality and get America back to being great because America is good when America is good America is great.
Does persecution start in your own family?
He says it starts in their own family: the more you want to serve God and do what is right, the more people want to separate from you, and your friends change.
Will wisdom be restored in the church?
From Daniel 12 he says the wicked shall not understand but the wise shall understand, so there is going to be a restoration of wisdom.
Are wars and earthquakes signs of the end?
He says many end time prophets focus on wars, earthquakes, famines and plagues, but Jesus said that is not a sign of the end; it is just going to happen.
What are two biblical reasons Christians are persecuted?
He says when we have an encounter with Jesus to follow him, and when we live godly in this present world, people are going to mistreat us.
What is the top reason Christians are persecuted?
He says speech is the top one: when you start talking about and living Bible morality, they are going to hate you and persecute you.
Can Christians hide that they are Christians?
He says Christians are exposed when they live morally; you cannot hide the fact that you are a Christian.
For what beliefs did the Inquisition persecute people?

He says people were persecuted for saying the Bible is the only source of God’s truth, the cup and bread are not Jesus’ body and blood, penance is not necessary, and for rejecting idols, the mass and indulgences.
He says Protestants turned around and did what had been done to them, persecuting Catholics, Protestants and pagans over sacraments and baptisms and different doctrines.
He says they need to flee the public opinion of legalizing sin, crime and immorality, get in a group that embraces morality, and get America back to being great.

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Isaiah 43 that God’s people are victorious in afflictions because God created, formed, redeemed and called them by name, and will be with them in the waters…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Isaiah 43 that God’s people are victorious in afflictions because God created, formed, redeemed and called them by name, and will be with them in the waters and the fire. He ties the waters to baptism, teaches that grace says no to ungodliness, and warns that living for Christ brings conflict. He ends with the hindrances to victory (not calling on God, impatience, forgotten offerings) and the invitation to “state your case” to God.
Why are God’s people victorious in afflictions?

He goes to Isaiah 43:1–3 and says God “directly makes four statements himself that explain, totally explain, why Christians are victorious in afflictions.” He defines afflictions as “misery, pain,” and says they can come through sickness, poverty, persecution, acts of war, acts of God, or be self-inflicted.
Why are God’s people victorious in afflictions?

Isaiah 18. Why God’s people are victorious in afflictions. We’re going to go to Isaiah chapter 43, verses 1 through 3, and we’re going to see there that God makes four statements. He directly makes four statements himself that explain, totally explain, why Christians are victorious in afflictions. Afflictions is misery, pain. And in the Bible, afflictions can come through sickness, poverty, persecution, acts of war, acts of God, or self-inflicted. How many you know, a lot of us go through our own afflictions, we self-inflict them. And so, but God’s people are going to be victorious in these things. Verse 1.
Why are God’s people victorious in afflictions?

Isaiah 43:1-3: But now, thus says the LORD, who created you, O Jacob, And He who formed you, O Israel: “Fear not, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by your name; You are Mine. When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; And through the rivers, they shall not overflow you. When you walk through the fire, you shall not be burned, Nor shall the flame scorch you. For I am the LORD your God, The Holy One of Israel, your Savior; I gave Egypt for your ransom, Ethiopia and Seba in your place.
What does it mean that God created and formed you?

He says the first statement, “created and formed you,” is in the New Testament “being born again”: “God personally comes to us when we come to him, and he births us by the Spirit and by the word.” He says Jesus is forming us into “the likeness, the character of Jesus Christ,” and “therefore we can handle afflictions.”
What does it mean that God created and formed you?

Number one, “Thus saith the Lord who,” number one, “created and formed you.” I created you. In the New Testament we call it being born again. “Anyone in Christ,” if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creature, a new creation, “all things are passed away, all things are made new.” Why? Because God personally comes to us when we come to him, and he births us by the Spirit and by the word, and we become a new creature, and therefore we can be victorious in afflictions. In Galatians 4:19, “I labor in birth again till Christ is formed in you.” You see, Jesus is forming us, and the Bible says in Corinthians that we come into the same image of Christ. “By the Spirit of the Lord” we are changed, transformed, metamorphosed into the same image of Christ. See, he’s fashioning us into his image, not your pastors, not the great mighty man of God in the earth, but we are fashioned unto the likeness, the character of Jesus Christ. And so therefore we can handle afflictions when they come, pain and poverty, whatever, whatever faces us, we can handle it, be victorious, because he, number one, has created us, and he, number two, has fashioned us and formed us. Then he says the second reason is, “Fear not.” Don’t be afraid, “for I have redeemed you.” Now I remember when I first read the Bible through, and I came to Isaiah, I understood a little bit about chapter one, I didn’t understand beans till I got to Hezekiah
What does it mean that God created and formed you?

2 Corinthians 5:17: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new. Galatians 4:19: My little children, for whom I labor in birth again until Christ is formed in you, 2 Corinthians 3:18: But we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, just as by the Spirit of the Lord.
What does it mean that God redeemed you and called you by name?

He says “I’ve purchased you,” and compares it to taking care of a car you bought: “we’re his property.” He says God “personally called you by my name,” so “Satan is not my problem… I belong to Jesus, and nobody’s big enough to mess with him.”
What does it mean that God redeemed you and called you by name?

and the 185,000 getting killed, because I already read that in the book of Kings. But when I came to chapter 43, I understood that I needed this. I was going through things that I needed answers for, and this part of Isaiah just exploded to me. And uh, one of the things here, he not only formed us and created us, but he says, “Don’t be afraid, Dave. Don’t be afraid, church. I’ve redeemed you.” I’ve purchased you. Anyone that purchases something, when you purchase a car, you take care of it because it’s an investment for you. You purchase a gun, you take care of it, it’s an investment. You don’t lay it out in the rain, let it rust, and all that. You know, you take care of things. So God’s going to want to take care of us, he’s purchased us, we’re his property. Amen. And that just really just ignited my, my spiritual growth when I was younger. “I have called you,” number three, “by your name. You are mine.” He, again, “I’ve redeemed you, you belong to me, you’re my property, and I have personally come to you, Dave Kincer, and revealed myself to you, drawn you to me. I personally called you by my name, Dave Kincer, come, come over to the kingdom of light.” Aren’t you glad God’s a personal God? Hallelujah. Yes, I belong to him. Satan is not my problem, the kingdom of darkness is not my problem, I belong to Jesus, and nobody’s big enough to mess with him. Number four, “When you pass through the waters I will be with you, and through the rivers they shall not overflow you.” And this is what was happening in my first year of, of salvation. I was struggling
What does it mean that God redeemed you and called you by name?
Isaiah 43:1: But now, thus says the LORD, who created you, O Jacob, And He who formed you, O Israel: “Fear not, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by your name; You are Mine.
Does baptism have anything to do with salvation?

He reads 1 Peter 3:20–21 and asks, “How can you tell me that baptism has nothing to do with salvation?” He says “water baptism is just as important as the sinner’s prayer,” that “people will defend their denominational doctrine above scriptural truth,” and that for him baptism was “my signature on the contract.”
Does baptism have anything to do with salvation?

a lot of times because I didn’t understand things, and a lot of times because people didn’t want anything to do with me, uh, my old friends. After I changed, they left me, and I had to learn to let them go, and it was painful, I didn’t want to lose friends, but I had to make a choice. I had to keep serving God. And so I needed, I needed this verse, this chapter in Isaiah to confirm and ignite me as I went through these things. The waters is talking about, 1 Peter 3:20, “In the days of Noah, eight souls were saved by water. The like figure, baptism, now saves us, not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God by the resurrection of Jesus Christ.” Now, when I was in China, I asked a lot of questions, and one of the questions I asked is how quick someone should be baptized, and over there they waited six months to a year to baptize them. Folks, that is not Bible. And a lot of people teach that baptism has nothing to do with salvation. This verse tells you different. Let’s read it again. “In the days of Noah, eight souls were saved by,” what? Water. “In like model and like example, baptism. Water baptism now,” what? “Now saves us.” How can you tell me that baptism has nothing to do with salvation? Did John the Baptist say, “Repent and be baptized for the remission of sin”? Were there two things that needed to be done? Yes. Jesus, when he came along, did he say, “Repent and be baptized for the remission of sin”? Two things had to be done, and he added one thing to it: “I believe the gospel.” Do we need to believe the gospel, trust in the gospel? Yes. You see, people will defend their denominational doctrine above scriptural truth. And so, and water baptism is just as important as the sinner’s prayer. You ask God to repent, and then you get baptized, bam. And so I had a big debate with him all the time over there about water baptism. I said, “You’re robbing the people. You are robbing the people with your ignorance of the Scripture. Baptism is a powerful work.” Now, in this scripture he’s talking about “not the putting away the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God by the resurrection of Christ.” He’s talking about coming out of the water, the resurrection of Christ, we have a good conscience. And see, I understood as a young Christian that water baptism was my signature on the contract, and Jesus’s signature on the contract, the new covenant. And so when I went through anything, I could go back to my baptism and I could say, “No, God’s going to finish the good work he began in me. God’s gonna, he’s gonna keep forgiving me, he’s going to keep cleansing me, I am going to make it, because I’ve been water baptized, I put my signature on the contract, and he always keeps his word.” Can I hear an amen? Water baptism is very important.
Does baptism have anything to do with salvation?

1 Peter 3:20-21: who formerly were disobedient, when once the Divine longsuffering waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was being prepared, in which a few, that is, eight souls, were saved through water. There is also an antitype which now saves us—baptism (not the removal of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God), through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
What do the Red Sea and the Jordan teach about baptism and deliverance?

He says the “waters” are the Red Sea and the “rivers” the Jordan, and “both baptisms delivered them from the affliction.” He says “passing through the Red Sea is a model of water baptism,” and “if you haven’t been baptized, I’d get baptized next Sunday.”
What do the Red Sea and the Jordan teach about baptism and deliverance?

And that first year I was going through a struggle, Mike hit it last week, well, you know, the king of Egypt could come after, and he didn’t want him serving God even after he’d let him go, he still was after his people. And that’s what Satan did. “You had nothing really happened, you weren’t really born again, you know, you’re just making a fool out of yourself.” How many went through that as a young Christian? Man, I don’t believe that. I don’t believe that only a few of us went through that. I know this book, and I know Satan, how he works. Now, the waters, of course, is talking about the Red Sea here, in Isaiah. Egypt was after them, they were afflicted in Egypt, okay, and “through the rivers” is talking about the river of Jordan, 40 years later they had to go through the river of Jordan. The Red Sea parted and they went through it, river of Jordan piled up in heaps in the north until Israel got across, and they were afflicted by the wilderness, and see, both baptisms delivered them from the affliction and the pain of what they had been going through. Are you there? Hallelujah. And so I learned that. You know, these afflictions, they’re going to be, but God is going to deliver me out of every one of them, and I learned this in Isaiah, and then I found it all through the Scriptures. 1 Corinthians 10:1-2, “Our fathers were under the cloud, they passed through the Red Sea and were all baptized.” See, passing through the Red Sea is a model of water baptism. Noah’s judgment of water was an example of water baptism. Are you there? Water baptism is very important, and people that don’t get immediately baptized, they’re just missing it, and people that don’t believe that you need to get baptized as part of your salvation plan, they are just wrong. So if you haven’t been baptized, I’d get baptized next Sunday. I’m serious. The thing that helped me, an old man in the Assembly God church led me to Christ, and he knew how to do it, took me right through the Scriptures. I knew what was happening, the power of God through the word that he was bringing to me and making me read delivered me. I got, say, I got born again that night, that load of sin went off of me that I didn’t even know I had. I didn’t know I had a burden of sin, it was gone. He said, “Son, you got to get baptized next Sunday.” “Well, okay, whatever.” What’s next? Whatever. The first thing was good, second thing, huh, whatever. I didn’t even, they didn’t even, they didn’t tell me what a baptism was. I tell people what baptism is so they understand. I got in that baptismal pool and the power of God came all over me, the presence of God just flooded me, but they didn’t teach, you know, other than tongue, some kind of, they didn’t teach you about the power and the presence of God. But see, they came under the cloud, that’s the presence of God, and through the sea, the waters, the water baptism. The presence of God in water baptism is a powerful thing, church. And the Red Sea parting, the Bible says, was a model of water baptism. Hallelujah. And if nothing today, get your baptism doctrine right. You know, we pass on error to other people, we read error and we pass on error without really finding out and experiencing these powers in God, these principles. So, I’m delivered from the afflictions of sin. See,
What do the Red Sea and the Jordan teach about baptism and deliverance?

Isaiah 43:2: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; And through the rivers, they shall not overflow you. When you walk through the fire, you shall not be burned, Nor shall the flame scorch you. 1 Corinthians 10:1-2: Moreover, brethren, I do not want you to be unaware that all our fathers were under the cloud, all passed through the sea, all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea,
How does Jesus bring us out of the “furnace” of affliction?

He says Pharaoh was Israel’s slave master and “sin is also a slave master,” and “Jesus comes and delivers us from those slave masters.” He says the iron furnace in Deuteronomy 4:20 is Egypt, and “we can be victorious through afflictions because he created us, he formed us, he called us by our name.”
How does Jesus bring us out of the “furnace” of affliction?

Pharaoh, see, was the master, the slave master of Israel, afflicting them. They’re going through afflictions and pain and misery. Sin is also a slave master, and Jesus comes and delivers us from those slave masters, and part of it is not just being born again but being baptized. It’s a package. Could I hear an amen? “Let God be true and every man a liar.” Yeah, we need to get back to the Bible. All right, now, “When you walk through the fire you shall not be burned, neither shall the flame kindle upon you, for I am the Lord thy God.” Okay, now, Deuteronomy 4:20, “The Lord brought you out of the iron furnace.” Out of where? Who is the iron furnace? Egypt. You see, that 400 years of affliction, that slave masters’ control over their life. He said, “I brought you out of the iron furnace,” a furnace is a place where there is a fire, right? “And I brought you out to be my people and my inheritance.” Isaiah 43:10, “Behold, I have,” 48:10, “Behold, I have refined you, but not as silver. I have tested you in the furnace of,” what? Affliction. So the furnace of affliction was this furnace in Egypt. Who had them in slavery? Who were making their lives miserable and caused them to call upon God to deliver them? So plainly he’s talking about the afflictions of God’s people. Amen. And we can be victorious through afflictions because he created us, he formed us, he called us by our name specifically, and he gets us through these things, he redeemed us, we’re his property, and we’re going to get through these afflictions. I don’t care if it’s financial, physical, spiritual, mental, emotional, you’re going to get through, and you’re going to be victorious. Is that a good amen? Yes. And that just changed my life that day when I hit this verse. I didn’t understand the rest of it before that, but I sure got this one, and it really came at a good time in my life. Now,
How does Jesus bring us out of the “furnace” of affliction?

Deuteronomy 4:20: But the LORD has taken you and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be His people, an inheritance, as you are this day. Isaiah 48:10: Behold, I have refined you, but not as silver; I have tested you in the furnace of affliction.
Does believing in Jesus mean nothing bad will happen to you?

He says people told him “nothing’s going to happen to you,” but “a couple of weeks after being saved I had more problems than I’d ever had before.” He cites 1 Thessalonians 3:3, “we are appointed to this,” and Psalm 34:19, “Many are the afflictions of the righteous,” and says Paul testified “God delivered me.”
Does believing in Jesus mean nothing bad will happen to you?

1 Thessalonians 3:3, “No one should be shaken by these afflictions. You know that we are appointed to this.” We’re appointed to what? Afflictions. We’re appointed to what? Afflictions. Now, when I got saved, everybody was saying, “If you believe in Jesus, nothing’s going to happen to you. You’re going to roller skate right into him. You’re going to skate through life, no problem.” You know, a couple of weeks after being saved, I had more problems than I’d ever had before, because now I see who I really am. Are you there? I didn’t know I was so bad. I wasn’t murdering people and committing adultery and, uh, you know, joining gangs and all that, but you’re still bad. “There’s none righteous, no, not one.” You come into his life, man, I got a lot of changing to do. Isn’t that right? And see, if we really get born again, we get into this thing, this is exactly how it works. You just join a church, you don’t know beans, you just say a little mechanical sinner’s prayer, you got nothing, born again. Don’t ever laugh at it, people laugh at it, don’t let them laugh at it. That’s how we become a new creature. And I don’t care if you’re a Catholic, a Baptist, a Pentecostal, a Lutheran, a Jew, I don’t care what you are, you get born again, you’re going to become a new creature, old things are going to pass away and all things are going to [unclear], got nothing to do with denominationalism. Can I hear an amen? Thank you. Psalm 34:19, “Many are the afflictions of the righteous.” How many? Many. Man, they were teaching me wrong back there, the faith camp. They were just totally out of it. “You’re going to prosper and everything’s going to be, nothing bad is going to happen.” The other, read the life of Jesus. Did bad things happen to him? Do you ever read the life of the twelve apostles? Did bad things happen to them? Yeah. Were they afflicted? Yes. Paul said God delivered me out of all my affliction, and he lists them. I had, I had afflictions with, with robbers, that affliction with countrymen, I was, I was stoned twice, and I was, you know, been in jail and beaten in prison. He had all kinds of afflictions, but Paul said God delivered me. How? Out of how many? All of them. And you live for Christ and you really preach the gospel, and people will afflict you because you are a threat to them. They want to justify their low level of Christianity as a high level, and you get to a high level, they don’t like you because you exposed them.
Does believing in Jesus mean nothing bad will happen to you?

1 Thessalonians 3:3: that no one should be shaken by these afflictions; for you yourselves know that we are appointed to this. Psalm 34:19: Many are the afflictions of the righteous, But the LORD delivers him out of them all.
Why does living for Christ bring conflict with others?

He says if you live your life for Christ, “you’re going to be in conflict with those who don’t,” including believers who do not pursue righteousness. He cites 2 Thessalonians 1:6, “It is a righteous thing with God to repay with tribulation those who trouble you,” and says “Don’t mess with the church.”
Why does living for Christ bring conflict with others?

Are you there? Conflicts. Now he’s going to deal with conflicts. Two conflicts here: conflicts of right and wrong, and the conflicts of right people doing wrong, contradictory. Isaiah 43:3, [unclear], “I gave Egypt for your ransom.” I gave Ethiopia, the nation just below Egypt, for your [unclear], and Seba, a province next to Egypt in Ethiopia, for your [unclear]. And remember, Moses married an Ethiopian woman when he was down in Egypt, so Ethiopians were prominent in Egypt, they were right next door, and they came over and they were part of the Egyptian population. Do you understand that? Okay. Did God destroy Egypt? Did it kill a lot of people? Did he kill a lot of Egyptians? Yes, he did. “I will give men for you and people for your life.” Hallelujah. 2 Thessalonians 1:6, “It is a righteous thing with God to repay with tribulation those who trouble you.” Wow. Don’t mess with the church. The church that follows and pursues righteousness, not just a believer, and, and in China we met all kinds of people. We may have disagreements in other doctrines, but every one of them, Mr. [unclear] can attest to this, had that pursuit of righteousness. They had the high mark plan, and it was beautiful, right, Mr. [unclear]? It was beautiful. You know, we don’t have to agree on every jot and tittle, but we need to agree on Jesus Christ saving us from his sins, making us new creatures, and we pursue righteousness. Amen, that’s the thing. Now, he goes on to say in Proverbs 28:4, “Those who forsake the law praise the wicked, but to keep the law oppose them.” You say, “You don’t have to go out and witness door-to-door or anything.” That we need to, don’t get me wrong, but if you live your life for Christ, you’re going to be in conflict with those who don’t. You’re going to be in opposition, and I’m talking about believers also. Believers who don’t pursue the high mark of the calling of God, to love Jesus, which is keeping his commandments, doing right, they’re going to be in conflict with you. And so you live your life, you’re going to, all you have to do is go through the day, live in your life for Christ, and you’re going to be at war with the enemy. Isn’t that beautiful? Hallelujah. Yeah, you may be too timid, like me, to share Christ with anybody. I broke that within a year, but, but you know, just living, just making that decision for Christ, you’re in conflict with people. Ah. Now, in Noah’s day, did God destroy the whole earth and save Noah? Did he give people that Noah might live? Are you out there? Okay. Job, was he afflicted? Yeah. Lot, did God destroy Sodom and Gomorrah, kill all the inhabitants, babies, children, everyone
Why does living for Christ bring conflict with others?

Isaiah 43:3-4: For I am the LORD your God, The Holy One of Israel, your Savior; I gave Egypt for your ransom, Ethiopia and Seba in your place. Since you were precious in My sight, You have been honored, And I have loved you; Therefore I will give men for you, And people for your life. 2 Thessalonians 1:6: since it is a righteous thing with God to repay with tribulation those who trouble you, Proverbs 28:4: Those who forsake the law praise the wicked, But such as keep the law contend with them.
Will God judge the world to defend his church?
