He says “there’s a time coming before Christ returns that this world is going to be shaken by the power of God and his jealousy for his church,” and “he’s going to show the world his church is glorious.” He points to Noah, Lot, the 185,000 Syrians, Herod and the sorcerer on Cyprus as places where God struck enemies and delivered his people.
Will God judge the world to defend his church?

and delivered Lot to live? Yeah. Are you understanding this scripture? I’m telling you, there’s a time coming before Christ returns that this world is going to be shaken by the power of God and his jealousy for his church. And Isaiah is making this very plain. That’s why Christ isn’t coming today, that’s why he isn’t coming tomorrow, that’s why he isn’t coming when these people predict it. They don’t know when he’s coming, but he’s going to manifest himself before he comes, and he’s going to show the world his church is glorious. Hallelujah. Amen. And the people who want to harden their heart and all that, they’re going to pay, they’re going to pay a price. Okay, did he slay 185,000 Syrians to deliver Jerusalem? Yes. Herod, did he smite Herod with worms? Yeah. Yeah. Did he smite the sorcerer on the island of Cyprus with blindness? Yes. Did he kill the Roman soldiers who had, was given the responsibility to watch Peter, and Peter was delivered by an angel? Were those soldiers killed? Church, we don’t have a skosh of an idea how much God loves us and what his [unclear] intention is for his [unclear]. But one day the world is going to have this. Hallelujah.
What does it mean to be God’s witnesses?

He reads Acts 1:8 and says “You shall be what? Witnesses. Proof that I’m real.” He says of speaking in tongues, “that’s not the proof,” and from 1 John 3:7 that “he who practices righteousness is” righteous. He explains “All born of God do not sin” to mean “you cannot flagrantly, habitually sin.”
What does it mean to be God’s witnesses?

Don’t mess with the church. The church that is pursuing righteousness, I don’t care if they’re Catholics, I don’t care if they’re Protestant, I don’t care if they’re a Jew, if they’re pursuing Jesus and righteousness, don’t mess with them. They may not believe everything you believe, but those two things are the priority things. Could that be an amen? No. Then he says, “You are my witnesses.” A witness is an evidence, a witness is a person that experienced the event, they’re the proof that someone’s guilty or someone’s innocent. And in Acts chapter 1, verse 8, “You shall receive power after the Holy Ghost has come upon you, and you shall be,” tongue-talkers. You shall be Baptists. You shall be Pentecostals. You shall be Catholics. It’s not there. Why do we put that word in there? You shall be what? Witnesses. Proof that I’m real, proof that I can do what I set out to do, you are my proof. Hallelujah. And I speak in tongues, but that’s not the proof. 1 John 3:7, “Don’t be deceived, he who practices righteousness is,” what? Righteous. Well, I’m righteous by the blood of Christ. Well, wonderful, but that doesn’t help your wife you’re beating up. That doesn’t help your kid that you break their arms when you spank them. That doesn’t help your family when you’re squandering the money gambling on sports and, and drugs and other things. Hey, so you’re righteous by the cross, what good does that do you or anybody? Can I hear an amen? “He who practices righteousness is,” what? Righteous. “All born of God do not sin, for his seed,” what is the seed? Okay, Jesus and the word, yes. Say, Jesus is in us, the word is in us, so he cannot sin because he’s been born of God. Now what that really means: you cannot flagrantly, habitually sin because you’ve got Christ and the word gnawing at you, convicting you, and you repent and you get up, you do not continue in sin. Why? Because you were really born of the Spirit, that Spirit of Jesus and that Spirit of the word, and yeah, you may not be perfect today, but you keep changing. Why? Because that birthing is real.
What does it mean to be God’s witnesses?

Isaiah 43:10: “You are My witnesses,” says the LORD, “And My servant whom I have chosen, That you may know and believe Me, And understand that I am He. Before Me there was no God formed, Nor shall there be after Me. Acts 1:8: But you shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you shall be witnesses to Me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.” 1 John 3:7: Little children, let no one deceive you. He who practices righteousness is righteous, just as He is righteous. 1 John 3:9: Whoever has been born of God does not sin, for His seed remains in him; and he cannot sin, because he has been born of God.
What does grace teach, according to Titus 2:11?

He quotes Titus 2:11, that grace “offers salvation to” all, and says “it’s not just divine favor, it’s divine enablement by keeping the word of God.” He says “Grace says no” to ungodliness and worldly passions and yes to self-control, so that we live “upright and godly lives in this present world.”
What does grace teach, according to Titus 2:11?

Amen. And you’re just joined the church, there’s no power, but when you join the Jesus and his word, there’s power. Be convicted and live for him. Is that a good amen, church? Titus 2:11, “The grace of God offers salvation to,” how many? All. I’m not saved by grace, I’m not saved by faith, I’m saved by grace through faith, not of works, that’s in [unclear] both, okay. These people say, “By grace” and “Saved by grace,” I get sick of them justifying their life using the word grace. Let’s look at grace, how the apostles used it. Grace offers salvation to all men, but it also teaches us. So does grace have a doctrine? Yeah, it’s not just divine favor, it’s divine enablement by keeping the word of God. Wow, that was good. Did you guys get that? See, grace has a [unclear]. That we say no to ungodliness and worldly passions, worldly desires. We say what? No. I’m not going to get drunk, I’m not going to take drugs, I’m not going to join a gang, I’m not going to beat up my spouse, I’m not going to, uh, not work and be lazy and not provide for my [unclear]. No, I’m not going to do those things. Grace says no. So when you say, “I’m saved by grace,” you have the power to say no. Hallelujah. Now, and to live self-control. Every man and every woman wants to marry someone with self-control. Instead of shooting off their mouth all the time and displaying their anger and all this stuff, you know, yelling and screaming in front of the kids, arguing, which is just stupid, it’s fools do that. I’m just pausing, let it sink into you. Self-control comes from grace, as well as the Holy Spirit, as well as the Bible. And self-control is just controlling yourself. Work, provide for your home, go to church, pay your tithes, worship God, seek God, raise your family, your kids, in the way they should go. You say, “Self-control.” “Upright and godly lives,” living right, living godly lives in this, what? Present age. Don’t give me this rapture stuff, don’t give me this any-minute-coming. Okay, you have a goal of God for him to bring you to a place where you live self-control, upright and godly lives in this present world, so that they see the light in you and come and inquire of your God and bring honor to Jesus Christ. And that’s much better than him coming a second time. Church, this present age he wants to bless your life, he wants you to make a difference now.
What does grace teach, according to Titus 2:11?

Titus 2:11-12: For the grace of God that brings salvation has appeared to all men, teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly in the present age,
What does he say Romans 1:25 means for the world today?

He reads Romans 1:25, “Who changed the truth of God into a lie,” and asks whether governments are “changing the truth of God into a lie right now through this homosexual acceptance.” He says in the New Testament “idolatry is greed,” applies that to welfare for illegal aliens, and quotes “If a man doesn’t work, neither let him eat.”
What does he say Romans 1:25 means for the world today?

Romans 1:25, “Who changed the truth of God into a lie, worshiping the creature,” the human being, “instead of the Creator.” Or the living animals, human beings, and as you know, they were talking about idols, making idols of birds of the air and animals and planets and all this, and they were talking about homosexuality, women with women, men with men. You see, they change what? The truth of God into a what? Lie. Is our Congress, are our governors, are our state legislatures changing the truth of God into a lie right now through this homosexual acceptance? Amen. Are they? Now, in the New Testament, idolatry is greed. I don’t know if you’re aware of that, but that’s what the New Testament says. Are by money turning the truth of God into a lie by giving the, the illegal aliens freedom to come in, giving them welfare, giving them food stamps, giving people two years or more of, of, of unemployment pay so they don’t have to work. That is idolatry. “If a man doesn’t work, neither let him eat.” See, you got to know, you’re about us Christians have got to know our Bible. It sounds so sympathetic, these little kids are coming across our border, “Oh my gosh, it’s the,” and I heard on Fox News that it’s the Christian duty to help people. I said, that’s also the Bible duty to punish criminals, as homosexuals. Isn’t that right? You can’t use the Bible in one area and then distort it in another area. That was good. Hallelujah. Now, who was full of grace and truth? Jesus, right? And you see, when we mess around with grace, we’re messing around with who Jesus is. When we mess around with truth, we’re messing with who Jesus is. And the same glory that Jesus has is the same glory the church has, and what is that? Grace that says no to ungodliness and worldly lust, and grace that says yes to self-control and living right.
What does he say Romans 1:25 means for the world today?

Romans 1:25: who exchanged the truth of God for the lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen. 2 Thessalonians 3:10: For even when we were with you, we commanded you this: If anyone will not work, neither shall he eat.
What does “You have not called upon me” mean as a hindrance to victory?

He lists this as the first hindrance, from Isaiah 43:22. He says “people go to church to be entertained in America,” while in poorer countries “they really pray,” and that “corporate prayer is important in the Bible.” He says lifting hands is “recognizing that there’s a higher power than us.”
What does “You have not called upon me” mean as a hindrance to victory?

Folks, that’s good, that should make it plain to you. Hallelujah. Then he repeats, “I will do a new thing, remember not the former things, I’ll make rivers in the desert to give to my people drink.” He repeats it, you can go to those lessons and learn that. “These people have I formed, fashioned for myself, they shall show forth my,” what? Praise. My honor, my boasting, and what is, how do we do that? By living right. Amen. And if we mess up, we, we repent, we get up, we keep going. Now, [unclear] he’s going to hit the hindrances to victory over afflictions. Number one, “You have not called upon me,” Isaiah 43:22 through 28. “You have not called upon me.” You know, people go to church to be entertained in America. People go to church in third world countries to exist, to survive. They don’t fake prayers, they really pray just for food, clothing, and shelter. See, they don’t have the abundance. They really worship Jesus, they’re genuine, they don’t stand there like a knot on a log, they worship Jesus because they need him and they love him. America is really, in a large portion of a Christian America, a big difference. A very big difference. They won’t call upon Jesus. They don’t have time for prayer in a service, they gotta be out so that the next crowd can come in, so there’s no time for prayer. Corporate prayer is important in the Bible. Amen. We won’t call on the Lord, we’re too proud to bend our knee, raise our hands, as the Bible says, “I would that men everywhere lift up holy hands without anger, without doubting.” Get the hands up. Amen. That’s giving recognition to a sovereign one. When we near, when we do these humiliating things, it’s recognizing that there’s a higher power than us, and that is Jesus Christ. Higher authority, we’re the peasants, he’s the power. Number two, “You’ve grown weary of me,” you’ve been weary of me, impatient with me. Isn’t that what Israel did in Egypt? They got impatient with God. Moses came down and they got impatient. Yeah, I know none of you this morning ever get impatient.
What does “You have not called upon me” mean as a hindrance to victory?

Isaiah 43:22-28: “But you have not called upon Me, O Jacob; And you have been weary of Me, O Israel. You have not brought Me the sheep for your burnt offerings, Nor have you honored Me with your sacrifices. I have not caused you to serve with grain offerings, Nor wearied you with incense. You have bought Me no sweet cane with money, Nor have you satisfied Me with the fat of your sacrifices; But you have burdened Me with your sins, You have wearied Me with your iniquities. “I, even I, am He who blots out your transgressions for My own sake; And I will not remember your sins. Put Me in remembrance; Let us contend together; State your case, that you may be acquitted. Your first father sinned, And your mediators have transgressed against Me. Therefore I will profane the princes of the sanctuary; I will give Jacob to the curse, And Israel to reproaches. 1 Timothy 2:8: I desire therefore that the men pray everywhere, lifting up holy hands, without wrath and doubting;
How do impatience with God and forgotten offerings hinder victory?

He says the second hindrance is impatience: “you get impatient with God,” and “we take matters in our own hands.” The third is “No burnt offering”: he says Jesus is our burnt offering, “the way into the presence of God is thanksgiving,” and “If you are a silent saint, you’re not a growing saint.”
How do impatience with God and forgotten offerings hinder victory?

I know you’re just perfect Christians. You don’t want to get impatient with your spouse, you get impatient with God. “God hasn’t changed him yet. God, how come you don’t straighten that spouse of mine out? I’ll do it for you, you [unclear], son of a [unclear].” When the Bible plainly says that bad words and good words don’t come out of the same fountain. That was good too. Hallelujah. There’s something wrong with the source when you do that, you understand? Hallelujah. So we get impatient, we get tired, and so we take matters in our own hands. If God wants to straighten my kids out, I’ll straighten them out. Burn them, I’ll stab them. I’ve dealt with burnt kids, stabbed kids, whatever. Beaten with a razor strap or whatever. Number three, “No burnt offering.” Now I mean, you know that in Leviticus, as I just read Leviticus this week, there’s five offerings. The burnt offering is the covering for sin, the meal offering is the remembrance, it’s the remembrance offering. There, you remember that the burnt offering covers your sin. Who’s our burnt offering? Jesus Christ. We don’t do animal sacrifices because he already did it. The meal offering reminds me that Jesus Christ still forgives, still cleanses and delivers from sin even though I’m saved. And then you had the thank offering, the peace offering. That’s where you just thank God, “Thank you, Lord.” “I will enter his gates with thanksgiving in my heart.” You see, the way into the presence of God is thanksgiving. Hebrews, the last chapter, says, “By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise,” that thank offering, that peace offering, and then explains what it is: “the fruit of our lips giving thanks unto God.” If you are a silent saint, you’re not a growing saint. You got to learn to lift up your lips. It’s a sacrifice, because you don’t want to do it. Man, it was humiliating when they said, you know, “Lift your hands and, and, you know, praise God.” Oh gosh, this guy died a thousand deaths. But I had to get to the place where I wanted God or I wanted myself. Then you have the sin offering and the trespass offering, the guilt offering. How many know your sins are forgiven? How many still get some guilt over sin? Yeah. See, God knew that, so he had a guilt offering. He comes and kills the guilt that you haven’t let go of from the sin offering. You still feel guilty. Hallelujah, isn’t that good? Yeah. “And honor me by sacrifices,” which is the peace offering, the fruit of our lips. Now, this is hindrances to victory over afflictions. We won’t humble ourself and call on God. We get impatient with God when we’re doing our own thing. And we forget the burnt offering, Jesus can cleanse us and forgive us, and the praise offering. You burden God with your sins, you’re accepting sin in your life. That’s a hindrance to victory over afflictions. But God comes and he said, this is powerful, church, this is so powerful: “State your case, state your cause, that you may be acquitted,” set free. He says, you know, you got sin in you, you’re impatient with me, you won’t call upon me, so just come and state your case.
How do impatience with God and forgotten offerings hinder victory?

Hebrews 13:15: Therefore by Him let us continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name. Psalm 100:4: Enter into His gates with thanksgiving, And into His courts with praise. Be thankful to Him, and bless His name.
What does it mean to “state your case” to God?

He reads “state your case, state your cause, that you may be acquitted,” and says “You got a complaint, don’t go to body members.” He tells of throwing down his guitar after a year without feeling God’s presence and listing what he was doing for God, and a still small voice said “It’s about time. You’re doing this all on your own strength,” after which peace and power came.
What does it mean to “state your case” to God?

All right, Moses stated his case. People, and all these people are, he stated his case, so what did God do? He came and gave himself the over 70 elders that caused him nothing but trouble for 40 years. And that’s what elders do in the church today, they are nothing but trouble if they are not a real elder, a Bible elder. They are nothing but trouble. They don’t have no spiritual growth to stand for righteousness and stand for truth at all, they just got a title. And that’s a good amen. Moses, when God wanted to destroy the people for sinning, he went and stated his case and said, “God, kill me instead of the people.” And what did God do? He saved the people. State your case. You got a complaint, don’t go to body members. We learned last Sunday that when we start [unclear] complaining, we’re on our way back to Egypt. That was good last Sunday. That’s a sign you’re on your way back to the old life. Go to Jesus and state your case, complain to him. I remember as a young man, I’ve used this before, I’d been saved about three or four years, and I was, man, I was ministering at the prisons, at the juvenile halls, on the street corners, door-to-door, I was doing all these things. I had my guitar, my banjo, I put in tune, I was ministering, really soon, you know, hallelujah. But almost a year went by and I had not felt the presence of God, and this day I had to go minister, and I’m getting songs together, and I know there’s nothing in the songs, I know there’s nothing in my message, I know there’s nothing, because I know when there’s something. And so I get mad at God. I threw my guitar down, broken, this was a thousand-dollar guitar back then. I mean, I was, I was stating my case like an idiot, but I was stating my case. And I went through the list, “Man, I’m saving souls, and I’m administering here, and I’m doing this, and I’m in the church, and I’m teaching Sunday school, and I’m leading the youth service, and I’m doing all this, and you’re not doing nothing.” That was my case. And that still small voice came to me and says, “It’s about time.” I said, “I quit, I quit.” He says, “It’s about time. You’re doing this all on your own strength, all in your own head knowledge. You left me back there. You need to get back with me.” And just the tremendous peace and power, God come on me, began to weep. See why? Because I stated my case, I complained to him, and he come and set me free from my own initiated affliction. Are you there, Jeff? So don’t complain to people. If you’ve got a complaint, go to him. He can set you free. Powerful. We, we, we’re in sin, and he’s going to free us from those sins, we’re impatient, and he’s going to free us from that impatience. Hallelujah. “Remember me, who blots out your sin, remember me.
What does it mean to “state your case” to God?
Isaiah 43:26: Put Me in remembrance; Let us contend together; State your case, that you may be acquitted.
What does he say to remember about God when we face afflictions?

He says “forget your pastor, forget your elders, forget the pope, forget the rabbis, remember who? Jesus Christ,” who can blot out your sin. He says God “created and formed you,” called you by name “so you don’t have to be afraid,” “he is not out to destroy you,” and “He will finish the good work he began in you.”
What does he say to remember about God when we face afflictions?

Don’t forget me.” Church, forget your pastor, forget your elders, forget the pope, forget the rabbis, remember who? Jesus Christ. “I can blot out your sin, I can do it.” Hallelujah. You know, we go through 12-step programs, seven-step programs, this kind of program, that kind of program, and Jesus is up in heaven’s, and, “Folks, remember me. I’m the one that can acquit you, I’m the one that can set you free, and I will if you state your case honestly before me. I will deliver you.” Remember, he can heal sicknesses, the physical sicknesses, the mental sicknesses, the emotional affliction. He can improve your poverty level. You can have peace in the middle of battles. Remember, God created and formed you, God is involved in this, he come to you personally and called you by name, so you don’t have to be afraid. He’s not out to destroy you. I don’t care how bad of a Christian you are, he is not out to destroy you. Do not be afraid. He will finish the good work he began in you. Be patient with yourself, be patient with others. He’s with us, and if he’s with us, we’ll get through anything. And for our charity, “I will deal with those that trouble you.” We may look like we’re losing the battle in America today, but there is coming a day of reckoning, and we want to be ready as righteous Christians in that day of reckoning. Amen. He will trouble those who trouble us, and we’ve got to state our case before God.
What does he say to remember about God when we face afflictions?

Isaiah 43:25: “I, even I, am He who blots out your transgressions for My own sake; And I will not remember your sins. Philippians 1:6: being confident of this very thing, that He who has begun a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ;
Why does he compare being redeemed to buying a car?
He says “when you purchase a car you take care of it because it’s an investment.” He concludes “God’s going to want to take care of us, he’s purchased us, we’re his property.”
What did he see in China about baptism?
He says “over there they waited six months to a year to baptize them. Folks, that is not Bible.” He says he asked a lot of questions about how quickly someone should be baptized.
Does he say John the Baptist and Jesus both said to repent and be baptized?
He asks, “Did John the Baptist say, ‘Repent and be baptized for the remission of sin’?” and says “Jesus, when he came along,” said the same, and “he added one thing to it,” to believe the gospel.
How does he say he came to Christ?
He says an old man in an Assembly God church led him to Christ, taking him “right through the Scriptures.” He says “that load of sin went off of me that I didn’t even know I had.”
What does he mean by “get your baptism doctrine right”?

He says “we pass on error to other people, we read error and we pass on error without really finding out and experiencing these powers in God.” He says the presence of God in water baptism “is a powerful thing.”
What does he say about people who just join a church and say a prayer?
He says “you just say a little mechanical sinner’s prayer, you got nothing,” and “That’s how we become a new creature” by being born again, whatever the denomination.
What does he say was wrong with what he was first taught about suffering?
He says “they were teaching me wrong back there, the faith camp,” who said “nothing bad is going to happen.” He points to the lives of Jesus and the twelve apostles, who were afflicted.
Does he say you must witness door-to-door to be in conflict with the world?
No. He says “all you have to do is go through the day, live in your life for Christ, and you’re going to be at war with the enemy.”
Was he timid about sharing Christ?
He says “you may be too timid, like me, to share Christ with anybody. I broke that within a year.”
Whom does he say not to mess with?
He says “if they’re pursuing Jesus and righteousness, don’t mess with them. They may not believe everything you believe, but those two things are the priority things.”
Does he say being righteous by the blood of Christ is enough?
He says someone may say “I’m righteous by the blood of Christ,” and answers “that doesn’t help your wife you’re beating up.” He says real birth from God means “you do not continue in sin.”
Where does he say self-control comes from?
He says “Self-control comes from grace, as well as the Holy Spirit, as well as the Bible,” and that “self-control is just controlling yourself.”
What does he say about living for God in the present age?
He says to live “so that they see the light in you and come and inquire of your God,” and that “he wants you to make a difference now.” He says that is “much better than him coming a second time.”
What does he say the guilt offering is for?
He says God knew some still feel guilt after forgiveness, “so he had a guilt offering. He comes and kills the guilt that you haven’t let go of from the sin offering.”
What does he list as the hindrances to victory over afflictions?
He says “We won’t humble ourself and call on God. We get impatient with God when we’re doing our own thing. And we forget the burnt offering.”

items.t: Was the U.S. Supreme Court Fully Right About Studying The Bible?
items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer reviews the 1980 Supreme Court line (quoting 1963) that the Bible may be used in studying history, civilization, ethics and comparative religion, then asks what the Court…
items.ser: Clarity on Crucial Choices · Full sermon
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer reviews the 1980 Supreme Court line (quoting 1963) that the Bible may be used in studying history, civilization, ethics and comparative religion, then asks what the Court missed: Jesus, eternal life, last-day judgment, the spirit world and true happiness. He applies 2 Peter’s “add to your faith” to civil crime, defines just government’s purpose, and cites midwives, Daniel, the apostles and John the Baptist as models for standing against unjust laws including Roe v. Wade and same-sex marriage.
What did the 1980 Supreme Court say about studying the Bible?

He says the 1980 decision, quoting 1963—two witnesses—declared the Bible may constitutionally be used in appropriate study of history, civilization, ethics (Bible morality), comparative religions, or the like.
What did the 1980 Supreme Court say about studying the Bible?

Today we’re going to ask this question: was the United States Supreme Court fully right about the constitutional right to study the Bible? We’re going to remind you of the 1980 Supreme Court decision that quoted from a 1963 Supreme Court decision—so thus two witnesses confirming. And this is what the Supreme Court said: the Bible may constitutionally be used in an appropriate study of history, civilization, ethics—what we know as morality, Bible morality—comparative religions, or the like. The Supreme Court thusly said it is constitutionally legal.
How does he say the Bible covers history, civilization and ethics?

He says Scripture records over 4,000 years from creation to 100 A.D., civilizations from pre-flood through Rome and Canaan’s peoples, and Bible morality summing Exodus through the prophets; comparative religion contrasts one holy God with sects and idolatry.
How does he say the Bible covers history, civilization and ethics?

History in the Bible: it’s true from creation to 100 A.D., or over 4,000 years of history. Civilization: the pre-flood civilizations to Abraham and the Hebrews, to the Assyrians, the Syrians, the Persians, the Greeks, the Roman Empire, and all the other civilizations that came with it—all the Canaanites and all the “-ites” in Canaan land. We have a recorded history of civilization. Ethics: as we have shown you, Bible morality sums up all the law—Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy and the prophets. Comparing religion: the Bible’s one holy God versus a sect, a group out of that group, and the doctrines of men which create sect groups in groups, and then idolatry,
What did the Court miss about Jesus?
From Luke 24:44 he says the Law, Prophets and Psalms concern Jesus—Exodus through Malachi and the Psalms wrote about Him—so Jesus is the first thing the Court’s list missed.
What did the Court miss about Jesus?

devils, the worship of devils, witchcraft, and animism—which is a spirit is in the rocks and the trees and everything—and even the evolutionists say that humans are part of nature. Now, what did the Supreme Court miss? See, they gave us these things, but what did they miss and just told us to deal with it? Well, Jesus, number one. And Luke 24:44: all things must be fulfilled which are written in the law of Moses and the prophets and the Psalms concerning Me. So Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Isaiah, Jeremiah down to Malachi and all the prophets in between wrote about Jesus, and 150 Psalms wrote about Jesus.
What did the Court miss about Jesus?

Luke 24:44: Then He said to them, “These are the words which I spoke to you while I was still with you, that all things must be fulfilled which were written in the Law of Moses and the Prophets and the Psalms concerning Me.”
What about eternal life and last-day judgment?

From John 5:39 he says the Scriptures testify of Jesus, the door to eternal life. From Matthew 12:36 and Revelation 20:12 he says idle words and works are recorded for judgment—the Court overlooked that.
What about eternal life and last-day judgment?

Eternal life. John 5:39: search the Scriptures, the Bible; in them you think you have eternal life, and they testify of Me. The Scriptures tell us about life after death. And you won’t come to Me that you might have life. So not only is there eternal life, but the door to eternal life is Jesus Christ. The last-day judgment they overlooked. Matthew 12:36: every idle word men shall speak they will give an account in the day of judgment—and thus just idle words. But in Revelation 20:12, at the great white throne judgment, they were judged according to their works, their behavior, written in the books. God’s keeping a record of our speech and of our behavior.
What about eternal life and last-day judgment?

John 5:39: You search the Scriptures, for in them you think you have eternal life; and these are they which testify of Me. Matthew 12:36: But I say to you that for every idle word men may speak, they will give account of it in the day of judgment. Revelation 20:12: And I saw the dead, small and great, standing before God, and books were opened. And another book was opened, which is the Book of Life. And the dead were judged according to their works, by the things which were written in the books.
Who judges, and what spirit world does the Bible describe?
John 5:22: the Father gives all judgment to the Son. He says the Court also missed God as Spirit, the Holy Spirit, ministering angels, cherubim and seraphim, demons and Satan.
Who judges, and what spirit world does the Bible describe?

In John 5:22, the Father judges no one but gives all judgment to the Son. So Jesus is what the Bible talks about. Jesus is the door to eternal life, and Jesus is the one we are going to have to give an account to of the words that we speak and the lifestyle that we lead. They also missed that the Bible talks about the spirit world. For instance, God is a Spirit, an invisible Spirit; the Holy Spirit is a Spirit; angels are ministering spirits; cherubim and seraphim are creatures of the spirit world; demons and Satan are spirits.
Who judges, and what spirit world does the Bible describe?
John 5:22: For the Father judges no one, but has committed all judgment to the Son,
What does the Bible say about happiness the Court missed?
From Psalm 144:15, happy is the people whose God is the Lord; John 16:22, joy no one can take; Acts 5:41, apostles rejoicing after being beaten—joy circumstances cannot take away.
What does the Bible say about happiness the Court missed?

Witchcraft: except for drugs and witchcraft of the flesh, the Bible says there’s three sources of witchcraft, but one of them source is demonic. The next thing they missed is happiness. Everybody is looking for happiness, and the Bible says in Psalms 144:15, happy is the people whose God is the Lord. John 16:22: Jesus summed it up and says your joy, your happiness, no one can take from you. That’s how powerful it is in the Bible. Acts 5:41: we have proof of that. The apostles were beaten, and after they were beaten they departed rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for His name. So we actually see a fulfillment of joy that people could not take away and circumstances could not take away.
What does the Bible say about happiness the Court missed?

Psalm 144:15: Happy are the people who are in such a state; Happy are the people whose God is the LORD! John 16:22: Therefore you now have sorrow; but I will see you again and your heart will rejoice, and your joy no one will take from you. Acts 5:41: So they departed from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for His name.
How does the Declaration tie to Bible happiness and escaping judgment?

He reads life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness as a right to Bible happiness, then says escaping the lake of fire means faith in Jesus, confessing sin, repenting, water baptism, and adding virtue to faith—even for humanists and atheists.
How does the Declaration tie to Bible happiness and escaping judgment?

Now the Declaration of Independence, by the way, gives us the right to Bible happiness. “We hold these truths to be self-evident, that all men were created equal,” and they were endowed by their Creator with certain unchangeable rights, and among these rights are life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness. Happy is the people whose God is the Lord—a joy that no situation and nobody can take away. Another thing they missed is how to escape the lake of fire judgment. We’ve told you this before: I believe and have faith in Jesus. You’ve got to admit you’re wrong, confess your sin, confess your crimes. You’ve got to repent and turn from those wrong. items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Isaiah 59:19 that the enemy comes in like a flood and the Spirit of the Lord lifts up a standard against him. He lists philosophies he says oppose God, then…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Isaiah 59:19 that the enemy comes in like a flood and the Spirit of the Lord lifts up a standard against him. He lists philosophies he says oppose God, then shows from Genesis and the flood that God makes a way of escape, and urges the church to warn people.
What does Isaiah 59:19 mean when the enemy comes in like a flood, and what defeats him?

He says there is “an enemy against God and an enemy against the Word,” and a flood “does nothing but damage.” He says the church is “trying to do this stuff on their own,” but the key to defeating the enemy is the Spirit: “the Spirit will lift up a standard against him.”
What does Isaiah 59:19 mean when the enemy comes in like a flood, and what defeats him?

We neglect, we disregard many priority doctrines, and one of these is Isaiah 59:19. Isaiah 59:19 says, “When the enemy comes in like a flood.” Number one, the enemy. We have an enemy. There is an enemy against God and an enemy against the Word, and when the enemy comes in like a flood (and all of us know a flood does nothing but damage; when you hear the word “flood,” you know there is damage, you know the water is out of control). Secondly, “the Spirit of the Lord will lift up a...” The Spirit of the Lord. Now, folks, this is where we’re missing it. The church is trying to do this stuff on their own. If we could have done it on our own, why we have needed Jesus? Why would we need the Holy Ghost? And it’s amazing, we start out right, we get saved and we start out right, and then we start leaning on ourself and on our own knowledge and understanding, but the key to defeating the enemy is what? And if you read, read, and you know the book and you don’t keep the book, what good does it do you? And “you read to assemble yourself even the more so as you see the day approaching,” and yet you can’t get up enough energy to even go to church and be a part of it. “Bring all the tithes into the storehouse,” and yet you cannot discipline your finances to put 10 cents of every dollar away for God. What good is it?
What destruction does Jesus save us from, and what must we do? (Matthew 13:40, 19:16-19, John 14:23)

Matthew 3:12: His winnowing fan is in His hand, and He will thoroughly clean out His threshing floor, and gather His wheat into the barn; but He will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.” Matthew 13:40: Therefore as the tares are gathered and burned in the fire, so it will be at the end of this age. Matthew 25:46: And these will go away into everlasting punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.” Matthew 19:16-19: Now behold, one came and said to Him, “Good Teacher, what good thing shall I do that I may have eternal life?” So He said to him, “Why do you call Me good? No one is good but One, that is, God. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.” He said to Him, “Which ones?” Jesus said, “‘You shall not murder,’ ‘You shall not commit adultery,’ ‘You shall not steal,’ ‘You shall not bear false witness,’ ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ ” John 14:23: Jesus answered and said to him, “If anyone loves Me, he will keep My word; and My Father will love him, and We will come to him and make Our home with him. Hebrews 10:25: not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as is the manner of some, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching. Malachi 3:10: Bring all the tithes into the storehouse, That there may be food in My house, And try Me now in this,” Says the LORD of hosts, “If I will not open for you the windows of heaven And pour out for you such blessing That there will not be room enough to receive it.
What does he say are our responsibilities, and what is the warning in the story of Lazarus and the rich man? (Luke 16)

He says our responsibility is to love and follow Jesus first: “I got to obey Jesus no matter what my pastor does.” From Luke 16 he says the rich man in torment wanted someone sent to “testify to my brothers… lest they too come into this place,” and he says “hell’s real.”
What does he say are our responsibilities, and what is the warning in the story of Lazarus and the rich man? (Luke 16)

See, our responsibility is to what? Love Jesus. Love our pastor? Yeah, but not like Jesus, not even the same degree, not even in the same ballpark. I’ve got to follow Jesus. I got to obey Jesus no matter what my pastor does. Is that correct? Yeah. Well, I got to love my husband. Yeah, but the way to love your husband is love that Man, Jesus, because He will shape you into being someone that can love when you’re not loved, without whining and crying, and behave in a manner that He wants to love you, and the same with a man. Are you there? Second thing, Luke 16:26. Let me have your attention. This is important. Lazarus died, and the angels carried him to heaven. The rich man died, and the demons carried him to hell, or, yeah, no angels. Uh, he was in hell. Somebody put him in hell, and in hell he lifted up his eyes and saw Lazarus afar off, up in heaven. Just, hallelujah, everything’s fine up there. And he said, “Send Lazarus down that he might dip his finger in water and touch my tongue, because I am tormented in these flames.” You young ones, get that, that you’re going to stand before God one of these days and be held accountable. Yeah, and hell’s real. It’s real. And then he says, “Okay, if you can’t do that, send Lazarus back, resurrecting from the dead, and send him back to my brothers, to testify to my brothers,” to teach them, instruct them, admonish them and warn them, notify them, advise them, caution them “lest they too come into this place of torment.” See, “testify” means and “warn” means to teach, to advise, to caution in regard to some future happening from a personal knowledge and experience. Do we, through the Bible, have a personal knowledge of a hell? Yes. How many don’t want to experience it? Yeah. Well, this guy experienced it, let me tell you. See, he not only had the knowledge, now he had the experience, and he wants his brothers to avoid this. Now, folks, if that is so urgent, how much more urgent should it be for us, the church, to be getting the message out and warning and telling people, so that God can raise up a standard in their life and they can escape?
What does he say are our responsibilities, and what is the warning in the story of Lazarus and the rich man? (Luke 16)

Luke 16:19-31: “There was a certain rich man who was clothed in purple and fine linen and fared sumptuously every day. But there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, full of sores, who was laid at his gate, desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table. Moreover the dogs came and licked his sores. So it was that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels to Abraham’s bosom. The rich man also died and was buried. And being in torments in Hades, he lifted up his eyes and saw Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom. “Then he cried and said, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.’ But Abraham said, ‘Son, remember that in your lifetime you received your good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things; but now he is comforted and you are tormented. And besides all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed, so that those who want to pass from here to you cannot, nor can those from there pass to us.’ “Then he said, ‘I beg you therefore, father, that you would send him to my father’s house, for I have five brothers, that he may testify to them, lest they also come to this place of torment.’ Abraham said to him, ‘They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.’ And he said, ‘No, father Abraham; but if one goes to them from the dead, they will repent.’ But he said to him, ‘If they do not hear Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded though one rise from the dead.’ ”
Why must the church keep warning people, and does it matter how it is said?

He says the burden is to get the Word out and “warn them,” and that “it doesn’t matter how it’s said, it’s the message we need to listen to.” He tells a story of a police officer telling him to evacuate a fire, and says people should not turn off a message because of how it is delivered, since “it’s the message that will set you free.”
Why must the church keep warning people, and does it matter how it is said?

Amen. And so we have a burden on us to get the Word of God out, and we need, every year I’m saying this, and we’re still not getting the Word of God out like we should: the printed word, the audible word, the video word, the Internet word. We need to take on [unclear] personally and get the word out to them, warn them. And then some people say, “Well, it’s all in how you say it.” Well, let me give you a little illustration here. At this fire that came over this property, we evacuated the kids from the school. Christina was on the ball and had the kids out by 12:30 or so. We took the horses out. I had the tractor down there scraping down the brush behind the house. I didn’t want the house to burn down. That fire is coming over that mountain, and it’s moving pretty quick, you know, covering a mile in two hours is pretty fast, and that fire is about 300 feet from me, and I’m still knocking down this brush. And one of the firemen comes over and says, “Sir, you did a great job, you’ve saved the building, but it’s time to go.” And he said it with empathy, with feeling, and I already knew it. It’s time to go. I already had my exit route planned out. I, the, the, the gas, the smoke was up here in the air, it wasn’t down here where you’re breathing, so you could last a lot longer. If that smoke would have dropped, I’d have been out of there early. How many know that? But anyway, he was right. He said it nice and politely. I didn’t have to leave the property, just like Harry Truman at Mount St. Helens, when they told him to leave his property, the Mount St. Helens was going to erupt. He said, “I ain’t leaving here, I lived here all my life, I’m going to die here,” and he stayed there and he died, and I could have stayed there. Well, anyway, I go around and I drop the tractor off, and I come around, and this guy pulls up in a car, and he says, “You got to evacuate now,” and I go, “Who are you?” I said, “Are you the fire department?” He said, “No, I’m a police officer.” I go, “Oh,” and I kept on doing what I was doing, and he says, I said, “You got to leave now.” I didn’t even pay him any mind. He was grouchy, grumpy, authoritative, and anything else, but I know who I am, and I know my rights, and I know what I got to get done. I had three more things to get done. I was going to get them done. Now, I could have been stupid and said, “Well, if that’s the way he’s going to talk to me, I’m not leaving, I’ll show him,” and I could have burned with him. He didn’t talk to me right. How many know, folks, it doesn’t matter how we say it, it’s still the truth, and you better listen. You know, if your mentality is, “Well, talk to me, say please, and I’ll listen,” grow up. Not all of us are going to talk to you the sweet way: “You poor little thing, we don’t want to hurt your feelings, but you’re going to hell.” Oh God, you’re going to hell. We may say, “Idiot, turn or burn.” It doesn’t matter how it’s said, it’s the message we need to listen to. Can I hear an amen? It doesn’t matter if you’re there smiling like Joel, smiling, never, never misses a smile. I’d like to see him in real life. You got it. Folks, don’t turn off the message because a tooth is missing in someone, or they can’t say the English language right, or they may say it harshly, or they may say it whiny. The thing is, listen to the message. It’s the message that will set you free. “Smoking: Surgeon General’s warning: causes cancer, heart disease, emphysema, and may complicate pregnancy.” It doesn’t “may” now, it is affecting your baby, they know that. Now, is there a protest on Washington to take that label off? No. Is the atheist offended by that and said, “You know, get that label off, you’re offending us, you’re taking away our right to kill ourself and get cancer”? Is the homosexuals rallying to get rid of that? No. But they don’t like God telling them what to do. They don’t like God telling them that He wants to rule over their life. Amen. Now, if I was a smoker, that would be offensive to me. I mean, you know, millions of Americans don’t pay any attention to that warning, and it’s there every pack you get, it’s there every carton you get, it’s there. Church, should we keep on warning just because they don’t listen? Should we keep telling? Yes, and that’s what we got to get done this year. We got to get the word out, the word of righteousness, and let God raise up a standard and defeat the enemy in people’s life and give them a way of escape, that they can have a new life in Christ Jesus. Amen. That’s our job. That’s what we got to do. So today, are you in love with Jesus? Are you going to love Jesus, accepting and living by the standards of Bible morality? And are you going to admonish, instruct, and warn and notify and advise, the best of your ability? Don’t worry about how you say it. How many just say, “I’m going to give it a shot”? Would you raise your hand? Yeah. Your approach may be all messed up, but you’ll learn. You’ll learn by giving it a shot.
What does the “flood” mean in Isaiah 59:19?
He says “a flood does nothing but damage. When you hear the word ‘flood,’ you know there is damage, you know the water is out of control,” and the enemy comes in that way.
What does he say is the key to defeating the enemy?
He says it is “the Spirit… the very part of God that will defeat your enemies,” rather than leaning “on our own knowledge and understanding.”
What are the two meanings of “standard” in Isaiah 59:19?
He says one is “to flee, to escape, to take flight,” and the other is “attacking the enemy,” to “fly to the attack, to put to flight.”
What does he say the Bible promises about temptation?
He says there is “no temptation come upon anybody” that God will not make “a way of escape that you might bear up under it.”
What is his “finger in the socket” illustration?

He says most Pentecostals “only experience putting our finger in the socket. We didn’t learn how to channel it,” but “at least we felt the power of God, right?” and “then we can learn how to channel it.”
Who does he say we wrestle against?
He says “it’s not the people. We wrestle not against flesh and blood… we wrestle against the principles of men that try to capture our mind.”
What does he say about people who follow their denomination above the Bible?
He says a religionist “will defend their denomination above Jesus Christ Himself and the Bible,” and asks, “We’re not told to follow a man. Who are we told to follow? Jesus.”
Did God kill Adam and Eve as He said He would?
He says no: “He didn’t kill Adam and Eve like He said He would,” but gave “a way of escape.” He says he asks this to show God is the same “yesterday, today, and forever.”
Why does he say God shed an animal’s blood for Adam and Eve?

He says it was “the first written illustration of God’s plan,” and “God already knew He was going to die for the sins of the world.” He says “the Bible says His blood was shed before the foundation of the world.”
Why does he say God said “woman” in Genesis 3:15?
He says “all through the Bible His people, God’s church, is an allegory of a bride,” and that God “didn’t say Adam, He said woman.”
How many converts did Noah have?

He says Noah “only had seven converts: his wife, his three boys, and three girls,” after preaching righteousness for 100 years. He says Noah was successful “because he did what God told him to do. You’re not measured by numbers.”
How does the Bible show it is God’s word, according to him?

He says God named Babylon, Persia and Greece and predicted what they would do “hundreds of years before they were a nation, and they did it,” and that “only God can tell what the future holds and bring it to pass.”
What does he say Jesus told the man who asked about eternal life?
He says Jesus told him, “If you will enter into life, keep the commandments,” and then listed the commandments about how we treat others, ending with “you shall love your neighbor as yourself.”
What did the rich man in hell ask for?
He says he asked for Lazarus to dip his finger in water to cool his tongue, and then asked that Lazarus be sent to warn his brothers “lest they too come into this place of torment.”
Does it matter how the warning is said?
He says no: “It doesn’t matter how we say it, it’s still the truth, and you better listen.” He says to “listen to the message. It’s the message that will set you free.”

items.t: What Does the Baptism of the Holy Spirit Have to Do with This?
items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer calls the baptism of the Holy Ghost the third promise that brings us into the divine nature, a baptism of power he says is for today. Using Luke 24, Acts 1 and 2, Ezekiel…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer calls the baptism of the Holy Ghost the third promise that brings us into the divine nature, a baptism of power he says is for today. Using Luke 24, Acts 1 and 2, Ezekiel 36 and John 14, he says the Comforter is Jesus coming back in spirit, and that this promise is for all flesh with no respect of persons. He then separates the gifts of the Spirit from the fruit and shares an experience about tongues.
Is the baptism of the Holy Spirit for today?

He says the baptism of the Holy Ghost is the promise of the Father, a baptism of power or spiritual ability, and that Peter said the promise is to you, your children and all who are afar off. He says there is no dispensation where it started and stopped, and that dispensationalism is man-made.
Is the baptism of the Holy Spirit for today?

So today we’re going to look at the third promise that God promised to help bring us into the divine nature and it is the baptism of the Holy Ghost. Baptism of the Holy Spirit. We argue about it. We fight over it. We divide over the doctrine of the baptism of the Holy Ghost. And that just should not be. And today I hope that you will get the word of truth in you and get rid of the quarreling, get rid of the division and get the ghost. He’s very important and I’m going to show you who the ghost is today clearly. All right. Luke 24:49. I send the promise of my father upon you. See here it is the promise. Remember the exceedingly great and precious promises by that by these we may be partakers of the divine nature. Here he plainly says, “I send the promise of my father upon you. Wait in Jerusalem until you be clothed with power from on high.” So the Holy Spirit baptism is a baptism of power. Spiritual ability. Spiritual ability. Say that. Spiritual ability. Spiritual ability. Yes. Supernatural ability. Ability that comes from God. All right. Acts 1 verse four and five. So Jesus comes after he rose from the dead, appears to his apostles, and he was assembled together with them. Jesus commanded them not to depart from Jerusalem, but wait for the promise. There it is again. Wait for the promise of the father. Which he said, “You have heard of me.” Not only did the Father tell you, but I’m told you. For John baptized with water, but you shall be baptized with the what? Holy Ghost not many days from now. And that was 10 days. 10 days later after he ascended. And so the baptism of the Holy Ghost is being clothed with power. It is the promise of the father, one of the exceedingly great and precious promises to bring us into the divine nature. Acts 2:38. After the Holy Ghost was poured out, Peter said, “Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins, and you shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.” So the prerequisite for being filled and baptized with the Holy Ghost is to repent from your sins and get water baptized. And he says, “Everyone that repents from their sins and gets water baptized shall,” and the word shall there is nothing can stop it from happening. For the promise, there’s that word again, the promise is unto you, to your children, and all that are afar off, as many as the Lord our God shall call. So, here’s that promise again. Now, the fundamentalists and the Pentecostals and the charismatics and the Lutherans and the Methodists, we’re all in a big fight whether the baptism of the Holy Ghost is for today or not. The fundamentalists, they got these dispensations, their dispensationalist and and so they have a dispensation where miracles and baptism of the Holy Ghost only happened back in the early church. There is no doctrine in the Bible about dispensationalism. It’s man-made. All right? I’m just going to tell you bluntly right here tells us plainly that the promise is not only to those apostles but to or those 120 that was in the upper room, but to their children and to all a far off. How many you know we’re a far off? Yeah. To all as many as the Lord shall call. So there is no dispensation where the Holy Ghost started and stopped. And the fundamentalists are wrong here. They say it’s not for today. And they you just get the Holy Ghost when you’re baptized in water.
Is the baptism of the Holy Spirit for today?

Luke 24:49: Behold, I send the Promise of My Father upon you; but tarry in the city of Jerusalem until you are endued with power from on high.” Acts 1:4-5: And being assembled together with them, He commanded them not to depart from Jerusalem, but to wait for the Promise of the Father, “which,” He said, “you have heard from Me; for John truly baptized with water, but you shall be baptized with the Holy Spirit not many days from now.” Acts 2:38-39: Then Peter said to them, “Repent, and let every one of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins; and you shall receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. For the promise is to you and to your children, and to all who are afar off, as many as the Lord our God will call.”
What does the promise of the Spirit include, according to Galatians 3 and Ezekiel 36?

He says the blessing of Abraham came through Jesus, and that we might also receive the promise of the Spirit, which is part of the divine nature. He reads Ezekiel 36:26-27 that God will put a new spirit within us and cause us to walk in his statutes, which he says means God’s own Spirit will be an active force in us.
What does the promise of the Spirit include, according to Galatians 3 and Ezekiel 36?

That’s a lie, too. And I can show you in the Bible. And I have showed you the baptism of the Holy Ghost is a an experience in God of power. And we we’re going to see something here. All right. So, aren’t you glad that this promise is to us a far off? We need power. How many need power, supernatural spiritual power in your life? We do, folks. We can’t serve God on our own brain power and own willpower. We need his power. All right. Now, let’s continue here. Galatians 3:14. The blessing of Abraham might come upon the Gentiles through Jesus Christ. Now, there’s two things here. The blessing of Abraham. Acts 3:25 tells us that the blessing of a blessing of Abraham was fulfilled when God raised up Jesus to bless you by turning every one of you from your sins. See, see in Abraham all the earth shall be blessed. How did he do that? By raising up Jesus. And Jesus turned us from our sins. But there’s another part to this. That we might receive the promise. There it is again. The promise of the what? Spirit. That Holy Spirit. Exceedingly great and precious promises that bring us into being partakers of the divine nature. Now, our ears and our eyes and our mind should be alert right now because God is promising something tremendous. What does the baptism of Holy Ghost have to do with the divine nature? Now, if it does have to do with the divine nature, we need to quit arguing about it. We need to quit dividing over it. We need to quit fighting about it. And we need to participate of it. Could that be an amen? Cuz the divine nature is a big deal. All right. Are you with me so far? Ezekiel 36. We’re going to go back to the Old Testament’s promise. I gave you the New Testament promises. Now, here’s the Old Testament promises. Ezekiel 36:26. I will put a new spirit within you. I will put a new spirit within you. Man, I could use that. And then he tells us exactly what the new spirit is. And where’s the spirit going to be put? Within us. Not out here. Not that omnipotent presence that people feel but inside. I’m going to put it inside you within you. And then he tells us exactly who the new spirit is. I will put my spirit. How many you know the Bible says God is spirit and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and truth. You see? So when God says I’m going to pour out my spirit, what’s he saying? I’m going to pour out myself. I am a spirit. See, this trinity is word is great, but it still helps us think God is three different persons. And yet, it it really is a good word to explain the three parts of God, but we lose sight that he’s still one God. And we’re going to help you straighten that out today. I will put my spirit within you. So that new spirit is his spirit and cause you. This word cause, I’m going to trigger you. I’m going to affect you. I’m going to move you. I’m going to be an active force in you. I needed that as a young Christian. I needed an active force within me. I need it as an old Christian too, but especially that vulnerable new Christian walk. You need a drive within you. And I’m going to move you to walk in my statutes and my judgments, keeping my commandments and keeping I’m going to cause you. It’s not you just trying to discipline yourself to obey. I’m going to cause you.
What does the promise of the Spirit include, according to Galatians 3 and Ezekiel 36?

Galatians 3:14: that the blessing of Abraham might come upon the Gentiles in Christ Jesus, that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith. Acts 3:25-26: You are sons of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying to Abraham, ‘And in your seed all the families of the earth shall be blessed.’ To you first, God, having raised up His Servant Jesus, sent Him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from your iniquities.” Ezekiel 36:26-27: I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you; I will take the heart of stone out of your flesh and give you a heart of flesh. I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My statutes, and you will keep My judgments and do them. John 4:24: God is Spirit, and those who worship Him must worship in spirit and truth.”
What does the Spirit do about uncleanness and famine in Ezekiel 36?

He says that in the new covenant God will deliver us from our uncleanness and put no famine on us, and that the famine he means is spiritual, a famine of hearing the word of the Lord as in Amos 8:11. He says the Holy Ghost will keep revealing the word to us.
What does the Spirit do about uncleanness and famine in Ezekiel 36?

I’m going to move you. I’m going to affect you in such a way you’re going to keep my word. Hallelujah. Yeah. It’s a good place for a good clap offering. See, God says he’s going to be a participator in this Christian walk. He says, “You will be my people and I will be your God.” If you know the new covenant, that’s part of the new covenant found in Hebrews 6 and 8 found in Jeremiah. So this new covenant is we’re going to walk in his statutes. This new covenant is we’re going to do it by the power of the spirit of God that he is going to baptize us with. I will deliver you from all your uncleanness. How many of you Christians found out you still needed things to be cleansed from after you got saved? I’ll raise both hands. That really frustrated me at first because from the pulpit, man, if I came to Christ, my problems were over, man. Just skate through life, no problem. I mean, that’s the way they implied that it was. And I got saved. And I didn’t know I had so many problems. I didn’t know I had so many wrongs in me until the light shined on me. And I needed changing in many different areas. But he said he’ll cleanse us from all of them when he puts that spirit in us. That that fire of the Holy Ghost burns it out. I will multiply the grain and bring no famine upon you. Now, here is the Everybody’s always talking about the sign of the Holy Ghost. There’s all kinds of signs of the Holy Ghost. Here we have 1 2 3 four of them. Ain’t that right? Because the promise is the Holy Ghost would cause me to do these things. I will multiply the grain and bring no famine upon you. Now, we know he’s not talking about natural famine. And I’ll tell you why. Now, when I was a young preacher, yeah, I preach, oh, yeah, God’s going to take care of you financially. No, he’s talking about spiritual things still. And I’m going to prove it to you, okay? The early church had a soup line. Acts chapter 6, Stephen was one of the administrators of that soupline. There were poor people in the church and they only served soup to the church and they only served soup to the people in the church who didn’t have family to help them. If you know your Bible and they only serve soup to the people in the church that were widows if they were 60 years old and up. Otherwise, those widows should be out working and taking care of themselves and that that widow was involved in the house of God. Just reminding you of things I’ve preached before. All right. We also know that Apollos prophesied that a famine would come. Now, if God’s going to put no famine upon us, and Apollos prophesied of a famine to come, that makes him a false prophet. Except, the famine came and they had to send help to the church where that famine hit. You see, so he’s talking about spiritual things. What he’s saying is in Amos it says, “I’m going to send a famine among you, not of hungry for bread, where you want bread or food, nor a thirst for water, but I’m going to send a famine in Amos 8:11 of hearing the words of the Lord.” Now, God says, “When you get this, Holy Ghost, you will not be in a word famine. I will keep revealing the word to you. Wow. So, see, I need this Holy Ghost. I need to quit arguing about it, fighting about it, and I need to get it because it’s going to bring me into the divine nature. And I want to be like Jesus.
What does the Spirit do about uncleanness and famine in Ezekiel 36?

Ezekiel 36:28-30: Then you shall dwell in the land that I gave to your fathers; you shall be My people, and I will be your God. I will deliver you from all your uncleannesses. I will call for the grain and multiply it, and bring no famine upon you. And I will multiply the fruit of your trees and the increase of your fields, so that you need never again bear the reproach of famine among the nations. Acts 6:1-6: Now in those days, when the number of the disciples was multiplying, there arose a complaint against the Hebrews by the Hellenists, because their widows were neglected in the daily distribution. Then the twelve summoned the multitude of the disciples and said, “It is not desirable that we should leave the word of God and serve tables. Therefore, brethren, seek out from among you seven men of good reputation, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business; but we will give ourselves continually to prayer and to the ministry of the word.” And the saying pleased the whole multitude. And they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit, and Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas, a proselyte from Antioch, whom they set before the apostles; and when they had prayed, they laid hands on them. Acts 11:28: Then one of them, named Agabus, stood up and showed by the Spirit that there was going to be a great famine throughout all the world, which also happened in the days of Claudius Caesar. Amos 8:11: “Behold, the days are coming,” says the Lord GOD, “That I will send a famine on the land, Not a famine of bread, Nor a thirst for water, But of hearing the words of the LORD.
Who is the other Comforter in John 14?

He reads John 14:16 that the Father will give another Comforter, and says the first Comforter is Jesus and the other is the Spirit of truth who abides forever, so there is no time when it stops. items.t: What God’s Word Does to the Gentiles
items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer continues through Isaiah to show how God deals with the Gentiles, including religionists who change His word like Esau, and says the church’s part is to speak the gospel…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer continues through Isaiah to show how God deals with the Gentiles, including religionists who change His word like Esau, and says the church’s part is to speak the gospel to them. Using Isaiah 35 he says God’s “vengeance” is the desert blossoming like a rose, the highway of holiness and everlasting joy for the redeemed.
Who are the Gentiles in Isaiah 34, and what is the sword on Edom? (Isaiah 34:1-5, Isaiah 2:17)

He says “the Gentiles used in the Bible is pagan heathen nations… non-Jew, ungodly people,” and that Isaiah 34:1 invites them to come near and hear. He says Edom is Esau, who “despised his birthright” and sold it for a bowl of soup, and that God will deal with people who have heard of God and “changed the things of God.” He says today he will address the Gentiles from the religionist side, because God will humble the pride that creates our own doctrines.
Who are the Gentiles in Isaiah 34, and what is the sword on Edom? (Isaiah 34:1-5, Isaiah 2:17)

Remember, the Gentiles used in the Bible is pagan, heathen nations, Gentiles, which means non-Jew, ungodly people. That he’s going to address now. A brief review, it’s not on your sheet, it’s on the other sheet. Brief review: Isaiah addresses the Gentiles in Isaiah 34:1, “Come near, you Gentiles.” He’s he’s inviting them to come close to hear, so somebody’s got to be speaking the word, and heed, or obey the word. “You people, let the earth hear, and all that is in it, the world and all things that come forth from it, for the in indignation, the anger, the wrath of the Lord is against all Gentiles.” Now, that sounds like he’s a bull, snort and smoke out of his nose, his horns down, ready to just destroy these people, all right? And then he says in verse 5, “My sword shall come down on Edom, the people of my curse, for judgment.” And you remember, Edom is Esau, and Esau despised his birthright. He was ungodly. The Bible says despised his birthright, didn’t want anything to do with the birthright, sold it for a bowl of soup. And uh uh so so God’s going to address people that have heard of God. Esau knew about God, he heard of God, and he knew he had a birthright, he he knew he had an inheritance, but he didn’t care about it. So he changed the things of God. In Isaiah 21:17 it says, “The loftiness of man shall be brought low, and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day. The idols he shall utterly abolish.” Now, we talked about the Gentiles being the humanist, the atheist and so forth, but today we’re going to address it from the religionist side, okay. Idols is a area of religion that God does not approve of, and it’s idols, it’s more than one religion, okay? He’s going to, in that day he’s going to humble people. they We get prideful, we get cocky in our religion, uh okay and we even create our own doctrines and our own way of worshiping God, and God’s going to deal with them in that day.
Who are the Gentiles in Isaiah 34, and what is the sword on Edom? (Isaiah 34:1-5, Isaiah 2:17)

Isaiah 34:1-5: Come near, you nations, to hear; And heed, you people! Let the earth hear, and all that is in it, The world and all things that come forth from it. For the indignation of the LORD is against all nations, And His fury against all their armies; He has utterly destroyed them, He has given them over to the slaughter. Also their slain shall be thrown out; Their stench shall rise from their corpses, And the mountains shall be melted with their blood. All the host of heaven shall be dissolved, And the heavens shall be rolled up like a scroll; All their host shall fall down As the leaf falls from the vine, And as fruit falling from a fig tree. “For My sword shall be bathed in heaven; Indeed it shall come down on Edom, And on the people of My curse, for judgment. Isaiah 2:17: The loftiness of man shall be bowed down, And the haughtiness of men shall be brought low; The LORD alone will be exalted in that day,

He says Isaiah 2:2 says “in the latter days” the Lord’s house will be established and all nations shall flow to it, which was fulfilled in part when Christ came but, he says, “has not been accomplished globally.” He says there is “a lot of stuff that’s got to be done yet” before Christ comes. He says our New Testament birthright is believing on the Lord Jesus Christ and also keeping the commandments and bearing fruit suitable for repentance, and neglecting that is neglecting our birthright.
Will all nations flow to the Lord in the latter days, and what is our birthright? (Isaiah 2:1-4, Isaiah 34:4)

Just reminding you of Isaiah 2. Also in Isaiah 2 verse one, “It shall come to pass in the latter days,” plural. Now, we know this has already been fulfilled when Christ came to the earth, but it’s latter days, plural, so it’s going to be continually fulfilled, “that the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established on top of the mountains and be exalted above the hills.” Now, we know that the nations worship their gods on the hill, on the mountains, and we know that Israel worshiped other gods and worshiped God their own way on the hills. This is previous lessons, okay? So when when people like Esau, when people do like Esau did, they change God’s word, they change who God’s is and God’s purpose is. That’s who God also is going to deal with, not just atheists and humanists and uh evolutionist and so forth. “In that day all nations shall flow to it,” all Gentiles, all pagans, all heathen, all ungodly. “He shall judge between the nations and rebuke many people. This has not been fulfilled gl. It has been fulfilled in part when Christ came and the Gentiles came into the kingdom of God. Amen. Hallelujah. And yes, he can do do it quickly, but the fact is he’s got to do it. Can I hear an amen? Now, a global encounter with those that hear about Jesus but reject him. Okay, a global encounter. All their host, the stars, the planets, the meteor and the all the things in heaven is going to fall down as a leaf falls from the vine and the fig tree. And here’s that scripture: the sword’s going to come down on Edom, these people that have redesigned God’s word, redes designed God rejected their birthright. Now, our birthright in the New Testament is if we believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, that God has raised him from the dead, we shall be saved from the day of wrath, from the lake of fire and from our sins and so forth. Amen. The other part of our birthright is keeping the commandments. Remember the rich man asked him, “What shall I do that I can and inherit eternal life?” He said, “Keep the commandments.” So bringing forth fruit suitable for repentance, suitable for believing in Jesus, is just as important as believing. Could that be an amen? All right, so when we neglect that, we’re neglecting our birthright. All right, that makes us an Edomite, an Esauite.
Will all nations flow to the Lord in the latter days, and what is our birthright? (Isaiah 2:1-4, Isaiah 34:4)

Isaiah 2:2-4: Now it shall come to pass in the latter days That the mountain of the LORD’s house Shall be established on the top of the mountains, And shall be exalted above the hills; And all nations shall flow to it. Many people shall come and say, “Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, To the house of the God of Jacob; He will teach us His ways, And we shall walk in His paths.” For out of Zion shall go forth the law, And the word of the LORD from Jerusalem. He shall judge between the nations, And rebuke many people; They shall beat their swords into plowshares, And their spears into pruning hooks; Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, Neither shall they learn war anymore. Isaiah 34:4: All the host of heaven shall be dissolved, And the heavens shall be rolled up like a scroll; All their host shall fall down As the leaf falls from the vine, And as fruit falling from a fig tree. Matthew 5:18: For assuredly, I say to you, till heaven and earth pass away, one jot or one tittle will by no means pass from the law till all is fulfilled. Romans 10:9: that if you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus and believe in your heart that God has raised Him from the dead, you will be saved. Matthew 19:16-17: Now behold, one came and said to Him, “Good Teacher, what good thing shall I do that I may have eternal life?” So He said to him, “Why do you call Me good? No one is good but One, that is, God. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.” Luke 3:8: Therefore bear fruits worthy of repentance, and do not begin to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I say to you that God is able to raise up children to Abraham from these stones.

He says that in that day “a man shall cast away his idols of silver and gold,” and that whatever man has devised to worship God, God will expose and change when He visits the earth globally before Christ comes. He says Isaiah 34:8 is the day of the Lord’s vengeance and “the year of recompense for the cause of Zion,” and that “who is he putting vengeance on is the real secret here.” He cites Isaiah 34:16, “Seek ye out of the book of the Lord and read it,” and says we have time for sports and soap operas “and no time to read God’s word.”
