Somewhere we need a plan to get on the internet and get focused and get this word out. You can on the internet, we’ve tested it, you can get it out to the world. Somewhere we need to get a plan for our community to get the word of God into every home. Sitting here and getting fed every Sunday and then going home and enjoying the luxuries of life and not getting a a a desire, a a motivation to tell others is wrong. Somewhere we got to regroup, and we we got to get organized, and we got to get this word out.
What does the gospel do for the Gentiles: open eyes, unstopped ears, water in the desert? (Isaiah 35:5-7)

Isaiah 35:5-7: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, And the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped. Then the lame shall leap like a deer, And the tongue of the dumb sing. For waters shall burst forth in the wilderness, And streams in the desert. The parched ground shall become a pool, And the thirsty land springs of water; In the habitation of jackals, where each lay, There shall be grass with reeds and rushes. Luke 4:18: “The Spirit of the LORD is upon Me, Because He has anointed Me To preach the gospel to the poor; He has sent Me to heal the brokenhearted, To proclaim liberty to the captives And recovery of sight to the blind, To set at liberty those who are oppressed; Revelation 12:9: So the great dragon was cast out, that serpent of old, called the Devil and Satan, who deceives the whole world; he was cast to the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.
What is the highway of holiness, and why does God give everlasting joy? (Isaiah 35:8-10)

He says a highway in the desert is “a road not only out but going somewhere,” and the redeemed are those who have been purchased by Christ’s blood. He says Satan can’t mess with them, and the redeemed shall “come to Zion with singing” and everlasting joy. He says Christians should have joy, to “rejoice and be glad” because “Jesus is touching the nations,” and the church needs a plan to get the word out, and “the cross is way bigger than knowledge of science.”
What is the highway of holiness, and why does God give everlasting joy? (Isaiah 35:8-10)

So this message just is Mountainside. If you were out there, you would want to know that there’s waters that will liberate you, deliver you. Look how powerful this is. This is so powerful. I just, and I know every time you read your Bible through that this one stops you, because it’s just so powerful, you just you just get jarred by it. “A highway shall be there, called the highway of holiness.” A highway in the desert, okay, these difficult places, a road out. Allelujah. A road not only out but going somewhere. “The unclean shall not pass over it, but the redeemed.” So these Gentiles are accepting Christ, these Gentiles are accepting the blood of Christ for forgiveness and cleansing of sin. He’s redeemed them. Redeem is you’ve been purchased. See, you’ve been purchased, you’re free from that old slave master, and you come under Jesus Christ, you repented from your sins. Unclean. “And the wayfaring men.” The walker, the drifter. Right now in America, Christianity is not growing. All we’re doing is moving from one church to another, and we usually descend. We go from a church preaching the word, that “Oh, they don’t, I don’t like that,” so we we descend to another level because they agree with what I agree with. Then there’s something though they don’t agree with, so you descend again until you get down here at a level you’re at. That’s the wanderer. And American Christians are going from one church to another, finally winding them some megachurch somewhere or TV church. They don’t even go to church. And we’re not saving souls. We’ve descended from 86% in America to 78%. We are not saving souls in America. “The simple,” easily persuaded and enticed. There are some people that Jehovah Witness can come along and just got them just like that, because their mind is so simple, they’re easy, because they don’t have the word in them. And fools, “the fool saith in his heart, there is no God.” See, he said, “All of these three shall not err in this road and lose their way.” Wow. King Jesus has showed up. Amen. Now, “no lion shall be there.” Satan as a roaring lion seeks whom he may devour. Satan’s not allowed to mess with you, that dragon that came to that troubled time you’re in, Jesus comes and doesn’t allow the dragon to mess with you. “No ravenous beast,” no false prophets, they ain’t going to mess with them, “but the redeemed shall walk on it.” Therefore, for this reason, “the redeemed of the Lord shall return and come to Zion with singing, an everlasting joy.” How long? Everlasting. Folks, the kingdom of God is not meat or drink, but righteousness, peace and joy in the Holy Ghost. Where is the Christians in America’s joy? They write and they sing songs over and over that have no joy. It blows my mind. What is the second fruit of the Spirit? Jo Joy. And why shouldn’t we be joyful? Why shouldn’t we have joy? Why should we be depressed and cast down every time something doesn’t go right, goes wrong? Let me get it right here. Hallelujah. He says he’s given us everlasting joy, where most Christians do not have joy. They get depressed, they get cast down at the lightest little thing. The Bible says to come into his gates with depression, come into his courts with sadness? No, it doesn’t. H “I will enter his gates with the thanksgiving in my heart, I will enter his courts with praise.” Amen. See, “Make a joyful noise unto the Lord, 10% of you saints, all ye, all ye make a joyful, of where have we gone? Where’s the joy? Hallelujah. Now, if the church has got to tell these people there’s joy, there’s deliverance, how mean, know we got to, we need to experience it. Hallelujah. “This is the day the Lord hath made. I will be sad, not glad in it.” No. I will rejoice, be joyful and be glad in it. I don’t care if I don’t like my job or not, I don’t care if things are going, I’m going to rejoice and be glad because Jesus is touching the nations of the earth and I can be a mouthpiece for him and I can inherit my promises. How many you know sorrow continues to the night? We do have a period of sorrow, but how many you know the Bible says, “With joy shall you draw waters out of the wells of salvation”? Salvation itself isn’t a totally depressing thing. You know, when he set you free, it’s not a time to be depressed anymore. Amen. Amen. I’m not not picking on anybody, I’m just telling you. Isaiah. All right. “Everlasting joy, they shall obtain.” They shall what? Obtain, possess. “Gladness and joy, and sorrow and mourning will” what? “Flee away.” See, he’s given us a garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness, the oil of joy for mourning, he’s did an exchange in our life. And this is what we got to offer these people that have distorted Jesus Christ, God and his word. Hallelujah. Hallelujah. And I’m done. If you believe Isaiah this morning, and God is going to do something big before Jesus comes back, n global, worldwide, and you believe that the church has a part in this by sharing God’s word, living God’s word, we don’t have to look down on these people, we don’t have to be afraid of them. I was telling somebody the other day, I don’t have to prove the Bible to you, I don’t have to do that. I have to preach the gospel to you, and you got to decide if you’re going to accept Jesus’ forgiveness of sin, get baptizing him and inherit eternal you got to decide that. Don’t come asking me about creation and billions of years, and I don’t have to do that. I don’t have to debate with you one bit. Now, what are you going to do with Jesus? I said, what are you going to do with the fact he said all have sinned, and his blood will cleanse you from sin, and everyone will stand before the judgment and be accountable for what they say and do? What are you going to do? I don’t care where Cain’s wife come from, I don’t care how many times the rooster crowed. What I care about is what are you going to do? And that’s what the Bible says with this man Jesus. Are you going to love him and love people? Hallelujah. Now, I will debate them when they say yes or no, then they want answers, I’ll show them their false science. I do know my science. But the cross is way bigger than knowledge of science.
What is the highway of holiness, and why does God give everlasting joy? (Isaiah 35:8-10)

Isaiah 35:8-10: A highway shall be there, and a road, And it shall be called the Highway of Holiness. The unclean shall not pass over it, But it shall be for others. Whoever walks the road, although a fool, Shall not go astray. No lion shall be there, Nor shall any ravenous beast go up on it; It shall not be found there. But the redeemed shall walk there, And the ransomed of the LORD shall return, And come to Zion with singing, With everlasting joy on their heads. They shall obtain joy and gladness, And sorrow and sighing shall flee away. 1 Peter 5:8: Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil walks about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour. Romans 14:17: for the kingdom of God is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit. Psalm 118:24: This is the day the LORD has made; We will rejoice and be glad in it. Isaiah 12:3: Therefore with joy you will draw water From the wells of salvation. Isaiah 61:3: To console those who mourn in Zion, To give them beauty for ashes, The oil of joy for mourning, The garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; That they may be called trees of righteousness, The planting of the LORD, that He may be glorified.”
Why does he say Christ cannot come any minute?

He says Isaiah’s prophecies “has not been accomplished globally,” and that the idea that the rapture can happen any minute “is just full of baloney” because “there’s a lot of stuff that’s got to be done yet.” He adds that God can do it quickly but still has to do it.
What does he say our birthright is?

He says it is that “if we believe on the Lord Jesus Christ that God has raised him from the dead, we shall be saved,” and also “keeping the commandments.” He says bringing forth fruit suitable for repentance is “just as important as believing,” and neglecting it is neglecting our birthright.
Why does he expect a large harvest in the last days?

He says there are over 7 billion people now, and “billions of people in these last 100 years” beyond all who lived before, so when God says Gentiles in heaven “cannot be numbered,” he is going to manifest Himself in these last days. He says looking for Jesus to come in a minute misses the purpose of God to fill heaven with people.
What does he say about reading the Bible?

He says it is “the most precious book in the world,” yet we make time for baseball, football and soap operas and “no time to read God’s word.” He says we read other authors but can open the Bible and find out what it says.
How does he say people twist scripture?

He says putting in your own opinions is “adding to the word,” and taking verses out of the Bible is “taken away from the word.” He says if people follow us after we alter it, “we’re leading them to destruction.”
What does he say about the saying that all roads lead to the same God?

He says “they change the scriptures” and that “all roads lead to the same God” is a statement a lot of leaders make “not understanding it comes directly from” another religion, not the Bible. His view is stated as he spoke it and is not verified here.
How does he explain the Trinity?

He says Jesus is God, God the Father, God the Son and God the Holy Ghost, and asks “how many gods?” and answers “one.” He says “we’re not talking about three gods,” though we may use the word Trinity.
Does he say Paul wrote some things as his own opinion?

He says in 1 Corinthians Paul wrote “I write this, not the Lord,” giving his own permission, but that the rest God was telling him to write, so the writers wrote “as the Holy Spirit gave him the inspiration.”
He says love is not “that fear feeling” but “that principle of doing nothing and speaking nothing to hurt others.” He says you don’t have to have vibes or feelings, “you just do it.”
Does he say our sin hurts God?
He says God is not “up on the throne worried” and that “your bad choices hurt you and they hurt others.” He says God’s plan cannot be rattled: “he knows what he’s doing, he knows where he’s going.”
Why does he say chapter breaks do not change the subject?
He says “a chapter does not separate necessarily a subject. Chapters are put in there by man,” so Isaiah 35 continues the subject of God’s visitation on the Gentiles from Isaiah 34.
What does he say the desert is a picture of in the Bible?

He says the desert “is always referred to as a place where you get tested and humbled during life’s difficulties.” He says God led Israel 40 years in the wilderness to “know what was in their heart, not to seduce them with sin.”
Does he say every bad thing that happens is because of sin?

He says no: “it’s not our own choice, it’s not God, and it’s not sin” in every case. He cites the tower that fell, saying “it wasn’t their sin that the tower fell,” and that an accident can “just happen.”
Does he say we should look down on people of other beliefs?
He says no: “we got no right looking down on the Mormons,” or anybody. He says if we have truth, “the key to their survival is us speaking it, sharing it.”
What does he say about people moving from church to church?

He says in America “Christianity is not growing, all we’re doing is moving from one church to another,” and cites a drop from 86% to 78% saying “we are not saving souls in America.” These are his figures as spoken, without a source.

items.d: In this short message, Pastor David G. Kincer says that when you die your body decays, your spirit leaves your body, and you immediately stand before Jesus Christ to be judged for what you did in this body. He…
p: In this short message, Pastor David G. Kincer says that when you die your body decays, your spirit leaves your body, and you immediately stand before Jesus Christ to be judged for what you did in this body. He tells of visions of hell and the judgment day and says ministers should persuade people to turn, because Christ died so they would not have to burn.
What happens to your body after you die?

He says just a few minutes after you die your body starts decaying; if you are not buried, maggots and bacteria begin to eat it, and if you are buried, worms and insects do. He says all the beautiful stuff we spend so much time on suddenly is not so beautiful anymore, so we must be buried or burned.
What happens to your body after you die?

What happens after we die immediately just a few minutes after you die your body starts decaying rotting. [unclear]. As time goes by if you’re not buried. Maggots will begin to eat your body and [unclear] will begin to eat it the bacteria in your body will begin to eat your body if you’re buried the worms and the insects and critters in the ground will begin to eat your body. And uh. All this beautiful stuff that we spend so much time on suddenly isn’t so beautiful anymore. Or we can be burned we either got to be buried or we got to be burned because we start stinking.
What is the first thing that happens when you die?

He says the body you worshiped all your life starts rotting away, and the first thing that happens is your spirit leaves your body. From James 2:26 he says people say you are dead when your heart or brain waves stop, but God says you are dead when he takes the spirit out of your body.
What is the first thing that happens when you die?

And so immediately this physical body that you have worshiped all your life and did everything to clothe it with the latest clothing and the latest hair fashion and all the rest just starts. Rotting away the bacteria inside your body just takes over the first thing that happens when you die is your spirit leaves your body. James chapter 2 verse 26. As the body without the spirit is dead you see they say when your heart stops beating you’re dead they say when your brain waves stop waving you’re dead. But God says when my spirit when I take that spirit out of your body you’re dead and as we’ve seen in the Bible those were resurrected because he put the spirit back in them.
What is the first thing that happens when you die?
James 2:26: For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.
What do Stephen and Jesus show about the spirit at death?

He says Stephen, as he was stoned, said “Lord Jesus receive my spirit,” knowing his spirit would leave his body. On the cross Jesus said “father into your hands I commend my spirit” and gave up the ghost; he says no man could kill Jesus, because he was God and had to give up his life himself.
What do Stephen and Jesus show about the spirit at death?

And one day science is going to catch up with the Bible. They’re already having a hard time figuring out why some people’s been dead several days came back to life and nothing was wrong. So that’s going to happen one of these days you’re going to croak you’re gonna die and your spirit will come out of that body. In acts chapter 7 verse 59 they stoned Stephen calling up on God saying Lord Jesus receive my spirit. Stephen knew what was going to happen his spirit was going to leave his body Luke 23:46 Jesus said father on the cross he’s hanging on the cross and he’s going to die he said father into your hands I commend my spirit and having said this he gave up the ghost see no man could kill Jesus he was God he had to give up his life himself.
What do Stephen and Jesus show about the spirit at death?

Acts 7:59: And they stoned Stephen as he was calling on God and saying, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.” Luke 23:46: And when Jesus had cried out with a loud voice, He said, “Father, ‘into Your hands I commit My spirit.’ ” Having said this, He breathed His last.
Who will you stand before after you die?

He says the next thing that happens is you stand before Jesus Christ, immediately, “not Allah, not Buddha.” From Hebrews 9:27 he says it is appointed for men to die once and after that the judgment, and from Second Corinthians 5:10 that we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, which includes believers.
Who will you stand before after you die?

No one could kill God and so he gave up the spirit and that body that he was in died. Just like we done. The next thing that happens is you stand before Jesus Christ. Immediately. Not Allah not Buddha. Jesus Christ. Hebrews 9:27 it is appointed for men to die once. But after that the judgment. You’re going to die and you’re going to stand before Jesus Christ second Corinthians 5:10 we must all how many all and includes believers.
Who will you stand before after you die?

Hebrews 9:27: And as it is appointed for men to die once, but after this the judgment, 2 Corinthians 5:10: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive the things done in the body, according to what he has done, whether good or bad.
Why should preachers try to persuade people about the judgment?

He says we receive the things done in this body, whether good or bad, and “knowing therefore the terror of the Lord we persuade men” should be every minister’s real motivation. He tells how, as a young Christian, God showed him the sin in homes he passed and he would weep, because those people would be held accountable and somebody needed to tell them.
Why should preachers try to persuade people about the judgment?

Appear before the judgment seat of Christ to receive the things done. By our faith. In our faith. In our grace. No done what in this body how you lived. While you were in this body. Whether you did good or whether you did bad. Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord we persuade men what should be the real motivation of every minister preaching the gospel. To persuade people to avoid the judgment of Jesus Christ. I can remember as a young Christian driving down the freeway and God would just open my eyes to the sin going on in the homes that I was passing by now I didn’t have x-ray vision and actually see what was happening but he just said this is what’s you know he just showed me and I would just weep. Because these people were doing things that they were going to be held accountable to God for and somebody needed to tell them. See this is the basic message of the gospel. See you think the Muslim terrorist are bad. You read the Bible about having to stand before God and it should scare you into eternal life. Hallelujah people love one of that scary gospel. Didn’t he say it’s a terror doesn’t he say it’s a fearful thing yeah. You think you’re not wanting to hear the bad news of the gospel that it’s going to change the gospel.
Why should preachers try to persuade people about the judgment?

2 Corinthians 5:10-11: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive the things done in the body, according to what he has done, whether good or bad. Knowing, therefore, the terror of the Lord, we persuade men; but we are well known to God, and I also trust are well known in your consciences.
What did he see of hell and judgment day?

He says once, between two jobs, his eyes were opened to see hell and the judgment day, where people stood before Christ and no one said a word because they knew they were wrong. He says hell is not a pleasant place, and those who say they will have friends there are fools, because isolation is one of the parts of hell.
What did he see of hell and judgment day?

Again I was working two jobs and I come home in between jobs I had just enough time to eat and I was sitting there and suddenly my eyes were open to see hell and it wasn’t pleasant. And then my eyes were open to that judgment day and people were standing before Christ and no one was saying a word because they knew they knew they were wrong when they did the wrong. There was no debates there. And it was a horrible thing to be in hell and people that say well I’m going to go hell that’s where my sons and daughters are my best friend you are a fool yeah hell is not a pleasant place and if you think you’re going to have friends down there forget it. Isolation is one of the parts of hell.
Can a church or minister save you on judgment day?

He says Christ died on the cross so you would not have to burn, but if you do not turn you will burn. No church, book, minister or the pope can save you in that day; you will be judged by what you did in this body, and from Romans 14:10 everyone shall give account of himself to God.
Can a church or minister save you on judgment day?

Knowing the terror of the Lord we try to persuade men we try to get them to turn. And that’s why Christ died on the cross so you would not have to burn. Hallelujah that’s the good part of the gospel the bad part is if you don’t turn you’re going to burn. There’s no church can save you in that day there’s no book written it can save you in that day there’s no minister on earth can save you and that day the pope can’t save you in that day the only king is going you’re going to be judged by what you did in this body. Whether what good or bad. Unbelievers need to know there is a judgment waiting for you Romans 14:10 we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ everyone shall give account of himself to God.
Can a church or minister save you on judgment day?

Romans 14:10-12: But why do you judge your brother? Or why do you show contempt for your brother? For we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ. For it is written: “As I live, says the LORD, Every knee shall bow to Me, And every tongue shall confess to God.” So then each of us shall give account of himself to God.
Can you blame others for your sins at the judgment?

He says you cannot blame your pastor, spouse, parents or children; you are responsible for choosing to do wrong. He says the light from the throne exposed everything impure with no arguments, and from Matthew 12:36-37 that men will give account of every idle word, and by your words you will be justified or condemned.
Can you blame others for your sins at the judgment?

You’re going to you know you can’t blame your pastor in that day. You can’t blame your spouse. Will my spouse just drug me down into drugs no you are responsible for your own actions. You can’t blame your parents you can’t blame your children you can’t blame anyone but yourself. For choosing to do wrong and knowing you are doing wrong when you did it so you’re going to stand before God and you’re going to give an account and that’s what these people were doing they weren’t saying a word the light that’s shown from that throne just permeated their whole being and every little thing that was unpure was just exposed just like that and they knew that everything that was exposed they knew they were wrong when they did it just like that no arguments no nothing in Matthew 12:36 every idle word. That men shall speak they will give an account of it in the day of judgment. By your words you will be justified or by your word you will be condemned. Punished.
Can you blame others for your sins at the judgment?

Matthew 12:36-37: But I say to you that for every idle word men may speak, they will give account of it in the day of judgment. For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”
When is a person really dead, according to the Bible?

He says people say you are dead when your heart stops or your brain waves stop, but God says you are dead when he takes the spirit out of your body; those resurrected in the Bible came back when he put the spirit back in them.
Will science catch up with the Bible on death?
He says one day science is going to catch up with the Bible, since they already have a hard time figuring out why some people dead several days came back to life with nothing wrong.
He says no man could kill Jesus because he was God; he had to give up his life himself, and he gave up the spirit and the body died.
Will believers also stand before the judgment seat of Christ?
He says “we must all” appear before the judgment seat of Christ and that includes believers, to receive the things done not by our faith or grace but in this body, whether good or bad.
Is it wrong to preach a “scary” gospel?
He says reading in the Bible about standing before God should scare you into eternal life, and asks “doesn’t he say it’s a fearful thing.”
Will you have friends in hell?
He says if you think you are going to have friends down there, forget it; isolation is one of the parts of hell.
Why did Christ die on the cross?
He says Christ died on the cross so you would not have to burn; that is the good part of the gospel, and the bad part is that if you do not turn you will burn.
Will people argue with God at the judgment?
He says in what he saw there were no debates and no arguments; the light from the throne exposed every impure thing and they knew they were wrong when they did it.

items.d: In this message a speaker at Vine Cluster Church teaches that the church is a people called out of darkness, built on Jesus Christ as its foundation, and given authority and a calling that angels and…
p: In this message a speaker at Vine Cluster Church teaches that the church is a people called out of darkness, built on Jesus Christ as its foundation, and given authority and a calling that angels and principalities watch. He goes through what the church does when it gathers (praise, prayer, ministering to the Lord, fasting), the qualities it should show the world, and closes with Philippians 3: the goal is to know Christ now.
What does it mean that the church is called out of darkness, and why do believers in China risk prison to gather? (1 Peter 2:9)

He says the church “is a people that’s called out of sin and to his light, and the light exposes us,” and you can’t live as a Christian thinking you can stay in darkness. He points to churches in China where people put their lives on the line just to gather, and says “we should have that same desire in America. It’s scriptural, it’s important.”
What does it mean that the church is called out of darkness, and why do believers in China risk prison to gather? (1 Peter 2:9)

1 Peter 2:9, “Who has called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.” He’s called you more than just gathering. He’s called us out of darkness. he The church is a people that’s called out of sin and to his light, and the light exposes us. How do we know? With these lights on you can see things. I can see Christina, she’s got a stain on her jacket. Just kidding. And people, the Bible says that people don’t like the light because it exposes them. That’s right. That God has called us out of darkness, I mean, these scriptures make it plain. You can’t live your life as a Christian thinking that you you can stay in darkness. No way. Why are the churches in China risking their lives, risking prison, to gather? The unofficial church. Mr. Kincer, our pastor, is over there right now cuz he wants to see what’s happening, he wants to be a part. You know, those people are are putting their lives on the line just to gather. You know, they could all stay home. They’re not taking the excuse, “I’m just going to stay home and live for Jesus.” They’re putting everything on the line together. And why? Is it ignorance because they’re just ignorant people? No, they have something inside of them that wants to gather with God’s people, and we should have that same desire in America. It’s scriptural, it’s important.
What does it mean that the church is called out of darkness, and why do believers in China risk prison to gather? (1 Peter 2:9)

1 Peter 2:9: But you are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, His own special people, that you may proclaim the praises of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light;
What is the foundation of the church? (Matthew 16:18, 1 Corinthians 3:11, Isaiah 28:16)

He says that in Matthew 16:18 Jesus “talking about himself. He’s going to build the church on himself,” not on Peter, John, James or the apostles. He says “Jesus is the rock,” the word has not changed in 2,000 years, and he wants “a sure foundation” rather than a philosophy that can be proven wrong.
What is the foundation of the church? (Matthew 16:18, 1 Corinthians 3:11, Isaiah 28:16)

The church has a foundation, and I’ll tell you why this is important. And we’re going to go back to the verse that we talked about, Matthew 16:18, and he says, “Thou art Peter.” Now Peter, the word means piece of a rock, “and upon this rock.” This rock, you know, nonverbal communication is so helpful. You know, if we had a video of Jesus and Peter talking, it would be very helpful, you know, because this is what Jesus would be doing. Okay, say I’m Jesus and Peter’s standing here, “Thou art Peter, and upon this rock,” that’s what he’s saying. You know, I’ve read the scripture several times and you always think he’s talking about Peter. No, he’s talking about himself. He’s going to build the church on himself. And we know that’s true in 1 Corinthians 3:11, it says, “For no other foundation can anyone lay than that which has been laid, which is Jesus Christ.” He is the rock. He didn’t say which is Peter, which is John, which is James. he said He didn’t say the apostles. He said the foundation is Jesus Christ. He’s building the church on himself. In Isaiah 28:16 it says, “I lay in Zion, I lay...” And you read right through that, but he’s saying, “I’m laying down in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation.” And how many know, when when you build a building you better have a good foundation. He says there will come a time in your Christian walk when you give up the things you did not want to give up for Christ, and “it’s going to be rubbish.” He says the goal is to win Christ.

He says “we don’t have to wait till we die and go to heaven,” and that Jesus is saying “you can know me now.”

p: In this short message, Part 4 of his Bible morality series, the speaker says what is added to faith after the Holy Spirit is virtue, moral excellent behavior with the courage to do it, from 2 Peter 1. He says a justice system should punish those who harm others, reads Romans 13, Proverbs 21:11 and Isaiah 5:20, compares today’s opponents to the Pharisees, and speaks about religious freedom and the Bible in early America.

He says “virtue moral excellent behavior with valor is going to be what we’re going to add to the Holy Spirit,” citing 2 Peter 1. He says “virtue is moral excellent behavior with the courage to do it,” and that adding it to faith keeps you from being “barren nor unfruitful.”

items.ser: When the Field Won’t Respond · Part 1
p: In “When the Field Won’t Respond Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Ezekiel 2 on what a Christian is to do when immoral, sinning believers will not listen: do not be afraid of them, do not be dismayed by their looks, speak God’s words rather than your opinions, and take in the judgment Scriptures along with the encouraging ones. He gives examples from a protest he attended, urges Bible studies that ask what God is saying, and says ministers, politicians and church members bend Scripture to keep votes, members and benefits.
What should a Christian do when people who should know better won’t listen?

He says God sent Ezekiel to a rebellious people and told him to speak whether they listened or not. He teaches that “we got to speak anyway,” because the charge is to speak, not to guarantee a response.
What should a Christian do when people who should know better won’t listen?

What do we do when the harvest field is unresponsive, impossible to reach, they won’t respond? What is a Christian to do? Sound like a good question? Yeah. So we’re going to begin with: what if immoral believers will not listen? Okay, we’re not even going to talk about unbelievers here. What if immoral believers that are sinning, what if they will not listen? Ezekiel 2:3-5. God comes to Ezekiel after showing Ezekiel the likeness of the glory of the Lord in chapter
What should a Christian do when people who should know better won’t listen?

Ezekiel 2:3-5: And He said to me: “Son of man, I am sending you to the children of Israel, to a rebellious nation that has rebelled against Me; they and their fathers have transgressed against Me to this very day. For they are impudent and stubborn children. I am sending you to them, and you shall say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD.’ As for them, whether they hear or whether they refuse—for they are a rebellious house—yet they will know that a prophet has been among them.
Why does he say God’s presence comes to say something and not just to feel good?

He says that when the presence of God comes, “He comes to say something, not to just make you feel good,” so we have to hear what He has to say. He applies this to Ezekiel, whom God sends to the children of Israel, a rebellious nation.
Why does he say God’s presence comes to say something and not just to feel good?

1. And everybody likes to preach on that, but we’re going to just remind you that it’s there. We’re not in the likeness of the glory of the Lord. The Bible says that the glory of the Lord shall cover the earth as the waters cover the sea. His glory, His presence has been predestinated to be upon those who seek Him and worship Him. But as I’ve told you for 40 years, when the presence of God comes, He comes to say something, not to just make you feel good. And I love the feeling of His presence. How many like to feel that presence of God? It’s beautiful. Yeah, it’s just beautiful. But you know, we got to hear what He has to say. And so He says to Ezekiel, “I’m sending you to the children of Israel, a rebellious nation that has rebelled against Me.” Okay, He’s [unclear] them. And see, Ezekiel came into captivity about 5 years after Daniel did.
Why does he say God’s presence comes to say something and not just to feel good?

Habakkuk 2:14: For the earth will be filled With the knowledge of the glory of the LORD, As the waters cover the sea. Ezekiel 2:3-5: And He said to me: “Son of man, I am sending you to the children of Israel, to a rebellious nation that has rebelled against Me; they and their fathers have transgressed against Me to this very day. For they are impudent and stubborn children. I am sending you to them, and you shall say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD.’ As for them, whether they hear or whether they refuse—for they are a rebellious house—yet they will know that a prophet has been among them.
Why was Ezekiel sent to a rebellious people who would not listen?

He says God sent Ezekiel to the Jews in captivity who were being corrected for their sins and were still rebellious, disrespectful and stubborn. God said they would know a prophet had been among them whether they listened or not, and so Ezekiel had a charge to speak anyway.
Why was Ezekiel sent to a rebellious people who would not listen?

The second captivity came and Ezekiel went into captivity. Now Daniel was ministering to the Babylonians, but Ezekiel God sent to the Jews that were in captivity, being corrected for their sins. Okay, number one, they are a rebellious nation. They are disrespectful. They are stubborn. Wow, sound like anybody you know? “I send you to them, saying, ‘Thus saith the Lord.’ Whether they hear or whether they refuse to hear, they are a rebellious house.” Okay, so He’s sending, He’s describing God’s people in captivity being punished for their sins, and they’re still rebellious. They’re still disrespectful. They didn’t learn their lesson. He says, “They will know that a prophet has been among them,” whether they listen or not. They’re going to know a prophet has been among them. Now we see here that Ezekiel was given a charge, a responsibility, to speak to the immoral believer anyway. Hallelujah. “Well, they’re not going to listen, so I’m not going to say anything.” No, we got to speak anyway. He’s given a commandment, He’s given a charge, He’s given a mission to speak to them anyway, whether they listen or whether they don’t.
Why was Ezekiel sent to a rebellious people who would not listen?

Ezekiel 2:3-5: And He said to me: “Son of man, I am sending you to the children of Israel, to a rebellious nation that has rebelled against Me; they and their fathers have transgressed against Me to this very day. For they are impudent and stubborn children. I am sending you to them, and you shall say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD.’ As for them, whether they hear or whether they refuse—for they are a rebellious house—yet they will know that a prophet has been among them.
What are the “two harvest fields” in this message?
He says unbelievers (the Babylonians) were reached by Daniel and others, while Ezekiel was sent to God’s hard-headed, hard-hearted people. This message is about the second field: sinning believers.
What are the “two harvest fields” in this message?

Okay, now there are two harvest fields, remember. The unbelievers were being reached by Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego, Esther, [unclear], other people. They were reaching the Babylonians. But Ezekiel was sent to God’s hard-headed people, hard-hearted people. Have you ever met one? Yeah. Just look in the mirror. Just look in the mirror and look real close and you’ll see one. We think we know it all and we know nothing at all. Right. Now, the requirements to preach to a hard harvest field of immoral, sinning believers. Remember, this message is a synonym to the

believers. Okay, number one, in Ezekiel 2:6-8, number one: do not be afraid of them. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be scared of these people. So many Christians are afraid of offending, or afraid of the retaliation of, homosexuals, adulterers, pedophiles, incest people, those that use abortion as a contraceptive, those that get intoxicated, and drug users. 177,000 people die and millions get hurt by drugs each year. 450,000 people die from tobacco-related deaths. Okay, 1.3 million babies are aborted just because they’re using it as a contraceptive, not because there’s a real need. 85,000 people die every year in America from alcohol-related deaths, plus all of the millions of injuries that come from it, and the billions of dollars spent in each area correcting the problem. 30,000 die in America every year from sexually transmitted diseases, and over 50% of Americans have a sexually transmitted disease or have had one. And we’re afraid we’re going to offend them, or they’re going to retaliate, not be our friend anymore, or beat us up or whatever. And Ezekiel is told, don’t what? Be afraid. Don’t be scared. How many could use some courage in your Christian walk? Yeah. See, courage replaces fear. You don’t even think about retaliation and offending. Number two: nor be afraid of their words, or I’m sorry, that’s part of number one. Don’t be afraid how they talk. Number two: don’t be

Ezekiel 2:6-8: “And you, son of man, do not be afraid of them nor be afraid of their words, though briers and thorns are with you and you dwell among scorpions; do not be afraid of their words or dismayed by their looks, though they are a rebellious house. You shall speak My words to them, whether they hear or whether they refuse, for they are rebellious. But you, son of man, hear what I say to you. Do not be rebellious like that rebellious house; open your mouth and eat what I give you.”
What does it mean to speak God’s words and not be dismayed by how people look at you?

He says number two is not to be dismayed by their looks, and number three is to speak God’s words, the truth. He describes a protest he attended, says he was attacked at first, and says he told the people there that their claims, such as being born that way, are a lie.
What does it mean to speak God’s words and not be dismayed by how people look at you?

dismayed by their looks, the way they look. See, when I protested against the homosexuals last year at Chick-fil-A, I told them the truth. You know, they gave me the looks. They attacked me when I first went, and then they realized the cameras were on them and they backed off and became real perfect gentlemen. But number three says: speak My words to them. Speak the truth. I just told them the truth. I told them that homosexuals are liars. You know, they say they were born that way. There is no homosexual gene. Scientifically, it has not been found. Scientifically, it can’t be done. It’s a lie. They say that animals, hundreds of animals, have homosexual tendencies. When I looked at their proof, it was a joke. Two horses rubbing against each other in a pasture. That’s what horses do. They’re not putting the penis in the anus of the other animal. There’s a big difference. Are you with me? They’re lying. I told them, you guys are liars. And they say that the Bible’s a book of myths. They said it right there, right in front of the cameras, and the Bible’s a bunch of bull [unclear]. That’s the words they use. They say the Bible’s for slavery, and so does President Obama and liberals. And I’ve showed them in the Bible where it can’t be for slavery, because you cannot kidnap anyone, and they ignore me. If you cannot kidnap a person and force them to do your will, how in the world are you going to make a slave out of anybody? Can I hear an amen? Yeah. See, they read the Bible the way they want to read it to put lies across, to get dumb Christians. They’re dumbing down believers that don’t follow on to know the word.
What does it mean to speak God’s words and not be dismayed by how people look at you?

Ezekiel 2:6-8: “And you, son of man, do not be afraid of them nor be afraid of their words, though briers and thorns are with you and you dwell among scorpions; do not be afraid of their words or dismayed by their looks, though they are a rebellious house. What does he say about people twisting Scripture, such as eating shrimp or Sodom and Gomorrah?

He says people read the Bible the way they want in order to put lies across. He says the shrimp law was a shadow pointing to the righteousness God required through Christ, and that the Bible is plain that Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed because of their sin.
What does he say about people twisting Scripture, such as eating shrimp or Sodom and Gomorrah?

And they get them on their side. They say you can’t eat shrimp or you get stoned for it. That’s a lie. No one in the Bible got stoned for eating shrimp. It was a shadow law pointing to the righteousness that God required through Christ, because when Christ came, He empowered us, and the Bible plainly says in the New Testament that you can eat what you want. You see, but see, they lie, and they get dumb Christians believing these lies. They say that Sodom and Gomorrah was destroyed for lack of hospitality, not sodomy. That is a lie. The Bible’s very plain that they were destroyed because of their sin, and one of the biggest sins in Sodom at that time was sodomy. Homosexuality. Come on, stop twisting. You guys lie. And I got to say that to them in front of all the
What did he tell the cameras about breaking a moral law?

He says he told the newscasters that when we break a moral law it is a crime, that homosexuality is immoral, and that in his view such people “should be punished for it, disciplined for it, fined or something, not put on display for everybody to imitate.” He adds that the news did not repeat what he said. This is the speaker’s own strongly stated opinion.
What did he tell the cameras about breaking a moral law?

cameras. You know, NBC was there, all the TV stations were there. I got to tell them. But you didn’t see me getting repeated on the news, everything I told them. The news just uses what’s good for them, what they like. Hallelujah. I told them that homosexuality is criminal, it’s a crime. And the newscasters, the camera people, they came up and said, “What do you mean by that?” I said, “When we break a moral law, it is a crime, and homosexuality is immoral, and they should be punished for it, disciplined for it, fined or something, not put on display for everybody to imitate.” Right? We don’t put the pedophiles on display. We don’t put incest people on display. Why are we letting these homosexuals get on TV and public places and everything like it’s normal and not a crime? It is a crime. Amen. See, we got to preach the word of the Lord. And yeah, they didn’t like it, and yeah, they got mad at me, and yeah, they attacked me at the beginning, till the leader got them in control. And I know why they did it, ’cause they attack me all the time. But when that camera comes, they are the nicest, most mannered people you can’t believe, because they don’t want the real attitude coming out.
Should we speak God’s words or our own opinions?
He says to speak God’s words, “not your opinions, not what you believe.” He says God cares that you believe what He believes, and that we must change our thinking when it doesn’t line up with His.
Should we speak God’s words or our own opinions?

Hallelujah. Speak My words, not your opinions, not what you believe. God doesn’t care what you believe; He cares that you believe what He believes. And we got to change our belief, and we got to change our thinking when it doesn’t line up with His. “Whether they hear, whether they refuse, for they are a rebellious house. But you, son of man, hear what I say to you. Do not be rebellious like the rebellious house.” Don’t follow their ways. Don’t accept their speech. Don’t accept their behavior. Don’t follow their ways. And this is what’s happening in America today: dumbed-down Christians, because they really don’t get into the Bible and seek God. Don’t know the Bible, and they let these famous authors and these famous mega-church pastors tell them what God is saying, and they’re not telling them what God is saying. They’re telling them what they believe. God. Hallelujah. How many want to be able to speak the word of God? Yeah. Doesn’t matter what your opinion is, especially if you got one of these criminals in your home. He says the scroll Ezekiel was told to eat was written with judgment, mourning and woe, because there is a judgment of God. He says God corrects us now, and if we do not get corrected, He will correct us for eternity.

us. Now number five, verses 9 and 10: eat the scroll of the book. He gave him a scroll of the book written on both sides, and it was written not with Disneyland scriptures, not with positive scriptures. hell. They were all goody [unclear]. I swear, I couldn’t believe it. And I knew a lot of these people through other acquaintances of theirs. lives. And I don’t care how you were baptized. Amen. apologize. I don’t have to say, “I don’t wear my religion on my sleeve.” If I’m going to be a light to the world, they’re supposed to see you. little. And that’s where America is. “Don’t tell us the truth. He says some ministers do it to keep their ministry and get members so they can get rich on tithes and offerings. He says Paul and Peter were beaten, stoned and put in prison because they spoke truth, and that speaking truth will get people disliking you.

From Ezekiel 2 he lists: do not be afraid of them, do not be afraid of their words or dismayed by their looks, and speak God’s words. He later adds eating the scroll, which carries the judgment Scriptures.
What replaces fear in a Christian walk?
He says “courage replaces fear,” so that you do not even think about retaliation or offending.
Does God care what we believe?
He says God doesn’t care what you believe; He cares that you believe what He believes, and we must change our thinking when it doesn’t line up with His.

He says they don’t get into the Bible and seek God, and let famous authors and pastors tell them what God is saying, and so they speak opinions and beliefs instead of the word of God.

He says there is no way into the kingdom but one, and that is through Christ. You cannot bend the scriptures to get someone accepted.
Does “God is love” mean He doesn’t correct us?
He says God is love, and the Bible says a father who loves his child will discipline and correct him to spare him from death and destruction, and the spiritual Father does the same with us.

He says the scroll was written on both sides with the judgmental scriptures of lamentations, mourning and woe, not with “positive scriptures,” because there is a judgment of God.

He says yes, and points to Jesus telling a man to go and sin no more lest something worse come upon him: God will correct you now, and if you don’t turn around, He will correct you for eternity.

He calls it a judgment scripture to believers who are weak, sick and die before their time because they do not learn and recognize the body of the Lord Jesus Christ, which is His church.
What does he say is the focus and goal of God?
He says the focus and goal of God is that you live right and speak right, bridle your tongue and bridle your body. When you make mistakes, you repent, get up and keep going.

He says they told Isaiah, “Do not prophesy to us right things, but speak to us smooth things, flattery,” and to prophesy deceits.
What does he say happened to Paul and Peter when they spoke truth?
He says they were beaten, stoned and put in prison because they spoke truth, and that if you speak truth, you will get people disliking you.

p: In “Why Is the U.S. Church Mocked and Rejected?”, Pastor David G. Kincer reviews America’s four great spiritual awakenings and says the church fell asleep while the enemy sowed tares. He says Christians invite mockery by speech that sounds insane and by behavior no different from the world, including fighting over doctrines that hurt no one. His answer is to stop shunning those who disagree, live by the two commandments of love, do good, and respond with love.
What were America’s great spiritual awakenings?

He asks why the U.S. church is mocked and rejected and says history records four great awakenings, the first in 1730 before the Revolutionary War and the second from 1800 to 1840, which addressed alcohol, tobacco, slavery and women’s rights.
What were America’s great spiritual awakenings?

And we thank you and appreciate you joining us in further pursuit of clarity on crucial choices. Today we’re going to ask the question: has the United States of America church made the best choices? Or, why is the United States church mocked and rejected today? Now, we know from history there have been four great spiritual awakenings. The first was in 1730, preceding the Revolutionary War and preparing us for it. The second was in 1800 through 1840, where alcohol, tobacco, the abolition of slavery and women’s rights was addressed.
Why does the church keep needing revival?

He describes the third and fourth awakenings and says that when you go to sleep you have to be reawakened. From Matthew 13:25 he says that while men slept the enemy sowed tares among the wheat, and that is what happens when the church goes to sleep.
Why does the church keep needing revival?

The third one was 1850 through the 1900s, and pre- and post-Civil War, and they address the social ills of the drunks, the orphans, the widows and so forth. The fourth was in 1948 through ‘80, where the Holy Spirit was poured out, miracles happened, praise and worship was introduced to the church, unity. And in the, the secular world, In God We Trust was put on our money in 1954, and One Nation Under God was put in our pledge in 1956, and throughout the ‘50s millions of Americans made a decision to serve Jesus Christ. Now, why do we need four awakenings? Well, when you go to sleep, you have to be reawakened, either by yourself naturally or an alarm. In Matthew 13:25 Jesus said, while men slept, his enemies came and sowed tares among the wheat. So the children of the wicked one, the children of Satan, among the wheat, while men slept. And so that’s what happens when the church goes to sleep: we need an awakening. In the ‘60s, Bible, prayer and Jesus was put out of public places and public schools; the sexual revolution and evolution was replacing them.
Why does the church keep needing revival?
Matthew 13:25: but while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat and went his way.
Why do people think Christians are crazy?

He traces what replaced the Bible in each decade since the 1960s and says the gap between awakenings has been 10, 30 and 50 years. He says Christians talk “like they’re crazy,” citing 1 Corinthians 14:9 and 14:23.
Why do people think Christians are crazy?

In the ‘70s, abortion, drugs, homosexual agenda and rock and roll was the main focus of America. In the ‘80s, corrupt activist leaders fighting against these evils, and corrupt ministers and priests were exposed; many gave up the fight and left the enemy seeds to grow by themselves. In the ‘90s, psychology, grace and faith, entertainment, seeker-friendly church, intellectual reasoning replaced the Holy Spirit’s power and the power of the Bible. It took between the previous awakenings was 10, 30 and 50 years. There is 30 years between the last awakening and the one we are looking for. Now, what are the reasons for mockery and rejection of Christians? Christians talk like crazy, like they’re crazy. First Corinthians 14:9: unless you utter by the tongue words easy to understand. Verse 23: they will, will they not say that you are out of your mind? You are, you people are nuts.
Why do people think Christians are crazy?

1 Corinthians 14:9: So likewise you, unless you utter by the tongue words easy to understand, how will it be known what is spoken? For you will be speaking into the air. 1 Corinthians 14:23: Therefore if the whole church comes together in one place, and all speak with tongues, and there come in those who are uninformed or unbelievers, will they not say that you are out of your mind?
Is it a blessing to be insulted as a Christian?

From 1 Peter 4:14 he says you are blessed if insulted for the name of Christ, but not if insulted as an evildoer. He says “once saved, always saved” is insane talk, because you got to back up your salvation with proper behavior.
Is it a blessing to be insulted as a Christian?

In First Peter 4:14, if you’re insulted because of the name of Christ, you are blessed, and happy are you. But if you’re insulted as an evildoer, you are not blessed. And so our behavior and our speech invite mockery and rejection and insults. Eternal salvation: here’s some, a list of some insane Christian speech. Once saved, always saved from sin, sin’s penalty, that they have wrath, and Satan. That’s like saying the blind man and the leper and all them that got healed from their diseases would never have to be delivered from sickness again, when Jesus said, go and sin no more, lest something worse come upon you. You don’t get something for nothing; you got to back up your salvation with proper behavior.
Is it a blessing to be insulted as a Christian?

1 Peter 4:14-15: If you are reproached for the name of Christ, blessed are you, for the Spirit of glory and of God rests upon you. On their part He is blasphemed, but on your part He is glorified. But let none of you suffer as a murderer, a thief, an evildoer, or as a busybody in other people’s matters. John 5:14: Afterward Jesus found him in the temple, and said to him, “See, you have been made well. Sin no more, lest a worse thing come upon you.”
Does faith alone make you rich or healthy?

He calls “faith only” and “pray only” talk insane: believing God will make you rich without a job skill, healthy without doctors, or employed without education. He says constantly announcing Jesus is coming any minute makes Christians sound like idiots.
Does faith alone make you rich or healthy?

Another one is faith only. All I got to do is believe God, get rich, don’t have to go to college, don’t have to learn a job skill. God, God, faith to get me rich, faith will get me healthy, faith to get me healing, don’t need medicine, I don’t need doctors. Uh, eternal life, faith is all there is, no matter how I live, I, faith is it. Pray only: pray for a job, don’t have to get in a job skill, don’t have to get an education, just pray for a job; pray for healing; pray to pass the college examination or my [unclear] test; just pray; just pray for the wicked to be saved in America, that’s all I got to do. You know, that’s insane talk. Imminent or predicted time of Jesus’ return: for hundreds of years the church world, he’s coming any minute, he’s coming soon, he’s coming in a minute, he’s coming soon, and he hasn’t come any minute and he hasn’t come soon. So we sound like a bunch of idiots.
Should Christians predict when Jesus will return?

He says authors predicted years for Christ’s coming and all missed, and that claiming to interpret Revelation, Daniel and Ezekiel, tongues without interpretation, false healings and failed prophecy invite the insults.
Should Christians predict when Jesus will return?

Then we predicted years, from LaHaye to all these other authors predicting the coming of Christ, and they all missed, including, uh, Smith of Calvary Chapel. We claim interpretation of the books in the Bible, of Revelation and Daniel and Ezekiel, when the authors didn’t even know what they meant, but oh, we know what they mean, and we sound crazy. Tongues without interpretation: First Corinthians plainly says people are going to think you’re nuts. False healings: people have been proclaimed to be healed that died. Prophecy that didn’t come to pass. And so yes, when we talk like that, when our doctrines and our speeches like that, the humanists think we are a bunch of nuts. We invite the insults.
Why do Christians divide over doctrine?

He says Christians divide over sectarian issues that hurt no one, such as water baptism, tongues, worship, women in ministry, hair and clothing, and asks why we fight over them. He says when believers sin like others, outsiders say “you’re no different than I am.”
Why do Christians divide over doctrine?

And so we’re going to look into why Christians are insulted and mocked because of their behavior. Sectarian issues that we divide over that directly hurt no one, like water baptism, tongues, worship, second coming, anointing or holy water, women in the ministry, hair, clothing, jewelry and so forth. They hurt nobody. Why in the world do we fight and argue over things that don’t physically or financially, mentally hurt anybody? And the humanists look at us and go, man, you guys are a bunch of crackpots, all of you are saying the different things. And so they insult us and they mock us, and we invite it in our behavior. We may, we commit crime or sin that humanists commit or don’t commit; as the Bible says, even the pagans don’t do this, he told the Corinthian church. And yet we say we got eternal life and they’re going to the lake of fire, and so the people outside of the church go, that’s insane, that’s nuts, you’re no different than I am.
Why do Christians divide over doctrine?
1 Corinthians 5:1: It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and such sexual immorality as is not even named among the Gentiles—that a man has his father’s wife!

From Galatians 5 and the Ten Commandments he lists what Christians must avoid, and says Christians are to work, provide for themselves and assemble one day to worship. When we violate these, he says, we invite mockery.

And Galatians 5:20 plainly tells us how Christians are supposed to be behaving: no idolatry, no sorcery, no witchcraft, no hatred, no quarreling and jealousies and outburst of anger, selfish ambition, I gotta have it my way or no way, rebellion, heresies, we invent our own doctrines, envy, murders, drunkenness, unlawful sex, whether it’s homosexuality, adultery, incest or whatever. Plus you got the Ten Commandments: thou shall not murder, steal; you’re supposed to honor your parents; you’re not supposed to be greedy; you’re not supposed to lie. And Christians are supposed to work and provide for their own self, and you put one day aside and you assemble in the church to learn about God and worship him. And so when we violate these things, the humanists, they mock us and they laugh at us, because we invite it by our behavior as well as our speech. In James 4:17:

Galatians 5:19-21: Now the works of the flesh are evident, which are: adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lewdness, idolatry, sorcery, hatred, contentions, jealousies, outbursts of wrath, selfish ambitions, dissensions, heresies, envy, murders, drunkenness, revelries, and the like; of which I tell you beforehand, just as I also told you in time past, that those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
Quoting James 4:17 and 1 Peter 3:10, he says “Christianity is about doing good.” From 1 Peter 2:14 he says we need to be involved in politics and government to promote good.

He who knows to do good and does not do it, to him it is sin. Christianity is about doing good. First Peter 3:10: let him refrain his tongue from evil and his tongue from deceit; let him turn from evil and do good; let him seek peace and pursue it. We’re supposed to be people that do good, folks. First Peter 2:14: governors are for the punishment of evildoers and for the praise of those who do good. And so we need to be involved in politics and in government, because we need to be promoting good, and that’s what Christianity is, it’s good. Now, how do we prevent insane and insult reactions? Many theological doctrines directly hurt no one.

James 4:17: Therefore, to him who knows to do good and does not do it, to him it is sin. 1 Peter 3:10-11: For “He who would love life And see good days, Let him refrain his tongue from evil, And his lips from speaking deceit. Let him turn away from evil and do good; Let him seek peace and pursue it. 1 Peter 2:14: or to governors, as to those who are sent by him for the punishment of evildoers and for the praise of those who do good.
What two commandments sum up the Bible?

He says to stop shunning those who disagree with our petty doctrines, because the whole Bible hangs on two commandments: love God, and love your neighbor as yourself. He adds Romans 13 (love does no harm) and Matthew 7:12 (treat others as you would have them treat you).
What two commandments sum up the Bible?

So let’s stop mistreating and shunning those that disagree with our petty little doctrines. We got more important things to work on. The Bible now is summed up in two doctrines. The Bible says on these two doctrines hang all the law and the prophets, the whole book. Another scripture says it is the law and the prophets. And these two doctrines summarize the Bible, and humanists are wrong when they say the Bible is a bunch of lies, because there’s nothing wrong with these two doctrines. First one is to love God, Matthew 22:40. And Romans 13 tells us that love does no harm to his neighbor, therefore love fulfills the law, and everyone has to agree we should not be harming each other, whether you’re a humanist, an atheist or a Christian. That is a good law, and that sums up the Bible. The next one is love your neighbor as yourself, that’s the second one. And to clarify it, he says in Matthew 7:12, treat others as you would have them treat you.
What two commandments sum up the Bible?

Matthew 22:37-40: Jesus said to him, “‘You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’ This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like it: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ On these two commandments hang all the Law and the Prophets.” Romans 13:10: Love does no harm to a neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of the law. Matthew 7:12: Therefore, whatever you want men to do to you, do also to them, for this is the Law and the Prophets.
What is love, according to 1 Corinthians 13?

He reads that love is patient and kind, not envious, rude or proud, doesn’t demand its own way, and never gives up. He says Bible morality, doing good, is the priority doctrine, and 1 Corinthians 5:11 deals with harmful behavior, not theology.
What is love, according to 1 Corinthians 13?

You don’t want robbed, don’t rob. You don’t want people talking bad about you, don’t talk about bad about other people, you see. And how can anyone fault that issue? First Corinthians 13 clarifies love: patience; love is kind; it’s not envious; it’s not rude; it’s not proud; it doesn’t brag about itself; doesn’t promote evil; doesn’t think evil; is not eagerly angered, easily angered; and it doesn’t demand its own way. Here it is again, I want my way. And it never quits; love never gives up. So the bottom line is, Bible morality, doing good, is the priority doctrine of the Bible and what the Bible is all about. First Corinthians 5:11 says if there’s a brother who claims to be a Christian and he is sexually immoral, he’s greedy, he’s a, he’s an idolater, a drunkard, an extortioner, don’t keep company with him. You say, there is no theology listed here, just harmful behavior by believers, how we’re supposed to react to believers who are sinning, so that they can correct themselves.
What is love, according to 1 Corinthians 13?

1 Corinthians 13:4-7: Love suffers long and is kind; love does not envy; love does not parade itself, is not puffed up; does not behave rudely, does not seek its own, is not provoked, thinks no evil; does not rejoice in iniquity, but rejoices in the truth; bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. 1 Corinthians 5:11: But now I have written to you not to keep company with anyone named a brother, who is sexually immoral, or covetous, or an idolater, or a reviler, or a drunkard, or an extortioner—not even to eat with such a person.
How should Christians respond to being mocked?

He says civil government is there to punish evildoers and honor the good, not to enforce theology, and God will deal with spiritual things. His conclusion: speak and behave so as not to invite mockery, and respond with love.
How should Christians respond to being mocked?

No theology at all. Romans 13 again says civil penalty of evildoers: the civil government’s there to penalize evildoers, to punish them for correction, not theology, and they’re there to honor the good. God and spiritual things, God can and will deal with them. And the conclusion is this: we need as Christians to speak and behave in a manner that doesn’t invite these things, and respond with love to love violators. That’s the way of our Creator.
How should Christians respond to being mocked?

Romans 13:3-4: For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to evil. Do you want to be unafraid of the authority? Do what is good, and you will have praise from the same. For he is God’s minister to you for good. But if you do evil, be afraid; for he does not bear the sword in vain; for he is God’s minister, an avenger to execute wrath on him who practices evil.
When was the fourth awakening he describes?
He says 1948 through 1980, when the Holy Spirit was poured out, miracles happened and praise and worship came into the church.
What does he say happened in the 1960s?
He says the Bible, prayer and Jesus were put out of public places and schools, replaced by the sexual revolution and evolution.
What does he say replaced the Holy Spirit’s power in the 1990s?
He names psychology, entertainment, the seeker-friendly church and intellectual reasoning.
What does 1 Corinthians 14 say about speech in church?
He says unless you speak words easy to understand, people will say you are out of your mind.
What does he say about “once saved, always saved”?
He says you don’t get something for nothing; you got to back up your salvation with proper behavior.
What is wrong with “just pray” for a job or healing?
He says praying without getting a job skill or education, or without medicine and doctors, is insane talk.
What does he say about tongues without interpretation?
He says First Corinthians plainly says people are going to think you’re nuts.
Which doctrines does he say Christians should stop fighting over?
He lists water baptism, tongues, worship, the second coming, anointing, women in the ministry, hair, clothing and jewelry, which he says hurt nobody.
Should Christians be involved in politics?
He says yes, because governors are for punishing evildoers and praising those who do good, and Christians need to be promoting good.
He quotes Matthew 7:12, treat others as you would have them treat you: if you don’t want to be robbed, don’t rob.
How should the church treat a believer living in sin?
From 1 Corinthians 5:11 he says don’t keep company with them, so that they can correct themselves.

items.d: In this message, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches on the “young men” stage of 1 John 2: those who have overcome the wicked one by the blood of the Lamb, the word of their testimony and sacrifice. He calls…
p: In this message, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches on the “young men” stage of 1 John 2: those who have overcome the wicked one by the blood of the Lamb, the word of their testimony and sacrifice. He calls forgiveness the top weapon, tells stories of hurting young people, and ends with the armor of God, alertness, and speaking the word.
What does he say marks the “young men” stage? (1 John 2:13, John 15:5)

He says the young men have “overcome the wicked one” and are “victorious over Satan,” that “they’re not weak at all,” and that “they don’t follow a group, they’re not sectarian, they don’t quarrel, they just stand for truth.” He adds that “you don’t have to argue when you know you’re right,” and that “the word of God abides in you,” citing John 15:5, “you will be fruitful.”
What does he say marks the “young men” stage? (1 John 2:13, John 15:5)

And today we’re going to hit the stage of spiritual growth that John, in 1 John chapter 2, calls the young men stage. John gives us these stages of growth, and this is the young men stage. John calls it very powerful. Stage, 1 John 2:13: “I write unto you, young men, because you have overcome the wicked one.” Hallelujah. Or overcome evil, overcome bad, overcome harm, you’re victorious over Satan, you’re victorious over evil. Hallelujah, it’s very powerful. Now, how many Christians do you know are at the young men’s stage? “I have written unto young men because you are strong.” You are powerful, you are not weak. See, what was the problem with the newborn? They were weak, they were carnal, they were jealous, they quarreled, they followed little heroes, and they followed little groups, and they had problems in the flesh with sexual immorality and anger and hatred and heresies and so forth. But the young men’s stage, they’re not weak at all. They don’t give in to the flesh. You see, they don’t follow a group, they’re not sectarian, they don’t quarrel, they just stand for truth. You don’t have to argue when you know you’re right, you don’t have to argue, you don’t have to defend yourself. Powerful, strong. Number three: “The word of God abides in you.” And he repeats that they’ve overcome the wicked one. The word of God abides in you. The Bible tells us that Jesus is the living word, the bread that came down, the living bread that came down from heaven, so Jesus is abiding in him. In John 15:5 Jesus said, “If you abide in me and my words abide in you, you will be fruitful.” See, the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, patience, gentleness, kindness, meekness, temperance, and faith. You see, this is where God wants us to go; he wants us to grow and obtain these things, and this stage, they are obtaining.
What does he say marks the “young men” stage? (1 John 2:13, John 15:5)

1 John 2:13: I write to you, fathers, Because you have known Him who is from the beginning. I write to you, young men, Because you have overcome the wicked one. I write to you, little children, Because you have known the Father. John 15:5: “I am the vine, you are the branches. He who abides in Me, and I in him, bears much fruit; for without Me you can do nothing. Galatians 5:22-23: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Against such there is no law.
How does he say we overcome the wicked one? (Revelation 12:11, Romans 12:1)

He says “they overcame Satan by the blood of the Lamb,” which “cleanses us from all sin,” and that when Satan accuses, “I overcome Satan’s accusations by going back to the blood, going back to the cross, and asking for forgiveness.” He says too many Christians “fail 10 or 15 times on one issue and they quit,” and that we also overcome by the scriptures and by sacrifice, quoting Job: “Though God slay me, yet will I trust him.”
How does he say we overcome the wicked one? (Revelation 12:11, Romans 12:1)

The word of God abides in you; they not only have a desire for the word, but the word of God is alive in them, it lives in them, both Jesus and the Word. Now, let’s look at overcoming the wicked one. All right, how do you overcome the wicked one? Revelations 12:11 says they overcame Satan by the blood of the Lamb. See, what does he mean by the blood of the Lamb? Well, the blood of the Lamb cleanses us from all sin. And so, see, when I mess up as a Christian, I do something I shouldn’t do, Satan comes and he accuses me: “You are no good, you need to quit faking it, quit pretending, and just leave, and quit acting like you’re a Christian, you need to give up on this Christianity.” But see, the blood tells me as a Christian I can go to Christ, and that same blood that cleansed me at the beginning and washed my sins away and delivered me from, is the same blood that will cleanse me today. So I overcome Satan’s accusations by going back to the blood, going back to the cross, and asking for forgiveness, turning from that sin, rising up, and keep walking in God. See, overcome Satan by the blood of the Lamb. Too many Christians, they fail 10 or 15 times on one issue and they quit and give up, but you got to go back to the blood and let the blood cleanse you, however many times it takes until you’re free from that sin. Could that be an amen? Yeah. See, that’s how we overcome Satan. He accuses us, and you know, he’s got a lot to accuse us about. You, we say we’re Christians, we look in the mirror and go, “Wow, I’m a mess,” and so Satan brings these things out, but we overcome him by the blood of the Lamb. Secondly, you overcome by the word of their testimony. See, when Satan accused Jesus in the garden, Satan asked Jesus to make stones bread and jump down off the pinnacle of the temple, and, uh, Jesus always answered, “It is written.” He always answered the scriptures, and so we overcome Satan by, what? Referring to the scriptures. Hallelujah, so it’s important that that word abides in us. You see, the word of their testimony, and “they love not their lives unto death.” And remember, in the past we’ve told you, Romans 12:1: “Present your body as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable unto God. Don’t be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind.” Okay, so we offer our bodies a living sacrifice, we sacrifice to serve God and not give into sin and not follow the crowd to do evil. That’s how you love your life and death. Okay, and remember Job said, “Though God slay me, yet will I trust him.” Things may be going bad, finances may be difficult, your health may be down, the family may have problems, you know, there may be trouble all around you, like the song said, but you keep serving Christ, even though it’s a sacrifice, it’s not going easy, but you sacrifice, and that’s how we overcome Satan.
How does he say we overcome the wicked one? (Revelation 12:11, Romans 12:1)

Revelation 12:11: And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, and they did not love their lives to the death. 1 John 1:7: But if we walk in the light as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus Christ His Son cleanses us from all sin. Matthew 4:4: But He answered and said, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God.’ ” Romans 12:1: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your reasonable service. Job 13:15: Though He slay me, yet will I trust Him. Even so, I will defend my own ways before Him.
How do we resist the Devil? (James 4:7, 2 Corinthians 2:10)

He quotes James 4:7, “Resist the Devil and he will flee from you,” and “draw nigh to God and God will draw nigh to you,” and says we resist by praying, worshiping, going to church and reading the Bible. He says “just zip the lip,” since “even a fool is wise when he keeps his mouth shut.” From 2 Corinthians 2:10 he says “Satan doesn’t want you exercising forgiveness.”
How do we resist the Devil? (James 4:7, 2 Corinthians 2:10)

And we overcome evil. James 4:7 says, “Resist the Devil and he will flee from you.” So we got to resist him, we got to put up some resistance, and he goes on to say in the next verse that if you draw nigh to God, he tells us how to resist Satan: “Draw nigh to God and God will draw nigh to you.” So I resist Satan by what? Praying, worshiping, going to church, getting in the Bible studies, reading my Bible. I resist Satan by pursuing God. Hallelujah. And he says, “Cleanse your hands,” and don’t speak evil of one another. Don’t let Satan get you into measuring other people by you or you by other people. Just zip the lip. The Bible says even a fool is wise when he keeps his mouth shut. Learn to zip the lip. That’s how you resist the Devil.
