You know, you don’t got to attack everybody every time you, you know, you get opposed by somebody, especially in your home. Just zip the lip. Resist the Devil. The Devil loves for you to start speaking out. And then in 2 Corinthians 2:10, this is really good: “Whom you forgive anything,” Paul says, writing to the Corinthians, “whom you forgive anything, I forgive also. Whom you pardon anything, I pardon also. Whom you release anything, I release also, lest Satan get advantage of us, for we are not ignorant of his devices.” Satan doesn’t want you exercising forgiveness. Why? Because when you don’t forgive, you open the door to anger, you open the door to hatred, you open the door to conflict between you and the person, separation.
How do we resist the Devil? (James 4:7, 2 Corinthians 2:10)

James 4:7: Therefore submit to God. Resist the devil and he will flee from you. Proverbs 17:28: Even a fool is counted wise when he holds his peace; When he shuts his lips, he is considered perceptive. 2 Corinthians 2:10: Now whom you forgive anything, I also forgive. For if indeed I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven that one for your sakes in the presence of Christ,
Why does he call forgiveness the top weapon of the young men stage?

He says “forgiveness is a top weapon of the young men stage” and “if nothing else, you will free yourself.” He says people either forgive themselves and go on sinning or stay down defeated, but “we should forgive ourselves for doing wrong, get up and start doing right.”
Why does he call forgiveness the top weapon of the young men stage?

Forgiveness is a top weapon of the young men stage. Forgiveness is a very important weapon. Okay, forgiveness: you pardon, you give freedom. If nothing else, you will free yourself. Hallelujah. Very, very powerful weapon. People either forgive themselves and go on sinning, or they don’t forgive themselves and stay down and become defeated. But we should forgive ourselves, get up, and walk in the pathway that’s right. Amen. We should forgive ourselves for doing wrong, get up and start doing right, not just forgive myself and then go back and do it again, and go back and do it again, and knowing you’re going to go back and do it again. Or people don’t forgive themselves; there’s people that just can’t believe that God will forgive them, and they can’t forgive themselves, and so that brings guilt, that brings condemnation. But the young men stay just forgiving others, forgiving themselves, and getting up and doing what’s right and never quitting, and this is the top weapon of the young man stage: forgiveness. Now, let me explain a little further. The Bible opposes, is against, homosexuality and other sexual immorality. Okay, 30,000, over 30,000 people die every year in North America from sexually transmitted diseases, and so the Bible’s right.
What statistics does he cite, and what is his point?

He lists figures on sexually transmitted diseases, drug and alcohol deaths, child abuse, births to unwed mothers, divorce, abortion, sexual assault and suicide, saying “God is just trying to save you from harm and danger and evil,” and criticizing the government and public schools. His figures are as he stated them and are not verified here. He concludes “it is our job to preach the word.”
What statistics does he cite, and what is his point?

You know, why give yourself to something that’s going to harm you? The Bible opposes drug and alcohol intoxication. 177,000 people die every year and 1 million are injured from drug-related deaths and accidents. 85,000 die every year and 4 million are hurt from alcohol-related incidents. And so God is just trying to save you from harm and danger and evil. God is against abusing children, and yet in America 5 million children are abused every year, not just verbally but physically, sexually, and over 1,800 die from that abuse every year. 48% today are born to unwed mothers, and 44% of children in America live with a single-parent home, and God is against that. He wants us to marry, stay married, raise those kids in the way they should go; that’s God’s way. God is against witchcraft and idols and murder. We kill over a million babies every year in America. God’s against divorce, and yet there’s 50% divorcing. God’s against lies, teaching lies in education, and yet our public schools teach lies. God is against welfare without work, and yet our government is increasingly giving people money without any responsibility of working to earn that money. 93,000 males were raped last year in America. 70% of female soldiers are raped. 7%, or 140,000, male soldiers are sexually abused and raped, and yet our government is wanting to give freedom to all of these sexually immoral practices, and it is hurting people. See, the Bible opposes that. There are 38,000 suicides every year, and a half a million people every year have self-inflicted injuries because of depression, loneliness, wanting to give up. Now, it is our job to preach the word.
What statistics does he cite, and what is his point?
Proverbs 22:6: Train up a child in the way he should go, And when he is old he will not depart from it.
Why must the church forgive as well as preach? (Luke 24:47, 1 John 1:9)

He says “the church must preach the word, but we must also forgive,” so “we oppose them with a forgiving attitude.” Citing Luke 24:47 and 1 John 1:9, he says “there is a requirement, not just to admit you’re wrong, but there’s a requirement to, what? Turn from the wrong.” He also says civil government “is there to correct by punishing people for doing wrong.”
Why must the church forgive as well as preach? (Luke 24:47, 1 John 1:9)

Okay, but if you don’t have forgiveness and forgive these people for what they do, or it could have happened to you, and if you don’t have this forgiveness power in you, you’re going to walk around depressed and heavy and angry, resentful, and if nothing else, it will free you. And so the church must preach the word, but we must also forgive so that they can come in, hear the word, and get free. You understand? So there’s a balance between, no one, God opposes these things, so we oppose them, but we oppose them with a forgiving attitude. Repent: Luke 24:47, “repentance for remission,” or for forgiveness, “of sin should be preached.” 1 John 1:9: “If we confess our sin, he is faithful and just to forgive.” So if we confess and we turn from our sin, God will forgive us. So there is a requirement, not just to admit you’re wrong, but there’s a requirement to, what? Turn from the wrong. Hallelujah. See, how else are you going, see, civil government is there to correct by punishing people for doing wrong. They are there to correct them by punishment, either a fine or a beating or a, uh, house arrest, you know, secluded place, or, you know, something should be done to get their attention. But see, our civil government is more and more not correcting people, they are approving of harmful lifestyles. Isn’t that true? Yeah. Just since the ‘50s it’s been a dynamic turnaround. See, and so when somebody hurts me, my responsibility is to admit I’m hurt. That hurt, my spirit is wounded.
Why must the church forgive as well as preach? (Luke 24:47, 1 John 1:9)

Luke 24:47: and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in His name to all nations, beginning at Jerusalem. 1 John 1:9: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
How does forgiveness free you, and what about perceived hurt? (Matthew 6:15)

He says that when someone hurts you, “forgive them immediately,” because “forgiveness means you’re pardoned, you are free.” He says “I forgive them ahead of time,” and that “a lot of people are hurt totally from perception,” not from what the other person meant. He cites “if you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your heavenly Father forgive your trespasses.”
How does forgiveness free you, and what about perceived hurt? (Matthew 6:15)

But if I don’t repent from that, and I want that person, God, put a [unclear] and strike them dead, or let him get in an accident, or let something bad happen, you know, get them, God, and the Bible says in the Old Testament, when you want God to get them, he won’t get him, because see, your attitude’s wrong. And this is why you’re wrong: because you make mistakes and you don’t want God getting you until you have a chance to correct it, am I right? Hallelujah. So this person hurts me, does really something bad to me, he say I must forgive them immediately so that anger, resentment does not arise and I wind up reacting and hurting them, then the thing I didn’t want them to do to me, now I’m doing. Are you out there? So see, forgiveness: I go to God, “I’m hurt, I want that guy to pay for what he did to me,” and I’m wrong. “I want you to forgive me, Lord, forgive me. I forgive that person that hurt me.” Now, that doesn’t change that person at all, but it changes you. See, now you’re free. See, forgiveness means you’re pardoned, you are free. See, you’re free from the penalty of the wrong that you’re doing, and you’re free from the hurt that that person put on you, because now you’ve forgiven him. Hallelujah. See, it’s amazing, but it is a powerful principle in God. Someone once told, well, several people have told me that nothing seems to bother you. No, it doesn’t, because I learned to forgive them. I know they’re going to hurt me, so when they hurt me, I’ve already forgiven them. I forgive them ahead of time, because the Bible says offenses are going to come, people are going to offend you. Now, this same person may not have done anything to hurt me, and here’s, here’s where you need to listen: I just perceive that they did something to hurt me. I perceive that they said something they didn’t say or meant something they didn’t mean. I perceived it, I supposed it. See, I supposed their action was out to get me, and so I get hurt, not because they actually hurt me, but because my perception was that they hurt me, so I’m just as hurt. Are you there? And honestly, being a pastor and talking to a lot of people, a lot of people are hurt totally from perception. The other person didn’t really mean it that way at all, but they got to get forgiveness the same way. You see, and then you go to that person and say, “I forgive you what you did wrong to me,” and they go, “What? I didn’t say that, I didn’t do that, I didn’t mean that,” and then you get hurt again. You won’t be honest, you know, you just won’t admit you need to get before God and repent. See, now we’re back into our bad attitude again. You see how forgiveness is very important. Yeah. Matthew 16:15 says, “If you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your heavenly Father forgive your trespasses.”
How does forgiveness free you, and what about perceived hurt? (Matthew 6:15)

Matthew 6:15: But if you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses. Luke 17:1: Then He said to the disciples, “It is impossible that no offenses should come, but woe to him through whom they do come!
What do Jesus and Stephen show about forgiveness, and how does he say to treat other believers? (Luke 23:34, Acts 7:60, 1 Peter 2:22–23)

He says “spouses need to forgive each other, parents need to forgive their kids, kids need to forgive their parents.” He points to Jesus’s “Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do” and Stephen’s “Lord, don’t lay this sin to their charge.” He says “Christians have hatred and resentment for one another, especially if you don’t belong to my camp,” and that he accepts a profession of faith “until we have evidence that their life doesn’t match up.” He cites 1 Peter 2:22–23: Jesus “committed himself to God that judges righteously.”
What do Jesus and Stephen show about forgiveness, and how does he say to treat other believers? (Luke 23:34, Acts 7:60, 1 Peter 2:22–23)

Wow. So forgiveness is what? Very important in the home. You really need to exercise forgiveness, both from actual hurt from your family member or perceived hurt from your family member. Amen. See, spouses need to forgive each other, parents need to forgive their kids, kids need to forgive their parents, both from actual hurt or perceived hurt. It doesn’t matter, it’s still going to affect you. You’re going to get angry, you’re going to get resentful, you’re going to retaliate, you’re going to seek for revenge. Jesus was the example on the cross. He said, “Father, forgive them.” They killed him, they beat him, they stabbed him, they put a crown of thorns, they really mistreated him, they mocked him, they made fun of him, and he said, “Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.” Stephen was another example. All he wanted to do was show them a more perfect way in the scriptures, and they got angry at him. These were believers, got angry at Stephen and took him out and stoned him, and he said, “Lord, don’t lay this sin to their charge.” See, he forgave them, and all he wanted to do is help the believer. See, Christians have hatred and resentment for one another, especially if you don’t belong to my camp. I brought this, “Love one another,” the new commandment, God gave it recently in a foreign nation, and, man, they almost kicked me out of that nation to actually exercise loving other believers that wasn’t in your camp. We got to protect ourselves from false doctrines, and you can’t be with your sheep 24 hours a day to protect them from false doctrine. We’re to love one another, and you might learn something when you mix. When you accept people, somebody asked me Friday when I was witnessing what do I think about Obama, and I said, “Listen, it’s just like you, you say you’re a Christian. Obama says he’s a Christian until I know different and have fruit different, I have to accept his word.” Somewhere we got to accept one another, even if it’s at the embryo stage or the newborn stage, we got to accept until we have evidence that their life doesn’t match up. Could that be true? If a Catholic says, “I believe in Jesus, I’m a follower of Jesus,” it’s not my job to say, “Well, you can’t be and be a Catholic.” It is my job to love. The new commandment I give to you, Jesus said, “Love one another,” do no harm one to another. Amen. See, so you got to forgive, you got to forgive. The Bible says in 1 Peter 2:22-23 that when Jesus was spoken evil of, he didn’t speak evil back, and it says there he’s our example. You see, when he was hurt by people, he didn’t hurt back; when he was threatened, he didn’t threaten back, but this is the kicker: he committed himself to God that judges righteously. He just let it go, he forgave them and let God deal with it, and trust me, folks, God knows how to deal with us.
What do Jesus and Stephen show about forgiveness, and how does he say to treat other believers? (Luke 23:34, Acts 7:60, 1 Peter 2:22–23)

Luke 23:34: Then Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do.” And they divided His garments and cast lots. Acts 7:60: Then he knelt down and cried out with a loud voice, “Lord, do not charge them with this sin.” And when he had said this, he fell asleep. John 13:34: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another; as I have loved you, that you also love one another. 1 Peter 2:22-23: “Who committed no sin, Nor was deceit found in His mouth”; who, when He was reviled, did not revile in return; when He suffered, He did not threaten, but committed Himself to Him who judges righteously;
How does he say to confront sin with love, including homosexuality?

He says “we got to confront, but we got to have genuine love and genuine forgiveness,” so confrontation is not “just an argument.” He says “I do not hate homosexuals; I have led over 50 of them to Jesus Christ,” that “when you think you’re right there’s no need for repentance,” and “that’s not hate, that’s love.” He asks, “how in the world are you ever going to reach people if you’re afraid of them?”
How does he say to confront sin with love, including homosexuality?

He deals with us for our good; we have a tendency to deal with each other for our destruction. Are you there? So the balance between forgiveness and punishment for criminals is to love and forgive while we’re confronting. You see, we got to confront, but we got to have genuine love and genuine forgiveness so that our confrontation isn’t just an argument, “I’m right, you’re wrong,” it is an approach to bring them out of wrong. Hallelujah. So when people tell me, “I hate homosexuals because I tell them they’re going to hell,” they’re lying. I do not hate homosexuals; I have led over 50 of them to Jesus Christ. And it’s hard to lead them to Christ because everybody’s telling them they’re okay, and see, when you think you’re right there’s no need for repentance. So somebody has to give them the word that not only homosexuality is wrong, but adultery is wrong, and fornication’s wrong, and sex with children is wrong, and incest is wrong. All these things are wrong because God says they’re wrong, and he’s going to punish you eternally in the lake of fire if you don’t correct the wrong. Somebody’s got to tell them, and that’s not hate, that’s love. And yes, I go into their home and I eat with them. I don’t hate them. I’m not afraid to use their toilet that they sit on. You see, a lot of Christians want, oh man, they’re going, “I’m going to catch a disease.” I’m yeah, but you can be wise, you can be wise. You don’t have to ostracize people because you, you know, need to be safe; you can be wise. Are you there? See, when’s the last time you sat down with an adulterer, a prostitute, or a homosexual and ate at their table and sat on their toilet seat? And I said that because I meet so many Christians that are petrified they’re going to catch something. Well, how in the world are you ever going to reach people if you’re afraid of them? Are you there? Now, let me give you a little story. I’m going to call this lady Alice.
What story does he tell about a rejected teenager he calls “Alice”?

He says “this is a real person,” a teenager bullied at school, lonely at home with alcohol- and drug-using parents, who he says died after stepping between her parents during a fight. He asks, “wouldn’t it have been nice if teenagers at school would have really taken the time to understand that girl,” and “have you tried to understand the rejected one?” This is a sensitive account and is his own telling.
What story does he tell about a rejected teenager he calls “Alice”?

Alice is a teenager. This is a real person, things I’ve experienced in my lifetime. She’s bullied at school, mocked at school, she’s one of these oddballs, and she’s an oddball because at home her parents are alcohol and drug users, and they fight all the time. The money’s consumed with alcohol and drugs, there’s really not much in the home. She doesn’t have the stylish clothes to wear or anything else, she doesn’t even have exactly healthy food to eat. She’s kind of an unacceptable look, and teenagers hate unacceptable looks, so they mock and they make fun of them, but you teenagers wouldn’t do that, right? Yeah. She’s lonely, no one will be her friend at school, she’s lonely at home, she just has to go up to a room which has no bed. She just sleeps on the floor. So she comes home one day, and she’s going to church, she’s in our children’s church program, had been in it. She comes home one day and Mom and Dad are fighting, and Dad has a knife, and Dad is lunging, you know, at the mom, not necessarily to just, you know, being the macho man, but the daughter, Alice, sees it differently, and she steps in between Dad and Mom just as he lunges, and boom, in goes the knife. Well, the parents are petrified, they’re high on drugs, alcohol, if they call the police they’re in trouble, so they try to cover it up and they try to deal with it on their own. They don’t know that inside this girl is bleeding profusely, and the girl died, and they got caught. Anyway, wouldn’t it have been nice if teenagers at school would have really taken the time to understand that girl, and she would have a true friend, understand? Wouldn’t it be nice if the people of the church would have taken more time to understand that girl and help her get out? If you teenagers have ever done that, have you tried to understand the rejected one? Have you? Good, praise God.
What does he say about another young woman who “took a wrong turn”?

He says “too late to forgive for Alice, too late,” then describes a girl from a good Christian home who was hurt by feeling poor, turned to boyfriends who bought her things, and “took a wrong turn.” He says “her choices were destroying her,” and asks where were people “that would forgive.” He says “we have to confront sin for their good, but at the same time we got to forgive them and try to help them.” This is a sensitive account.
What does he say about another young woman who “took a wrong turn”?

See, we can mock and we can laugh and we reject people, but we need to find out if there’s something in their background, something in their life that we can help them with. Too late to forgive for Alice, too late. Let’s talk about Britney. Came from a good home, Christian parents, blue-collar dad, but she’s hurt because she don’t have the latest clothing and the latest electronics, and her mom and dad drive this 15-year-old used car. She’s embarrassed of her dad, she’s embarrassed of her home, she’s embarrassed, and so she gets a boyfriend who buys her stuff, you know, and then, of course, gets sex for it, and then he leaves her, and other boys buy stuff, and so she turns into a teenage prostitute. And this is a girl that went to the Vine church in La Habra several years, in our children’s church program, grew up to be a teenager, and then just took a wrong turn. She got an incurable sexually transmitted disease, and the last time I seen her was on the corner of [unclear] Boulevard in Cypress, very unhealthy looking, very anemic looking, and she was out there trying to pick up a trick. She looked at me and turned away, and I looked at her. Her choices were destroying her. And yes, where were people that would forgive and that would go beyond to help, beyond the children’s church program, beyond the teen program? Beyond, I don’t know what happened to that young lady, but when I saw her she was about 18 or 19 years old, and she didn’t look like she was going to live to the next year. Are you out there? There’s people hurting, and yes, we’re against sin, but at the same time we are for them changing. See, that’s the thing: yes, we have to confront sin for their good, but at the same time we got to forgive them and try to help them in their problem. Could that be an amen?
What does he say about holiday pressure on families?

He says “a lot of pressure on the homes during these holiday seasons,” with anger and resentment when families expect fancy gifts. He recalls a Thanksgiving when “all I could afford was cheese sandwiches,” and says “Thanksgiving is not in the food, it’s in the family, the love that you have for one another and the love you have for God.”
What does he say about holiday pressure on families?

Husbands and wives, lives, and, uh, every year at this time I get a lot of counseling, and it’s homes with the pressure on them to live up to some kind of holiday, uh, standard, and the guy especially if he’s out of work and not making a lot of money, man, the guilt trip is put on him. Now, we want fancy gifts, we want a fancy tree, we want, you, we want a big turkey, we want all this stuff, and you’re not getting it, you’re just a lousy man, and so anger comes up, resentment comes up, clashing in the home, and then they call me, this husband, and we spent hours talking, trying to get it sorted out. A lot of pressure on the homes during these holiday seasons. Kids have a lot of pressure, and, uh, they’re not getting gifts and they’re not being treated like the guy next door and all this, so they get depressed and they get cast down and they think life is meaningless. Somewhere we got to forgive people and just accept. You know, I told you before one Thanksgiving all I could afford was cheese sandwiches, and it was one of the best Thanksgivings I had, honestly, because it’s not in the food. Thanksgiving is not in the food, it’s in the family, the love that you have for one another and the love you have for God. That’s the richness of these holidays, and if you got a big spread, that’s fine too, but that’s not where it’s at. Could that be an amen, church?
What does he say about guilt and forgiving yourself?

He says “she’s got to forgive herself,” of a woman from the church who left her family for rich men, and says she never did and later died by suicide. He says “until we forgive ourselves we live under the guilt of it, the weight of it,” and that “forgiveness will set you free.” He says the church must forgive divorced people “so they can reach them,” and that without the balance of truth and forgiveness “you’re just going to separate people from you.” This is a sensitive account.
What does he say about guilt and forgiving yourself?

See, we need to forgive, we need the pardon, we need to set people free from having to line up to preconceived ideas that mean nothing in the end. Hallelujah. There was a married woman in the church, left a good husband and left her children for a rich man, then he left her and she got another rich man. As time went by, she really went mentally off, spent a lot of money on psychiatric treatment, trying to get help, trying to sort things out in her mind, because she’s got all this guilt. See, she’s got all this guilt built up, and we learned how can she get rid of the guilt? Through forgiveness. She’s got to forgive herself, she’s got to go to God who can only forgive, she’s got to forgive herself. And I find people have a hard time forgiving themselves. They did something really bad in the past. How many of you teenagers did something really bad in your past? Just one, two. Oh man, we got some good teens over here. Okay, how many teenagers have done something not so good, not so really bad in the past, just bad? All right, and you see, we can turn from that, but the guilt of it, until we forgive ourselves we live under the guilt of it, the weight of it, and we’re angry at ourself and we resent ourself. But forgiveness will set you free. You got to forgive yourself, and this woman never did, and she finally killed herself at an early age. A wasted life, because they don’t know the power of forgiveness, they didn’t grow to this place where they could forgive themselves. You see, somebody divorces, okay, God’s against divorce, somewhere the church has to forgive them for the divorce so they can reach them and get them to change and grow in God. Are you with me? You can’t just keep separating people. Somewhere the forgiveness of God has got to be powerful in the church, and yet we confront the truth so that they can repent and change, and without the balance of the two you’re just going to separate people from you, or you’re going to accept people the way they are and there’s no change because they don’t see a need for change, and so they go through life miserable and hurting other people because no one’s told them the truth. Hallelujah. Being strong. This youth chapter here, Ephesians 6:10, every youth group teaches on it two or three times a year: “Be strong in the Lord and in the power of his might. Put on the whole armor of God that you might be able to stand against the deceits of the Devil.”
What does he say about the armor of God, praying in the Spirit and being alert? (Ephesians 6:10, Romans 8:26)

Citing Ephesians 6:10, “Be strong in the Lord and in the power of his might,” he says “the armor is the armor of truth, righteousness, the gospel of peace, faith, salvation, and the word of God.” He adds “you pray in the Spirit, that’s an armor,” since “the Spirit knows how to pray,” and that “being watchful, being alert is a vital part of our armor.”
What does he say about the armor of God, praying in the Spirit and being alert? (Ephesians 6:10, Romans 8:26)

Okay, the armor is the armor of truth, righteousness, the gospel of peace, faith, salvation, and the word of God. All these are connected to the word. See, his word is a word of righteousness, truth is the word, the gospel of peace is the word, salvation is the word. See, all of these are the word, it’s connected to the word. That’s why it’s vital that we go through that child stage and get the word and keep the word. Amen. But most of them leave out the fact that you pray in the Spirit, that’s an armor, not your little “Now I lay me down to sleep, I pray the Lord my soul to keep,” but you get connected and you pray in the Spirit for your children, for your marriage, for the church, for your neighbor, because the Spirit knows how to pray. The Bible says you don’t know how to pray as you ought, that’s what the Bible says, but the Spirit knows. See, the Spirit knows how to pray through you to get you; we’re always praying for the other person, but the Spirit knows how to get to you through prayer to change you. Be alert. What soldier, even if he’s got weapons and he’s got a tank, the super tank and everything else, yet if he’s sleeping in that tank and not paying attention, the enemy is going to blow him up? So being watchful, being alert is a vital part of our armor, isn’t it? And speak confidently the mystery of the gospel.
What does he say about the armor of God, praying in the Spirit and being alert? (Ephesians 6:10, Romans 8:26)

Ephesians 6:10: Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord and in the power of His might. Romans 8:26: Likewise the Spirit also helps in our weaknesses. For we do not know what we should pray for as we ought, but the Spirit Himself makes intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. Ephesians 6:19: and for me, that utterance may be given to me, that I may open my mouth boldly to make known the mystery of the gospel,
Why does he say living the word is not enough?

He says “nothing happened till Jesus opened his mouth and started teaching the word,” and “our weapon is to speak the word, not just live the word.” He says “we got to confront, but we got to confront with what? Forgiveness.” He ends, “this is the young men stage: they are alert, they are prepared, they’ve overcome the wicked one,” and “let’s grow up.”
Why does he say living the word is not enough?

I was witnessing again this week and I was telling this guy, you know, he said he was a Christian, I said, you know, nothing happened till Jesus opened his mouth and started teaching the word. Nothing. He was God, but yet nothing happened because he was God until he started speaking the word, then people hated him or people loved him. I said, until you start speaking the word, you’re not going to stir up anybody. Our weapon is to speak the word, not just live the word. “I’m just going to live the word.” Living the word is great, Jesus lived it for 30 years, there was no sin, and he lived the word for 30 years, no one got saved, no one hated him, there was no problems until he opened his mouth and started speaking the word that he was living, then they wanted to kill him, or they wanted to love him and embrace him and follow him. See, no one was following Jesus till he opened up his mouth. There wasn’t crowds coming to Jesus’s house, not until he opened his mouth. Are you there, church? We got to open our mouth and we got to confront, but we got to confront with what? Forgiveness. Amen. “Alert” means to be attentive, to be prepared and ready to act. How many need some preparation in your life? Yes. And see, this is the young men stage: they are alert, they are prepared, they’ve overcome the wicked one, and they’re ready to roll. So this morning I challenge you, let’s grow up.
What does he say marks the young men stage?
He says John writes to young men “because you have overcome the wicked one,” and that they are “victorious over Satan.”
How does he contrast young men with newborn Christians?
He says the newborn “were weak, they were carnal, they were jealous, they quarreled,” while young men are “not weak at all” and “just stand for truth.”
How does he say we overcome Satan’s accusations?
He says “I overcome Satan’s accusations by going back to the blood, going back to the cross, and asking for forgiveness.”
What does he say about Job?
He quotes Job: “Though God slay me, yet will I trust him,” and says that even when finances and health are bad, “you keep serving Christ.”
What does he mean by “zip the lip”?
He says “you don’t got to attack everybody every time,” especially in your home: “Just zip the lip.”
Does he say to forgive yourself?
Yes, but he says “not just forgive myself and then go back and do it again.” He says to “forgive ourselves for doing wrong, get up and start doing right.”
Why does he say the church must preach and forgive?
He says “the church must preach the word, but we must also forgive so that they can come in, hear the word, and get free.”
Does he say forgiving changes the other person?
He says “that doesn’t change that person at all, but it changes you.”
What does he mean by perceived hurt?
He says “I get hurt, not because they actually hurt me, but because my perception was that they hurt me,” and that forgiveness applies to both.
Who does he say needs to forgive at home?
He says “spouses need to forgive each other, parents need to forgive their kids, kids need to forgive their parents.”
Does he say we should accept someone’s claim to be a Christian?
He says to accept it “until we have evidence that their life doesn’t match up,” and that “it is my job to love,” citing the new commandment, “love one another.”
What does he say about reaching people in sexual sin?
He says “somebody has to give them the word,” that “that’s not hate, that’s love,” and “yes, I go into their home and I eat with them.”
What does he say about Thanksgiving?
He says “Thanksgiving is not in the food, it’s in the family,” and recalls a year when “all I could afford was cheese sandwiches.”
Why does he say praying in the Spirit is part of the armor?
He says “you pray in the Spirit, that’s an armor,” because “the Spirit knows how to pray.”
Why does he say you must speak the word, not just live it?
He says Jesus lived the word for 30 years and “no one got saved, no one hated him” until “he opened his mouth and started speaking the word.”

items.d: No. Pastor Kincer says God is not just for emergencies — we need Him every day of our life.
p: No. Pastor Kincer says God is not just for emergencies — we need Him every day of our life.

He recalls that after 9/11 the churches filled with people praying, then emptied again in about 60 days, because people think God is only good for an immediate necessity. In the hospital, he says, he didn’t need a healer to come in — he needed the Healer, Jesus.

🎙 From the sermon “9/11 came and the churches were filled with people praying. See, that’s how quickly God can change things. But did it last? No. 60 days. Churches were empty again.” ▶ 16:05 “They think God is only good for an immediate necessity. And that God will be there at the snap of their finger. And they are totally wrong. We need him every day of our life.” ▶ 16:22 “I don’t need a healer to come in here. I need the Healer. Jesus. I’m not panicked.” ▶ 17:22 9/11 came and the churches were filled with people praying. that's how quickly God can change things But did it last? No. 60 days. Churches were empty again. They think God is only good for an immediate necessity. God will be there at the snap of their finger. We need him every day of our life. When I was dying in that hospital ... I don't need a healer to come in here. I need the Healer. Jesus. I'm not panicked ... I'm in his hands. He makes the decisions.
📖 Scripture (NKJV) Matthew 6:11 — Give us this day our daily bread.

items.d: No. God has no grandchildren and no stepchildren — only children.
p: No. God has no grandchildren and no stepchildren — only children.
Pastor Kincer says you have to be born again yourself and have your own first contact with Him. You can’t use your parents, your church or your minister as an excuse on judgment day.

🎙 From the sermon “The problem in America is if my granddad was a Baptist and my dad was a Baptist and I’m a Baptist, don’t bug me.” ▶ 13:19 “God does not have grandchildren. He does not have stepchildren. He has children. In other words, you got to get born again by him. You got to have that initial first contact with him.” ▶ 15:02 “I can’t use my parents for an excuse on judgment day. I can’t use my church or the minister on judgment day because I’m accountable to find him and serve him and follow him.” ▶ 15:27 if my granddad was a Baptist and my dad was a Baptist and I'm a Baptist, don't bug me If my granddad was a Catholic ... and I'm a Catholic, don't bug me God does not have grandchildren. He does not have stepchildren. He has children. you got to get born again by him You got to have that initial first contact with him. I can't use my parents for an excuse on judgment day. I can't use my church or the minister I'm accountable to find him and serve him and follow him.
📖 Scripture (NKJV) John 3:3 — Jesus answered and said to him, “Most assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”

items.t: Can the Word still turn a nation?
items.d: Yes. Pastor Kincer says that if the church gets the message out, the Word does the work — it convicts and convinces people.
p: Yes. Pastor Kincer says that if the church gets the message out, the Word does the work — it convicts and convinces people.
Pastor Kincer points to God’s promise that His word will not return void. He says it is the Word — not a denomination — that must get out, and the turning of a nation starts with the church.
Can the Word still turn a nation?

🎙 From the sermon “But if we can get the message out, and the word will work. Remember the Bible says the word will not return what? Void — but it will be profitable into the purpose that I have purposed it.” ▶ 31:16 “But it’s the word. It’s not the Catholics. It’s not the Protestants. It’s not the Jews. It’s the word that’s got to get out.” ▶ 31:32 “You speak the word and the word convicts and convinces people. The word does it. You don’t have to force them.” ▶ 32:12 Can the Word still turn a nation? Isaiah says God’s Word will not return unto Him void, but it will accomplish what He pleases. Pastor Kincer says it is the Word that must get out: it convicts and convinces people, and the turning of a nation starts with the church getting beyond its four walls.
Can the Word still turn a nation?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) Isaiah 55:11 — So shall My word be that goes forth from My mouth; It shall not return to Me void, But it shall accomplish what I please, And it shall prosper in the thing for which I sent it.

items.t: Do we only want to hear smooth things?
items.d: Many people do. They want to be told they’re okay, so they hire ministers to say what they want to hear instead of what is right.
p: Many people do. They want to be told they’re okay, so they hire ministers to say what they want to hear instead of what is right.
Pastor Kincer cites Isaiah 30:10, “Speak to us smooth things.” He says Scripture is given for righteousness and good works, but people don’t want to hear what is right.
Do we only want to hear smooth things?

🎙 From the sermon “There’s many groups doing what’s right in their own eyes, hiring and appointing ministers to flatter them, to please them, not God, as it says in Isaiah 30:10, speak to us smooth things, speak to us deceit, don’t speak to us right things.” ▶ 19:34 “We don’t want to hear about good works, we don’t want to hear about what’s right, we want to hear that we’re okay.” ▶ 20:08 “And so they get the money, they get the big fancy houses, they get the cars, they get the fame, they pay ministers to preach what they want to hear.” ▶ 20:12 Do we only want to hear smooth things? Isaiah says, “Prophesy not unto us right things, speak unto us smooth things, prophesy deceits.” Pastor Kincer says they pay ministers to preach what they want to hear. They want to be told they are okay, but Scripture is given for righteousness.
Do we only want to hear smooth things?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) Isaiah 30:10 — Who say to the seers, “Do not see,” And to the prophets, “Do not prophesy to us right things; Speak to us smooth things, prophesy deceits.” 2 Timothy 3:16 — All Scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness.

items.t: Should church be as consistent as a Big Mac?
items.d: In what is preached, yes. Pastor Kincer says the Holy Ghost, salvation, righteousness and holy living should be preached the same in every church.
p: In what is preached, yes. Pastor Kincer says the Holy Ghost, salvation, righteousness and holy living should be preached the same in every church.

Paul urged believers to speak the same thing, with no divisions. A Big Mac is identical in Brazil, Korea, China and every state, Pastor Kincer says — but in America church teaching isn’t, and that confuses everybody.
Should church be as consistent as a Big Mac?

🎙 From the sermon “He says, I want you to all speak the same thing.” ▶ 9:19 “I can go to McDonald’s, order a Big Mac and it’s identical. They didn’t change the Big Mac.” ▶ 9:38 “See, the Holy Ghost shouldn’t be preached different in one church and in another way in another church. It should be the what? Same. Salvation should be what? The same. Righteousness and holy living should be what? The same.” ▶ 10:38 “Everything should be the same like McDonald’s is, but in America, do we have that? No! And so we confuse everybody.” ▶ 10:53 Paul says, “I want you all to speak the same thing” (1 Corinthians 1:10). Pastor Kincer says that in Brazil, Korea, China or any state in America, a Big Mac is identical, the fries are the same, and the Coke is the real Coke. The Holy Ghost, salvation, righteousness and holy living should be preached the same way in every church, but in America they aren’t, and it confuses everybody.
Should church be as consistent as a Big Mac?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) 1 Corinthians 1:10 — Now I plead with you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.

items.d: It can feel that way. Pastor Kincer says church was boring to him as a teenager because he wasn’t involved and had lost his desire for Jesus.
p: It can feel that way. Pastor Kincer says church was boring to him as a teenager because he wasn’t involved and had lost his desire for Jesus.

Pastor Kincer contrasts that with David, who was glad when they said, “Let us go into the house of the LORD.” Pastor Kincer says the church is made up of people, and the people determine what a church is.

🎙 From the sermon “When I was 17, 16, 18, church is boring because I didn’t get involved. I wanted to do my thing.” ▶ 3:50 “Or we just lost our desire for Jesus.” ▶ 4:33 “David said, I was glad when they said unto me, let us what? Go to the house of the Lord. Man, he was excited. It’s assembly time. Oh, glory, let’s go.” ▶ 4:40 “But the church is made up of who? People. And it’s the people that are the determination of a church.” ▶ 5:00 Young people say church is boring. Pastor Kincer says he said the same thing at 16, 17 and 18, because he didn’t get involved and was a clock watcher. David said, “I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the LORD.” Many Christians have lost that gladness and blame the church, but the church is made up of people.
📖 Scripture (NKJV) Psalm 122:1 — I was glad when they said to me, “Let us go into the house of the LORD.”

items.t: Who was really crucified for you?
items.d: Christ was — not Paul, and not any church name, group or minister.
p: Christ was — not Paul, and not any church name, group or minister.

Corinth had four groups — “I am of Paul,” “of Apollos,” “of Cephas,” “of Christ.” Pastor Kincer says only the group focused on Christ is right, because only Christ can save — not a church name, group or minister.
Who was really crucified for you?

🎙 From the sermon “You’ve got four groups here and only one is right. Can you rationally, reasonably, logically tell me which group is right? Yeah, the Christ group.” ▶ 15:48 “He says, was Paul baptized or crucified for you? See, was the Pope crucified for Catholics? Can the Pope save Catholics? No.” ▶ 16:51 “They’re focused on Christ who can do something. Not their church name, not their church group, not some minister.” ▶ 17:29 “It is Christ and the Scriptures.” ▶ 17:41 “I am of Paul; and I of Apollos; and I of Cephas; and I of Christ.” Pastor Kincer says there were four groups in Corinth, and only one was right: the Christ group. Is Christ divided? No; He is one with the Father and the Scriptures. Was Paul crucified for you? No church name, church group or minister can save anyone. It is Christ and the Scriptures.
Who was really crucified for you?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) 1 Corinthians 1:12–13 — Now I say this, that each of you says, “I am of Paul,” or “I am of Apollos,” or “I am of Cephas,” or “I am of Christ.” Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?

items.t: What if a nation turns back to God?
items.d: God says He will relent from the judgment He planned. Pastor Kincer adds that Bible morality is an umbrella of protection when God judges.
p: God says He will relent from the judgment He planned. Pastor Kincer adds that Bible morality is an umbrella of protection when God judges.
Jeremiah shows both sides: a nation that won’t obey is plucked up, but one that turns from its evil is spared. That is why, Pastor Kincer says, we need to get the Word out.
What if a nation turns back to God?

🎙 From the sermon “If they will not obey, I will utterly pluck them up and destroy that nation.” ▶ 21:54 “But, Jeremiah 18:8, if that nation I have pronounced destruction, turn from their evil ways, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them.” ▶ 22:19 “You see, if we get them to embrace Bible morality, it is also an umbrella of protection when God judges.” ▶ 22:54 Jeremiah 18:8 says, “If that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them.” Pastor Kincer says God warns before He judges. If a nation turns from its evil ways and back to Bible morality, God can relent from the judgment He planned.
What if a nation turns back to God?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) Jeremiah 18:8 — if that nation against whom I have spoken turns from its evil, I will relent of the disaster that I thought to bring upon it. Jeremiah 12:17 — But if they do not obey, I will utterly pluck up and destroy that nation,” says the LORD.

items.t: Can a divided home still stand?
items.d: No. Jesus said a house divided against itself will not stand.
p: No. Jesus said a house divided against itself will not stand.

Pastor Kincer says husband and wife need to stand together in the same truth and moral standards, showing their children Jesus by their lives. When they go different ways, conflict follows and the kids can’t wait to get out.
Can a divided home still stand?

🎙 From the sermon “Jesus said these words. If they’re divided against themselves, they will not stand.” ▶ 12:16 “In the home, is it imperative that the husband and wife stand together with the same truth, the same moral standards? Is it important? And being an example to their children, not just telling their children about Jesus, but showing them in their life. Yes, it is. Why? Or the home isn’t going to stand.” ▶ 12:44 “Because the husband and wife go two different ways.” ▶ 13:13 Jesus said every kingdom, city and house divided against itself shall not stand (Matthew 12:25). Pastor Kincer says “stand” is a military word: an army that isn’t united loses the war. In the home, husband and wife must stand together with the same truth and moral standards, showing their children Jesus by their lives. When they go two different ways, conflict comes, and the kids can’t wait to get out.
Can a divided home still stand?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) Matthew 12:25 — But Jesus knew their thoughts, and said to them: “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.”

items.t: Do we want God’s blessings — or His rule?
items.d: God wants to rule our lives, not just bless them. Too many want heaven and His blessings without doing what He says.
p: God wants to rule our lives, not just bless them. Too many want heaven and His blessings without doing what He says.

Pastor Kincer says Israel rejected God and did what was right in their own eyes, and Jesus’ parable shows citizens refusing the king’s rule. People want God’s blessings and approval, he says, but God wants His Scriptures to rule their lives.
Do we want God’s blessings — or His rule?

🎙 From the sermon “God said to Samuel, they have rejected me that I should not rule over them. They haven’t rejected you, Samuel. They rejected me.” ▶ 10:36 “See, the people didn’t want God telling them what to do. Is that America? Yeah, we want to go to heaven. You see, we want his blessings. We want him to prosper us, but we don’t want to do what he tells us to do.” ▶ 10:45 “People want God’s blessings and God’s approval. But God wants to rule in their life. He wants the Scriptures to rule in their life, and they don’t want it.” ▶ 11:23 They rejected God, rejected the Scriptures, and did what they wanted in their own eyes. People want to go to heaven and want His blessings, but do not want to do what He tells them to do. Luke 19:14 says, “We will not have this man to reign over us.” People want God’s blessings and approval, but God wants to rule in their life — and He wants the Scriptures to rule in their life.
Do we want God’s blessings — or His rule?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) 1 Samuel 8:7 — And the LORD said to Samuel, “Heed the voice of the people in all that they say to you; for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected Me, that I should not reign over them.” Luke 19:14 — But his citizens hated him, and sent a delegation after him, saying, ‘We will not have this man to reign over us.’

items.d: No. Pastor Kincer says “be perfect” means spiritual maturity and completeness, not a life with no flaws.
p: No. Pastor Kincer says “be perfect” means spiritual maturity and completeness, not a life with no flaws.
Pastor Kincer says people hear “be perfect” and think it means never sinning. He points to Hebrews 5:14 and James 1:4 to show it is about growing up and being complete, lacking nothing.

🎙 From the sermon ““Be you therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” This is Jesus talking.” ▶ 16:08 “And they thought perfect was just living a life that had no flaws in it. No, it’s coming to what? Spiritual maturity, spiritual completeness.” ▶ 16:24 “Let patience have her perfect work, that you may be what? Perfect and entire, lacking what? Nothing.” ▶ 16:50

📖 Scripture (NKJV) Matthew 5:48 — Therefore you shall be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect. James 1:4 — But let patience have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking nothing. Hebrews 5:14 — But solid food belongs to those who are of full age, that is, those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.

items.t: What if my gifts are just noise?
items.d: Without love, even speaking in the languages of men and angels is just noise — a clanging cymbal.
p: Without love, even speaking in the languages of men and angels is just noise — a clanging cymbal.
Pastor Kincer explains Paul’s picture: a cymbal clanging by itself would drive you nuts in about 30 seconds. He says love is more important than both kinds of languages — men’s and angels’.
What if my gifts are just noise?

🎙 From the sermon “Though or if I speak with tongues of men and angels, but have not love, I am become a sounding brass or a clanging cymbal.” ▶ 0:23 “And if I had someone over there just clang the cymbals together, you know, in about 30 seconds, you would go, “You’re driving me nuts. What’s the point?”” ▶ 0:37 “There’s languages of men, like they spoke on the day of Pentecost. And there are languages of angels. But the key is love is more important than both of those.” ▶ 1:01
What if my gifts are just noise?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) 1 Corinthians 13:1 — Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal. 1 Corinthians 12:31 — But earnestly desire the best gifts. And yet I show you a more excellent way.

items.t: Does real love insist on its own way?
items.d: No. Real love doesn’t demand its own way. It wants the right way — the truth.
tg: love does not demand its own way
p: No. Real love doesn’t demand its own way. It wants the right way — the truth.
Pastor Kincer walks through Paul’s description of love: patient, kind, not proud or rude. Love doesn’t demand its own way in the family, the church or the community, and it keeps no record of wrongs.
Does real love insist on its own way?

🎙 From the sermon “Love does not seek its own way. Well, it’s going to be my way. I’m going to hit the highway. You know, love doesn’t demand its own way in the family, in the church, or in the community. It demands the right way, the truth.” ▶ 6:47 “Love is not easily provoked. It, you know, they’re not touchy. You know, if you don’t say the right thing or do the right thing, they’re all ticked off. And love doesn’t do that.” ▶ 7:03
Does real love insist on its own way?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) 1 Corinthians 13:4–5 — Love suffers long and is kind; love does not envy; love does not parade itself, is not puffed up; does not behave rudely, does not seek its own, is not provoked, thinks no evil.

items.t: Can I serve God and still miss knowing Him?
items.d: Yes. You can be used by God — even prophesy and do mighty works in Jesus’ name — and still miss the most important thing: love.
p: Yes. You can be used by God — even prophesy and do mighty works in Jesus’ name — and still miss the most important thing: love.

Pastor Kincer points to Jesus’ warning about people who prophesied and cast out demons in His name, yet hear “I never knew you.” He says they were used by God but missed love, which he describes as obeying God.
Can I serve God and still miss knowing Him?

🎙 From the sermon “See, love is to obey God. And he had the message, but he didn’t have the love.” ▶ 2:18 “See, they had faith to do all these things and these gifts and these spiritual manifestations were working in them. And Jesus said, “I will say to them, I never knew you.” Depart from me, you workers of iniquity.” ▶ 3:02 “You see, you didn’t have love. You might have been used of God to do things, but you missed the important thing, and that is love.” ▶ 3:14
Can I serve God and still miss knowing Him?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) Matthew 7:22–23 — Many will say to Me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in Your name, cast out demons in Your name, and done many wonders in Your name?’ And then I will declare to them, ‘I never knew you; depart from Me, you who practice lawlessness!’ 1 Corinthians 13:2 — And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.

items.t: What is the real goal of God’s Word?
items.d: Love from a pure heart. Paul says that is the goal of the commandment.
p: Love from a pure heart. Paul says that is the goal of the commandment.
Pastor Kincer says “end” in this verse means goal. We tend to think the goal is eternal life or the gifts of the Spirit, he says, but it is love.
What is the real goal of God’s Word?

🎙 From the sermon “Now the end of the commandment is love out of a pure heart. The word end means the goal. You see the goal of the word of God is love out of a pure heart.” ▶ 23:10 “See, we think it’s eternal life. No, you’re going to live eternally no matter what.” ▶ 23:41 “We think that it’s the gifts of the spirit in our circles.” ▶ 24:04 “And it’s not. It’s love. And that’s why we have such phoniness in the spirit-filled world as we try to push something that God isn’t doing.” ▶ 24:14
What is the real goal of God’s Word?
📖 Scripture (NKJV) 1 Timothy 1:5 — Now the purpose of the commandment is love from a pure heart, from a good conscience, and from sincere faith.

items.t: Is God looking for fruit — or fireworks?
items.d: Fruit comes first. Love is the first fruit of the Spirit and the peak of God’s character, and you can’t have the manifestations of the Spirit without it.
p: Fruit comes first. Love is the first fruit of the Spirit and the peak of God’s character, and you can’t have the manifestations of the Spirit without it.

Pastor Kincer notes that love is listed first among the fruit of the Spirit, that God is love, and that love sits at the top of sharing in the divine nature. His point: the fruit and character of God come before the manifestations.
Is God looking for fruit — or fireworks?

🎙 From the sermon “Love, joy, peace. It’s the first fruit. 1 John 4:8 says, “God is love.” See, that is exactly what God is. He just gave us the description of God.” ▶ 8:29 “So the love is at the peak of divine character and it’s at the beginning of the fruits of the spirit. And believe me, Paul is telling us, you can’t have the manifestations of the spirit without the fruit and the divine character of God. That’s what he’s telling us. This is the way to get it.” ▶ 9:01
Is God looking for fruit — or fireworks?

📖 Scripture (NKJV) Galatians 5:22–23 — But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Against such there is no law. 1 John 4:8 — He who does not love does not know God, for God is love.
